# GMT-inspired shader improvements for RFF_Super

> **Final review entry point (2026-10-08):** [Improving RFF_Super with GMT as a reference](GMT_to_RFF_Review_EN.md). All 3,727 inventoried GMT files have completed inspection records and unchanged hashes. This companion preserves chronological evidence: earlier progress counts, pending review statements and provisional priorities describe their recording time, not current coverage. Later corrections and the final entry point govern recommendations. Source inspection does not establish runtime correctness or measured GPU benefit.

This is the target-facing adoption plan accompanying the [broader review](GMT_Fractals_Feature_Review_EN.md). It distinguishes useful mechanisms from GMT implementation defects. Scores estimate incremental benefit to RFF users, not GMT quality or measured speed. Source inspection is ongoing; no application code is changed and no GPU performance result is claimed.

## Provisional top ten beyond bloom: visible benefit to RFF

This ordering answers the requested ranking of shader-related appearance improvements beyond bloom. It is an engineering judgment from the inspected code, not a measured speed ranking or the numerical ordering of the broader workflow scores below. Relief appearance is the primary criterion; for flat 2D, footprint filtering takes precedence over environment reflection. Source/host integration is included where required, and unresolved capability checks remain explicit in the detailed sections.

| Rank | Incremental proposal | Main visible benefit | 2D applicability |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Editable gradient/image environment with roughness-aware reflection | Directional bright bands and colored reflections emphasize relief and material character | Existing relief normals; no 3D fractal conversion |
| 2 | Footprint-aware filtering of image layers | Reduce minification/warp aliasing and animation shimmer | Flat and relief |
| 3 | Reusable field-driven material masks | Selectively vary roughness and material amounts across fractal bands | Primarily relief, with reusable 2D masks |
| 4 | Independent U/V field selection | Two-variable image/color lookups beyond fixed coordinate pairs | Flat and relief |
| 5 | Field histogram with palette-range assistance | Place palette variation over the intended field range | Flat and relief; requires authoring controls |
| 6 | Palette/image emission-source routing | Use a chosen pattern as self-illumination independently of paint visibility | Flat and relief; no implied indirect lighting |
| 7 | Vector-noise warp of decorative coordinates | Flowing and marbled image/pattern structures | Flat and relief; distinguish from existing turbulence |
| 8 | Additional independently colored/directed lights | More deliberate multicolor highlight placement | Relief; remaining control overlap must be checked |
| 9 | Mirror/sector repetition of decorative coordinates | Reusable radial and kaleidoscopic patterns | Flat and relief |
| 10 | Logarithmic spiral color/image transform | Radius-dependent spiral patterning | Flat and relief; screen-anchored scope first |

Existing GGX, clearcoat, procedural emission, image layers and shader-layer ordering are foundations, not missing features. Image-derived palette authoring and render-channel inspection remain valuable broader workflow proposals but are outside this particular ten-effect ordering. Implemented/measured benefit is not claimed.
## Current priorities

| Proposal | Existing RFF capability | Actual additional work | Difficulty / 10 | Effectiveness / 10 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Continuous bloom threshold knee | Bloom, sharp/blurred mixing, linear-light/HDR paths | Continuous highlight extraction shared by sharp and blurred components | 4.2 | 8.1 |
| Field histogram with palette-range assistance | Double-precision iteration buffer, palette curves; contrast histogram for adaptive shading | User-facing field distribution, robust range selection, freeze/apply workflow | 5.8 | 8.2 |
| Inspect/export render channels | Multiple shader inputs and existing relief/material effects | Named, documented views of selected fields with masks and export semantics; full channel availability still to inventory | 6.8 | 8.6 |
| Broader field-driven material masks | Ordered shader layers, rim masks, procedural decoration | Reusable masks with consistent sampling and layer composition; exact missing controls still to establish | 7.0 | 8.2 |
| Gradient/image environment for relief materials | Existing two-color hemispheric environment and GGX/clearcoat | Editable directional lighting/reflection source with roughness-aware filtering | 7.1 | 8.3 |
| Footprint-aware image-layer filtering | Final-image downsampling and bilinear image-layer sampling | Mip storage, matching samplers and field-aware footprints across fragment/compute paths | 6.7 | 8.4 |
| Prepare replacements before switching shader modes | Specialization constants, asynchronous preparation and progress reporting | Retain a valid pipeline/state while building its replacement; bounded reuse and stale-result rejection | 7.4 | 8.0 |

For an isolated shader improvement, **the bloom knee is the clearest current candidate**. For a broader creative workflow, **field inspection plus histogram-guided palette mapping offers more reach**, but needs more integration. These are provisional engineering priorities, not claims of benchmark superiority.

## A. Continuous bloom extraction

RFF's [threshold pass](../shdsrc/vk_bloom_threshold.frag) uses a binary brightness comparison. Its [composition pass](../shdsrc/vk_bloom.frag) repeats the comparison for sharp glow, then blends sharp and blurred signals using Softness. Existing sRGB transfer helpers and scene-linear/HDR handling must be retained.

GMT's reference mechanism is a bright pass followed by a multi-resolution blur. Borrow the goal of a gradual knee, not its defective ramp: S26 in the [deep audit](GMT_Fractals_Deep_Code_Audit_EN.md) demonstrates a discontinuity in GMT's extraction. Define one continuous extraction function for both RFF sites, with knee zero reproducing the legacy threshold. Keep Softness as the existing sharp/blur mixture; introducing a knee must not silently reinterpret that saved control.

Expected benefit: less abrupt bloom onset on narrow filaments and during palette animation. Validate a brightness sweep, a moving subpixel highlight, preview/video agreement, and bloom-disabled identity. Specify whether threshold operates in the current stored color domain or linear light; do not silently change that along with the knee. New saved settings must follow append-only ConfigIO rules.

## B. Field histogram and palette-range assistance

### What GMT contributes

GMT separates geometry-derived values from image luminance. Its coloring panel displays a value histogram with a palette range, repeat count, phase and bias. A selected interval [a,b] is mapped using `scale=repeats/(b-a)` and `offset=phase-a*scale`. Changing repeats/phase can preserve the selected interval. That workflow makes an otherwise abstract mapping understandable and repeatable.

Relevant source: [worker readback](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/worker/WorkerHistogram.ts), [coloring range logic](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/components/panels/gradient/ColoringHistogram.tsx), [analysis/range helper](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/histogramUtils.ts), and [probe scheduling](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/components/HistogramProbe.tsx). This is a source-level workflow comparison, not a screenshot-based UI audit.

### What RFF already provides

[vk_iteration_palette.frag](../shdsrc/vk_iteration_palette.frag) reads existing iteration data, distinguishes the zero/interior path, applies animation/warp and optional escape-angle offsets, and evaluates the palette. [palette_sampling.glsl](../shdsrc/palette_sampling.glsl) contains double-precision coloring curves and row-oriented iteration access. Only the cited sections of this large shared file were inspected for this comparison; complete host/buffer ownership remains to be audited.

### Proposed integration

1. **Define the analyzed field.** Start with valid exterior iteration values before palette animation. Offer display-luminance analysis as a distinct view. Record exclusions for interior/max-iteration, unfinished, invalid and nonfinite data according to the producer's actual validity contract; a single numerical sentinel is insufficient until those contracts are traced.
2. **Read existing data.** Add a separate compute reduction over the existing iteration buffer. Do not run new reference orbits or bypass MPA. Compute the normalized bin coordinate in double precision before conversion to a small integer; large nearby iteration values must not collapse through an early float conversion.
3. **Keep counts separate from presentation.** Store raw counts for percentiles/CDF. Draw logarithmic-height bars only as a display choice. Use local workgroup histograms and merge them if profiling shows global atomic contention. Handle count capacity explicitly for large output images.
4. **Connect to palette semantics.** Show a suggested interval and let the user apply it to the current curve/cycle controls. GMT's affine formula is exact for an affine mapping, but RFF also supports nonlinear coloring curves, separate channel intervals, warps, animation freeze and angle shifts. Define which stage the interval controls and evaluate that same stage for the preview; do not force a linear scale onto all modes.
5. **Make updates predictable.** Tag results by frame/field/settings generation; reject stale completions. Refresh after meaningful field changes or on demand, with at most one outstanding request. Keep range fitting explicit or frozen during video so the palette does not pump from frame-to-frame distribution changes. An optional animated adaptation needs its own temporal policy.

An optional later CDF-equalized mapping is separate from fitting an interval. It would redistribute color according to data density and change the character of existing bands; preserve it as a new mode with an explicit source distribution and frozen/video behavior.

### What not to copy from GMT

- GMT's helper first log-normalizes bucket heights, then its smart-range function accumulates those displayed heights as mass. That is a visual heuristic, not a percentile of raw pixel counts. Preserve raw counts if the control promises percentiles.
- `val > -0.9` treats a numeric interval as invalid based on a background sentinel; generic fields can have valid negative values. Explicit masks are safer.
- The inspected geometry histogram rerenders an approximate scene, including fixed normals and projection differences (S17). RFF can avoid that mismatch by reducing its already rendered field.
- GMT's request loop uses every 60 animation frames, not a fixed elapsed-time interval, and does not itself prevent overlapping requests or invalidate late callbacks. Borrow asynchronous feedback, not this exact scheduling policy.

### Verification criteria

Use analytically countable buffers: constant fields, two populations with strongly unequal counts, valid negative values for generic channels, all-invalid input and values separated only in double precision. Verify crop/row orientation against the displayed field. Confirm no change to orbit/MPA results, no render-thread stall from readback, and deterministic frozen ranges in video export. These checks are proposed; this document does not claim an implemented RFF histogram feature.

## C. Do not duplicate existing texture and material work

RFF's palette pass already invokes image textures, procedural patterns, iteration-band gradients, warp offsets and escape-angle color shifts. Its ordered shader-layer controls and relief masks also exist. Consequently "add textures", "add GGX" or "add shader layers" is not an adequate recommendation.

The targeted comparison below establishes a concrete U/V extension beyond the four inspected modes. Orbit-wide traps remain different from the already present escape endpoint angle and require acceleration-compatible statistics; they are not a cheap shader-only toggle.

Full 3D raymarching/path tracing remains low priority for this 2D target. Useful transfers are field organization, masks, stable filtering and authoring tools. Preserve the high-precision perturbation/reference/MPA pipeline and verify Vulkan descriptor/push-constant agreements whenever the display pipeline is extended.

## D. Independent field selection for image coordinates

**Verified existing RFF behavior:** [ShdTextureUVMode.h](../src/rff2/attr/ShdTextureUVMode.h) defines four paired coordinate modes: cycle/angle, cycle/screen, screen/screen and cycle/band direction. The `decor_uv` implementation in [palette_sampling.glsl](../shdsrc/palette_sampling.glsl) implements those pairs and uses full-canvas coordinates for tile continuity. [ShdTextureAttribute.h](../src/rff2/attr/ShdTextureAttribute.h) already supports four image layers, independent axis scale/scroll, opacity, palette-follow, an independent iteration period, image size and aspect preservation. The sampled image alpha already controls layer coverage. These are existing strengths to keep.

**GMT reference mechanism:** [texturing.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/texturing.ts) exposes independently chosen U and V mapping fields. Its [getTextureColor](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/coloring.ts) obtains two mapping values, scales/offsets them and samples a 2D image. In RFF this can act as a two-variable color lookup, not merely a photograph pasted over the fractal.

**Concrete added expression:** choose U from iteration cycle and V from escape endpoint angle. A lookup image can then use horizontal position for escape progression and vertical position for angular structure, allowing independent hue/value families for different escape directions. This differs from RFF's existing escape-angle *offset of a one-dimensional palette*: the two values remain independent coordinates instead of being added together. Other useful pairs include cycle/gradient magnitude, gradient direction/screen radius and screen X/cycle. The exact channels available on each render/export path must still be verified before enabling each option.

**Implementation outline:**

1. Add an advanced field-pair mode while preserving existing mode identifiers and exact old mappings. Use per-axis field selection with an explicit domain contract (periodic angle, unbounded iteration, normalized screen position, bounded strength).
2. Read the existing iteration/angle/gradient data where available. Endpoint angle is already consumed by the palette shader, but availability across saved maps and every perturbator/export path is not yet proven. Disable unavailable choices with a reason rather than silently substituting zero. New orbit-wide traps are outside this shader-only first scope.
3. Preserve double precision until the periodic iteration coordinate has been reduced. Apply scale, wrap and scroll afterward. Keep full-output screen coordinates so tiled export does not repeat the projection per tile.
4. Treat angular endpoints as a seam: periodic filtering and repeat counts must agree. For highly compressed field coordinates, derive texture footprints from field variation or a suitable sampled approximation; do not automatically inherit GMT's fixed base-LOD sampling.
5. Revisit aspect-fit semantics for arbitrary field pairs. A cycle/angle cell has no universal physical aspect ratio. Keep existing fit behavior for old modes and provide an explicit new-mode policy instead of silently reusing screen-space assumptions.

**Difficulty 6.3 / effectiveness 7.9.** This is a concrete creative addition, with no requirement to replace MPA or introduce 3D rendering. The cost is mainly display-field plumbing, mapping semantics, filtering, editor controls and persistence. Preserve the four-layer descriptor budget unless there is a separately justified change. Append saved fields under the existing binary format rules and align host/shader layouts.

**Verification:** a known 2D lookup image whose axes have distinguishable colors; each supported field pair; negative/wrapped angles; large iteration values with small differences; zero gradients; missing angle buffers; old-scene image identity; preview/video and single/tiled export agreement. Measure additional gradient fetches and reuse the palette pass's existing band gradient when possible. This proposal is based on actual source differences, not a claim that the full feature is implemented or tested.

## E. Field-driven material controls, extending existing relief

**Existing RFF implementation:** [studio_surface.glsl](../shdsrc/studio_surface.glsl) already evaluates GGX-related lighting, metalness, IOR, clearcoat, iridescent tint and environment response. Roughness is modified by wetness and normal variance; material behavior is not uniformly constant already. [chrome_surface.glsl](../shdsrc/chrome_surface.glsl) also blends multiple native material styles, preserves moving/held palette cycles, and applies detail-density/flat-region treatments. The inspected functions consume global layer amounts and dedicated masks rather than a generic user-selected field source per material property. This is a bounded source observation, not a claim that every RFF material control has been inventoried.

**GMT reference:** the inspected `MATERIAL_LOGIC` in [materials.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/materials.ts) selects emission from final albedo, layer 1, layer 2, procedural noise or a fixed color. Its [shared material evaluator](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/material_eval.ts) assembles those channels before material overrides. The transferable idea is **explicit source selection and shared evaluation**. GMT's inspected roughness remains a global scalar; a general roughness-mask editor is an extension proposed here, not a feature falsely attributed to GMT.

### Useful RFF additions

- **Roughness by band/field:** make selected iteration-band regions polished and others matte without changing palette colors. A scalar field passes through a range/soft-edge remap and mixes low/high roughness values.
- **Material amount by field:** restrict an existing metal/frost/print layer to a selected range, using the same mask consistently in ordered and combined compositions. This is more general than introducing another global opacity control.
- **Emission source selection:** let an existing image/palette field supply independently controlled self-illumination. RFF already has procedural-effect emission and band glow; the concrete increment is reusable source routing, described below. This is distinct from threshold bloom, which derives glow from finished brightness.

For a mask m in [0,1], `property=mix(low,high,m)` is only the parameter-selection step. Roughness interpolation needs a declared convention (artist/perceptual roughness versus microfacet alpha); retain the convention already used by the RFF BRDF. Apply variance-based broadening after resolving the intended base roughness, and keep the clearcoat's independent lobe policy. Do not average arbitrary final material colors and call that an equivalent BRDF mixture.

### Integration boundary

Create a small shared field-sampling/remapping layer usable by texture coordinates, histogram preview and material masks. Begin with already available iteration cycle, band direction/magnitude and supported endpoint angle, with explicit validity. Reuse computed gradients instead of adding separate neighbor taps for every consumer. A mask-off path must preserve old output and avoid additional sampling. Animated masks must respect the existing moving/held cycle split rather than bypassing animation freeze.

Avoid inserting distinct copies of the whole material graph for each property or layer. RFF already shares material evaluation to limit shader expansion; preserve that architecture and profile compilation as well as frame time. New data must fit the current descriptor/push-constant/UBO contracts and be added to persistence compatibly. Keep actual scene illumination/emission separate from preview-only mask visualization.

**Difficulty 7.0 / effectiveness 8.2** for reusable field-driven material control. A single band-mask prototype would be cheaper, but does not establish the whole integration. The user benefit is selective polished/matte and multi-material patterning on the existing 2D relief renderer, without adopting GMT's 3D raymarcher.

**Verification:** mask=0/1 endpoints; smooth transitions and periodic seams; old presets unchanged with masks disabled; constant fields and invalid/interior pixels; ordered versus combined layer behavior; animation freeze; preview/video/tile agreement; and extra texture/field fetch counts. For emission, test a dark unlit source with bloom off/on so self-illumination is not confused with a post-process glow.

### Emission follow-up: existing functions and the actual missing connection

[ShdEffectsAttribute.h](../src/rff2/attr/ShdEffectsAttribute.h) already defines four effect layers, glow strength, two colors, masks and composition modes. [effects.glsl](../shdsrc/effects.glsl) carries an explicit `SurfaceEffects.emission`; flame, embers, flow and aurora paths generate emission from procedural coverage and tint. `surface_effect_finish` adds it separately from the tinted base and wetness reflection. [band_decoration.glsl](../shdsrc/band_decoration.glsl), `apply_band_decoration`, also adds band glow in linear light. Existing sea/material styles contain additional appearance-specific glow. Thus "add self-illumination" would duplicate existing work.

GMT's `MATERIAL_LOGIC` selects final albedo, the first or second coloring layer, procedural noise color, or a fixed color, then multiplies the selected RGB by an emission amount. Its [material evaluator](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/material_eval.ts) evaluates the second layer/noise when needed for emission even if it is not contributing to visible albedo. This dependency is the useful detail: a source may be hidden as paint while remaining active as an emitter. The inspected RFF effect attributes do not offer that generic palette/image source selection; the recommendation is limited to that verified comparison.

For RFF, start with a nonrecursive source contract: fixed color, palette color before lighting, or a selected image-layer sample. Reuse the same UV mapping, alpha coverage, filtering and animation phase as its ordinary image path. Define explicitly whether source opacity participates. Turning off visible painting must not automatically invalidate an explicitly referenced emission source; conversely an absent image must yield no emission, not the placeholder white texel. Use stable layer identifiers and a defined missing-source state when loading presets.

A conceptual new emission channel is `E = intensity * mask * coverage * sourceLinearRGB`. Add E at a documented composition point before the intended tone map and optional bloom, preserving the existing handling for old effects. This equation defines a proposed channel, not a replacement for all legacy blend modes. Do not sample the final image including its own emission or bloom as the source: that creates feedback and ambiguous ordering. Prefer a shared source evaluator over retaining every intermediate layer in a full-resolution image; measure extra fetches and only introduce a cached channel when justified.

The inspected [vk_slope.frag](../shdsrc/vk_slope.frag) calls the effect finish in both linear and encoded paths, and one encoded branch clamps the result to [0,1]. Integration must trace those consumers so a new HDR emission value is not accidentally clipped early, converted twice or added twice in ordered composition. Raising an existing procedural glow slider is not equivalent to adding this routing feature. Keep source evaluation and emission application distinct so the palette source can be reused without re-evaluating fractal orbits.

**3D-to-2D boundary:** direct self-illumination and downstream bloom transfer naturally. GMT's path-tracing-only emission multiplier scales contributions on indirect bounces; it has no equivalent in RFF's ordinary 2D relief pipeline. Do not promise that an emitting band physically lights adjacent bands. A screen-space light-spread effect would be a separately named approximation, not transported 3D illumination.

**Emission-routing subproposal: difficulty 6.6 / effectiveness 7.8.** Validate visible layer off/emitter on, missing source, zero intensity, alpha-zero colored texels, palette freeze and animation, ordered stacking, linear/HDR and legacy paths, and bloom disabled. Compare the source pattern against the ordinary layer lookup before judging the glow. Exact host controls and persistence plumbing remain to be inspected; this is not an implemented feature.

## F. Channel inspection and selective export

**GMT reference:** the inspected [WorkerExporter](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/worker/WorkerExporter.ts) branches between beauty, alpha and depth outputs, and image-sequence export can loop over selected passes. Its [post shader](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/post_process.ts) bypasses beauty tone mapping for auxiliary outputs. Borrow explicit output semantics and selection, not its exact alpha implementation (see S13).

**Existing RFF evidence:** [RFFDynamicMapBinary.h](../src/rff2/io/RFFDynamicMapBinary.h) already exposes double iteration matrices and lossless compressed-map operations. Raw iteration saving is therefore not new functionality. [vk_slope.frag](../shdsrc/vk_slope.frag) consumes a double iteration SSBO and a float relief cache, derives local gradients/AO and computes `materialNormal`; the inspected output remains an RGBA color. Those locally computed quantities are not automatically persistent images. [SharedImageContextIndices.hpp](../src/rff2/vulkan/SharedImageContextIndices.hpp) names primary/secondary/downsampled color targets and a shading-rate image, not a ready-made normal/AO channel set. This is evidence for implementation planning, not proof that every diagnostic UI/export path is absent.

### Proposed output set and its purpose

| Channel | User benefit | Semantic requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Iteration/selected palette field preview | Understand why colors occupy particular regions | Keep existing raw map export; preview normalization is separate and recorded |
| Exterior/interior/invalid mask | Select regions for external compositing or inspect unfinished data | Trace actual validity producers; never classify invalid pixels as set interior merely because a value is zero |
| Relief normal | Tune light direction and detect shading artifacts | Identify coordinate handedness, axis signs and whether procedural/groove perturbations are included |
| AO factor | Separate cavity shading from palette darkness | Export the actual scalar used by the chosen shading path, before tint/composition |
| Selected material mask | Tune the proposed field-driven material controls | Define coverage, remap range and animation state; retain invalid masks |
| Shading-rate preview | Explain adaptive-quality decisions | Mark as a diagnostic, not a property of the fractal |

Do not call a normalized iteration field or relief scalar "camera depth". GMT's 3D ray distance has no direct counterpart in RFF's ordinary 2D view. If height is exported, name the exact derived relief function and scale; it is not geometric depth reconstructed from the 2D Mandelbrot set.

### Implementation and cost

Select a diagnostic output at the stage where its value already exists, or reconstruct it using the same shared helper when cheap. A normal preview must not use a different gradient formula from the beauty renderer. Start with one selected channel; do not allocate a full G-buffer merely to display a scalar. One RGBA32F image at 3840x2160 occupies approximately 126.6 MiB before allocator overhead, so always-on multi-channel images can add significant memory pressure.

For exports, reuse the computed iteration map across channels and record a stable settings/frame snapshot. If extra shading passes are needed, run those without recomputing perturbation/reference orbits. Preserve image barriers, descriptor layouts and preview/export resource ownership. Treat display diagnostics and data files separately: a normal encoded as `0.5*n+0.5` for an image is a representation, and a tone-mapped/dithered screenshot is not a raw vector buffer. Pick precision and file format explicitly; no new codec or format implementation is implied by this proposal.

**Difficulty 6.8 / effectiveness 8.6** for inspection plus selected channel export. This supports palette design, material-mask authoring and external compositing while making the existing renderer easier to diagnose. It has higher integration cost than the bloom knee but benefits several proposed improvements.

**Verification:** normal axes on simple analytic fields; constant AO/masks; interior/invalid separation; data outputs bypass grade, tone map and dither; correct row orientation; identical channel meaning across live/video/tile paths; repeated exports from a frozen state; and no increase in fractal iteration work when switching inspection views. Full host-side capture/persistence paths still require detailed inspection before implementation.

## G. Editable environment illumination for 2D relief

**Verified target difference:** RFF's [studio_environment](../shdsrc/studio_ggx.glsl) rotates a reflection direction and linearly blends two colors, sky and ground, multiplied by 0.12. [studio_surface](../shdsrc/studio_surface.glsl) already uses this environment for both the base surface and clearcoat, with Fresnel and intensity controls. The existing helper takes no roughness input. This is a useful low-cost lighting model, but cannot represent an artist-drawn bright stripe, several colored regions or a panorama's directional detail.

GMT's [environment shader](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/lighting/env.ts) and [material settings](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/materials.ts) provide solid, gradient and panorama sources. The panorama is sampled from reflection direction; roughness selects filtering, and a separate light-strength control decouples illumination from backdrop visibility. These are useful mechanisms for RFF even though its underlying fractal is 2D: its relief normal already defines a direction for reflecting an environment.

**Visible benefit:** move a bright strip through existing metallic bands, create warm/cool reflection zones, and art-direct glossy or coated appearances without changing the palette or adding actual 3D geometry. The reflection is of a lighting environment, not of neighboring fractal geometry. No path tracer or additional fractal orbit computation is needed.

### Proposed scope

1. Preserve the current two-color environment as the default legacy mode. Add an editable multi-stop gradient source first; reuse suitable palette-authoring infrastructure after checking its resource and persistence contracts. A gradient provides controllable lighting bands with less asset complexity than a panorama.
2. Add an optional image source with explicit projection, orientation, color interpretation, intensity and asset persistence. Do not claim HDR image support merely because the shader can store HDR values; audit the decoder/upload/export path before exposing that format capability.
3. Feed base roughness and clearcoat roughness separately to environment evaluation. Distinguish roughness filtering from minification filtering. A simple mip chain is an artistic approximation, not automatically the GGX-convolved environment used by the direct BRDF. Choose and document either that approximation or a prefiltered environment plus an appropriate integrated BRDF response.
4. Keep illumination independent of visible background. RFF's interior color and background semantics must not be silently replaced by a sky. An optional backdrop is a separate display feature; environment intensity zero should preserve the existing absence of environment illumination.
5. Include scene-linear/HDR behavior, per-frame resource lifetime and additional sampler bindings in the design. Cache preprocessing by source/filter settings; rotating the environment should not regenerate the texture. Validate video and tiled export against the same source and orientation.

GMT's pole/seam filtering and solid-angle average are useful subjects to study, but its CDF sampler is unnecessary for deterministic RFF lookup. Do not import the entire path-tracing importance-sampling stack. Likewise keep the original source/license record for any distinctive filtering implementation rather than copying shader constants under a generic technique name.

**Host-setting follow-up:** the complete `materials.ts` read confirms that panorama assets request generated mipmaps and trilinear minification, with a separately linked color-profile setting. Sky source definition remains independent of the visibility and illumination consumers; switching off one consumer does not make the asset irrelevant to the others. This supports a shared source asset with explicit consumer strengths in RFF. It does not establish HDR decoder compatibility by itself. The inspected feature also scales the direct-render environment control by 0.33 through a header macro; that is GMT's appearance calibration, not a lighting constant to copy into RFF. Preserve RFF's established default calibration and define any new mode's intensity convention explicitly.

**Difficulty 7.1 / effectiveness 8.3** for gradient plus image environment with reliable filtering and persistence. A gradient-only version would be smaller in scope; do not present it as completion of panorama support. This is one of the stronger 3D-to-2D appearance transfers because RFF already supplies the relief/material foundation.

**Verification:** a constant environment preserves constant radiance under rotation; a labeled directional panorama verifies axes and seams; increasing roughness broadens detail under the chosen filter contract; base and clearcoat use their own roughness; intensity-zero and legacy modes preserve old presets; bright HDR sources survive until the intended tone-mapping stage; and rotations agree across preview/video/tile paths. Performance and visual benefit remain to be measured in RFF.

## H. Footprint-aware filtering for existing image layers

**Target benefit:** reduce texture shimmer, moire and unstable fine detail when an image is compressed into narrow iteration bands or animated across them. This improves existing RFF texture features; it does not require a new fractal formula or a 3D renderer. The artifacts are a predicted consequence of the inspected sampling path, not a claim of a reproduced visual failure.

### Verified RFF baseline

- [TextureDescriptor.cpp](../src/rff2/vulkan/TextureDescriptor.cpp), `uploadImage`, decodes RGBA bytes into `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM` and calls `imageFromByteColorArray` with `useMipmap=false`. The [upload helper](../src/vulkan_helper/util/BufferImageContextUtils.hpp) already has an optional mip-generation path; its existence does not establish that its filter/color semantics meet this proposal.
- [GPCIterationPalette.cpp](../src/rff2/vulkan/GPCIterationPalette.cpp) and [CPC2MapIterationStripe.cpp](../src/rff2/vulkan/CPC2MapIterationStripe.cpp) create repeating, bilinear samplers with nearest mip selection, `maxLod=0` and anisotropy disabled.
- [palette_sampling.glsl](../shdsrc/palette_sampling.glsl), `sample_texture_layer`, explicitly samples level zero for all four layers. `apply_texture` wraps the field coordinates, applies image-size/aspect fitting and rejects samples outside the fitted image. The same sampling helper also supplies an image-driven palette warp.
- [vk_resample.frag](../shdsrc/vk_resample.frag) already integrates multiple samples over the final output footprint, with an exact area-overlap branch for very large reductions. Do not propose generic final-image downsampling as a missing feature. Later resampling cannot reliably remove aliasing already introduced while looking up the texture in the initial render.

Changing only the shader LOD would therefore be insufficient: the uploaded image has no mip chain and both inspected samplers clamp to zero.

### GMT mechanism and its 3D-to-2D translation

GMT's [environment shader](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/lighting/env.ts) estimates how many environment texels a ray cone covers, converts that span to a mip level with `log2`, and uses the larger of the footprint and roughness demands. Near the base level it optionally uses four bilinear taps to reconstruct a cubic B-spline filter, with a continuous transition to mip sampling. The important transferable mechanism is **choosing a filtering scale from the region represented by one output pixel**. Its ordinary [material image lookup](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/coloring.ts) still uses `textureLod0`; do not claim GMT already implements this solution for all material textures.

For RFF there is no ray cone to trace. Estimate the change of the selected two-dimensional field coordinates across one output pixel. For unwrapped coordinates `q`, image dimensions `(W,H)`, and pixel-coordinate differences `qx` and `qy`, a practical isotropic estimate is:

```text
gx = (W, H) * qx
gy = (W, H) * qy
rho = max(length(gx), length(gy))
lod = clamp(log2(max(rho, 1)), 0, lastMip)
```

This is a practical footprint approximation, not exact integration of nonlinear field mappings. For a strongly elongated footprint it can blur the narrow axis excessively; evaluate anisotropic sampling or a bounded multi-tap alternative only after the basic path is correct. Ordinary color-image minification needs no material-roughness term. The environment proposal in section G needs both kinds of filtering, with its own approximation contract.

### Concrete implementation requirements

1. **Coordinate upload, sampler and shader changes.** Allocate and initialize a full image/view mip chain, allow its levels in both samplers, and pass an explicit footprint or LOD to the common sampling helper. Check image-format capabilities and the actual mip generator's barriers/usages before selecting a GPU blit path. Preserve a working fallback. Small and one-pixel images must remain valid.
2. **Estimate footprints before discontinuous operations.** Derive periodic coordinate differences before `fract`; crossing the wrap boundary must not look like a nearly full-image jump. Preserve double precision through iteration differences and periodic reduction. Include scale, image fit, aspect and domain-warp variation in the final footprint. Angular fields need a local seam-aware difference; a shortest-angle difference alone cannot recover multiple turns within one pixel.
3. **Support both shader stages deliberately.** Fragment derivatives must be evaluated in a suitable uniform execution region before divergent layer/interior/crop decisions. Do not replace explicit sampling with an implicit lookup inside the current layer control flow. The compute export path needs explicit finite differences or an analytically supplied footprint unless an appropriate derivative capability is deliberately introduced and validated. Define differences in output-pixel units so live, video and tiled renders agree.
4. **Filter coverage as well as color.** The fitted image currently has a hard in/out test. Texture mips alone will not antialias that cell boundary. Resolve image coverage over the footprint, respecting the intended repeated-cell gap. Build alpha-aware levels with a declared color-space contract; if premultiplied storage is used, adapt the existing straight-color blending and image-warp consumers consistently. Averaging hidden RGB in transparent texels can create colored fringes.
5. **Separate color filtering from warp semantics.** An image used as a displacement field currently mixes luminance toward the neutral midpoint using alpha. Filtering that field can change the palette displacement, not just smooth the overlaid image. Specify whether its levels represent the effective scalar field or filtered color/alpha, and compare against supersampled displacement evaluation. Filtering a nonlinear warped lookup is not generally equivalent to evaluating it at a filtered displacement.
6. **Preserve established output.** Provide a compatibility mode for saved scenes if the new filter changes their appearance. Keep the existing four texture bindings and high-precision fractal data. A full mip chain for a large square power-of-two image adds about one third of its base texel storage; elongated images have a different ratio. Account for four layers and asset replacement lifetimes rather than assuming this is free.

The cubic magnification filter is a separate optional refinement. It may smooth visible texel transitions when a small image is enlarged, but it cannot replace minification filtering. If adopting GMT's recognizable four-tap formulation, verify the original source and license and record provenance in `NOTICE`; the source comment alone is not license clearance. No external filtering code is copied by this proposal.

**Difficulty 6.7 / effectiveness 8.4.** This is a strong candidate for image-heavy animated scenes and a prerequisite for reliable independent-field U/V mapping. Its effect is smaller for scenes without image layers. The bloom knee remains the smaller isolated change; footprint filtering addresses a broader sampling problem with more host/shader integration.

**Verification:** compare against a high-sample reference using checkerboards, thin colored lines and transparent edges; test slow scrolling, zooming, strongly unequal U/V compression, angular seams, fitted-image gaps and image-driven warp. Compare identical output resolutions across fragment preview and compute/video paths, including tile boundaries. Verify constant-image preservation, old-mode identity and large-iteration coordinate stability. Measure GPU time, load time and memory separately. No implementation, rendered comparison or performance measurement has been performed for this proposal.

## I. Prepare shader-mode replacements while retaining a valid display

**Existing RFF capability:** [ShaderModeSpecialization.hpp](../src/rff2/vulkan/ShaderModeSpecialization.hpp) already packs smoothing, stripe, animation, decoration, freeze and dither choices into specialization words. The shared palette shader selects specialized constants or uniform-driven behavior. Decoration is conservatively enabled if any image, pattern or warp might need it. Consequently, neither "add specialization" nor "remove disabled shader branches" is a new recommendation.

[PipelinePreparation.hpp](../src/vulkan_helper/impl/PipelinePreparation.hpp) already supports asynchronous creation jobs, batches, elapsed-time observers and paint-message processing while waiting. [Pipeline.hpp](../src/vulkan_helper/impl/Pipeline.hpp), however, implements a changed `respecialize` request by finishing prior preparation, waiting for device idle, destroying the current pipeline, replacing its specialization words and initializing again. Identical words with a valid pipeline return early. Graphics and compute creation sites already obtain a Vulkan pipeline-cache handle. A driver pipeline cache is not the same as retaining ready-to-bind pipeline objects for recently used configurations.

### GMT's useful scheduling mechanism

[CompileScheduler.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/CompileScheduler.ts) and [ADR-0040](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/adr/0040-two-stage-shader-compile.md) distinguish keeping the current material, temporarily using a cheaper preview, and a single-stage fallback. The scheduler coalesces configuration messages, builds a full material separately, checks a generation number before publishing it, then swaps and synchronizes the new material's parameter mapping. A stale completed material is disposed instead of replacing the latest request. It records source-generation, compilation and first-draw timings separately.

Transfer the ownership and scheduling principles, not browser APIs, fixed delays or GMT's reported timings. RFF's Vulkan architecture and existing asynchronous preparation are the starting point. The primary benefit is smoother editing while a new shader mode is prepared; steady-state rendering is not automatically faster.

### Concrete RFF extension

1. **Build a replacement object rather than mutate the active one.** Keep the current pipeline handle and compatible descriptor/settings snapshot alive until the new pipeline is ready. Existing asynchronous lambdas capture their owning object; a replacement design must own all creation inputs, specialization backing memory and resource references until completion. Do not merely remove `waitDeviceIdle` from the existing destructive operation.
2. **Publish one coherent render generation.** Commit the new pipeline together with settings that match its baked modes at a frame boundary. Updating a uniform for a newly selected mode while the active pipeline still contains the previous mode can show a mismatched result. Either keep the prior coherent appearance temporarily or use a previously prepared compatible generic pipeline that evaluates the new uniform settings. The generic route is a candidate because the shader supports uniform fallback, not a verified ready-made host feature.
3. **Coalesce mode changes and reject stale results.** Key requests by shader identity, specialization words and all relevant pipeline compatibility state. A generation change makes an old result ineligible for publication; it does not necessarily cancel a driver call already in progress. Bound concurrent jobs and deduplicate identical requests. A short quiet period may help interactive toggles, but do not import GMT's 200 ms delay as a universal optimum.
4. **Retain a bounded set of useful completed variants.** Reusing a ready pipeline can avoid rebuilding when users alternate between familiar modes. Use a complete compatibility key and a memory/count budget; driver cache availability alone does not establish this reuse. Synchronize shared creation/cache access according to the actual host implementation. Cache invalidation must include shader or layout changes, not just the mode words.
5. **Retire resources after GPU use completes.** Keep old handles until submitted command buffers no longer reference them. Frame completion or an appropriate deferred-deletion mechanism must prove that lifetime. Preserve safe shutdown, resize and device-error behavior. This requires host-side ownership work beyond changing shader text.
6. **Use different publication rules for editing and export.** Interactive display may temporarily show the previous coherent state with a preparation indicator. An exported video frame or still must use the exact requested generation and wait when necessary. Never silently export a cheaper preview or stale mode in order to maintain responsiveness.

**Difficulty 7.4 / effectiveness 8.0**, conditional on measured mode-switch stalls. This is a direct 3D-to-2D architectural transfer and can make the growing shader feature set more usable, but it does not change fractal precision, MPA, image quality or the cost of orbit calculations. Its priority should rise only if cold or repeated mode changes cause material waits on supported hardware.

**Verification:** measure first usable display, replacement-ready time and first draw separately for cold and repeated switches. Exercise rapid A/B/A changes, failed creation, shutdown and resize during creation, simultaneous preview/export requests and bounded-cache eviction. Verify the published settings match specialization words, old resources survive all in-flight uses, failures retain a usable display, and final exports exactly match the requested mode. Current source evidence establishes the opportunity; no responsiveness improvement has been implemented or measured.

## J. Use existing RFF measurements to decide which optimization pays off

GMT's [measurement ADR](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/adr/0073-compile-time-measurement-protocol.md), [switch-isolation harness](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/debug/measure-pt-switches.mts) and the inspected measurement sections of its [compile policy](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/policy/shader-compile-optimization.md) provide a useful engineering workflow: isolate one feature, separate compilation from rendering, control cache state, and compare repeated paired runs before accepting small differences. Their numerical results, browser switches and approximately one-second noise threshold belong to GMT's documented machines/backend, not RFF.

**RFF already has the substrate.** [LogicalDevice.cpp](../src/vulkan_helper/impl/LogicalDevice.cpp) loads saved pipeline-cache data and writes it through a temporary file. [PipelinePreparation.hpp](../src/vulkan_helper/impl/PipelinePreparation.hpp) reports preparation elapsed time. [GpuPassTimer.hpp](../src/rff2/ui/GpuPassTimer.hpp) records timestamp-query intervals, collects them after frame completion and reports accumulated averages; the inspected [RenderSceneRenderer.hpp](../src/rff2/ui/RenderSceneRenderer.hpp) rendering path enables these marks on request. Do not describe persistent caching or GPU pass timers as absent.

### Proposed comparison protocol

| Question | Measurement | Control required |
|---|---|---|
| Does section I reduce interruption? | Setting request to first coherent display; replacement-ready latency | Same requested mode sequence and final feature set; identify temporarily retained display |
| Does shader restructuring reduce creation work? | Pipeline-creation duration, separate from device-idle wait and orchestration | Shader/build identity, GPU/driver and cache provenance recorded |
| Does the shader execute faster? | Existing GPU pass intervals across repeated completed frames | Same resolution, quality, enabled effects and input map; isolate orbit calculation |
| Is video export faster overall? | Completed output frames per elapsed time plus GPU/CPU breakdown | Same sequence, codec, precision, dimensions and output quality |
| Does a quality change help? | Still and temporal reference comparisons alongside GPU cost | Same scene, animation phase, exposure and sampling convention |

Distinguish a normal warm application run, an empty application pipeline cache, and an actually controlled driver-cache experiment. An empty Vulkan cache does not prove all driver caches are cold. Use an isolated benchmark configuration if a cache experiment is implemented; do not delete the user's normal cache merely to obtain a number. Report unavailable cache control explicitly. The current investigation has not run those experiments.

For small timing changes, alternate baseline and candidate in paired runs, retain raw samples and report variability. Establish RFF's own repeatability with a no-change control. Do not label a difference a win just because it has the expected sign. The current aggregate pass report is useful for a baseline but cannot by itself supply per-frame percentiles or confidence intervals; retaining individual samples would be incremental tooling work. Attribute intervals to their actual recorded command regions, including barriers when present, rather than claiming isolated arithmetic throughput.

The GMT harness illustrates useful feature isolation, but its fallback to a total or observed wait when a detailed timing field is absent should not be copied into a metric labeled pipeline creation. Missing phase measurements should remain missing. Likewise, successful shader compilation is necessary but does not establish correct pixels, precision or resource lifetime. RFF needs numerical checks for unchanged fractal data and visual/temporal checks appropriate to each proposed display change.

### Practical priority by user-visible outcome

- **Small, isolated appearance change:** section A, continuous bloom extraction. Its limited integration surface makes it the clearest first implementation candidate, pending reference-image comparison.
- **Texture-heavy animation:** section H, footprint-aware sampling. Prioritize it when shimmer or moire is reproduced; it adds less value to image-free scenes.
- **Color-authoring control:** sections B and D, field distributions and independent lookup coordinates. Their value is creative control, not a promised frame-rate gain.
- **Material appearance:** sections E and G, field-driven properties and editable environments. These extend the existing 2D relief foundation and need quality/cost comparisons.
- **Editing stalls:** section I, retain a coherent display while preparing replacements. Raise its priority when measured mode changes interrupt editing; do not confuse responsiveness with faster cold compilation.
- **Understanding and external composition:** section F, selected channel inspection/export. It benefits several workflows but is a broader integration project.

These conditions refine the numerical scores rather than proving them. There is no defensible single measured "most effective" improvement yet. The proposal scores remain engineering estimates, and none authorizes reduced perturbation precision or a change to MPA.

## K. Field semantics and an optional logarithmic spiral color transform

The complete [GMT mapping registry](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/coloring/MappingModes.ts) exposes 15 mappings. They are not 15 ready-made RFF features: some use geometric position or normals, others require orbit statistics, and several labels depend on the producing formula's data contract.

| GMT field family | RFF adoption boundary |
|---|---|
| Spatial radius and azimuth | Cheap in full-canvas coordinates; define the center and aspect convention. Fractal-plane anchoring at deep zoom requires a different precision-aware coordinate contract. |
| Surface-normal direction | Available in relief evaluation; exposing it to an earlier palette pass requires shared reconstruction or another channel. A 2D relief normal is not a GMT ray-hit normal. |
| Iterations and raw iterations | RFF already supplies iteration coloring. Preserve its actual smoothing/count convention; do not copy GMT's formula-dependent scaling or its near-one trap modulation. |
| Decomposition and angle-plus-iteration | RFF already has escape-angle coloring. Verify endpoint data availability and distinguish it from screen azimuth. Independent two-field image lookup remains the separate addition in section D. |
| Per-component and geometric orbit traps | Need statistics over the orbit, including skipped intervals. A shader cannot reconstruct an orbit minimum from the final iteration count/escape angle. Preserve MPA and require a proven compatible accumulation scheme. |
| Z-depth | No direct 2D Mandelbrot equivalent. Name any proposed relief-height channel by its actual derivation rather than copying this label. |
| Potential | GMT's inspected mapping takes a log-log transform of `result.y`, documented there as a trap/magnitude holder. That code alone does not establish a physical escape potential for every formula or for RFF. Verify the producer before adopting the name or equation. |

### Concrete small addition beyond RFF's existing swirl

RFF's [palette sampling](../shdsrc/palette_sampling.glsl), `animation_offset_iterations`, already has turbulence and a psychedelic mode combining radial, spiral and liquid sinusoidal fields. [vk_iteration_palette.frag](../shdsrc/vk_iteration_palette.frag) separately shifts the palette using the escape endpoint angle. [ShdWarpAttribute.h](../src/rff2/attr/ShdWarpAttribute.h) and [ShdWarpSource.h](../src/rff2/attr/ShdWarpSource.h) support noise/image-driven palette displacement. These existing features rule out a generic recommendation to add swirl or domain warp.

The incremental GMT idea is its [coloring helper](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/coloring.ts), `gmt_colorSpiral`: add an angular term with an independently chosen arm count and a logarithmic radial term before periodic palette sampling. A proposed 2D version, expressed in palette cycles, is:

```text
p = aspect-correct position relative to the chosen center
theta = atan2(p.y, p.x), with a defined value at the center
r = length(p)
phaseOffset = integerArms * theta / (2*pi)
            + twist * log(max(r, centerRadius))
```

This provides independently controlled logarithmic rings and multi-arm spirals, rather than the existing mixture of animated sinusoidal effects. Leave the fractal field unchanged. The mask/texture/palette consumers should share an explicitly defined placement of the transform; do not silently change whether existing decorative layers follow it.

**Seams and scaling:** integer arm counts make the angular jump an integer number of palette cycles only when the downstream palette operation is periodic in those cycles. With RFF's separate RGB intervals, adding one shared iteration offset may not satisfy that condition for every channel. Either apply the phase in each channel's cycle domain or document/restrict the mode appropriately. Under uniform scaling `r -> s*r`, the radial term changes by `twist*log(s)` away from the center clamp. The pattern is self-similar with a phase shift, not necessarily pixel-identical at every zoom. Define whether that phase shift is preserved or compensated.

**Stable 2D integration:** use full-output coordinates for a screen-anchored mode so tiles agree. Define the center clamp in the same units as the coordinates and filter the rapidly varying central region using a footprint; do not blindly copy GMT's fixed 0.001 threshold. Treat a fractal-anchored mode as additional work: sending absolute deep-zoom coordinates through floats can erase all local variation. Keep animation freeze, palette phase and persistence semantics explicit, and preserve legacy enum values and output when disabled.

**Difficulty 4.9 / effectiveness 6.5** for the screen-anchored transform with filtering and compatible persistence. This is an optional artistic control, lower priority than fixing reproduced texture instability or improving palette-range authoring. The score does not cover a precision-safe arbitrary fractal-plane anchor. Verify center behavior, angular seams, unequal RGB intervals, negative twist, static/frozen phases and tile/video agreement. No new orbit computation or replacement of MPA is required for the screen-anchored scope.

### Orbit-trap follow-up: define the 2D statistic before designing acceleration

The complete [coloring feature](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/coloring/index.ts) read establishes a concrete geometric-trap contract: an enabled per-iteration minimum, a selectable shape, and an optional capture-iteration cap. Its injection accumulates pre-step positions after the initial iteration; comments and the linked DE path describe complementary post-step capture. It maintains a final captured scalar separately from the scratch accumulator used during later distance probes. The transferable requirement is that shading must consume the statistic for the intended orbit/pixel, not scratch data overwritten by a normal or other neighbor evaluation.

For a future RFF implementation, use explicit 2D definitions on the complex orbit `(x,y)`:

| Intended 2D trap | Candidate distance/statistic | Transfer constraint |
|---|---|---|
| Point | Euclidean distance to a specified 2D center | Define whether z0 participates and which iteration range is captured |
| Circle boundary | Absolute difference between distance to center and radius | Distance to the circumference, not to the filled disk |
| Axis cross | Minimum of the absolute X and Y offsets | GMT's three-component minimum cannot be reused with Z fixed at zero: that would force every sample's trap distance to zero |
| Line | Absolute signed line equation with a normalized nonzero 2D normal | Normalize or explicitly retain a scaled statistic; handle a zero normal without inventing valid geometry |

These formulas specify candidate scalar meanings, not an implementation or a provenance clearance for any copied code. GMT's inspected plane branch uses the supplied dot product directly, so an unnormalized normal scales its value. RFF should choose whether its control promises geometric distance or an artistic field and label it accordingly.

An early capture cap can define a useful finite-prefix feature, but does not automatically make it compatible with MPA. If approximation skips over part of that prefix, the missed minimum must still be accounted for exactly or with a justified error contract. Track capture range, validity and orbit identity alongside the scalar. A trap-shape edit may require recomputation when only one scalar minimum was saved; final iteration and endpoint-angle buffers cannot reconstruct arbitrary new traps. Any saved trap channel needs a versioned meaning, rather than being treated as a generic spare float.

The same feature file emits real mapping logic for Main/Histogram variants and a stub for other variants. RFF likewise needs explicit channel capabilities per rendering path, but must never silently interpret a stub zero as measured data. This follow-up strengthens the conditions on the existing long-term orbit-trap proposal; it does not raise its priority above shader-only changes.

## L. Image-derived palettes feeding the existing shader

**RFF baseline:** [PaletteSources.cpp](../src/rff2/ui/workspace/PaletteSources.cpp), `readPaletteSource`, accepts RFC/RFSP color settings and KFR/KFP color lists; its inspected extension dispatch does not extract colors from raster images. [ShdPaletteAttribute.h](../src/rff2/attr/ShdPaletteAttribute.h) already provides host-side OKLab transforms and palette interpolation corresponding to shader behavior. The additional feature is image analysis that produces a normal RFF palette, not a new shader, new color space or a replacement palette editor.

GMT's [image extraction entry point](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/img2grad/index.ts) offers Distill, Tone and Trace, producing a 256-sample RGB ramp and a perceptual-space ribbon. The Distill dependency chain and the subsequent Tone/Trace, decoding and gamut helpers have now been read in full. This establishes source behavior, not executed cross-platform equivalence or a completed review of every image-editor component.

### Distill mechanism, traced through the implementation

1. [Ingest](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/img2grad/ingest.ts) consumes an already reduced image, converts pixels to OKLab and groups RGB into five-bit-per-channel bins. Each bin stores mean perceptual color, count and a spatial center preference. It measures global color contrast against up to 160 frequent bins, normalizes it, and combines it with center preference. This is a color/spatial heuristic, not semantic recognition of a subject. The caller's documented working-image target is a maximum edge of 160 pixels; the pure ingest routine itself does not resize.
2. [Weights](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/img2grad/weights.ts) balance frequency, standout colors and light/dark preference. In the inspected code, weight is `count^(1-0.62*s) * (saliency+0.05)^(3*s) * exp(1.9*g*(L-0.5))`. These constants describe GMT's implementation, not universal optimal settings. RFF can use the idea with separately justified controls and provenance if adapting the implementation.
3. [Distill](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/img2grad/distill.ts) seeds clusters deterministically: start with the highest-weight bin, then choose the bin maximizing weight times distance squared to its nearest center. It performs 12 weighted Lloyd iterations. There is no random draw in this selection, so ordinary recomputation does not randomly reorder a palette. The comments call this k-means++/medoid snapping; more precisely, it is deterministic weighted farthest-point initialization followed by selecting the highest-weight bin assigned to each cluster. That final representative is a bin-average color, not necessarily an original pixel or a mathematical medoid.
4. [Order](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/img2grad/order.ts) begins an open nearest-neighbor path at the darkest node and applies bounded 2-opt refinement to reduce perceptual travel. This favors smoother transitions; it does not guarantee strictly increasing lightness or a globally optimal route.
5. [Resample](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/img2grad/resample.ts) constructs two paths through the same nodes: one sampled by perceptual arc length, the other by cumulative cluster mass. It mixes their sampled Lab colors according to the spacing control, allowing dominant colors to occupy more of the ramp. The entry point optionally reverses the result and converts it to display RGB through the gamut-handling helper described below.

### RFF integration and user benefit

Use a photograph or artwork as a starting color vocabulary while retaining RFF's current palette editing, cycling and interpolation. A dominant-color mode should let the user choose a color count, frequency-versus-accent balance and spacing. It runs when source/settings change, not per rendered pixel; the resulting palette goes through the existing GPU upload. Fractal reference orbits and MPA are unaffected.

Keep extraction as a candidate until applied, with one undoable palette replacement and no unrelated shader-setting replacement. Do not let a late image decode or analysis result overwrite a more recent source/edit. Store the resulting palette colors/stops as ordinary non-recipe data. The [recipe stability contract](notes/palette-recipe-stability.md) freezes existing generator IDs and RNG behavior: an image source must not reuse a recipe ID or change `genPalette()` for existing presets. Persist editable extraction settings/source references separately only if re-extraction is part of the intended saved workflow; the rendered palette must remain usable after the original image moves.

**Important adaptation choices:**

- Define image color interpretation and alpha handling before downsampling. GMT excludes alpha below 8 from histogram bins but otherwise counts included pixels equally. A partially transparent overlay may call for coverage-weighted counts in RFF. Test transparent RGB so invisible colors cannot unexpectedly dominate.
- Specify stable tie-breaking and algorithm versioning. Deterministic control flow in one implementation does not establish byte-identical results across JavaScript, C++ and different image decoders. Saving final colors avoids dependence on reproducing the clustering after every load.
- GMT's open path is not a cyclic palette solution. RFF's repeated palette can expose a large last-to-first transition. Offer an explicit cyclic ordering/closure policy or preserve a deliberate seam; do not silently append a long closing transition to every extraction.
- Preserve perceptual-space interpolation and gamut policy consistently between extracted preview and shader output. Reuse RFF's established helpers where appropriate, while verifying that their expected units match the image analysis. A 256-sample GMT ramp is not a reason to cap all RFF palettes at 256 entries.
- Bound source decode memory and analysis cost, and report all-transparent/empty input without unexpectedly replacing the current palette with a fallback gray ramp. License/source review is still needed before porting the distinctive weighting or ordering implementation; this document copies no executable extraction code into RFF.

**Difficulty 5.5 / effectiveness 8.5** for dominant-color extraction integrated with existing palette editing and saving. The score excludes a full freehand Trace editor and the broader Gradient Explorer application. This is a strong authoring addition even for flat 2D rendering; unlike image texturing, it borrows a source's colors without projecting its picture over the fractal.

**Verification:** one-color input, known two-color proportions, tiny accent regions, grayscale, transparent borders, all-transparent input, tied bins and repeated extraction; candidate cancellation/undo; save/load after source removal; gamut/preview agreement; and the final-to-first cyclic transition. No extraction UI or algorithm has been implemented in RFF by this review.

### Tone and Trace: two different authoring needs

| Extraction | Actual mechanism | Useful RFF application |
|---|---|---|
| Distill | Representative color clusters, reordered for a smooth path | Borrow a photograph's overall color vocabulary |
| Tone | Group by perceptual lightness and derive a representative hue/chroma per occupied group | Preserve a source's dark-to-light color progression |
| Trace | Sample a selected image path in spatial order | Deliberately pick a sunset, painted stripe or other specific sequence without cluster reordering |

[Tone](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/img2grad/tone.ts) assigns each bin to `floor(L * bucketCount)`, then accumulates weighted mean lightness and chroma. Hue uses a circular mean: sum cosine/sine of hue with weight `binWeight * (0.15 + chroma)`, then recover the angle with `atan2`. It emits occupied groups in increasing lightness order and applies a chroma multiplier. This is a representative color at each tonal range, not the source's literal sequence of pixels. Opposing hues can nearly cancel the circular direction while mean chroma remains substantial; a RFF adaptation should define a stable neutral/dominant-hue fallback rather than amplify an unstable direction. Bucket count and gamut mapping should remain bounded and explicit.

[Trace](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/img2grad/trace.ts) accepts a two-point line or a freehand polyline. An optional uniform Catmull-Rom curve is subdivided into 24 steps per span. It walks that dense path by cumulative pixel-space arc length, sampling 256 positions. At each position it averages a Gaussian-weighted band perpendicular to the path, then optionally applies triangular smoothing along the output sequence. This separates tolerance across the image path from smoothing along the palette; expose those as different meanings rather than one generic blur amount. The same generated polyline supplies the source overlay and sampling geometry, keeping displayed and sampled paths consistent.

The automatic Trace suggestion evaluates 24 lines through the image center, with 48 samples per line. Its score rewards perceptual color travel and alignment of successive color differences while penalizing changes of direction. It is a bounded deterministic suggestion, not a search for an optimal arbitrary curve or a detected object boundary. For RFF, a manually adjustable two-point trace is a useful first scope; freehand editing, curve handling and suggestions are additional work. Define width in source/working-image units and preserve it predictably when analysis resolution changes. Handle coincident points and one-pixel image dimensions explicitly.

### Decode, gamut and saved-state details worth carrying over

[decode.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/img2grad/decode.ts) keeps a small analysis image (maximum edge 160) separate from a larger display thumbnail (maximum edge 1920). This separation makes editing responsive without showing the tiny analysis buffer as the source preview. Those sizes are GMT choices: narrow color stripes or tiny accents can disappear in a 160-pixel reduction, so RFF should evaluate its analysis resolution against representative sources. Trace uses nearest pixel lookup into the reduced Lab buffer; a smoother preview alone does not increase extraction detail.

[oklab.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/oklab.ts), `oklabToRgbSafe`, converts to linear RGB to test the gamut and, when needed, performs 18 binary-search steps reducing chroma at fixed Lab lightness and hue. It then applies the sRGB transfer and channel clamp. This offers a useful alternative to independent RGB clipping when Tone's chroma multiplier produces an out-of-gamut color. The finite gamut tolerance and final clamp mean that source comments saying hue is "never" changed should not be treated as a strict numerical guarantee. Keep RFF's existing color conversions canonical; add an explicitly scoped extraction gamut policy rather than another unsynchronized set of color matrices.

The analysis `ImageModel` stores Lab per pixel without a parallel alpha buffer. Histogram modes exclude nearly transparent pixels during ingestion, whereas Trace samples the Lab buffer directly. A RFF port that promises transparency-aware extraction should carry alpha into the trace band and normalize only valid coverage, with an explicit fallback when the band is empty. This is a relevant adoption condition, not a separate GMT repair task.

[imageDocument.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/store/imageDocument.ts) saves the trace path plus a JPEG-encoded display thumbnail and re-ingests the image on restore. It caches the restored encoded source to avoid another lossy JPEG generation on each subsequent reload, and uses a restore generation token to reject older asynchronous decodes. Borrow those lifecycle ideas, but do not assume JPEG regeneration preserves exact extracted colors or transparency. RFF should save the applied palette as the authoritative rendering result; if editable re-extraction is promised, preserve a suitable source representation, extraction version and path independently. Reopening a scene must not silently recompute and replace its approved colors.

**Extended scope estimate:** Tone plus a two-point Trace on top of the proposed image import raises the combined implementation difficulty to approximately **6.2 / effectiveness 8.7**. Full freehand/spline editing raises it further and is not included in that estimate. Validate tonal ordering, nearly canceling hues, neutral images, short/degenerate paths, band edges, transparent areas, analysis-resolution changes and save/reopen identity. These are proposed validation cases; this review has not run the image extraction application.

## M. Geometry modifiers: separate decorative transfer from new fractal mathematics

The complete [geometry feature](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/geometry/index.ts), [shared transforms](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/geometry/transforms.ts), [fold contract](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/geometry/types.ts) and all seven [registered fold implementations](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/geometry/folds/index.ts) were read in this batch. Their most important RFF adoption boundary is where the operation occurs: changing decoration coordinates is a display operation, while changing the orbit recurrence is a different fractal.

### What the GMT mechanisms actually do

- **Burning modifier:** when enabled for a compatible formula, the feature injects `mix(z, abs(z), amount)` into the iteration. A compile gate removes the operation entirely when unavailable; runtime controls vary its amount afterward. This acts on orbit coordinates, not on the final color image. It is not automatically identical to every convention called Burning Ship.
- **Rotation and twist:** the shared helper precomputes a Rodrigues axis and sine/cosine for reuse within shader execution; another helper rotates XY by an angle depending on Z. Moving invariant work outside a repeated formula evaluation is the transferable idea. The helper is GLSL state, so its source comment about once-per-frame preparation is not evidence of CPU-side frame-global computation.
- **Standard and mirror folds:** the standard component rule is clamp-and-reflect; mirror applies nested absolute values and an offset. A 2D adaptation can fold image coordinates to create symmetry without modifying the Mandelbrot orbit, but that is a decorative effect with its own filtering semantics.
- **Kali fold:** constant minus absolute position, with rotation designated after the fold rather than wrapping the fold between a rotation and its inverse. Operation order changes the resulting map and must be retained deliberately.
- **Tetrahedral, octahedral and icosahedral folds:** conditional plane reflections followed by scale about an offset. These implementations also scale the distance-estimator derivative accumulator and mark themselves self-contained so an outer sphere-fold/scale is not applied again.
- **Menger fold:** absolute coordinates, descending axis ordering, scale-dependent offset and an optional Z fold. Its 3D axis coupling has no direct two-dimensional equivalent obtained simply by deleting Z.

The fold registry uses stable codes with retired values reserved, independent of list position. This is a useful configuration contract for any new RFF modifier catalog and agrees with RFF's existing append-only/stable-ID requirements. Provenance comments name several outside algorithms; one explicitly mentions a decompiled source. Those are origin clues, not permission to transplant the implementations. Any actual adaptation requires original-source/license verification.

### Existing RFF constraints
