[FractalAttribute.h](../src/rff2/attr/FractalAttribute.h) already exposes Mandelbrot/custom formula selection, rotation and projection controls. The complete inspected [CustomFormulaPerturbator.cpp](../src/rff2/formula/CustomFormulaPerturbator.cpp) uses a dummy reference and evaluates parsed expressions directly in `std::complex<double>`, starting at zero with the selected pixel coordinate as c. It does not establish deep-precision or MPA support for arbitrary folds. Consequently, "add custom formulas" would be redundant, while "arbitrary GMT geometry works with RFF acceleration" would be unsupported.

The completed read of [weave.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/weave.ts) shows independent parameter banks for up to six slots and runtime interval/start/count controls for combining formulas. The subsequently completed [schedule.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/weave/schedule.ts) builds an intro-plus-cycle slot plan and emits static or runtime phase selection, as detailed below. The actual fused-formula emitter remains outside this completed scheduler read. These structures suggest explicit composition contracts; they do not prove a ready-made RFF hybrid engine.

**Completed scheduler follow-up:** count schedules advance a `(slot, remaining-count)` cursor until that state repeats, retaining an initial prefix separately from the cycle. Block schedules expand repeated introductory segments followed by one cycling segment. The emitter encodes absolute slot indices in a constant lookup table and uses modulo only after the prefix. Negative counts are marked as silent steps in the host plan, but `stepSlot` removes that marker for this particular emitted phase function: escape-counter behavior must be established in the downstream consumer, not inferred from the lookup alone. The count walker has a finite outer guard and a fallback; any independent RFF design must validate that the reachable repeat segment contains work and impose bounded schedule sizes rather than rely on comments claiming exactness for arbitrary input.

Runtime modulo schedules select a secondary formula at an interval after a start, with an optional invocation limit. The layered variant checks layers in order and returns the first matching layer, so overlap means precedence, not summation or blending. Its nonpositive beat limit means unlimited; the simpler modulo emitter's provided maximum has different nonpositive behavior. A disabled count schedule selects the first slot of the repeating cycle, whereas disabled modulo schedules select base phase zero. These are user-visible recurrence semantics that require explicit saved-state contracts. Keep them distinct from the iteration period found by FPG and the periodic structure used by MPA. An initially nonperiodic schedule prefix and subsequent phase must both be represented in any accelerated recurrence state. The source header references an MB3D implementation; its provenance must be resolved before adaptation.

### Recommendations for RFF

**Near-term candidate: decorative symmetry, difficulty 5.2 / effectiveness 6.8.** Consider an explicit mirror/sector transform of selected image or pattern coordinates. The value is a reusable transformation for existing layers, rather than a fixed mirrored source image. Apply it after choosing the coordinate field and before sampling, with a specified center, angular repeat policy and full-canvas anchoring. The current reviewed UV modes expose paired fields and axis scale/scroll, not a general fold stack. Check remaining pattern controls before committing to a new catalog. At fold boundaries, propagate the local footprint or supersample; a visually sharp fold should not become an accidental large derivative jump. Do not market this as generating a new Mandelbrot formula.

**Longer-term research: accelerated hybrid formulas, difficulty 9.4 / effectiveness 7.2.** Define recurrence, Julia/parameter-plane semantics, escape and smoothing rules, derivative/statistics propagation and phase state before considering optimization. A schedule period alone is not the periodic reference structure that MPA requires. Any reference reuse/skip must account for the active formula phase and all relevant state, with proven precision and error control. Absolute-value folds introduce branch boundaries requiring particular care. The existing direct custom path can inform a correctness reference only within its valid precision range; it is not a deep-zoom guarantee. This work belongs below the verified palette/material improvements in priority.

For either scope, retain stable identifiers, preserve old scenes, and make operation order explicit. Test symmetric input fields, fold boundaries, disabled identity, full/tiled output and animation continuity for decoration; use separate high-precision mathematical validation for any future recurrence changes. No formula or shader implementation has been changed by this investigation.

## N. Quality controls: transfer workload policy, not 3D precision shortcuts

The complete [quality feature](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/quality.ts), [core-math feature](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/core_math.ts) and [optics feature](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/optics.ts) distinguish several unrelated meanings of quality. Keeping those meanings separate is essential when proposing a 2D transfer.

| GMT mechanism | RFF conclusion |
|---|---|
| Ray-hit epsilon, step multiplier, overstep recovery, hit refinement | These govern a distance-estimator raymarch. They are not settings for RFF perturbation accuracy or MPA skipping. Do not import their numbers or weaken RFF precision. |
| Numerical distance estimation and probe-width smoothing | The core-math feature switches to repeated perturbed-seed evaluation when that estimator is selected. This is not equivalent to RFF's complex perturbation theory; probe smoothing can change represented detail. No direct adoption recommended. |
| Float32 versus Float16 render targets | A display-buffer choice is separate from orbit and iteration-buffer precision. Evaluate dynamic range and error per resource before any change; no blanket half-precision recommendation follows from GMT's setting. |
| Camera aperture and focus distance | Meaningful with 3D ray geometry. An iteration-selected or screen-selected blur can be an artistic effect in RFF, but must not be presented as physical depth of field. |
| Perspective, orthographic and panoramic projection | RFF already has projection controls. GMT's menu alone does not establish a missing RFF feature or matching projection semantics. |
| Responsiveness target and progressive work division | Potentially useful for interaction policy; requires comparison with RFF's existing scheduling rather than a second generic quality switch. |

The inspected progressive-band section of [FractalEngine.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/FractalEngine.ts) seeds its band count from estimated full-frame cost and requested frame period, then adjusts with a dead band and bounded multiplicative changes. It waits between adjustments and freezes feedback at the accumulation sample cap. A target of zero explicitly selects one full-screen band. The useful principle is **budget the duration of each work unit using measurements that represent actual active work**. Idle/converged FPS is not a valid cost estimate. This is a selective read of that controller, not a full scheduler audit.

For RFF, first measure which work causes interaction latency: orbit calculation, shader passes, transfers, pipeline creation or presentation. More shader bands will not fix a CPU reference-orbit bottleneck; lower resolution will not fix pipeline creation. If a measured gap remains, a responsiveness controller could vary bounded work chunks or existing preview sampling within the user's quality limits, with hysteresis and a clear return to the requested final quality. Preserve numerical precision and output resolution/quality for export. Device-specific responsiveness preferences should not be unexpectedly replaced by loading an artistic preset; GMT marks its relevant settings as user-scoped.

**Conditional proposal: difficulty 7.0 / effectiveness 7.7.** This is a workload-policy investigation, not an established missing feature or a ready implementation task. Its priority depends on the remaining RFF scheduling audit and latency measurements. Validate response latency and completed useful work separately, especially when idle, after expensive configuration changes and across devices. Do not accept a higher reported FPS obtained only by delaying full-quality completion indefinitely.

## O. Bundled 2D reference shaders: useful ideas with explicit boundaries

This batch reads six complete files in GMT's [bundled Fragmentarium 2D reference directory](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/tree/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems). They are reference examples, not proof that GMT's current renderer exposes each technique as a native feature. Their includes and runtime have not been executed. The broad shader-related coverage count includes these reference assets; it is intentionally wider than the core GMT shader directory.

### Nested vector-domain warping

`DomainDistortion2.frag` constructs two noise components q, evaluates a second vector field r at positions displaced by q, then evaluates another scalar field at positions displaced by r. Its color combines those intermediate fields. This is nested two-axis coordinate displacement, distinct from RFF's inspected `warp_offset`, which derives a scalar displacement of palette position from noise or an image.

**RFF candidate:** an optional vector warp on existing texture/pattern UV coordinates, reusing the original fractal field. It could generate flowing or marbled texture detail with independently controlled displacement components. This adds expression beyond scalar palette displacement, but overlaps existing turbulence aesthetically; validate that the result is useful before adding controls. Derive or estimate the final warped footprint, enforce periodicity where promised, and cap noise octaves according to visible detail. The example evaluates several multi-octave fields per lookup, so it supplies no evidence of a cheap replacement. **Difficulty 6.4 / effectiveness 7.1**, provisional. Its header attributes domain distortion to an external source; verify original provenance before adapting a recognizable implementation.

### Recursive image zoom rather than fractal zoom

`Droste.frag` and `DrosteGrid.frag` use a complex-power transform and powers of a radius ratio to bring coordinates back into a repeated source region, with a periodic time scale. One samples an image and the other renders a diagnostic grid. This suggests a recursive picture/pattern mapping mode; it does not calculate additional deep fractal detail.

**RFF candidate:** a decorative layer transform for recursive posters or looped visual effects, lower priority than sampling quality. Define a valid nondegenerate radius ratio, center/axis behavior, complex-log branch convention, filtering and wrap continuity. Validate the animation seam rather than relying on `fract(time)` to guarantee a seamless loop. A final-image version requires a coherent source image across tiles; sampling only a current tile would be insufficient. **Difficulty 6.1 / effectiveness 6.3** for a layer transform. Both examples explicitly credit ArKano22, and license clearance is unresolved here; use them as conceptual references until provenance is checked.

### Orbit averages and cellular statistics

`Mandelbrot-AverageColoring.frag` adds `0.5 + 0.5*sin(density*arg(z))` after a configurable initial skip, retains the last added value, and interpolates current/previous averages using an escape-based fraction. RFF's [vk_stripe.frag](../shdsrc/vk_stripe.frag) instead derives periodic stripe values from the final iteration count; its existing stripes do not provide this orbit-angle average. A true average requires sum/count/last-sample semantics and a defined smoothing convention. Protect zero/one-sample cases and establish the bailout convention independently. **Difficulty 9.0 / effectiveness 7.8** for a precision-preserving, acceleration-compatible feature, not a shader-only patch.

`Mandelbrot-Cellular.frag` retains the nearest and second-nearest squared orbit distances to a trap, then combines their ratio with an inverse-distance halo. This can produce internal cellular patterning beyond a single minimum trap. The second minimum must have an explicit repeated/tied-sample policy. Exact hits and vanishing distances need defined output limits, not an uncontrolled reciprocal. In RFF, interior classification and early periodic termination also matter: final iteration/color buffers do not preserve these statistics. **Difficulty 9.2 / effectiveness 7.7** with complete computation/storage/MPA integration. It belongs with the orbit-trap research scope in section K, not with inexpensive post-processing.

### A wrapped recurrence is a new formula

`mandel_mobius.frag` performs a quadratic iteration and then wraps X across selected boundaries while reversing Y. Despite the filename, its inspected `mobius` helper is a conditional strip wrap, not the general fractional-linear complex transform `(az+b)/(cz+d)`. It changes the recurrence and its starting-state convention differs from the usual z0=0 Mandelbrot path. This is a formula-exploration reference, not a ready improvement to existing Mandelbrot rendering. Do not claim MPA or deep-zoom compatibility from the GLSL example. No additional implementation priority is assigned before the broader custom-formula design is established.

For these six examples, the strongest near-term transfer is optional **decoration-coordinate** warping. The orbit-statistic examples are useful precisely because they expose what data RFF would need to compute; copying their final color expressions alone cannot reproduce them. No examples or shader code have been copied into the application.

### Follow-up: derivative distance and the precise meaning of orbit statistics

Five additional complete references in the same directory extend the comparison below. These are source inspections, not executed Fragmentarium tests. They do not change the distinction between a bundled example and a native GMT feature.

**`Mandelbrot-DE.frag`: derivative-based exterior distance.** The example advances the complex derivative before updating the orbit: `d_next = 2*z*d + 1` for the parameter plane, or `d_next = 2*z*d` for Julia initial-position differentiation. It starts z at zero for Mandelbrot and at the pixel coordinate for Julia. The derivative starts at one in both branches; in the Mandelbrot branch the first update with z=0 makes it one regardless. After escape at squared magnitude greater than 100, it computes a quantity proportional to `|z|*log2(|z|)/|d|`, scales it by `Zoom/100`, and compares it with a user threshold. The returned image is binary black/white; the source does not implement smooth pixel coverage. Its logarithm base, zoom multiplier and threshold form a display convention, not a calibrated physical pixel-distance contract.

RFF already has [boundary_reflection_mask](../shdsrc/lustre_relief.glsl), which searches a 5-by-5 neighborhood for texels classified as interior, estimates distance to their pixel footprints, and attenuates reflection near them. That is useful local image evidence, but it is explicitly not a fractal distance estimator. An orbit-derived exterior-distance channel could support boundary contours or a more continuous boundary-dependent material mask where no neighboring interior sample is available. Whether it improves a particular image must be measured; it cannot recover arbitrary unresolved detail or certify exact coverage.

**Conditional RFF proposal: difficulty 9.1 / effectiveness 8.0.** First establish which derivative state is already available in the perturbation and MPA paths; a keyword search alone does not establish its absence. Propagate the derivative of the represented orbit with respect to the correct coordinate, including every accelerated skip, rather than differentiating only the final displayed iteration field. Use a representation that preserves its range at deep zoom, and convert the result to pixel units using the actual view/projection mapping. Store validity separately for interior, unresolved and invalid estimates. A smooth coverage-style display mask would be a new RFF design, not a port of this example's binary comparison. Keep existing supersampling as the correctness baseline; examine thin filaments, near-boundary escape, zoom and tile consistency, and compare with high-precision unaccelerated samples. This is research below the lower-cost bloom and texture-filtering candidates, despite its potentially broad visual use.

| Reference | Exact statistic or operation inspected | RFF adoption consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `MandelbrotCheckers.frag` | Samples a checker pattern with circular cell inversions at each updated orbit position that remains inside the bailout. Accumulates its RGB and retains the last accepted value; a switch chooses average versus last. Exterior escape coloring modulates that result. | An orbit-pattern average is different from placing a checker texture on final image coordinates. It needs sample sum/count or the last accepted orbit sample. A final escape angle and iteration count cannot reconstruct it. Pattern edits require recomputation unless sufficient orbit data is retained. |
| `MandelbrotOrbitTrap.frag` | Takes the minimum of `abs(length(z)-Radius)` after the update and only before bailout. Uses that minimum to modify color phase and reciprocal-power intensity; returns black for nonescaping samples. | A circle-boundary trap is transferable to 2D, but the contributor interval and exclusion of the escaping point are part of its appearance. Reuse the orbit-trap research design in section K, with an explicit empty-sample state and bounded intensity at an exact hit. |
| `2016-02-26_lyapunov_atom_domains.frag` | Starts at z=c, sums `log(|p*z^(p-1)|^2)` over a fixed iteration budget, and adds a color whenever the current logarithmic derivative is below its previous record, initialized at zero. It averages colors of those record events and mixes with a function of the mean logarithmic derivative. | The recorded minimum concerns the current derivative contribution, not the running sum. This needs both derivative-log accumulation and record-event semantics. Neither FPG's detected period nor the final escape count is the same statistic. |
| `mandelexOptimised.frag` | Applies conditional pulls, periodic reduction, a box fold, circle inversion, scale, rotation and offset as a new recurrence. Its grayscale statistic sums `exp(-1/abs(r2_current-r2_previous))` before bailout, then normalizes and applies a power. | The coloring statistic requires successive orbit magnitudes; the folded recurrence is a separate custom-formula task. Its filename and historical optimization comment are not evidence of a speedup on current Vulkan hardware. |

For checker averages, **difficulty 9.0 / effectiveness 7.3** is a provisional estimate for a complete precision-preserving feature, sharing infrastructure with the orbit averages already discussed. For circle traps, the section K orbit-trap scope applies; this reference adds a particular shape and contributor convention rather than an independent engine feature. A skipped orbit interval cannot be treated as one ordinary sample without changing an average, minimum or record-event result. Exact statistics require a justified summary for that interval or a compatible computation path; disabling acceleration may be a reference method but does not satisfy production performance by itself.

The Lyapunov example has no escape early-out and supports negative powers, so singular or nonfinite trajectories and a zero record-event count need an explicit definition before adoption. Treat its result as this example's finite-orbit statistic, not an automatically validated stability classification for every RFF formula. **Difficulty 9.5 / effectiveness 6.4**, provisionally, makes it an exploratory feature behind the more broadly useful distance/trap channels. Do not equate a new coloring method with improved numerical precision.

For `mandelexOptimised.frag`, keep operation order and branch semantics explicit. Replacing conditionals with arithmetic `mix`/`step` expressions does not ensure that singular operands are skipped: circle inversion still forms a division by squared radius. The zero-iteration escape case also needs a defined normalization if adapting its color statistic. These are reasons to design a valid RFF implementation, not a recommendation to repair GMT's reference file. Named authors in its header provide provenance leads; original-source and license verification remains required before copying distinctive code or constants. No separate implementation priority is assigned to this recurrence before the section M custom-formula requirements are met.

**Priority conclusion for this follow-up:** the derivative-distance channel has the strongest potential general-purpose benefit among these five references, but it also needs substantial numerical and acceleration work. None displaces the existing near-term recommendations for bloom transitions, sampling footprints or image-derived palettes on evidence from this read alone. All effectiveness estimates remain judgments, not measured results.

## P. Lighting feature contracts: useful controls without importing a 3D integrator

The full [lighting feature](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/lighting/index.ts) and [visible light-sphere feature](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/lighting/light_spheres.ts) were inspected. These files establish shader assembly, state and control contracts. Performance figures and physical-accuracy descriptions embedded in their UI metadata are source claims, not independently reproduced measurements.

### Existing RFF baseline and incremental scope

RFF already provides key and fill directions and intensities in [ShdSlopeAttribute.h](../src/rff2/attr/ShdSlopeAttribute.h). [studio_surface.glsl](../shdsrc/studio_surface.glsl) applies its existing GGX BRDF to both directions, including the clearcoat contribution. [studio_ggx.glsl](../shdsrc/studio_ggx.glsl) includes anisotropic roughness, visibility and Fresnel terms; [effects.glsl](../shdsrc/effects.glsl) also uses the fill in its shading path. Consequently, neither "add a second light" nor "add GGX" is an incremental proposal.

GMT stores a bounded list of individually identified lights, with type, position, rotation, color, intensity, shadow behavior and emitter-related properties. It normalizes missing legacy fields and gives duplicates fresh IDs. A possible RFF extension is an editable collection of independently colored light directions for relief shading, beyond the current key/fill arrangement. **Conditional difficulty 6.8 / effectiveness 6.9.** The value would be deliberate multicolor highlight placement, not more physically accurate fractal geometry. Establish the remaining UI/preset capabilities before declaring a general light-list feature absent. Bound shader work, preserve the original key/fill rendering exactly for old scenes, and define whether directions follow the canvas or the view. Positional falloff additionally needs a declared relief-space length scale; raw deep-fractal coordinates are not automatically meaningful lighting distances.

### Separate runtime controls from compilation gates

GMT uses compilation gates for entire subsystems such as shadows, path tracing and environment sampling modes. Within the compiled shadow subsystem, the inspected feature exposes quality and jitter through uniforms. Its assembly comments explain that both shadow-quality bodies remain compiled, while direction jitter precedes one shared march. The lesson is to measure the cost of retaining an alternative versus the cost and delay of compiling another variant; it is not a blanket instruction to replace RFF specialization constants with branches.

For the pipeline replacement proposal in section I, classify each control by what it changes: ordinary numeric uniforms, a coherent runtime algorithm choice, or resource/layout/subsystem structure. Consider runtime selection for frequently edited alternatives only when representative GPU and compilation measurements support it. Keep descriptor and push-constant layouts synchronized. The feature's direct and path-traced routes inject different integrators, and non-main variants receive stubs: valid shader compilation alone does not show that a requested effect is active. RFF's channel diagnostics should distinguish unavailable data from a legitimate zero-valued result.

Changing a runtime control can still invalidate an accumulated image. GMT's jitter control intentionally omits the flag that suppresses accumulation reset because changing the sampling mode changes the target appearance. For RFF, apply the same dependency principle to any cached or progressively assembled display: refresh every affected result even if the orbit remains reusable. This is an integration requirement, not evidence that RFF currently mishandles such invalidation.

### Visible emitters, shadows and 2D transfer limits

`LightSpheresFeature` separately injects sphere intersection, miss handling and final composition, depending on the lighting feature's uniform arrays. Its final composition receives volumetric accumulation as an in/out value so fog can be reconciled with emitter depth. This separates a visible source's geometry from its lighting parameters. For a RFF decorative glow layer, an analogous separation between visible glow, bloom contribution and material illumination could be useful; it must not imply indirect illumination unless such transport is actually computed. It also overlaps the emission routing proposal in section E, so it should share that design rather than create another unrelated glow system.

A 2D iteration-derived normal does not supply the 3D distance field, occluders or world-space lengths needed by GMT's shadow marches and sphere-area-light sampling. Actual self-shadowing would require a specified height representation and visibility method, with tile margins, missing/interior-data policy and scale behavior. Environment importance sampling and multiple-importance sampling serve stochastic transport; they are not prerequisites for section G's deterministic environment lookup. Likewise, the path tracer's firefly clamp intentionally biases sample energy and should not be copied into deterministic RFF highlights as if it were a free denoiser. No direct path-tracer or shadow-loop port is recommended from these feature contracts.

Validate any adopted control with old-scene identity, independent light edits, zero-intensity identity, view/zoom/tile consistency and measured cost per additional light. Shader mechanisms and lifecycle conditions above are source-grounded; the conditional scores are engineering estimates and no lighting benchmark has been run.

## Q. Compile-time estimates: refine RFF's existing measurements

The complete [profiles.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/engine/profiles.ts) uses one estimator for both prospective quality selections and live compilation. It starts with a fixed base of 3600 ms and adds costs from active compile-marked parameter metadata. Boolean switches contribute when enabled; option fields contribute the selected option's cost. Path-tracing-family costs are gated on the render mode. A prospective selection constructs feature defaults, applies tier overrides, adds tier adjustments and runs the same sum. This avoids two separately maintained formulas, but it remains an additive calibration model: the source does not prove independence between compiler costs, and these GMT/WebGL numbers cannot predict RFF Vulkan preparation time.

The complete [engine feature host](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/engine/index.ts) only controls visibility of a compiler tab; it does not itself implement optimization or a new preparation pipeline. The complete [feature type map](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/types.ts) aggregates state/action contracts and reexports shared engine feature types. It is a useful navigation boundary, not evidence that every shared shader feature has been audited. In particular, the broad `engine-gmt` progress denominator is not a substitute for reviewing the shared `engine/` implementation.

**RFF already implements measured estimates.** The inspected observer/update portion of [PipelinePreparationWindow.hpp](../src/rff2/ui/PipelinePreparationWindow.hpp) records successful preparation durations, asks its history for an estimate keyed by device plus shader name, and displays either a previous-run estimate, a first-measurement message or an overrun message. [PipelinePreparation.hpp](../src/vulkan_helper/impl/PipelinePreparation.hpp) supplies elapsed-time progress. Therefore a new generic progress bar or fixed cost table would duplicate existing behavior.

**Conditional refinement: difficulty 5.3 / effectiveness 6.5.** If measurements show that one existing key groups materially different creation costs, investigate distinguishing specialization/layout or shader revision, driver context and warm/cold cache conditions. First inspect the timing-history storage, existing shader-name granularity and cache lifecycle in full; those details are not established by this observer read. Keep history bounded, expose uncertainty for sparse observations, and do not treat an elapsed-time fraction as actual compiler completion. If adding a before-apply preview, resolve the same effective configuration that will be built, rather than an approximation that silently discards preserved settings. A shared resolver is more valuable than importing GMT's constants.

This refinement improves expectations, not rendering speed. It remains subordinate to section I's actual pipeline-switch latency work and section J's measurements. Validate estimates against held-out observed preparation times across supported configurations, and distinguish queued delay from active pipeline creation. ## R. Adaptive output dithering: an optional refinement of an existing RFF feature

The complete shared [dither chunk](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/fractal/shaders/ditherTail.ts), [fullscreen wrapper](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/gradient-explorer/fullscreen/ditherTail.ts) and [raw WebGL noise loader](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/utils/createBlueNoiseWebGL2.ts) were read. The wrapper reuses the shared chunk instead of maintaining a second implementation. Its historical comments describe a different asset and integration state from the shared chunk's current requirements, so those comments alone do not establish which noise asset every live consumer binds. The compositor and asset distribution still require separate verification.

### What the shader computes

The shared chunk samples four noise channels and forms RGB perturbations from `(r+g-1, b+a-1, a+r-1)`. Assuming independent uniform input channels, each component has a triangular marginal distribution. Distinct pairs do **not** make the three outputs mutually independent: the first and third share r, while the second and third share a. Under that idealized assumption, each shared-pair covariance is 1/12 and its correlation is 1/2. This is a direct consequence of the inspected expression, not a measurement of the supplied texture. Spatial blue-noise quality and actual channel independence require examining the asset and sampling path; source comments do not prove them.

The adaptive amplitude uses the maximum RGB component of `fwidth(c)*255`, a local change measured in 8-bit code steps per pixel. A smooth gate suppresses almost constant regions. The reciprocal slope controls amplitude, bounded by a ceiling interpolated from eight steps in dark colors to four steps in brighter colors. A separate per-channel taper suppresses noise at black and white. The coordinate is static, avoiding an explicit frame-to-frame reseed. This is a heuristic for trading band visibility against grain, not a general theorem that a gradient needs noise amplitude equal to its band width. Its calibration script is referenced but has not been executed in this batch.

### What RFF already does

[vk_linear_interpolation.frag](../shdsrc/vk_linear_interpolation.frag) already applies static interleaved-gradient noise, using the same scalar offset for all three RGB channels and preserving alpha. Its nominal offset is within half an 8-bit step, and it bypasses this dither when the transfer selector is nonzero. The inspected ordered output path applies SDR encoding before dithering and excludes the diagnostic display mode. In the inspected legacy path, `print_finish` follows the dither call, so any future claim that dithering is always the final color operation would need a routing change or qualification. The new feature would therefore be an optional amplitude/distribution policy, not "add dithering."

**Conditional proposal: difficulty 5.9 / effectiveness 7.2.** Evaluate an adaptive SDR policy only if RFF's existing output still shows objectionable gradient bands. Compare the existing half-step scalar noise, a restrained triangular policy and slope-gated amplitudes on actual final encoded images. Do not transplant GMT's four/eight-step caps as universal defaults. Preserve old-scene output when the new policy is disabled, keep alpha and diagnostic channels untouched, and evaluate chromatic grain as well as luminance banding. A scalar noise option may be preferable for neutral ramps; the RGB pair strategy is not automatically superior.

Apply quantization noise in the domain of the actual quantizer and scale it for the real output format. An eight-bit SDR expression cannot be reused unchanged for PQ/HLG, ten-bit output or floating-point intermediates. A single shared output helper is useful only when every caller supplies the correct encoded color and performs no later transformation that invalidates the assumption. Dithering before an intermediate low-precision write may have a different purpose from final-output dither; inventory actual storage boundaries before moving calls.

For texture-based noise, use a verified asset/license and a sampling contract that preserves intended statistics. The inspected loader defaults to `/blueNoise.png`, permits an explicit URL, uses repeat plus linear filtering, and temporarily uploads RGBA bytes of 128. That fallback is 128/255 rather than exactly 0.5; plugging it into the triangular expression is not precisely zero-centered. RFF could avoid a transient output shift by disabling the texture policy until valid data is ready or supplying an exactly neutral representation. Ensure pixel-center alignment and the intended color-space treatment rather than assuming every filtered PNG supplies independent uniform samples.

Validation should cover smooth dark/neutral/saturated ramps, intentional flat fills, endpoints, high-frequency fractal detail, resizing, full-frame versus tiled exports and animated palette motion. Anchor the pattern to final-canvas pixels across tiles, and examine whether changing slope gates causes visible temporal modulation even with static noise. Compare error and grain after actual quantization; a metric that merely shortens constant-value runs can reward excessive noise. Retain the present bloom-knee priority until these comparisons establish additional benefit. No asset was copied and no dither implementation or calibration test was run.

## S. Environment preprocessing and what sampling tests actually establish

This follow-up revisits the fully read [environment CDF builder](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/reflections/env_cdf.ts), inspects the upload/rebuild portion of [MaterialController.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/MaterialController.ts), and completes the source read of [test-env-sampling.mts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/debug/test-env-sampling.mts). It strengthens the section G environment proposal without recommending a CDF sampler for deterministic RFF reflection.

### Transferable preprocessing

The builder samples an equirectangular image on a default 256-by-128 grid. Each cell receives nonnegative luminance times the sine of its row-center polar angle. It forms a cumulative distribution within each row and another across row totals, stores both as nearest-filtered single-channel float textures, and forces their final entries to one. Separately, it accumulates RGB with the same sine weighting to obtain a spherical average. The weighting compensates for the fact that equal rectangular texels near the poles cover less solid angle than equatorial texels.

For RFF, the average is useful even without stochastic sampling: it can provide a stable broad-reflection fallback instead of the biased top level of an ordinary rectangular box-mip chain. It is still a global average, not a directional diffuse-irradiance solution or a GGX-prefiltered environment. A material's high-roughness limit needs an explicit approximation model; interpolating toward this average is an artistic/engineering choice, not proof of full image-based-lighting correctness.

The inspected implementation samples the original image bilinearly at each analysis-cell center. It does not integrate every source texel covered by that cell. Consequently, a tiny bright lamp or sun between sample centers can disappear from the analysis; its declared mip bias does not make that CPU sample an area average. For a RFF implementation, derive the broad average and any filtered representation from an energy-preserving reduction, and test bright features at different positions relative to the reduction grid. Avoid importing a fixed 256-by-128 resolution as a universal quality setting.

The extraction path handles byte RGB(A) and float/half-float data, but byte scaling by 1/255 is not sRGB decoding. The builder intentionally describes its average as raw texture space. RFF should specify a canonical linear-light representation for environment filtering and averaging, along with the later exposure/profile operations. A nonlinear profile applied to a raw average generally differs from averaging the transformed image. Preserve that distinction when deciding whether a profile edit invalidates preprocessed resources. No claim is made here that RFF's existing image loader already supplies HDR environment support.

### Resources and fallback contracts

The inspected controller enables environment mip generation, records its maximum mip, uploads the image, and then rebuilds the analysis. Failed extraction selects a one-by-one sampling sentinel and a negative average-color sentinel. A fully black readable source is different: the builder returns uniform CDF tables, a black average, and a nonzero normalization fallback. For RFF's deterministic environment path, keep missing, still-loading, black and invalid sources distinguishable; valid black must remain black. Prepare the image and its derived data coherently before replacing the active environment, using the stale-result rejection principle already described in section I. This is a RFF design requirement; the selected controller read is not a complete resource-ownership or asynchronous-lifecycle audit.

### Useful test structure, limited proof

The completed GMT test file examines generated shader strings. It first establishes that environment sampling functions and their fetches exist, then checks explicit LOD use, four bicubic taps, selected constant arguments, cone-footprint expressions and cleanup of a temporary global. Checking existence prevents a removed implementation from passing a negative assertion such as "no implicit fetch." That is a useful validation pattern for a future RFF filtering change.

These checks do not render images or measure GPU compilation time. Exact source fragments do not establish numerical continuity, energy preservation, correct texture formats, asset binding or visible alias suppression. One block's label says the LOD has no footprint term, while its actual assertion merely finds the roughness expression; another block checks that the cone term is present. The label therefore cannot be used as evidence that current sampling lacks footprint handling. Likewise, checks for selected absent/present strings do not by themselves prove byte-identical output or zero compilation cost, despite stronger wording in comments.

For RFF, supplement narrowly targeted source/assembly checks with final-image comparisons of a constant environment, a latitudinal ramp, a small bright spot, seams and poles, several roughness values, and base/clearcoat normals. Compare full-frame and tiled results and vary resolution independently of roughness. Run timing measurements separately. This follow-up adds conditions to the existing environment proposal; it does not raise its effectiveness score without rendered evidence. The GMT sampling test was read, not executed in this batch.

## T. Modulating shader inputs without changing the underlying fractal

Complete reads of [ModulationEngine.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/features/modulation/ModulationEngine.ts), [paramMapping.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/features/modulation/paramMapping.ts), [applyAt.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/features/modulation/applyAt.ts) and the [modulation feature](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/features/modulation/index.ts) establish the following mechanism. Target routing, audio analysis and the full RFF timeline evaluator remain separate review work.

GMT generates sine, triangle, sawtooth, pulse or noise signals. Direct oscillator bindings map the waveform to a relative minimum/maximum offset, with a symmetric amplitude fallback for older settings. Rules can also consume normalized oscillator signals or audio bands, apply thresholds, attack/decay and secondary smoothing, then add gain-scaled contributions to a target. Offsets are cleared once per update and summed within that update. Clearing only the output does not reset the persistent envelope and noise state.

Attack/decay smoothing uses `1-exp(-dt/tau)`, with time constants derived to preserve the former response at 60 Hz. This removes dependence on a fixed per-frame interpolation factor for a held input; it does not make differently sampled, changing input histories identical. Noise samples use time divided by period and a per-oscillator seed created with `Math.random()`. That seed is stable within the engine instance, not demonstrated as durable across restarts by these files. The export helper accepts controlled time and delta, but still uses the singleton's state. Its presence alone therefore does not prove arbitrary seeking or independently rendered frame chunks are reproducible.

The parameter mapper can compose offsets in slider coordinates for nonlinear ranges. It converts the base through the slider mapping, adds a fraction of display travel derived from offset/range, clamps in that domain and converts back. This makes a given modulation depth occupy comparable slider travel at different base values. It is an explicit alternative to adding a fixed amount in physical parameter units. Linear and zero-offset paths return directly; clamping is not universal. RFF should expose or document this choice rather than silently reinterpret existing animation amplitudes.

**Existing RFF baseline:** the inspected target declarations in [VidTimelineTarget.h](../src/rff2/attr/VidTimelineTarget.h) already include palette motion, light directions and strengths, material-related controls, bloom and image-layer transforms. Thus generic shader animation is not a missing feature. A conditional addition is reusable periodic modulation of existing continuous targets, layered over the timeline's base value. **Difficulty 7.2 / effectiveness 7.6** for deterministic non-audio modulation, subject to the remaining timeline audit. Audio-driven input adds analysis, synchronization and persistence work and is not included in that estimate. This is a creative animation feature, not a still-image quality or shader-speed improvement.

For a RFF design, evaluate base tracks and modulation through one composition path shared by preview and export. Persist seeds and stable target identifiers, define wrapping versus clamping, and specify whether multiple contributions are summed before nonlinear mapping. Ensure UI edits cannot alternate raw base values with modulated shader values; GMT explicitly tracks uniform ownership to coordinate those writers. Disabling a source must restore the appropriate base result rather than freeze a cached signal. Reordering or deleting a layer must not redirect an existing binding to another layer.

Separate continuous display targets from discrete shader modes and orbit-changing settings. Repeatedly crossing a compile-sensitive mode threshold could cause pipeline churn; changing formula parameters invalidates computation rather than merely recoloring the old field. For history-dependent envelopes, define replay, checkpoints or an equivalent reproducible evaluation method for seeks and parallel export. Validate the same timestamp after forward playback, backward seek, restart and split export, plus disabled identity and different preview frame rates. RFF's stable timeline IDs and append-only settings rules continue to apply. No modulation code or source noise implementation has been copied, and no animation test was run in this batch.

## U. Shader import: explicit capabilities before automatic translation

This batch completely reads the V4 [public entry](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/v4/index.ts), [type contracts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/v4/types.ts), all four files under its `ingest/` directory, and [import-capabilities.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/import-capabilities.ts). It establishes the import boundary, not the correctness of the still-unreviewed complete preprocessing, analysis and emission chain.

The public function separates format ingestion, preprocessing, analysis and emission, returning structured failure information when a stage rejects the input. Strong Fragmentarium directives or a `.frag` filename take precedence; DEC detection follows, then weak uniform annotations, then plain GLSL. This distinction matters because adding slider annotations to an otherwise DEC-shaped formula should not by itself change the recognized language. DEC ingestion actually invokes its own preprocessor and tests the resulting signature; it does not call the Fragmentarium ingest function despite an older header description suggesting that handoff.

The current V4 ingest contract is for **3D distance estimators**. Recognized 2D camera/includes, buffer shaders and custom `providesColor`/`providesBackground` declarations are rejected. Plain GLSL is accepted provisionally on a recognized distance-function signature taking `vec3`; this is a classification heuristic, not a compiler or a mathematical validation. Therefore the bundled 2D references in section O are conceptual material for RFF, not examples of a proven automatic V4-to-RFF conversion path. Presets, parameter annotations, reachable helper functions and mutable/global initialization have distinct representations downstream, which is a useful architecture for preserving source meaning.

Capability derivation inspects assembled GLSL text for named rotation helpers, cutting-plane symbols, selected c swizzles, assignment to `trap`, and changes to `dr`. It also records whether the formula is emitted as self-contained or per-iteration. These are useful hints for enabling compatible controls, but symbol matches do not prove mathematical semantics: the cutting-plane expression matches a reference rather than proving a write, and updating a derivative variable alone does not prove that a meaningful smooth-iteration channel is exported. Comments and unusual equivalent syntax also complicate regex inference. A RFF importer should treat inferred capabilities as candidates to validate, not as authority to enable MPA or advertise deep precision.

**RFF baseline:** [CustomFormulaPerturbator.cpp](../src/rff2/formula/CustomFormulaPerturbator.cpp) already parses custom complex expressions and iterates with `std::complex<double>`. The inspected path converts the center and pixel offsets to double and starts at z=0; it is not a GLSL distance-field importer. A complete port of GMT's importer would therefore target a different execution contract. Merely accepting GLSL or replacing vec3 with vec2 would not produce a correct perturbation recurrence, derivative propagation or periodic approximation.

**Conditional near-term idea: explicit formula capability reporting, difficulty 5.6 / effectiveness 6.8.** If the remaining RFF custom-formula UI audit confirms a gap, communicate supported precision, acceleration, derivative/statistic outputs and recurrence semantics alongside a formula. Explain why a requested combination is unavailable instead of showing an apparently functional control backed by dummy data. Derive these claims from the selected implementation and validated contracts, not its display name or source keywords. This complements section F's channel inspection without promising new numerical algorithms.

**Longer-term import design:** distinguish an expression recurrence, an orbit-statistic extension and an image/material shader. Each needs a different interface and invalidation scope. Preserve original source/provenance, parameter units, defaults and imported preset values; retain an explicit name-to-stable-target mapping for later animation. Keep import success, shader compilation, runtime execution and numerical equivalence as separate milestones. A usable 2D importer needs declared initial state, bailout/smoothing conventions and output-channel definitions, followed by precision validation for any accelerated route. No implementation priority or supported-format claim is assigned before the remaining emitter and RFF evaluator review. No importer or third-party formula code has been copied.

### Completed preprocessing follow-up: preserve meaning before stripping syntax

All five V4 `preprocess/` files and the shared `parsers/uniform-annotation.ts` matcher were subsequently read in full. The orchestrator normalizes line endings, collects curated builtin code from includes, extracts preset blocks, strips/replaces directives, parses annotations, applies the exactly named `Default` preset to parameter defaults, then prepends builtin code. These ordering decisions affect the result; inspecting the annotation parser in isolation is insufficient to establish the behavior of the complete import path.

| Source mechanism | RFF adoption requirement |
|---|---|
| Includes select curated helper strings by recognizable names; other includes are tolerated and later removed. Implicit math/time names can trigger generated definitions. | Distinguish renderer scaffolding intentionally replaced by RFF from required mathematical dependencies. Retain an import manifest of resolved, substituted and unresolved dependencies. Unresolved helpers must not silently become a claim of equivalent rendering. Check declarations and source tokens before injecting aliases. |
| Presets are maps of finite parsed scalars, comma-separated vectors or booleans. The orchestrator uses the exact `Default` name for overrides. | Define precedence and name matching explicitly, preserve the other named presets, validate vector dimensions and target types, and report unsupported values. `parseFloat` accepting a numeric prefix is not equivalent to validating an entire expression. Do not silently turn an unsupported expression into a plausible default. |
| Annotation parsing extracts ranges, defaults, a preceding comment, groups and inferred angle units. Numeric conversion falls back to zero when parsing fails. | Treat invalid numeric metadata as an explicit diagnostic, retain original text, and separate inferred units from declared units. Zero can be a meaningful or singular parameter, so it is not a neutral substitute. Validate range order and integer semantics before exposing controls. |
| `vec4` float-color annotations store a scalar in x and RGB in yzw. Lock suffixes are recognized by the syntax but not retained as a field in the returned parameter record. | Do not assume every vec4 is RGBA. Preserve semantic component layout and decide explicitly whether a source lock means a compile constant, a UI restriction or unsupported metadata. That decision affects pipeline specialization and animation. |
| A `sampler2D file[...]` annotation retains a uniform and produces a warning that its texture is ignored. | A syntactically retained sampler is not an imported material. Resolve and bind a supported asset or explain that the effect cannot be reproduced; keep source licenses and resource identities with the imported definition. |

There is a concrete pipeline-order limitation worth avoiding in RFF: the stripper removes `#group` before the annotation parser gets an opportunity to capture it. Thus the parser's group-handling code is not proof that this orchestrated path preserves source groups. Collect metadata before destructive stripping, and retain original source locations so later diagnostics still refer to the imported file. This is a requirement for an independent RFF design, not a request to repair GMT.

Macro handling also has a narrower contract than a complete language preprocessor. Object-like definitions are collected and substituted textually; `#replace` rules apply to subsequent lines as substring replacements, despite a comment describing word-boundary behavior. Vertex blocks and an identified `main` are removed. Do not reproduce these operations as a generic shader conversion algorithm without specifying supported macro ordering, conditional directives, scope and replacement semantics. An importer for a restricted formula language can reject unsupported constructs clearly rather than alter the recurrence while still producing compilable code.

The shared annotation-marker definitions reduce drift between format detection and parsing warnings, an architecture worth borrowing. Their existence does not prove full parsing coverage. For any future RFF importer, build end-to-end examples that retain initial values, units, component layout, grouping, resources and named presets from source through final runtime bindings. Verify an imported result against a valid reference renderer within a stated precision range; a successful parser or shader compiler is only an intermediate check. This follow-up does not change section U's provisional priority, and no importer tests were executed.

### Analysis and adapter follow-up: types are not mathematical contracts

The complete V4 `analyze/index.ts` and `emit/rename.ts`, `emit/slots.ts`, `emit/wrapper.ts` were read next. The analyzer uses comment stripping, signature matching and brace depth, not a full GLSL syntax tree. It selects a distance-function candidate by familiar-name priority and otherwise the first matching function. Other candidates are retained as helpers. Contrary to the stronger type-description language, this stage does not compute a reachable call graph: it collects other extracted functions. Parameter reconciliation against actual uniforms is explicitly left for future work in the code. A RFF implementation should separate discovered candidates from verified entry points and validate the complete callable signature before generating an adapter.

Globals are classified from initializer shape: numeric literals and numeric vector/matrix constructors enter the `constGlobals` collection, while other initializers enter the mutable collection. That is not a write analysis and does not establish immutability or the correct reset frequency. A variable initialized to zero may later accumulate orbit statistics. For RFF, determine whether state belongs to each pixel, each orbit, each evaluation or the immutable formula definition. Preserve initialization dependencies and explicit writes, especially when sharing a reference or skipping iterations. Inspecting this analyzer alone does not establish how the later emitter declares or resets every collected global.

The slot mapper deduplicates names, selects typed pools and warns when capacity is exceeded. It additionally routes the first matching iteration-like scalar name to a shared iteration uniform and recognizes selected Julia names. This illustrates why an import preview should expose the resulting mapping: a name such as `MaxRaySteps` can govern ray visibility work rather than orbit iterations. A RFF importer must distinguish iteration budget, ray steps, derivative state and display controls by explicit semantics. If a field is fixed at its default because no slot exists, show that limitation and retain its value; do not silently imply that it remains animatable. The actual constant-slot handling remains to be checked in the main emitter.

Renaming is sequential word-boundary text replacement. It casts scalar uniform slots back to int/bool uses, prefixes a selected collision list, and redirects `orbitTrap` into a shared adapter global. It also removes the vec4 type token from local declarations with that redirected name. This is more than cosmetic renaming: removing a local declaration changes ownership. RFF should use scope-aware symbol identity or a deliberately restricted accepted language, namespace imported definitions independently, and test shadowing and multiple instances. A sanitized formula name is a valid-identifier aid, not a uniqueness guarantee.

The wrapper calls the chosen distance function once, takes x from vector returns, applies `abs` to the distance and encodes that magnitude in an XY vector at the input position's angle. The outer loop then breaks; the distance reader recovers vector length. Trap data uses an adapter-owned reset and publication step, with squared input-position length as fallback when no accepted trap value was written. These are GMT adapter conventions. The packed vector is **not an orbit endpoint**, its angle is **not a computed escape angle**, the absolute distance loses the original sign, and the fallback trap is **not a measured orbit minimum**. Material IDs or other vector-return components are not retained by this wrapper.

For RFF, give distance, orbit endpoint, escape angle, iteration count and optional statistics separate validated channels rather than overloading one vector to satisfy an existing interface. Missing statistics should be unavailable, not a plausible substitute fed into coloring. A future adapter should retain signedness where the consumer needs it and define how extra return values are represented. This source batch reinforces the capability-reporting proposal; it supplies no evidence that arbitrary imported distance shaders can participate in RFF perturbation or MPA. The principal emitter and per-iteration transformation still require review, and no conversion was executed.

### Completed principal emitter: ordinary import versus composable iteration

The principal `v4/emit/index.ts` and its neighboring `parameters.ts` have now been read completely. The per-iteration transformer itself remains pending. The actual dispatcher attempts it only when `globalThis.V4_ENABLE_PER_ITER` is enabled. Otherwise it directly emits the self-contained wrapper. An unsuccessful optional transformation or failed parser probe falls back to that wrapper. Header statements that the self-contained route "always works" mean that this routine returns a generated definition; the routine does not establish successful engine compilation, execution or image equivalence.

The optional parser probe assembles a minimal GLSL fragment with selected uniforms, preamble, formula function and wrapped initialization/distance bodies. It does not include the generated loop body or full engine scaffold. Accordingly, passing that probe is a limited syntax check, not proof of engine integration or valid perturbation semantics. RFF should retain an explicit supported execution mode in the resulting definition and show a fallback's capabilities, rather than let import success conceal a change from accelerated/composable evaluation to a direct reference path.

The completed emitter resolves the earlier global-initialization question in part. Numerically initialized globals classified in the analyzer's `constGlobals` list are emitted as ordinary global declarations with initializers, **without a GLSL `const` qualifier**. Uninitialized globals are declared without resets here. Only the mutable-initializer collection receives assignments in `loopInit`, followed by the renamed source `init()` body. Thus the analyzer's collection name is not evidence that the output forbids later writes. The surrounding engine's invocation frequency still determines when `loopInit` runs; it must be checked before claiming that every distance evaluation resets all state. This remains a state-lifetime lesson for RFF, not a proposal to modify GMT.

Overflow parameters are concretely emitted as typed constants using imported defaults or zero fallbacks. That preserves some formula inputs while removing their editability; it is not parameter-capacity expansion. Unsupported samplers also enter the generic ignored-parameter path, so a successful generated result cannot be taken as evidence of usable external textures. A RFF implementation should handle resource-valued parameters separately from numeric constants and present fixed-versus-editable bindings explicitly.

The main emitter builds visible controls and a complete default preset through the older Workshop `buildFractalParams` helper, then overrides the shared iteration default when an imported iteration parameter supplies one. It collapses vector ranges to one encompassing scalar minimum/maximum. The neighboring `parameters.ts` offers another construction route, but the inspected principal emitter does not call it; an `engine-gmt` source search found only its function definitions. Do not infer the active import behavior from that alternative helper's comments. The reused Workshop builder still needs a complete read to establish which camera, material and coloring defaults are applied.

For RFF, preserve per-component constraints where they carry meaning, distinguish formula defaults from unrelated scene appearance, and make default application a coherent operation that can be undone. Keep one authoritative parameter-to-runtime mapping for controls, presets, serialization and animation. Validate the final assembled program and actual initialized parameter values, then compare images within a declared numerical range. This follow-up completes the principal emitter read, leaves the larger optional transformation and integration checks open, and makes no new GPU or numerical-equivalence claim.

### Completed Workshop builder: parameter storage versus artistic defaults

The full `workshop/param-builder.ts` and shared `parsers/angle-detection.ts` now clarify the remaining preset-building boundary. `buildFractalParams` creates two directional lights, a default gradient, atmosphere values, a quality step multiplier and an iteration default before filling formula slots. These are starter settings chosen by GMT, not a reconstruction of all visual settings in the imported source. No camera default is constructed in this helper. The V4 emitter subsequently replaces the iteration default when available, as described above. A RFF import should offer a formula-only application separately from an optional appearance preset so an existing palette/material composition is not unintentionally replaced.

The same file also contains an earlier Workshop parameter-discovery path. It can prefer values from a supplied first preset, normalize scalar/vector default shapes, allocate spare vector slots and pack booleans into vector components. Its availability therefore does not prove that V4 automatically uses every packing opportunity.

The final builder groups component mappings by their shared vector base and delegates combined controls/default values to `VecControlAccumulator`. It also encodes multiple booleans sharing a scalar as flag bits. For RFF, physical packing and logical parameter identity should be separate: a packed component must retain its own meaning, constraints, stable animation target and serialization identity. Matching CPU/shader decoding is essential; bit flags in float storage have representational limits and should not become a continuously interpolated material parameter. A space-saving representation is not itself evidence of lower shader cost. The shared occupancy/accumulator implementation remains pending review.

The angle detector requires both an angle-like name and a degree-like range. This is an inference, not unit metadata. The builder keeps the internal degree value while scaling the scalar control step into displayed pi units; otherwise a degree-sized step could span most of the display track. RFF should preserve explicit units through import, editing, animation and shader upload, with heuristics identified as suggestions. Narrow degree ranges and unconventional names can evade this heuristic. A vector-packed control follows a different route, so scalar unit behavior must not be assumed for every vector component.

Finally, `filterDeadParams` removes comments and looks for the mapped uniform's base name in generated text, while retaining Julia/builtin targets. This is a cheap availability hint, not dependency analysis: one used component can keep all controls sharing that base, and a textual occurrence need not affect an output. If RFF later reports a control as effective or unused, derive that from a supported mapping/dependency contract or state the uncertainty. Validate default application, component independence, exact boolean round trips and angle steps through the active import path. These findings refine the existing import proposal; they do not justify a new renderer feature priority or claim that GMT presets reproduce source appearance.

### Completed shared allocation and rotation contracts

The complete [uniformSlots.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/utils/uniformSlots.ts) resolves the previously pending packing implementation. Six scalar uniforms, three vec2, three vec3 and three vec4 uniforms form the fixed vocabulary. The scalar allocator uses the six scalars, then six vec2 components, then twelve vec4 components. A separate vec3 allocator uses the three vec3 units first and takes whole vec4 units from the opposite end when needed. It avoids colliding with scalar allocations already occupying that shared pool. Starting a new formula slot advances to a fresh vector boundary so unrelated formula slots do not create controls/defaults with the same vector ID. This deliberately leaves some components unused in exchange for independent ownership; the cursor's consumed count is not necessarily the number of useful parameters stored.

The occupancy helper describes component sets and supports whole vectors, scalar components and selected swizzles. It is not a complete validator for arbitrary user-supplied slot strings. Its set representation also does not retain how many parameters own a component: excluding the current control's components presumes an already-valid mapping. For RFF, validate mappings before accepting them and retain ownership identity or counts when diagnosing overlaps. Distinguish actual capacity exhaustion from invalid mappings. This is relevant to imported parameter extensibility, not a reason to replace RFF's existing Vulkan layouts with GMT's fixed WebGL pool.

`VecControlAccumulator` combines labels/defaults while widening min/max and taking the smallest step across occupants. It presents all-boolean vectors as toggles; a mixed bool/value vector gets a gating control only when explicit gating metadata is supplied. It retains rotation metadata only for a sole occupant and presents a vec3 held in a vec4 as three editable components. `slotWriteValue` supplies w=0 for that sole-vec3 representation. These are useful centralized write contracts, but merging storage does not make unrelated parameters share a valid mathematical range. Keep independent logical constraints in a RFF design even if values share one buffer block. Never clear a fourth component that a different logical parameter owns.

The complete [rotationDescriptor.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/rotationDescriptor.ts) separately identifies Euler angles, spherical-axis-plus-angle, unit direction and scalar twist, along with stored angular units and named Euler composition conventions. Its legacy fallback maps earlier control modes into those contracts. This is a stronger model than inferring semantics from a vec3 type alone. The descriptor itself does not implement or verify the conversion matrices; those remain a separate source review.

For RFF's 2D use, retain a clear distinction between canvas/image rotation, tangent-axis orientation and a light direction defined by angular coordinates. A 3D Euler order need not be exposed for an ordinary 2D texture rotation, but converting a material or light preset must respect the source convention. Preserve stored units independently of display notation and timeline interpolation. A future importer should test same-value read/write, two packed parameters edited independently, capacity limits, formula-slot reordering and known rotation fixtures across CPU and shader conventions. No packing or rotation implementation was copied or executed in this batch.

### Completed math helpers: compatibility includes operation conventions

The full `parsers/builtins.ts` and [rotationMath.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/utils/rotationMath.ts) show why the preceding contracts matter. The builtin bank is a curated subset, not a complete Fragmentarium installation: it supplies selected rotation, homogeneous-transform, box-fold, distance and complex helpers. The complex subset includes multiplication and a polar real-power function, not every complex helper a reference may call. A recognized include name must not be reported as complete library compatibility.

The real-power helper uses the principal `atan` angle and returns zero at z=0 for every exponent. A RFF adaptation must explicitly define branch cuts and zero with zero/negative exponents. For integer recurrence powers, a trigonometric polar implementation is not automatically numerically equivalent to repeated complex multiplication. Keep precision-sensitive recurrence operations separate from decorative coordinate transformations and never use this generic helper as justification for replacing RFF's existing arithmetic.

The builtin mat3 axis-angle helper normalizes its axis, whereas the mat4 helper uses the supplied axis directly. Both convert their angle from degrees. Matrix constructors, multiplication side and storage layout also determine orientation; equal function names or equal angle values do not establish equivalence. Before using such a helper in a 2D texture transform, verify a quarter-turn of a basis vector and transform order, including the screen-coordinate Y convention. Zero-length axes require a declared policy.

The CPU conversion module keeps separate GMT Z·X·Y, sequential Rz·Ry·Rx and MB3D Rx·Ry·Rz paths, plus six-plane 4D composition. Its spherical-axis helper preserves a small-angle dead zone and half-angle sine/cosine values for the corresponding GMT shader contract; its display helper uses a full angle. These are distinct conversion contracts, not interchangeable "rotation optimizations." Imported settings must retain the chosen convention rather than normalize them silently to a preferred one. Named MB3D/Fragmentarium provenance in headers requires original-license verification before copying code.

One potentially useful performance principle is to prepare parameter-only matrices or sine/cosine pairs once per parameter update. RFF's inspected `studio_basis` already shows why that must be selective: sine/cosine of a uniform tangent angle is invariant, but projecting that direction onto each pixel's varying normal is not. Moving the entire basis to the CPU would change the image. Consider only measured repeated invariant work, with synchronized host/shader layouts and dirty-state handling for animation. Driver optimization may already remove redundant work, so no speedup or priority score is assigned from source inspection alone. Validate mathematical equivalence and measure the affected shader before recommending an implementation.

The comments describe historical render evidence and a drift guard; this read has not reproduced either. Author/collection metadata also does not constitute a redistribution license.

For any future RFF formula library, retain original editable source, dependency/provenance records and the applied parameter mapping separately from generated code.
