### Completed DEC conversion: making selected constants editable

The full 751-line `parsers/dec-preprocessor.ts` was read across three contiguous ranges. It expands macros, finds selected constants in a recognized distance function, injects a limited set of missing helpers, replaces selected values, and emits annotated uniforms plus a default preset. Detected candidates include loop limits, scale factors, fold offsets, apparent rotation angles, clamp limits, translations and minimum sphere-fold radius squared. Ranges and names are inferred from local syntax and values, with a skip list for common literals. This is useful assistance for exploring a formula, not general discovery of meaningful or numerically safe controls.

**Conditional RFF idea: selected constant-to-parameter promotion, difficulty 7.8 / effectiveness 7.0**, after the existing expression parser and parameter UI have been audited for overlap. Allow an identified constant occurrence or declared group of linked occurrences to become an editable parameter with its original default. For a 2D recurrence, expose the effect as changing the formula and its required computation; for a decorative shader, limit invalidation to its dependent display stages. Do not imply that turning a constant into a uniform automatically preserves an accelerated implementation's assumptions. This exploratory workflow remains below the verified near-term display improvements.

GMT's extraction is context-sensitive, but the subsequent scalar replacement operates across the source using the literal text, rather than only the originally identified syntax node. Consequently, a RFF adaptation should bind promotion to source locations or symbols: the same numeric value in a bailout, scale and return expression need not be one parameter. Equal defaults are not evidence of intended coupling. Generated names must also be checked against existing symbols, and suggested ranges must respect singularities, sign constraints and the formula's supported numerical domain. Verify identity at the original parameter values before assessing edited results.

Macro expansion handles nested parentheses in arguments and repeats constant and function-like substitutions with a fifteen-pass bound. That bound is not proof of completed preprocessing. A RFF accepted-language contract should explicitly handle or reject unresolved/cyclic macros, argument count mismatches, definition ordering and unsupported conditional directives. Preserve operator precedence according to the source language rather than adding assumptions based on a likely expression shape. Missing `rotate2D`/`rotate3D` helpers receive specific radian implementations here; helper injection therefore also requires the unit/convention checks already discussed.

This pipeline masks source comments and does not restore them into the generated result. Keep original source and attribution independently; generated GLSL alone is insufficient provenance. Its generated vector preset values are space-separated, while the previously inspected V4 preset reader recognizes comma-separated vectors and otherwise uses scalar `parseFloat`. Therefore, passing this output onward is not evidence that vector defaults survive unchanged. RFF should share a typed representation between conversion stages instead of generating and reparsing an intermediate textual preset when avoidable. Validate vector default arity at the final binding, not merely at initial extraction.

An appropriate verification set includes repeated equal literals with distinct roles, nested macros, unchanged default rendering, negative/zero-sensitive controls, vector defaults, declared parameter collisions and round-trip save/reopen. These are adoption requirements derived from source inspection; no conversion, rendering or macro fixture was run in this batch.

### Documentation cross-check: architecture decisions versus verified support

Complete reads of [ADR-0058](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/adr/0058-v3-v4-dual-pipeline-with-catalog-autopick.md), [ADR-0059](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/adr/0059-feature-capability-protocol.md) and the historical [Fragmentarium format specification](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/history/gmt/26b_Fragmentarium_Spec.md) were compared with the inspected implementation. These are local project documents; their statements about upstream behavior/licenses and historical benchmark counts have not been independently verified here.

ADR-0058 explains the reason for retaining two import paths: preserving feature composition where supported while accepting other formulas through self-contained evaluation. It describes editable-source metadata for V3 and its omission from V4 at the time of writing. That is useful evidence of the intended round-trip contract, but current Workshop/serialization code must still confirm the present behavior. It also uses a legacy self-contained boolean that newer capability documentation says was retired. Treat that terminology as historical rather than a new RFF data-model template.

The format specification promises broader builtin coverage than the currently inspected curated bank: it lists noise, emulated-double and additional complex functions not supplied by that bank. It also describes group preservation and categorical texture/vertex rejection, whereas the inspected preprocessing path strips groups before parsing them, warns on texture annotations and removes vertex blocks. These differences mean that a document's "support" table cannot be used as proof of current behavior. Section U's RFF recommendations therefore rely on the narrower source evidence and explicit preservation/validation requirements.

ADR-0059 provides a useful architecture for the earlier capability-reporting proposal: formulas declare capabilities, features declare requirements/rejections, and a common evaluator produces status plus reasons for consumers. The complete current [capabilities.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/types/capabilities.ts) contains ten tokens, including later dIFS and true-fourth-spatial-coordinate distinctions; the original ADR table lists eight and its update discusses nine. The current type declaration is the vocabulary evidence. The evaluator and every consumer still require review before claiming uniform enforcement.

For RFF, use capabilities tied to actual computation/data contracts, such as supported precision path and availability of a genuine derivative or orbit statistic. Share the same decision between controls and execution so an unavailable option cannot merely appear disabled while another entry point enables it. Keep migration at file boundaries, retain stable identifiers, and return a specific reason when required data is unavailable. A declarative capability check complements numerical and shader validation; it does not replace them. The documentation check adds no new immediate shader-effect priority and leaves the complete UI, persistence and runtime enforcement audit open.

### Completed compatibility evaluator: availability is a declared contract

Complete reads of `engine-gmt/engine/compat/{evaluateCompat,pairHasCapability,index}.ts` and `engine-gmt/engine/FractalRegistry.ts` establish the actual decision semantics. In `evaluateCompat`, all required primary tokens must exist; secondary requirements are checked only when secondary capabilities exist; each pair token may come from either side. Rejection tokens disable the feature when present on the specified side. Features with no requirements receive `ok`. Although the status type allows `partial`, this implementation produces only `ok` or `disabled`. It reads the global feature registry, so its output depends on that registry as well as the supplied scene. The optional `enabledFeatures` field is not consulted.

For RFF, this supports a shared, reason-bearing eligibility decision, not a claim that controls and rendering are already uniformly enforced. A pair-level OR is useful for a feature that genuinely needs data from either participant; it does not prove that two recurrence steps compose correctly, that both provide a derivative, or that their combination supports perturbation or MPA. Represent an absent secondary separately from an incompatible secondary, and explicitly define which participant must provide each required result. Runtime consumers and saved-scene loading still need to use the same decision.

`FractalRegistry.register` checks the presence of capabilities before storing a definition, but does not validate the set's contents or establish numerical correctness. Registration replaces an existing ID. `registerAlias` stores the current definition object under another key; `getAll` deduplicates object identity. For a future RFF imported-formula workflow, keep source/version identity separate from display names and explicitly define replacement and alias behavior so cached compilation and saved scenes resolve the intended definition. These are adoption requirements; this review does not propose changing GMT's registry.

### Completed per-iteration emitter: composition requires explicit state and termination

The full `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/v4/emit/per-iteration.ts` was read in contiguous sections. Its `tryEmitPerIteration` converts an eligible distance function into initialization, one-step evaluation and final distance extraction. Recognized patterns cover a vec4 tracker, a vec3 working position, a scalar scale/derivative accumulator, or a min/max accumulator; implementations of imported V3 pattern helpers still require their own complete review. Structural rejection returns control to the self-contained route. Successful emission is not proof of compilation or numerical equivalence.

**Useful mechanism for RFF:** separating initialization, persistent recurrence state, one recurrence step, orbit-statistic updates, termination and final output can make composition and data availability explicit. For a 2D formula, those stages must retain the immutable pixel parameter separately from the evolving complex value, plus every additional state component. This is a design principle for a future custom-formula extension, not a ready-made conversion of arbitrary 3D distance estimators into Mandelbrot perturbators. Supporting an ordinary recurrence, a high-precision reference, perturbation and MPA are separate obligations; MPA depends on periodic structure and is not supplied by extracting a loop body.

The source demonstrates why that distinction matters. `hasCounterDependentLogic` removes certain counter-comparison patterns before checking remaining references. Later conversion removes matching `if (counter < NAME)` gates while retaining their bodies; the source explicitly acknowledges losing the first-N-iterations coloring behavior. A subsequent replacement removes `break` statements throughout the loop-body text, delegating bailout to the engine. Thus neither a successful match nor the emitted `shape:per-iteration` capability means original termination and orbit-coloring semantics are preserved. For RFF, retain the counter and an explicit stop result where supported, or reject the conversion with a specific reason. Do not silently reinterpret an imported formula to obtain feature composition.

State lifetime is equally important. `partitionPreLoopDecls` drops recognized tracker declarations, hoists declarations directly referenced by the return expression into global declarations plus per-pixel assignments, and leaves other statements in the per-step function. That is a syntactic partition, not dependency or liveness analysis. RFF would need to preserve transitive initializer dependencies, once-per-pixel side effects, nested scopes, helper-function writes and every persistent accumulator. A declaration's absence from the final expression does not make its repeated initialization mathematically harmless. The separate unrecognized-state check is also a textual heuristic, not a complete analysis of those cases.

The emitter rewrites the return expression onto engine state, substitutes the engine iteration count, and inserts a radial minimum trap fallback. That fallback should be identified as its own statistic; it cannot stand in for every imported orbit trap. Likewise, replacing a scale coordinate with `dr` requires a declared meaning for that state component rather than relying on its spelling or storage location.

**Verification required before RFF adoption:** compare original and converted step sequences and final outputs for nonzero loop starts, non-unit increments, early exits, nested-loop breaks, first-N trap updates, helper-mutated state and dependent initializers. Then separately verify the supported precision paths and any acceleration. This read adds no measured performance or visual benefit and does not displace the near-term filtering/environment proposals. No shader conversion, compilation or rendering test was executed in this batch.

### Shared pattern helpers: preserve what each state channel means

Full reads of `v3/generate/patterns.ts`, `v3/generate/loop-body.ts` and `v3/generate/get-dist.ts` complete the helper-level follow-up to the V4 emitter. These files expose reusable transformation ideas, but also show why generated-code acceptance must remain distinct from mathematical equivalence. The V3 top-level dispatch and fallback policy are not established by these three files alone.

**Orbit-trap channels are a useful 3D-to-2D transfer; collapsing their meaning is not.** `transformTrapMin` recognizes selected vector-trap expressions and replaces them with a scalar minimum of vector lengths. Componentwise minima and a minimum length encode different histories: for samples `(1,10)` and `(10,1)`, the componentwise minimum is `(1,1)`, whose length is approximately 1.414, while the minimum sample length is approximately 10.050. A RFF orbit-statistic extension could expose independent axis/shape minima and an explicitly separate radial minimum to drive color, roughness or emission masks. Preserve channel definitions and update windows in saved data; do not label a scalar replacement as preserving an arbitrary source trap. Computing these statistics during MPA skips remains the separate, unresolved acceleration requirement discussed earlier.

**Single evaluation before component writes is transferable.** `expandSwizzleWrites` saves a non-monotonic swizzle assignment's right-hand side in a temporary before writing its components. This preserves simultaneous-read behavior for operations such as swapping coordinates; sequential writes without a temporary could read an already modified component. A RFF compiler transformation should use typed, collision-free temporaries, validate legal destination components, and distinguish assignment from compound assignment. The inspected helper uses textual matching and fixed temporary-name construction. Its comment about backend rejection is not evidence that RFF's Vulkan toolchain requires the same workaround.

**A storage slot is not a derivative contract.** `detectScalarDRAccumulator` accepts multiplicative, inverse, additive and min/max accumulation when the variable occurs in the final distance expression, returning the first matching candidate. `detectAccumulatorPattern` can place a maximum-distance accumulator in `dr` and a scale accumulator in `z.w`. `detectVec4Tracker` uses initialization syntax and, for two forms, a numeric threshold of 0.5; the component-assignment form has no corresponding check. These mechanisms help fit particular source shapes into GMT's state layout. For RFF, an accumulator stored in a field called `dr` must not automatically enable derivative-based shading or distance estimation. Record the mathematical role, initial value and recurrence of each channel, and prove any mapping before enabling consumers.

Anchor rewriting similarly maps copies of a recognized position tracker onto `c.xyz` (or its vec4 form). For a 2D adaptation, establish whether that input represents the original pixel, a Julia constant or another invariant; matching copy syntax alone cannot decide. The initial parameter and evolving state must remain separately accessible when both are required.

`generateGetDist` maps position lengths to the engine's `r`, maps counters to `int(iter)`, and substitutes computed globals in a name-length order. Name length is not dependency order, and a substituted engine radius must have the same dimension and evaluation point as the original expression. `hasOutOfScopeRefs` is an identifier whitelist check, not lexical scope or definite-initialization analysis. The integer-literal repair helper likewise infers likely floating arithmetic from neighboring text rather than operand types. RFF should use typed expressions and dependency-aware lowering for precision-sensitive recurrence code; do not copy these heuristics as a precision optimization.

The reviewed V3 loop extraction also removes breaks and rewrites value-returning statements into void returns. These observations reinforce the preceding requirement to compare complete control flow and per-step state, not just successful compilation. No new immediate effect ranking follows from this batch; the practical proposal is richer, explicitly defined 2D statistic channels, conditional on computation cost and numerical validation. These sources were read but their transformations were not executed.

### Full-function fallback, initialization frequency and parameter fidelity

Complete reads of `v3/generate/full-de.ts`, `init.ts`, `rename.ts` and `uniforms.ts` clarify four additional adoption boundaries. They refine the custom-formula proposal rather than introduce a new immediate visual-effect priority.

`generateFullDE` keeps the original DE body together, resets initialized globals, inserts initialization, caches the returned distance, and forces the engine's outer bailout by assigning a large position. This is useful as an architectural alternative when splitting a function would lose local state. It is not an unchanged-source execution route: it can replace a hardcoded loop limit of at least four with the engine iteration control, inject trap/count updates, rewrite names and append a radius-based fallback return. For RFF, a fallback execution mode should preserve the accepted formula's semantics or explicitly describe the change. A syntactically valid fallback distance is not evidence of the intended mathematical result.

`injectOrbitTracking` places updates at the closing brace of the first matched braced loop. Breaks, returns and continues before that location can bypass them. Therefore the resulting counter is a count of executions reaching that instrumentation point, not automatically the original escape iteration or number of executed recurrence steps. RFF's channel definitions should specify whether statistics observe pre-step or post-step values and whether the terminating step contributes; test those conventions before using a generated channel for smooth coloring or material masks.

**Transferable performance mechanism: compute each expression at its true update frequency.** `generateInitCode` separates work executed before the outer loop from work emitted inside each formula call. Despite the name `perPixel`, that latter output runs per iteration in this route. Uniform-derived rotations and constants may be reusable, while recurrence-dependent expressions are not. The classification scans a small set of position-like names and treats an init block as a whole; it does not trace dependencies through globals or helper calls. RFF should distinguish per-setting/per-frame work, per-sample initialization and per-iteration state through actual dependencies. This strengthens the earlier rotation-precomputation proposal, but supplies no new measured speedup and does not establish additional overlap with RFF's current implementation.

`buildHelperRenameMap` usefully excludes DE-local position mappings from helper rewriting. The underlying AST visitor, however, substitutes matching identifier names without resolving lexical bindings, and some replacements are expression strings. Text fallback applies sequential replacements. A RFF importer should resolve declarations and uses, preserve shadowed helper parameters, and insert typed expression nodes when mapping an integer, boolean or vector component to a GPU parameter. Merely using an AST does not establish scope-correct transformation.

Finally, `formatGLSLLiteral` formats float/vector defaults with `toFixed(6)`, whereas explicit fixed values follow a different path. For example, that formatting turns a numeric default of 0.0000001 into 0.000000. This is direct evidence that this serializer is unsuitable as a precision-preserving RFF template. ## V. MandelTerrain: editable relief transfer curves for the existing 2D surface

The complete 599-line [MandelTerrain.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/MandelTerrain.ts) was read, including its shader, controls and full default preset. It evaluates a 2D Mandelbrot/Julia orbit inside a self-contained 3D height-field formula. The shader adds several independently weighted height terms: an exterior distance-derived term, a half-cosine ledge term, brightness sampled from a second mapped gradient, and an attenuated sum of near-origin orbit contributions. It clamps the combined height, then encodes a vertical residual for the surrounding marcher. This is evidence of a layered height construction, not proof that the returned residual is an exact signed distance.

**RFF candidate: a separately editable relief transfer curve.** The current [lustre_relief.glsl](../shdsrc/lustre_relief.glsl), symbols `lustre_height` and `lustre_sobel`, already computes a stable logarithmic relative height plus optional waves and derives local gradients from neighboring iteration samples. The targeted read of these functions confirms substantial overlap: height-based 2D shading itself is already present. The useful addition is control over the mapping from an available scalar field to relief, enabling rounded terraces, broad raised bands or narrow grooves while retaining the existing material/light model. Full overlap with every RFF layer remains to be checked before treating this as a missing feature.

A practical design would map a normalized, explicitly chosen field through a scalar curve H(t), then use differences H(t_neighbor) - H(t_center) for the existing normal construction. Provide separate amplitude, phase and smoothing controls, keep the current mapping as the legacy default, and preserve precision through iteration differences and periodic reduction. At high iteration values, do not first cast absolute values to float and then subtract them. Filter the transformed height over the output pixel footprint so narrow bands do not create false normals or shimmer; agreement between preview, video and tile boundaries is part of the contract.

GMT's layer-two contribution samples a color gradient and reduces RGB with fixed weights to a scalar. RFF should prefer a dedicated scalar height curve, with an explicit optional link to color if desired: changing a palette's hue should not silently change physical-looking relief. Define working color space if a color-to-height mode is offered, preserve held/moving phase semantics, and prevent a feedback dependency from final shaded color back into its own normal. The half-cosine segment has zero endpoint slopes, but wrapping or concatenating it into repeated bands still needs an explicit continuity rule; smooth endpoints alone do not prove seamless terraces.

The orbit-sum term illustrates a different, more expensive source. It weights near-origin visits by a geometric decay of 0.777 per step. That history is not recoverable from the final iteration count. In RFF it would require an additional statistic, storage and an exact or explicitly bounded treatment of skipped iterations. Do not silently disable MPA or synthesize the statistic from current scalar data. Likewise, the distance-height term needs a genuine derivative-based channel; this source's standard complex derivative is not a general proof for nonanalytic Burning Ship operations. These remain longer-term data-channel extensions, separate from a curve applied to existing iteration data.

For 2D geometric orbit traps, adapt the shapes to the complex plane explicitly. This source projects the orbit into XZ with Y=0; a three-axis minimum trap can become identically zero when a zero plane component participates. Use meaningful 2D point, circle or line distances rather than copy a 3D trap expression mechanically. The shader's actual geometric accumulation skips the first inner sample and has no inner color-iteration cap, despite older nearby commentary; define and validate RFF's own update window.

**Verification and priority:** compare the identity/legacy curve, smooth terraces and narrow grooves at multiple scales; test flat/interior regions, invalid neighbors, periodic seams, large iteration values and tile margins. Measure additional texture accesses and filtering cost. A transfer curve using existing fields is a plausible display-only extension; orbit histories and true terrain geometry are separate work. No effectiveness score is increased and no performance gain is claimed without rendered comparisons. The inspected preset has all four height weights at zero, so loading that default alone would not exercise these mechanisms. No shader or rendering test was run in this batch.

## W. Projection domains and periodic recurrence state

Complete reads of [MandelMap.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/MandelMap.ts) (586 lines) and [SineJulia3D.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/SineJulia3D.ts) (184 lines), including their presets, add two different transfer mechanisms. MandelMap is not a 2D Mandelbrot solver: `planeToBulb` maps a planar domain plus height into a sphere, cylinder or torus before evaluating the 3D bulb recurrence. Its spherical branch uses linear angular coordinates, despite a comment calling it Mercator; the implemented equations are the evidence.

**Conditional 2D transfer: periodic domains for procedural appearance layers.** At fixed radius, the torus coordinates repeat when either angular input advances by a full turn. This can supply a continuous periodic input to a procedural texture evaluated on that domain, useful for tileable backgrounds or decorative material patterns. It does not make an arbitrary bitmap seamless simply by transforming its UVs, and rendering actual Mandelbulb geometry requires a 3D evaluator. RFF already exposes a panorama projection in the inspected ExploreModel, so a new generic panorama option is not justified by this read. First check overlap with existing pattern mappings, then consider an explicitly periodic appearance-layer domain.

Preserve the chosen domain's local scale in texture filtering and normal construction. `formula_MandelMap` estimates an expansion factor from vertical scaling and radius times map scale, then modifies `dr`; that heuristic is not proof of a conservative Jacobian bound for every projection. For RFF's display-only mapping, propagate the coordinate derivatives or a validated finite-difference footprint rather than importing that raymarch correction. Test poles, repeated boundaries and highly stretched regions. If the mapping instead changes fractal sampling coordinates, it becomes a calculation/projection feature requiring consistent precision and export behavior.

The formula also subtracts phase divided by `max(1, power - 1)` from mapped angles to compensate visual movement while changing recurrence phase. This suggests an optional anchoring control for a procedural effect, but the same denominator is not a general law for RFF palette or texture motion. Derive compensation from the actual chosen transform, and distinguish a fixed appearance anchor from unchanged fractal geometry. Its use of `dr == 1` to trigger initial mapping further reinforces the earlier recommendation for explicit initialization stages instead of inferring execution phase from a numeric accumulator.

SineJulia3D explicitly places persistent derivative-product and wrapped-constant state in its preamble, initializes them before iteration, and declares those names for composition. Each step wraps periodic x/z inputs, evaluates trigonometric/hyperbolic terms, accumulates a derivative-related scalar and records the minimum absolute x/z trap. RFF's parser header already lists complex SIN and other transcendental operations; do not propose complex sine itself as missing. A Julia family additionally needs pixel-dependent initial z and an independently specified constant, unlike the inspected custom evaluator's z=0 initialization. That is a separate calculation-model extension, not merely a new shader preset.

Per-step periodic reduction may keep trigonometric arguments bounded, but cannot recover phase already lost through finite-precision arithmetic, and it does not bound the hyperbolic coordinate. Likewise, this 3D derivative estimate should not replace the exact derivative recurrence of an analytic 2D sine family. A future RFF implementation must specify valid numeric ranges, overflow behavior and supported precision/acceleration paths, then validate them independently.

The SineJulia3D header attributes the distinctive formula/DE to an external author and asserts a noncommercial share-alike license based on hosting defaults. That assertion has not been independently verified and does not establish permission to adapt the implementation. Preserve it as a provenance lead only; verify the actual original license before any code reuse. No external source was consulted, no formula code was copied into RFF, and no render or performance comparison was executed. These candidates remain below the already identified filtering/environment improvements in near-term confidence.

## X. Fold-based formulas: operation order, scale tracking and signed masks

Complete reads of [MengerSponge.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/MengerSponge.ts), [SierpinskiTetrahedron.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/SierpinskiTetrahedron.ts) and [MarbleMarcher.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/MarbleMarcher.ts), including controls and presets, deepen the earlier decorative-fold proposal rather than introduce a duplicate feature.

The important mechanism is an ordered transform sequence. Menger rotates, takes absolute coordinates, sorts axes, then scales/translates with an optional correction. MarbleMarcher puts one rotation after the absolute fold and other rotations after sorting. Sierpinski uses signed pairwise reflection folds followed by anisotropic scale, a precalculated rotation and translation. Moving a rotation across a fold changes the pattern because the operations generally do not commute. A RFF 2D appearance-layer adaptation should make order explicit and save it as part of the effect definition. Mirror/diagonal folds plus rotation and translation could create structured, repeating masks or kaleidoscopic image layouts while leaving the Mandelbrot recurrence intact. A 2D analogue is not the same object as the original 3D fractal.

For a two-coordinate sorting fold, direct min/max preserves the selected values without reconstructing a middle component by summing and subtracting. GMT's three-axis Menger implementation uses that latter reconstruction, while MarbleMarcher uses a subtraction-based sorting sequence. Neither source supplies a GPU timing comparison or an error bound. RFF should select operations for correctness at its supported scale, then benchmark; branchless syntax alone is not proof of faster code. Precalculate uniform-only rotations at the appropriate update frequency. MarbleMarcher's comment says once per frame, but its call is in `loopInit`, providing source evidence of initialization before the formula loop rather than CPU-per-frame evaluation.

**Mask extension:** MarbleMarcher's box trap records a signed box-distance expression, unlike a purely nonnegative radial minimum. A 2D rectangle analogue can distinguish interior fill, an outline around the boundary and exterior falloff. This could feed the existing material-mask proposal without a 3D raymarcher. Keep sign, units, operation (minimum versus maximum) and accumulation window explicit; taking an absolute value or clamping negatives changes its meaning. Applied to display coordinates this is a procedural mask; accumulated over an orbit it needs additional iteration statistics and the previously described MPA treatment.

The cutting-plane trackers in Menger and Sierpinski combine face constraints across iterations, rescaling by the accumulated transform. They are not a drop-in exterior-distance estimate for RFF's Mandelbrot set. In particular, Sierpinski's derivative tracker uses the arithmetic mean of per-axis scales, which its source calls approximate. RFF filtering or a conservative distance bound under anisotropic scaling needs the appropriate directional derivative or maximum stretch, not that average. Fold boundaries also require coverage-aware filtering because a pixel may cross multiple branches.

Verification should compare transform orders, unequal axis scales, zero/near-zero rotation transitions, signed-mask interiors/boundaries and minified folds, including full-frame versus tiled output. Full preset inspection matters: these presets include noncanonical offsets/rotations, so their displayed names do not establish a canonical mathematical reference image. No shader rendering, performance measurement or original-source license verification was performed; do not copy distinctive third-party-derived sequences before checking provenance.

### Hybrid and four-dimensional follow-up: state dimension is not a display option

Complete shader/control/preset reads of `engine-gmt/formulas/MixPinski.ts`, `BoxBulb.ts` and `Quaternion.ts` add concrete examples to sections M and X. MixPinski composes six four-dimensional pair folds, two scale/offset stages and a three-dimensional rotation. BoxBulb composes box/sphere folds, scaling and a power transform in each step. These are ordered compositions, not interpolation between two finished images. For RFF, a decorative transform stack can reuse the composition principle on layer coordinates; a recurrence stack is a new fractal calculation requiring its own derivatives, precision and MPA eligibility. The two proposals should remain separately selectable and described.

MixPinski's w component is actual evolving state: it participates in folds, offsets, the final maximum-component norm and trap magnitude. Quaternion similarly squares a four-component value and mixes visible coordinates with w through rotations. A 2D slice of either system still requires four-dimensional iteration; merely omitting z/w changes the dynamics. A future RFF exploration mode could define a two-dimensional sampling plane through a higher-dimensional state space, but it would need an explicit origin/basis and new evaluator. This is a substantial formula-family extension, not an immediate shader-only improvement to existing Mandelbrot maps.

Quaternion provides a more direct appearance-layer idea: an optional radial inversion of coordinates around an editable center. A 2D version could create inside-out image/pattern layouts. The source blends original and inverted positions and separately rotates the result; RFF should expose inversion radius and blend strength with clear units, define behavior at the singular center, and propagate the rapidly growing footprint into filtering. A hard denominator floor is a changed mapping near the center, not an exact inversion. Apply this to an appearance layer first if existing mapping controls do not already cover it; changing calculation coordinates requires separate precision and projection validation.

Read the feedback equation rather than its label. Quaternion's so-called damping adds `(newZ - oldZ) / (2 + 100*abs(amount))` to the newly computed value, which extrapolates along the step rather than interpolating toward the old state. It is enabled only above a threshold. This is not evidence of generic smoothing or a continuous identity limit as the control approaches zero. RFF should define any proposed recurrence feedback mathematically and derive its derivative/state updates accordingly; the inspected derivative expression precedes that feedback and does not by itself validate the modified map's distance estimate. No feedback feature is recommended as a numerical optimization.

The two four-dimensional examples also show why capability declarations need independent semantic checks: evolving w state is visible in the equations even when the listed tokens do not explicitly name four-dimensional distance use. RFF must validate state dimension, bailout metric and output channels together. Likewise, MixPinski's trap combines positional components with a squared radius before taking a length, which is an artistic statistic, not simply geometric distance. Preserve such channel semantics when designing generalized masks.

These reads add no measured speed or quality improvement. Validate transform-stack order, inversion identity/center behavior, slice-basis invariants and feedback derivatives before implementation. MixPinski names an original author and Quaternion names variant sources; those comments are provenance leads, not verified reuse licenses. No third-party implementation was added to RFF and no runtime tests were performed.

## Y. Stateful recurrences and Julia-parameter morphs

Complete reads of [Phoenix.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Phoenix.ts) and [JuliaMorph.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/JuliaMorph.ts), including controls and presets, identify two calculation extensions. They are useful 3D-to-2D transfers but are not post-processing effects and do not displace the near-term environment/filtering proposals.

### Phoenix: make orbit memory an explicit evaluator capability

Phoenix stretches the current position, applies ordered rotations and a position-dependent twist, evaluates a spherical power with phase offsets, optionally folds components, and adds a powered blend of two historical positions. Its complex history coefficient acts on XY while only its real part scales Z. The history blend is taken before the optional history power, so powering each historical value and then blending would define a different recurrence. The default history-depth value is one, selecting the older of the two stored states, despite the short description mentioning only the previous value.

The history update is significant: the stored current position is the already stretched/rotated/twisted position, not the raw incoming orbit value. Both history positions and derivative trackers start at zero for each evaluation. A RFF port must define this ordering and initialization explicitly and keep state local to each pixel/sample; frame feedback or an image trail is a different operation. The currently inspected [ExpressionParser.h](../src/rff2/formula/ExpressionParser.h) exposes `evaluate(z, c)`, and [CustomFormulaPerturbator.cpp](../src/rff2/formula/CustomFormulaPerturbator.cpp) calls that interface without history arguments. Supporting this family therefore requires new evaluator state and expression semantics, not merely a new formula string.

For an independently specified analytic 2D variant with no folds or spatial deformations, a useful starting contract is `z_next = F(z) + c + k*((1-h)*a + h*b)`, followed by `b = a; a = z_old`. Its complex derivative follows the same dependency structure: `D_next = F'(z)*D + Dc + k*((1-h)*Da + h*Db)`. This is a proposed simplified variant, not an assertion of equivalence to GMT's 3D formula. Define whether differentiation is with respect to the pixel's initial value or its parameter; Julia and parameter-plane initialization differ. Fractional powers require a branch convention, while absolute-value folds and anisotropic deformations require an appropriate real Jacobian treatment instead of blindly using a holomorphic derivative.

GMT's scalar derivative tracker combines the current power term, a history term weighted by the coefficient magnitude, and a Julia-dependent constant contribution. It does not establish a conservative bound for every enabled twist/deformation. Do not copy it as a precision or distance guarantee. RFF's perturbation and MPA support would need separate derivation over the extended state: recurrence of the current z alone is insufficient to establish recurrence of both history slots. Until such work is validated, expose the new family only through an explicitly supported calculation path, without implying existing deep-zoom acceleration applies.

Validate initial steps against the declared equations, h endpoints, zero history coefficient, independent pixels/tiles, derivative finite differences away from singularities, and save/load of every recurrence parameter. Keep reset semantics deterministic during animation. No numerical experiment or render comparison was run for this proposal.

### Julia Morph: turn the stack axis into a controlled 2D parameter path

JuliaMorph performs a complete inner quadratic Julia iteration and exits the outer formula loop immediately. It bends sampling coordinates, derives a clamped height parameter, applies taper and twist, and interpolates the Julia constant with `t*t*(3-2*t)`. Each sample's interpolated constant remains fixed throughout its inner orbit. It then combines an estimated lateral distance, a height bound and optional repeated slice bounds using maxima. The final vector packs the last complex orbit value, distance and smooth iteration count; these components are output data, not four interchangeable coordinates.

The most direct 2D transfer is to replace the stack coordinate with an explicit slider or deterministic animation time: `C(t) = (1-s(t))*C_start + s(t)*C_end`, and render a Julia set with that constant. This changes the fractal itself, unlike crossfading two rendered pictures. A contact sheet of selected t values could help choose paths before exporting a morph. The existing timeline should be evaluated for reuse rather than proposing a second animation system. Each changed constant requires recalculation; a palette-only update cannot reproduce it. A spatially varying t would instead define a parameter field and needs separate derivative semantics.

The shader initializes its complex orbit from the sample coordinates and its derivative magnitude to one. This initialization must be supported explicitly in RFF's Julia calculation path; changing only the constant in a Mandelbrot-style zero-initialized loop is not equivalent. Preserve export-time determinism and sufficient precision for the intended zoom range. The source's hard inner limit of 3000, fixed bailout, derivative clamp and smoothing convention are implementation choices, not requirements to import into RFF.

For 2D appearance work, the repeated slice operation suggests a periodic band mask on an existing scalar field. That would be an artistic analogue of the stack, not an actual 3D cut. Filter band coverage over the pixel footprint and retain a consistent phase at tile boundaries. This is a specialization of the previously proposed field-driven masks, not an additional independent high-priority feature.

Do not interpret JuliaMorph's interior value, derived from the minimum orbit radius, as measured boundary distance. Its deformation corrections and max-based intersection also do not prove an exact signed-distance field. In particular, variation of the Julia constant along the stack adds dependence that a fixed-C planar derivative alone does not describe. For RFF, keep orbit statistics, escape smoothing and genuine derivative-based distance channels separately named and validated. Test morph endpoints and intermediate constants against direct 2D iteration, along with preview/export agreement. These source reads provide mechanisms and integration requirements; they establish no measured speedup or image-quality gain, and no third-party code was copied.

### Julia-family follow-up: separate angular maps, sampling charts and distance claims

Complete reads of [Julia3D.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Julia3D.ts), [Julia3DKucera.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Julia3DKucera.ts), [Julia3DLattes.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Julia3DLattes.ts) and [Julia3DZorich.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Julia3DZorich.ts) reveal several distinct angular constructions. Their historical/proof/numerical-probe comments are source claims, not independently reproduced results in this audit. Some cite research notes or probe scripts outside the repository; those claims must not become RFF guarantees.

**Conditional circle inversions and angular partitions.** Julia3D's limit-set branch translates, folds Y/Z, then conditionally inverts in a fixed sequence of spheres. The inversion is identity at an individual sphere boundary before numerical regularization, but the composed map still depends on order. Its surface tracker is overwritten each iteration; despite its name, it is not a running minimum over the orbit. The escape-time branch instead selects a nearest angular cap, applies one inversion and a half-turn, then applies radial power and adds c. Sphere radius and centre-distance controls affect the limit-set branch; the escape branch uses fixed sphere constants. For RFF, distinguish controls by the active formula variant and distinguish last-step geometry from accumulated orbit statistics. A two-dimensional circle-inversion pattern is a plausible new recurrence or decorative mapping, with separate semantics for those two uses.

**A planar recurrence is available in the inflated construction.** Julia3DKucera normalizes the XY azimuth, chooses one of three complex fractional-linear expressions by angular interval, normalizes the result, and retains latitude before multiplying by the squared radius. With zero Z in both the initial state and c, the implemented update preserves the XY plane. This gives a concrete candidate for a new 2D formula family: a radial-square extension of the piecewise circle map. It is not numerically identical to ordinary complex squaring just because the source discusses conjugacy. The optional absolute-value fold occurs before the circle map and changes the recurrence. Test both sides of all three angular junctions, the origin, mode changes and parameter-plane initialization. The source's nearest-coordinate-plane trap becomes identically zero on the invariant XY plane because it includes abs(Z); a 2D port must deliberately choose a useful trap rather than retain that collapsed channel.

**Spherical chart transforms can be appearance controls.** Julia3DLattes projects a direction stereographically, squares a complex value, applies a rational transform and projects back. Optional folds precede that map. An optional rotation aligns c to a nearest X pole and is undone afterward; this is a change of orientation for the corresponding aligned construction, not evidence of a new independent shape family. Its separately named post-rotations actually execute in loopInit, once per orbit evaluation, whereas Julia3D's shared rotation executes each step. An RFF transform stack should expose this distinction explicitly. For image/material coordinates, a spherical chart transform could provide a new warp, but needs pole-aware sampling and derivatives; the inspected small denominator additions/clamps alter the map near singular regions and should not be copied as a generic stability proof. A 2D sample plane through the full 3D recurrence is also different from iterating only two coordinates, since this map can leave that plane.

**Mirror-tiled square charts.** Julia3DZorich converts a sphere direction to a square chart, multiplies chart coordinates by n, folds tiles using floor/parity, and maps back to a hemisphere with parity-dependent sign. The square ring uses its maximum absolute coordinate for latitude and a piecewise linear perimeter coordinate for azimuth. Its inverse uses the matching convention. For RFF appearance layers, that chart pairing suggests repeatable mirror-tile or square-to-circular coordinate controls, extending section M's ordered mappings. Carry local sampling scale through the transform and filter across tile edges; a continuous coordinate construction alone does not make an arbitrary image seamless. The declared power control selects integers 2, 3 and 4, but the shader only clamps a floating value. Preserve the discrete contract in persistence and animation if an adopted construction depends on integer tiling; do not assume the control's step size validates all imported or animated values.

**Derivative and precision boundary.** These shaders mostly track a scalar radial expansion and then use a logarithmic escape-distance expression. Angular transformations, branch boundaries and parameter-dependent additions require independent derivative analysis. Julia3DKucera itself notes differing angular expansion, while its implemented tracker remains `2*r*dr`; a smaller ray step factor is not a derivation of an exact distance. RFF should not import these trackers into perturbation, MPA or a true-distance output channel without validation. At minimum, check local Jacobians away from singularities, one-sided behavior at boundaries, and parameter-plane versus Julia derivatives. Keep higher-dimensional exploration as an explicit new calculation backend rather than weakening the existing precision contract.

The near-term value of these reads is additional coordinate-mapping and capability design detail, not a demonstrated improvement over environment lighting or footprint-aware filtering. Attribution headers name Kučera, amoser and Zorich/Mayer-related constructions, but publication approval and local attribution are not a verified code-reuse license. Verify the original sources and actual license before adapting recognizable implementations, and update NOTICE at implementation time. No external mathematical source was verified, no numerical probe was executed, and no application code was changed in this batch.

## Z. Box/sphere-fold families: reusable operators with explicit units

Full reads of [AmazingBox.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/AmazingBox.ts), [AmazingSurf.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/AmazingSurf.ts), [AmazingSurface.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/AmazingSurface.ts) and [KaliBox.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/KaliBox.ts) refine the existing transform-stack proposal. The shared box/sphere helper definitions in `shaders/chunks/math.ts` were also rechecked. These are four different recurrences; similarly named formulas must not be treated as interchangeable presets of one equation.

AmazingBox rotates before applying the componentwise box fold `2*clamp(p,-L,L)-p`, then sphere-folds, scales and adds c. AmazingSurf instead uses a fixed box limit, a sphere fold, scale/addition, a vertical shift and a cross-axis sine/cosine displacement. Its twist phase is computed from Z before the vertical shift. AmazingSurface takes absolute values and sorts three axes, scales around a box-size vector, clamps an inversion, and adds a uniform offset augmented by the Julia control; its formal c argument is unused. KaliBox rotates, takes absolute values plus translation, applies its clamped inversion factor and then rescales/adds c. Transform ordering, constant source and coordinate dimension belong in a future RFF operator contract.

**Units and valid parameter combinations.** The shared AmazingBox helper squares its min/fixed radius arguments; KaliBox's `MinRad2` is already a squared-radius quantity. In AmazingSurface, `Inv Max` is a maximum inversion multiplier, not a radius. A RFF control model should store and label these units explicitly, especially when exposing reusable operators or animating between presets. The shared sphere helper uses clamp bounds of 1 and fixedRadiusSquared/minRadiusSquared. Bounds cease to be ordered when the minimum radius exceeds the fixed radius, a combination not prevented by the independent slider ranges. AmazingSurf has the analogous ordering issue for min radius above one. Before implementing the operator in RFF, define a valid parameter domain and enforce it consistently at editing, loading and animation boundaries; do not silently rely on clamp to repair invalid bounds.

**A bounded 2D wave-warp candidate.** AmazingSurf's displacement can inspire an appearance-layer operator that offsets U by a sine of V and V by a cosine of U. Expose amplitude and frequency separately, with zero amplitude giving identity. Treat this as a refinement of RFF's mapping proposals, subject to checking overlap with existing warp controls, not as proof that generic warping is currently absent. If `U'=U+A*sin(f*V+phase)` and `V'=V+A*cos(f*U+phase)`, the off-diagonal derivatives are `A*f*cos(f*V+phase)` and `-A*f*sin(f*U+phase)`. Thus increasing frequency changes the sampling footprint even when amplitude stays fixed. Propagate this variation into section H's filtering; if phase itself depends on position, include that dependence too. The source's 3D twist loses its variation on a zero-Z plane, so a 2D version needs an explicitly chosen phase source rather than an unexplained dropped axis.

AmazingSurf updates its scalar derivative for sphere scaling and the main scale/addition but not the later wave displacement. This source observation does not quantify a rendering defect; it identifies why RFF must derive a warp's derivatives rather than copy the distance tracker. AmazingSurface's unconditional `+1` likewise is not proof of the derivative of its actual uniform-offset recurrence. Keep display-coordinate Jacobians, orbit derivatives and raymarch distance estimates as separate contracts. The two-dimensional appearance operator does not require changing the Mandelbrot calculation or MPA.

**Precomputation scope and orientation.** KaliBox prepares its rotation in loopInit, so the source establishes once-per-orbit preparation, not once-per-frame CPU work despite the comment. Its vector multiplies the matrix on the left; preserving only the matrix entries while changing multiplication side changes the transform convention. AmazingBox instead constructs rotations inside its per-step function. RFF can consider precomputing parameter-only trigonometry when profiling justifies it, while keeping per-pixel state and animated parameter updates correct. Neither source alone establishes a GPU speedup from moving this work.

**Masks and planar restrictions.** AmazingBox accumulates minimum abs(X), AmazingSurf minimum abs(Z), and the other two minimum radial length. These are different artistic statistics. An XY-only AmazingSurf recurrence with zero Z constant makes its Z trap zero; choose a non-degenerate 2D channel deliberately. AmazingSurface's three-axis sorting cannot generally be reproduced by simply deleting the third component because sorting can move a visible coordinate into it. A two-axis fold is a valid newly defined 2D pattern, while a slice of the original recurrence still needs its three-dimensional state. Thickness in AmazingSurface is subtracted from the selected final metric before division by dr; it is not automatically a world-space outline width for a 2D mask.

Validate operator identities, order, unit conversions, both sides of fold/inversion boundaries, degenerate centres, large frequencies and tile/export agreement. For new recurrences, separately verify initial state, constant source and supported precision/acceleration. These reads yield detailed requirements and optional pattern controls, not a newly proven highest-impact shader feature. The files name Tglad, Kali and Rrrola as provenance leads; actual reuse licensing remains to be checked before implementation. No RFF application code was changed and no runtime/performance tests were run.

### Kleinian follow-up: inversion placement, shell masks and alternating state

Complete reads of [Kleinian.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Kleinian.ts), [PseudoKleinian.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/PseudoKleinian.ts), [PseudoKleinianAdv.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/PseudoKleinianAdv.ts) and [PseudoKleinianMod4.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/PseudoKleinianMod4.ts) add the following requirements to sections E, M and Z. The Adv filename exports/registers `PseudoKleinian06`; the registry import was checked. A future importer must preserve the actual formula identifier rather than deriving it from a source filename.

**Inversion placement changes the result.** PseudoKleinian06 optionally transforms the initial sample as `radiusSquared*p/|p|² + offset`, then adds the box Z extent before starting its recurrence. The control named InvCenter is an output translation in this expression; the code does not subtract it before inversion. Mod4 instead optionally inverts the evolving point each iteration, before sign-offset, box fold and sphere fold. RFF's proposed inversion operator should distinguish input centre, output translation and execution stage. A single decorative inversion can wrap an existing pattern; repeating inversion inside a recurrence changes the generated set and has a different performance and precision cost. Do not advertise these as equivalent toggle placements.

**A shell mask is a useful 2D analogue.** PseudoKleinian06 combines a cylindrical radial term with its named Thingy expression using max, divides by a derivative tracker, subtracts an offset, then takes an absolute value. It subsequently applies an inversion-distance correction using the original sample radius. Mod4 selects plane, cylindrical or Thingy expressions; thickness enters different positions in these branches. These suggest an artist-facing mask built around a selected scalar level, for example a filtered band of `abs(field-level)`, with width and feathering in declared units. This is an extension of the earlier field-mask proposal, not a true-distance guarantee. Taking abs discards inside/outside information, so retain signed input separately when consumers need it. Do not copy the 3D inversion correction onto a 2D field mask or treat all branch-specific thickness controls as interchangeable.

**The sample stage is part of a trap's definition.** Kleinian records squared radius after its box fold but before inversion, scaling and translation. PseudoKleinian likewise records the pre-inversion radius. Mod4 takes the minimum of both a pre-sphere-fold radius and the radius after translation/alternating offset. Those channels can differ even for similar final orbits. A RFF orbit-statistic contract should name the stage and aggregation explicitly; a post-processing shader cannot reconstruct these statistics from escape count alone. Computing a decorative mask from an already available field remains a separate, cheaper option.

**Alternating offsets require state semantics.** Mod4 starts its sign at +1 for each orbit and flips it only when the alternating offset is enabled and that formula step executes. Its offset is along Z, which can move an initially planar orbit out of the plane. A two-dimensional alternating translation is possible as a newly defined variant. Store/reset its phase explicitly and define how hybrid schedules advance it. An MPA skip would need to preserve both orbit state and schedule phase; an even/odd shortcut alone does not validate the skipped nonlinear recurrence.

**Parameter guards are part of the map, not proof of accuracy.** PseudoKleinian's control labelled Power is used as a subtraction from Magic Factor, then as a radius multiplier, not an exponent. For a nonpositive difference, the denominator floor dominates and produces a very large multiplier. RFF should explain the actual parameter meaning and specify its admissible domain instead of copying a misleading label or silently accepting every slider combination. The Thingy expressions can encounter zero denominators at a zero translated point with zero thickness. Mod4's `dr *= k + 0.005` is an empirical tracker adjustment, not a derived Jacobian, and its position-dependent twist adds derivative requirements of its own. These observations define adoption checks; they are not proposals to repair GMT.

Validate stage order, inversion centres, mask sign/width, trap sample stages, orbit resets, hybrid phase, zero-thickness centres and disabled-operator behavior. Sign-based offsets have jumps at zero for nonzero offsets, so ordinary local filtering on one side does not integrate a pixel crossing that boundary. Compare such pixels explicitly. Source headers name Knighty, Theli-at, darkbeam and upstream projects; verify their actual licenses before reuse. No third-party implementation was copied, no rendering or numerical tests were run, and this batch does not change the current highest-impact recommendations.

### Repeated domains, branch-count coloring and sample-dependent constants

Complete reads of [KleinianJos.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/KleinianJos.ts), [KleinianMobius.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/KleinianMobius.ts) and [Apollonian.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Apollonian.ts) add three concrete mechanisms to the RFF adoption plan.

**Shear-repeat-unshear as a pattern operator.** The two Kleinian formulas add a Y-dependent shear to X, wrap XZ using floor-based periodic reduction, then subtract the shear. Conditional reflection, sign-based offset and inversion follow. This provides a useful model for skewed repeating 2D patterns: transform into a lattice coordinate system, reduce there, and transform back. It extends the earlier mapping-stack proposal rather than requiring 3D raymarching. Preserve the unreduced footprint for filtering and define behavior at lattice boundaries. Signed period semantics need care: Jos's preset includes a negative X extent, so blindly replacing periods with absolute values does not reproduce its coordinate convention. Zero period is undefined. RFF should use explicit orientation plus positive repeat lengths for a newly designed control, or preserve signed semantics when importing a supported format.

Apollonian has a different repeat: multiply each axis by `cc`, map to [-1,1) with fract, then divide by `cc`. Its effective period is 2/cc for positive cc. The source stores cc as one plus the exposed vector; the allowed endpoint -1 produces zero cc. Specify invertible scale values in a reusable RFF operator rather than relying on a slider name. Within a cell, scale and inverse scale cancel in the local coordinate derivative, but the discontinuity and repeat frequency remain relevant to filtering. Repetition is not a mirrored fold, and an arbitrary image need not match across the resulting edges.

**A separate branch-count color channel.** Both Kleinian implementations increment a counter whenever their reflection condition is taken. Despite the comments calling it a crossing count, the code does not compare consecutive condition states: repeated visits to the same branch also increment it. getDist adds a sigmoid of the final radius and returns the result as smoothIter, clamped using the configured iteration limit. This is a useful artistic statistic for patterns whose escape count varies little, but is not the ordinary smooth escape-time quantity. For RFF, a future orbit-statistic extension could expose branch occupancy/count, with a separately named optional fractional modulation, without overwriting the existing iteration channel. Define treatment of interior pixels, early termination and zero/small iteration budgets. The sigmoid does not remove discontinuities in the integer count. Such a channel needs calculation support and MPA-compatible aggregation, or a supported unaccelerated path; it cannot be recovered from an existing escape-count map alone. No new map-format mode is proposed without the existing lossless/versioned format requirements.

**Last-two aggregation is not global periodicity detection.** The Kleinian distance expressions retain the last two local estimates and take their minimum, rather than minimizing over every iteration. This is a formula-specific choice intended to handle two-phase behavior, not a general proof of a two-cycle and not a replacement for RFF's period logic. Distinguish final value, running minimum and a bounded history window in any generalized statistic interface. The formulas also keep their own accumulated inversion factor instead of updating the common dr argument; an importer must retain that separate state and its initialization.

**Constant during an orbit can still vary between pixels.** Apollonian computes a cosine-modulated inversion multiplier from the initial coordinates, recomputes it after an enabled inversion pre-transform, and holds it throughout the orbit. Moving it to a frame-global uniform would change the image. Conversely, reevaluating it from the evolving z each step would change the recurrence. For a 2D procedural pattern, this suggests spatially modulated but orbit-fixed parameters. Include their dependence on the sampled coordinate when deriving derivatives: tracking only inversion factors does not account for that parameter gradient. Source comments saying constant per ray should not obscure that loopInit belongs to an individual distance evaluation, which can occur repeatedly along a ray.

The Jos and Mobius variants also differ in threshold constants, initialization offsets, inversion enablement and reflected Z offset; their shared structure does not establish equivalence. Their inversion pre-transform squares the radius, while the later correction contains the unsquared radius; Apollonian's correction uses radius squared. These are source expressions to verify against each intended definition, not interchangeable correction recipes. Preserve numerical precision and validate centres, radius units, repeated boundaries and statistic resets before any RFF adoption. The original-author/license comments, including the Mobius Unlicense assertion, remain provenance leads pending original-source verification. This batch copied no code and ran no numerical, shader or rendering tests; it does not change the near-term filtering/environment priorities.

## AA. Power-family controls: reuse RFF expressions and preserve the selected plane

Full reads of [Mandelbulb.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Mandelbulb.ts), [Mandelbar3D.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Mandelbar3D.ts), [Buffalo.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Buffalo.ts) and [Bristorbrot.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Bristorbrot.ts) identify authoring improvements and concrete planar restrictions. RFF's current [ExpressionParser.cpp](../src/rff2/formula/ExpressionParser.cpp) was checked at function recognition, opcode mapping and evaluation for conj/rabs/iabs/riabs: these operations already exist. Do not propose them as missing math primitives.

**Expose stage-aware fold recipes over existing functionality.** Buffalo folds selected components before rotation/power and independently folds selected components after power but before c addition. For a deliberately defined complex 2D variant, RFF can already express examples such as `riabs(z)^2+c` and `riabs(z^2)+c`; these are different equations. A useful addition would be an optional recipe editor with explicit before/after toggles and a visible generated expression, subject to checking the existing editor's controls. Keep abs (complex magnitude) distinct from componentwise rabs/iabs/riabs. Rotation and c addition must retain their declared positions. Such recipes improve discoverability and reproducibility, not numerical capability or deep-zoom acceleration by themselves. They are 2D analogues, not claimed exact slices of Buffalo's spherical power.

**Choose an invariant plane deliberately.** With twist and rotation disabled and constants/offsets restricted to the chosen plane, Mandelbar3D's XY restriction updates `(x,y)` as `(x*x-y*y, 2*x*y)`, while its XZ restriction updates `(x,z)` as `(x*x-z*z, -2*x*z)`. The first is complex squaring; the second is conjugate squaring. A label saying 3D Tricorn is not enough to choose a 2D implementation. Bristorbrot's unrotated XY restriction similarly reduces to complex squaring; its distinctive cross-terms require nonzero third-coordinate state. For RFF, a plane selector through a 3D recurrence and a standalone two-component formula are different features. Rotations, offsets and hybrid steps must preserve the plane before an exact restriction is claimed. The Bristorbrot preset enables hybrid mode, so it is not an isolated validation scene for the bare polynomial.

**Clipping the orbit is not clipping the final image.** Mandelbulb's Radiolaria option caps Y after power, optional twist and c addition. A 2D counterpart would cap a chosen component after a declared recurrence stage, yielding a new piecewise formula. An appearance-layer height cap is separately possible using the scalar transfer-curve proposal in section V, but does not reproduce that orbit mutation. Preserve separate naming, recalculation scope and derivative support for these alternatives. The source attributes the mutation to Tom Beddard; original provenance/license verification is still required before adapting recognizable implementation material.

**Derivative placement and singularities need independent treatment.** Mandelbar3D and Bristorbrot form their scalar `2*r*dr+1` term before multiplying the tracker by the main scale, although c is added after scaling the polynomial. That tracker is not automatically the exact derivative for the parameter-plane recurrence. Coordinate folds, caps and twists also need their actual piecewise real derivatives. Mandelbulb computes the polar angle using z/r without a local zero-radius guard, whereas Buffalo floors r before its power and angle calculations. A RFF formula definition should specify the origin's mathematical behavior and implement that deliberately; adding an arbitrary floor changes the recurrence near zero and is not precision preservation. Test actual initialization and first steps, not only escaped points.

**Optimization evidence remains platform-specific.** Mandelbulb shares one radial power between the radius and derivative expressions and reuses trigonometric terms. Its comments report unsuccessful approximate inverse-trigonometric substitutions on ANGLE/D3D11, including numerical drift. The linked benchmark handoff was located and partially inspected, not fully audited or rerun in this batch. These historical statements are not Vulkan performance results. RFF should preserve its precision contract and only adopt measured common-work elimination that retains the intended numerical behavior; no approximate-math speedup is recommended. Likewise, Buffalo's branchless label is not a measured advantage over branching on RFF's target GPU.

Finally, Buffalo records a radius from before its power update, while Mandelbulb records length after the update and optional cap; Mandelbar3D/Bristorbrot record squared length after their update. A shared color-channel interface must preserve stage and units. Validate fold-order examples, planar invariance, c initialization, cap boundaries and derivative behavior separately from visual recipe previews. No shader implementation, rendered comparison or numerical test was performed, and these findings do not supersede the higher-confidence environment/filtering candidates.

### Coupled-state and editable-plane follow-up

Complete reads of [MakinBrot.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/MakinBrot.ts), [Tetrabrot.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Tetrabrot.ts), [Claude.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Claude.ts) and [Modular.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Modular.ts), plus `engine-gmt/data/initialPipelines.ts`, refine the formula-authoring proposal without introducing four separate high-priority features.

MakinBrot changes the third polynomial component to `2*z*(x-y)`. With no out-of-plane transforms or constants, its XY restriction again reduces to complex squaring, so merely dropping the third coordinate loses the distinguishing behavior. It shares the scale/derivative placement issue discussed above: the scalar tracker is updated before the full scale, whereas c is added after scaling the polynomial. A RFF recipe based on a planar reduction should describe the resulting equation rather than promise the appearance of the original 3D preset.

Tetrabrot's fourth component is evolving state, including the term `2*(x*w+y*z)`, and feeds back into the first three components on the next step. Its positive w-squared contribution to the first component also distinguishes this particular squaring map from ordinary quaternion squaring. The existing DE initialization was spot-checked: it initializes z.w from ParamB and constructs c with ParamA in Julia mode before formula execution. A supported higher-dimensional RFF explorer therefore needs separate initial-slice and constant controls, a declared 2D sampling basis, and a full-state bailout metric. Fixing w at every iteration would define another formula. The declared formula capability list does not itself prove these dimension/metric requirements. Validate zero and nonzero hidden components and rotations; do not reuse a two-component perturbator or its MPA tables by analogy.

Claude applies three ordered half-space reflections, an optional fourth reflection whose normal rotates around a fixed axis, a sphere fold, scale/offset and an optional position-dependent twist. The practical 2D appearance transfer is an editable set of fold lines. For unit normal n, `p -= 2*min(0,dot(p,n))*n` leaves one half-plane unchanged and reflects the other. Rotating a normal changes the fold direction, while rotating the entire image afterward is a different operation. Such a control could extend section M's decorative transform stack to adjustable kaleidoscopic layouts. A small explicitly ordered set of lines need not produce exact global rotational symmetry, so avoid promising that from the fold count alone. Across a fold the coordinates meet continuously but their derivatives change; filter the resulting pattern at the crease.

The source's optional fourth plane is controlled by an angle, not reflection strength. Its precalculation runs in loopInit, despite a once-per-frame comment, and its radius controls are already squared quantities. Its subsequent twist is absent from the scalar derivative update. These details reinforce the earlier requirements for parameter units, execution stage and derivative contracts. A newly designed 2D fold-line control does not require copying the source's distinctive golden-ratio normal set or adopting its descriptive uniqueness claims.

Modular.ts contains empty shader strings, a modular capability token and a reference to an initial node pipeline; it is a descriptor, not the implementation of the graph compiler. The fully read initialPipelines.ts defines ordered nodes with stable-looking IDs, enable flags, parameters, optional slider bindings and explanatory Note nodes. Its supplied pipelines illustrate box-fold/sphere-fold/scale/addition and repeat/rotation/power/addition compositions. For a RFF recipe editor, inline explanations and explicit parameter bindings could make the proposed stage-aware controls easier to understand. Treat those as authoring metadata separate from executable operations. A zero repetition value appears in the supplied Z parameter, so the actual node implementation must be checked before interpreting zero as a disabled axis or an invalid divisor. The descriptor and preset data do not establish current compiler behavior, successful shader generation or full graph capability propagation; that audit remains open.

No new visual-effect score is assigned from these files. Validate full-state initialization, order, coordinate-plane preservation, fold identities and binding/save-load behavior before adoption. This batch changed documentation only and ran no numerical or rendering tests.

## AB. Fold-and-cut fields for geometric masks

Full reads of [Dodecahedron.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Dodecahedron.ts), [RhombicDodecahedron.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/RhombicDodecahedron.ts) and [RhombicTriacontahedron.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/RhombicTriacontahedron.ts) clarify a shared fold-and-cut mechanism. The cutting-plane consumer in `engine/estimators.ts` was spot-checked; its result is `vec2(abs(cp_dmin), cp_trap)`. This observation also reinforces that a second result component is not universally an iteration count.

Dodecahedron explicitly applies nine ordered half-space reflections. RhombicDodecahedron runs three rounds of four different reflection normals. RhombicTriacontahedron alternates componentwise abs with a diagonal reflection five times.
