Each then samples a particular plane in the folded coordinates, accumulates `max(previous, reciprocalScale * planeValue)`, scales/translates the point, and updates reciprocalScale by dividing by the current positive scale. The plane measurement occurs before that iteration's scale/translation. A translation or Julia addition afterward changes subsequent cuts, not the cut already accumulated. Source comments claiming complete symmetry, convergence for all points or measured distance error are not independently verified by these reads.

**2D transfer:** extend the existing field-mask proposal with a procedural fold-and-cut source: fold a coordinate through an ordered collection of lines, evaluate a line offset, accumulate a signed field over a specified number of stages, and map the field to fill/outline/feather controls. This can create nested angular layouts without a 3D raymarcher. Define a genuine two-dimensional construction rather than dropping a component from the supplied 3D normals; their reflections can move points out of the sampling plane. It is an optional pattern source for RFF's material/image layers, distinct from modifying the Mandelbrot orbit. Existing maps need no additional orbit statistics for a screen-anchored version.

**Metric and sign:** reciprocal scale compensates uniform scaling under a declared coordinate convention; it is not automatically correct for added anisotropic scaling or position-dependent twist. The maximum of normalized plane values can be a useful signed field, but it is not generally the exact Euclidean distance outside corners. Do not describe feather width as a geometric distance unless that property is established. Preserve the signed accumulator for inside/outside consumers and take abs only for an explicitly unsigned outline. The GMT estimator does take abs; copying only its output would erase the sign needed by a filled mask.

**Scale and filtering:** the offered scale range includes values below, equal to and above one. Those regimes change reciprocal-scale growth and pattern behavior. Define finite-stage behavior at each regime and avoid assuming that every allowed setting contracts to a fractal attractor. Evaluate antialiasing at fold creases and max-switch boundaries, with the output-pixel footprint and full-frame/tile coordinates treated consistently. A smaller render scale or generic final downsample is not by itself a guarantee that narrow procedural bands are integrated correctly.

**Shared state:** the formulas update three separate engine-owned quantities: accumulated cut field, reciprocal scale and a trap copied from the running minimum of the selected length metric. A compatible node or formula interface must initialize and preserve those quantities as a coherent contract. A capability token alone is insufficient for a hybrid composition if one participating step changes scale/coordinates without corresponding state updates. These requirements concern adoption into RFF; this batch does not establish that GMT's complete hybrid path violates them.

Validate identity folds, reflected-pair behavior, transform order, a one-stage reference shape, positive/zero/negative field values, scale near one and tile seams. Keep references to Knighty/Syntopia and distinctive normal sets as provenance leads until original licensing is verified. No source implementation was copied, no mathematical symmetry proof or numerical/rendering experiment was performed, and the new detail does not increase this optional pattern feature's priority over filtering or environment illumination.

### Parameterized symmetry, moving cut planes and neutral controls

Complete reads of [Coxeter.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Coxeter.ts), [GreatStellatedDodecahedron.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/GreatStellatedDodecahedron.ts) and [MengerAdvanced.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/MengerAdvanced.ts) refine section AB's proposed geometric pattern controls.

Coxeter derives a reflection normal, cutting-plane normal and offset direction together from N, then uses five abs/reflection rounds per iteration. N changes the geometry of the operators, not their repetition count. Its UI accepts fractional values and reaches six, where the square-root component tends to zero. For RFF, distinguish named discrete symmetry presets from continuous artistic deformation; fractional N should not be described as a verified finite symmetry group. A 2D fold-line implementation can offer angle controls with selected symmetric presets, without claiming to reproduce the 3D construction or its complete fold domain. Validate normal length and boundary behavior across the supported range. The precalculation is called from loopInit; the file's once-per-frame wording does not establish host-side caching.

GreatStellatedDodecahedron constructs two face-normal directions using a reflection sequence, takes a normalized linear blend, and recomputes the plane offset as the dot product with a fixed reference point. Its moving plane therefore passes through that reference point scaled by the size control. The per-iteration coordinate folds and offset direction do not vary with stellation; the cut plane does. The high-level description of pushing points outward should not replace this actual mechanism. A 2D analogue is a line rotating through an anchor inside a folded domain, producing changing angular cuts. Normalized linear interpolation does not give constant angular speed; if RFF exposes an animation control, define its interpolation law explicitly. Check near-zero blended normals before normalization in a general editor.

The stellation control permits extrapolation outside [0,1], and its shipped preset value 2.88 exceeds the declared slider maximum of two. That source observation does not establish how every GMT loading path handles the value. It does show why RFF should distinguish an editing range from the accepted serialization domain: define whether valid extended values can be displayed/edited, and avoid silently changing saved appearance merely by opening a control. Do not reuse existing recipe IDs or modify their generation order to add these patterns.

MengerAdvanced rotates, sorts absolute coordinates and samples its cube-face field before applying an optional inner box fold, uniform scale/offset and a separate Z scale. Its top-level text uses outdated parameter letters; the executable controls bind Inner Fold to ParamC and Z Scale to ParamD. The source explicitly describes its cutting-plane result as approximate when those deformations are active. The directional stretch factor used for dr depends on the point's Z alignment, not on a propagated tangent/Jacobian, so it should not be adopted as a general anisotropic derivative bound. A RFF 2D pattern may support independent axis scaling, but its filtering footprint and any distance interpretation need the appropriate transform derivative.

A particularly useful authoring lesson is the difference between disabled and zero-limit operations. MengerAdvanced skips the inner fold at zero. For a positive limit L, the component map is `2*clamp(x,-L,L)-x`, whose limit as L approaches zero is -x, not x. Thus animating the limit down to zero is not a smooth fade to the disabled state. The source also substitutes 1.001 for scales close to one and suppresses Z scaling within a tolerance of one. For new RFF controls, make enablement, geometric limit and optional blend amount separate concepts. If a smooth blend is offered, it defines a new mapping with its own derivative and possible degeneracies; it is not an exact replacement for the source recurrence.

These details can improve the proposed pattern editor and preset reproducibility. They do not justify a separate feature for each source formula or a higher effectiveness score. Validate active/disabled limits, interpolation endpoints and extrapolation, scale near one, animation continuity and preview/export agreement. No application code, numerical tests or render comparisons were produced in this batch; original formula/provenance licensing remains to be verified before adaptation.

### Initial folds and multiple cutting planes

Full reads of [Octahedron.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Octahedron.ts), [Cuboctahedron.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Cuboctahedron.ts), [Icosahedron.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Icosahedron.ts) and [TruncatedIcosahedron.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/TruncatedIcosahedron.ts) complete another set of concrete fold-and-cut examples.

Icosahedron and its truncated variant perform an initial abs/reflection sequence using n1, n2, n3 and n2 again. Their repeated step uses only abs and n1, after the optional twist/rotation. Their conditional reflections act on positive dot products, unlike several previously inspected formulas' negative-half-space folds. A RFF recipe format must preserve the initial transform list, repeated transform list, normal orientation and reflected side separately. Repeating the full prefold every step or reversing the sign test would define another pattern. This is a concrete reason to include initialization in the authoring/import contract, rather than treating a formula as only its loop body.

Cuboctahedron folds with four abs/reflection rounds and evaluates three normalized plane expressions, combining them with max before the existing across-iteration maximum. Octahedron uses four conditional swaps/sign-swaps and only the resulting X plane. Their names and symmetry descriptions do not establish identical domains or exact signed-distance behavior. For RFF's proposed procedural masks, a bounded list of independently defined line cuts provides a direct 2D counterpart to the multi-plane mechanism. Keep normals and offsets coherent, specify whether they share an anchor, and retain the previously described distinction between a signed half-space field and Euclidean distance at corners. Adding several planes changes the shape without requiring an image-space blur or fractal-orbit change.

TruncatedIcosahedron clamps its control to [0,1], normalizes a blend between two directions, and uses the result for both the cutting-plane normal and the IFS translation direction. Thus its interpolation changes repeated dynamics as well as the cut, unlike the stellated example where the IFS offset direction is fixed. The overview and inner comments describe the endpoint shapes differently; neither is sufficient evidence that a particular intermediate value produces a geometrically exact named solid. In a RFF editor, distinguish cut orientation from recurrence translation, optionally linking them as an explicit recipe choice. Normalized blending is not generally constant-speed rotation. Validate endpoints from the equations and reference geometry before attaching exact shape names.

All four presets include substantial lighting/color/quality state in addition to the formula. Geometry comparisons should use a common display setup so palette contrast or relief lighting is not mistaken for a formula difference. Several presets contain both nested and top-level light records; these files alone do not establish load precedence, so a future import cannot select one merely by position in the object. The relevant loader needs independent inspection. No GMT preset is being imported into RFF in this audit.

These reads add implementation requirements to the existing mask/recipe ideas rather than four new feature recommendations. Required validation includes first-step versus later-step behavior, reflected-side selection, multiple-plane boundaries, coupled versus independent controls and save/load reproducibility. No shader, numerical or rendering tests were run, and original-source licensing remains unverified for adaptation.

## AC. Shared operator definitions and stable recipe identities

Full reads of [boxFolds.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/boxFolds.ts) and [formulas/index.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/index.ts), with the fold-list index rechecked, show how GMT turns shared operators into registered formulas. This is an architectural transfer for the proposed RFF pattern/recipe system, not a new rendering effect.

The builder consumes each fold's GLSL and metadata, remaps uniform names into generic slots, and adds a wrapper. Ordinary folds receive rotation/shift/fold/unshift handling, a sphere fold, scale and optional c addition. Self-contained folds omit the outer sphere fold and scale because their own body supplies the IFS step. Rotation has two contracts: wrapping a fold with a matrix and its transpose, or applying a rotation after the sphere fold. Preserve these operator boundaries in a RFF design; applying a generic wrapper indiscriminately can double a scale or change the order of noncommuting operations. A displayed description that always says fold/sphere/scale is not sufficient to describe self-contained variants.

The source reuses one fold definition rather than maintaining manually copied bodies. RFF could similarly generate its recipe editor, parameter bindings and shader operations from a typed operator description, with initialization and state requirements included. The inspected builder uses regular-expression renaming and checks that the expected helper name appears; that check alone does not validate all bindings, GLSL types or compiled behavior. Use a constrained typed representation or narrowly validated templates for newly designed RFF operators, and verify the resulting host/shader interface. Capability metadata should reflect enabled behavior and state requirements, not merely a shared function signature.

Several names require precise interpretation. Scale Variation computes `s = A + B*(abs(A)-1)` on each call; it does not accumulate a changing scale over successive iterations. For non-self-contained folds, the derivative wrapper adds one regardless of whether Add Constant is enabled. Those are actual source semantics to preserve or explicitly redesign, not evidence of a general derivative formula. Only selected fold kinds expose a Fold Limit control, which is a useful model for avoiding ineffective controls in RFF's recipe editor.

Identity is also separate from display order. The fold list uses stable numeric codes with retired gaps; lookup searches by code rather than array index. One retired code maps to the standard fold and another has no successor. The adapter comments explicitly acknowledge dropped custom values and an unsupported legacy constant permutation. For RFF, preserve existing recipe IDs and generation order, store operator versions independently from UI ordering, and report unsupported or lossy migrations explicitly. A similarly named replacement should not be treated as equivalent without parameter-level evidence. This proposal does not authorize changing the existing binary config or map formats.

The formula aggregator registers built-ins and explicit legacy aliases. BoxFold definitions instead register through a separate registration function; the fold-list index currently contains seven types. Therefore, a formula catalog audit must include generated definitions and registration paths, not only the aggregator's array. This batch fully reads the builder and aggregator, but does not establish end-to-end migration correctness or shader compilation for every generated combination. Registration, successful compilation, numerical equivalence and visual equivalence remain separate checks.

No application code was changed, no generated shader was compiled and no performance result is claimed. For adoption, validate representative ordinary/self-contained operators, both rotation modes, optional constants, duplicate instances, stable-ID round trips and unsupported legacy settings. Upstream decompilation/certification wording in comments is not independently verified provenance or permission to reuse code; follow RFF's original-source/license and NOTICE requirements before implementation.

## AD. Coupled-coordinate derivatives and a lifted planar formula

A complete read of [MandelBolic.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/MandelBolic.ts), including its controls and full preset, identifies a derivative-analysis technique relevant to RFF's proposed coordinate warps. Its 3D recurrence consists of a complex-plane power multiplied by a height-dependent factor, together with a separate height recurrence. The height recurrence combines linear amplification, an odd quadratic term and a sine term. The last two terms vanish at zero height, but the additive height constant and offset must also vanish for that plane to remain invariant.

**Separate a planar restriction from a 3D extension.** With height T=0, zero height injection, power two and zero phase, the ideal unregularized planar expression reduces to ordinary complex squaring plus c. Other powers and phases change that planar formula, and the implemented multiplier is `r²/(r²+1e-20)` at T=0 rather than identically one. Its power evaluation also floors small radii. Thus the description's exact-Mandelbrot claim is not a license to replace RFF's current precise recurrence with this shader. The default preset enables a burning geometry option as well, so it is not an isolated reference configuration for the bare formula. Validate the full initialization/geometry/bailout path before making equivalence claims. A genuinely new 3D height-state evaluator would be substantial work; RFF's existing display relief does not acquire those dynamics by changing a height color curve.

**Transfer the matrix method, not an unverified bound.** The shader constructs four nonnegative stretch/coupling entries and computes the larger singular value of that 2-by-2 matrix using its squared-entry sum and determinant. Accounting for off-diagonal terms is a useful principle for RFF's 2D texture-coordinate warps: an X offset driven by Y can enlarge the footprint even when both diagonal derivatives equal one. For an actual Jacobian J, its largest singular value can provide an isotropic minification scale, while anisotropic filtering needs directional information too. Preserve the distinction between a mathematically derived Jacobian and a hand-built matrix of estimated stretch terms.

Here that distinction is material. The planar multiplier depends on both height and planar radius. Differentiating the product requires the planar derivative of the multiplier as well as its height derivative; the implemented jA term alone does not include the former explicitly. For example, in the unregularized power-two, unit-cone, zero-phase case with height scale and nonlinear height terms zero, at `(x,y,T)=(r,0,r)` for r>0 the multiplier vanishes. The X output still has radial derivative 2r and height derivative -2r, while jA is zero and jB is 2r. This shows why a singular-value formula applied to the chosen block does not by itself prove the full map's bound. This is an analytical adoption check, not a measured GMT rendering defect or a request to change GMT. RFF must derive every coupling term for its own mapping and validate finite differences away from branches/singularities before relying on a footprint or distance bound.

**Numerical range matters.** The direct singular-value expression squares an already squared-entry sum; large entries can overflow before the final square root. A future RFF implementation should use a scale-normalized calculation, handle a zero matrix explicitly, and retain an error/precision contract rather than inserting arbitrary clamps. Check weak shear, strong shear, isotropic and anisotropic scale, rotation and near-singular transforms. A matrix-based footprint estimate applies to the appearance pipeline; it does not replace perturbation or MPA error analysis.

The custom getDist supplies logarithmic distance and smoothing expressions independent of the selected estimator setting, but its smoothing uses base-two logs while the power control is variable. The appropriate smooth-count convention needs derivation for each supported recurrence and escape rule, rather than copying the source's claim of exact matching. The trap is a scaled final-position length accumulated by minimum, not a new physical height channel. These findings strengthen the filtering and typed-channel requirements already proposed; they do not add a measured speed or quality gain. No application code was changed and no numerical, shader or rendering tests were run in this batch.

## AE. Ring and cross-section coordinates for annular patterns

A full read of [Mandelorus.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Mandelorus.ts), including its embedded preset, establishes a three-coordinate recurrence: the function reads and writes XYZ, not an evolving fourth component. It decomposes a point into ring angle phi and cross-section coordinates `(length(XY)-R, Z*(1+verticalControl))`, twists the cross-section by a phi-dependent rotation, raises that complex cross-section to a power, multiplies the ring angle by the same power, and reconstructs XYZ before adding c. The short description's topology language is not a mathematical equivalence established by this audit.

**2D appearance transfer:** add an annular coordinate mode to the earlier mapping-stack proposal, with ring radius, angular phase and cross-band phase as separate controls. One independent 2D design can use angle and signed distance from a selected circle as the two image/pattern coordinates. Another can use those coordinates to drive a procedural band warp. These are useful artistic analogues; replacing the source's Z coordinate with an existing field defines a new mapping, not an exact 2D restriction of the toroidal recurrence. Keep the full 3D recurrence as a separate optional calculation feature if ever pursued, with its own initialization, precision and bailout contract.

**Phase position matters.** The source adds cross phase before multiplying the cross-section angle by power, while ring phase is added after multiplying the ring angle. Consequently the same numerical phase change has different angular effects in the two controls, and changing power also changes the cross-phase effect. Twist is divided by max(1,power) before the cross power. Preserve these units if reproducing the behavior, or expose output-angle phase in a newly designed RFF control. Avoid treating phases as interchangeable generic offsets during animation or preset migration. The positive-looking GLSL mat2 entries also need to be interpreted with GLSL's column-major multiplication convention when reproducing the twist direction.

**Seams are a property of the complete map.** atan returns an angle with a branch cut. Multiplying it by a noninteger power does not generally match on the two sides of that cut, and the fractional twist control can change cross-section orientation there too. Integer settings can restore particular periodicities, but the complete composed mapping and texture content must be checked. RFF should offer an explicit periodic mode with validated parameter constraints or label the visible cut as part of an artistic warp. Filter periodic coordinates before wrapping and define behavior near the ring axis, where angular derivatives grow without bound. The source's derivative padding by vertical scale and `1+0.3*abs(twist)` is heuristic; it does not substitute for the coordinate Jacobian required by section H's footprint filtering.

**Component cap placement differs from the bulb example.** Mandelorus applies its optional symmetric Y mutation before c addition; Mandelbulb applies its cap after addition. For nonnegative limits the intended branch caps magnitude, and for negative limits the other expression rescales magnitude. However, the source computes both expressions as inputs to a floating-point mix, including a denominator `1-limit` that vanishes at positive limit one. A newly implemented RFF piecewise operator should keep evaluated operands finite throughout the accepted domain or use appropriate conditional evaluation. A branchless label does not establish numerical safety or a speed advantage. The cap acts on global reconstructed Y, so it is not uniformly a cross-section-thickness control around the ring.

The trap records squared cross-section radius before the power update, including the vertical scaling; it is neither final 3D radius nor the distance to the reconstructed surface. Keep that statistic separately named if adapting a formula, and do not infer it from an ordinary escape-count map. Validate phase placement, seam limits, centre handling, cap enablement and preview/video/tile agreement for the 2D appearance version. This adds detail to the existing coordinate-mapping proposal, not a measured new priority. No shader or numerical experiment was run and no implementation was copied into RFF.

## AF. Appell and cyclic coupling: separate appearance controls from recurrence mathematics

Full reads of [Appell.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Appell.ts) and [Borromean.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/formulas/Borromean.ts), including their complete presets, finish the current inventory's top-level formula TypeScript files. This does not finish the nested formula/reference directories, shader feature integrations, documentation, or the whole repository audit.

### Appell: radial subtraction and an artistic distance multiplier

The actual operation is a spherical power of XYZ, followed by subtraction of `k*(r*r+bias)` from the X component, then addition of c. Phase is added to the azimuth before multiplication by power, so its output-angle effect scales with power. The function has no evolving fourth coordinate: the control labeled Ghost Shift / fourth-dimension bias contributes a constant X displacement of `-k*bias` at fixed k. A physical four-dimensional slice is not established by that label. The source's theoretical balance and Appell terminology remain source descriptions, not independently verified mathematical claims.

The Cloud Density control leaves the position recurrence unchanged. It multiplies the derivative accumulator by `1-0.1*density` at each step, after an update whose multiplier is `power*r^(power-1)-2*k*r`. This is neither a sampled volume density nor an optical-depth integral. The signed multiplier can cancel or become negative and is not a conservative norm of the full real Jacobian. The source also divides by r for its polar angle without a local zero-radius branch. These are reasons to derive the RFF adaptation independently, not reasons to spend this audit repairing GMT.

**Useful 2D transfer:** an independently defined custom-formula recipe can use `z^p-k*(norm(z)+b)+c`. RFF's [ExpressionParser.cpp](../src/rff2/formula/ExpressionParser.cpp) already maps norm to std::norm, the squared complex magnitude, so this ingredient does not require a new parser primitive. This is an artistic complex-plane analogue, not a claimed invariant slice of the spherical map. Fractional powers require an explicit branch convention and origin behavior. For power two and no phase, its real-coordinate update and local Jacobian are:

```text
x' = (1-k)*x*x - (1+k)*y*y - k*b + real(c)
y' = 2*x*y + imag(c)
J  = [[2*(1-k)*x, -2*(1+k)*y],
      [2*y,         2*x      ]]
```

The radial term is non-holomorphic for nonzero k; one complex derivative cannot replace this real Jacobian. Any distance shading, perturbation or accelerated skipping needs the appropriate state propagation and error analysis. Existing Mandelbrot MPA is not automatically applicable. At k=0 the proposed recipe reduces to ordinary complex power, and bias then has no effect; these are useful future verification cases.

**Appearance-only alternative:** reuse sections E and V to map a documented orbit/iteration field into opacity, emission or a soft material mask, while preserving the numerical field and any derivative used for geometry. Call the result a stylized haze or shell effect, not volumetric scattering. This lets an artist obtain a ghostlike appearance without making a numerical distance accumulator double as a density knob. The embedded GMT preset uses substantial glow, ten iterations and a 0.01 ray-step fudge factor; its appearance cannot be attributed solely to the recurrence or density control. Controlled visual comparisons must hold those other effects fixed. This finding refines an existing material-mask proposal rather than introducing another bloom proposal.

### Borromean: simultaneous coordinate feedback, not three sequential complex powers

After an optional XY rotation, the shader computes the three absolute coordinate powers from the same position, then simultaneously assigns all three outputs. With q=power, a=repulsion, b=balance and t=invert*connection, the unshifted update is:

```text
X = abs(x)^q - a*abs(y)^q - b*abs(z)^q + 2*t*z*x
Y = abs(y)^q - a*abs(z)^q - b*abs(x)^q + 2*t*x*y
Z = abs(z)^q - a*abs(x)^q - b*abs(y)^q + 2*t*y*z
```

The code then adds c. Its description of one plane feeding the next is a conceptual description of coupling, not an instruction to update X before evaluating Y and Z. A sequential in-place implementation would calculate a different recurrence. The mixed products remain quadratic even when q changes, while the absolute-power terms have degree q; consequently the full update is not generally homogeneous of degree q. Do not infer a generic power-law scaling or escape smoothing solely from the Power slider.

**2D transfer boundary:** a screen displaying a slice of a three-coordinate orbit can retain XYZ internally, but RFF's existing complex state cannot represent that extra independent coordinate. Nor does starting at z=0 generally preserve the XY plane: before c addition, the next Z is `-a*abs(x)^q-b*abs(y)^q`. With constant cz, this vanishes for every XY input only under appropriate restrictions (in the displayed map, a=b=0 and cz=0 suffice). Dropping the third equation gives a new planar formula, not the original coupled system. The most reusable idea is therefore a clearly ordered mapping/recipe editor, already discussed in sections M and X, with simultaneous vector updates distinguished from sequential operator composition. A full cyclic-family feature is a lower-priority separate evaluator project, not a shader-only material improvement.

**Derivative and animation details:** the source's scalar derivative multiplier is `q*r^(q-1)` and does not account for coupling strengths. For phase zero at `(x,0,0)` with x>0, the derivative of the output vector with respect to x alone has norm `q*x^(q-1)*sqrt(1+a*a)`, exceeding that multiplier when a>0. This analytic observation is enough to reject the multiplier as a general Jacobian norm bound; no rendered failure is claimed. The XY phase branch is skipped for abs(phase)<=0.001, introducing a small activation discontinuity that should not be inherited accidentally by a smoothly animated RFF mapping. GLSL's column-major matrix convention also determines the actual rotation direction. Trap accumulation uses squared radius after c addition, whereas Appell records radius before the update; exported or material-driving fields must preserve that distinction.

**Adoption priority and validation:** these formulas provide recipe and field-semantics ideas, but do not displace editable environment reflections as the current provisional choice for broad material appearance. Before implementing a recipe, check zero/axis inputs, phase boundaries, fractional-power branches, simultaneous versus sequential updates, bailout behavior and any Jacobian against independent references. Compare preset appearances under common lighting and postprocessing. No formula implementation was copied, no RFF application code changed, and no numerical, shader-compilation or visual tests were run in this batch.

## AG. Direction controls and runtime shadow choices: host-to-shader transfer

Full reads of [LightDirectionControl.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/lighting/components/LightDirectionControl.tsx), [GizmoMath.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/lighting/utils/GizmoMath.ts) and [ShadowControls.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/lighting/components/ShadowControls.tsx), followed by targeted checks of the already inspected lighting schema and shader chunks, extend section P's lighting discussion. This is source analysis of parameter semantics, not a screenshot-based usability audit.

### Aim existing relief lights with a shared directional pad

GMT maps a two-dimensional control coordinate to a direction on the sphere. Normalized pad radius one means a 90-degree deviation from forward; its polar angle is `min(length(pad)*pi/2,pi-0.001)`. The azimuth comes from atan2. The resulting vector is `(-sin(theta)*cos(phi), sin(theta)*sin(phi), -cos(theta))`; camera orientation rotates it into world space unless the light is camera-fixed. A quaternion mapping from local negative Z to that vector is converted to YXZ Euler angles for storage. The displayed handle performs the reverse direction projection, using the live camera orientation. Both the pad and another light-placement interaction share the same helper, avoiding two independently defined aiming conventions.

**RFF improvement:** a direction pad can edit the existing main-light, fill-light and independent-specular azimuth/zenith controls without introducing another shading model. [CallbackShader.cpp](../src/rff2/ui/CallbackShader.cpp) already exposes these controls, while [studio_surface.glsl](../shdsrc/studio_surface.glsl) forms the specular and fill direction as `(cos(azimuth)*sin(zenith),sin(azimuth)*sin(zenith),cos(zenith))`. The material foundation therefore already exists; the addition would improve placement and comparison rather than claim a new light capability. Preserve the independent-specular link behavior so moving a highlight need not move the main light's shadows.

Do not copy GMT's Euler values into those RFF fields. Define whether each vector points toward the source or follows emitted light, account for the screen-Y convention, and convert a normalized vector to RFF's own spherical coordinates. The environment editor in section G can share directional convention helpers, but rotating an environment and moving a direct light remain distinct controls. A camera/world mode is useful only if RFF has a corresponding coordinate-frame requirement; the pad alone does not justify importing a 3D camera subsystem.

**Boundary and persistence details:** the poles have no unique azimuth. Retain the previous azimuth when appropriate to avoid control jumps, and preserve equivalent saved angle representations unless the user actually edits them. RFF currently allows angles across a full turn, so converting all loaded settings to a canonical half-sphere parameterization could change interpolation even when the instantaneous light direction is equivalent. The pad must have a declared accessible angular range and sufficient area to display it: GMT's ring radius is 35 percent of width/height, while the theoretical rear direction lies at twice that radius and can extend outside the rectangular control in some azimuths. A newly designed RFF control should explicitly support either the front hemisphere or a visible, selectable rear hemisphere. Test the mapping and inverse at axes, horizons and poles, and compare a simple known relief under each light rather than trusting matching angle labels.

**Animation and gesture contract:** GMT's automatic recording on pointer release writes three rotation tracks, while its manual keyframe/status actions cover only pitch and yaw. A reusable RFF direction control should have one declared track group and consistent set/delete/status operations. Direction-only lighting does not require an artist-facing roll control; however, conversion and interpolation must preserve the intended direction across angular wrap and antipodal cases. Treat a whole drag as one edit transaction, including cancellation and capture loss, and route all input surfaces through the same conversion. The component delegates cancellation to an interaction hook; this read alone does not prove the hook also resets all local and transaction state, so that behavior remains to inspect rather than being reported as a confirmed GMT failure.

### Runtime quality controls must be traced to shader consumers

ShadowControls changes `shadowAlgorithm` between zero and one. The lighting feature schema maps it to `uShadowQuality`; the shadow chunk selects HQ below 0.5 and Lite otherwise. Both branches occupy the generated shadow shader. HQ computes a previous/current-distance penumbra correction with a validity fallback, whereas Lite uses the current h/t ratio and a larger step floor. Thus the inspected path supports the claim that this quality choice changes a uniform rather than selecting separate shader source variants. Comments asserting an approximately twofold speed difference or negligible branch overhead remain unverified performance claims and do not establish Vulkan behavior.

The Jitter button writes the historically named `areaLights` setting, mapped to `uAreaLights`. In the direct-light PBR path it perturbs shadow direction and target distance, changes the hardness parameter, then calls the same shadow march once. It does not duplicate the complete march into both toggle branches. This stochastic shadow-direction option is distinct from sampling a physical spherical emitter. The feature schema intentionally does not exempt either quality or jitter changes from accumulation reset, because each can change the image being accumulated; verifying the actual global reset dispatcher remains separate from reading this declaration.

**RFF transfer:** use small runtime controls for inexpensive coherent choices when they improve interactive comparison, and keep expensive structural shader choices subject to measurement and the replacement-pipeline workflow in section I. A single expensive call after lightweight parameter selection is worth considering where two branches otherwise duplicate it, provided input and output semantics agree. Do not promise that a uniform branch is free, that a driver never predicates work, or that an ANGLE observation predicts Vulkan compilation. When a rendering change invalidates a cached or accumulated result, rebuild that result from the changed state rather than blending incompatible images. This is a state-management requirement, not a proposal to add temporal accumulation to RFF solely for this feature.

For 2D relief, shadow quality must be defined against the actual height/field representation. GMT's 3D distance-estimator penumbra and ray-step floors cannot be inserted unchanged into a height-field shadow pass. Compare time, stability and fine-feature retention on representative reliefs before selecting a quality policy; do not trade perturbation precision for shadow speed. This batch adds implementation conditions to existing lighting and responsiveness proposals, not a measured new top-priority effect. No application code changed and no interactive, shader-compilation or rendering tests were run.

### Follow-up: light units, attenuation and emitter visibility

Full reads of [LightControls.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/lighting/components/LightControls.tsx) and [lightMenuUtils.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/lighting/utils/lightMenuUtils.ts), plus targeted consumer checks in [UniformManager.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/managers/UniformManager.ts), establish several concrete requirements for a future RFF lighting editor. These refine the existing lighting proposal; they are not an argument to add every GMT light type.

**Exposure is a representation with animation consequences.** GMT packs EV intensity as `2^(storedIntensity+modulation)` and raw intensity as `storedIntensity+modulation`, then clamps nonnegative and gates it by visibility. The same additive modulation therefore means multiplicative brightness changes in EV mode and additive changes in raw mode. The unit menu converts and rounds the stored value: raw-to-EV clamps to [-4,10], rounds to 0.1, and maps raw zero to EV zero; EV-to-raw rounds to 0.01. The sphere-light control separately offers EV values up to 20. These code paths show why unit selection cannot be assumed to preserve all values or their animated meaning. This audit has not tested the complete store/update flow.

For RFF, keep a canonical linear intensity and an explicit off/zero state when offering alternate numeric displays. Convert only at the editing boundary, retain precision internally, and avoid rounding merely because the display mode changes. If an exposure-based animation track is offered, give it explicit interpolation and modulation semantics; a representation switch must not reinterpret existing keyframes silently. Preserve authored extremes on load even if a compact slider shows a narrower range. RFF already has image exposure controls in [CallbackShader.cpp](../src/rff2/ui/CallbackShader.cpp), including a linear HDR exposure control; a per-light stops display would be a separate authoring convenience, not a missing global exposure feature or a faster shader.

**Range is not a finite support radius.** For non-directional lights, UniformManager converts positive range R to either a quadratic coefficient `99/(R*R)` or a linear coefficient `99/R`. The inspected direct-light shader consumes those coefficients in attenuation `1/(1+k2*d*d+k1*d)`. Consequently attenuation at d=R is 0.01; the source does not cut illumination to zero there. The added constant one also means this is a softened artistic attenuation convention, not unmodified inverse-square falloff. When range is at most 0.001, the packer instead uses the legacy falloff plus its modulation, clamped nonnegative. Thus a UI label of Infinite at small range is insufficient evidence of constant attenuation for every loaded legacy state. Define the actual contract in any RFF positional-light extension, and do not cull at the nominal range unless an explicit bounded approximation and its error are acceptable. Existing directional relief lights do not need distance attenuation merely to reuse the improved direction controls.

**Emitter visibility and illumination are independent dimensions.** The sphere-light UI toggles hideEmitter while retaining radius, whereas the point-light visible-sphere toggle switches radius between zero and 0.1. Sphere selection ensures a finite initial radius. The UI also explicitly announces a point-at-center fallback when physical sphere sampling is unavailable and offers the required renderer/feature change. Useful transfer: keep the artist's source extent, visual representation and contribution controls distinct; disclose an approximation rather than showing a control whose advertised behavior is inactive. Section G's independent environment background and illumination strengths follow the same principle. A sphere-source simulator is a much larger project than an editable environment lookup and is not currently prioritized for RFF.

**Coordinate-frame changes should preserve the current appearance.** The anchor handler converts position between camera-local and world coordinates using the camera quaternion, camera position and scene-offset high/low components; directional lights instead transform their direction and reconstruct Euler angles. The host packer then negates the negative-Z forward direction to supply a normalized toward-light shader vector. This confirms the sign conversion required by the preceding pad proposal. Changing a coordinate-frame selector should preserve the instantaneous rendered light, while subsequent camera motion may change it as intended. This conversion alone cannot preserve an entire animated trajectory; switching frames for an animated light needs a defined track conversion policy. RFF deep-zoom coordinates must continue to use its own precision contract rather than copying a JavaScript vector conversion.

**Temperature is a color-authoring aid.** The panel computes a hex RGB color when temperature changes and stores it with the temperature metadata; the uniform packer consumes the resulting color. A targeted read of kelvinToRgb in [colorUtils.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/colorUtils.ts) shows a clamped, piecewise log/power RGB approximation with integer output. It does not introduce spectral light transport. A temperature aid could feed existing RFF light-color controls, but its working color space, normalization and provenance need an explicit choice; the distinctive constants have not been cleared for copying. Keep an arbitrary manually authored color intact until the user chooses a temperature-derived replacement. The remainder of colorUtils was not fully read in this batch and is not counted as completed.

Validation for an eventual implementation should include raw/EV round trips at zero and extreme intensities, unit changes with existing tracks, range-to-attenuation checks, visibility independent of extent, and frame-switch continuity under translated/rotated views. This batch performed source checks only; it did not change application code or measure appearance, timing, or interactive behavior.

### Follow-up: keep visual handles and shader controls in the same coordinate state

Full reads of [LightGizmo.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/lighting/LightGizmo.tsx), [SingleLightGizmo.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/lighting/components/SingleLightGizmo.tsx), the [GMT ViewportRefs shim](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/worker/ViewportRefs.ts), and its [engine-core implementation](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/worker/ViewportRefs.ts) clarify how these controls remain associated with a rendered view. The shim re-exports the same singleton camera/canvas references rather than creating a second state holder. The engine-core implementation snapshots position, orientation and projection into a display camera; for orthographic optics it constructs extents from orthoScale and aspect. The light handle update and drag calculations both request this display camera. This establishes a shared consumer contract, but does not by itself verify synchronization with an asynchronously presented GPU frame.

**RFF transfer:** use a coherent displayed-view transform for both drawing a manipulation handle and interpreting pointer positions. Associate it with the image/view state actually being edited, particularly during smooth zoom, resized previews or delayed rendering. A native 2D control normally needs the inverse of its image-to-client transform, not a 3D camera library. Keep high-precision fractal centres separate from local screen deltas; do not reconstruct deep coordinates by converting the entire centre to ordinary floating point. RFF's [RenderScene.cpp](../src/rff2/ui/RenderScene.cpp) already clears canvas/smooth-zoom drag flags on WM_CAPTURECHANGED, so capture-loss handling is an existing pattern to extend for any new light or texture handle, not a wholly absent capability.

**Drag geometry and its limits:** GMT's free-position drag intersects a camera-facing plane through the light and preserves the initial pointer-to-origin offset. Constrained-plane drags use the selected geometric plane, rotating its normal for camera-fixed lights. This offset is a useful mechanism for preventing a jump to the pointer on first movement. Axis drags instead project an axis to a screen direction, fall back to horizontal when the projection is nearly zero, and multiply pointer displacement by camera distance times 0.0025. That last path is a sensitivity heuristic, not a complete inverse-projection scale; viewport size, field of view and orthographic scale are not all represented. For RFF's planar controls, derive the displacement from the actual displayed transform and define what happens when an axis has no visible projection rather than inheriting that constant.

Shift snapping rounds all three computed world coordinates to a 0.25 grid. This can move components that an oblique axis/plane constraint would otherwise hold, so a new RFF constrained control should declare whether snapping is in image axes, the selected local frame, or the constrained parameter itself. A cosmetic overlay must not silently redefine the mathematical coordinate system used by a texture or light.

**Stable identity and interaction lifetime:** the gizmo registry is keyed by light ID, but an active drag stores an array index and reads that index again on every move. For any future RFF collection of editable layers/lights, resolve the active object by stable identity or explicitly freeze collection changes during manipulation. A delete or reorder should end or preserve the intended drag, never redirect it to another object. GMT starts its interaction and pointer capture before checking camera/canvas availability; cleanup is guarded by an initialized drag record. This source ordering motivates checking all prerequisites before beginning a RFF transaction and providing one idempotent release path for completion, cancellation, capture loss and destruction. No failure in the running GMT application was reproduced here.

**Overlay semantics must be honest.** The range circle projects a camera-right offset of the selected range and enforces a minimum screen radius of eight pixels. Combined with the preceding attenuation contract, it is an approximate authoring guide, not a hard light boundary or an exact sphere silhouette. The directional drag glow projects the source direction into screen XY and places its centre on an ellipse in percentage coordinates; despite the border-oriented description, it does not compute the intersection with the rectangular canvas boundary. Its opacity depends on the XY magnitude and therefore cannot distinguish front and rear directions with the same transverse magnitude. These choices can be useful visual feedback, but RFF should not make them the sole indicators of direction, influence or occlusion. Keep such feedback separate from the final exported shader image.

A complete read of [navigation.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/navigation.ts) additionally confirms settings for fly speed, collision auto-slow and cursor-anchored orbit/zoom. This file is a schema only: it contains no collision, picking or zoom implementation, so it does not justify claiming those mechanisms verified or absent from RFF. Collision slowing is predominantly a 3D-navigation concern; cursor-anchor consistency can inform 2D interaction after checking the actual consumer. These additions refine implementation conditions for existing proposals. No runtime, interaction or rendering tests were performed in this batch.

## AH. Bundled 2D examples: orbit statistics and calculation contracts

Full reads of the bundled Fragmentarium examples [Mandelbrot.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/Mandelbrot.frag), [BurningShip.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/BurningShip.frag), [Metabrot.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/Metabrot.frag), [Newtonian.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/Newtonian.frag), and [Progressive2DJulia.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Progressive2DJulia.frag) reveal transferable authoring ideas. These are bundled reference sources, not proof that the GMT importer supports every include, preset or execution mode they use. Their cited authors and forum inspirations do not by themselves establish copying permission; no implementation was copied.

**Orbit-history coloring is the substantive addition.** Progressive2DJulia offers a radius average, an exponential moving average of radius, and an escape-based color. It begins collecting after the configured pre-iteration threshold and applies nested logarithms before a cosine palette. A radius-history field could drive existing RFF palette coordinates or material masks, providing distinctions that final escape count alone cannot recover. Keep this within sections E/F's typed-field proposal rather than presenting each palette formula as a separate shader feature. Define a valid-sample count, the exact first collected iterate, invalid/interior semantics, and a finite fallback before applying logarithms. In the example, pre-iterations also delay the escape test, so this is not merely a switch that hides early samples while preserving the same stop rule.

For a new RFF implementation, accumulate sum and count for an arithmetic mean, or explicitly initialize an exponential moving average and record its weight convention. The example's strict `i>PreIterations` sampling and index-based denominator require separate treatment of early escape and loop exhaustion; do not use a loop index as an assumed sample count. Zero, empty histories, C=0, and logarithms outside their domain need specified results. A shader consuming these fields should never silently equate an invalid statistic to a valid dark color.

**MPA compatibility must be demonstrated.** A skipped block's orbit-radius sum or maximum is not available merely because the state at its endpoint is available. For an exponential moving average `m'=(1-alpha)*m+alpha*r`, a known block can be represented as `m_out=A*m_in+B`, where A is `(1-alpha)^blockLength` and B is the weighted sum of that block's radii. Such transforms compose associatively, but computing B for each pixel's actual orbit remains the substantive problem; a reference-orbit aggregate is not automatically valid for its perturbed pixels. Variable MPA skip lengths and sample/escape thresholds must also be respected. Preserve the existing precision and acceleration contract; if an exact field needs a separate calculation mode, disclose that cost rather than claiming a free postprocessing effect. Existing compressed iteration maps cannot reconstruct missing history without recalculation or separately stored channels.

**Initialization and termination are part of a formula.** The simple Mandelbrot example uses zero initial state for Mandelbrot and the pixel as initial state for Julia. Progressive2DJulia instead starts from the pixel in either mode, and its parameter-map inset also starts from the parameter position. BurningShip applies componentwise absolute value, complex squaring, imaginary negation, then c addition; preserving that conjugation/order matters. In the currently inspected [CustomFormulaPerturbator.cpp](../src/rff2/formula/CustomFormulaPerturbator.cpp), RFF starts z at zero and uses the pixel as c, with magnitude escape and a maximum-iteration limit. Therefore an expression alone does not reproduce all of these reference modes. A reusable formula recipe should specify initial state, variable/fixed parameters, termination and coloring fields alongside the recurrence. No new generic absolute-value primitive is justified: the componentwise operations were already established in section AA.

Metabrot starts at the pixel and composes a selectable quadratic map f as `f(f(z)+C)+f(C)+z`, with optional preliminary iterations of `f(z)+C`. Its variants use f(z)=z*z, z*z+z or z*z-z. This suggests reusable composition and warm-up settings, not a new class of coloring-only shader. The maximum-radius statistic is declared globally in the reference; its reset behavior must be checked against the included sampling framework before reproducing multiple samples. The example's nested-log smoothing depends on its bailout parameter and is not a general degree-four potential formula established by this review.

**Convergence fractals require a distinct stop contract.** Newtonian terminates on the size of the update, not escape radius, and its two modified variants retain the previous update components as recurrence state. At zero perturbation, the first variant follows a Newton-style cubic quotient; changing the C offset modifies the update and should not be described as merely coloring root basins. Its displayed grayscale is an average of a radial weighting function for visited points inside Radius. The accumulator starts with weight one and value zero, so after N accepted samples it divides the sum by N+1, not N. Negative weighting exponents and points at the boundary need finite-domain handling. There is no root-identity palette in the inspected return expression. A genuine root-basin feature for RFF would need residual/convergence criteria, singular-derivative handling, root classification and a suitable evaluator; the current magnitude-escape expression path alone is insufficient.

**Linked parameter-map preview:** Mandelbrot.frag embeds a small parameter-plane view around the selected Julia constant. This can inspire a linked parameter preview while exploring a Julia family, but the example performs additional iterations for that inset and does not establish click-to-select behavior. Reuse an existing suitable RFF preview surface if available after a separate UI-path inventory; do not recompute an unchanged inset on every material-only adjustment. Keep preview overlays optional in exports and preserve their coordinate/readout precision independently of the main view.

These findings add orbit-statistic and recipe-contract detail without changing the provisional material-appearance priority of section G. Source and target code were inspected, but no shader import, numerical comparison, benchmark or rendered-image test was performed.

## AI. Procedural tilings and the sampling contract of bundled 2D shaders

Full reads of [PenroseTiles.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/PenroseTiles.frag), [plasma.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/plasma.frag), [Kali.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/Kali.frag), [Thorn.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/Thorn.frag), and the include files [2D.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/2D.frag), [Progressive2D.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Progressive2D.frag), and [BufferShader.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/BufferShader.frag) extend the procedural-pattern and filtering proposals. Availability in this reference directory is not evidence of successful GMT import or RFF compatibility.

**Quasiperiodic material masks:** PenroseTiles keeps a discrete triangle-type state, selects affine transforms using linear half-plane tests, and assigns one of two final colors from that state. Each transform includes the same inflation magnitude, the golden ratio. It is a finite-depth classification algorithm; this review does not prove an exact infinite Penrose tiling from the descriptive name. RFF could use an independently implemented tiling classification as a procedural texture or material mask in existing mapping coordinates, without changing the fractal orbit. Preserve the discrete state and operation order; a collection of independent mirrored coordinates would not reproduce the algorithm. The source uses row-vector compound multiplication (`z *= matrix`), so transcribing it as matrix-times-column-vector without adjusting the matrices changes rotations.

Inside an unchanged branch sequence, the coordinate footprint grows by the inflation factor each iteration; after N iterations its scale contains that factor to the Nth power. Near branch boundaries, however, a derivative of one branch does not represent all covered classifications. Filter classification coverage, limit detail according to the footprint, or supersample the procedural mask before material shading. Simply smoothing the final two colors without considering coverage cannot establish stable thin tiles. An adaptive iteration cutoff is an artistic level-of-detail choice and needs transition testing, because it changes the classification itself. This is a specific pattern candidate within the existing mapping proposal, not a reason to replace RFF's palette or add a ray tracer.

**Plasma is a fixed sample effect, not a distance proof.** The source takes eight steps along a constructed view ray, evaluates a time-rotated trigonometric field twice per step, and combines color multiplicatively. Its offset field sample uses the same scalar offset in all three coordinates; this is not a full surface normal. Its local color accumulator is read before explicit initialization, so no reproducible appearance should be inferred from that expression as written. A RFF analogue could be a bounded animated procedural texture with explicitly initialized state and deterministic export time. A cheaper planar field slice would be a distinct design, not an exact reproduction of the ray-sampled effect. Neither the name nor its use of a displacement field establishes physically simulated plasma or volume scattering.

**Inversion and singular formulas retain their own contracts.** Kali compares squared radius m against MinRadius, but divides the inner branch by MinRadius squared; Scaling is applied only to the outer branch. This differs from the usual continuous sphere-fold parameterization and can have a branch jump. At MinRadius=0 and z=0, its outer expression divides by zero. Thorn divides x by cos(y) and y by sin(x); at zero initial state the second quotient is undefined. These examples therefore reinforce section AH's explicit initialization and singular-value policy. Do not silently clamp denominators and call the changed dynamics equivalent. Componentwise folds and trigonometric operations alone do not make the original recipes compatible with RFF's zero-initialized magnitude-escape evaluator.

**The sampling includes resolve one earlier uncertainty.** In Progressive2D's ordinary path, each fragment invocation calls color once, with a disc offset derived from the subframe. Metabrot's global radius maximum therefore does not carry across multiple color calls within that ordinary invocation; the framebuffer retains accumulated color/weight, not that orbit variable. This resolves the specific question left in section AH for the inspected include. An importer that batches several samples into one invocation must still reset per-sample orbit state explicitly. The nonprogressive 2D include does make AntiAlias squared calls to color and uses positive grid offsets, making sample-state lifetime and sample-centre conventions important when moving examples between the two wrappers.

Both includes transform the central coordinate for rotation/stretch, but their aaScale does not include the same matrix. For a new RFF procedural sampler, transform the two footprint vectors or sample offsets through the complete coordinate map; axis-aligned offsets in transformed space are not generally the footprint of the original screen pixel. Progressive2D uses a frame-wide disc offset, optional radial weights, and an RGBA sum/weight buffer. BufferShader divides by alpha before its tone-mapping/output stage. Alpha here means accumulated sample weight, not image transparency. Define zero-weight and nonfinite handling, reset conditions and export determinism before adapting such accumulation. The source NaN equality check alone does not reject every infinity.

**Preserve color-space semantics rather than copying the wrapper.** The progressive include optionally raises samples to Gamma before summing; its buffer shader normalizes, applies a selected mapping and grading, then raises to inverse Gamma. This is a configurable power-law convention, not proof of exact sRGB decoding. Several named tone-mapping implementations and HSV helpers carry external source references, which require separate provenance/license verification before reuse. RFF already has tone mapping and output controls; more copied curves are not established as a missing high-impact feature. The transferable requirement is to accumulate/filter in the declared working space and keep display transforms separate from stored numerical channels. No numerical or rendered-image tests were run and no application implementation changed.

## AJ. Stateful pattern textures and sign-coverage contours

Full reads of [Reaction-Diffusion.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/Reaction-Diffusion.frag), [Game of Life.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/Game%20of%20Life.frag), [GraphPlotter.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/GraphPlotter.frag), and [BufferShaderX.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/BufferShaderX.frag) establish a separate class of reference effects: stateful texture simulation. They are not additional Mandelbrot formulas or ordinary recoloring of an existing iteration map.

### Reaction-diffusion as an optional texture source

The reaction-diffusion example stores two concentrations in red and green. It reads the previous buffer with repeat wrapping, computes a nine-point stencil (cardinal weights one, diagonal weights one half, centre weight minus six), and takes an explicit Euler step. Its local reaction is `u*v*v`; feed adds `f*(1-u)` to u, while `(f+k)*v` removes v. The five-point helper is present but not selected by color. During the first three subframes it instead writes a noisy radial seed. Host directives request ten iterations between redraws, unlimited subframes, and retention on parameter changes. BufferShaderX simply displays RGB from the state buffer; it does not perform the sum/weight normalization used by the progressive antialiasing buffer.

**RFF use:** generate an independent pattern texture that can feed an existing material mask, roughness modulation or color layer. Freeze/bake a chosen state for still images, or animate the evolution as an optional source. This offers organic spots and stripes without modifying the fractal orbit. It requires simulation resources and scheduling beyond a stateless material shader, so it is a lower-priority extension than section G's editable environment. The inspected presets suggest artistic ranges, not a numerical stability guarantee.

Use distinct read/write state images with explicit synchronization for every update; in-place writes must not let neighboring pixels observe different generations. Keep simulation channels linear and separate from tone mapping, transparency and display color. Fix a simulation grid independently of preview resolution unless a deliberate resampling/reset policy is selected. The source stencil has no explicit physical cell-size factor: changing grid resolution changes the texture's spatial behavior, and must not be disguised as merely improving display quality. Validate update stability for the accepted diffusion, timestep and reaction ranges; clamping concentrations after unstable updates is not evidence of an accurate integrator. At zero timestep a non-seeding update should preserve state, and a constant field should have zero discrete diffusion, useful future checks.

**Deterministic video needs a state contract.** Advance a declared number of fixed simulation steps per export time interval, independent of screen refresh, shader redraws and adaptive resolution. Scrubbing backwards or rendering tiles out of order requires replay from a seed or a compatible checkpoint, not simply setting a time uniform. Checkpoints need grid dimensions, boundary mode, step index, parameters and seed identity. Any parameter animation must be sampled at the specified simulation step. A restart and a live parameter change are different artistic actions; make that distinction explicit. Tiled export should sample a shared simulation texture or exchange the correct neighbor boundaries, rather than independently simulating each image tile. Cross-device bitwise identity of floating-point reaction evolution is not established; baking a state is a separate stronger reproducibility option.

### Cellular automata: separate logical state from trails

The Game of Life example counts eight neighbors using exact red-channel equality to one, with nearest magnification and repeat boundaries. Surviving cells and births return white, while many other cells return independently decaying RGB values; an annulus continuously injects time-dependent random cells. Thus the visible result combines discrete updates, a persistent visual trail, and an ongoing source. It is not only a one-time seeded binary automaton.

If adapted as a RFF texture, retain the binary cell state separately from trail color/intensity. Display filtering can then be smooth without changing the next generation's neighbor count. Use a declared discrete sampling rule for the simulation, a stable seed/step sequence for injection, and an independently controlled trail-decay law. The reference's ten/twenty-updates-per-redraw directives are host instructions, not guarantees that GMT's importer executes them. Import capability must be demonstrated before presenting these effects as already available through GMT. The sine-based hash includes a source comment, but its constants and license have not been independently verified for reuse.

### GraphPlotter: local sign balance is a contour heuristic

GraphPlotter samples the sign of `function(x)-y` over a jittered quarter-disc-like grid, then uses the absolute signed count divided by sample count as grayscale. Equal positive/negative counts make a dark contour; a one-sided footprint remains white. This suggests coverage-based boundaries for a field mask, not a general fixed-width curve-distance estimator. The sample grid is not centred on the pixel and costs up to Samples squared function evaluations, on top of the progressive wrapper's repeated frames. The source permits Samples zero and uses a singular oscillatory function, so valid counts and finite function results need an explicit policy in a new implementation.

For RFF, apply such boundary visualization only to a field that is actually available and filter in its mapped footprint. A continuously varying scalar field may support a cheaper derivative-based coverage approximation locally, but discontinuities, multiple crossings and very thin features need more than that approximation. Compare against supersampled references before advertising high-frequency antialiasing. This refines sections E/H's field-mask and filtering proposals; it does not establish that a nested stochastic plotter loop is faster or sharper than RFF's existing sampling.

No simulation, imported shader, image comparison or benchmark was executed in this batch. Only the English report and audit coverage were changed; all performance, determinism and image-quality claims remain implementation requirements rather than measured results.

### Follow-up to AH: Ducks, composed folds and derivative-aware recipes

Full reads of [Ducks.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/Ducks.frag), [Metaship1.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/2D%20Systems/Metaship1.frag), [Complex.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Complex.frag) and [ComplexBase.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/ComplexBase.frag) complete the remaining two files in the inventory's immediate 2D Systems directory and trace their complex-function dependency. This does not finish the many other bundled example directories.

**Ducks needs a recipe contract, not a new logarithm primitive.** The source folds only the imaginary component to its absolute value, takes a complex logarithm, then adds c. RFF's [ExpressionParser.cpp](../src/rff2/formula/ExpressionParser.cpp) already implements iabs with the real component unchanged and log through std::log. The recurrence can therefore be expressed as `log(iabs(z))+c`, but that does not reproduce the source's pixel-initialized state, Julia option, warm-up/escape rules or orbit-mean coloring from Progressive2DJulia. In RFF's currently inspected zero-initialized custom evaluator, the first logarithm is singular. Preserve a nonzero/pixel initial-state choice rather than silently substituting a small epsilon, which defines a different recurrence.

ComplexBase's normal logarithm uses log(magnitude) and atan(y,x); its optional legacy branch subtracts a full turn from positive arguments. A recipe that depends on the legacy behavior can therefore differ by an imaginary full-turn offset even though both functions are called cLog. Preserve branch conventions and signed-axis behavior explicitly when comparing implementations. The reference attributes the fractal to Samuel Monnier and the implementation to Syntopia; those are useful provenance leads, not verified licensing permission. Several preset keys such as TrigIter are not consumed by the inspected Ducks function or its coloring wrapper; do not expose every serialized key as an effective control without tracing a consumer.

**Metaship's two inner additions use the original z.** Its recurrence is componentwise absolute value of `(z*z+z)^2+z`, followed by c. The inner squaring sequence must not replace the second added z with the intermediate result. An RFF expression analogue is `riabs((z*z+z)*(z*z+z)+z)+c`, but the source's non-Julia initial state is a fixed nonzero complex value and its Julia state is the pixel. Its dist variable is reset every outer iteration, so the bailout statistic is the current squared radius, not a running orbit maximum despite the use of max in the helper. Z2, Z3 and map-related declarations do not affect the inspected color path. The oscillatory palette `cos(x+2*cos(8*x))` and additional higher-frequency term are independent artistic mapping ideas; they need footprint filtering if reused on an existing RFF scalar field, and do not justify changing the fractal calculation. The source smoothing expression is not treated here as a validated potential for the folded quartic recurrence.

**Automatic differentiation is useful infrastructure with a limited domain.** ComplexBase packs a complex value in XY and one complex derivative in ZW. Its product and quotient helpers propagate the product/quotient rules, while variable and constant constructors seed the derivative with one and zero. This suggests an independently implemented derivative-aware custom-expression evaluator for the analytic subset, supporting the distance/normal work described in section O. For an orbit `z_next=F(z,c)`, the requested derivative must be named: differentiation with respect to the pixel parameter requires propagating both initial-state dependence and the c term, whereas a Julia initial-value derivative treats fixed c as constant. A single unnamed derivative channel is insufficient to distinguish those modes.

Do not treat this reference header as a complete or verified differentiation library. The VEC4 norm, abs and arg helpers return only a scalar value, discarding derivative state. Componentwise absolute value, conjugation and folded formulas require real-coordinate derivatives or an equivalent richer representation; extending complex-analytic propagation to them blindly is incorrect. Inspecting the VEC4 cosine expression also shows why algebraic checks are necessary: its division by two applies only to the second exponential, making its value 1.5 at zero rather than one. The ordinary complex square-root helper multiplies the imaginary root component by sign(y), so an exactly negative real input with y=0 loses that component. These are source-level counterexamples against copying the helper wholesale, not a reproduced GMT runtime failure or a request to repair GMT.

Complex.frag instantiates float helpers and conditionally instantiates doubles based on GLSL version. That mechanism does not establish RFF Vulkan device capability, precision adequacy, or deep-zoom support. The header also acknowledges borrowed implementations and incomplete credits. Any RFF derivative feature should use independently derived, tested elementary operations or a clearly licensed source, record attribution where required, and retain existing high-precision/MPA constraints.
