Future verification should cover elementary values and derivatives, branch axes, zero denominators, initial-state/parameter derivative differences, and comparison with independent numerical references away from singularities. No shader or numerical tests were executed in this batch.

## AK. Slice-and-profile inspection for distance and relief fields

Full reads of [Mandelbox - Dual Numbers DE.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Theory/Mandelbox%20-%20Dual%20Numbers%20DE.frag), its [Slicer variant](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Theory/Mandelbox%20-%20Dual%20Numbers%20DE%20-%20Slicer.frag), and [DE-Raytracer-Slicer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Raytracer-Slicer.frag) provide a useful inspection workflow, but not a verified derivative implementation to transplant.

**What the slicer actually displays:** its upper regions render the original surface and a clipped version. The lower left samples a fixed-X plane, classifying a point by DE below a threshold and marking the selected Z line. The lower right plots DE along that line, a central finite difference along Y, and an alternate DE selected by an integer argument. The supplied Mandelbox slicer ignores that integer argument, so its alternate curve is the same evaluator; it is not an independent reference. Plotting uses nine positively offset samples with fixed graph-space line tolerances. The displayed slope is the derivative of the returned distance-estimate field, not a direct display of an orbit Jacobian.

**2D RFF transfer:** extend section F's field inspection with a selectable line across the existing iteration, mapped-height or material-mask image, showing the sampled field and its slope alongside the final shaded image. This can explain why a height curve produces narrow highlights or why a mask changes abruptly, without importing the 3D ray tracer. Let the user select the field, line endpoints and graph scale; expose validity/interior gaps rather than interpolating through them as ordinary data. Separate raw iteration values from normalized heights and final display colors. Reuse available field data where possible, with explicit recalculation only for channels that were not stored. This is a diagnostic/authoring enhancement rather than a measured improvement in final image quality.

For comparisons, identify both evaluators and their parameters; two curves produced by the same function are not validation. Finite-difference spacing should be stated in the selected coordinate/field units, distinct from graph zoom and line thickness. Adapt display coverage to pixels and use an appropriate local spacing without rounding away deep-zoom coordinates. A planar scalar-field profile does not need a surface-hit test, AO, camera lights or a bounding sphere. The large number of lighting declarations inherited by the source slicer does not make them all active in each quadrant.

**Matrix propagation needs an independently derived contract.** The examples initialize a 3x3 Jacobian to identity, apply componentwise box-fold signs to its columns, scale rows for anisotropic scaling, and attempt to propagate the c addition. However, in the inversion branch they multiply the matrix only by `s=fixedRadius2/r2`. For the position map `z_next=s*z`, the local Jacobian is `s*(I-2*z*z^T/r2)` away from zero, using the pre-inversion z. Omitting the reflection factor does not preserve a full directional derivative, even though its norm can equal the scalar factor for this individual conformal inversion. Later additions and anisotropic transforms make those directions consequential.

Likewise, the position addition is componentwise `c*Offset`, whose derivative with respect to the input c is the diagonal matrix of Offset. The source instead adds `dc*mat3(Offset,Offset,Offset)`: GLSL constructs three identical columns, not that diagonal matrix. At identity dc these already differ for an ordinary Offset such as (1,1,1). These direct algebraic discrepancies prevent treating the final `dot(z,z)/length(z*dz)` as a validated distance formula from automatic differentiation. Even a correctly propagated Jacobian would still require a separate justification of that distance estimate and its zero-denominator behavior. No failing rendered scene is asserted.

**Adoption conditions:** for a 2D fold/inversion evaluator, propagate a real 2x2 Jacobian or the required richer derivative state with explicit matrix conventions, folding-boundary rules and initialization. Independently check each primitive before testing a composed orbit. A 3D plane slice retains three orbit coordinates and derivatives with respect to its two input coordinates; it is not automatically a two-coordinate recurrence. Do not replace RFF's established Mandelbrot derivative or MPA logic with this example. The non-slicer rotates the orbit after the c addition, while the slicer omits that rotation, so comparisons must also align the recurrence settings rather than assuming the two filenames describe identical computations.

Future verification should compare analytic primitive Jacobians with finite differences away from nonsmooth boundaries, examine one-sided limits at folds, and compare field profiles under matched settings and precision. The current batch adds the inspection proposal and its mathematical requirements only; no shader compilation, numerical test, visual test or application modification was performed.

## AL. Environment convolution and precision boundaries

Full reads of [Convolution.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Theory/Convolution.frag), [Mandelbrot - Emulated Doubles.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Theory/Mandelbrot%20-%20Emulated%20Doubles.frag), [EmulatedDouble.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/EmulatedDouble.frag), and [2D-HP.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/2D-HP.frag) strengthen the implementation requirements of section G while ruling out a shortcut for RFF's precision-sensitive calculation.

### Directional averaging is different from ordinary image blur

Convolution maps each output texel to a sphere direction, constructs a tangent basis, samples the corresponding hemisphere and looks up an equirectangular HDR texture. The unbiased-sampling branch draws uniform solid-angle samples and weights radiance by cosine raised to Power. The biased branch draws cosine-power distributed directions using `cos(theta)=u^(1/(Power+1))`, then returns sampled radiance divided by Power+1. Optional stratification cycles through a 10x10 grid in random-number space. This is a hemisphere convolution example, not a screen-space convolution or an implementation of GGX prefiltering.

**Normalization matters for RFF.** Under arithmetic averaging, with Multi=1, both branches estimate the same hemisphere integral divided by 2*pi. For a constant environment C their expectation is C/(Power+1), so changing the lobe exponent changes the output amplitude. A normalized constant-preserving lobe average would instead compensate for that factor. Which quantity RFF needs depends on the downstream diffuse/specular lighting convention; do not silently multiply an existing environment term by an unrelated normalization. The uniform branch alone applies Multi, so branch comparisons also need matched scale. Derive the intended radiometric/artistic contract before tuning intensity by eye.

The included Progressive2D default path raises each sample to Gamma before accumulating, and the supplied preset has Gamma=2.2. Therefore equality of the two arithmetic estimators does not establish equality of the images produced through that nonlinear accumulation path. For RFF, prefilter radiance in a declared linear working space, normalize the filter there, and defer display transforms. A constant environment, a small bright emitter, and a labeled directional panorama are useful separate checks for brightness preservation, lobe width and orientation. Ordinary image mip levels average rectangular texel neighborhoods and do not by themselves produce the required directional BRDF convolution. A cosine-power lobe could be an explicitly labeled approximation; it must not be described as exact GGX roughness filtering.

**Seams, poles and rotation:** the source tangent basis degenerates when the direction lies on the X axis. Use a robust independently implemented basis with validated axis cases. Adding a two-component offset to longitude/latitude texture coordinates is not a general 3D environment rotation: latitude translation changes pole behavior and requires an explicit wrapping policy. Rotate directions before projection for a true orientation control. Verify the actual image-up convention from a labeled source rather than trusting the helper's comments. Keep cursor overlays and preview exposure out of any baked lighting asset. Build/cache prefiltered data when its source or filter contract changes, rather than resampling many hemisphere directions in every RFF material lookup. The cost and quality of that preprocessing remain unmeasured.

### Two-float arithmetic does not replace RFF deep-zoom precision

The emulation helper represents a real number as high/low floats and a complex number as real-high/real-low/imaginary-high/imaginary-low. It implements compensated addition/subtraction, split multiplication, corrected division and pair comparison. However, the example still uploads Center as a float vector, promotes it with zero low parts, and computes 1/Zoom as a float before promotion. Lost coordinate information is not recovered by performing later operations on pairs. The final coloring also extracts only high components for squared magnitude. 2D-HP moves scaling/centering out of the vertex shader, but contains no antialiasing loop despite the exposed AntiAliasScale control.

This is a historical experiment in extending float arithmetic, not arbitrary precision, not a demonstrated binary64 substitute, and not an MPA or perturbation implementation. The vendor-specific fast-math pragmas do not establish the optimization behavior of a Vulkan compiler. Before using compensated arithmetic for any independently justified RFF auxiliary path, its required range, rounding, contraction/reassociation behavior, exceptional values and host-side split representation would need tests on the actual target. Never substitute it for the existing high-precision centre/reference pipeline to claim a speed improvement.

The helper itself also illustrates why packed layouts require direct verification: its complex-by-real multiplication overload supplies the imaginary pair as a.wz, while dcSet and the other operations establish that pair as a.zw. This reverses high/low order; neither the filename nor the word double proves the primitive correct. The example's non-emulated and emulated loops must additionally be compared with their exact iteration/bailout conventions, not only with a visually similar palette. The header credits Henry Thasler and a Fortran double-single package, but original licensing has not been verified for adaptation. No helper implementation was copied and no numerical, compiler or rendered-image experiment was run in this batch.

### Follow-up to AK: compare estimator variants without confusing them with ground truth

A full read of [Mandelbulb-Slicer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Theory/Mandelbulb-Slicer.frag) clarifies another comparison mode. Its ordinary recurrence starts z at pos and dr at one, applies one of two spherical power conventions, adds pos, measures radius, then rotates z. The alternate DE argument adds one more unit to dr on every iteration while leaving the position recurrence unchanged. Consequently its plotted alternate curve compares two denominator recurrences, not an independent geometric distance or a second orbit. The extra addition alone does not establish which approximation is more accurate. The separately declared DE2 test function is not called by the inspected slicer path.

The AlternateVersion checkbox is different: it switches acos-based polar power to asin-based elevation power and therefore changes the position recurrence. For RFF field comparisons, distinguish a changed evaluator applied to the same orbit from a changed fractal definition. Label both clearly and retain matched parameters for a meaningful comparison. The source computes a logarithmic estimate even for points that remain below bailout when the iteration limit is reached; that output is not proof of a signed inside distance. Origin/axis inputs and degenerate rotation vectors need their own finite-domain rules before any analogous evaluator is adopted. This extends the field-inspection proposal rather than adding another distance effect.

### Membership-only tracing: reusable candidates, with explicit validity and coverage limits

Full reads of [26 - 3D fractals without a DE.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tutorials/26%20-%203D%20fractals%20without%20a%20DE.frag), [Brute-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Brute-Raytracer.frag) and [Brute3D.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Brute3D.frag) show how an inside predicate can replace a DE for approximate rendering. The formula returns whether a finite orbit stays below bailout; it is not a proof of membership in the infinite set. Its declared rotation controls are not applied in the inspected inside function.

The tracer stores a candidate ray position as a normalized fraction of the Near/Far interval in alpha. Each new invocation reads the prior candidate, optionally tries the 3x3 neighborhood's candidates on the current ray, and accepts a neighbor only after re-evaluating whether its inside state differs from the state at Near. It then searches the interval up to the candidate using either a randomly offset stratified grid or random probes, retaining a closer point with opposite membership. This is stochastic interval sampling, not DE sphere tracing or binary root refinement. Thin alternating regions can fall between probes, and finite samples do not certify that the candidate is the nearest boundary.

**RFF transfer:** when reusing neighboring or previous results as an acceleration hint in a future field/contour tool, revalidate them in the current query and track the view, field and parameter state that makes them meaningful. A candidate is not an answer until the current evaluator accepts it. Membership sampling could produce an exploratory mask for a formula without a reliable DE, but should not be advertised as exact distance shading. Deriving a pixel-distance transform from a rasterized mask would also measure distance to the sampled boundary, not recover a deep-fractal distance estimate; keep that distinction visible.

Brute3D overwrites its output each invocation with the new RGB/candidate pair rather than accumulating radiance weights. Alpha therefore has different semantics from both image transparency and Progressive2D's sample weight. Camera, Near/Far, formula and resolution changes invalidate or require explicit reprojection/revalidation of the candidate. The include names a separate DepthBufferShader for later display; that downstream shading implementation was not read in this batch, so the tracer's declared normal/AO settings do not by themselves establish how those effects are computed. Deterministic sampling and invalidation would be required before using this approach in video or tiled export. No performance advantage for RFF is established.

### Follow-up to AK: screen-space depth shading versus existing RFF relief

A full read of [DepthBufferShader.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DepthBufferShader.frag) completes the display-consumer trace for the membership-only example. It reads RGB plus a normalized ray-position fraction from the front buffer, builds either central or one-sided differences of that fraction, and crosses two camera-basis tangent vectors to produce a normal. It then applies diffuse/specular lighting, tone mapping, gamma and grading, followed by a separate neighborhood darkening pass. The AO-like pass counts nearby samples whose depth is greater than or equal to the centre; background pixels instead receive a glow based on the complement of that fraction.

**RFF already has the core capability.** Targeted checks of [vk_slope.frag](../shdsrc/vk_slope.frag) confirm normals from height gradients and a bounded concavity term from neighbor heights, with interior/invalid-neighbor suppression in that path. [lustre_relief.glsl](../shdsrc/lustre_relief.glsl) additionally evaluates selectable radii for fine, smoothed and macro relief and AO. Thus this reference is not evidence that RFF lacks screen-space normals or local cavity shading. Its potentially useful contribution is a comparison/debugging workflow, including inspecting depth/height separately from material color and comparing central versus one-sided stencils under matched conditions.

**Do not equate normalized ray distance with planar height.** The reference's normal tangents use normalized depth differences along a constant camera-forward direction; they do not reconstruct each neighboring world position using its own ray and Near/Far interval. For perspective depth normals, reconstruct those positions with the actual projection and valid-hit mask before forming a geometric cross product. For RFF planar relief, retain the existing height mapping and its units. At discontinuities, select valid same-surface neighbors or use a defined fallback; a miss sentinel must not create a false cliff. NormalScale zero can collapse the finite-difference vectors, so a usable parameter domain or explicit flat-normal result is required. The debug view uses abs(normal), which loses component signs; a new signed-normal inspection channel should preserve them in a documented encoding.

**The darkening is a heuristic, not visibility integration.** A simple depth-order fraction has no hemisphere visibility integral, no geometric falloff and no rejection of unrelated surfaces. It can be useful artistically, but replacing RFF's existing concavity response with it is not an established improvement. The reference darkens already tone-mapped/graded color, whereas RFF's inspected non-studio composition applies AO to the base term and retains additive highlights/rim contributions separately. Keep the intended lighting-space and material-component contract explicit. Any proposed wider neighborhood mode should be compared on flat fields, narrow ridges, pits, interior boundaries and image/tile edges, including temporal stability and sampling cost. Existing functionality should be extended only when those comparisons show a useful difference.

### Follow-up to G/AL: the legacy IBL renderer is an approximation reference

A full read of [IBL-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/IBL-Raytracer.frag) resolves the earlier scene-only limitation. The renderer samples Diffuse using the normal and Specular using the reflected viewing ray. Each is scaled by its own strength; specular is capped componentwise by SpecularMax and added after diffuse/base multiplication. There is no per-material roughness input, roughness-level selection, Fresnel term or GGX BRDF integration in this environment-lighting function. Its RotateMap is a UV offset, not a full 3D rotation. This supports the usefulness of separate consumers, but does not supply the missing roughness-aware implementation for section G.

The optional shadow ray samples around one manually selected Sun direction. The resulting visibility factor attenuates ambient, diffuse environment and specular environment together. It does not integrate occlusion over every contributing environment direction. SunSize is encoded through `cos(theta)=1-u*SunSize`, with a matching dot-product threshold for the debug disc; it is not directly an angular radius in radians. Avoid reusing that parameter label or scale without defining its meaning. A prefiltered reflection lookup also does not imply interreflection between neighboring fractal regions.

For RFF, preserve existing GGX/clearcoat and their roughness parameters, add the environment as a controlled lighting input, and validate prefilter normalization and orientation as described in AL. Do not adopt the legacy specular clamp as an unexplained default or globally shadow an entire panorama from one directional test. HDR values should survive to the chosen output stage under the established material convention. The source's 3D ray marching, floor, AO and depth writes are separate renderer features, not prerequisites for using an environment on 2D relief. Neither this comparison nor the depth-buffer inspection measured an image-quality or performance gain; no application code or shader was changed.

## AM. Tutorial cross-checks: sampling tests, procedural time and texture gradients

Full reads of tutorials [03 - Dynamic Systems.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tutorials/03%20-%20Dynamic%20Systems.frag), [04 - Textures.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tutorials/04%20-%20Textures.frag), [20 - Progressive 2D.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tutorials/20%20-%20Progressive%202D.frag), [21 - Progressive 2D Escape Time Fractal.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tutorials/21%20-%20Progressive%202D%20Escape%20Time%20Fractal.frag), [22 - Progressive 3D Rendering.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tutorials/22%20-%20Progressive%203D%20Rendering.frag), [23 - Working with the back buffer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tutorials/23%20-%20Working%20with%20the%20back%20buffer.frag), and [24 - Pure 3D.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tutorials/24%20-%20Pure%203D.frag) add concrete test and integration ideas. Similar examples are kept separate in coverage because their presets and state behavior differ; they are not counted as separate product features.

**A demanding filtering test pattern:** tutorial 20 thresholds the fractional part of squared radius, then reverses the black/white result across one half-plane. Ring frequency rises with distance from the origin, making it useful for checking whether a proposed RFF procedural-mask filter preserves average coverage and avoids moving moire during zoom. The source's claim of high-quality progressive AA is not a measured result of this audit. Compare fixed sample budgets and a well-converged reference, include transformed/aspect-ratio cases, and report both residual aliasing and loss of contrast. Tutorial 21 repeats the Kali recurrence already covered in AI with different initialization/color settings; it adds no new inversion primitive, and retains the same singular-input and branch-contract concerns.

**Separate animation time from sample index and simulation state.** Tutorial 03 is stateless: its trigonometric RGB function can be evaluated directly at any time. Tutorial 20 accumulates samples of one image, while tutorial 23 evolves a state buffer. RFF should preserve these three distinct execution contracts if it adds procedural sources. Export time should come from the requested frame/sample schedule, not elapsed preview time. Advancing an antialiasing sample must not inadvertently advance a simulation; conversely, evolving a simulation must not be mistaken for accumulating another sample of an unchanged image. Some trigonometric RGB outputs can be negative, so the working-space/domain policy must be explicit before gamma or display conversion.

Tutorial 23 is not byte-for-byte the earlier Game of Life example: underpopulation leaves a decaying RGB trail instead of returning black, and its general decay rates differ. It declares RGBA16 before including 2D.frag, which declares RGBA32F. The effective buffer format depends on the host's directive resolution and must not be inferred from the first declaration. For RFF simulation sources, choose and document the logical-state and trail formats directly. Keep rules, decay and seed schedules in the saved simulation identity; a familiar effect name alone is insufficient for deterministic replay.

**Texture-derived gradients require units and a coordinate Jacobian.** Tutorial 04 creates tunnel UVs from reciprocal radius and angle, then takes four offset texture samples around the centre sample. It subtracts RGB-vector lengths to estimate a two-component gradient and normalizes it before a rotating-light dot product. This loses the magnitude of the texture slope and has an undefined normalization on a flat texture. RGB length also depends on the sampled color space and is not a declared physical height channel. A RFF adaptation should select an explicit height/luminance source, retain slope magnitude with a strength control, and use finite differences divided by their spacing. Transform that gradient through the UV mapping into the surface basis before using it as a normal perturbation; UV-space components alone are not screen- or surface-space slopes.

The reciprocal-radius map has a centre singularity and the angular map has a branch seam. Finite-difference sampling and mip/anisotropic footprints must follow the full composed map, including its time-varying scale. The commented texture parameters demonstrate host syntax, not active sampler configuration. This example supports section H's filtering requirements and the mapping-stack proposal, but does not establish a missing basic bump-lighting capability in RFF.

**3D examples can supply controlled previews without becoming the main renderer.** Tutorial 24 analytically intersects a few spheres and samples one environment by reflection direction and another by normal, with independent strengths. Its sphere helper selects only the near root and excludes exact tangency, so it is a limited test scene, not a robust general ray-intersection library. A small synthetic normal-field preview could help tune the environment editor on a known shape, while the final feature remains RFF's 2D relief. The function has no roughness/Fresnel integration; preserve the section G design rather than treating this two-lookup sum as a replacement for existing GGX.

Tutorial 22 supplies a repeated angular tube field to a separate progressive ray tracer. Its two angular frequencies use integer numerators over a common denominator; the Rotations control explicitly enumerates angle offsets by full turns. Seam continuity depends on covering the intended distinct phase branches, not only on increasing ray samples. For a 2D patterned band analogue, define the repeat period and branch count mathematically and filter at the mapping footprint. The ray tracer's advertised soft-shadow, AO and depth-of-field behavior lives in Soft-Raytracer and is not verified by this scene file alone. These reads refine existing proposals and provide future test cases; no tests or application changes were made in this batch.

### Follow-up to AM: faster rendering can mean fewer active features

Full reads of tutorials 00, 01, 02, 10, 11 and 12 in the [Tutorials directory](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/tree/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tutorials), together with [Fast-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Fast-Raytracer.frag), establish what the introductory examples actually delegate to their wrappers. The simple 2D examples add trigonometric color functions, a quadratic recurrence and slider/preset declarations; they do not add a new rendering capability beyond the previously inspected wrappers. Tutorial 01 includes 2DJulia rather than Progressive2DJulia, so the latter's behavior must not be assumed for it without checking that dependency.

**A concrete fast-mode tradeoff:** tutorial 12 retains the same Menger-like folded/scaled recurrence as tutorial 11 but selects Fast-Raytracer. The fast wrapper performs one primary trace per pixel and finite-difference normal evaluation, with simple lighting, step-count-based darkening/glow and fog. It declares controls for antialiasing, hard shadows, reflection, a floor and a bounding sphere, but those corresponding rendering paths are not present in its inspected main/trace implementation. In particular the AntiAlias setting does not drive a sample loop, and no bounding-sphere intersection skips empty primary-ray space. The speed claim in the tutorial is not a benchmark of equivalent active features. Unused serialized controls also do not establish that an effect was enabled in the resulting image.

**RFF implication:** sections I/Q's interactive rendering profiles should state which effects or sample budgets are temporarily reduced, restore the requested final settings, and avoid offering controls that appear effective when the current profile omits their consumer. Keep full-precision fractal computation, MPA semantics and final export quality intact. Compare equivalent feature sets before claiming an optimization; compare clearly labeled different profiles only when evaluating responsiveness/quality tradeoffs. Constant specialization is a separate choice from removing an effect entirely, with compile latency and cache cost to measure. RFF already has specialization/pipeline infrastructure, so this is a contract and measurement requirement rather than a proposal to add another shader framework.

**Step count is not geometry.** Fast-Raytracer derives its AO-like factor from steps divided by GlowMax. A change to ray-step policy can therefore alter apparent cavity darkness even with the same shape and camera. The RFF equivalents should remain explicit field-based or artistic signals; avoid conflating work performed by an algorithm with physical occlusion. Its depth debug uses inverse travelled distance, while alpha is written as one and gl_FragDepth follows a separate mapping. Keep those meanings distinct from linear distance, normalized candidate fraction and transparency when designing section F's outputs. A miss or zero travelled distance also requires an explicit display convention.

**Distance-function composition needs a stated guarantee.** Tutorial 10 combines sphere, cylinders and plane values with min/max and negation to make unions and cutouts. The corresponding 2D idea is useful for procedural mask composition, but min/max composition need not give exact Euclidean distance to every resulting boundary. A mask can use the sign/zero contour without claiming an exact distance suitable for arbitrary ray steps or constant-width outlines. Tutorial 11 sorts absolute coordinates, scales/translates, performs a conditional Z adjustment and returns scaled final radius. The appearance and distance-estimate meaning depend on iteration count and scale; the allowed scale-zero endpoint does not justify applying the inverse scale power without a valid-domain policy. Preserve the ordered-fold requirements already recorded in AB rather than treating the example as a universally valid SDF.

**Preset parsing is observable behavior.** Tutorial 02's second preset repeats Y with two different values. The tutorial describes build-time preset discovery, but does not specify duplicate-key precedence. Any compatibility importer must establish the source/target precedence or diagnose ambiguity; a newly designed RFF recipe format should be unambiguous and preserve stable existing IDs. Default application, omitted-value retention and inactive controls also require an explicit contract. The source declaration and explanatory comment alone are not evidence that the GMT importer implements those host semantics. No source implementation was copied, no shader was compiled, and no timing or image-quality comparison was executed in this batch.

### Follow-up to AH/AL/AM: preserve recurrence semantics across wrappers and precision helpers

Full reads of [2DJulia.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/2DJulia.frag) and [Math.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Math.frag) resolve two dependencies behind the imported examples. Their useful contribution to RFF is a more explicit formula/precision contract, rather than another general-purpose replacement math library.

**A wrapper can change the fractal, not just its sampling.** Both 2DJulia and the previously inspected Progressive2DJulia initialize z from the pixel coordinate and select either that coordinate or the Julia constant as the recurrence parameter. However, 2DJulia tests escape immediately, while Progressive2DJulia delays escape until i exceeds PreIterations. Switching these wrappers can therefore change termination and coloring even with identical formula parameters. In both, EscapeSize is the decimal exponent of a squared-radius threshold: the radius is 10^(EscapeSize/2). Importing it as a radius exponent would change the orbit contract.

For RFF formula recipes, record the initial state, parameter source, pre/post-update sampling point, warm-up policy, bailout units and whether warm-up suppresses termination. Keep the termination counter separate from the number of valid statistic samples. The ordinary mean in 2DJulia divides by i-PreIterations despite possible early escape and empty history; its inset similarly divides an accumulated sum by the loop index. A new implementation should count accepted samples explicitly, define an empty-history result and validate the domain before nested logarithms. An exponential moving average is a different statistic with its own initial state and weighting, not an interchangeable faster mean. These requirements support section AH's orbit-statistic feature without changing RFF's established escape semantics or pretending MPA can skip arbitrary statistics for free.

**Double precision declarations are not an accuracy guarantee.** Math preserves built-in float operations but overloads many double operations under a GLSL version condition. Its double sine/cosine reduce the argument by repeated division by three, evaluate a truncated series and reconstruct with triple-angle identities. TrigIter and TrigLimit control that approximation. This qualifies the earlier Ducks observation: the controls have consumers in the included double helpers, but the inspected float-valued Ducks path does not thereby use those double overloads. A language-version branch also does not establish that a target Vulkan device and compiler support the required operations.

Three source-derived boundary cases explain why this helper should not replace RFF's numerical foundation:

| Helper | Observed mechanism | RFF adoption requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Double exponential | The integer exponent loop consumes only bits 0 through 7. At input 256, no integer multiplier is selected and the result is near one. | Establish the full supported domain and compare against an independent reference before adopting an approximation. |
| Double logarithm | A positive offset is added before special-case handling; zero consequently enters the finite-positive path. Negative inputs and NaNs return signed zero. | Specify singularities and invalid values explicitly; do not inherit the source comment's accuracy claim for the modified whole function. |
| Double square root and vector length | Non-positive or NaN square-root inputs return zero; vector length forms an unscaled dot product first. | Preserve invalid-state diagnostics and use an appropriate overflow/underflow strategy where the supported domain requires it. |

These are deductions from source, not GPU test results. Derived power and hyperbolic operations inherit their dependencies' range and special-case behavior. Such behavior can change escape, branches and orbit statistics before any final color is computed. Keep imported helper names scoped to their recipe, distinguish deliberate compatibility semantics from corrected mathematics, and never expose a precision-reducing approximation slider as an optimization of RFF's perturbation or MPA computation. Finite display masks may use explicitly bounded artistic approximations only with their own documented domain and validation.

The source contains named contributors and external origins for distinctive approximations. Original provenance and licenses remain to be verified before adapting their code or coefficient sets; no implementation or coefficient set was copied into RFF. This batch strengthens the import requirements and does not change section G's provisional material-appearance priority. No shader compilation, numerical execution, rendering comparison or performance test was performed.

### Follow-up to G/AG/AM: sampled visibility, lens blur and accumulation are separate mechanisms

Full reads of [Soft-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Soft-Raytracer.frag) and [3D.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/3D.frag) resolve tutorial 22's renderer dependency. The useful 2D transfers are controlled sampling and clearly separated lighting signals; these files do not justify replacing RFF's existing material model with this older renderer.

**Soft shadows come from averaging visibility samples.** Each invocation chooses one direction in a spherical cap around Sun, using a uniform azimuth and cos(theta)=1-u*SunSize. A distance-estimator march returns binary visibility. The 3D wrapper accumulates contributions across subframes, producing a soft boundary as directions become partly occluded. SunSize is a cosine-span parameter, not an angle in radians or a material roughness. SpotLightSize is declared but not consumed by this lighting implementation; Reflection and floor settings likewise do not establish active reflection/floor tracing in the inspected color path. Lighting direction is computed from SpotLightPos, while the shadow direction comes from Sun, so a new RFF control should explicitly associate visibility with the light it attenuates.

For RFF relief, the corresponding feature would sample visibility against a defined height field, with declared height scale, coordinates, maximum reach and edge behavior. A 3D fractal distance estimator cannot be substituted for that field. The existing slope shader already computes cavity darkening, and studio_surface applies AO to diffuse and partly to environment response; a new cast-shadow feature must demonstrate an additional benefit over those controls. Match the visibility sample to the direct-light contribution rather than attenuating all ambient/environment illumination with one sun test. Filtered environment reflection from section G remains a separate, smaller-scope material improvement: reflection roughness broadens incoming radiance, whereas soft-shadow sampling estimates how much of an extended source is blocked.

**The AO path is not a cosine-weighted hemisphere estimator.** Soft-Raytracer generates a point in a centered cube, flips its hemisphere against the normal and normalizes it. That is a nonuniform directional distribution without a compensating probability-density factor. Its return value combines hit distance and a finite reach; budget exhaustion has another explicit return path. The alternate AO mode is based on primary march step count. Both can supply artistic darkening, but neither should be described as a measured physical ambient-occlusion integral. DetailAO also enters the active reach as 10^(DetailAO/10), while a separately computed 10^DetailAO value is unused. Design RFF controls around the actual consumed quantity rather than copying the label or range.

**Progressive camera sampling is a different use of blur.** The 3D wrapper offsets the camera origin on a circular aperture and aims the ray toward a focal-plane point. It independently constructs a subpixel disc sample for antialiasing. Its square-root radial mapping is uniform in disc area if the two random inputs are uniform, despite a nearby comment claiming nonuniform density. The accumulated pixel is a weighted color sum plus weight in alpha; the optional radial exponential weight is a reconstruction kernel over that disc. Alpha therefore represents sample weight, not scene transparency or depth. The wrapper accumulates c directly; unlike the previously inspected Progressive2D path, it does not raise each new color sample to Gamma before accumulation. The color function still needs an explicit linear-radiance contract before that difference can be called physically correct.

An RFF depth-of-field analogue needs a defined depth/height model and an occlusion-aware reconstruction policy. Blurring a colored 2D image by an arbitrary iteration field would be an artistic depth effect, not the same thin-lens geometry. Keep this optional and lower priority than environment authoring and stable image filtering. If progressive visibility or lens sampling is added, use independently controlled sample dimensions, deterministic pixel/sample indexing across tiled export, and reset accumulation when scene, light, material or camera inputs change. Those reset semantics are host responsibilities and are not proven by these two shader files. Preserve accumulated sums and weights through display changes only when the stored representation permits it.

**Depth and intermediate state require explicit ownership.** The DepthToAlpha option changes gl_FragDepth here; it does not write depth into the wrapper's accumulation alpha. An EXR depth-in-alpha claim consequently depends on an additional host export path. Normal and AO evaluation call DE after the primary hit and before getColor reads the global orbit trap; because DE implementations can mutate that trap, retain a dedicated primary-hit material record when designing an equivalent pipeline. Do not let derivative or visibility probes overwrite the fields intended for surface coloring. This supports section F's typed output channels and the shared material-evaluation proposal.

The source's normal epsilon, distance-dependent termination threshold, first-step dither and shadow-step policy are specific to its 3D march. They are not precision settings to transplant into RFF's perturbation/MPA calculation. Named random/hash implementations also need original-source and license verification before reuse. No application code was changed, and no shader compilation, stochastic convergence, image comparison or timing test was run for these findings.

### Follow-up to G/S: environment lookup, importance sampling and indirect transport

Full reads of [IBL-Pathtracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/IBL-Pathtracer.frag) and [Path-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Path-Raytracer.frag) clarify which parts of these legacy renderers can inform RFF. An environment image can be a source of illumination without requiring a path tracer. These files add transport experiments, not a prerequisite for the section G environment editor.

**Cosine sampling is useful, but the label is misleading.** IBL-Pathtracer offers a uniform hemisphere direction with a throughput factor 2*Albedo*cos(theta), or a cosine-weighted direction with throughput Albedo. For a Lambertian integrand and the respective normalized probability densities, these are two estimators of the same diffuse response. The source calls the second choice BiasedSampling, but importance sampling itself does not imply estimator bias. The derivation only applies to this local sampling/weight pair, not automatically to the entire path algorithm. This mechanism is useful for an independently implemented diffuse-environment preprocessing pass: choose directions where the diffuse integrand has more weight, accumulate in linear radiance, and verify a constant environment before comparing noise under a bright localized source. Keep diffuse convolution separate from the GGX specular prefilter required by RFF's existing material model.

**The panorama is not sampled according to brightness here.** IBL-Pathtracer samples surface directions and reads the environment only when a path misses. Its Stratify option puts samples into a repeating 10 by 10 grid in the two-dimensional sampling domain; it does not build a luminance-weighted environment distribution. This differs from the native GMT environment-CDF proposal already recorded in section S. Small bright regions may benefit from source-aware sampling in an offline prefilter, but adopting that optimization requires consistent directional PDFs, spherical area factors and an estimator matching the chosen lobe. Do not claim these reference files already supply that complete implementation.

**Selection probabilities and material weights must agree.** IBL-Pathtracer selects the diffuse branch with probability 1-reflectivity, then multiplies throughput by that same factor; the mirror branch similarly selects with reflectivity and multiplies by reflectivity again, followed by an extra cosine. Those operations do not establish an energy-preserving diffuse/mirror mixture. A newly designed sampler should explicitly define its target BRDF, branch probability and weight divided by the sampling PDF. Preserve RFF's existing Fresnel, roughness and clearcoat conventions rather than replacing them with this reflectivity slider. The same pixel/subframe seed is reused for successive bounce decisions and direction samples, with no bounce index in the seed; section G's preprocessing should allocate sample dimensions deliberately and compare convergence, rather than assume that more subframes guarantee an unbiased result.

**Direct-light sampling is a separate transport choice.** Path-Raytracer's NextEvent mode adds explicit sun/sky visibility contributions at each hit and excludes background contributions from later escaping bounces. This avoids adding those two paths naively, but the inspected implementation has no general multiple-importance weighting and uses separately calibrated sun/sky expressions. Its Bias mode changes sky direction distribution and weighting around a fixed world axis, so it is not proven equivalent to its alternate branch for arbitrary surface normals. The finite RayDepth and deterministic low-throughput cutoff also limit transport. These examples illustrate why importing a complete legacy lighting loop would be much larger and riskier than adding a controlled environment input to RFF.

**RFF scope and validation:** first implement the already-proposed environment source, orientation, linear-radiance storage and independently filtered diffuse/base/coat consumers. Cache preprocessing by source and filter settings. A future height-field indirect-lighting mode would additionally need geometry, visibility, bounce termination and temporal convergence contracts; it remains lower priority and is not implied by an environment-reflection feature. Compare a constant environment, one bright patch, multiple colored patches and a labeled panorama. Check brightness preservation, lobe width and axes separately from time-to-convergence. None of these source reads provides a measured RFF speedup or quality score.

The reference trace functions also show why primary depth should be a separate result: IBL-Pathtracer returns on a hit before its depth-write block, allowing a later miss to consume depthFlag, whereas Path-Raytracer places the write before the hit return. Do not derive a reliable first-surface depth channel from their shared option name. Source declarations include further compatibility concerns, such as a repeated global depthFlag declaration in Path-Raytracer; actual importer/compiler acceptance was not tested. These observations are adoption constraints, not a request to repair GMT. No third-party implementation was copied and no numerical, shader-compilation, visual or performance tests were run.

### Follow-up to G/S: a procedural sky is an optional environment source

Full reads of [Sunsky.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Sunsky.frag) and [Sky-PathTracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Sky-PathTracer.frag) add a third possible environment source alongside editable gradients and user images. For RFF, the useful feature is a controllable warm sun/blue sky lighting pattern reflected in existing 2D relief. It does not require turning the fractal into a 3D scene or running the supplied path tracer.

**Mechanism:** Sunsky combines wavelength-dependent Rayleigh coefficients, a turbidity-dependent Mie term, angular phase functions and exponential extinction along an approximate atmospheric path. A separately generated solar disc supplies a small bright region. Sun direction and turbidity change the distribution of color and brightness, while the same direction-to-radiance interface could feed section G's cached diffuse and specular preprocessing. Treat this as a procedural artistic sky model with a declared valid domain; the inspected source is not evidence of a complete calibrated atmosphere simulation.

**The source's three consumers are not interchangeable.** sun returns a hard-edged disc, sky returns only the atmospheric contribution multiplied by SkyFactor, and sunsky combines atmosphere with a smoothed disc but does not apply SkyFactor. A zero-size disc also selects a red special-case output in sunsky. Thus sky plus sun does not reproduce sunsky for arbitrary settings. RFF should define one underlying source with explicit sky/disc components and consistent strengths, then route those components to background, environment lighting and any direct-light consumer. Decide whether disc size changes integrated energy or maintains it, and label the control accordingly. The actual threshold cos(sunSize*pi/180) defines an angular radius even though a variable name says diameter; do not inherit the ambiguous label.

**Horizon and filtering contract:** the optical path divides by max(0, dot(up, view)), reaching a zero denominator at and below the horizon. A newly implemented source needs a defined horizon limit and lower-hemisphere/ground policy before it can illuminate every reflected direction of RFF's relief. Normalize directions, bound inverse-trigonometric inputs against rounding, and verify poles and the horizon. The disc's fixed cosine-space smoothing width is not tied to the output pixel footprint. Preserve its energy when baking a small disc into an environment texture, and apply both minification filtering and the intended material-lobe filtering. A low-resolution bake that misses the disc is not fixed by increasing final surface samples.

**Direct-light duplication matters.** Sky-PathTracer samples the solar cone explicitly in diffuse branches and, when DirectLight is enabled, excludes the solar disc from later environment misses. That illustrates the need to count each lighting contribution deliberately. However, the explicit contribution uses a fixed 1E-5 scale instead of showing the cone-solid-angle/PDF normalization, and it inherits the already-updated continuation throughput. It is not a transferable radiometric estimator. RFF should not add a sun light over an environment containing the same sun without defining whether the intended result is a combined artistic effect or a nonduplicated lighting model. Roughness filtering of environment radiance and finite-source shadow sampling remain different operations.

The sky tracer advances a mutable seed for direction samples, improving on the earlier fixed-seed direction calls, but its diffuse/mirror branch still uses a pixel/subframe-only random value at every bounce. This is not proof of independent transport samples. Its main relevance is to the sampling contracts already recorded in S, not a new high-priority path-tracing proposal. A procedural sky can follow gradient/image environment support if users need natural lighting presets; it should not delay the simpler environment editor.

**Provenance:** Sunsky's own header explicitly states uncertainty about the fragment's license and lists a chain of adaptations leading to a claimed MIT origin. That is a lead for later original-source verification, not a verified license for this exact fragment. No source code or distinctive coefficient set was adapted. Compare any future independently sourced implementation using a constant-source baseline, horizon/zenith views, sun-size changes and roughness sweeps. These two files were reviewed as source only; no atmospheric accuracy, shader compilation, image-quality or performance validation was executed.

### Follow-up to E/H: evolving procedural masks, not another basic noise feature

Full reads of [IQ-Clouds.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/IQ-Clouds.frag), [Ashima-Noise.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Ashima-Noise.frag) and [QuilezLib.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/QuilezLib.frag) support refinements to procedural material sources. RFF already has interpolated value noise in effects.glsl, multiple noise scales in dark_surface.glsl and normalized, tiling octave noise in palette_sampling.glsl's warp_fbm. Basic noise, cloud-like mottling and palette displacement are therefore existing capabilities, not new proposals justified by these files.

**The useful extension is a shared evolving field.** Ashima-Noise implements textureless simplex noise in two, three and four dimensions: it identifies a simplex cell, hashes its corners through polynomial permutations, assigns gradient directions and sums compactly supported gradient contributions. Three-dimensional noise evaluated at (u,v,time) can evolve the shape of a 2D mask instead of merely translating it. Four-dimensional noise evaluated at (u,v,r*cos(phase),r*sin(phase)) offers a mathematically closed animation path, provided phase and its endpoint conventions are consistent. This looping construction is a proposed RFF application of the available dimensionality, not an existing feature demonstrated by the reference file. It does not automatically make the spatial U/V boundaries tile seamlessly.

Expose such a field through section E's source/remap mechanism so it can drive roughness, wetness or other supported material parameters with one explicit coordinate and time contract. Preserve existing recipe IDs, random sequences and saved appearances; use a new source/version where a changed algorithm would alter an old field. Textureless evaluation exchanges memory lookups for arithmetic and is not automatically faster than RFF's current noise. Select a noise family only after comparing appearance, cost and repeat behavior for the intended use. The modular lattice hash also does not recover fractional precision already lost by passing very large float coordinates; keep deep-zoom mapping separate from fractal computation.

**Filter the composed signal.** Neither the simplex helper nor the cloud's fixed octave sum integrates over a pixel footprint. Fade unresolved octave contributions smoothly using the footprint in the actual mapped coordinates, and account for any later threshold or domain warp that introduces sharper features. Avoid abruptly dropping octaves during a zoom. Distinguish mean preservation from contrast preservation when adjusting octave weights; blindly renormalizing the remaining amplitudes can visibly change the field. Compute shaders need an explicit footprint or neighboring-coordinate information rather than an assumption that fragment derivatives are available. Normal perturbations additionally need derivative consistency as the field's frequency and filtering change. These requirements extend section H beyond image textures without claiming a verified defect in every existing RFF procedural path.

**Cloud rendering is a different, lower-priority feature.** IQ-Clouds combines four scales of 3D value noise with a vertical density gradient and wind translation. It marches fixed-length ray segments, estimates directional shading from a second density lookup, and composites premultiplied contributions front to back. The fixed per-sample opacity multiplier is not derived from segment length; changing the step spacing without recalibrating opacity would change the appearance. CloudSteps also changes the maximum reached distance because spacing stays fixed. After integration it converts toward straight color using an offset denominator and clamps the result. A genuine volume extension would need transmittance tied to segment length, an explicit finite domain, early termination, HDR and alpha contracts. A 2D noise mask needs none of that ray integration and should not be advertised as volumetric scattering. The Attenuation uniform is declared but unused in the inspected cloud implementation.

**Shape composition can complement noise masks.** QuilezLib provides primitive fields and min/max union, subtraction and intersection. In 2D, independently implemented circles, boxes and half-planes could supply editable mask shapes combined with a noise source. Record sign, units, transformation and operand order; this library's subtraction returns max(-d1,d2), corresponding to the second operand minus the first. Do not assume every function labeled signed or unsigned is an exact Euclidean distance. For example, sdToBox returns the maximum component outside in cases where Euclidean corner distance is larger. Such fields can still classify regions, but constant-width outlines and distance-based stepping need a stronger contract.

IQ-Clouds declares a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike license; Ashima-Noise names authors and an MIT license with a separate LICENSE reference; QuilezLib names its source page without including a license grant. These are source records, not independently verified permission to copy the exact bundled files. No code, hash constants or coefficient sets were adopted. A future implementation should verify original provenance and update NOTICE as required. This batch made no application changes and ran no shader, animation, filtering or performance tests.

### Follow-up to F/AK/AJ: buffer semantics determine which postprocess is valid

Full reads of [ZBuffer3D.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/ZBuffer3D.frag), [ZBufferShader.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/ZBufferShader.frag), [BufferShaderRD.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/BufferShaderRD.frag) and [BufferShaderIFS.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/BufferShaderIFS.frag) provide four different buffer interpretations. Their transferable lesson is explicit typed intermediate outputs and matching display adapters, not one universal postprocessing shader.

**Nearest candidate is not an accumulated average.** ZBuffer3D retains the entire new RGBA tuple when its alpha is smaller than the previous alpha, or during initial subframes; otherwise it retains the old tuple. This preserves color/depth association for a nearest candidate. It supplies neither progressive radiance averaging nor subpixel antialiasing in its inspected main function. The file nevertheless names BufferShader.frag, whose active display path divides color by alpha after hue conversion. That is appropriate only under a compatible weight contract, not automatically when alpha means depth. No references to ZBuffer3D or ZBufferShader were found in the searched bundled reference tree, so this pairing is a source-level integration concern, not proof of a currently executed GMT rendering failure.

RFF's proposed auxiliary outputs should identify color space, numeric units, invalid/miss encoding and update rule. Separate radiance sum plus weight, nearest depth plus associated attributes, scalar simulation state and coverage/transparency. Select a display adapter by that contract. A nearest-depth reduction also needs scene-change invalidation: keeping the old minimum after geometry moves farther away would preserve a stale candidate. It cannot replace a temporal average simply because both use a previous-frame texture.

**Depth-derived normals need the correct projection.** ZBufferShader reconstructs world position as Eye plus the normalized perspective ray multiplied by Near+depth*(Far-Near), then crosses screen derivatives of that position. This differs from the earlier DepthBufferShader approximation and is a meaningful mechanism when depth stores linear distance along the ray. Hardware depth, camera-axis distance and height would each need a different reconstruction. ZBuffer3D offers an equirectangular ray mode, but this display shader reconstructs only the perspective ray. The two modes therefore cannot share this reconstruction unchanged. At silhouettes, invalid samples and depth discontinuities, screen derivatives may mix unrelated surfaces; a RFF implementation should validate neighbors and retain a stable fallback rather than turn a discontinuity into a surface normal. Compute passes require explicit neighbor reconstruction rather than fragment derivative built-ins.

The local AO loop compares sampled depth order over a jittered screen-space disk and applies darkening after tone mapping and gamma. It does not reconstruct hemisphere visibility or a world-space radius. NormalScale is declared but unused. These are artistic screen-space operations; RFF already has cavity darkening, so importing them would need demonstrated benefit under matched scenes. For lighting-oriented AO, define its linear-light consumer separately from a deliberate display-space contrast effect. DebugNormals uses absolute normal components and loses sign; a signed normal inspection channel is more informative for diagnosing orientation.

**Simulation display should remain separate from simulation state.** BufferShaderRD derives a normal from neighboring red-channel values, lights a modulo-colored state and blends an external image after grading. Its initially pixel-sized stencil is overwritten by a fixed 1/740 UV step, so it samples a fixed normalized radius rather than consistently adjacent texels across resolutions. The useful RFF transfer is optional relief shading of a simulation/material field with explicit sample spacing and height units. Keep this downstream of the state update described in AJ; applying gamma, lighting or an image blend to stored simulation values would change the evolution. The final external-image blend also needs a common declared color space.

BufferShaderIFS instead applies log to RGB, then a Gamma power and exposure mapping; alpha is ignored. It is a density-style display transform, not the accumulated-radiance adapter its generic header might suggest. A future RFF histogram/density view needs a nonnegative domain, a defined zero-count mapping and separation of display normalization from saved data. Values between zero and one produce negative logarithms, which cannot be passed unconditionally to a general real power. Verify the producer's value range before choosing the transform. These requirements refine existing inspection and field-source proposals without changing the precision or meaning of fractal iterations. No application code was modified and no shader compilation, projection test or image comparison was run.

### Follow-up to E/H/L: periodic gradient fields and signed palette weights

Full reads of [Classic-Noise.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Classic-Noise.frag), [ColorPalette.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/ColorPalette.frag) and [ColorPalette2.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/ColorPalette2.frag) refine the procedural-source and palette proposals without adding a duplicate basic noise feature.

**Periodic noise requires a lattice contract.** Classic-Noise supplies two-, three- and four-dimensional gradient noise with nonperiodic and explicitly periodic entry points. Each evaluates corner gradient dot products and interpolates using a quintic fade. The periodic variants wrap lattice coordinates before hashing while retaining the local fractional coordinate. To obtain the advertised repeat in the input coordinates, use positive integer lattice periods: adding a noninteger period also changes the fractional coordinate, so wrapping lattice indices alone does not prove continuity. Zero periods are invalid. For a normalized RFF UV tile, scale the coordinates and the lattice period together; match every octave's frequency and repeat, including negative coordinates. Existing RFF warp_fbm already implements tiling value noise, so replacing it globally would change saved appearances and is not proposed.

The gradient construction and quintic interpolation offer a different texture character and smooth lattice joins. They do not by themselves solve spatial aliasing, temporal aliasing or a later threshold's sharp edges. Three-dimensional periodic noise can use a third, integer-period coordinate for a looping evolution of a 2D mask. This is another option alongside the circular four-dimensional sampling path described earlier. Compare appearance and evaluation cost before choosing; four-dimensional classic noise evaluates sixteen corner contributions, whereas the inspected four-dimensional simplex implementation uses five. Corner count alone is not a GPU benchmark, because arithmetic, register pressure and compiler behavior also matter.

For section E's material masks, validate both values and derivatives across the spatial and temporal seam. A seamless grayscale field can still reveal a discontinuity after normal construction if the derivative or coordinate convention changes. Keep the user-visible loop duration separate from the integer lattice period, use the same time mapping for preview and video export, and avoid duplicating the terminal frame in a loop unless explicitly requested. Gradient normalization and amplitude constants belong to the chosen noise algorithm; they are not a reason to modify fractal arithmetic or existing palette recipe generation. The file names Stefan Gustavson, acknowledges Ian McEwan and refers to an MIT license file; original licensing remains to be verified before copying an implementation.

**The palette is an affine color cycle, not a convex three-stop gradient.** Both palette files rotate the vector (1,0,0) about the equal-component axis, using Coloring(p)*ColorDensity+ColorOffset as the angle, then use the rotated components as weights for three user colors. Their weights sum to one, but can be negative: at a half turn they are (-1/3,2/3,2/3). Consequently the result can leave the range spanned by the three colors. These are source-derived mathematical properties, not rendered observations. The normal parameter is unused. ColorPalette provides baseColor while ColorPalette2 provides color despite the shared providesColor declaration, so the renderer's required entry point must be checked rather than inferred from that macro.

For RFF, an optional analytic color-cycle recipe could expose this kind of continuous parameterization, but it must declare its color space and negative/HDR-value policy. A hard clamp changes the cycle and can create flat color regions; a gamut-mapping policy is a separate artistic choice. This is not equivalent to physically rotating light, interpolating an ordinary three-stop palette or guaranteeing perceptually uniform hue. Preserve stable palette recipe IDs and old generation sequences, and consider baking a new analytic recipe into the existing palette infrastructure rather than adding per-pixel matrix evaluation. RFF already has extensive palette and cycle support, so this is a lower-priority authoring variant, not a missing core capability. No source implementation was copied and no shader compilation, seam/derivative test, image comparison or timing measurement was performed.

### Follow-up to E/V/X: terrain and inversion fields as material sources

Full reads of [MathUtils.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/MathUtils.frag), [terr_incl.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/terr_incl.frag), [Kaliset3D.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Kaliset3D.frag) and [Kaliset3Dtex.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Kaliset3Dtex.frag) add two scalar-source mechanisms to the existing material-field proposal. They need not become alternative deep-zoom fractal solvers.

**Terrain is an unnormalized octave sum.** The terrain helper samples classic noise on the XZ plane, increases frequency by TerrFreq, and scales successive amplitudes by TerrAmp. It subtracts the resulting height times TerrSlope from Y. Unlike RFF's inspected normalized warp_fbm, this sum changes its amplitude envelope when octave count or gain changes. The sum starts with amplitude one, so TerrAmp controls persistence of later octaves rather than overall amplitude. Wind translates the sampling coordinates; its Y component has no effect on the XZ-only height function. The active surf function applies a transform and returns the terrain field capped above at one; the commented surface-mode alternatives are not active features.

For RFF, this is a possible height/mask source with separate amplitude, frequency, octave persistence and time controls. Reuse the existing field pipeline rather than advertise basic octave noise as new. Preserve a declared normalization convention when varying detail, and keep footprint filtering consistent with that convention. The value Y-height(X,Z) is a vertical residual, not generally Euclidean distance to the terrain. It is suitable for a height representation, but copying it into distance-based ray stepping would require a slope/Lipschitz bound or another justified intersection method. The surface transform multiplies rotations by translation before applying the matrix to a column vector; the translation is therefore applied first. A user-facing object transform should explicitly define whether controls transform the object or the lookup coordinates.

**Kaliset provides a different scalar texture.** Both Kaliset files implement the same recurrence: translated/scaled input, component fold abs(p+fold)-fold, row-vector rotation, inversion by squared radius, then scale and a fixed Julia offset. The output is either the last radius or a sum of exp(-1/abs(previousRadius-currentRadius)), followed by a power and scale. This sum weights large radius changes more strongly; it is not an exponential moving average of the radius and not a distance estimator. Bailout is checked before adding the current smoothing contribution. Kaliset3Dtex declares texture/height controls but its function does not consume them; actual application of those controls belongs to its callers and remains a separate trace to inspect.

A 2D adaptation could feed this scalar into color or material masks, or use a two-component recurrence as a distinct procedural recipe. A slice of the 3D field and a genuinely 2D recurrence are different outputs: out-of-plane rotation or a nonzero third Julia component can leave the slice during iteration. Preserve fold order, rotation convention, initial state and bailout sampling. Zero inversion radius, zero rotation axis and zero output raised to a zero power require explicit domain choices. Do not silently regularize the formula and call the changed result a compatible import. Limit detail according to the displayed footprint, and do not replace RFF's perturbation/MPA core with this display-source calculation.

**Shared utility contracts matter.** MathUtils' axis-angle helpers take degrees and assume an appropriate axis, while the previously inspected palette helper takes radians. Matrix multiplication side determines rotation direction. Its optional integer hash hashes floating-point bit patterns and converts the full unsigned result to float; rounding can reach the nominal upper endpoint after division by 2^32. RFF sampling should define the required open/closed interval and use explicit pixel, sample and dimension indices rather than assume arbitrary float-coordinate hashing supplies reproducible independent samples. The alternative sine hash and the integer hash have different source/provenance requirements; neither branch has been benchmarked or adopted here. Capability directives should be derived from the operations actually required by a Vulkan implementation, not copied wholesale from these OpenGL-era includes.

These findings strengthen the typed material-source and coordinate contracts already proposed. The additional Kaliset source is an optional artistic extension, lower priority than environment authoring and stable filtering. No algorithm, constants or application code were copied or changed, and no numerical, shader-compilation or rendering tests were executed.

### Follow-up to H/U/AL: double-valued wrappers do not guarantee double-valued sampling

Full reads of [Progressive2D-4.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Progressive2D-4.frag), [BufferShader-4.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/BufferShader-4.frag) and [Shadertoy.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Shadertoy.frag) refine the importer and sampling contracts. None of these files establishes a replacement for RFF's high-precision reference/perturbation pipeline.

**Trace precision through the entire data path.** Progressive2D-4 declares double Zoom and Center, but the vertex path converts Zoom to float, stores the transformed coordinate and sampling scale in float varyings, and only later adds Center in double precision. The accumulation target is RGBA32F. The non-linearGamma color path additionally converts color to float before exponentiation. This can be useful mixed precision, but it is not evidence of an entirely double-precision camera, integrand or accumulation buffer. RFF should document each representation separately and retain its existing deep-zoom coordinate construction; changing uniform types alone cannot restore information lost upstream.

**Transform the sampling footprint with the coordinate map.** Rotation and reciprocal-axis stretch affect coord, while aaScale remains axis-aligned and does not contain that matrix. Thus the center mapping and the jitter mapping describe different footprints when a transform is active. The disc sample depends only on subframe, so every pixel uses the same offset in that pass. Such coherent jitter may be a deliberate pattern, but it is not independently scrambled sampling per pixel. A new RFF sampling path should apply the complete map to its sample offsets and define reconstruction weights in the intended image-space domain. This also matters for anisotropic filtering: equal area under a reciprocal-axis stretch does not imply equal shape or bandwidth.

The GaussianAA expression uses a truncated radial exponential weight over the sampled disc; AARange scales the offset after the weight is evaluated. AAExp=0 and a zero accumulated weight need explicit handling. The NaN comparison rejects NaN color but does not establish a finite-value check for infinity, nor does it validate the weight.
