The providesFiltering branch delegates both color and weight to the caller and skips the built-in jitter, so it requires a separate producer contract. Those branches cannot be treated as identical merely because they share a buffer.

**Accumulation and display changes have different invalidation rules.** This wrapper always adds to the previous buffer; it has no decay, motion compensation or scene-change reset in the inspected shader. It therefore provides static progressive integration, not by itself motion blur or an animation trail. When Gamma is applied to every sample before accumulation, changing Gamma changes the stored integrand and requires restarting that history. Exposure or other transformations applied only in the display pass can be edited without recalculating unchanged source samples. An RFF design should distinguish these dependencies explicitly and avoid retaining stale samples after material, coordinate or animation changes.

BufferShader-4 divides float RGB by float alpha before assigning the result to a double vector. Several later operations also cast back to float; in particular its exponential branch uses a scalar float conversion of the vector expression, so it does not preserve independent RGB exponential responses. Its sigmoid normalization has a zero denominator at zero contrast. These are source-level reasons to reuse RFF's established color pipeline and explicit channel operations instead of importing this older postprocess wholesale; compilation and rendered behavior were not tested.

**A compatibility include is only a partial host interface.** Shadertoy.frag supplies resolution from reciprocal pixel size and maps time to iGlobalTime. It does not implement texture channels, mouse state, frame counters, multipass scheduling or a mainImage bridge. Importer capability reporting should describe what the actual host supports, with logical canvas dimensions and time units consistent across preview and tiled/video export. This small file cannot establish full Shadertoy compatibility. No code or constants were adopted, and no precision, accumulation, shader-compilation or visual tests were performed.

### Follow-up to A/G: additional tone curves need an output contract

Full reads of [BufferShader-1.0.1.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/BufferShader-1.0.1.frag) and [BufferShader-1.0.2.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/BufferShader-1.0.2.frag), compared with RFF's current vk_linear_interpolation.frag, establish that tone mapping is already a target capability. RFF has white/headroom-normalized curves, scene-linear exposure and distinct SDR, PQ and HLG output paths. The reference files should inform optional appearance controls, not replace that output pipeline.

**Curve mechanisms:** the Lottes function derives its coefficients from input/output middle gray and an HDR reference, then evaluates a rational power curve. Uchimura combines a powered dark region, a linear middle region and an exponential shoulder using transition weights. Its convenience overload fixes all shape parameters, so the reference does not itself expose a full curve editor. Uncharted2 uses a rational curve, a fixed internal exposure multiplier and a fixed white normalization. GMT then applies brightness/saturation/contrast and clamps most branches before its final gamma power. RFF's inspected filmic curve already uses the same general rational family with a different white/headroom convention. Identical technique names therefore do not imply identical exposure or output appearance.

An optional RFF curve editor could make shadow roll-off, middle-tone slope and highlight compression understandable through a preview curve and representative material patches. This is a proposal extending the inspected fixed presets. Define which controls preserve middle gray, white level or chromatic ratios, rather than suggesting they can all be adjusted independently without consequence. Keep the chosen curve in the existing output stage and preserve the established transfer-function routing. A manual gamma power is not a substitute for RFF's linear-to-sRGB, PQ or HLG operations. Any new named curve requires original-source/license verification and matching NOTICE attribution before implementation.

**Compare color behavior, not only brightness.** The reference curves operate independently on RGB components, which can change chromatic ratios as channels reach the shoulder at different times. RFF's scene-linear SDR branch instead uses a common scale above a peak threshold to retain those ratios. Neither policy should be silently substituted for the other in existing presets. Compare saturated metallic highlights, dark gradients and neutral ramps at matched exposure and white level. Mode 9 in these reference files multiplies color by its own luminance, making it degree-two with respect to exposure-scaled input; it is a contrast-like artistic operation followed by clipping, not a highlight compressor. Sigmoid mode bypasses the usual saturation adjustment and needs a defined zero-contrast limit. User-visible controls should describe these mode-dependent consumers.

**Version differences change filtering, too.** The 1.0.1 bloom kernel uses cubed polynomial axis weights; 1.0.2 uses squared weights and adds BloomStrong to scale sample spacing. Both blur accumulated RGBA and then divide the blurred RGB by blurred alpha. Consequently their apparent sample-count normalization cancels in that final ratio for nonzero weight; the result weights neighboring colors by their accumulated sample weights. It is not generally an equal-weight blur of individually normalized pixels when their history weights differ. Zero support/weight and BloomTaps=0 need an explicit policy. Both apply a power to the blurred color without bright-pass thresholding, so they are not the soft-knee bright-region extraction proposed in A. Lens-flare code in 1.0.1 is commented out and is not an active demonstrated feature.

These distinctions are useful when designing regression comparisons and saved-mode compatibility. They do not establish that another tone-map preset would outperform section G's environment improvement. No shader was modified or compiled, no coefficient set was copied, and no colorimetric, visual or performance tests were run.

### Follow-up to H/AM: footprint-coupled relief evaluation versus fuzzy ray marching

Full reads of [SoC.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/SoC.frag) and [testSoC.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/testSoC.frag) reveal a different approach from the progressive thin-lens renderer. SoC means Sphere of Confusion here. It uses one ray and an expanding evaluation radius to approximate antialiasing, defocus, shadow softness and reflection blur together. Its header's speed description is not a measured comparison with RFF or an equivalent reference renderer.

**Mechanism:** the radius is the maximum of an aperture-scaled distance from the focal setting and a pixel-size-dependent floor. When the distance field falls within that radius, the marcher evaluates a six-probe normal using offsets proportional to the radius, gathers colors during those same probes, and adds a partial surface contribution through a linear coverage-like ramp. Front-to-back accumulation ends near opacity 0.9 or at the distance/step limit. Shadow evaluation grows another cone and multiplies soft visibility factors. This is a deliberately fuzzy surface model; its accumulated alpha is not an exact geometric pixel coverage or physical volume transmittance.

The transferable RFF idea is to coordinate the scale of material-field sampling, normal estimation and visibility with the displayed footprint. Fine noise should not produce a sharp unstable normal after its color has already been filtered away. However, broadening normal probes alone is not equivalent to integrating the BRDF over unresolved normals. Retain RFF's existing normal-variance/roughness treatment and define how any filtered height field contributes to it, avoiding duplicate broadening. Separate output-pixel footprint, artistic relief softness, material roughness and camera defocus in the user model even if an implementation shares intermediate scale information.

**This is not the same camera model as aperture sampling.** No lens-origin samples or previous-frame accumulation appear in SoC's main path. It estimates blur through the radius and march rather than averaging thin-lens rays. Its pixel floor uses pixelSize.x and its own distance expression, so a transplant would need explicit FOV, aspect, canvas-size and tiled-projection handling. The focus correction and radius should be validated on off-axis surfaces rather than assumed equivalent to the earlier 3D wrapper. In RFF's ordinary 2D view, use an image-space footprint derived from the actual coordinate mapping; do not invent camera distance from iteration count.

**Color and geometry have a special coupling.** SoC enables bColoring during normal probes and expects DE to accumulate a vec4 material sample into mcol. It averages those probe colors; mcol.a controls its quick-reflection branch. testSoC demonstrates this by coloring a bulb and a plane differently and assigning reflection only to the plane. A normal stencil crossing their boundary therefore also mixes material identity. This differs from preserving a primary-hit color while probing geometry, described earlier. For RFF, choose deliberately between footprint-filtered material data and point material data, and keep reflection amount separate from coverage and output alpha. A reusable field interface should make these meanings explicit rather than depending on side effects of a distance function.

**Reflection blur is heuristic.** The reflection branch changes ray direction and adds ReflectionBlur to the travelled-distance variable, which subsequently influences the confusion radius; it does not sample a rough microfacet lobe. FudgeFactor also affects contribution opacity as well as step distance, so changing it can change appearance rather than only convergence speed. The final depth uses the completed traversal's distance, potentially including reflection adjustments, despite a first-hit comment. A RFF auxiliary depth output should preserve a separately defined primary result. Randomized stepping is seeded from fragment coordinates and time, with no demonstrated global tile/sample contract; deterministic exports would need one.

The example's spherical-power recurrence and floor union serve to demonstrate the renderer's callback contract, not a new Mandelbrot or MPA algorithm. Its preset includes a specular value beyond the declared slider maximum, which reinforces the need to distinguish saved numeric values from UI constraints when importing presets. SoC explicitly names eiffie and a CC BY-NC-SA license; retain this provenance lead and verify permissions before any implementation reuse. These source reads support footprint-aware material evaluation as a design principle, but do not justify copying the renderer or claiming physical defocus. No application code changed and no compilation, visual equivalence or timing tests were performed.

### Follow-up to H/U/AM: verify the active call graph before combining rendering techniques

A full read of [SoC-DE-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/SoC-DE-Raytracer.frag) narrows the previous SoC adoption finding. This file contains a conventional distance-estimator renderer's controls and helper functions, but its active trace is an experimental confusion-radius march; much of the conventional trace is commented out. Declared lighting, AO, floor and quality settings therefore cannot be counted as active capabilities of this path merely because their helpers remain in the file.

**Active behavior:** trace uses a fixed loop of 63 iterations and a fixed distance limit, samples DE directly, constructs a normal with six CE calls, and composites fuzzy surface color with a hard-coded light/background. CE also adds a procedural perturbation to the geometry probes and can read the previous buffer using world XY as UV coordinates with an LOD bias. The normal therefore derives from a perturbed field while the main march uses the unperturbed DE. For RFF, decide whether a procedural field is actual geometry, a shading normal perturbation or a color source. Keep its derivatives and filtering consistent with that decision rather than allowing a color callback to alter geometry implicitly.

The outer color function contains a reflection branch, but the active trace never fills its hit or hitNormal output arguments. The caller initializes hitNormal to zero and returns the first trace when it remains zero, so the advertised second reflection trace is not reached through this implementation. The ordinary lighting, shadow and ambientOcclusion helpers are likewise not called by the active trace. This is a concrete reason to require reachable consumers in a shader capability inventory. It does not imply these techniques are unavailable elsewhere in GMT.

**History has two incompatible roles.** The included 3D wrapper stores weighted color sums and sample weights. The experimental trace reads that buffer divided by subframe and uses its alpha as an opacity accumulator, then the wrapper adds the returned RGB as another weighted sample. A sample index is not the accumulated weight when reconstruction weights vary. The result is feedback, not independent Monte Carlo integration of a fixed scene. A fresh history also needs an explicit initial-subframe convention before dividing. RFF should keep sample sums, reconstruction weights, coverage and simulation/feedback state as distinct resources or explicitly typed channels. Intentional feedback can be an artistic effect, but must not masquerade as convergence toward a static image.

**Do not compound blur accidentally.** The included 3D wrapper already performs lens sampling using FocalPlane and Aperture. This trace additionally derives a confusion radius from its own camera-position expression, a fixed minimum radius and Aperture; it does not use the same focal-plane formula. Combining the two therefore does not establish a coherent thin-lens estimator. A RFF implementation should select an explicit approximation or a defined sampling model and explain which parameters control it. Ordinary material roughness, image reconstruction and defocus should remain independently understandable.

For the report's proposed RFF work, the result is a stronger implementation gate rather than a new effect: check the reachable shader path, confirm each output's meaning and trace ownership of history before adapting a reference. Keep the footprint-aware normal/material idea from the previous section, but do not use this experimental integration as a working template. The source repeats the eiffie attribution and CC BY-NC-SA notice for the distance-based defocus block. No code was copied or changed, and no import, compilation, runtime or visual tests were performed.

### Follow-up to H/N/AM: ray differentials and footprint-dependent stopping

A full read of [Subblue-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Subblue-Raytracer.frag) adds a concrete ray-differential example. The vertex setup passes two camera-plane direction increments, dirDx and dirDy, to the fragment stage. A regular AntiAlias by AntiAlias loop offsets the base ray with those increments. The marcher scales its stopping threshold with travelled distance and a screen-scale factor, then uses that threshold for normal and AO probe spacing. These are display-resolution-dependent evaluation choices, not a relaxation of the underlying fractal arithmetic.

**RFF transfer:** carry the Jacobian or equivalent neighbor-coordinate differences of a material lookup through its transformations, and use it consistently for sampling, filtering and relief derivatives. In a 2D pipeline those differences describe field coordinates per output pixel rather than 3D rays. This reinforces section H's footprint design. The reference's grid offsets run from zero toward positive X/Y, so reproducing its sampling pattern requires an explicit pixel-center convention; simply calling it centered supersampling would be inaccurate. At AntiAlias=1 it evaluates the base ray. Tile projections and output dimensions must produce the same global sample positions as an untiled render.

**Ray parameterization is a prerequisite.** The reference passes the offset ray directly to trace without normalizing it, while its bounding-sphere quadratic omits a dot(direction,direction) coefficient. Its boundingRadius is subtracted directly from squared origin length, so it behaves as a squared-radius parameter in that expression. These source facts limit the implementation's usefulness as an intersection template. For any RFF height-field preview that introduces rays, choose normalized-distance or a general parameterized-ray contract and carry it through bounds, stepping, depth and footprint calculations. A bound should restrict work without changing the valid visible surface; verify inside, outside, tangent and off-axis cases independently.

The march checks a candidate hit on a subsequent step to reduce isolated filament detections. This is a heuristic confirmation, not proof of an exact intersection, and the tolerance is also affected by surfaceSmoothness scaling of the DE. Do not transpose it into a Mandelbrot membership or precision rule. Similarly, glow is based on work performed (steps/stepLimit), and normal-direction AO sums weighted distance deficits. Those artistic signals can change when the sampling strategy changes. RFF's field-based materials should not silently depend on such algorithmic work counts.

**Preserve established material/output behavior.** Despite the Blinn-Phong label, the lighting helper raises the normal/light-direction dot product to the specular exponent without constructing a view/light half-vector. It is not a reason to replace RFF's existing GGX shading. AO multiplies the combined lit color, whereas existing RFF paths distinguish its material consumers. The transparent option clears a miss to zero internally, but trace returns only RGB and main always writes alpha one; this path therefore does not demonstrate transparent image export. A source control is a capability only if its value reaches the intended output. The trailing depthFlag assignment also has no declaration in this file, so standalone importer/compiler viability remains unverified.

The file includes Tom Beddard/Subblue copyright and GPL Version 3 provenance for the raymarcher. No source code was adopted. These observations refine footprint, capability and output contracts; they do not add a measured high-priority feature or request fixes to GMT. No shader compilation, intersection tests, image comparisons or timing measurements were run.

### Follow-up to H/U/AM: polygonal apertures and an artificial focus interval

Full reads of [3DKn-1.0.0.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/3DKn-1.0.0.frag) and [3DKn-1.0.1.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/3DKn-1.0.1.frag) add polygonal aperture sampling and a widened in-focus interval to the earlier camera comparison. These are optional ideas for a future depth/height preview, not prerequisites for RFF's main 2D renderer or editable environment reflections.

**The ray is a structured, piecewise path.** SRay stores origin, principal direction, lens offset, parameter position, a step multiplier and reciprocal focal distance. SRCurrentPt adds a lens-offset coefficient consisting of a linear term plus a clamped correction. With zero InFocusAWidth it converges at the focal parameter; with nonzero width the offset vanishes throughout a finite parameter interval around that point. This deliberately creates a sharp focus region rather than a conventional thin lens's single focal surface. An implementation should label it as an artistic focus-width control. The renderer callback actually takes SRay, despite the older vec3 camera-position/direction signature in the introductory comment.

The versions also change the principal direction from unnormalized to normalized while retaining reciprocal FocalPlane in the path expression. In the perspective zero-width case, the former makes the focal parameter correspond to a camera-axis plane, whereas the latter places convergence at a fixed distance along normalized principal rays. A saved focal value therefore cannot be assumed to mean the same focal surface across versions. A new RFF depth effect should explicitly distinguish ray distance, camera-axis depth and image-derived height. SRReflect transforms origin, direction and offset together; 1.0.1 additionally advances the ray parameter by eps, while 1.0.0 ignores that argument. Preserve the complete representation when adapting a camera path, rather than reflecting only one vector.

**Aperture shape controls the blur kernel.** The code samples a circle for two sides, otherwise transforms a random pair into a polygon-sector sample, with an optional star-like variant and a rotation. The rotation expression uses ApertureRot*pi/360, giving half the conventional degree-to-radian angle. Sector selection uses a second random pair and folds the resulting angular index through full rotations; its distribution should be validated before calling the entire aperture sampler uniform. For RFF, a polygonal bokeh option would require an actual depth/occlusion model or an explicitly artistic image-space approximation. It is not interchangeable with GGX roughness, bloom or an environment-map blur. Independently verify kernel normalization and shape orientation using isolated highlights before offering saved presets.

**Version identity also affects sampling and postprocessing.** Version 1.0.0 applies PixelScale.y to both jitter axes; 1.0.1 uses the two-component PixelScale and introduces an equirectangular branch. Match the mapping Jacobian and tile projection rather than assuming either expression is universally correct from its square-pixel comment. The later file selects BufferShader-1.0.1 and declares lens-flare controls, but the selected buffer shader's lens-flare implementation is commented out, as established in the preceding comparison. AutoFocus is declared without a shader consumer here; any host behavior requires separate verification. These observations reinforce a versioned capability inventory based on the connected, reachable implementation.

For RFF, retain the common requirements already identified: independently specified sample dimensions, weighted accumulation, scene-change invalidation and stable preview/export coordinates. A focus-width or polygon-aperture feature remains lower priority than material-source and filtering improvements for the 2D target. The files credit Syntopia and knighty; any reuse requires verifying their original provenance and applicable license. No camera model, shader or source constants were adopted, and no compilation, focal-surface, aperture-distribution or rendering tests were performed.

### Follow-up to H/U/AM: later camera versions are not interchangeable upgrades

Full reads of [3DKn-1.0.4.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/3DKn-1.0.4.frag) and [3DKn-1.0.5.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/3DKn-1.0.5.frag) complete the four bundled 3DKn camera includes. Their differences support version-specific import contracts rather than automatically substituting the highest-numbered file.

Version 1.0.4 adds film-gate/focal-length framing and an optional external camera. The vertex coordinate uses FilmGate/(2*FocalLength) when enabled, but the fragment's perspective jitter still uses the separate FOV uniform. Therefore framing and sample footprint can use different scales. For a future RFF height preview or any shared coordinate mapping, derive both center position and differentials from the same effective projection parameters. The external-camera branch linearly blends forward/up vectors, takes right directly from the external camera, and has no local initialization branch when the external-camera macro is defined but its weight is zero. A camera-transition feature needs a valid orthonormal basis throughout the transition and a defined zero-weight endpoint. This source alone does not establish a robust camera interpolation implementation.

**Smooth focus control changes the path.** Both versions add DofCorrect, replacing the earlier clamped focus-width expression with a smoothstep-based correction. It smooths the transition but does not preserve an exactly flat in-focus interval. At zero InFocusAWidth the smoothstep edges coincide; implement the intended zero-width limit explicitly rather than relying on multiplication by zero to neutralize an undefined intermediate. Version 1.0.5 further uses Pos+fudge in the focus expression, coupling focus location to a quantity otherwise used to scale marching steps. Its step-factor estimate also replaces an earlier reciprocal-minus-one expression with a reciprocal of FocalPlane-1. These changes do not prove a more physically correct lens model. Keep sampling geometry independent from performance controls unless a derivation establishes the required relationship.

Version 1.0.5 omits the preceding file's film-gate and external-camera paths, changes defaults, and selects BufferShader-1.0.2. Its lens-flare controls have no active consumer in that already-inspected postprocess. An importer should preserve the selected dependency version, defaults and supported parameters; a larger version suffix does not mean a superset of all previous features. The repeated old version label in #info is also insufficient as a semantic identifier. The coverage ledger's content hash identifies the actual source inspected here.

**Panorama sampling needs its own differential.** Both files perturb the forward basis supplied to the equirectangular direction function while using the unjittered angular coordinates. That perturbation is multiplied by the longitude/latitude coefficient of the forward direction and is not equivalent to jittering the panorama's longitude and latitude. A panorama renderer should derive sample directions from jittered angular coordinates or another explicitly defined spherical footprint, including seam and pole behavior. For RFF's proposed environment consumer, this strengthens section G/H's direction-to-texture filtering requirements; importing an entire panoramic camera is unnecessary.

The additional feature candidates remain those already recorded: explicit camera/field transforms, coherent filtering and optional artistic depth effects. These reads mainly identify how to preserve their meanings across implementations. No RFF code changed and no camera-transition, focus, panorama, shader-compilation or rendering tests were performed.

### Follow-up to E/G/V: additive volumetric glow is distinct from participating media

A full read of [Volumetric.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Volumetric.frag) resolves a consumer of Kaliset3D. Its active effect is a surface trace followed by an additive path integral of a procedural scalar field and proximity-based light glow. This is useful as an artistic reference, but it does not implement general absorption and scattering through a participating medium.

**Active mechanism:** the surface trace includes a spherical light field centered at -LightPos. For non-light hits, a later loop samples Kaliset along the camera ray from MinDistance up to the hit or MaxDistance. Each sample is multiplied by an exponential distance factor and the sum is multiplied by VolumetricRayStep, making this part a rectangle-rule approximation to a path integral. That step-size factor is an important distinction from the earlier cloud's fixed per-sample opacity. However, there is no accumulated transmittance attenuating the background/surface or successive volume contributions. The final effect adds colored glow based on the minimum light distance found during the surface march. It is not a normalized phase-function scattering model.

For RFF, a lower-cost 2D analogue could combine an existing procedural mask with a light-distance falloff to create a colored haze/glow layer. This would be an explicitly artistic image/height-field effect, separate from bloom and from section G's environment reflection. A true volume preview would require a 3D density domain, extinction units, segment-length-aware transmittance, a scattering/emission model and visibility. Do not call a 2D scalar mask or additive line integral physical fog. Existing RFF noise and material sources should be reused where suitable; another Kaliset evaluation per volume sample would multiply the iteration cost and needs a measured quality benefit.

**Follow values through the active consumers.** The volume loop initializes sh to zero and leaves its shadow call commented out, so it does not evaluate volumetric shadowing. FogColor is used to construct FColor, but FColor does not reach the returned color. Kaliset already applies KFinalScale internally and the volume loop multiplies it again, so a compatible source description must record that repeated scaling. The declared defaults set MinDistance and MaxDistance both to 50, leaving no active integration interval under the strict upper bound. These facts constrain what this file demonstrates; they do not show that all callers or presets render the same appearance.

The origin dither adds the same scalar offset to all three coordinates, rather than jittering only the integration phase along the ray. A new RFF implementation should keep view geometry fixed when its purpose is merely to decorrelate integration bands, and use a deterministic sample-index/tile convention. Handle an empty integration interval and a final partial segment explicitly. Zero glow radius and other domain endpoints also need defined limits. Keep the artistic distance attenuation separate from a density-driven optical depth so users can reason about how step count, reach and intensity affect the result.

The spherical light is a visible field in the primary trace, but shading points toward its center through the light normal; its finite size does not establish sampled area-light illumination. The early light-hit return also bypasses the later primary-depth write. Preserve independent light visibility, illumination, volume contribution and depth-output contracts when reusing the design ideas. The file's ordinary surface fog is another distance-based blend and remains separate from its additive volume loop. No source code or formulas were adopted, and no shader compilation, step-size convergence, image comparison or performance tests were run. This remains an optional lower-priority artistic extension, not a replacement for the environment and filtering priorities.

### Follow-up to H/S/U: the Montecarlo filename does not establish a light-transport sampler

A full read of [Montecarlo-DE-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Montecarlo-DE-Raytracer.frag) resolves another active-path distinction. The color entry point calls monty; its conventional trace call is commented out. The active path is a fixed-budget fuzzy-surface march resembling the SoC experiment, combined with the included 3D wrapper's stochastic camera samples. It does not perform BRDF importance sampling, environment-luminance sampling or random indirect-light bounces. It therefore adds no new evidence for section S's environment importance-sampling proposal.

monty uses a confusion radius, six geometry/color probes, front-to-back partial contributions and a hard-coded light/background. The ordinary trace's shadow, AO, floor and material helpers are not its consumers. CE samples raw backbuffer RGB as material color at world XY coordinates with a large radius-dependent LOD bias, without dividing by accumulated weight. Since 3D.frag stores weighted color sums, this introduces history-dependent feedback whose scale can change with accumulated weight; it is not a normalized environment or material lookup. The file's radius expression uses dot(Target,Eye) rather than a declared focal distance. These are source constraints on reuse, not evidence of a physically defined defocus or transport estimator.

For RFF, keep accumulated image history separate from a texture/mask input. If a feedback material is intentionally offered, give it its own state, normalization, reset and export-time semantics. Do not use a previous display buffer as a stable texture merely because it is already available. Distinguish camera sample count, material field iteration count and ray-march work: increasing one does not correct the meaning of another. A progressive implementation should converge toward a fixed defined integrand when the scene is unchanged; intentional feedback instead evolves a state and needs a different validation criterion.

The random step perturbation is indexed by fragment coordinates and the local march iteration, not subframe; the camera wrapper supplies separate subframe variation. This combination does not prove independent or low-discrepancy sampling, and no statistical comparison is available. Preserve section H's useful footprint-aware normal/material idea, but implement it through RFF's defined coordinates and existing shading pipeline. This reference is another experimental variant, not an additional high-priority shader feature. No implementation was copied, and no compilation, feedback stability, convergence, rendering or performance tests were executed.

### Follow-up to F/AG/AM: distinguish shadow quality from a changed visibility model

A full read of [DE-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Raytracer.frag) confirms active primary tracing, floor selection, normal estimation, AO, directional lighting and one optional reflected trace. Unlike the previously inspected experimental variants, these helpers are connected to color. Initializing floor normal and distance scales inside color also makes their per-invocation setup explicit.

**QualityShadows is not simply more samples of the same estimator.** The optional branch changes the softness scale and constructs three perturbed directions, but two of the loops actually use the same second direction, leaving the third constructed direction unused. A blocking hit in any loop returns full shadow immediately rather than averaging blocked and visible directions. The transverse vectors are not normalized, and the axis fallback checks only positive X alignment. These source facts prevent interpreting the option as a validated three-sample area-light visibility average. A new RFF quality setting should preserve the intended lighting model while varying a declared sample budget; any softness/model change should be a separate parameter. For 2D relief shadows, first define the height-field visibility query and light extent, then compare equivalent scenes at multiple sample counts.

The ordinary shadow term estimates penumbra from a minimum distance-to-travel ratio. It is a distance-field heuristic, distinct from the earlier stochastic sun-cap visibility method. The lighting function attenuates diffuse by the shadow strength but switches specular fully off for any positive shadow value; ambient remains unaffected in this version. Do not copy that discontinuous specular rule into RFF's GGX/clearcoat pipeline. Apply visibility consistently to the contributions of the corresponding light, with any separate ambient/environment occlusion policy explicitly defined.

**Primary auxiliary data should be stored separately from appearance.** depthFlag limits hardware-depth writing to the first trace. However, ShowDepth replaces the returned color within each trace, so the later Reflection mix can blend two inverse-distance debug values even though the hardware depth still describes the primary trace. RFF's proposed depth/normal inspection should bypass material reflection composition or consume a dedicated primary record. This is another reason to avoid encoding data inspection as an incidental material color. Misses and near-zero distance need defined display mappings and invalid-state indicators.

The reference's fSteps counter is incremented by geometry/AO helper calls and is not reset at trace entry, so reflected-trace step-based glow can depend on earlier work in the same invocation. Keep performance counters and artistic fields separate in RFF. Its Dither range also extends beyond one, allowing a negative first-step multiplier for some random values; this parameter cannot be treated as harmless output dithering. The valuable transfer remains explicit quality controls, typed outputs and coherent material evaluation, not wholesale adoption of this renderer. No code was copied, and no shader-compilation, shadow-quality, debug-output or rendering tests were run.

### Follow-up to E/F/AG: capture material inputs before auxiliary probes

Full reads of [DE-Raytracer-v0.9.0.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Raytracer-v0.9.0.frag) and [DE-RaytracerX.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-RaytracerX.frag) give a useful comparison of material evaluation order. Both actively trace and optionally reflect; their relevant differences are contracts, not additional independent feature proposals.

| Source distinction | Consequence for an RFF adaptation |
| --- | --- |
| v0.9.0 computes the normal before reading the orbit-trap color; X reads color before computing the normal. | Preserve the intended primary field values explicitly so derivative probes cannot replace them. |
| X calls baseColor(hit,hitNormal) before filling the current hit normal. | A color callback requiring a normal cannot be made correct merely by moving it ahead of geometry probes. Construct a complete material input record. |
| v0.9.0 writes hardware depth in every trace; X gates it with a primary-trace flag. | Separate primary depth ownership from reflection shading. |
| Both use a square-root distance/travel penumbra expression; the inspected standard DE-Raytracer uses a differently scaled linear ratio. | ShadowSoft values are not portable between these modes without a defined conversion or compatibility policy. |
| Their maximum march distances differ by three orders of magnitude. | Match scene reach before attributing image or performance differences to the shader algorithm. |

The ordering issue suggests a concrete RFF design for section E's shared material evaluator: capture the selected iteration/orbit/field channels at the primary sample, derive the normal using isolated read-only probes, and evaluate material properties from that complete record. When a deliberately footprint-averaged material is desired, accumulate it into a distinct value rather than accidentally reusing the last geometry probe's global state. RFF's 2D field maps can implement this separation without adopting 3D ray marching. Additional buffers or recomputation should be justified by actual consumers and measured cost; the architectural requirement does not mandate a particular storage layout.

Version X clamps each trace's returned color to nonnegative values before reflection mixing. v0.9.0 does not make the same clamp at that point. Both apply a Gamma power to the base material unless linearGamma is defined, but replace floor color after that operation. A compatibility importer must consequently track the selected renderer, defines and material path, not only numeric settings. A new RFF feature should instead use its existing declared color spaces and apply conversions consistently at the relevant boundary. This comparison does not demonstrate a need to replace RFF's GGX, AO or output pipeline.

These sources strengthen the already-proposed typed fields and inspection outputs. No new highest-priority effect emerged. No source was copied or modified, and no callback, depth, color-space, shader-compilation or image comparison tests were run.

### Follow-up to F/H/U: finish the legacy DE wrapper comparison

Full reads of [DE-Raytracer-v0.9.1.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Raytracer-v0.9.1.frag) and [DE-Raytracer-v0.9.10.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Raytracer-v0.9.10.frag) complete the three explicitly versioned DE-Raytracer files in this Include directory. They reinforce the need to identify a renderer by its complete dependencies and callback contract.

Version 0.9.1 contains its own camera and a regular AntiAlias-squared sample loop, writing an averaged RGB result with alpha one. Version 0.9.10 instead includes 3D.frag and participates in its progressive weighted accumulation and lens sampling. Switching between them therefore changes the sampling architecture, not merely the distance-estimator implementation. In 0.9.1 each trace writes hardware depth, so the final depth is not an average or nearest reduction of the color samples. Reflections can write it again. RFF's auxiliary outputs should specify their reduction independently from color antialiasing, especially at object boundaries.

The material callback in 0.9.1 is color(point,normal), whereas 0.9.10 uses baseColor(point,normal). This resolves a concrete consumer for the earlier ColorPalette2 signature: it matches the former declaration. It does not prove that every preset using the helper resolves that dependency correctly. Reflection also changes meaning: 0.9.1 adds reflected RGB times Reflection to the original sample, while 0.9.10 linearly mixes primary and reflected results. Identical numeric values will not preserve brightness. The former tests hit position against the zero vector to decide whether to reflect, which cannot represent a valid hit at the origin; use an explicit hit flag in a newly designed interface.

Both versions bound the primary traversal with a sphere while their field helper can add an infinite floor. A bound valid for the fractal alone is not automatically valid for the combined scene. For a future RFF height preview, either bound all included geometry or handle unbounded components separately. This is an acceleration invariant, not an invitation to alter the fractal's extent for speed. Both shadow loops use integer MaxRaySteps/10 as their budget, so small primary budgets can eliminate shadow sampling entirely. RFF quality profiles should expose or derive an intentional minimum for each active effect rather than silently tying every effect to one integer quotient.

Their light-direction convention also differs from the later standard renderer: diffuse and shadow tests use the negative of the named spot direction. Preserve a canonical direction convention when adapting controls. These reads add no new top-priority effect; they provide concrete compatibility and sampling requirements for the existing proposals. No code was copied or changed, and no compilation, antialiasing/depth comparison or performance tests were run.

### Follow-up to E/F/H/U: occupancy boundaries and temporal depth in NODE-Raytracer

A full read of [NODE-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/NODE-Raytracer.frag) adds a renderer that can use an inside/outside predicate instead of requiring a distance estimate. Its active trace advances by FixedStep, searches for a classified sample before the previously stored depth, and then halves a search displacement SearchSteps times. The formula adapter accepts either inside(p) or a thresholded DE(p), with a side inversion. This is an occupancy search followed by local refinement, not sphere tracing or a conservative distance bound.

**Potential 2D transfer: refine a detected mask boundary.** A RFF mask or contour inspector could refine an already detected transition along a segment using repeated predicate evaluations. Require explicit endpoint classifications and a bracket before refinement; preserve the coordinate precision of the source field. Reducing a bracket can improve boundary placement, but cannot recover a thin component skipped by the initial samples or guarantee the first crossing when multiple transitions occupy one interval. SearchSteps therefore does not provide a complete quality control. Separate detection coverage from refinement accuracy, and compare narrow bands, multiple crossings, tangencies and constant masks. This is an optional extension to the typed-field proposal, not a replacement for RFF's perturbation computation or evidence that escape-time classification is an exact set-membership oracle.

**Depth history is a different reduction from color history.** This renderer stores RGB and a ray parameter in RGBA32F. It retains the previous depth unless a nearer classified sample is found; subframe one resets the candidate depth to MaxDistance. Randomizing the initial fixed-step offset can expose an earlier intersection in later frames, but the retained minimum alone cannot follow a surface moving farther away. RFF would need an explicit reset or validity test on geometry, camera, projection and relevant field-setting changes before adopting any similar history. The primary ray is not normalized in the camera construction, so this alpha value is a parameter along that ray, not automatically world-space distance. Keep its units and projection contract separate from an artistic 2D height value.

**Use coherent geometry data for shading.** Normal reconstructs tangents from neighboring previous-frame depths and camera basis vectors; SSAO also samples that history, while the current pixel may already have a newly refined depth. Its normal differences choose the numerical maximum of two one-sided differences, which is not a general silhouette-safe derivative rule. For RFF, compute normal and occlusion from the same declared field/version, define behavior at invalid or discontinuous samples, and maintain consistent pixel scale across preview, tiles and export. The alternative AO method counts occupied probes around the point and applies an empirical remap; it is not a cosine-weighted hemisphere visibility estimator. Neither mechanism justifies replacing RFF's existing AO without a measured improvement.

**Do not copy the feedback blend as accumulation.** After the initial frames, trace mixes its new shaded color with previous RGB, then multiplies the returned RGB by two. Because the next frame reads that returned value, the source path is not a normalized running average; with the non-SSAO history weight of 0.9, the linear feedback coefficient alone is 1.8 before other effects. Blur and glow also consume previous color. This source observation is a reason to design separate scene-linear history, display gain and depth storage in any RFF transfer, not a demonstrated runtime result or a request to repair GMT. Reset histories deliberately and test constant-color stability before evaluating denoising quality.

The optional volume path averages callback contributions by a sample counter and applies artistic distance/inside fades. It does not implement segment-length-calibrated extinction and transmittance. Its DOF blur weights neighboring colors using their focus values but does not establish a complete occlusion-aware lens model. Keep such effects optional and clearly distinguished from physical volume or lens rendering. The separate DEtrace path draws light-position gizmos; it does not turn the main occupancy traversal into distance-estimator marching.

This read strengthens boundary-detection, auxiliary-output and temporal-history requirements. It does not change the provisional priority of editable environment reflections for RFF material appearance. No source or constants were copied, application code was not changed, and no shader compilation, boundary-convergence, temporal-stability or performance tests were run. The header credits Pablo Roman Andrioli and parts derived from Syntopia; exact licensing must be verified before any implementation reuse.

### Follow-up to G/H/S: DE-kn9 fog sampling, multiscale proximity and reflection contracts

A full read of [DE-kn9.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-kn9.frag) finds an active combination of positional lighting, repeated reflections, colored height fog, optional clouds and stratified volumetric sampling. It includes 3DKn-1.0.4 and Kaliset3Dtex, but its Kaliset surface-mapping statements are commented out. Including that helper does not establish active displacement or texture mapping in this renderer.

**Height fog integrates a density profile along a segment.** The fog helper combines exponentially varying density along HF_Dir with a constant term, integrates optical depth between endpoints, then exponentiates its negative to obtain transmittance. It evaluates both camera-to-surface and surface-to-light paths, so fog affects incident lighting as well as the final view. This is a more meaningful reference for a future height/volume preview than a post-process tint based only on final depth. The factor (1-exp(-A))/A has a finite limit of one at A=0; a new implementation needs a stable near-zero evaluation, not just clamping the argument of exp. Zero-length segments and invalid direction vectors require explicit treatment. For ordinary RFF 2D output, a mapped-height haze can be an artistic option, but that scalar mapping alone does not establish a physical 3D density path.

**Sample where a point light matters.** The active ptLightGlow3 constructs the squared distance from a point on the segment to the light as a quadratic in the segment parameter. Its inverse-CDF calculation uses atan/tan to distribute samples according to inverse squared distance, and the normalization factor compensates that selected density in the contribution. The sample evaluates view transmittance, light transmittance, local density, an anisotropy factor and optional shadowing; HF_FogIter stratifies the unit sampling interval and averages contributions. This illustrates separating the sampling distribution from the remaining integrand. It is distinct from section S's environment-luminance sampling and does not make an entire volume renderer physically calibrated: the phase normalization is intentionally omitted, the colored density conventions differ between extinction and scattering, and endpoint clamping changes the sampling contract.

For a new implementation, reset the stratum index for each integration segment. Here fogstrata advances across reflection segments without a corresponding reset, allowing later samples outside the intended unit interval before clamping. Also provide a defined fallback for zero-length or light-collinear segments, where the discriminant vanishes, and for cancellation near that case. Choosing a distribution based on distance alone can still leave large variance with strongly peaked anisotropy or extinction. Compare estimators and convergence before adopting a more complicated mixture; no speed or quality improvement has been measured here. This feature remains low priority for RFF's main 2D renderer.

**Multiscale AO is a proximity heuristic.** Its AO samples fourteen points along the normal, grows distance by 1.5 each step, computes field distance relative to probe distance and retains the minimum ratio encountered. That minimum propagates nearby obstruction to later scales, and the final result averages clamped obstruction estimates. RFF already has AO: the inspected [vk_slope.frag](../shdsrc/vk_slope.frag) path derives local concavity from eight neighboring relative heights, normalizes it by gradient magnitude and excludes interior/invalid boundaries; an enabled lustre path can replace that result. A potential extension is independently controllable broader-scale cavity shading, not simply adding AO. A 2D height field needs its own neighbor/horizon construction and cannot consume the 3D DE ratio unchanged. The subsequent DE-Kn8 comparison below verifies that the existing Lustre AO already has a configurable radius and a two-scale mixture; broader-scale AO is therefore not a new capability by itself.

**Keep the material and light contracts already established in RFF.** The source's point-light falloff is a power of squared distance, so an exponent of one corresponds to inverse-square falloff. It also ties a Fresnel-like reflectance calculation to the specular exponent; RFF already separates roughness and reflectance through its GGX/material controls and should retain that separation. Multiple reflections add each segment's shaded color using a throughput multiplied by Reflection and fog transmittance. This is a colored artistic reflection chain, not an energy-conserving diffuse/specular transport model. Reflections, visible light spheres, proximity glow, scattering and background emission need separate controls if such a preview is ever added.

The cloud branch uses five noise octaves with a distance-dependent discrete cutoff and increasing march spacing. That is a useful cost-control example, but cutoff transitions are not footprint-continuous filtering, and opacity per sample is not calibrated to the changing step length. The existing noise/filtering proposals remain the appropriate starting point for 2D material clouds. No implementation was copied or modified, and no shader compilation, transmittance, sampling-distribution, image or performance tests were executed. Attribution and licensing for the documented adaptation chain remain prerequisites for implementation reuse.

### Follow-up to D/E/H/U: color-field neighborhoods are not height-map displacement

A full read of [DE-Kn2ColorandHeightmap.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Kn2ColorandHeightmap.frag) resolves the mechanism behind its filename. The wrapper provides palette mapping, orbit-driven image coordinates and repeated color-field probes around a surface hit. Its texture samples feed color, not the distance returned to the primary marcher. No image-height displacement implementation is established by this wrapper; any formula-specific behavior responding to orbitBoolSet would need to be checked in that formula. Do not list this file as proof of ready-made texture displacement for RFF.

**An explicit scalar-to-color pipeline.** Its four-color palette forms a weighted sum of the four orbit-trap components, takes an absolute value, scales and wraps it, adds a cyclic offset, then selects a segment whose width is normalized from four user distances. Each segment can hold its starting color or interpolate to the next color. This illustrates separating field selection, phase mapping and palette interpolation. RFF already has palettes and mapping controls; the useful extension remains section E's selectable field sources, not another fixed four-stop palette. A new implementation must define zero-total segment width, zero-length segments and discontinuities, and preserve existing recipe generation. The palette function's parameter is unused in favor of the global trap, reinforcing the value of explicit immutable field inputs.

**Two independently selected field combinations can drive image UVs.** MapType 2/3 use two separate weighted sums of the four trap channels; those two branches are identical in this file. Other modes use coordinate pairs, angular projection, folded angular sectors, projective lookup, camera direction or screen coordinates. RFF's existing [palette_sampling.glsl](../shdsrc/palette_sampling.glsl) already has multiple image layers with per-layer UV mode, scale, scroll and palette-follow settings. The possible addition is a clearly typed pair of field combinations, where needed, rather than generic image-texture support. Keep screen-locked, fractal-field and surface-direction mappings distinct when saving or animating them.

Angular mapping also needs a valid domain: the asin-based mode consumes a trap component without first normalizing the vector, so it is not automatically a valid spherical direction. The projective mode divides by the supplied fourth coordinate; multiplying every homogeneous component by the same nonzero speed cancels in that division rather than providing ordinary UV scaling. Folded angular sectors introduce seams and derivative discontinuities. A RFF transfer should specify coordinate normalization, zero denominators, seam behavior and footprint filtering, then validate with labeled grids and animation. Mode names alone are insufficient to describe those contracts.

**Shift a color query without moving the visible surface.** After finding a hit and normal, the wrapper evaluates DE again at a point offset along the normal or the original camera direction, then obtains coloring from the resulting field state. This can produce layers of color apparently beneath or above a surface while retaining the original geometry. For RFF, a lower-cost analogue is an offset query into an existing high-precision scalar field or material mask. Define whether the offset is in output pixels, fractal coordinates or relief coordinates; a screen-space offset and a field-space offset will behave differently under zoom. It should not silently modify the numerical fractal result. The wrapper's direction option uses the original camera dir even on reflection traces, so it is not a model for a general current-ray offset contract.

**The neighborhood mix is an artistic recurrence, not surface antialiasing or indirect lighting.** Nested loops evaluate the formula at angularly distributed points around the hit, deliberately without checking intersections, then repeatedly mix absolute RGB values into a running color using a fixed InteriorWeight. Later samples therefore receive different weights from earlier ones. The theta/phi grid is not uniform in solid angle and is not generated through an orthonormal cone basis. It has no visibility, BRDF or sampling-density correction. Preserve it only as an intentionally ordered artistic effect if desired; use normalized weights and a defined domain for an actual filter.

The extra probe count for the sampling block is (SampleStepsLong+1)*(SampleStepsShort+1)*(ThetaSteps-1)*(PhiSteps-1): 72 at the declared defaults, up to 41,209 at the declared maxima, per eligible surface hit before considering reflections. PostWeight defaults to zero, but that value does not gate the source loop. Sample depth also accumulates across the nested loops rather than restarting an independent short-depth sequence for each long step. For RFF, first assess whether a cached field can supply a bounded neighborhood filter; avoid rerunning the complete fractal at each material tap without measured benefit. If the effect is disabled, its expensive evaluation should be skipped under an explicit output-equivalence contract.

These observations strengthen independent field mapping and bounded material sampling as extensions to existing RFF functionality. The source's shared trap state and orbitBoolSet writes require formula-specific inspection before transplanting the mechanism. Existing fog, cloud and reflection mechanisms overlap the preceding DE-kn9 analysis; their compile-time gates differ here. No source was copied, no application code was changed, and no shader compilation, image comparison, sampling-order or performance tests were run. Header credits identify the renderer adaptation chain and Benesi's color-sampling experiment; licensing remains to be verified before reuse.

### Follow-up to E/G/H: DE-Kn8 and the existing RFF multiscale AO

A full read of [DE-Kn8.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Kn8.frag) adds adjustable AO probe count, distance growth and weighting to the previously inspected family. Its loop performs AoStep-1 probes, multiplies each successive weight by 1+0.1*AoWeight and each distance by 1.5+AoPower, while propagating the minimum distance ratio. Those controls change the artistic obstruction profile as well as cost; they are not purely quality settings. AoStep zero or one produces no accumulated weight, so a new interface needs defined disabled/empty behavior instead of exposing raw loop bounds as a quality scale.

**Target recheck: RFF already covers the broad-scale idea.** Reading [lustre_relief.glsl](../shdsrc/lustre_relief.glsl) confirms a dedicated surface_ao_radius scaled by canvas height, plus a second radius at approximately 0.66 of macro_radius. Each stencil returns mean height relative to the center as well as the gradient. The AO mixes 65% of the dedicated-radius mean with 35% of the mid-radius mean, clamps to positive concavity and applies a bounded exponential response controlled by relief depth and AO intensity. Disabled AO omits its dedicated stencil; the middle stencil is shared with macro relief when required. Thus radius-controlled, two-scale cavity shading already exists in RFF. Do not prioritize adding generic multiscale AO on the basis of the simpler vk_slope fallback alone. A future extension would need a demonstrated benefit from independently editable scale weights or a different visibility model, balanced against extra field taps and saved-appearance compatibility.

**Cavity tint and light visibility are different consumers.** DE-Kn8 mixes the material color toward AO.xyz before lighting, so that tint also affects the specular contribution in this renderer. With hard shadows enabled, lighting additionally invokes the same AO helper using the absolute LightPos as its direction argument and subtracts the result from diffuse, with AoCorrect as compensation. That input is neither a normalized surface normal nor a normalized point-to-light direction. This is not a reusable directional visibility estimator. In RFF, retain an explicit distinction between material tint, diffuse cavity darkening, direct-light shadows and specular/environment occlusion. Exposing a color control for cavities could be an artistic extension, but must not be described as more accurate AO.

**The SSS switch is a shadow-softening approximation.** It evaluates shadow a second time with a different initial radius, takes a square root and blends that scalar with the first shadow. It does not estimate thickness, integrate subsurface transport or produce spatial color diffusion. A 2D translation could provide a softer relief-shadow style if a suitable shadow path exists, but should be named for that appearance rather than advertised as physical subsurface scattering. RFF's GGX and clearcoat should not be replaced by this renderer's specular model to obtain that effect.

**An environment editor needs actual directional distinctions.** This version's Horizontal and Vertical background branches both use the same sum of ray X and Y, only written in reverse order, so they do not implement two distinct gradient orientations. The background interpolation factor is also not clamped. Section G's proposal should define a single orientation transform and an explicit gradient domain, with labeled directional test inputs; the source control names alone are not an implementation specification. Its background callback remains separate from incident environment illumination, which supports keeping visible backdrop and reflected-light controls distinct in RFF.

The palette differs from the earlier color-and-height-map experiment: DE-Kn8 square-roots the fourth trap component before palette evaluation and applies OrbitStrength plus a factor of three after selecting the palette. Transferring identical palette settings across the wrappers will therefore not preserve the same appearance. Its cloud controls also replace the prior distance-dependent octave cutoff with a fixed CloudIter count and add density threshold and step-growth controls. Their per-sample opacity still lacks step-length calibration; retain the earlier filtering and integration cautions. These are version-specific contracts, not additional high-priority RFF features.

No application code was changed and no shader compilation, cavity-rendering comparison, shadow/SSS validation or performance tests were run. The source and target reads narrow the incremental proposal rather than claiming that every additional control should be adopted.

### Follow-up to E/H/S/U: DE-Kn2 experimental versus baseline contracts

[DE-Kn2exp.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Kn2exp.frag) was read in full. [DE-Kn2.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Kn2.frag) was then reviewed through the complete non-whitespace diff against that inspected file, covering all changed statements and retaining the shared implementation context. The experimental filename is not evidence of a superset: the baseline has additional hit refinement and AO controls, while the experiment has the four-stop palette already discussed above.

**Separate AO estimation from its artistic influence on light groups.** The baseline returns a normalized proximity estimate and applies separate AO_ambient, AO_camlight and AO_pointlight strengths to three lighting contributions. Its camera light also has a specular response rather than serving only as diffuse fill. This supports an optional RFF control for where cavity shading affects illumination, but does not justify automatically multiplying every light by the same AO term. RFF already distinguishes direct, environment and coating contributions. Preserve direct shadow visibility, avoid unintended duplicate attenuation, and evaluate whether additional controls provide useful appearances beyond current settings. A scalar cavity estimate is not directional light visibility, especially for polished reflections.

**MULTI_SAMPLE_AO selects one direction per call.** The baseline builds an orthonormal frame around the normal, draws azimuth uniformly, and sets squared tangent radius to a uniform variate times coneApertureAO. At aperture one this is the cosine-weighted hemisphere construction; smaller values restrict it to a cone whose maximum sine-squared polar angle equals the parameter. It then takes multiple distances along that single direction, rather than sampling many directions in the same call. Changing subframe changes the seed, so progressive accumulation is intended to integrate directional variation over time. The distance-ratio calculation divides by the direction-normal cosine and FudgeAO, then propagates the minimum and averages clamped deficits. That remains a proximity heuristic, not a binary-visibility Monte Carlo AO estimator. Empty probe counts, zero FudgeAO, zero starting distance and near-tangent directions need defined handling in any reuse.

For RFF 2D, a directional horizon/cavity experiment would require a defined height surface and temporal policy; the existing two-scale Lustre AO is deterministic and should remain the comparison baseline. A single stochastic direction can add flicker to animation unless sampling, accumulation reset and motion handling are designed together. More distance probes cannot substitute for more angular coverage. This option is lower priority than environment authoring and stable material filtering.

**Refinement is not a precision guarantee.** The baseline separates its ray-dependent hit threshold from FudgeFactor and, after a hit trigger, repeatedly advances by the current field step minus 1.5 times the retained threshold, reevaluating the field at each new position. It stores an explicit hit flag. This is neither bracketed bisection nor proof of convergence to the nearest surface, and the threshold is not recomputed inside that refinement loop. RFF should keep termination tolerance, geometric offset and numerical precision distinct; adding refinement iterations must never be described as recovering floating-point precision lost by a different computation. This is primarily relevant to a future 3D relief preview, not to the existing perturbation algorithm.

**Sampling state belongs to each integration operation.** Unlike the earlier variants, the baseline resets fogstrata before the main per-segment fog sample loop. However, when both clouds and volumetrics are enabled, clouds calls the same scattering helper again without a new reset and adds that scattering into cloud RGB, while the main color path has already evaluated fog scattering. A future combined effect needs explicit ownership of the scattering contribution and its sample sequence. Its wind also moves the ray origin and recomputes direction toward the unchanged endpoint, changing the integration segment rather than merely translating a noise field. For animated 2D textures, keep field advection separate from camera/view geometry.

The experimental file additionally defines a two-component random helper whose body names pos rather than its co argument; dependency resolution and compilation cannot be assumed from the helper name or hash toggle. This is a reuse constraint, not a benchmark or a new RFF feature. Existing palette, fog, shadow and color-space observations still apply. No implementation was copied or modified, and no compilation, convergence, directional-sampling or rendering tests were executed.

### Follow-up to F/H/S/U: DE-Kn2cr11 separates controls but changes their meaning

[DE-Kn2cr11.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Kn2cr11.frag) was reviewed through its complete non-whitespace diff against the inspected DE-Kn2 baseline, with a direct reread of the volume-sampling and composition entry points. It changes the camera dependency to 3DKn-1.0.5, moves derived values and the AO seed into the color entry point, adds a depth view and changes shadow and cloud controls. It is not an appearance-compatible replacement for the baseline.

**Shadow width can be independent of visible emitter size.** The soft-shadow branch now derives cone growth from ShadowBlur divided by light distance; the alternative shadow branch uses the reciprocal relationship. This separates the artistic shadow width from the visible light sphere. For a future RFF relief-shadow feature, explicitly decide whether softness follows a physical emitter size or an independent artistic control. Do not interchange numeric values between the two cone conventions. The same version restores FudgeFactor in the hit tolerance and applies it in the shadow field helper, reinforcing that traversal speed, stopping tolerance and appearance are coupled in these reference renderers and must be separated deliberately in a new design.

**Dither must not silently change the integration domain.** The volume sampler multiplies the entire stratified unit-interval coordinate by Dither, including the stratum index, while retaining the original inverse-CDF normalization. At the default 0.5 this restricts the intended inverse-CDF input to half its interval; values above one extend outside it before the later path-parameter clamp. This differs from changing random jitter inside each stratum. For RFF sampling controls, distinguish stochastic jitter, sample count and domain extent. If offering a deterministic zero-jitter mode, place samples at defined positions within all strata rather than collapsing them to one endpoint. Any deliberately changed sampling distribution requires a corresponding weighting contract. This conclusion follows from the source expression, not a runtime convergence test.

**A displayed depth channel needs a separate output path.** ShowDepth replaces each trace's color with one minus scaled reciprocal ray position, but the caller still applies clouds, fog, glow and reflected-path accumulation. The visible-light early return also bypasses this replacement. Thus this is an artistic depth preview within the beauty pipeline, not an isolated primary-depth export. RFF's section F proposal should store the chosen primary field, its validity and units separately, and bypass beauty composition for a diagnostic view. Preserve raw numeric data for export independently from any contrast curve used to display it. This applies directly to 2D iteration, height, normal and mask inspection, without requiring a 3D renderer.

**Composition order belongs to the saved effect definition.** This variant composites clouds before fog, removes the cloud helper's additional scattering call, and carries the previous hit position explicitly between reflection segments. Its cloud offset translates both endpoints, while wind translates the sampling origin with unchanged direction and segment length; lighting still refers to the fixed LightPos. For a RFF procedural layer, define whether a transform moves the field relative to lighting or moves the entire scene. Preserve the established blend order when extending presets rather than treating reordered fog/cloud operations as equivalent. The terrain include and terrain field union remain commented out and provide no active terrain capability in this file.

These changes reinforce independent diagnostic outputs and explicit sampling/coordinate contracts; they do not supersede the environment-reflection priority. No source was copied or modified, and no compilation, depth-export, sampling-distribution or image tests were run.

### Follow-up to D/E/H/V: DE-Kn10 image-driven terrain versus material height

A full read of [DE-Kn10.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Kn10.frag) supplies an actual image-dependent geometry path, unlike the earlier ColorandHeightmap wrapper's color probes. Under USE_HMAP, hTextureIT modifies the terrain coordinates before DEfloor evaluates its field; under USE_TERRAIN, the resulting field is a vertical residual against procedural noise. These are compile-time branches whose combinations matter, not a universally enabled height-map renderer.

**Separate height from domain warping.** hTextureIT samples an image at scaled/offset XY, multiplies RGB by an intensity, takes RGB vector length, and adds the resulting scalar times hscale to all three components of the query point. It therefore shifts X and Y as well as Z. The later procedural terrain sees a warped domain, not merely an image added to surface height. The sample also includes a small positive random XY shift and subtraction before RGB length; its normal probes can consequently evaluate different perturbations. For RFF, use separate, named scalar-height and coordinate-warp operations, with a declared channel or luminance conversion. RGB vector length is not luminance and gives different heights to equally bright colors. Keep imported height data's interpretation separate from the color texture's transfer function.

The direct 2D transfer is a material-height source that feeds the existing relief/normal pipeline while preserving fractal iteration values. If an image-driven height source is missing in the intended RFF layer path, implement it through the typed-field contract rather than reusing palette RGB implicitly. A genuine 3D displacement preview is a different feature: it changes silhouettes and requires geometry traversal, bounds and visibility. This file's residual is not established as a conservative Euclidean distance bound, particularly after nonlinear image warping and nonuniform TerDistorsion. Do not infer safe sphere-tracing steps from a height function alone.

**One geometry definition should serve every consumer.** DEfloor returns the plain plane before image mapping when TerrainMode is zero. For other modes, enabling USE_HMAP without USE_TERRAIN leaves the returned tmix at its constant initial value despite evaluating the image. Conversely, the primary DEF uses DEfloor only under USE_HMAP, whereas the shadow helper DEF2 uses it whenever the floor is enabled. The classic-noise implementation and its dispatch are commented out even though mode five is listed. These source conditions show why a new RFF feature needs a complete supported-mode table and the same field evaluator for primary geometry, normals, shadows and inspection. They are not a reason to modify GMT during this review.

**Match color and height coordinates deliberately.** The floor's image color is sampled from the rotated/translated point using the same initial scale and offset, but it does not reproduce hTextureIT's subsequent XY warp. Color and displaced features need not align. RFF should allow explicit sharing or separation of UV transforms, and filter the height field consistently with its normal derivatives. The source declares repeat wrapping, while its explicit mip/filter directives are commented out; no footprint-aware height filtering is established here. Define both texture minification and the normal probe scale, and verify seams, fine checker patterns, zoom and tiled output.

**Noise controls do not all mean global amplitude or frequency.** The procedural functions apply Freq/Amp to an initial contribution, then begin additional octaves with frequency and amplitude accumulators of one. The mixed modes use separate loop families and additional gain factors; mode four's active implementation contains only 3D noise despite its mixed label. Reuse RFF's established noise where possible and define predictable scale, gain, octave count and normalization for any new field.
