Adding a higher octave count without footprint filtering would increase both cost and aliasing risk.

The equirectangular environment helper and general image-color mapper in this file are commented out, so they add no active support for section G. Shared AO, cloud, fog and reflection mechanisms largely repeat the already reviewed family; the fog-stratum reset present in DE-Kn2 is absent here. File numbering is therefore not a monotonic capability or correctness guarantee. No code or constants were adopted, and no shader compilation, displaced-surface, texture-alignment, filtering or performance tests were performed.

### Follow-up to N/O/U: Shipbulb finite-difference distance and fixed-power specialization

[Shipbulb_DeltaDE.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Shipbulb_DeltaDE.frag) was read in full, including its presets. [Shipbulb_DeltaDE_FastPow2.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/Shipbulb_DeltaDE_FastPow2.frag) was covered through the complete non-whitespace diff against it, including both additional presets. The useful distinction is between numerical differentiation and algebraic specialization, neither of which should replace RFF's precision-preserving perturbation/MPA machinery without a separate mathematical justification.

**Four synchronized trajectories approximate a Jacobian.** The general version initializes the central orbit and three positively offset orbits. Each receives its own position as the additive parameter in non-Julia mode, or the same Julia constant in Julia mode. All four run for the iteration count selected by the central orbit's bailout. Dividing each endpoint difference by delta approximates a column of the iterated map's Jacobian; taking the length of the three column lengths produces its Frobenius norm approximation. This is not the derivative of final radial magnitude and not an exact spectral norm. The final logarithmic escape-distance expression is therefore a heuristic distance estimate, not an established conservative bound for every folded triplex map.

Delta is a power of two scaled by position magnitude, with a fixed minimum corresponding to 2^-18. That balances representable offsets and cancellation only heuristically; it is not tied to the output-pixel footprint or RFF's deep-zoom precision. Fold crossings are nondifferentiable, offset orbits may overflow before the central orbit stops, and the angular power function divides by orbit radius. A RFF diagnostic implementation would need domain handling and comparisons against analytic or higher-precision references. Do not independently terminate perturbed trajectories and then treat their different iteration endpoints as the same Jacobian sample. The four-trajectory method also multiplies orbit work before the renderer's separate normal and AO probes; no performance advantage is demonstrated.

**FastPow2 changes the supported formula.** It substitutes algebraic triplex squaring for the arbitrary-power trigonometric routine and removes the rotation applied after each iteration. Power remains declared and appears as eight or even a noninteger value in some presets, but the active recurrence does not consume it. Rotation initialization remains, but its matrix is unused by that recurrence. Thus it is a fixed-power, unrotated formula variant, not a drop-in faster evaluation of every general-version preset. AlternateVersion is also not used by the active iteration selection. A future RFF specialized formula should have explicit eligibility, preserve formula identity, and avoid showing controls that imply a nonexistent numerical effect.

The algebraic routine still normalizes the XY pair by its length before two complex squarings; the Z axis needs a separately defined limiting value. Algebraic equivalence away from singularities does not establish bitwise equivalence in floating point. Any specialization must retain RFF's accuracy requirement and be checked around the axis, folds, bailout transitions and extreme magnitudes before claims about speed or fidelity.

**A concrete 3D-to-2D reduction exists under restricted conditions.** In the fixed-power recurrence, restricting the third coordinate to zero and keeping the additive parameter's third coordinate zero preserves that plane. Away from the normalization singularity, the in-plane update is the square of the componentwise-absolute complex value followed by the chosen parameter: the Burning Ship-type recurrence. The general version has that reduction only for power two with a rotation that preserves the intended map; identity rotation is the straightforward case. Its time-dependent rotation angle means a preset RotAngle of zero alone does not guarantee identity at all times. A 2D implementation can express the recurrence directly and avoid the triplex normalization, but must state initial-state and Julia conventions. The source initializes the orbit at the position, so iteration/color counts should not be assumed identical to a z=0 implementation.

Orbit coloring uses a separate start index and end index, updating the trap only from the central orbit. The test is i>=SkipColorIterations and i<ColorIterations before increment, so ColorIterations is an endpoint rather than a count after the skip. CutZ combines the estimated distance with a clipping half-space; it is a 3D shape operation, not additional iteration precision. These distinctions belong in any preset conversion or optional formula extension. No formulas or constants were copied into RFF, and no numerical equivalence, shader compilation, image or timing tests were run.

### Follow-up to E/O/AH: sliding-parameter formulas and iteration-budget semantics

Full reads of [Mandelbrot-Cellular-Sliding-C.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/Mandelbrot-Cellular-Sliding-C.frag), [MandelbrotDE-Sliding-C.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/MandelbrotDE-Sliding-C.frag), [Metabrot-Sliding-C.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/Metabrot-Sliding-C.frag) and [OrbitTrap-Sliding-C.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/OrbitTrap-Sliding-C.frag) extend the 2D formula review. These are formula variations, not merely shader coloring modes: they mutate the additive parameter during iteration.

**Separate formula identity from computation budget.** In the DE and ring-trap variants, the non-Julia recurrence first updates the parameter by adding i/(N+i) times the current orbit, then squares the orbit and adds that updated parameter. The cellular variant instead multiplies the parameter by 1+i/(N+i). N is the same setting as the maximum iteration count, so changing the iteration budget changes earlier points of the trajectory, not just how long an otherwise fixed trajectory is observed. For RFF, an optional sliding-parameter formula should either preserve this dependence explicitly as part of its identity or introduce a separate, saved shape-timescale parameter. Do not silently substitute that redesign when importing a preset. Adaptive iteration budgets and comparisons between preview and export must use the same formula definition.

**Derivative propagation must follow every evolving state.** The DE variant retains the ordinary Mandelbrot derivative recurrence despite updating the parameter from the orbit. For the orbit-driven sliding recurrence, let Z and C denote derivatives of the current orbit and current parameter with respect to the pixel. At a fixed iteration index and fixed N, the updated parameter derivative is C_next=C+a_i*Z, and the updated orbit derivative is Z_next=2*z*Z+C_next, using the pre-update z and Z. This requires coupled derivative state, with initialization matching Mandelbrot versus Julia conventions. Reusing the ordinary additive derivative of one does not describe the non-Julia sliding map. Even a corrected derivative does not automatically validate the usual Mandelbrot escape-distance formula for this non-autonomous system. Treat its output as a diagnostic/heuristic until justified; it is not a precision-preserving replacement for RFF's existing distance or perturbation logic.

The Julia branches in the cellular, DE and ring-trap files continue to mutate their local c, but the orbit update adds the fixed Julia constant instead. That mutation therefore does not provide sliding Julia dynamics in those paths. The cellular Slide uniform is declared and saved but is not used in the recurrence. These details should be reflected in any formula selector rather than inferred from filenames or controls.

**Keep reusable trap fields separate from the recurrence.** The cellular variant maintains closest and second-closest squared distances to a point trap, then combines their ratio with an inverse-distance halo. The ring variant records minimum absolute radial difference from a configurable circle, skipping the sample that triggers its loop bailout. These are useful sources for section E's material masks and palette mapping. They are orbit-space distances, not distances to the visible fractal boundary. Define zero-distance/zero-second-distance behavior, the initial sample, iteration window and bailout inclusion explicitly. The ring file also uses different norm thresholds for loop termination and final color selection, so its final branch is not proof of the same escape classification.

**Double declarations do not settle the precision contract.** Metabrot evolves a parameter alongside a composed quadratic map and optionally performs preliminary iterations with the same mutation rule. Its iteration ratios are explicitly computed as float before combination with double state, and its interior-color expression converts z to vec2 for one norm. Global mutable c and dist also assume a particular callback lifetime; a RFF implementation should initialize such state for every independent sample. Use the already-reviewed Progressive2D-4 limitations when assessing full-path precision, and preserve RFF's high-precision computation rather than porting this float/double mixture blindly.

These four files support optional new formula families plus independent trap-field extraction. The Julia locator in the DE/ring examples remains a conventional Mandelbrot inset, not a map of the sliding non-Julia system. No source or constants were copied into RFF, and no recurrence, derivative, deep-zoom, shader-compilation or image tests were run.

### Follow-up to E/F/AH: convergence states, composed quadratics and spherical orbit descriptors

Full reads of [BrokenNewton.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/BrokenNewton.frag), [Newt.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/Newt.frag), [JuliaMand.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/JuliaMand.frag), [ManJul.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/ManJul.frag) and [LagrangianMandelbrot.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/LagrangianMandelbrot.frag) add distinct 2D field and formula ideas. Their active computations must be distinguished from their descriptive names.

**Convergence needs its own result type.** Newt terminates when the squared update length falls below a fixed threshold. Its first mode resembles a rational Newton update with adjustable divisor and offset; the other modes alter the denominator state using the preceding update, componentwise sine or exponential terms. Formula four duplicates formula three but lies outside the declared selector range. Small updates alone do not prove convergence to a designated root. For a RFF convergence-fractal extension, store convergence status, residual, update magnitude, iteration count and optional root identity independently from ordinary escape status. Define singular-denominator and nonfinite states explicitly, and keep the per-sample mutable state local. Reusing escape-time smooth coloring for a convergent orbit does not automatically give valid logarithm domains.

BrokenNewton evaluates a cubic-like product, inverts a real 2x2 derivative matrix, rotates/mixes the resulting update and accumulates a weighted path statistic. Its termination uses that statistic rather than a root residual. Changing fSampleOffset changes both components of two roots through scalar-to-vector addition, while the hard-coded derivative expressions do not incorporate that offset. The closest-root classification computed at the end is overwritten by a tent function of accumulated distance before coloring. Therefore this source is an artistic modified iteration, not evidence of a validated root-basin renderer. The transferable idea is exposing a trajectory statistic as a field; porting its matrix constants is unnecessary. Any new root-solving mode needs derivatives consistent with the chosen function and a residual-based validation strategy.

**Composition order defines the fractal.** JuliaMand initializes z at the pixel and applies a square plus a fixed CC followed by another square plus the pixel parameter. ManJul initializes the orbit at zero and applies those additions in the opposite order: pixel first, fixed C second. Both execute a quartic composition per outer loop; ManJul's cubic description does not match its active code. A formula editor or preset format must preserve initial state, inner-operation order and where traps are observed. Two quadratic operations are not interchangeable just because they have the same total degree.

The two files accumulate angular stripes at different stages: JuliaMand includes the sample that triggers escape, whereas ManJul breaks before adding it. Their previous/current average formulas need defined behavior for zero or one recorded sample. JuliaMand's blend coefficients sum to two, and its log2 smoothing should not be assumed to match the quartic outer iteration. ManJul uses log(4) but compares ordinary radius against Escape squared. A RFF transfer should define a counted-sample record and derive smoothing for the actual recurrence; preserve an imported artistic mode separately if reproducing its original appearance matters. JuliaMand also provides point-trap statistics for its interior/fallback coloring, so those fields can be separated from final RGB under section E.

**A bounded-coordinate orbit descriptor is promising as a coloring source.** LagrangianMandelbrot maps complex values to the unit sphere through stereographic coordinates, sums componentwise absolute differences raised to p, and averages over iterations. In this implementation the compared pair is the current orbit z and the fixed parameter c, not successive orbit points despite the nearby comment. Treat it as an orbit-to-parameter spherical descriptor unless intentionally implementing a different definition. Comparing consecutive iterates would be a separate field with different meaning and saved output. For 0<p<1 the expression is not an ordinary norm, and p=0 needs explicit treatment at zero differences.

The sphere mapping can bound geometric differences mathematically, but its direct squared-magnitude evaluation can overflow before division; the averaging denominator also uses the loop index rather than an explicit number of added samples when a break occurs. For RFF, compute such optional diagnostics without reducing orbit precision, use a numerically stable mapping for large magnitudes, and count successful samples. Export the raw descriptor and remap it through existing palettes or material masks instead of baking in a cosine palette. This is a 2D addition already; a 3D display could reuse the resulting scalar as material data without changing its mathematical meaning.

No algorithm or coefficients were copied into RFF, and no root-convergence, derivative, smoothing, shader-compilation or rendering tests were performed. Named-method and linked-source provenance must be verified before implementation reuse; source comments alone do not establish equivalence to the named method.

### Follow-up to E/AH/AI: attractor density, coupled states and transcendental maps

Full reads of [Cyclic.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/Cyclic.frag), [DiscreteAttractor.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/DiscreteAttractor.frag), [Holomorph.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/Holomorph.frag) and [sinhJulia.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/sinhJulia.frag) add four distinct mechanisms. None is evidence that an ordinary Mandelbrot shader can acquire these shapes through color grading alone.

**Attractor density can be an independent reusable image.** DiscreteAttractor evaluates Clifford or Peter de Jong trajectories, starting from a random value derived from each pixel coordinate. At every step it adds a radial proximity kernel around the current trajectory point, then clamps the sum and applies two palette blends. Its density setting is the kernel radius, not a normalized probability-density scale. The literal smoothstep call has reversed edges, so a new implementation should define the intended decreasing kernel explicitly. No burn-in is discarded, no sample-count normalization is applied, and increasing iterations changes saturation as well as coverage.

For RFF, an optional attractor generator could write a scalar density texture once and reuse it for palette coloring, masks or relief. A shared trajectory with point deposition would avoid repeating an entire trajectory at every pixel, but it is a different estimator from this source's pixel-dependent seeds and cannot be presented as an output-preserving optimization. Specify seed, burn-in, number of trajectories, sample count, kernel footprint and normalization; retain raw density before tone mapping. A GPU deposition path needs deliberate accumulation precision and reproducibility across previews, tiled output and video. This is an additional image-generation mode with possible material reuse, not a substitute for fractal orbit computation.

**Cyclic's Power is a construction parameter, not ordinary complex degree.** Several branches repeatedly square each real component Power-1 times, producing an exponent of 2^(Power-1) on the initial sine/cosine quantity. Another branch repeatedly multiplies by a coordinate instead. The coupled real updates are evaluated from the same prior state and are not generally holomorphic. A RFF formula extension would need a real two-component derivative/Jacobian treatment where derivatives are required, rather than assuming the complex derivative machinery applies. Its maximum squared-radius threshold and polynomial-style smooth coloring are artistic choices, not proof of escape behavior for these trigonometric maps.

**Holomorph carries two complex states.** The ordinary branch updates z from old z and w, and w from old w and a saved old z. The Foam branch instead divides by the newly updated z. Preserve that update order and pole behavior; simultaneous and sequential updates define different maps. Its initialization uses vector sqrt, which the included float math wrapper delegates to componentwise square root, rather than the library's distinct complex-square-root helper. Therefore negative components can make that initialization invalid even when a complex root exists. If replacing this with complex square root in a new formula, treat the changed initialization and branch choice as an intentional definition, not a transparent repair of a saved result.

The optional positive-X and negative-Y folds explicitly destroy holomorphic behavior. A RFF implementation must retain both state variables, track their derivatives or real Jacobians consistently, and establish bailout semantics for the selected polynomial/rational mode. Do not assume current single-orbit MPA support extends to the coupled state without a derivation. Both states' magnitudes or their relationship could be exported as separate coloring fields if the new formula is implemented.

**sinhJulia composes functions before collecting a trap.** Its update is the complex square of sinh(z squared), followed by either a fixed Julia constant or the pixel parameter. It then updates nearest and second-nearest point-trap distances and applies the familiar cellular palette. The trap mechanism is reusable independently, but the finite squared-radius cutoff of 24 is not established as a rigorous escape radius for this transcendental map. Large exponential growth can become nonfinite before the cutoff is tested. RFF should distinguish finite-threshold termination from proven escape, preserve the initial-sample convention and define trap degeneracies. Any generalized perturbation support would need a recurrence and error analysis for the full composition.

These sources favor typed density/orbit fields and clearly identified optional formula modes. No formula or distinctive constants were copied into RFF, and no distribution, derivative, escape-bound, shader-compilation or rendering tests were run. The named attractors and source attribution chains remain provenance leads to verify before implementation reuse.

### Follow-up to E/F/AH: singular maps and fixed-budget trajectory coloring

Full reads of [Essential_Singularities.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/Essential_Singularities.frag), [Misc.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/Misc.frag) and [lcosz-esinz-lexpz-lyapun.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/lcosz-esinz-lexpz-lyapun.frag) add source-level constraints for optional transcendental formulas. The useful RFF transfer is a clearly defined formula/result interface plus independent trajectory statistics, not wholesale adoption of their escape coloring.

Essential_Singularities evaluates z squared times exp(A/z), followed by the Julia or pixel parameter. It mirrors the pixel's imaginary coordinate before initialization and optionally folds individual orbit components. For A=0 the mathematical expression away from zero reduces to the quadratic map, but evaluating A/z at z=0 still needs a defined removable-singularity branch. For nonzero A there is no single finite extension at that essential singularity. Preserve this distinction: an arbitrary epsilon denominator changes the map, while treating a mathematically removable case explicitly need not. Record invalid/nonfinite evaluations separately from escaped and iteration-limited samples, and derive any generalized perturbation support for the actual map. The existing finite bailout and polynomial-style smooth-color expression do not establish a rigorously bounded exterior for every parameter.

Misc's inversion maps a coordinate to itself divided by squared magnitude plus an offset, applied to the negated pixel. This is circle inversion with the same imaginary sign, not complex reciprocal with conjugated imaginary part. If RFF adds a reusable input transform, save the exact convention and define its pole. Its first three formulas combine exponential, reciprocal and trigonometric steps; their two-component control is reduced to abs(XY.x)+XY.y. The fourth uses the two controls separately in a sequential real recurrence, where later expressions consume already updated state. Treat these as different formula definitions, with explicit parameter relevance, rather than interchangeable presets under a generic complex power.

The lcosz/esinz/lexpz file reuses related operations but changes their parameter reductions and applies the Julia offset before each selected map. Its ordinary escape breaks are commented out. For those branches the normal output is therefore a fixed-budget mixture of accumulated angular stripes and average orbit magnitude, not escape-time coloring; Escape does not terminate their loops. Such trajectory fields could drive a RFF palette or material mask if kept separate from classification. Explicitly choose whether a sum or a sample-normalized mean is intended, since a sum changes color phase when the iteration budget changes even on a stable orbit.

The branch labeled Lyapunov rotates an eight-bit pattern to choose how the two evolving coordinates are assigned, updates those coordinates, and accumulates a logarithmic term. However, its accumulator a is not initialized on that branch, it mutates the outer loop counter in a nested loop, and the logarithmic value also becomes one of the next state coordinates. This is not evidence of a validated Lyapunov-exponent implementation. If RFF adds a stability field, define a separate dynamical state, tangent/derivative update, burn-in, valid sample count and logarithm convention, then validate against a map with known behavior. A periodic selector is a reusable scheduling idea; the source's label alone does not justify importing its numeric output as stability.

These are already 2D examples. Their scalar trajectory statistics can also feed the existing relief materials without making the underlying formula 3D, but singularities and nonfinite values must be masked before normal estimation or palette lookup. No implementation was copied or modified, and no singular-limit, stability-exponent, shader-compilation or image tests were performed. Source-linked mathematical claims and provenance remain to be checked before adopting a named method.

### Follow-up to AH: explicit cubic and rational formula identities

Full reads of [BurtsBisector2D.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/BurtsBisector2D.frag) and [Magnet.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/3DickUlus/Magnet.frag), including all presets, reinforce a practical requirement for RFF formula additions: describe the active recurrence and initial condition explicitly instead of inheriting a title or comment.

In BurtsBisector2D, with w denoting the current complex orbit, the non-Julia update is w-w^3-w^2-O. Its Julia branch is w-w^3-C*w-O. Both start at the pixel. The header's positive quadratic term does not match the active non-Julia subtraction. The Julia switch changes polynomial coefficients here, rather than selecting the conventional Mandelbrot-versus-Julia parameter role. A RFF cubic-family option could expose coefficients deliberately, but must preserve the imported variant's signs and initial state. Its exterior stripes exclude the escaping sample and need zero/one-sample handling; its interior color combines a stripe sum with mean radius, so changing iteration count changes phase independently of convergence.

The following complex expressions are algebraic readings of Magnet's component code. Let c be the transformed pixel, X=XY.x+i*XY.y and w the current orbit. Any optional input inversion is performed before these definitions.

| Mode | Initial orbit | Active update |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | w=c | ((w^2+XY.x+3)/(2*w+XY.y+2))^2 |
| 1 | w=0 | ((w^2+c+X)/(2*w+c-1))^2 |
| 2 | w=c | ((w^3+9*w+6)/(3*w^2+6*w+7)+X)^2 |
| 3 | w=c | ((w^3+3*c*w+c*(c-1))/(3*w^2+3*(c-1)*w+c^2-c+1)-X)^2 |

This table makes otherwise subtle differences reviewable: mode zero uses the two XY components as separate real offsets, modes two and three place a complex offset after division, and mode one has a different initial orbit. A common quotient/square building block is possible, but changing offset placement or initial state changes the map. These expressions have not been numerically checked against the shader.

All four Magnet branches terminate only when the running maximum squared magnitude exceeds 10000 or the iteration budget ends. They do not test attraction to a finite fixed point, distinguish poles or validate finite arithmetic. Thus black output is iteration-limited classification, not proof of a converged basin. For a RFF rational-map mode, retain denominator validity and optional convergence residual as separate outputs; a diagnostic view of proximity to a pole could be useful if explicitly labeled, but it is not a geometric distance estimate. Use stable complex division without silently replacing poles with arbitrary clamped denominators, and derive any derivative/perturbation support for the exact quotient composition.

These files contribute optional 2D formula families rather than a new high-priority lighting effect. Their fields can later drive relief/material mapping, subject to the precision and validity contracts already described. No code was copied or changed, and no algebraic-equivalence, pole, convergence, shader-compilation or rendering tests were run.

### Follow-up to AH: folded planar reductions, sample ownership, and formula-version identity

Full reads of reference `3DickUlus/BuffaloBulb.frag`, `LionBulb.frag`, and `HiddenBrotCos.frag`, including all presets, add the following RFF adoption constraints. The public BuffaloBulb copy was verified byte-identical; the public LionBulb copy was reviewed through its complete non-whitespace diff against the fully read reference. These are source/algebra observations, not rendered or numerical validation.

**BuffaloBulb provides a concrete conditional 3D-to-2D reduction.** Its iteration is a fixed quadratic triplex expression; the declared `Power` does not select an exponent. With third coordinate and parameter component zero, and rotation preserving that plane, its non-singular XY expression reduces to `(x*x-y*y, 2*x*y)`, followed by independently enabled component absolute values and parameter addition. Initial pre-absolute controls execute once before the loop, whereas output absolute controls execute every iteration. Initial state is the sample position in both parameter and Julia modes. Preserve these distinctions in a proposed RFF folded-map recipe; do not silently replace initial state with zero or move folds across addition. At `x*x+y*y==0`, the actual 3D expression divides by zero, including the planar origin: the algebraically reduced polynomial would be an explicitly defined extension at that point, not byte-for-byte source behavior. Arbitrary rotations or nonzero third parameter components invalidate this planar reduction.

The alternative distance estimate evaluates seven independent orbits: centre and positive/negative offsets on three axes. Each component uses the **minimum absolute one-sided radial change**, divided by delta; it is neither a signed central difference nor the norm of a full orbit Jacobian. Delta is `max(length(p)*1e-6, DEScale*0.1)`, each orbit chooses its own escape count, and all seven update the same global orbit trap. Consequently, enabling numerical distance estimation can alter color statistics as well as geometry. For RFF, keep centre-orbit color data separate from derivative/normal probes, explicitly specify escape alignment, and test folds and zero denominators before treating such a result as a distance or relief-height field. The analytic branch's scalar derivative multiplies by `2*r` without the parameter derivative term; it is not a ready-made parameter-plane derivative recurrence. This is an adoption requirement, not a proposal to repair GMT.

**LionBulb demonstrates why a formula name and a shared filename are insufficient identities.** Its reference lower-case `mul3` returns early using `sqrt(length(a)*length(b))` and asymmetric normalized-vector terms; the later trigonometric return is unreachable. The public copy instead delegates to upper-case `Mul3`, which multiplies radii and adds spherical angles. This is a semantic change for the Lambda and Ikenaga menu branches, despite the public comment's “same result” wording. Record source variant/hash with any imported recipe. The two implementations must not share a supposedly compatible saved formula identity without an explicit migration policy.

For the public spherical multiplication, nonzero operands confined to the XY plane reduce to ordinary complex multiplication. With plane-preserving transforms and folds disabled, its Lambda branch therefore gives `c*w^P-c*w^(P+Q)` (before the common Scale and rotation); the reference lower-case helper does not establish that identity. The Ikenaga menu branch actually evaluates `(w^P+c-1)*(w-c)` under that public planar reduction, rather than the cubic printed in its comment. Fractional/negative powers need declared angle-branch and zero-domain behavior. Its common scalar derivative update depends only on P, radius and bias, even for nested-power, multiplication, scaling and folded branches; branch labels do not validate this as a Jacobian or distance bound. The fourth trap component is `r*dr`, not radius squared. RFF should expose typed orbit statistics and separately validated derivatives, and must not assume existing Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA support for these maps.

**HiddenBrotCos is a directly useful real-map extension, not complex cosine.** After optional input component folds, it computes `t=Two*x*y`, then `(x*x-y*y+cx, t*(One+cos(t))+cy)`, followed by optional upper-side reflections about RX/RY. The caller always passes the enabled reflection boolean as the direction, so the helper's lower-side branch is not selected. Input pixel Y is flipped, and initial state is that transformed pixel even in parameter mode. Its bailout compares squared magnitude with Bailout. Presets named Mandelbot or Tricorn describe variants; their nonconstant cosine term does not establish exact equivalence to those familiar maps.

Away from folds, the state Jacobian is `[2*x, -2*y; Two*y*h, Two*x*h]`, where `h=One+cos(t)-t*sin(t)`. This supplies a specific starting point for a separately validated real two-component derivative implementation; folds/reflections require their own local signs and boundary treatment. The source's nested-log escape coloring is an artistic continuation of a polynomial-style expression, not a proved smooth escape potential for this map, and the allowed small bailouts can enter invalid log/square-root domains. A RFF extension should retain escape validity/count separately from palette mapping and define finite fallback behavior without relabeling invalid samples as interior. This requires formula work, not just a post-processing shader, and does not displace environment reflection/filtering as the near-term appearance priority.

The source headers give Mandelbulber/3Dickulus/youhn, cbuchner1, forum authors, and a Quilez coloring lead. These are provenance leads rather than independently verified reuse licenses. No formula implementation was copied into RFF, no external license claim was verified, and no shader compilation, numerical comparison, rendering, or timing test was run in this batch.

### Follow-up to AH: history-dependent folds and independently mapped orbit statistics

Full reads of `3DickUlus/PetraBox.frag`, `BioMorph.frag`, and `terrain_test/test.frag`, including presets, provide additional RFF formula/statistic candidates. The local README says these fragments are modifications of existing examples rather than original-from-scratch implementations; its sharing statement does not independently establish licenses for inherited code. The two-line `.gitattributes` only assigns GLSL language classification to fragment files.

**PetraBox: preserve previous-state feedback as actual state.** The sample begins with `z=(position,1)` and a separate previous vector initialized from JuliaC or `(0,0,0,1)`. Each iteration saves the incoming z, applies the component box fold, multiplies all four components by `scale/clamp(dot(z.xyz,z.xyz),sphereFold,1)`, adds either the previous vector or half of `(previous+initialSample)`, stores the saved incoming vector as previous, records a trap, and rotates XYZ. Thus previous-state feedback refers to the pre-fold, pre-current-rotation input, while the next iteration receives the rotated result. A 2D variant can retain XY plus its previous XY and the auxiliary scalar, provided the third components remain zero and rotation preserves the plane. It cannot be reduced to a one-state complex power without changing the formula.

The reported scalar is the absolute ratio of an accumulated radial-change statistic to the final fourth component: the numerator sums `abs(length(current.xyz)-length(previous.xyz))/iterationIndex` after rotation. It is not an ordinary escape count, normalized average, or demonstrated signed distance. There is no escape test; the iteration budget defines the field. The fourth trap channel records the absolute auxiliary component, not radius. `Power`, `DerivativeBias`, `AlternateVersion`, and `Petra` are declared but do not affect the shown recurrence; preset Bailout entries have no local recurrence use. For RFF, a history-dependent fold could be offered as a distinct procedural field or formula with explicit statistic mapping, with no claim that these controls or ordinary Mandelbrot acceleration apply. Define the valid fold-radius domain, zero-divisor behavior, and the role of the iteration budget before making stable recipes. Negative boxFold reverses clamp limits, sphereFold above one reverses its limits, and allowed zero denominators are additional reasons not to import UI ranges as mathematical guarantees.

**BioMorph: axis-distance channels and independent interior/exterior mapping.** The sample records componentwise minima of absolute orbit coordinates after each main update and before testing squared-radius escape. Its stalk mapper combines the maximum, minimum, and length of that two-component minimum, with different color weights and nested square roots. Those minima may come from different iterations; they are not a single closest orbit point. RFF could expose these as typed scalar channels with separate interior/exterior mapping policies, feeding palettes or material masks rather than baking RGB during iteration. This adds artistic control beyond the existing final escape field, but needs orbit-statistic generation: it cannot be recovered exactly from an existing iteration-count image, and preservation across MPA skips requires separate work.

PreIter is a formula prelude, not merely a coloring warm-up: it always applies `z^Power+c`, even when the subsequent selected map uses complex sine, complex cosine, or a nested-power MetaBrot expression. It does not collect traps or check bailout. Main-loop i already starts at PreIter, yet stalk intensity uses `i+PreIter`; preserve this if reproducing the source, or explicitly version a different count convention. When PreIter reaches or exceeds Iterations, no main samples update the sentinel minima. A new RFF implementation should distinguish empty statistics, exhausted budget, escaped samples and invalid arithmetic rather than display a sentinel-derived color as valid interior detail. The default non-Julia state is zero; the Julia state is the mapped pixel. Optional domain mapping evaluates `-pixel/dot(pixel,pixel)+InvertC`, a circle inversion with a sign and translation, not an ordinary complex reciprocal.

Its smooth-color expressions have formula-dependent logarithms but no demonstrated smooth-potential derivation for the transcendental branches; Power=1 also makes several denominators zero. Keep a validated escape/statistic layer separate from an artistic color remap, with finite-domain handling. Preset names are not formula identifiers: the preset named MetaBrot2 selects Formula=1, while MetaBrot3 selects Formula=4. Stable RFF recipes should serialize the actual formula and prelude parameters rather than infer them from a label.

**Terrain example: a 4D slice is different from deleting two coordinates.** `terrain_test/test.frag` couples XYZ and W through six ordered conditional coordinate swaps/negations, offsets, sphere clipping, affine scaling, an optional W trigonometric transform, and independent log expressions equivalent in real arithmetic to scaled asinh. W participates in subsequent folds even though the final norm excludes it. Therefore a two-coordinate image can sample a slice of the full state, but dropping Z/W does not generally preserve this map. This offers a possible structured procedural-mask source for RFF, not a ready-made replacement for Mandelbrot calculation or its acceleration.

The loop always runs MI steps; its commented bailout description has no matching early exit. Output is final XYZ norm times `scaleM^-MI`; the separately accumulated Dd is unused in the active return. Optional nonlinear transforms and their scale factors are not accounted for by this sole scale correction, so do not advertise the output as a validated distance bound. Scale zero enters divisions; the literal log-plus-square-root implementation can suffer cancellation for large negative values and overflow on squaring. A precision-preserving implementation should validate stable evaluation of the intended function instead of reducing arithmetic precision. The source defines USE_TERRAIN and saves terrain controls, but the previously reviewed DE-Kn2cr11 include has terrain code commented out; declarations/preset values alone do not prove an active terrain effect. Shader preprocessing and rendered evidence would be required to establish that behavior.

These reads refine formula and typed-mask proposals; they do not establish higher visual benefit than the current environment-reflection priority. ### Follow-up to AH: Lambda coefficient placement and product-map variants

Full reads of `3DickUlus/Pengbulb.frag` (including all six presets) and `Magnetic-Curiosity.frag` (including all eight presets) further constrain possible RFF formula extensions. This batch is source and symbolic analysis only.

**Pengbulb: separate coefficient semantics from the shared Lambda label.** Subject to an XY-invariant plane, disabled absolute folds, and well-defined angular operations, its intended planar Lambda expression is `c*w^P - Scale*c*w^(P+Q)`. Scale affects only the second term. Its other branch is `w^P + Scale*c`. This differs from LionBulb's common multiplication of the entire updated state by Scale. The parameter-plane initial state is m1, whereas the Julia initial state is the pre-rotated sample and its parameter is JuliaC. Rotation follows trap collection. Preserve coefficient placement, initialization, and the distinction between coordinate rotation and per-step rotation in any RFF recipe; the same P/Q/Scale tuple is not portable between these files without conversion.

The source angle uses `acos(x/sqrt(x*x+y*y))*sign(y)`. On the negative X axis with y exactly zero it yields zero instead of an angle of pi, and on the Z axis it divides by zero. Thus a blanket claim that its planar powers/multiplication equal complex arithmetic is false at those inputs. An explicitly defined 2D complex implementation would be a new variant with declared branch behavior, not an exact source port. Presets with tiny nonzero initial states are part of the supplied settings, not evidence that an arbitrary epsilon is safe for RFF deep zooms. Fractional and negative exponents also require a domain and branch policy.

For a proposed unfolded, unrotated 2D Lambda variant, write `F(w,c)=c*(w^P-s*w^(P+Q))`. On a chosen differentiable branch, `F_w=c*(P*w^(P-1)-s*(P+Q)*w^(P+Q-1))` and `F_c=w^P-s*w^(P+Q)`. The parameter derivative therefore evolves as `D_next=F_w*D+F_c`, with initial derivative determined by the chosen initial-state mapping; the Julia state derivative has no varying-c term. These expressions are a derivation to validate, not an implementation or proof of MPA compatibility. The existing 3D scalar update uses only P and radius; Lambda evaluates that radius after the update while the other branch uses the previous radius. It does not establish these derivatives or a valid distance bound for both branches. Its fourth color statistic `r*dr` additionally ties color to the derivative heuristic. Keep orbit-derived color channels independent of any replaceable distance estimator.

**Magnetic-Curiosity is a product-map family, not the rational Magnet formula printed in the header.** The source explicitly changes division to multiplication, and triDiv is unused by the active recurrence. With planar non-singular multiplication, the first branch forms `(w*w+c-m1)*(2*w+c-m2)` and then applies triPow(Power). The second multiplies two factors: a cubic-like numerator and a second factor containing `triPow(2,3*w)`. Even if the radius epsilon is removed to obtain a clean algebraic model, that latter term is `9*w*w`, not the `3*w*w` in the header. For that explicitly altered, epsilon-free planar model, the factors are `A=w^3+3*(c-m1)*w+(c-m1)*(c-m2)` and `B=9*w^2+3*(c-m2)*w+(c-m1)*(c-m2)+1`, followed by `(A*B)^Power`. Do not describe this as a compatible rational Magnet implementation or use its name to select a saved RFF formula.

The actual triPow first adds `1e-10` to radius, even for nonzero arguments, including inner powers and the final power. Consequently the polynomial expressions above are a useful independently defined candidate, not exact algebraic equivalence to the source. triMul still divides by the product of XY radii, so the radial epsilon in triPow does not make every operation finite. Parameter mode starts at `(1e-14,1e-14,1e-14)`, which is not precisely on the XY plane; an exact 2D reduction also changes this initial state. Its first bailout condition uses squared radius, subsequent conditions use radius, and its derivative heuristic ignores the product and inner powers. A RFF candidate should define consistent bailout units, genuine initial-state semantics and branch-specific derivatives before exposing a relief-height or distance channel.

For RFF, the practical opportunity is a small set of clearly identified polynomial/Lambda variants and associated orbit masks, with exact coefficients and reproducible initial states. It is not a reason to carry over all 3D DE machinery or offer duplicate named formulas whose behavior differs invisibly. Validate sample sequences, axes, zero/negative powers, transforms and saved-recipe round trips, then assess reference-orbit and MPA support independently without sacrificing precision. This remains a longer-term formula extension, below editable environment reflection/filtering for near-term shader appearance work. Source headers name Peng Kuan, Edgars Malinovskis, 3Dickulus and external triplex-math discussions; original-source licensing remains to be verified before adapting recognizable code. No app code, numerical test, shader compilation, render comparison or timing measurement was produced by this batch.

### Follow-up to G and AH: environment orientation and shaped procedural relief

Complete reads of `3DickUlus/Burningbulb.frag` and `AndyPolygon-Landscape.frag`, including all presets, add two practical appearance details and conditional formula transfers. These are source-derived proposals; no compilation, render or timing test was run.

**Environment orientation should be explicit and reproducible.** Burningbulb supplies a cube-map background callback that rotates a direction, adds bgOffset, multiplies components by bgScale, and directly samples the cube map. Sign changes can correct handedness/orientation, whereas a nonzero offset or unequal component scales distort directions rather than merely rotate the environment. The active callback has no roughness argument or explicit roughness-dependent filtering; its computed distance t is unused, and the randomized focus/fog version is commented out. A saved bgFocus value therefore does not prove active filtering. For RFF's proposed environment source, keep orientation/handedness controls separate from optional artistic distortion, apply a consistent transform to background and material reflection, and retain independent base/coat roughness filtering. Do not mistake an offset cube lookup for roughness filtering or a physically translated light probe.

The source includes CJR_IQPath.frag and keyframes.frag. A repository file search found neither basename in the current checkout, so this review does not establish how its background callback feeds lighting/reflections or whether the standalone example compiles. The callback itself is evidence of cube-map direction control; its presets are not evidence of a working complete pipeline. No missing asset was fetched or substituted. This does not block adopting an independently implemented environment control in RFF's already inspected material path.

**Burningbulb's two spherical powers do not share the same planar reduction.** Both apply selected component absolute values before power, add the Julia or sample parameter, rotate the result, and then collect coordinate minima plus radius squared. The initial state is the sample in either mode. For the latitude-based AlternateVersion, zero third coordinate remains zero under the power step, so with planar parameters and plane-preserving rotation its non-singular XY map can provide folded complex-power variants. The default colatitude version instead gives third component `r^P*cos(P*pi/2)` on the XY plane: at P=2 this is `-r*r`, so simply deleting the third coordinate does not reproduce that map. At nonzero radii, odd integer P can preserve the plane mathematically, but the XY factor `sin(P*pi/2)` also matters. At zero radius both source routines have a division requiring a separately specified extension. RFF should identify the spherical convention when offering a 2D slice or derived formula, and avoid treating the derivative-bias scalar heuristic as a validated folded-map derivative. Post-rotation trap coordinates should not silently become pre-rotation coordinates.

**Landscape's useful transfer is shaped, normalized scalar noise.** Its FBM sums simplex octaves with amplitude starting at 0.5 and multiplied by roughness, then divides by the sum of amplitudes. The four modes use signed noise remapped after accumulation, absolute noise, one minus absolute noise, or the square of that ridge expression. The last mode is a quadratic shaping operation despite the menu's “exponential height” wording. Modes above zero also halve the starting coordinate frequency. Octaves is a float control truncated to an integer, so changing it can introduce discrete detail changes. Optional distortion adds the same scalar FBM value to both coordinates, producing a correlated diagonal warp; a two-channel vector warp would be an explicitly different proposed effect.

The steps operation subdivides height into bands and uses a piecewise quadratic ease-in/out inside each band; it does not simply quantize height to flat levels. RFF could add ridge/valley shaping and eased terrace profiles to its existing procedural-mask/relief facilities, rather than add another generic FBM feature. Keep the chosen transform, effective frequency, octave convention and seed behavior in stable recipes. Mask strength should be independent of overall height scale. For display and animation, test ridge cusps, terrace boundaries and domain-warp magnification at multiple resolutions; fading unsupported octaves requires a declared amplitude/mean policy because renormalizing only surviving octaves can shift mask values. This extends the prior footprint-filtering proposal, not a claim of measured anti-aliasing quality.

Do not transplant the landscape's DE return as RFF relief height. With H equal to volume_size.z*hscale and h the shaped height, its return is `u*u-u`, where `u=z/(H*h)`. For nonzero h this has zero surfaces at z=0 and z=H*h, and is negative between them; it is neither the height h itself nor a proved distance. Without terracing, h already contains H, so the upper surface scales as H squared times the normalized noise. Volume clipping is commented out and a zero h is singular. The reusable RFF channel is the deliberately defined normalized noise or shaped height before this geometric wrapper. The embedded simplex implementation carries an Ashima/McEwan/stegu MIT attribution, while the landscape names AndyPolygon and 3Dickulus; verify the original source/license chain and update NOTICE before copying distinctive code. No new code or third-party material was incorporated into RFF in this batch.

### Follow-up to AH: composing scalar fields without conflating their statistics

A full read of `3DickUlus/MMM.frag`, including its eleven presets, distinguishes a useful composition idea from formula iteration. The active DE evaluates enabled Mandelbulb, Menger-sphere and Mandelbox branches independently at `abs(position)` and adds their scalar results. It does not alternate their maps along a shared orbit. The combination is an implicit sum field, not a min-based union, max-based intersection or demonstrated distance to either constituent. If all iteration counts are zero, the return is zero everywhere. For RFF, the transferable idea is explicit composition of separately defined relief/mask channels; do not label this as hybrid-orbit acceleration or infer that MPA applies to the sum.

**Define the composition contract before exposing controls.** Each source channel should retain a type, valid-sample mask, coordinate transform, range mapping and weight. For a proposed 2D relief `h=sum(weight_j*remap(field_j))`, derive or sample the final height gradient after the remaps; averaging already shaded RGB or unit normals is not equivalent. A sum of gradients follows only for differentiable, consistently scaled height fields with fixed weights. User-selected masks and coordinate warps add their own derivatives. The source's initial absolute-position transform imposes mirror symmetry on all branches; it should be an explicit optional domain transform in an independently designed RFF field compositor. This is an extension to the existing typed-mask proposal, not a claim that MMM supplies a complete material-layer system.

**Shared trap storage hides different channel definitions.** MMM resets one orbitTrap to 10000 at each DE entry, then all enabled branches minimize into it. The bulb writes radius squared in W; Menger writes radius to the fourth power; Mandelbox writes the fourth power of the radius sampled after box folding but before its sphere fold/affine update, while its XYZ channels use the updated state. The Mandelbox escape test uses that earlier radius and breaks before recording the escaping sample; the bulb records its newly escaping sample. Thus the shared minimum can combine different units, states and escape inclusion policies. In RFF, keep branch-local statistics and choose/normalize channels explicitly before blending. A shape control should not silently alter an unrelated material channel by introducing a smaller value with a different meaning. A finite sentinel also caps minima when all visited values exceed it, so an explicit no-sample flag is preferable in a new statistic representation.

**Menger-sphere is a warped field, not a verified spherical distance transformation.** Its input is multiplied by `length(p)/max(abs(p))`; the denominator is zero at the origin. The accompanying distance correction includes an empirical factor 1.6, explicitly described in the source as trial-and-error. It then sorts absolute coordinates, folds Z about one third of an offset, applies scale/translation and rotation, and uses a spherical bounding expression at the end. The cubic bounding alternative is disabled. Zero scale can also make its distance divisor zero. A 2D image can sample a fixed slice of this full map, but simply dropping Z changes the sorting/folding dynamics. An independent planar sorted-fold procedural mask is another possible effect and needs its own identity. Neither interpretation supplies a ready-made Mandelbrot perturbation recurrence.

**Transformation and parameter lifecycle must remain explicit.** Menger multiplies its vector as `msrot*p`; bulb and Mandelbox use vector-on-left rotation expressions. Reusing the same numeric angles under one matrix convention can therefore reverse the intended rotation. Mandelbox's mbscale and final correction constants are uniform-dependent global initializers, unlike the three matrices computed in init. A port must recompute all derived values after parameter changes rather than cache only the explicit init assignments. Its zero min-radius control causes a divisor singularity, and the final correction depends on configured iteration count even when the loop exits early. These observations specify compatibility/validation cases for RFF rather than recommending unrelated GMT repairs.

For a first RFF experiment, reuse existing well-defined scalar channels where available and add explicit normalized composition for artistic relief or material masks. Computing additional fractal branches would carry separate cost and precision/acceleration requirements; it should not be assumed to be a cheap shading-only feature. Test each branch alone, mixed signed ranges, disabled/empty channels, mirrored boundaries and independent parameter changes, then compare final normals and highlights at several resolutions. No such experiment was executed in this batch. The source names knighty, Buddhi, Rrrola/Jan Kadlec, Enforcer and external Mandelbulb discussions; these are provenance leads requiring original-source/license verification before distinctive code is adapted. Application code remains unchanged and the near-term environment-reflection priority is unchanged.

### Follow-up to AH: maximum composition and color-only orbit transforms

A complete read of `3DickUlus/3Dickulus.frag`, including all presets and embedded animation settings, provides a distinct companion to MMM. Its active composition is `max(0, enabledBulb, enabledMenger, enabledMandelbox)`; the additive composition is commented out. The initial zero clips negative branch results, so this is not the full signed maximum field. Even if each branch had a valid signed-distance interpretation, zero-clipping would erase interior sign and create a flat interior region. The actual empirical component estimates do not establish exact distance behavior in the first place.

**RFF transfer: explicit height/mask operators and material ownership.** In a proposed 2D scalar compositor, addition, minimum, maximum and an optional baseline clamp should be separate named operations with declared range semantics. For height fields, maximum can select the upper of two surfaces; its gradient comes from the selected branch away from equal-value boundaries, with a crease or undefined unique derivative at ties. A smooth transition would be a separately specified blend that changes the resulting field. Keep an explicit winning-source identifier if materials follow the selected surface; alternatively let the user select an independent material source. Do not infer material ownership from the final scalar or from whichever branch happened to execute last. This is a concrete refinement of the previous scalar-composition proposal, not evidence that the existing RFF already lacks every possible blend operator.

The source illustrates why that separation matters: bulb resets orbitTrap on entry; Menger resets it again, discarding the bulb trap when enabled; Mandelbox then minimizes into the surviving trap without resetting locally. The maximum-distance winner does not control any of these color updates. With Mandelbox alone, reset responsibility is outside that local function. Therefore this example's combined color is neither winner-based coloring nor a consistent minimum over all enabled branch histories. A new RFF composition implementation should return branch-local values/statistics with validity and combine them through an explicit policy, making evaluation order irrelevant unless an ordered artistic operation is deliberately requested.

**Color-only inversion is a transferable orbit statistic.** Each active branch records absolute components of `domainMap(-orbitPosition)`, equal to `-p/dot(p,p)+InvertC`. This transformation affects collected color data, not the recurrence or geometry. In RFF it could provide a configurable trap-coordinate transform before statistic reduction, enabling different color/material patterns on unchanged fractal geometry. Preserve the order of inversion, translation, absolute value and minimum; applying the transform to a final already-reduced trap is not equivalent. It also cannot be reconstructed from a final escape-count image. Recoloring after changing InvertC may require orbit-statistic recomputation or richer stored data; this should not be presented as an inherently cheap palette-only operation. Exact preservation through MPA skips remains unresolved.

Unlike MMM, all three fourth components here use radius squared, but their sampling times still differ: bulb and Menger use their updated positions, while Mandelbox records immediately after rotation/box fold, before sphere fold/affine addition and before its bailout break. ColorIterations refers to each branch's own loop. Keep branch/update-stage identity with imported statistics. Inversion at the origin is undefined and near-origin values can exceed the finite trap sentinel; validity handling must be explicit without silently substituting an arbitrary epsilon that changes deep-zoom behavior.

The underlying spherical-power, Menger warp and Mandelbox parameter-domain limitations recorded for MMM still apply. The candidate 2D feature here is independently controlled field composition and trap-coordinate mapping, rather than a claim that all three 3D recurrences reduce to ordinary complex iteration.
