MapZoom scales the sampled coordinate range, so its increasing value widens the shown range rather than necessarily matching the main view's zoom convention. The inset has separate aspect corrections, a black border and grayscale coloring. Its bailout uses squared magnitude 200 versus 100 in the main image.

For a future or existing RFF Julia exploration workflow, a synchronized parameter-plane locator could make the connection between parameter selection and Julia appearance visible. This recommendation is conditional on the relevant Julia capability; this batch does not prove that RFF lacks such a locator or request a new Julia computation engine. Keep the inset as an independently cached view with defined precision and update triggers, then composite it outside the material/postprocessing chain if it is an editing aid. Do not rerun a full Mandelbrot loop for every inset pixel on every lighting-only change as a matter of design. Define whether it appears in exports and use full-output coordinates if it does. A locator marker can use mapped coordinates, while accurately resolving deeply zoomed nearby parameters still requires a precision-safe calculation.

**Coloring and progressive sampling are distinct.** The example computes an escape smoothing expression from the final squared magnitude, applies sqrt(co/256), then uses phase-shifted cosine channels. Interior points are black. The smoothing convention and initial iteration indexing are part of its appearance; changing log bases or bailout without checking the additive phase would not preserve its palette. For very distant inputs the square-root argument can become negative, so it is not a robust drop-in coloring function over the entire plane. RFF already has smooth coloring and palettes; this is not evidence that it needs another hard-coded cosine palette or a lower-precision recurrence.

The example itself computes each orbit from scratch in ordinary float vectors. The wrapper accumulates weighted color samples and their weights in the history image; progressive refinement is not perturbation, reference reuse or MPA. Targeted wrapper lines also show gamma-related conversion before accumulation in one configuration. Any RFF sampling change needs an explicit linear-color accumulation contract and reset behavior for changed formula, palette, camera or sample weights. Preserve numerical orbit precision independently of the sample count. No throughput or visual advantage over RFF was measured.

**Animation fixture: preserve time intentionally across rebuilds.** AnimationModeTest derives a rotation from time/10 seconds and supplies two compile-time ballSize alternatives inside a simple folded spherical-shell field. Its comments ask the operator to toggle the branch, rebuild and compare playback-cursor behavior under a preference. Those are proposed manual test steps, not observed outcomes. The transferable validation case for RFF is a deterministic visible animation phase before and after a shader/settings rebuild: specify whether playback continues, stays paused at the current frame or restarts, and reset any image accumulation accordingly. The selected time policy should agree between interactive playback and frame-indexed export. This can validate existing animation infrastructure without introducing a new animation system.

**Logarithmic control fixture: domains are deliberate.** LogSliderTest declares a positive interval, an interval crossing zero, and an entirely negative interval, all annotated Logarithmic, then exposes their values in RGB. The shader does not implement the slider mapping or demonstrate that any interval is supported correctly by the host. ### Follow-up: folded knot stripes and iterative image-feedback patterns

**Complete reads:** Experimental-directory `Knot.frag` (113 lines), `IFS.frag` (119), and `Raytracingtestfrag.frag` (68), under `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/`. The complete 67-line `Examples/Include/BufferShaderIFS.frag` dependency was also inspected to distinguish feedback values from display conversion; its existing review record is retained separately.

**Knot stripes use the same transformed coordinates as geometry.** Knot converts XY radius to an offset around R1, rotates XZ by (a+b/polyfoldOrder)*atan(y,x), quantizes another angle into sectors, rotates YZ by R5, applies the sector rotation, and subtracts R3. The geometry then uses length(transformed XZ)-R2, while baseColor uses the angle of that same cross-section to draw narrow black stripes on a value-two background. Reusing one well-defined coordinate transform makes painted bands follow a shape rather than slide across it. This is useful for RFF procedural material sources, but RFF does not need the knot's 3D geometry merely to support a shared mapping for color, roughness or emission masks.

A 2D folded/angular pattern can reproduce a related visual motif in layer coordinates; a planar slice does not reproduce the knot's over/under topology or hidden surfaces. The sector order is a float and permits zero, so an independent implementation must specify valid order and singular behavior. Noninteger orders and angle wrapping also need an explicit seam convention. The hard modulo stripe threshold is not footprint filtered, and the point-dependent twist is not an isometry simply because its local operation is a rotation. The returned residual is therefore not proved to be an exact signed distance by this file. For RFF, use a pattern/coverage field with filtering rather than treating it as a certified marching bound. Preserve HDR material values until the appropriate output stage if value-two colors are intentional.

**A distinct 2D feature candidate: affine image feedback.** IFS samples its previous image at the current location and at three row-vector affine mappings. Each valid lookup contributes 0.8 times previous RGB plus inNoise*(u,v,1); out-of-domain coordinates contribute zero. Despite its name, inNoise injects a deterministic coordinate ramp, not random noise. The result combines a center branch and three transformed branches with BIAS/BIAS2 and applies BIAS again. It is an image recurrence, not orbit-based Mandelbrot iteration or unbiased progressive color averaging. time is declared but does not drive the local mapping: the number of feedback updates determines the evolution.

RFF could consider a separate feedback-pattern layer for recursive branching textures, with an explicit seed image, transform list, update count and decay/injection controls. This is optional new behavior, not another name for its existing FBM noise. Such a layer needs deterministic simulation steps independent of UI refresh rate, ping-pong resources, reset rules, and a defined warm-up policy for video or seeking. A tiled export cannot independently initialize each tile when transformed samples reach other tiles; evaluate a common field or provide an equivalent global sampling scheme. Cache a frozen state for material-only redraws. The effect should remain outside the high-precision fractal recurrence.

For constant input over valid samples, the linear gain bound from the intended four lookups is 0.8*BIAS*(BIAS+3*BIAS2); at the defaults it is 2.006. This is a worst-case local gain calculation, not proof that the actual cropped transform system diverges. It does show that per-lookup attenuation alone does not establish a contraction. The shader also declares a local vec3 v2 while referencing v2 inside its initializer, sharing the name of a vec2 uniform; compilation and identifier binding need resolution before claiming the intended transform executes. The design above describes the evident affine-feedback intent, not a tested output.

**Feedback state and display must have different contracts.** BufferShaderIFS reads RGB directly, applies log, then pow with Gamma before exposure and contrast/saturation/brightness. It does not divide by an accumulation weight. Values below one produce negative logarithms, which do not form a generally valid input to a noninteger power. A RFF implementation should keep a finite linear simulation state and apply a separately defined visualization remap, with supported zero/negative ranges and no display transform fed back unintentionally. The dependency's historical color-adjustment references also require their own provenance review before code reuse. The source shows intended RGBA32F storage, but this batch does not verify actual host allocation or update order.

**Repeated primitives as a compact validation scene.** Raytracingtestfrag repeats YZ by period S, evaluates a rounded box, and unions it with a sphere centered at SpotLightPos and the X half-space. Moving the light position thus also moves scene geometry. This is not an isolated lighting benchmark. For RFF, a deterministic repeating rounded-rectangle mask could help validate mapping seams, filtering and tile agreement, but these generic primitives do not by themselves justify a new feature. The 3D lighting/occlusion behavior cannot be inferred for ordinary 2D images.

**Provenance and status.** Knot explicitly identifies DarkBeam's formula; Raytracingtestfrag imports QuilezLib, and IFS's display dependency names separate color-adjustment sources. Local example presence is not permission to adapt their distinctive code. No code was copied, no external source/license check was performed, and no compilation, numerical recurrence test, rendering or timing was run. ### Follow-up: stereographic source mapping versus quaternion dynamics

**Complete reads:** Experimental-directory `Stereographic4DJulia.frag` (148 lines) and `StereographicQuaternionJulia.frag` (146), under `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/`. Despite their similar headers, these files implement different dynamics and different coloring data.

**The shared mapping.** For r2=dot(position,position), both construct (Mul*position, r2-1)/(r2+1), then add Offset to the first three components. Mul=2 gives unit length before that offset: 4*r2+(r2-1)^2=(r2+1)^2. Other Mul values change that property, and nonzero Offset moves the result away from the unit sphere. The Quaternion file's Default preset uses Mul=2.10237 and Offset=(1,1,1), so even its preset is not a unit-sphere embedding. Do not infer a conformal unit-sphere map from the helper's name for arbitrary settings.

For RFF, stereographic mapping is useful as an optional coordinate source for a pattern or environment-style material. A 2D analogue maps local XY to a sphere and can feed an independently defined spherical pattern; it does not require importing either Julia recurrence. A planar slice of the four-dimensional construction is also possible as a new mathematical visualization, but has different semantics. Define the projection, axis ordering, offset and scale explicitly and propagate its pixel footprint. At large coordinate magnitudes, most of the plane approaches the projection pole, so filtering and stable evaluation matter. Keep this mapping in local coordinates for display effects instead of converting arbitrary deep-zoom absolute coordinates to ordinary float vectors.

**The first file is not an active quaternion Julia implementation.** Stereographic4DJulia splits the mapped vector into a complex initial value p=xy and a complex parameter c=zw, then iterates p=p*p+c. Both initial value and parameter vary with the input position. Its declared quaternion constant C is unused, and it does not update orbitTrap in its local DE. The scalar dp update 2*length(p)*dp+1 is not a full derivative of this composite mapping, where p0 and c both depend on the stereographic coordinates. For RFF, a parameterized surface through the combined (initial value, parameter) space is a separate exploration feature; it cannot be substituted for ordinary Mandelbrot or fixed-parameter Julia calculations, nor does a matching header establish equivalent coloring channels.

**The second file does iterate quaternion squaring.** StereographicQuaternionJulia treats x as the real component, updates (x*x-dot(yzw,yzw), 2*x*yzw)+C, and records the minimum of absolute XYZ and squared four-dimensional radius after each update, before bailout. Its dp begins at the real unit quaternion and is updated by twice quaternion multiplication p*dp. General quaternion differentiation of squaring acts on a perturbation h as p*h+h*p, so a single multiplication recurrence is not automatically a full Jacobian for arbitrary perturbation directions. In addition, the initialization does not incorporate the stereographic mapping's spatial derivative. These source equations do not establish a conservative world-space distance bound. Neither file supplies a proof that its scalar log-radius estimate remains valid under the input deformation.

A RFF adoption should either treat such results as an explicitly new field visualization with its own validation, or derive the mapped recurrence and derivative/error model before considering acceleration. Its state, quaternion/complex algebra and observation rules differ from RFF's current Mandelbrot perturbation and MPA. A color-only spherical pattern is much smaller in scope and can reuse existing material shading; full four-dimensional dynamics is lower-priority formula research.

**Boundary and provenance conditions.** Threshold is compared against squared norm; zero iterations return an estimate from the initial state; zero norm, zero derivative length and nonescaping finite orbits need defined behavior in a new implementation. The headers credit Subblue's implementation and its Keenan Crane antecedent, but contain no explicit local license grant. Those attributions should guide verification before any distinctive implementation is copied. No code was adapted, and no external license check, shader compilation, numerical derivative test, render or timing was performed. The unit-length identity and derivative comparison above are algebraic source analysis, not executed tests.

### Follow-up: rational complex transforms versus sign-flip bulb variants

**Complete reads:** `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Experimental/Mobius.frag` (159 lines) and `Moebiusbulb.frag` (236), including presets. The shared naming does not indicate equivalent mathematics.

**Rational mapping as a 2D pattern source.** Mobius first squares a complex input, then evaluates (CA*z+CB)/(CC*z+CD) on that squared value. The complete recurrence is therefore a rational degree-two map in the generic nondegenerate case, not just a degree-one Mobius coordinate transform. It iterates from the input point without adding that point as a Mandelbrot parameter each step. Its color statistic accumulates orbit magnitudes after a selected initial interval, remaps the result with nested logarithms and cosine RGB phases, and is used as a surface color on either a sphere or a plane. The nearby Ducks attribution comment is a provenance lead; the active rational equation, rather than the comment's title, defines what is evaluated.

For RFF, two distinct proposals follow. A single nondegenerate fractional-linear map can be an optional coordinate warp for a procedural/image material, with a mapping derivative and explicit pole policy. Repeating the squared rational map is instead a new procedural fractal pattern or formula. A layer-local pattern can remain separate from the high-precision Mandelbrot computation; an actual deep-zoom formula requires its own perturbation and acceleration derivation. Do not merge these scopes under a generic Mobius checkbox or assume RFF's current MPA can skip this recurrence unchanged.

**Color-statistic boundaries must be specified.** The accumulation condition is i>PreIterations, evaluated after the recurrence and before the escape test. The denominator is i-PreIterations. When the loop exhausts its iteration budget, that denominator exceeds the actual contributing sample count by one; early escape before any eligible contribution can produce zero/negative denominators. The escape comparison uses squared magnitude against 10^EscapeSize. ColC can be zero, and the nested logs require an appropriately positive ratio. A RFF mean-orbit feature should track the actual sample count, define empty-window output, name the bailout units, and distinguish log-range compression from palette phase. The example is not evidence that a generic mean statistic is already compatible with skipped MPA intervals.

**Sphere/plane mapping has a scale convention.** Sphere colors use 2*XY/(1-Z), while the plane uses XY directly. The unused inverse helper maps a plane point to (2*XY, r2-1)/(r2+1); composing that helper with the active sphere-to-plane function yields twice the original point, not identity. This is consistent with different projection-plane scales, not proof of one interchangeable forward/inverse pair. The north pole is singular. The material callback resets its floor flag and reevaluates DE at the center sample before choosing a mapping, which avoids simply accepting a floor flag left by a normal probe. RFF should similarly resolve the selected mapping/material for the intended sample, preferably through an explicit result rather than a mutable global flag.

**The bulb helper is a conditional reflection, not a complex fractional transform.** Moebiusbulb's moebius(p) leaves p.x unchanged and negates p.y whenever p.x is nonzero; it returns p unchanged when p.x is exactly zero. Applying it to XY then YZ gives (x,-y,-z) away from the coordinate planes, a half-turn about X, with different exact-axis behavior. This operation is inserted after the spherical power and before parameter addition, so it changes the recurrence even though its generic branch preserves norm. Its exact-axis exceptions also prevent treating the entire helper as one smooth global rotation. It is unrelated to the rational map in Mobius.frag.

A simple mirror/rotation mode in RFF material coordinates is much smaller than a bulb formula and may already be covered by existing layer transforms; this example alone does not justify another named effect. A recurrence variant would require explicit branch semantics and derivatives. The scalar derivative recurrence remains the existing bulb expression, and the file supplies no validation of a full world-space distance bound. Both presets omit MoebiusVersion; they do not demonstrate the enabled variation. time only feeds an unused local value in init, so this is not an active animation mechanism either.

**Provenance and verification.** Mobius identifies Samuel Monnier and Syntopia; Moebiusbulb cites spherical-coordinate, IQ and Enforcer sources. The local files do not establish a complete license grant for recognizable adaptations. No implementation was copied. Findings come from complete source reads and algebraic simplification; no external source verification, shader compilation, numerical iteration test, render or timing was performed. These are optional mapping/formula ideas below environment/material-source improvements in immediate RFF priority.

**Combining complete fields is different from alternating formulas.** Mixed evaluates two independent folded recurrences from the same input, then returns their maximum. DE2 sorts absolute coordinates, applies a Scale+1 expansion and axis offsets, and rescales the terminal length by (Scale+1)^(-iterations). DE3 uses normalized plane reflections and an affine expansion about a fixed offset, rescaling by Scale^(-iterations). The user-facing Offset controls DE2, while DE3's matrix uses a separate fixed lowercase offset. There is no shared orbit alternating between the two maps. Its maximum resembles an intersection operation when the operands have suitable signed-field semantics, but these particular terminal lengths are nonnegative; the code alone does not prove exact signed-distance intersection behavior.

For RFF material masks, independent procedural sources can be combined with an explicitly selected min/max or other operator, without changing the Mandelbrot recurrence. A max of two arbitrary palette values is a value selection, not automatically a geometric intersection. Smooth blending also needs its own gradient and coverage policy; it is absent from this reference.

Both branches update the same orbitTrap with componentwise minima. Thus the selected scalar distance can come from one branch while its coloring contains observations from both. For RFF, offer a deliberate choice between material data from the selected source and a separately combined color/mask statistic. Keep the normal, value and source identity together when selecting a field. Do not assume the maximum operation makes evaluation cheap: both complete recurrences execute at each query here. Scale=0 and empty iteration/color windows require defined behavior in a new implementation.

**A practical 2D pattern: cavities at multiple scales.** SphereSponge shifts the input, then repeatedly forms a centered periodic cell with mod(z*k,4)-2, starting at k=2 and multiplying k by Scale. At each level it maximizes (BubbleSize-length(cell))/k against the accumulated value, initially zero. This produces a nonnegative multiscale cavity constraint; it is not an average of noise octaves and has no active sphere crop. The sphere-cropping code is commented out. Scale below one reverses the progression toward larger features, Scale=1 repeats the same level, and zero makes later division invalid.

A 2D version using circular cell distances could serve as a perforation, pore or stippled material mask, optionally driving both height and roughness. That is a lower-cost transfer than importing the 3D marcher. The visual effect depends on the max reduction, cell alignment and scale sequence, so it should be named and parameterized distinctly from FBM. Stop or integrate levels once their footprint is unresolved, and define global pattern coordinates so tiles agree. An artistic height based on this field is not a claim of actual holes or visibility through a 3D solid.

The color trap in SphereSponge observes the unchanged shifted input z, not the level-specific cell p2. For any positive eligible count, repeating this minimum yields the same coordinate statistic; changing ColorIterations does not make it a multiscale cell-color average. A RFF source wanting per-level color would need to retain or reduce the intended cell quantity explicitly. This distinction avoids promising a coloring capability that the example does not implement.

**Provenance and verification.** Mixed credits Syntopia and Knighty's kaleidoscopic IFS work; SphereSponge credits Buddhi and Knighty. Neither local file supplies a complete explicit reuse license. ### Follow-up: normalized quadratic remapping and a two-phase hybrid

**Complete reads:** Experimental-directory `LogisticBulb.frag` (238 lines) and `Spudsville2.frag` (143), under `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/`. Both change the orbit itself. Their names and historical speed comments do not establish compatibility with RFF's current computation or measured performance on current hardware.

**A normalized direction map is not ordinary complex squaring.** LogisticBulb first performs a spherical power, adds the parameter/Julia constant, then applies domainMap before the next radius test and rotation. domainMap optionally scales its input when domainMapScale is nonzero, evaluates normalize((x*x-y*y,2*x*y,2*z*z)), subtracts the scaled input and adds K. Setting domainMapScale to zero bypasses only the initial scaling; it does not disable the remap. For nonzero scale, the normalization removes that scale's squared magnitude from the quadratic directional term, while the subtracted linear term still changes with scale and sign. Consequently the comment that scaling only affects resulting scale is not a general equivalence of the whole recurrence.

In the Z=0 plane, the quadratic term encodes doubled complex angle but normalizes away the squared radial magnitude. The result is a normalized-square-minus-input map, not the conventional complex logistic polynomial. At the origin normalization has no defined nonzero direction. RFF could use an independently specified angular remap as a layer-local procedural pattern, but this should be named by its actual operation and use an explicit center policy. Inserting it into the fractal recurrence requires a new formula and derivative/error model. The existing dr update only covers the spherical power and does not propagate the subsequent nonlinear normalized remap; the returned log-radius expression is therefore not a demonstrated distance bound for the composed field.

The color trap records rotated XYZ and the radius squared after the domain map, over an initial iteration window. This makes its source stage different from a pre-remap trap. A RFF field selector should state that stage if hybrid coloring is introduced. time is declared but unused locally; the file does not implement time-varying deformation. The shipped presets omit the new K/domainMapScale controls, so complete preset behavior depends on host default/partial-application semantics rather than the preset names alone.

**Spudsville is a prefix followed by a different map, not alternating independent fields.** Its loop has a fixed maximum of 14 iterations and stops when radius reaches 10. For n<MN it performs a box fold, sphere fold and Scale multiplication. Later iterations use a second box-fold limit, a latitude-style spherical power with ZMUL applied to Z, then Scale2 multiplication. MN=0 skips the first stage; MN>=14 suppresses the second stage within this loop. The original input is stored as c, but additions of c are commented out, and Offset2 has no active use. Do not describe this as ordinary Mandelbox-plus-Mandelbulb parameter addition or as blending two completed distance fields.

For RFF, the useful longer-term design is an explicitly scheduled prefix/suffix formula with independently defined state, stage-specific coloring and acceleration rules. The same ordering concept can be used more cheaply for a material coordinate pipeline, but that yields a texture pattern rather than this 3D set. The local color trap samples only the first two iterations, scales XYZ by four and leaves squared radius unscaled. With MN>=2, it sees only the first phase; changing later-stage settings can change geometry without adding later-stage orbit observations. This supports explicit observation windows rather than assuming one generic ColorIterations value captures every phase.

**Anisotropic derivative scaling needs a bound, not an average.** Spudsville multiplies the spherical-power derivative factor by sqrt((2+ZMUL*ZMUL)/3), then adds one. The linear Z stretch alone has operator norm max(1,abs(ZMUL)); its root-mean-square axis scale is smaller whenever the stretch is anisotropic. Thus the RMS factor is not by itself a conservative bound on that operation, and the added-one term also needs justification for the actual recurrence with parameter additions removed. The Default preset uses ZMUL=-26, outside the declared nonnegative slider range, so host loading/clamping behavior is another unverified part of reproducing the example. No precision-preserving RFF speedup should be inferred from its compact formula or tiny FudgeFactor setting.

**Provenance and validation.** LogisticBulb points to a forum transform and existing spherical-power sources; Spudsville credits Lenord's parameters and carries a historical compiler/performance warning for a GeForce 310M. Neither establishes complete current licensing or performance evidence. No source code was adapted, external provenance verified, shader compiled, numeric derivative test executed, image rendered or timing measured. These are lower-priority formula/pattern research ideas; the environment/material-source recommendations remain more direct RFF improvements.

### Follow-up: DoubleTest is a formula experiment, not a precision benchmark

**Complete read:** `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Experimental/DoubleTest.frag` (414 lines, including all presets). It requests GLSL 4.10 compatibility, defines USE_DOUBLE and uses dvec/double inputs with Progressive2D-4. A targeted include check confirms double-typed zoom and sampling controls. It provides neither a high-precision reference comparison nor numerical error measurements; its name and 1e14 zoom preset are not evidence of correct deep-zoom detail.

**The active recurrence has several independent stages.** An optional input inversion evaluates -c/dot(c,c)+InvertC. PreIter performs ordinary Plot(z)+c without the later absolute-value folds, Y negation, Meta/Sin selection or trap collection. The main loop selects full absolute values, absolute Y, or absolute X, then negates Y and evaluates one of four formulas combining Plot, an optional nested Plot, optional complex sine and sometimes the prior z. Plot computes a polar power using atan(y/x,1), with a pi adjustment for negative X. This is not a robust drop-in atan2 construction at X=0, including the zero initial state; noninteger powers additionally require a deliberate branch convention. A RFF formula design must name the prelude and repeating map separately and derive the precision behavior of each.

**Retry changes the mathematical orbit.** When squared magnitude exceeds RetryEntry and retries remain, z is divided by RetryBias, i is decremented, and execution continues before updating dist, zmin or testing Bailout. The for-loop increment then restores the same logical iteration index, although another recurrence evaluation has occurred. RetryMax therefore adds evaluations without advancing the displayed iteration counter for those attempts. This is a rescaled-orbit formula with a retry-state variable, not numerical recovery, a perturbation glitch correction or a way to improve accuracy of the original set. A RFF adaptation would require that state in its reference/MPA model and an explicit coloring counter convention. RetryBias=0 is permitted by the declaration; the default avoids the division only because RetryMax=0.

**Pickover-style stalk fields are a more direct appearance idea.** The code records separate minima of absolute real and imaginary coordinates on accepted main-loop steps. StalkColor derives max/min/radial combinations of those minima and an iteration-dependent nested-square-root response, with separate toggles for inside and outside coloring. The minima may originate at different orbit steps, so length(zmin) is not the minimum distance of one orbit sample to the origin. RFF could consider independently defined axis-trap sources for material/palette masks, provided the required statistics are available or can be propagated through skips without losing precision. A selected scalar iteration count cannot reconstruct them. Keep sample eligibility, prelude exclusion, retry exclusion and interior handling explicit, and reset per-sample state if a callback is evaluated multiple times.

**Smoothing is formula-specific.** IQColor selects four different nested-log expressions according to Meta/Sin, using combinations of final radius, squared radius, Power and Bailout, then applies sqrt(co/ColDiv) and cosine channels. These formulas are not a demonstrated common escape potential for all four recurrences, especially those with sine or orbit rescaling. Power=1, nonpositive logarithm inputs and negative square-root arguments need defined behavior. The large numerical constants printed in presets do not prove that the host, camera mapping, transcendental functions and final image preserve the required precision. A future RFF formula validation should compare actual orbit/statistic outputs against an appropriate reference, rather than infer accuracy from a detailed-looking render or double declarations.

**2D scope and priority.** This example is already 2D. Its useful transfers are explicit formula-stage scheduling and distinct inside/outside trap-driven materials; its optional input inversion can also be an independently defined layer warp. None requires replacing RFF's existing high-precision Mandelbrot path with this direct loop. The wider formula family is research work below the immediate environment/material-source improvements.

**Provenance and validation.** The file credits an IQ coloring scheme, Chris Thomasson's retry idea and the FractalForums community. No explicit local license grant establishes permission for distinctive adaptations. No code was copied, external provenance checked, shader compiled, precision test executed, image rendered or timing measured. This is source analysis of the actual stages and their limits, not a report of successful double-precision validation.

### Follow-up: coloring-only inversion and an invariant complex plane

**Complete read:** `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Experimental/3DMandel.frag` (404 lines, including Default and P3/P4/P8 presets). This is a spherical-power variant with transformed orbit coloring, not a height extrusion of RFF's iteration map.

**A useful separation: transform the observed orbit without changing the orbit.** The active recurrence applies one of three spherical power functions, adds the input or Julia constant, records radius, then rotates. Only the coloring statement applies domainMap(-z)=-z/dot(z,z)+InvertC to its XYZ trap channels; the fourth trap channel remains the untransformed radius squared. InvertC therefore shifts the observed color coordinates, not the local geometric recurrence. A change to it need not change the mathematical set even though it can strongly change its appearance.

This supports an RFF material-field design in which observation transforms are explicitly separate from formula transforms. A transformed axis-distance trap could feed palette position, roughness or emission while preserving the current recurrence. However, it still requires the relevant orbit samples: min(abs(transformed orbit)) cannot generally be reconstructed by transforming an already reduced minimum, and a scalar iteration map is insufficient. An implementation must either propagate the selected statistic through precision-safe computation/skips or identify a different available field as an artistic approximation. Merely making the final material evaluation cheap does not make acquisition of new orbit statistics free.

**The third power function has a particular planar restriction.** powN3 uses atan(z.z,length(z)) for elevation instead of asin(z.z/length(z)) or polar acos. On the Z=0 plane away from the origin, its elevation is zero and XY follows the ordinary polar complex-power formula. With a plane-preserving rotation, a zero-Z additive constant and an integer power, this plane remains invariant. For the parameter case, the initial z is pos rather than zero, so it starts at the usual Mandelbrot orbit's first value; finite iteration counts and smoothing conventions still need alignment. This conditional planar identity does not prove the whole 3D field is equivalent to Mandelbrot, nor does it justify claiming identical Julia images for arbitrary rotation/constants.

For RFF, the 2D restriction provides little new geometry when it reduces to an already supported complex power. The more interesting incremental appearance idea is the coloring-only transform. A full 3D extension remains a separate formula/rendering project with its own distance and derivative analysis. All three branches reuse a scalar radial derivative recurrence; that alone does not establish a conservative spatial derivative for the modified angular mapping. Preserve RFF's existing precision guarantees rather than transplanting the estimator as an optimization.

**Singularities and sample semantics.** The inverse-color mapping divides by squared norm and is undefined at zero; values near zero can dominate the mapped scale before the componentwise minimum. Define the behavior of a singular observation separately from orbit escape/interior classification. The vector trap is measured after rotation, while its radial value was captured before rotation; the norm agrees only under the intended orthogonal transform. Invalid rotation axes need a defined policy. ColorIterations gates post-update samples, including a sample that has just passed the bailout radius because the next loop condition performs the exit. A new RFF statistic should document this eligibility explicitly.

The presets use the third branch and powers 2, 3, 4 and 8, but also change camera and lighting-related settings. Their existence is not a controlled visual comparison or evidence of sampling convergence. The local time uniform is unused, so this example adds no automatic animation mechanism.

### Follow-up: scale-corrected geometric traps versus color traps

**Complete read:** `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Experimental/OctahedronOT.frag` (394 lines, including all seven presets). This example uses a geometric orbit trap to construct a field, in addition to a separate orbit statistic for color.

**Two reductions with different roles.** Each iteration rotates the current point, performs four sign/swap plane folds, then scales and translates it. The color orbitTrap records componentwise minima of absolute XYZ and squared radius for n<ColorIterations, before incrementing n. The geometric result separately takes the minimum of trap(z)*Scale^(-n) after incrementing n, across all iterations. Thus ColorIterations restricts coloring but not the geometric trap. An RFF field-source design should distinguish these independent observation windows and reductions rather than assume one orbit-trap control means both.

The active trap rotates a copy of z by fracRotation2 and returns abs(length(rotated.xz-O3.xy)-val). This is an unsigned cylindrical-shell residual independent of the rotated Y coordinate; it is not the capped cylinder described by the unreachable code after the first return. cylRad, cylHeight and O3.z do not affect that active expression. Angle2 changes the trap orientation while Angle1 changes the recurrence at every step. That separation is useful: RFF could allow a pattern/trap to move relative to its source field without changing the source recurrence, provided the necessary observations are retained.

**2D adoption scope.** A circular trap evaluated after a sequence of planar folds can yield nested rings, filaments or a relief mask. Rescaling each observation by the accumulated expansion expresses contributions from different levels in comparable source-space units. This is distinct from taking a raw minimum of orbit coordinates. For positive Scale and valid rotation axes, the individual rotations/reflections are norm preserving and the explicit scale supplies that level factor; nevertheless the file does not prove the composite minimum is the exact Euclidean distance to the folded union. Treat it as a defined procedural field and filter its thin features before using it as height or material coverage.

For RFF's current Mandelbrot orbit, Scale^(-n) is not a substitute for the actual derivative or a justification for MPA skipping. A similar transformed statistic would need a derivation for that recurrence and a way to recover contributions from skipped iterations. A layer-local folded pattern is the smaller independent feature. If material identity should follow the level producing the minimum, retain its index or associated data; the current componentwise color minimum can combine different iterations and need not belong to the geometry's winning sample. Define ties and empty windows explicitly.

**Boundary and preset semantics.** Iterations=0 returns the literal initial value 10900. Scale=0 makes negative powers undefined for positive iterations, and negative val cannot describe a positive-radius cylindrical shell even though the slider permits it. The presets omit the added val/O3/cylinder controls, so they are not self-contained evidence of particular trap shapes. Cold also supplies a Rot2 component outside its declared range. Host default retention and out-of-range handling must be established before reproducing presets, not guessed from their visual names or the word Artifact.

### Follow-up: box-folded Kleinian maps and transformed-field bounds

**Complete read:** `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Experimental/boxfold_kleinian.frag` (403 lines, including both presets). The header identifies Jos Leys's original idea/code, Knighty's modifications and pupukuusikko's subsequent changes. Its license text explicitly says to ask Jos Leys; this is not a permissive grant or proof that the surrounding repository license covers adaptation. Treat the implementation as a design reference pending provenance resolution.

**Active map structure.** Each main iteration shears X by (KleinI/KleinR)*Y, applies either periodic wrapping or a box fold, reverses the shear, optionally applies a separation-region point reflection, records the orbit trap, then performs inversion plus translations/sign changes through TransA. FourGen includes Y in the wrap/fold stage; otherwise only XZ is processed. The box-fold branch uses an asymmetric scalar interval from -box_size_x*fold to box_size_z*fold for both X and Z, not independent symmetric axis limits. Negative fold can reverse clamp bounds. Zero periodic widths divide by zero in the alternate wrapping mode. A RFF pattern should specify these intervals and supported domains rather than infer them from control labels.

The inversion accumulator DF is multiplied by reciprocal squared radius. It does not explicitly track the full differential of the shear/fold/unshear composition. Although the two shears cancel when the intervening operation is identity, that is not a general bound for all folded branches. Optional separation also reflects all three coordinates about a point even though its decision surface is expressed in X/Y. These operations are not automatically equivalent to an exact Kleinian group for arbitrary artistic settings. The named group and its historical parameter restrictions should not become an unsupported mathematical guarantee in RFF.

**A bounded terminal evaluation is distinct from an orbit trap.** The main loop uses a squared-distance threshold of 1e-12 against the state from two iterations earlier. It is an approximate two-cycle stopping condition, not RFF's period discovery or MPA mechanism. Final_Iterations then repeats only TransA and minimizes a height-like residual divided by max(DF,Clamp_DF); one such residual is evaluated even when Final_Iterations is zero. ShowBalls selects min(Y,KleinR-Y) instead of Y. Clamp_y applies an upper min, so negative residuals remain negative. Color minima are gathered only in the main loop, not during those final evaluations. A RFF implementation must distinguish transformation depth, terminal refinement and color-observation range.

**2D transfer and inversion.** A separately defined planar fold/inversion pattern could produce recursive cells or spirals for a material layer. This is optional pattern construction, not a modification to the existing high-precision Mandelbrot recurrence. If a transformed field supplies relief, derive its gradient/footprint through the mapping and define poles. The outer DoInversion path subtracts InvCenter and ReCenter, maps by InvRadius squared divided by radius squared, then applies r2*d/(InvRadius squared+r*d) to the returned field. InvRadius is squared by the code despite its radius-squared comment. Because the underlying clamped estimator can be signed and is not proven exact, this expression is not a general certified distance correction; its denominator can also approach zero. For a color-only coordinate warp, such a distance conversion is unnecessary, but filtering near the inversion center still matters.

Preset fog, cloud and aperture settings belong to the included DE-Kn2cr11 renderer. They do not make those effects part of this local fractal map. The file selects WANG_HASH and leaves the volumetric define commented; dependency-specific behavior must be established from reachable code rather than preset fields alone. No new RFF fog/lighting recommendation is inferred from these labels.

### Follow-up: Mandelcup's angular map and recurrence animation

**Complete read:** `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Experimental/mandelcup.frag` (334 lines, all three presets). The header credits Pupukuusikko, Tglad's tetrahedral/dihedral ideas and Knighty's implementation; the generic Mandelbulb info label does not describe all active operations.

**Direction and radius are deliberately separated.** Each step normalizes the orbit by its radius, divides its XY complex value by (Z,c1), squares that quotient and multiplies by c2, then maps it back to a sphere as (2*u,2*v,abs(w)^2-1)/(abs(w)^2+1). For finite quotient values this last expression has unit length. The code rotates that direction, restores magnitude r squared, optionally takes absolute values of selected coordinates, and adds the parameter or Julia constant. c1/c2 therefore reshape the angular map; c2 is not simply an overall radial multiplier after the sphere mapping.

For RFF, a independently defined planar rational warp followed by spherical-pattern lookup could be a material-coordinate option. That would reuse the appearance mechanism without implementing this 3D recurrence. It needs a precise inverse/forward mapping convention, sampling footprint and pole policy. Restricting the complete map to Z=0 is not generally a closed ordinary complex-power system: after mapping back to the sphere, the new Z need not remain zero. A 2D slice is a new visualization, not a claim of equivalent Mandelbrot dynamics.

**Singularities can sometimes be chart problems, not intentional holes.** The code divides by r and by the squared magnitude of (Z,c1). With c1=0, the latter is singular on Z=0. Large quotient magnitude has a finite limiting direction under the sphere map, but direct division/squaring can overflow or produce undefined intermediates before reaching that limit. A new implementation could evaluate the composed rational-to-sphere expression with stable homogeneous coordinates or another derived chart, after establishing its zero/zero behavior. This is a precision-oriented design possibility, not a tested replacement formula. Do not hide singular cases with arbitrary clamps that alter the intended fractal.

**Animation changes the formula itself.** init builds its rotation with RotAngle+10*time, and that rotation is applied on every orbit iteration. Even RotAngle=0 therefore does not freeze the local shape when time advances. This is not a camera orbit or a rotation of a completed image. RFF should distinguish recurrence animation from material-coordinate and view animation, with separate recomputation and accumulation invalidation costs. If this mechanism is ever adopted as a new formula, time/rotation belongs in the formula state used for references and caches; it cannot reuse an unchanged reference merely because the camera stayed fixed.

The derivative update remains 2*r*dr+1 and does not explicitly account for the angular rational mapping's differential or its parameter dependence. DEtuner scales the final log-radius expression, and InsideDE only negates it. Neither supplies a proof of accurate interior distance or a conservative world-space bound. RFF must not interpret these controls as precision correction. Its ordinary 2D material warp would not need a ray-marching distance estimator at all.

**Coloring and presets.** The trap gathers absolute XYZ and squared radius after the full transform and parameter addition. The next loop test performs escape, so the last escaping update can contribute. The inside preset combines sign inversion, Julia mode, a different c2 and a bailout value outside the declared slider range; it is not an isolated sign-flip comparison. Source presets also use settings from different renderer generations. Host loading and actual visual behavior remain unverified.

**Provenance and status.** The local header provides historical attribution and a source pointer, not a complete explicit license grant. ### Follow-up: Benesi-folded Mandelbulb as a staged material-pattern source

**Complete read:** `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Experimental/BenesiFoldedMandelbulb.frag` (829 lines), including all ten presets. The useful RFF transfer is an optional folded coordinate/pattern source with explicit stage scheduling. This is a lower-priority appearance extension than editable environment reflection, not an acceleration or precision improvement for RFF's Mandelbrot computation.

**Actual stage order.** The shader initializes z from the sample position and calls BenesiFold exactly once, before the iteration loop. That function mixes coordinates with square-root coefficients, applies absolute-value folds, then applies component-wise bscale and boffset. Each subsequent iteration performs the selected spherical power, optionally calls BenesiPine when the zero-based index equals PineIterAt, adds either JuliaC or the original sample position, computes radius, rotates the vector, and collects the color trap. A selected index beyond the executed loop simply never runs. The time uniform is declared but unused. This is not a repeated Benesi fold on every iteration and not a smoothly animated blend between two formulas.

**Assignment order is mathematical behavior.** In the fold's second coordinate mixing block, the final x assignment reads the already updated z. It must not be casually replaced with an assumed inverse orthogonal matrix. In BenesiPine, t is computed from the original x divided by sqrt(y*y+z*z), then x and z are replaced, and the y assignment uses that new z. Rewriting all three components as simultaneous expressions of the old vector would change the map. The final length comparison retains the original vector whenever the candidate is longer. This is a branch selecting between two maps, not a continuous interpolation; the axis denominator and branch boundary need an explicit mathematical policy before adaptation. Adding an epsilon without analysis would itself change the formula.

**Concrete 3D-to-2D opportunity.** A separately authored RFF material source could embed local 2D coordinates into a declared plane in 3D, apply a small, bounded sequence of folds, and return a scalar pattern for an existing material or color input. Plane position/orientation, scale, offset, iteration budget and selected transform stage should have explicit semantics. Such a slice samples a 3D field; discarding a coordinate after every step would instead define a different recurrence. A simpler independently defined planar fold is also possible, but should be named as a separate pattern. Keep this optional display computation separate from the high-precision reference orbit and MPA. Propagate or estimate the transformed pixel footprint so dense folds do not become unstable stripes during zooms and video export. The example does not provide that filtering.

**Trap ownership and required data.** The shader minimizes absolute XYZ and squared radius after parameter addition and rotation, restricted by ColorIterations. Radius is evaluated before rotation; the spatial components after it. With a valid orthogonal rotation these refer to the same norm, but they retain different coordinate semantics. The original one-time fold is not sampled as an independent trap stage. If RFF exposes stage-specific masks, it must define where each statistic is measured instead of treating every orbit trap as interchangeable. A new display-only pattern can compute its own statistics; reproducing statistics from the fractal orbit requires the relevant orbit data and cannot generally be recovered from a final scalar iteration count.

**Distance estimation is not a transferable guarantee.** The scalar dr update accounts for the spherical power expression but does not explicitly propagate the initial anisotropic fold or the Pine branch's differential. The final log-radius expression therefore does not establish a conservative distance bound for the composite transform. A 2D material pattern needs no ray-marching bound; a new geometric formula would need independent derivative/bound work. None of this justifies reducing RFF's numerical precision.
