Its fog distance is length(from-dir) before negating dir, not a measured ray-surface distance. baseColor forms I=point-from, calls refract(I,-N,1/RefractiveIndex), applies the same Y/Z permutation and returns the sampled RGB. Unlike reflection of a normalized view vector, this is a refraction-style lookup used as the base color. I is not explicitly normalized, and there is no local handling for index zero, total internal reflection/zero returned direction, incident-medium selection or a matching exit surface. These observations mean the example should not be presented as physical glass or roughness-aware environment lighting.

**Why the RFF environment proposal remains different.** RFF already has material BRDFs and relief normals. The proposed addition should supply a scene-linear environment evaluated with a documented reflection-direction convention and separate base/clearcoat roughness filtering, not replace material albedo with this tutorial's cube sample. If an artistic refraction layer is added later, name its approximation, normalize its vectors, define refractive-index domains and reflection fallback, and distinguish it from transmission through finite geometry. A 2D relief normal can orient environment lookup without requiring a 3D fractal. However, a full refractive object needs thickness/exit visibility that a scalar escape map does not provide.

**Orientation, footprint and resource contracts.** The background's negation and XZY mapping are explicit conventions, not portable defaults. Use an axis-labeled test environment to check orientation consistently across backdrop, reflections and export, and keep backdrop visibility independent of illumination strength. This file has no explicit roughness input, prefilter selection or color-space conversion in either callback; implicit sampler behavior cannot be inferred as GGX filtering or HDR support. In RFF, document image decoding, linear-light processing, minification versus roughness convolution, resource lifetime and persistence before adding image environments. No cubemap asset or code was copied in this batch.

**The attached Mandelbulb is independently parameterized.** Both power branches update a scalar derivative with max(previous derivative times DerivativeBias, conventional power expression plus one). The recurrence starts at the query, adds either JuliaC or the query, then applies row-vector rotation. Radius is measured before rotation, and post-rotation XYZ with that radius squared feeds the first ColorIterations trap samples. A rigid rotation preserves radius ideally; this does not prove the scalar derivative is exact for every branch or Julia mode. Zero radius, power zero and zero axis remain domain conditions. The declared time is unused in the local formula. The optional intersection code is commented out.

**Presets deliberately isolate simpler shapes.** Refraction and Reflection set Iterations to zero; the active field is then 0.5*r*log(r), whose nonzero finite radial zero is at r=1. They are primarily environment demonstrations on a sphere-like zero set, not evidence of a complex refractive fractal. Default uses index 0.1; Octobulb omits explicit environment/index settings, so its effective state depends on host preset semantics. Reflection changes renderer reflection strength but does not remove the refraction-based baseColor callback. Therefore preset titles alone do not establish which lighting path dominates.

**Evidence and priority.** This tutorial strengthens the integration requirements for the already prioritized RFF environment feature, rather than introducing a better replacement BRDF. Validate with labeled directions, constant/ramp/HDR environments, separate roughness levels, finite vectors, color-space checks and full-frame/tiled/video comparisons. No shader build, image rendering, physical validation, timing or external source/license verification was performed. The referenced power-function authors and derivative-bias attribution must be resolved if distinctive formula code is later adapted; no such adaptation is proposed here.

## Animation tutorials 30–32: distinguish host tracks, shader time and object motion

**Complete reads:** `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tutorials/30 - Simple Keyframe Animation.frag` (214 inventory lines), `31 - Simple Focal Plane Tracking Target.frag` (282) and `32 - Simple Multi-Parameter Easing Animation.frag` (187), including all preset blocks and trailing easing records. These are historical Fragmentarium examples, not proof that every imported animation record is supported by GMT's current runtime.

**Host animation versus local shader behavior.** Tutorial 30 provides a complete Default and four partial KeyFrame camera presets. Its time reference is confined to an unused dummy function, so no active local recurrence interpolates those keys. Tutorial 32 similarly has no active time-based motion in its formula; its Default ends with colon-delimited records named Cycles1:CosineCurve, Power1:SineCurve and RotAngle1:OutInBack. Those records are metadata for a host parser, not executable GLSL easing. The file alone does not establish their numeric field meanings, timing units, overshoot behavior or import support. Do not derive a new RFF animation format from their labels or assume an imported shader retains their motion.

**Tutorial 31 contains actual time-dependent formula changes.** Before iteration, positive TRotSpeed replaces the shared rotation matrix with a time-dependent one and rotates the initial state. The same matrix is then used at every orbit step, so this control changes both initialization and the recurrence's repeated transform. Positive TransSpeed offsets only the initial state by normalized TransVector*time*TransSpeed*10. Positive ImpulseStrength adds normalized TransVector*(0.8+sin(time*ImpulseRate+ImpulseOffset))*ImpulseStrength. In non-Julia mode the repeated additive parameter remains the original untransformed pos. Therefore these controls are not generally rigid translation/rotation of a fixed Mandelbrot-like object. In Julia mode an initial-coordinate transformation has a different interpretation, but the repeated rotation still matters. A RFF material-layer transform should act on documented sampling coordinates if the intended result is moving a fixed pattern, rather than inadvertently morphing its generating formula.

**Focus tracking is delegated.** Tutorial 31 enables AutoFocus and nonzero aperture in its Default and provides ten partial camera keys. The local AutoFocus declaration is commented out and no focus calculation is implemented in this formula body; effective tracking belongs to the included renderer and host. Several keys hold Eye while changing Target, illustrating intended focus/view changes, but not establishing the exact focal-distance calculation. All Default motion-control strengths/speeds are zero, so the preset does not itself demonstrate the additional shader-time branches. Partial camera keys depend on inherited/default scene state and cannot be treated as complete independent render recipes.

**Shared formula semantics.** All three use the two previously documented Mandelbulb power variants, query-initialized orbit, optional Julia constant, scalar derivative update and a configurable early orbit-color window. Radius is measured before an orthogonal row-vector rotation; the trap uses post-rotation coordinates and that radius squared. Formula origin/axis domains and the Julia derivative interpretation still need independent validation. These examples introduce no new verified distance estimator, high-precision calculation or MPA-compatible recurrence.

**RFF adoption.** RFF already has timeline/video infrastructure; adding a generic timeline is not the proposal. For the environment-reflection feature, route orientation, strength and any intended roughness animation through its existing frame-time evaluation and persistence contracts. Evaluate one resolved parameter state per output frame (or explicitly defined temporal subsample), reuse it across tiles, and keep playback wall-clock time separate from export time. For periodic angles and palettes, define wrap/turn behavior; for nonperiodic material values define admissible ranges when an easing curve overshoots. These are implementation requirements inferred from the split host/shader mechanisms, not functionality verified in these tutorial files. Audit existing RFF interpolation and parameter coverage before claiming any missing easing or track type.

**Validation and evidence.** Compare scrubbing, preview, resumed rendering and deterministic frame export with the same parameter state; distinguish intended formula morphing from layer movement. Resolve partial keyframes explicitly and test constant camera/moving target independently if a future 3D relief camera mode uses focus. No animation parser, shader, playback or video export was executed in this batch, and no external reference/license verification was performed. This supports the usability and reproducibility of proposed RFF shader features, without changing their provisional appearance priorities.

## TGlad examples: hexagonal domain reduction and a rational angular map

**Complete reads:** `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/TGlad/SphereTree.frag` (139 inventory lines, one preset) and Tetrahedral.frag (190, two presets). Folder placement identifies the collection, but original author/license documentation must still be resolved before copying distinctive formulas. No code was adapted.

**SphereTree mechanism.** PackRatio and Rotated determine an inner sphere, an outer buffer, an inversion/shift scale and a terminal sphere. Each step tests early inside/outside conditions, then either performs a sphere inversion or combines inversion with a Z shift/reflection, uniform scale and optional 30-degree XY rotation. Both branches accumulate the inversion's squared-radius factor; the scaled branch additionally divides the accumulator by its scale. XY is then reduced through oblique coordinates modulo one, a triangular fold and a nearest-region kite fold, while the transformed height is restored. The final sphere residual is multiplied by the accumulated factor. This is a nonlinear inverse-domain construction, not an ordinary list of independent sphere instances.

PackRatio zero makes the shift expression singular, and a zero query radius makes inversion undefined. The first step uses a special maxH of -100 whereas later steps use 0.4, so it cannot be replaced with an identical repeated body without preserving that branch. Source comments call early exits 'definitely' inside/outside; this local file supplies no general proof across the full PackRatio range. The preset only specifies six iterations and omits PackRatio/Rotated, whose effective values depend on host defaults or retained state. No orbitTrap assignment exists in the local field.

**2D transfer.** The oblique-lattice modulo and kite-domain reduction can inform an optional hexagonal motif layer. Its seams need consistent motif orientation and filtered coverage; retaining only fractional coordinates discards cell identity unless explicitly recorded. The complete sphere-tree map generally changes Z, so deleting Z does not preserve it. A full fixed-Z slice or a newly specified planar inversion pattern are distinct options. A RFF layer should separate the repeat-domain transform from its terminal motif, preserving existing high-precision Mandelbrot navigation rather than warping the fractal's reference coordinates.

**Tetrahedral mechanism.** The active recurrence normalizes the orbit direction, maps it to a complex plane with XY/(1-Z), evaluates a rational function with a degree-four numerator and degree-three denominator, then maps back to a unit sphere and multiplies by the original radius squared. It adds JuliaC or the original query. The rational map supplies angular structure; it is not the exposed Power-controlled Mandelbulb from the copied header. Power, AlternateVersion and ColorIterations are unused in the active recurrence. init computes a rotation using RotAngle+10*time, but DE never applies that matrix. No local trap update exists. Thus these declarations and the preset named Octobulb do not demonstrate animated rotation, power variation or orbit coloring.

The scalar dr update accounts for radial quadratic growth but does not explicitly propagate the rational angular map's differential. Treat the returned 0.5*r*log(r)/dr as an estimate requiring independent analysis, not an exact distance or gradient bound. Origin normalization, the projection pole and rational denominator zeros require defined behavior. A rational-function pattern could be evaluated directly in a RFF layer's complex coordinates, with domain coloring or masks and appropriate pole/seam filtering; that is different from restricting the full radial/angular recurrence to a plane. An XY input plane is not generally preserved by the inverse sphere map, so all components must be retained for a true slice.

**RFF value and validation.** The useful ideas are reusable hexagonal domain transforms and independently defined complex rational motifs, both optional sources for existing materials/relief. Validate coordinate seams, singularities, transformed footprints and intended parameter effects before exposing controls. The two Tetrahedral presets differ in inactive values as well as camera/rendering settings; they are not evidence that those controls work. No shader build, geometry/bound test, rendering, benchmark or external provenance/license check was performed. These exploratory patterns remain below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in immediate priority.

## Primitive fields: reusable 2D masks with explicit repetition semantics

**Scope and evidence.** Read the complete [primitives.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/primitives.frag), including its sole `ggg` preset. This imported reference supplies sphere, capped cylinder, torus, box, triangular prism, hexagonal prism and tubular XY-grid fields. It is a source of optional mask/relief ideas, not evidence that RFF lacks every comparable shape feature. The reviewed RFF [effects helper](../shdsrc/effects.glsl) already applies iteration-cycle and gradient-strength masks; a new primitive field should integrate with existing layer composition rather than create a separate shading system.

**Mechanism and field meaning.** The sphere is length(pos)-rad; abs(pos) does not change that length. Cylinder and box combine outside Euclidean distance with a negative interior term, while the torus measures distance to a circle in the radial/Z plane. The triangular prism uses a maximum of plane expressions, which does not supply the exact outside-corner Euclidean distance. The hexagonal prism reflects XY into a wedge, measures distance to a bounded segment, then combines that signed result with the Z cap. The grid computes distance to the nearest X or Y grid line and combines it with Z before subtracting the tube radius. These fields can share a coverage interface, but their exact-distance properties must not be assumed identical.

**Repetition is a coordinate operation.** Repeat centers each XY coordinate in a periodic cell and then applies abs; Z repetition is commented out. That extra reflection can change an asymmetric motif. Clamp separately subtracts clampd times a clamped rounded cell index. Here clampd is spacing and repeat3d.xy are index bounds; in Repeat, repeat3d.xy are spacing instead. Both switches can execute sequentially. The axis-angle row-vector rotation occurs afterward, rotating the shape coordinates inside the repeated domain rather than rotating the entire lattice. rotB is computed from the three Rotation controls but never consumed; hexPr2 is also unused. RFF should expose spacing, finite cell count and motif/lattice rotation as distinct meanings, and explicitly choose whether to preserve mirror folding.

**Concrete 3D-to-2D transfer.** Add independently defined disk, annulus, rectangle, polygon and grid mask sources only where they add to the existing layer catalog. A native 2D signed field gives useful border width, soft coverage and optional relief height without marching rays. A fixed-Z slice of a 3D field is a different contract: its zero contour may be useful, but its negative interior distance can be constrained by an off-plane cap and need not equal the native planar signed distance. Preserve high-precision fractal coordinates when selecting a fractal-anchored field; screen/layer coordinates are simpler for decorative overlays. Define transformed pixel footprints before wrapping, filter coverage at seams and thin borders, and use full-output coordinates for tile consistency.

**Integration safeguards.** The source's Boolean shape tests return the first enabled shape in sphere/cylinder/torus/box/prism/hexPr/grid order; they do not form a union. No fallback return is written when none is selected. The sole preset chooses only box, zero rotation and no repetition, so it does not exercise most operations. A RFF implementation should use an explicit shape selector or separately specified composition operators, valid positive spacing, defined degenerate extents and a valid rotation axis. The original file links Inigo Quilez's distance-functions page; the recognizable constants and formulas require original-source/license verification and matching NOTICE attribution before adaptation. No source code has been copied into RFF and no visual/performance test was performed. This is a secondary authoring feature, below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in immediate priority.

## Variable inner folds: directional and iteration-dependent pattern controls

**Scope.** Read the complete [aboxMinR2Bias-6.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/aboxMinR2Bias-6.frag) and [aboxMinR2Cuboid-2.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/aboxMinR2Cuboid-2.frag), including both Default presets. The transferable idea is controlling a repeated fold's inner region by query direction or axis-dependent extents. These are optional procedural pattern sources, not changes to RFF's Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA.

**Bias variant: two distinct dependencies.** Before the loop, temp3 = MinR2 + dot(optional_abs(pos),biasScale)/length(pos). Thus the initial query direction controls the inner squared-radius threshold; the current orbit does not continuously recompute this directional bias. Each iteration box-folds p3, obtains its squared radius, and optionally evolves actualMinR2 = temp3 + varyMinR2Scale*(abs(actualMinR2)-varyMinR2Offset) during the half-open Start/Stop interval. At and after Stop, the most recent actualMinR2 is retained. The running threshold is initialized from temp3, so an empty interval retains that initial value. The fold scale uses MaxR2/minR2 inside the threshold and MaxR2/r2 in the surrounding region, multiplied by Scale. Rotation follows the fold-radius query; the next state adds cJulia and the original query multiplied componentwise by c3Mul. This provides independently controllable directional asymmetry and iteration-window variation, rather than a single animated radius.

**Cuboid variant: axis-dependent region and scaling.** After the same box fold, temp3 is abs(p3), or its componentwise square when z2 is enabled. If every component is below limitMinR2, First is the minimum of limitMinR2/component, minR2 becomes min(r2*First,MaxR2), and the scale is multiplied by MaxR2/minR2. Otherwise the outer radial fold applies below MaxR2. The z2 switch changes both membership and the scale ratios. In the unsquared mode, r2*First is not the squared distance to the ordinary ray/cuboid intersection, which would involve First squared; the comments must not substitute for the written formula. Treat this as a deliberately specified pattern map until its geometric interpretation and differential are independently established. The preset selects unsquared mode and unequal extents 0.2/0.4/0.4.

**Color-channel timing matters.** Both variants update orbitTrap during ColorIterations using the post-transform XYZ state but the squared radius measured before scaling/rotation/translation. This mixed-stage statistic can create useful color variation, but it is not a four-channel measurement of a single state. A RFF auxiliary layer should label the channels by their actual sample stage, keep geometry iteration count independent from the color window, and avoid changing established iteration-map meanings.

**2D adaptation and precision.** A new planar recurrence can retain XY folds, planar rotation, direction-based bias and an iteration window, with a defined origin fallback. A faithful slice instead evaluates the full 3D recurrence; restricting the state to XY is equivalent only when rotation and added constants preserve Z=0. Even in that case, the cuboid implementation explicitly divides by the Z component, so merely setting Z=0 is not a robust native 2D implementation. Define the planar region and its two-axis ratios directly. Such fields could modulate existing color, roughness or relief masks; they do not justify replacing high-precision Mandelbrot computation with float coordinates.

**Adoption gates, not a GMT repair proposal.** Both files use Dd = Dd*abs(m)+1 and return length(p3)/abs(Dd) only on bailout. That scalar recurrence does not explicitly propagate all derivatives of a spatially varying inner threshold, nor the actual c3Mul contribution; it is not by itself proof of a conservative Euclidean distance bound or a correct relief gradient. Define an interior/non-escaping result, origin/zero-axis behavior, positive valid thresholds and finite scale values before using the fields. For relief, independently verify the gradient away from fold boundaries and apply a coverage/filter policy at discontinuities. The sources credit mclarekin's sphere-fold variations and Buddhi's estimator, with historical Mandelbox references; trace their actual licenses before copying distinctive implementations. No compilation, numerical derivative test, render comparison, timing or external license verification was performed. These pattern controls remain lower priority than improving the existing environment reflection and palette sampling.

## Cylindrical orbit wrapping and sign-conditioned constants

**Scope.** Fully read [abox inCyl-10.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/abox%20inCyl-10.frag) and [aboxMod14a.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/aboxMod14a.frag), including their single presets. These references suggest optional coordinate/pattern operations for RFF, rather than a replacement for its fractal engine.

**Cylindrical wrapping is not reciprocal inversion.** inCyl first applies an absolute-value box fold, a radial factor clamp(max(MinRad2/r2,MinRad2),0,1), scale Scale/MinRad2, rotation and query/Julia additions. At exactly iterA or iterB it maps (x,y,z) to ScaleInv*(x*cos(y*ScaleY),x*sin(y*ScaleY),z*ScaleZ). The name/header should not obscure that this is a signed-radius/angle cylindrical map, without a reciprocal-radius operation in this added stage. Equal event indices execute the stage once because the condition uses logical OR. The preset activates consecutive iterations 5 and 6, with ScaleY about 0.316 and ScaleInv 0.8; its ColorIterations is only 3, so its explicit trap window does not directly record those later wrapped states.

**Useful planar form and differential.** The XY part can be a native 2D domain transform for a motif layer: one coordinate becomes signed radius and the other an angle. Away from degeneracies, its Jacobian columns are ScaleInv*(cos(a),sin(a)) and ScaleInv*x*ScaleY*(-sin(a),cos(a)); they are orthogonal and have magnitudes abs(ScaleInv) and abs(ScaleInv*x*ScaleY). Thus a single constant scale cannot describe its sampling footprint. In 3D the Z scale adds abs(ScaleInv*ScaleZ). A RFF implementation should propagate the actual footprint or evaluate suitable neighboring samples, especially where angular detail becomes dense. The example updates Dd only by abs(ScaleInv) for this stage, which does not capture these variable/anisotropic factors. A planar transform is straightforward; a slice of the full recurrence still needs the full state unless rotation and constants preserve the plane.

**Sign-conditioned constants.** Mod14a box-folds XZ and optionally Y (Asurf skips Y), applies a conditional radial scale, captures an orbit trap, applies global scale, then adds query-derived and Julia constants before rotation. Its radial multiplier is 1/invMin below invMin, 1/r2 below invMax, and 1/invMax outside. Thus its outer branch is a constant scale, not necessarily identity. pSign adds sign(current p)*abs(scaleP0*query) instead of scaleP0*query. JCSignP uses the sign after that first addition; JCSignP0 instead uses the initial query sign and has lower precedence. This gives different symmetry controls, not interchangeable Boolean aliases. A RFF motif could expose query symmetry and current-state symmetry separately, with a declared order; sign-zero behavior and discontinuities must be intentional.

**Validity and evidence limits.** inCyl uses the pre-radial-fold r2 for bailout while returning the final state's length/Dd, and has no return after exhausting its loop. Mod14a's loop condition reads an uninitialized outer rr while the body declares a different local rr; its written source therefore cannot demonstrate reliable bailout behavior. Its sole preset disables all added constants and rotation, and selects invMin zero. These are adoption gates for a separately specified RFF pattern, not a request to repair GMT. Initialize state, define non-escape results and singular cases, and derive any distance/gradient contract independently. Source comments identify darkbeam/mclarekin, Buddhi/Rrrola, Tom Lowe and conditional-inversion references; their actual licensing still needs verification before code reuse. No compile, numerical differential test, render or benchmark was performed. These optional patterns do not displace environment reflection or dense-palette filtering as immediate priorities.

## Color trials: separate orbit statistics, palette evaluation and reduction

**Scope.** Read all of [AboxColourTrial_mcl_1.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/AboxColourTrial_mcl_1.frag), its complete Default preset, and its 448-line [DE-RaytracerColour.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/DE-RaytracerColour.frag) consumer. The useful RFF extension is explicit composition of orbit-derived scalar fields and intentional reduction semantics, while retaining RFF's established palette/material infrastructure.

**What is actually accumulated.** Each formula iteration builds ColorValue from enabled weighted statistics: radius (optionally divided by Dd), squared orbit/query radius, sphere difference, Dd, maximum/minimum absolute component, a box-related component maximum, per-axis terms and query-dependent cross terms. DistEst adds Dd itself, not the returned length(p3)/abs(Dd). XYZbias switches choose a squared coordinate when noXYZbiasAbs is true and an absolute coordinate otherwise; they do not simply toggle signed/unsigned coordinates. Sphere difference uses the post-update squared radius RR, but its two conditional multipliers compare sphereR2 against the earlier r2. BoxTrap uses max(limitsBox - selected_coordinates), not a general signed box distance. Names should identify these authored statistics rather than imply geometric distance.

**Composition order.** Optional cosine remapping precedes division by i*i+1, addition of i, division by Dd and final scalar scaling. Despite the divideI label, the implemented denominator is quadratic in the iteration index. The resulting scalar is mapped to RGB before temporal/orbit reduction. minValueMode takes componentwise minima of abs(vec4(paletteRGB*ToolXYZ,0.1*ToolW)) within ColorIterations; the other mode keeps the last eligible iteration's vector without abs. These are not equivalent to finding the minimum scalar and evaluating its palette once. RGB minima can combine different iterations into a color absent from the palette. The last eligible iteration also need not be the terminal orbit iteration when the color window is shorter. A RFF control should distinguish scalar-minimum, last-sample and componentwise-color-minimum modes rather than hide the choice behind a generic minimum setting.

**Palette implementation versus prose.** The header describes cosine interpolation and recommends a lookup table, but that interpolation block is commented out. Active code linearly interpolates between ColorBase and five stops using independently evaluated interval tests. Values at or above the final stop retain ColorBase, rather than clamp to Color5. Negative values can extrapolate in the first interval. The preset's ColDist3 (12.03319) exceeds ColDist4 (11.61826), creating overlapping active intervals and later-branch overwrite; it is not a monotonic six-stop gradient example. scaleColorBase is declared and serialized but unused. RFF should reuse its validated palette representation, specify clamp/repeat behavior and interpolation space, and avoid copying this ad hoc interval logic. A lookup table is not a newly missing RFF capability, and ordinary linear interpolation alone does not solve dense-pattern aliasing.

**Consumer and query-state contract.** getColor blends the legacy weighted orbit color with orbitTrap2.xyz*orbitTrap2.w using NewColor, then blends BaseColor with three times that result using OrbitStrength. The renderer resets orbitTrap at trace entry and each march step, but never resets orbitTrap2 inside these functions. The formula's global compound scale state also is not reset at DE entry. Normal reconstruction calls DE six more times before getColor; AO and shadow queries invoke it later, and a reflection trace repeats the process. Consequently, a straightforward adaptation must not assume material color belongs exclusively to the final surface query. In RFF, keep per-query orbit/color state local, return the required statistics explicitly, and evaluate or cache color for the intended sample independently of normal/AO/visibility queries. The default preset's varyScale zero masks the compound-state issue; it does not establish correctness for varying scale.

**Geometry and renderer details relevant to transfer.** standardMode chooses its radial factor from p3 before reverseOffset, but applies that factor after adding the offset, then subtracts it. This is not the same as measuring radius about the shifted center. Variable scale uses Scale+compound and updates compound for the next iteration within a half-open window; mode1 replaces it with -vary, while the other branch subtracts vary. Bailout still uses the earlier r2, and no non-escaping return is written. The renderer uses distance-scaled hit tolerance, six central-difference normal samples, five weighted normal-direction AO offsets, fog and at most one reflection blend. Its QualityShadows branch computes three perturbed directions but uses sdir2 for both additional marches; the third direction is unused. These are reasons to specify and verify a new RFF implementation, not reasons to port this renderer. RFF already has surface lighting and AO; its 2D relief does not acquire 3D scene visibility merely by adopting the coloring idea.

**Practical 2D recommendation.** Start with combinations of fields already available to the RFF shading path and permit those fields to drive color or material masks. New per-iteration orbit statistics require deliberate support in the fractal computation/map path; they cannot generally be reconstructed from a stored escape count alone. Preserve perturbation precision, compression and MPA semantics, and measure the added memory/computation before promising interactive controls. Where only palette mapping changes, keep it a shading-only update. Validate sample-stage definitions, independent color windows, degenerate denominators, palette ordering and preview/video/tile consistency. Original comments attribute the trial to mclarekin and some controls to Mandelbulber; retain/verify provenance before adapting distinctive code. No shader build, render, numerical test or external license check was performed. This strengthens the previously proposed field-driven material controls but does not establish a measured improvement or a new top priority.

## Bounded surface folds and four-dimensional auxiliary patterns

**Scope.** Fully read [darkbeam_surfbox.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/darkbeam_surfbox.frag), [darkbeam_MixPinski.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/darkbeam_MixPinski.frag) and [Aexions_TetraBox2.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/Aexions_TetraBox2.frag). None contains a preset block. The first suggests a compact 2D coordinate-warp control; the others illustrate how a 2D image can sample a higher-dimensional auxiliary field without reducing its state dimension.

**SurfBox: cap fold displacement instead of blending results.** For each component, the shader computes the standard absolute-value box fold T, then subtracts sign(p)*min(abs(p-T),foldMod) from p. For nonnegative fold extent a and cap b, this can be written as p-sign(p)*min(2*max(abs(p)-a,0),b). Its positive-axis intervals are identity below a, reflection 2*a-p from a to a+b/2, and translation p-b beyond that. Thus b=0 disables that axis; a sufficiently large cap reproduces the ordinary fold over a bounded coordinate range. A finite value such as 2000 is not a global equivalence on an unbounded domain. For positive a,b the branches meet continuously and have slope magnitude one away from their boundaries. This is a displacement cap, not an interpolation weight between the original and folded positions. The source permits negative fold extents too; the simplified positive-extent interpretation must not be extended to those settings without analysis.

**RFF application.** Expose independently bounded XY folding as an optional transform of an existing pattern/image layer, with axis extents, displacement caps and explicit transform order. It can create folded or translated strips while leaving the underlying Mandelbrot calculation intact. Evaluate the transformed footprint and antialias the resulting motif, especially when a pixel spans a fold boundary; a single local derivative cannot represent both sides of that boundary. Keep screen/layer-space controls distinct from deep-zoom fractal anchoring. RFF's palette/image/filter infrastructure remains the destination, not the entire SurfBox fractal renderer.

The surrounding SurfBox recurrence captures its trap immediately after the surface fold, then performs a radial fold, variable scale, rotation and query/Julia additions. Its compound scale state is global and is not reset at DE entry; a reusable RFF field must initialize its own recurrence state on every query. Bailout tests the earlier squared radius, and the function has no return when the loop exhausts. The scalar DEtweak update does not establish the complete derivative of arbitrary query multipliers. These implementation details bound what can be inferred from the example; no distance-bound or render-quality claim follows merely from its fold formula.

**MixPinski: ordered 4D reflections and a terminal box field.** The state starts as (query.xyz,w). Six tests reflect across pair-sum planes in the written XY, XZ, YZ, XW, YW, ZW order; later tests see earlier updates. It scales by scaleS, adds offsetS, applies a scaleM/offsetM transform with a separate folded Z construction, then optionally rotates in six planes in XY,YZ,XZ,XW,YW,ZW order. The earlier rotation call is commented out. General plane rotations do not commute, so these controls should not be represented as order-independent orientation sliders. The full four-component squared length controls bailout; the terminal field instead uses max(abs(x),abs(y),abs(z),abs(w))-offsetD divided by abs(Dd). These are different norms for different jobs. The header's comment suggesting offsetD defaults to zero disagrees with its slider default of one; a terminal field offset also is not generally equivalent to changing ray-hit tolerance.

The trap is updated after rotation and only if the new radius has not already exceeded bailout. Therefore the escaping iteration is excluded from its color samples. Dd accumulates scaleS and scaleM, while the folded Z expression divides by scaleM; its allowed zero setting needs a separately defined limit or rejection. A 2D display can evaluate this full field on a fixed input plane, retaining Z/W throughout all folds and rotations. Removing those components would change pair tests, offsets, bailout and the terminal field. A newly designed planar fold pattern is another valid feature, but should be named separately rather than advertised as an identical port.

**TetraBox2: folded tetrahedral embedding, not a three-component orbit.** The initial query becomes CT = abs(abs(A*query)-CToffset), where the four rows of A have signs (+++), (--+), (-+-), (+--). Before the absolute-value branches, A has orthogonal columns of squared length four, so its Euclidean scale factor is two. The recurrence box-folds all four components, measures rr, adds offsetSph, applies the rr-selected radial scale, subtracts offsetSph, scales all components, rotates only XYZ and adds CT. The radial decision is measured before offsetSph; it is not simply a sphere inversion centered at that offset. The repeated addition is the folded CT rather than the raw query.

Its scalar dd starts at one and uses dd*Scale+1 after the radial multiplier. This does not explicitly account for the embedding's scale factor or all spatial dependencies of the shifted radial construction. A correct shading gradient or conservative distance bound therefore requires a separate derivation. The source returns length(z)/dd and has a fixed squared-radius bailout of 10000; neither establishes a planar signed-distance field. RFF can use a full 4D slice as an optional pattern source, retaining the four-component state and explicit slice parameters, without modifying perturbation or MPA.

**Trap-channel meaning must survive the port.** TetraBox2 takes componentwise minima of four absolute signed combinations of abs(z). These are directional linear-combination statistics, not XYZ minima plus a squared radius. The included [DE-Raytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Include/DE-Raytracer.frag) nevertheless square-roots orbitTrap.w in getColor. A RFF port should label and remap each statistic explicitly; inheriting a generic radius-channel conversion would silently alter the fourth channel. Expose these optional fields to the existing material-mask system only with their reduction window and value range documented.

**Priority and verification.** Bounded planar folding is the smaller and more direct transfer. Higher-dimensional motifs have greater computation and authoring cost and should be evaluated as optional layers, below the current environment-reflection and dense-palette-filtering priorities. Verify boundary continuity, coordinate anchoring, dimension-preserving slice behavior, query-local state and preview/video/tile agreement. The source headers identify DarkBeam, mclarekin, Aexion, M3D and earlier estimator authors; verify actual source licensing and update NOTICE before adapting distinctive code. This batch performs source analysis only: no shader compilation, numerical validation, visual comparison, benchmark or external provenance verification was performed.

## SphereBox and Menger variants: embedding scale, rotation order and reusable schedules

**Scope.** Read all of [AexionnSphereBoxRot4D.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/AexionnSphereBoxRot4D.frag), [menge4 4D rot-1.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/menge4%204D%20rot-1.frag) and [menger3_1.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/menger3_1.frag), including their two, two and one presets respectively. The useful RFF ideas are full-state planar slices, separate transform stages and deterministic iteration schedules for optional procedural layers.

**SphereBox's radial fourth coordinate.** The initial state and repeatedly added constant are CT=(query.xyz,length(query)). This differs from TetraBox2's folded linear embedding. Away from the origin, the embedding's Jacobian has J-transpose*J = I + u*u-transpose, with u the normalized query, giving singular values sqrt(2),1,1. The origin needs a separate derivative convention. A scalar derivative initialized to one and increased by one for CT addition does not explicitly represent this embedding's largest differential. The orbit box-folds four components, selects a radial multiplier from rr before adding offsetSph, applies that multiplier to the shifted state, subtracts offsetSph, scales, rotates XYZ, optionally performs six ordered 4D plane rotations, then adds CT. A shifted radial operation is therefore not automatically an inversion about the shifted center.

SphereBox's terminal radius is the full 4D length, with a length-based bailout of 1000 and four directional combination traps captured before bailout. Both presets disable the optional 4D rotation; fgf uses a nonzero XYZ rotation and both use nonzero sphere offsets. They do not validate the W-plane rotation controls. With zero iterations, r remains its initialized zero although the initial state need not be zero. RFF should define zero-iteration and singular-parameter behavior when specifying an auxiliary field, rather than adopting this incidental result. A 2D slice still needs the radial W coordinate and all subsequent four-component operations; setting W to zero or dropping it changes the pattern.

**Menger4: sorted coordinates are not fixed spatial axes.** The state starts as (query.xyz,w). During a half-open iteration window it adds PreAddM, then takes abs and sorts all four components into descending order through six swaps. Optional 4D rotation follows sorting and precedes scaling/offset. X, Y and W receive scaleM*z-offsetM; Z uses a folded construction centered on opt2=0.5*offsetM.z/scaleM before scaling. offsetM here is already the subtracted offset; unlike MixPinski, it is not multiplied by scaleM-1. The six plane rotations have the same explicit XY,YZ,XZ,XW,YW,ZW order, but moving them across sorting or translation changes the recurrence.

Despite the four-component orbit, Menger4 measures bailout and its returned numerator using XYZ only. W still influences subsequent sorting, rotation and color, so omitting it because the terminal norm ignores it is invalid. Dd multiplies signed scaleM and is used without abs in the return; negative scale can change the returned sign with iteration parity, while zero scale also enters opt2's denominator. There is no final return for a non-escaping orbit. These prevent treating its written expression as a validated unsigned distance bound. The vvv preset disables rotation; bbb enables all six angles. bbb also opens a pre-add window but leaves PreAddM zero, so that window makes no numerical change in the supplied preset. Neither preset tests negative/zero scale.

**Menger3: the scale schedule is local and independent of position.** Each query initializes addScale=0 and Dd=1. It pre-rotates, takes abs, sorts XYZ, scales by Scale+addScale and accumulates abs(useScale) into Dd. It then updates the next iteration's addScale using vary=scaleVary*(abs(addScale)-scaleOffset), either replacing it with -vary or subtracting vary. A second rotation follows scaling, then Offset is subtracted and Z receives Offset.z when it lies below -0.5*Offset.z. This last coordinate selection has a jump for nonzero Offset.z; smoothness of a final scalar must be assessed separately, rather than inferred from the local coordinate map. The trap captures the resulting XYZ and squared radius. Its bailout compares squared radius, and the return is sqrt(rr)/(Dd+DEtweak), including when no loop executes. DEtweak is an additive terminal denominator adjustment, not a propagated differential term.

**RFF application and bounded optimization opportunity.** Keep pre-fold rotation, post-fold rotation and offsets as distinct layer operations with documented order. For a separately implemented variable-scale motif, its scale sequence depends only on settings and iteration index. It could be prepared once per immutable frame/settings snapshot and reused across pixel queries; early-escaping queries consume a prefix. This avoids persistent cross-query recurrence state and may avoid repeated schedule arithmetic. It is only a candidate optimization: a short sequence may be cheaper to recompute than to fetch, and moving floating-point evaluation between CPU/GPU or changing precision/order needs output validation. Do not modify RFF's precision-sensitive perturbation or MPA based on this analogy. A 2D motif should have an explicitly planar recurrence, while a faithful slice retains every component that sorting, constants or rotation can bring back into the visible result.

**Material-channel and sampling contract.** SphereBox and Menger4 use minima of four signed combinations of abs(state), rather than XYZ plus squared radius. Their fourth channel must not silently inherit the common renderer's square-root radius conversion when brought into RFF. Menger3 does use squared radius for that channel. Label these statistics and their iteration windows explicitly before routing them into color, roughness or relief. Define a transformed pixel footprint and behavior at sorting/fold boundaries; additional fractal detail is not useful if it aliases during animation or tiled export.

**Priority and evidence limits.** These files refine optional pattern-layer architecture and validation; they do not supersede environment reflection or dense-palette filtering as immediate improvements to existing RFF images. Verify slice definitions, embedding derivatives, valid parameter domains, fixed-state determinism and preview/export agreement before implementation. Headers identify Aexion, Darkbeam/M3D, mclarekin, Knighty's kaleidoscopic IFS and Buddhi's estimator; actual licensing remains to be traced before copying distinctive code and recording it in NOTICE. No shader compilation, numerical derivative/bound test, rendering, performance measurement or external license verification was performed.

## Delta-distance examples: numerical probes are not automatically reliable relief gradients

**Scope.** Fully read [mengerDeltaAnalytic.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/mengerDeltaAnalytic.frag), including its three presets, and [msltoe riemann_DeltaDE.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/msltoe%20riemann_DeltaDE.frag), including its Default preset. The RFF lesson is to separate an orbit-radius sensitivity estimate, a distance estimate and a signed surface gradient. These are useful validation references, not a recommendation to add seven full fractal evaluations to every RFF shading sample.

**Exact finite-probe mechanism.** Both evaluate a center orbit and six axis-offset orbits. Let F(p) be the length of the returned orbit state and h=max(length(p)*1e-6,0.1*the_scale_control). Each component is min(abs(F(p+h*axis)-F(p)),abs(F(p-h*axis)-F(p)))/h, and dr is the Euclidean length of those three nonnegative values. This is neither the signed central difference (Fplus-Fminus)/(2*h) nor the full orbit Jacobian. It selects the smaller one-sided change independently on each axis. At a smooth point with sufficiently small h it can approximate derivative magnitudes; at folds, differing bailout counts or cancellation it has no general conservative-bound guarantee. In particular, underestimating dr increases the returned distance. Discarded derivative signs mean this vector cannot be used directly as a relief normal.

Menger returns F/dr in DeltaDE mode, versus F/(Dd+DEtweak) in its scalar mode. The Riemann example returns 0.5*F*log(F)/dr. The logarithmic factor is an additional estimator assumption, not a consequence of numerically estimating dr; the two modes are not interchangeable. Zero h, zero dr, nonfinite orbits and the logarithm's domain need explicit handling. A negative scale control does not provide a positive step floor at the origin. The Riemann preset chooses DEScale=2, which gives a minimum h of 0.2 in query-space units, not a tiny relative perturbation. It cannot be presented as evidence of fine-scale derivative accuracy.

**Iteration and color semantics.** Every probe independently follows its own bailout path, so neighboring samples can return different iteration depths. Both DE1 helpers also mutate orbitTrap; the wrapper does not preserve a center-only trap while performing six probes. Its color may therefore combine neighboring orbit statistics rather than exclusively describe the center. RFF should keep derivative probes free of material-state side effects, or explicitly return separate statistics and use the intended center sample. If a numerical reference is intended to check a fixed-depth analytic derivative, lock that depth and compare the same mathematical function, then test bailout boundaries separately. A fixed-depth check is a validation technique, not permission to change a user's rendering semantics silently.

**Menger comparison limits.** DE1 uses abs and XYZ sorting, scalar Scale, conditional Z offset and a row-vector rotation, accumulating Dd as the product of Scale. Its scalar return adds DEtweak only after the recurrence. All three presets select DeltaDE=false; none provides a paired numerical-versus-scalar comparison. DEtweak is ignored in DeltaDE mode, so a toggle can change both derivative handling and denominator adjustment. A meaningful RFF comparison must isolate the intended change with the same scene, output dimensions and all other settings fixed. The written arithmetic is seven orbit evaluations per DeltaDE call rather than one, but runtime is not necessarily seven times greater because iteration counts and GPU execution differ. The common ray renderer can call DE repeatedly for normals, AO and shadows, multiplying this cost further.

**Riemann orbit structure.** The helper begins with query radius r, normalizes/scales z by scale/r, then projects with s=x/(1-z.z), t=y/(1-z.z). It computes exponent p=1+s*s+t*t before replacing s and t with abs(sin(pi*s+ssh)) and abs(sin(pi*t+tsh)). The radial update is -0.25+pow(r*r,p). It maps the modified plane coordinates back through (2*s,2*t,-1+s*s+t*t)/(1+s*s+t*t), multiplies by that signed radial value, then adds shift. This is a direction-dependent power map with angular folding, not a fixed-power Mandelbulb. The origin and projection pole are singular; scale values other than one also mean the pre-projection state is not generally on the unit sphere. iter starts at one and runs while iter<imax, giving at most imax-1 updates. Color sampling uses that same one-based counter. The preset's imax=18 therefore permits at most 17 updates, and ColorIterations=9 permits eight trap updates.

**Concrete RFF transfer.** For an optional Riemann-like decorative field, a native 2D source can use explicitly defined stereographic/periodic coordinates with filtered coverage, or a full three-component recurrence can be sampled on an input plane. Dropping Z from the latter is not equivalent. For existing RFF relief, use the signed gradient of the actual height field being shaded; evaluate neighboring stored-field samples when appropriate, rather than rerun the high-precision orbit solely to imitate this estimator. An analytic gradient and an independent signed finite-difference reference can help validate a new auxiliary field away from discontinuities. Choose probe spacing in meaningful layer/output units, test convergence across several spacings, and preserve high-precision differences before conversion. Fragment and compute export paths need the same field definition and output-pixel scale.

**Evidence and priority.** The Riemann file uses DE-Kn2cr11 with volumetric, Eiffie-shadow and multisample-AO defines; its many lighting/cloud preset keys do not establish that all those features are active or suitable for RFF. Its very small FudgeFactor and large ray-step limit are author settings, not a benchmark demonstrating estimator quality. These examples strengthen the report's gradient-validation and field-filtering recommendations, but do not add a higher-priority appearance feature than environment reflection. Source comments identify Knighty, mclarekin, msltoe, sabine and Buddhi; actual source licenses still require verification before adapting distinctive code and recording provenance in NOTICE. No numerical convergence/derivative test, shader compilation, visual comparison, timing or external license check was performed in this batch.

## Polynomial prewarps and branch-history coloring

**Scope.** Fully read [PseudoKleinian_3D_Quaternion_Julia_1.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/PseudoKleinian_3D_Quaternion_Julia_1.frag), including Default and ex1, and [sym4_1.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/sym4_1.frag), including all five presets. The RFF opportunities are an optional polynomial domain prewarp and explicit fold-event statistics for material masks. Neither requires treating the supplied distance estimators as proven geometric distances.

**One prewarp followed by a different recurrence.** The PseudoKleinian file evaluates (x*x-y*y-z*z-wSeed, x*y, x*z), multiplies it componentwise by Quat_Scales, adds jC and adds the original query multiplied by origPtScale. This happens once, before the Kleinian loop. wSeed is a scalar subtraction in the first component; there is no evolving fourth quaternion component and no repeated quaternion Julia iteration. The default Quat_Scales=(1,2,2) supplies the doubled cross terms, but arbitrary scales change that map. Expose a RFF version as the explicitly specified polynomial prewarp, not as a complete 4D quaternion solver.

The following loop box-folds p with clamp, records a trap from that folded state, multiplies by max(Size/dot(p,p),1), and adds C. It terminates after MI iterations or when exact consecutive states compare equal. Its Dp multiplier uses k+0.05 rather than k. The terminal expression is max(rxy-PK_holes,abs(rxy*p.z)/r)/abs(Dp), where r still means the original query length; it is not recomputed from the final state. TThickness, DEoffset, Offset and the local USE_INF_NORM definition have no active role in this formula body. A RFF adaptation should retain only meaningful controls and explicitly define sample stages, terminal fields and stopping behavior.

**Prewarp differential and planar behavior.** The polynomial's Jacobian before axis scaling has rows (2*x,-2*y,-2*z), (y,x,0), (z,0,x). Compose it with Quat_Scales and add the diagonal origPtScale contribution to obtain the actual prewarp differential. The source's initialization Dp=2*length(query) does not express all arbitrary parameter choices. A planar input can remain planar when the Z constants in jC and C are zero; then its terminal p.z term vanishes and the max expression has a zero-valued disk interior for positive PK_holes, rather than a signed disk distance. The origin also enters divisions by r and Dp. These are important distinctions when deriving a relief height or mask: define a native 2D field and filtered coverage instead of interpreting the returned number as a ready-made signed distance. Default preserves that plane; ex1 has nonzero jC.z, so the same reduction does not apply.

**Sym4 coloring records fold events.** Each iteration scales the state by XYZscale and adds query*OrigPtOffset, then sorts components by absolute magnitude using three ordered swaps. On each swap it accumulates the negative magnitude difference times the corresponding ColFactor component into Col. It then aligns Y/Z signs with X, evaluates the quadratic map (x*x-y*y-z*z,2*x*y,2*x*z), adds JuliaOffset and rotates. The trap takes minima of abs(Col+z) and squared radius during ColorIterations. Thus these are weighted cumulative branch differences mixed with the current state, not counts of swaps or pure orbit-coordinate minima. Col updates are unconditional; the declared IterCol Boolean is never tested. time is also unused. All five presets serialize IterCol, but switching that value alone does not enable or disable the written effect.

**RFF transfer: expose branch history as its own field.** For a new auxiliary fold pattern, offer a separately named fold-event field, with an intentional choice among count, weighted branch displacement and current-state coordinate. Remap it into the existing color/roughness/relief mask system instead of silently adding it to coordinate channels. Preserve the color window and query-local initialization. For Sym4's planar form, keep the relevant sign alignment and swaps: it is not ordinary complex squaring merely because Z stays zero. A true slice with nonzero JuliaOffset.z or a rotation that mixes axes must retain all three components. Computing analogous history for the Mandelbrot engine would require new orbit statistics; it is not recoverable in general from an existing escape-count image and must preserve perturbation/MPA and map-format contracts.

**Derivative and preset limits.** Sym4 updates Dd by 2*r, then by the ratio of the scaled/translated state's length to the previous length. A radial length ratio is not generally a bound on an anisotropic or translated map's Jacobian, and the original-query addition has a spatial derivative of its own. Define origin and logarithmic-return behavior before using the result for normals or distance. Default has OrbitStrength=0, hiding the orbit-color contribution despite nonzero ColFactor values; basicSphere and the other presets use different visibility and geometry settings. They are not controlled comparisons proving the effect of IterCol or estimator accuracy. This batch performs source analysis only, with no rendering, compilation, numerical derivative test, benchmark or external license verification. The source headers credit Knighty, mclarekin, msltoe/Mandelbulb3D and linked formula discussions; verify actual licenses and record provenance before adaptation. These optional pattern/material features remain below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in immediate priority.

## Mixed powers: distinguish a weighted map from a valid derivative combination

**Scope.** Fully read [Mandelbulb_pwrs1234_ cosmix.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/Mandelbulb_pwrs1234_%20cosmix.frag) and [Mandelbulb_pwrs1234_sinmix.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/Mandelbulb_pwrs1234_sinmix.frag), including both presets in each file. Their useful authoring idea is a weighted blend of several maps evaluated from the same orbit state. This is a possible auxiliary pattern feature for RFF, not justification to generalize its precision-sensitive Mandelbrot engine without new mathematics.

**Parallel map evaluation, not composition.** In each iteration, enabled degree-two, degree-three and degree-four helpers receive the same input radius and angles. Their outputs and the degree-one identity term are multiplied by w8ts and summed; JuliaC and query*cPixelMul are added once afterward, then the result is rotated. This implements a sum of maps, not applying degree two, then three, then four in sequence. The weights can be negative and are not normalized, so the operation is not a convex blend and can strongly change cancellation, escape behavior and detail density. The trap records rotated XYZ with the radius squared measured just before that rotation; an orthogonal rotation preserves that radius mathematically.

**The two angle conventions produce different maps.** cosmix uses theta=acos(z.z/r), phi=atan(z.y,z.x) and reconstructs (sin(n*theta)*cos(n*phi),sin(n*theta)*sin(n*phi),cos(n*theta))*r^n. sinmix instead uses theta=asin(z.z/r) and reconstructs (cos(n*theta)*sin(n*phi),cos(n*phi)*cos(n*theta),sin(n*theta))*r^n. The sine/cosine order in XY is swapped as well as the polar convention. These must be documented as distinct definitions, not interchangeable implementations of a generic power operator. The first-degree term bypasses both helpers and uses z directly.

**Precise 2D transfer.** In the sinmix map, Z=0 remains zero for degrees two through four before offsets/rotation. For the conventional complex coordinate u=x+i*y, each such XY term is i*conjugate(u^n), not u^n. The degree-one term is still u. Thus an exactly matching planar recurrence can be written without spherical trigonometry, provided Julia/query additions and rotation preserve the plane and disabled terms have defined zero contributions. A new holomorphic polynomial sum of u^n would be a different, separately specified feature. In cosmix, even degrees generally generate a nonzero Z component from an XY input, so discarding Z does not reproduce a generic mixed-power slice. Evaluate the full 3D state for that slice. Neither set of supplied presets demonstrates a plane-preserving configuration: preset 24 uses three 90-degree rotations, while 13 uses a nonzero Y-axis rotation.

**Derivative contract.** Each higher-degree helper independently updates its scalar with n*r^(n-1)*dr+1, while the identity branch sets dr1=r. The wrapper adds these scalars with signed weights, adds DEoffset and takes abs. This is not the chain-rule derivative of the weighted vector map and not generally a conservative norm bound. In particular, signed scalar cancellation does not prove cancellation of the maps' Jacobians, and adding +1 separately in multiple helpers does not represent a single query-dependent addition with arbitrary cPixelMul. The angular maps also need their directional derivatives. For a new RFF field, derive the complete map differential, or an explicitly justified norm bound when distance stepping actually requires one. A planar non-holomorphic map needs a real 2-by-2 Jacobian or equivalent treatment of both complex and conjugate dependencies, not an ordinary holomorphic derivative alone.

**Validity and sample evidence.** z1/z2/z3/z4 are declared without initialization, and a disabled branch leaves its corresponding vector unset even though the final weighted sum reads every vector. Both presets disable two powers while retaining all weights at one. Accordingly, those presets are not reliable evidence of correctly isolated 2+4 or 1+3 mixtures as written. A RFF implementation should explicitly initialize each disabled contribution to zero. Define behavior for the origin, polar axes, inverse-trigonometric domain rounding, zero derivative and logarithmic return before exposing the controls. The preset's large ray-step limit is an author setting, not measured proof that the estimator converges or performs well.

**RFF priority and integration.** The reusable design is a small, explicit map-combination layer with named coordinate semantics, bounded settings and separate color/material outputs. If it only supplies an auxiliary pattern, keep it separate from Mandelbrot reference computation, MPA and existing saved iteration maps. New fractal formulas would require their own precision/perturbation support and compatibility design and are a substantially larger project. Filter the resulting high-frequency field using its actual output-pixel footprint and test parameter animation against fixed snapshots in preview and export. These exploratory patterns remain lower priority than environment reflection and dense-palette filtering. Headers credit mclarekin and work by 3DickUlus and sabine62; verify actual source licenses and add appropriate NOTICE provenance before adapting distinctive implementations. No shader compilation, numerical derivative test, visual comparison, benchmark or external license verification was performed.

## Scheduled powers and evolving constants: model the state explicitly

**Scope.** Fully read [Mandelbulb_messC.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/Mandelbulb_messC.frag), including four preset blocks, and [Mandelbulb_plus.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/mclarekin/Mandelbulb_plus.frag), including seven presets. Their transferable ideas are iteration-indexed map schedules and explicit memory of prior orbit states for optional RFF patterns. These are separate from parameter animation over wall-clock time: both declare time but do not use it.

**messC's evolving constant.** The query initializes both z and C. Before SwapIter, Mbulb1 creates a fresh local Ztemp=0 on every call. If i==CIter it first clears C using that zero value; only afterward, when i>=ZtempIter, it copies the incoming z into Ztemp. It applies the first spherical power and adds the current C, then assigns C=Ztemp for the next iteration. Consequently, before the capture threshold C is replaced by zero, and afterward it holds the preceding input orbit state. CIter clears the addition for that particular iteration; it is not a persistent clear of the next stored value. At SwapIter the second helper begins using the captured C multiplied by CScale, without updating C further. Global declarations named C and Ztemp do not supply the active memory in these functions; the local/inout variables do.

**Derivative consequence.** Both helpers use a radial scalar recurrence with +1 for the additive term. Here that term may be zero, the original query, an earlier orbit state or a frozen captured state with a nontrivial spatial derivative. A correct differential needs the state pair (z,C) and their derivatives, including the capture/reset operation. For example, a reset sets the current addition's derivative to zero, while capturing an orbit state stores that state's derivative for subsequent use. This is a concrete reason not to transplant a familiar Mandelbulb scalar DE update into a stateful map unchanged. A RFF layer should use an explicitly initialized state object and immutable per-frame schedule, not implicit global storage.

**Preset interpretation.** bnb stores SwapIter=19 even though the declaration's slider maximum is 10, with only 13 total iterations; the written recurrence would therefore never reach stage two if that value is retained. Whether a particular import UI clamps it is a separate host question. The two bmnn blocks share a name but use different stage-switch and power settings, so they are distinct serialized blocks, not independent uniquely named recipes. Preserve unambiguous recipe identity if adapting this authoring idea. The other examples use a two-iteration first stage and demonstrate different reset/capture relationships; their camera and color settings are not controlled estimator tests.

**plus: exponent and angular schedules.** Each iteration sets Power=Power0+i*PowerScale. The exponent can grow beyond the Power0 slider range or become nonpositive when PowerScale is negative; validate the actual executed sequence rather than just its initial value. The default helper adds betaAngleOffset to asin(z.z/r) and alphaAngleOffset to atan(y,x), then multiplies latitude by Power*thetaScale and longitude by Power. The alternate helper starts from acos(z.z/r) but still reconstructs with cosine in XY and sine in Z, so it is a different angular map rather than a cosmetic option. These angle offsets enter radian-valued expressions directly despite their -180..180 slider range; no local degree-to-radian conversion is present. RFF controls must declare their units and convert explicitly.

OrigPt is initialized as query*OrigPtScale. SignOrigPt multiplies by sign(query), making it abs(query)*OrigPtScale componentwise; it is not the current orbit's sign and it is not a squaring operation. The map adds JuliaC and this fixed query-derived term before rotation. Its derivative is anisotropic and, in signed mode, piecewise dependent on the original query sign. The scalar +1 update does not generally encode that derivative, latitude scaling or the alternate angular map. The first three presets omit the later angle/latitude controls, whereas later presets serialize them. Resolve omitted fields against the actual import/default policy before claiming standalone reproducibility; do not assume omission means zero for every setting, since thetaScale defaults to one.

**2D application.** messC's sine-latitude formulation preserves Z=0 when initialized on that plane. For integer powers and nonzero radius, its XY power is ordinary complex exponentiation, but the delayed/frozen additive state still makes it a different recurrence from standard Mandelbrot. In plus's default helper, betaAngleOffset zero, plane-preserving constants and rotation also permit a planar map; integer exponents avoid the azimuth branch ambiguity of fractional powers. Nonzero latitude offsets, arbitrary rotation or the alternate formula generally require retaining the full state for a faithful slice. A RFF procedural layer could expose a bounded two-stage recipe or exponent schedule, with clear reset/capture semantics and filtered output for color or material masks. Adding such a recurrence as a new deep-zoom fractal formula would instead require new precision, perturbation and approximation work; the existing MPA cannot be assumed compatible.

**Validation and priority.** Define origin/pole behavior, noninteger branch seams, zero/negative powers, logarithmic-return domains and derivative state. Compare schedules and saved recipes under identical preview/video/tile snapshots, and distinguish an auxiliary shader field from a new core fractal type. These are optional pattern features, below the established environment-reflection and dense-palette-filtering priorities. Source comments reference historical Mandelbulb code, mclarekin, Mandelbulber additions, Quilez and Enforcer; trace actual source licenses and record provenance before adapting distinctive code. No shader compilation, numerical derivative test, rendering, benchmark or external license verification was performed.

## Geode/PlanetEarth and cross-eyed rendering: separate the field from its camera

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [PlanetEarth.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/PlanetEarth.frag), [Geode.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Geode.frag), both Default presets, and Geode's complete [DE-Raytracer-XId.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/DE-Raytracer-XId.frag) and [3D-XId.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/3D-XId.frag) includes. This distinguishes the reusable field construction from stereo camera, accumulation and ray-renderer behavior.

**Same field, different setup.** PlanetEarth and Geode implement the same init/DE operations: scale=Scale/100, n1=normalize((-1,CY-1,1/CY-1)), n2=n1*(scale-1). Each iteration rotates XY, sorts the signed coordinates into descending order, rotates XZ then YZ, and applies scale*pos-n2. These swaps compare signed values, not absolute magnitudes; replacing them with a common abs/sort fold would change the field. Angles enter sin/cos directly in radians. PlanetEarth has a lower allowed scale range (including contraction), different angle/CY limits and a standard renderer include; Geode uses the XId renderer. The name PlanetEarth does not imply a geographic texture, terrain dataset or atmosphere implementation.

An iteration that exceeds radius four exits before recording its orbit trap. The final length is multiplied by scale^(-i). On an early exit at loop index i, i+1 transforms have executed; on normal exhaustion, i equals the executed count. Thus this exponent is not consistently the number of applied scales. Do not claim its return is an exact distance or a verified inverse-scale bound. Both presets use expansive scales but different cameras, lighting, colors and parameters; neither is a controlled performance/quality comparison.

**RFF transfer.** A signed-sort/rotation motif could be a separate layer field feeding color or relief. A fixed input plane can sample the full three-dimensional recurrence, but arbitrary rotations and the offset derived from CY generally leave that plane. A native 2D design would define its own two-component sort, rotation and offset. Preserve transformation order, coordinate anchoring and output-pixel filtering, and expose the terminal statistic as an authored field unless a distance contract has been proved. This remains an optional pattern source rather than an improvement to RFF's Mandelbrot iteration algorithm.

**Stereo camera mechanism.** 3D-XId constructs forward/up/right camera vectors and has three modes: a single view, anaglyph with two color() calls, and a side-by-side cross-eyed mode with one call per pixel. The anaglyph origins use opposite EyeSeparation/2 offsets; their directions converge toward ProjectionPlane. The side-by-side mode selects an eye using the sign of the jittered X coordinate, recenters its half-view using 0.5*pixelSize.y/pixelSize.x, and uses EyeSeparation/32. These separation conventions are different and should not be copied as an unexplained shared control. For a new implementation, determine the eye from the fixed output viewport rather than allowing subpixel jitter to switch eye ownership at the dividing edge, and calculate aspect/pixel scale for each eye explicitly.

The single-view path supports equirectangular direction mapping. The two stereo paths do not invoke that mapping, so its presence does not establish equirectangular stereo support. Single-view depth of field targets FocalPlane; the stereo branches construct their target using ProjectionPlane and lensOffset. AutoFocus is declared but is not used inside this camera include. These are distinct control semantics to resolve before adapting the camera, not evidence of a complete interchangeable camera system.

**Sampling and accumulation.** uniformDisc uses sqrt of one random component as radius and the other as angle, giving uniform-area disc sampling for ideal independent uniform random inputs despite a nearby comment claiming nonuniform density. The same helper supplies lens samples and antialias jitter. Each invocation reads the previous RGBA buffer and adds (color*weight,weight), with either a radial tent weight or a Gaussian-derived weight that goes to zero at unit radius. Alpha therefore holds accumulated weight, not image opacity. This include declares post controls and references BufferShader.frag, but does not itself apply the full display transform; it must not be read as a complete export-color contract. A RFF accumulation feature would need explicit invalidation on all relevant frame/material/camera changes and deterministic seeds based on full-output coordinates and sample index for tiled rendering. Existing RFF sampling/export behavior must be checked before proposing another accumulator.

**Renderer audit relevant to reuse.** DE-Raytracer-XId uses distance-scaled hit tolerance, six DE calls for central-difference normals, a five-offset normal-direction AO estimate, weighted orbit color, direct lighting, fog and one optional reflection. Normal queries mutate the shared orbitTrap before getColor, so surface color is not isolated from derivative samples. fSteps is global and not reset inside trace, which matters when color/trace runs more than once for reflections or anaglyph eyes. The quality-shadow path computes a third perturbed direction but repeats the second direction in its third march. These findings support query-local material/visibility state in any RFF implementation; they are not a proposal to port or repair this renderer wholesale. RFF already has material lighting and AO.

The lighting expression uses SpecularExp both as the lobe exponent and in a Fresnel-like factor; its comment does not establish a physically calibrated BRDF. Retain RFF's existing GGX/material foundation. First-trace depth is written to gl_FragDepth, either reciprocal distance or a near-plane expression. A name such as DepthToAlpha does not prove that the shown shader writes a distance to output alpha, which the camera uses for sample weight. Two eye colors also do not establish two independent depth outputs. Any RFF stereo/depth export needs explicit per-eye data and a documented depth meaning.

**3D-to-2D scope and provenance.** A flat 2D Mandelbrot image does not acquire meaningful stereo geometry merely by applying these camera offsets. Stereo relief would need an actual height-surface visibility/reprojection design with disocclusion handling, and must be presented as relief rather than true 3D fractal geometry. This is substantially larger and lower priority than environment lighting using the existing relief normal. Both formula headers explicitly say 'License unknown' and attribute the original IFS work to Knighty.
