The camera names kosalos and claude, while the renderer contains other named technique references. Do not copy these implementations under an assumed repository-wide license; establish the relevant provenance/license or implement a separately specified technique from suitable sources first. No code was copied into RFF, and no stereo render, shader build, numerical distance test, benchmark or external license verification was performed.

## Apollonian variants: periodic inversion fields and an approximate deeper-surface view

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [Apollonian.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Apollonian.frag), [Apollonian2.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Apollonian2.frag), [Apollonian2-FirstSurface.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Apollonian2-FirstSurface.frag), all six presets, and the complete 489-line [DE-Raytracer-FirstSurface.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/DE-Raytracer-FirstSurface.frag). The transferable mechanisms are a periodic inversion pattern and explicit inspection of a derived field; the deeper-surface renderer is not a direct 2D feature.

**First variant: anisotropic cells, query-dependent inversion strength.** Apollonian computes t=foam*(foam2+0.25*cos(pi*multiplier*(input.z-input.x))) once per query. Each iteration multiplies coordinates by (cx,cy,cz), wraps them to [-1,1), divides by those same components, and applies z*=t/dot(z,z). Thus the cell periods are 2/cx,2/cy,2/cz, while the local derivatives of the scale/wrap/unscale operation cancel away from seams. The product scale accumulates the inversion factors. The terminal field is 0.375*abs(z.y)/scale. Its trap is updated only once after the loop, with terminal XYZ and the square of the last inversion factor; the fourth channel is not squared orbit radius. A radius-oriented consumer will therefore give that channel a different meaning than in most examples.

Because t depends on the initial query, multiplying inversion factors alone does not account for its spatial derivative. The permitted foam2 range also allows t to cross zero, so positivity of the accumulated scale cannot be assumed for all UI settings. Define denominator, sign and singular-center behavior before treating the expression as a relief or distance field. The two presets use different iteration counts, geometric parameters and render settings, not just an inversion toggle.

**Second variant: foam offset and a compound terminal shape.** Apollonian2 uses a fixed two-unit wrapped cell, subtracts sign(pos)*Foam, and applies the same form of radial inversion with t=Foam2+0.25*cos(Bend*pi*Multiplier*(input.z-input.x)). The sign offset is discontinuous across a zero component; it is not a smooth shrink operation. The terminal d1 is the minimum distance to the three coordinate axes minus 0.02, equivalent to the minimum of three cylinder fields. It then takes min(d1,abs(y)), mixing those signed cylinder fields with unsigned distance to a zero-thickness plane, and returns half that value divided by scale. This is not automatically a conventional closed signed solid. Unlike the first variant, its trap takes minima of XYZ magnitudes and squared radius on every iteration. Apollonian2-FirstSurface contains the same field and inversion wrapper, with a different renderer, init declaration and presets; its surface selection is implemented outside the formula.

**Outer inversion and coordinate order.** All three wrappers translate around invCenter, map the displacement by invRadius squared over its squared length, translate back, and then rotate XY about the global origin using atan plus invAngle. That final rotation is not about invCenter. The returned field is remapped as r2*d/(invRadius squared+r*d), with r measured before inversion. For a RFF coordinate-only pattern warp, the geometric distance remapping is a separate concern and should not be applied to color or mask values indiscriminately. The inversion-center singularity, negative incoming distances and a vanishing correction denominator require an explicit contract. The local coordinate magnification grows as radius-squared/distance-to-center-squared, so sampling/filtering must follow the warp near its center.

**2D transfer.** With outer inversion disabled, Z=0 is preserved by the wrapped/inverted recurrence, including sign(0)=0 in Apollonian2. In that plane, Apollonian2's terminal cylinder minimum reduces to min(abs(x),abs(y))-0.02; the plane term is never smaller, so the final local zero set is a pair of strips around the axes rather than a disk-packing boundary. This is a useful reminder that a planar slice's actual terminal field must be derived rather than inferred from its 3D name. Outer inversion also preserves the plane only under appropriate center/rotation conditions; a nonzero invZ generally changes it. A RFF implementation could offer a separately specified planar periodic-inversion pattern feeding existing color/material masks, with seam-aware coverage and transformed footprints. Keep all required components for a faithful off-plane slice, and retain deep-zoom precision if coordinates are fractal anchored.

**What 'second surface' actually does.** The renderer first marches normally. When SurfaceIndex=2 and a hit is found, it saves dist, totalDist and orbitTrap, multiplies totalDist by SurfaceGap, and restarts marching with a fresh MaxRaySteps allowance. SurfaceGap is a multiplicative factor on distance from the camera, not an additive world-space gap despite the descriptive comments. It does not explicitly find an exit, count sign crossings or guarantee the nearest next surface; it can re-hit the same region or skip multiple features. The two FirstSurface presets both use SurfaceIndex=2 and a gap of about 1.116. A meaningful inspection feature should be named for its actual behavior, not advertised as exact layer extraction or physical transparency.

On a failed second search the implementation restores only the three saved values, leaving epsModified, steps, floorDist and fSteps from the later search. Subsequent shading still tests dist<epsModified and may clear the trap when steps reaches its limit. Therefore the written fallback is not evidence of an unchanged first-hit result. Any RFF implementation with alternate visibility queries should store a complete hit record, restore it atomically when needed, and isolate normal/AO/color state. This renderer otherwise retains the previously reviewed central-difference normals, five-offset AO, orbit color, direct lighting, fog and one reflection blend, including shared-state and repeated-shadow-direction limitations. Its depth output corresponds to the selected trace result, not necessarily the first geometric surface when SurfaceIndex=2.

**RFF priority and provenance.** The low-scope opportunity is a filtered inversion-domain transform or independently defined planar pattern. Deeper-surface ray searching has no direct counterpart in a flat Mandelbrot iteration image; a useful RFF inspection mode would instead expose existing height, normal or material fields, as proposed earlier. It does not justify importing a full ray marcher. The FirstSurface formula explicitly labels its IQ-derived source as Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0, while the neighboring Apollonian2 file links the same source without repeating that license text. Preserve this provenance flag; omission in one copy is not evidence of broader reuse permission. Actual source licensing and any intended reuse must be verified before adapting distinctive implementation code. No shader code was copied into RFF, and no compilation, numerical bound test, rendering, benchmark or external license check was performed. Environment reflection and dense-palette filtering remain the more immediate RFF priorities.

## Flower and Floral: auxiliary scale state and hybrid squaring

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [Flower.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Flower.frag) and [Floral.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Floral.frag), including both inversion presets in each. Their names describe authored appearances; they do not implement a shared botanical model. The RFF opportunities are optional procedural fields and domain transforms, with explicit state and differential definitions.

**Flower's fourth component is active state.** It initializes q=(query.xyz,1), takes abs of XYZ, divides all four components by clamp(dot(q.xyz,q.xyz),0,Scale), then applies q=2*q-(OffsetX,OffsetY,OffsetZ,1). The denominator is capped above, not bounded away from zero. q.w evolves through both the division and subtraction of one; it is not merely a product of Jacobian scale factors. The terminal expression is length(q.xy)/q.w-0.003. q.z therefore influences the result through the repeated denominator even though it is absent from the final numerator. q.w can change sign or become zero under the allowed settings, so neither an unsigned distance nor a benign normalization is guaranteed.

The trap accumulates abs(q) at every iteration. Its fourth channel is the auxiliary q.w magnitude, not squared orbit radius, and should not inherit an automatic square-root conversion when brought into RFF. A native planar version can preserve Z=0 when OffsetZ=0 and outer inversion preserves that plane, but it must retain the separate w recurrence. Both supplied presets have nonzero OffsetZ and use Stereo=2, so dropping Z would not reproduce them. Their different cameras, iteration counts and offsets also mean they are not a controlled inversion comparison.

**Floral's ordered hybrid.** The map first box-folds pos with clamp(pos,-n1,n1), then applies n2-abs(abs(pos.zyx+n1)-n2)-n1. The ZYX permutation is part of this nested fold, and cannot be removed when making a faithful slice. It measures squared radius and exits above 100 before scaling, applies k=max(kX/r2,0.1)*kY, then performs triplex squaring and subtracts the offset n3. Its trap mixes the resulting XYZ with r2 from before the radial scale/square/translation. That sample-stage difference needs an explicit name if exposed as a RFF material field.

**Triplex squaring and planar reduction.** Away from the XY axis singularity, tsqr uses a=1-z*z/(x*x+y*y) and returns ((x*x-y*y)*a,2*x*y*a,2*z*sqrt(x*x+y*y)). On Z=0 this reduces to ordinary complex squaring in XY. However, the surrounding ZYX fold and arbitrary offsets generally do not preserve that plane, so a planar helper identity does not prove the complete recurrence has a faithful two-component reduction. At x=y=0, the source assigns (-z*z,0,0); for nonzero z the directional limit of the XY components depends on the approach angle, so that branch is an explicit pole convention rather than a globally smooth extension. The unused talt helper does not add an active alternative mode.

**Derivative and parameter contracts.** Floral multiplies its scalar scale by k and then by twice the length of the already squared and translated result. This is not the same as propagating the derivative of the squaring stage from its input. Even the identity that the triplex output length equals the input length squared does not establish a full directional Jacobian bound. The permitted n1 components can be negative; both presets select at least one such component, reversing the corresponding clamp bounds. Treat those saved values as data requiring a defined replacement contract, not evidence of portable GLSL behavior. Zero radial denominators, kY=0, vanishing accumulated scale and fold/pole discontinuities also need defined behavior before using the result as relief height or distance.

**Shared outer inversion.** Both files invert about invCenter, translate back, rotate XY about the global origin, and remap the returned scalar using r2*d/(invRadius squared+r*d). As in the preceding Apollonian analysis, coordinate warping and distance remapping are separate operations. For a RFF decorative mask, use the chosen field/coverage definition rather than applying the distance correction to arbitrary color values. Track the magnification near the inversion center, filter the actual transformed pixel footprint, and preserve high-precision coordinate differences for fractal-anchored layers. These requirements apply equally to preview and tiled/video export.

**Practical recommendation and limits.** If these motifs are useful, define small independent layer recipes with query-local state and intentional planar or full-slice semantics; feed their values into the existing RFF palette/material system. Distinguish an auxiliary denominator channel from a derivative, and keep gradient probes from mutating material statistics. Their serialized antialias scale is zero and their lighting/step settings vary, so the presets do not demonstrate animation stability, reliable distances or performance. Both source files point to named Shadertoy originals (FlowerHive and Floral Hybrid) without establishing their actual licenses locally; verify original authorship/license and update NOTICE before adapting distinctive code. No code was copied into RFF, and no build, numerical derivative/bound test, render, benchmark or external license verification was performed. These optional motifs remain below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in immediate priority.

## Tetrahedral and KIFS variants: explicit reflection planes and terminal fields

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [HalfTetra.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/HalfTetra.frag), [SierpinskTetra.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/SierpinskTetra.frag) and [KIFS.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/KIFS.frag), including their six presets. They refine the proposed RFF auxiliary fold-pattern layer: reflection planes, translation and the terminal field must be explicit rather than inferred from a fractal name.

**Two different reflection families.** HalfTetra rotates XY, sorts signed XYZ by swapping when x-y, x-z or y-z is negative, rotates YZ, then applies scale*pos-n2. SierpinskTetra instead reflects across pair-sum planes: when x+y is negative, XY becomes (-y,-x), and analogous XZ/YZ operations follow. Its second rotation is XZ, not YZ. Both derive scale=Scale/100 and n2=normalize((-1,CY-1,1/CY-1))*(scale-1). These sequential conditional reflections operate on updated coordinates. Replacing one family with abs/sort, or moving the rotation across a fold, changes the motif.

HalfTetra returns length(pos)*scale^(-i); SierpinskTetra returns (length(pos)-2)*scale^(-i). The subtraction changes the terminal zero set from a point-radius field to a sphere-radius field, not merely the brightness or ray tolerance. Both break above radius four before recording the trap. As in Geode, early exit at index i follows i+1 transformations, whereas loop exhaustion leaves i equal to the transform count. Their exponent therefore does not consistently equal the number of applied scales. The slider ranges also permit scale below one, so expansive escape behavior is not universal. Treat the written outputs as estimates requiring validation, not exact Euclidean signed distances.

**KIFS uses a different auxiliary W contract.** Its four-component state starts as (pos,1). Each iteration takes abs, sorts XYZ by magnitude, multiplies all components by kY, subtracts offset*(kY-1) from XYZ, and conditionally adds q=0.5*(kY-kZ) to Z when Z<-q/2. Unlike Flower, W receives no additive offset and, for the positive allowed kY, equals kY raised to the executed iteration count. It supplies a scale product rather than a fourth spatial dimension. kX controls the X offset, kY controls scale and all base offsets, and kZ controls the conditional Z adjustment; these are not three axis scales. Both supplied presets have kZ>kY, hence negative q, so assumptions based only on a positive Menger-like Z offset do not cover them.

The terminal expression is (length(max(abs(XYZ)-1,0))-0.05)/W. Outside the unit box, the numerator measures distance to that solid box minus a shell width; inside it is a constant -0.05. It omits the usual varying interior signed-box term, so it should not be described as a full signed box distance throughout the interior. The trap takes minima of abs(XYZ,W); W is not squared radius. For a fixed positive kY and fixed iteration count, its per-query W sequence is position-independent, so that fourth minimum alone supplies no spatial orbit detail. A RFF material source should label or omit such constant channels instead of calling them geometric radius.

**2D application.** A native planar layer can define a two-component reflection, scale/translation and explicit terminal disk/box/line field. A faithful slice of these examples generally needs all three spatial coordinates: swaps and pair-sum reflections can bring Z into X/Y even when the input starts on Z=0, and rotations/offsets add further coupling. KIFS still needs its scalar scale product if implemented in two dimensions. Feed separately defined coverage, height or orbit statistics into RFF's existing material/palette system; do not interpret all returned values as interchangeable distances. Resolve fold boundaries over the output pixel footprint and preserve full-output anchoring for video/tiled export.

Keep its coordinate operation separate from any new mask-value mapping, define center/denominator behavior and filter increasing detail density. ## KaliBox and Kleinian: distinguish spatial state, scale state and parameter names

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [KaliBox.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/KaliBox.frag) and [Kleinian.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Kleinian.frag), including all four presets. They supply optional folded-pattern ideas for RFF, with important distinctions between scale tracking and a true fourth spatial coordinate.

**KaliBox recurrence.** The state starts as (query.xyz,1). Each iteration rotates XYZ in XY then XZ using the same radian Angle, takes abs and adds the translation vector, measures r2, and multiplies all components by clamp(max(MinRad/r2,MinRad),0,1). It then multiplies XYZ by Scale/MinRad and W by abs(Scale)/MinRad. If doJulia is true it adds (juliaX,juliaY,juliaZ,1). W therefore follows a positive-scale recurrence with an optional +1, while negative Scale reverses the spatial components. It is not a quaternion coordinate. The +1 must not automatically be interpreted as the derivative of adding a constant Julia vector, whose derivative with respect to the query is zero.

The terminal expression is (length(XYZ)-abs(Scale-1))/W - pow(abs(Scale),1-MaxSteps). Both correction terms are part of the particular estimator and need justification for this modified recurrence; they are not generic conversions from an orbit radius to distance. Scale=0, MinRad=0 and folded r2=0 require explicit handling. For finite nonzero r2 and MinRad>=1, the clamped factor becomes one throughout, so the radial-dependent fold disappears and only the remaining scale applies. The Inv ON preset uses MinRad about 1.076, whereas OFF uses about 0.690. Thus those presets differ in the active radial-fold regime as well as inversion, translation, angle and camera; they cannot isolate the inversion effect.

KaliBox accumulates abs(XYZ,W) in orbitTrap. Its W channel is a scale/offset accumulator, not squared radius. For a RFF layer, label such a statistic explicitly and decide whether it is useful for material variation instead of automatically applying the common radius-channel square root. A planar recurrence requires plane-preserving rotations, translation and Julia terms; the shared XY/XZ angle and nonzero Z terms in the supplied presets generally require a full 3D slice.

**Kleinian's W-named controls are scalars, not dimensions.** Only XYZ is iterated. Each fixed-count iteration reflects around the independently specified clamp interval, using 2*clamp(pos,pmin,pmax)-pos, then scales by max(minW/dot(pos,pos),power). minW controls the inversion numerator; maxW controls a terminal radial threshold; power is the lower bound on the radial multiplier, not an exponent. The accumulated scale multiplies the same k. Valid ordered clamp intervals must be enforced explicitly, since independent sliders permit reversed bounds. Negative minW makes the positive power floor dominate at finite nonzero radius; the origin still requires defined division behavior.

The terminal expression is 0.7*max(rxy-maxW,rxy*z/length(pos))/scale. Its second term retains the sign of Z; unlike several related PseudoKleinian examples, it has no abs. Substituting a superficially similar absolute-value terminal field changes the result. When a nonzero XY point remains on Z=0, the expression reduces to 0.7*max(rxy-maxW,0)/scale, a zero-valued disk interior rather than a signed disk distance. Plane preservation requires the Z clamp interval to contain zero and any outer inversion to preserve the plane. No orbitTrap update occurs in the local Kleinian formula, and both presets use OrbitStrength=0; their serialized cycle/color weights do not demonstrate available orbit-based coloring.

**RFF transfer.** A reusable planar folded-domain layer could provide explicit asymmetric interval bounds, radial scaling and a chosen terminal mask, with a separate scale accumulator where mathematically needed. Do not expose inherited control names such as minW/maxW as if they were fourth-axis bounds. Define signed distance, coverage and relief height separately; a zero-valued interior cannot supply a meaningful interior slope merely by being called a distance field. A faithful 3D slice retains all coupled spatial components. These auxiliary patterns must remain independent of RFF's precision-sensitive Mandelbrot reference computation and MPA.

**Shared wrapper and validation.** Both use the previously reviewed outer inversion, global XY rotation and rational distance remapping. Preserve that order only when reproducing the intended field; do not apply its distance correction to arbitrary material channels. Validate transformed footprints near the inversion center, fold-boundary coverage, scale/denominator ranges and consistent preview/video/tile state. The files do not establish the original licenses of their distinctive formula implementations locally; trace provenance before reuse and update NOTICE as appropriate. No shader code was copied, and no compile, numerical derivative/bound test, render, performance measurement or external license verification was performed. These findings refine optional pattern-layer design; environment reflection and dense-palette filtering remain the more immediate RFF improvements.

## Gold and Rontgen: periodic domains versus minima across transformed motifs

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [Gold.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Gold.frag) and [Rontgen.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Rontgen.frag), including all four presets. Their names do not imply a gold BRDF or an X-ray volume renderer. The transferable RFF mechanisms are a repeated coordinate domain and a minimum over successive transformed motifs.

**Gold's periodic pre-transform.** It wraps XZ to [-1,1) once before the loop, leaving Y unwrapped. Each iteration takes abs(XYZ)-offset1, then updates the entire four-vector as 2*q/clamp(dot(XYZ,XYZ),0.4,1)-offset2. offset1=(cx,cy,cz), while offset2=(cw,dx,dy,dz); notably cw offsets X and dz offsets W. These names are not conventional XYZW groups. The denominator has a positive floor, unlike several previously reviewed inversion examples, but W still receives an additive offset and can require independent sign/zero handling. The terminal result length(XYZ)/W is not automatically a conservative distance merely because its radial denominator is bounded.

The four-vector's W is an auxiliary accumulator, not a fourth spatial dimension. Both presets set dz=0, so their W is a positive product of the loop's multiplicative factors; the wider parameter range permits other behavior. No local orbitTrap update is written. Inv ON uses OrbitStrength=0, while Inv OFF uses a nonzero value, but that setting does not create orbit statistics absent from the formula. Several declaration defaults exceed their slider maxima, so recipe import must define whether values are preserved or clamped. RFF should use semantic parameter names and resolved settings rather than reproduce this ambiguity.

**Rontgen accumulates geometry candidates across iterations.** Each iteration transforms p=(query,1) to abs(p)/dot(p.xyz,p.xyz). Before translation or rotation, it evaluates a radius-0.03 cylinder around the local Z axis, shifted by 0.01 in Y, divides that value by W, and takes the minimum with d. It then subtracts (kX,kY,kZ) from XYZ, rotates XZ by Angle and records abs(p) in orbitTrap. Thus the distance candidate and color statistic come from different transform stages. The final field is the minimum across visited stages, not just the terminal orbit radius, and the color minimum is not tied to the stage that won the distance minimum.

The test d>4 occurs after updating the running minimum and before the translation/rotation/trap. Once any candidate is at most four, this nonincreasing d can never pass that test later. For finite ordinary values it therefore acts as a first-candidate rejection, not a conventional orbit escape test. Discarding later candidates would need a separate bound if a RFF implementation promises the full minimum. Also define the finite initial cap of 10000, inversion-axis singularity and any overflow/underflow in W. An accumulated scale factor does not by itself prove that the transformed cylinder expression is exact distance everywhere.

**Concrete RFF application.** A procedural layer could expose repeated planar cells and a small sequence of transformed disk/line motifs, with a minimum field and optional winning-stage identifier. For material consistency, capture the stage's own attributes when it wins, rather than independently minimizing color across unrelated stages; intentional cross-stage coloring should remain a separate mode. RFF's existing masks/materials can consume the result without changing Mandelbrot iteration or MPA. The Gold XZ repeat needs an explicitly chosen 2D coordinate pair; simply renaming it XY changes which direction was originally unbounded. A faithful slice retains the 3D recurrence unless its offsets preserve the plane.

For Rontgen, Z=0 with kZ=0 and a plane-preserving rotation reduces the local cylinder to a 2D disk motif, but W remains necessary. The supplied presets use nonzero kZ and XZ rotation, so their field requires a full spatial state even when the input is a 2D slice. Neither pattern should be presented as an existing RFF capability without checking the complete layer catalog. Define signed coverage versus relief height, track transformed footprints and antialias minimum/fold boundaries. If stage identity drives color, verify transitions and tie handling during animation and tiled export.

**Wrapper, priority and provenance.** Both retain the common outer inversion, global XY rotation and rational distance-remapping wrapper analyzed above. Keep coordinate warping distinct from value remapping, and handle center singularities explicitly. ON/OFF presets change geometry and display settings as well as the inversion flag, so they are not controlled validation. Gold links a Shadertoy source, and Rontgen links Kali Rontgen; the local files do not establish actual original licenses. Verify authorship/license and record NOTICE provenance before adapting distinctive code. No code was copied into RFF and no compile, numerical bound test, render, performance measurement or external license verification was performed. These optional motif controls remain below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in immediate priority.

## EvilSpuds and Monster: signed traps and parameter-driven affine folds

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [EvilSpuds.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/EvilSpuds.frag) and [Monster.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Monster.frag), including all four presets. These provide optional pattern-layer ideas: signed orbit statistics and a compact parameter-driven affine fold. They do not demonstrate a new RFF lighting model or measured speed improvement.

**EvilSpuds field and color stages.** Each iteration box-folds with 2*clamp(p,-fold,fold)-p, measures squared radius, applies k=max(1/r2,kMax), and accumulates that scale. The trap takes minima of (post-scale signed XYZ,pre-scale r2), without abs on XYZ. Negative channel values are therefore intentional consequences of the written reduction, unlike most neighboring examples. A RFF port should specify signed minima, magnitude minima and their sample stages separately instead of silently converting everything to unsigned orbit distance.

The terminal field is max(length(XY)-offset1,-length(XY)*Z/length(XYZ)-offset2)/abs(scale). It uses negative signed Z, not an absolute plane term. When a valid fold and outer transform preserve Z=0, the numerator becomes max(length(XY)-offset1,-offset2): a disk-like signed radial field with a capped negative interior. That cap creates a flat interior region and affects relief gradients. Native planar coverage and height should be defined deliberately rather than assuming a full signed distance throughout the disk. Both supplied presets contain negative fold extents, which reverse corresponding clamp bounds; their serialized images/settings are not evidence of portable semantics for those values. The origin's radial division and terminal length division also require explicit handling.

**Monster's affine transform is shared across iterations and queries.** It builds a rotation from (cz,0.1,cy) plus two sinusoidal functions of cx, scales the matrix's spatial columns by cw, and supplies a sinusoidally varied translation. The loop applies this same affine map to abs(pos) each time. cx is a parameter controlling the transform; a local variable named time1 is assigned cx but unused, and no time uniform drives the formula automatically. A RFF recipe can expose a morph parameter and animate it through the existing timeline, evaluating a frozen setting snapshot consistently in preview and export.

The loop computes m=min(m,dot(pos,pos)/(k*k)), but never uses m in its result or trap. There is no local orbitTrap update, and both presets set OrbitStrength=0. Do not advertise closest-orbit coloring merely because an unused minimum is present. The active terminal field is 0.25*(length(pos)-0.5)/k. k is multiplied by cw only after the transformed point passes the radius-one bailout test; on early exit the spatial state has undergone one more scale than k records. On loop exhaustion the counts match. This requires an explicit executed-transform count if designing a separately justified inverse-scale field. The allowed cw includes contraction as well as expansion, so bailout behavior depends on its regime.

**RFF application and optimization candidate.** A new 2D auxiliary motif could use abs followed by a planar rotation/scale/translation and a chosen terminal disk field. Reproducing Monster's actual 3D slice requires all coordinates because its rotations and translation mix axes. Its matrix depends only on parameters, so a separately implemented layer could compute it once per settings/frame change rather than once per field query. Verify whether the target shader compiler already hoists such expressions before claiming savings; CPU/GPU evaluation and matrix composition changes must preserve the chosen numerical contract. This is an optimization candidate for an optional pattern, not permission to alter RFF's precision-sensitive perturbation or MPA.

For both examples, route explicitly defined mask/height/statistic outputs into the existing material system. Signed color channels need a chosen remapping range; flat interior plateaus and branch boundaries need suitable gradient/coverage handling. Preserve full-output coordinates and transformed pixel footprints, especially when the shared outer inversion magnifies fine detail. That wrapper again rotates XY about the global origin after inversion about a center and remaps the distance separately; it must not be applied blindly to arbitrary material values.

**Provenance and verification limits.** EvilSpuds explicitly credits EvilRyu and labels its source Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0. Monster links a Shadertoy source and forum post without establishing a local original-license record. Record these differences and verify actual provenance/license before adapting distinctive code into RFF. The ON/OFF presets also change formula and viewing settings, so they do not isolate the effect of inversion or show estimator accuracy.
