## Tower and Vertebrae: thickness units, smooth unions and actual animation state

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [Tower.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Tower.frag) and [Vertebrae.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Vertebrae.frag), including all four presets. The RFF lessons are to define thickness in a chosen coordinate space, distinguish geometry blending from antialiasing, and make animated deformation state explicit.

**Tower's twist is spatially dependent.** Before folding, it computes aa from a clamped, smoothstepped cosine of CY-0.4*inputY and multiplies it by pi. It shifts Y and wraps it through abs(3-fract((shiftedY-CY)/2)). Since fract is in [0,1), this last value lies in (2,3]; the abs adds no extra mirror fold there. The loop takes abs(XYZ), subtracts a Y offset, applies 2*p/clamp(dot(XYZ,XYZ),0.3,1), subtracts (0.5,1.5,0.5,0), and rotates XZ by aa*Twist. The same angle is used in all iterations of a query, but varies between query positions. The two-unit Y wrap therefore does not make the entire field two-unit periodic, because aa depends on the unwrapped input. W tracks the multiplicative factor, but omits the differential of this input-dependent rotation.

**Terminal shape and width convention.** Let u=XYZ/W; W stays positive for finite values in this recurrence. fr=max(abs(u.z)-0.01,length(u.zx)-0.002) simplifies to the second term, because length(u.zx)>=abs(u.z) and 0.002<0.01. bl=max(abs(u.x)-0.01,length(u.zy)-0.0005) instead combines a slab and an axial cylinder field. The result blends bl and fr with a polynomial smooth minimum of width 0.02. That width lowers the field by 0.005 when inputs are equal, substantially larger than either tube radius; it is a geometric blend parameter, not a subpixel edge filter. These dimensions are expressed after division by W and are not fixed widths in raw orbit coordinates or screen pixels.

For a RFF layer, expose motif thickness, union blend width and coverage filtering as distinct controls with documented units. At a smooth union, interpolate material ownership consistently with the chosen blend if that is intended; antialias the final coverage using its transformed pixel footprint separately. Preserve the spatial derivative of twist when deriving a relief normal. Tower's repeated XZ rotation and Z translation generally require full 3D state for a faithful slice; a native planar twist motif should have its own definition.

**Vertebrae is one deformation evaluation, not an iterative orbit.** It initializes a four-vector from (query,0), performs one quaternion square, and adds an animated c. Then XYZ passes through Log*log(XYZ+sqrt(dot(XYZ,XYZ)+1)), followed by Scale*sin(XYZ+Offset)+XYZ*Slope and two rotations. The square-root term is shared across components; this is not componentwise asinh. Finally z+=(z-oldZ)/Smooth extrapolates away from the original input. It is not temporal smoothing, and the subsequent oldZ assignment is unused because there is no loop. A RFF control inspired by it should be described as deformation/extrapolation strength, not smoothing or convergence.

init sets c=0.5*(C,Cw)*sin(time*Aspeed)*Ascale and the first rotation angle to Angle1*sin(time*Aspeed/2)*Ascale*3. The second rotation stays at Angle2. At time zero, or when Aspeed or Ascale is zero, c and the first rotation vanish; the remaining log/sine/linear deformation remains active. Both presets serialize nonzero speed and amplitude, so time belongs to the required render snapshot. Comparing saved parameter blocks without a common evaluation time is not a controlled image comparison.

**Gradient and color contracts.** Vertebrae's md2 only receives 4*the initial squared radius, while its final expression is 0.3*sqrt(finalSquaredRadius/md2)*log(finalSquaredRadius). It does not propagate the later log, sine, rotations and extrapolation differentials; a correct relief gradient or distance bound requires the complete chain. The origin and zero final norm also need defined handling. Its orbitTrap=min(orbitTrap,mz2) applies the same scalar squared norm to all four channels, not four independent statistics. The shared renderer subsequently treats W differently by square-rooting it, so channel labels must reflect the actual consumer. Tower instead accumulates abs(XYZ,W), with W again an auxiliary scale rather than squared radius.

**RFF application and limits.** The strongest transferable pieces here are independently controlled smooth mask composition and deterministic animated domain deformation for optional layers. Reuse RFF's existing animation/material infrastructure and preserve high-precision fractal coordinate differences. A 2D implementation can define a planar deformation and mask field; removing components from these formulas does not automatically reproduce their slices. Both use the already analyzed outer inversion and distance-remapping wrapper, whose center and denominator behavior need explicit contracts. Both headers declare Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0; Tower credits Kali and Vertebrae credits kosalos with multiple upstream sources. Verify actual provenance/licensing before distinctive code reuse and record it in NOTICE. No implementation code was copied, and no shader build, derivative test, render comparison, benchmark or external license verification was performed. These layer features remain below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in immediate priority.

## Orbit-increment tweaks: genuine history versus a first-order extrapolation

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [Mandelbulb.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Mandelbulb.frag), its Default preset, and [Quaternion.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Quaternion.frag), including both inversion presets. The RFF lesson is to specify the actual recurrence before offering an orbit-history or smoothing control. Similar variable names here implement different mechanisms.

**Mandelbulb uses a previous input to modify angle.** It forms diffVec=(0.001,0.001,0.001)+oldZ-z, then saves oldZ=z before updating the orbit. The polar tweak is 1-(radialAngle/100)/(length(diffVec)+thetaTweakOffset/100). This modifies the XY-radius argument of atan(XYlength*tweak,Z), followed by angular offsets, scheduled Power=Power0+i*PowerScale and thetaScale. The powered spherical vector is added to the existing z, not assigned in its place; JuliaC and query*OrigPtScale are then added, followed by rotation. The two conversion branches use different sine/cosine polar conventions. A faithful field therefore needs both current and previous input states, the identity contribution and the declared angular convention.

The fixed vector added to diffVec does not guarantee a positive lower bound on its length: a later orbit difference can cancel it. The allowed negative thetaTweakOffset can also cancel the denominator. Define singular and near-singular behavior rather than treating the comment as proof of stability. Angle offsets enter radian expressions directly. time is declared but unused. Its scalar derivative update adds the previous dr through +=, but does not propagate the history-dependent polar tweak, all angular scaling or arbitrary query multipliers; it is not a verified Jacobian norm. The preset's noninteger power and nonzero polar offset do not supply a plane-preserving complex-power example.

**Quaternion's oldZ can be eliminated algebraically.** It initializes q=(query.xyz,seedW) and oldZ=q. In each iteration, it squares the quaternion with X as the real component, adds either a fixed four-component c or (query.xyz,0), applies q+=(q-oldZ)/den with den=2+100*radialAngle, then sets oldZ=q. Thus at every iteration entry oldZ equals the current q. The map can be written qNext=(1+1/den)*(Q(q)+addition)-q/den. It is a first-order extrapolated map, not a two-step memory recurrence or temporal smoothing. The allowed radialAngle gives den between 2 and 502, so larger radialAngle weakens the added extrapolation. Exact floating-point behavior can still differ if this algebraic rewrite changes evaluation order; it is a semantic explanation, not a tested code replacement.

The scalar md2 multiplies by 4*dot(q,q) before each square, but does not explicitly account for the extrapolation or the query-dependent addition in non-Julia mode. The differential of the extrapolated map includes (1+1/den)*DQ-I/den, plus the scaled derivative of the addition when applicable. The final expression 0.3*sqrt(mz2/md2)*log(mz2) needs zero/nonfinite handling and an independently justified distance contract. Quaternion.frag writes no local orbitTrap values; both presets set OrbitStrength=0. The unused dr/r-related remnants do not establish additional active derivative or coloring paths.

**2D transfer and RFF scope.** For Quaternion, an XY complex subspace can be preserved with seedW=0 and no Z/W additions, with a plane-preserving outer transform; the extrapolated quadratic is still not the standard Mandelbrot recurrence. The supplied presets have nonzero seedW and nonzero Z/W Julia constants, so faithful slices must retain all four components. For the history-modulated Mandelbulb, arbitrary angular settings/rotation generally require the full spatial state and previous-state data. A native planar analogue should be specified separately and tested at angle branch seams.

RFF could use an independently defined incremental-deformation recipe as an optional layer source, with named strength and state semantics, then map its output to existing color or material masks. It must not silently alter the main Mandelbrot formula, precision, perturbation or MPA. Any new orbit statistics require an explicit computation/storage design. For relief, derive the gradient of the actual complete map and filter rapidly varying detail over output-pixel footprints. Deterministic settings and frame coordinates must agree in interactive, video and tiled paths.

**Evidence limits and provenance.** The Quaternion wrapper repeats the already reviewed inversion-about-center, global XY rotation and rational distance remapping. Its two presets keep the core formula settings but change camera target as well as inversion, so they are not a fixed-view benchmark. The Mandelbulb file credits kosalos, mclarekin and additional Mandelbulber options; Quaternion links a forum source. Neither local file establishes complete original licensing for distinctive implementations. Verify provenance/license and update NOTICE before adaptation. No code was copied into RFF and no shader build, numerical derivative test, render comparison, benchmark or external license verification was performed. These optional deformation ideas remain below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in immediate priority.

## Sponge and SpudsVille: compose fields without losing scale or stage semantics

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [Sponge.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/Sponge.frag) and [SpudsVille.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/SpudsVille.frag), including their two and three presets. Their RFF value is in explicit staged procedural layers: a transformed domain feeding a terminal motif, or one recurrence stage switching to another. This is distinct from the core Mandelbrot algorithm.

**Sponge uses normalization before another field evaluation.** Its outer loop box-folds against independent XYZ bounds, applies k=max(minW/r2,1), and accumulates scale. Afterward it divides the transformed coordinates by scale, multiplies them by scl=maxW*pScale, and evaluates sdSponge, finally dividing that scalar by scl. This is not the same as evaluating the inner field first and then dividing its result by the outer scale, because sdSponge is nonlinear. A RFF composition interface must specify whether a scale changes coordinates, field values or both.

sdSponge multiplies coordinates by pShape, performs exactly four abs/sort/scale-three Menger-like folds with a conditional Z offset, then evaluates the standard signed unit-box expression. Its final calibration is 0.2*3^(-3), followed by the outer factor 0.1. Four folds but a power of minus three, together with the calibration factors and omitted explicit abs(pShape) compensation, do not establish an exact transformed distance. Negative pShape has the same mathematical effect as positive pShape because the first inner operation is abs; zero collapses the inner input to a constant. maxW=0 causes division by zero, and negative scl changes the returned sign even though the inner abs removes coordinate sign. Define parameter semantics and admissible values before using such a field for relief or coverage.

No local orbitTrap values are written, and both presets disable orbit coloring. The inversion-enabled preset also has minY greater than maxY, reversing that clamp interval. Treat this as an adoption constraint, not a portable reference image specification. A faithful 2D slice still needs XYZ because the inner sorting and offsets mix components. A new planar box/carpet motif can be designed independently, with explicit scale/width compensation and filtered boundary coverage.

**SpudsVille is a fixed two-stage schedule.** For iteration indices zero through five, it applies a box fold, a radial fold and Scale. From index six onward, it applies a different box fold, recomputes radius, applies a sine-latitude spherical power with Z multiplied by ZMUL, and then applies Scale2. The switch is hard-coded at six; maxSteps at most six never reaches the power stage. The orbit starts at the query and no Julia or query constant is added inside either stage. This is a composed fold/power map, not a standard Mandelbrot recurrence with interchangeable settings.

The radial-fold thresholds compare squared radius directly with MinRad and FixedRad despite their names. In Inv ON both thresholds are negative, so neither branch executes for finite squared radius. Inv OFF has MinRad greater than FixedRad and a negative FoldLimit; the former changes branch coverage, while the latter reverses clamp bounds. lagrande uses positive ordered thresholds. These materially different regimes, noninteger powers and different cameras/render settings make the presets unsuitable as a controlled inversion or accuracy comparison.

**Derivative and query-local color.** The power-stage scalar update multiplies by sqrt((2+ZMUL*ZMUL)/3), an RMS axis factor, then adds one. For the anisotropic diagonal map (1,1,ZMUL), the Euclidean operator norm is max(1,abs(ZMUL)); RMS is not generally an upper bound. The spherical angular map also needs its own differential, and no query addition in the written recurrence explains the usual Mandelbrot +1. Do not treat dz as a proven conservative bound. Negative/zero scales, radius zero, noninteger angular seams and the logarithmic return need explicit contracts.

DE_SPUDS resets orbitTrap at entry and records post-stage XYZ plus squared radius after every executed iteration. This prevents simple accumulation across DE calls, but does not make the caller's final trap automatically belong to the surface center: the existing renderer makes subsequent normal probes before consuming color. Return center statistics explicitly or preserve them around derivative/visibility queries. Sample ownership remains necessary even when a helper initializes its own reduction state.

**2D transfer and priorities.** With valid plane-preserving folds and outer transforms, Z=0 is preserved by SpudsVille's sine-latitude power. For integer power, its XY part is a complex power preceded by folds; noninteger power needs an intentional branch convention. A RFF auxiliary recipe can expose stage boundaries and independent field/material outputs, with full-output pixel footprints and frozen frame settings. Any use as a new deep-zoom fractal formula needs its own precision/perturbation/MPA analysis and storage compatibility work. Sponge's full-state slice and a native planar motif are separate options. Both wrappers repeat the already analyzed outer inversion and distance correction. SpudsVille links a Fragmentarium upstream source; neither local file establishes a complete original-license record. Verify provenance/license before distinctive code reuse and update NOTICE. No code was copied, and no compile, numerical bound test, render comparison, benchmark or external license check was performed. Environment reflection and dense-palette filtering remain the more immediate RFF improvements.

## FirstSurface formula variants: geometry selection belongs to the renderer

**Scope.** Fully read kosalos' [PseudoKleinian-FirstSurface.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/PseudoKleinian-FirstSurface.frag) and [PseudoKleinianMenger-FirstSurface.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/kosalos/PseudoKleinianMenger-FirstSurface.frag), including all three and seven preset blocks respectively. They reuse the previously reviewed FirstSurface renderer. Their names do not introduce a new exact cross-section or transparency algorithm: the renderer still multiplies the first-hit distance by SurfaceGap and searches again.

**Plane terminal variant.** The outer recurrence box-folds, records a trap, applies k=max(Size/r2,1), adds C and records another trap. It stops at MI or exact consecutive-state equality. The active terminal field is abs(0.5*abs(p.z-Offset.z)/DEfactor-DEoffset). The RoundBox and Thingy helpers are not called; TThickness and Offset.xy therefore do not affect the active geometry. USE_INF_NORM is defined but does not select a norm in this local body. A RFF adaptation should expose active controls and explicitly distinguish terminal-plane offset from shell offset, rather than copy an unused shape-control panel.

For Z=0 preserved by the fold and C.z=0, with Offset.z=0, the terminal value becomes the constant abs(DEoffset) away from singular cases. Both Default and P3 use those values and DEoffset=0; an XY slice of their active field is therefore not automatically an interesting planar contour. Kleinian Forest has nonzero C.z and Offset.z and does not share that simplification. A useful RFF planar analogue should choose its own terminal line/circle/box field or retain a nontrivial full 3D slice. The two trap updates sample different recurrence stages and should be named accordingly when driving materials.

**Menger terminal variant.** This outer loop uses maximum absolute component below 60 for its bailout, while radial scaling still uses Euclidean squared radius. Its fourth trap component contains the maximum absolute component after translation, not squared radius; the common renderer's square root would change its meaning. ColorIterations restricts only this outer trap. The subsequent Menger helper performs an initial abs/sort and a fixed Z reflection around 1/3, then a separately bounded scale-about-MnOffset loop with a Z reflection around MnOffset.z/3. Its own trap statement is commented out. Outer MI and inner MnIterations are sequential costs, not a nested MI-times-MnIterations evaluation in this body.

The Menger return uses float(z.x-MnOffset), selecting the first component of that vector expression, then multiplies by MnScale^(-n). It is not a complete box-distance evaluation. The outer result takes abs after scaling and DEoffset subtraction, producing an unsigned terminal field. The post-sort Z reflection can change component ordering; inferring a max-component terminal from the preceding sort alone would be unsafe. MnScale=0 and contraction regimes require defined handling; preset k4 uses a scale below one. A RFF field implementation needs an independently specified terminal statistic and differential rather than assuming every Menger-labeled helper is equivalent.

**Preset and renderer contract.** Only the plane variant's Default preset explicitly selects SurfaceIndex=2 and SurfaceGap about 1.18. Its other two presets and all seven Menger presets omit those fields. Their actual selection depends on the host's defaults/apply semantics; omission is not proof of second-surface rendering. Older serialized AntiAlias and BoundingSphere keys likewise do not establish active controls in the included renderer. Resolve a complete settings snapshot before comparing images or preserving a recipe. When a second search is requested, keep the earlier report's complete-hit-record and fallback-state requirements; these formula files do not repair or replace that algorithm.

**RFF transfer and priority.** The reusable design is an explicit outer-domain transform plus selectable terminal motif, with material statistics tied to their actual stage and norm. Offer planar masks or full-state slices as different layer definitions, preserving RFF precision, MPA and existing map meanings. The FirstSurface search itself has no direct counterpart in a flat iteration image; existing height/normal/material diagnostics remain the more practical inspection extension. Filter fold/shell boundaries over the output pixel footprint and verify query-local statistics in preview and export. Source comments credit Theli-at and Knighty but do not establish a complete original-license record here; trace actual provenance before distinctive implementation reuse and update NOTICE. No shader build, numerical test, rendering, benchmark or external license verification was performed. Environment reflection and dense-palette filtering remain the immediate appearance/stability priorities.

## Neural implicit fields: optional 2D masks, not a Mandelbrot accelerator

**Read scope.** Both complete Kashaders/With_CRrenderer formula files, [LittleBunny_NN_SDF_03.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/LittleBunny_NN_SDF_03.frag) and [Monkey_NN_SDF_02.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/Monkey_NN_SDF_02.frag), including every coefficient block and their Default presets. The color-selection branch in their actual relative include, renderer/DE-Kn2.frag, was rechecked. These are bundled inference examples; this read does not establish a training/export workflow or an error certificate.

**Actual network mechanism.** Each field starts with 32 sine activations of affine XYZ input, stored as eight vec4 values. Four subsequent dense 32-to-32 stages each evaluate sin(W*h+b)/a+h, with a=1.0, 1.4, 1.7 and 2.0 respectively. The division scales the sine output, not its input frequency. A final 32-component linear projection plus bias returns one scalar. The two coefficient sets differ, and their final biases are 0.166 and 0.167. GLSL mat4 constructors are column-major; an independent exporter must preserve matrix orientation rather than transpose the learned operation accidentally.

This explicit topology contains 4,385 scalar weight/bias entries: 128 in the input affine map, four times 1,056 in the hidden maps, and 33 in the readout. A full unpruned field query expresses 160 scalar sine activations and 256 mat4-vector products, before considering compiler folding of zero coefficients, fusion or hardware execution. These are source-level structural counts, not an instruction count or timing measurement. Repeated distance, normal and AO queries can multiply this cost. A compact coefficient representation is therefore not proof of faster shading than a filtered texture lookup.

**Domain and field semantics.** Outside radius one, both scene functions skip the network and return length(p)-0.7; at radius exactly one they still evaluate the network. Nothing in these bodies enforces continuity with the limiting exterior value 0.3, nor proves that the learned field is a conservative distance bound. The exterior expression is the distance to a radius-0.7 sphere, which is only a safe lower bound to an enclosed object under an independently established containment condition. The unit-domain comment alone does not establish that stronger condition. Both presets select FudgeFactor about 0.437 and MaxRaySteps=1027, but a safety factor is not a mathematical guarantee against overstepping. Use learned values as approximate fields unless error/bound evidence is supplied.

Monkey additionally maps input Y to abs(Y) before scene evaluation, forcing reflection symmetry irrespective of the learned weights. This can introduce a derivative seam at Y=0 unless the underlying Y derivative vanishes there. Its copied info text still names a bunny; asset identity should be established from training metadata or a verified render, not that header. Neither formula updates an orbit trap. Their shell-striped baseColor helper uses a hard mod threshold, but providesColor is commented out; the included renderer calls that helper only under the macro, and both presets set OrbitStrength=0. The helper is therefore not evidence of active neural coloring in these presets. Bloom is also disabled in both.

**3D-to-2D transfer.** Evaluating f(u,v,z0) gives a cross-section field that can drive a contour mask, a bounded decorative height layer or material roughness. It is not a silhouette projection, which would require a separate visibility/projection definition. Even an exact 3D signed distance restricted to a plane is not generally the exact planar distance to the section contour. Describe widths in the chosen field or screen-space units; do not promise a constant planar offset from an arbitrary learned value. Freeze z0, coordinate mapping and asset version in the recipe, and define behavior outside the valid domain. For a fixed slice, a cached scalar texture with appropriate filtering may be the more practical RFF implementation; compare reconstruction error and cost before choosing direct inference. A changing slice needs cache invalidation or direct evaluation, not reuse of stale data.

**Differentials and filtering.** An optional analytic gradient can follow the same network: J0=diag(cos(W0*p+b0))*W0; each residual stage propagates Jnext=[I+diag(cos(W*h+b))/a]*J; the readout multiplies by its weight row. This is the derivative of the represented field, not proof that the field matches a true distance. Apply the slice/coordinate transform by the chain rule, and the sign of Y for the mirrored wrapper away from its seam. Separate treatment is needed at the domain switch and mirror seam. For masks, use a pixel-footprint estimate from this gradient or screen derivatives and test against supersampling; a local linear estimate alone can miss multiple oscillations within one pixel. Analytic gradients are a candidate to reduce repeated full-network finite differences, but their extra matrix work and register use must be measured.

**RFF recommendation and acceptance evidence.** Keep this as a lower-priority optional material/mask asset format. Do not replace exact iteration data, perturbation, MPA, reference compression or lossless saved maps with neural approximations. If pursued, compare direct inference against a cached 2D field on identical output footprints; validate gradient direction, mirror/domain boundaries, minification, preview/video/tiled export consistency and reproducible asset loading. A 2D-native trained field would be a separate asset pipeline, not a mechanical deletion of Z terms from these learned networks. These local headers credit blackle and link a Shadertoy example and SIREN, but do not establish licenses for code, learned weights or source geometry; trace each before reuse and record applicable provenance in NOTICE. No external license verification, shader build, rendering, numerical error test or benchmark was performed. This evidence does not displace editable environment reflection or palette-footprint filtering as RFF's nearer-term appearance/stability priorities.

## Kn camera 1.0.5 / buffer 1.0.2: reproducible weighted reconstruction

**Read scope.** Full [3DKn-1.0.5.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/neozhaoliang/Boyd-Maxwell-Ball-Packings/3DKn-1.0.5.frag) and [BufferShader-1.0.2.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/neozhaoliang/Boyd-Maxwell-Ball-Packings/BufferShader-1.0.2.frag). Their counterparts in Hyperbolic-Honeycombs-Kn2 were verified byte-for-byte identical. This completes these four source inventory entries; it does not complete the associated DE-Kn2cr11 renderer audit. The earlier 1.0.1 accumulation discussion remains applicable, with the following details confirmed for this pair.

**Reconstruction is distinct from blur.** The camera generates a disc sample with radius sqrt(r.y), adds an offset scaled by AntiAliasScale*PixelScale.y*FOV, evaluates color at the resulting ray, and adds (c*w,w) to an RGBA32F history. GaussianWeight=0 selects w=1-radius; positive G selects exp(-radius^2/G)-exp(-1/G). These are radial reconstruction weights over disc-distributed samples, not uniform integration over a square pixel. The buffer shader divides accumulated RGB by accumulated weight before exposure and display transforms. Alpha here is sample weight, not transparency or depth. Tiny positive G can underflow many weights; empty or zero-weight histories need an explicit defined result in a new implementation. Long accumulation also needs a precision/overflow policy even with a float32 buffer.

RFF's inspected [vk_linear_interpolation.frag](../shdsrc/vk_linear_interpolation.frag) already offers a normalized 3-by-3 reconstruction of an existing canvas: center weight 9, axial neighbors 3 each, diagonal neighbors 1 each, total 25. That operation does not independently reevaluate the fractal/material at new subpixel positions. The transferable extension is optional sample accumulation for genuinely evaluated subpixels, particularly high-frequency relief reflections or masks. A later blur cannot recover details absent from the source samples. Conversely, repeatedly shading an unchanged low-resolution iteration map cannot establish exact fractal-boundary supersampling; specify separately whether a mode samples only material appearance or recomputes the necessary underlying data. Do not imply that all existing RFF antialiasing paths have been inventoried by this local comparison.

**Sample identity and tile geometry.** Jitter uses uniformDisc(coord*(1+subframe)); aperture uses a related viewCoord product. A coordinate exactly zero remains the same seed across subframes, and multiplication of coordinates and sample indices is not an injective sample key. The source alone therefore does not establish independent dimensions or full-image/tile equivalence. Its PixelScale includes projection diagonal factors, and its aspect correction uses pixelSize.y/pixelSize.x before FOV. Carry equivalent full-image footprint information into RFF, but define randomness from integer global pixel identity, frame, sample index and dimension before mixing. Keep spatial, shutter and optional lens dimensions distinct; stable identities also allow resumed export. Test full-frame and tiled results under the same global samples, rather than accepting a visually similar noisy result as equivalence. This is a design requirement inferred from these contracts, not a measured rendering defect.

**Thin-lens features are geometry-dependent.** Camera basis construction projects Up perpendicular to the viewing direction; coincident Eye/Target or parallel Up/view vectors require a defined fallback. AutoFocus is declared but not used by this file. An equirectangular helper exists but main constructs a perspective ray. Circular sampling is area-uniform only under the assumption that its random inputs are uniform; the radius square root supplies the needed radial mapping. Polygon/star sampling constructs and rotates triangular pieces, and its rotation expression uses ApertureRot*pi/360, so do not assume a conventional degrees-to-radians interpretation from the control name. Neither statistical distribution nor image quality was measured here.

The SRay stores a lens offset and reciprocal focal distance. SRCurrentPt modifies the ray's offset as a function of travel distance, with a smooth in-focus-width formula or a clamp-based alternative. These are specialized depth-of-field trajectories, not a screen-space blur filter. The smooth branch uses smoothstep(-1.5*width,1.5*width,t); a zero width needs a separately defined limiting expression in an independent implementation. The fallback branch's clamp has a defined zero-width result. The camera also sets a heuristic advance multiplier from FPO1 and reflects the offset/origin for reflected rays. These mechanisms require meaningful surface positions and visibility. A flat RFF iteration image has no physical focal plane by itself; any relief-depth blur should state its height/depth model and handle occlusion, rather than adopting this camera wholesale.

**Display transform contracts.** Buffer normalization precedes the selectable linear, exponential, filmic, rational compression or sigmoid branches. Most branches then apply brightness, saturation and contrast around a fixed 0.5 pivot; the sigmoid branch instead incorporates brightness and contrast directly and does not apply Saturation. The filmic branch raises its rational curve to 2.2 before the shared inverse-Gamma power. The sigmoid normalizer becomes 0/0 at Contrast=0, Gamma=0 is admitted by the declared camera slider, and contrast/saturation can produce negative channels before a fractional power. A RFF adoption needs deliberate finite endpoint and negative-color policies, not an assumption that these old curves are a drop-in output standard. RFF already has tone maps, transfer selection and dithering; preserve those contracts and insert any accumulation at an explicitly defined linear-light stage. The sample wrapper itself cannot prove what color space color(Ray) returns.

**Bloom-side observation, not a new priority.** This buffer version scales the sample footprint by BloomStrong. Its separable polynomial tap weights are accumulated in RGBA and later divided by accumulated alpha, so the nominal samples-squared division cancels in that ratio. With unequal per-pixel histories, the neighborhood result weights by both the spatial kernel and each pixel's accumulated sample weight; that differs from blurring independently normalized pixels. An adaptive-sample RFF implementation must choose which quantity to filter. This is relevant even if bloom remains unchanged, because reuse of a color/weight buffer by other neighborhood effects can silently inherit that behavior.

**RFF adoption and validation.** Prioritize a well-defined appearance-supersampling mode only where palette-footprint filtering or analytic filtering cannot adequately handle the signal. Keep opacity separate from reconstruction weight, normalize once, define history reset keys for geometry/material/palette/time changes, and do not blend nominally different video frames unless a shutter interval is explicitly requested. Validate a constant-color field, thin stripes, varying sample counts, zero-weight initialization, restart/resume, and preview versus tiled/video export at identical settings. Benchmark against the existing filter and a supersampled reference. The headers credit syntopia/knighty and the buffer names third-party color/curve/kernel sources, but this local inspection does not verify their original licenses; independently implement generic reconstruction and resolve distinctive-source provenance before reuse. No shader compilation, rendering, statistical sampling test, timing test or external license verification was performed.

## Unit-ball packing: planar mirror motifs and full-state slices

**Read scope.** Complete [Ball-Packings-UnitBall.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/neozhaoliang/Boyd-Maxwell-Ball-Packings/Ball-Packings-UnitBall.frag), including its sole default preset. This formula includes DE-Kn2cr11.frag; its local body is reviewed here without claiming completion of that renderer. The useful RFF transfer is a new optional procedural material/mask layer, not a replacement for Mandelbrot computation.

**Construction mechanism.** The formula constructs five mirror objects and four selectable terminal objects from a Euclidean triangle choice and dihedral parameters. The triangle choices are 236, 244 and 333. A parameter value exactly one is a special infinity convention returning cosine one, while other values use cos(pi/value); fractional slider values therefore have numerical meanings but are not automatically discrete reflection groups. Matrices and inverse solves determine sphere centers/radii. The row-vector product b*inverse(M) is intentional source behavior and must not silently become inverse(M)*b in an independent implementation. A special B0 plane case requires all three angle parameters to equal two, not their sum to equal six.

The plane/sphere construction uses square roots, matrix inverses and divisions by a sphere-center Z coordinate. A RFF procedural layer should validate a complete parameter set before installing its derived data, distinguish invalid geometry from a genuinely empty selection, and cache uniform-only construction when parameters change. This source read does not prove how often the host/compiler executes init or that CPU preprocessing would improve performance. The default chooses triangle 244, angle triples (3,2,4) and (3,3,3), pair angle five, active terminal slots one and four, and 100 iterations.

**Infinite planar folding is the directly reusable part.** inffold wraps a coordinate with period twice the tile extent and mirrors it into [0,extent]. fold244 applies that operation to X/Y, then reflects across a diagonal. fold236 first folds into a rectangle with extents 3 and sqrt(3), then uses two oblique folds separated by abs. fold333 uses a shifted origin, a triangular Y fold, a temporary oblique X coordinate with period six, and an ordered reflection sequence. These routines map an unbounded plane into a fundamental triangle with fixed work; they do not explicitly enumerate an unbounded number of neighboring tiles. The oblique coordinate changes in fold333 are part of the construction, not permission to drop the inverse coordinate change or reorder reflections.

For RFF, apply these maps to a bounded material coordinate and evaluate a terminal motif such as a disk, line or palette ramp. This supplies triangular and kaleidoscopic patterns with a fixed folding cost. It is a 2D-native transfer independent of the sphere-packing solver. Track reflection orientation when transforming a directional texture or normal; a scalar mask can share values across a fold while its gradient changes direction. Filtering must account for footprints crossing mirror or wrap boundaries, since a local derivative within one folded cell may not cover both sides. Test mirrored asymmetric motifs as well as symmetric ones, so an unnoticed orientation error is visible.

**The full packing is not obtained by dropping Z.** Before iteration, map shifts Z by one, applies p=2*p/dot(p,p), then shifts Z back. An input on Z=0 generally emerges with Z=2/(X^2+Y^2+1)-1, which is not zero. The subsequent loop applies the planar Euclidean fold and then reflections/inversions in the first two mirrors. Sphere inversion multiplies the scale tracker by radius-squared/distance-squared; planar reflections leave it unchanged. The loop stops at the iteration budget or exact equality of all three coordinates with the saved pre-fold state. This exact fixed-state check is not a tolerance convergence certificate.

The initial inversion multiplies the tracker by 1/dot(p,p), whereas its local geometric scale is 2/dot(p,p). With the final return factor 0.25, the output is half the terminal distance divided by that initial-inversion-plus-reflection local scale, away from singularities. That algebra explains the constants but does not certify a conservative distance to the globally inverted surface. A true full-state 2D slice must retain the intermediate Z coordinate, inversion singularity policy and complete recurrence. Expose it as a slice of this field, distinct from the simpler planar mirror-motif layer.

**Terminal field and color semantics.** dist2balls minimizes the absolute signed distance to enabled terminal planes/spheres, then divides by the accumulated scale. It represents unsigned proximity to surfaces, not a signed union of solid balls. With no active terminal objects, its sentinel 1e5 is still divided by scale; define an explicit empty mask in a new RFF implementation rather than interpreting that sentinel as geometry. Slot zero remains a default inactive ball and is excluded from the terminal loop, despite the earlier comment saying the s0-associated ball is always active. section_height is computed but never read locally; this shader does not expose a section-height control through that variable.

DE resets orbitTrap to vec4(1) on every query. try_reflect records min(abs(p),dot(p,p)) before each of the two mirror attempts, including attempts that make no change. The initial unit-ball inversion and planar fold therefore precede these observations; the final transformed point after the second mirror is not sampled until a subsequent loop iteration. The initial value caps recorded statistics at one. With zero iterations no trap samples are collected, although initial inversion and terminal evaluation still occur. Use these exact meanings if creating a material statistic; do not label them generic radius or iteration counts. Query-local reset prevents history leaking between DE invocations, but a renderer must still preserve the intended hit's statistics while performing normal, AO or shadow probes.

**RFF priority and verification.** The fixed-work planar mirror maps are a plausible small feature for decorative layers. The full inversion packing, its solver and its unsigned surface metric are a larger optional field system and rank below environment lighting and dense-palette filtering for immediate benefit. Keep all such layers separate from precision-sensitive perturbation/MPA and existing map data. Verify seam behavior under zoom, mirrored normals, invalid parameter rejection, empty selections, zero iterations and identical tile/video coordinates before publishing an implementation. No rendering, numerical solver test, performance measurement, shader compilation or original-source license verification was performed. Trace the actual authorship and license of distinctive folding/packing implementations before adaptation and record provenance in NOTICE; the mathematical description here is not a license grant.

## Upper-half-space packing: ordered reflection events and terminal-plane masks

**Read scope.** Full [Ball-Packings-UpperHalfSpace.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/neozhaoliang/Boyd-Maxwell-Ball-Packings/Ball-Packings-UpperHalfSpace.frag), including all five presets. This complements the preceding UnitBall audit. The shared DE-Kn2cr11 renderer is not credited as fully read by this entry.

**An ordered first-applicable reflection, not a five-reflection sweep.** The loop computes cond=cond && try_reflect(...) for five mirrors. With GLSL short-circuit evaluation, once an attempted reflection returns false, subsequent mirror calls in that iteration are skipped. Thus each outer iteration performs at most one actual reflection/inversion, then starts again from mirror zero. It terminates when every attempted mirror returns true. Replacing this with an unconditional five-mirror pass changes the finite-budget trajectory, scale and trap statistics; it is not a transparent optimization. By contrast, UnitBall explicitly performs its fixed-work planar fold followed by two unconditional mirror calls and uses an exact coordinate fixed-state check. Their Iterations controls count different amounts of work and should not be compared numerically as equal-quality settings.

Plane attempts reflect only for negative signed plane distance. The sphere branch's invert flag selects the accepted side: the constructed B1 and spherical B0 are flagged inverted, so points outside their spheres are accepted and inside points are inverted. At k=1 neither strict comparison accepts the point; it passes through the transform and returns false even though its mathematical position is unchanged. This boundary behavior can consume the remaining iteration budget. If an independent RFF layer adopts a different tie rule, version the resulting recipe behavior and compare boundary images; do not silently reinterpret an existing saved procedural recipe.

**Construction and terminal selection differ materially from UnitBall.** The upper-half-space variant identifies the B0 plane case by the sum of the three angle parameters equaling six. UnitBall instead tests that each equals two. The former also admits triples such as (1,2,3), so these implementations are not interchangeable parameter decoders. This file activates terminal objects only when the corresponding isRealBall component equals exactly one; intermediate slider values do not gradually blend their contribution. section_height is calculated but unused locally. A RFF layer should use explicit enable controls and a validated derived-geometry snapshot, with the mathematical angle convention and special plane case documented.

The terminal distance begins at abs(p.z), then takes the minimum absolute distance to any enabled terminal planes/spheres. The original Z=0 terminal plane is therefore always present. Four of the five presets disable every optional real ball; they still display inverse images of that terminal plane. The 333-pseudoKleinian-like preset additionally enables terminal slot one. There is no initial unit-ball inversion in this map. The return is 0.25 times this unsigned terminal-surface distance divided by accumulated sphere-inversion scale; no global distance-bound proof is provided by the scalar factor.

**Event-driven coloring has a different meaning here.** Only sphere transformations update the trap, immediately before transformation, with absolute world coordinates and squared distance from the current sphere center. Plane reflections and accepted/no-change sphere attempts do not record samples. The fourth component therefore changes its reference center with the selected mirror; it is not squared distance from the origin as in UnitBall. The formula also does not reset orbitTrap at DE entry, so the included renderer's query/reset contract must be checked before using its colors as a stable per-point feature. A RFF adaptation should return query-local statistics together with the field and preserve the selected hit's record across auxiliary normal/AO evaluations.

A useful independent extension is to expose reflection-event statistics as optional material signals: selected mirror identity, number of applied sphere inversions, and minimum center-relative radius, each with an explicitly defined reduction. Those proposed signals are not all implemented by this sample. Finite-budget values depend on reflection order, and minima across differently centered objects cannot be renamed as one physical distance without qualification. Keep palette mapping separate from field construction so recoloring can reuse appropriate cached statistics without rerunning the exact fractal orbit.

**2D transfer and limitations.** A constant-Z image evaluated with full intermediate XYZ state is a valid slice of the represented field. Its sphere transformations can change Z whenever their centers leave the selected plane; dropping that coordinate changes the recurrence. A planar reflection/inversion system using lines and circles is also possible, but needs its own construction and terminal line/circle definition. For a Z=0 slice, the always-present terminal plane can dominate or produce zero regions in plane-preserving cases; choose and label the intended mask rather than assuming a rendered 3D packing's silhouette will appear. Exact 2D motif distance, learned/approximate field value, unsigned shell distance and color event statistics should remain distinct layer outputs.

**Preset evidence and adoption priority.** The five budgets are 246, 246, 250, 500 and 250. All presets enable DepthToAlpha, while some enable floors or request cloud settings even though local volumetric/cloud defines are commented out. These keys establish stored intentions, not a verified active cloud path or alpha export format; the renderer/host contracts still decide their effects. Duplicate AutoFocus entries also require actual preset-application semantics to resolve. The RFF proposal is limited to reproducible optional patterns and event-driven material masks. It does not justify replacing existing GGX lighting, precision-sensitive perturbation/MPA, or lossless map storage. Validate mirror-boundary ties, invalid solver inputs, budget changes, empty optional selections, color-query independence and tiled/video coordinates. No shader compilation, rendering, numerical test, benchmark or external provenance verification was performed. Resolve distinctive implementation licensing and NOTICE attribution before source reuse. Immediate priorities remain environment reflection for appearance and footprint filtering for dense-pattern stability.

## Knighty packing variant: distinguish visible geometry from traversal assistance

**Read scope.** Complete [Ball-Packings-Knighty.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/neozhaoliang/Boyd-Maxwell-Ball-Packings/Ball-Packings-Knighty.frag), including five presets and both preprocessor alternatives. This closes the three local packing-formula comparisons; it does not complete their shared renderer audit.

**Hybrid recurrence and statistics.** This version combines the fixed-work Euclidean triangle folds of UnitBall with the always-present terminal Z=0 plane of UpperHalfSpace. There is no initial unit-ball inversion. Each iteration unconditionally folds XY and attempts the first two mirror transformations, then tests exact equality against the saved pre-fold XYZ point. Sphere transformations scale the differential tracker; plane folds/reflections do not. Initialization uses the all-components-equal-two B0 plane test, constructs all four terminal objects even when disabled, and enables each only for an isRealBall component exactly equal to one. Thus disabled terminal objects still require valid solver results in the active correction path. section_height remains unused locally.

DE resets orbitTrap to vec4(1). Both mirror attempts record absolute coordinates and origin-relative squared radius before checking their reflection condition. This differs from UpperHalfSpace's transformed-sphere-only, center-relative observation. The observed points already include the Euclidean XY fold. A procedural RFF layer must preserve which space, norm, stage and initial cap define each color signal; calling these variants the same orbit-trap mode would lose reproducibility.

**The active DEcor mechanism.** The selected preprocessor branch evaluates every terminal object, even inactive ones. For an active object, its candidate is abs(distance)/scale. For an inactive object, the algebraic candidate is DEcor+abs(distance)/scale, assuming finite positive scale. The minimum also includes abs(p.z)/scale. DE finally multiplies this value by 0.3. Consequently DEcor is a floor on each inactive-object candidate in the returned coordinate scale, rather than an offset that shrinks with accumulated inversion scale. It is not a blend weight or a conventional shell thickness. The inactive candidates can only reduce the minimum relative to ignoring those objects, but the file provides no proof that the resulting scalar is a conservative distance bound for the complete packing.

At DEcor=0, active and inactive objects have identical candidates, so visibility flags cease to distinguish their zero sets. At positive DEcor, an inactive surface alone does not create a mathematical zero through its candidate, but a renderer threshold at or above 0.3*DEcor can still classify such a small returned value as a hit if it wins the minimum. This is a conditional consequence of the field formula, not a measured artifact. Simply feeding this traversal-oriented scalar into an RFF contour or height layer could therefore expose helper surfaces or alter thickness. A future implementation should explicitly return visible-surface proximity separately from any traversal assistance, and use the former for masks, normals and material widths.

**Final versus path-minimum distance.** map initializes a distance and updates its minimum during the loop, but the active final branch returns a fresh dist2balls evaluation at the terminal point. The accumulated minimum is not the returned field. The alternate slow branch would return that path minimum, which changes semantics as well as potential cost. The source-level calls that feed only the unused accumulator may be eliminated by a compiler because dist2balls has no side effects; neither comments describing the branch as fast nor the raw source call count establish actual GPU cost. Inspect generated code and benchmark if this distinction matters to an RFF adaptation. If both reductions are offered as artistic fields, assign explicit recipe modes rather than silently switching between them as a performance setting.

**Preset evidence.** The five stored iteration budgets are 8, 10, 15, 15 and 15; four presets select triangle 236 and the default selects 244. Only Noname3 and Noname1 enable a terminal ball (slot three); the remaining presets still retain the base plane and the inactive-object assistance. None stores DEcor, so their final effective correction requires the host's default/application rules; the declared slider default is 0.1, not proof of a resolved loaded snapshot. All five disable bloom and set zero reflected bounces. Default has OrbitStrength=0 while the other four use about 0.437, so formula-level trap availability is not evidence that every preset displays it. Stored historical Glow keys likewise require renderer support before being treated as active effects.

**RFF transfer.** The useful additions remain fixed-work triangular mirror textures, full-state slices of inversion fields, and clearly named material statistics. A planar circle/line analogue should define its own visible terminal motifs; a full-state slice must retain intermediate Z when sphere centers move it. The active DEcor hack should not be ported into palette lookup, relief height, exact Mandelbrot computation or saved iteration data. For a later 3D/height visibility feature, define the distinction between step bounds and actual hit/normal fields from the outset. That separation also makes debugging overlays useful: show the visible field, helper bound and selected terminal object independently.

**Acceptance and priority.** Verify enabled/disabled terminal selection at correction zero and positive values, thresholds near the correction floor, final versus path-minimum modes, solver validity of inactive objects, trap independence across auxiliary queries, and seams under minification/tiled export. Preserve RFF's perturbation precision and MPA semantics. No compile, render, numerical test, GPU benchmark or external license verification was performed. The local author annotations are provenance leads, not a complete license determination; resolve distinctive-source licensing before reuse and update NOTICE. This optional pattern family remains lower priority than editable environment reflection and palette-footprint filtering for improving existing RFF output.

## MultiIFS: ordered fold recipes and independent material observations

**Read scope.** Full [Tryptophan/MultiIFS.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Tryptophan/MultiIFS.frag), including all nine presets. The rotation helpers in Include/MathUtils.frag were rechecked: they accept degrees, and rotationMatrixXYZ constructs the X/Y/Z matrix product. This is a configurable folded-field example, not a modification of Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA.

**Operation order is part of the asset.** Input receives Position, optional tiling and a row-vector full rotation. Each iteration applies the first scheduled rotation, the selected hybrid fold, abs(z+Fold)-Fold, subtraction of Julia, scaling about offset=Offset+(1,0,0), and the second scheduled rotation. The hybrid modes combine a nonnegative component sort, pyramid reflections and nine ordered plane reflections (three normals repeated three times). Julia is added between the first and subsequent hybrid operations, then subtracted only after the later Fold operation. These translations generally do not cancel across intervening folds. The helpers accept a lowercase julia argument but actually read the global Julia; all current callers pass that same uniform, so the distinction matters when designing reusable nodes rather than changing current behavior.

Mode zero applies the Menger abs/sort, adds Julia, then performs the pyramid fold. At Julia=0 the already sorted nonnegative vector satisfies every pyramid test, so that second stage does nothing. This is an exact local simplification for that parameter case, not a general equivalence between the modes. Modes one, two and three add the repeated three-normal reflections. Their normals depend on Phi=1.61803398875*PhiMult and reciprocal Phi-1; arbitrary PhiMult changes the geometry, so the dodecahedron helper's name is not a guarantee of regular dodecahedral symmetry throughout the slider range. Phi=1 is singular. Validate derived normals rather than letting invalid values become a saved procedural layer.

**Scheduling and distance semantics.** Rotation ranges compare against zero-based n before n increments. The controls' minimum is one, so the first iteration receives neither scheduled rotation under declared values. A window [1,3] affects the second through fourth iterations. The loop always performs Iterations operations, without a radius bailout. ColorIterations restricts only the trap update, not the geometric recurrence. The final terminal is a full signed box distance to z-BoxPosition with extents BoxSize, multiplied by Scale^(-Iterations), then reduced by Fatness*0.1. Fatness is therefore an offset after scale normalization, not an extra box-space extent. Scale=1 removes the offset*(Scale-1) translation, and Scale=0 makes the inverse-power normalization undefined; a new layer must define valid scale ranges explicitly.

For finite normalized reflection normals, valid rotation axes and positive Scale, the fold/rotation portion is piecewise composed of isometries and uniform scaling. That explains the inverse-scale normalization. It does not establish an exact signed distance to the global folded preimage, especially with tiling, fold boundaries or nonstandard domain maps. A RFF contour/relief layer should name this as its represented field and test widths under zoom, rather than promise exact geometric distances from the helper name alone. Preserve row-vector multiplication order when translating the matrices.

**Three different tiling expressions.** Tile one uses mod with a negative period and an absolute-value fold. Tile two uses a positive four-times-extent period and a triangular fold around a translated cell. Both require nonzero extents in each used coordinate. Tile three is a nested clamp expression whose bounds depend on -z and z; where a coordinate is negative these bounds reverse, so its behavior cannot be treated as a conventional periodic mirror map. Mode0_A, Mode0_B and Default select this third expression with TileOffset=(0,0,0); this avoids modulo division in that branch but does not resolve reversed clamp bounds. Do not reproduce this as an undocumented portable 2D tiling convention. Define a mathematical mirror/wrap mode independently, preserve any imported legacy behavior only as an explicit compatibility choice, and validate seams with asymmetric motifs.

**Color field contract.** After the complete per-iteration transform, the formula records minima of abs(XYZ) and squared radius for n<ColorIterations. It then applies ColorScale and ColorOffset to all four trap channels. No query-local reset occurs in this formula, so the included renderer's reset/preservation behavior matters. A negative ColorOffset can make a nominal squared-radius channel negative; color consumers must know whether they receive raw statistics or already remapped values. For RFF, cache raw named statistics and apply color remapping separately where practical. This permits material recoloring without changing geometry and avoids treating a signed remapped value as a squared radius. A ColorIterations budget greater than Iterations simply observes all available iterations; it does not add geometry detail.

**2D transfer.** A compact ordered recipe of planar folds, translations, uniform scales and scheduled 2D rotations can provide procedural masks, roughness patterns or decorative relief. That would be a separately defined planar system. The current XYZ component sorting and mixed-axis reflections can move a nonzero coordinate into Z even from a Z=0 input, and its Julia/Fold/offset controls and rotations can move points off the plane. A faithful slice therefore retains full XYZ state. The signed box terminal restricted to a slice also retains its Z contribution; deleting that term is another change of field. Offer full-state slices and planar recipes as distinct modes with stable operation order and parameters, not as an automatic dimensionality toggle.

**Preset and adoption implications.** The nine presets cover modes zero, two and three; none exercises mode one. The mode-zero presets use six or eight iterations, Mode2A uses eighteen, Mode2_B nine, and the mode-three presets six or eight. Several rotation windows are serialized while their angles are zero, so their presence alone is not evidence of an active rotation effect. Mode2A supplies a nonzero second angle and a finite schedule, making it a useful future schedule test. All presets set PhiMult=1. The detailed Default preset additionally records newer renderer settings absent from earlier examples; resolve host defaults before visual comparisons rather than assuming all omitted fields match.

**RFF recommendation.** The reusable design is an ordered procedural-material recipe with independent geometry and observation budgets, explicit coordinate mapping, and reusable precomputed uniform transforms. It is an optional feature, below environment reflection and footprint filtering in immediate priority. Validate operation order, zero-based schedules, plane preservation, terminal offset units, invalid normals/scales, mirrored texture orientation, minification and tiled/video reproducibility. Keep these fields separate from RFF's exact fractal values and lossless maps. No shader build, rendering, numerical comparison, timing benchmark or external license verification was performed. The source path/author naming is not a verified license; resolve original provenance before adapting distinctive code and record applicable attribution in NOTICE.

## Voxel11: animated cell motifs with explicit occupancy and filtering

**Read scope.** Complete [Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/voxel11.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/voxel11.frag), including seven presets. The info line names a Pythagorean tree, but the active DEbase is simply length(p)-Radius. The box/subtracted-sphere alternative is commented out. This entry does not credit voxel12 or the included renderer as fully audited.

**Cell construction.** The helper named round selects a lattice center with spacing 2*halfWidth and offset halfWidth*Offset. It is a custom floor-based nearest-cell expression, not the standard GLSL round operation. Near the base sphere, DEvox evaluates eight combinations of that center and a neighboring center in the sign of the query displacement along each axis. Exactly on a center plane, sign=0 causes duplicate candidates along that axis. Each candidate gets its own size from vWidthMod at the cell center, so the size remains spatially constant inside that cell's primitive rather than warping continuously with query position.

The active size expression clamps SFactor times a weighted sum of sinusoidal X and Z signals; Y's coefficient is zero. The waves have phase pi*time, hence period two in the host's time units. SFactor is a maximum scaling control rather than a uniform shrink setting, because cell position and phase still change size. At SFactor=1 the sum can exceed one before clamping, producing saturation plateaus. A RFF layer should expose cell spacing, lattice phase, size modulation and time phase separately. Do not describe these cells as random noise or infer seconds from an unverified host time convention.

**Occupancy is decided at centers.** DEboxH receives h=DEbase(cellCenter). Negative h becomes zero; h>=0 becomes at least 2*halfWidth. The remaining expression is sqrt(length(max(abs(localP)-a*(1-RFactor),0))^2+h^2)-RFactor*a. Under the declared nonnegative size controls, a<=halfWidth and RFactor<=1, so an outside/on-surface center contributes a strictly positive value of at least halfWidth when halfWidth>0. Thus visible zero surfaces come from centers strictly inside the base sphere. This is center-sampled occupancy, not clipping every cell against the exact sphere boundary. A thin base feature without an interior cell center can disappear.

For occupied cells, RFactor=1 yields a sphere primitive of radius a. At intermediate values the zero surface is that of a rounded box, with a constant negative value in its inner core. At RFactor=0 the helper is zero throughout the box interior, not a fully signed box distance. These distinctions matter when adapting the output to a relief height or contour mask: surface location alone does not define a useful interior gradient. The independent DEbox helper supplies a signed box expression but is not called by the active base field.

**Broad phase and neighborhood limitations.** HWS=sqrt(3)*halfWidth bounds the cell's half-diagonal. Far outside the base sphere, the function returns DEbase(p)-HWS without visiting cells; near it, the initial fallback is max(halfWidth,DEbase(p)-HWS). That bound relies on the active base being a correctly scaled distance and cell extents staying bounded by halfWidth. It must be reconsidered if the base is replaced with an arbitrary RFF iteration statistic. The eight-candidate search is a bounded local approximation to nearby cells, not a proof of the nearest surface for arbitrary occupancy and position-dependent shrink. An omitted opposite-side neighbor can matter when a nearer-center cell is absent or small. Validate against wider cell enumeration before using the value as a traversal bound; a direct 2D coverage/mask evaluation can instead choose an explicitly sufficient neighborhood.

**Preset evidence.** All seven presets set OrbitStrength=0 and the formula never writes an orbit trap. All disable bloom. The Atomic preset has Radius=0 with positive halfWidth; then no cell center has negative base distance, so under finite declared values every candidate and fallback is positive. It therefore has no zero-level voxel surface from this active formula, despite its name; any visible result must be assessed with renderer thresholds, floor/fog and actual host settings, not inferred as an atomic object from the label. Other presets vary cell width down to 0.02, with Mesoscale02 choosing RFactor=1 and small SFactor. Such settings motivate footprint filtering, but this read contains no render-based evidence of aliasing or timing. The breath preset enables aperture and fog settings, which are separate renderer effects rather than additional local shape logic.

**2D transfer for RFF.** Build a material layer from a 2D lattice of rounded squares or disks, optionally occupied by a selected mask and sized by a deterministic phase field. Four neighboring cells are the direct dimensional analogue of this eight-cell stencil, but sufficiency still depends on occupancy, size bounds and the chosen coverage calculation. Define screen-space versus fractal/material-space cell size, use global coordinates for tiled exports, and filter subpixel cells toward their integrated coverage rather than letting center sampling flicker. A continuous occupancy control can soften thin-mask disappearance, but it changes the represented design and should be an explicit mode. A full 3D slice of the existing cells must retain the Z center and its size phase; it is not identical to a 2D disk/square lattice.

**Adoption and verification.** This is an optional decorative/relief feature, not a reason to pixelate RFF's underlying fractal data or alter saved maps. Validate positive cell width, boundary-center tie rules, zero size, occupancy near thin features, rounded-square versus disk endpoints, wider-neighborhood agreement, time-period consistency and minification across preview/video/tile paths. If animation changes while progressive accumulation is retained, use a specified shutter interval or reset history. No shader compilation, rendering, numerical sampling test, performance benchmark or external license verification was performed. The source's metadata does not establish original authorship/license for all helpers; trace distinctive implementations before reuse and update NOTICE. Existing environment and palette-filtering proposals retain higher immediate priority.

## Voxel12: shell occupancy and contour-band decoration

**Read scope.** Complete [voxel12.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/voxel12.frag), including eight presets, compared with the fully read voxel11 body. The active geometry change is DEbase=abs(length(p)-Radius)-0.1*Radius. The other body change is an explicit renderer subdirectory in the include. Identical field helpers do not imply identical include resolution or full renderer behavior.

**A shell at cell centers, not clipped shell geometry.** For positive Radius R, accepted centers satisfy 0.9R<length(center)<1.1R. The shell's full radial thickness is 0.2R. The strict inequality comes from DEboxH accepting only negative base values. A selected rounded cell can protrude beyond either shell boundary; the algorithm does not intersect every cell primitive with the smooth shell. Lattice offset and spacing can therefore change how many cells survive, and narrow shells can contain no centers locally. The R=0 Atomic preset again has no occupied centers and no zero-level voxel surface under finite positive cell width, independently of its suggestive name.

The base field is a correctly scaled distance to this concentric shell, so the half-diagonal broad-phase argument still has a meaningful geometric basis on both the external side and inside the hollow center. That property does not transfer to an arbitrary RFF iteration-value band. Replacing length(p)-R with a smooth iteration statistic generally changes distance units and gradient magnitude; the same early-out bound would require new justification. The eight-center neighborhood, spatially varying shrink, and positive fallback remain as described for voxel11, including the need to verify omitted-neighbor cases before claiming an exact nearest-cell distance.

**What changes in a 2D slice.** A slice through the smooth shell at height z0 has an outer radial boundary sqrt((1.1R)^2-z0^2) when |z0|<1.1R. It has a central hole only when |z0|<0.9R, with inner radius sqrt((0.9R)^2-z0^2). These describe the continuous base shell, not the final cell union. Near the poles the section becomes a disk rather than an annulus. A faithful slice of the voxel geometry additionally retains discrete Z layers, their center occupancy and their Z-dependent size modulation. A 2D annular lattice is a separate, simpler feature and should be identified as such.

**RFF opportunity: cells along a selected contour band.** Use an existing, explicitly chosen scalar material field to define a band around a level, then evaluate a 2D tile/disk lattice within that band. This can produce beaded outlines, broken contour accents or shallow tiled relief without changing the underlying fractal calculation. Offer field-value width and screen-space width as distinct controls. A local conversion from field deviation to approximate screen distance can use its screen gradient, but flat regions, critical points and multiple crossings require defined handling and footprint integration; division by a small gradient is not a universal distance reconstruction. The layer should preserve RFF's exact iteration/map values and operate only on appearance data.

Center occupancy gives a crisp discrete design but can pop as the band or lattice moves. An independently defined coverage-weighted occupancy mode could reduce that transition, with a visible distinction between fading cell opacity and shrinking its geometry. Those choices have different silhouettes and material responses. For subpixel cells, filter both the band and cell footprint; averaging only the base band cannot remove the lattice's high frequencies. Keep global sample coordinates and time phase consistent across preview, tiled export and video. This is a proposed RFF layer, not functionality already present in these sample bodies.

**Preset and provenance details.** The first seven preset names match voxel11, and this file adds a separate breathe preset alongside breath. The added preset selects RFactor=0, halfWidth about 0.370 and Radius about 4.557, changes Gamma/ToneMapping and fog parameters, and keeps nonzero aperture. A visual comparison must separate its shell/cell differences from those display, lighting and camera changes. All eight presets disable bloom and set OrbitStrength=0; the local formula does not write trap statistics. The inherited Pythagorean-tree info text is not an accurate description of this active shell field or sufficient attribution. Resolve the actual source/license before copying distinctive helpers, and record provenance in NOTICE.

**Acceptance evidence still needed.** Compare shell-center occupancy with an independent reference for inner/outer boundaries, several lattice phases, small shell widths and zero radius; compare the local stencil with wider enumeration; verify rounded-box/disk endpoints, band widths, animation continuity and tile seams. No shader compile, render, numerical test, performance benchmark or external license verification was performed. This decorative feature remains lower priority than environment reflection and palette-footprint filtering for improving existing RFF images.

## Hyperbolic 3-5-3 tessellation: feature identities and two thickness metrics

**Read scope.** Full [hyperbolic-tesselation-3-5-3-colored-named-00.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Knighty%20Collection/Hyperbolic-tesselations-named/hyperbolic-tesselation-3-5-3-colored-named-00.frag), including eleven presets. This particular named variant is distinguished from the already inventoried Klein/half-plane and other similarly named examples; filename similarity does not grant coverage to them.

**Coordinate and folding mechanism.** The field lifts an input point with radius r to (2*pos,1+r^2)/(1-r^2), then applies a Lorentz boost and repeated reflection into a fundamental region. With hdot(a,b)=dot(a.xyz,b.xyz)-a.w*b.w, finite points inside the unit ball lift to hdot(z,z)=-1 with positive W: a hyperboloid sheet, despite the source comment's paraboloid wording. The fold makes X/Y nonnegative and performs reflections in nc and nd on each of exactly Iterations passes. There is no convergence test. U,V,W,T form a weighted sum of four principal vectors, normalized with the Lorentz norm to select the motif node; their sum need not be one. Scaling all four weights by the same positive factor leaves the normalized node unchanged. The all-zero combination is invalid, and a new implementation must validate the norm rather than normalize indiscriminately.

RotAngle enters cosh/sinh directly and is a hyperbolic displacement parameter, not an angle in degrees. Its axis is normalized RotVector or normalize(Eye-Target). The latter makes field geometry depend on camera orientation. For a RFF material mapping, keep this displacement explicit and independent of viewport navigation by default; camera-coupled behavior should be a deliberate effect with matching history invalidation. A zero axis or coincident Eye/Target needs defined behavior even when the displacement happens to be zero.

**Vertices, segments and thickness.** Vertex distance is derived from Lorentz inner products with the principal node. Segment distance projects onto the span of the node and a mirror normal, constrains the projection coefficient with min(0,beta), then renormalizes; it is not simply Euclidean point-to-line distance. Four such segment families and one vertex candidate are evaluated. Hyperbolic radii are applied by the cosh/sinh subtraction identities before the DD conversion to projected-space distance. useUniformRadius instead subtracts VRadius/SRadius after conversion, changing the thickness metric. This is a useful distinction for RFF: material-space thickness and screen-space thickness should be separate settings with defined units. Uniform projected-space radius here is not automatically uniform screen pixels under a perspective camera.

DD uses the original query radius r even after the boost/fold. This read documents that estimator, without establishing exact Euclidean signed distance or a global conservative bound under every parameter setting. The final field is max(r-CSphRad,min(vertex,segments)), intersecting the motif field with a cutting sphere. The clip is applied after evaluating the lift, so it does not protect against the r=1 denominator or invalid square roots/normalizations.
