A robust independent 2D disk pattern should define its valid domain and handle the outer boundary before singular operations; arbitrary clamping of coordinates would change the represented pattern.

**Color follows feature identity.** baseColor repeats the lift, boost, fold and all five distances, then chooses a segment or vertex color from the minimum. Exact ties are resolved by later assignments: vertex wins over D, then C, then B, then the initial A color. This is semantic feature coloring rather than an iteration palette. The cutting sphere is absent from color selection, so a clipped cap receives the nearest underlying feature's color rather than its own material identity. The normal parameter is unused. DE assigns orbitTrap=z4, containing signed folded homogeneous coordinates, not a minimum of absolute positions and squared radius. Keep that raw vector distinct from conventional trap statistics.

For a RFF procedural layer, return field value and feature identifier together from a shared evaluator, or reevaluate only at the selected shading point when storing metadata is more expensive. Do not cache a mutable last-query identity across normal/shadow probes. A shared result is a design candidate, not a measured speedup: the current color evaluation deliberately reconstructs its query-local state. Explicit tie order and clip-surface identity make reproducible material assignment possible. Antialias feature boundaries by coverage; blindly blending numeric IDs has no meaningful material interpretation.

**3D-to-2D transfer.** A full-state constant-Z slice can supply hyperbolic-looking line/vertex masks, but the mixed Z/W reflections and boost generally do not preserve the input plane. A native Poincare-disk tiling would require its own lower-dimensional mirror/node construction. Reuse the architecture of lift, isometry, fold, feature evaluation and projection-aware thickness rather than deleting Z terms from this 3D Coxeter construction. Near the disk boundary, pattern density increases and the finite fold budget may be insufficient; test both convergence of the motif and footprint integration. An adaptive iteration budget is not free if it changes visible topology between preview and export.

**Preset evidence and priority.** All eleven presets choose nonuniform projected thickness (useUniformRadius=false). Ten use camera-directed boosts and a cutting radius of 0.999 with thirteen fold passes; the outside-view icosa to see :) preset uses a fixed axis, seven passes and a smaller cutting radius near 0.602. Default has zero boost but still requests the camera axis. None exercises uniform-radius mode or a zero barycentric vector. These are useful future coverage cases, not tested behavior. This remains an optional mask/material family below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in immediate priority. Preserve RFF's precision-sensitive computation and stored maps. No shader compile, render, numerical metric test, benchmark or external license verification was performed. The header credits knighty 2012; trace the original implementation/license before adaptation and record applicable provenance in NOTICE.

## Bifurcating 5-3-3: symmetry-aware procedural material families

**Read scope.** Full [hyperbolic-tesselation-bifurcating-5-3-3-colored-named-00.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Knighty%20Collection/Hyperbolic-tesselations-named/hyperbolic-tesselation-bifurcating-5-3-3-colored-named-00.frag), including twelve presets. The previous 3-5-3 section describes the shared projection, boost, thickness conversion and feature-color architecture. This variant changes the mirror system and principal vectors; it is not merely a different palette for the same field.

**A different reflection graph.** The three coordinate mirrors are the X, Y and Z axes in homogeneous form. Each iteration takes abs of all XYZ components, then reflects across nd=(-cos(pi/5),-0.5,-0.5,-sqrt(cos(pi/5)^2-0.5)). Its Lorentz norm is one. In contrast, the preceding 3-5-3 variant takes abs of XY and performs two oblique reflections. One oblique reflection per pass is a lower source-level operation count, but equal pass counts do not prove equal fold convergence or equivalent images. The principal vectors and their normalized U,V,W,T combination are also different, so reusing coefficients across the two families does not preserve node position or feature topology.

The word bifurcating names this fixed mirror configuration. There is no time evolution, stochastic branch choice or numerical bifurcation detector in the local formula. A RFF procedural recipe should store its mirror family explicitly and avoid presenting this as an animated branching algorithm. Derived constants can be prepared when the family changes, while node weights, radius settings and boost remain separately identifiable parameters.

**Symmetry provides a meaningful future check.** The fixed nd has equal Y/Z coefficients, and the principal vectors for W and T exchange under Y/Z permutation. Therefore swapping Y/Z together with W/T and the boost-axis Y/Z components gives a corresponding symmetry of the finite fold and scalar field in exact arithmetic. Segment families B and C exchange while A/D remain associated with the same mirrors. A RFF implementation can use this as a differential consistency test for the coordinate mapping, provided the slice/camera mapping and feature colors are transformed too. Do not treat every rendered preset as visually symmetric: their node weights, camera-directed boosts and separately assigned B/C colors can break that appearance. Exact tie handling also needs an explicit convention because sequential B-then-C color assignment gives C priority.

**Geometry and feature outputs.** The evaluator still combines four constrained segment candidates and one vertex candidate, clips with the cutting sphere, and assigns the complete folded vec4 directly to orbitTrap. baseColor independently reconstructs the query and chooses the minimum feature with vertex>D>C>B>A tie priority. It does not color faces or expose a transparency model; a comment proposing face projections is not implemented functionality. Uniform-radius mode remains projected-space subtraction rather than constant pixel thickness. All-zero node weights, zero boost direction, the unit-ball boundary and invalid normalization/square-root inputs need the same explicit policies described for 3-5-3. A cutting sphere evaluated at the end is not a guard against singular intermediate operations.

**Preset coverage.** All twelve presets use thirteen iterations, Eye=(0,0,0), camera-directed boosts, CSphRad=0.999 and useUniformRadius=false. They vary node weights, vertex/segment radii and viewing direction; several reuse the same view and boost while selecting different weight combinations. This is evidence of a family of motif choices, not coverage of uniform-radius mode, outside-domain queries, zero iterations or an independent material-space axis. Preset names such as truncated and rectified identify the intended constructions but are not runtime topology checks or certification of the generated mesh; this shader does not generate an explicit mesh.

**RFF transfer.** Extend the optional hyperbolic mask/material proposal with selectable mirror families, stable feature IDs and explicit thickness units. The full-state 3D slice must keep intermediate Z/W because nd couples them even when the input Z is zero. A native 2D disk family needs separately derived mirrors; substituting abs(XY) and deleting Z would change this group. Filter feature coverage near the disk boundary, keep appearance statistics separate from exact fractal data, and version recipes by their actual transformation sequence. Symmetry-based comparisons, zero-weight rejection, fold-budget convergence, feature tie tests and preview/tile/video consistency would provide useful validation. No shader compilation, rendering, numerical verification, timing benchmark or external license check was performed. Resolve the knighty 2012 provenance and applicable license before adapting distinctive code and update NOTICE. The new family broadens optional patterns but does not displace environment reflection or palette-footprint filtering in the immediate RFF priorities.

## General honeycombs: boundary checker patterns and selectable face materials

**Read scope.** Full [hyperoblic-honeycombs-DEKn2.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/neozhaoliang/Hyperbolic-Honeycombs-Kn2/hyperoblic-honeycombs-DEKn2.frag), including three presets. This extends the earlier fixed-group examples with six mirror-angle parameters, explicit face geometry and a separate boundary-pattern evaluator. The shared DE-Kn2cr11 renderer remains a separate audit item.

**Parameterized mirror construction needs validation.** AB,AC,AD,BC,BD,CD determine negative cosines in a triangular construction of four Lorentz mirror normals. The seed vertex is the Lorentz-normalized row-vector product activeMirrors*inverse(H-weighted mirror matrix). activeMirrors is a continuous weight vector here, not four Boolean toggles. A second mirror representation uses three Euclidean planes and an inversion sphere for points on the ideal boundary. The construction requires valid divisions, nonsingular matrices and a timelike seed. abs inside two square roots accommodates sign errors numerically but does not certify that arbitrary slider combinations describe the intended hyperbolic group. For RFF, validate the Gram/mirror geometry and normalization domains, then cache an immutable derived-parameter snapshot. Do not treat all integer combinations in the UI range as established valid recipes.

**Different convergence contracts.** fold4d performs an X absolute fold plus three Lorentz reflections and sums their nonpositive reflection amounts. For finite values, a zero sum means none of the three changed the point in that pass; the X fold is not part of that sum. This is the code's termination condition, not an independent final-domain residual check. DE records the folded homogeneous vector and computes geometry even when fold4d reports failure. baseColor instead returns BackgroundColor on that failure. Thus geometry and appearance have different exhausted-budget behavior. A RFF material evaluator should return convergence status explicitly alongside its value and feature ID, rather than silently turn an unresolved sample into an ordinary background-colored region.

**Face geometry is implemented in this variant.** Each enabled pair of mirror normals forms a 3-by-3 Gram system with the seed vertex. dFace solves for the projection, rejects positive mirror coefficients with a large sentinel, normalizes the projected point, then applies hyperbolic face thickness before flat-distance conversion. It does not clamp an out-of-face projection to the nearest edge; the separately evaluated segment/vertex fields supply other candidates. Up to six face systems share parameters that are constant per scene, so precomputing their inverse matrices and thickness sinh/cosh is a candidate optimization subject to compiler inspection and measurement. facesColor is declared but unused; the six specific face colors provide the active assignments.

Color selection recomputes feature distances. Face ties prefer CD, then BD, BC, AD, AC, AB through sequential assignments; a face wins an overall tie over a vertex, which wins over segment D/C/B/A. In upper-half-space mode the floor wins last. Disabled faces retain sentinels, so carry an explicit validity bit in a new evaluator rather than treating every minimum-valued sentinel as a real feature. This supports RFF material channels keyed to face/edge/vertex identity, with deliberate boundary coverage and tie behavior.

**The upper-half-space switch is more than a display projection.** The input receives the translated inversion p+Z, scaled by 2/lengthSquared, then translated back before the ball lift. The geometry distance is evaluated in that ball representation, while h=originalZ-0.001 remains in original input units. The final return unions the motif with this plane using min, with no explicit inversion-scale compensation in this body. Therefore the switch must not be described as automatically preserving Euclidean distance units or a proven safe step bound. In ball mode the cutting sphere is intersected by max after the singular lift. drawFloorPattern only controls floor color; it does not remove the plane from upper-half-space geometry. A faithful RFF 3D slice would require a specified coordinate/metric contract, while a pure 2D boundary material can avoid this traversal machinery entirely.

**Direct 2D opportunity: parity coloring on the ideal boundary.** For the floor, planeToSphere maps XY to (2X,2Y,X^2+Y^2-1)/(1+X^2+Y^2), a point on the unit sphere. fold3d applies three plane reflections and a sphere inversion unconditionally in order, counting each applied operation. It stops after a pass in which all four report acceptance, with a separate fixed budget of 300. Success chooses one of two colors by count parity; failure uses floorLineColor. This is an orientation/parity pattern, not a unique cell identifier. Distinct cells can share a color. Unlike lifting to the hyperboloid at radius one, this Euclidean plane/sphere representation operates directly on the boundary.

Sphere inversion treats an exactly zero center-relative denominator as accepted, while k=1 still increments the count and reports a transformation despite no mathematical movement. Define explicit boundary and singularity policies in an independent material implementation; these affect parity and termination, not just speed. The local original floor-color branch runs only after the 4D geometry fold succeeds and the floor wins the distance comparison. A RFF 2D implementation should call its boundary-pattern evaluator directly, with its own convergence result, rather than unnecessarily compute 3D vertices/faces first.

**Line width is currently an intensity multiplier.** After boundary folding, distABCD measures Euclidean proximity to the four mirrors in folded sphere coordinates. The mix weight is (1-smoothstep(0,0.005,edist))*floorLineThickness. The smoothstep width is fixed; floorLineThickness multiplies blend strength and can exceed one, causing color extrapolation rather than widening the distance interval. Two presets select values about 2.230 and 1.102. For RFF, offer separate line width and opacity, and account for the plane-to-sphere and repeated-inversion derivatives when converting to screen footprints. A fixed folded-space width changes apparent thickness across the image. Near highly compressed regions, supersampling or integrated coverage is needed beyond a single local derivative.

**Preset coverage and acceptance.** All three presets use upper-half-space mode and the floor pattern, with 4D iteration budgets 131,353,131; the boundary budget stays 300. They enable different face subsets and nonzero vertex/edge sizes. The default sets floorLineThickness=0, which removes the additional edge blend but does not change the failure color. Their CSphRad=1 is not used for clipping in the active upper-half-space branch. Validate legal mirror sets, seed weights, 3D/4D convergence separately, parity ties, line width/opacity, feature validity and global-coordinate consistency before a RFF prototype. The direct boundary pattern is a stronger 2D transfer than copying the entire ray marcher, but remains an optional material feature below environment reflection and palette filtering. Preserve exact Mandelbrot/MPA data. No shader compilation, rendering, numerical test, timing benchmark or external license verification was performed; resolve original author/source licensing and record distinctive adaptations in NOTICE.

## Shared DE-Kn2cr11 renderer: explicit hit records and stable sampling contracts

**Read scope.** Complete [Boyd-Maxwell-Ball-Packings/DE-Kn2cr11.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/neozhaoliang/Boyd-Maxwell-Ball-Packings/DE-Kn2cr11.frag), including inactive alternatives and optional cloud/volume branches. The Hyperbolic-Honeycombs-Kn2 copy is byte-for-byte identical. The inventory counts 841 lines including its terminal newline; Get-Content returns 840 text lines. Its 3DKn-1.0.5 camera and BufferShader-1.0.2 were already fully audited, so the local formula-to-camera-to-display chain is now traced for these two directories. No runtime execution is implied.

**Hit refinement is a field query contract.** trace initializes the trap, takes a dithered first step, then advances using the minimum of light-sphere distance and FudgeFactor times the object/floor field. The hit threshold grows with Ray.Pos and has a fixed MIN_EPS floor. Refinement advances by dist-1.5*epsModified repeatedly; it is not bracketed root finding. Floor and light classifications use equality with the selected distance. These mechanisms depend on the supplied scalar being meaningful for tracing and do not convert the previously documented approximate fields into exact distances. A RFF height/visibility experiment should define distance, hit status, feature ID and refinement interval explicitly, rather than import a scalar minimum and infer material ownership later.

**The material-statistics concern is confirmed.** Object normals use six central-difference DE calls at a backed-off point, before getColor reads the global orbitTrap. There is no save/restore of the hit trap around those probes. Formula-local resets therefore leave a probe's statistics, while formulas that accumulate minima without per-query reset can merge statistics from multiple march/refinement/normal queries. getColor additionally mutates W by taking its square root. A providesColor formula instead evaluates baseColor(hit,normal) after normal estimation; the reviewed honeycomb implementation independently recomputes its field there. Its result is blended with BaseColor by OrbitStrength, so semantic feature colors are not necessarily displayed at full strength. For RFF, pass immutable sample/hit statistics or deliberately reevaluate the selected shading position, keeping auxiliary derivative/visibility queries from changing material input. Reuse the existing relief normal where it already meets the intended model; six extra fractal-field evaluations are not a free normal improvement.

**AO is geometric visibility sampling, not ordinary image contrast.** With MULTI_SAMPLE_AO, one random direction is drawn from a normal-oriented cone, then sampled at geometrically increasing distances (factor 1.61). The normalized distance ratio is forced nonincreasing across levels before averaging its deficit. The loop runs from one to less than maxIterAO; budgets zero or one leave zero weight and the final division has no local identity fallback. FudgeAO=0, a zero initial field scale or a grazing direction also need defined handling. These are acceptance conditions for a new implementation, not a request to repair the GMT sample. RFF's 2D relief would need a specified height geometry and visibility method before adopting this AO; it should not reinterpret iteration differences as world-space free distance.

**Shadow and lighting distinctions.** The Eiffie branch derives cone growth from ShadowBlur/lightDistance; ShadowSoft participates in the step expression. perf selects between formulas with different assumptions about interior field validity. SSS blends a second shadow query using a different radius and a square root; it is an artistic shadow approximation, not a full subsurface transport model. The surface model is a normalized Blinn-Phong-like lobe with a Fresnel term whose f0 is derived from SpecularExp. This differs from RFF's existing roughness/IOR-based GGX and is not a reason to replace it. Preserve the useful separation of AO influence on ambient, camera and point light, but measure any added visibility samples and maintain coherent units.

**Color and output ordering.** Unless linearGamma is defined, hit color is clamped and raised to Gamma before lighting. FloorColor is assigned afterwards and bypasses that conversion in this path. Colored specular and diffuse are both multiplied by hit color at the end of lighting. The later buffer normalizes weighted samples and applies display transforms, as already documented. An independent RFF adaptation needs one explicit linear-light contract for every material source and effect, rather than inheriting these uneven conversions. DepthToAlpha writes gl_FragDepth=1/Ray.Pos on the first trace reaching the depth block; it does not assign alpha. Alpha in the camera output is accumulated sample weight. Light hits return before the depth block, and the final EXR channel mapping belongs to the host. Thus the setting name alone cannot establish a usable RFF depth export format.

**Fog has analytic limits and per-segment sample state.** fogAmount3 evaluates (1-exp(-A))/A, with A proportional to ray displacement along the fog direction. At A=0 the mathematical limit is one, but this implementation divides directly; exponential clamping does not supply that limit. A stable independent implementation should use an analytic limit/series near zero, including disabled-density and horizontal-ray cases. The volume sampler draws distance-to-light importance samples using a discriminant sqrt(A*C-B^2); zero-length or collinear configurations need their own finite handling. Its global fogstrata counter increments per sample without being reset at each reflected segment. After the first segment, its stratum index can exceed the local HF_FogIter interval, pushing nominal sample fractions beyond the intended unit interval before t is clamped. A new renderer should key samples explicitly by segment/bounce and dimension, with a local stratum index for each segment, rather than reuse this mutable counter.

The volume phase expression deliberately omits a normalization factor and uses per-channel anisotropy. Constant-density color treatment also differs between the transmission and scattering-density expressions. These are appearance choices/limitations, not verified physical transport. RFF should only consider volumetric integration after defining real depth, path length and occlusion; this is not an immediate 2D shader transfer. The optional cloud branch is compiled only under USE_IQ_CLOUDS, so serialized cloud settings in files without that define do not activate clouds. Its noise-octave sum, altitude envelope, increasing step length and premultiplied front-to-back accumulation form a separate effect, not the same density as the exponential height fog.

**Reflection and progressive rendering.** color traces up to ReflectionsNumber+1 segments, adds each shaded/fogged segment with a color throughput, then multiplies throughput by Reflection and transmission. It stops on zero normal, small throughput, light hit or distance exhaustion. This is not a stochastic GGX environment integrator or a general path tracer. Ray state, trap state, fSteps and volume sample state have different lifetimes; an RFF implementation should model those lifetimes explicitly and preserve deterministic global sampling for tiled/video rendering. Normal fallback to zero when normalization yields NaN avoids propagating that vector but can also end reflection; it does not prove a correct normal was obtained.

**Practical RFF conclusions.** The strongest reusable lessons here are immutable per-hit material data, explicit geometry-versus-display quantities, valid zero-sample identities, stable analytic limits and independent sampling dimensions. These strengthen existing appearance work and future height/mask layers without changing precision-sensitive Mandelbrot/MPA computation or lossless map formats. Keep environment reflection and palette-footprint filtering ahead of a full 3D visibility/volume port. Validate probe-order independence, constant-color reconstruction, zero AO/fog cases, first-hit depth semantics, reflected-segment sampling and preview/tile/video equivalence. No compile, numerical test, rendered comparison, benchmark or external source-license verification was performed. Header credits and embedded links identify syntopia, knighty, Eiffie, ChrisJRodgers and other source leads; resolve the actual licenses of distinctive reused components and update NOTICE before implementation.

## AlgebraicSurfsViews_01: derivative-normalized implicit shells

**Read scope.** Complete [AlgebraicSurfsViews_01.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/AlgebraicSurfsViews_01.frag), including all eight presets and seven active polynomial choices. The local header credits knighty 2016 and an earlier algebraic-surface estimator. The separate ess15 variant is not covered by this entry.

**Polynomial and coordinate mechanism.** ImpType selects Barth6, Labs7, Barth10, Sarti12, Sarti8, Togliatti_5 or Chmutov8. These are explicit homogeneous polynomial expressions in four coordinates, with degrees five through twelve, not escape-time fractals. Several constants are rounded decimal approximations, including the Labs cubic-root parameter and PHI powers; this read does not establish equivalence to an exact symbolic original. The Togliatti, Labs and high-degree Sarti terms were read in full, including unused intermediates; changing algebraic rearrangement or precision would require numerical verification near cancellation and singular points.

Trans uses p.xyz=2*z/(1+GFactor*lengthSquared(z)) and p.w=(1-GFactor*lengthSquared(z))/(1+GFactor*lengthSquared(z)), then rotates ZW and XYZ. At GFactor=0 this is (2*z,1), not (z,1). It saves fff=1/(1+preRotationW) before the rotations. Thus the later correction factor is tied to the pre-rotation chart, while the polynomial sees rotated homogeneous coordinates. Negative GFactor introduces a denominator singularity on a finite sphere. RotVector is normalized without a zero-axis fallback, and the declared time uniform is unused. A RFF layer should define coordinate scale, chart, rotations and valid domain explicitly, with derived transforms cached per parameter snapshot.

**Finite differences are in ambient four-space.** Fn evaluates the polynomial at the transformed point and four positive coordinate offsets, using Eps=1/2048 and IEps=2048. It takes the norm of this forward-difference vector, adds param2*abs(v)/(abs(v)+1)+0.001, divides the residual v by that denominator, then multiplies by abs(fff). A label calling param2 a Lipschitz correction does not supply a proven Lipschitz bound. The derivative estimate is with respect to four independent transformed coordinates; it is not explicitly the chain-rule gradient with respect to the original XYZ query. An independent RFF contour or normal implementation must choose the intended coordinate-space derivative rather than equate those norms.

There is also a level-set-specific distinction: v is reduced by LevelSet before subtraction from the four unshifted polynomial samples. Each difference therefore includes LevelSet/Eps in addition to the forward polynomial derivative. A constant level shift should not change the derivative of the residual; this code's denominator nevertheless changes that way. Every supplied preset uses LevelSet=0, so those presets do not exercise the distinction. In a new implementation, form consistent residual differences or compute the polynomial gradient analytically, then apply the transformation Jacobian as required. Analytic differentiation or automatic differentiation can avoid four extra polynomial samples, but increased intermediate storage and numerical cancellation still require measurement; no performance improvement is claimed here.

**The shell is one-sided in normalized-field coordinates.** DE transforms the normalized field f into abs(f+IntThick)-IntThick. For positive thickness this is nonpositive on [-2*IntThick,0], with zero surfaces at both endpoints. It is not a band centered at f=0. At zero thickness it becomes an unsigned zero-set field. Thickness is measured after the estimator's normalization, not guaranteed Euclidean or screen-pixel distance. CutByPlane intersects using -rotatedW*min(1,fff), and CutBySphere uses the original query's sphere distance. Both cuts occur after Fn and another Trans call, so they do not protect singular chart evaluation. The plane-at-infinity term is a transformed homogeneous-plane test, not generally a simple Euclidean plane distance.

baseColor reevaluates Fn and uses normal-dependent tint 0.2*n+0.6 above the inner shell threshold, otherwise red. It does not explicitly identify sphere/plane caps, and writes no orbit trap. With normalized normals that tint spans roughly 0.4 to 0.8 per component; it is not a conventional [0,1] normal visualization. For RFF, material identity for outer shell, inner shell and cuts should be explicit if such a layer is offered, with immutable field/gradient results to avoid unnecessary repeated computation or probe-dependent colors.

**2D transfer.** A full-coordinate slice of the transformed implicit surface can supply decorative contours or relief masks without ray marching. Retain the ZW rotation and all homogeneous coordinates; dropping W or assuming W=1 after that rotation changes the curve. A simpler 2D implicit layer can use its own f(u,v), level and gradient. Locally, (f-level)/length(screenGradient(f)) can approximate screen-distance for contour-width control where the gradient is nonzero, but fails near critical points and does not integrate multiple crossings inside a pixel. Use explicit fallback/coverage rules and validate against supersampling. The architectural lesson transfers to RFF appearance fields; the exact Mandelbrot iteration, perturbation and MPA calculations must remain unchanged.

**Preset evidence and implementation scope.** The eight presets cover all seven polynomial choices: Barth6 appears twice, while the other choices each appear once. All set GFactor=0, LevelSet=0, param2=0 and IntThick=0.00191. Default uses a ZW angle of -90 degrees and the plane cut; Derwich uses +90 and a sphere cut; the remaining named polynomial views use zero rotations and sphere cuts of varying radii. Thus nonlinear charts, nonzero levels and the correction parameter are untested by these examples. The first preset retains an undeclared param1 key, and the #version 460 line contradicts its trailing 1.10 compatibility comment; neither establishes importer or driver support. These are integration conditions to verify if adapting the example, not separate RFF feature proposals.

**RFF recommendation and validation.** Treat analytic/chain-rule gradients and well-defined contour-band units as the useful reusable mechanisms. A gallery of algebraic masks is optional and lower priority than improving existing environment reflection or dense-palette filtering. Validate nonzero levels, chart singularities, critical points, inner/outer shell boundaries, cut materials, finite-difference/analytic agreement and preview/tile/video footprints. No compilation, rendering, symbolic/numerical comparison, benchmark or external license verification was performed. Trace the original formula implementations and actual licenses before copying distinctive coefficient sets; record named sources and adaptations in NOTICE.

## Benesi PineV322: scheduled orbit observations and geometry feedback

**Source coverage.** The complete [PineV322.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Benesi/PineV322.frag), including all five presets, was read. The useful RFF direction is explicit observation timing and channel semantics for appearance fields. This hybrid 3D iteration is not a replacement for RFF's Mandelbrot recurrence or a shader-only acceleration of it.

**Transform order is part of the formula.** Iteration starts at 1 and continues while i<Iterations and r<Bailout, so the maximum number of executed rounds is Iterations-1. Each round performs an optional X warp, two independently scheduled transform blocks, the mandatory Transform1, up to two polygonal transforms, PinePart, the visible trap update, two possible geometry-feedback operations, a stored-trap update, and finally the Julia constant or component-scaled input addition. Two matching schedules execute in sequence; they are not alternatives. Rotation is active from RotIter1 onward, rather than only at that iteration. The second optional block uses its own offset/scale/count but dispatches on tType1 again. An independent RFF operator system should give each stage its own selector and retain the exact stage order in recipes.

Transform1 and T1 rotate into an orthonormal basis, apply componentwise absolute value and scale, optionally rotate there, then undo the basis and translate X. T2 replaces components with offset pairwise Euclidean lengths; T3 uses pairwise sums of absolute components; T4 uses pairwise squares; T5 uses fourth roots of sums of eighth powers. T5 is degree two, not the degree-one L8 norm. Polygonal shaping reduces an angle by repeated sector subtraction and rescales the YZ pair with a cosine ratio; the optional polyhedral step also rescales the full vector. Fractional side counts and singular cosine denominators need explicit semantics. SquareCube is defined but never called by this file's active iteration.

**Three visible-trap modes have different meanings.** ColorIteration=0 or ColorIteration>=Iterations accumulates componentwise minima of squared XYZ and squared radius after PinePart. However, the starting trap is min(vec4(pos,length(pos)),10), with signed XYZ and a linear radius; negative initial components can remain negative when minimized against subsequent squares. For an interior selected iteration, trapmode=1 replaces the trap with signed XYZ and linear radius, while trapmode=2 minimizes that one sample against the initial trap. The latter is not a minimum over all preceding iterations. If bailout occurs before the selected iteration, the initial trap remains. Thus mode selection changes observation window, aggregation, units and signedness together. RFF should specify those separately: sampling stage, index/window, axis/radius definition, minimum versus snapshot, and a validity/fallback value when the window is never reached. A squared-radius consumer cannot silently accept a signed snapshot or linear radius.

**Stored history also changes geometry.** orbitstore1 begins as capped absolute XYZ plus linear radius and records componentwise minima through orbititer1. At orbititer1app it is first reweighted: the new W is the length of the old four-component vector times orbit1.w. A second four-component length then controls a translation along orbitApp1.xyz plus a shared orbitApp1.w offset. This happens before the current round's stored-trap update, so feedback normally uses prior stored history; the current value can enter afterward when the recording window still applies. Even orbititer1=0 retains the initial sample, rather than representing absent history. zlapp separately translates by the length of component-weighted current XYZ. These feedback paths alter subsequent orbit values and the shape. They cannot be added as postprocessing while claiming to preserve the original fractal.

**Distance and precision contracts must be derived independently.** dr receives signed transform scales and ends each round with 2*r*dr+1 using the radius after the additive term, regardless of manPower. The terminal estimator is 0.5*log(r)*r/dr. This is not a demonstrated conservative distance bound for the nonlinear transforms, polygonal shaping, warps or history feedback. In particular, their Jacobians are not represented by simply multiplying by a scale. Negative powers use radial magnitude raised to abs(manPower) while changing angular signs; they do not implement a reciprocal radial power. The power-two branch divides by the YZ radius on the X axis. Zero radius, zero or signed derivative factors, and signed inputs to floating-point pow in T5 require attention before reuse. These observations define adaptation requirements, not a proposal to spend RFF work fixing this reference renderer.

**3D-to-2D transfer.** The strongest reusable mechanism is an immutable, explicitly typed orbit observation that can independently drive palette, roughness, emission or relief. A cheaper initial feature can remap fields RFF already stores; new per-orbit observations require computation and map-format design. MPA skips cannot be assumed to preserve an arbitrary minimum or selected-iteration snapshot: derive a compatible aggregate/reconstruction or explicitly account for the extra work without sacrificing precision. A decorative 2D fold or polygonal texture can use analogous operators with footprint filtering, but discarding Z from the hybrid recurrence is not equivalent to taking a full 3D slice. Geometry feedback belongs to a separate formula extension with its own perturbation and acceleration analysis.

**Presets and verification limits.** The five presets are lolcolors, colorstest, Christmas, fire and Default. Earlier presets retain controls not declared by this formula, including old transform names and texture/palette settings whose support depends on the included renderer and importer. Christmas assigns false to the integer trapmode; this is not proof of a valid parsed mode. Default explicitly disables optional transform, polygon and feedback schedules, uses Julia mode, Iterations=3 and ColorIteration=3, and therefore selects the accumulation branch rather than a third-iteration snapshot. The examples do not establish coverage of the more elaborate feedback paths. Before implementation, test scheduled observations reached/unreached by bailout, signed versus squared channels, coincident stages, cached-field persistence and MPA agreement. No shader compilation, rendering, numerical comparison, benchmark or external license verification was performed. Original implementation provenance and actual licensing must be established before adaptation, with matching NOTICE entries where required. This optional appearance-field extension does not supersede the environment-reflection or dense-palette-filtering priorities.

## Cyclic hyperbolic tessellation, Knighty named-00 variant: finite-node contracts

**Coverage and comparison method.** The complete active shader body of [hyperbolic-tesselation-cyclic-m-3-n-3-colored-named-00.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Knighty%20Collection/Hyperbolic-tesselations-named/hyperbolic-tesselation-cyclic-m-3-n-3-colored-named-00.frag) was read and the entire file was diffed against the previously fully reviewed Kashaders cyclic variant. The prior source's inventory hash was rechecked. All 40 preset payloads and intervening comments match byte-for-byte after removing only preset-title lines; the title encodings differ. Shared preset content therefore reuses that completed review rather than being counted as new behavior. The changed executable code was inspected directly. This is full comparison-based coverage, not a claim that the two files are interchangeable.

**The important difference is the principal node's domain.** This version immediately normalizes the weighted seed U*pabc+V*pbdc+W*pcda+T*pdba by sqrt(w*w-dot(xyz,xyz)). It always includes vertex distance in geometry and color selection. The Kashaders variant retains pp=-hdot(seed,seed), normalizes only when pp>1e-4, and otherwise omits the vertex feature while using pp in segment projection. In the normalized pp=1 branch, the segment formulas are algebraically equivalent: this variant's negative determinant and opposite numerator signs cancel. That equivalence does not extend to non-timelike seeds or the other variant's threshold branch. The all-zero seed is already invalid for unconditional normalization. A RFF pattern generator should validate the seed's metric class explicitly and either restrict its controls to supported finite nodes or implement a separately derived ideal/other-node model; replacing a negative radicand with abs would change the geometry rather than establish validity.

The TypeN slider ends at 5 here, compared with 6 in the other variant. The mirror construction still contains sqrt(3/4-cos(pi/M)^2) and the denominator 3-4*cos(pi/M)^2: its direct zero-denominator restriction concerns M, not an interchangeable M/N label. The displayed controls bound M to 4..5 and N to 3..5, but imported recipe validation must independently enforce the supported domain. Slider metadata is not proof that loaded settings or generated shader uniforms obey it.

**Reusable shader mechanism.** The Poincare-ball query is lifted to four coordinates (2*pos,1+r*r)/(1-r*r), optionally boosted along a fixed or camera-derived axis, then folded for a fixed number of rounds by absolute XY and two ordered Minkowski-plane reflections. This maps repeated structure into a representative region, where four segment distances and one vertex distance determine the field and material identity. The lift is a hyperboloid construction despite the source's paraboloid comment. The cutting sphere is combined afterward, so it does not itself protect evaluation at r=1. The boost makes camera-derived orientation a geometry input; a RFF material pattern would usually benefit from a separate stable pattern transform so camera movement does not unintentionally change the texture.

Segment projection clamps one coefficient with min(0,beta) before normalization. Thickness is applied either in hyperbolic distance before DD conversion or as a projected-space subtraction afterward. Neither choice is automatically a constant screen-pixel line width. baseColor recomputes the same fold and distances, ignores its normal argument, and resolves exact ties in vertex>D>C>B>A order. It does not assign a separate cutting-sphere material. For a new RFF procedural layer, return field value, feature identity and validity together, and reuse that immutable result where practical. Screen-space filtering should integrate coverage across feature boundaries instead of assuming interpolated categorical identities are valid materials.

**2D adoption and priority.** A full 3D slice could generate colored arcs, nodes and edge masks for RFF's palette, roughness or relief inputs without tracing rays. Keep all lifted coordinates, mirror operations and the chosen slice coordinate; dropping the third coordinate from these mirrors is not a derivation of a native hyperbolic-disk tessellation. A native 2D pattern needs its own mirror construction. Both options need pixel-footprint handling near the disk boundary, where repeated features become arbitrarily small. A finite fold budget also needs a defined unresolved-region policy. This is an optional pattern family, below improvements to existing environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in near-term priority.

**Preset scope and validation.** The 40 recipes comprise Default plus numbered entries 38..76. Their ordered (M,N) pairs are (4,3), (5,3), (4,4), (4,5) and (5,5), with Default also (5,3). They explore seed combinations, boost and radii but do not demonstrate arbitrary parameter-domain validity or ideal-node behavior. In a future RFF implementation, compare eligible normalized-node cases against the generalized variant, explicitly test zero and near-null seeds, verify material ties and cut boundaries, and compare supersampled full-frame, tiled and video output near densely packed edges. No rendering, shader compilation, numerical geometry comparison, benchmark or external license verification was performed. The source identifies knighty (2012); verify original licensing and record appropriate provenance in NOTICE before adapting distinctive implementation code.

## 5-3-n named-00 variant: keep feature eligibility consistent

**Coverage.** The active body of [hyperbolic-tesselation-5-3-n-colored-named-00.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Knighty%20Collection/Hyperbolic-tesselations-named/hyperbolic-tesselation-5-3-n-colored-named-00.frag) was read in full, and a complete file diff was inspected against the previously reviewed Kashaders 5-3-n named source. That prior source's hash still matches the audit inventory. The entire preset section, including all 25 names, settings and intervening text, is byte-identical. This entry records comparison-based full coverage and the behavioral differences rather than duplicating the earlier detailed family analysis.

**Finite-node specialization.** This version restricts the displayed Type range to 4..5 instead of 4..6 and unconditionally normalizes the weighted principal node as a timelike vector. The other version retains pp=-hdot(seed,seed), normalizes only for pp>1e-10, and omits vertex geometry otherwise. Its segment projection carries pp; the current version assumes pp=1. Their determinant and coefficient sign differences cancel algebraically in that normalized case. Outside it, the current version supplies no alternative node model. Zero seeds and nonpositive normalization radicands need an explicit validity policy in an independent implementation. The 1e-10 threshold in the other version is also different from the 1e-4 threshold in the cyclic family; neither should become a universal tolerance by copying a convenient constant.

Unlike the cyclic pair, the 5-3-n baseColor path is effectively unchanged: it always considers vertex distance, including in the generalized source whose DE can exclude vertex geometry. The finite-node specialization consistently considers vertices in both places where normalization is valid. For RFF, the transferable requirement is a shared feature-eligibility mask for field evaluation and material selection. An absent geometric feature must not win a color/roughness selection merely because its distance function was still evaluated. Keep ties deterministic and define a separate material policy for clipping boundaries. This is a requirement for a new procedural material layer, not a claim that RFF currently has this reference implementation's mismatch.

**Mechanism and 2D use.** Here nc=(0,-cos(pi/n),sin(pi/n),0), while nd combines the fixed cos(pi/5) with cot(pi/n) and a derived fourth component. These are a chain-family construction, distinct from the preceding cyclic family. The remaining lift, boost, ordered reflections, constrained segment projection and hyperbolic/projected thickness choices follow the already documented pattern. Reusing a common evaluator with family-specific validated mirror data is plausible; swapping a title or one integer while retaining the wrong mirror construction is not. A full-coordinate 2D slice can produce decorative edge and node masks without ray marching. A native 2D disk pattern requires its own geometry, and either route needs footprint filtering near increasingly dense boundary features. It does not accelerate Mandelbrot calculation or justify changing perturbation precision.

**Recipe evidence.** All 25 recipes use 13 fold rounds and nonuniform (hyperbolic) radii. Fifteen use Type=4 and ten use Type=5, including Default. Seed combinations range from individual nodes to mixtures, and boosts vary. These presets are useful comparison cases, but do not exercise Type=6, uniform-radius mode, zero seeds or every invalid-domain boundary. Before adapting a procedural layer, validate eligible feature identities, normalized-branch agreement, singular inputs, fold-budget behavior, and stable antialiasing across preview, export tiles and video. No rendering, shader compilation, numerical comparison, benchmark or external license verification was performed. Verify the original knighty implementation's license and preserve appropriate NOTICE attribution before code adaptation. This adds conditions to the optional pattern proposal without changing the current environment-reflection and palette-filtering priorities.

## Honeycombs with DE-Raytracer: direct planar patterns and reproducible recipes

**Coverage.** The complete 1,478-line [hyperbolic-honeycombs-DERaytracer.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/neozhaoliang/Hyperbolic-Honeycombs-DERayTracer/hyperbolic-honeycombs-DERaytracer.frag), including all 14 preset blocks, was read. Its geometry follows the same general mechanisms previously documented for the DEKn2 honeycomb example, but the included renderer is DE-Raytracer.frag. KN_VOLUMETRIC, USE_EIFFIE_SHADOW and MULTI_SAMPLE_AO are defined before that include; definitions alone do not establish that this renderer consumes those names or reproduces the other renderer's behavior.

**Direct 2D opportunity.** The floor evaluator maps XY to the unit sphere using (2*x,2*y,r*r-1)/(1+r*r), then applies three Euclidean plane reflections and one sphere inversion per round. It records reflection parity to select two checker colors and uses the minimum distance to the transformed mirrors for edge tint. This is a direct plane-to-pattern calculation: a RFF layer can call the planar evaluator without a 3D ray, surface intersection, or the enclosing baseColor function's successful 4D-fold requirement. It could produce a color overlay or a mask for roughness and relief while leaving Mandelbrot computation unchanged. The reflection count must count actual transformations under a declared boundary convention; the source's sphere routine also increments at the identity scale k=1, and uses a fixed 300-round budget separate from Iterations. Return convergence explicitly instead of treating exhausted work as a valid chamber classification.

floorLineThickness multiplies the blend weight after smoothstep(0,0.005,edist); it changes tint amplitude rather than the transition's width. The first preset sets 1.10232 and the last 1.85, allowing extrapolation toward/beyond floorLineColor. For RFF, expose width and opacity separately, define their units, and compute filtered coverage in the original output pixel footprint. A fixed distance in folded sphere coordinates is not constant pixel width on the input plane. Finite differences or a propagated transformation Jacobian can help estimate local footprint, but multiple cells within a pixel still require appropriate integration. Do not introduce arbitrary coordinate clamps that silently change the pattern near singularities.

**Geometry and material contract.** Six integer mirror relations produce a triangular mirror basis and a normalized weighted vertex. Absolute values inside square roots do not validate every input group, and matrix inverses and timelike normalization need their own domain checks. Face distances project onto a span of the vertex and two mirrors, reject positive constrained coefficients with a sentinel, and normalize the remaining projection. The six face projection matrices depend on settings rather than the query point: caching valid inverses is a candidate optimization if this feature is implemented, subject to measurement and unchanged precision. Return validity independently of the sentinel so a disabled face cannot acquire a material through an equality tie.

DE uses the folded coordinates even when fold4d reports failure, whereas baseColor returns BackgroundColor in that case. The upper-half-space branch adds the original Z floor distance to the union regardless of drawFloorPattern, which controls coloring only; its ball-map distance is returned without an explicit scale correction for that map. A standalone RFF 2D layer should specify convergence, footprint and masking independently and should not import this estimator as a proven distance bound. The final folded four-vector is assigned to orbitTrap; it is not an accumulated minimum. These are adaptation constraints, not a request to repair GMT.

**Recipes need complete state and stable identity.** There are two blocks named default with different camera, lighting and geometry settings. The first explicitly enables upper-half-space mode, patterned floor and faces AD/BD; the second omits those settings and uses a different mirror group. Later presets similarly omit many new controls. Their effective behavior depends on whether the importer resets defaults or applies patches to current state, so the names and omitted fields cannot establish reproducibility. A RFF procedural-layer recipe should have a stable identifier, complete normalized settings, schema version and a defined defaulting rule. This is separate from RFF's existing palette recipe IDs and must not change their frozen generation sequence.

The last preset explicitly enables an upper-half-space checker floor and uses CD=7; the preceding upper-half-space preset's title says 1110 while its activeMirrors value is 1,1,0,1. Actual fields take precedence over display names when constructing comparison cases. Fold budgets range up to 1,000 and do not establish convergence or performance. No shader compilation, rendering, benchmark, numerical geometry comparison or external license verification was performed. The planar checker mechanism is an optional material/pattern extension, not a higher-priority replacement for environment reflection or dense-palette filtering. Verify original implementation provenance and licensing before adapting code and maintain NOTICE acknowledgements.

## Kleinian_test23: invariant-plane patterns and transform-aware filtering

**Coverage and provenance.** The complete [Kleinian_test23.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/Kleinian_test23.frag) and its ten presets were read. The header credits Jos Leys (December 2016) and cosmetic modifications by Knighty, but its license text says to ask Jos Leys. This is not an established reuse license. The mechanisms below are investigation leads for RFF; do not copy the distinctive implementation or its constant sets without verifying permission and recording provenance in NOTICE.

**The main round is a specific ordered composition.** With a=KleinR and b=KleinI, it first shears X by (b/a)*Y, wraps XZ into centered periodic intervals, optionally also wraps Y into [0,a), and undoes the shear using the resulting Y. A curved separation test then optionally applies the full-vector central inversion (-b,a,0)-z. It updates componentwise orbit-trap minima at that stage, before TransA. TransA combines inversion in the unit sphere with sign changes and translation: the resulting components are (x/r2-b, a-y/r2, -z/r2), and DF is multiplied by 1/r2. TransAInv is provided but never called by the active evaluator. A squared separation below 1e-12 from the stored two-step-old iterate ends the main loop. This is a finite-precision near-cycle test, not proof of an exact period or a transferable replacement for RFF's fast-period-guessing and MPA.

**Terminal refinement is a different phase.** After the main rounds, Final_Iterations repeatedly samples min(y,Clamp_y)/max(DF,Clamp_DF), applies only TransA, and finally samples once more. Here y is either z.y or min(z.y,a-z.y), depending on ShowBalls. There is no wrapping, separation reflection or trap update during this phase. Increasing Final_Iterations changes the minimum over terminal candidates and can change the field; it is not merely a more accurate evaluation of a fixed number of main rounds. The returned value can be negative. DF tracks the inversion's local scale within smooth branches, while the clamps and minimum construction do not by themselves prove a signed distance bound. Keep any RFF pattern mask definition separate from a claimed ray-marching distance.

The optional outer inversion uses p'=R^2*(p-InvCenter-ReCenter)/lengthSquared(p-InvCenter-ReCenter)+InvCenter. Despite the control comment calling InvRadius a squared radius, the code squares it. Its distance conversion is r2*d/(R^2+r*d), not just division by a local scale. For negative d its denominator can vanish; the inversion center itself is singular. ReCenter changes the input center but is not added to the output center. A future coordinate-warp UI should define these units and transformations explicitly rather than inherit ambiguous labels.

**A concrete 3D-to-2D restriction exists here.** For positive wrap widths, an input with Z=0 remains on that plane through the wraps, full-vector reflection and TransA. The outer inversion also preserves it when InvCenter.z=ReCenter.z=0. Thus a direct XY evaluator can reproduce the restricted iteration with r2=x*x+y*y, including its branch tests and terminal phase. This is stronger than merely deleting a coordinate from an arbitrary 3D formula. For nonzero centers or a different slice, retain the full 3D state. The ten supplied presets all use zero Z components in those two centers, but that does not establish behavior at singular points or a guaranteed planar distance field.

A RFF appearance layer could use the restricted field as an optional ornamental mask or use the pre-TransA trap channels for color and roughness. These are extra procedural calculations, not accelerated Mandelbrot pixels. The source does not reset orbitTrap inside JosKleinian or DE, so an independent evaluator must initialize per-query state and return it explicitly; otherwise normal, shadow or neighboring sample evaluations can contaminate appearance. Trap XYZ represent absolute components and W represents squared radius. The final refinement's unobserved iterates should not silently be included by a new implementation presented as equivalent.

**Filtering and validation.** Within a fixed wrap/branch region, the shear and unshear cancel in their local derivative; each inversion has isotropic local scale 1/r2, and reflections preserve lengths. This gives useful local footprint information. The product DF alone still cannot integrate a pixel crossing wrap seams, the separation boundary, an inversion singularity or a near-cycle stopping boundary. Use a defined coverage/filtering policy and compare against supersampling. Zero box widths are allowed by the displayed sliders but make the wrap division invalid. Near-cycle early exit can omit later trap minima even when the positional difference is small, so compare appearance as well as geometry before relying on it for speed.

The presets are Default, QF, QF2, QF3, QF4, Balls, Lace, Dragon, Hydra and Necklace. All disable bloom and set ReflectionsNumber=0. Main iteration budgets range from 20 to 100; QF3 explicitly sets ten final rounds, while Hydra and Necklace set one. Several others omit Final_Iterations and FourGen, so effective defaults require the loader contract rather than inference from neighboring recipes. No shader compilation, rendering, numerical equivalence test, performance benchmark or external license verification was performed. This optional pattern mechanism remains lower priority than improving RFF's existing environment reflection and dense-palette filtering.

## Kleinian_angles_10: resolved symmetry settings and observation-stage compatibility

**Coverage.** The full active body of [Kleinian_angles_10.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/Kleinian_angles_10.frag) was read, and its complete file diff against the fully reviewed Kleinian_test23 was inspected. The prior file's inventory hash was verified. All ten inherited preset blocks are byte-identical; the additional Pluton block was read in full. This comparison covers the entire file while distinguishing inherited content from changed behavior.

**The angle control resolves a discrete order, not a nearest-angle choice.** init maps each Alpha below 1 to cos(pi/floor(pi/acos(Alpha))), then sets the corresponding wrap half-width to sqrt((1+resolvedAlpha)/2). Values at least 1 skip snapping and use the same square-root width mapping continuously. The comment's nearest-angle description does not match the floor operation: for valid inputs below 1 the implied real order is rounded downward. This produces plateaus and jumps as Alpha crosses order boundaries. A future RFF procedural pattern should expose discrete symmetry order directly, or clearly display both requested and resolved values. Continuous animation through a discrete mode should not be presented as smooth geometric interpolation. At and near Alpha=1, precision and branch behavior require a stated policy; validate imported values instead of relying only on UI slider limits.

A scalar arithmetic check of Pluton's AlphaX=0.83871 yields order 5 and half-width approximately 0.9510565163. AlphaZ=0 corresponds mathematically to order 2 and half-width 1/sqrt(2). This is a CPU arithmetic interpretation, not a GPU agreement or rendered-image test. The distinctive conversion must also be considered alongside the separate license restriction described below.

**Two further changes affect compatibility.** In test23 the shear, wrap and unshear occur even with FourGen=false; here shear and unshear occur only in the FourGen branch. Thus a three-generator pattern's wrap boundaries change for nonzero KleinI. Matching numerical wrap widths alone cannot reproduce the older recurrence. The orbit-trap update also moves from after the separation reflection to before it. Even where the geometric transformation sequence otherwise agrees, the recorded XYZ and squared-radius minima can differ. RFF should version a procedural layer's observation stage and coordinate convention with the formula rather than treat them as interchangeable palette settings. If users want pre/post-transform appearance choices, make those explicit and preserve them in saved recipes.

The terminal TransA-only refinement, near-two-cycle stopping rule, outer inversion and derivative-factor clamps retain the previously documented behavior and limitations. Z=0 remains invariant under the active iteration with positive widths, and under outer inversion when both center Z components are zero. This supports a direct 2D ornamental-mask evaluator under those conditions. It does not make the return value a proven planar signed distance or make the formula compatible with Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA. Pixel filtering must handle discontinuities at wrap and branch boundaries as well as the continuous local inversion scale.

**Legacy preset fields do not reproduce legacy images.** The ten inherited blocks still contain box_size_x and box_size_z, but those uniforms are no longer declared here. They omit AlphaX/AlphaZ, so they cannot themselves specify the new wrap widths; actual behavior depends on importer defaults and unknown-field handling. Treat these blocks as compatibility evidence, not validated visual regressions. Pluton explicitly supplies the new controls, disables FourGen, uses 33 main rounds and ten final rounds, and enables outer inversion with zero Z centers. Like the inherited examples it disables bloom and uses zero reflection bounces. A RFF migration would need explicit field mapping, formula-version selection and complete defaults; silently ignoring removed fields can change appearance without changing a recipe's name.

**RFF recommendation.** The reusable design lessons are resolved-value controls, independent observation-stage selection, and versioned procedural recipes. They strengthen the optional 2D pattern proposal without displacing environment reflection and palette filtering. Validate snap boundaries, imported values, three/four-generator mode transitions, pre/post-reflection traps and preview/export equivalence. No shader compilation, rendering or performance measurement was performed. The header again attributes the original to Jos Leys and says to ask him for licensing; no actual reuse license was verified. Do not adapt distinctive implementation code or constants until permission is established, and record applicable provenance in NOTICE.

## Kleinian_angles_24: oblique lattices change both geometry and trap meaning

**Coverage.** The active body of [Kleinian_angles_24.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/Kleinian_angles_24.frag) was read completely. Eight of its fourteen preset blocks were verified byte-identical to blocks in the hash-verified, fully reviewed angles_10 source; the six changed/new blocks were read in full. Nothing except whitespace remains between/after preset blocks. This establishes full source/preset coverage by direct reading and exact comparison.

**Oblique lattice construction.** AlphaX and AlphaZ retain the floor-based order snapping described for angles_10; AlphaXZ is not snapped because that line is commented out. From lx=sqrt(2*(1+ax)) and lz=sqrt(2*(1+az)), init computes ct=(lx*lx+lz*lz-2*(1+axz))/(2*lx*lz). Only when abs(ct)<1 does it set Tx=lx/2, Tzx=lz*ct/2 and Tzz=lz*sqrt(1-ct*ct)/2. Otherwise these globals are left unchanged, rather than reporting invalid settings; their declared initial values describe a square lattice. Near abs(ct)=1, division by Tzz in wrapping is ill-conditioned. In RFF, distinguish a valid requested pattern, a deliberate fallback and an invalid parameter combination. Expose the resolved lattice basis, validate imported settings and define animation behavior at degeneracy instead of silently switching patterns.

wrapit subtracts (Tzx/Tzz)*Z from X, performs centered axis wrapping (plus the optional Y/shear path), then restores the oblique shear. correctz subsequently searches nine lattice offsets with nx,nz in {-1,0,1}; its ny loop only evaluates zero, even with FourGen enabled. It chooses the candidate with the smallest Euclidean squared distance using a strict comparison, so equal-distance ties retain the first candidate in traversal order. The bounded search is not a demonstrated global nearest-lattice solution for every allowed skew or aspect ratio. A general RFF lattice layer should use a validated reduced basis/search bound or restrict the supported domain. Its filtering must account for representative-cell boundaries, not merely use the smooth derivative inside one selected cell.

**The generator and its branch rule also change.** TransA now maps to (x/r2+b, a-y/r2, z/r2). TransAInv subtracts b from X and reflects Y about a before taking the reciprocal squared length and scaling. The active branch directly chooses TransA or its inverse; it does not use the older separation reflection followed by a single generator. The separation expression changes sign and its exponential coefficient from 3.2 to 3. The alternate reflection branch is disabled by preprocessing. Together with the new wrap geometry, these differences mean angles_24 cannot be reproduced by merely adding an angle slider to angles_10.

**Trap W becomes a stopping statistic.** The XYZ minima are updated after the chosen generator and after the near-two-cycle test. A round that breaks does not contribute its sample. The threshold is 1e-10 squared distance, versus 1e-12 in the previous variant. After the loop, W is overwritten with i/Box_Iterations: this is the zero-based break index divided by the budget, or 1 after full exhaustion. It is not squared radius and is not exactly the fraction of executed transformations; a break at index zero follows one transformation but reports zero. The final TransA-only refinement still does not update the trap. For RFF, keep termination reason, executed-round count and geometric trap channels as separate typed outputs. A convergence-derived mask could drive appearance, but must not be mistaken for an escape-time value or assumed compatible with MPA-skipped orbit observations.

**2D transfer requires more care than the preceding variants.** An oblique lattice's correction can select nz!=0 for an input whose Z was zero, producing nonzero Z. Thus the invariant-plane argument established for the axis-aligned variants does not automatically apply. A RFF layer can still evaluate a 2D input slice while retaining the complete 3D state at every round. A genuinely planar variant requires its own invariant plane and matching lattice/generator derivation. Alternatively, reuse the general idea of oblique coordinate repetition in a separate 2D texture layer with a well-defined nearest-cell rule. Neither route should change Mandelbrot computation or relax its precision.

**Preset evidence and prioritization.** Default and Necklace are changed; INF2-3-6, INF2-4-4, INF-2-2-inf and INF-3-3-3 are additional cases. All six explicitly use FourGen=false and Final_Iterations=0, so they do not validate the four-generator nearest-cell behavior or nonzero terminal refinement. All fourteen disable bloom and use zero reflection bounces. The eight inherited blocks retain legacy width fields and omit the new lattice controls, making loader defaults material to their meaning. Default itself retains stale box_size fields alongside Alpha values. Treat names as labels, not proof of the implemented symmetry or reproducible appearance.

The source header explicitly describes discontinuities and uncertainty about their origin. That is not rendered evidence attributing them to geometry, cell selection, distance estimation or the ray marcher. Validate those causes separately if implementing an RFF layer: compare lattice selection against a wider reference, test cell-boundary continuity and ties, track termination masks, and compare filtered slice output across preview, tiles and video. No rendering, shader compilation, numerical lattice test or benchmark was performed. The header still directs readers to ask Jos Leys for licensing; no reuse permission was established. This remains an optional procedural-pattern direction below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering; verify provenance and licensing before adapting distinctive code.

## Simple Kleinian slow-DE pair: optimization must preserve the actual field

**Coverage.** The complete [Simple_Kleinian-Slow-DE-02-----.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/Simple_Kleinian-Slow-DE-02-----.frag), including fourteen preset blocks, was read. A full-file diff against [Simple_Kleinian-Slow-DE-02----l.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/Simple_Kleinian-Slow-DE-02----l.frag) contains only the explicitly inspected inversion, bounding-field and loop changes. The complete preset suffix is byte-identical. These are different fields, not equivalent quality/performance settings.

**Precompute geometry that depends only on settings.** The vertex-stage init squares the three SR radii, derives pairwise center distances from TP/TQ/TR cosines, solves axis-center squares C2, and computes a weighted intersection point P. A normal to the plane of centers and extrema of P/normal define two offset bounding spheres; extrema of C2-R2 provide two origin-centered alternatives. The fragment receives these as varying values. In a Vulkan adaptation, uniform-derived geometry should have an explicit shared parameter layout and be recomputed only when its inputs change; the Fragmentarium vertex/varying arrangement is not itself a portable Vulkan resource contract. Negative center/radius squares, zero denominators and degenerate normals need validation. The header's claim that the result is Kleinian additionally assumes SR components do not exceed the corresponding C components; merely selecting integer angles does not prove those inequalities.

**The original field retains evidence from every round.** Each round conditionally inverts inside three spheres in X/Y/Z order, accumulates their scale factors, records componentwise absolute XYZ and squared-radius minima, and folds into the positive octant. The active bounding field is max(length(p-Cs0)-BRsq0, BRsq2-length(p-Cs2)), combining an outer sphere and an inner exclusion. The result is the maximum of the initial and each round's scaled bounding values. It stops when either the iteration budget is reached or the latest unscaled bounding value reaches 0.1. Because this is a do-while loop, Iterations=0 still performs one round. The trap is reset per query, unlike the previously reviewed JosKleinian examples. The header explicitly allows occasional distance overestimation; it is not a certified conservative estimator.

**The l variant changes the map and its derivative.** Its factor is max(1,R2/(s-0.01)), with s=lengthSquared(p-center), instead of max(1,R2/s). Inside s<0.01 the unclamped factor is negative and the operation becomes identity; at s=0.01 the denominator is singular, and just above it the expansion is unbounded. This is not a harmless small-denominator safeguard. On the smooth active branch, tangential scale is k=R2/(s-epsilon), while the radial derivative is -R2*(s+epsilon)/(s-epsilon)^2. Its magnitude exceeds k for positive epsilon and s>epsilon. Thus multiplying the accumulated derivative factor only by k no longer represents the largest local stretch of an ordinary sphere inversion. This is algebraic analysis, not a numerical or rendered verification.

That variant also replaces the bounding field with max(-1,length(p-Cs2)-BRsq2), removes per-round field accumulation and the distance-based stop, and returns only the final field divided by accumulated k. The removed square roots may reduce work per round, but more rounds can execute and the output geometry differs. No speedup or equivalent image quality can be inferred. For RFF, preserve reductions and termination conditions during performance work; if a different procedural appearance is desired, give it an explicit formula identity rather than presenting it as an optimized version of the same result.

**2D transfer.** A query plane can supply an ornamental mask or relief input while retaining full 3D state. Under the original formula, Z=0 is preserved by the X/Y inversions; the Z-centered inversion is also inactive everywhere on that plane if C.z^2>=R2.z. An outer inversion preserves it only with a center on the plane. The modified denominator strengthens the inactive-branch condition to C.z^2-0.01>=R2.z away from singular cases; do not reuse the original restriction without checking it. A native 2D circle-inversion layer would instead need independently derived circles and bounds. In both cases, use the correct transformation footprint, explicit trap units and filtered mask coverage; this does not accelerate Mandelbrot or justify modifying perturbation/MPA precision.

**Preset evidence.** The fourteen blocks include three distinct entries named Noname, so titles cannot serve as stable identifiers. They mix renderer-era fields, partial settings and both scalar/vector Reflection values; several HF_Anisotropy assignments have four components. Acceptance and meaning depend on the actual renderer/importer contract. Four blocks explicitly enable bloom, whereas others omit it or disable it; sample images would therefore need controlled postprocessing before comparing the two fields. Their shared settings do not prove comparable output after the executable changes. Outer InvRadius is used directly as radius squared here, unlike the JosKleinian examples that square their same-named control; a shared RFF editor must preserve semantic units in recipe versions.

The useful RFF lessons are cached uniform geometry, explicit transform derivatives, preserving field reductions during optimization, and typed/versioned procedural inputs. Optional inversion patterns remain below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in priority. Validate degenerate geometry, zero-round semantics, all branch thresholds, derivative bounds and full-frame/tile/video sampling before adaptation. No shader compilation, rendering, numerical test or benchmark was performed. The source credits Knighty and points to an earlier spheirahedron reference; original sources and actual licenses remain to be verified before copying distinctive implementations or constants, with appropriate NOTICE records.

## Benesi Menger multisample formula: height images are geometry inputs

**Coverage.** The complete [mengermultisampleKN2.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Benesi/mengermultisampleKN2.frag), including nine appearance presets and two camera-only keyframes, was read. It includes DE-Kn2ColorandHeightmap.frag. The formula itself implements coordinate deformation, traps and height-image lookup; its name and renderer sampling settings are not evidence of a new pixel-antialiasing algorithm in this file.

**Smooth folding has a concrete spatial scale.** Each round optionally rotates, optionally applies the image deformation, replaces each absolute component by sqrt(component*component+s), and performs three smooth compare/swap operations. For a pair difference t, the correction is (t-sqrt(t*t+s))/2; at s=0 this reproduces descending sorting. Positive s rounds the folds over a coordinate scale of approximately sqrt(s), rather than adding ordinary pixel antialiasing. It then smooth-reflects Z around C.z*(Scale-1)/Scale with C=(1,1,0.5), scales and translates the state, applies scheduled history-dependent warps, and records traps. The final field is length(z)/Scale^executedRounds, not an explicit box SDF. Scale=0 makes the intermediate division invalid. HoleSphere is declared but unused in this body, while the stellation code is commented out.

**Height mapping changes the recurrence.** At HeightIter or HeightIter2, hTextureIT samples tex2, scales RGB by HighStrength*0.02, replaces W with RGB vector length, forms a weighted scalar from hscale, and adds that same scalar to all three coordinates. Equal iteration indices execute the deformation once because the condition uses OR. This is a translation along (1,1,1) with a position-dependent magnitude, not displacement along a surface normal. For negative HighStrength, the RGB contributions change sign but the length contribution does not. It is not generally an odd-symmetric amplitude control.

Mapping modes 0..10 include angular, polygonal, trap-weighted, position/radius-weighted, planar, projective, ray-direction and screen-coordinate sources. The displayed hMapType range extends to 13, but 11..13 assign no new sample, leaving mutable hcolor at its prior value. Mode 0 applies asin(z.y) without normalizing z, so arbitrary iterates may fall outside its domain. Projective mode can divide by zero; polygonal and angular modes introduce seams. Ray/screen modes make geometry evaluation depend on viewing context. These modes need explicit contracts in any RFF adaptation, especially for tiled export, normal probes and video.
