For a RFF appearance-only feature, sample a declared height image in a stable mapping, filter it over the pixel footprint, combine it with the existing relief height and derive normals consistently. Do not insert it into the Mandelbrot recurrence. A separate formula extension that does deform iterates needs the image gradient and mapping Jacobian in its derivative analysis: z -> z+ones*h(z) has Jacobian I+ones*gradient(h)^T. The source's accumulated scale w only multiplies by Scale; it does not account for that image deformation or the history-feedback warps. This is not evidence of a safe distance bound or of compatibility with perturbation/MPA.

**Separate observation from termination.** trapmode=true initializes signed XYZ and linear radius, then later minima use absolute XYZ and linear radius; negative initial components can therefore persist. With trapmode=false initialization depends on renderer state. At ColorIterations, a renderer-provided orbitBoolSet can set n=Iterations and end the geometry loop. Thus an apparently color-related control can affect geometry and the returned scale denominator. An independent RFF implementation should keep observation windows, early termination and validity separate. The stored history starts with an initial sample even if its recording window is zero, and feedback is applied before the current round updates that history.

orbitCut partitions a weighted history radius into four bands, using repeated subtraction of the sum of orbitGap1. Its strict r>period condition retains r=period at the upper endpoint, unlike ordinary modulo mapping that sends it to zero. Very small positive periods can also produce excessive work or subtraction that stops changing a large floating-point value. A bounded wrapping method needs an explicit endpoint and precision policy before replacing this loop. The bands alter geometry through CutXYZmult and orbitAdd1; they are not just palette segments. A 2D material-mask adaptation can reuse the idea of independently weighted bands without carrying geometry feedback into the fractal calculation.

**Preset evidence.** Default schedules image lookup at round four but sets all hscale components to zero; this expresses zero intended deformation, although it does not make invalid intermediate sampling arithmetic safe. The heightmap preset uses nonzero channel weights but saves hintensity, which is a derived global rather than the declared HighStrength uniform. smoothmenger actually saves s=0, demonstrating why names alone cannot establish smoothing. Multisample and CitadelMenger include renderer sampling settings but explicitly disable height scheduling. The two KeyFrame blocks contain only camera fields and require a base scene. These are loader/state and validation conditions, not separately proven features.

**2D transfer and priority.** The smoothed sorting can move coordinates between axes, while rotations and common-axis height translation also generally leave an input plane. Preserve full 3D state for slices; derive a distinct planar fold if a native 2D procedural pattern is wanted. Image-driven relief and typed field mapping are more direct RFF transfers than importing the full recurrence. Validate sample domains, missing modes, signed strength, schedule collisions, band boundaries and preview/export footprints. No shader compilation, rendering, numerical derivative test or performance benchmark was performed. The source credits Benesi and Knighty's kaleidoscopic IFS and cites an external spherical-texture example; original licenses and implementation provenance remain to be verified before adaptation, with corresponding NOTICE records.

## Funball Colors Accordion: planar kaleidoscope stages and signed observation channels

**Coverage.** The complete [FunballColorsAccordion.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Benesi/FunballColorsAccordion.frag) was read, including ten scene presets, one palette-only block and two keyframes. The active renderer is Fast-Raytracer-with-Palette.frag; the feedback and texture-renderer includes are commented out. Preset keys from those other paths do not establish active functionality.

**Sector splitting is a piecewise rigid transform.** split selects a YZ angular sector by repeatedly subtracting 2*pi/splits, translates by splitrad along the selected sector midpoint, then rotates the translated YZ point using the accumulated angle. X is unchanged. The strict sector-boundary comparison is part of the mapping, including the wrap from negative atan angles into [0,2*pi). Within a fixed sector the operation is a translation and rotation, not an expanding power map. This suggests an optional planar kaleidoscope mapping for RFF image/material layers. Preserve cell-boundary conventions and filter across them; a unit local scale inside a sector does not establish continuous output or coverage across adjacent sectors.

The four trap channels are signed minima at two different stages: X/Y store translated Y/Z before the sector rotation, while Z/W store Y/Z afterward. W is not radius or squared radius. DE does not initialize this trap itself. An RFF implementation should return independently named pre/post-transform observations, initialize them per query and preserve their signed meanings. Feeding W into a consumer that assumes a radial channel would change the appearance semantics. These observations belong to the procedural layer, not to Mandelbrot orbit statistics that MPA would automatically supply.

**Stage counts are not ordinary repeat counts.** A local counter starts at one. Stage one uses m<=splititer1; subsequent stages use strict m<successive cumulative sums. At or beyond the final sum the code calls split with the current mutable splits/splitrad, resets m to zero and then increments it. With all four durations equal to one, the resulting stage sequence is 1,3,4,4; stage two is skipped. This follows directly from the branch inequalities. A clean RFF operator sequence should use explicit stage ranges and immutable per-stage parameters. Reproducing a source preset requires its actual scheduling semantics, whereas designing a new sequence editor can use clearer counts with a distinct recipe version.

**Accordion is a finite-interval mirrored repetition.** It handles ascending and descending intervals separately, leaves coordinates on the outside-start side unchanged, folds interior cycles about their midpoints, handles a remainder near the endpoint, and translates coordinates beyond the end. Repeated subtraction is bounded by 3,000 iterations. cycle is clamped and then shortened to the interval length, but cyclemod is computed earlier using the original AccCycle. Equality boundaries use strict comparisons and can fall through without transformation. This is not automatically equivalent to a generic triangle wave. Define endpoint, zero-span and remainder behavior before replacing it with a constant-time mapping. A RFF texture-domain repetition can use a separately specified mirrored-repeat operator with pixel-footprint filtering rather than inheriting these accidental conventions.

Z accordion applies once before the main loop. Up to three Y accordion stages apply at specified iteration indices; coincident indices execute sequentially. XY rotation applies on every round from RotIter onward, followed by sector splitting. The local sc stays one. The terminal field is max(length(z.xz)-widthC,abs(z.y)-lengthC), an intersection field for a capped cylinder, not the exact Euclidean distance outside its corners. widthC=0 collapses the radial extent to a line segment; negative widthC gives a strictly positive radial term and therefore no exact zero surface. Ray-hit thresholds can still produce an apparent image, so a screenshot would not prove a finite-width geometric object.

**A useful native 2D restriction.** If XY rotation is identity, an initial X=0 stays zero through all active sector and accordion operations. The resulting YZ evaluator is planar, and the terminal field reduces to max(abs(Z)-widthC,abs(Y)-lengthC), a rectangular intersection field for positive dimensions. Nontrivial XY rotation generally leaves that plane; retain full state for such slices or derive a different planar operator. The direct RFF opportunity is controlled kaleidoscope/mirrored repetition of an existing image or mask, with optional signed stage observations driving color, roughness or relief. It is not a replacement for the Mandelbrot recurrence or its precision/acceleration mechanisms.

**Preset and validation conditions.** The ten scene blocks include Carpet1 and Splitrad2n20to80 with explicit accordion settings; many others omit them. Several save removed cylinder/rotation/feedback fields and absolute asset paths on the original author's machine. funplane3 explicitly sets widthC=-0.05; several others set it to zero. PaletteSet intentionally supplies only appearance fields, while the two keyframes carry identical camera/feedback values. A reproducible RFF recipe should distinguish complete scenes from patches, use stable asset references and define missing-field defaults. Validate stage counts, signed trap initialization, all fold endpoints, degenerate widths and planar/full-state equivalence before adaptation. No shader compilation, rendering, numerical comparison or benchmark was performed. The source identifies Benesi; actual original licensing remains unverified. Establish permission and NOTICE provenance before reusing distinctive implementation code. This optional mapping extension remains below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in priority.

## AlgebraicSurfsViews-ess15: gradients and shell normals

**Coverage boundary.** Lines 1..550 of [AlgebraicSurfsViews-ess15.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/AlgebraicSurfsViews-ess15.frag) have been read, covering the entire formula body and the first complete preset. That initial body review is now supplemented by the completed preset review below; all remaining lines have been read and the inventory hash verified.

**The chosen function is compile-time state.** Fn1 is defined as Barth6. The body additionally contains Cayley, Kummer, two Togliatti forms, Dervish, Labs, two Endrass forms, Sarti, Chmutov/Chebyshev and Escudero expressions. Merely saving Mu, Lambda or ChN does not switch the active surface. Function-name comparisons in #if directives must not be assumed to provide reliable identity-based selection: function identifiers are not integer macro tags. An independent RFF procedural layer should use explicit, stable surface IDs and expose only applicable parameters, with a deliberate policy for parameter retention when switching modes. No preprocessor or shader compilation has been executed to establish this source's actual compilation path.

**Keep homogeneous and affine formulas distinct.** Most listed surfaces retain the fourth coordinate in polynomial terms. Escudero9_2 instead replaces that coordinate's factors with constants in the active expression; it is an affine variant rather than automatically equivalent under arbitrary ZW rotation. The parameterized Chebyshev helper uses a recurrence carrying w squared and separately computes w to the requested degree. A RFF implicit-pattern layer must declare which coordinate chart each formula expects. A gallery entry is not safely interchangeable with another solely because their names describe the same polynomial degree.

**Distance normalization and lighting normal use different derivatives.** Trans maps XYZ to (2*XYZ/(1+g*r2),(1-g*r2)/(1+g*r2)), saves a pre-rotation factor fff=1/(1+w), rotates ZW and then XYZ. Fn takes four forward differences in the resulting ambient four-dimensional coordinates, normalizes the polynomial value by their length plus param2*abs(v)/(abs(v)+1)+0.001, then multiplies by abs(fff). param1 is declared but does not participate in this active calculation. This ambient gradient is not the full spatial gradient of the composed normalized estimator; the transformation Jacobian and normalization derivative are distinct issues.

The custom normal instead takes three forward differences of Fn1(Trans(p)) in original XYZ space, normalizes them and multiplies by sign of the raw polynomial value. Its normalDistance argument is unused and the step is the fixed Eps=1/2048. This captures the composed raw polynomial's direction approximately, but not the gradient of the complete DE after shell construction and clipping. The shell remains abs(Fn+IntThick)-IntThick, with zeros at normalized values 0 and -2*IntThick; the raw sign switch does not track the shell derivative's switch at Fn=-IntThick throughout the band. The custom normal also lacks explicit sphere/plane-cut branches. Near zero raw value or a critical point, sign/normalization need a defined policy.

For RFF, return the selected field branch and its gradient together. A contour/relief normal should describe the actual displayed field, while cap normals should describe the winning cut. Analytic differentiation or automatic differentiation can reduce repeated polynomial evaluations and improve control of sample spacing, but needs numerical validation and GPU measurement. A footprint-aware finite-difference fallback is still useful near complex branches; do not claim a fixed spatial step is resolution-independent.

**Material transfer.** baseColor selects PSide or NSide by the normalized field's inner-shell threshold, then mixes that RGB directly with the signed normal vector. Negative normal components are not a conventional [0,1] normal-color encoding. RFF could offer an explicitly artistic direction-based tint or independently assign inner/outer/cap materials, using a declared linear-color mapping rather than silently treating a normal as radiance. A 2D full-coordinate slice can use the implicit field for contours and relief; preserve the fourth coordinate and spatial transform rather than dropping them. This remains a supplemental material/pattern idea below the established environment-reflection and palette-filtering priorities.

**Verification still required.** The first preset selects a sphere cut, GFactor=0, WAngle=0, param2=42.857 and a nonzero thickness; that single case does not validate singular charts, cap normals, other polynomials or nonzero rotations. The completed preset coverage and its limits are recorded below. No rendering, compilation, numerical differentiation test, benchmark or external source/license verification was performed. Source comments identify Knighty and named mathematical surfaces; verify original implementation provenance and licenses before adapting distinctive formulas or coefficients, and maintain NOTICE records.

## PseudoKleinian06 CR-renderer reference: terminal-field comparison

**Coverage boundary.** Lines 1..310 of [PseudoKleinian06---.frag](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/With_CRrenderer/PseudoKleinian06---.frag) have been read, covering all executable formula code and the complete simple and Default presets. The remaining presets were subsequently read through line 2078; the completion review below supersedes the initial partial coverage. Both copies receive full-file credit only after byte equality and inventory hashes are verified. This supplements the previously reviewed native PseudoKleinian06 and historical plane-terminal variants rather than treating their similar names as equivalent implementations.

**This variant actively uses the shaped terminal primitive.** After subtracting Offset, Thingy combines radial=length(p.xy)-TThickness2 with (length(p.xy)*abs(p.z)-TThickness)/sqrt(dot(p,p)+abs(TThickness)), using max. The final evaluator returns abs(0.5*Thingy/DEfactor-DEoffset). Unlike the plane-terminal historical variants, TThickness, TThickness2 and all components of Offset participate in the active field. RoundBox and the plane alternatives remain unused. USE_INF_NORM does not change this file's active dot(p,p) radial denominator. For RFF, the useful distinction is an explicitly selected terminal primitive after a coordinate pipeline; do not expose inactive controls or infer a primitive from a family name.

The primitive's two thickness controls have different meanings: TThickness2 offsets a cylindrical radial field, while TThickness offsets a product involving radial and axial coordinates before a normalization. The enclosing absolute value selects a level of the scaled signed residual and discards its sign; DEoffset is not automatically geometric shell thickness. At p=0 and TThickness=0, the product term evaluates a zero denominator. A filtered 2D band could use the residual as an artistic field, but requires a declared singular-point policy and screen-space coverage. It is not a proven Euclidean distance merely because the function is named DE.

**Iteration stage and stopping state matter.** Thing2 first shifts Z by CSize.z. Each round applies the componentwise box fold, records absolute XYZ and squared-radius trap minima, expands by max(Size/r2,1), multiplies DEfactor by that expansion and adds C. The loop tests exact equality with the previous complete point, not an escape-radius test or a proven period. Its initial previous state is p+1, which is only a reliable unequal sentinel where floating-point addition changes the value. MI=0 skips all rounds, but still includes the initial Z shift and terminal evaluation. Trap initialization is inherited from renderer state, unlike the self-contained reset in the Simple Kleinian pair.

The box folds are piecewise reflections and the radial branch is an ordinary sphere inversion or identity away from singularities. That explains the local scale product, but does not prove the terminal primitive or full composition is a conservative distance. A RFF procedural evaluator should return trap data, termination reason and field result independently, preserving exact evaluation stages. None of this supplies a substitute for Mandelbrot perturbation, fast-period-guessing or MPA.

**Inversion controls require distinct units and centers.** The outer map is InvRadius*p/dot(p,p)+InvCenter: the input-center subtraction is commented out. InvCenter is therefore an output translation, and InvRadius is used as radius squared. The later correction r2*d/(InvRadius+r*d) uses the original radius. This differs from examples using a translated input center or squaring a radius-valued control. A shared RFF layer editor should name input center, output translation, radius convention and execution stage explicitly, with stable recipe fields. It must not normalize same-named controls across imported formulas without a semantic conversion.

**2D adaptation.** A full-coordinate slice is straightforward to specify, but deleting Z is not equivalent: the initial CSize.z shift and the coupled radial fold generally retain a nonzero evolving Z. For an inexpensive native 2D ornament, independently define a box/circle fold pipeline and a line, circle or band terminal field. For a faithful slice, keep all three state components and filter the output field over the 2D pixel footprint. The first simple preset sets TThickness=0 and TThickness2=2 with six rounds; Default instead uses nonzero TThickness, a Z offset, twenty rounds and three renderer reflection bounces. These are different geometry and lighting cases, not a matched performance comparison.

This body review adds implementation conditions to the existing optional field-mask proposal. The completed preset review follows below. No compilation, rendering, numerical comparison, benchmark or external license verification was performed. The file names Theli-at's idea and Knighty's implementation and provides an original discussion link; verify actual reuse permission and maintain NOTICE provenance before adapting distinctive code. Environment reflection and dense-palette filtering remain the higher-priority RFF improvements.

**Useful RFF transfer: compose a coordinate pipeline with an explicit terminal field.** The opening entries separate repeated folds/inversions from a final plane, cylinder, line, rounded-loop or box-exterior measurement. | de5 | Box fold, clamped sphere scaling and input-point injection update both XYZ and W; the final expression subtracts scale-dependent terms. This differs from simply multiplying a running scale. Its nine-loop count and final constants must be treated as one formula definition rather than independent cosmetic controls. |
| de6/de7 and de9/de10 | Box/radial fold pipelines feed a max of a radial offset and a radial-times-Z expression. The paired versions replace dot(p,p) with dot(p,p+sin(0.3*p.z)); that changes the transform derivative and can change denominator sign. A scalar product of k does not prove the same distance bound for both versions. |
| de8 | Periodic wrapping, a sign-directed offset and six inversions end in the minimum of a plane and three thin axial tubes. The local minimum-radius variable orb is not returned or exported. A RFF trap channel would need an explicit output, observation stage and unit contract. |
| de15, de16, de17, de18, de19 | Variants combine coordinate ordering, folds and radial scaling with box-exterior or plane terminals. de17 adds smoothed plane reflections and rotation; de18 uses an L5 norm in its radial rule; de19 uses two different smooth-absolute scales and a minimum-component rule. These are distinct geometric mappings, not interchangeable antialiasing settings. |
| de20, de21, de22, de23, de24, de25, de26 | Repetition/fold variants use line, box-exterior or selected-coordinate terminals. Several derive an additive offset from the input point before iteration. Its derivative contributes to the total mapping; the displayed scalar scale accumulator alone does not include that contribution. Negative per-step scales require consistent magnitude/sign conventions. |
| de27, de28, de29 | Three rounds of ordered folds produce a rounded-loop terminal after clamping X. de27/de28 normalize by accumulated powers of two before evaluating the terminal; de29 omits iterative scaling. Terminal widths therefore live at different stages. A shared width slider needs declared units rather than name-based parameter substitution. |

Cross-product terminals measure distance to a line only with a unit axis; de31 uses vec3(0.5), so its magnitude carries an extra factor. de36 uses s-0.1 in its denominator. de38 alternates inversion with constant scaling by iteration index. Preserve these distinctions in a versioned recipe. |
| de40, de41, de43, de44, de45, de46, de47, de48 | Ordered plane reflections, input-derived offsets, rotations and periodic terminals produce further patterns. de40 executes nineteen rounds and de48 fourteen because their loop tests pre-increment. de46 executes six rounds and includes sinusoidal coordinate warps whose derivatives are absent from its scalar scale product. de47 repeats the already scale-normalized terminal coordinates, so its fine grid has a different placement from repetition at the pipeline input. |

**Filtering must follow the actual mapping.** In de17, the smoothed reflection maps the signed plane component g to sqrt(g*g+0.1), retaining tangential components. This changes the shape over a fixed coordinate width; it is not pixel-footprint filtering. In de19, sqrt(x*x+0.1) and sqrt(x*x+0.001) likewise serve different geometric scales. For RFF, expose geometric smoothing separately from image antialiasing. Preserve high precision through the existing fractal field and estimate the final mask's pixel footprint before periodic reduction; cell seams and thin terminals need explicit coverage treatment.

**A 2D slice is not automatically a native 2D recurrence.** Component swaps, nonzero translations, rotations between planes and cross-axis terminal measurements often require retaining full XYZ state for a faithful slice. The opening de3 is a simpler candidate: starting with Z=0 preserves Z under its particular centered wrap and scalar inversion away from singularities, and its terminal uses X only. This supports a separately validated planar implementation of that specific mapping, not deletion of Z throughout the collection. It also remains an optional procedural appearance layer, not a replacement for Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA.

**Selection and provenance should be explicit in an RFF design.** The single selector indexes with Math.random; the multiple selector sorts with a random comparator before slicing. Such a comparator does not define a stable random permutation, and negative n follows JavaScript's negative slice-end semantics rather than selecting zero items. For a future RFF exploration feature, use a documented seeded selection/permutation, validate the requested count and save the selected stable IDs plus parameters; do not change existing palette recipe RNG ordering. Individual records here have no license field and several authors are unknown. The de43 snippet declares rotate/pmod but calls rotate43/pmod43, illustrating why dependency/name resolution must precede adaptation; it is not evidence of a running GMT failure without an integration path. Verify original permissions before copying distinctive implementations and record NOTICE provenance.

No shader compilation, rendering, numerical derivative validation, performance measurement or external-source/license verification was performed for these entries. The remaining compendium entries still require review. These optional procedural-layer ideas remain below environment reflection and dense-palette filtering in RFF priority.

**Explicit 3D-to-2D condition.** de108 preserves Z=0 through its XY rotations and scalar doublings; consequently sin(p.z)=0 at every octave, all products vanish and the function returns the constant 0.1. In RFF, preserve the unwrapped cell identity before local coordinates, use a specified reproducible hash with verified provenance, and save algorithm/version/seed explicitly. A change of hash or integer-bound convention changes the resulting image. These snippets' sine hashes and distinctive constants have not been independently licensed or tested for cross-device reproducibility.

**Share field and material decisions.** de93 is a useful model for returning a terminal branch alongside its scalar value: one branch samples a five-round cylinder and the other a three-round box-exterior field. A RFF mask layer could use the winner for material selection while deriving its normal from that same selected field. Keep tie behavior explicit: the snippet's strict d1<d2 selects branch 1 at equality. Its p2 capture is initialized under the fixed five/three schedule; making those counts editable requires a valid capture for every permitted combination.

**Coordinate-chart effects are transferable, with explicit footprints.** de124's radial/angle mapping and de131's log-polar mapping could inspire circular or spiral material patterns in RFF. A chart changes local scale: log radius and polar angle become rapidly varying near the origin, and the angle seam requires periodic treatment. de131 also divides Z by radius, adds one and applies a fractional XY shear; it is not simply a texture rotation. For a native 2D layer, independently specify the radial/angular chart, origin policy, angular repeat count and seam-aware filtering, and keep this appearance mapping separate from high-precision Mandelbrot coordinates. Its normal should follow the displayed filtered field through the chart Jacobian.

**A useful height-field path exists in de148.** Its shape is y-0.5*z+h(x,z), with h assembled from nine rotated absolute sine products at doubling frequencies. The final max(0,...) discards the negative side and creates a region of zero gradient. For a RFF relief layer, use a separately declared 2D height function and derive its normal before any mask-specific clamping. Keep height, signed contour residual and coverage as distinct outputs. The absolute sine ridges need filtering at their cusps as well as octave attenuation when the pattern becomes subpixel. The snippet's rotation helper is external; no cross-renderer equivalence has been established.

**A second concrete slice degeneracy appears in de137.** At Z=0, the third component of sin(p)+cos(p*0.5) equals one. Its returned length minus 0.4 is therefore at least 0.6: the zero-level contour has no intersection with that plane, although the positive scalar can still vary as an artistic height. A native 2D two-component field or a different slice is a new, explicitly named option. Distinguish an empty contour from a constant field and from an unusable material input.

**Input warps need their own derivative budget.** de163 begins with sin(2.8*p+5*sin(0.3*p)); each component's derivative magnitude is bounded by 4.3 before subsequent operations. de167's sin(p+3*sin(0.5*p)) has a corresponding bound of 2.5. These elementary bounds concern only the initial componentwise warp, not the complete estimator. de179 instead reuses a noise-derived scalar throughout its trajectory, so its influence propagates through every round. Caching that scalar saves repeated evaluation but does not make it constant with respect to the input. These are useful lessons for RFF normal generation and footprint estimation, rather than reasons to modify Mandelbrot precision.

**Rounded unions and material identity.** de211 computes f=max(0,1-abs(b-d)) and combines fields as min(d,b)-0.25*f*f. This provides a finite transition region for an optional soft mask union. It does not automatically produce physically correct material blending or a Euclidean distance from arbitrary input fields. Return the field/blend information once and use it consistently for coverage, height and material assignment. de195's local branch code and de200's discarded material tag likewise show that a visually useful selector must be explicitly exported; their mere presence in a formula does not expose an existing coloring feature.

For RFF validation, compare shared-pipeline/different-terminal pairs, iteration endpoints, original versus transformed coordinate clips, chart seams, zero-radius behavior and empty/degenerate slices. Preserve recipe identity when replacing approximate matrices, changing coordinate units or adding filtering. **Useful transfer: an orbit-weight material mask.** The exp(-alpha*r2) sums in de222..225, de228 and de253/de255/de256/de261..263 favor visits near the transformed origin. Unlike a minimum-radius trap, a sum records repeated visits; its range depends on the number of observed iterations, and the alpha value depends on coordinate units. RFF could expose this as an optional color/roughness/relief mask with explicit observation stage, raw-versus-normalized accumulation and iteration-range settings. It is not ambient occlusion, even if it produces dark cavities visually. For Mandelbrot, skipped MPA intervals do not automatically provide the intermediate observations needed for the exact sum. First specify how those observations would be obtained and stored; this cannot be promised as a shader-only addition or a free byproduct of the current escape-time image.

**Water-like relief is a more direct 2D appearance extension.** The water snippet first rotates YZ by 0.7, initializes e=p.y+5, then performs thirty waves. Each wave uses w=exp(sin(x)-1), subtracts w*a from height and also shifts p.xz by -m*w*cos(x)*a. Frequency grows by 1.2 and amplitude decays by 0.8. Because each displacement feeds the next wave, the result is not a sum evaluated at fixed UVs. A native RFF 2D height layer can define this coordinate feedback explicitly and derive the final height gradient through it, or use a separately named simpler fixed-coordinate wave model. The vector m starts as vec2(1), so its length is sqrt(2), not one. The snippet's time term is commented out and its active phase is zero; an animated RFF control would be a new feature.

The local i remains zero, making the conditional p-=0.001 branch inactive. That branch should not become an unexplained compatibility knob. Evaluate normals and filtering from the same chosen wave model, attenuate subpixel waves smoothly, and test preview/video/tile agreement. This wave material can use screen or declared layer coordinates without changing Mandelbrot iteration. Any distinctive copied wave recurrence requires original-source licensing and NOTICE attribution; none has been verified here.

**Control warp bandwidth explicitly.** de236 applies Q+=2*sin(Q) before each XZ wave sample; de238 uses Q+=2*sin(1.05*Q), while de240 uses Q+=sin(0.5*Q). Their coordinate derivatives differ, so equal octave frequencies do not mean equal screen footprints. swirl is especially demanding: its sine phase scales as 0.2*s*s while amplitude scales as 1/s, so derivative contributions can grow with s. Reusing a simple amplitude threshold to drop layers can leave strong normal aliasing. Include the warp derivative or a conservative footprint estimate in the filter decision, and keep geometric smoothing distinct from antialiasing.

**Variable norms are not automatically safe controls.** de242 uses n=2+10*originalY inside pow(abs(p),n), but clamps only the reciprocal exponent denominator to max(n,0.001). The inner powers can still use zero or negative n. It also switches between a length terminal and an absolute-Y terminal at originalY=1.3. A RFF material input needs a declared exponent domain and explicit branch transition, not a generic epsilon inserted after the fact. de246's final value is at least 0.005 after its outer factor; that is a positive residual floor, not an actual zero contour. Treat threshold-based renderer hits separately from the mathematical field.

**Planar Kleinian reuse is conditional.** curly1 uses centered XZ wrapping, a separating reflection and TransA; Z=0 is invariant away from singularities. curly2's outer inversion center is (1,1,0), so the same plane can remain invariant. curly3's center is (0,1,1), which generally moves a zero-Z input out of that plane; a faithful slice must retain XYZ. Its negative X box-size component also needs the exact signed-wrap convention rather than an absolute-width substitution. curly1/2 multiply DF by max(1,iR), whereas curly3 uses iR directly; these yield different contraction tracking. All cap the terminal numerator by 0.3 and denominator below by 2. Their near-two-cycle test is a numerical stopping condition, not proof of periodicity.

The outer maps in curly2/3 use rad*rad, but their final correction denominator uses rad+d*DE. Do not standardize these units by copying another variant's correction without derivation. Their previous-point sentinels are initialized before outer inversion, making the first stopping comparisons different from a history initialized in transformed coordinates. For RFF, version the full mapping and termination semantics, preserve the full state for slices where necessary, and independently define a native 2D ornament if exact compatibility is unnecessary.

These optional masks and relief layers do not displace environment reflection and dense-palette filtering as the leading RFF priorities. **Branching 2D ornaments are a useful separate feature.** TreeBell's segment projection clamps its parameter to [0,1] and multiplies point-to-segment distance by a position-dependent factor before subtracting width. The local sg normalization also feeds an exponential color accumulator. TreeBell2 changes widths, rotations, count and color weighting. For RFF, independently define a planar branching field using 2D segments, branch-length/width ratios and an explicit material output; deleting one coordinate from these rotated 3D pipelines does not preserve their image. Since widths shrink faster than lengths in the supplied recipes, distant generations quickly become subpixel. Filter their coverage and define when later branches can be omitted without visible popping. Do not call the accumulated color an available output when the snippet returns only a scalar.

**Julia offers a direct 2D transfer, but is not a ready-made RFF computation backend.** Its inner routine iterates z=z*z+c with a complex derivative, a 200-round limit and a squared escape threshold of 1e10. It returns zero for an unescaped point. The derivative starts at vec2(1), meaning 1+i rather than the conventional complex unit (1,0); its magnitude is therefore scaled by sqrt(2) along the same recurrence, affecting the returned estimate. The outer 3D function adds another factor of 0.5 and combines the XZ result with two Y-plane expressions. A native 2D feature should specify the intended derivative normalization, interior treatment and precision independently. Deep-zoom Julia support would require integration with RFF's computation, reference and approximation infrastructure, not just copying this fragment function. The unused cpow helper does not establish arbitrary-power support in the active iteration.

**Whorl2 needs a different stage contract.** Its h update uses the previous k before k is recomputed from the current z; escape is tested before the next complex-square update, and the loop is limited to eight rounds. Thus its final k can describe a different stage from the final z. Its parameter c also depends on Z. A fixed-Z plane can produce a 2D pattern, but silently replacing this estimator with the preceding Julia routine would change termination and normalization. Name the mapping, state stage and estimator separately in any versioned RFF recipe.

**Charts, deformations and noise must feed the same normal calculation.** The log/spherical charts in whorl/castleRing/hatRing have origin and angular-seam conditions. snowflake rotates across axes using an external time value and derives per-cell variation before local wrapping; it is a full-coordinate slice unless a separate planar model is designed. noby0/noby1 add discontinuous floor-cell noise after scale normalization and gate it with original Y. Such a detail mask can be useful artistically, but a finite-difference normal crossing cell boundaries will respond differently from a smooth noise derivative. RFF should offer declared mask/height semantics with pixel-footprint filtering, stable cell identity and verified hashing provenance rather than assuming a noise term is automatically a safe geometric displacement.

No compilation, rendering, numerical comparison, timing or external license verification was performed for these forty entries. Their integration and numerical caveats constrain RFF adaptation; they are not a request to repair GMT. Environment reflection and dense-palette filtering remain higher-priority improvements than the optional motifs catalogued here.

| sinugoid/heartcube/manscaped/chorse/gripple | sinugoid's multi-statement F macro is invoked in different expression contexts, including a trailing multiplication that affects its update; expand semantics before adaptation. heartcube minimizes five toroidal samples. manscaped combines a sheared base height, tanh profile and octave ripples. chorse uses a literal phase; gripple performs a coordinate-dependent angular rotation after sinusoidal displacement. |
| getwork/flor/mipple/prisnm/braind/gweave | getwork clamps the scalar denominator but not the p/=e update. flor/mipple use six update-only iterations. prisnm is a four-component fold that permutes W into spatial coordinates; its terminal assignment is outside the loop. braind's final d+=e also occurs after its loop. gweave's unused g accumulation reads an uninitialized local, while the returned e is assigned after its loop. |
| tokamak/rincut/torii/bali/kalib/schwarz/munger | tokamak chains two polar charts. rincut combines the torus union with a box using a max-equivalent choice, then with a plane using min; its local material tags are discarded. torii omits that clip. bali/kalib differ in input units, repetitions and terminal scaling. schwarz defines a thin trigonometric shell clipped by a box. munger uses a 1.6 clamp fold rather than a reflection with coefficient two. |
| viking/knitt/knittt/chiral | Helical phase, periodic strips and coordinate-dependent offsets create woven motifs. viking wraps a tubular chart, knitt uses two shifted coils, knittt samples two phase offsets, and chiral repeatedly remaps polar coordinates with a changing scale. Their angular conventions, time dependence and chart derivatives must be specified separately. |
| rifs/swizz/swizz2/kalic/gonuts/amoeba | rifs combines the last and two-round-earlier scalar samples after five rounds; its early history assignments read uninitialized locals, though the final required history is overwritten by the fixed schedule. swizz variants subtract multiscale periodic spheres via max. kalic adds a Z-dependent twist and sine translation. gonuts/amoeba use quantized angular folds with positive terminal offsets. |
| twiggy/twiggy2/spicy/blocktree/threddy | twiggy variants use nine rounds followed by a single final measurement. spicy feeds accumulated gyroid values back into later octave coordinates. blocktree drives rotations with interpolated hash values and uses maximum-component boxes; its squared interpolation weight is not derivative-continuous at integer time boundaries. threddy's normalization and measurement occur after seven fold rounds. |
| Lewpen_snowflake/OriginFlowers/Converge | Lewpen_snowflake chooses a dominant coordinate axis and accumulates scaled sphere minima. OriginFlowers and Converge specify negative box extents, requiring an explicit fold convention rather than reliance on reversed clamp bounds. Converge also uses coefficient 1.9 rather than two. |
| mrange_apollo1/mrange_apollo2/mrange_tree1/mrange_tree2 | Apollo variants use iteration-dependent powers of inversion scale, an unusual inverse-scale accumulation and an early threshold; their local layer value is not returned. Tree variants share mirrored repetition and clipping but set radial strength from original Y using different functions. That input dependence contributes to the derivative across all rounds. |
| mrange_mandelbox/PhilosopherStoned/ballFlake/greenDragon | The Mandelbox variant smooths the box fold with k/dr, switches terminal primitive by iteration and overwrites fd for the first three rounds before minimizing later values. PhilosopherStoned applies 64 rotating plane folds and diminishing translations. ballFlake changes its fold extent each round from time. greenDragon mixes four-dimensional normalized complex-plane rotations and input injection; once r2 exceeds 100, continue leaves its state unchanged for remaining iterations. |
| feeingers/hexx/abbox/sonolith/blobelisk/ringoo | feeingers computes two local coloring terms but returns only a scalar. hexx uses a triangular cell map and a scale-dependent terminal thickness. abbox/blobelisk combine original-coordinate planes with transformed fields. sonolith returns an absolute plane sum. ringoo applies the same additive radial regularizer to coordinates and scalar scale, which changes the mapping rather than merely preventing a crash. |
| shreddissimo/gnollum/cage/stairs | Log/spherical or periodic base fields receive multiscale trigonometric detail. shreddissimo's sqrt(abs(...)) creates sharp derivative behavior near zero. cage uses chained assignments inside a vector expression; independent code should make every state transition explicit. stairs' Q-Q+1 is a vector of ones only for finite inputs. |
| jumpthecrater/toomanytrees/holeinone/aroundtheworld/bewareofbumps/mountainclimbing/mindthegap/thesponge/aroundthecitadel/megacitadel/buildupspeed | Eleven parameterized variants share ordered folds, two rotations, eleven scales/translations, a signed box terminal and global componentwise maximum orbitColor. Each set of scale, angles, translation and color weights was read. Negative weights and zero-initialized maxima affect which signed orbit coordinates contribute. |
| ripplecube/kaleidomecha/tree4/trail | ripplecube displaces a box-like residual using feedback gyroid layers and then forms an absolute shell. kaleidomecha takes minima after eight time-dependent folds and segment projections. tree4 uses fourteen inversions with different coordinate and scale denominators, plus state-dependent rotations in the loop update. trail performs eighty degree-based rotations/folds with a constant Julia-like translation and returns only the scalar; its local OrbitTrap is unused. |

**Woven relief is a practical 3D-to-2D direction, with a different representation.** The viking/knitt/knittt/chiral family provides phase-shifted coil and periodic-strip ideas. For RFF, independently specify two planar strand families, their alternating over/under phase, widths and a height profile, then derive normals from the same filtered height. A plane slice of a 3D tube network is generally a cross-section, not a woven surface. Preserve that distinction in feature names and examples. Coordinate-dependent rotations and polar charts change sampling density; thin strands require coverage filtering rather than a smaller global ray-march step. Stable time/phase controls must agree across preview and video.

**Feedback detail differs from ordinary summed octaves.** spicy adds result/a to each later gyroid input. ripplecube mutates p by the previous result and advances its Z phase before each of three layers. The derivative therefore propagates through the accumulated result as well as the base frequency. For a RFF relief/material extension, return value and gradient together or use a footprint-aware finite-difference fallback; do not apply a derivative from an independent-octave noise model. A filtered variant must account for the fact that suppressing an early layer also changes later sample coordinates. This is a new procedural appearance model and does not justify reducing fractal precision.

**Keep shared geometry, material and iteration stages explicit.** In mrange_mandelbox, frame terminals are used before the last sphere terminal, but the first three rounds overwrite rather than accumulate the running result. That is a selected-stage composition, not a minimum across every iteration. In the eleven michael0884 variants, orbitColor is reset for each evaluation and updated after scale and translation. It is an unbounded feature vector, not automatically scene-linear RGB or a normalized normal. RFF should expose chosen channels through a documented mapping to palette/material properties and preserve their observation stage. Repeated field evaluations for normals must not accidentally overwrite the center sample's material result. For Mandelbrot-derived observations, exact support still requires handling MPA-skipped states.

**Planar invariance needs both transform and terminal checks.** hexx's triangular XY mapping preserves Z=0 through its centered Z repetition and scalar inversions, away from singularities, making a native planar specialization plausible. The mrange Apollo variants preserve Y=0 under XZ rotation and centered wrapping, but their terminal abs(Y) then vanishes: that plane is a degenerate choice for a useful contour pattern. prisnm and greenDragon carry a fourth coordinate that participates in subsequent operations; deleting it changes the formula. A full-state slice or an independently specified 2D model are distinct deliverables.

**Completed shader-related reading milestone.** The 763-file shader-related audit set now has full-file reading evidence, including this entire compendium. The set includes formula, feature/settings and shader-builder integration code, not just GLSL. It is a reading milestone, not completion of all GMT code/docs, a runtime test pass or license clearance. The next review area is the remaining application/engine integration and documentation. The inventory still contains unreviewed code and documents outside this set.

No shader compilation, rendering, numerical equivalence/gradient validation, GPU benchmark or external licensing verification was performed in this completion batch. The strongest RFF appearance priority remains editable environment reflection with roughness/footprint filtering; dense-palette filtering remains the leading stability-oriented priority. These rankings are source-based judgments awaiting controlled RFF image and timing comparisons.

## Application integration follow-up: editor handoff, recoverable state and diagnostics

**Full reads.** This review covers app-gmt/AfxRenderAdjunct.tsx, FbxRenderAdjunct.tsx, DiagnosticsOverlay.tsx, explorerTrip.ts and favientsMigration.ts; engine/animation/renderAdjunctRegistry.ts; engine-gmt/engine/webglDiagnostics.ts; engine-gmt/utils/stashLiveScene.ts and sceneStash.ts; and palette/core/explorerHandoff.ts. The export writers, boot restoration consumer, storage helpers and complete palette-store behavior require their own review before end-to-end claims. Comments describing earlier tests are source documentation, not tests executed in this audit.

**Keep auxiliary editors tied to the current document.** explorerTrip records the last applied favorite only in the current module instance, then revalidates both its shelf membership and the destination's current content before using it. Otherwise it chooses the selected host destination, then gradient 1. Flat-color stop gradients are skipped, while ramp configs with empty stops are allowed through the shared config validator. This is a useful RFF design pattern for opening a palette or environment-gradient editor on what the user is actually seeing. Whether to skip a flat color is a product choice, not a mathematical necessity. Favorite identity and color content should remain separate, and a color-space flag must not be discarded merely because a content signature ignores it for identity matching.

The handoff transports a versioned gradient config as a one-shot record with a two-minute lifetime, validates it before returning it, and preserves the submitted config. A separate trip ID answers a liveness ping, with a 300 ms timeout triggering fallback. These mechanisms provide a design reference for a helper process or detached editor in RFF: carry the exact selected content, correlate requests to the initiating document, and restore gracefully if that document is no longer available. A liveness answer proves only that a responder answered; it does not prove focus returned to the intended window or that its state still matches the initial handoff.

**Snapshot the latest state without restoring unrelated libraries.** stashLiveScene first flushes the debounced live camera into the store, then serializes getPreset and captures dirty status. Its stated intent is to exclude the separately persisted gradient shelf, preventing a scene restore from resurrecting deleted library items. For RFF, inspect the equivalent live-navigation, pending-control and palette state before adding a handoff snapshot: flush pending edits once at a defined boundary, retain unsaved status, and separate document state from shared libraries. A new snapshot must not alter the frozen palette recipe generator or existing binary configuration ordering.

**Use distinct recovery reasons and explicit consumption semantics.** sceneStash has separate OAuth and gradient-trip slots, with five-minute and 24-hour lifetimes respectively; only the latter carries dirty state. The gradient restore requires a matching query flag and otherwise consumes nothing. Writes clear the old slot first and roll back partial new writes. Reads consume the slot before later scene parsing. These are clear single-slot semantics, not a transaction across every window or a durable recovery journal. The scene timestamp check also differs from the gradient handoff's finite/future-time validation. For an RFF helper-editor workflow, use a document/request identifier in the recovery record, validate before committing restoration, and preserve an existing usable recovery copy until a replacement is complete. The current GMT trip IDs distinguish liveness messages, but its scene and incoming-gradient storage keys remain shared slots; do not infer multi-document isolation from the ID alone.

**Make library migration restartable if RFF ever needs it.** favientsMigration reads the legacy shelf in reverse order because the destination prepends entries, preserving visible order, and avoids duplicates through isFav. However, it writes its completion flag before parsing/importing and explicitly never retries after partial failure. The transferable idea is preserving order and identity, not copying that failure policy. A future RFF migration should retain its source, define per-item validation/deduplication and mark success only after the intended destination is durable. This is a proposed migration contract, not a claim that RFF currently needs a new palette format.

**Provide an inspectable renderer report.** DiagnosticsOverlay captures one report on initial mount when the URL requests it, supports copying, and sends only after a user action through submitFeedback with includeScene:false. webglDiagnostics gathers application/version, URL, user agent, pixel ratio, screen size, WebGL limits, fragment precision and extensions using a temporary main-thread context; cleanup attempts to lose that context. Its exception handling can produce a partial report. The actual code measures capability queries, not framebuffer completeness, successful shader execution, worker-context equivalence or the claimed sub-frame runtime.

For RFF, compare existing diagnostics before adding a user-visible copy/save report containing the actual selected Vulkan device and driver, enabled features, relevant image-format usage support, render extent, shader/pipeline failure stage and last successful frame stage. Existing RFF pipeline-cache code already uses device/driver identifiers, so those values are not wholly absent; this limited check does not establish an existing complete support-report feature. Separate queried support from a real pipeline/attachment test and label unavailable values. Such evidence would make the proposed environment textures, HDR filtering and new material paths easier to validate across GPUs. Let the user inspect the report; omitting a scene payload alone does not remove identifying data from a full URL. No report was sent during this audit.

**Keep export actions separate from the primary render path.** The render-adjunct registry stores label/title/dialog descriptors, replaces matching labels, and exposes stable array identity until registration changes. The wrappers supply animation timing; the After Effects wrapper additionally chooses fixed resolution or canvas pixels divided by DPR with a minimum dimension of two. These wrappers do not establish exported camera conventions, frame-end inclusivity or successful file compatibility. RFF could offer a supplemental animation-data export using a stable action ID and a shared evaluated timeline, but its 2D view requires high-precision center/zoom/rotation semantics rather than assuming a 3D camera mapping. Those details and the actual GMT writers remain pending. Native application code need not reproduce React registries to adopt the separation of concerns.

These are source-grounded integration recommendations supporting RFF's existing workflows and the proposed shader features. No application runtime, export-import round trip, storage-failure test or GPU probe was executed in this follow-up.

## Timeline export internals: relative precision, sampling time and appearance parity

**Full reads.** engine-gmt/components/timeline/RenderPopup/afxExport.ts, fbxExport.ts and sceneSampler.ts, plus engine-gmt/components/timeline/exportModulations.ts, were read completely. The FBX node builder/binary serializer and export dialogs remain separate pending dependencies. Both exporters now call the shared sceneSampler; the older FBX header's statement that its sampler is still cloned is superseded by the actual imports and implementation. Source comments asserting byte-identical output or successful DCC imports are not independent verification performed here.

**The strongest transferable mechanism is high-precision rebasing before conversion.** sceneSampler captures a start look-at reference using split sceneOffset plus the local camera/forward-distance component. Each camera sample subtracts high and low parts separately before adding local displacement. The AE adapter scales that relative vector by FOV-derived zoom/start distance; the FBX adapter uses 100/start distance. This avoids first collapsing a large absolute coordinate and its small motion into a single double. For RFF, use its existing arbitrary-precision center representation to subtract a chosen reference before converting a local overlay trajectory to ordinary numbers. Export the reference center separately in a lossless representation, along with the zoom convention, rotation and frame times. GMT's split-double representation, 1e-12 start-distance floor and nominal 3D lens scale are not replacements for RFF's precision model.

The sampler treats lights differently: it forms the reference position as a summed ordinary-number rUnified and subtracts that from plain light positions. This does not provide the same cancellation protection as the camera path. A RFF export contract should state which coordinates are high-precision fractal coordinates, which are screen/layer coordinates and which are merely decorative lighting positions. Do not promise deep-zoom spatial fidelity for every channel just because one channel is rebased.

**Separate canonical timeline data from format conventions.** AE uses centered composition pixels with Y/Z sign changes and converts quaternions to ZYX Euler angles, unwrapping each component by multiples of 360. FBX instead exports raw evaluated XYZ Euler tracks in degrees and delegates a fixed camera correction to its scene builder. The matrix diag(1,-1,-1) used in AE has determinant +1; its code operation is a basis transformation, so the header's loose handedness terminology is insufficient to derive all orientation conventions. For RFF's 2D overlay export, define orientation sign, origin, pixel aspect and zoom mapping with labeled test points rather than copying a 3D camera convention. Preserve accumulated 2D rotations when turns beyond 360 degrees are intentional; nearest-angle unwrapping can erase intended motion between sparsely sampled frames.

**A sample index is not a frame time.** The shared sampler includes frames start+i*max(1,step), with count floor((end-start)/step)+1 and a minimum of one. FBX computes times from that clamped step. AE writes key times using the requested step but sets duration to sample count/fps. With step greater than one, that duration is not the sampled timeline span, and a nonpositive requested step is handled inconsistently between sampling and AE timestamps. This is a concrete source-level reason for RFF to carry explicit source frame/time in every sample and derive output duration from the chosen interval convention, not array length. Validate positive finite FPS, integral frame ranges and step, single-frame output, non-divisible endpoints and final-frame hold. No actual AE import was run, and dialog constraints may limit which inputs reach these functions.

**Export the same evaluated appearance as the render.** Each sample scrubs animation then invokes applyExportModulations with time=tf/fps and dt=1/fps. The modulation path uses shared target classification/planning and composite accumulation before sending uniform values to the worker; this is a useful architecture for matching preview/video/material exports. However, the sampler's raw Euler/selected track values are then obtained through evaluateTrack, while quaternion and position are read from the viewport camera. Whether those observations include every worker-applied modulation requires inspecting the downstream application paths. The dt also does not grow with frameStep, so stateful modulation needs an explicit sampling policy. RFF should evaluate base tracks and modulation into one canonical frame result, then use that result for rendering and metadata export. Do not infer matching values simply from matching track names.

**Restoration should cover all temporary evaluation state.** Sampling saves the current frame/play state, pauses playback and restores them in a finally block around the sampling loop. The initial reference scrub/setup occurs before that guarded block, and the visible restoration does not independently snapshot every modulation/uniform state. For an RFF implementation, prefer a pure or isolated frame evaluator; otherwise guard setup and sampling together and restore all touched transient state on errors and cancellation. Verify that exporting does not alter the current view, dirty status or subsequent playback. This is a design requirement, not a tested failure claim for GMT.

**Document interchange limits.** FOV is captured once before scrubbing, so these adapters do not export a per-frame animated lens. AE rounds positions/orientations to four decimals and scalar tracks/times to six, creates light-position nulls rather than reproducing light shading, and references separately rendered footage with a placeholder fallback. The FBX wrapper likewise carries a camera/parameter rig and optional plate reference, not fractal geometry or shader implementation. RFF can provide a useful compositing companion file containing camera-like 2D transforms and selected material controls, but should identify exactly what is sampled, rounded or omitted. Native high-precision project data must remain authoritative.

This follow-up adds an optional interoperability direction and strengthens preview/export parity requirements for the shader proposals. No exporter was executed, external application opened, file-format round trip validated or numerical precision benchmark performed. The FBX builder and serializer remain pending before any stronger compatibility claim.

## FBX scene construction and binary serialization: limits of a compositing companion

**Full reads.** engine-gmt/components/timeline/RenderPopup/fbxScene.ts and fbxBinary.ts, plus plans/fbx-export-findings.md, were read in full. This completes the previously pending scene-builder and serializer review; export dialogs and importer/runtime validation remain separate. The findings document reports C4D experiments but explicitly describes Fusion as assumed-working and unverified. Its broad compatibility assertions and dated library-availability claims are not independently verified here and should not become RFF product guarantees.

**Separate semantic data from the byte container.** fbxScene constructs object IDs, models, camera attributes, animation nodes/curves, connections, definitions and takes. fbxBinary serializes a generic node tree using little-endian scalars, UTF-8 strings, uncompressed arrays, absolute end offsets, sentinel records and fixed header/footer data. This separation is useful for RFF: a canonical sampled animation model can feed multiple adapters, while the container writer remains independent of fractal computation. It also permits distinct checks for byte structure, object references and actual imported motion. A structurally readable file alone does not prove correct lens, timing, colors or orientation.

**Animated values lose precision at a specific boundary.** Initial model properties are written as doubles, but animation curves use KeyValueFloat and fbxFloatArray, which writes IEEE float32 values. Thus adding animation can change the available precision relative to a static value. Rebasing helps keep ordinary camera motion representable; it does not make this a lossless carrier for RFF's high-precision center or arbitrary-depth zoom. Retain the reference center and exact view parameters in a separate lossless native/companion representation, and describe FBX values as a normalized compositing rig. Judge any approximation against projected pixel error across the intended video rather than only coordinate round trips.

**Metadata and interpolation must agree with sampled time.** The scene builder receives sample.fps but writes fixed timeMode:6, which its local helper documents as 30 FPS. Curve timestamps still come from the exporter-generated KTime array. For RFF, declared rate, key times and range convention must match, including non-integer frame rates if supported. Animation curves request linear interpolation. Dense linear keys reproduce their stored sample values; they do not prove the correct continuous motion between samples, particularly for rotation or nonlinear zoom. State the supported interpolation contract and validate intermediate-frame behavior when exporting sparsely.

**Scalar controls are currently spatially encoded.** Each selected parameter becomes a null whose raw value is Position Y, without a parameter-unit field. An importer may apply scene-unit or axis conversion to transforms, so a downstream consumer must not assume that raw scientific/material values survive every import setting. Sanitized labels can also collide, and metadata does not retain the original track ID. A RFF interchange design should carry stable parameter IDs, units, ranges and exact source values separately; use a format's custom-property facility only after verifying its importer support. Label-derived names can remain human-readable aliases.

**The plate is a reference, not an embedded render.** buildPlate creates a camera-child quad at nominal depth, sizes it from FOV/aspect, assigns UVs and a camera-facing normal, and links filename-based Video/Texture nodes to diffuse and emissive material properties. No video bytes are embedded. This can help composite external objects over a rendered RFF video, but does not export the fractal's material model or reproduce HDR/color-management behavior automatically. Verify orientation, frame synchronization, footage resolution, color space and importer texture/material handling. A 2D RFF workflow may be better served by direct composition transforms and a referenced image sequence than by a fabricated perspective scene; preserve the user's intended output rather than selecting FBX merely because GMT offers it.

**Container limits should be enforced at an adapter boundary.** The serializer is structurally a 7400 writer: node lengths/offsets are 32-bit, names have a one-byte encoded length, and child sentinels are thirteen bytes. Its version argument does not switch those layouts. Integer writes coerce/truncate widths, long-number inputs are rounded before conversion to bigint, and array sizes/offsets are not visibly range-checked. A separate RFF writer should reject unsupported versions, overlong encoded node names, nonfinite values, unsafe integer times, inconsistent track lengths and oversized output before serialization. Uncompressed arrays simplify dependencies but increase memory/file size; the growable buffer and final copy should be budgeted for long bakes. These are design constraints, not measured failures in an actual GMT export.

**Provenance is explicit but permission remains unverified.** The binary writer says its sentinel rules and footer/header constants were taken verbatim from Blender's exporter, despite describing the broader implementation as hand-authored. The local findings also recommend copying a known exporter routine. Before adapting any distinctive portion to RFF, inspect the original revision and actual license, preserve required attribution and update NOTICE. Independently implementing a documented format is different from copying another exporter. No external source/license check was performed in this batch.

Recommended validation for a future RFF adapter: static versus animated precision, multiple FPS values, fractional-rate timestamps, unicode/colliding labels, varying parameter units, long sequences, a labeled camera/plate orientation scene and actual round trips in each advertised target. No FBX was generated/imported or benchmarked during this review. This optional interoperability work remains secondary to the shader appearance/stability improvements identified earlier.

## Startup ordering: complete scenes before renderer initialization

**Full reads.** app-gmt/main.tsx and docs/adr/0006-registerfeatures-as-side-effect-import.md were read completely. The entry-point output was initially truncated around plugin installation; that omitted section was re-read separately before full-file credit. Imported implementations are not automatically covered by this entry-point read.

**Resolve one scene before starting rendering.** The boot resolver tries a serialized share hash, a server-backed share ID, a specifically flagged gradient-editor return stash, an OAuth stash, then the default formula. Invalid sources can fall through with diagnostics. The asynchronous resolver is awaited before store hydration and React mounting, so the first renderer configuration can contain the intended render mode and scene. For RFF, define similarly explicit precedence among an opened file, a requested recovery and a default view, and commit the selected state before initiating expensive reference computation or shader-resource setup. A restored dirty scene must retain its unsaved status; the gradient-return branch explicitly requests this after loadScene.

**Resources need lifecycle-aware delivery.** Before a scene is loaded, the entry point installs listeners that keep pre-boot texture updates in pendingTextures and queue custom formula registration through the renderer proxy. This is directly relevant to adding environment-gradient/image resources in RFF: loading the document before the renderer is ready must not lose its texture, and a late resource from an older document must not replace the current one. Use an explicit document/resource generation and apply the latest complete resource set when the device/pipeline is ready. Replay order should satisfy formula/pipeline/layout dependencies before the first render. The current file shows event capture; actual worker replay and upload guarantees require the worker-path implementation.

**Keep derived shader values independent of open panels.** main installs coloring animation binders because phase/repeat controls need conversion to shader offset/scale even when the coloring panel is closed. This is a valuable RFF principle for the proposed environment and material extensions: a model-level evaluator should derive all shader inputs for preview, video and export, with panels only editing the source settings. Likewise, its render-scale selector is explicitly wired to the field the GMT renderer consumes, rather than a generic field used by another application. Avoid introducing a second UI value that does not control the actual render path.

**Separate UI publication from frame evaluation.** The entry point sets live-modulation publication to 50 ms while documenting a separate per-frame render read. This offers a possible RFF responsiveness improvement when rapidly changing material values cause expensive panel updates: publish presentation indicators at a bounded rate while preserving the renderer's exact frame-time evaluation. The source comment reports a previous measurement, but no timing comparison was performed here. Validate this only if RFF profiling shows relevant UI overhead; do not reduce computation precision or animation sampling to make the interface cheaper.

**Registration ordering is a documented contract, not merely import placement.** ADR-0006's update corrects its older explanation: registry freezing occurs on first store access, not simply importing the store. The entry point registers features through an early side-effect import and installs preset fields before consumers can initialize state. The uncorrected wording later in the ADR should not override that update. For RFF, the transferable design is a defined setup phase for feature metadata, serialization fields and shader resources before dependent state is constructed. C++ need not imitate JavaScript side-effect imports; explicit initialization and a clear rejection of late incompatible registrations can make the dependency easier to verify.

**Recovery and failure are separate paths.** The selected share query is removed before fetching, and consumed stashes are parsed afterward; recovery data is not retained indefinitely by this flow. A loadScene exception is handed to an error boundary as initialError, but the final resolver promise has no explicit rejection handler in this file. The deferred gradient-return warning polls for a booted renderer, so it depends on successful boot to become visible. For an RFF implementation, preserve actionable recovery evidence until successful application, show failures without requiring the renderer to become healthy, and make retries/cancellation explicit. These observations constrain a new design; they are not runtime failures reproduced in GMT.

Other inspected wiring includes canvas-specific snapshots, flushing the live camera before saving, embedded-formula registration, partial-load/menu actions, shortcut priority overrides, separate camera undo, optional performance probes and gallery URL consumption. Those consumers remain separate review targets. No startup, recovery, UI performance or worker race test was executed. This integration review strengthens the reliability requirements for RFF's shader additions without changing their appearance priority.

## Animation binders: deterministic palette evaluation and precision-preserving view capture

**Full reads.** engine-gmt/animation/coloringBinders.ts and cameraBinders.ts, plus engine/animation/binderRegistry.ts, logTrackRegistry.ts and cameraKeyRegistry.ts, were read in full. The evaluator, curve-fitting tools and camera precision helpers remain separate dependencies; the log-track registry's comments about measured curve-tool failures are not reproduced tests in this review.

**Derived palette controls belong outside panels.** The four coloring binders handle phase/repeat controls for two layers. Phase updates add newPhase-oldPhase to the current offset; repeat updates retain the current scale/repeats ratio and multiply it by the new repeat count. This supplies actual shader-facing fields even when no gradient panel is mounted. For RFF's proposed environment gradient and existing animated palette controls, centralize this conversion in a frame evaluator used by previews, videos and exports. Retain a canonical anchor/range instead of relying exclusively on previous-frame state, so seeking directly to a frame agrees with playing through intervening frames.

The repeat binder returns immediately when the OLD repeat magnitude is below 0.0001, before writing the new repeat value. A zero repeat can therefore require a separately defined recovery/anchor policy if this design is adopted. Phase delta accumulation can also accumulate rounding over repeated seeks, and simultaneous changes of range/repeat/phase need an explicit ordering. These are reasons to specify deterministic RFF evaluation, not to replace its established palette mapping with GMT's formulas. Validate direct seek, reverse playback, repeated seek, zero/near-zero repeats and both layers with panels open and closed. Preserve frozen palette-recipe generation independently of animated presentation controls.

**Commit a view as one coherent frame.** Camera binders read live state before scrubbing, buffer axis writes and emit one teleport after scrubbing only if a camera track changed. This avoids publishing partially updated coordinates after every axis. RFF can use the same transaction concept for high-precision center, zoom and rotation, including recalculation scheduling: one evaluated frame should start one coherent render request. A buffer must be valid even when the live viewport is absent, and its lifetime/dirty flags should be reset at a defined boundary.

**Splitting a rounded number does not recover lost precision.** The inspected preScrub sums sceneOffset high+low+local into ordinary THREE.Vector3 numbers, and postScrub later splits those numbers again. This path therefore cannot be assumed to preserve arbitrary sub-double motion just because its emitted structure contains high/low fields. RFF must retain its arbitrary-precision or explicitly paired representation through key capture, interpolation and frame application; use ordinary numbers only for a justified local/rendering conversion. The registry supports hidden low-word tracks for other applications, but the GMT-specific capture function writes six ordinary scalar tracks. Do not transfer its storage model unmodified to a deep Mandelbrot zoom.

**Capture all view channels with one undo action.** GMT's capture function takes one snapshot, creates/upserts six tracks in a single state update and updates adjacent Bezier tangents. It chooses Linear for the first position-X key and Bezier thereafter unless overridden. The generic registry fallback resolves finite values first and also takes one snapshot, but writes tracks individually and delegates interpolation to addKeyframe. For RFF, the useful contract is one user capture/one undo operation, with center/zoom/rotation captured atomically. Choose interpolation intentionally; a convenience default based on one channel's first key is not a proof of suitable zoom behavior. The registered custom capture callback also has a separate lifecycle from the returned camera-binder teardown, which should be considered if implementing detachable modules.

**Logarithmic zoom needs consistent units throughout editing.** logTrackRegistry only stores IDs; the documented interpolation and tangent behavior lives elsewhere. Its useful design requirement is that evaluating, drawing, fitting and simplifying a zoom curve all agree on log-value units. A positive scale's log interpolates multiplicative zoom naturally, but RFF may need to represent the logarithm directly when the underlying scale exceeds ordinary floating-point range. Tangent units, invalid-value policy and simplification error should be explicit and stable in saved data. Merely registering a track as logarithmic is insufficient evidence that every curve-editing path honors it.

**Stable IDs and ownership-aware replacement help integration.** binderRegistry replaces by ID and its unregister callback removes an entry only if it still owns that exact registration. This prevents an old module teardown from deleting a newer binding. cameraKeyRegistry maintains stable cached ID arrays for subscribers. These are useful implementation patterns if RFF adds configurable animation/material channels, but no React-style registry is required to adopt their ownership and notification guarantees.

No animation playback, precision benchmark, curve test or rendering comparison was executed. The actionable RFF priorities from this batch are deterministic shader-input evaluation, atomic view updates and preservation of center/zoom precision across the entire animation path.

## Coupled pan/zoom and local-coordinate navigation

**Full reads.** docs/adr/0015-animation-log-and-camera-pair-value-spaces.md, engine-gmt/engine/PrecisionMath.ts, engine/plugins/navigation/core/VirtualSpace.ts and engine/animation/cameraPairRegistry.ts were read completely. A truncated portion of the camera-pair header/imports was re-read separately. PrecisionMath is only a re-export shim.
