The ADR's update supersedes its older claim that log tracks cannot use Bezier curves; the underlying AnimationMath implementation still requires its own review.

**A useful 2D transfer is coupling pan to visible scale.** The camera-pair evaluator maps progress through (z(t)-z0)/(z1-z0), then interpolates center endpoints with double-double arithmetic. When z represents visible world scale and follows an exponential curve without extra easing, this avoids the rapidly increasing screen displacement of a constant world-speed pan. It is not a universal constant-screen-speed guarantee: eased/nonmonotonic zoom, independent pan easing, rotation and the definition of zoom all affect that interpretation. For RFF, compare the existing video path before introducing a selectable coupled-pan mode, and use its high-precision centers and explicit visible-scale convention.

**Preserve pairs as one value.** The implementation subtracts endpoint pairs, multiplies the difference by a progress scalar and adds it back using two-sum and split-product operations. It samples low-word endpoints at the corresponding high-word key times within a segment. This is a stronger design than independently interpolating the two words. RFF should preserve its existing arbitrary-precision representation rather than adopt double-double as a precision ceiling. The ordinary-number progress and zoom ratios remain separate numerical limits, especially when zoom spans extreme ranges; a log-domain or exponent-aware evaluation may be required.

**Edge behavior belongs in the saved animation contract.** Flat endpoint zoom falls back to eased time, while other segments sample zoom at a virtual frame derived from pan easing. Very small high-word center differences bypass Bezier pan easing; low-word-only motion therefore deserves a dedicated case. Outside the high-word key range, the implementation takes the first/last low key rather than evaluating it at the high endpoint, so unsynchronized key ranges need explicit semantics. An existing zoom track with no keys yields zoomAt=1, despite the header's claim of no override. RFF should define aligned high-precision keys, endpoint behavior, overshoot and zoom reversal intentionally and test direct seeking as well as playback.

The cache uses zoom ID plus axis and validates frame/sequence identity. It does not include the complete pair identity or registry revision. A reusable RFF evaluator should key cached results by the actual view-track grouping and data revision; immutable sequence replacement is a valid invalidation strategy only if all editing paths uphold it. These are adoption requirements, not a demonstrated RFF defect.

**Local rendering coordinates are useful without replacing the mathematical center.** VirtualSpace accumulates movement in low components, periodically moves integer portions into high components, and keeps the camera near the origin. Its split operation uses float32 rounding plus a residual. Several methods later sum the components into one ordinary number before splitting or forming light positions, so the class header's arbitrary-depth language must not be read as an unlimited-precision guarantee. RFF can retain a high-precision reference center while expressing decorative lighting, normals and local overlays in bounded coordinates. Never rebuild the authoritative center from a rounded shader representation.

**Interaction smoothing and export evaluation need distinct policies.** VirtualSpace smooths position with 1-exp(-40*delta), uses lock/unlock thresholds, and copies rotation/FOV directly to avoid misaligning overlays. Large offset changes reset smoothing. For RFF, any optional navigation smoothing should use elapsed time, keep overlays synchronized and snap for deterministic frame export or explicit jumps. Fixed world-distance thresholds are not automatically appropriate across Mandelbrot zoom depths. Validate behavior in screen units and preserve the exact authored camera path for saved/video frames.

No numerical precision test, motion render or timing experiment was performed. Named numerical algorithms and any copied implementation require original provenance/license verification and NOTICE attribution before adaptation. This batch adds a concrete 3D-navigation-to-2D-animation direction without changing RFF's perturbation or MPA algorithms.

## Animation curve mechanics for reliable 2D zoom and material motion

Full reads of [AnimationMath.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/math/AnimationMath.ts), [BezierMath.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/BezierMath.ts) and [TrackUtils.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/algorithms/TrackUtils.ts) establish the interpolation mechanics behind the preceding animation recommendations. These are animation infrastructure mechanisms, not additional shader algorithms. Their useful RFF destinations are zoom, palette phase, environment orientation and material parameters; they do not require a 3D camera or changes to perturbation/MPA.

**Make the value space part of the track contract.** Step interpolation returns the first value immediately. Positive log tracks interpolate log(value), including Bezier control-point heights, and exponentiate the result. Linear interpolation in that space gives a constant multiplicative change per unit time. Automatic tangents use log differences only when the current key and every available adjacent key are positive. Segment evaluation instead checks only its two endpoints. Consequently, a nonpositive neighbor can make a positive segment consume handles generated in ordinary-value units as log units. RFF should validate the entire domain of positive-only tracks or define an explicit conversion/segment policy; silently switching units is unsuitable for saved animation. The ordinary-value fallback can still be Bezier, despite wording in the source that might suggest a straight-line fallback. Extreme Mandelbrot zoom needs an exponent-aware or existing high-precision representation rather than a requirement to materialize every scale as an ordinary floating-point value.

**Time inversion needs an accuracy contract.** The cubic solver starts with normalized linear time, performs at most four Newton iterations, exits early for a small slope and clamps only the final parameter to [0,1]. It checks neither the final time residual nor convergence and has no bracketed fallback. Default handle constraints only enforce left/right signs; sufficiently long manual handles can make the time component nonmonotonic, so one frame may have multiple candidate curve parameters. For RFF, enforce a monotonic-time curve or specify a deliberate branch rule, then use a bounded solver with a residual check and fallback. Final clamping alone does not establish that the returned value belongs to the requested frame. An error in log space becomes a multiplicative zoom error. This is a source-level adoption condition, not a measured playback failure.

**Preserve intentional edits with explicit retiming semantics.** Automatic tangent generation flattens local extrema and limits a same-direction interior slope to three times the smaller neighboring slope magnitude. Endpoint slope calculations assume distinct frame times; validate sorted, unique keys before reaching them. TrackUtils recomputes only adjacent Bezier keys with autoTangent enabled, preserving manual handles, and does not recompute the edited key itself. Its continuity comment is therefore not a guarantee for arbitrary manual/Step/Linear neighbors. New keys inherit the preceding key's interpolation mode, or Linear before the first key. These are useful predictable editing rules for RFF. The retiming helper scales both handle coordinates by the change in neighboring time interval: it preserves the handle angle, not the same value trajectory under a pure horizontal time stretch. Offer a clearly defined retiming rule, including key crossings, rather than promising both properties simultaneously.

**Insert keys without changing the authored curve.** The split helper uses de Casteljau subdivision and returns the split point plus both segments' control points. This supports inserting a palette, light or zoom key on an existing curve while retaining its shape. The insertion must use the parameter corresponding to the requested frame, preserve both resulting handle sets and perform the subdivision in the evaluator's value space. For a log track, split the log-value curve, exponentiate the new key value and retain handle heights in log units. Re-running automatic tangents afterward can change the curve and should be an explicit editing choice.

**Angles need separate cyclic and accumulated semantics.** Rotation interpolation adjusts the endpoint by only one full turn when its difference exceeds pi. This is not a general normalization for arbitrarily many turns and cannot express both shortest-path orientation and intentional repeated spins without additional track semantics. RFF environment rotation and palette phase should declare whether values represent a wrapped orientation, accumulated cycles or an explicitly selected direction. Keep saved curves and direct frame seeking consistent with that choice.

The soft-selection helper supplies linear, circular-dome, fourth-power and cosine falloffs for nonnegative distance within a positive radius. These are editing weights rather than antialiasing filters; their existence does not address shader pixel coverage. Validate these input domains if reused for timeline influence tools.

Before adopting this infrastructure, check exact key endpoints, nearly flat time derivatives, long manual handles, duplicate times, positive-domain violations, extreme zoom ranges, shape-preserving insertion, key retiming and direct-seek/playback/export agreement. No numerical solver tests, rendered animation, shader build or performance measurement was performed in this batch. No implementation was copied into RFF, and source provenance/licensing must be established before any later adaptation.

## Sample fitting and local smoothing for editable RFF palettes and animation

Full reads of [CurveFitting.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/CurveFitting.ts) and [ConstrainedSmoothing.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/ConstrainedSmoothing.ts) identify a useful authoring feature: turn a sampled palette channel or drawn parameter curve into a smaller editable Bezier representation, then smooth a selected interval. This transfers directly to 2D RFF. It is an editor/preparation operation, not a reason to approximate the precision-sensitive fractal computation.

**Fit the representation that playback actually evaluates.** The newer sample-fitting path pins the endpoints and solves a two-by-two least-squares system for the two cubic control values. It compares the resulting curve's maximum absolute sample error against the straight chord and retains the better option. Least squares minimizes a sum of squared errors, so this additional maximum-error comparison has a distinct purpose. Fitted time handles use exactly one third of the segment duration, making cubic parameter equal normalized time. They are marked autoTangent=false so later authoring-oriented tangent generation does not erase the fit. Neighbor-derived automatic easing and sample fitting solve different problems and should remain separate in RFF.

**Use an honest error budget.** dpIndices measures perpendicular distance in mixed sample-index/value coordinates. That tolerance does not bound vertical value error, and converting its polyline to a cubic does not repair the mismatch. optimalKnotIndices instead accepts spans using the maximum sample error of the same fitter used to store their handles. It tries the final endpoint, probes exponentially increasing distances and scans a limited window beyond a failure. Despite its name and introductory wording, this is not an exhaustive minimum-key solution: fit feasibility is not prefix-closed and the source itself acknowledges nonoptimal key counts. The guarantee is limited to supplied samples, finite valid inputs and the matching parameterization; it does not bound between-sample extrema, displayed RGB/perceptual error or a changed downstream evaluator. Source comments contain benchmark numbers and reported tests, neither independently reproduced here. For RFF, expose quality in the domain users care about and verify the final palette reconstruction, including gamut handling and cyclic seams.

**Respect the sample times.** fitKeysToSamples fits using sample index and maps only the chosen key positions through frameOf. Its reconstruction assumptions require an affine mapping of index to time within each fitted span. smoothSpan normally samples at a fixed stride but appends the exact interval end when it is not stride-aligned, creating a shorter last interval. A RFF implementation should fit against actual sample times or resample uniformly, and should reject nonpositive/nonfinite strides. For zoom, transform both fitting samples and tangent units to the established log/exponent-aware domain; these generic fitting helpers and reTangentBezier do not take the log-track flag.

**Treat the older simplifyTrack path separately.** Its internal evaluator uses normalized frame time directly for Bezier Y and ignores stored X handles, so it does not reproduce an arbitrary weighted-time curve. Resampling uses max(requestedStep, duration/50), which limits a long clip to roughly fifty intervals rather than sampling every frame as a nearby comment implies. It then uses approximately one-third time arms (0.333), and accepts subframe spans without checking their internal error. It also converts Step segments into fitted Beziers and offers no log or rotation-space handling. RFF should reuse its canonical evaluator, preserve discontinuity boundaries and adaptively sample narrow features before simplification. Do not transfer the newer sample-fitting path's claims to this older API.

**A localized edit includes a defined seam policy.** spliceSpan removes keys inside the inclusive interval and retains keys outside it, but it can change the outside neighbors' tangent metadata. It resizes fitted boundary arms to one third of the new gap, shortens overreaching manual arms on the retained neighbors and recalculates selected automatic tangents. Thus the source's statement that outside keys survive verbatim is too strong. Matching outward and inward slopes can improve the join at a fitted boundary; it does not establish unchanged curvature or a universally smooth surrounding curve. For RFF, state whether an interval edit may alter neighboring transitions, include those modifications in undo and preserve key values outside the selection. Validate sorted unique keys, incoming span bounds, tangent direction and Step boundaries rather than assuming the helper accepts arbitrary data.

**The smoothing kernel operates on key adjacency, not physical time.** Selected contiguous blocks solve an implicit diffusion system, with unselected neighboring values moved into the right-hand side as anchors. Open track ends use reflected-neighbor conditions; an isolated selected endpoint is skipped. Coefficients do not depend on frame spacing, so irregularly spaced keys receive the same adjacency weights as uniformly spaced keys. The function returns value patches only, and cannot by itself guarantee the C1 continuity claimed in its header. RFF should choose either uniform resampling or a time-aware operator, define endpoint/tangent treatment and retain the original samples for reversible editing. For finite nonnegative strength, the constructed diagonal exceeds the off-diagonal magnitude sum by the fidelity weight; the generic solver's zero/skip fallback should not be mistaken for an explicit error report if invalid inputs reach it. The absolute variance cutoff and cancellation-prone sum-of-squares variance in the fitting solver also deserve scale-aware handling for large offsets or tiny variations.

The per-span scratch pool is keyed by span length. Its comment assumes at most 256 lengths, but the public fitter itself imposes no such bound. RFF should bound caches using actual accepted input sizes, and measure probe count and responsiveness on the intended corpus before choosing an interactive fitting strategy. Before copying distinctive implementations, establish their actual provenance/license and add appropriate NOTICE records. No solver test, palette render, animation export or performance benchmark was executed in this batch.

## Shared animation bindings and tick installation

Full reads of [trackBinding.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/animation/trackBinding.ts), [modulationTick.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/animation/modulationTick.ts) and [Easing.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/math/Easing.ts) add integration requirements to the proposed material/palette animation workflow.

Track IDs derive from feature and parameter IDs, with explicit vector-axis suffixes or composeFrom scalar bindings. A partially modulated vector takes untouched components from its base value; camera-style additive modulation adds offsets only on affected components. RFF can use one typed binding definition for editor controls, evaluation and export, preserving unaffected values and distinguishing absolute values from offsets. The helper assumes vector lengths of two through four and does not validate duplicate IDs or finite values, so those are schema responsibilities rather than inferred guarantees.

Modulation installation is idempotent and registers the canonical animation tick in the ANIMATE phase; uninstallation removes that registration. Connecting the animation engine to store handles is a separate prerequisite described by the wrapper. Debug globals and a cumulative tick counter remain after uninstall, so the counter measures historical execution rather than installation health. The actual AnimationSystem body still requires separate inspection; the wrapper's description of oscillator/rule ordering is not sufficient evidence of export determinism. The small easing module supplies unclamped linear interpolation and quadratic ease-in-out with an assumed [0,1] parameter; these are appropriate transient UI helpers, not precision-preserving deep-zoom interpolation.

## Live animation execution: separate rendering, UI publication and recording

A full read of [AnimationSystem.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/animation/AnimationSystem.tsx) completes the dispatcher inspection deferred above. The useful RFF feature is deterministic animation of existing palette/material/environment controls, optionally driven by audio. Shared target routing is valuable, but sharing the branch implementation alone does not establish equality between preview, seeking and export.

**Keep render values current while reducing UI work.** The dispatcher retains an unthrottled live-value map for the renderer and separately publishes changes into the UI store at a configurable interval. RFF can apply this distinction to rapidly changing shader controls: every rendered frame consumes current values, while meters and numeric readouts update less often. Structural changes are intended to publish immediately, but this implementation tests only key-count changes for that bypass; replacing one target with another at equal count can wait for the interval. Define structural identity explicitly. Uniform ownership is rebuilt each tick, and the previous target set is processed once more after removal to restore baselines before the idle early return. That cleanup principle is useful for any RFF effect that temporarily overrides a saved setting.

**Use one coherent frame snapshot and explicit clocks.** This function captures animation/store snapshots before animationEngine.tick and continues using those objects afterward. Confirm immutable-store timing and refresh the snapshot when evaluating the newly advanced frame. Oscillator time switches to frame/fps only when deterministic playback is enabled AND the timeline is playing; paused scrubbing still uses wall time. The deterministic oscillator delta is one frame, while rule processing receives the live tick delta. Stateful smoothing, envelopes and audio analysis therefore require additional reset/replay or precomputed data to make arbitrary seeking reproducible. For RFF, define canonical evaluation from frame time and authored state, and give any history-dependent process an explicit checkpoint or bake mechanism. Camera-pair evaluation must remain part of the clean recording base; this source explicitly notes that its evaluateTrack call omits the paired-track step.

**Record from an immutable base, and make gaps honest.** The live recording path supplies cleanBase so modulation is added to the pre-recording track or captured static value instead of compounding previously modulated values. Records are buffered and flushed every 400 ms or on a recording-stop transition. That interval is about 2.5 periodic flushes per second, not the approximately six mentioned in an earlier comment. Recording begins with lastFrameRecorded=-1, so arming later on the timeline can fill from frame zero; backward seeking does not record until the old maximum is exceeded. RFF should explicitly define the recording start range, loop/overwrite semantics, cancellation, final flush and undo boundary.

**The audio back-fill intention is not the current record output.** The subframe loop retrieves past analysis snapshots and evaluates rule offsets, but calls planModulationTarget with only isRemoved=false. Inspection of that planner's record gate shows that records are enabled by the presence of cleanBase; consequently the subframe calls cannot populate the staged subRecords through this path. The live pass falls back to repeated current records for the gap. Moreover, the subpass does not update oscillators for each historical frame and does not supply an evaluated historical base. Treat the source comments about measured per-frame reconstruction as an intended design, not a verified implemented guarantee. A RFF version should test distinct recorded values across a deliberately stalled interval and distinguish measured samples, reconstructed values and held values. Re-evaluating history must not emit past uniforms into the current viewport or accidentally advance the live envelope state twice.

**Invalidate from relevant resolved state.** Accumulation reset compares successive offsets using an absolute 0.0001 threshold, then replaces the previous-offset snapshot on every tick. A sufficiently slow cumulative drift can stay below that threshold indefinitely; nonlinear parameter composition also makes equal offset changes unequal in visible effect. Other uniform/reset paths may cover particular targets, so this is not proof that all such GMT scenes retain stale accumulation. For RFF, track invalidation against the state actually used for cached rendering, include base-value changes and classify whether a change requires fractal recomputation, shading only or final composition. This provides a concrete route to responsive material animation without weakening mathematical precision.

## Optional audio-driven 2D visuals: clock, asset and export contracts

Full reads of [audioTick.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/animation/audioTick.ts), [audioClipSync.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/animation/audioClipSync.ts), [audioExportMix.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/animation/audioExportMix.ts) and [audioFileCache.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/animation/audioFileCache.ts) provide supporting mechanisms for audio-reactive palette, light or relief animation. This is an optional creative workflow, below the current environment-reflection and filtering priorities; it has no inherent 3D dependency.

Analysis registers in the SNAPSHOT phase before modulation's ANIMATE phase and reads current audio settings each tick, allowing operation independently of an open panel. Clip synchronization avoids repeated seeks during steady playback and tracks deck ownership so timeline operations do not routinely stop unrelated manual playback. Those principles transfer well, but the implementation detects seeks from a frame-jump threshold of half a second. It cannot distinguish an explicit small scrub from ordinary progress, and a long render stall can look like a seek. On first invocation in a playing state, justResumed is false; entering a clip during ordinary progression also does not explicitly seek to its trim start. Deleted clips are not reconciled against the owned-deck set here. RFF should pass explicit playback/seek/clip-entry events, reconcile removed assets and define behavior when multiple clips reference one deck, rather than infer all events from frame differences.

**Export should use a declared sample timeline.** The mixer decodes cached source files, intersects trimmed clips with the inclusive video frame range, sums stereo samples and hard-clips the result. Mono is duplicated; sources with more than two channels use only the first two. There is no per-clip gain, fade or limiter in this helper. Source sampling is linear interpolation, without a dedicated antialias filter for rate reduction. RFF should use an appropriate resampler and explicit gain/headroom if this feature is added. Floor/ceil placement of a clip's output sample range and sampling from its exact audible start can introduce a sub-sample origin mismatch; derive sample time from the output sample index and use a consistent boundary policy.

The mix spans (endFrame-startFrame+1)/fps and allocates the entire interleaved buffer. Comments assert agreement with a stepped video export running at fps/frameStep, but this helper alone does not prove the last encoded frame duration matches arbitrary non-aligned ranges. Verify actual encoder timestamps and tail duration, and consider chunked mixing for long exports. Missing cached files are silently skipped (or yield null when none remain); the cache is a page-lifetime singleton keyed by only two deck indices, not a persistent asset store. For RFF, preserve durable source references and report missing assets before export rather than silently rendering incomplete audio.

No playback, recording, audio decode, exported-video synchronization or performance test was run. These findings define RFF adoption requirements from source inspection; they are not a request to repair GMT, nor evidence that RFF currently has these defects.

## Fit the palette to a view, then keep the mapping fixed

Full reads of [fitIterationRange.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/fractal/fitIterationRange.ts) and [FitGradientButton.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/fluid-toy/components/FitGradientButton.tsx) provide a concrete 2D implementation of the earlier histogram-assisted palette proposal. The user requests a fit once; the resulting offset and scale persist until another fit or reset. This avoids continuously changing colors as the view moves. It is a strong usability companion to shader improvements, rather than a new shading model.

The helper reads normalized smooth iterations from the second component of a GPU attachment, excludes nonfinite values and values outside (0.0001,0.999), builds a 256-bin histogram over the surviving range and chooses approximate 2nd/98th percentiles. It multiplies by the active iteration cap, transforms with log(1+iteration), and returns offset=lowerLog and scale=1/max(upperLog-lowerLog,0.001). RFF should adapt the operation to its actual coloring field, transform and authoritative interior mask. GMT's numerical cutoffs are a heuristic for its own attachment encoding: they are not a general escaped-pixel classifier, and half-float readback does not preserve RFF's iteration precision. Empty and constant-range views need an explicit no-op/result state.

The percentile helper returns a selected bin center, despite its comment describing interpolation. Histogram assignment rounds onto 255 intervals while reconstruction uses 256 bin centers. This is approximate range assistance, not an exact quantile computation. RFF can document that approximation or use matching bin edges and within-bin estimation; tiny visible ranges and outlier-heavy views need validation. Keep the fit anchored during video export unless the user explicitly animates its parameters, and offer undo/reset without changing palette recipe generation or saved recipe IDs.

The source performs a full RGBA readback and CPU scans on demand. It queries only the supported read type, treats every non-FLOAT result as HALF_FLOAT and resets the framebuffer binding to null rather than restoring the prior binding. These WebGL details should not become a Vulkan design. For RFF, consider a GPU reduction/histogram and asynchronous readback with a request tied to the view generation, rejecting stale results. Verify cost before choosing the mechanism; no speedup is measured here. Distinguish unavailable data/readback failure from an all-interior view rather than presenting every null result as 'no range'. The button resets to its host's specific anchor (0,0.125), which is not a universal RFF default.

## Editable palette channels, deliberate bands and bounded approximations

Full reads of [channelCurve.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/channelCurve.ts), [colorBoxFit.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/colorBoxFit.ts), [easings.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/easings.ts) and [curveFitPref.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/store/curveFitPref.ts) extend the prior fitting analysis. A targeted read of generatorPipeline.decomposeRamp confirms that its decomposition consumes exactly 256 RGB samples and produces OKLCh channels; the rest of that file remains separately pending.

**Reuse curve editing without coupling palette data to the timeline.** channelCurve maps the palette domain onto frames 0..255 in a private Track representation and samples it through the existing track-value evaluator. RFF can similarly share curve mathematics and editing behavior while preserving separate palette and animation ownership. The generic linear fit uses Douglas-Peucker; the Bezier fit can choose the sample-error-tested placement described above. Validate at least two source samples and at least two output samples: these APIs divide by length-1/count-1 without singleton handling. Since each channel is evaluated with rotation=false, hue unwrapping and achromatic behavior must be owned explicitly by the caller rather than inferred from the track type.

**Preserve intended discontinuities.** flatRuns detects spans of at least four exactly equal samples in every channel and classifies a ramp as banded when such spans cover at least 60% of it. Banded conversion uses Step keys for holds and Linear keys in intervening gaps. This is a useful RFF authoring option for striped palettes: applying smooth automatic tangents everywhere would erase intentional edges. Exact equality is suitable for identically decoded texels, not a robust classifier of noisy imported images. Quantized smooth ramps can also contain repeated samples, so expose or validate the classification. The Douglas-Peucker gap tolerance still measures perpendicular mixed-coordinate distance; claims of a strict vertical eps bound in comments are stronger than the actual metric. Judge reconstruction using the displayed palette and preserve deliberately sharp boundaries separately from antialiasing their final screen coverage.

**Simple sweep controls cannot reproduce every palette.** ColorBox fitting fixes each L/C/h channel's endpoints and selects the least-squares best of 25 easing curves after normalizing channel values between those endpoints. Nearly equal endpoints are treated as flat, even when the interior contains a large excursion. Hue follows shortest signed angular differences, so a full color-wheel traversal with matching endpoints collapses under this model, and half-turn ties need explicit convention. Low-chroma hue needs weighting or stabilization. The returned parameters discard the easing-fit SSE, and independent normalized-channel errors are not a perceptual RGB reconstruction metric. RFF should keep the source ramp, preview approximation error and let the user retain channel curves or stops when a simple sweep cannot represent the input. This is an optional conversion, not a lossless palette format.

The easing set includes Back curves with deliberate overshoot, contradicting a broad opening statement that every curve maps the unit interval into itself. Define whether lightness/chroma excursions are clamped or gamut-mapped, and evaluate that final behavior during fitting. Preserve stable easing identities if saved data uses indices; the source explicitly requires append-only ordering. Penner/easings.net naming and distinctive Back constants are provenance leads, not proof of a verified reuse license. Check original sources and NOTICE requirements before adapting them.

The tri-state fitting preference stores auto/on/off and resolves auto against the current device flag at fit time. Separating an automatic policy from an explicit override is useful, but the preference file's assertion that both placement methods hold the same eps guarantee conflicts with the inspected fitter's metric distinction. Its performance claims also differ from later comments in CurveFitting.ts. Neither set is a current RFF benchmark. Choose a measured interactive policy and keep quality guarantees independent of device defaults; avoid silently changing an existing saved palette merely because the preference changed.

## A narrow integration boundary for ramp-to-stop conversion

Full reads of [gradientStopFitter.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/gradientStopFitter.ts) and [createSingleSlot.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/createSingleSlot.ts) show a small dependency boundary: the host registers a conversion callback, while the generic editor reads it without importing the palette implementation. The callback contract preserves colorSpace and returns a stop gradient; these two files do not prove the fitter's numerical fidelity or the editor's undo behavior. The underlying stopFit implementation remains separately pending.

The slot preserves reference identity between replacements, skips Object.is-equal writes and notifies subscribers synchronously. It is last-writer-wins, with no owner-checked unregister token. For a modular RFF editor, this pattern can isolate optional conversion services, but service replacement, teardown and one-action undo should have explicit ownership. Do not mistake registering a callback for validation of its color-space conversion or saved-format compatibility.

No palette reconstruction test, GPU readback experiment, UI screenshot audit or benchmark was performed in this batch. These recommendations concern RFF improvements informed by GMT's mechanisms and limitations, with direct 2D applicability.

## Palette stop fitting: evaluate the displayed result and preserve an exact sample alternative

Full reads of [stopFit.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/stopFit.ts), [reduceStops.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/reduceStops.ts), [gmtGradient.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/gmtGradient.ts) and [gradientRamp.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/gradientRamp.ts) resolve the previously deferred conversion layer. The practical RFF proposal is an explicit, reversible 'make editable / reduce control points' operation for imported or generated palettes, retaining the original sample data when a compact representation is inadequate. This is directly applicable to 2D and supports the image-derived palette workflow.

**Measure through the same interpolation implementation.** gmtGradient is a re-export of the canonical color utility, avoiding a separate fitter-only sampler. stopFit seeds endpoints, optional existing stop positions/interpolation/bias, flat bands and strong corners, then repeatedly evaluates the rendered ramp in the selected blend space. It attempts coarse/fine bias and linear/smooth interpolation trials on the worst segment before adding a new stop. RFF should fit against its actual palette renderer, including transfer functions, hue conventions, quantization and interpolation settings. A fit in another color space can produce a similar current ramp but changes subsequent editing behavior; preserve the original space by default and make any alternative an explicit choice.

**Identify bands relative to quantization.** Plateau detection compares rounded RGB byte values, not arbitrary floating-point equality. It uses run length, coverage and an edge-specific floor: take the edge's RGB direction, scale its largest component to one byte level, and measure the resulting OKLab difference. This helps distinguish dark quantization steps from intended bands more appropriately than one global color-difference threshold. It remains a heuristic for an 8-bit sRGB ramp, not a general classifier for HDR or floating-point palettes. The current default run length is four despite an older header mentioning three. Corner detection distinguishes isolated jumps from sustained steep transitions; over-budget corner sampling includes a color-diversity correction to avoid selecting only one phase of an alternating pattern. RFF should validate those mechanisms on its own palette corpus rather than reuse reported source benchmarks as proof.

**Boundary conventions are part of fidelity.** GMT holds a Step segment through its right boundary, so inserted boundaries are shifted by half a texel to reproduce the discrete samples without cumulative edge drift. Do not copy that shift into RFF until its endpoint/texel-center conventions are established. Existing seeds are deduplicated by rounded sample index, and their colors are reconstructed from the ramp rather than retained as original authored colors; multiple stops within one sample interval cannot all survive that representation. Retain high-resolution originals and intentional discontinuities when supporting repeated edits. These functions fit the finite 0..1 strip and do not independently enforce a periodic end-to-start seam; RFF cyclic palettes require seam-aware evaluation and explicit repeat-edge tests.

**The direct fitter has a budget, not a universal error certificate.** Refinement skips sample indices marked used, stops at a stop-count cap or a 512-iteration guard, and returns only a config. A result can therefore exceed targetDE, including at stop/step-boundary samples. Input length is checked, but finite channel values, tolerances and sensible budgets also need validation; two endpoint stops are created even if maxStops is below two. RFF should return achieved maximum/mean error, unresolved regions and budget exhaustion separately from the requested tolerance. Do not label the conversion lossless or guaranteed merely because it terminated.

**Keep sample form when editability costs too much.** rampToGradientConfig tries one stop beyond the effective limit (default maxStops 32, further bounded by cap 48). It retains stop form only within the count limit and with at most four texels whose error exceeds max(0.05,2.5*targetDE). This is a relaxed display-oriented policy, not 'every texel within targetDE'; the four accepted misses have no further magnitude bound here. Otherwise it keeps a 256-texel RGB ramp. Exactness applies to byte samples, not arbitrary floats: encoding rounds/clamps channels to bytes. RFF can adopt the choice of representations while defining an honest quality contract and retaining its existing higher-precision palette capabilities. This should not change genPalette RNG/order or reinterpret existing recipe IDs.

## Stop reduction as a progressive, measured editing operation

reduceStops offers a candidate at each smaller stop count, built from greedy removal, fresh fits, and insertion into lower-count candidates. Removal evaluates the merged segment with local context and retunes bias/interpolation; full-ramp scoring measures each retained candidate. Named amounts choose the fewest candidate stops meeting a maximum sampled color-difference threshold, while a manually selected count promises only that count and its measured result. NaN scores become Infinity in the main scoring path. This distinction between a requested size and an achieved quality is useful for RFF.

The optional blend search tries other spaces, selects one alternative based on improvement across counts and uses it where its error is below 80% of the own-space error. This reduces mode switching while exploring better representations. It is heuristic, not a global optimum: removal does not move retained stops, bias searches are grids, only a few refit tolerances are tried, and later refits with the same resulting count are skipped even if their locations differ. Stop insertion tests finitely many sample positions and byte-quantized colors. The 'axis repair' replaces a worse higher-count candidate only if a trial improves it; it does not mechanically guarantee error falls below the lower-count result. Its monotonicity claim is a reported corpus result, not a universal theorem. RFF should measure the finished count/error curve and handle any remaining nonmonotonic choices explicitly.

The generator yields partial plans between stages and work units. Its nominal 12 ms slice is cooperative: a whole fit, removal search or snapshot repair can exceed it before reaching a yield. RFF can provide an immediate preview followed by refinements, but should run expensive preparation off the UI thread or bound individual work units, attach results to the source palette revision, and make cancellation discard stale work. Results preserve config colorSpace and remove a stale ramp; elimination preserves surviving IDs/positions/colors but may change interpolation and bias. Undo must include all those changes. The error is measured at 256 displayed samples; zoomed strips, subtexel stops, cyclic sampling and a higher-resolution shader palette need additional validation.

## Ramp storage and ownership boundaries

The ramp codec stores exactly 768 RGB bytes as 1,024 base64 characters, with length/alphabet checks and a decoded-length check. Stops take precedence when both forms are present; normalization removes stale ramp data but deliberately does not validate stop contents. makeRampGradient accepts an existing string without validating it, and the buffer encoder assumes a meaningful RGB/RGBA stride. RFF should validate at import boundaries and keep representation normalization distinct from full schema validation.

Decoded bytes are cached in a 512-entry insertion-order cache and returned by reference. This is FIFO-style eviction, not access-refreshing LRU, and read-only use is a convention rather than type-enforced immutability. Return immutable data or explicit copies where callers might edit. Nonfinite RGB inputs can become byte zero through typed-array conversion, so do not treat encode/decode round-trip success as input validation. Base64 is a serialization choice suitable for GMT's JSON boundaries, not a required RFF on-disk format; any native integration must follow RFF's documented append-only/versioned persistence rules.

No palette-fit harness, renderer comparison, reduction timing or persistence round-trip test was executed here. Reported source experiments were read as documentation only. No third-party implementation was copied, and original-source licensing/provenance remains a prerequisite to adaptation.

## Preserve palette transform order and unclipped authoring data

Full inspection of [generatorPipeline.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/generatorPipeline.ts) completes the file previously read only around decomposition. It supplies a concrete RFF authoring proposal: combine lightness, chroma and hue from two palettes independently, optionally replace channels with editable curves, and retain the unclipped result alongside the display ramp. This is directly useful for 2D fractal coloring; it does not require a 3D field or orbit changes.

The actual order is source reversal and coordinate remapping, source contrast/chroma/hue adjustments, per-channel mixing, a base snapshot, optional channel replacement, global reversal, global scale/phase/mirror/posterization, global channel adjustments, output-indexed noise, and RGB reconstruction. Preserve this order as part of any saved recipe. The returned base precedes curve overrides, while final stores post-global channels before lightness/chroma clipping. Rebuilding editable curves from already clipped RGB would lose recoverable excursions and alter subsequent edits. This supports a non-destructive RFF design, but new generators must use new stable recipe identities without changing existing RNG/order.

**Hue is not an ordinary scalar.** Mixing uses a weighted circular mean, not constant-angular-speed interpolation. Opposite hues at equal weight approach a zero-length vector, so the resulting angle is ill-conditioned; gray/low-chroma hues need a separate policy. Lightness/chroma mix factors can extrapolate, whereas hue mixing clamps by selecting an endpoint outside [0,1]. The unwrap helper chooses local shortest differences and assumes finite nonempty inputs; it cannot infer intentional multiple revolutions from sparse samples. Define those semantics before animating independent palette channels.

**Coordinate remapping is not filtering.** Both source and global remapping choose the nearest of 256 samples. Global scale supports fractions down to 0.1, but per-slot repeat merely clamps to at least one without integer rounding, despite a header calling it integer-only. At the exact identity mapping the final endpoint is preserved; entering any remap branch wraps it with fract, potentially producing a visible endpoint change for a noncyclic source. Mirroring is a triangular coordinate wave, and posterization samples band centers. For RFF, distinguish clamped strips from periodic palettes, define endpoint behavior and filter the transformed coordinate footprint instead of relying on a 256-entry nearest lookup. Large repeat counts, phase animation and small bands can alias independently of palette fitting quality.

**Noise ownership affects the picture.** Three deterministic streams use related integer seeds, then linearly resample their arrays. Noise is applied using the output sample index after palette coordinate remapping, so it does not travel with a source palette when phase changes. Its resample frequency is rounded and bounded below by two but not above the 256-element backing array; callers must enforce the valid finite range. Seed zero aliases seed one in seededNoise. RFF should choose whether noise follows palette coordinates or output coordinates, specify seed/version semantics and validate bounds. The current random endpoints do not enforce periodic noise continuity. None of this authoring noise substitutes for final-output dithering or screen-space antialiasing.

The separate ColorBox builder sweeps L/C/h with independent easings and a shortest hue path. It uses chroma-reducing gamut mapping, whereas the mix builder calls the ordinary RGB conversion; matching parameters across the modes does not imply matching gamut treatment. ColorBox floors negative chroma before storing final channels, so its 'unclipped' output is not identical in scope to the mixed builder's raw final channels. RFF should declare a consistent authoring/display conversion contract and preserve source values wherever reversible editing requires them. The box smoother averages a truncated neighborhood at the ends and uses 2*floor(width/2)+1 samples for an even width; it neither wraps a cyclic palette nor handles hue circularly by itself.

## Palette previews as fields, with explicit sampling and dithering

A full read of [rampGeometry.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/rampGeometry.ts), including an overlapping recovery of the initially truncated middle, reveals a useful separation between a scalar palette-coordinate field, coverage and color lookup. Linear, radial and conic previews reuse one palette without modifying its stored data. RFF could use such previews to reveal banding, cyclic seams and color progression before applying a palette to the current fractal, or reuse the fields as explicitly decorative material masks.

Linear projection and radial/conic coordinates account for aspect ratio using isotropic units. The radial law can modulate its outer reach by a sine of angle; integer lobe counts close the angular seam, whereas fractional counts need an explicit discontinuity policy. Amplitudes that make the reach nonpositive fall onto a small positive clamp, introducing sharp behavior. The conic mapping supports separate rise/fall easing and a radius-dependent twist proportional to log(1+r). This is a regularized spiral law, not an exactly scale-invariant logarithmic spiral down to the origin. Domain validation, center singularities, angular seams and footprint filtering remain necessary for a shader adaptation. Coverage is one everywhere in the shipped CPU fields; merely storing a coverage channel does not mean geometric antialiasing has been implemented. The 'fractal' selector is a placeholder here and is rendered by another component.

**Two output paths have materially different quality.** renderGeometry rounds the palette lookup to a sample index. renderFieldDithered instead linearly interpolates the ramp, blends coverage with the background and optionally applies serpentine Floyd–Steinberg diffusion before writing eight-bit RGB. The latter carries quantization error to the next horizontal pixel and three pixels of the next row using two row buffers. Flattening RGB objects into a numeric lookup table avoids repeated property access; source timings were not independently measured. The implementation operates on display RGB values, so it should not be transplanted into RFF's scene-linear lighting stage.

Error diffusion has sequential dependencies, boundary error loss and clipping effects; its comments' exact local-average language is stronger than a universal guarantee. It can be useful as an optional still-export quantizer but is not a drop-in parallel fragment shader. Independent tiles need shared diffusion state or a documented alternative, and changing frames can produce unstable spatial patterns. RFF should compare its existing dithering against a proposed alternative on smooth dark ramps, flat colors, animations and tiled exports before adding another method. This remains distinct from the higher-priority footprint filtering that prevents undersampled palette detail.

The module includes named Mulberry32, Quilez gain and Floyd–Steinberg mechanisms. Their implementations and constants need original-source/license verification and NOTICE attribution before reuse. Parameter-default compatibility comments also document a historical exception for spline defaults; do not infer universal compatibility from one default-value test list. No source code was copied, no preview was rendered and no numerical, GPU or performance test was executed in this batch.

## Palette editing operations and persistence: verify the intended picture, not only stop positions

A full read of [stopOps.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/stopOps.ts) identifies reusable interaction primitives for RFF: move a selection, distribute it within its current extent, scale it around either endpoint, duplicate the palette, and adjust a segment's bias. The helpers return transformed data without store or rendering dependencies, enabling one undo transaction per completed gesture and reuse across editor hosts. These are directly applicable to 2D palette authoring.

**Separate position reversal from visual reversal.** invert mirrors stop positions and reverses the array, but retains each stop's outgoing bias/interpolation metadata on that stop. For asymmetric interpolation or Step segments this need not produce the old rendered palette sampled at 1-t. Signed scaling can similarly reverse selected stops without transferring segment ownership. RFF should specify whether the command reverses control-point positions or the actual color function, and implement/test the latter using its own endpoint and interpolation conventions. This is an adoption requirement, not a verified RFF defect.

Move clamps each selected position independently, so dragging beyond an endpoint can collapse spacing rather than stop the group as a rigid selection. Scale also clamps individual positions, accepts a negative factor for inversion and leaves array sorting to the caller. Distribute sorts the selected entries to compute positions but returns them in the original array order. Duplicate preserves original IDs and generates collision-checked deterministic duplicate IDs, while allowing coincident stops at the half-way join. Define stable tie ordering, coincident-stop semantics and selection behavior in RFF; these details affect sharp palette boundaries. A baseline snapshot should drive each gesture update rather than repeatedly transforming an already changed selection.

Bias belongs to the left stop's outgoing segment and its drag delta is divided by segment width; degenerate intervals are left unchanged. The helpers' small-width cutoffs are editor conventions, not general rendering precision limits. Deletion leaves minimum-count enforcement to the caller. Contrary to the module-wide comment that every operation returns a new array, several no-op branches return the original array. Consumers should use documented change semantics and avoid treating reference identity as evidence of a particular operation's completion.

Paste normalization accepts a stop array or stops wrapper, normalizes three/six-digit hex colors and clamps finite converted positions/biases. It permits duplicate supplied IDs, preserves input order and can retain a single stop; Number coercion also accepts some nonnumeric source types such as null or numeric strings. It extracts only stops, losing wrapper-level blend/color-space information. For RFF, distinguish 'paste stops into the current palette' from importing an entire palette, validate unique identities and supported interpolation values, and report rejected entries rather than silently implying complete import fidelity. Public pure transforms assume valid finite numeric inputs; they are not import validators themselves.

## Documentation cross-check: samples, editable stops and preview-before-apply

Full reads of [ADR-0122](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/adr/0122-the-ramp-is-the-gradient.md) and [ADR-0128](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/adr/0128-reduce-stops-is-a-stop-count-axis.md) confirm that GMT intentionally treats dense samples as a valid palette form and stops as an optional editing representation. The documentation explicitly records the relaxed four-missed-texel fit policy, old-client compatibility tradeoffs, representation-dependent identity and a preview/apply reduction workflow. Those choices explain the inspected code; they do not establish equivalent requirements for RFF.

For RFF, preserve authored recipe identity separately from a render cache or fitted approximation. A cache rebuilt after a shader/color-space change should not silently redefine deduplication, credits or the original palette. If sample and stop forms are introduced, all loaders, drag/drop paths, clipboard actions, previews and exporters must agree on their discriminator and precedence. GMT's use of an empty stop array prevents a particular older loader from deleting entries, but an old client may still display them incorrectly; that is partial compatibility, not full backward compatibility. RFF must follow its own versioned/append-only format rules instead of copying that workaround.

The reduction ADR distinguishes a fixed requested count from a named quality level: a count stays fixed as better candidates arrive, while a quality preset may move to a lower count. It also requires one undo action for both the selected stops and any blend-mode change. This is a useful RFF interaction model, with an explicit changed-mode readout and source-revision checks before applying asynchronous results. The ADR reports indivisible fitting work as long as 129 ms, reinforcing that cooperative yields alone are not a frame-time guarantee. Its universal monotonic-quality wording remains subject to the implementation limits described in the preceding code analysis. No timings, UI behavior or source-reported test results were independently reproduced in this batch.

## Palette import and document boundaries: preserve meaning as well as usable data

Full reads of [editorConfig.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/editorConfig.ts), [gradientDocument.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/gradientDocument.ts) and [gradientFile.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/gradientFile.ts) add persistence requirements to the proposed RFF palette workflow. A common validated document representation can serve clipboard, library import, undo and export while keeping names, interpolation, color-space metadata and provenance attached. This is a direct 2D improvement opportunity; it is independent of the 3D shader renderer.

**Repair identities without silently redefining color.** editorConfig reuses the stop validator and then ensures unique nonempty IDs. Its sequential ID repair checks only IDs already encountered: an earlier replacement can take the name of a later otherwise valid stop, causing that later stop to be renamed too. This is acceptable only when external references are absent or repaired consistently. RFF should reserve existing valid identities before generating replacements where selection/history references depend on them. The envelope permits explicit ramp form and at least two valid stops, retaining retired hsv-far as a loadable blend mode. Unknown color/blend-space values silently default to srgb/oklab. For RFF, distinguish a genuinely omitted legacy default from an unknown newer mode; report or preserve unsupported semantics rather than unexpectedly recoloring an imported palette.

The shared validator can discard malformed individual stops while still returning a usable gradient. Its 'never throws' comment is not an arbitrary-JavaScript-object guarantee because coercion and property access can throw; the higher-level document reader wraps its decoding branch in a catch. For ordinary parsed JSON, the practical issue is reporting data loss. applyEditorChange preserves envelope settings for a bare stop-array edit, including any stale ramp until normalization; do not send such an intermediate dual-form object to persistence without the canonical boundary. Snapshot serialization deep-copies through JSON after normalization, assuming validated serializable data rather than validating it anew.

**Make strict and lenient import policies visible.** The document decoder rejects unsupported explicit document versions, handles a BOM on JSON text, recognizes legacy collections and routes a session envelope separately. Bare configurations require every input stop to survive validation. Collection/document entries are more lenient and may retain a single well-formed stop; they can also lose malformed stops without increasing the skipped-entry count if the remaining gradient is accepted. RFF should report both skipped palettes and repaired/discarded stops, with an explicit choice of strict import versus recovery. A successful 'all stops kept' check still permits clamping, ID replacement and unknown-mode fallback, so it is not proof of exact reproduction.

The entry reader bounds collections at 50,000 entries and truncates names/source strings, while the encoder accepts unbounded entry counts and does not apply the same name/source limits. Exact round-trip claims therefore apply only to the valid bounded domain, not all encoder inputs. Limits after JSON parsing do not bound input byte size or stops per entry. RFF should align writer/reader limits, validate before allocation, and preserve the original file when recovery is partial. Group keys reject prototype-related names; this is useful boundary discipline, but metadata bounds and the separately delegated global/origin readers still require their own coverage.

**Separate a palette file from its display preview.** buildGradientFile chooses PNG or JSON around the same versioned payload and keeps download side effects outside the pure builder. The PNG encoding and its metadata extraction are not established by this wrapper and remain a separate inspection target. For RFF, a viewable palette image with embedded editable data is a plausible sharing feature, provided import distinguishes embedded authored data from pixel extraction and preserves its provenance. Implement any compatible format independently and verify the relevant format specifications before implementation.

Filename construction retains Unicode, spaces and case, strips common forbidden characters and truncates by code point. That is more informative than replacing an entire name with an ASCII slug, but it does not handle every native Windows filename condition: reserved device basenames and trailing periods need separate treatment for RFF's desktop saves. The embedded title should remain authoritative even when the filesystem name must change. Single-gradient and set exports derive useful default titles without changing palette data.

No import round-trip, malformed-input test, native file-save test or PNG inspection was performed in this batch. No RFF application or saved-format code was modified.

## A viewable palette file with recoverable pixels

Full reads of [gradientPng.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/gradientPng.ts) and [pngCodec.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/pngCodec.ts) complete the PNG mechanism deferred above. For RFF, an optional palette-sharing image could carry both a recognizable preview and an editable, versioned payload. The useful distinction is between exact authored-data import and recovery of sampled display colors when metadata is absent; this is a 2D workflow feature, not a shader-speed optimization.

**Two layers preserve different things.** The writer embeds the gradient document in compressed iTXt and paints 256 rounded/clamped display RGB samples as uniform column blocks. A single palette width is a multiple of 256 from 256 through 4096; a set uses width 1024 and repeated identical rows per palette. Pixel bands cover at most 2,048 palettes while metadata can carry more. The reader prefers valid nonempty metadata, then recognizes scene keywords, then tries the band layout. RFF should expose whether an import retained names, stops, interpolation, grouping and provenance or recovered only display samples. A resized, color-transformed or recompressed-through-lossy image does not meet the exact pixel-recovery contract.

Band recovery validates repeated rows, uniform column blocks and opacity, and tries the fewest bands first. Identical adjacent palette bands can collapse into one without metadata. At widths other than 1024 it only considers a single palette; matching flat images may legitimately be accepted. Recovery checks decoded pixel count before allocation, but that does not limit metadata decoding, which occurs first. Empty-document PNGs do not return an empty document through this reader because metadata is accepted only when it contains gradients; the intentionally non-band-shaped black placeholder then falls through. A RFF design should treat an explicitly valid empty collection separately from corrupt metadata.

**Do not downgrade unsupported data silently.** A newer/unreadable metadata version falls back to displayed colors. That can be useful recovery, but it loses editability and must not look like a faithful load of the original document. Retain the source file and name the recovery mode. Likewise, scene detection here is based on a text keyword's presence, not validation of the scene body. The metadata and pixel payload are not cross-checked for visual agreement; embedded data wins even if a third-party tool changed only the image. RFF should define that precedence and optionally show a mismatch rather than assume both representations remain synchronized.

**Color bytes and displayed color are separate contracts.** The writer emits no color-profile/gamma chunks. That preserves its own raw pixel bytes, but absence of metadata does not establish identical appearance across color-managed viewers. Conversely, the band reader does not interpret such chunks in externally modified PNGs before tagging recovered bytes as sRGB. For RFF, define the display color space and profile policy explicitly, while keeping exact palette payload values independent from the thumbnail. The maximum painted set is about 48 MiB of RGB before intermediate encoding buffers; use bounded/streamed export where large libraries would otherwise stall the UI.

## Codec scope and resource limits for any RFF adoption

The codec supports noninterlaced eight-bit RGB/RGBA, all five row filters and concatenated IDAT data. Other PNG representations are refused by this decoder. An indexed PNG can preserve the same palette pixels yet fail this recognition path; unsupported representation is not proof that its colors were lost. RFF can use a mature existing image decoder for general import and reserve strict strip recognition for pixel patterns after decoding. No external PNG specification or library behavior was verified in this batch, so this is not a standards-conformance assessment.

Chunk reading retains a valid prefix when a later chunk is truncated, does not verify CRCs and does not require IEND. Header reading does not validate the compression/filter-method bytes. The image path bounds its expected decompressed buffer, but the source itself notes that oversized inflate output is ignored; short-stream detection depends on the behavior of the supplied-buffer decompressor and is not demonstrated by this read. Text inflation allocates first and checks a 64 MiB limit afterward. readPngText decodes every text chunk before selecting its keyword, so unrelated compressed text also consumes resources. RFF should select the requested keyword before inflation, enforce cumulative compressed/decompressed limits during decoding and report corrupt versus unsupported data distinctly.

The text reader accepts iTXt/tEXt/zTXt with limited validation of compression flags/methods; tEXt is decoded using UTF-8 to mirror an older local path. The encoder checks pixel-buffer length and keyword syntax but relies on typed callers for valid dimensions, channels and filter values. These helper assumptions must not be promoted into a blanket claim that arbitrary inputs are validated. stripPngText rebuilds chunks with newly calculated CRCs, so successful rewriting is not evidence that the original file passed integrity checks.

The strongest RFF reuse is the product design and separation of preview/payload/recovery, not copying this small codec wholesale. Preserve RFF's native format contracts, independently implement any desired compatibility and verify source/license attribution before adaptation. No PNG round-trip, corrupt-file corpus, memory measurement or viewer comparison was executed here; only source inspection and report/coverage updates were performed.

## Separate source lineage, content identity and catalogue publication

Full reads of [catalogOrigin.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/catalogOrigin.ts), [catalogPacks.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/catalogPacks.ts) and [catalogSigs.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/catalogSigs.ts) reveal three distinct mechanisms: showing source credit, deciding which packs are available, and detecting catalogue duplicates. RFF can benefit from explicit source metadata for imported palettes and an intentional library-loading policy, but should not conflate these mechanisms or inherit GMT's publication decisions.

**Keep lineage through edits.** CatalogOrigin stamps a ref, short credit and content key at selection time. Export appends that credit only while the current key matches; an edit normally removes the visible suffix. RFF's project instructions require provenance to remain synchronized with NOTICE when adapting third-party material. For RFF, retain source identity, known source/license references and modification history independently of the current-content comparison. A changed palette can be labeled modified without deleting its origin. This is a project-specific provenance design recommendation, not a determination of any pack's legal status. The actual licenses and redistribution conditions of the named collections were not externally verified here.

**The 'unmodified' key is approximate and incomplete.** Stop positions are quantized to 1/10000 and bias to 1/1000, while colorSpace is omitted for both stop and ramp forms. Tiny edits can retain the key and a change of output transform can retain credit despite changing displayed output. Equivalent colors with different string spellings, stop order or implicit defaults can differ in key. Thus the function tests its chosen serialization semantics, not exact equality of all editable or rendered state. For RFF, separately define authored identity, rendered-cache identity and approximate visual similarity; use each only for its intended purpose. coerceOrigin bounds the credit to 80 characters but does not bound ref/key or verify the claimed source. Imported metadata is a claim to retain and inspect, not authenticated authorship.

entryOrigin omits origins for userMade bundles. That flag describes a catalogue category and is not independent evidence that its entries have no upstream source. RFF should allow user-created derivatives to retain lineage. Display formatting can stay concise while structured metadata carries fuller provenance; putting all information in a filename suffix is insufficient for reliable round trips.

**Pack availability is configuration, not source permission.** PACK_PUBLISH distinguishes built-in repository data, CDN data, explicitly enabled optional packs and unpublished data. PACK_BUNDLES gives ordered source membership. The file explicitly separates publication location from licensing. The table alone does not prove that loading, baking, upload manifests or deletion of old published copies enforce it; those consumers require separate inspection. RFF can separate bundled palettes from optional user-selected libraries, with clear source metadata, without automatically adopting any named GMT pack or changing network state during this audit.

## Catalogue signatures are purpose-specific duplicate hints

Stop signatures round positions to 1/1000, normalize hex, sort by position and reduce interpolation to Step versus everything else. They omit bias, blend space and colorSpace. Ramp signatures include byte samples but omit the output transform. These are deliberately coarse server-facing canonical forms, not faithful complete-palette fingerprints: visually distinct configurations can match, and visually equivalent stop/ramp representations can differ. The hash uses two multiply/xorshift lanes with constants described as derived from a named mixer; it is not an integrity or authentication mechanism. RFF should use exact canonical data comparison where collisions or coarse equivalence would discard user work, and reserve visual deduplication for a reviewable suggestion.

The signature-list parser checks the version and divisibility of string length by 16, but not hexadecimal characters, declared count, algorithm, sortedness or a maximum size. Its loader caches a successful nonempty set globally without including base URL in the cache key; failures become empty sets and retry later. Empty therefore conflates no matches with unavailable/malformed data at this interface. The source says a server repeats the check, but this client read does not verify server enforcement. For RFF, represent loading/error/ready states separately and scope caches by source and version. Do not let an unavailable optional catalogue check silently authorize a destructive deduplication action.

The comments acknowledge a mirrored client/server canonicalizer and possible cross-runtime rounding differences. A future RFF interoperability feature should version its canonicalization and keep representative golden fixtures across implementations, including ramps, tiny position/bias edits, equal-position stops and output-space changes. A source comment stating parity is not test evidence from this audit. Verify original provenance/license before adapting the distinctive hash implementation and record it in NOTICE if used.

No catalogue was fetched, no contribution/publication was performed, and no licensing conclusion or cross-runtime test was made. These reads add library/provenance requirements for RFF's 2D palette workflow without changing the shader-effect priority ranking.

## Loading large palette libraries without confusing availability, validity and identity

A full read of [catalogLoader.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/catalogLoader.ts) establishes the consumer of the pack table inspected above. RFF could offer a small bundled library plus explicitly selected optional libraries, caching successfully decoded palettes so toggling a source does not repeat I/O. This is a 2D library-management improvement; no remote catalogue was fetched during this inspection.

The registered group list is derived from publication flags, and a separate replace-by-ID registry supports live sources. Baked loading fetches compressed metadata and ramp bytes concurrently from the same base, trying the configured mirror before a local fallback for non-core groups. Sub-filtered RGB rows are reconstructed with modulo-byte cumulative sums into opaque RGBA. This is a compact distribution design, but RFF should evaluate it against its existing asset system rather than add another codec automatically.

**Validate a pack before making it visible.** The loader casts parsed metadata to its expected type, then uses stride and entries without checking count/stride/payload-length consistency. Truncated ramp data can feed undefined values into integer arithmetic and typed-array writes, producing incorrect colors rather than a deliberate rejection. Format version is used for manifest merging, not a supported-version gate. Decompression and entry allocation are unbounded here. RFF should validate the schema, supported version, exact byte layout and bounded expanded size, then decode into temporary storage and commit the catalogue plus labels/counts together. This also avoids the current ordering in which manifest/collection state changes before all entries are reconstructed successfully.

**Fallback should distinguish missing, corrupt and unsupported sources.** The retry loop covers HTTP/network failures, while gzip/JSON/entry decoding happens after the selected base is accepted. A fetched but corrupt pack therefore does not try the local fallback. Define whether RFF should fall back in that situation, show the chosen revision and retain a useful diagnostic. Binary and JSON assets should share a content revision or manifest digest; two successful downloads do not alone prove they belong to the same bake.

The successful cache is keyed only by group ID, so changing a mirror or passing another explicit base does not refresh an already cached group. Concurrent first loads are not coalesced by an in-flight promise. There is no cancellation/unload method here, and returned entries/manifests are mutable references. RFF should scope caches by source/revision, coalesce duplicate requests, make publication generation-aware and separate 'hidden from the browser' from 'evicted from memory'. A valid empty live library should be distinguishable from a failed request rather than permanently disabling its toggle.

**A format version is not a data revision.** mergeManifest prevents an older format from overwriting known newer-format labels/counts, but same-version files merge in arrival order, and collections merge without that version comparison. Even the newer-format branch retains old bundle labels absent from its incoming table. RFF should decide whether an incoming manifest is a complete replacement or a patch and use explicit revision semantics for both. The default registry hides unpublished groups, but loadGroup itself accepts any string and falls back to local addressing for unknown IDs; the broad comment that nothing can request an unregistered group is stronger than this helper enforces. Validate requested IDs at the relevant public boundary.

Finally, rampToCssGradient samples only 25 points by default. Such a preview can miss narrow bands or alias periodic patterns and is not a faithful basis for judging a dense palette. RFF should render library thumbnails with the actual palette sampling path or label coarse previews as approximate. Source license labels remain metadata claims, not verified permissions. No network, malformed-pack, concurrency, rendering or performance test was performed in this batch.

## Search palettes by descriptive features, without mistaking them for rendering quality
