Full reads of [facets.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/facets.ts) and [facetName.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/facetName.ts) establish a directly transferable RFF library feature: filter palettes by average lightness, chroma, fine variation and hue spread, and suggest descriptive names for unnamed imports. These metrics help navigation; they do not rank artistic merit, legibility on a particular fractal or shader image quality.

The extractor converts samples to OKLab. It averages L and chroma, measures fine variation as the mean magnitude of the residual after a width-nine box average in L/a/b, and estimates hue spread with a 36-bin chroma-weighted wheel. Samples below chroma 0.04 do not contribute to hue statistics; occupied bins exceed 5% of the peak weight. Spread is 360 degrees minus the largest circular gap. A separate hue-order statistic counts the dominant direction of distinct hue-bin transitions. The so-called dominant hue is a circular mean, not the histogram's most populated hue. For RFF, label these quantities accurately and retain raw values alongside display-normalized controls.

**Sampling and domain matter.** Complexity depends on sample density and the fixed nine-sample window; it is not an intrinsic count of bands or screen-space aliasing risk. The box average truncates and renormalizes its support at the strip ends despite being described as edge-clamped, and does not wrap a cyclic palette. Repeating/reversing a palette, changing its sample resolution or crossing a repeat seam can affect metrics independently of its usefulness. RFF should choose a fixed analysis resolution/domain and a cyclic policy, then separately evaluate visibility against the actual fractal field distribution when offering scene-specific recommendations. This connects to the earlier histogram-assisted palette mapping proposal without replacing it.

Hue spread is quantized in ten-degree bins and even one occupied bin contributes ten degrees. A circular mean becomes unreliable for balanced opposite colors; when no samples pass the hue floor, the current implementation returns angle zero. passesFilters checks positive mean chroma rather than the validity of that hue statistic, so a very low-chroma palette can pass an active red-angle window despite having no accepted hue samples. It also uses a plain inclusive interval and cannot represent a wrapped hue range in one pair. RFF should carry a hue-validity/concentration value and support circular intervals. Empty/nonfinite input should be rejected or given an explicit unavailable state instead of letting NaN enter metrics and filters.

The warmth proxy uses only mean OKLab a. That axis is a particular opponent-color direction, not a complete perceptual warm/cool model; retain it as a documented heuristic or calibrate a more suitable descriptor before exposing strong semantic labels. Normalization constants for chroma, fine variation and warmth are tuned to GMT's catalogue and clip at the extremes. They are not universal physical units or verified thresholds for RFF's palettes.

Automatic names combine optional Dark/Bright, Warm/Cool, Muted/Soft/Vivid and Rainbow words. Neutral is a fallback only when no word applies, despite an opening comment suggesting it always fills the warmth slot. Complexity and hue order do not contribute to names, and many distinct palettes naturally get the same label. RFF should treat this as an editable suggestion, preserve an existing authored name, and use a separate stable ID for identity. configToName renders using the config's own output-space path; before analyzing those values as RGB, establish that the metric's input encoding matches that path. Names derived from a different color encoding should not silently change on save/load.

No classifier corpus, perceptual study, rendering comparison or timing test was run. The concrete proposal is optional feature-based library search and naming for 2D RFF, with explicit descriptor limits; it does not change the current shader priorities.

## Color-space-aware curve authoring without changing the shader contract

A full read of [curveSpaces.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/curveSpaces.ts) adds a concrete extension to RFF's palette-editing possibilities: expose different authoring axes while converting their sampled output to one established pipeline representation. GMT keeps its downstream L/C/h channels and lets the editor use polar OKLCh, rectangular OKLab, RGB, CIE LCh or HSV. Spectral blending is deliberately excluded because a mixing model does not automatically define three editable scalar axes. This mechanism transfers directly to 2D coloring and need not enlarge every shader interface.

**Channel metadata should own units and capabilities.** Each axis declares a stable key, label, role, range, fitting tolerance and angular flag. CIE L*/C* use different keys and scales from OKLCh L/C; all hue curves use radians, while HSV conversion explicitly translates degrees and percent saturation/value at its boundary. A role lookup returns no lightness channel for RGB instead of arbitrarily choosing one. RFF can use this to disable inapplicable curve operations and avoid interpreting saved keys in the wrong units. HSV V is assigned the lightness role for operation routing, but it is not perceptual lightness; retain accurate labels and space-specific behavior.

Per-channel eps values are scaled to relevant axis ranges, which helps keep fitting effort comparable. Equal fractional tolerances are not equal perceived color errors, especially for hue at different chroma. The final reconstructed palette still needs the display-space validation described above. Plot ranges also are not automatic clamps: the polar and rectangular conversions permit values outside the displayed ranges. Keep authoring bounds, valid mathematical domains and final gamut handling separate.

**Switching axes can be lossy even before fitting.** The RGB, HSV and CIE paths go through gamut-mapped sRGB; they cannot preserve every out-of-gamut source value. Rectangular OKLab avoids that intermediate gamut restriction, but polar conversion can discard explicit hue winding, negative-chroma representation and hue at zero chroma even when the resulting color is equivalent. Re-fitting adds another approximation because a cubic in one space generally is not a cubic in another. RFF should preserve the original curves in undo, make conversion an explicit operation and distinguish a temporary alternate view from replacing the authored representation. Source comments report a two-byte-level in-gamut round-trip test; that test was not run here and does not establish losslessness.

Hue unwrapping follows successive shortest angular differences. It removes plotting cliffs at a normal wrap but cannot recover a deliberately undersampled full rotation or resolve unstable hue at near-zero chroma. The helper handles empty arrays, yet assumes finite angles and a positive finite period; infinite differences or a zero period can make its adjustment loops fail to terminate. Conversion helpers derive length from the first channel without validating the other two. RFF should validate equal lengths and finite values at the editor boundary and preserve explicitly authored turn counts rather than re-infer them on every conversion.

Unknown space IDs fall back to OKLCh for display. That can keep controls available but must not silently reinterpret persisted RGB/CIE tracks. Moreover, the lookup uses ordinary object indexing without an own-key check, so arbitrary inherited property names are outside the claimed safe fallback behavior. RFF should validate a closed set of identifiers and verify the stored channel-key triple before choosing any legacy default. The distinction between blend space and authoring space should remain explicit even if their labels share vocabulary.

No curve-space round-trip, gamut render or malformed-input test was performed in this batch. The result is a scoped RFF authoring proposal with conversion requirements, not a new top-priority shader effect or a claim that existing RFF color handling is deficient.

## One palette-transfer contract for multiple RFF destinations

Full reads of [favientDnd.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/favientDnd.ts), [favientTargets.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/favientTargets.ts), [sendTargetRegistry.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/sendTargetRegistry.ts) and [createListRegistry.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/createListRegistry.ts) describe a useful integration pattern for RFF: a single palette payload can be applied to a coloring layer, an editor input or a library entry through destinations that declare their capabilities. This is a direct 2D workflow improvement and could also serve the proposed editable environment gradient.

The drag payload includes the complete first palette, its name, optional source/origin and optional library IDs. Multi-selection adds IDs while retaining the single-palette top-level shape, preserving older consumers' behavior. That is suitable inside one live library, but IDs alone are not a portable snapshot across documents, sessions or processes. RFF should explicitly distinguish local reorder/move operations from palette-copy operations and attach a source document/revision when resolving a batch. A target supporting only one palette should communicate that scope rather than appear to apply the whole selection.

**Transport parsing and render validation serve different purposes.** The reader intentionally checks only a name and a config with a stops array, allowing an unreadable stored palette to reach organization or trash actions by ID. It strips stale ramp data on stop form, but does not validate colors, finite values, origin or batch IDs. This is an explicit organizational choice, not a ready-to-render validation guarantee. RFF should use separate validated operations: local item identity for moving/deleting an existing entry, and a fully validated palette plus provenance for applying or saving new content. A custom drag type or internal marker is not proof of trusted origin. The text fallback contains only the name, so it cannot recover the actual palette when custom transfer data is unavailable.

GMT separates payload capture from its custom drag avatar because browser drag-over events expose types rather than payload data. Copy/move effects permit both library organization and application to a target. The eagerly created transparent drag image is a browser-specific attempt to have a decoded image ready; it does not itself await decode success. RFF's native implementation can reuse the interaction distinction without reproducing DOM lifecycle machinery. Cleanup, cancelled drags and a failed application need explicit behavior so the visible selection and saved palette stay consistent.

**A destination registry can unify application and reveal behavior.** Each target declares a stable ID, label, host/mode grouping, optional applicability checks, application callback, reveal callback, parameter identity and optional live screen rectangle/reveal path. The registry itself does not execute transactions, validate payloads or guarantee that apply succeeds before reveal. RFF should keep one successful apply operation and one undo unit as the authoritative event; showing the destination should follow that event. Runtime payload validation remains necessary despite generic TypeScript declarations. The source header says the pure targetsForPayload selector currently has no production caller, so its tests alone cannot establish actual menu/drop filtering.

The underlying map preserves insertion order and caches a stable array between mutations. This avoids unnecessary view updates, but its unregister closure deletes by ID without checking that it still owns the registered item: an old owner can remove a newer replacement. Returned snapshots and entries are mutable references. A RFF registry should use owner tokens/generations for teardown and immutable/read-only snapshots where appropriate. The separate select-mode/studio capability slots are likewise last-writer-wins; keep them scoped to the owning editor or document instead of leaking one host's mode into another.

No drag interaction, UI screenshot, undo test or multi-document transfer was executed. The recommendation is shared, typed transfer semantics with explicit destination ownership, not a claim that RFF currently lacks or mishandles drag-and-drop.

## Export the sampled palette to external material tools, with a destination-specific color contract

Full reads of [dccExport.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/dccExport.ts), [blenderImport.py](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/dcc/blenderImport.py) and [c4dImport.py](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/dcc/c4dImport.py) describe optional interoperability for RFF: export its 2D palette as a reusable ramp in another application's material system. This transfers a color function, not RFF's fractal geometry, lighting or complete rendered appearance. The scripts' stated Blender/Cinema 4D test versions are source documentation; neither application nor current API compatibility was tested here.

**Resample the source interpolation before translation.** The exporter accepts 256 RGB samples and selected sample indices, emits byte sRGB colors and four-decimal normalized positions, and requests linear interpolation in the destination. Reusing only the original authored stop positions would discard source-specific interpolation between them. However, this wrapper does not choose or enforce the advertised 32-stop budget: indices arrive from its caller, whose reduction strategy still needs separate inspection. Source comments reporting Douglas-Peucker accuracy are not a guarantee for arbitrary ramps. RFF should measure the final destination reconstruction after color conversion and position rounding, and offer a texture/LUT alternative for dense bands that cannot fit an editable ramp budget.

**Scene-linear values are not display colors.** The Blender template applies the sRGB transfer function to RGB components unless the input is declared linear. It does not query arbitrary scene working primaries or view transforms. The Cinema 4D template instead asks the document's color converter in its OCIO branch and uses a legacy sRGB-to-linear transform otherwise. These are materially different contracts. RFF should declare source encoding and destination working space, and validate ramp values separately from a lit material rendered through a view transform. Matching input colors cannot by itself guarantee matching screenshots.

The generated Blender material uses UV X to drive the ramp and connects its color to a Principled base-color input; it neither assigns the material to an object nor connects alpha to opacity. Its reusable node-group alternative exposes factor, color and alpha. The C4D standard material owns a gradient shader, while the Redshift path creates a ramp and tries to connect it to a discovered material node. Missing/null connection targets can leave a created but unconnected ramp without an explicit failure result. Redshift availability is a plugin-presence check, not proof of compatible node/port APIs. RFF exports should describe precisely what was created and report an incomplete connection instead of treating material creation as appearance parity.

**Template behavior and generated behavior differ.** The standalone samples demonstrate alpha and non-linear interpolation, but the TypeScript payload emits opaque stops and explicitly linear interpolation. C4D's alpha-gradient branch does not mirror all color-knot interpolation settings, and its Redshift branch does not consume the alpha/brightness fields used by the standard gradient path. Do not advertise common support merely because fields exist in a sample dictionary. Validate finite ordered positions, nonempty stop lists and supported target capabilities before creating destination objects. Generated IDs/names are not an idempotent reimport strategy; repeated execution creates additional materials/groups.

The templates create host data progressively, without a whole-import preflight and rollback/undo transaction visible here. A malformed later entry can leave earlier creations in place. A RFF integration should prevalidate the complete payload and group successful changes into the destination's supported undo mechanism. Keep export itself separate from executing generated scripts; this audit did not run them or modify any external application.

The payload replacement checks for marker presence but not their ordering or uniqueness. The source templates are compiled into a generated TypeScript module, which remains a separate coverage item; reading the Python does not prove that shipped generated strings match it. RFF should retain a reproducible template-generation check and safe string serialization for Unicode names, quotes and line breaks. The serializer uses JSON string syntax for a Python string literal; validate the accepted text domain rather than generalizing that JSON and Python literals are interchangeable for every value.

No export script was generated or executed, no downstream color comparison was made, and no external software API/version claim was verified. This is a lower-priority interoperability proposal with explicit 3D-tool-to-2D-palette scope; original template provenance/license must be verified before reuse.

## Optional shared libraries: keep remote discovery separate from saved user assets

Full reads of [globalSet.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/globalSet.ts) and [globalSetStore.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/store/globalSetStore.ts) show a reusable separation for RFF: browse a remote library in memory, then explicitly copy a selected palette into a local document/library. The fetched collection is deliberately not registered as scene data or undo state. This avoids embedding an entire changing catalogue into every saved fractal. A future online library is optional and lower priority than the current shader recommendations; no network request or contribution was made in this audit.

Incoming configurations use the shared gradient validator and receive local stop identities. Collection item IDs use a reserved prefix and duplicate IDs are dropped. The parser does not validate the wire version or bound collection size, and fallback index-based IDs depend on response order. RFF should use stable source-scoped identities, supported-version checks, bounded input and explicit reporting of skipped/repaired palettes. The reserved prefix alone does not establish ownership; deletion/reordering should operate only on locally owned records. Imported names are accepted by this parser even though the current contribution design describes an unnamed service, illustrating why a reader's actual accepted shape matters more than a service comment.

**Expose freshness and recovery state.** Loading tries the live endpoint, a CDN starter copy and then a local starter copy. An empty successful live result falls through to starter data, but a successful CDN response parsed as an empty collection returns immediately instead of trying the local copy. The returned array has no source/freshness marker, so the store cannot distinguish a current shared set from a fallback snapshot or a valid empty result from failure. RFF should return structured status with source, revision and diagnostics, and treat empty-ready as a valid state. Fallback availability is useful, but it should not imply the user is seeing current remote content.

The initial store load is guarded once per tab; failure leaves the guard set, so ordinary remounting cannot retry. Refresh retains old data when a new result is empty and has no generation check or cancellation. Concurrent refresh/initial requests can therefore publish in completion order rather than request order. RFF should allow explicit retry, retain stale data with a visible status, accept legitimate empty updates and reject late obsolete responses. A pending fetch has no timeout in these files, so a promise waiting for a settled state can remain pending with it. Separate request lifecycle from panel mounting and keep expensive palette/facet reconstruction bounded for large collections.

**A contribution path needs explicit data semantics.** The POST builder sends only the config envelope (with stale ramp excluded for stop form), but passes its stop objects through directly; their local IDs are not removed by this function despite the wire-format commentary. It omits name, origin and source metadata. Successful JSON is cast to SubmitResult without validating its fields. The client alone does not prove duplicate enforcement, quota behavior, authentication policy or server storage rules described in comments. Those backend sources remain independently auditable. For RFF, preserve necessary source metadata in any proposed shared format, validate responses and keep publication an explicit user action; fetching a library is not authorization to upload anything.

The live-source descriptor explicitly says no license is recorded for anonymous contributions. That is a metadata limitation, not evidence of permission or public-domain status. RFF's existing provenance requirements remain applicable when adopting material. The code's userMade flag should not erase a known upstream origin. No external license, service availability, CORS configuration or current backend behavior was verified in this batch.

## Stable palette collections and preview caches

Full reads of [groundSets.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/groundSets.ts) and [favientBlocks.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/components/favientBlocks.ts), plus targeted inspection of favientsStore.favientSig, identify useful RFF library behavior: stable named collections, date-grouped recent palettes, retained empty groups and cached preview bodies independent of renaming/reordering. These improve 2D palette selection without touching fractal computation.

The list builder keeps catalogue/shared sources distinct from owned groups, aggregates split runs of named groups and retains explicitly named empty groups. Recent bins follow contiguous runs in the underlying shelf rather than being independently sorted/aggregated here. The documented newest-first/unique-bin behavior therefore depends on upstream ordering; repeated noncontiguous days can produce repeated bin IDs. RFF should state and enforce the store invariant or aggregate bins explicitly. Unknown set IDs fall back to catalogue identity, so a corrupt persisted selection can look like an intentional switch; distinguish a missing selection from a valid catalogue selection when restoring the UI.

Multi-set membership builds a desired-ID set and walks the local shelf followed by shared entries. That preserves input order but assumes IDs are unique across both sources; duplicate records with the same ID would still be emitted by the final filters. Including All is documented as a caller-owned special case, not enforced by this helper. Keep ownership, membership and display order as separate concepts in RFF, and validate batch actions against the resolved owned items.

Preview bodies cache the rendered display ramp and computed facets by favourite ID, content signature and blend space. Names and sprite row indices are supplied afterward, so rename/reorder can avoid re-rendering the palette. However, the inspected signature rounds positions and biases to 1/1000; edits below that granularity can reuse a stale preview. The body also retains the stop-array reference and returns shared ramp/facet objects, requiring immutable consumer behavior. RFF should use an exact content revision for preview invalidation rather than a deduplication signature, and scope mutable GPU/CPU preview resources to their owner. Excluding output colorSpace is deliberate for this display-only rendering path; shader-bake caches need their own key including every rendering dependency.

The cache clears wholesale after passing 4,000 entries rather than incrementally evicting old bodies, which can cause a burst of recomputation while browsing large sets. RFF can use a bounded cache with measured memory cost and incremental eviction. Rebuilding rows 0..n-1 is appropriate for a new sprite, but selection should remain keyed by palette identity rather than row. Tile sizes change at discrete count thresholds and never go below the configured base; preserving scroll/selection anchors across threshold crossings matters more than copying these exact dimensions.

Date labels use local calendar keys, but Yesterday is computed by subtracting exactly 86,400,000 milliseconds, which is not always the previous local date across daylight-saving changes. Invalid timestamps and timezone changes also need explicit handling. RFF should store absolute timestamps and derive calendar labels consistently, keeping chronology independent of translated labels. No UI audit, cache benchmark or date-boundary test was run; these are source-derived integration requirements, not measured RFF failures.

## Palette consumers need explicit display, radiance and editing semantics

Full reads of [gradientSeam.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/gradientSeam.ts), [gradientCss.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/gradientCss.ts), [gradientMapChannels.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/gradientMapChannels.ts) and [rampTween.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/rampTween.ts) connect palette authoring to actual consumers. For RFF, the important improvement is a declared conversion boundary for each destination, especially when an environment gradient is used for both visible background and surface lighting.

**Do not copy destination tags without their shader contract.** GMT's application adapter forces coloring gradients to linear output and environment gradients to sRGB output. It changes the texture-bake setting, not the underlying authored color strings. This documents two consumer expectations; it does not prove that encoded environment values are physically suitable for RFF's lighting accumulation. RFF should retain one source palette and explicitly derive display or linear-light textures as needed, preventing missing or double transfer-function conversion. The adapter returns false when the host lacks the destination setter; a successful setter call is not a GPU-render confirmation.

The catalogue-entry conversion preserves a supplied stop list but unconditionally assigns OKLCh blending; it cannot preserve another source blend mode unless that information survives the entry representation and is applied elsewhere. Ramp entries instead pass through the fitted-or-sampled policy already inspected. RFF should preserve authored interpolation metadata across library adapters, or deliberately carry the exact display ramp when metadata is unavailable. Do not reinterpret every editable stop list as the same interpolation model.

CSS previews explicitly subsample the canonical display ramp and let the browser interpolate, while swatch previews use hard boundaries. This is appropriate for decorative indicators, not picking exact colors, evaluating fit error or validating dense palettes. The default 33 sampled points cannot guarantee a faithful preview at every frequency/width despite an optimistic helper comment. RFF should use the same high-quality lookup as its renderer for analytical previews and validate the sample-count argument rather than accepting zero/nonfinite counts.

**Image channels can drive a 2D recoloring layer.** The map helper offers encoded RGB components, a weighted encoded-byte brightness proxy, OKLab lightness/chroma and wrapped OKLab hue. This can inform an optional RFF image-layer gradient map or reusable material mask. Preserve the distinction between the encoded-byte proxy and linear luminance; the source's Photoshop comparison was not independently verified. Hue is atan2(b,a) in OKLab, so its wrap is the positive-a axis, not necessarily exact sRGB red as the introductory wording implies. Near-gray hue is mapped to zero by a small a/b threshold, which can turn a neutral region into the palette's endpoint color. Offer an explicit achromatic mask/fallback and periodic seam handling. The chroma divisor 0.4 is an artistic normalization, not a universal maximum. Source tests sample a 32-cubed lattice plus corners, not every possible RGB byte triple; a range claim should be supported by the actual clamp/domain analysis and appropriate tests.

**Cross-fading variants is a separate operation from source-channel mixing.** tweenRamp blends each sample in rectangular OKLab and gamut-maps the result. Unlike the generator's separate circular hue mix, opposite colors may lose chroma at the midpoint. This is a valid alternative look, not a universally superior interpolation. Output length follows the first input; the second is nearest-resampled, so unequal-length inputs can lose fine detail and swapping the arguments changes the sampling grid. RFF should choose a common resolution and footprint-aware reconstruction for animated palettes, retain exact endpoints when identity matters, and assess temporal stability. Here even t=0/1 undergoes a conversion round trip unless the second ramp is empty; source comments acknowledge byte-level drift. Nonfinite t resets to zero, while invalid RGB values are not validated. No palette interpolation, image-map render or shader comparison was executed in this batch.

## Wave authoring for 2D palettes and material masks

Full reads of [waveGen.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/waveGen.ts) and [wavePresets.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/wavePresets.ts) suggest a useful optional RFF authoring tool: apply a periodic or seeded pattern to a selected palette channel, or to an artistic roughness/wetness mask, without modifying fractal computation. This is a transfer of procedural authoring concepts to 2D, not a requirement for 3D ray marching. These files describe baking into fitted keys; the actual UI commit path is not established by reading the pure helpers alone.

**Mechanism.** Sine, triangle, sawtooth and pulse evaluate a phase on the full normalized axis; wavelength does not silently change when the selected span shrinks. A power on phase provides horizontal bias, and a power on the normalized wave value provides vertical skew. Seeded noise instead interpolates lattice values with cubic smoothstep; wavelength controls grain scale and phase bias is not applied. Amplitude is expressed relative to the destination channel's range. Add, replace and multiply first construct a target value, then blend from the existing value using span envelope times strength. This target blend makes feathering meaningful even for replace mode. RFF can reuse the interaction model for lightness, chroma and hue, and separately for bounded material masks with explicit units.

**Retain artistic detail without aliasing.** The helper samples only at integer frames before fitting. The minimum wavelength permits 10,000 cycles over the full axis, far beyond a 256-sample ramp's capacity. A faithful RFF implementation needs a resolution/frequency policy, adaptive baking or footprint-aware integration, and explicit discontinuities for hard bands. Filtering a mask must not reduce perturbation precision or blur the underlying fractal computation. This is an authoring extension, not a replacement for the higher-priority environment-reflection and palette-filtering improvements.

**Endpoint rules must match the consumer.** The positive-integer phase special case selects phase one at every exact positive cycle boundary, not only at the last palette sample. This matters for sawtooth/pulse edges and animated phase. Noise is not inherently periodic. The cyclic preset controls one channel, so it cannot guarantee a seamless full-color ramp when other channels or the retained base differ at the endpoints. RFF should declare clamped versus repeated lookup, check the final color/mask seam, and evaluate animated phase under the same filtering convention as static output.

**Local editing has conditions.** The envelope returns the original sample outside the selected span, but matching boundary slopes requires positive, valid feather widths and a bounded wave. Zero feather can leave a step, and the helper does not enforce the documented upper feather limit. Identity outside the span at sample evaluation does not itself prove that fitted curves and their spliced neighbor handles remain unchanged. RFF should preserve the surrounding curve explicitly and preview the actual fitted result. Validate finite parameters, positive exponents, ordered spans and usable sample dimensions at the authoring boundary.

**Channel coordinates and recipe identity need explicit contracts.** Replace uses offset times range with no channel minimum; a signed channel such as rectangular OKLab a/b therefore needs a separate origin policy. Presets select semantic roles rather than blindly selecting a component, which prevents lightness edits from becoming red-channel edits in RGB. However, preset application merges with live parameters: strength and seed survive even whole-axis presets, while texture presets also retain span/feather. A preset ID alone does not identify the result. Preserve RFF's existing recipe ID/RNG order contract; any new saved recipe must capture the full resolved parameters and use a new stable identity. The ease-in/out presets use powers 2.2 and 0.45, while the in-out preset is a rising sine half-wave; these are not a general implementation of all named easing families. Shape glyphs preview the raw wave, not the combined base, strength and feathered output.

**Do not assume cross-language noise equivalence.** The JavaScript hash uses ordinary floating-point multiplication before bitwise conversion, including products exceeding exact integer precision; a C++ or GLSL implementation using 32-bit modular multiplication will not automatically reproduce it. Choose and freeze a specified deterministic algorithm for new RFF recipes, verify its source/license and record recognizable constants in NOTICE before adoption. Source comments cite tests, but no wave harness, shader rendering or cross-language equivalence test was executed in this audit batch.

## Preserve source identity while keeping palette edits responsive

A full read of [workingPipeline.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/workingPipeline.ts) identifies another transferable improvement for RFF's palette and future environment authoring: keep source data, the live preview and the committed representation distinct. The same single-source pipeline drives all inputs by passing identical channels to the shared generator with slot modifiers disabled and mix weights zero. This reduces divergent rendering paths, although even the identity branch computes the generator result before returning the original configuration.

An identity edit passes the original configuration object through and renders its display ramp directly, preserving stop count, interpolation and exact ramp data. An untouched fitted curve view also retains the original configuration, but its preview ramp comes from the fitted curves. Consequently, configuration and preview are intentionally not identical representations in this state. RFF should make consumer ownership explicit: opening an editor must not rewrite recipes, saved stops or environment textures through a lossy fit, and a temporary fitted preview must not silently become the export result. Store/UI wiring and the cited test harness were not executed in this batch.

During a drag, GMT can retain stop positions, interpolation and biases while refreshing their colors from the live ramp. Expensive knot refinement is deferred; the interaction still changes visibly. The held-stop preview uses nearest sampled ramp colors, so it is an approximation between stops, not a fidelity certificate. A held ramp is replaced only when the current ramp has exactly 256 entries; otherwise that branch returns the held data. For RFF, a live texture preview plus deferred editable-stop reconstruction is preferable when dense patterns cannot be represented by the held knots. Cancellation, final refinement and export should use one clearly identified committed revision.

Output representation follows source editability: inputs with stops or supplied stop seeds always fit back into stops, whereas seedless ramp inputs may remain sampled ramps when a compact fit is inadequate. This preserves editing affordances, but a bounded stop fit cannot promise exact appearance merely because the source was editable. RFF should retain the source recipe or exact baked lookup alongside an optional editable approximation and report fit error when converting deliberately. Adding stops is explicit here and preserves the output color-space hint; transformed-output metadata must also be restored by a defined consumer contract rather than assumed to survive a generic fitter.

The Detail mapping provides a target color error and a stop budget (56 through 152 stops over the documented 2..10 range), not a guarantee that either perceptual error or frame time meets a bound. It does not validate arbitrary Detail inputs. Identity checks likewise depend on normalized parameter semantics, including integer band coercion and scale normalization. RFF should validate saved/imported parameters before this layer and invalidate previews from exact revisions. These are source-derived design recommendations; no responsiveness measurements or visual comparisons were made.

## Perceptual palette browsing and reversible look variants

Full reads of [paletteSample.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/paletteSample.ts) and [variantsCore.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/variantsCore.ts) support two RFF extensions: perceptually distributed palette swatches/search, and named snapshots for comparing alternative looks. Neither file extracts colors from an image; the former samples an existing RGB ramp and the latter defines snapshot helpers rather than procedural variant generation. Both features transfer directly to 2D and can also serve an environment-gradient editor.

**Perceptual swatches.** Cumulative Euclidean OKLab distance allocates swatches to regions with more color change, unlike equal spacing on the gradient axis. The implementation selects the first sampled texel at or beyond each target cumulative distance; it does not interpolate to an exact arc-length position. Several requested swatches can therefore select the same texel across a strong edge. Flat ramps fall back to even positions. Stop-based sampling reads the rendered ramp at the stops' clamped positions, not necessarily the original stop color at a discontinuity. RFF should retain sample positions as editable state while updating their colors from the current palette; an explicit conversion to authored stops should preserve the intended edge side. These swatches are an authoring view, not adequate shader reconstruction data or an error bound.

**Similarity is useful for browsing, not identity.** GMT builds 32-sample OKLab descriptors and combines a band-limited dynamic-time-warping score (forward or reversed), a lightness-sorted color comparison and a near-flat-neighbor fraction. This can inspire a RFF library's related-palettes search while allowing reversed versions to remain close. However, the allowed warp is only three sample indices; arbitrary cyclic shifts are not fully invariant. The DTW result is divided by sequence length, not the chosen path length. Sorting colors only by lightness does not provide full order independence when different colors have equal lightness. The bandedness statistic depends on sample spacing and a fixed color threshold, so narrow stripes can be missed or aliased. Cache descriptors by palette revision and treat the weighting as a browsing heuristic to be evaluated on real RFF palettes. The source's millisecond performance claim was not benchmarked here.

The separate pointwise rampDistance samples only 16 locations by default. Zero distance is a necessary result for identical ramps, but it cannot establish byte identity: differences between the sampled locations are invisible. RFF should use exact representation comparison for saved recipes/cache identity, dense or adaptive checks for fitting accuracy, and a perceptual heuristic only for search. Public descriptor helpers also assume nonempty ramps and usable integer sample counts; unlike the swatch dispatcher, they do not guard those domains. Position helpers clamp finite values but do not reject NaN, and duplicate sample positions are possible. Imported data needs validation before reaching these routines.

**A/B/C look snapshots.** GMT's variant model captures palette-authoring feature slices and documents, with a separate sampled ramp for thumbnails and tweening. Its intended separation from full project loading is valuable: switching a look should not rename the RFF project, reset unrelated undo state or merge old favorites back into the shared library. The helper explicitly removes the shared favients document on capture. Actual capture/restore ordering and undo integration reside in the store and are not proven by this core-file read. RFF can extend this concept to coordinated palette, relief, roughness and environment settings, while keeping fractal location/calculation parameters outside a look snapshot unless explicitly included.

**Snapshot fidelity and persistence.** JSON cloning returns the original value when serialization fails, so this helper alone cannot guarantee immutable history for unsupported/cyclic values; stripFavients would then delete from that returned original object. RFF should require serializable, versioned snapshot values and fail a capture without mutating the source. The load gate validates outer bags and rejects three unsafe own keys at that level, but nested payload validation belongs to their providers; it neither proves strict plain-object prototypes nor checks every feature payload. Ramp validation accepts any finite numeric array length, while decoding clamps bytes and ignores a trailing incomplete RGB tuple. Capture nearest-resamples to 256 RGB byte texels, which is appropriate only as a declared display preview, not an exact high-resolution or HDR environment archive.

The list cap keeps the final twelve entries in list order rather than sorting createdAt, and parsed IDs need not be unique. Serialization failure returns an empty-list string; a caller that persists it could replace recoverable history with an empty collection. For RFF, preserve the last valid save, validate unique IDs and versioned domains, bound imported payloads before costly work, and store exact source data separately from thumbnails. No snapshot restoration, library ranking, UI interaction or shader render was tested in this batch.

## Direct palette painting and scalar-mask authoring

Full reads of [paintRamp.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/paintRamp.ts) and [ADR-0129](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/adr/0129-the-paint-face-paints-a-ramp.md) support an optional RFF palette-painting feature. A one-dimensional brush edits color along the palette coordinate; the same interaction can author scalar roughness or wetness masks indexed by a chosen fractal attribute. This is direct 2D transfer, not screen-space painting over the mathematical fractal. A scalar mask needs its own bounded-value blending rules rather than the RGB color operations used here.

**Brush mechanism.** Each dab covers texel centers with a hard inner plateau and a smoothstep shoulder, multiplied by a one-texel edge factor. Dabs are spaced along traveled distance, with a residual distance carried between pointer events. Wash tools accumulate coverage as old + (1 - old) * dabWeight * flow * pressure, average their source colors by the coverage increments, then composite against an immutable stroke-start base using coverage times opacity. Thus opacity acts as the stroke ceiling for valid normalized inputs, while flow controls approach to that ceiling. Clone reads the stroke-start base and Restore reads the session-opening base; neither accidentally samples its own accumulating wash. Float32 RGB storage avoids rounding after every dab, although gamut conversion/clamping and the selected blend implementation can still alter values before final byte encoding.

Build-up tools have different semantics: Smudge transports colors carried at offsets from the brush center, Soften moves rectangular OKLab values toward a neighborhood box mean, Sharpen moves away from it, and Tone changes OKLCh lightness, chroma or hue. The soften/sharpen neighborhood is captured before each dab, preventing traversal-order feedback within that dab; mirrored dabs are sequential and can influence one another. These are artistic palette edits, not edge-preserving filtering of the fractal image. Repeated sharpening can amplify noise and invoke gamut mapping, so preview the actual result rather than promising preserved fine structure.

**Color and sampling contracts.** Separable blend modes act on encoded sRGB channels; the four color-component modes use OKLCh, and build-up mixing uses rectangular OKLab. These are appearance-authoring choices, not physically linear radiance composition. For an environment-light texture, convert the finished authored result to the lighting representation at a separate boundary. The one-texel brush rim is an approximate coverage treatment, not a proof of alias-free behavior for every brush/zoom level. GMT fixes the canvas at 256 texels; constructor input is copied/truncated or extended by repeating its last color, not resampled, and empty input is not accepted safely by this core. RFF should explicitly normalize source resolution and retain higher-resolution/exact source data where required.

**Periodic and interactive details.** Wrap affects both brush destinations and clone/neighborhood sampling, while mirror places a second dab at the reflected coordinate and negates clone offset. Overlapping mirror dabs, including a brush centered on the symmetry axis, accumulate twice; wrapping a very wide footprint can also revisit a texel. Decide whether RFF intends repeated deposition or a union of brush coverage. The core accepts a new brush during a stroke but initializes clone/smudge instances only at stroke start; tool/mirror changes therefore need a host policy or a new stroke. Pressure is applied at each event's supplied value rather than interpolated along inserted dabs. hold() advances one dab per call for every tool except Smudge, including wash tools; temporal consistency depends on the caller's tick policy. For reproducible recording, preserve final texels or a specified seed plus resampled stroke/timing data, since jitter defaults to Math.random.

**Transaction model.** The ADR specifies local stroke undo, explicit apply/cancel, exact ramp commit without an automatic stop fit, and one application-level undo entry when leaving/applying the tool. This preserves painted details that a stop fit might lose. It also states that unapplied painting is absent from session autosave. For RFF, retain a recoverable draft and make cancellation/commit ownership explicit, particularly if the source palette changes during painting. The core limits stroke history to 100 entries and lets the last Paint stroke be recomposited from saved coverage/base data when selecting a blend mode. Its change test uses a 1e-4 per-component tolerance, so 'unchanged' is not byte identity; public buffers are mutable, and finite-value/brush-domain checks must precede the core. Documentation describes the host integration, but these reads alone do not verify every navigation/undo path. No painting harness, UI interaction, spectral-library audit or render comparison was executed in this batch.

## Keep palette navigation coordinates consistent

Full reads of [lensBand.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/lensBand.ts) and [padAxes.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/padAxes.ts) identify a modest supporting improvement for a future RFF palette browser: derive its map, range indicator and scrollbar from one coordinate model. GMT rounds the inverted vertical axis once, clamps both band edges and shares the band computation. The three-pixel minimum intentionally enlarges very narrow ranges, so the visual band is not always the exact mathematical span; keep hit targets separate from exact extent indicators if precise selection matters.

The visible map span intersects bucket reach with the selected window; disjoint or merely touching intervals fall back to the whole selected window while stale layout data catches up. This fallback is a continuity choice, not evidence that results exist throughout that range. Color-axis selection maps vividness to chroma, uses a color row axis vertically, and uses a distinct color sort axis horizontally when available. If the row axis is not a color axis, the vertical axis falls back to lightness and rowsOnY disables the lens, but a color sort can still change the horizontal axis; the introductory claim of always returning the default pad in that case is broader than the implementation. RFF should label active axes from the actual derived model, validate finite ranges/nonnegative dimensions and allowlist axis identifiers instead of assuming arbitrary object-key lookups are valid. These helpers do not establish gamut accuracy or perceptual uniformity of the displayed map.

## Library browsing: preserve exact sources behind display swatches

Full reads of [presetCatalog.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/presetCatalog.ts) and [pickerModel.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/pickerModel.ts) connect previously inspected palette math to browsing. For RFF, the useful architectural separation is exact editable/source channels versus a gamut-mapped byte preview. GMT's custom-channel entries retain copied, unclipped OKLCh arrays while rendering a bounded 256-texel RGBA swatch. This can preserve a palette transform's intermediate values and support an environment-authoring workflow, but the display swatch is neither an HDR lighting source nor proof that all original values survive every later consumer.

**Use exact revisions for editable sources.** Custom byte ramps are deduplicated by a 32-bit FNV-1a hash without a subsequent byte comparison. Custom-channel signatures sample only every fourth texel, round values to thousandths and retain sixteen bits per value before hashing. Different unsampled values or quantized values can therefore share a signature even without a hash collision. A channel hit replaces the ramp/channels under the same catalog index without refreshing facets; an index-only consumer cache can then remain stale. RFF should hash full canonical source data, compare after a hash hit where identity matters, and increment a revision whenever any render dependency changes. Keep recipe identity, content equality and perceptual similarity separate. Named hashing/provenance requirements still apply before adopting implementation code.

The byte-ramp registration assumes at least 256 input colors, builds its thumbnail from the first 256 rounded/clamped entries, but computes facets from the supplied ramp; longer or noncanonical input could describe a different distribution than the thumbnail. Built-in IDs use array indices, and ad-hoc IDs use a process-local sequence. Neither is suitable as a newly invented persistent RFF recipe identity. The catalog cache is mutable and its growth is not explicitly bounded in this helper. RFF should normalize imported sample dimensions, retain stable serialized IDs, and budget catalog/cache storage instead of depending on expected modest usage.

**Browse efficiently without changing the artwork.** Search concatenates names, themes and source/collection labels once, then applies case-folded token-AND substring matching. Filters combine that search with source exclusions, themes, an optional selected-ID set and six facet windows. Arrange separates grouping, facet buckets and within-bucket sorting; a copied array is sorted so the caller's catalog order survives. Similarity scores can be computed once for an anchor/catalog revision and reused as filters change, with ranked results explicitly read row-major. These patterns transfer directly to a 2D RFF palette library. Search labels may expose attribution for discovery, but a label containing a license name is not independently verified permission to redistribute an entry.

**Define ordering and reset behavior precisely.** Groups are ordered by population, buckets descend from high to low, and the reverse option reverses entries within a band rather than reversing the whole grouping hierarchy. Reversing after sorting also reverses ties. Name order uses localeCompare, so portable saved ordering should not depend on an unspecified runtime locale. Hue is bucketed on a linear 0..1 axis, which introduces a cut at the circular seam. Selection carve preserves displayed order and requires the complete displayed-ID list, including virtualized off-screen entries. The clear patch resets facet/source/theme/carve fields but search is explicitly separate; an RFF 'clear all' action should visibly reflect whichever scope it actually clears.

The similarity adapter samples packed display RGBA directly and renders the anchor in display space, preventing texture-output encoding from changing browsing rank. Its buffer helper assumes a valid stride and complete nonempty pixel data. ID-keyed search/similarity maps assume unique entry IDs; duplicate IDs overwrite descriptors. Unknown row axes use an ordinary object lookup, and filter-window conversion supplies defaults without finite/domain validation. RFF should validate library records and axis enums at the boundary, cache by revision, and use the browsing score only for ranking. No catalog-scale benchmark or end-to-end picker interaction was performed.

## Spatial library selection and persistence helpers

Full reads of [selectionGeometry.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/selectionGeometry.ts), [wallLayout.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/wallLayout.ts) and [storage.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/storage.ts) complete the supporting pure helpers for this batch. Rectangle/lasso selection tests swatch centers, not overlap of their full bounds; rectangle edges are inclusive, while even-odd polygon edge behavior is not explicitly normalized. Paint selection uses a separately accumulated ID set. A future RFF library should document the selection rule, keep IDs stable across reflow, and apply the same scroll/DPI transform to the overlay and hit tests. These helpers alone do not prove the virtualized host supplies all relevant centers.

The layout heuristic narrows columns only for a small globally counted set of rows, avoiding overcompacting a large library just because individual groups are small. Its square-root estimate uses an approximate rectangular packing and is not a strict maximum-aspect guarantee after integer rounding/group gutters. Positive finite dimensions and column limits are caller assumptions. This is a modest browsing improvement, not a rendering optimization.

The storage wrappers separate guarded localStorage access from JSON parsing, but a successful parse is cast to the requested type without schema validation. JSON.stringify remains outside a catch in lsSetJson, so cyclic/unsupported values can fail before the guarded storage call. The wrapper exposes no save-success result. For native RFF persistence, use versioned validation, an atomic replace with a recoverable prior file and explicit success/failure propagation; do not translate silent browser-storage fallback into a claim that a palette was saved. The underlying safeLocalStorage implementation was not re-read as part of this batch, and no persistence failure was induced.

## Collection exchange and review sheets for RFF palettes

A full read of [favientsExport.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/favientsExport.ts) suggests an immediately transferable 2D workflow: export a palette collection as individual files in an ordered ZIP, a native collection where supported, or a labeled contact/swatches sheet for comparison. Continuous ramps and discrete swatches are separate subjects; unsupported swatch formats return no result instead of silently exporting a different subject. RFF should preserve this distinction and include a native lossless collection alongside any approximate interchange files.

The export source is explicitly the display ramp, independent of the shader texture's color-space hint. This avoids exporting linear-light byte values as though they were display-encoded colors. It does not establish that every destination format or application renders identically: format-specific reduction, interpolation and color management remain separate checks. The quality-warning dispatcher uses each reducing format's configured stop budget; a format without stop reduction receives no warning from this function, which is not equivalent to having no possible loss of metadata, alpha, precision or color-space information. Export-format implementations still require their own review.

ZIP member names prepend a numbered index, sanitize path separators and shorten the stem by Unicode code points until the complete name meets a UTF-8 byte budget. This preserves collection order and handles repeated names better than a lossy ASCII slug. Filename portability also depends on the full path and destination filesystem, so the helper's comments overstate extraction guarantees. An unknown continuous-ramp format silently falls back to the first registered format; RFF should report the chosen format explicitly or reject a stale selection. The ZIP construction and compression are synchronous and retain the entire collection in memory. Large collections need bounded work, cancellation and measured memory consumption rather than assuming export is cheap.

Contact sheets reuse one scratch ramp canvas, which avoids per-entry canvas allocation, but their gradient swatches rescale 256 source pixels to 240 logical pixels with smoothing. They are visual overviews, not exact inspection or round-trip storage. Swatch sheets include hex labels; both sheet types use display-dependent pixel ratio and installed system fonts, truncate names by string length and place all rows on one growing canvas without pagination. RFF can improve the deliverable with fixed export dimensions, width-aware text fitting, pagination and a companion manifest carrying full names/IDs and attribution. The optional credited filename stems in the ZIP path do not themselves supply complete license metadata. No ZIP round-trip or sheet rendering was tested in this batch.

## Native design-application exchange requires independent validation

A full read of [indesignIdml.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/indesignIdml.ts) shows an optional, lower-priority RFF exchange route: a package with named gradient swatches rather than a solid-color-only swatch list. GMT reduces a 256-sample ramp to selected indices, writes RGB color resources and linear gradient stops at index/255 times 100, and patches the root color group. This loses the original procedural recipe and interpolation semantics; it should be presented as an approximation for design work, not an exact RFF palette archive or a shader improvement.

The implementation preserves other parts from a compressed template and relies on the template's stored order to put the uncompressed mimetype member first. It does not verify that ordering or validate the resulting package, so template reuse does not by itself guarantee destination validity. The graphic header fixes DOMVersion 21.4, the designmap patch replaces the first matching ColorGroup rather than checking its identity, and RGB values are rounded without local range/finite validation. XML escaping handles ordinary markup delimiters but does not exclude all invalid XML control characters. A future independent RFF writer should validate structure, references, input domains and target-version behavior with actual exported files.

Name uniquification counts repeated base names but does not reserve generated suffixes: inputs named 'A', 'A', and 'A 2' can still yield duplicate display names. Use a global allocated-name set, including reserved names, and retain source IDs separately. Do not copy the bundled template merely because IDML is a public format; its provenance and license must be established independently under RFF's NOTICE policy. The compressed template payload and destination application's behavior were not inspected in this batch, so neither redistribution permission nor successful InDesign import is claimed.

## Reuse drop commands, but revalidate gesture state

A full read of [pointerGradientDrag.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/pointerGradientDrag.ts) provides a supporting interaction lesson for a RFF palette/environment editor. GMT allows a gesture that began as selection to become a whole-gradient drag and reuses existing target handlers by dispatching synthetic drag events with the same payload. Acceptance is read from a canceled dragover event. In a native application, reuse a typed application command and payload-validation path rather than assuming browser event construction maps directly to native dragging.

The helper tracks the last hovered element and acceptance result; release does not hit-test again. A move with no element under the pointer returns without clearing the previous accepted target, and blur/lost capture is not handled in this module. RFF should validate the current target on release, cancel on capture loss/deactivation and make cleanup exception-safe. The synthetic event builder forwards coordinates and payload but not modifier keys or mouse-button state, so modifier-dependent copy/move behavior requires an explicit contract. This helper supports mouse events, not a complete pen/touch gesture system. The historical manual checks in the source were not rerun, and no current browser or native drag behavior is asserted from them.

## Text palette import: distinguish color extraction from faithful interpretation

A full read of [importFormats.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/importFormats.ts), with a targeted dependency recheck of editorConfig.ts, establishes a useful RFF feature scope: import common palette lists and gradient descriptions while reporting whether their structure was preserved or merely sampled. The parsers cover MAP, GPL, a subset of GGR/CPT/CSS, color-list JSON, supported GMT configurations and selected design-token shapes. This is directly useful to 2D coloring and environment-gradient authoring; it does not imply full compatibility with each named format.

**Common sampling mechanism.** Most paths collect positioned or evenly spaced colors, sort and clamp positions, then sample 256 points using straight interpolation of the encoded RGB channel values. 'Linear RGB interpolation' in the helper comment means linear arithmetic on those values, not decoding sRGB to linear light. Adjacent coincident anchors, endpoints and sample-grid alignment affect which side of a discontinuity survives. Byte-grid exports can preserve their sample colors, but gradients with narrow bands, nonlinear interpolation, alpha or wider gamut cannot generally survive this interchange unchanged. RFF should keep positioned source data when available, preserve an exact native representation, and explicitly label a sampled approximation.

MAP/GPL read the first three extracted numeric values from qualifying lines and treat colors as an evenly spaced continuous ramp; this discards any categorical palette semantics unless the caller restores them. Numeric extraction is permissive rather than a complete numeric grammar: leading-dot decimals such as .5 are not parsed as 0.5 by the shared expression. It can also extract numbers embedded in malformed tokens. A RFF parser should tokenize each supported record grammar and report skipped/invalid rows rather than silently normalizing every plausible triplet.

**GGR/CPT fidelity.** GGR takes endpoint RGB and midpoint, using a piecewise linear factor that reaches 0.5 at the midpoint. It does not implement the stored blend/coloring modes, alpha or dynamic endpoint-color semantics, and does not check the declared segment count. It also does not explicitly validate all segment positions/midpoints as finite or enforce a continuous nonoverlapping partition. CPT treats records as RGB, rescales the original scalar domain to 0..1 and ignores background/foreground/NaN records and color-model comments. HSV or other unsupported CPT forms should not silently become RGB, and the lost scalar range can matter when mapping scientific values. For RFF, distinguish categorical versus continuous input and retain invalid/interior/background color roles only through an explicit mapping to RFF's own semantics.

**CSS is a restricted color extractor.** Hex and rgb()/rgba() are recognized, with alpha discarded; named colors, general CSS color spaces, variables/references and geometry are not fully interpreted. The parser locates the literal substring gradient(, so other gradient geometries can enter the same 1D path and case/whitespace variants need not behave consistently with sniffing. A stop's percentage is taken from the first percent token in the entire fragment, which may be inside rgb(100%,0%,0%) rather than its stop position. Two-position stops and interpolation hints are not faithfully represented. Non-leading comments are not globally tokenized away, and custom-property color extraction searches inside declaration values rather than requiring a pure color value. An independent RFF importer should expose a strict supported subset or use a suitable licensed parser, with unsupported constructs reported before applying the palette.

**JSON 'exact' needs a qualified meaning.** The exact-config branch checks that coercion keeps the same number of stops, but coerceGradientConfig also clamps/normalizes fields, supplies default blend/output spaces and repairs IDs. Equal count therefore proves no stops were dropped, not literal or semantic identity of every malformed/unknown input field. When that branch fails, the fallback reads surviving colors and redistributes them evenly, potentially losing otherwise valid positions without an explicit warning. RFF should return structured diagnostics and distinguish unchanged, normalized, sampled and rejected results. A single invalid stop should not silently turn a positioned gradient into a different evenly spaced ramp.

Design-token traversal supports inherited color type, selected string/hex/sRGB-component values and a depth limit, but not a general token-reference resolver or arbitrary color space. Integer-like object keys follow JavaScript's numeric ordering rather than original textual order; descending numeric scales can reverse. When an object supplies both hex and components, hex takes precedence. Alpha is again absent from the returned RGB representation. Preserve array order or explicit positions for ordered RFF palettes and treat unordered token groups as swatch collections until an order is chosen.

**Bound work and validate outputs.** The dispatch wrapper restricts text length and extensions, catches exceptions and requires a 256-element result. Its length limit counts JavaScript UTF-16 code units rather than bytes. Direct exported parsers bypass that top-level size/catch gate, JSON is fully parsed before anchor limits apply, and several loops bound accepted colors rather than all traversed nodes. The CSS splitter allocates all fragments before the accepted-stop cap. These are useful partial limits, not a universal bounded-memory/no-throw guarantee. The dispatcher also does not validate every output channel as finite; for example, nonfinite segment positions/midpoints may contaminate interpolation despite finite endpoint colors. RFF should enforce byte/node/depth/sample budgets, validate output values and distinguish truncation from successful complete import. Source test comments themselves acknowledge that one nonsense string per direct parser is not fuzz coverage. No import harness, external-format conformance suite or rendered round-trip was executed in this batch.

## One import pipeline with explicit batch outcomes

A full read of [importGradientFiles.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/importGradientFiles.ts) suggests a strong supporting design for RFF's future palette exchange: route file-picker, drag-and-drop and collection imports through one parser/result model, then apply a prepared batch in one undoable operation. The router distinguishes gradients, sessions, scenes, ordinary PNG images and unreadable inputs. This allows a user to understand why a dropped image needs color extraction rather than receiving a generic import failure. It is a 2D workflow improvement, independent of the fractal shader's dimensionality.

**Route by validated content and caller intent.** PNG/ZIP signatures and JSON document decoding precede ordinary text parsing, but this is not completely extension-independent: remaining text still passes through the extension allowlist. Unsupported document versions are refused rather than reinterpreted as color lists. A separate scene-loader claim is deliberately narrower: it leaves scene-key PNGs and ambiguous JSON with their original owner. RFF should adopt this separation so a palette importer cannot accidentally take over scene/location files. The general gradient route and the scene route have different precedence on mixed scene/gradient PNG metadata; such ambiguity should be explicit in the integration contract. The fallback image route here covers PNG input, not every general image format.

**Preserve fidelity and report conversion.** Parsed native configurations are kept when recognized; otherwise the ramp is passed to an automatic fit with target error 0.02 and a 32-stop budget, using sampled-ramp fallback where the fitter requires it. This avoids forcing dense palettes into too few stops, but does not remove the parser losses documented above. A 256-element array alone does not guarantee that fitting is safe or semantically faithful; finite channels and supported color domains must also be validated. RFF should attach normalization/sampling diagnostics to each imported item and keep exact source data where useful, especially for repeatable environment or material-mask authoring.

**Plan destinations before writes.** GMT groups items per destination before insertion, preventing repeated head insertion from reversing a multi-file drop and allowing files naming the same new set to reuse one group. Multi-set documents use a collection merge; otherwise the caller's owned set wins, then a named source set, then the default set. For RFF, prepare a visible destination/count summary and keep source-local group IDs namespaced until labels/IDs have been reconciled. The helper's owned-group check excludes recent groups but does not itself prove the supplied group belongs to the user; that assumption is delegated to the caller. It executes ordinary destination plans before collection merges, so mixed inputs do not necessarily retain their global original file order. Timestamps carried in parsed entries are not forwarded through the ordinary insertMany path, unlike collection-merge entries.

File reading is asynchronous, while destination writes are synchronous; keeping the undo transaction out of the file-read await prevents an unrelated gesture from replacing a shared interaction snapshot. However, the helper mutates multiple destinations sequentially and provides no rollback if a later store operation fails. RFF should validate the entire plan before committing and use a transaction or recoverable staged update. The exact store-level deduplication behavior and undo integration require the store/caller audit; the core count arithmetic alone is not proof of lossless merging.

**ZIP limits need aggregate accounting.** GMT restricts the outer file to 64 MiB, selected entries to 2,000, declared entry size to 32 MiB and nested ZIP depth to one. These limits do not bound the total expanded bytes: synchronous unzip materializes all selected entries before routing, and many individually allowed members can exceed a practical memory budget. readGradientFiles also reads all supplied files concurrently without a batch-byte/concurrency bound and retains bytes plus decoded text. RFF should stream or stage imports with aggregate compressed/expanded-byte limits, cancellation and bounded concurrency. Text-only router callers do not pass through the outer byte-size gate before native-document decoding.

Archive filtering silently omits hidden/platform metadata entries and entries rejected by size/count limits; omitted members are not individually included in the reported skipped count. Directory-only archives become one unreadable result. For RFF, distinguish intentionally ignored metadata from rejected payloads, duplicates and conversion failures, and identify affected archive/member paths. No extraction to the filesystem occurs in this GMT helper; these observations concern parsing/memory and result accounting, not a demonstrated path-traversal write.

**Names and collection identity.** Ordered ZIP fallback naming recognizes a numeric filename convention, but the source explicitly acknowledges that new ASCII underscore names can be mistaken for legacy slugs and converted to spaces. A companion manifest with stable IDs, original names, order, grouping and provenance avoids this inference. Collection aggregation uses Object.assign for group-label dictionaries from multiple files, so identical local IDs can overwrite labels before merge. Its document flag means at least one contributing input was a document; a caller considering replacement must not assume every accompanying item came from the same authoritative collection. Import summaries distinguish many outcomes, but filtered ZIP entries and other loss of information need richer diagnostics than the current counters provide. No archive stress test, store mutation, undo test or cross-format round-trip was executed in this batch.

## Export writers: serialized fidelity and capability contracts

Full source review of [exportFormats.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/core/exportFormats.ts); source SHA-256 matches the audit inventory. The following findings incorporate the supplementary review saved during the execution outage.

## RFF adoption

Use a capability-based exporter that distinguishes continuous gradients, discrete swatches, single files and collections. This transfers directly to RFF's 2D palettes and can also exchange environment gradients with 3D tools. It remains lower priority than improvements to RFF's own environment reflection and palette filtering.

| GMT export family | Actual representation | RFF requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MAP, hex, arrays, CSV, color-list JSON, GPL | Rounded RGB values, generally 256 samples | Declare display encoding; retain recipes separately |
| GGR/CPT | 255 linear segments with decimal coordinates | Evaluate coordinate rounding and special-color/domain semantics |
| CSS/SVG/GRD/AI/IDML/UGR | Reduced stops with target-specific coordinates | Measure error after serialization and destination interpolation |
| ASE | Discrete colors with no original stop positions | Do not describe it as an equivalent continuous gradient |
| Tokens/CSS variables/Tailwind-shaped fragment | Eleven evenly sampled colors for ramp exports | Disclose loss of narrow color bands |
| Paint.NET text | Ninety-six evenly sampled colors | Report sampling loss despite having no stop-budget control |
| Blender/Cinema 4D scripts | Reduced stops passed to script builders | Validate destination limits and color conversion |

## Reduction and diagnostics

The reducer splits at the largest encoded-byte RGB deviation from a line between rounded endpoints. It always retains samples 0 and 255, starts at tolerance 1.5 and multiplies tolerance by 1.35 until the requested budget is met or forty retries expire. This is adaptive simplification, not global minimum-stop fitting or a perceptual-error guarantee. A large budget still begins with simplification. Validate finite bounded 256-sample input and budgets of at least two.

The warning metric measures maximum RGB Euclidean error only on the original sample grid. Its threshold 24 is an application heuristic, not OKLab Delta E or a universal visibility threshold. CSS/SVG then round positions to 0.1 percent, GRD to integer 0..4096, and UGR to integer 0..399; GGR/CPT also round coordinates. RFF should serialize, decode and compare source samples plus edge neighborhoods and the cyclic seam.

ASE single-gradient export accepts a budget override, but ASE collection export uses the fixed ASE_MAX value. The collection warning can therefore evaluate a different conversion from the file actually written. Fixed eleven-/ninety-six-sample exports also lose information without a stop-reduction warning.
