RFF should derive preview, diagnostics and output from one conversion result. stopBudgetOf does not enforce finite overrides or destination hard caps; validate those in the writer itself.

## Precision, names and interoperability

GRD writes opaque transparency stops and expands byte RGB values by 257 into sixteen-bit fields, without restoring original precision. It truncates a UTF-8 Pascal name at a character boundary, but its encoding compatibility still requires destination validation. ASE stores RGB floats after byte rounding, writes UTF-16BE names, and lacks a local bound preventing its sixteen-bit name-unit count from overflowing.

AI uses an elementary RGB-to-CMYK fallback rather than ICC-managed print conversion. Name escaping handles parentheses and backslashes but not all control characters in line-oriented records/comments. AI/ASE duplicate-name suffixing can collide with an existing suffixed name. UGR sanitizes and truncates names again inside the block builder, potentially removing a generated uniqueness suffix. Allocate unique names after final truncation/encoding.

UGR retains endpoints at 0 and 399 and packs red into the least-significant byte. This avoids a broad unspecified wrap interval, but unequal endpoint colors still produce a cyclic seam. A ring representation does not automatically create continuity. Preserve explicit clamped/repeated semantics and assess target-grid edge reconstruction.

Token/CSS-variable exports keep a display name separate from the sanitized identifier but omit source positions, bias, interpolation, alpha and the original color-space contract. Eleven colors named 50..950 are not necessarily monotonic in lightness or accessible contrast. The JSON exporter writes a colors array, not the exact gradient-document form. Several exported extensions are not accepted by the inspected import suite, so export coverage is not symmetric import support.

Compatibility claims and historical measurements in source comments were not rerun. Do not treat application stop-budget defaults as universal format limits. An independent RFF implementation needs original format specifications, provenance/license checks and destination fixtures. No external application, export test harness or rendered comparison was run in this batch.


## Snapshot integration: distinguish available code from a shipped feature

Full reads of variantsStore.ts, paramUndoBracket.ts, imageDocument.ts and docs/adr/0112-variants-bypass-the-scene-loader.md refine the earlier snapshot recommendation. ADR-0112's dated update explicitly says the Variants UI was removed and identifies the shared snapshot helpers as the live session path. Thus A/B look comparison is an RFF feature proposal supported by reusable GMT code, not evidence of a currently exposed GMT product feature. The ADR's importer inventory was not independently re-enumerated in this batch.

The store captures declared palette feature slices plus all registered documents except the shared favorites library. Application again strips favorites on restore and ignores feature IDs outside the caller's allowlist. This is a useful foundation for RFF look/session snapshots, but document scope is broader than the feature allowlist: future registered documents enter the snapshot unless explicitly excluded. Prefer document-provider capabilities declaring session, look, history and shared-library ownership. The stored thumbnail ramp is used as snapshot data, but restore applies feature/document state rather than directly reinstalling that ramp; do not mistake the thumbnail for authoritative source reconstruction.

**Code supersedes stale comments.** applyStudioSnapshot merges current declared feature defaults below each supplied patch before calling its setter. This addresses missing fields within a present feature patch despite an older header warning saying new parameters retain their current values. An entirely absent feature patch is still skipped, and current defaults can change across releases, so RFF needs versioned migration/default semantics for reproducible archived looks. Missing setters are also skipped silently. Capture/update/duplicate change activeId, but activeId alone does not prove the live rendering matches that snapshot; update without a supplied ramp retains the old thumbnail even when source state changed. Keep a dirty/revision distinction in RFF's comparison UI.

**Undo grouping is not asynchronous atomicity.** paramEdit calls start, mutation and end without try/finally. An exception can leave bookkeeping open. Nested palette starts preserve the existing snapshot, but the first nested end closes it unless paramGroup is active; dragDepth is a separate notion and may remain positive afterward. paramGroup uses finally for synchronous cleanup, while direct engine transaction callers can still bypass its ownership. The outside-transaction queue rechecks before draining, then clears its queue and invokes callbacks without rechecking between callbacks or isolating exceptions. For RFF, use scoped transaction ownership, guaranteed cleanup, cancellation and explicit completion of asynchronous resource loading before committing an undo entry.

**Image restoration has its own lifecycle.** The image provider serializes a thumbnail as JPEG at quality 0.85 and re-ingests that image on restore. This is lossy source substitution, not proof that image-derived colors remain identical. It caches by canvas identity, so in-place canvas edits require an explicit revision or invalidation policy. It preserves the original saved data URL after restore to avoid another JPEG generation on every subsequent reload, which is useful. RFF should retain a lossless extraction source or the exact extracted palette and trace result when reproducibility matters.

The implementation now increments a restore token and ignores stale decode completions, superseding the ADR's older claim that a token is absent. Valid image-less snapshots reset the store, contrary to the older introductory no-op description. A decode failure only clears loading and logs a warning; it does not explicitly clear the previous model despite another comment claiming an empty stage. A malformed non-object snapshot invalidates older decodes but returns without resetting loading. The token covers calls to this restore function, not every possible user image edit elsewhere. RFF should unify resource-generation tokens across restore/manual load/undo and keep the prior state or an explicit error placeholder consistently.

Trace-path coercion supplies finite defaults but does not bound normalized coordinates or the number of freehand points. exportFmt is passed as a string without an enum check in this provider. Image decode finishes after the synchronous restore bracket closes, so one bracket alone cannot guarantee that asynchronous image changes are included in undo. The store's header calls this out; the actual history-provider and UI integration still require separate inspection before making an end-to-end undo claim. Persistence updates live variant state before a save whose success is not exposed, reinforcing the need for recoverable native saves and truthful status in RFF. No snapshot/undo harness, image comparison or UI restoration test was run in this batch.

## Reproducible image-derived palettes and session ownership

Full reads of palette/store/imageStore.ts, palette/store/coerceJson.ts, store/documentRegistry.ts and palette/store/workingSession.ts extend the RFF image-palette proposal from extraction math to persistence. GMT keeps heavy image/model/trace data outside scalar feature settings and feeds both into one pure extraction entry point. The React hook and imperative bake path call the same extract function, which reduces semantic drift. However, useMemo is per hook instance rather than a global result cache; multiple consumers may recompute independently. RFF should share a revision-keyed extraction result across preview, export and bake, with exact source/trace/parameter versions attached.

The image hook falls back to defaults only when the whole feature slice is absent, not for individual missing properties. Mode indices fall back to distill, while other fields pass through as supplied. Store setters retain references without validation or copying; in-place model/path mutation can evade identity-based memo invalidation. Loading does not gate extraction: an older model remains eligible while a replacement loads. reset clears model/path/loading but retains exportFmt. RFF should define whether pending-load previews deliberately show the prior result, disable committing that stale result when appropriate, and validate every restored parameter domain. The small coerceJson helpers enforce finite scalar types but not numeric ranges, string limits, enums or strict plain-object prototypes.

**Persist all authoring state, with explicit failure reporting.** GMT's document registry separates non-feature authoring state from generic settings. Providers use stable IDs, and restore iterates registered IDs with own-property checks, ignoring unknown document keys. This is a useful RFF extension point for editable palettes, curves and image traces. Provider exceptions are caught independently so another provider can proceed, but a failed save provider is silently absent except for a console warning and a failed restore can leave a partially changed session. The registry does not validate JSON serializability, deep-clone returned snapshots, track asynchronous completion or roll back earlier providers. RFF should return structured per-provider diagnostics, validate before committing and preserve the last complete session instead of announcing an incomplete save as successful.

Missing documents intentionally leave existing state untouched. That is a backward-compatibility policy, not proof of an independent full-session restore: old/unregistered/missing components can combine with the current session. Registration replaces a provider by ID and unregister removes by ID without ownership tokens. Use explicit required/optional/migrated/reset semantics and registration ownership in RFF, with provider IDs restricted to an allowlist and a dictionary representation that safely stores those IDs. The registry's current object test accepts any non-array object; per-document validation remains essential.

**A compact session may depend on live state.** The working session captures generator/image feature slices, excludes shared favorites and viewer filter preferences, and requires a readable working document when validating. File application clears the incoming Recent session ID/pinned state so it cannot silently edit an existing local entry by identity. These are useful ownership boundaries for RFF. Compact capture omits the image document entirely rather than storing an explicit empty image; omission leaves the current image unchanged on restore. If the restored working input depends on image extraction, a compact session is therefore not necessarily self-contained. RFF should label a compact snapshot's dependencies or include the exact extracted ramp as a stable fallback.

Validation checks the working document but returns the other document payloads for provider-level handling; it is not all-or-nothing validation of every dependency. Boot application avoids creating an undo entry, while file application uses a synchronous bracket and inherits the previously documented asynchronous image-undo limitation. Applying a session unconditionally neutralizes Mix slot modifiers, even if the file supplies nondefault values, because the current UI offers no control for them. This is a deliberate migration/product policy, not exact restoration of every serialized field. RFF should version and document comparable normalizations rather than silently claiming bit-identical restoration.

Source comments list a specific set of documents, but the shared snapshot helper actually includes all currently registered providers except favorites. Keep that extensibility aligned with session ownership and forward compatibility. No image-extraction benchmark, provider-failure injection, session round-trip or undo test was executed in this batch; the findings are implementation-derived requirements for RFF's 2D palette and optional environment authoring.

## Autosave should distinguish complete, degraded and failed recovery

Full reads of engine/plugins/Session.ts, store/sessionEnvelope.ts, engine/store/autosaveStore.ts, store/safeLocalStorage.ts and gradient-explorer/v2/session.ts connect the session adapter to its actual lifecycle. For RFF, the transferable improvement is recoverable editing of palette, relief and environment settings with explicit restoration precedence and truthful save status. The mechanism is independent of 3D rendering and applies directly to 2D workflows.

**Shared adapter and version gate.** GMT uses one capture/validate/apply adapter for boot restore and session files. The JSON envelope checks format, version equality and an object body; the app validates contents. This avoids inconsistent file/autosave decoders. However, the envelope has no input-size/depth limit, no migration implementation, no checksum and no meaningful timestamp validation. Strict version equality protects unsupported data from accidental interpretation but is not a substitute for migrations. RFF should preserve its established file-format stability rules and use a separately versioned recovery format if adding a new session container.

**Explicit precedence.** Autosave off clears the recovery slot; an incoming share/handoff preempts restore; otherwise a valid saved session is applied before rendering. The Explorer installs autosave afterward and uses its own preference keys. This prevents one app's toggle from changing another app's recovery behavior. Disabling autosave also deletes the prior stored recovery rather than merely stopping future writes; RFF should make retention behavior explicit. Boot application catches an exception and returns fresh, but it does not undo providers already changed, so that result cannot prove a clean initial state. Stage and validate a complete RFF restoration before swapping it into the active document.

**Change detection and resource timing.** The autosave baseline is the full captured JSON at installation; subsequent interval/page-hide/hidden-tab events capture again and write only if that body differs. Timestamp generation is outside the comparison, avoiding writes merely because time passed. This still serializes the whole body to discover changes; revision tracking can avoid repeated heavy captures in RFF. Installation after a synchronous restore does not guarantee an asynchronous image restore has finished, so the initial baseline and an early close can observe incomplete resources. Coordinate restoration completion with autosave activation. Incoming content is persisted only if the captured state differs from the baseline; preemption alone does not prove the old recovery slot was replaced.

**Degraded saves need visible status.** A failed full write triggers one compact capture/write. On compact success GMT records the FULL body as the last-saved baseline, suppressing further attempts while the session is unchanged. Combined with the inspected adapter, the stored session may omit the source image indefinitely even after storage space becomes available. If both writes fail, it retries on later triggers but only emits a console warning once. RFF should retain a last-complete checkpoint, identify omitted resources, expose recovery quality to the user and retry upgrading a degraded checkpoint under a controlled policy. A compact result should never be presented as complete preservation of source-dependent palette editing.

The low-level storage writer returns success/failure, but preference setters update in-memory state even when saving those preferences fails. Removal has no success result. A user can therefore see an autosave setting that does not survive reload. The settings factory is keyed only by the enabled key, so two callers supplying different interval keys with the same enabled key reuse the first store; callers must provide a consistent namespace. Stored intervals are finite-checked and clamped, while the setter rounds/clamps without rejecting NaN. Separate tabs have separate in-memory stores and this code installs no cross-tab conflict/version coordination. RFF multi-window recovery should use per-document/instance ownership and detect competing writers rather than sharing a last-writer-wins recovery file accidentally.

**Completion messages must match completion.** File save announces success after initiating a browser download; it does not confirm durable destination-file creation. File load announces success after synchronous adapter.apply returns and promises undo, even though the inspected image provider may still be decoding outside the undo bracket. Provider-level caught failures can also bypass that outer success/failure distinction. A native RFF workflow should await resource preparation and durable write/atomic replacement, then report the actual result. File reads have no local size check or request-generation token here, so overlapping reads can apply in completion order; validate limits and supersede older load requests before commit.

Visibility/page-hide flushing is a useful additional checkpoint but cannot guarantee recovery from every crash or forced termination. The source itself limits its historical browser measurement, despite stronger wording in the settings description. Preserve periodic checkpoints and test abrupt termination rather than relying solely on exit events. Uninstalling the generic autosave removes timer/listeners without a final flush; the Explorer installer discards cleanup handles and retains an installed flag for the page lifetime. These are lifecycle assumptions to adapt explicitly in a native RFF implementation. No crash test, quota simulation, multi-window test or session harness was executed in this batch.

## Palette-editor handoff should carry a specific source revision

Full reads of docs/adr/0121-the-session-restores-itself.md, gradient-explorer/v2/fromGmt.ts, palette/core/explorerHandoff.ts and app-gmt/explorerTrip.ts connect the separate palette editor to the 3D studio. For RFF, the transferable workflow is opening the selected palette or environment gradient in a dedicated editor while retaining the scene/location and its render state. This does not require adopting GMT's multi-tab architecture; a native editor panel can use the same explicit source/destination ownership with fewer persistence dependencies.

ADR-0121's amendments supersede its original on-by-default/shared-key decision: current intent is opt-in autosave with per-app keys. Its old-shell consequence is also explicitly retired. The document still describes the asynchronous image undo gap. Treat amended decisions as historical context, and the inspected implementation as the evidence for current behavior; neither the document's recovery promises nor its named tests establish a crash guarantee without running the relevant tests.

**Resolve what the user is actually editing.** The studio prioritizes its last-applied favorite only if that favorite remains on the shelf and a content signature matches its current destination; otherwise it uses the selected destination, then gradient 1. Keeping the last-applied record in tab-local memory is useful for avoiding cross-scene confusion. However, the signature previously inspected rounds/omits some fields, so equality does not prove exact source identity. RFF should pass a source ID plus exact revision and the current editable configuration, preserving the destination's role (coloring versus environment) independently of display conversion.

Flat-color rejection is representation-dependent: stop gradients are rejected when their uppercased color strings are all equal, while sampled-ramp gradients bypass that flatness test. Equivalent color spellings can also differ as strings. This is an application preference, not a general validity condition; a flat environment or mask can be useful in RFF and should remain editable. Both the studio reader and incoming decoder use coerceGradientConfig as a boolean gate but return the original object rather than the normalized result. A coercer that repairs/drops invalid fields is not proof that the original is safe; RFF should either retain a strictly validated exact payload or use the normalized value with explicit diagnostics.

**Bind payloads to requests.** GMT's incoming gradient uses one shared localStorage key, while the trip ID travels separately in the URL/channel. The payload has a two-minute timestamp allowance but no matching trip ID. Multiple rapid opens or studios can overwrite/consume one another's payload. Read-then-remove is not a cross-tab atomic transaction, and the storage removal helper provides no failure result, so the claimed one-shot property depends on successful storage access. RFF should use request-scoped payload IDs, acknowledgements and expiration, or an in-process typed handoff when both editors share one application.

The receiver reads/removes the incoming payload during boot preemption, caches it and consumes the cache before applying. A failure after removal has no retry record here. If favId exists locally, it uses that favorite's current config/name rather than the transmitted snapshot, so concurrent edits can change what arrives. This may be intentional live-reference behavior, but it must not be described as exact snapshot transfer. Offer a clear reference-versus-snapshot contract in RFF and only acknowledge a transfer after the intended revision is active.

**Return and recovery are different guarantees.** A matching BroadcastChannel pong establishes that a source tab answered within the 300 ms window; it does not prove that closing the editor will focus that tab or that the current scene has a durable backup. The receiver tries close, waits briefly if necessary and otherwise navigates to a fallback scene route. Returning changes no gradient directly; shared Recent entries are the documented route back into the library. The source stashes a scene before opening and warns if that backup fails, so the fallback cannot be called lossless in that case. Existing stash scoping/restore behavior requires its own code evidence, not the trip ID alone.

The source keeps a growing set of trip IDs, installs an answer channel once and discards its cleanup handle. It clears the newest trip's stash after a returned notification, but browser close/notification delivery is still lifecycle-dependent. Source comments cite historical browser measurements that were not rerun. For native RFF, track editor lifetime explicitly, use per-document backup ownership and keep a last-complete checkpoint until restoration or return is confirmed. These recommendations support 2D palette and relief/environment editing; no actual handoff, scene stash restoration or browser-close test was executed in this batch.

## Persist generator sources, not transient catalog indices

Full reads of palette/store/generatorDocument.ts and palette/store/favientsDocument.ts distinguish two RFF persistence needs: reconstructing the current authoring operation, and exchanging a shared palette library. A targeted recheck of generatorStore.ts:568 confirms that slotSnapshot returns a resolved RGB ramp and name. The generator document stores these for both sources rather than their process-local catalog indices, then re-registers them on load. This avoids restoring an index that now refers to another palette. RFF should retain stable recipe IDs and exact source data, while treating runtime catalog indices as ephemeral.

The stored slot representation contains RGB samples and names, not a separate full-precision channel payload, source stops, interpolation or catalog provenance. The previously inspected catalog can carry unclipped channels separately; that richer source is not represented explicitly by this document schema. A RFF equivalent should preserve both exact editable sources and a display preview, especially when later transforms depend on out-of-gamut values. Re-registering a byte-ramp source can also quantize and invoke the previously audited signature deduplication, so stable slot identity alone is not an exact-authoring round-trip guarantee.

**Validate curve contents, not only containers.** sanitizeRamp accepts arrays with at least 256 entries, discards the remainder and replaces missing/nonfinite RGB components with zero rather than rejecting every malformed component. It does not enforce channel bounds; the catalog registration subsequently clamps/rounds its byte preview. sanitizeTracks checks that the selected space's three track objects each have a keyframes array, but does not validate each key's frame/value/handles, ordering or size. Therefore the header's broad sampler-safety guarantee is stronger than this local gate establishes. RFF should validate each track and its domain, reject or diagnose truncation/repair, and constrain finite Detail, smoothing and seed values to their actual accepted ranges.

Invalid source ramps retain the current corresponding slot, while other generator settings are restored from defaults or valid fields. This can combine a loaded document with an unrelated live source. Decide explicitly whether RFF supports partial patches or full restoration; a full restore should stage all required source/curve data before replacing the active edit. Slot registration happens before the final history restore, so a later failure may already have altered the ad-hoc catalog. Preserve transactional ownership across both catalog and editor state.

**Shared favorites are a different document.** The favorites bridge serializes the whole library through its canonical collection exporter and merges unseen content on scene load. Its early signature check avoids repeated writes when all signatures already exist, but can also ignore changed names, grouping or provenance for otherwise equal colors. The coarse signature limitations already documented still apply. Add-only merging protects current entries from deletion, yet can resurrect items the user deliberately removed after the scene was saved. RFF should keep library import explicit and preserve scene-used palettes as local dependencies rather than embedding/restoring an unrelated entire shelf by default. Session/look snapshots already exclude favorites in GMT; retain that distinction when designing RFF's palette/environment editing. No generator round-trip or library merge test was run in this batch.

## Follow-up: scene-trip backups are reason-scoped, not trip-scoped

Re-reading the already audited engine-gmt/utils/sceneStash.ts and stashLiveScene.ts, plus the boot resolver at app-gmt/main.tsx:641, resolves an open question from the handoff review. GX backups use one global slot per reason, not one slot per trip or source tab. A later studio trip can replace another tab's backup, and a returned notification can clear the reason-wide slot. RFF should bind editor recovery checkpoints to a document and handoff ID rather than just the reason for leaving.

Capture flushes the live camera before serializing, a useful RFF pattern for keeping a recovery location synchronized with the visible view. On flush failure it falls back to the stored pose. The stash clears the previous keys before writing new scene/timestamp/dirty keys; this sacrifices the prior valid checkpoint if replacement fails. Cleanup and consume use removal without a success result, and the multi-key operations are not atomic across tabs despite all-or-nothing wording in comments. A single versioned record with atomic replacement and a retained previous checkpoint is a stronger native design.

The reader clears before parsing the GMF at boot, so a failed decode consumes the recovery copy. Its timestamp check rejects missing/zero and excessive past age but does not explicitly reject infinity or future timestamps. GX restores the stored unsaved flag; OAuth intentionally does not. Shared-scene URL handling precedes GX and OAuth restore. These are specific policies to preserve or deliberately change, not general recovery guarantees. The earlier reads already credited these files; this follow-up adds integration evidence without counting them as newly audited files. No backup/restore runtime test was performed.

## Live shader previews need explicit ownership and commit fidelity

Full reads of palette/store/paintStore.ts, gradient-explorer/v2/paint/workingPaintSink.ts and palette/store/gradientStudio.ts establish the editing-to-rendering bridge. GMT's Studio edits a gradient addressed by feature ID and parameter key and can send a temporary gradient texture directly to its uniform without updating the persisted parameter. This is a useful RFF improvement for interactive 2D palette, relief-material and environment-gradient authoring: preview adjustments immediately, then commit one coherent undoable edit. In Vulkan, the equivalent needs explicit texture/resource ownership, lifetime and synchronization rather than copying GMT's event transport.

**One source, two representations.** previewGradient publishes a preview to other editor surfaces and emits the generated texture buffer with the parameter's noAccumReset policy. It does not verify that a uniform exists before publishing the editor preview; a missing uniform can therefore leave the editor showing a preview that the renderer never received. Ending a preview attempts to resend the stored value. Rebuilding shaders or resynchronizing uniforms can replace the temporary buffer; the source header acknowledges that an unchanged editor may not resend it. RFF should maintain an effective render-state layer keyed by target/revision and replay it after pipeline or descriptor recreation. Correct accumulation invalidation must follow the visual dependency, including lighting changes.

The fast Studio preview bypasses expensive stop fitting using the held-ramp path. On commit, however, a source with stops is fitted back to stops at the Detail budget. The exact sampled preview and committed fitted representation can therefore differ. RFF should preview the final representation or retain the exact sampled texture alongside an editable approximation, reporting fit error where relevant. An untouched fitted Curves view is treated as restatement: preview uses the original config even though the derived ramp may be the fitted curve drawing. Different consumers must intentionally choose which representation they display. The destination color-space hint is restored at bake, preserving the separation between display authoring and texture encoding.

**Source revision matters during painting.** syncPaintBase compares the incoming ramp against the session-opening samples with a 0.5-channel tolerance; it is not exact identity and can ignore a small real source change. While a stroke is active it refuses to replace the base at all. This allows the stroke to finish, but the host must subsequently reconcile a changed target before commit rather than assuming the old painting is still valid. RFF should bind drafts to target ID and exact source revision, and explicitly cancel/rebase when that source changes. Discard reconstructs the original through the rounded byte-ramp path, so cancel is not necessarily a floating-point-identical reset of an initially fractional session base.

Brush persistence sanitizes enums and most numeric ranges when loading. Runtime setBrush simply merges a patch and does not apply the same validation; nonfinite stored numeric values use the lower limit rather than always the advertised default. Brush writes are debounced 300 ms without a close flush in this module. Draft painting itself is not persisted. RFF should validate the shared command boundary, separate brush preferences from recoverable drafts, and retain the exact original data for cancel.

**Commit must acknowledge the destination write.** commitPaint ends a changed stroke, rounds to a ramp, invokes the registered sink inside paramGroup and replaces its draft with a new clean session. The sink returns void, so a silent no-op is indistinguishable from a successful write. Studio writeTarget similarly does nothing when a setter is missing, after which bake can still reset the authoring controls. A single global sink assumes one host per page, which is insufficient for multiple native RFF editors. Use an owned target-specific sink returning success/revision, and clear a draft only after the intended destination accepts it. The Explorer sink first folds a live source into its editing document, then stores a ramp while retaining output-space/blend metadata; both changes need to belong to the same undo operation.

Leaving Paint calls commit and then ends the session without checking a false return. Closing Studio or switching targets also commits the active face. Cancel has face-specific behavior: resetting Adjust, dropping edited curves or discarding painting, followed by the normal leave path. A robust RFF implementation should test each transition with missing targets, concurrent edits and pending strokes, not infer behavior solely from the Apply button. Saved scene state intentionally excludes render-only previews, so save/export policy must explicitly settle or label pending edits. No shader-rebuild preview test, paint commit/cancel test or rendered preview-versus-bake comparison was executed in this batch.

## Preview publication, target selection and close ownership

Full reads of components/gradient/gradientParamPreview.ts, palette/installGradientStudio.ts, palette/store/armedTarget.ts and palette/store/heroSelection.ts refine the proposed RFF live-editing architecture. Publishing one target's temporary gradient to every display surface is useful: the rendered fractal, sidebar strip and expanded editor should agree. GMT stores preview configurations in a map keyed by feature/parameter and notifies external-store subscribers. This is an application-state mechanism supporting shader authoring, transferable to 2D coloring and environment reflection.

The preview map uses object identity for change detection and keeps references without cloning. In-place mutation followed by publishing the same object does not notify; callers therefore need immutable configurations or explicit revisions. All listeners are notified for any changed target, and cleanup depends entirely on the writer. There is no preview-owner token, scene generation or automatic clearing on document replacement. RFF should key previews by document, parameter and editor owner, reject stale updates and make owner cleanup conditional so an older editor cannot clear a newer preview. The NUL-delimited composite string assumes identifiers cannot contain that delimiter; typed tuples or nested maps avoid this assumption.

**The actual Paint sink resolves its target at commit time.** Studio installation registers a global sink that reads the current Studio target, obtains its current color-space/blend metadata and writes the supplied ramp there. This confirms that source-revision binding is not enforced by the sink itself. A missing target returns silently, and an unreadable source falls back to default metadata. RFF should capture the intended target and source revision when opening the draft and require an acknowledgement from that same destination before resetting it. Separate editors should receive separate sink instances.

The close watcher listens for a panel's open flag changing to false and queues closeGradientStudio in a microtask. It does not capture which target/face was closed or recheck whether the panel reopened before that microtask executes. Rapid close/reopen/retarget can therefore make a deferred callback operate on newer state unless the surrounding lifecycle prevents it. Repeated mounting installs subscriptions without a returned cleanup handle or idempotence guard. RFF should associate deferred commits with a generation token and use owned subscriptions; closing a window must not commit an unrelated later draft. Lazy loading keeps editor code off the initial path, but this installer alone does not prove loading-failure recovery or all close paths.

**Separate selection identity from content revision.** heroSelection keeps one remembered pick per surface plus a distinct active surface, allowing deselection to remove the active command target without blanking every preview. This is a useful interaction model for RFF palette browsing. However, equality compares only mode/key; re-picking or dragging the same key with changed config, name, provenance or destination retains the old payload. Incrementing the click serial signals a repeat action but does not refresh that payload. A stable favorite ID is not a complete content revision. RFF should preserve selection by ID while updating the resolved payload by revision, and resolve a current source again when executing a command.

The armed-slot store holds only A/B/null; it provides no consume-once operation, source-document identity or reset hook tied to a project change. Caller code must implement the documented fill-and-clear sequence. For RFF, represent 'choose a source for this slot' as a bounded editing interaction with target ownership, Escape cancellation and automatic invalidation when the document/target disappears. These files establish mechanisms and assumptions, not an observed wrong-target edit. No interaction smoke, shader-preview synchronization test or deferred-close race test was run in this batch.

## Palette filing should use explicit move/copy and ordering contracts

Full reads of palette/store/favientFiling.ts, groundSet.ts, favientsPanelPersist.ts and watchPersisted.ts suggest supporting improvements for a RFF palette/environment library. One filing command is shared by multiple drop surfaces, and insertion anchors use stable IDs rather than indices in a filtered view. This can prevent a drop from moving to the wrong position when search hides intervening items. Keep navigation preferences separate from palette documents and undoable content changes.

GMT intentionally moves an existing favorite, including one matched by content, instead of creating another copy in a second group. That is an ownership model, not ordinary multi-collection membership. RFF should state whether an action moves, copies or adds membership, especially when a library palette also serves as an environment gradient. The code's ID/content precedence is narrower than its prose: when a payload carries a stale favId, the lookup does not fall back to content. Coarse signature matching also cannot prove exact equality of authoring data. Resolve identities explicitly and retain provenance when relocating or copying a palette.

Batch filing constructs moving items in the supplied ID order, not by scanning current shelf order, despite the header claiming shelf-order preservation. Repeated input IDs can create repeated moving entries before replaceAll, and an insertion anchor is not checked to belong to the destination group. Single-item helpers share the latter assumption. RFF should deduplicate and validate IDs, decide the intended batch order and resolve the anchor within the target collection before one atomic update. The caller owns undo here; calling a shared helper alone does not establish one undo entry or successful persistence.

**Selection persistence needs normalization on read too.** groundSet normalizes writes so All is exclusive, duplicates disappear and an empty selection falls back to All. Its initial loader only filters nonempty strings from a JSON array; it does not apply the same normalization, so malformed stored combinations can enter the initial state. Unknown IDs are left to another caller. Non-array parsed values fall back to the raw stored string as a legacy ID. RFF should version legacy preference migration, normalize on both load and mutation, and reconcile missing collections against the actual library. The exposed array is mutable, so either return immutable state or copies to prevent unannounced selection changes.

**Remember placement without confusing it with visibility.** The panel helper distinguishes an open panel from one actually shown in an expanded active dock. Revealing a docked shelf respects its placement; hiding it collapses the whole dock, which also affects sibling panels. This is a product choice rather than a universal hide operation. For RFF, preserve panel placement separately from active visibility and restore floating windows inside the current monitor work area. The inspected preference loader accepts JSON fields without local numeric/enum validation or viewport clamping; downstream panel setters may impose constraints, but that is not established here.

Per-host preference keys keep layout separate while the collection remains shared. Window-state writes merge the existing view-mode field and view-mode writes merge window fields, preventing routine sibling-field deletion within one process. Read-modify-write is not conflict detection across windows. The active key is a mutable module-global value set by the last host registration, so native multi-window RFF should pass explicit per-window preference ownership rather than relying on a singleton.

**Debouncing is not durable completion.** watchPersisted gates writes on selected-object identity and captures that selected reference in a timer closure. The comment's claim to read the latest selection at flush time is not literally implemented: it does not re-run select in the timer. If selection becomes null, an existing timer is not canceled and can write stale state. In-place changes can evade the reference gate, and the helper exposes neither unsubscribe nor flush/cancel, so repeated installation accumulates watchers and quick termination can lose the last change. RFF should use owned persistence subscriptions with explicit flush/cancel, immutable revisions, failure reporting and atomic preference writes. No drop/reorder, docking, multi-window or shutdown-persistence tests were executed in this batch.

## Palette authoring state and asynchronous catalog ownership

Full reads of `palette/store/paletteEditorStore.ts`, `paletteFiltersPersist.ts`, `pickerSearch.ts`, `pickerSimilarity.ts`, `wallSelection.ts`, `pickerStore.ts`, `dragVisual.ts` and `heroPrefs.ts` establish supporting design choices for RFF's palette and proposed environment-gradient editor. These are workflow improvements, not evidence of a shader speedup or a replacement for the rendering priorities above.

**Keep the gradient document separate from scalar rendering controls.** GMT stores a complete GradientConfig outside the scalar parameter slices and provides the same capture/validated-restore functions to history and document I/O. This is a useful model for RFF: stops, interpolation metadata and a dense ramp should remain an authoring document, while exposure, rotation and intensity remain rendering parameters. Retain dense ramps when a compact stop fit is inadequate; make conversion to editable stops explicit and disclose its approximation. This applies equally to 2D fractal palettes and a gradient sampled as a 3D environment.

The editor store normalizes ordinary setConfig writes and validates snapshot restoration, but setConfig, reset and loadRamp do not themselves bracket undo. Only addStops self-brackets through paramEdit. Callers must therefore provide a command boundary for a complete gesture or import. Invalid restored data is silently ignored, leaving the existing document in place; this helper alone does not establish an all-or-nothing project restore. RFF should share validated capture/restore between undo and serialization, return restoration outcomes, and ensure a palette plus its shader parameters form one transaction when they are edited together. Do not assume a successful no-op means the requested document loaded.

**Separate preferences from transient navigation.** The layout whitelist persists swatch size, padding, grouping, sorting, rows and reverse order, while search and similarity anchors are module-local and reset on a page reload. This avoids unexpectedly hiding the library after restarting. RFF can persist layout independently from a fractal file and keep a clearly visible, cancellable search/similarity state. These module-local stores do not automatically reset on an in-process document or catalog replacement, so that lifecycle still needs an explicit policy. Similarity holds the supplied config reference; it does not bind to a source revision or clone the document.

The preference whitelist restricts field names, not their values: restorePaletteFilters passes selected values to another setter without local type/range/enum validation. heroPrefs similarly spreads parsed JSON over defaults without validating enlarged as a boolean; a string value such as "false" is truthy in the height selector. Neither helper provides a durable-save acknowledgement. For RFF, validate at the preference boundary, normalize legacy values and keep a recoverable default. The shared module slot synchronizes mounted consumers in one context, not independently running windows. The layout watcher also inherits the previously documented watchPersisted flush/cancel and reference-gating limitations.

**Stable selection snapshots reduce unnecessary preview work.** wallSelection compares set membership before publishing a new snapshot, so a no-op selection change need not invalidate every visible swatch. Its IDs should be reconciled with the current collection before batch commands; the helper does not validate their existence or own a document generation. Object.freeze on a JavaScript Set does not prevent mutation of its internal entries through add/delete/clear; ReadonlySet is a compile-time interface rather than runtime immutability. Preserve the useful stable-reference contract with encapsulated ownership instead of relying on freezing alone. The source mentions selection tests, but they were not run in this batch.

**Lazy catalog loading needs desired-state and request revisions.** pickerStore merges groups in registry order and assigns packed sprite rows after every merge. Copying live-source entry objects before changing row protects those source objects' row fields, although nested ramps remain shared. RFF should distinguish permanent palette IDs from temporary GPU texture rows and publish the row mapping and corresponding texture as one revision. Theme chip colors here are averages of the middle encoded ramp samples; they are display hints, not a perceptual summary or a lighting-energy estimate.

Both ordinary and live group loading can finish after a caller requested unloading: the off path returns when the group has not yet entered _groups, and the completion path has no desired-enabled check or generation token. Live refreshes can also overlap and apply out of order. Unloading then reloading does not distinguish an older refresh from the new incarnation when the old promise completes. In RFF, maintain the latest desired enabled state and a monotonically increasing request revision, discard outdated completions and commit decoded content only if ownership still matches. This matters when large environment images or external palette libraries finish loading after the user has chosen a different source.

An empty initial live load and a failed load both become failedGroups, disabling another attempt through this store for the remainder of the session. An empty live refresh, conversely, leaves the previous entries visible because take returns false; it does not publish an empty collection. RFF should distinguish loading, a valid empty collection, temporary failure and stale retained content, and provide retry without requiring a restart. Core fallback is installed directly as catalog rather than in _groups, so a later rebuild can replace that fallback with only the currently populated groups; usingFallback is not reset by rebuild. Model fallback as an explicit source with consistent metadata, rather than as an alternate one-time assignment. These are source-level lifecycle observations, not reproduced network failures.

**A drag preview is not command authority.** dragVisual separates the in-flight payload from hero selection, allowing a drag preview without changing the selected palette. Its end fallback clears state on a mousemove only after more than 200 ms without dragover; no autonomous timer performs that cleanup. Any captured dragover refreshes the timestamp, a repeated begin while active does not reseed it, and this module has no explicit Escape/blur cleanup. The payload is cleared by clearNativeDrag only when its active flag was set. Historical browser behavior described in comments was not independently verified. RFF should use an owned drag session with explicit cancellation and resolve the current source and destination again before a move or deletion. A visual timeout or payload containing a favorite ID is insufficient authorization for a destructive operation.

Recommended acceptance checks for an eventual RFF implementation are: undo one continuous stop drag in one step; preserve a dense ramp until explicit conversion; change source while a load is pending; complete two refreshes in reverse order; publish an empty live library; retry after failure; and cancel a drag after its source disappears. No application code was changed, and no rendering, interaction or performance tests were executed for this batch.

## Preserve authoring channels through generation, fitting and preview

Full reads of `palette/store/generatorStore.ts` (795 lines), `palette/store/fullscreenStore.ts` (313 lines) and `gradient-explorer/v2/SourceBands.tsx` (143 lines) strengthen the palette/environment-authoring recommendations. These mechanisms can support both 2D iteration coloring and the proposed 3D-style environment reflection on RFF relief. They do not establish that RFF should copy GMT's complete editor or its storage formats.

**Preserve unclipped channels, not just the swatch.** Generator slots can carry unclipped L/C/h arrays; slotChannels copies those arrays when present instead of decomposing the display RGB ramp. bakeSlot applies modifiers in that channel representation and registers the result as custom channels before resetting the slot controls. This avoids an unnecessary gamut-clipped RGB round trip during editing. RFF should keep an explicit authoring representation and derive its display texture from it, so lowering chroma after an extreme edit can recover information that a clipped intermediate would have discarded. This is a color-authoring improvement; it does not change perturbation or MPA precision.

The persistence boundary is narrower: slotSnapshot saves the display RGB ramp and name, not the original channel arrays. Consequently, source-code comments claiming exact slot restoration should not be read as proof that out-of-gamut authoring values survive saving and loading. History captures catalog indices and assumes that catalog remains available in the same session. For RFF, store stable source identity, authoring channels or the complete recipe, conversion version and random seed as appropriate. Preserve the existing RFF recipe IDs and RNG order; introduce any new recipe format through an explicit compatible extension. Preview equality and continued-editing equivalence are different acceptance criteria.

**Preview an approximation before committing it.** fitChannelsToTracks converts once into the chosen authoring space, uses each channel's own error scale, detects flat runs and selects stepped fitting for banded sources. Smoothing is disabled when such runs are found. The detail setting also changes the minimum recognized run length, so a short band can cease to be classified as a hold at lower detail. Prospective curve values and key positions use the same fitter as the fitting action. RFF could show the original ramp and the proposed editable approximation together, preserving hard palette boundaries unless smoothing is explicitly requested. Record approximation error against the displayed result as well as channel-space error; a shared fitting implementation alone is not a proof of perceptual accuracy.

Changing curve space samples the current curves in the previous space and refits those samples into the new one, rather than merely relabeling axes. This preserves the intended edited source better than refitting the unedited input, but repeated switches can still accumulate approximation. The implementation enables curves after a refit even if they were previously off; with no base it can change the space without replacing old tracks. RFF should distinguish changing editor coordinates from enabling an effect, retain an authoritative source for reversible space changes, and update the space and compatible tracks atomically. Reject invalid detail/smooth values at the command boundary; these setters do not locally bound them.

**Use one color-space conversion path for every consumer.** The exported sampleCurves resolves keys for the chosen space and converts sampled tracks back into pipeline L/C/h. In contrast, useGeneratorDerived directly reads tracks.L, tracks.C and tracks.h without consulting curveSpace. trackToRamp dereferences track.keyframes, so incompatible keys are not protected at that older call site. The newer useSampledCurves path uses the shared conversion correctly. SourceBands still invokes useGeneratorDerived for stripA/stripB, so the older hook cannot be treated as entirely unreachable merely because the main Working result uses another pipeline. This is a static path discrepancy, not a reproduced UI failure. For RFF, derive a source strip through a narrow source-only function and share the same validated space conversion for preview, export and commit.

**Bake is not automatically lossless.** bakeMainToCurve starts from unclipped final channels but fits Bezier tracks, whereas fitChannelsToTracks has an explicit stepped-band path. The former therefore does not itself preserve every discontinuity or sample exactly. It also reads fullResult, whose ColorBox branch returns the sweep directly, and then resets global modifiers. RFF should define bake separately for each mode, compare the resulting rendered ramp before accepting it and keep a dense representation whenever the fit cannot meet the declared tolerance. fitFromSource and fitCurvesFromRamp do not explicitly reset tracksEdited, unlike fitFromChannels; resetAll leaves several non-scalar values intact. These details reinforce the need for explicit command contracts rather than inferring behavior from names such as Reset all or Fit.

**History needs both restoration state and meaningful-change state.** GMT captures tracksEdited with the curves so Undo can restore whether closing the editor should bake them, but excludes that flag from the comparison deciding whether to create an entry. This avoids history steps for a bookkeeping-only transition. RFF can use the same distinction for preview ownership and draft status, provided every actual change in the rendered document still produces the expected undo state. The capture function returns track references and restore casts a snapshot directly; cloning/validation must therefore be guaranteed by the history infrastructure, not assumed from this provider alone. Export-format selection is deliberately outside this undo capture.

## Share the actual rendered ramp with secondary previews

fullscreenStore exposes a host-resolved source containing both its gradient configuration and, optionally, the actual rendered ramp. That distinction is valuable for RFF: an environment preview, palette strip and final fractal should not independently refit a processed ramp and then disagree. Publish a single immutable result revision with its color-space, transfer-function and precision metadata. SourceBands provides a compact before/after view, and keeping the source can cancel an operation through a caller-supplied callback; these are useful ways to make palette changes reviewable without altering fractal computation.

The store's rampToLut converts to a 256-entry RGBA8 array by nearest-index resampling and direct byte assignment. It assumes a nonempty ramp, does not check finite/range validity and does not round or clamp before assignment; fractional values are truncated and out-of-range integers can wrap through byte conversion. This is a display-LUT packing seam, not a suitable general HDR environment upload. RFF should validate inputs and choose the intended texture format explicitly. An environment used for lighting may need linear floating-point radiance, while a palette preview may intentionally use display-referred bytes. Do not treat the same numerical RGB triplet as interchangeable between those roles.

The fullscreen interface calls its input a snapshot, but open/set retain the supplied config reference. Closing clears config while retaining resolved source, interaction state and geometry. Updating the config likewise does not immediately clear resolved. The overlay may manage the remaining lifecycle, but this store alone does not guarantee it. RFF should bind published preview results to their source revision, release stale GPU resources on close and ensure an abandoned interaction cannot leave the next preview in reduced-quality mode. setFullscreenResolved deduplicates by identity, so in-place ramp mutation would also evade its change notification.

Batching a two-axis geometry update into one emission prevents subscribers observing a half-updated position. Split-divider input is finite-checked and bounded; geometry patches only check finiteness and rely on TypeScript for key names and downstream code for domain constraints. The global live-source hook setter does not notify subscribers, matching its documented boot-registration expectation rather than supporting arbitrary hot replacement. Carry these ownership assumptions explicitly into a native multi-window RFF design.

The interacting flag is intended to let the renderer reduce preview resolution while dragging and restore it afterward. This file exposes that signal but does not prove the renderer performs the transition. Any RFF adaptation should preserve full-precision fractal data, make temporary display quality explicit and restore full-quality output after release/cancellation and before export. Dither is also only a toggle here; its actual shader mechanism was reviewed separately. No render, fit-error benchmark, history test or interactive smoke was executed in this batch; test claims in source comments remain historical evidence rather than new verification.

## Responsive editing without reducing fractal precision

A full read of `palette/store/workingStore.ts` (812 lines), with a targeted cross-check of runWorkingPipeline in the previously reviewed `palette/core/workingPipeline.ts`, identifies an actionable responsiveness improvement for RFF: update the actual color ramp during a gesture, but defer rebuilding editable control points until the gesture ends. This is CPU authoring work, not a faster fractal shader. It can make both 2D palette editing and a gradient-driven environment-light editor more responsive without reducing perturbation precision or changing MPA.

The reactive derive passes its last fitted configuration as holdFit while either palette-owned parameter dragging or the engine interaction flag is active. The pipeline continues to calculate the live ramp and recolors the retained stop positions; it does not simply freeze the old colors. On release it fits again and records the resulting configuration. The imperative derive used by commands always passes no held fit, so applying or exporting can obtain a fresh result. RFF should preserve this separation explicitly: a current rendered result, a provisional editing representation and a committed document are distinct states with revisions. A save/export command must resolve the current result rather than serialize a cached provisional fit.

Each hook instance has its own lastFit and memoization. The ref is not cleared when input becomes empty or a different input is selected, so a source switch during an active interaction can offer a fit from a previous source. Passthrough/restated paths bypass it, but other paths can reuse its topology. Scope the cache to the source/document revision and clear it on replacement. Also avoid running a complete generator and image extraction derive in every consumer when only one input kind is active: this hook subscribes to both producer paths before choosing a base. Sharing a derived-result cache keyed by actual dependencies is a candidate for RFF; performance improvement remains unmeasured.

**A fold must reset precisely what it incorporates.** The Working input is a tagged choice among a fixed gradient, live Build, live image extraction, editable stops or empty. beginEdit materializes the current output into the stops document, turns curves off and resets the main adjustment chain inside one parameter-history bracket. An untouched input or untouched fitted curve can retain a clone of the original gradient config instead of accumulating another lossy fit. Adding stops is a separate explicit conversion. This model could let RFF users move from a generated palette to manual editing without applying phase, repeats or contrast twice. Keep the complete source recipe available when reversibility is promised.

**Structural return is not a complete historical snapshot here.** BakedFrom stores the input, name, main adjustment keys, tracks, enabled state and curve space. It omits tracksEdited, noise frequency/targets/seed, fitting controls, generator slot state and image source state. A build/extract input is a live tag, so returning to it resolves the producer's current state, not necessarily the state at folding. A remembered stops input similarly refers to the shared stops store rather than carrying its own config. Re-folding retains the earliest fold memory. These are useful return-to-source semantics only if described accurately; they are not evidence of exact restoration of every pre-edit pixel. RFF should decide between returning to the current live source and restoring an immutable source revision, then implement that contract explicitly.

cancelLive and returnToSource restore the fields captured by BakedFrom but do not restore tracksEdited. cancelFace clears curves and resets MAIN_DEFAULTS, whereas selecting a new gradient through use resets the larger ADJUST_FACE_DEFAULTS, optionally fitting fresh untouched curves in the same bracket. setInput is a still narrower operation: it does not clone/validate the input or clear all naming, live-source or modifier state. For RFF, centralize user-visible commands rather than exposing these differently scoped setters interchangeably. A reset, cancel, replacement and bake need separate documented outcomes and tests covering both rendered colors and subsequent editing behavior.

**Recent history should follow a work session without polluting edit history.** GMT associates a working session with one Recent entry, updates that entry through injected collector/updater functions and pins a palette picked from Recent until it changes. The unchanged-pick check includes ramp samples, avoiding the mistake of treating all ramp gradients with empty stop lists as equal. Deferred synchronization runs outside parameter transactions through a stable callback identity, reducing history entries caused only by background collection. This is applicable to RFF palette exploration: preserve the source favorite, keep meaningful variants and avoid adding an undo step merely because an autosave timer fired during a cancelled drag.

The store catches collector/updater exceptions and converts them to null. That protects editing but does not distinguish a missing entry from a storage/service failure; after a failed update it can attempt collection. Direct syncRecent is intentionally allowed inside an undo bracket for commands that immediately use the collection, and its side effects therefore differ from the deferred path. Resolve these outcomes explicitly in RFF and report persistence failure without blocking color editing. The deferred callback reads the current working state when executed rather than capturing the earlier document; bind it to a session revision if an old document must be flushed before replacement. The actual date-rollover and collection-write behavior belongs to favientsStore and is not established solely by this caller.

**Validate complete restoration dependencies.** coerceWorkingSnapshot checks the input kind and uses the gradient validator, but accepts curve tracks when the space's three properties are objects without validating their keyframe arrays. Adjustment validation checks JavaScript types rather than finiteness or ranges. Build seeds are filtered and positions clamped, but their count is not capped and bias is only finite-checked. RFF should validate nested curve data and numeric domains, cap imported collections and validate every referenced producer document before publishing a restored Working state. Capture uses JSON cloning, while the same snapshot includes liveFrom, sessionId and sessionPinned for both history and document serialization; the older header's shorter field list is incomplete. The separate session loader's clearing of transient collection IDs must remain part of the round-trip contract.

**Do not confuse exact provenance with appearance similarity.** configKey compares structural JSON of stops, color/blend spaces and ramp data, so it is not a rendered-color equivalence test. Reordered object properties or alternative authoring representations can differ despite the same visible result. Conversely, provenance used to identify an unmodified catalog item should not imply that a temporary curve-fit drawing is exactly the original: the pipeline's restated path deliberately returns the original config while its live ramp can be the fitted drawing. RFF should keep immutable attribution/ancestry separately from an exact-unmodified marker and a visual-similarity score. Adapting this mechanism does not remove licensing or NOTICE obligations.

Swatch positions are viewer preferences, validated as finite values, clamped and sorted on load; the rule label does not replace the actual positions. This supports user-chosen sampling points without changing the fractal palette. Position moves currently write preferences immediately, so a native implementation should coalesce disk writes and flush on a defined lifecycle boundary while updating the display immediately. No timing, rendered-color comparison, Undo/Redo or save/restore experiment was run for this batch. Proposed acceptance cases include a source switch mid-drag, a no-op curve visit, repeated bake/return cycles, a noise-setting change before cancel, a Recent update failure and exporting while the control-point fit is held.

## Keep exploration history separate from deliberately saved palettes

A full read of `palette/store/favientsStore.ts` (908 lines) completes the current palette/store source batch and verifies the collection side of the preceding Working-session analysis. The transferable feature is a palette library with automatic exploration history, explicit saved favorites and portable authoring documents. In RFF this could serve both 2D color exploration and environment-gradient presets for relief shading. The library mechanism itself does not improve shader quality; it helps retain and compare the results of shader/palette tuning.

**Use different retention policies for automatic and explicit saves.** GMT caps auto-collected Recent entries at 60 when collectRecent runs, while add redirects a deliberate save away from Recent into a user/default group. Removing a group rehomes its palettes rather than deleting them. The automatic collector also leaves content already kept in a user group alone. These are useful defaults for RFF: exploration may be bounded, but an explicit save should not disappear when the automatic history fills. Keep the capacity visible and provide an export/backup path. The cap is enforced by collection, not universally by import, bulk insertion or every mutation; a later collection can truncate a larger imported Recent run.

**Daily history has narrower guarantees than an immutable archive.** updateRecent leaves an unchanged signature/name alone and creates a fresh entry when a changed session resumes from an earlier local day. For a same-day update, matching Recent duplicates that are not earlier than today are removed; future-dated entries also satisfy that condition if the clock moved backward. collectRecent without fresh promotes a matching entry by replacing its timestamp with the current time, including an older day's entry. Explicit rename, deletion and moves remain possible. Consequently, the daily-preservation rule applies to the session-update path, not every operation. RFF should distinguish a mutable recent-work list from immutable checkpoints and decide how timezone or clock changes affect day grouping.

**Do not deduplicate valuable edits using a coarse similarity key.** favientSig rounds stop positions and bias to thousandths, includes color/interpolation/blend space and omits colorSpace intentionally. Ramp signatures use the ramp string. Thus two valid stop configurations can differ in a meaningful fine adjustment while receiving the same signature. updateRecent can return early without applying such a change when the name also matches; collect and import can reuse or skip it. Conversely, differences in representation can produce distinct keys for visually equivalent ramps. For RFF, use canonical exact authoring identity for destructive deduplication, and reserve approximate rendered/perceptual similarity for optional grouping or suggestions. A claim about equivalent displayed colors is not a general license to ignore transfer-function metadata in an environment-lighting asset.

Promotion retains the matched Recent entry's existing config, name and source, optionally adding origin metadata only when missing. A merge also ignores duplicate entries' alternative names, group membership and provenance, and a merge with no fresh content returns before merging labels. These choices may be acceptable for a small browsing shelf but should be explicit in RFF import previews: report which entries will be added, matched, renamed or kept separately. Preserve immutable source attribution separately from the marker used to identify an unmodified catalog preset.

**Loading old data should preserve recoverable content without treating it as render-ready.** GMT's local-storage load gate deliberately retains stop-less configurations whose ramp a particular build may not understand, avoiding silent deletion on the next save. The import decoder is stricter. This is a useful forward-compatibility idea for RFF: retain unsupported entries in a recoverable form and disable applying them until validated, rather than deleting them or feeding unknown values to the GPU. The local gate checks ID, stops array, color string and finite stop position, but does not fully validate name, timestamp, group, color syntax, ranges or ramp encoding. Group-label loading likewise accepts an object without validating string values. Use separate preservation and rendering-validation states.

Stop-ID healing supports old authoring documents without discarding them. It does not establish uniqueness of favorite IDs, and the timestamp-plus-module-counter newId/newGroupId scheme is not a proof of uniqueness across independently running windows created in the same millisecond. RFF should use durable globally unique item IDs and validate duplicates on import. Several typed producer operations normalize rather than deeply clone or validate input; replaceAll and history restore trust their callers. Keep ownership and validation at a shared command boundary.

**Organize groups independently of incidental flat-array order.** GMT represents each group as a contiguous run. Merge consolidates Recent and sorts it by local day, placing new entries after an existing group's last member. It does not consolidate arbitrary already-split non-Recent groups; replacement only consolidates Recent while preserving the rest's order. moveFavient and insertFavient delegate group/index consistency to callers. For RFF, explicit group membership and a separate ordering field avoid making display correctness depend on every caller maintaining contiguous runs. If a flat representation is retained, normalize and validate it before committing a batch.

**Shared storage notifications are not conflict resolution.** The storage listener and focus reload make another window's collection visible, but every mutation saves a whole array from its current in-memory state. There is no revision comparison, merge log or lock in this store. Two writers or a local Undo restoring an old whole-shelf snapshot can overwrite another window's newer work. Palette entries and labels are written as separate keys, so they are not committed as one transaction. RFF should use a transactional library document or database, per-operation revisions and conflict-aware Undo, especially if multiple rendering windows share a palette/environment library.

Persistence helpers return no success to these commands, so an ID/count return and a changed visible shelf do not confirm durable storage. A later reload can replace unsaved memory with older disk data. The one-time preset seed flag is written separately from entries/labels; a partial failure can leave the flag inconsistent with the stored collection. Preserve failed edits in memory, expose a recoverable persistence error and mark seeding complete only after its transaction succeeds. No storage failure or multi-window race was reproduced here; these are guarantees absent from the inspected implementation.

The history provider returns references to the current array/labels and relies on its host to clone them; restore accepts an array without full entry validation and writes the entire snapshot through to storage. This is suitable only for trusted, isolated snapshots under the surrounding history contract. RFF should test Undo after an external library update and after a failed save, not just ordinary in-window Undo/Redo. Suggested feature acceptance checks also include sub-thousandth stop edits, recollecting yesterday's palette, import beyond the Recent cap, an unreadable future-format entry, duplicate IDs, and deleting a collection while retaining its palettes. No new runtime tests were executed in this batch.

## Match preview encoding and sampling across every palette surface

Full reads of `palette/components/GradientStrip.tsx`, `GradientHoverPreview.tsx`, `GradientDragAvatar.tsx` and `CanonicalHero.tsx`, with a recheck of the already reviewed canonical sampler re-export, show why sharing color-generation code is necessary but insufficient for matching previews. RFF should use a common generated ramp plus explicit display-encoding and sampling contracts for its palette strip, drag preview, material preview and final shader input. This applies directly to 2D palettes and to proposed environment gradients; an environment's radiance representation must still remain distinct from its display preview.

**Treat discontinuities as authoring information.** GradientStrip calls a ramp banded when at least 60 percent of adjacent rounded RGB samples match. It uses nearest-neighbor scaling plus pixelated CSS rendering for those ramps and smoothing for other ramps. This preserves many deliberately posterized boundaries, but the heuristic is not a proof that a ramp is intended to be stepped: a smooth low-contrast byte ramp can contain many equal neighbors, while a ramp with a few important discontinuities can fail the threshold. RFF should carry interpolation/discontinuity metadata from the authoring document where possible. During minification, integrate the pixel footprint to prevent aliasing rather than globally forcing nearest-neighbor sampling. Distinguish preserving an intended edge during magnification from correctly averaging unresolved bands during minification.

GradientStrip uses a fixed 512-pixel canvas backing width and accepts exactly 256 source samples; its display size can differ through CSS. It creates a temporary canvas and ImageData on each ramp/height update. By contrast, the hover preview and drag avatar size their backing canvas using devicePixelRatio. Neither observes pixel-ratio changes independently of its effect dependencies. RFF can share cached texture resources and react to actual viewport/DPI changes, avoiding repeated allocation while retaining the right sampling at different monitor scales. These are implementation opportunities, not measured allocation or frame-time savings.

**Byte conversion must agree too.** GradientStrip assigns into ImageData's clamped byte array, while the previously reviewed fullscreen rampToLut assigns into an ordinary Uint8Array. Fractional and out-of-range values therefore need not be converted identically. Define rounding, clamping and the valid numerical range once at the display-upload boundary. Prefer a higher-precision working representation and only quantize when the destination requires it. A shared sampler does not remove discrepancies introduced afterward by texture packing or scaling.

The avatar explicitly requests sRGB output from generateGradientTextureBuffer and always enables image smoothing. CanonicalHero accepts a supplied ramp unchanged or falls back to renderGradientToRamp using the config's own colorSpace. The canonical palette sampler module re-exports the engine sampler rather than keeping a second copy, which is a useful architecture, but these consumers still select different encoding/sampling policies. For RFF, provide an explicit display-ramp API and a separate shader-data API, with the transfer function named in their types or metadata. Verify the complete CPU/GPU path using the same test palettes. Do not blindly force sRGB on environment lighting data merely because that fixes a canvas preview.

**Make drag feedback independent of document selection and expensive regeneration.** GradientDragAvatar reads the dedicated drag payload and updates cursor position from captured dragover events. Its texture painting depends on config identity and the first available position, so ordinary position changes do not rebake the image. This is a useful split for RFF: move a lightweight overlay while retaining a cached palette texture. The avatar is not displayed until a dragover supplies coordinates, and its placement is not viewport-clamped. The hover overlay clamps coordinates and flips its tooltip, but does not shrink an oversized preview and only recomputes on hover-object changes. These are source-level lifecycle boundaries; no browser behavior or visual interaction was tested in this batch.

**Resolve saved identity before executing a command.** CanonicalHero's saved state finds the first signature match anywhere in the shelf, including Recent, and its star removes that ID on a second click. It is therefore not a separate explicit-kept-membership flag. With the coarse signature discussed above, a content-similar entry can determine the action. This component calls add/remove directly without a local undo bracket and passes a source label but no catalog-origin object. RFF should resolve exact item identity at command time, distinguish automatic history from deliberate favorites and carry provenance through every save path.
