**Share frame state, but define cross-pass sample identity.** WorkerExporter applies camera, offsets, modulation and time once, then renders the requested passes. Each pass clears its own ping-pong history, blends samples with 1/(s+1), uses a centered first sample and Halton bases 2 and 3 thereafter. A session-wide internal frame counter continues across samples and passes. Therefore matching jitter does not prove identical stochastic samples across beauty and alpha if another shader input depends on that counter. RFF should define random/sample identity explicitly from export frame, pixel and sample, with pass identity included only when intentionally different. This helps masks line up with color at fine boundaries, and supports consistent 2D palette/noise animation as well as relief material outputs.

The caller supplies time; this class does not derive timeline time from output fps. It sets the camera aspect from output dimensions and synchronizes the engine before drawing. It also resizes the ordinary pipeline even though export owns separate accumulation targets. For RFF, inventory all export allocations and shared mutable uniforms, then give an export job an immutable frame snapshot and explicit ownership. Reuse valid fractal fields where appropriate, rather than copying the 3D renderer's entire per-pass computation structure.

**Keep visual auxiliary outputs distinct from numerical maps.** Accumulation targets are FloatType, but every pass is resolved into an unsigned-byte target and read into Uint8Array. PNG combines beauty RGB with the alpha pass's red channel; depth is a separate grayscale file. Video uses RGBX, so an alpha pass is a separate visual mask video, not transparency in the beauty stream. These are useful compositing features, but the depth path is quantized to eight bits before encoding, including for PNG. RFF should retain its lossless map contract and use an explicitly designed higher-precision field export for iteration values or relief heights. An attractive grayscale preview cannot substitute for numerical data.

The class supplies depthMin/depthMax defaults of 0 and 5 to uniforms, clarifying the configuration binding left open in VideoExportTypes; final normalization still belongs to the shader. It skips appearance bloom on auxiliary passes and resets the pass selector for preview/cleanup. This illustrates a useful general rule: data outputs bypass appearance effects. The preview reads the last pass's accumulation texture through the display material rather than replaying the encoded bytes, so it is a rendering preview, not verification of codec, quantization or color-management results. VideoFrame explicitly labels bytes with BT.709 metadata; matching that label to the shader's actual transfer function needs an end-to-end check.

**Make progress and cancellation reflect completed work.** Long sample loops emit heartbeats after a synchronous one-pixel readback, scheduling later beats from measured elapsed time. This is more meaningful than reporting only submitted draws, but a heartbeat cannot arrive during one long sample, and the synchronous loop does not yield to incoming cancellation messages. RFF can use GPU completion/timestamp information and bounded submission batches to report useful progress without repeatedly draining the whole queue. Distinguish a slow in-flight operation from a dead worker; no real-GPU timing claims were validated here.

EXPORT_FRAME_DONE follows frame rendering/encoder submission or image-write scheduling, not durable saving. Image passes are copied into queued per-frame buffers, and a serialized promise chain overlaps file I/O with later renders. Neither that chain nor the video/audio submission paths impose a local backlog budget. A RFF pipeline should bound outstanding bytes as well as frame counts, especially with several full-resolution passes. Audio is submitted in 1024-frame chunks, but all chunks are queued in one loop before flush; chunk size alone does not bound queue memory.

**Require a session-wide success result.** Image write errors are caught and reported, allowing the chain to resolve and finish to later emit EXPORT_COMPLETE. Audio mux errors are logged without a persistent failure flag, while video mux errors invoke cancel. These outcomes need a unified RFF session result listing failed/missing outputs so a later completion cannot erase evidence of failure. Capture encoder and filesystem errors, close or abort writers in guaranteed cleanup, and report success only after all requested outputs finalize.

Cancellation drops the current session and disposes its render targets; already queued image closures retain their session and can continue writing. Audio encoder closure is not part of cancel/cleanup. Callback handlers look up the current session rather than receiving an immutable originating-session token, so callback ownership must be checked when cancelling and starting another export. finish also calls cleanup against the current field after asynchronous waits. For RFF, bind every completion to its originating job, make cancellation/draining explicit and prevent an old job from publishing results or releasing a newer job's resources. Initial allocations occur before this.session is assigned, so startup failures likewise need scoped cleanup. The full-screen pass's geometry and private post-processing resources require lifetime ownership beyond simply disposing the three listed targets.

The audio finish sequence checks audioFlushed before awaiting the muxer chain, although that chain starts the audio pump asynchronously. The file alone does not establish that the pump has started before the check. Use an explicit startup/completion barrier and await all producers before finalizing their shared sink. Per-track timestamp subtraction also does not by itself prove correct codec priming compensation or audio/video synchronization; verify impulses and known frame boundaries in decoded output before adopting a correction.

**Use timeline names and an explicit overwrite policy.** exportFrameFileNumber maps a contiguous export index to startFrame+index*frameStep, keeping filenames aligned with the timeline while video timestamps remain contiguous. This is useful for resumable RFF image sequences. It does not guarantee that different ranges never collide: overlapping ranges, repeated runs and the same basename still address the same files. File creation here supplies no conflict policy. Preflight a concrete output manifest and choose resume/replace/new-destination behavior explicitly. Validate finite integer inputs consistently; the naming helper floors startFrame while session frame-count setup does not.

Finally, image dimensions are rounded down to even values too, and scale/sample inputs are assumed valid rather than validated here. Export accumulation always requests full-float linear-filtered targets, independently of the interactive pipeline's format chooser. RFF should preserve exact requested image dimensions where its format permits, validate allocation limits before allocating, and retain required precision when selecting supported image/filter combinations. Acceptance checks should include pass-edge alignment, slow disk backpressure, one failed image write, audio startup during finish, cancel/restart, odd image dimensions, resumed numbering and decoded color/rate checks. No export was run during this batch.

## Export frame driver: preserve clocks and state across all requested passes

The full `engine-gmt/components/timeline/RenderPopup/exportRunner.ts` (525 lines), its 27-line exportHelpers wrapper and the common 55-line exportHelpers module have now been read. The already-reviewed exportModulations module was reread to connect the frame driver to uniform dispatch. This supplies the main-thread orchestration evidence missing from the preceding WorkerExporter section; proxy/worker message handling remains a separate dependency.

**GMT's frame driver distinguishes the two clocks.** It computes timelineFrame from the requested start and step, evaluates time using cfg.fps, and separately sends config.fps=cfg.fps/max(1,frameStep) to the worker. Consequently, the demo caller's previously identified output-rate/modulation discrepancy must not be attributed to this GMT implementation. The remaining boundary to verify is the plugin configuration supplying cfg.fps. For RFF, retain this explicit timeline/output separation in a validated export plan rather than passing similarly named rate fields whose meaning depends on the caller. The driver uses the unnormalized step for frame counting and timeline advancement, while the worker floors/clamps it in other places; establish a single finite integer value before starting either side.

The driver awaits renderExportFrame for each frame. This bounds outstanding render requests from this loop, but not the worker's queued encodes or file writes: FRAME_DONE there precedes their finalization. RFF should retain sequential or bounded render submission while also applying independent byte limits to downstream stages. Camera/offset/render-state are serialized after scrubbing and modulation, and the interaction hold signal is forced off for export. This is useful for exporting a fixed frame independently of viewport interaction state.

**Make replayed passes deterministic, including feedback.** Video creates a new session for every selected pass and reruns the frame pump; image sequences render all passes inside one frame session. Focus lock updates optics after receiving a measured distance, affecting later frames rather than the frame just rendered. Only beauty video enables this feedback, whereas the image-sequence caller enables it even when no beauty pass was selected; the worker's image path updates its distance probe only on beauty. A stale positive distance can therefore be consumed unless another owner establishes freshness. For RFF, return a validity/generation-tagged measurement and define whether focus is authored animation, an offline precomputed trajectory or intentional previous-frame feedback. Capture the same resolved focus trajectory for beauty and auxiliary passes so alpha/depth files align with color. This concern transfers to any 2D effect driven by measured field statistics, not just 3D depth of field.

The runner pauses playback and restores the saved timeline frame in finally, an improvement over the demo loop. It does not snapshot all scene settings, live modulation state or feedback-controlled optics. It clears modulation offsets on exit rather than restoring an earlier snapshot. RFF should explicitly define the export-owned state and restore or recompute it on every terminal outcome. General live editing and stateful modulation still require ownership beyond pausing timeline playback. The shared modulation dispatcher is useful for preview/export parity, but exportModulations skips near-zero offsets and omits removed-target cleanup; check that every frame restores the relevant base values before assuming transitions through zero cannot leave stale uniforms.

**Describe partial output honestly.** Finish-early finalizes the current video pass and stops the outer pass loop, so later requested passes do not exist. Image finish-early drains existing writes. The final status still uses general completion wording, without an output manifest identifying the actual frame range and skipped passes. RFF should report completed ranges/files, incomplete requests and cancellation separately. Audio is mixed for the original beauty range before rendering; early finish needs a matching trim policy or explicit treatment of the longer audio track. The mix helper and final container timing need separate verification before making a duration claim.

Audio mixing exceptions are logged and video proceeds silently; the comment also mentions encoder failures, but encoder startup happens outside that catch. Do not generalize the fallback to all audio failures. RFF should make omission of requested audio visible in the result. Likewise, disk-picker failures can trigger a RAM fallback here; a large export needs a memory-budget decision rather than assuming the alternative is affordable. Per-pass save-picker calls occur after long asynchronous work, so the comment claiming preserved transient activation is not evidence of browser support. No browser behavior was tested in this batch.

**Close the full lifecycle, not only the dialog.** Both outer catches report errors and the finally blocks restore UI state, but they do not themselves cancel an active worker export or close/abort an acquired file stream on every exceptional path. The proxy may perform some cleanup; that must be checked before concluding the entire path is safe or broken. RFF should make job ownership explicit so a dismissed dialog cannot leave a renderer paused for export, a writer open or late callbacks attached to a new job. A triggered browser download is also not proof of durable saving.

The progress helper estimates remaining time as total outstanding frames times the cumulative mean and displays an arbitrary plus/minus ten percent. This is a heuristic band, not a confidence interval. The caller labels cumulative mean time as last-frame time and includes pauses in elapsed time. RFF can improve useful feedback by separating render, paused and finalization time, using recent measured costs and indicating that future fractal frames can vary greatly. Multi-pass progress should include remaining passes and pending saves. Runtime/export comparisons and actual disk/codec tests remain unperformed; these are source-grounded design conditions for RFF.

## Audio-driven shader controls: time-based analysis and reproducible export

Full reads of `engine/features/audioMod/dsp/autoGain.ts`, `bandAnalyser.ts`, `spectrumFrame.ts`, `fft.ts` and `engine/features/audioMod/bandMath.ts` establish the numerical analysis core. The previously read `engine/animation/audioExportMix.ts` was revisited against the newly inspected video frame driver. RFF could use this architecture for optional audio-driven palette phase, color-layer strength, relief lighting and environment intensity. This is a feature opportunity, not a change to fractal orbit precision or a claim that RFF currently lacks every form of animation. The worklet transport and complete rule application remain separate dependencies.

**Separate analysis from drawing.** SpectrumFrame applies a periodic Hann window to scratch samples, runs a radix-2 FFT and produces reusable per-bin logarithmic magnitudes. BandMath builds overlapping kernels on a logarithmic frequency axis. BandAnalyser converts bins to linear power once, computes each band's weighted mean power, converts back to dB, applies a fixed spectral tilt and maps into a bounded control range. A reused, contiguous kernel array avoids rebuilding band geometry for each audio frame. In RFF, run this preparation independently of expensive fractal rendering and pass only resolved control values to the shader. A slow viewport must not change how the same audio is interpreted.

This implementation reports mean power, not total energy in a band. Its tilt compensates that chosen statistic; it should be an explicit artistic/calibration control, not presented as an intrinsic physical property of the source. Low bands narrower than an FFT bin are marked resolution-limited and can share source bins. More displayed bands do not create additional frequency resolution. The kernel evaluates bin cells at (i+0.5)*binHz, so compare that convention against the actual FFT coefficient frequencies when verifying narrow tones; do not assume the comments alone establish exact spectral placement.

**Smooth in audio time and detect rises separately.** The level follower uses a=1-exp(-dt/tau), giving a declared time constant rather than a fixed blend per rendered frame. Flux compares the current smoothed level to the maximum of neighboring previous-frame bands, keeps only positive rises and divides by hop duration. This suppresses some responses to tones moving across adjacent bands while preserving new attacks. It is useful for distinct RFF controls: sustained energy can move palette/lighting smoothly, while onset events trigger short accents. A rate normalization cannot recover an event faster than the analysis window/hop resolves, and this detector is not a complete beat/tempo tracker.

The first analysis frame and geometry reconfiguration suppress flux because there is no valid previous spectrum. Changes to tilt or dB mapping retain that reference, however, so a user adjustment can itself look like a rise. RFF should define reset/warm-up behavior for calibration changes, seeks and source replacement, and keep such transitions from generating unintended shader flashes. Deterministic export should evaluate the same analyzer at a fixed audio-sample schedule, with a reproducible warm-up state, then sample its output at each requested video time. Sampling only the selected video frames does not reproduce stateful envelopes between them.

**Use gain control with explicit silence behavior.** AutoGain tracks the loudest bin, attacks immediately, releases over elapsed time, and freezes both peak and gain when the live input is below its silence floor. That avoids increasing boost throughout a quiet gap. It caps amplification and resets when disabled. The actual release expression is exp(-4*dt); the nearby comment suggesting roughly 2.5 seconds per decade does not match the coefficient's roughly 0.576-second excess decay per decade for a constant nonzero target. Use the expression and measured response to specify RFF behavior, not the comment. Clamp or reject non-finite inputs and distinguish stale/missing analysis from silence. Carry exact constants only after provenance and behavior are checked.

**Calibration is not full backend equivalence.** SpectrumFrame offsets Hann magnitudes using the ratio of 0.42 and 0.5 coherent gains to match a legacy scale. This can align an appropriate tone amplitude, but it does not make Hann and Blackman spectra identical for off-bin tones, leakage or noise. Claims in comments about universal separation advantages and JavaScript-versus-WASM speed were not verified here. RFF should benchmark its own CPU implementation and validate tones, sweeps, silence and broadband signals across supported sample rates. FFT tables and work arrays are Float32; this is an audio-control implementation choice and gives no reason to lower precision in the fractal renderer. Validate finite power-of-two lengths and exact buffer sizes at the boundary, beyond JavaScript's bitwise power-of-two test.

Named techniques in the comments include Cooley-Tukey, SuperFlux and Brown/Puckette-related kernels. The current inspection establishes what the code does, not original-source licensing or equivalence to complete published algorithms. Before adapting distinctive implementations, verify the earliest practical source and actual license and update RFF's NOTICE. No source code was copied in this batch.

**Resolve the export tail explicitly.** AudioExportMix covers the inclusive interval (end-start+1)/timelineFps. With constant-duration stepped video, the inspected runner/worker instead produce (floor((end-start)/step)+1)*step/timelineFps. These match only for suitable range lengths. For example, start=0, end=10, step=3 and fps=30 yield 11/30 seconds of audio and 12/30 seconds of video. Thus the mixer's comment that stepping aligns durations by construction is too broad. RFF should choose and document whether to shorten the last video frame, pad/trim audio, or extend the requested interval, and apply the same rule to early finish. This arithmetic check is source-derived, not a decoded-media test.

The mixer loads whole files, sums two channels (duplicating mono), linearly resamples and hard-clips overlaps. It has no per-clip gain or anti-alias low-pass for substantial downsampling. Its full-length PCM allocation also scales with duration. For an RFF audio feature, specify a channel/downmix policy, gain/headroom, suitable resampling and bounded processing; render the identical resolved mix to the analyzer and export path. Short reads, corrupt audio and missing cached assets should produce explicit outcomes. Suggested validation includes a stepped range with a remainder, seeks into sustained audio, a long silence followed by an attack, calibration edits, mono/stereo input and a slow renderer. No DSP tests, audio playback or video render was run in this batch.

## Audio scheduling: timestamped history without depending on viewport speed

Full reads of `engine/features/audioMod/worklet/protocol.ts` (83 lines), `analysisProcessor.ts` (221 lines) and `WorkletAnalysis.ts` (405 lines) connect the numerical analysis to its producer/consumer scheduling. The RFF opportunity is to keep audio-responsive 2D color and relief lighting responsive while fractal rendering is expensive, and to record those controls with explicit timestamps. This does not prove offline export parity: recorded or offline analysis must still share the same time mapping and state initialization.

**Transmit compact semantic measurements.** The producer sends band levels, onset flux, raw-bin peak and timestamps rather than a full FFT spectrum. Both ends construct band geometry from the same configuration. The processor keeps a circular sample buffer, waits for a complete FFT window, linearizes it for each hop and batches several measurements into one message. Missing input feeds silence rather than leaving the last audible samples frozen. For RFF, preserve this separation between audio acquisition, analysis, control evaluation and GPU upload; the renderer needs resolved control data, not raw spectral bins on every draw.

Multichannel input is averaged to mono here. Opposite-phase channels can cancel even when the stereo signal has substantial energy, so a RFF design should choose and document whether it analyzes a mono mix, per-channel power or a selected channel. The default hop helper aligns to 128-sample quanta; process handles only one hop per invocation and assumes 128 frames for disconnected input. Validate the actual processing block contract and sample rate rather than generalizing this implementation to arbitrary block sizes. Timestamp values use currentTime directly while the protocol calls them window-end times; verify their relation to the just-consumed block before aligning recorded shader events to video frames.

**Use different retention rules for levels and events.** The receiver keeps 512 snapshots, publishes the latest smoothed level and takes the per-band maximum flux across unread retained snapshots. A slow viewport can therefore still notice a brief onset rather than averaging it away. Counting unread hops avoids aliasing an entire ring wrap with no new data. For RFF, use this approach for responsive live effects, but distinguish a maximum event summary from exact event timing, count or integrated energy. Multiple onsets in a long gap collapse into one maximum; recording requires the timestamped sequence, not just that summary.

A bounded history ring bounds retained storage, not the incoming message queue or total burst-processing work. onBatch loops over every received snapshot; old queued batches can still cost time before the newest state is reached. MAX_SNAPSHOTS_PER_POST limits one producer batch, not undelivered messages. Use a defined overflow policy and report dropped history. The comment claiming process allocates nothing is also too strong: subarray creates view objects, flush creates a message object, and structured cloning performs copying. The useful property is reused numerical buffers, not proven allocation-free execution or measured negligible overhead.

**Version configuration and source identity.** The receiver rejects old batches only when bandCount differs. An FFT-size, tilt, dB-range or other change can retain the same band count while changing the meaning of its values. The producer resets staging only on band-count changes, so a batch may also span a calibration change. RFF should attach a configuration generation and source identity to every batch, atomically switch matching geometry/calibration, and invalidate incompatible history. Resetting the FFT ring should establish a fresh hop/priming policy as well as a new buffer. Validate message lengths, finite timestamps and expected ordering at the boundary.

**Make historical queries explicit about coverage.** snapshotAt returns the nearest retained entry even if the requested time lies outside the retained interval; its comment promising null for insufficient history is not implemented. applySnapshotAt adds an absolute-age tolerance, which is a different contract. The returned snapshot also references mutable ring storage. For RFF recording, return coverage/freshness metadata and copy or own retained values when necessary. Choose explicitly whether nearest-future data is permitted for retrospective reconstruction; a causal live controller should not silently use future data.

Historical application writes levels, normalized levels and flux, but intentionally does not reconstruct AGC or per-band normalization state. This protects the live cursor but means a past frame is not a full replay of all live processing. Reproducible RFF export should either record final modulation values or replay every stateful stage from a checkpoint/pre-roll. hasSignal means only that a snapshot has arrived, not that audible input is currently present or recent. A suspended/failed source needs a separate freshness status so old values do not remain authoritative indefinitely.

**Present latency compensation as an approximation.** The receiver subtracts an estimated half-window delay from a response-time budget and clamps the remaining smoothing time at zero. Once the FFT window exceeds that budget, this cannot preserve the requested total response time. Windowed magnitude analysis plus envelope smoothing is not an exact single-delay system. Expose the resolution/responsiveness tradeoff honestly and verify transients at supported FFT sizes. The AGC and optional band normalization still advance on main-thread updates using the latest snapshot, so moving spectral analysis off-thread alone does not make every downstream stage independent of polling cadence.

Attachment is one-shot once ctx is assigned, and load failure sets a flag with no retry/detach operation in this class. An RFF implementation needs explicit attach, failure, retry, source replacement and shutdown ownership. The code's cited tests and performance assertions were not rerun here. Acceptance checks should include same-band-count reconfiguration, a stalled consumer longer than history, an out-of-range historical query, opposite-phase stereo, source suspension, load failure and offline/live modulation parity. No implementation was copied or application code changed.

## Audio control semantics: stable frequency ranges and optional normalization

Full reads of `filterBank.ts`, `AudioAnalysisEngine.ts`, `freqScale.ts` and `audioMod/index.ts`, plus ADR-0105 and ADR-0106, clarify the control values and persistence semantics around the previously reviewed analyzer. These support an optional RFF audio-animation feature: map an authored frequency range to palette phase or layer strength in 2D, or to lighting/material controls on relief. No claim is made that audio modulation outranks the environment-reflection proposal for general image quality.

**Persist intent in physical units.** Rules use real lowHz/highHz values; the filter bank resolves them into the current analysis geometry, and quick presets use finite frequency bounds. This avoids changing an authored band merely because another device has a different sample rate. RFF should similarly persist frequency ranges in Hz and times in declared units, with stable parameter IDs. A visualization's normalized coordinate or an FFT bin number should not become the saved artistic meaning. The quick labels Kick/Bass/Mids/Highs are frequency selections, not source-separation algorithms; other instruments in the same band can trigger them.

ADR-0106 documents a legacy migration that assumes 48 kHz because the old representation omitted its authoring rate. That is deterministic recovery under an explicit assumption, not exact recovery for every file. RFF should retain the metadata needed for future migrations, make old-format assumptions visible in documentation and test repeated loads for idempotence. Existing RFF binary formats and palette IDs retain their own stability requirements; GMT's JSON migration approach does not authorize changing those contracts.

**Name the statistic that actually drives the effect.** FilterBank.aggregate computes RMS across bounded, possibly normalized control levels. Those levels have already undergone logarithmic mapping and clipping, so this is not waveform RMS, physical band power or a calibrated loudness measure. aggregateFlux returns the arithmetic mean of per-band rise rates. Widening a selected range can therefore dilute an isolated onset. For RFF, define whether a mapping uses mean, maximum, integrated energy or a calibrated loudness quantity, and keep the meter and shader-control path consistent. Do not label all such quantities simply as volume.

bandRangeForHz selects whole bands and guarantees at least one when bands exist. It does not weight partial overlap, and even a requested range beyond the analyzed frequencies can resolve to an edge band. RFF should validate ordered finite bounds, distinguish unsupported coverage from a valid silent result, and show the effective analysis range. A narrow selection cannot exceed the FFT's frequency resolution. Integer, bounded band indices should be established before aggregate queries rather than trusting arbitrary numeric inputs.

**Keep adaptive normalization optional.** The per-band follower attacks immediately, releases toward current level, freezes its peak in silence and divides by a minimum-bounded running peak. When disabled, normalized values equal levels and the stored peaks follow current levels. This prevents enabling the mode from reusing arbitrarily old peaks, but toggling it can still change output amplitude abruptly. A RFF control should describe that behavior and optionally transition deliberately, without changing the authored raw signal.

ADR-0105 records an owner-run preference for unnormalized material over a peak follower and PCEN in GMT's visual use case. This is local evaluation evidence, not a universal rejection of those audio techniques. Its decision wording mentions compatibility, while its consequences explicitly say those settings had not been distributed; use the stated optional artistic role rather than inventing a compatibility obligation. For RFF, preserve spectral contrast by default and let individual mappings choose their input range. Fixed tilt can help high bands reach useful values, but downstream clipping still limits dynamics; the prose claim that tilt costs no dynamics is not absolute after the complete bounded mapping.

**Separate device/session controls from authored rules.** AudioFeature preserves its whole live slice during scene loading whenever isEnabled is true, while the comments identify modulation rules as scene content. It declares response, FFT size, band width, dB window, gain and normalization as separately configurable. RFF can preserve a user's active input setup while loading artwork, but an enabled flag is not proof that an input or analyzer is operational. Provide explicit state for enabled, connected, analyzing, failed and stale. A user-requested full reset should remain distinguishable from loading only a look.

The feature default response is 0.5, while the underlying receiver initializes its smoothing parameter to 0.8 until synchronized; the feature's default tilt is 3 while the receiver initializes to 0. The initialization/update caller must establish those defaults before results are treated as calibrated. Static detail labels such as 12 Hz for 4096 samples are approximate at 48 kHz and change with sample rate. RFF should derive such readouts from the active device. The feature's response description also overstates constant total delay when the analysis window exceeds the requested budget, as the previous section explains.

AudioAnalysisEngine is a delegating facade with a transport-init hook that attaches analysis, and exposes failure and context-time access. This is a useful boundary for RFF: keep capture/playback ownership separate from reusable numerical analysis and animation mapping. The singleton facade and singleton filter bank are not evidence of independent per-export sessions. Build offline export instances or record resolved controls so rendering one export cannot overwrite live analysis state. Hidden legacy parameters in the feature declaration do not prove active filters or envelopes; inspect consumers before proposing them as implemented functions. No runtime audio comparison or setting-import test was executed in this batch.

## Audio transport: define exactly which signal drives the artwork

The complete 466-line `engine/features/audioMod/AudioTransport.ts` has now been read. It separates capture/playback from analysis through one analysis bus. For RFF, this offers a concrete design for an optional audio input driving 2D palette animation or relief lighting: the source, analysis trim and listening volume should have explicit, independently understood roles. This is an architectural opportunity, not a recommendation to transplant browser capture APIs into a native Vulkan application.

**Trace the actual gain graph.** Decks feed individual crossfade gains, then masterGain, which connects to both speakers and analysisBus. Changing deck monitoring volume therefore also changes analysis levels. Live input instead passes through inputGain into analysisBus. Microphone input has no speaker connection; system capture also connects directly to the destination, bypassing masterGain and inputGain on that listening branch. Thus a generic Volume control does not govern every audible path, and a claim that deck volume is monitoring-only would be inaccurate. RFF should decide whether visuals follow pre-monitor or post-monitor audio and display that choice clearly. Retain an analysis-only microphone path by default and make monitoring deliberate.

The equal-power crossfade uses cosine gains. This preserves the sum of squared gains, not constant amplitude for correlated sources: two copies of the same signal can be louder in the middle. A RFF mixer needs appropriate headroom and an explicit relationship between the live mix, exported audio and modulation analysis. The offline mix reviewed earlier sums source clips without this deck crossfade/master graph, so matching source files alone does not prove live/export signal equivalence.

**Make source switching transactional.** Microphone connection pauses decks and releases the old live input before awaiting capture. System capture waits for a usable stream before replacing the old input, and does not pause decks in this method. Loading a file releases live capture, but playing an already loaded deck does not. Consequently, source exclusivity is not a universal invariant of this class. RFF should declare whether mixing is allowed and use the same rule across every entry point, including shortcuts and imported sessions.

Concurrent asynchronous capture requests have no request-generation check. A late result can replace a newer choice or become active after a disconnect. Accept a capture result only for its still-current request and release obsolete streams immediately. Also own cleanup when node construction or connection fails after acquisition; the local catch reports failure but does not guarantee all newly acquired tracks are stopped. Device-ended events are not handled in this class, so UI state should not infer continued capture solely from isMicActive. Requested processing constraints are not proof of the settings actually negotiated by a device.

**Keep lifetime and readiness separate.** init is guarded once the context exists, but partial initialization failure has no rollback. Resume/play promises are either not awaited or only logged, so a successful connection method does not establish that playback and analysis are running. Add explicit ready/suspended/failed states and lifecycle cleanup for devices, graph nodes, object URLs and the context. The class has no overall dispose operation. Deck deactivation stops playback and clears an activity flag while retaining its file/source; hasTrack therefore differs from active or playing.

Metadata readiness is handled with events and a timeout rather than polling, which is useful for RFF media loading. However, the wait is attached to a reusable deck element, with no loaded-file generation. Replacing the file while waiting can resolve the request with another file's duration. Return readiness tied to a specific asset, distinguish timeout/decode failure from a true zero-length asset, and reject non-finite durations. Settings such as input trim are also ignored when their node does not yet exist; persist desired values and apply them during graph creation.

The long source header records owner-observed focus-dependent rendering slowdowns and browser capture hypotheses. Those are historical observations, not profiling performed in this audit, and they do not establish native RFF performance. A RFF implementation should measure audio analysis, UI publication, GPU rendering and capture separately. Avoid importing unverified claims about browser-wide behavior or choosing a new capture backend merely from those comments. Suggested checks are source-switch races, disconnect while capture is pending, device removal, volume-versus-analysis behavior, correlated crossfades, metadata replacement and offline/live mix parity. No capture device was opened, recording started or audio played during this review.

## Audio design-record reconciliation: use the current pipeline as the adoption baseline

ADR-0104 (148 lines) and ADR-0110 have now been read in full and compared with the implementation reads above. These records explain why analysis was moved off the display-driven loop and why logarithmic bands were introduced, but contain superseded details. RFF proposals should use the current implementation for behavior and the ADRs for historical rationale, keeping owner observations distinct from measurements performed here.

ADR-0104's Nyquist-fraction storage description is superseded by ADR-0106's real-Hz representation. Its PCEN addendum is superseded by ADR-0105 and the current optional peak follower; PCEN is not present in the reviewed live analyzer. The statement that fractional-octave bands cannot create frequency information below FFT resolution remains consistent with the code. Its proposed dual-resolution analysis is deferred, not an implemented GMT feature to claim as readily portable. A future RFF experiment could analyze bass with a longer window and treble with a shorter one, but would need explicit alignment and latency controls; it is lower priority than adopting a clear, deterministic single-window control path.

ADR-0110's own correction explains that the old analysis was bound to main-thread frame rate, not specifically throttled to one update per second by the cited worker-dispatch branch. Do not use that superseded mechanism to predict RFF performance. Separating analysis scheduling from UI/rendering is the transferable principle; native RFF needs profiling of its own threads and queues to establish the benefit.

Several listed follow-ups have moved on. The reviewed facade and receiver now use only WorkletAnalysis and explicitly expose failure rather than falling back to a second analyzer. setSmoothing computes and sends smoothingTauSec; it is no longer a no-op. hasSignal replaces the old raw-buffer liveness query. A targeted search of current `engine/animation/AnimationSystem.tsx` finds applySnapshotAt in its recording back-fill and restoration paths, so the ADR's statement that no back-fill exists is stale. That search establishes presence, not full replay correctness; the historical-state limitations discussed above still require end-to-end verification.

There is also a concrete calibration discrepancy between comments. BandAnalyser's header mentions a 1200-per-second full-scale figure, whereas targeted inspection of current `engine/features/modulation/ModulationEngine.ts` confirms TRANSIENT_FULL_SCALE=20 and raw=min(1,aggregateFlux/20). ADR-0110's correction agrees with the latter. RFF should document producer units and consumer scaling together, then validate responses with known test signals. Do not multiply a threshold by frame rate based on a stale comment or assume moving analysis to another thread changes the intended units.

Global AGC is applied after FilterBank.aggregate in the inspected level branch; transient mode uses aggregateFlux directly. Thus general statements that global gain simply cancels inside per-band normalization do not describe this dispatch order. A RFF mapping should explicitly choose which source channels receive automatic gain, and test the combined mode rather than relying on the algebra of a different ordering.

The ADR's historical throughput, FFT-error and browser-build claims were not rerun. Its allocation-free claim is narrower in reality, as the already-reviewed processor creates views/messages while reusing large buffers. Named algorithms and referenced products are not license evidence or independent comparative benchmarks. Before implementing an audio-driven RFF shader feature, verify provenance, actual signal calibration, bounded queue behavior and preview/export parity. This reconciliation changes the accuracy of the adoption baseline; it does not change the provisional priority of editable environment reflection for general appearance improvement.

## High-resolution scheduling: distinguish work regions from allocation tiles

The complete `engine/export/BucketRunner.ts` (622 lines) and `BucketRenderTypes.ts` (136 lines) have now been read, replacing the runner's earlier partial coverage. The transferable RFF design separates renderer-specific behavior behind a host contract from image partitioning, work scheduling, compositing and export. It applies to 2D fractal images and relief shading, but the comments' VRAM-safety terminology needs qualification from actual allocations.

**A smaller bucket does not necessarily allocate a smaller image.** The runner asks the host to render at the entire current image-tile size and allocates a Float32 RGBA composite of that size. Buckets are scissored regions within it. Thus decreasing bucketSize reduces work per region but does not reduce that composite's dimensions or the requested host target dimensions. The outer image-tile grid is the relevant allocation partition. For RFF, calculate the full budget for orbit/field data, accumulation, shading, composite, post-processing, readback and encoder buffers before selecting tile dimensions. Preserve precision and compression; do not substitute lower-precision data merely to meet a guessed memory budget.

The outer grid partitions integer coordinates and covers the requested output with remainder pixels distributed by floor boundaries. Validate finite positive dimensions and clamp row/column counts to avoid zero-sized tiles. bucketSize needs a strictly positive finite integer; this implementation directly uses it in division/loop bounds. A single validated export plan should also supply names and progress, instead of later reading unnormalized configuration values. Buckets are sorted by distance from the center, which gives center-first feedback; it is not a literal spiral traversal.

**Use completed-sample evidence, not a tick convention.** The runner advances using bucketFrameCount-1 because its concrete engine invokes update before drawing. Its method-level documentation instead says the host already rendered. A reusable RFF scheduler should receive an explicit completed-sample count or completion token so changing host order cannot produce an empty first bucket or omit a sample. Null output texture currently causes compositeCurrentBucket to return without success, after which update still advances. Failed compositing must not count as completed work.

The current path uses a sample budget for every bucket and no convergence early-out, consistent with the later design records. However, updateConfig permits changing that budget mid-render; completed buckets retain their old count while future buckets use the new count. Equal configured counts are also insufficient to prove bit-identical neighboring pixels without matching sample seeds, global coordinates and shader state. RFF should snapshot output-quality settings per export or explicitly reschedule already-completed work when they change. The accumulation flag is stored but does not alter the stopping logic in this runner; the host's actual sampling behavior must be checked separately.

**Separate mask tolerance from filter support.** The runner expands the UV region by four pixels while keeping an exact integer scissor. The type documentation still describes a half-pixel expansion. This guard helps prevent a valid pixel from failing a floating region test, but it is not a computed halo: pixels beyond the scissor are not produced. Post-processing runs after buckets are assembled into an image-tile composite, which can avoid inner bucket filter boundaries, but there is no explicit outer-tile overlap contract here. RFF needs halos derived from every neighborhood filter and global-coordinate handling for warps, noise and image lookup. Verify seams after all effects, not only at raw fractal coloring.

**Export the composed image, with clear data semantics.** The host supplies final post-processing and the runner resolves to RGBA8, flips vertically and forces alpha to 255. This particular still-image path therefore exports opaque eight-bit images, unlike the worker video/image-sequence multipass path reviewed earlier. RFF should expose transparency and numerical field exports through explicit compatible paths. A retained HDR composite is useful for preview, but does not make the saved PNG HDR or preserve depth/iteration data.

The optional passthrough fallback reuses compositeMaterial without rebinding its map to compositeTarget.texture. That material was last pointed at a host bucket output, so fallback behavior does not establish that the complete composite is saved. This is a conditional source finding, not proof that GMT's concrete host uses the fallback. A RFF host interface should require a correctly bound complete image or fail clearly. Keep ownership of host materials separate from runner-owned full-screen geometry and transient targets; the reviewed disposal path releases target/material objects but does not explicitly release the pass geometry.

**Count saving separately from rendering.** Worker mode emits pixel data for another component to save, while the DOM path starts asynchronous PNG creation and immediately continues. Neither establishes durable save completion before the runner advances or reports stopped. RFF should bound pending tiles and return explicit per-tile save results. Embedded scene metadata is useful for reopening an image, with a visible warning if requested embedding fails, but it is not a replacement for a complete project/asset package. Save a manifest of tile coordinates, full image dimensions and completed files for reliable assembly/resume.

Progress currently multiplies the current tile's bucket count by the number of tiles. Uneven edge dimensions can give different bucket counts, so precompute the true total work or weight by planned samples/pixels. Retaining the final composite for Refine View is useful, but a multi-image-tile job retains only the final tile, not a composed full-output overview. Keep that distinction visible. Cleanup/state restoration also requires exception-safe handling around host hooks and draw/readback operations. Acceptance cases include one-sample buckets, odd dimensions, excess tile counts, missing host output, a mid-job quality edit, long-radius effects across tile boundaries and a delayed/failed save. No high-resolution render or GPU memory measurement was run in this batch.

## GMT tile host: global coordinates, sampling scale and preview ownership

Full reads of `engine-gmt/engine/GmtBucketHost.ts` (276 lines) and `BucketRenderer.ts` (96 lines) connect the generic runner to GMT. Targeted reads of FractalEngine.update and its pixel-size override establish two additional call-site details; they do not constitute a new full-class review. The host abstraction remains a useful RFF pattern: keep high-precision fractal generation and Vulkan details in the renderer, while a scheduler owns progress and output partitioning.

**Carry full-image coordinates explicitly.** beginRender sets full-output resolution and camera aspect. beginImageTile supplies normalized origin/extent plus an integer pixel origin, while setRenderSize allocates the pipeline at image-tile dimensions. beginGpuBucket sets both a tolerant region mask and an exact scissor. This confirms that inner buckets restrict work, whereas outer image tiles determine the requested allocation size. For RFF, retain full-image coordinates through palette sampling, environment reflection, noise and post-processing so changing a tile grid does not change the artwork. Correctly bound coordinate uniforms are necessary but not proof that every shader consumer uses them consistently.

**Keep sampling identity coherent at region transitions.** FractalEngine.update selects the per-bucket accumulation count for FrameCount, rather than a session-global frame number. This is intended to make stochastic sampling independent of bucket order. However, that assignment occurs before bucketRenderer.update, which can reset accumulation and advance the bucket. On that transition tick the earlier assignment can refer to the previous bucket's count unless another writer refreshes it. This batch does not establish the complete later binding sequence, so it is a follow-up condition rather than a claimed reproduced seam. A RFF scheduler should resolve region identity, completed sample count and random index together after any transition and before submission. Verify the first sample of every bucket, not only the steady-state loop.

The wrapper calls updateConfig on each update, confirming that live budget edits reach the runner; the uniform-sample-budget caveat in the prior section is therefore relevant to the wiring. UI quality changes need a documented policy for already-completed regions. A deterministic seed does not compensate for unequal sample counts or different filtering footprints.

**Separate output pixel footprint from a preview-matching quality policy.** GmtBucketHost saves the viewport PixelSizeBase, and the inspected compute branch substitutes it during bucket rendering whenever it is positive. The comment describes preserving trace precision, normal epsilon and shadow bias during supersampling. For RFF, do not equate matching a preview with obtaining all the detail available at the final output resolution. Keep the output sampling footprint, relief derivative scale and any geometric/iteration accuracy controls distinct. Never transfer this policy into a lower-precision perturbation computation. Compare preview matching and final-resolution detail using the same scenes before selecting a default.

**The concrete readback host binds the completed composite.** getReadbackMaterial assigns map=composite, sets tile output resolution and explicitly enables output encoding. Thus the generic runner's conditional passthrough binding concern is not the normal initialized GMT host path. RFF should make that binding a required interface contract rather than rely on an incidental last-used texture. The host also computes post-processing from each image-tile composite; it adds no outer-tile neighborhood data. The missing explicit halo remains an adoption concern for any spatial effect, including non-bloom filters.

Post-processing scale is partly derived from the original viewport dimensions when the full output is larger. That may preserve one intended appearance but means the result depends on preview geometry unless the complete mapping compensates. RFF export should define effect sizes in a stable unit and pass the resulting scale explicitly. Saved target size here comes from renderer.getSize, while other paths may use drawing-buffer or internal render size; verify the size domain before restoration, particularly under display scaling or adaptive resolution.

**A retained composite needs retained display dependencies.** The wrapper can re-blit a held final texture through GmtBucketHost. endRender resets region/tile state, restores pipeline size and camera aspect, resizes the shared post-process pass and resets engine accumulation. A later held-image blit uses the current display material and post-process output, not a self-contained snapshot of the original resolved frame. A RFF implementation should either retain the fully resolved display image or retain all inputs needed to reproduce its appearance until released. Restore prior state deliberately; resetting to full-screen defaults is not restoration of an earlier region selection. The host's explicit flush submits work but is not proof of presentation completion.

The wrapper snapshots scene metadata by serializing the preset before starting. That is useful for associating an image with its settings, but later mutable render edits must not silently make the metadata describe another image. The host header's claim of convergence-poll ownership is stale: this class has no convergence measurement methods. Acceptance checks should cover first-sample identity after bucket switches, different tile grids, different viewport sizes at the same export dimensions, held-preview stability and metadata/settings agreement. No rendered comparison or GPU timing was performed in this batch.

## Frame uniform preparation: precompute invariants without weakening precision

The complete 604-line `engine-gmt/engine/managers/UniformManager.ts` has now been read, superseding partial coverage. It centralizes adaptive target sizing, camera basis, virtual-space inputs, time, environment rotation, fog conversion, light packing and formula-specific derived rotations. The most direct RFF transfer is to compute pixel-invariant material/environment quantities once per frame or setting change and publish a coherent GPU parameter block, while preserving the distinct accuracy requirements of fractal computation.

**Move repeated invariant work out of pixel evaluation.** Environment rotation becomes a two-by-two sine/cosine matrix. Light orientation becomes a normalized toward-light vector, and attenuation modes become coefficients for linear or quadratic distance terms. Formula-specific angle lanes are converted into matrices or sine/cosine pairs before shader use. For RFF's proposed editable environment, this supports preparing orientation and related lookup constants on the CPU; 2D texture rotations and relief lighting can share the same principle. Confirm which calculations RFF already performs before claiming new savings, and measure affected shader paths. CPU precomputation is not permission to reduce numeric precision or change matrix order.

The generic geometry rotation builds Z*X*Y, while lights use Euler order YXZ and camera modulation uses XYZ. Derived rotations have explicit conversion tags and source accessors. These are separate conventions, not interchangeable rotations. RFF should encode units, order and storage convention in typed descriptors, validate source/target shapes, and test basis directions. The derived-bank loop silently skips missing targets and defaults missing components to zero; do not let an invalid formula binding become an apparently valid identity-like transform without diagnostics. Unused bank entries are not cleared here, so formula switching also needs an explicit ownership/invalidation policy.

**Zero is a valid animation time.** syncFrame assigns Time using state.clock?.elapsedTime || performance.now()/1000. An explicitly requested zero therefore becomes wall time. WorkerExporter passes a deterministic clock through this method, so this assignment is an actual path to check for a non-reproducible first frame, not merely a theoretical API issue. RFF should distinguish absent time from zero, reject non-finite values and use the same supplied clock for every animated shader input. A later writer could alter the final value; no end-to-end rendered reproduction was performed here.

This full read finds no FrameCount update inside UniformManager.syncFrame. It therefore does not resolve the previous bucket-transition concern, where FractalEngine assigns that value before the runner may reset accumulation. Other callers/bindings must still be checked. Publish sample identity only after the scheduler has selected the region and sample to render.

**Measure effective resolution, not just the requested scale.** Interactive sizing uses physical canvas dimensions, while the adaptive decision is skipped entirely during export/bucket rendering. Smart resizing applies a five-percent guard based only on width; a height-only change can leave an old target height while camera aspect changes. A minimum of 64 pixels per axis can also make the actual downscale differ from the requested scale. PixelSizeBase is derived from Resolution.y multiplied by stored adaptive.scale rather than a separately recorded physical viewport height. Rounded/guarded dimensions, or a stale scale retained when exporting, need checking before treating that product as exact. RFF should track actual viewport, render-target and full-output dimensions separately and derive each footprint from its intended domain.

The implementation passes ignoreAccumDrop=false despite an earlier comment describing its retirement. It uses explicit gesture/animation signals plus low accumulation during active changes, excludes idle-band timings from its cost estimate, and passes the renderer when resizing to preserve the previous image. Those are useful responsiveness ideas, but retained pixels are provisional display content after invalidation. A downscaled preview must never become precision-reduced orbit data or a completed export. Pure display adjustments should reuse valid upstream fields rather than triggering fractal work.

**Color conversion needs a named domain.** The fog block inverts a particular rational tone curve using fixed coefficients and clamps its input to 0.99. Its comment calls the result linear fog derived from sRGB, but this code contains no explicit sRGB transfer decoding, and inverting one tone curve is not a generic color-space conversion. RFF should distinguish display-encoded color, scene-linear radiance and inverse tone mapping, match the selected tone operator, and retain provenance before adapting recognizable constants. Do not use this block as an unqualified recipe for the proposed environment's HDR color handling.

**Resolve lights and camera in the same coordinate frame.** Camera basis and virtual-space position incorporate modulation, but fixed light direction uses the unmodified camera quaternion and light-position packing receives the original camera object. Check the intended headlamp behavior under camera modulation before adopting that combination. Light intensity supports additive exposure-stop modulation followed by 2^EV, or additive linear intensity; these have different meanings and should be explicit in RFF controls. The range-based attenuation makes intensity fall to one percent at range, rather than defining a hard cutoff or a complete physical light model. When a valid lights array is absent, this block does not reset LightCount; import validation or explicit clearing must prevent stale lights.

Full-output resolution is synchronized from the local target only when tile size is near one in both axes. This supports the coordinate contract already reviewed, but approximate identity detection should not replace an explicit export mode in a generalized RFF design. Recommended checks are time zero versus repeat export, height-only resize, small viewports, export immediately after adaptive interaction, light/camera modulation together, formula-bank switching and fog behavior under each tone mapper. This batch adds source evidence and design requirements; no shader benchmark or rendered comparison was run.

## Configuration diffs: precise invalidation and explicit rotation contracts

Full reads of `engine-gmt/engine/managers/ConfigManager.ts` (269 lines) and ADR-0099 complement the already-reviewed rotationDescriptor/rotationMath modules, which were reread without additional full-read credit. The RFF benefit is to distinguish source-setting changes, derived GPU values and shader structure so editing an environment angle or material amount can remain responsive without unnecessary compilation or incorrect reuse of old data.

**Return explicit consequences of a change.** ConfigManager returns rebuildNeeded, uniformUpdate, modeChanged and needsAccumReset. Feature metadata drives compile versus runtime behavior, and noAccumReset is considered separately. This is a useful shape for RFF, extended to its actual dependency stages: reference orbit, per-pixel fields, shading and final presentation. A change should invalidate exactly the stages that consume it. The manager's 50 ms timer batches diagnostic logs/compile estimates only; it does not debounce shader rebuilds. Do not credit it with compilation coalescing that must be implemented by another scheduler.

**Do not import a generic epsilon into precision-sensitive settings.** areValuesEqual uses an absolute 1e-6 tolerance for numbers and selected vectors/colors. This can be reasonable for some display controls but must not hide meaningful changes to RFF's high-precision coordinates, formula parameters or zoom. Moreover, the new value is merged even when a small difference was classified as equal, potentially leaving configuration changed without the corresponding reset/rebuild flag. Use parameter-specific equality or exact versioned state for sensitive values, and make the published configuration agree with the invalidation decision. Validate finite numbers before comparison; JSON equality for arrays is not a general numerical or resource-equivalence contract.

The constructor shallow-copies initialConfig, syncUniform stores value references, and feature merges are shallow. In-place mutation of a shared nested object can make an identity comparison report equality after content changes. RFF should own immutable input snapshots or maintain explicit generations, avoiding mutable aliasing between editors, live shaders and exports. The gradient-buffer exclusion is a useful distinction: generated texture bytes must not replace editable gradient source data. Generalize that distinction with typed source/derived-resource boundaries rather than a marker property alone.

**Resolve authoritative modes once.** update mutates its incoming partial object to fill root defaults from runtimeState, then processes feature lighting mode and later a root renderMode override. If those sources disagree, the later override can reverse an earlier feature decision. That is a conditional source-level conflict, not a reproduced application failure. RFF should canonicalize one effective mode before diffing and never modify a caller's input as a hidden side effect. Unknown feature keys are merged but do not participate in parameter invalidation checks here; schema validation must reject or deliberately preserve them according to a documented policy.

Modular structure relies on pipelineRevision: a revision change recompiles the Modular formula, whereas a pipeline update without a revision change is treated as runtime data and resets accumulation. This makes the caller's revision discipline part of correctness. RFF can use stable structure keys plus parameter versions, but should verify that a structural edit cannot bypass compilation merely because a caller forgot a counter. Formula, render-mode and resource changes should converge through one validated publication step with a compatible pipeline.

**Rotation descriptors transfer to 2D too.** ADR-0099 separates Euler conventions, axis-angle encodings, directions and twists, with stored degrees/radians explicit. This helps RFF environment orientation, directional lighting and 2D image/palette transforms share controls without silently changing saved semantics. Its fixed derived-uniform bank makes some imported rotations runtime-editable rather than rebuilding the shader on each edit. The same idea can be adopted selectively in RFF's Vulkan layout, with descriptor/push-constant contracts checked together. Bank exhaustion in GMT is handled by baking a slot according to the ADR; that behavior is not a guarantee that every rotation is always runtime-editable.

The ADR explicitly says native Rodrigues transforms still compute in GLSL loop initialization, so the broader claim that all rotations are already CPU-converted is false. The reviewed rotationMath also preserves a legacy half-angle/dead-zone convention for one encoding, while its display helper can use a full angle. RFF should retain existing saved meanings through explicit compatibility conversions and define new settings in clear units; do not copy unusual constants or conventions merely because a helper has a familiar name. Original-source attribution and licensing remain prerequisites for adapting distinctive imported implementations.

Suggested checks include sub-epsilon meaningful changes, nested object mutation, conflicting root/feature modes, a gradient upload followed by save/reload, structural edits without a revision bump, multi-turn rotation animation and preview/export orientation agreement. The ADR's cited test counts and performance effects were not rerun. No application code was changed in this batch.

## Progressive work scheduling and capability-checked estimator selection

**New full reads:** [BandScheduler.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/BandScheduler.ts) and [estimators.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/estimators.ts). Selected integration sites in `FractalEngine.ts` were also inspected; this does not constitute a complete read of that file.

### Transfer to RFF: bound interactive work without reducing mathematical precision

GMT's scheduler visits horizontal bands in center-out order. For pass p (zero-based), every band receives sample count p+1 and blend weight 1/(p+1). Only after all bands have been issued does the pass index advance. A requested band-count change is deferred until that boundary, preserving complete coverage under the new partition. This is a scheduling technique, not a lower-precision fractal method and not an approximation-table algorithm.

The inspected engine integration uses a full-resolution cost estimate to seed the band count, then adjusts it from measured frame rate at roughly 500 ms intervals. A target of zero selects one band. It freezes adaptation at the sample cap and explicitly clears the region/blend override when export or bucket rendering takes ownership. These controls matter as much as the scheduler itself: a region left behind can constrain an unrelated render path. Measured frame rate includes more than GPU tracing; it should not be described as a GPU timestamp measurement.

**RFF proposal:** if profiling identifies a long, indivisible shader submission as an interaction bottleneck, divide that workload into bounded regions while preserving the same precision, field values, and final sampling rules. Reuse RFF's existing work scheduling where possible; this read does not establish that RFF lacks region scheduling. The likely gain is lower input latency during expensive refinement, not faster final convergence. Per-region dispatch, history preservation and repeated full-screen composition can increase total cost. Cheap palette-only changes should not automatically acquire this machinery.

Important implementation contracts:

- Track *completed* work separately from issued work. `BandScheduler.next()` advances state before the caller performs the draw; the final issued band makes `passCount` advance immediately. This is safe only under the caller's successful ordered execution contract. A Vulkan adaptation should associate completion with the appropriate submission/fence or timeline value, especially across cancellation and device errors.
- Use integer pixel partitions with an explicit boundary convention, keeping global coordinates for noise, palette mapping and image sampling. Fractional UV bounds alone do not prove every pixel belongs to exactly one region. Keep filter halos separate from the owned output region.
- Keep one immutable scene/settings generation throughout a refinement pass. Invalidate accumulation when its input changes; display-only changes may reuse valid underlying results.
- A partially completed pass contains different sample counts across the image. A uniform full-frame update followed by `resumeFrom()` needs a proved history-weight contract; a monotonic scalar counter alone does not establish equal per-pixel sample weights. GMT's method assumes that the full-frame interlude advanced the whole screen uniformly. Before adopting the mechanism, verify interruption at each band boundary, not only at completed passes.
- The constructor accepts an unchecked initial band count, whereas `setBandCount()` floors and clamps to 1..64. Neither that clamp nor `resumeFrom()` rejects NaN. Validate finite integer scheduling inputs at the boundary rather than relying on slider ranges.
- Test the final-band sample cap, canceled submissions, resize, a scene edit halfway through a pass, and transitions to export. Compare the completed image against an equivalent full-frame render. Do not claim a responsiveness or throughput gain before measuring both.

This transfers to both flat 2D and relief rendering. It does not justify changing perturbation arithmetic or MPA, and a CPU reference-orbit bottleneck requires its own scheduling rather than merely splitting shader output.

### Transfer to RFF: declare shader capabilities independently of UI availability

GMT's estimator catalog combines stable selection values, UI labels, capability predicates and GLSL generation. Special estimators are considered in descending threshold order; an unavailable special coerces the selection to Linear before lower checks, preventing emission of undeclared cutting-plane or dIFS accumulators. The UI's disabled state is only advisory; the generator has the actual guard. Numeric DE uses a separate kernel gate and is deliberately excluded from the generated-body list.

For RFF, the useful transfer is a shared capability contract for optional shader inputs: a material effect that requires a derivative, orbit field, normal or texture must be validated by the pipeline builder as well as by the UI. Record the chosen fallback or report the unavailable effect explicitly, so a loaded preset cannot silently look unrelated to its saved intent. This is a proposed design pattern; it is not evidence that RFF currently emits missing-field shaders.

Do **not** port GMT's estimator menu wholesale into RFF's Mandelbrot perturbation pipeline. The catalog contains formula-specific 3D distance estimates: logarithmic, offset-linear, raw, dampened, cutting-plane and orbit-trap variants. The scalar shader uses `max(abs(dr), 1e-20)` and a small-radius early return; those guards are not a proof of deep-zoom accuracy or conservative distance bounds. The dampened implementation uses `0.34657359 * log2(r*r) * r / (dr_safe + 8.0)`, twice the logarithmic numerator coefficient used by its analytic entry; its comment is not a substitute for checking that formula's intended normalization. Numerical DE is documented as re-evaluating nearby orbits, but its cost and numerical reliability are not established by this catalog read.

Persisted estimator values also have threshold semantics rather than integer equality. Exact boundaries and fractional animation values can select different formulas; NaN falls through to the final scalar entry, while positive infinity also activates the separately queried numeric gate. A new RFF design should use validated stable identifiers and explicit transitions where discrete effects are intended, while preserving any existing saved-format contract. Changing a dropdown's display order must not renumber stored choices.

**Priority:** region scheduling is conditional on measured latency, and capability checks are infrastructure for reliable new effects. Neither displaces environment reflection as the current leading *appearance* proposal for relief materials. Provenance and licensing of distinctive formulas must be verified before adapting any implementation; source comments naming earlier programs are not license evidence.

## Screen-driven material controls: readback, picking and camera contracts

**Full source reads:** [PickingController.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/controllers/PickingController.ts), [WorkerDepthReadback.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/worker/WorkerDepthReadback.ts), [CameraController.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/controllers/CameraController.ts), and [SceneController.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/SceneController.ts). The shared hit predicate and selected worker call sites were checked separately; no full-read credit is assigned to those files by this section.

### Useful RFF feature: place and inspect effects directly on the image

A screen picker could select a relief height/normal or field value for light placement, material-mask ranges, and inspection of a reflected highlight. This is a supporting control for the environment/material proposals, not a demonstrated existing GMT reflection-placement tool. Flat 2D can select iteration/palette/image coordinates directly; it needs no artificial world-depth reconstruction. A relief height derived from an iteration field must be labeled as such: it is not a physical camera-ray distance, nor an excuse to reduce coordinate precision.

GMT's synchronous picker converts normalized screen coordinates using the *render target's* dimensions, so adaptive resolution does not make canvas coordinates address the wrong buffer. It either performs nine individual one-pixel reads and averages valid depths, or performs a single read for dragging. World reconstruction then adds `ray.direction * distance` to the ray origin and combines this with virtual-space high/low offsets. Equirectangular rays use longitude/latitude and the camera quaternion; other camera types use Three's raycaster.

For RFF, preserve that explicit coordinate-domain mapping, including viewport crop, scaling, and orientation. Do not adopt the nine separate synchronous calls by default: a small contiguous readback or reduction can avoid repeated synchronization. Mean depth across a silhouette can lie between separate surfaces and on neither one; select a center hit, robust neighborhood statistic or explicitly defined edge-aware result according to the interaction. A missing hit should remain distinguishable from a valid zero-valued 2D field.

The inspected picker accepts finite depths in (0,1000), while the worker uses the shared `isSurfaceHit` predicate, currently (0,50). Thus these paths do not have one shared validity contract. At normalized coordinate +1 the fast picker rejects the out-of-bounds index, the neighborhood picker can still use adjacent in-bounds pixels, and focus picking clamps to the edge. These differences are reasons to define a single RFF picking policy, not proof of a reproduced GMT UI failure. Combining `offset.x + offset.xL + localPos.x` into one JavaScript number also does not preserve an arbitrary high/low pair; RFF's deep-zoom center must remain in its existing high-precision representation when applying picked offsets.

### Async readback is a lifecycle, not merely a fence

The worker issues a center-pixel read every third rendered tick when no read is pending. It writes into a pixel-pack buffer, inserts a fence, polls with zero timeout, and reads the buffer only after signal. Allocation and conversion follow the target's actual half/float type, not the requested setting. Its half-float subnormal conversion uses `mantissa * 2^-24`; this is a separate implementation from the earlier RenderPipeline conversion finding and should not inherit that finding automatically. A missed/sky result updates `centerIsSky` while retaining the previous valid navigation distance. That is intentional last-known-value behavior, not a fresh valid hit.

**Vulkan adoption:** use a small staging allocation, explicit image layout/access transitions and a completion token. Record the scene/view generation and pixel mapping with the request. Consume only matching results; a completed GPU copy can still refer to a superseded camera or render target. Bound outstanding requests and choose a drop/coalesce policy for fast pointer motion. GMT's readback object carries the format and pending state but no view-generation tag. The source's approximately 40 ms synchronous-stall claim is not a measurement made in this audit.

The local class handles `WAIT_FAILED` by clearing the pending fence, but if `fenceSync()` returns null it still sets the pending flag and subsequent fence checks return early. It also has no disposal method for its PBO/fence or explicit context-recreation path. For an RFF implementation, specify allocation failure, cancellation, renderer recreation and destruction upfront. Restore graphics bindings on every exit. These are static lifecycle observations; actual context-loss behavior has not been exercised here.

### Cached focus picking trades one stall and memory for cheap repeated queries

GMT's focus interaction is *not* the async center-pixel path. On the next tick it synchronously reads a full RGBA image into Float32 storage, returns the clicked depth, and retains that snapshot for subsequent drag samples until `endFocusPick()`. At 3840×2160 that array alone occupies 132,710,400 bytes (about 126.6 MiB), although the consumer needs only alpha. Sampling while the request remains pending replies with -1; there is no queued latest sample. A ready snapshot has dimensions and pixels, but no request/view generation. The incoming ID is echoed for each sample rather than checked against the snapshot's creation ID.

For RFF, prefer an existing CPU field map when it already contains the desired data; otherwise compare a compact single-channel snapshot, local asynchronous queries and a small reduced inspection buffer. Make snapshot lifetime visible in the contract: freeze the relevant view during a drag or invalidate/reissue when it changes. Use separate statuses for pending, miss, stale and failure. These changes support reliable 2D interaction without importing a full 3D focus system or a large unnecessary readback.

### Camera motion lessons relevant to environment rotation and 2D navigation
