**Job ownership is stronger than global booleans.** Bucket-status events set exporting/bucket flags and clear the active sample-budget override on a false edge. This is useful cleanup for the normal serial flow, but the event handler has no job identity to prevent a late completion from clearing another operation's status. A future RFF background environment preprocess or export should associate completion and cleanup with its owner/revision and restore prior state only for that operation. This is an adoption safeguard, not a demonstrated concurrent GMT failure.

**A diagnostic must measure its own effect.** The optional performance probe separates callback cadence, render-tick method calls, returned frames, picking latency and long main-thread tasks. Quiet mode still adds a callback sampler, wrappers, sorting and periodic console output; it is not zero overhead once enabled. The recorded source history specifically reports probe-induced frame-rate loss, without a controlled measurement identifying the cause. For RFF, prefer existing GPU pass measurements plus bounded CPU counters, leave expensive live overlays optional, and compare probe-on/probe-off behavior before interpreting a slowdown.

The probe labels interval counts as per-second rates but does not normalize them by actual elapsed interval time; a delayed timer can overstate the rate. Its tick count measures wrapper invocations, not confirmed worker acceptance. Rejected picking promises increment the completion denominator without adding latency, lowering the reported mean, and requests/completions can cross interval boundaries. A low returned-frame rate with high callback rate narrows the investigation but does not uniquely identify a GPU bottleneck. Report actual elapsed time, successes/failures and queue/completion events separately in a RFF diagnostic. Multiple probe installs also wrap methods repeatedly, with no local guard; cleanup needs explicit ownership to avoid restoring another probe's wrapper.

**Validation:** cover initial startup and renderer recreation with nondefault settings, live material edits while camera interaction is idle, animation with partial rendering enabled, late job completion, delayed diagnostic timers and rejected readbacks. Verify full-image updates and eventual static convergence, then measure overhead independently. No runtime interaction, probe or rendering test was executed in this pass.

## Surface lifetime and capabilities: preserve appearance resources across recreation

Complete reads of [GmtRendererCanvas.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/renderer/GmtRendererCanvas.tsx) and [HardwareDetection.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/HardwareDetection.ts), with selected proxy initialization/resize checks, identify lifecycle requirements for RFF's proposed environment assets.

**Separate the render surface from its presentation and ownership.** GMT inserts a dedicated canvas with a stable identity, initializes it from the measured container size with a prop fallback, and transfers rendering to the worker. This avoids selecting an unrelated panel canvas for snapshots. The browser-specific transfer mechanism is not a Vulkan optimization to port. The useful RFF principle is explicit ownership of the scene's render target and a snapshot path that names that target rather than whichever image is currently visible in a panel.

The component retains an initialization flag, disconnects its resize observer on effect cleanup, and deliberately leaves the worker alive. An effect setup/cleanup/setup cycle with the same retained flag therefore skips observer recreation. A genuine remount creates a new canvas, while the inspected proxy initializer returns immediately if its worker already exists. These paths demonstrate why surface lifetime and renderer lifetime require coordinated reattachment; they do not establish a reproduced production failure. For RFF, device/surface recreation should restore both subscriptions and resource bindings, retain the CPU-side appearance definition, and only reuse GPU resources when their device/lifetime permits it.

**Queue the latest desired size while export owns the target.** The resize observer drops notifications while bucket rendering is active. This component has no explicit replay of a dropped size when bucket rendering ends, though other paths may reconcile it. It also reads browser DPR at startup and resize notifications rather than observing DPR independently. RFF should retain the latest desired preview size during exclusive export and reconcile once ownership returns; do not infer that no notification means size/DPI is unchanged. Environment filtering footprints must be recomputed from the actual output dimensions used by each frame, especially after restore or tiled export.

**Failure reporting needs one owner or a subscriber list.** The canvas saves the proxy's private crash callback, replaces it with a console logger, and restores the saved callback on cleanup. While mounted it does not call that prior callback; the proxy exposes a single setter in the inspected section. A RFF appearance-resource loader or device recovery path should not silently replace application-level failure handling when a view is opened. Preserve error routing and make cleanup conditional on ownership so a later handler is not overwritten by an older view's teardown.

**Capability detection must match the intended operation.** GMT's optional GL branch tries a 1×1 RGBA32F framebuffer attachment; without a context it derives defaults from a coarse pointer or a viewport narrower than 768 pixels. That heuristic can change when a desktop window is resized, and it is not a measurement of GPU arithmetic precision or HDR texture support. Even a successful attachment probe does not prove linear filtering, mip generation, blending, multisampling or the intended memory budget. The GL probe also changes bindings without restoring the prior texture/framebuffer state, and its exception path has no resource-cleanup finally. Those are reasons to isolate capability probing from normal rendering state rather than port the probe literally.

For RFF, query Vulkan support for the exact environment/filter/render-target formats and usages, then validate required resource creation and sampling paths. Treat unsupported HDR/filter combinations explicitly; do not silently substitute a lower-precision representation for fractal arithmetic. Keep layout choices and interaction defaults independent from precision requirements. A low-end policy may reduce optional preview workload while preserving the user's final appearance and numerical contract.

**Verification:** exercise view reattachment, device/resource recreation, a resize during export, DPI changes, failed resource initialization, and unsupported image/filter combinations. Verify that the final scene uses the matching source asset, preprocessing revision, dimensions and shader bindings. These checks remain proposed; no browser lifecycle or Vulkan capability test was run in this pass.

## Viewport coordinates: keep presentation scale separate from shading resolution

Complete reads of [ViewportFrame.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/plugins/viewport/ViewportFrame.tsx), [FixedResolutionControls.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/plugins/viewport/FixedResolutionControls.tsx) and [resolutionUtils.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/resolutionUtils.ts) clarify the size contracts behind the previous lifecycle review.

**Use distinct coordinate spaces.** GMT's outer frame observer records the available region in device pixels; Fixed mode independently creates a content box with the requested width/height and applies a CSS fit transform capped at 1. The stored outer `canvasPixelSize` is therefore not inherently the Fixed render target's dimensions. Composition guides use the inner dimensions, while outer overlays remain attached to the available region. This is a useful separation for RFF: presentation scale, output dimensions, supersampling and temporary preview quality should not be one ambiguous “size.” Reflection texture footprints and relief derivatives need the actual shading grid; pointer picking needs the inverse presentation transform; export uses its own output grid and tile offsets.

**Borders and layout are not image pixels.** Fixed mode explicitly uses content-box sizing so a decorative border does not subtract two pixels from the requested content. That intent is relevant to RFF's output contract even though Win32 layout differs from CSS. Verify encoded image dimensions and viewport mapping independently of frame decoration. A fitted preview need not allocate fewer samples merely because it occupies less screen space, and an enlargement must not be mistaken for additional computed detail.

**Size suppression needs reconciliation.** The frame updates its local layout size before the optional resize predicate rejects the store write. The effect captures its initial predicate rather than subscribing to changes in the callback identity; this is valid only under the documented convention that the predicate reads current state externally. There is no explicit flush of a skipped write when the predicate later becomes true. Combined with the separately observed worker resize path, this reinforces a RFF requirement: maintain one effective-dimensions authority per render target and reconcile pending requests after export or recreation. A claim of one authoritative store writer does not imply there is only one observer or only one size channel in the application.

**Do not silently turn alignment into a format constraint.** `snap8` rounds each dimension to the nearest multiple of eight and applies a lower bound of 64. It supplies neither an upper bound nor finite-number validation. The custom input's HTML maximum of 32768 is not enforced by the button/Enter submission path itself. Aspect-fit dimensions are rounded independently, so the final ratio can differ slightly from the requested ratio; a drag keeps its initial ratio rather than deriving one from the current snapped dimensions. For RFF, validate finite dimensions, device limits, byte counts and memory budgets before allocation. If a shader dispatch benefits from block alignment, pad the internal allocation or dispatch and bound accesses while preserving the user's exact output dimensions, unless rounding is an explicit product choice.

**A reversible size gesture must also handle cancellation.** The drag code captures a pointer but stores no pointer identity and has no cancellation/lost-capture handler here. When the computed displacement returns to zero it skips the setter, so returning to the starting pointer position does not itself restore the original dimensions after a previous nonzero update. These source observations motivate RFF tests for resize gestures, not a recommendation to duplicate GMT's interaction code. Record the initial requested size, publish the current candidate consistently, and close the gesture on every termination path; coalesce redundant reallocation requests while preserving the final requested value.

**Verification for an appearance extension:** compare reflection/detail filtering across a small fitted preview, a 1:1 view, supersampling, DPI changes and tiled export; confirm that changing presentation alone does not alter the stored scene or requested image size. Test arbitrary output sizes as well as aligned ones, cancelled/reversed gestures and deferred resize restoration. These files were inspected only; no UI or image-output test was run in this pass.

## Render dispatch: idle completed images and wake on appearance revisions

A complete read of [GmtRendererTickDriver.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/renderer/GmtRendererTickDriver.tsx) connects the earlier state/worker reviews. Its current implementation contains active animation, texture replay and convergence logic despite the obsolete phase-shell note in the header.

**Avoid repainting an unchanged finished image.** After running registered frame phases, the driver skips worker dispatch when the sample cap is reached and no camera change, interaction, autonomous animation, busy state or recent invalidation demands work. This saves repeated post-processing and cross-thread traffic for settled images. It does not stop the main frame callback or its registered ticks, which still run before the gate. RFF could use an equivalent appearance-dirty policy to avoid unnecessary material/environment recomposition after a static result is complete, while preserving UI activity independently. First verify which idle work RFF already suppresses; this file does not prove that RFF currently redraws redundantly.

**Wake on display-only changes as well as fractal recomputation.** The wake subscription includes uniforms, config, textures, offsets, formula registration and compile status. It also invalidates the proxy's convergence mirror rather than relying only on a 500 ms wake period. This addresses a key circular dependency: if no frame is requested because an old counter says complete, the renderer cannot return a new frame that updates the counter. For RFF, give appearance changes their own revision and request the necessary post-processing even when the fractal iteration map remains valid. An environment rotation should not require recomputing the fractal to make the image refresh.

A requested dispatch is not a completion acknowledgment. The driver updates its last-camera record after calling `sendRenderTick`; downstream flow control may still govern acceptance. The camera comparison uses fixed positional/quaternion thresholds, with offset changes handled by events, and the wake window after movement is time-based. For deep 2D navigation, do not transplant these 3D thresholds: use the exact high-precision view revision or a screen-error bound consistent with the existing RFF coordinate representation. Keep dirty state until a matching completed frame confirms the update, including after a slow compile or resource upload.

**Readiness has multiple stages.** Boot completion checks worker readiness, a compiled-shader latch and no active compilation, then re-sends current size, replays a stashed teleport and starts pending texture updates. It sets the component ready immediately afterward; it does not await those texture uploads or a first frame containing them. A RFF environment asset should expose loading/preprocessing/ready states separately from basic pipeline readiness. Publish the new texture and its filtering data together, and only mark the requested appearance ready once that resource revision is usable.

The watchdog distinguishes failure to begin compilation from a compile still in flight, allows a longer ceiling for the latter, and reports recoverable failure without destroying the worker. That is a useful recovery pattern for expensive pipeline creation. Its timers are heuristics, not proof of a deadlock; late success remains possible. RFF should retain authoritative completion/error handling alongside any timeout message rather than discard a usable late result solely because a duration estimate expired.

**Use one live parameter snapshot per frame.** The driver obtains current modulation values directly for optics instead of a throttled UI copy, uses them for both the camera projection and worker render state, and sends the set of uniforms owned by modulation so base-setting synchronization does not overwrite them. This pattern transfers to RFF's animated materials: base settings, current animated values and UI readouts may update at different rates, but the displayed frame and export frame must evaluate a coherent time and ownership set. The UI's throttled display must not become the source of stepped animation.

**Check phase order where projections matter.** The camera snapshot tick runs in the registered SNAPSHOT phase, followed by animation/overlay/UI work; this component merges optics and updates camera FOV only after `runTicks` returns. Consequently its source alone does not establish that every overlay snapshot already uses that newly applied FOV. For a RFF environment handle or light gizmo, evaluate live parameters before deriving both image and interaction transforms. Verify their agreement with moving parameters rather than trusting a shared base setting.

**Keep control-loop clocks explicit.** The driver calls `viewport.reportFps` at approximately 500 ms intervals with a computed main-callback rate. As established in the slice review, its adaptive algorithm uses invocation timestamps rather than that supplied numeric FPS. The worker separately self-measures adaptive resolution, while the render state forwards delivered-frame rate for band scheduling. These are distinct loops with distinct cadence; copying the generic report API does not reproduce the worker's feedback. A RFF controller should receive the actual measurement and applied scale it is intended to regulate.

**Validation:** let a static image settle, then edit only an environment intensity, rotate an environment, replace its source asynchronously, resize, and trigger a long pipeline build. Confirm each requested revision appears and the loop idles afterward; include subpixel deep-zoom changes and live/export animation timing. No rendering, power or timing measurement was performed in this pass.

## Deterministic appearance updates: separate export time from dispatch timing

Full reads of `engine/TickRegistry.ts`, ADR-0001 through ADR-0004, and `store/slices/installAccumulationBindings.ts` refine how animated environment/material features should be integrated into RFF. The previously reviewed display-camera references were reread for context, without new coverage credit.

**One logical update per output frame needs an identity, not a clock heuristic.** GMT orders registered work by numeric phase and passes a seconds-valued delta unchanged. It suppresses calls arriving less than 1 ms after the previous accepted call. As ADR-0003 itself records, this catches closely spaced duplicate drivers but can also discard legitimate offline frame steps and misses staggered duplicates. For RFF video, derive appearance values from the requested frame index/time and evaluate each logical frame exactly once, independent of how quickly encoding/rendering completes. Separate an interactive pacing guard from deterministic frame evaluation; do not slow an exporter artificially to satisfy a duplicate-call heuristic.

**Phase order is a dependency contract.** The registry sorts lazily after registration and preserves insertion order within a phase, but walks the live array. A callback removing itself can shift the next entry past the loop index; a newly appended callback can execute during the current pass before the next phase sort. Therefore the implementation's ordinary sorted-order guarantee does not cover arbitrary registration changes during dispatch. A RFF scheduler should defer such mutations or dispatch an immutable frame list. Decide explicitly when animation values, view transforms, material masks and overlay coordinates become final for the frame; the preceding tick-driver review showed why merely naming a phase SNAPSHOT is insufficient.

**Keep runtime ownership explicit.** Duplicate names are ignored rather than replacing a callback, and the duplicate registration returns a no-op disposer. The registry is module-scoped, so callers share both entries and timing guards. ADR-0004's statement that duplicate-name guards survive a newly executed module cannot be treated as an unconditional guarantee: the current array is newly initialized by module execution, and actual hot-reload state retention depends on the host. For RFF, let independent preview/export render contexts own their scheduling state, or deliberately share a scheduler with per-context frame identities. Do not let one context's tick suppress another's work.

**Exception isolation must not certify a valid frame.** GMT catches each callback's synchronous exception, reports it once per name, and continues invoking remaining callbacks and later frames. This prevents a broken overlay from freezing every later task, but a failed material update can leave a mixed or stale appearance while rendering continues. RFF can isolate nonessential diagnostics/overlays while treating failed required appearance preparation as an invalid frame revision. Export should report or retry that failure rather than silently encode a partial update. Once-per-name logging also needs a separate current failure state if users must know that the error persists.

**Sample-cap changes are not necessarily image invalidations.** The accumulation binding forwards pause/cap changes and returns cleanup subscriptions; it does not send initial values, report samples automatically, or forward reset events. Raising a cap can continue compatible accumulation, and lowering it can stop additional work while retaining the existing buffer. This resolves the earlier render-control comment mismatch: the binding explicitly documents no reset on a cap change. RFF should similarly separate requested quality budget from changes to the image's underlying distribution. A new environment source, changed material or changed view requires the relevant appearance samples to be invalidated; requesting more samples of unchanged settings does not inherently do so. For deterministic RFF paths, keep this as a scheduling principle rather than add accumulation without a visual need.

The registry's TypeScript `as const` supplies static literal/read-only typing, not runtime object freezing, despite ADR-0001's frozen-object wording. Its exception catch covers synchronous callback throws, not asynchronous work completing later. These scope distinctions matter when translating the design to C++: use explicit time units and lifecycle contracts, and await required asynchronous preparation before committing an output revision.

**Verification:** render identical frame indices at different wall-clock speeds, run preview and export together under the chosen ownership policy, change registration during dispatch, inject a required-stage failure, and raise/lower a sample budget without changing appearance. Confirm identical evaluated scene state and appropriate invalidation. No scheduler or image tests were run in this pass.

## Quality profiles: preserve authored appearance and version the meaning of tiers

Complete reads of `types/viewport.ts`, `engine-gmt/types/viewport.ts` and `store/slices/scalabilitySlice.ts` establish the actual quality-profile mechanism. They separate reusable profile data from the generic registration/application code, but do not implement a non-destructive preview override layer.

**A preset is an edit to the scene.** Applying a GMT preset merges sparse feature overrides and invokes the corresponding feature setters. Changing one subsystem tier recomputes overrides for all registered subsystems, so manual edits elsewhere can be overwritten as well. The slice seeds profile metadata at construction but does not apply those overrides during initialization. Thus a selected/default label alone is not proof that all current feature values match it. For RFF, distinguish an authored material/environment preset from temporary interaction-quality policy. A temporary reduction in reflection filtering or preview resolution should leave the saved source, intensity and material choices intact, with an explicit final-quality evaluation for export.

**Resolve shared parameters explicitly.** GMT merges in subsystem order, with later assignments winning. Its path-tracer tier is deliberately last so it can override lighting-tier values such as `ptNEEAllLights`. `renderContext` metadata is not consulted by this slice's application loop, and `controlledParams` is not used to constrain writes. Those declarations therefore do not prove that inactive-path settings are protected or that parameter ownership is exclusive. A RFF profile design should define ownership and render-path applicability at the application boundary, not rely on display order or a disabled-looking control. Validate the resulting effective settings before activating resources.

**Tier indices need a compatibility policy.** The application clamps an oversized stored index to the current top tier, while preserving the supplied index in profile state. It does not normalize negative, fractional or NaN inputs; missing/invalid selected tiers may be skipped. In-range indices can also acquire a different meaning if a list is reordered or an earlier tier is removed. Named master preset IDs are more stable than indices, but they do not by themselves stabilize the nested tier indices. For new RFF appearance profiles, use stable identifiers or an explicit versioned mapping, and preserve existing palette-recipe IDs and ordered ConfigIO contracts. Do not silently reinterpret an old “Full” setting as a different visual effect.

The generic preset detector checks only keys present in each preset and returns the first match. Extra subsystem values do not prevent that match. Registration stores supplied arrays/objects by reference, and a later registration without a default retains the prior default. These are implementation contracts, not a validated schema. Freeze or copy profile definitions as appropriate, reject ambiguous/incomplete profile data, and derive status from the effective configuration if that status is meant to guarantee a visual mode.

**Hardware policy must not silently lower fractal precision.** The fully read slice's `setHardwareProfile` writes `compilerHardCap`, `precisionMode` and `bufferPrecision` through the quality setter, then emits a full config when its bound serializer exists. Combined with the earlier heuristic detector, this is a policy write rather than proof of physical device limits. RFF must retain its precision requirement: hardware adaptation can limit optional preview work or choose a supported appearance-resource representation with explicit consequences, but cannot silently lower perturbation arithmetic precision or required iteration correctness.

**Choose profile dimensions that correspond to actual user benefits.** GMT distinguishes environment-only reflection from marched scene reflection and reflected-surface shadows; those are different capabilities, not simply stronger versions of one effect. Its expensive volumetric option is deliberately kept outside automatic quality presets. RFF can similarly make gradient/image environment sources and their filtering policy explicit, with costly optional effects remaining deliberate choices. The current tier comments include historical timing and convergence claims; this data file is not a benchmark, and “Full” is not universally fastest to reach an equal-error image. The previously reviewed current shadow implementation also supersedes some shadow-tier commentary. Reconcile any adopted tier with its actual shader path before naming or ranking it.

**Verification:** round-trip profiles across schema changes, edit a material manually before switching one quality dimension, switch render paths, and restore final quality after interaction. Assert both effective values and preserved authored settings, including unsupported-device handling. No profile, rendering or performance tests were run in this pass.

## Shader assembly documents: shared layouts and purpose-specific derived uniforms

Complete reads of the archived `docs/history/archive/10_Shader_Architecture_Refactor.md` and ADR-0044, ADR-0050 and ADR-0055 were reconciled with selected current `GraphCompiler.ts`, `UniformManager.ts`, the previously reviewed builder and current shadow paths. They support implementation patterns for RFF, not a requirement to replace its Vulkan pipeline framework.

**Generate one parameter layout for both producers and consumers.** ADR-0050 correctly treats compile/runtime slot agreement as critical, but rejects a CPU map from `(node,input)` to slot on the mistaken premise that GLSL would need string indexing. It would not: the compiler can use that map to emit literal numeric indices, and the uploader can reuse the same layout. The current unbound `getParam` closure still increments a counter per call, while runtime packing uses declared input order; fixing known node templates does not structurally eliminate that dependency. A future RFF material-mask graph should build one validated layout artifact and use it for shader generation, buffer packing and diagnostics. Duplicate reads of a parameter should reuse its assigned slot. Reject capacity overflow rather than silently substitute zero. Preserve exact C++/GLSL alignment and descriptor/push-constant contracts.

**Precompute values that are constant over a draw.** The current uniform manager computes an environment rotation matrix from the current scalar angle and derives fog-color parameters on the CPU. This is the useful mechanism in ADR-0044: schedule derived values after their dependencies and avoid identical per-pixel preparation. For RFF environment rotation, consider a per-frame/per-resource matrix or cached transform after checking the existing push-constant space and compiler output. Do not assume a measured speedup from moving a few trigonometric operations; uniform expressions may already be optimized. Recompute source filtering only when its dependencies change, not simply because orientation changes.

**Keep geometry tolerance and texture filtering footprints separate.** ADR-0044 says pixel size is anchored to the post-adaptive viewport. Current code instead multiplies the internal height by the adaptive divisor before deriving `uPixelSizeBase`, intentionally recovering a pre-adaptive viewport scale for trace precision, normal epsilon and shadow bias. This supersedes the historical description. For RFF, a quality-stable geometric/relief tolerance may deliberately use a reference output scale, while texture minification must account for the actual shading sample footprint. The earlier recommendation to use actual shading resolution for image filtering should not be read as requiring all geometry tolerances to coarsen during a draft preview. Name these quantities separately and verify behavior across adaptive changes and supersampling.

**Color transforms must retain their actual meaning.** The inspected fog derivation solves a quadratic inverse of the fitted filmic curve with input clamped below one. That is not general sRGB transfer-function decoding and cannot recover arbitrary HDR radiance from a display color. If RFF exposes artist-authored fog/environment colors, define whether they are display colors, scene-linear radiance or a chosen tone-mapped appearance; apply the corresponding conversion. Do not copy distinctive curve constants or claim a full color standard without checking provenance and the implemented transform. This pass does not verify external authorship/license claims.

**Compilation metadata is a contract, not proof of zero runtime cost.** ADR-0055's feature-owned compile/runtime grouping is reusable, but its historical AreaLights example has been superseded by the reviewed runtime-jitter-before-one-march implementation. A runtime toggle can avoid pipeline creation yet still alter ALU, register pressure, sampling or traversal work. RFF should classify changes by actual pipeline/layout/resource effects and measure enabled/disabled paths. Heavy optional features should not become permanent cost merely because their runtime strength is zero.

**Assembly order still needs variant checks.** The archived builder report describes feature-provided dependencies, stubs and deferred shading. These reduce central hardcoding, but string assembly does not by itself enforce symbol signatures, transitive dependencies or equivalence of Main/Physics/Histogram ordering. The report also shows older positional method signatures alongside a later note about named parameters. Use current interfaces and test every consuming variant. For RFF, prioritize shared helper contracts and validated layouts over adopting GMT's entire source-generation system. No compiler, shader benchmark or rendering test was executed in this documentation pass.

## Shader validation: distinguish compiler acceptance from numerical and image correctness

Full reads of `docs/history/gmt/36_Shader_Testing_Suite.md` and `debug/validator.html`, with selected current sections of `debug/native-config-sweep.mts`, clarify which evidence can support RFF adoption. The sweep script was only selectively inspected in this pass and is not credited as a full-file read.

**State which program and which gate passed.** The document describes replacing the production fragment entry point with a diagnostic preview. The current config sweep supplies a constant-zero dummy sample shader and derives its final pass/fail solely from `webglCompile`. The validator itself has additional finite/nonconstant/gradient/thumbnail gates, but the caller overrides their overall result. Thus a green native config row does not mean those numerical gates passed or that the production scene rendered correctly. For RFF, separately validate the production SPIR-V/pipeline interface, the actual effect with its bound resources, and independent numerical/image properties. A reduced entry point is useful for isolating functions, but can remove reachable work and cannot certify all production behavior.

**Numerical probes need valid input contracts.** Despite an older comment saying 4×4, the validator uses an 8×8 RGBA32F target and checks 64 sample outputs. It accepts at least 56 finite distances and 48 gradient magnitudes in a broad fixed range; these are heuristic thresholds, not conservative-distance or derivative-accuracy proofs. The thumbnail uses 64×64 byte RGB variance and interprets orange pixels as NaN markers. Ordinary orange output can trigger that heuristic unless the diagnostic shader reserves the color, and image variance does not prove correct fractal detail. For RFF environment/material work, directly test finite HDR outputs, constant-source behavior, orientation/seams, roughness response and reference image error at representative resolutions. Preserve separate high-precision fractal tests rather than infer correctness from a textured thumbnail.

The validator's uniform uploader handles scalar floats and ordinary arrays of length two to four. It does not generally upload integer/sampler uniforms, matrices, texture resources or longer arrays. It also does not inspect GL errors after uniform writes/draw/readback. Compile/link success therefore remains meaningful as that narrow result, but a render diagnostic requires an appropriate complete binding setup and error handling. RFF tests should use the same descriptor/push-constant layouts as the production pass, with known resource content.

**Backend and coverage are part of the result.** The inspected native sweep launches SwiftShader, so its compile result is not a Vulkan-driver test or real-device performance measurement. The historical document's 43-formula count is not a current coverage claim; the current script contains a 54-formula minimum to catch missing registrations. A count floor is useful but still cannot prove that every expected identifier and required variant is present. Record an explicit case manifest and shader/config hashes for RFF material variants, including disabled paths and export variants.

**Resume results must be tied to the source revision.** The selected sweep code skips prior JSONL rows by formula/mode, without checking a source hash or requiring the previous row to have passed. If every requested key is already present it exits successfully without new execution. That is continuation bookkeeping, not fresh validation of changed shader code. For RFF, invalidate cached results when source, compiler options, layout, resource format or driver changes, and preserve failing/incomplete status until a matching successful rerun exists. Test logs should distinguish reused evidence from cases executed now.

No validator or sweep was executed here. Historical durations, source comments about successful tests and permissive diagnostic thresholds are recorded as descriptions of the harness, not evidence that a RFF optimization has passed acceptance.

## Native sweep follow-through: test effective variants and preserve incomplete status

The complete 479-line read of [native-config-sweep.mts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/debug/native-config-sweep.mts) extends the preceding selective review. This is source analysis only; neither the historical mutation tests nor the sweep was rerun.

**Case names are not variant coverage.** The script's own updated header records that its legacy hybrid controls no longer affect generated shaders and that an earlier hash comparison found identical source for all three named modes. The implementation still writes those old fields. That historical comparison is not a newly reproduced result, but it establishes why the older suite document's mode table cannot be used as current hybrid coverage. For RFF, verify that each requested environment/material variant actually changes the intended pipeline, resources or runtime parameter state. Source equality is expected for legitimate uniform-only changes, so distinguish structural coverage from runtime-value coverage rather than demand different shader text for every case.

**The diagnostic entry point has a narrow purpose.** The sweep uses a greedy regular expression to remove the production main through the last closing brace, then appends a four-slice `map()` visualization. It is not a GLSL parser and can remove later helper definitions along with main. Its uniforms are fixed generic values regardless of formula ID, including only 16 iterations and a small parameter set; they do not recreate each formula's authored preset. The diagnostic also uses a reversed-edge `smoothstep(0.03, 0.0, abs(d))`, so the thumbnail should not serve as a portable image oracle. For RFF, retain a test of the unmodified production entry point and use explicit diagnostic shader variants with complete known inputs when isolating normal, mask or reflection computations.

**A random nonce does not prove a cold driver compile.** The generated source receives an unused random integer constant. This changes source text but a compiler may remove it or cache equivalent intermediate code. The recorded `timeMs` also includes source generation, browser validation, rendering/readback and thumbnail writing. It is not a clean compile timer or per-frame GPU benchmark. RFF measurements should separately record pipeline/module creation, preprocessing, draw execution and output transfer, with cache conditions declared. Retain deterministic source hashes separately from any intentional cache-disturbing annotation.

**Timeout is a result, not cancellation.** `withTimeout` races a promise against a timer; it does not stop the underlying browser evaluation. The recovery path closes/reopens the page in the same browser, and the main routine does not guarantee browser cleanup through a surrounding finally if setup or recovery throws. For a RFF test runner, tie pending GPU work/readback to an owned job, wait for or explicitly retire that job before reuse, and clean up on all exit paths. Do not interpret a timeout as proof that the original work has terminated.

**Incomplete must remain distinct from passed.** SIGINT sets an abort flag and lets the current case finish, but the final exit status depends only on the number of failures already observed. A run interrupted after successful early cases can therefore exit zero with untested cases remaining. Together with the previously identified resume-by-name behavior, this makes an external manifest necessary for a trustworthy completion claim. RFF verification should report expected, attempted, passed, failed and incomplete cases separately, and preserve failure/incomplete status across resume. Thumbnail filenames here depend only on formula/mode, so a later run overwrites earlier visual evidence; attach revision/configuration identity when retaining comparison images.

These findings strengthen the validation plan for the proposed RFF features; they do not add a new visible effect or establish a speedup. The priority remains a correctly filtered editable environment source for existing relief materials, evaluated with production-path images and actual GPU timing.

## Capability contracts for RFF material inputs

Full reads of GMT's [compatibility test](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/debug/test-compat.mts) and [capability protocol history](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/history/gmt/35_Capability_Protocol.md), reconciled with the current [evaluator](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/compat/evaluateCompat.ts), support a shared eligibility contract for the proposed RFF material-field controls. This is integration guidance, not a new measured visual effect.

**Transfer the input contract, not the formula vocabulary.** RFF controls could declare that they need a valid relief normal, a particular scalar field, or a filtered environment resource. Resolve those requirements once for both the UI and shader configuration, including a readable reason when an input is unavailable. A control that silently substitutes zero for an unavailable orbit statistic can produce a plausible but unintended image. In particular, an orbit-derived mask must remain valid across MPA skips; declaring a capability does not prove that the skipped statistics were preserved. Environment reflection can reuse the existing relief normal without adding a 3D distance estimator.

**Define optional and combined inputs precisely.** GMT checks secondary requirements only when secondary capabilities exist. Its pair requirements use a union: each requested token may come from either formula, rather than both. These semantics are appropriate only when the consumer really accepts either provider. For RFF, distinguish a mandatory second input from restrictions on an optional one, and distinguish independently available fields from fields evaluated at compatible coordinates and revisions. Two providers advertising different capabilities do not by themselves establish a valid combined material evaluation.

**Keep validation independent of mutable registration.** The evaluator has no writes, but reads the external feature registry; its result is not determined solely by its scene argument. The test temporarily replaces registered feature requirements to evaluate individual panel sections, then restores them after the call without a finally block. A RFF implementation can pass immutable requirement data directly to the evaluator, avoiding temporary registry mutation and making the same contract usable by preview, export and tests. Validate externally loaded capability names: an unknown required token fails eligibility here, whereas an unknown rejection token never matches. Type assertions alone do not validate loaded data.

**Test semantics as well as registration structure.** The harness checks nonempty shader blocks (except Modular), a parameter array and exactly one recognized shape token, then snapshots non-OK compatibility rows. It supplies no secondary formula and performs no shader compilation or image evaluation. Registry and snapshot-row floors protect against empty workloads, but do not establish exact expected identities, branch coverage or correct numerical fields. For RFF, cover missing required inputs, absent optional inputs, each combined-input rule and each rejection explicitly; then separately verify shader/resource layouts and representative output images. Updating a snapshot accepts a new baseline and cannot establish that the new behavior is correct.

The historical document mixes an early infrastructure-only status with later migration completion and older formula counts. Its sample feature declarations are explanatory examples, not proof of current registered requirements. No compatibility suite or rendering test was executed in this review, and the historical test comments' workload counts were not independently reproduced.

## Adaptive preview: expose the applied quality state, not a proxy label

Full reads of the [archived adaptive-resolution audit](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/adaptive-resolution.md), the [generic badge](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/plugins/viewport/AdaptiveResolutionBadge.tsx), and [GMT's badge](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/topbar/AdaptiveResolution.tsx) were reconciled against the current `engine/AdaptiveResolution.ts`. The useful RFF transfer is a responsive preview with explicit, trustworthy recovery to final quality; these sources do not establish a new shader speedup.

**Use actual activity, then restore quality regardless of cursor position.** The archived audit describes off-canvas pointer position as an engagement condition and idle FPS as the initial scale seed. Current code instead uses activity/grace, with optional accumulation-drop inference, and seeds from a scale-normalized full-resolution cost estimate. Its `mouseOverCanvas` input no longer drives the decision. For RFF material/environment editing, a continuous gesture can enable temporary preview reduction, but resting the pointer over a settings panel should not keep the image blurred. Keep final export dimensions and fractal precision independent of that preview policy.

**Separate user intent, suppression and applied resolution.** The generic badge derives its label from configuration and suppression; it does not inspect the applied scale. GMT's separate badge uses an accumulation threshold of eight and cursor location for Locked/Auto/Always labels. The controller instead protects full-resolution accumulation with a configurable threshold or a default ranging from eight to fifty, and ignores cursor location. Consequently these labels are not authoritative evidence of the controller's actual state. GMT's Off label also says max GPU, whereas disabling dynamic resolution alone cannot prove continuous maximum GPU load, particularly after accumulation caps stop dispatch. A RFF indicator should report the actual preview dimensions/scale and restoration state, with user enablement and export suppression represented separately.

**Preserve the chosen responsiveness setting when toggling.** GMT's badge writes a target of zero on disable and thirty on enable, replacing a previously chosen positive target. The generic badge retains positive targets, but while suppressed its click selects the enable branch and does not lift suppression. For RFF, keep the user's enabled preference and saved target separate from temporary export locks, and make the toggle's effect explicit. An export lock should not be cleared merely to make the button appear responsive.

**Treat timing normalization as an estimate with an explicit workload.** The current controller estimates full-resolution cost as observed frame time multiplied by the square of the downsample factor. It filters large stalls and cadence-limited samples, and can exclude idle tiled work. This is useful for pixel-dominated shading but does not model fixed CPU cost, reference-orbit generation, different tile coverage or asynchronous GPU work automatically. RFF can use its existing GPU pass timing to evaluate the marginal shading cost before adopting a similar seed. Do not reduce numerical precision to meet an interaction FPS target. Also distinguish the hold applied to later feedback updates from a universal no-downscale guarantee: the inspected initial seeding and manual-mode assignments do not consult the hold condition.

**Verification:** exercise a nondefault FPS target across disable/enable, export suppression, a heavy material drag followed by release over a panel, a settled image with capped dispatch, and a resize during restoration. Check applied dimensions and the completed image revision, rather than trusting a label or a requested scale. No runtime measurements were made in this pass. This supplements the earlier exact-final-quality and resize-deadband findings.

## Engine integration: invalidate only affected work and preserve environment source fidelity

A full read of [FractalEngine.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/FractalEngine.ts) connects the previously reviewed material, configuration, accumulation and export components. These are concrete integration requirements for RFF's proposed environment/material features, rather than additional GMT repair tasks.

**Separate structural compilation, appearance reevaluation and display-only changes.** The engine branches on configuration-manager results: structural changes schedule compilation, uniform changes synchronize values, and only changes marked as affecting accumulation reset the accumulated image. Unchanged uniform writes do not reset it. Live modulation owns a set of uniforms that base-configuration synchronization skips, preventing a slider write from briefly restoring an unmodulated value. In RFF, environment orientation/intensity and material controls should normally reuse available fractal fields and avoid regenerating high-precision orbits. A change to how a required field is computed may need deeper invalidation; a display-only operation should invalidate only its downstream passes. Express those dependencies explicitly rather than treating every shader-related edit as a complete fractal recalculation.

**Schedule progressive work against an image revision.** GMT bands a static accumulating scene, excludes autonomous animation directly, and restores the full region when leaving tiling unless another render mode owns it. It also exposes an explicit region-clear operation for export paths that bypass the usual exit branch. The engine chooses fresh-pass versus resume behavior using reset/count state; a frame or sample count alone is not a universal image identity. RFF should retain a revision for source fields, appearance and output dimensions, so a resumed tile cannot blend an old environment/material revision into a new one. Continuous scene-changing edits require a complete current preview; repeatedly resetting a band sweep can otherwise leave most of the image stale. The observed source comments' historical FPS gains are not RFF measurements.

**Budget full-image overhead when splitting work.** The band controller seeds from estimated full-frame cost, adjusts the band count multiplicatively toward a responsiveness target, and freezes feedback at the sample cap. More bands reduce individual tracing work but add repeated history/display overhead and delay completion of a full sample. For RFF, judge a progressive appearance pass by both interaction latency and time to a complete image. Do not infer total throughput from the frequency of partial updates. The adaptive-to-idle guard detects a width increase and may skip one draw while keeping the previous image; a RFF readiness signal must still wait for the requested dimensions and revision to finish, not merely for the target allocation.

**Save the environment asset separately from its preview.** `captureEnvMap` sends float/half-float sources through an HDR readback path capped at 512 pixels per dimension; byte sources go through a fitted tone curve and JPEG. Both paths clamp width and height independently. Thus the HDR path preserves values above one in principle, but neither path is an exact source round trip: resampling, shared-exponent quantization or tone mapping/JPEG can change illumination and sharp reflection detail. For RFF, preserve original source data or an explicitly defined scene-linear working asset, together with color interpretation, projection and orientation. Keep gallery thumbnails or compact preview assets separate. Independent axis resampling preserves normalized UV locations when loaded under the same projection, but changes directional sampling density; do not describe it as guaranteed identical lighting.

**Verify radiance and transfer behavior instead of relying on comments.** The local RGBE helper clamps negative channels and chooses its exponent with `ceil(log2(maxChannel))`; exact powers of two reach a mantissa value of 256 that is clipped to 255, showing that this path is not lossless even before resizing. It has no explicit finite-value or exponent-range validation. The byte capture shader applies distinctive fitted tone-curve constants, while its comments assume the target color-space setting supplies output encoding. This file alone does not prove the final compiled encoding path. Before adapting any such implementation, verify provenance under RFF's NOTICE rules and validate the actual GPU output. A constant linear source, labeled direction map, values above one, small bright texels and seam-crossing rough reflections are useful round-trip cases. No external format conformance or source-license verification is claimed here.

**Restore temporary rendering state on every outcome.** Capture methods temporarily replace render targets and, for snapshots, display uniforms, then restore/dispose on the normal path. The shown methods do not wrap those operations in exception-safe cleanup. RFF's equivalent should own temporary resources and guarantee restoration if allocation, drawing or readback fails. Keep snapshot display encoding distinct from environment-radiance serialization; using the final display image as a lighting asset changes its meaning.

**Keep numerical policy specific to RFF.** This engine chooses mobile precision defaults and uses fixed absolute camera/offset thresholds. These are not appropriate defaults for RFF's deep-zoom perturbation pipeline. Reuse the scheduling and ownership ideas while preserving RFF's required precision, MPA semantics and pixel-sensitive view invalidation. This pass inspected source only; no build, GPU benchmark or image round-trip test was run.

## Output-size evidence: distinguish layout checks from rendered-file checks

The full [e06 survey](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/e06-adaptive-resolution.md), [recorded audit results](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/plans/overnight-audit/results/e06-adaptive-resolution.json), and current [fixed-viewport smoke test](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/debug/smoke-viewport-fixed.mts) complete this historical-document follow-through. The survey is tied to older source hashes and repeats pointer-driven adaptive behavior already superseded in current code. The JSON records previous guard passes and mutation experiments; these are historical claims, not tests executed during this review.

**Adopt assertions that observe the output of a setting.** The current smoke goes beyond reading a saved resolution: it checks one inline-sized container, computed box sizing, its outer dimensions, and the canvas child's layout dimensions. Locating the container independently of the property under test is valuable: a broken property should fail an assertion rather than hide the target. RFF's equivalent should confirm that changing output size actually reaches the rendering destination, rather than merely round-tripping a configuration field.

**Keep the claim within the measurement.** This test measures `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight`, not the canvas backing-store dimensions, GPU attachment dimensions, decoded exported image dimensions, sampling footprint or pixel correctness. Its screenshot captures the page viewport rather than exercising file export. A correct 960-by-540 CSS layout therefore does not prove a 960-by-540 rendered export or correct image filtering. For RFF's proposed filtered environment/image layers, verify actual output-file dimensions and compare the same image region across preview scaling, supersampling and tiled export. Include a labeled high-frequency source to reveal mismatched footprints; a layout-only pass cannot establish texture-filter quality.

**Wait for the required state, not a fixed delay.** The smoke uses fixed waits after navigation and setting changes, so the source does not establish image-completion synchronization. A RFF visual check should wait for the requested render revision and dimensions before readback. This also keeps adaptive restoration and asynchronous texture preprocessing from being mistaken for a completed final-quality image. The test's fixed viewport and default device scale provide one layout case; they do not cover high-DPI, fit-down transforms or resized-window cases automatically.

No new feature ranking follows from these files. They strengthen the verification plan for existing recommendations; no browser smoke, mutation experiment or export was run in this pass.

## Reusable lighting gradients: keep working history separate from saved recipes

A full read of [ADR-0124](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/docs/adr/0124-recent-follows-the-working-gradient.md), checked against the current `syncRecent` and `updateRecent` implementations in `palette/store/workingStore.ts` and `palette/store/favientsStore.ts`, adds an editing-workflow option for RFF's proposed gradient environment. Only the ADR receives new full-read coverage here; the store functions were targeted reconciliation reads.

**One working session should not create a preset on every slider movement.** GMT follows the derived working output, refreshes one recent entry during a session, and separates automatic Recent collection from deliberate keeping. An entry selected from Recent is pinned so its first changed output opens new work instead of overwriting the source. For RFF, this supports experimenting with bright reflection bands or warm/cool lighting zones without losing a previously useful setup. Keep bounded automatic history and deliberately saved lighting presets distinct; automatic retention should not silently change the destination of an explicit save.

**Autosave must respect undo transactions.** The amended design routes delayed collection through `syncRecentOutsideUndo`, while the current function delegates to `outsideParamTransaction`. This makes automatic bookkeeping wait for an open parameter-edit transaction to finish rather than adding an unrelated history change to a long gesture. RFF should distinguish restoring the edited gradient from maintaining its recent-use shelf. Verify a long drag, cancellation, undo after selecting an old entry, and an explicit save during editing. The current pin logic compares against the picked content when a session has no entry yet; the older failure description later in the ADR is superseded by its update block and current function.

**Use rendering identity, not a convenient shelf signature, for GPU caches.** GMT's inspected `favientSig` rounds stop positions and bias to thousandths, includes interpolation and blend space, and deliberately omits color space; ramp content takes a separate signature path. That is a product deduplication convention, not proof of radiometrically identical environments. For RFF environment resources, cache keys must preserve all source distinctions affecting radiance and filtering, including color interpretation and preprocessing settings. A history-entry ID, source-content identity and prefiltered GPU-resource identity serve different purposes. Preserve RFF's frozen `{presetId, seed}` recipe-generation contract rather than adapting an automatic-history signature into existing recipe IDs or changing their regeneration order.

**Choose retention and provenance rules explicitly.** Current `updateRecent` leaves an unchanged earlier-day entry alone, but creates a fresh entry when its content or name changes on a later day, retaining source/origin metadata. This refines the older body text that says sessions always rewrite their original day's entry. RFF can use stable timestamps for presentation without making local calendar boundaries part of shader behavior. Retain known source attribution for adapted or imported assets even when appearance is edited; GMT's product-level rule for displaying unmodified catalogue credit is not a substitute for license obligations or RFF's NOTICE requirements.

This is a supporting workflow improvement for reusable environment lighting, not an additional shader technique or measured performance gain. The ADR's historical tests and multi-document assumptions were not rerun or verified here.

## Export planning: show effective quality before committing an image

A full read of [ExportPanel.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/gradient-explorer/fullscreen/ExportPanel.tsx), with rereads of `exportSize.ts` and `exportRender.ts`, adds concrete requirements for exporting RFF's proposed gradient/image appearances. The latter two files receive no duplicate coverage credit.

**Resolve one plan for the controls and renderer.** GMT separates requested PNG dimensions from internal supersample dimensions, applies orientation and budgets in a pure resolver, and passes the resulting plan to the owner of rendering. This transfers well to RFF: report both final output size and effective sampling quality before export, and let the same resolved plan configure rendering. GMT's 4K and CPU pixel budgets are product-specific limits, not Vulkan limits to inherit. RFF's existing higher-resolution/tiled workflows should retain their capabilities.

**Availability and effective application are different.** The panel's supersampling checkbox reflects the saved preference and whether the mode supports the option, while the resolver can drop the factor to one when the render budget is exceeded. A note explains that downgrade, but a clamped-size note takes precedence, and the collapsed phone branch shows neither note. Likewise a mode without arbitrary-size support gets a screen-export note while the main size label still comes from the requested plan. For RFF, the final export summary should report the effective dimensions and sampling factor together whenever they differ from the request; a checked option alone must not imply it will actually be applied. Retain the user's preference separately so a temporary capability or budget restriction does not erase it.

**Preserve the live image while exporting.** GMT's compositor export creates a separate canvas/compositor and disposes it in a finally block. This supports an RFF export job with its own output resources and immutable appearance snapshot, preventing an export resize from disturbing the interactive viewport. The panel itself only hands off a size plan; it does not establish a snapshot of all render inputs. Changing controls during an in-flight export must affect the next job rather than silently mixing settings into the current one.

**Make filtering and dithering completion explicit.** The inspected export path waits at most 1500 ms for its noise tile, then renders anyway. Its supersample downsampling requests a browser's high-quality image smoothing, without specifying a mathematical kernel in this code; when no 2D context is available it returns the larger source canvas instead. These are fallback policies, not proofs of identical preview/export quality. For RFF, use the established resampling implementation with a declared footprint and ensure requested dithering resources are ready, or report a failed/degraded job. Dither intended for final display quantization should not be baked blindly into a high-precision lighting asset that will later be filtered and tone-mapped.

**Measure the artifact as well as the plan.** GMT reads the finished PNG header to report actual dimensions, accommodating mode-specific limits and fallback sizes. This is useful for truthful reporting, but a header-size read is not an image-integrity or visual-correctness test. RFF validation should combine actual dimensions with decoded representative pixels and the expected render revision. No export or browser test was executed during this read.

## Worker integration: latest-state preview and coherent environment resources

A full read of [renderWorker.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/worker/renderWorker.ts) completes the worker-entry review. The RFF-facing opportunities are responsive preview scheduling, coherent image-resource replacement, and export-resolution region inspection. Web Worker/Three.js APIs themselves are not a Vulkan implementation plan.

**Coalesce disposable preview requests while retaining required state changes.** The worker keeps the newest render tick, but preserves a pending offset-synchronization flag when replacing an older tick. Explicit offset messages discard a buffered tick whose camera data is stale. A GPU-busy tick remains pending for retry, and a finally block clears the rendering guard. RFF can similarly discard obsolete preview work while preserving the latest complete view/material revision. Essential commands such as reference-origin updates or resource replacement must not disappear with a dropped preview. Offline export frames require ordered completion, not this latest-state policy. The source's MessageChannel latency comments are not benchmark evidence for RFF.

**Publish environment texture and derived data as one resource revision.** Byte environment uploads configure horizontal repeat, generated mipmaps, a trilinear minifier, maximum LOD and a rebuilt environment sampling CDF. HDR uploads decode through RGBELoader into half-float data, configure linear magnification explicitly, and update the same environment fields. This establishes that sampler state, source orientation and derived sampling data are part of the image contract. For RFF, keep the source asset, chosen color interpretation, roughness filtering and any sampling tables coherent across asynchronous upload. Ordinary mipmaps do not by themselves establish GGX convolution. A deterministic relief-reflection implementation need not adopt an importance-sampling CDF unless it actually samples lighting stochastically.

**Treat clearing and replacement as explicit operations.** The inspected null-bitmap branch disables a color texture but does not clear the environment binding. The upload branch does not show disposal of the previous binding or a revision-tagged completion acknowledgement; ownership may be handled elsewhere and must not be inferred from this file alone. RFF should specify removal, replacement, failed upload and superseded upload outcomes, including when old GPU resources can be retired after in-flight draws. Do not expose a new source as ready before all required preprocessing is usable. Choose HDR storage from measured accuracy requirements; GMT's half-float decode path is not permission to reduce RFF fractal precision or assume every radiance value survives unchanged.

**Offer a region preview using final-output coordinates.** GMT maps a requested normalized rectangle to integer output-pixel bounds, sets full-output dimensions and tile origins, temporarily changes the sample cap, and suppresses idle band rendering until the region is cleared. This is useful for checking fine material reflections, image-layer filtering and antialiasing in a large RFF export without waiting for the whole image. A RFF implementation should derive the region's actual shading grid and filtering footprint from the final output, use global pixel coordinates for noise, and compare against a crop of the complete export. The shown handler's coordinate uniforms alone do not prove one-to-one final-pixel sampling; validate the downstream grid and projection. Reject nonfinite or invalid rectangles and handle the right/bottom boundary explicitly before deriving integer extents.

**An exclusive render must have a state-reconciliation policy.** While bucket rendering, this worker drops all messages except stop and render ticks. That prevents mid-job configuration changes but does not queue changes for later replay. RFF can protect an immutable export snapshot while independently retaining the user's latest preview state, then reconcile it on return. Diagnostic requests should receive an explicit busy/cancelled result rather than remain unresolved. The environment-capture branch replies even for null/error outcomes, whereas snapshot capture replies only for a non-null result and has no local promise rejection handler. Every request/response API should settle by request ID on success, failure, cancellation and renderer loss.

**Separate boot completion, compile success and presentation.** INIT reports READY before deferred GPU setup. The event bridge sends BOOTED on the first noncompiling notification and relies on compile-failure event ordering to report errors first; it does not independently gate BOOTED on a successful presented frame. Context restoration reports availability but deliberately does not rebuild resources or clear the lost-state gate here. RFF should keep these lifecycle states explicit and preserve the last usable image while a replacement pipeline/resource set is prepared. Rebuild descriptor-compatible resources before resuming after a device/context recovery.

**Diagnostics must capture the workload they claim to reproduce.** The uniform snapshot serializes numeric/vector/matrix values but replaces textures with sampler-kind sentinels. Such a snapshot cannot reproduce an environment-dependent benchmark without the actual image, sampler and preprocessing metadata. The extra counters count calls to readback and setRenderTarget (including duplicate targets), not GPU execution time or distinct framebuffer transitions. Pair counters with actual GPU timings and a resource/configuration revision. No worker, GPU benchmark or region-export comparison was run in this pass.

## Proxy follow-through: version asynchronous assets and settle every request

A full read of [WorkerProxy.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine-gmt/engine/worker/WorkerProxy.ts) completes the current `engine-gmt/engine` pending-file follow-through. This statement concerns that directory's recorded reading coverage, not whole-repository completion or runtime verification.

**Assign generations to asynchronous environment loads.** `updateTexture` fetches and decodes a source, then posts its result through the proxy's current worker. This function returns no completion promise, has no per-slot generation check or abort controller, and logs failures. An older request can therefore finish after a newer selection or clear; a request started before restart can post to the replacement worker. For RFF's proposed environment/image inputs, use an asset-slot generation and renderer generation, discard superseded results, and acknowledge the generation actually bound. Check response success and decode validity before publication. A completed fetch is not proof of completed GPU preprocessing or a displayed frame.

**Replay desired state after renderer readiness.** The proxy explicitly retains custom formulas for replay on every worker creation and separately stashes pre-boot textures/teleports. Its generic outbox is flushed before INIT, when most engine-dependent handlers cannot apply messages. This confirms that a queue alone is not a state-restoration design. RFF should rebuild from a complete desired scene/resource snapshot, then apply later revisions in order. Persist source descriptors rather than relying on a one-shot transferred bitmap to survive renderer recreation.

**Wake rendering when the desired image changes.** GMT clears its local converged-sample mirror when requesting an accumulation reset, so a main-thread stop condition cannot prevent the worker from rendering and reporting its new state. This is a useful RFF scheduling principle for completed images: environment replacement and material changes must invalidate the relevant completion revision immediately, then become complete only after acknowledgement. Avoid copying GMT's absolute offset-drift threshold as a deep-zoom readiness test; use revision identity and RFF's numerical/view contracts.

**Make recovery settle all outstanding operations.** The crash handler clears timers and resolves many diagnostic request maps, but omits `_pendingEnvMaps`; restart clears timers without settling the ordinary request maps. These source paths illustrate why RFF should use one owned request registry with explicit cancellation on renderer-generation changes. Timeout, absence of a resource and renderer failure should be distinguishable outcomes, not all an unexplained null. A cancellation request sent to a busy renderer is not confirmation that work has stopped or its resources are safe to reuse.

**Scope export progress to its job and frame.** The export-frame watchdog is based on silence rather than total duration, so legitimate long work can keep reporting progress. That is useful for RFF's expensive renders. Here frame callbacks occupy single slots, completion is not checked against the requested frame index in the handler, and any export heartbeat refreshes the active watchdog. The caller must serialize requests for this contract to hold. An RFF implementation should enforce that serialization or correlate every completion/heartbeat with export-session and frame IDs, reject obsolete replies after cancellation, and reconcile worker state before starting another session. Start/finish timeouts are separate from the frame watchdog and do not themselves prove worker termination.

**Keep compile status distinct from success.** The proxy's `hasCompiledShader` latch is deliberately not a successful-link certificate, while `lastCompileFailed` tracks post-boot errors separately. General worker ERROR messages are also routed through that compile-failure field after boot. RFF should attach structured operation/revision information to compile and upload failures, preserving the last good pipeline while exposing the precise failed stage. A completed progress bar cannot replace a successful pipeline result and first usable image.

**Reconcile presentation defaults with the sending code.** The worker-entry comment describes low-latency presentation as opt-in/default-off, but the current proxy enables it unless the page explicitly sets `lowlatency=0`. The proxy's historical single-GPU throughput claim is not reproduced here and does not transfer to Vulkan. Any RFF presentation change needs measurements on its actual swapchain path, including input-to-display latency, stable-image behavior and export integrity.

**Report image output and embedded metadata separately.** The bucket-image handler attempts PNG metadata insertion, falls back to saving image pixels when insertion fails, and reports the metadata loss. This distinction is useful if RFF offers reopenable rendered images: preserve the expensive render but make missing scene/resource data visible. A browser download trigger is not confirmation that the user saved a file; an RFF native save path can report actual write completion. No worker restart, image-race test, export-watchdog run or presentation benchmark was executed in this source review.

## Shared shader infrastructure: validate interfaces before assembly

Full reads of `engine/ShaderBuilder.ts`, `engine/ShaderConfig.ts`, `engine/ShaderFactory.ts`, `engine/utils/glHelpers.ts` and `engine/utils/FullscreenQuad.ts` clarify which generic mechanisms can support RFF's proposed material/environment additions. These are shared-engine helpers; their minimal factory is not the complete GMT raymarching assembler.

**Generate both sides of a shader interface from checked declarations.** The generic builder keys uniforms by name and silently replaces an earlier type/array size; exact source-string deduplication for functions and headers does not detect symbol conflicts. Named sections instead accumulate duplicates. The factory invokes each registered injector and does not itself filter by enabled state or compatibility. For RFF, preserve exact agreement between GLSL declarations, descriptor layouts and C++ configurators, rejecting incompatible duplicate declarations before pipeline creation. Explicit feature dependencies and variant eligibility belong in that validation, rather than being inferred from whether concatenated source compiles. A new environment sampler must be included consistently in every consuming variant.

**Typed fields do not make an open dictionary closed.** `ShaderConfig` includes an unrestricted string index signature. Declaration merging can type known fields, but does not remove that signature or guarantee that unknown misspellings are rejected, despite the comment suggesting restored typo safety. For RFF, use explicit configuration fields and validate imported settings at the boundary. Preserve existing append-only binary-setting rules; a flexible GMT feature dictionary is not a reason to alter RFF's file format contract.

**Treat pipeline construction as an owned transaction.** The GL helper deletes a failed shader and deletes the program on link failure. However, if fragment compilation throws after successful vertex compilation, the already-created vertex shader is not cleaned up by this helper. The useful RFF design is complete temporary ownership until a new pipeline is committed, with cleanup at every intermediate failure and the old usable pipeline retained. Uniform-location lookup here allows null; optional optimized-out values and mandatory interface omissions should have different validation rules in RFF.

**Centralize the dither asset contract without overclaiming its statistics.** The helper selects one RGBA noise asset with nearest filtering and exposes a load callback. This keeps consumers consistent, but selecting an RGBA file alone does not prove independent channels or a triangular output distribution; those depend on the asset statistics and the consuming formula. Reuse RFF's established provenance and final-quantization policy, and verify amplitude, mean and spatial/temporal behavior before adapting a distinctive noise implementation. This helper's asynchronous fallback is a readiness state, not proof that requested final-quality dithering has run.

**Share immutable draw resources with clear ownership.** The fullscreen-pass helper shares one geometry across scenes and explicitly leaves its lifetime outside individual passes. That can avoid redundant setup, but the same principle in Vulkan requires resources to outlive every in-flight command using them. The context-loss helper only registers callbacks; it does not rebuild shaders, textures or dependent tables. RFF recovery must reconstruct the complete resource set before publication. These source reads establish design requirements, not measured allocation savings or recovery correctness.
