The transferable principle is an explicit registration phase followed by validated initialization, with required feature and parameter bindings checked before renderer construction. Do not let opening or registering a panel implicitly decide which shader uniforms exist. For RFF, keep feature registration and Vulkan descriptor/layout construction consistent even when an editor panel is absent.

**Validation before adoption:** show the same field in two panels and verify one shared value; rename a visible label without changing its ID; replace a definition; switch layouts; hide an active section; float a panel; and register a feature before/after initialization. Verify the intended shader update independently of panel appearance. No interface was operated, no visual audit was performed, and no application code was changed in this pass.

## Inspection overlays: show renderer evidence without changing the rendering workload

**Read in full:** `engine/plugins/Hud.tsx` (167 lines), `engine/features/debug_tools/DebugToolsOverlay.tsx` (25), `engine/features/debug_tools/index.ts` (32), `engine/features/ui.tsx` (61), and `engine/plugins/viewport/InteractionSessionBadge.tsx` (96). The shared `store/createListRegistry.ts` was also read in full to follow the subscription mechanism.

**RFF application.** A small, optional inspection overlay could identify the selected field, material/environment revision, actual render dimensions, and preview state while users adjust reflection or masks. Keep it separate from shader-produced diagnostic images: a DOM/state overlay does not read back normals, iteration values, or GPU nonfinite flags. The generic debug feature still declares `shaderDebuggerOpen`, but the registered overlay mounts a state debugger and interaction badge, not a shader debugger. Do not count a parameter name as implemented GPU inspection. For RFF's 2D output, field inspection should use the existing numerical buffers and explicit validity masks rather than reconstruct values from displayed colors.

**Visibility needs an actual subscription.** `HudHost` subscribes to registry mutations and calls each item's `when()` during rendering. Contrary to the broad introductory comment, a predicate reading a separate store does not itself subscribe the host to that store. Changes can remain unseen until another render occurs. RFF should publish diagnostic visibility/state changes through an explicit observable contract, without relying on incidental UI updates. The registry caches its list between mutations, which is useful for stable subscription snapshots, but returns mutable item references; avoid changing them silently without notification.

**Overlay lifetime and cost.** The interaction badge self-gates on its open flag and cancels its animation-frame loop on cleanup. While open, it forces a React render every animation frame to poll nonreactive interaction sources. That is instrumentation overhead, not free observation. RFF should sample human-readable diagnostics at a suitable rate and measure performance with the overlay both disabled and enabled. The badge labels an edge/polled mismatch as '(tail)'; it does not independently establish every cause of the mismatch. Its current implementation has no divergence counter despite the older feature-state comment. Record the actual data source and meaning of each displayed indicator.

**Separate presentation from export and input.** The HUD supports hidden mode and top/bottom region hosts, with a pointer-ignoring outer container. These mechanisms allow unobtrusive readouts, but do not prove an interactive child cannot intercept input or that an export excludes every other overlay. For RFF, state explicitly whether diagnostic overlays are screen-only or intentionally captured, and keep ordinary image/video export free of accidental editor content. Anchor pixel/region readouts to the image rectangle, not merely the surrounding window, especially after aspect fitting.

**Registration ownership.** The common registry replaces an item by ID and returns a cleanup closure that deletes that ID without checking whether a newer registration replaced it. An old owner's cleanup can therefore remove the replacement. The HUD wrapper also assigns a new default ordering number on re-registration. Use owner/revision-aware cleanup and stable order where RFF supports dynamic inspectors. Lazy component registration in `features/ui.tsx` maps names to components but provides no renderer-level data validation; a loaded inspector must still verify the buffer/revision it reports.

**Validation before adoption:** toggle visibility without unrelated UI activity; replace and unmount an inspector; change image aspect; enter and leave region preview; export with inspection open; and compare overhead at fixed rendering work. No HUD was operated, no diagnostic buffer was read back, and no application source code was changed in this pass.

## External video overlays: a presentation feature, not environment-lighting evidence

**Read in full:** `engine/features/webcam/index.ts` (66 lines) and `WebcamOverlay.tsx` (409). No camera was requested or opened; this is source inspection only.

**Adoption decision for RFF.** GMT's webcam feature is a DOM/canvas presentation overlay with cropped mirrored video, input-key indicators, CSS blend modes, and a tilted visual plane. It does not upload a video texture to the inspected fractal material path or supply directional environment radiance. Therefore it is not evidence that GMT already supports live-video environment lighting. An optional presentation overlay could help demonstrations of RFF, but has lower priority than reflection-source editing and image-footprint filtering. A future video image-layer source for 2D coloring would be a separate renderer integration, requiring decoded-frame timestamps, texture lifetime, color encoding, filtering, and deterministic export policy.

**Separate opacity from intensity.** The 'Opacity' parameter extends to 3; values through 1 control CSS opacity, while higher values keep opacity at 1 and apply a brightness filter. This combines two different operations under one name. RFF should keep alpha/compositing opacity distinct from scene-linear intensity/exposure, especially for HDR environment sources. CSS screen/overlay/lighten/difference and the opaque 2D canvas are not a specification for RFF's linear-light GPU blending. The CRT appearance is also CSS: two repeating gradients over the canvas, not a fractal shader technique. If a scanline effect is ever desired, define it in output-pixel coordinates and filter it across scale changes and tile boundaries.

**Source and display coordinates differ.** The component crops in source-video pixels, mirrors the resulting image horizontally, then applies a CSS perspective/rotation to the visual child while leaving handles untilted. Its left/right crop handlers accordingly modify the opposite source crop edge. This illustrates why RFF image-layer editing needs explicit source, image, and screen coordinate transforms. It stretches the cropped source to the chosen rectangle rather than enforcing source aspect. Drag handlers allow crop values up to 0.9 individually although feature metadata specifies 0.45, and no joint positive-area invariant is enforced there; the draw path simply skips nonpositive source extents. Validate the crop rectangle as a whole and make fit/stretch behavior explicit in RFF.

**Asynchronous resources need generation ownership.** The capture effect awaits a media stream and assigns it through the current shared video ref, without a generation/cancellation check. Cleanup stops tracks already attached at cleanup time, but a later request completion can attach after that cleanup or to a newer video element. For any future RFF asynchronous image/video source, associate completion with its requesting generation and release superseded resources immediately. Successful source acquisition and successful playback are different states. This is a local lifecycle observation, not a reproduced capture leak.

**Do not copy the timing/input model blindly.** Video redraws are gated toward 15 Hz, while input fading runs on every animation frame using elapsed time since the last canvas update. That repeatedly subtracts overlapping intervals between draws rather than one elapsed interval per fade update, making the intended 0.7-second fade dependent on callback cadence. Use separate monotonic timestamps for simulation and presentation. Left/right modifier keys share one label in a Set, so releasing one can clear a label while the other remains held; there is no blur reset here. These presentation indicators are not reliable proof of actual renderer interaction state. Drag listeners are installed globally and removed on mouse-up, with no matching unmount cleanup in this component; any RFF overlay should own gesture cancellation explicitly.

**Verification before adoption:** test source replacement during loading, disable/unmount before completion, mirrored crop edges, extreme crops, aspect changes, different display rates, lost focus, and output with overlays enabled. Explicitly choose screen-only presentation or renderer-composited export; these files alone do not establish inclusion in exported fractal images. No RFF code, media permission, shader execution, or rendered comparison was changed or performed in this pass.

## Viewport adaptation: separate available space from device identity

**Read in full:** `engine/components/LandscapeGate.tsx` (38 lines), `MobileScrollIntro.tsx` (77), `MobileViewportShell.tsx` (86), `hooks/useMobileLayout.ts` (102), and ADRs `0038-asymmetric-mobile-gating.md` (66) and `0039-address-bar-collapse-svh-dvh.md` (83). The imported `HardwareDetection.isMobileViewport` predicate was checked directly. Browser behavior described in historical comments was not tested or independently verified in this pass.

**RFF applicability.** The native Windows application does not need a browser address-bar workaround. The transferable mechanism is separating user preference for compact controls from actual available image space and input capabilities. For RFF's 2D and relief views, derive presentation bounds and pointer mapping from the current client image rectangle after panels and scaling, while keeping requested export dimensions independent. A narrow window should not silently change material quality or the high-precision fractal coordinate system.

**Names are not device evidence.** All three components use the raw `isDeviceMobile` flag rather than the preference-resolved `isMobile`. However, the underlying predicate is coarse pointer OR window width below 768; a narrow desktop window can satisfy it. Thus the comments' 'real-device only' description is stronger than the executable test. RFF should distinguish compact layout, touch input, orientation, and platform-specific behavior. Do not block access to controls with a device-rotation prompt based solely on window shape. GMT's portrait test is strictly height greater than width, so square windows are classified as nonportrait.

**Initialization and observation are distinct.** The hook installs a module-level resize listener that updates the two flags only when they change; it does not call that synchronization immediately and relies on boot initialization elsewhere. It also does not independently observe changes to pointer capability. RFF should establish initial layout state explicitly and update it from the relevant window/DPI/input events, rather than rely on an unrelated future resize. The nonreactive snapshot helper must not be mistaken for a subscription.

**CSS layout is not render-grid validation.** The shell applies safe-area padding, a dynamic-height style with a class fallback, and sticky positioning; the intro supplies an earlier scrolling area. These components neither size the GPU render target nor establish image-coordinate alignment. The historical ADR's older shell description differs from the current explicit fallback, and its keyboard/address-bar guarantees remain historical claims rather than measured coverage. ADR-0038 itself retracts an earlier implication of automated gating coverage. For any future browser-based RFF viewer, test the actual displayed rectangle, backing resolution, scroll position, and selection mapping together. For native RFF, use the platform's client-area/DPI handling instead of porting CSS tricks.

**Validation:** resize through narrow, square, and wide layouts; change DPI; open panels; use compact-mode preferences; and compare a selected image point before and after each transition. Keep framing decisions explicit and verify export pixels separately from presentation. No native UI, mobile browser, pointer mapping, or shader behavior was exercised here; this is a limited architectural transfer, below the visual shader priorities already identified.

## Shared operation chrome: reactive controls and feedback with explicit ownership

**Read in full:** `engine/plugins/TopBar.tsx` (139 lines), `engine/plugins/topbar/ProjectName.tsx` (75), and `engine/components/ToastHost.tsx` (83). This completes these supporting components' source inspection, not an interactive UI audit.

**RFF transfer.** A common command/status area can expose field inspection, material presets, effective preview quality, and output state consistently across 2D and relief workflows. GMT uses an ID-keyed registry with ordered slots and separately registered controls. Keep canonical parameter/command ownership outside that presentation host, so moving or hiding a button cannot change shader availability or job lifetime.

**Reactivity is specific, not automatic.** Unlike the HUD host inspected earlier, the topbar explicitly subscribes to mobile preference and raw mobile classification in addition to registry changes. That supports predicates using those fields. It does not subscribe to every state field an arbitrary `when()` may read, so a material-capability or export-state predicate needs its own dependency notification. Orientation alone is not one of these subscriptions. RFF should derive command availability from the relevant state revision and avoid treating a registry notification as a universal state update. The first install chooses whether defaults are registered; repeated installs return early. Reconfiguration therefore requires an explicit contract rather than silently assuming later options take effect.

**Text editing must not drive navigation.** The project-name input stops keydown and keyup propagation, preventing ordinary bubbling navigation listeners from consuming typing. Capture-phase/global command handling still needs its own input exclusion; this local event code cannot prove that all shortcut paths are isolated. The visible name/version is metadata, not a completed save indicator.

The comment that it never blocks the viewport is therefore only true of the surrounding container; each message occupies an interactive area. For RFF, keep failures and output completion visible above the appropriate workspace, but avoid placing dismissible feedback over critical selection handles. Mount one host per intended feedback surface to avoid rendering the same queue repeatedly. The component provides no explicit live-region semantics or durable history; do not infer accessible announcement or retained error details from visible text alone. These observations do not establish a visual defect in the running application.

**Checks before adaptation:** update a predicate's underlying feature state without registry changes, switch layouts, rename during Japanese text composition, press Escape, and report an export error while a full-screen inspector is open. Verify commands affect the intended RFF state and that output success follows the real save result. No UI was driven and no shader or application implementation changed in this pass.

## Guided shader exploration: teach visible mechanisms without treating gestures as proof

**Read in full:** `engine/plugins/tutorial/types.ts` (70 lines), `runner.ts` (190), `actionBus.ts` (21), `lessons.ts` (32), and `triggers.ts` (324). This evaluates the tutorial engine, not the accuracy or coverage of every application lesson.

**RFF feature opportunity.** An optional guided comparison could teach the proposed environment shader in three concrete steps: rotate a bright gradient stripe to see directional reflection; increase base roughness to broaden it; then change clearcoat roughness independently. For flat 2D rendering, a second example could compare a detailed image layer before/after footprint-aware filtering at fixed output size. GMT's generic lessons separate explanatory text, highlights, entry/exit callbacks, and completion triggers. Transfer that separation, while keeping the demonstration reversible and preserving the user's high-precision view and authored appearance settings. This is a usability extension supporting the shader proposals, not a higher visual priority than implementing them.

**Match advancement to the intended evidence.** Value/bool/delta triggers observe store values; action triggers observe named broadcasts; key triggers observe browser events. None alone proves that the renderer accepted a new configuration or displayed it. A RFF lesson that says 'the reflection is now rougher' should wait for the matching displayed revision or ask the user to compare a frozen before/after view. Use a parameter-change event for a task about editing, and a completed-operation event for a task about rendering or saving. The simple action bus contains names and callbacks without payload/revision identity, so overlapping operations need a stronger contract.

**Compose triggers as logical conditions.** Compound and OR evaluators recursively set up children using the parent's `advance` callback. Passive conditions are combined by every/some, but active children such as delay/action/keypress can call that shared callback directly. Thus placing an active trigger inside a compound does not establish that every other condition was satisfied. A settling value trigger can also advance directly from its timer. For RFF, children should report their own satisfied state and only the parent should decide advancement. Reject unsupported combinations and unknown kinds during lesson validation. Keypress-all records keys ever seen rather than simultaneous chords; when armed, its keyup handler accepts any released key, not specifically the completing key described in its comment. Teach semantic commands rather than infer them from raw keys, and respect text entry/IME focus.

**Use lesson-scoped lifetime and identity.** The runner's duplicate-entry guard is only the step ID, and advancement checks active state plus step index without lesson identity. Switching lessons with reused IDs/indices or allowing old delayed callbacks therefore needs stronger generation ownership in a RFF implementation. The runner's onExit path searches the current lesson for the previous step and runs only during valid step-to-step entry; completion, skipping, and component unmount do not provide symmetrical onExit handling. Initial-check and auto-chain timers are not held for cancellation here. Capture a lesson-generation token, own all subscriptions/timers, and restore temporary settings on every terminal path. Do not depend on a tutorial component remaining mounted forever to make cleanup correct.

**Capture the right kind of baseline.** Delta uses JSON cloning of the value at entry, optionally after a delay, and a recursive enumerable-key comparison. This is not a general comparator for high-precision classes, maps, sparse arrays, or cyclic structures; it does not explicitly compare array lengths or key membership. RFF should compare the relevant typed parameter or accepted revision rather than JSON-clone its fractal state. The value trigger's wait-for-release reads `isUserInteracting`; any adaptation must use the actual canonical interaction state rather than a similarly named legacy field. Lesson hooks run before trigger setup, so an action emitted synchronously by onEnter can be missed by a later action subscription; define whether entry actions themselves may satisfy the step.

**Validation:** combine an action with an unmet value condition, use delayed settling, switch lessons mid-delay, reuse a step index, cancel at the final step, unmount during a key trigger, and fail a renderer update. Verify that the user can leave the demonstration with the original 2D location and appearance restored. No lesson was launched, no user setting was changed, and no shader behavior was measured in this pass.

## Guided comparisons: anchor explanations to the current control and step

**Read in full:** `engine/plugins/Tutorial.tsx` (66 lines), `tutorial/anchors.ts` (128), `tutorial/Highlight.tsx` (100), `tutorial/stepRenderers.ts` (39), and `tutorial/Overlay.tsx` (333). This completes the recorded tutorial plugin source files; application-specific lessons and whole-repository coverage remain separate.

**RFF transfer.** Stable control anchors and replaceable explanation bodies would support the earlier proposal to teach reflection, roughness, and 2D filtering with short before/after comparisons. GMT keeps anchor identity separate from visible text and permits multiple elements for one anchor ID. RFF should associate a lesson with the active layer/material and exact parameter identity, especially when several layers expose the same control. A generic 'roughness' anchor must not accidentally highlight every unrelated material editor. Keep tutorial decorations out of the image pipeline and export.

**Nonzero bounds do not establish visibility.** Anchor lookup prefers the first element with positive width/height and otherwise returns a fallback; it does not establish viewport intersection, clipping, opacity, or whether another panel covers it. Highlight draws all positive-size entries. The source registry's lifetime tracking is useful, but RFF should resolve the intended visible target in the active workspace and provide an explicit missing-target state. Do not move a user's view or mark a lesson complete merely because a stale control retains layout bounds.

**Observe replacement as well as resize.** Highlight and card positioning observe the elements present when their effects start. Registry updates trigger measurement but do not add replacement elements to that already-created ResizeObserver. Subsequent resizing of a replacement can therefore lack direct observation until the effect is rebuilt. Position-only changes and transforms also need separate handling; a size observer does not guarantee tracking a moved floating panel. RFF should bind observation to current target ownership and use window/panel movement notifications, while bounding measurement overhead rather than polling every frame indefinitely.

**Place cards using their actual size.** GMT uses a fixed 360-pixel card width and several assumed heights/clearance constants, then applies requested offsets after position calculation. The target-relative branch lacks the fallback branch's viewport-relative width. Long explanations, narrow windows, or offsets can exceed those assumptions. For RFF, measure the rendered explanation, keep it inside the usable client area, and avoid covering the control or image region being compared. The highlight and explanation should share a coordinate space; DOM portal choices in GMT illustrate that concern but are not a native Win32 implementation prescription. No actual clipping or positioning failure was reproduced here.

**Displayed and active steps must agree.** Overlay transitions retain the previous displayed step during a 200 ms fade while callbacks invoke current store actions. Opacity changes do not disable pointer input in this code. A user can therefore act on a departing card while the underlying step has already changed. Scope advance/finish commands to the displayed lesson generation and step, or disable them during the transition. Both the transition identity and several effects use step IDs without a lesson revision. Runtime lesson/renderer registries are also read without subscription in this overlay, so replacing content does not automatically guarantee a refresh. Validate unique identities and immutable lesson versions before activation.

**Keep fallback and completion explicit.** An unknown custom card kind silently falls back to text. The last-step auto-chain UI tests truthiness while the runner tests non-null, so a numeric lesson ID of zero has different handling. A final nonmanual step without manual allowance has no Skip button in this component. RFF should always offer a clear exit, validate renderer/trigger kinds, and use consistent optional-ID rules. Completion persistence is namespaced by installation, but a stored completion flag is not proof that a rendered shader comparison succeeded. Key-flash timers are presentation effects and should not outlive their step.

**Validation:** open multiple material editors, replace an anchor, move/resize a floating panel, scroll a clipped target, use long Japanese explanations, click during a transition, and cancel on the final step. Verify exact restoration of the user's 2D view and material state. No tutorial was launched, no interface screenshot was assessed, and no source implementation was changed in this pass.

## Update and release notices: preserve the rendering session

**Read in full:** `engine/plugins/PwaUpdate.tsx` (135 lines) and `WhatsNew.tsx` (94). Browser service-worker behavior described in the headers was not independently verified or exercised. Native RFF does not need this browser update implementation.

**Limited RFF transfer.** Separate update availability, application/restart, and release-note acknowledgment. GMT presents a user-operated reload button rather than reloading immediately in its own event handler. For RFF, preserve an ongoing deep-zoom render, export job, unsaved palette, and edited environment source before accepting a restart. This is operational support for both 2D and relief workflows, not a shader optimization. A tooltip telling users to save first is not an actual save or active-job check; the inspected click handler itself has no such gate.

**Availability and loaded version differ.** The PWA watcher fixes `hadControllerAtLoad` at installation and ignores every later controller change when it was initially false, not merely the first claim. It does not compare build identities. RFF should use explicit installed/available/running versions rather than infer them from a generic lifecycle event. The waiting-worker fallback schedules a reload and unregisters all registrations returned by the browser API; that is broader than targeting the application's own registration. Do not transfer this fallback pattern into an updater or renderer cache reset. Each subsystem should own only its resources.

**Lifetime must match ownership.** The service-worker update interval is installed from registration completion without retained cleanup here. Uninstall removes the topbar item and installation flag but does not remove the watcher, reset takeover state, or cancel those intervals. A RFF update service should have explicit session ownership and cancellation, keeping background version checking distinct from the visible button's lifetime. No interval, update check, unregister action, or restart was executed during this audit.

**Release-note indicators are presentation state.** `createWhatsNew` caches whether the stored string differs from the current version; this is inequality, not an ordered newer-version comparison. It marks the release seen before invoking an optional help-opening action, so the cleared indicator does not prove content was displayed. Its cached value does not observe other contexts changing storage. For RFF, scope acknowledgment to the application and release, confirm the content can open, and retain access after the indicator clears. New shader features should link to their mechanisms, defaults, and compatibility notes; release notes must not imply benchmark gains that were not measured. Existing RFF changelog rules still apply if implementation later warrants an entry.

**Checks if implemented:** offer an update during a render/export, cancel restart, fail saving, reopen release notes, and load a release older than the last acknowledged one. Confirm exact recovery of the 2D location and appearance assets. No updater, changelog, application code, or user settings were changed in this pass.

## Contextual shader help: connect each control to its mechanism and limits

**Source read in full:** `engine/plugins/Help.tsx` (589 lines). This is help/menu/overlay integration, not the topic corpus itself. Topic accuracy and renderer behavior cannot be established from the presence of a help link.

**RFF proposal.** Pair each new appearance control with a short visible-effect description and a link to a deeper mechanism explanation. For the environment proposal, distinguish source gradient/image, reflection direction, roughness filtering, pixel-footprint filtering, and base versus clearcoat response. For 2D image layers, explain why final downsampling cannot always remove aliasing introduced by an earlier lookup. GMT provides inline hints, longer lazy-loaded topics, tutorial entry points, and optional HUD shortcut hints behind one setting. This is a useful way to expose the detailed shader mechanisms requested in this review without making every normal control display implementation detail.

**Content should describe the actual implemented approximation.** RFF help should say whether environment filtering is an artistic mip approximation or a BRDF-prefiltered source, what field a mask reads, whether a control changes geometry or only appearance, and what extra cost is expected. Keep measured performance separate from estimates and preserve the distinction between MPA and BLA. Link recognizable adopted techniques to their verified provenance/NOTICE entry at implementation time. The Help plugin's support/about extension slots carry caller-supplied content; they are not independent evidence for algorithm claims or licensing.

**One preference still needs complete propagation.** The hint toggle and H shortcut update `showHints`, while registered HUD hints use a predicate reading that value. The previously inspected HUD host subscribes to registry changes rather than arbitrary store fields, so this plugin's shared flag does not alone guarantee immediate HUD refresh. RFF should connect every presentation consumer to the same observable setting. Similarly, the tutorial list subscribes to lesson count, not lesson content/revision: replacing a lesson under the same ID without changing count is not guaranteed to refresh its title through that subscription. Use a stable versioned snapshot when help content is dynamically replaceable.

**Separate transient menus from persistent explanations.** GMT lifts support-modal state outside the menu item so closing the menu does not destroy the modal. The same ownership principle suits a RFF mechanism viewer or comparison window opened from a menu. Use the common modal/window system for focus, dismissal, and stacking, and retain access to rendering status while help is open. The optional help-opening calls and a null Suspense fallback do not establish that requested content was shown; provide an explicit loading/unavailable state when appropriate. No running modal or keyboard behavior was tested here.

**Lifecycle and scope.** Uninstall removes the Help menu and shortcut but does not clear registered HUD hints or the support-modal singleton. If RFF supports dynamically replacing help modules, make the resources owned by each installation explicit. Disabling all hint controls while registering flag-gated HUD hints can also leave the preference inaccessible through this plugin's own controls; validate the chosen configuration. Keep tutorial completion markers as navigation history, not evidence of image correctness.

**Checks before adoption:** open help directly from a roughness/mask control, change the hints setting while the viewport is otherwise idle, replace a lesson title, fail a lazy topic load, and close the originating menu while retaining the explanation. Confirm that help operations do not alter RFF's 2D location, image appearance, or active export. No help UI was launched or application source changed in this pass.

## Shader benchmark handoff: validate active work and sharp highlights before ranking changes

**Sources reviewed:** all 989 lines of GMT's `docs/BENCH_SHADER_HANDOFF.md`; targeted current-code checks in `debug/bench-shader.mts` (reference selection and verdict handling), `engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/math.ts`, and `engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/lighting/pbr.ts`; RFF's `shdsrc/studio_ggx.glsl`. The benchmark script is not credited as fully read by this section. Historical timing tables were not reproduced, and their reported gains are not RFF performance predictions.

The handoff's most useful transfer is experimental design. It records a reflection benchmark where choosing raymarch mode compiled the code but the material's roughness exceeded the runtime cutoff, so reflection rays were not exercised. It also records a nested-array uniform serialization failure that disabled meaningful lighting. These histories support an RFF acceptance rule: verify the effective resource bindings, parameter values and visible response of the intended feature before interpreting its timings. A settings label alone is insufficient. The document's older blanket claims about uniform-branch predication are narrowed by its later function-call experiments; neither is a universal claim about RFF's Vulkan compiler or hardware.

### Direct application to the proposed RFF environment reflection

Use a small scene matrix: legacy environment; constant environment; a labeled panorama with one narrow bright stripe; and a multicolor gradient. Sweep rotation, base roughness and clearcoat roughness independently. Include a bright HDR source and a near-grazing normal. Capture the effective environment asset and its revision, mip/filter policy, intensity, material settings, output size and display transform with every result. A mirror-like material must visibly respond to stripe rotation before its cost can count as an environment-reflection measurement. Compare both fixed-quality GPU time and interactive update latency; compiling pipelines, filtering environment assets and drawing pixels are separate costs.

Current GMT benchmark code explicitly skips the default reference comparison for several scene overrides, including material, reflection and path-tracing variants. Missing references and diff exceptions can also leave the diff absent. Its displayed PASS/WARN/FAIL thresholds do not themselves throw or set an error exit status in the reviewed verdict block. Therefore a completed benchmark process is not a quality pass. For RFF, use matching per-scene references and distinguish `not compared` from `passed`; any future automated gate must actually enforce its declared result. Intentional appearance additions need expected-behavior checks as well as legacy-mode regression checks, since matching the old image would defeat the new feature.

### Numerical guard behavior is part of the material model

The handoff says changing the additive GGX denominator epsilon from `1e-4` to `1e-7` leaves the low-roughness peak intact. The currently inspected GMT expression is still `D = a2 / (PI * denom * denom + GGX_EPSILON)`, with epsilon `1e-7`. Using the document's own example, roughness 0.05 gives `a2 = 6.25e-6`; at the ideal peak the unguarded denominator is about `1.23e-10`. Adding `1e-7` still dominates it: the peak becomes about 62.4 instead of 50,930. This arithmetic contradicts the document's claim of an intact peak; it is not a newly measured image regression or a request to repair GMT.

RFF already takes a different approach: `studio_brdf` floors microfacet alpha at 0.02 and guards the anisotropic distribution denominator with `max(..., 1e-20)`. Do not copy GMT's epsilon change into it. The existing alpha floor means isotropic roughness values below approximately `sqrt(0.02) = 0.1414` share the same base alpha. That is an explicit sharpness limit to account for when defining the new environment filter's roughness convention. Evaluate base and coat call-site conventions separately; a shader helper alone does not prove their complete behavior. Preserve numerical stability, and test peak shape, finite output and temporal stability together rather than removing guards merely to raise brightness.

### What transfers from 3D to 2D

The scene-matrix method, active-path validation, matching references and separation of compile/upload/draw costs all transfer directly. Relief rendering additionally benefits from controlled reflection stripes and roughness sweeps. For flat 2D, replace the panorama matrix with fine grids and directional stripes under zoom, warp and animation; compare against a sufficiently sampled reference at identical field coordinates, and inspect localized aliasing rather than only whole-image average error. Path-tracing Russian roulette, bounce-count changes and 3D distance-estimator shortcuts are not direct optimizations of RFF's perturbation or MPA computation. None of this inspection justifies reducing fractal precision.

**Priority impact:** editable environment reflection remains the leading provisional appearance improvement beyond bloom for relief; footprint-aware image filtering remains the leading candidate for flat 2D. The handoff strengthens the required validation, not the evidence for a measured speedup or a completed implementation.

## Shader benchmark implementation: preserve resource identity and distinguish replay from production

**Source:** complete read of GMT `debug/bench-shader.mts` (1,287 lines). This completes the script read left partial in the preceding section; it does not claim a new execution or full revalidation of the separate `shader-bench.html` runner.

The useful architecture is to obtain the compiled shader and serialized uniforms from the running engine, replay a controlled workload, and save the output image with timing and provenance. RFF can adopt that separation as a native Vulkan diagnostic: capture the actual display pipeline and its resource state, then compare isolated GPU cost with complete application latency. Reimplementing a similar-looking shader separately would weaken the comparison. However, replay fidelity must be demonstrated; this script's introductory claim of perfect fidelity is stronger than its implementation establishes.

### Environment and texture resources must travel with the shader

The capture obtains shader text and uniforms through two concurrent proxy requests, then reads material/environment settings from the UI store. It supplies no shared render revision proving that all three belong to one accepted frame. Its settling loop checks `isCompiling` and silently ends after 25 seconds even without a successful quiet interval. A later accumulation increase proves some rendering activity, not that the requested resource revision was used. For RFF, capture the accepted pipeline, uniform, image and sampler revisions as one render snapshot, with an explicit failure if the requested revision cannot be observed.

The script removes all serialized `__sampler` entries before replay. Its configuration separately carries an environment URL/data URL, source selection and color-space flag, but does not package arbitrary gradient/image/noise textures through this interface. The comments explicitly describe dummy sampler binding by the runner. A remote URL also identifies a location rather than immutable image bytes. Therefore this capture interface alone is insufficient to validate RFF's proposed image-layer filtering or editable environment gradients. A useful RFF replay bundle should record actual asset hashes or immutable bytes, dimensions, format, color interpretation, mip contents or deterministic generation settings, sampler state and history policy. Validate which resources the separate runner reconstructs before accepting a replay as equivalent.

The script deliberately forces full-frame region bounds, resolution, frame count, jitter and time, and rescales the camera's horizontal basis to the test aspect ratio. This avoids accidentally timing only a progressive strip and improves repeatability, but it is an altered workload. Its default blend factor is 1; a lower override can activate different steady-state shader paths while blending with dummy history, which the source acknowledges darkens the image. For RFF, measure full-frame and interactive/progressive workloads separately, with real history where required. Do not interpret the reciprocal of isolated draw time as application FPS.

### References must describe the effective run, not just its command line

The fixed reference filename is Mandelbulb-specific, while the script supports other formulas, saved snapshots and direct shader overrides. Its scene-variant predicate does not include every appearance-changing option: formula selection, shadow/environment disabling, blend factor and marcher knob overrides are examples. Moreover, `--use-snapshot` bypasses the live scene setters, while metadata still includes command-line scene requests. RFF's reference selection should therefore use the effective captured state and asset identities, not a manually maintained subset of option names. A cached snapshot should report which overrides actually applied.

The metadata usefully records the adapter, shader hash, sample count and raw timings, but the `Software` string calls the shader hash a commit and the comment contains a fixed historical scene/optimization description. Neither establishes the current source revision or effective configuration. RFF should store source revision and shader binary/source hashes as separate fields, derive scene descriptions from captured state, and preserve immutable result bundles. Here the timestamped JSON archives can still point to a formula/resolution image filename overwritten by later runs, so retaining JSON alone does not preserve its visual evidence.

### Color and sampling validation require more than the preview difference image

`computeDiff` calculates RGB MAE, RMSE, maximum error and quadrant MAE, but its red/green visualization uses the difference of the arithmetic mean of RGB. Equal-mean color changes can produce a black difference image despite nonzero RGB error; this is especially relevant to colored environment bands and palette images. The function does not calculate the SSIM-like metric mentioned in its introductory comment. For RFF, retain RGB numeric errors and add a channel-sensitive absolute-error visualization, plus linear HDR comparisons before tone mapping when testing reflection energy.

Both reference and result are resized through a browser canvas to the requested dimensions. That can be convenient for inspection, but a rescaled reference is weak evidence for a footprint-filtering change: resampling itself changes high-frequency content. Use identical output sizes and field coordinates, a deliberately well-sampled reference, localized regions around sharp highlights/seams, and temporal sequences for shimmer. Record the display transform separately from linear-domain metrics.

The statistics helpers return zero for an empty timing array, and this script has no explicit finite-positive/minimum-sample acceptance gate before deriving timings and theoretical FPS. Treat absent or invalid samples as an invalid measurement in an RFF tool; do not let a plausible formatted report substitute for successful timing collection. Also keep compile timing distinct from repeated draw timing and environment preprocessing cost.

**3D-to-2D value:** these controls directly support the existing priority proposals. Relief environment reflection needs faithful angular/color resources and independent base/coat tests; flat 2D filtering needs faithful image/mip resources and matched pixel footprints. The implementation review adds verification requirements, not a measured benefit estimate or a recommendation to optimize GMT itself.

## Direct manipulation of gradient fields: useful controls for the proposed shader inputs

**Source:** full read of `gradient-explorer/fullscreen/GeometryHandleLayer.tsx` (1,101 lines), with targeted checks of shared `bias`, `conicTwistTurns` and `radialSineReach` in `palette/core/rampGeometry.ts`, and interaction/render wiring in `FullscreenGradientOverlay.tsx`. No interactive UI test is claimed.

GMT draws a separate SVG control layer over the gradient image. Linear controls change direction and symmetric ramp bias; radial controls change center, reach, bias and sinusoidal petal amplitude/frequency; conic controls change center, seam rotation, mirrored sweep, each half's bias and spiral twist. Its guides call the same mapping helpers as the sampled field: radial reach is `scale*(1+amp*sin(freq*angle))`, and twist is `twist*log(1+r)` turns. Reusing the mapping law makes the guide describe the actual effect; the sampled polyline remains an approximation, not an exact contour at every scale.

**RFF application:** offer direct handles for selected decorative UV fields and for a gradient environment's authoring preview. Define canvas-space versus environment-direction coordinates explicitly; dragging a gradient center in a flat preview is not automatically moving a physical light. Keep the original fractal iteration field unchanged. Store one parameter model shared by controls and shader evaluation, and verify CPU/GPU mapping parity before relying on the guide. These are authoring improvements to the environment/mapping proposals, not another standalone shader effect.

Most GMT gestures accumulate pointer deltas, scale each segment by the current precision modifier, and clamp to declared parameter ranges. Angular differences wrap across the seam. Display positions can be pinned inside the viewport without rewriting the underlying value. That combination is useful for offscreen centers and large texture transforms. The conic mirror gesture is an exception: it maps absolute angular distance to a mirror fraction and does not use the precision multiplier. A port should specify gesture semantics individually rather than claim all controls have identical delta/precision behavior.

The petal-count handle applies a nonlinear soft notch around integers rather than integer rounding. Fractional counts remain possible and can create a seam. The stored value is the notched value, but the next drag initializes its internal accumulator directly from that value rather than an inverse notch; even a zero-delta move can apply the notch again to a fractional value. For RFF, avoid cumulative remapping on re-grab, and make periodicity an explicit option rather than promising seamless fractional repetition. Filter the final transformed UV footprint; smooth pointer motion alone does not prevent shader aliasing.

The shell keeps faded handles hit-testable, clears the shared interaction flag on its own unmount, and reduces opacity after idle time. Individual gestures handle pointer-up/cancel but have no lost-capture handler or pointer-ID ownership check here. Switching the handled child or hiding handles need not unmount the shell. A native RFF implementation should finish/cancel one owned edit transaction on capture loss, control replacement, window deactivation and mode changes, restore full-quality rendering, and keep one undo record per gesture. Numeric controls and reset commands should remain available alongside pointer handles; this component alone provides no keyboard editing path.

Targeted overlay checks show interaction selects a smaller render cap and disables dithering until the release repaint. That is a preview policy to evaluate, not a precision optimization to apply to RFF's fractal computation. Keep export separate from the control overlay and force final-quality sampling for settled preview/export. Test wide/tall viewports, pinned handles, angular seam crossing, fractional-count re-grabs, modifier changes, cancellation and preview/export agreement. The main priority remains the shader feature itself; handles make its effects easier to author.

## Gradient preview integration: responsive editing must preserve the final source and export state

**Source:** full read of `gradient-explorer/FullscreenGradientOverlay.tsx` (964 lines). This extends the preceding direct-manipulation review through the preview host and its export call sites. No UI launch, benchmark or export was performed.

GMT resolves a live gradient supplied by its host, falling back to the opening snapshot. When the host supplies a rendered ramp, that ramp takes precedence over regenerating colors from fitted stops. This is useful for RFF: an environment/texture preview should consume the actual edited color result, because reconstructing it from an approximate stop representation can change the appearance. The same resolved source is published for stage editors and passed to render modes, reducing competing sources of truth.

The inspected preview uses a byte-oriented ramp signature and an RGBA8 lookup texture. Its signature masks each channel to eight bits and hashes those bytes; that is not an appropriate identity or storage representation for floating-point HDR radiance. For RFF's proposed environment reflection, retain a linear floating-point source and an explicit exposure/display conversion for the authoring preview. Do not bake preview dithering or display tone mapping into the illumination source. If a final processed ramp differs from its editable stop document, persist the representation needed to reproduce it, while preserving existing palette recipe identity and regeneration rules.

### Interaction and settled quality are separate rendering policies

The shared compositor sizes its image from the stage and device pixel ratio, capped at DPR 2 and a 2560-pixel long edge. While a handle is active the long-edge cap drops to 1280 and the compositor dither flag is disabled. A cpuField mode with a GLSL body uses the GPU path until a 180 ms quiet timer settles, then performs the CPU field/dither path. Thus the preview is not guaranteed to be native-resolution on every display, and a still pointer held during a drag can allow the timer to settle while the interaction flag remains true. The implementation's exact states matter more than the comments' shorthand of GPU-while-dragging/full-quality-on-release.

RFF can borrow coalesced edits and explicit final-quality completion for appearance parameters, without changing orbit precision or MPA computation. Reuse an existing fractal field while adjusting a gradient, mask or environment. Define the accepted final state by revision and completed render quality, not merely an elapsed timer. Compare CPU/GPU evaluators across seams, transformed coordinates and color domains before swapping between them. Do not assume GMT's historical CPU cost comments predict RFF's Vulkan costs.

The overlay coalesces state-triggered paints with requestAnimationFrame, and avoids repeated CPU rendering using a key for mode, parameters, dimensions and dither plus ramp/image object identities. ResizeObserver callbacks paint directly. This is a useful cache boundary, but it relies on immutable inputs; mutating a ramp in place can defeat identity-based invalidation. For RFF, explicit content revisions are preferable for asynchronous GPU uploads and live image replacement. Mark a cached frame successful only after its rendering succeeds; here the CPU cache key is set before invoking the field/raster presenter.

### Renderer lifecycle and export must carry one coherent state

The registry supports both a shared compositor and modes that mount their own renderer. The host forwards source context, readiness, errors, dither and export calls through that interface. A useful RFF implementation should explicitly initialize every new renderer with the complete current state. Here dither forwarding is in an effect depending only on the dither value; changing between renderer-owning modes with an unchanged value does not by itself trigger that effect. Ready/error callbacks also have no generation check at this host. Specify stale-callback rejection and mode disposal as part of an RFF preview contract rather than copying the lifecycle literally.

At-size export uses a separate render path and reads the resulting PNG dimensions for its filename, which is a good distinction between requested size and actual output. Modes without at-size rendering fall back to the screen image with a warning. The current implementation embeds a fractal scene in at-size exports despite older nearby comments saying otherwise. Both export paths read active fractal coordinates after asynchronous image creation; the image and embedded view are not explicitly captured as one immutable revision here. A future RFF environment/gradient export should freeze source, geometry, camera when relevant, dimensions and quality before rendering, then generate metadata from that same snapshot. Do not silently name requested dimensions as actual dimensions when size verification fails.

The visible controls are separate DOM/SVG layers from the exported canvas, so their separation is a useful architectural precedent. For native RFF, use a corresponding clean render target rather than capturing editor decorations. Preview/export agreement should cover the final ramp, HDR interpretation, geometry mapping, dither policy and orientation, with real-resource tests for each renderer type.

**2D transfer and priority:** the responsive editor and export contract support flat color-field authoring as well as relief environment lighting. They improve usability and reproducibility of the ranked shader proposals; they are not evidence that another lighting algorithm or additional fractal calculation is needed.

## Export actions: distinguish an editable palette from a sampled interchange result

**Source:** complete read of `gradient-explorer/v2/exportActions.ts` (685 lines). This review covers action routing and data passed to builders; it does not independently prove every target application's import fidelity or any third-party license grant.

GMT deliberately separates three subjects: the editable gradient configuration, a sampled continuous ramp, and a discrete swatch palette. Native gradient-file actions pass the real configuration and optional origin/source metadata to the file builder. Registry formats instead build from a ramp, optionally reducing it to a stop budget. Swatch actions use the explicit palette list, or sample each collection member according to a selected count and layout rule. This is a useful model for RFF: a rendered lookup texture is not interchangeable with an editable palette recipe, and exporting a few representative colors cannot preserve the whole continuous field.

**RFF proposal:** provide a clear distinction between saving the editable source and exporting colors for another program. Preserve stable recipe identifiers/seeds and regeneration order for recipe palettes; keep authored stops, interpolation and relevant color-space semantics for edited palettes. If an environment source is derived from a gradient, also preserve its projection and intensity/HDR interpretation in the environment settings. A generic sampled palette export should not silently become the authoritative source on the next load.

The action layer centralizes name resolution and byte generation. `exportText` and download actions use the same format builder, with the same ramp/swatches choice and stop budget; collection previews and downloads likewise share bundle construction. This is a strong pattern for RFF's preview of exported palette data. However, they are separate calls: matching builder functions does not freeze a source that changes between preview and click. Capture a versioned export input when starting an operation, and label any sampled/reduced representation accurately.

Loss warnings in this file concern stop-budget reduction: swatch exports return zero from the loss-count functions, and formats without a stop budget return no such warning. That does not prove lossless interchange in all respects, including color-space conversion, quantization or target interpolation. RFF should describe the specific loss being tested and verify the reconstructed ramp under the destination format's semantics. For the image/environment proposals, inspect narrow bright bands as well as average color error; a small region can materially affect reflections even when a global palette error is small.

Collection formats can produce one bundled file; otherwise the code generates individual files in a ZIP, except a one-member collection becomes that member's file. The transferable benefit is a common export plan that drives both the displayed output type and the actual builder. Keep per-member source metadata and avoid name collisions when implementing batch palette/environment export in RFF. A bundled file, ZIP and single palette should remain distinguishable in the saved result.

GMT's recent-export identity is action kind, format and subject, not the content or exact settings. It repeats an operation on the current working gradient. It also records copy actions before the clipboard promise succeeds and starts swatch-sheet creation without awaiting success before noting the recent. For RFF, distinguish a convenience list of recent commands from a history of completed saved artifacts; report success from the actual operation result. Repeating an export should make clear whether it uses current settings or the previous frozen input.

The source keeps catalogue origin in native gradient files, while display-name credit is conditional on the unmodified ramp and is not applied to swatch exports. Treat that as GMT's presentation policy, not as a licensing rule for RFF. Preserve known provenance for derived materials and consult the actual source license before adaptation; modification or swatch sampling alone is not evidence that attribution obligations disappeared. The existing RFF NOTICE and source-attribution rules remain applicable.

**3D-to-2D transfer:** source-preserving color export benefits flat 2D palettes, texture lookups and relief environment assets. It supports reproducible shader inputs without changing the fractal calculation. This is workflow infrastructure supporting the ranked shader improvements, not an additional visual effect or a measured performance gain.

## Image-derived palette integration: keep the analytical source separate from its presentation

**Sources:** full reads of `gradient-explorer/v2/ImageSlot.tsx` (192 lines), `ExtractStage.tsx` (114 lines), and `useGroundSource.ts` (96 lines), plus a targeted check of the already-reviewed `palette/store/imageStore.ts` model/thumbnail commit. These are source-level observations, not a visual UI audit or a new validation of the underlying extraction algorithms.

The image slot subscribes separately to the analytical model, display thumbnail and loading flag. During replacement it can keep the old picture visible under a loading indication; the store's `setModel` commits model and thumbnail together and clears loading. That is a useful RFF pattern for image-derived palettes and environment assets: retain the accepted source while decoding a replacement, then publish the new analysis and thumbnail as one revision. This store setter alone does not establish request ordering; the decode owner still needs cancellation or stale-result rejection. Show which accepted image generated the current palette instead of implying that an in-progress replacement already supplied its colors.

The image presentation can be grayscale, partially transparent and animated when it is no longer the active source. An `instant` option disables the transition for an eyedropper workflow, but does not itself remove the dim filter or opacity. For RFF, sampling original decoded pixels in a declared color space should be the default for source-color extraction. A screen eyedropper samples the displayed result, including presentation transforms and background composition, and needs to be described separately. Disabling animation alone is not proof that displayed and source colors match.

The compact image door encodes a thumbnail URL once per canvas identity. That is cheap for an immutable thumbnail, but changing the pixels of the same canvas does not invalidate this memoization. Use explicit image revisions or replacement objects in an RFF thumbnail/cache design. Keep the full extraction model independent of panel lifetime: collapsing or moving an image panel must not discard a drawn extraction path, source metadata or accepted colors.

`ExtractStage` connects three modes to one parameter store: Dominant, Tones and Path. These remain different creative operations: representative colors, colors organized by brightness, and colors sampled along a spatial route. The local controls call the existing extraction subsystem rather than creating another decoder. Entering Path invokes `autoPath(model)` and stores that route; it does not preserve a manually edited route in this handler. RFF should distinguish selecting a method from explicitly regenerating a route, so switching away and back need not destroy authored work. Keep reset/automatic-route actions reversible and preserve the exact generated palette as an editable output. The method labels alone do not prove perceptual smoothness or extraction quality; use the detailed algorithm checks elsewhere in this report.

The shelf adapter offers another useful supporting pattern: several selected sets become a deduplicated source while set bands retain their identities. Missing selected sets are removed and an empty selection falls back to the catalogue. Shared entries omit local shelf IDs so common drag/delete operations treat them as copyable inputs rather than owned items. That omission is a UI routing convention, not a complete permission or provenance model. In an RFF library, maintain stable asset identity separately from collection membership and retain known origin metadata when importing a shared palette. The adapter classifies shared entries by a source string and omits their origin in the returned item; do not copy that as a general provenance rule.

Date-based shelf bins are recomputed on relevant store changes, not by a midnight timer. Source identity is the joined set selection, while the source's entries can change independently. If RFF adds palette/environment collections, refresh content by asset/collection revision rather than only a selection label. A library reorganization should not silently alter the palette or image currently referenced by a shader preset.

**3D-to-2D transfer:** these mechanisms primarily support the image-derived palette proposal for flat 2D rendering. The same accepted-source and revision rules also support environment-image replacement in relief rendering. They add authoring reliability; they do not require 3D gamut visualization, a 3D scene renderer, or changes to RFF's numerical fractal pipeline.

## Editing context and interface brightness: make appearance experiments reversible

**Sources:** complete reads of `gradient-explorer/v2/uiHistory.ts` (172 lines), `FirstRunBrightness.tsx` (75), `firstRunDecision.ts` (58), and `main.tsx` (153). These establish registration and startup behavior; smoke-test claims in comments were not rerun.

GMT registers shell state, selected stops and filter-panel state as context providers on its existing undo system. Opening a panel is not itself a new content edit, but the panel/selection context accompanies a gradient-edit transaction. That is useful for RFF's proposed environment and material-mask editors: undoing an edit should restore both the parameter values and a meaningful selected stop, image layer or mask. Restoring a panel with a missing selected asset is not a complete recovery of editing context. Use stable IDs and resolve restored selections against the restored document.

The providers capture shallow shell/filter objects and the selection returned by a callback. They register under fixed global keys and unregister by key on unmount. This integration assumes one owner per key and immutable captured data; it does not establish safe simultaneous editors or deep snapshot isolation by itself. For RFF, scope providers to the editor/document, freeze mutable selection data, and restore context without generating another user gesture or undo entry. Keep GPU resources out of undo snapshots: restore the logical source and schedule its rendering, rejecting obsolete asynchronous results. History restoration must not replay exports or other external side effects merely because an export panel reopens.

The source describes its capture refs as the last committed render, but the hooks assign `live.current` during render. That code alone is not proof of a committed-state boundary under interrupted rendering. In a native RFF design, make transaction boundaries explicit and capture accepted model/UI state together. Test editing a stop then closing its inspector, replacing an environment image, undoing a masked-material adjustment, and switching the selected layer before undo/redo. The purpose is predictable experimentation with the new appearance controls, not turning every navigation action into undo history.

The initial-brightness dialog edits shared interface-theme controls. Its transparent backdrop allows the actual surrounding interface to remain visible while choosing brightness. It does not adjust the gradient source or shader exposure in these files. The pure startup decision leaves an existing brightness untouched, suppresses the dialog on a handoff from GMT, and asks only for an unseeded standalone visit without a stored brightness. Startup marks the visit before presenting the dialog; this is a visit marker, not confirmation that a choice was completed. A non-null stored string is sufficient for this decision; validation belongs to the theme store.

For RFF, preserve the separation between editor surround brightness, image exposure and scene-linear environment intensity. An optional neutral surround is useful for judging palettes and materials, but no mandatory new onboarding dialog is justified by this comparison. Reuse the current theme settings and preserve prior choices. These source files do not demonstrate colorimetric display calibration or HDR correctness.

`main.tsx` also establishes an explicit initialization order: feature registration precedes store use, undo/settings/menu integrations are installed before rendering, and session restore occurs before the first React render. Transfer that principle to new RFF editors so default initialization does not overwrite restored presets or create spurious undo entries. Global catalogue loading is invoked as a separate source; it is not a prerequisite for a locally saved palette to remain usable.

**2D relevance:** transaction context and theme/source separation apply equally to flat palettes, image mappings and relief materials. They improve the safety and clarity of shader authoring without altering fractal precision or changing the current visual-effect ranking.

## Portable palette state: preserve discontinuities, source semantics and provenance

**Sources:** full reads of `gradient-explorer/v2/shareUrl.ts` (231 lines) and `contributeToGlobal.ts` (115 lines). Inspection only: no link was published, no clipboard was written and no public submission was made.

GMT's share payload distinguishes stop gradients from sampled ramps. A versioned JSON record carries name, blend/color space and stop position/color/interpolation/bias; an empty stop list can instead carry a ramp string. Decoding regenerates stop IDs and passes the result through the shared configuration coercion function. This is a useful compact interchange pattern for an RFF palette editor, but not a complete RFF appearance preset: it omits material settings, texture mappings, environment orientation/intensity, extraction source, collection membership and origin metadata. A palette link should not be described as preserving an entire rendered look.

The most shader-relevant detail is stop-position serialization. Rather than always rounding to four decimals, the encoder checks how many of the fixed 256 ramp samples at `i/255` lie at or below each stop. It increases decimal precision if rounding would cross one of those sample locations. This protects step boundaries on that specific sampling grid: a boundary at exactly `85/255` must not be rounded below the sample and assign it to a different band. RFF can borrow the requirement to preserve discontinuity ownership, but should not copy the hard-coded 256-sample criterion without matching its own palette evaluation. It does not guarantee identical interpolation everywhere, at arbitrary resolutions or under another shader's boundary convention. Bias is still rounded to four decimals, and smooth interpolation can change even when sample-side counts remain equal.

For RFF, retain sufficient source precision and explicit interpolation/endpoint rules in saved authored palettes. Validate round trips at stop boundaries and neighboring values, including repeated stops and periodic seams. Keep existing recipe IDs/seeds and generator order unchanged. Sampled texture export may be a separate representation with a declared grid and reconstruction filter; an HDR environment additionally requires its own floating-point/color-domain contract.

The decoder rejects malformed outer structure and delegates deeper validation to the common coercion gate. This file does not impose a payload-length or stop-count limit before base64 decoding and JSON parsing. Its comment's typical short-link size is not an enforced maximum. If RFF adds compact import strings, bound decoding and allocation costs, handle unsupported versions explicitly, and leave the current document intact on failure. GMT's startup helper treats only a successfully decoded link as a reason to override session restore; that is a useful distinction between a usable import and merely the presence of a query parameter.

The public-contribution action is separate from local saving: it checks a catalogue signature, asks the person to publish, submits, and refreshes/flashes the shared set after an added result. The signature check is deduplication evidence, not a license grant. Its imported-source classification depends on a text prefix and at most the current or baked-from input; neither that convention nor editing a catalogue gradient proves provenance has been fully retained. For RFF, keep provenance as structured asset metadata through edits and copies. Do not infer permission to publish from changed stops, an absent duplicate signature or the absence of an import label.

The asynchronous contribution function retains a configuration reference across the signature lookup and submission rather than freezing an export object locally. For any future RFF sharing operation, freeze the exact source the user reviewed, tie completion to that revision, and keep publication distinct from undoable local edits. Shared-library functionality is optional workflow scope here; it is not necessary to realize the leading environment-reflection or texture-filtering proposals.

**2D transfer:** portable palette definitions and stable step boundaries apply directly to flat 2D coloring and material masks. They also support gradient environment authoring, provided the additional radiance/projection state is preserved separately. No new fractal iteration work is required.

## Swatch sampling controls: separate choosing colors from changing the gradient

**Source:** full read of `gradient-explorer/v2/PaletteRow.tsx` (271 lines), with targeted checks of `layoutPalette`, `addSwatch`, `removeSwatch` and `moveSwatch` in the previously reviewed `palette/store/workingStore.ts`. No clipboard or interactive test was performed.

GMT's swatches are positions sampled from a continuous ramp, not necessarily its authored stops. Dragging a swatch changes where it samples; clicking delegates stop selection/creation to the host; dropping a color delegates an actual gradient edit. RFF should preserve this distinction in any image-derived palette workflow: selecting representative colors must not silently rewrite the source gradient, while converting sampled colors into editable stops should be an explicit operation with a defined interpolation rule.

Even, Perceptual and Stops invoke layout actions rather than maintaining continuous constraints. Manual edits leave the selected rule label unchanged, and pressing it again reapplies the layout. The store also reduces the count to its hand-sized default when moving from Stops to another rule. For RFF, distinguish the last layout command from a currently enforced rule and preserve deliberate manual placement until the user requests redistribution. Perceptual spacing is an authoring option, not a guarantee that a rendered fractal receives equal visible color areas; the field histogram proposal addresses that separate distribution.

The row maps horizontal pixel travel to ramp position, enforces a 0.002 gap and hands a drag to an adjacent swatch instead of reordering slots. Each event hands over at most one neighbor and resets its pointer anchor, so a large event jump is not equivalent to moving through several neighbors in one event. If adopted, test sparse pointer events, close stops, endpoint clamping and a changed palette during dragging. The underlying store can sort positions and returns the moved index, while this row does not consume that return value; keep the UI's index/order assumptions explicit. Stable IDs are preferable when other controls can insert or remove samples concurrently.

Pointer cancellation uses the same completion handler as pointer-up, which can select/copy an unmoved sample; no lost-capture handler or active pointer-ID ownership is present in this component. RFF should separate cancel from click completion and group a drag as one reversible edit. Read-only mode blocks pointer dragging and add/remove controls, but color-drop handlers depend on the presence of a callback rather than the read-only flag, so callers must currently enforce that combination. Enforce read-only at the command boundary in a native port.

Displayed/copied hex colors clamp and round channels to 8-bit values. That is appropriate only for a declared display-color representation and cannot carry the proposed HDR environment radiance. Copy feedback is emitted without awaiting the clipboard promise here; a future RFF copy command should confirm actual completion. The useful part to transfer is the shared sampling model and explicit layout actions, not the incidental feedback behavior.

**2D relevance:** this is a practical companion to image-derived palettes and field-based color mapping in flat 2D. It can also help author gradient environment colors, with a separate intensity/HDR model. It does not itself improve shader sampling quality or replace the footprint-filtering proposal.

## Startup diagnostics and optional asset loading: capture evidence at the actual rendering boundary

**Sources:** full reads of `gradient-explorer/v2/bootTrace.ts` (199 lines) and `registerFeatures.ts` (80 lines). Historical device-failure and timing claims in comments were not reproduced.

GMT records a previous/current startup trail and can display it for copying on a device that cannot readily be inspected from the development machine. The transferable RFF idea is a small persistent diagnostic trail around concrete stages: palette/environment decode, GPU image creation, mip/prefilter completion, pipeline creation, resource binding and first accepted rendered frame. Include asset/settings revisions and actual errors so a failed environment import can be distinguished from a stalled shader compilation. Keep diagnostics independent of whether the rich editor successfully opens.

The inspected trace uses DOM polling: a canvas element marks `wall-canvas`, a hero element marks `hero`, and catalogue counts come from a DOM attribute. These are observations of UI construction, not GPU upload or rendering completion. It marks the run `ended` after 15 seconds alive and stops polling at 20 seconds; a later crash can therefore still leave an `ended normally` label. Conversely, a missing end mark alone cannot prove a process kill. For RFF, distinguish a startup-survival checkpoint, clean shutdown and incomplete observation, and connect renderer milestones to real completion signals rather than window/control existence.

`preMainMs` is the navigation-relative clock value at this module's evaluation. It is not an isolated measurement of network-plus-parse cost: earlier module evaluation and scheduling can contribute. Per-mark times use wall-clock differences, which are a separate clock domain. A useful RFF implementation should use a monotonic clock for durations and separately label startup origin, compile time, upload time and first-frame time. The current source writes synchronously through a safe-storage helper, but that call alone does not prove durable recovery after every crash or successful storage when writes fail. Do not describe an absent trace as proof that a stage never ran.

Feature registration installs the working gradient's document/history providers before ordinary store use, connects one recent entry to subsequent edits, and registers the actual processed ramp as the fullscreen preview source. The latter directly confirms why the preview must not reconstruct a processed gradient from an approximate stop fit. In RFF, a material/environment editor should subscribe to the accepted processed source while retaining its editable recipe separately. Source replacement, undo and save need a common ownership model rather than independent copies of the color pipeline.

The registry also chooses default palette packs based on a mobile-viewport heuristic and explicit query switches; optional packs remain separate. This is evidence for staged library loading, not a measured memory limit suitable for RFF. Native RFF should prefer on-demand asset decoding, bounded GPU residency and explicit memory accounting over inferring capacity from window size or pointer type. Thumbnail/library enumeration should not require uploading every full-resolution environment image. Preserve source/license metadata when deciding which packs to distribute or enable; a registry category is not itself a license verification.

**3D-to-2D relevance:** resource-stage diagnostics and lazy libraries support both flat image/palette shaders and relief environments. They improve robustness and help measure the proposals already ranked; they do not establish a new visual effect or justify reducing numerical precision.

## Library selection and save feedback: identify the asset and the destination explicitly

**Sources:** full reads of `gradient-explorer/v2/GroundList.tsx` (262 lines) and `setSaveFlash.ts` (137 lines). No interactive selection, rename or save was executed.

GMT offers named list rows alongside visual palette tiles, sharing entry identity, selection and action callbacks. The list provides a small ramp strip, a name and source/group caption. This is useful for an RFF palette or environment library: visual browsing helps choose a look, while named entries help retrieve a specific authored revision.
