Preserve one stable asset identity across views and keep collection placement separate from the asset referenced by a shader preset.

The list renders all supplied rows rather than virtualizing them. Each strip builds a 256-pixel temporary ramp canvas and scales it to a 56-by-22 display area at device pixel ratio. This is a thumbnail, not evidence of the full palette's precision or an environment's HDR energy. For large RFF collections, retain a bounded thumbnail cache and virtualize visible rows; do not upload full environment textures merely to enumerate a library. A change in display DPI also needs explicit invalidation, since this strip's effect depends only on the ramp object.

Mouse and keyboard selection paths differ here: plain mouse picking clears the multi-selection and updates its anchor, while Enter/Space only invokes `onPick`. Shift ranges use a flattened list of IDs, so repeated entries across group bands require a defined occurrence policy. The rename input stops its own keys from reaching the row, but the row's Delete/Backspace handler does not stop propagation after invoking the host. For RFF, route each command once and define whether it acts on the active asset or the multi-selection consistently across mouse, keyboard and context menus. Do not rely on a visual highlight alone to specify a destructive command's target.

Save feedback is a transient destination-chip animation containing a CSS approximation of the gradient. A serial number allows repeated saves to the same destination to animate again. That is useful feedback for local palette filing, but neither the CSS preview nor the animation is a durability check. The helper infers a destination by comparing set counts before and after a synchronous callback and taking the first increase, excluding recent-date bins. It can describe that narrow filing operation, but is not a general completion protocol for asynchronous saves, replacements with unchanged counts or writes affecting multiple collections.

For RFF, prefer a save result containing the asset ID, destination ID, revision and completion status. Drive feedback from that result after the operation succeeds, and keep persistent failure/status information available when needed. The module has one current flash; a later save replaces the previous flash and timer, so rapid batches cannot be treated as a complete operation log. Ordinary undoable library edits and external file writes should retain their distinct completion semantics.

**2D/relief relevance:** these are supporting improvements for reusable palettes, image layers and gradient/image environments. They make the proposed shader inputs easier to find and save accurately; they do not change the shader's numerical output or add a new lighting effect.

## Appearance editor panels: retain one source model while changing the editing tool

**Source:** full read of `gradient-explorer/v2/Tray.tsx` (365 lines). This file hosts the controls; the shell owns the face-switch/escape transactions, so the header's full commit/cancel claims are not established by this component alone.

GMT places mixing, image extraction, curves, adjustments, painting and stop inspection in one tool surface over a common working gradient. Shared face components avoid separate implementations between applications. RFF can use this pattern for palette, UV, material-mask and environment editors: the active tool changes, while the accepted source model and rendered preview remain consistent. The useful addition is coordinated editing of the proposed shader inputs, not copying the browser layout into the native application.

The inspector host stays mounted even when another face is shown, while most other face components mount conditionally. Consequently persistent source state must live outside those components, and transient state can reset on a tool change. In particular, the Mix face's Link toggle is local state and returns to false after remount. Decide explicitly which RFF controls are persistent document parameters, editor preferences and temporary gesture state; do not allow panel visibility to determine saved material values.

Mixing offers independent Lightness, Chroma and Hue blend amounts. When Link is enabled, editing any one slider assigns the same absolute value to all three; it does not preserve their previous offsets. Toggling Link alone does not synchronize them. This is a useful optional palette-authoring operation, but needs accurate naming and one atomic update in an RFF port. The handler calls three setters sequentially; the surrounding drag start/end brackets establish gesture boundaries but do not by themselves prove that intermediate downstream recomputation is suppressed. Batch related parameter changes before uploading shader resources and test undo as one gesture.

The Adjust Apply action obtains the current derived result and invokes the working store's bake only when there is a non-passthrough result and the source is not live Mix/Image. That separation prevents one generic commit from being applied to every source kind. RFF should retain a clear preview/apply/cancel contract and preserve the editable input when baking would be approximate. A fitted stop representation is not automatically identical to a processed ramp, and neither is an HDR environment representation. Keep legacy palette recipe regeneration stable.

The panel measures remaining viewport space, observes its parent and current children, and introduces internal scrolling when content exceeds the cap. The minimum cap is 160 pixels even if less room remains; this alone cannot guarantee every control is reachable in an extremely small viewport. Parent resizing is observed, but position-only movement and newly replaced children need consideration. For RFF, use actual client-space/DPI measurements and keep Apply/Cancel reachable after resizing or changing tools. Layout changes must not change image sampling coordinates or export dimensions.

The component reports its occupied box one animation frame after measurement so adjacent controls can avoid it. This is presentation coordination, not renderer synchronization. Keep editor geometry separate from full-output shader coordinates and treat control overlays as excluded from image export. Validate mode changes during a drag, close/cancel behavior, source replacement, small windows and final preview/export agreement at the integration layer.

**2D transfer:** independent color-channel mixing and shared editing context are directly useful to flat palettes; the same source/transaction model supports relief masks and gradient environments. These supporting controls do not alter the current ranking of visual shader improvements.

## Shared editor primitives: show state without confusing it with shader data

**Sources:** full reads of seven small modules in `gradient-explorer/v2/ui/` plus `useIsPhone.ts` and `version.ts`, nine files in total: `Act.tsx`, `Floating.tsx`, `Icon.tsx`, `bar.ts`, `MapScrollbar.tsx`, `StateChip.tsx`, `ZoneLabel.tsx`, `useIsPhone.ts`, and `version.ts` (358 lines total). The first three are compatibility re-exports, not independent widget implementations. No screenshot-based assessment is claimed.

`StateChip` separates live, edited, armed, picked and snapshot states, and can add an explicitly named action such as cancel or return to source. `gradientBarClass` gives armed state precedence over selected state. For RFF's proposed shader editors, use explicit wording for accepted source, live preview, pending resource preparation and edited-but-unapplied settings. A green UI label must not stand in for GPU completion; derive it from the relevant model/renderer state. Share this vocabulary across palette, image and environment controls without copying theme colors into rendered data.

`MapScrollbar` shares its value-to-pixel mapping with the adjacent color-map lens. It converts pointer height to a descending lightness axis, preserves the grab offset inside the thumb, and centers the thumb when the track is clicked. Its `reach` argument affects the track visualization only: seek values clamp to [0,1], not the reachable subrange. A RFF field-range or palette-distribution navigator should distinguish full domain, occupied domain and current view, and enforce any promised reach constraint at the model boundary. Histogram range selection is still a different operation from scrolling a palette catalogue.

The scrollbar ends interaction on pointer-up but provides no pointer-cancel/lost-capture cleanup or keyboard path in this component. Test cancellation and offer keyboard/numeric alternatives in a native implementation. Its wider invisible hit area preserves the visual track width while easing pointer use; that idea can transfer without tying the shader's sampling resolution to control dimensions.

`useIsPhone` simply returns the shared layout hook's device-mobile flag. The underlying heuristic includes viewport width and coarse pointer, so it must not be treated as actual hardware or memory-capacity detection for shader choices. `ZoneLabel` is presentation only. `version.ts` declares a separate application version/name, while the wrappers preserve old import locations after promotion to shared components. These files introduce no new shader algorithm; their practical lesson is to keep editor presentation, product version, asset schema version and renderer capabilities distinct.

**RFF scope:** reuse existing native controls where appropriate, keep palette recipe/config compatibility rules intact, and add only the state distinctions needed by new asynchronous appearance operations. This applies equally to 2D palettes and relief environments.

## Help and reproducible appearance reports: document what each artifact actually preserves

**Sources:** full reads of `gradient-explorer/v2/help/AboutGx.tsx` (133 lines), `ids.ts` (14), `installGxHelp.tsx` (137), and `topics.ts` (194). No help window was opened, feedback sent, screenshot captured or external license source verified in this batch.

GMT keeps small topic identifiers separate from lazily imported help text and supplies application-specific topics through the common help installer. This can inform RFF's shader documentation: connect environment source, roughness filtering, field mapping, emission routing and mask controls to short mechanism explanations, with the detailed mathematics available separately. Include the exact 2D interpretation: a relief normal can reflect an environment, but this does not turn a Mandelbrot view into a ray-traced 3D surface or make an emitting band illuminate neighbors physically.

The text distinguishes local keeping, share links, native editable gradient files, external sampled formats and wallpaper images. RFF should carry that distinction through labels and documentation. Claims such as an image file reopening exactly need a stated scope: editable configuration with metadata intact is different from sampled colors recovered after metadata removal. An exported palette alone cannot restore environment projection, material masks, source images or processing history. Validate the particular representation before promising full appearance round trips.

The feedback installer offers either a gradient configuration/link or a screenshot. The gradient capture calls the current derived configuration at capture time, while screenshot capture is requested when selected. This is useful for a future RFF diagnostic bundle, but the two choices answer different questions: a screenshot shows an observed appearance, while editable state helps reproduce it. The capture here does not include the exact processed ramp separately, despite the preview host using that ramp when it differs from a stop fit. RFF appearance reports should optionally include the accepted render revision, actual palette/environment source, settings and relevant resource metadata, with a preview of what is being attached. Nothing in this review authorizes automatic external reporting.

About reads catalogue attribution from loaded bundle manifests and separately names built-in palette sources. That is a useful way to avoid maintaining unrelated lists of loaded assets and displayed credits. However, the UI manifest and its license labels are not independent verification of original-source licensing. RFF should retain its canonical NOTICE records and verified provenance beside recognizable implementations, including assets no longer visible in the current library filter but still distributed or used by a saved scene. Do not infer that hiding or editing an asset removes its provenance requirements.

The help map can omit keyboard shortcuts based on the mobile heuristic when loaded, while the menu predicate queries that heuristic dynamically. Device category is not proof that no keyboard exists, and a one-time topic map can disagree with later layout changes. For RFF, expose supported shortcuts according to actual command availability rather than window size alone. The help installer is guarded as a one-time global setup, so switching hosts or locales would need an explicit lifecycle rather than assuming a second call reconfigures it.

**Transfer value:** accurate contextual explanations and reproducible source bundles support every ranked shader proposal in both 2D and relief rendering. These files add no shader algorithm; their value is making capabilities, approximations and saved-data limits clear enough to use and verify.

## Shared command entry points: keep appearance actions consistent across editor surfaces

**Source:** full read of `gradient-explorer/v2/ShellMenu.tsx` (169 lines). The shell consumes registered menu definitions and the common item renderer instead of copying Help actions into a separate list. A host can prepend its own commands while retaining the shared definitions and badge predicate. For RFF's palette/material/environment editors, use one command implementation and applicability check across toolbar, menu and keyboard entry points; changing the host surface should not change what Apply, Export or Reset means.

The menu anchor is captured from the button at opening, while available height is calculated from that stored position. The component does not itself remeasure the button continuously, and a minimum height can exceed the room in a very small viewport. Delegate repositioning to a well-defined layout owner and verify controls remain reachable after resize or content expansion. This source inspection does not establish actual popup behavior or a native Win32 menu fix; RFF's known show-before-first-paint menu flash remains a separate issue.

The feedback window uses the existing feedback open state and renders the shared form in a separate layer, marked for exclusion from feedback screenshots. That is a presentation contract, not proof that capture or submission succeeds. For a future RFF appearance report, keep the form state outside a transient menu so closing the menu does not discard a draft, and confirm the actual capture/submission result. No external action was taken during this review.

These are integration patterns supporting shader authoring in both flat 2D and relief. This module contributes no additional shader mechanism and does not change the visual-effect ranking above.

## Asset collection operations: separate destination feedback from completed storage

**Source:** full read of `gradient-explorer/v2/SetRail.tsx` (588 lines). This is supporting infrastructure for the proposed RFF palette, image and environment libraries, not an additional shader effect. The rail keeps collection positions stable, supports multiple selected sets, and delegates the export contents to its host. Its count and callback alone do not prove whether the exported union follows every visible filter; that contract must be checked at the host.

The useful transfer is destination-oriented editing: create an empty group before collecting assets, show which group receives a drop, and distinguish deleting a group from deleting its assets. The group deletion handler calls `removeGroup` in one undo bracket and announces relocation to Kept. RFF should preserve stable asset identifiers and revisions when library membership changes, so an environment or emission-source reference does not break merely because its collection is renamed or removed. Undo of membership is separate from retaining the underlying image data and GPU resource until active scenes no longer need it.

**Qualification to the earlier save-feedback section:** local drops call `flashSetSave` before `fileFavientInto`, deliberately showing feedback before the store mutation. The animation therefore indicates a destination and attempted action, not acknowledged storage or durable persistence. The public contribution branch delegates to a separate helper. An RFF implementation should report the actual operation outcome, including partial imports, separately from immediate hover/drop feedback. The scroll-to-destination effect uses the flash serial, but the animation element itself has no serial key; this file alone does not guarantee that repeated saves restart its CSS animation.

The drag-over handler declares `dropEffect='move'` for every accepted destination, although a catalogue item, an existing favourite and a public contribution have different semantics. For RFF, make copy, membership move and publication explicit in the operation model and its feedback. A local collection move should not imply removal of an externally linked source file. Freeze the selected asset IDs and revisions when an export begins so later selection changes cannot silently alter its contents.

Removal uses the payload's list of IDs and reports its length. That is not necessarily the number of distinct existing records actually removed. Group deletion similarly announces a count captured before the mutation. Return affected IDs/counts from the mutation when feedback promises an exact result. Renaming commits on Enter without an explicit composition guard in this component; Japanese IME confirmation should be distinguished from submitting the new name in an RFF editor.

Read executable branches rather than inheriting platform assumptions from comments: despite comments saying otherwise, the phone branch includes the conditional trash element. The save scroll also requests smooth movement directly. These are source observations, not reproduced UI failures. RFF should verify actual input capabilities and its own motion preferences instead of using a narrow layout as proof that dragging or a keyboard cannot be available.

**Transfer value:** reliable library operations make environment-reflection and image/emission-source experiments reusable in both flat 2D and relief workflows. This inspection adds no runtime measurement and does not alter the provisional shader ranking.

## Export window: preview the actual representation and its losses

**Source:** full read of `gradient-explorer/v2/ExportMenu.tsx` (1,316 lines). GMT separates continuous ramps from selected swatches, and a single gradient from a collection. Available formats come from registered builders, while text previews call the same export functions used by the actions. This is a useful RFF pattern: distinguish editable palette/environment definitions, sampled interchange data and rendered pictures, then expose only options that affect the selected output. A PNG extension alone does not establish which representation it contains or whether editable metadata survives another application.

Single-gradient swatches use the composed palette; collection swatches use a count and a rule read from the working store unless explicitly provided. Under the Stops rule, the requested count is a fallback rather than a universal member size. RFF should include the actual sampling rule and effective member counts in an export summary. Repeating a recent action here uses its recorded subject with the current ramp, palette and options; it is repetition of an operation, not recovery of the original output. This distinction matters when a palette also drives emission or environment reflection.

**Loss information must follow every action.** Normal rows compute stop-reduction notices, but collection ZIP rows do not request that notice unless the format bundles or exports a lone member. Recent-action previews omit the reduction note altogether. These are limits of the window's warning coverage, not proof that its output builders corrupt data. For RFF, obtain an export assessment from the same builder for ordinary, recent, single and batch actions. Report approximation separately from clipping, quantization, unsupported interpolation or omitted metadata; a stop-budget check alone cannot represent every loss. An environment's narrow bright band may be visually important even if a generic average color-error criterion considers it small.

**Limit work, not just visible text.** `previewSlice` limits presentation to 400 lines or 40,000 characters only after the complete text has been generated and split. Collection previews cache full strings by format, with cache invalidation depending on collection identity, subject, count, budget and rule. This can avoid repeated work, but it does not bound initial generation cost or retained memory. For large RFF libraries, generate a bounded preview independently of the complete export, or run cancellable preparation with explicit memory limits and immutable input revisions. Do not imply that a truncated on-screen preview means the saved file is truncated.

The preview request also stores its explanatory note separately from the generated text. Changing the budget can refresh the text while an existing request retains its earlier note. Changing section or subject clears preview state without clearing the pending open/hold timers in that effect. A delayed request can therefore outlive the selection that created it unless another handler cancels it. RFF should invalidate text, assessment and pending work together using the same export revision. Shared builders are necessary for agreement, but do not by themselves make separately timed preview and download calls an atomic snapshot.

The window positively distinguishes copy success from a click: its check mark waits for the returned success boolean. Size fields keep a draft, normalize on commit and flush a focused field before closing. Transfer these ideas while verifying that the actual export consumes the committed values; source comments about blur ordering are not a runtime test. Empty single-gradient swatches display guidance but format actions remain present in this component, so host/builder handling still determines the result. Disable or explain unavailable outputs consistently at the command boundary.

**Verification proposed for RFF:** compare preview and saved bytes for one frozen revision; repeat through recent actions; export a collection with mixed reductions; change budget during an open preview; switch subject during a pending preview; exercise empty palettes and IME input; and measure preparation time and peak memory on large libraries. Apply the same representation contract to flat 2D palettes and relief environment/emission sources. This source review does not claim these tests have run or change the shader-effect ranking.

## Working gradient integration: preserve the evaluated result while editing its source

**Source:** full read of `gradient-explorer/v2/WorkingHero.tsx` (1,164 lines). The strongest shader-authoring transfer is the distinction between the editable representation and the evaluated signal. When processing changes a gradient, the editor receives `previewRamp=derived.ramp`; it does not reconstruct that preview from a stop fit that may be held during interaction. An unchanged authored gradient instead uses its original representation. For RFF, use the actual evaluated palette/environment signal for appearance previews, while retaining the editable source separately. A fitted stop approximation can erase narrow reflection bands or show outdated positions with newly evaluated colors. This is a display-pipeline concern and must not reduce fractal-computation precision.

The component explicitly distinguishes sampled-ramp mode from editable stops. In ramp mode it avoids ordinary knot editing and offers conversion through Add Stops. If Paint is open, that action first leaves the face and then calls `deriveWorkingNow` so conversion sees the applied painting. RFF should make any conversion from sampled image/ramp to editable stops explicit and reversible, preserve the original source, and state its approximation policy. Do not silently fit an HDR environment to an 8-bit palette just to reuse a stop editor. The hexadecimal swatch path here clamps to 0–255 and is appropriate only for its specified display-color representation, not general radiance storage.

**Commit before saving, then read the result.** The Keep handler groups UI reveal, source commitment and filing. For Mix/Image it reads the committed working input after closing the source face; for Paint it derives the result again. That ordering is valuable for RFF: saving an environment or emission source must capture the post-commit revision actually being accepted, rather than a render closure from before the commit. The same accepted revision should own its name, source metadata and undo context. The component preserves source/inspector context through history providers; a restored inspector is useful only when its selected IDs still exist on the restored document.

When a source becomes empty, `lastGood` retains only the previous configuration and ramp so the display can remain recognizable, while editing and color drops are withheld. However, header actions remain rendered and the recent-export component combines `shown.ramp` with current derived name, palette, origin, configuration and source. This is an integration boundary needing an explicit contract, not proof of a particular exported-file failure. For RFF, either expose a complete, labeled last-valid snapshot or disable operations requiring a valid current source. Never present old pixels under unrelated current metadata as a newly accepted material state.

Asset identity and provenance also need consistent routing. The header drag obtains an imported-source string and includes it in its payload; marquee escape creates a whole-gradient drag with configuration and name only. The Keep route separately checks an unmodified catalogue origin, and its selected state is found by a content signature rather than a stable selected library ID. These paths demonstrate why RFF should centralize asset payload creation: content equivalence, library identity, derivation history and required attribution are different properties. Equivalent colors should not imply equivalent licensing or cause a save toggle to remove an unintended duplicate entry.

The drop coordinate is measured against the actual inset knot track, which is useful for matching a ghost marker to the eventual edit. In contrast, the temporary reveal guard intercepts presses anywhere in the gradient body for 450 ms after showing it; the event is consumed before the primary-button check. Such timing heuristics should not be transplanted as universal input rules. A future RFF editor should verify double-click continuity, deliberate rapid edits, pointer cancellation and IME name entry. The current rename handler commits on Enter without an explicit composition guard in this file.

**Transfer value:** evaluated-signal previews, reversible conversion and coherent commit/save snapshots directly support environment reflection, field masks and emission-source editing in both flat 2D and relief workflows. Proposed checks include a narrow bright band through preview/commit/reload, saving while each processing face is open, losing a source while export is available, undo with an inspected stop, and provenance parity across both drag routes. No application code or runtime behavior was changed or measured by this inspection.

## Editor shell: make source transitions and export scope explicit

**Source:** full read of `gradient-explorer/v2/GradientExplorerV2App.tsx` (1,137 lines). The shell coordinates the previously inspected editor, library and export modules. Its transferable mechanism is a defined transition between a live source, its processed result and a fixed editable document. Leaving Mix/Image derives and commits the result; changing processing faces groups related data writes into one undo operation. An untouched curve fit can be discarded without baking it. RFF can use this distinction for palette, mask and environment editors: inspecting a representation should not silently resample the source, while applying an actual transformation must capture its output and reset only the processing already incorporated.

Mix initialization neutralizes legacy slot modifiers that have no visible controls in this shell, starts at source A and arms a destination slot. That prevents hidden settings from tinting an apparently neutral operation. RFF should similarly define which saved controls remain effective when an editor hides or replaces them, and preserve legacy render behavior through explicit versioned semantics rather than silently changing old scenes. GMT's `addMixSeeds` merges stop seeds on a fixed 256-sample grid (`round(position*255)`), preferring a step edge when seeds collide. This is an approximation tied to that representation, not a precision-preserving strategy for arbitrary narrow HDR environment features. Retain source positions or use a declared adaptive fitting tolerance for RFF.

**Resolved export-scope boundary:** `groundMembers` is computed directly from selected set IDs, favourites and global entries with `membersOfMany`, and passed to `ExportMenu`. This host does not receive the browse panel's narrowed item list. Therefore its export contract is the selected-set union, not a host-proven snapshot of search-visible tiles. This resolves the earlier SetRail uncertainty at the call site. RFF should name full-group export separately from filtered-visible export and freeze membership plus asset revisions when starting preparation; this component continues to derive its export props from live stores while the window is open.

**Async reads and synchronous edits are separate here.** Explicit group import reads files first and then calls the import mutation inside one synchronous undo bracket. This avoids leaving an edit transaction open across unrelated user gestures. However, the generic drop route calls `ownedGroundGroup()` after awaiting the reads, so its destination follows selection at completion rather than necessarily at drop time. It also maps onward images by filename, which is not a unique identity for a multi-file input. For RFF, capture the intended destination and ordered file identities when the action begins, then validate them at completion; define what happens if a group disappears or another import finishes first. A successful read is not authorization to apply to whichever material slot happens to be selected later.

Paint has an explicit commit helper before Share, full Export and Wallpaper, and ordinary candidate selection commits Paint before replacing the gradient. The `startNewGradient` handler does not call that helper or `commitPaint` in this file. The recent-export flyout inspected in WorkingHero also calls `runExport` directly. These are boundaries to verify against the underlying stores rather than a demonstrated data-loss claim. RFF should route every action that consumes the current appearance through one accepted-state operation, or explicitly document that an action exports the uncommitted preview. Normal buttons, recent actions, new-document commands and drag routes must not disagree about the included processing.

**Qualification to the preceding last-valid snapshot concern:** full Share, Export opening and Wallpaper explicitly reject a missing `derived.config`; the full export window additionally requires `derived.ramp`. Those host guards prevent treating all header actions as unguarded. The recent-export flyout and Keep route still have their separately described contracts. A coherent fallback snapshot remains useful, but the evidence supports route-specific analysis rather than a blanket failure claim.

Escape distinguishes cancellation from normal face closure and honors nearer handlers through `defaultPrevented`. Debounced Recent synchronization is delegated to a helper that waits for gesture brackets; elapsed time alone does not define edit completion. For RFF, specify Apply, Cancel, navigation and autosave as distinct operations, restore matching editor context with undo, and keep durable saving separate from recent-history bookkeeping. Hidden or dimmed browser content also remains mounted here; styling alone does not establish that its renderer or effects stop running.

**Transfer value and checks:** these integration rules support every proposed shader-authoring workflow in flat 2D and relief. Verify apply/cancel/undo transitions, export scope under search, overlapping imports, duplicate filenames, source removal during load, all export entry points during Paint, and narrow-band fidelity through repeated Mix/apply cycles. Historical smoke-test claims in source comments were not rerun. No shader or application implementation changed during this review.

## Browsing appearance assets: keep filtering, selection and rendering costs separate

**Source:** full read of `gradient-explorer/v2/BrowseStage.tsx` (1,460 lines). The host reuses one picker model for catalogue and user collections, with separate canvas and named-list presentations. `pickOnDrag: false` keeps reorganizing a library item from replacing the working gradient. That is directly useful for RFF environment images and palettes: moving an asset between collections should not silently apply it to the active material. Empty-state messages also distinguish an empty collection from existing assets hidden by filters; that distinction prevents unnecessary reimports or apparent loss of saved materials.

The Group These action copies the currently narrowed model rows into a new collection, retaining catalogue origin, and clears the search before showing it. Despite the header's phrase “saved search,” the handler creates a materialized set of members; it does not save a query that automatically acquires future matches. RFF should distinguish a fixed collection from a dynamic search. The 400-item cap here is an interaction choice, not a measured universal capacity limit for RFF.

**Navigation graphics are not field statistics.** The pad's visible marker is derived from scroll fraction mapped into a reachable span; later code explicitly supersedes the header's band/lightness interpretation. Grouping can repeat color ranges, so the marker cannot be read as the actual distribution of colors currently visible. For RFF's proposed field histogram, keep a true distribution/range indicator separate from a library scrollbar. Reusing the same appearance for these two meanings could make a palette-range control promise information it does not contain.

**Command scope should be computed once.** Removal intersects requested IDs with current locally owned assets before mutating the collection, avoiding deletion attempts against catalogue/public items. However, the context-menu label chooses a batch count only when the clicked item belongs to the selection, whereas `removeFavourites` gives any nonempty selection precedence over its fallback item. Unless the canvas normalizes selection before invoking this callback, those two rules can disagree. This is a call-boundary condition, not a reproduced deletion bug. RFF should pass one immutable target-ID list to the label, command and outcome report. Its window-level Delete/Backspace handler should also respect active-editor/modal ownership and already-consumed keys; checking only text inputs does not establish complete focus scope.

**Avoid accidental computation through subscriptions.** The public-contribution button reads the derived configuration only on click, but this component still calls `useWorkingDerived().empty` for its empty-state hint. Therefore the imperative button read alone does not establish that the whole browser avoids updates during slider edits. For RFF, subscribe to the minimal validity/identity state required by the browser, keep thumbnail generation keyed by asset revision, and measure both grid and list behavior. The list branch builds rows for all supplied groups, while this host supplies no visible-range or suspension argument to either child. Actual virtualization and GPU-idle behavior must be established in the renderer, not inferred from the shell being hidden or drawn on a canvas.

Opening Filters can call the shell's fold operation, which closes and commits an active processing face. This is a cross-component consequence of making space for browsing, not merely hiding a panel. RFF should define whether changing library visibility is allowed to apply an unfinished material edit; navigation should preserve the preview transaction unless the operation explicitly accepts it. Similarly, the public contribution route derives the current configuration without calling the shell's Paint-settlement helper, so it belongs in the previously identified command-consistency checks.

The rename implementation commits on blur despite its nearby comment saying blur cancels. Source comments are not sufficient behavioral evidence. Proposed RFF checks include drag without application, fixed versus dynamic collections, deletion on an unselected tile while another selection exists, consumed shortcuts under dialogs, filter opening during an edit, and library frame/memory costs during continuous shader controls. These findings support both 2D and relief asset authoring; no runtime or performance result is claimed.

## Shared commands and temporary render suspension

**Sources:** full reads of `engine/plugins/Menu.tsx` (681 lines) and `hooks/useRenderPause.ts` (110 lines). GMT registers menu definitions and items by stable ID, shares item rendering across hosts, and evaluates visibility, disabled state, labels and toggle state through callbacks. RFF can apply this organization to shader commands so a toolbar, context menu and keyboard binding share one applicability check and action. However, GMT's `shortcut` field here only displays text; it does not register or enforce a shortcut. A shared menu renderer is not by itself proof that every command entry point behaves identically.

The registry responds to every engine-store change by scheduling `_notify` in a microtask. This defers notification, but no pending flag coalesces multiple queued notifications in this implementation. RFF should subscribe command status to the state it actually depends on, or coalesce dirty notifications, rather than refresh all menu predicates on every progressive-render update. Re-registering an item without an explicit order assigns a new insertion counter, so stable IDs alone do not preserve its prior visual position. Define stable ordering separately if dynamic shader capabilities register and unregister commands.

**A useful suspension mechanism, with a narrower guarantee than its comments suggest:** the first UI pause captures `isPaused`, nested requests increment a shared count, and the last release restores the captured state if the current boolean remains paused. This avoids independent nested dialogs restoring one another's temporary pause states. The native-select adapter adds a per-control guard and releases on change, blur, Escape or unmount, which demonstrates the importance of pairing every acquisition with cleanup.

The counter does not independently own the underlying render state. A manual unpause can leave rendering active while requests remain; a later manual pause cannot be distinguished from the UI pause and may be overwritten by the last release. For RFF, model user pause intent and temporary UI suppression separately, preferably with scoped ownership tokens and a derived effective state. Decide explicitly whether shader parameter edits may request a preview while a menu remains open. Broadly stopping all rendering can defeat the purpose of a live roughness, reflection or emission control; suspending unnecessary continuous work is different from suppressing an explicitly requested preview or a video export.

The menu anchor invokes `useRenderPause` for its own open state, including the mobile route. The standalone `MobileMenuHost` and `MenuItemList` do not acquire a pause themselves. Thus a custom host consuming the shared rows does not automatically inherit that lifecycle. Likewise the desktop dismissal hook explicitly disables Escape here; another shortcut layer may own it, but this file alone does not prove Escape behavior. In RFF, place rendering and dismissal ownership at a documented host boundary instead of assuming shared visual components provide both.

Menu button callbacks return `void` and close immediately after invocation. They do not establish that an asynchronous shader compilation, texture load or export succeeded. RFF commands should expose pending, accepted and failed states where work continues after the menu closes, reject stale results by resource revision, and preserve a valid current pipeline until its replacement is ready. Visual disabled state also should not replace validation at execution time.

**Verification proposed:** nested surfaces closed in either order, host unmount, manual pause changes while nested, a native select dismissed without changing its value, live shader edits while a menu is open, and command-state updates during progressive rendering. Measure actual scheduling/GPU work before claiming a performance benefit. These browser mechanisms do not diagnose or fix RFF's separately documented native Win32 show-before-first-paint menu flash. Their transfer applies to both flat 2D and relief editing, with no change to orbit computation or MPA.

## Startup and recovery: distinguish progress animation from accepted rendering

**Sources:** full reads of `app-gmt/LoadingScreen.tsx` (423 lines), `app-gmt/LoadingRendererCPU.ts` (132 lines) and `app-gmt/RenderContextLostOverlay.tsx` (60 lines). These components provide presentation and event handling, not independent proof that a worker has compiled the current shader or presented a valid frame. The loading screen separates a cosmetic percentage from `isReady`; once ready it allows a one-second grace period for an unfinished cosmetic bar, while a nonrecoverable boot error blocks the fade. This is a useful RFF principle: a progress animation must neither certify successful pipeline creation nor keep a verified working renderer inaccessible.

For RFF, tie readiness and failures to a pipeline/resource generation and a confirmed valid rendering result. Distinguish a watchdog timeout from a terminal compile/device error so a late success can clear only the matching transient timeout. GMT stores the first readiness timestamp once and does not reset it in its formula/file restart handlers; its fade completion timer is not retained for cancellation by the effect cleanup. These are lifecycle boundaries to avoid copying. A delayed completion from an old compilation must not close the status panel for a newer failed request.

The CPU loading animation directly evaluates a small Julia set into a reusable ImageData buffer. Its iteration cap grows with the displayed progress, up to 90 iterations per pixel. This avoids creating another WebGL renderer, but the header's universal 60-fps/no-contention claim is not established by inspection: it consumes main-thread CPU work each animation frame and still presents a canvas. The canvas is sized from CSS pixels, with no device-pixel-ratio scaling here. The clipping wrapper reveals the canvas progressively, while the implementation still redraws its full area every frame; the comment that the canvas paints once must not be treated as a measured optimization.

An RFF progress indicator should have a small bounded cost, pause when obscured, and use a static or throttled fallback during expensive compilation or failure. A decorative Julia spinner is optional and has no bearing on fractal calculation fidelity. Lowering indicator resolution is distinct from lowering the precision of the reference orbit or perturbation equations. GMT's Lite control selects broader scalability presets based on a precision-mode flag; RFF must not adopt any precision tradeoff from that control. Recovery can reduce optional display effects or preview workload while preserving the user's saved configuration and required mathematical precision.

The context-loss overlay listens for an event, displays its reason and offers reload with a lighter-mode promise. It does not itself set the recovery flag, save the scene, rebuild resources or prove that reload restores the intended state. Its display also depends on a nonempty reason string. RFF should use an explicit failure state independent of message contents, retain CPU-side settings/assets, and distinguish device loss from swapchain recreation and ordinary shader compilation failure. A recovery message should describe only the fallback actually prepared and confirmed by its owner.

Diagnostics are collected after a boot error, and report submission is a separate user-invoked action with sending/success/failure states and `includeScene: false`. This review sent nothing. For RFF, offer local diagnostic details and an explicit export containing device/driver, pipeline generation and error stage; inspect the actual payload before promising that a report excludes scene-sensitive information. These components alone do not establish what the submission helper includes.

**Proposed verification:** stale compile completion after a new request, timeout followed by matching readiness, terminal error followed by a generic boot signal, failure during the fade, missing reason text, retained settings after recovery, and indicator CPU cost while compilation proceeds. These mechanisms apply to both flat 2D and relief rendering. No startup, GPU recovery or performance test was executed in this inspection.

## Saved appearance compatibility and explicit application targets

**Sources:** full reads of `app-gmt/migrations.ts` (257 lines), `app-gmt/registerFeatures.ts` (109 lines) and `app-gmt/SettingsHost.tsx` (18 lines). These files connect shader-related parameters to saved scenes and reusable gradient tools. The transferable lesson is that a parameter's meaning, omitted default, animation routing and destination are part of its persistence contract. Changing a visible label or moving a control does not justify changing old rendered results.

GMT's migrations distinguish a coloring escape threshold from a geometry bailout, move a compiler-settings slice, delegate legacy weave conversion, rename a marcher parameter, adapt background/environment semantics, invert fog tint and convert modulation bands into Hz. They are evidence of compatibility mechanisms, not proof that every old appearance is preserved. In particular, the environment migration explicitly leaves a previously colored backdrop black for a combination whose lighting it chooses to preserve. RFF should avoid introducing that coupling when adding environment reflection: background display, diffuse illumination and reflected environment can share a source while retaining independently specified amounts and legacy defaults. A new environment option should leave existing scenes unchanged when disabled.

Animation needs more than a static parameter rename. The marcher migration retargets both modulation targets and sequence-track keys; assigning the renamed track can overwrite an already present destination key. RFF should define conflict precedence, preserve interpolation and all keyframe values, and assess semantic transforms separately from key renaming. An inversion such as `new = 1 - old` would require the same transformation for animated values if that path existed. GMT deliberately skips the historical fog animation route; that decision is not evidence that animation can generally be ignored in RFF migrations.

Several compatibility assumptions deserve explicit fixtures. If both legacy quality.escape and coloring.escape exist, version 1 keeps the coloring value but can seed MandelTerrain's geometry bailout from the quality value. The fog migration substitutes an omitted old default and writes the new tint whenever fog is active, so replay safety depends on migration-version routing rather than the body alone. The Hz conversion uses a fixed 24,000-Hz legacy Nyquist assumption because the authoring sample rate was not saved; if either new endpoint already exists it skips the whole rule. This favors deterministic decoding over reconstruction of unavailable history. For RFF, record units and source domains when introducing new fields, specify mixed-old/new-field handling, and validate finite values instead of relying on numeric type alone.

**RFF's own file contracts remain authoritative.** GMT's structured scene migrations are not a replacement for RFF's append-only ConfigIO stream, stable recipe IDs/seeds or versioned compressed-map modes. Add new shader controls with neutral trailing defaults and guarded reads; never renumber old enum meanings or mutate palette recipe generation to make a migrated scene look similar. If a change cannot preserve the old shader semantics through defaults, retain an explicit compatibility path and document the difference before changing the format.

Feature registration also exposes explicit application targets for Coloring Layer 1, Coloring Layer 2 and Environment Sky. Each target carries a stable ID, the affected parameter and a reveal action. This supports the proposed RFF environment editor: one reusable gradient library can feed different shader inputs without guessing the destination from the currently visible panel. Keep each target's accepted color domain, supported representation, validity and undo transaction explicit. Here application tracking is called before the actual apply helper, and a destination accordion is requested one animation frame after switching tabs; neither is proof that application or mounting succeeded. RFF should acknowledge the accepted resource revision and reveal the editor when its host is ready.

The registration module initializes features and compiler profiles before first store access; settings registration is separate from showing its modal. Preserve this ordering if RFF introduces dynamically described shader controls, so saved settings are decoded against the intended schema rather than whichever modules happened to initialize first. Proposed checks cover omitted defaults, both old/new keys, repeated loads, conflicting animation tracks, disabled-feature identity, and applying one gradient to each supported destination. This review did not execute migrations or rendering comparisons; all compatibility conclusions are source-level requirements for both 2D and relief workflows.

## Export quality controls: measure complete work and name auxiliary channels accurately

**Sources:** full reads of `app-gmt/renderDialogExtras.tsx` (301 lines) and `app-gmt/HelpExtras.tsx` (138 lines). The export extension exposes beauty, alpha and depth passes, a depth remapping range and an internal supersampling scale. The useful transfer is explicit output-channel selection with documented meaning. For RFF, iteration values, validity masks, relief height and normals are plausible auxiliary products only where their producer contracts are verified; a 2D relief-height image must not be advertised as camera-space 3D depth. State units, valid/background pixels, normalization, precision and whether the channel is raw data or a display visualization. Copying a fog range into depth controls is a convenience, not proof that it preserves all depth information.

Internal scale multiplies both dimensions, so 2x creates four times as many internal pixels before any extra buffers or passes. It can improve spatial sampling but does not substitute for field-aware texture filtering, nor does its label guarantee sharper final output for every downsampling kernel. RFF already has downsampling infrastructure; the incremental work is coherent export-quality selection and validation, not merely adding a second supersampling switch. Keep accumulation samples, spatial supersampling and fractal numerical precision as separate concepts.

**The displayed duration is a heuristic.** GMT polls accumulation count every 30 ms, starts timing when the effect mounts, detects a reset only when the sampled count decreases, and records the first observed crossing of the requested cap. If sufficient samples predate the measurement, the elapsed interval is not the cost of generating that frame. A reset and recovery between polls can also be missed. Its total estimate multiplies this duration by the target/viewport pixel ratio and frame count. It does not incorporate selected pass count, encoding, readback, disk I/O, compilation or changing scene complexity, and polling continues after the cap even though the comment says tracking stops.

For RFF, collect timings from an identified accepted render generation using a monotonic clock and distinguish computation, shader processing and output costs. Use representative frames for animated scenes, report an estimate range and update it from completed export work. Do not apply GMT's viewport-pixel scaling as a measured speed prediction for deep-zoom reference/MPA work: some costs are shared, resolution-independent or dependent on the view. No benchmark was run here.

The dialog temporarily changes the worker's preview sample cap and restores the current viewport cap on cleanup. It also sets a shared adaptive-suppression boolean true on mount and false on unmount, without recording another owner's request in this component. RFF should use scoped overrides so closing one panel does not cancel an export's or another panel's suppression. Explicit final-output settings must remain stable even while an interactive preview is allowed to adapt.

Image-sequence capability is accepted by this wrapper without probing worker encoding; a separate directory-picker gate controls starting. Browser-name warnings and fixed codec limits are source claims, not verified current platform facts. For RFF, validate the actual encoder, selected channels, dimensions and output destination at job preparation, including finite ordered channel ranges. Do not infer full capability from one file-picker or codec check, and keep old saved format indices stable.

About displays a renderer string immediately or after one delayed retry, while catalogue credit links follow loaded packs. This supports inspectable diagnostics and asset provenance, but does not prove the renderer string stays current after recovery or independently verify a license. RFF should report device/driver and active pipeline information from the current generation and retain canonical NOTICE records independently of which packs are loaded. These workflow improvements apply to flat 2D and relief export; actual channel implementations and runtime agreement remain separate verification requirements.

## Root integration: separate render ownership, analysis demand and presentation

**Sources:** full reads of `app-gmt/AppGmt.tsx` (498 lines) and `App.tsx` (166 lines). GMT's app-specific root narrows store subscriptions and gives each registered DOM overlay its own feature-slice subscription, whereas the generic root subscribes to the full store. This is a concrete architectural difference, not a measured comparison in this audit. RFF can keep camera/frame progress and unrelated UI state from invalidating every shader-control panel by routing updates to the consumers that need them. Stable callbacks and minimal state subscriptions help, but do not prove that child components perform no extra work.

The app-specific viewport has a worker-rendered canvas and a separate transparent R3F canvas for navigation and render ticks. For RFF, borrow explicit ownership of input, scheduling and image presentation rather than adding another graphics context merely to reproduce this arrangement. Keep one authoritative camera/view transformation and propagate it through a common action; GMT specifically delegates scene-offset changes to its shared store action so other consumers see the same virtual-space offset. For 2D RFF, the analogous requirement is agreement among viewport mapping, high-precision coordinates, screen-based decoration and tiled exports, without early conversion of the fractal center to low precision.

**Analysis runs on consumer demand.** Geometry and color histogram probes mount only while their corresponding active-consumer counts are positive. This supports the proposed RFF field histogram: start readback/reduction only when requested, separate field statistics from final-color statistics, and release analysis demand when its consumer closes. Counted mounting is not a complete request protocol; generation tagging, one-outstanding-request limits and stale-result rejection still belong in the analysis implementation. An inspector being hidden rather than unmounted must have an explicit demand policy.

**Clean presentation requires an explicit inventory.** Broadcast mode gates many docks, HUDs and editing overlays, but region/preview overlays, mobile-menu host and several root-level dialogs are not guarded by that flag here. The generic root differs again, leaving floating panels and its topbar mounted without the same root-level gates. Do not infer a guaranteed overlay-free capture from a mode name or comment. RFF should define which surfaces are excluded from an image/video output and obtain exported pixels from the render target where practical, with deliberate treatment of diagnostics and error notices. Screen recording is a separate contract from offscreen export.

Readiness in this root is a one-way local boolean set by the tick driver's callback. The callback named `isBootedOrRequested` actually returns only the proxy's `isBooted` property at this call site. The semantics of requested, initialized and rendering must therefore be verified in the startup/driver code, not inferred from this name. RFF's shader replacement should distinguish those stages and preserve the last valid pipeline until the matching new generation is accepted.

The mobile startup callback disables path tracing based on layout/device categorization. This is not a recommendation to reduce RFF mathematical precision or to infer GPU capability from window size. Use supported capabilities and measured display workload for optional shader-preview policy, and retain the user's intended final settings. The overlay registry list is memoized once, consistent with startup registration; dynamic plugin addition would need an explicit revision subscription instead.

**Proposed verification:** unrelated animated values do not refresh all controls, histogram demand stops when appropriate, all clean-output surfaces are accounted for, offsets agree across interactive and export paths, and boot/replacement callbacks belong to the current generation. Both flat 2D and relief workflows benefit from these boundaries. This inspection made no rendering, profiling or application-code changes.

## Compile scheduling: cancellation and generation identity must reach the worker

**Sources:** full reads of `hooks/useAppStartup.ts` (210 lines), `store/CompileGate.ts` (81 lines) and `store/CompileProgressStore.ts` (170 lines). These resolve the earlier startup-call-site question: the hook has its own `bootRequestedRef`, so normal duplicate requests are blocked even though AppGmt's supplied predicate reads only `isBooted`. Forced requests bypass that latch. This is a request guard, not evidence of successful compilation or rendering.

Startup schedules a 50-ms callback that reads the current configuration/camera/offset and queues boot work. The timer is not stored for cancellation on unmount or replacement. Multiple forced requests can therefore leave multiple delayed readers, each seeing whatever state exists when it runs. A fixed delay is not an acknowledgement that all intended source loading has finished. RFF should snapshot a validated revision after the necessary inputs are ready, cancel obsolete preparation explicitly, and associate the shader configuration, camera and resources with that same revision.

The outer `try/catch` surrounds timer scheduling, not execution of the delayed callback, so it cannot handle exceptions later thrown while reading configuration or queueing work. The hook also ignores the promise returned by `compileGate.queue`. That gate rejects an earlier pending promise when a newer closure replaces it; the startup call supplies no rejection handler. For RFF, treat supersession as a normal handled outcome, distinct from compilation failure, and settle every request even when work throws or is canceled.

**The gate waits for presentation opportunity, not compilation completion.** A flush runs the stored closure and resolves its promise immediately after that closure returns; here the closure posts boot work. The 500-ms safety timer can flush even without a confirmed spinner paint, so the header's guaranteed-visible description is broader than its implementation. Once work is flushed, the gate no longer owns or cancels it. A latest-pending-work policy does not prevent an older worker result from completing after a newer one. If `work()` throws, the gate has already cleared its stored resolve/reject callbacks and does not settle the promise in this implementation.

The progress store does make a failure sticky against a subsequent `finish()` in the same phase: finish only transitions from compiling. However, although `cycleId` increments at start, `finish` and `fail` accept no expected cycle ID, and failure events carry only a reason here. Thus the store itself cannot distinguish stale failure/completion messages from the current request. RFF's pipeline replacement should carry request identity through preparation, worker/device submission, completion and UI reporting. Retain the last valid pipeline and resources until the matching replacement is accepted; do not make a progress-store transition the ownership boundary.

Progress is an exponential estimate approaching 95%, then 100% on finish, not a count of compiler operations. The estimate is lower-bounded with `Math.max` but not explicitly checked for finiteness here. RFF can show elapsed time and the actual stage when the compiler cannot report progress, use finite validated estimates where available, and avoid interpreting a high estimated percentage as nearly guaranteed completion.

**Recovery-policy qualification:** startup consumes and clears the GPU-crash session flag before attempting recovery, then selects the fastest preset. It does not wait for a successful recovery frame before removing that marker. Mobile tuning also infers unmodified defaults from values such as balanced, 0 or 30; those values alone cannot establish whether a user deliberately chose them. For RFF, record explicit override provenance, separate temporary recovery settings from saved intent, and retain a bounded recovery state until success or a reported failure. Preserve reference/perturbation precision throughout.

Proposed checks cover rapid forced replacements, stale worker outcomes, unmount before the delay, work throwing during flush, handled supersession, failed recovery on the next launch and deliberately chosen default-valued settings. These are source-grounded requirements for reliable shader switching in both 2D and relief rendering, not reproduced failures or implementation claims.

## Progress and performance feedback: report the state actually being measured

**Sources:** full reads of `components/CompilingIndicator.tsx` (168 lines) and `components/PerformanceMonitor.tsx` (337 lines). The compile indicator retains failures until dismissal, extracts a short error line and exposes the full text as a tooltip. RFF can use a concise error summary with separately accessible full diagnostics, but dismissing the notice must not mean that the shader recovered. Preserve a valid prior pipeline where possible and keep failure status available after closing the notification.

The indicator schedules `compileGate.flush()` through an animation-frame callback followed by a timer. Its local guard records a cycle ID, but the delayed callback calls the global gate without passing that ID and is not canceled on supersession. It can therefore flush whichever request is pending at execution time. For RFF, a presentation callback should release only the matching request or delegate to a scheduler that validates ownership. Done-state hide timers are cleaned up when the phase changes, a useful contrast to the untracked startup fade timer previously inspected. Neither CSS transforms nor an estimated progress curve proves that rendering remains responsive under a blocked main thread; measure presentation and input latency separately.

The performance monitor reads the engine's smoothed FPS and accumulation count, avoiding the mistake of calling an idle UI tick rate rendering throughput. It suppresses low-FPS detection during compilation, export, pause, background-tab state, completed accumulation and several adaptive-render conditions. This separation is valuable for RFF: interaction latency, shader pass time, fractal computation and a deliberately finished still image require different signals. A stopped sample counter alone is not proof of successful convergence, however; its heuristic can also describe a stalled producer. Use explicit work/completion state and accepted generation IDs where available.

**Feedback controls must update the detector's state.** This implementation's tick uses module-level `performanceState.lowFpsBuffer`, while its temporary-dismiss and close handlers write a separate component-local `lowFpsBuffer` ref. Those writes do not establish the advertised detector cooldown. RFF should keep warning hysteresis, dismissal deadline and measurement validity in one owner, with time-based cooldown independent of frame rate. Check invalid/nonfinite samples and reset history when the view, renderer or measurement regime changes; old evidence should not silently carry over to a new workload.

The suggested Lite action changes both precision and buffer precision and disables shadows. That action is **not suitable for direct adoption in RFF**, whose numerical-precision requirements remain mandatory. Candidate remedies should explicitly address optional display cost, preview resolution or unnecessary updates without altering perturbation/reference accuracy or the requested final output. Resolution reduction here independently floors width and height after scaling and rounding, so it does not universally preserve aspect ratio. RFF should preserve the intended framing and label any preview-only reduction separately from export resolution.

The monitor subscribes to the full store even when it returns no visible warning. A hidden warning is therefore not proof of negligible UI work. Use narrow subscriptions for status and derive suggestions when needed, then profile actual cost. The component's browser-specific overhead statement and comments promising large gains are unverified source claims; this audit supplies no cross-browser or RFF performance measurement. Likewise background compilation is inferred from the word Lighting in a message string; use a typed stage/capability value in RFF rather than making behavior depend on wording or localization.

Proposed verification covers superseded indicator callbacks, dismissal under sustained low FPS, idle versus hung rendering, changing workload after a warning, aspect-preserving preview reductions and failure details remaining accessible after dismissal. These improvements support both flat 2D and relief shader workflows and do not alter the provisional appearance ranking.

## Authoritative state: batch configuration and preserve snapshot ownership

**Sources:** full reads of `components/EngineBridge.tsx` (23 lines), `components/ActiveSnapshotFeatures.tsx` (107 lines) and `store/engineStore.ts` (602 lines). The small EngineBridge claims to initialize store-to-worker subscriptions, but its current delegate only connects AnimationEngine to the two stores. Accumulation bindings are explicitly delegated elsewhere. This narrows the earlier architectural assumption: a mounted bridge is not evidence that all shader properties and textures are synchronized. For RFF, enumerate the actual owners of uniform updates, resource uploads, pipeline rebuilds and camera changes instead of relying on one nominal bridge component.

Post-boot scene loading groups migration/hydration, full shader-configuration emission, precise scene-offset forwarding and CONFIG_DONE. The useful transfer is an explicit complete-configuration boundary: do not compile a new shader against half of a newly loaded scene. RFF should stage compatible descriptor resources, shader settings and view state together, then accept their common revision. This module emits several messages; atomic worker application and compile coalescing remain the receiver's responsibility rather than a guarantee of consecutive sends.

`getShaderConfigFromState` shallow-copies each feature slice and retains pipeline/graph references. `getPreset` similarly includes animation and sequence objects directly. These functions create representations, but do not alone establish deep immutable snapshots. RFF should document ownership of queued configurations and keep nested arrays/images stable until the receiving job has copied or retained them. A delayed compile or export must not see a later mutation through a shared object. The formula-change closure also combines a captured formula/old graph reference with current settings read when it executes; this reinforces the need for one validated generation when switching modes.

**A saved baseline is a separate transaction.** Loading schedules a 50-ms callback that hashes the state as it exists then, rather than retaining the exact just-loaded snapshot. An intervening edit could become part of that baseline unless another layer excludes it. Export preparation updates version/hash metadata before this function has evidence of an output write succeeding. RFF should distinguish preparing an export, successfully saving bytes and setting the saved baseline; commit the baseline against the saved revision, not the current live document after asynchronous work. Camera framing is deliberately excluded from GMT's dirty hash, but framing/zoom is central content for a Mandelbrot location and must not be excluded from RFF by analogy.

The store's optional document serialization is also a useful distinction: a scene save can include auxiliary editable documents, while a share payload need not include the user's entire palette library. RFF should capture the assets actually referenced by its environment, image layers and masks under an explicit packaging policy. Referenced assets, full libraries and transient editor state have different scopes; including one must not silently include all three. Preserve RFF's established binary-format and palette-recipe contracts.

The active-snapshot footer displays ordinary live feature editors when a snapshot ID is selected. It does not itself write changes back into that saved snapshot. For RFF, distinguish selecting a saved material/view, editing its current instance and explicitly updating the saved entry. A highlighted library item or visible editor is not sufficient evidence that the asset on disk has changed.

Other concrete integration details include a canonical physical-pixel accessor, movement locking based on active tools/export state, lazy store construction after feature registration, and phase adjustment when an animation period changes. These should remain separate contracts: physical versus logical pixels must be clear for texture footprints; a mask/light drag should not pan the fractal simultaneously; period changes need a defined clock for deterministic video, not an unexamined wall-time phase rule. Proposed checks cover settings edited during load/save, nested resource mutation during queued work, complete configuration acceptance, view dirty tracking and updating versus merely selecting a snapshot. No application behavior was modified or tested here.

## Parameter updates: separate stored values, resolved uniforms and resource acceptance

**Evidence read in full:** [createFeatureSlice.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/createFeatureSlice.ts) and [createObservableState.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/createObservableState.ts). This is host-side support for the proposed shader controls, not an additional appearance effect or a measured performance improvement.

The feature slice distinguishes stored configuration from live uniform values. Its scalar/vector modulation path calls the same mapping/composition helper used by animation before emitting a uniform, while CONFIG receives the base value. This is a useful RFF design constraint: dragging a material control and advancing its animation must resolve through one evaluator. Otherwise two writers can alternate between the base and animated value. Preserve authored values for saving, and derive the rendered value at a declared time; deterministic export must supply that time rather than inherit an uncontrolled live clock. The composite-vector branch constructs values separately, so this file alone does not prove identical modulation semantics for every composite parameter.

Configuration emission is not synonymous with recompilation. Non-image parameters are forwarded even when unchanged, and the downstream configuration manager decides whether a compile-time change requires rebuilding. For RFF, classify a change as a uniform update, image/resource replacement, or pipeline replacement, then measure the work actually triggered. A reset notification alone cannot replace any of those operations. GMT's custom feature actions merge reducer output and emit a reset without using the ordinary setter's CONFIG/uniform/texture routes; other bindings may compensate, but that compensation is not established by this file. RFF's preset, undo, custom-action and direct-editor paths should converge on the same accepted render-state transaction.

**Commit and notify coherently.** Texture/uniform events are emitted inside the store updater before its new feature slice is returned; CONFIG and the final reset follow the store call. A synchronous subscriber that reads the store during an early event can therefore observe the prior slice. Prefer committing one validated state revision and then publishing notifications carrying that revision. Type conversion here covers vectors/colors, not general finite-value or range validation. Hook-generated extras are not recursively normalized, and hooks read the old slice rather than a progressively updated candidate. A RFF batch should define these dependencies explicitly and validate the complete candidate once; independent properties should not acquire accidental input-order semantics.

For images, the setter routes uploads from a uniform-name heuristic and automatically toggles related enable flags before receiving evidence that decoding/upload succeeded. Some sibling flag changes are made directly to the candidate slice and emitted as uniforms rather than necessarily joining CONFIG. The RFF environment/reflection proposal should instead use explicit resource and layer identities, retain the last accepted resource during replacement, and activate the new binding only when the matching upload generation is ready. Removing a referenced image needs a defined missing-source result, especially when paint visibility and emission usage are independent. These are integration requirements, not a claim that every GMT image path uses this generic branch.

Avoid copying incidental equality and dependency rules. GMT's numeric reset check uses an absolute `1e-9` tolerance even though a new uniform may still be emitted; the same object reference is considered unchanged, while newly allocated objects are conservatively changed. RFF must not borrow this epsilon for precision-sensitive fractal data. Establish equality and invalidation by parameter domain, and keep orbit/MPA precision intact. The composite dependency table maps each dependency to one composite key, so multiple consumers would overwrite that entry; shared RFF field/mask controls need a dependency-to-consumer set. Gradient/composite update paths also have their own invalidation behavior, so scalar deduplication does not establish universal deduplication.

The small observable-state helper assigns a shallow merged snapshot before synchronously notifying its listeners. It deliberately provides neither equality suppression nor domain validation; nested data and the returned snapshot remain shared references, and one throwing listener can interrupt that notification loop. It is suitable as plumbing only under an explicit caller contract. Do not infer an immutable shader snapshot, batched updates or reduced GPU work merely from a shared state helper.

**Proposed verification:** edit an animated parameter while its modulation is active and silent; restore a preset with dependent values supplied together; update one field consumed by multiple masks; replace an image twice with uploads completing out of order; clear an emission source; exercise identical updates and custom actions; and confirm uniform-only edits do not rebuild pipelines. Compare preview and fixed-time export from the same accepted revision. No RFF source implementation, GPU timing or runtime validation is claimed in this section.

## Animated appearance: preserve time semantics when changing frame rate

**Evidence read in full:** [playbackSlice.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/animation/playbackSlice.ts), [types.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/animation/types.ts), [audioClipsSlice.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/animation/audioClipsSlice.ts), [selectionSlice.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/animation/selectionSlice.ts), [uiSlice.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/animation/uiSlice.ts), and [animationStore.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/animationStore.ts). These modules establish state and action contracts; they do not by themselves prove the animation evaluator, recording flush or export clock obeys those contracts.

**Transfer to RFF:** animated environment rotation, material masks, emission and decorative UV transforms need one declared time domain. GMT exposes a deterministic-playback flag whose documented intent is integer project frames and modulation time derived from `currentFrame / fps`; the flag defaults to false here. The actual stepping/oscillator implementation is elsewhere. RFF should evaluate a requested output frame at an explicit timestamp, with identical parameter resolution in preview and export.
