A fixed timestamp alone does not guarantee deterministic stateful noise, audio analysis or simulation; such sources need reproducible samples or a declared bake/cache policy. Ordinary 2D palette and image-coordinate animation benefits from this just as relief lighting does.

The frame-rate setter offers two useful, distinct operations: keep keyframe indices (changing their times in seconds), or remap frame positions by `newFps / oldFps` (approximately preserving time). The remap scales Bezier handle horizontal offsets while retaining their value-axis components. It also rescales both duration fields, current frame and audio-clip start frames, leaving second-based trims untouched. This is the right dimensional distinction to preserve if RFF adds a richer material timeline. Do not scale a value tangent or an audio trim merely because it is stored beside a frame index.

There are important limits to the time-preservation promise. Positions are rounded to integer frames; collisions use the last key encountered at a resulting frame. Conversion to a lower rate can therefore discard distinct keys, and repeated conversion need not restore them. Incrementally remapping an already rounded sequence during an FPS drag can also accumulate loss. RFF should calculate a live preview from the original transaction snapshot, disclose collisions, and commit once, or retain higher-resolution/rational authored times where its file contract permits. This is an authoring representation proposal, not permission to alter existing saved formats or perturbation precision.

GMT saves an FPS undo item containing sequence, FPS, both relevant playback values and audio placements. Rapid changes are coalesced through a module-level 400-ms timestamp and the top undo-item type. That is a timing heuristic rather than an explicit gesture boundary. RFF should group one user operation by a transaction identity and clear incompatible redo history on every divergent edit, including edits absorbed into an existing transaction. In this setter, redo clearing occurs only when a new history item is pushed; full undo/redo interaction still requires the sequence implementation. Audio clip copies are shallow, so nested peak arrays should remain immutable if retained by history. The store does not enforce that ownership.

Recording starts with a separate JSON-cloned sequence snapshot, preventing the reference sequence from immediately following newly baked keys. This is transferable to recording animated shader controls: resolve against stable authored inputs rather than feeding the recorded result back into its own source. Pause/stop clear the recording snapshot in this slice; completion of any buffered recording writes is not demonstrated here. RFF should finish or explicitly discard pending samples before declaring a recording stopped. The range-recording interfaces describe filling skipped integer frames with sampled values; that contract is sample holding, not proof of reconstructing the missing waveform.

These state modules also show why editor plumbing and render semantics should stay separate. Track/key selection and collapsed groups are UI state; they should not invalidate a rendered frame unless an actual animated value changes. The audio setters accept shallow clip patches without validating trims or placement, while seek/duration/FPS setters do not collectively enforce a finite, consistent frame domain (`newFps < 1` alone does not reject NaN or infinity). RFF should validate at the shared command boundary and define whether duration is a frame count or an inclusive last-frame index. A typed interface or clamped panel widget cannot substitute for validation of loaded and programmatic values. Existing GMT performance comments are historical assertions, not timing results obtained during this audit.

**Proposed verification:** compare a fixed frame in interactive and exported rendering; convert 30 to 24 FPS with adjacent keys and nonzero tangent offsets; change FPS continuously then undo once; verify audio start/trim alignment; seek to both endpoints; reject nonfinite timing input; stop while recording samples are buffered; and confirm timeline-only selection changes do not trigger shader rebuilding. These checks are proposed, not executed RFF tests.

## Animation editing: preserve the evaluated curve and the recording source

**Evidence read in full:** [sequenceSlice.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/animation/sequenceSlice.ts). This follow-up resolves the preceding state-interface questions where this implementation provides evidence, while keeping evaluator/export guarantees separate.

FPS undo/redo does restore the saved sequence, FPS, duration, playhead and audio placements, and captures the inverse state for the opposite stack. Older entries without audio data leave current clips alone. Ordinary sequence history restores only the sequence; selection and the separate playback duration are not included. RFF should define transaction scope explicitly so a shader-animation edit and its timing metadata return to a coherent state together. Here history application and stack movement are separate store writes, and several operations snapshot before discovering that nothing can change. For RFF, validate an operation first, then commit its state/history coherently; avoid consuming history capacity for missing tracks or empty tangent changes. Direct key additions/updates do not snapshot internally, so gesture callers must own the history boundary rather than assuming every action is automatically undoable.

**A useful curve-editing addition:** inserting a key can split a cubic Bezier segment with De Casteljau subdivision. GMT solves for the requested frame along the curve, rewrites adjacent handles, inserts the evaluated value and disables automatic tangent replacement for the affected keys. This can let RFF users add control points to a smooth environment rotation, emission fade or palette animation without intentionally changing its shape. The inspected branch replaces the supplied key value with the evaluated curve value: expose “insert on curve” separately from “set this value at this frame.” Shape preservation must be checked against the actual interpolation domain; this branch operates directly on stored values, whereas its fallback tangent calculation explicitly consults the logarithmic-track registry. It is not evidence that subdivision preserves every logarithmically evaluated track. Solve and split in the same domain as rendering, with a defined policy for ambiguous/nonmonotonic time handles. No new fractal numeric approximation is proposed.

The recording methods confirm the earlier sample-holding interpretation: each provided value is repeated at every frame in an inclusive range. The multi-range variant groups operations per track, clones the track/key array once per batch and publishes one store update. Borrow the batching and stable identity of an overwritten final key, but do not describe filled frames as independently sampled audio or simulation. A forward append avoids sorting yet still copies the existing array; the entire update is not constant-time. Multi-range recording also materializes a frame/value operation for each filled frame, increasing transient memory. RFF should bound batches, validate finite integral ranges, and use offline source evaluation when exact per-frame modulation is required. Buffer flushing on stop remains the recorder caller's responsibility, not something this slice implements.

Changed-track references are replaced in the main batch/edit paths so selective subscriptions and curve caches can detect updates; untouched tracks retain identity in targeted operations. This is useful for responsive editing of many material channels without rebuilding every graph preview. It does not prove reduced shader execution time. Maintain immutable nested handles as well: clipboard records and pasted keys reuse tangent objects here, and the multi-key updater can modify the caller's patch object when switching interpolation. RFF should own copied edit data explicitly rather than rely on every future caller avoiding mutation.

Clipboard and loop operations require content-level semantics, not only array manipulation. Pasting targets original track IDs and silently skips missing tracks; it also resets tangent-mode flags. Duplicating invokes copy followed by paste, but a failed/empty copy leaves an older clipboard available. RFF should make duplicate operate on a validated current selection, preserve declared tangent semantics and report incompatible destinations. Looping finds selected originals in the array it is already modifying; replacing a boundary key can remove an original ID needed by later iterations. Build repetitions from an immutable source selection and define boundary ownership so adjacent periods do not accidentally replace their source. These are concrete adoption constraints for repeating 2D palette/UV motion as well as relief lighting.

Finally, simplification operates on selected keys and then merges the result with unselected keys. Its tolerance alone is not a bound on the fully evaluated mixed curve, shader appearance or physical parameter error. If offered in RFF, use parameter-domain error criteria, preserve discontinuities/periodic seams, and compare the complete resulting animation at relevant times before accepting lossy reduction. Do not apply such simplification to high-precision fractal state under a generic tolerance.

**Proposed checks:** curve insertion leaves sampled output unchanged for linear and logarithmic parameter domains; explicit-value insertion retains the requested value; recording fills exactly the declared range; undo/redo restores timing and audio together; empty duplication cannot paste stale data; loop endpoints remain stable across multiple repetitions; and simplification preserves unselected boundaries. Source inspection supports these requirements; no runtime or image-quality result is claimed.

## Appearance history: restore content and its editing context as one operation

**Evidence read in full:** [historySlice.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/slices/historySlice.ts). GMT separates parameter and camera undo stacks; animation history remains elsewhere. The transferable benefit for RFF is predictable intent: undoing a material slider should have a clear relationship to intervening navigation and timeline edits. Separate scopes are one option, not automatically the best RFF interaction model. If adopted, make the active scope and action label visible, and preserve high-precision location data under RFF's native representation rather than copying GMT's camera snapshot format.

The parameter transaction snapshots registered feature slices, render region, modular graph, modulation settings and optional external providers. At completion it compares content and pushes only changed top-level snapshot keys. External providers can define a comparison view distinct from their full restorable payload, and can declare context that never creates an entry by itself but accompanies every actual content edit. This is useful for the proposed mask/environment editors: undo can restore the edited gradient and the selected stop or panel without treating merely opening that panel as a material change. Content is applied before external context. Provider keys and lifetime require explicit ownership: this implementation replaces registrations with matching keys and silently skips restoration when a provider is absent. RFF should not discard an asset's undo information merely because its editor has closed.

“Diff” here means changed feature slices, not a compact field-level delta. Initial captures JSON-clone whole slices, potentially including large image strings, then compare serialized content at gesture end. The 50-entry limit bounds entry count, not memory. For RFF, preserve immutable asset handles and small parameter deltas with retained resource ownership; avoid copying environment images for every material drag. JSON cloning is not a suitable substitute for an exact snapshot of GMP-backed locations or other non-JSON numeric state. Redo capture in this implementation clones external values but retains ordinary engine-field references, relying on their immutability. Treat that as a required ownership contract rather than automatic snapshot isolation.

Restoration first installs engine fields, then invokes conventionally named setters (with a formula special case), restores external providers and resets accumulation. This verifies that generic shader setters are deliberately re-entered on undo. It does not guarantee an atomic worker update or that asynchronous textures and replacement pipelines are ready when undo returns. RFF should stage one restored render revision, synchronize uniforms/resources through the normal command path and reject late results belonging to the undone revision. A missing setter must have an explicit restore policy; a reset alone cannot synchronize an absent binding. The synchronous restore loop also has no local rollback for a failing provider, so commit/error semantics must be defined before using this architecture across independent editors.

The parameter bracket has one snapshot slot: a second begin replaces the first rather than nesting. Camera transactions use a module-level 1.5-second debounce, with early return before redo clearing when coalesced. These details support explicit gesture identities and cancellation in RFF, including nested color/gradient dialogs, rather than timing-only grouping. The action named `resetParamHistory` actually clears both camera and parameter histories in this source; command names and scope should agree in a target implementation. End-of-interaction also restores DPR/MSAA-related state before determining whether content changed. Keep interactive display-quality policy separate from history semantics and never reduce RFF's fractal computation precision as an incidental effect of a material gesture.

**Proposed checks:** undo a gradient edit after navigation; close/reopen its editor before undo; cancel a nested dialog; replace an image and undo before upload completes; undo then make a new gesture within the debounce interval; restore a provider that reports an error; and measure history memory with large images. Confirm both the accepted shader output and exact saved location after restoration. No runtime verification or RFF implementation is claimed here.

## Settings ownership and interaction scheduling for richer shader controls

**Evidence read in full:** [coreSettings.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/coreSettings.ts), [settingsRegistry.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/settingsRegistry.ts), [settingsPanelState.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/settingsPanelState.ts), and [createInteractionSlice.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/slices/createInteractionSlice.ts). The previously read [InteractionSessionMachine.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/InteractionSessionMachine.ts) was rechecked to resolve wrapper semantics; it is not counted as newly covered.

The settings registry describes controls but delegates reads, writes and persistence to their owning subsystem. It supports immediate scalar/enum controls, one-shot actions and custom staged forms. This separation is useful for RFF: interface brightness, editor layout and autosave preferences should not become saved material parameters, while environment rotation, roughness and mask ranges must remain part of the appearance being reproduced. GMT's core registration explicitly concerns interface color controls and app-selected autosave ownership; it does not implement file persistence itself. A registration descriptor or open-panel flag is not evidence that a setting is saved, migrated or undoable. Retain RFF's append-only ConfigIO rules when introducing actual saved fields.

Registration is guarded once per module, so the first core-settings options determine the selected autosave store and labels. If RFF uses a registry, make initialization ownership explicit and avoid silently reusing one document/window's preferences for another. Optional subscription and visibility callbacks also have different jobs: a visibility predicate alone does not notify the panel when its dependency changes. The registry's numeric limits are metadata, not validation at the value owner. An environment import or costly pipeline mode may benefit from a staged form, but its Apply action must commit a validated render revision rather than only updating visible controls.

**Responsive editing mechanism:** the interaction wrapper keeps high-frequency source activity outside reactive UI state and publishes only transitions between active and inactive. Render consumers can poll a richer activity result, including a short settling tail; this avoids a global UI-state write for every pointer event. RFF can use the same separation for material drags, texture transforms and palette editing. Keep gesture activity distinct from render dirtiness, animation progress and pending resource work: releasing a slider is not proof that its final shader state has rendered, and a stationary animation still needs its scheduled frames. This is a scheduling proposal, not a measured frame-rate gain.

The wrapper's boolean represents held gestures only. A discrete poke refreshes timestamps without setting that boolean, and the polled query can remain true after the boolean turns false. A consumer using the wrong representation can therefore miss wheel/key activity or the settling interval. Its 50-ms poke throttle is shared across sources, so a second source's poke inside the window is dropped even when a source-filtered consumer needs it. Preserve source-specific activity before coalescing notifications if RFF uses such filters. Likewise, the session instance is module-level: multiple store instances in the same module realm would share it, regardless of the comment's per-app intent. Allocate per document/window when independent interaction lifetimes are required.

The pure machine uses reference counts for overlapping begins and ends and an eight-second global inactivity watchdog. The watchdog is a fallback, not normal cancellation: activity from another source keeps the global timestamp fresh, potentially preserving a stranded source; a motionless held gesture can be cleared once the timeout expires. Contrary to one wrapper comment, `isInteracting()` itself does not expire a hard-active source; `tickWatchdog()` must actually run. RFF should handle pointer cancellation, capture loss and window teardown explicitly, then use a watchdog for recovery. Keep this separate from the known native Win32 menu show-before-paint interval; these modules provide no evidence about that behavior.

**Proposed checks:** two independent windows; simultaneous slider and navigation activity; discrete events inside the throttle interval; a held but motionless gesture; capture loss while another input remains active; final rendering after release; conditional settings changed elsewhere; and save/reload with interface preferences differing between machines. Verify that scheduling changes preserve fractal computation precision and the final output. No RFF code or runtime behavior was changed.

## Analysis panels: separate requested data, accepted data and panel layout

**Evidence read in full:** [store/slices/uiSlice.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/store/slices/uiSlice.ts). The most relevant RFF transfer is support for the proposed field histogram and material inspection tools, rather than a new shading formula.

GMT keeps histogram consumer counts, refresh counters, selected coloring layer and returned data as separate state. Switching the histogram layer emits its analysis uniform with `noAccumReset: true` and requests a refresh. This is a useful contract: selecting an analysis source should not invalidate the beauty image when the selection has no beauty-rendering effect. RFF can inspect iteration fields or material masks without recomputing the reference orbit or changing MPA. Verify separation in the actual shader variant and bindings before applying such an exemption; a shared flag that also affects appearance cannot safely be exempted merely because a histogram panel writes it.

This slice does not attach a source/revision ID to accepted histogram data: `setHistogramData` accepts the payload and clears one global loading flag. A layer switch leaves existing data present until a replacement arrives. RFF should associate each histogram with its field, mapping stage, view and render generation, label retained data as stale while refreshing, and accept only a matching completion. Consumer counts prevent unnecessary analysis only when registration and cleanup are balanced; clamping an underflow to zero can hide an ownership mismatch. Per-consumer leases and a single outstanding request per analysis target would make multiple visible inspectors predictable. Closing a panel must not invalidate data needed by another consumer, and an old completion must not clear the loading state of a newer request.

The source also establishes a practical persistence boundary: interface mode, hints, dock sizes and composition guides are local preferences, while histogram results and open popups are transient. For RFF, construction guides and diagnostic masks should remain distinct from exported artwork unless the user explicitly chooses to include them. A composition spiral overlay is an editing guide, not the proposed logarithmic-spiral image-coordinate shader. Likewise, opening the workshop with imported GLSL records editor source; this action does not establish compilation, validation, installation or licensing of that source. Do not count an editor-opening path as a completed shader import pipeline.

Panel operations reveal requirements for integrating additional material tools. Layout changes should preserve stable identities for unchanged panels while replacing every changed panel object; this implementation sometimes clones only the panel dictionary and mutates neighboring panel entries in place. Subscribers watching an individual panel by reference may miss those changes. Layout cancellation restores the panel snapshot but does not restore/rederive active-tab and dock-collapse values in this action. RFF should restore all dependent layout state coherently so canceling a drag cannot strand a histogram or environment editor behind an inconsistent selected tab. Panel movement/reordering should share the same dock constraints and effective-layout calculation; GMT's toggle path applies a mobile dock remap, while move/reorder use other paths. These are integration lessons, not evidence about RFF's existing native panels or the known Win32 menu flash.

Preference loading applies useful boolean and enum checks, but generic JSON loading only merges parsed values and numeric loading only checks finiteness. New RFF editor preferences need type/range validation and window-bound clamping, including after display changes. Persistent user intent should also survive temporary workflows: tutorial actions here overwrite `showHints` during entry/exit without restoring the pre-tutorial value. A future guided material tutorial should retain the user's setting and release its temporary override on completion or cancellation. Keep such transient overrides out of scene serialization and shader invalidation.

**Proposed checks:** switch analysis fields while a readback is outstanding; open two histogram consumers and close one; cancel a panel drag after changing docks; restore layouts on a smaller display; finish a tutorial with hints originally disabled; and confirm diagnostic selection neither changes exported beauty pixels nor starts new fractal computation. This section is source-based planning; no UI screenshots, runtime tests or performance measurements were made.

## Parameter-panel binding: one candidate configuration for controls and rendering

**Evidence read in full:** [AutoFeaturePanel.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/AutoFeaturePanel.tsx). This is a source-level binding review, not a visual interface audit. The useful RFF transfer is a shared parameter contract connecting material controls, animation and pending shader changes.

The panel derives scalar/vector animation bindings centrally and uses the same parameter-mapping helper as modulation. This supports consistent logarithmic or nonlinear slider behavior and separate display of authored versus live values. For RFF's proposed environment, mask and emission controls, declare the mapping once and use it for interactive editing, modulation and textual input. A displayed angle in multiples of pi still needs a declared stored unit. Hiding keyframe controls is a presentation decision, not proof that the parameter has no active animation; saved animation and resolved shader values must remain explicit.

Composite vector edits are decomposed into scalar backing fields before routing. The direct route sends a single batched update, but the override route calls once per scalar, and the compile route queues one event per scalar after a 50-ms timer. Borrow early canonicalization while retaining an atomic candidate across every route: an environment rotation or paired mask range should not briefly compile against only part of its new value. Compile routing here checks the aggregate parameter's original configuration, not each decomposed scalar's metadata. The timer is a delay, not acknowledgement that the destination is ready. RFF should queue to a revision-aware command owner and discard obsolete requests instead of depending on panel mounting time.

Displayed values can come from `forcedState`, while cross-feature conditions and option-capability predicates read the live global store. That store is read imperatively rather than subscribed for each dependency, so an unrelated capability change need not immediately rerender this panel. Dynamic configuration overrides are applied during control rendering, whereas update routing reads the original parameter configuration. RFF should evaluate visibility, limits, validity and compile/runtime classification against one complete candidate state, with explicit dependency subscriptions. Pending values and accepted shader values must not be conflated: a boolean's value alone is not evidence that the corresponding pipeline is compiled, despite the status wording in this renderer.

The paired-range widget coordinates gestures and two keyframe tracks but applies changed endpoints through separate callbacks. Its numeric entry intentionally treats displayed bounds as soft suggestions. This is appropriate for some artistic controls, but RFF needs separate hard validity constraints for roughness, allocation sizes, denominators and finite coordinates. The paired partner's visibility and disabled rules also need joint evaluation so one combined widget cannot expose an otherwise unavailable field or lose its only visible row. The read path assembles composed vectors of length two or three, while the write path supports a fourth axis; a generic RFF schema should verify read/write symmetry for every supported shape rather than infer support from the presence of a vec4 widget.

**Image/environment integration:** the file input advertises ordinary images plus HDR/EXR and reads a data URL. This component does not prove those formats are decoded correctly downstream, validate dimensions, report read errors, or reject an older read completing after a newer selection. Use stable layer IDs and request generations through decoding and GPU upload. Its DOM input ID contains only the parameter key, so repeated mounts/features with the same key can collide; editor identity should include its instance and target. The color-profile control cycles three numeric values and labels them sRGB, LIN and ACES. Those labels alone do not specify primaries, transfer functions or the exact working-space transform. RFF should expose only input interpretations implemented by its decoder/shader path, identify any approximation precisely, and preserve linear-light/HDR values through reflection filtering.

Gradient controls have a useful separate render-preview input: the preview bar can show a temporary evaluated gradient while editable knots still describe the underlying source until baking. RFF could use this for reversible palette/environment adjustments, with explicit commit/cancel semantics. Lazy loading has a failure fallback, but an empty suspense placeholder is not a readiness signal. Custom controls receive live actions and may bypass the normal update override, so shared transaction/validation behavior must be part of their interface rather than assumed from common visual placement.

**Proposed checks:** change a cross-feature capability while the panel remains mounted; edit a composed vector in direct and pending modes; verify four-axis read/write round trips; change both range endpoints; load two images with reversed completion order; mount two identical parameter editors; and compare authored/live/pending/accepted values before and after compilation. These requirements apply to flat 2D palettes and image mapping as well as relief materials. No RFF code, screenshots or runtime tests were produced in this review.

## Revealing an edit target and retaining pending shader changes

**Evidence read in full:** [Accordion.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/Accordion.tsx), [accordionReveal.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/accordionReveal.ts), [CompileDropdownSection.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/CompileDropdownSection.tsx), [CompileBar.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/CompileBar.tsx), and [CompileSection.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/CompileSection.tsx).

A useful authoring flow is to reveal the actual destination after applying a library gradient or environment: open its panel and then its target section. GMT supports independent sections, exclusive groups and a fallback section, with external open requests. This transfers to RFF's image layers and material-mask editors without introducing a 3D renderer. Treat reveal as navigation, separate from committing the asset. Opening a section is not proof that a texture upload or shader replacement succeeded.

The reveal bus broadcasts an ID and retains only the latest request for two seconds, allowing a newly mounted accordion to consume it. Live delivery does not itself clear the retained request; multiple live owners of the same ID can react, and a later mount can still consume it. This is a best-effort convenience, not reliable destination acknowledgement. RFF should identify the document, editor and layer, and use an explicit ready/consumed result when navigation matters to completing an operation. A request that expires before a slow panel mounts should not leave a success message claiming the user is viewing the destination. Several rapid destination changes also require an intentional latest-request policy.

Accordion state is initialized from sections once; recomputing defaults does not reconcile an existing open map when section definitions change. Initial open sections do not invoke the change callback here. That matters when the callback selects an analysis layer: initialize analysis selection explicitly rather than assuming a default-open section emitted an event. Changed-section callbacks run inside state updaters, so they should not be treated as exactly-once committed effects. RFF should publish analysis-demand changes after the layout state is accepted and release consumers on unmount. Collapsed bodies are conditionally unmounted, which can discard locally owned pending edits unless their owner lives above that boundary.

The compile-dropdown section illustrates useful staging: compile-time keys accumulate locally, runtime keys update immediately, and displayed candidate values merge pending changes over the current slice. However, Apply calls the setter and immediately clears local pending state; the active status shown when nothing is pending is not a worker compile-success acknowledgement. RFF should distinguish an unsubmitted candidate, a submitted generation, the last accepted pipeline and a failed replacement. Retain the candidate for retry and keep a valid previous render until acceptance. Reconcile local candidates against preset loads, undo and document switches instead of allowing stale values to overlay unrelated current settings. Primitive identity comparisons are sufficient for these dropdowns, but are not a general equality contract for gradients, vectors or images.

The shared compile bar and compile section are presentation components driven by caller-provided state. Their labels, disable flag and shading do not establish cancellation, serialization or successful compilation. The dropdown section also defines its own compile bar, so common status semantics cannot be assumed merely from similar appearance. If RFF adds expensive optional material variants, centralize their state machine and let each presentation render that state; do not infer pipeline readiness from a checkbox or an empty pending dictionary.

**Proposed checks:** apply an asset while its destination is unmounted; issue two reveals rapidly; change section definitions; collapse and reopen with pending compile changes; load a preset while a candidate exists; and fail a replacement compile after submission. Verify target identity, retained edits, analysis-source selection and continued display of the last accepted image. The same conditions apply to flat 2D palette/image work and relief material editing. No runtime verification is claimed.

## Optional shader features: distinguish runtime bypass from pipeline removal

**Evidence read in full:** [CompilableFeatureSection.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/CompilableFeatureSection.tsx). GMT models two distinct gates: whether a feature belongs in the shader variant, and whether an already included feature is currently active. A runtime toggle can bypass an included effect without requesting a rebuild; unloading changes the compile gate. Compile-only features instead stage their on/off change. This is a useful reference for expensive optional RFF material effects, provided the actual Vulkan specialization and uniform behavior supports the distinction. A runtime branch does not guarantee zero GPU cost, and removing code does not establish a speed gain without measurement.

First-time enabling batches the compile gate, runtime gate and pending settings in one setter call. Unloading similarly batches both off flags. Preserve that coherent intent in RFF, then extend it through pipeline acceptance: a single host-store update is not atomic GPU resource installation. This component derives `isCompiled` from a stored boolean, clears pending values after setter invocation and does not wait for a compile result. The previous report's distinction between requested and accepted state therefore also applies to this feature-level path. Keep old valid pipelines available during replacement and preserve retryable settings on failure.

The shortcut to the central compiler uses a different path: after a timer it queues a compile-enable flag only if currently uncompiled, then local pending settings, and clears those local settings. It does not transfer the pending on/off toggle or runtime-enable flag. Consequently this shortcut is not equivalent to the local Compile action for every state. RFF should transfer one complete candidate transaction, including intended activation, rather than reconstructing a subset at the destination. Avoid time-based handoff and protect against edits occurring between scheduling and delivery; clearing the whole local dictionary can discard newer edits that were not in the captured payload.

The capability mechanism offers another useful transfer: disable controls with an explanation while retaining their authored settings, so switching back to a supported context restores the user's choices. For RFF's field-driven masks and independent U/V inputs, availability can depend on which buffers a loaded map or render path supplies. Preserve unavailable settings for round trips, but define their effective rendering behavior explicitly and keep a way to remove an invalid combination. Merely graying out the editor is not shader-side validation. GMT's section-specific check temporarily mutates a shared feature definition and restores it after a synchronous evaluator call; RFF should pass requirements explicitly to a pure capability query, avoiding shared mutation and exception-dependent restoration.

Compile-settings previews force their enable gates true so users can configure a feature before activation. That is useful as editor-only candidate state and must not be mistaken for an accepted render configuration. Resetting a feature invokes a separate partial-preset operation, while this component does not explicitly clear its local pending dictionary or pending toggle. Reconcile reset, preset load, undo and document changes with outstanding candidates so applying later cannot unexpectedly resurrect pre-reset values. Override configuration also deserves explicit ownership: this component treats an explicitly supplied compile parameter as a distinct section definition instead of inheriting unrelated feature toggles. Use the same clarity when several RFF controls share one underlying material feature.

**Proposed verification:** compare local Apply and central-compiler handoff for first enable, pending disable and changed settings; edit again before the handoff completes; reset with pending changes; switch to a render path lacking a required field; fail compilation; and compare runtime-disabled output with an unloaded variant where equivalence is promised. Measure both switch latency and steady-state cost before deciding which effects deserve separate compiled variants. Flat 2D image/mask effects and relief materials can use this architecture; it does not require importing GMT's 3D formula system. No RFF implementation or benchmark is claimed.

## Shared color-wheel editing for palettes and environment bands

**Evidence read in full:** [ColorWheel.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/ColorWheel.tsx). The component maps angle to HSV hue and radius to saturation, with a separate value strip, and displays multiple handles. Harmony rules and actual palette mutation belong to its host. For RFF this is a potential shared authoring control for selected palette stops or colored environment bands, not an additional shader effect or evidence that RFF lacks all equivalent color controls. A multi-handle view can make relationships between chosen colors visible while leaving the gradient's interpolation and saved recipe contracts intact.

The disc raster is regenerated only when size or active value changes; hue/saturation movement updates the handle presentation without rebuilding that raster. Device-pixel ratio is capped at two for its backing image. This is a useful bounded-cost editor optimization, but does not accelerate fractal shading. The introductory comment calls the moving presentation an overlay canvas; the implementation uses SVG spokes and positioned elements. Recreate the actual separation of static background and dynamic handles rather than relying on that description. Display-scale changes alone are not effect dependencies here, so RFF should also refresh backing resolution when moving an editor between displays.

Keep the control's color domain explicit. Saturation enters the component in 0..1 units, while the converter receives percent saturation and value. Output is an eight-bit display raster; the strip rounds value to integer percent. This is an HSV editing presentation, not perceptually uniform spacing or an HDR lighting-energy control. RFF's environment/emission workflow should retain separate linear intensity/exposure and avoid squeezing HDR values into this display-oriented channel. Hue at zero saturation should remain meaningful authored state where desired, rather than being lost through repeated RGB round trips. Do not change frozen palette recipe generation to accommodate an editor.

The wheel provides keyboard hue/saturation nudges and brackets each nudge as a gesture. Clicking another handle selects it before a subsequent drag, while modified clicking invokes the host's add callback before hit testing; add/remove history therefore belongs to the host. For RFF, address handles by stable stop IDs and preserve the gesture's original target. Here cancellation stores all handles but restores only the active index's hue/saturation through `onMove`; it does not directly restore the full arrangement. A host that moves a linked harmony group needs its own complete transaction rollback, especially if selection changes during a drag.

The disc handles pointer cancellation and capture loss as drag completion, whereas Escape restores its starting hue/saturation. The value strip has pointer-up completion but no corresponding cancellation/capture-loss handler or Escape snapshot in this component. RFF should give both controls a common finish/cancel contract, including teardown, so a stranded brightness gesture cannot keep interaction state active or merge subsequent edits into its undo entry. Keyboard/numeric access should cover value as well as hue/saturation; the strip here supplies no keyboard handler. These are source-level integration observations, not a screenshot-based accessibility assessment.

**Proposed checks:** edit linked palette stops and cancel; switch the active stop mid-gesture; lose pointer capture on the value strip; move the window across display scales; edit gray/black colors while preserving intended hue; and verify HDR intensity remains independent of wheel value. Compare the resulting gradient preview with the actual shader's color-space conversion before accepting an implementation. Both flat 2D palettes and relief environment editing benefit; no implementation or measured improvement is claimed.

## Composition guides and editor-state boundaries

**Evidence read in full:** [CompositionOverlayControls.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/CompositionOverlayControls.tsx), [CollapsibleSection.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/CollapsibleSection.tsx), and [Button.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/Button.tsx).

The composition controls expose thirds, golden-ratio, grid, center, diagonal, spiral and safe-area guides, with adjustable color, opacity and line width. A movable/rotatable/scalable spiral is useful for positioning a 2D Mandelbrot detail or balancing relief highlights before export. This is an authoring aid, separate from the ranked spiral shader proposal, which changes sampled image/color coordinates. These controls only write overlay state; they do not implement the guide geometry or establish export inclusion. RFF should align guides to the actual output crop and aspect ratio, keep them out of beauty exports by default, and distinguish any requested guide export explicitly. Safe-area percentages require a declared convention rather than an implied universal delivery standard.

The spiral ratio is adjustable, so the “Ratio (Phi)” label does not mean every setting is the golden ratio. Grid divisions and guide positions are offered through sliders, but this component supplies no command-boundary validation. Validate finite values, positive scale, integral grid counts and viewport/output coordinate conversion at the owning subsystem. The preceding UI-slice review established that each guide-setting update writes local preferences; if RFF persists drag updates, coalesce disk writes while keeping the live guide responsive. Do not add these guides to fractal computation or material evaluation merely to share shader infrastructure.

The collapsible section conditionally unmounts its body. Its controlled and uncontrolled modes are distinct, and `defaultOpen` is an initialization value rather than a synchronized setting. Keep pending material edits, active gesture cleanup and analysis-consumer ownership outside a body whose lifetime follows disclosure state. A controlled section requires its owner to update `open`; an event callback alone cannot make a fixed controlled value change. The header uses a native button but does not supply expanded-state/body association attributes here; RFF's corresponding control should expose its state through the native accessibility mechanism. This is a source observation, not a rendered accessibility test.

The generic button's active styling is also only presentation. It forwards caller attributes and allows a later spread to override its help-context handler. Its declared `toggled` property is not translated into pressed-state semantics in this implementation. When RFF displays an enabled effect or selected inspection mode, derive both visual and accessible state from the accepted command state, rather than assuming a shared button wrapper supplies them. These small controls do not justify new appearance-effect rankings; their value is reliable operation of the proposed editors.

**Proposed checks:** change output aspect/crop while guides are visible; compare preview and tiled-export framing; enter invalid persisted guide values; collapse a section during a drag or pending shader edit; and verify selected/expanded states through keyboard and accessibility APIs. No RFF implementation, image comparison or runtime test is claimed.

## Finding material fields and assets through one categorized picker

**Evidence read in full:** [CategoryPickerMenu.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/CategoryPickerMenu.tsx). Its established callers select modulation targets, uniform slots and formulas; using the mechanism for RFF palettes/environment assets is a proposed extension, not an existing GMT asset-browser capability demonstrated by this file.

The transferable mechanism combines category browsing with cross-category search. Prefix label matches rank above substring labels, descriptions and category names; results retain their category label. A single category becomes a simple list. Clicking a category pins it so moving toward its items does not accidentally change the category. For RFF's independent U/V fields, mask sources and emission sources, this can make a growing set of choices discoverable without requiring users to know the exact parameter name. Keep unavailable choices identifiable with a reason, and validate capability again at selection time because render-path availability may change while a picker is open.

Selection callbacks receive only an item key, although search-result identity includes category plus key. RFF should guarantee globally unique target IDs or return a structured category/source identity; identical labels or local keys must not select a different image layer or field. Search here is a simple case-folded substring score, not fuzzy matching, localization-aware tokenization or an asset index. It regenerates every category's items and sorts all matches for each query, then renders every result. That is reasonable for modest parameter lists; profile and use indexed/virtualized results before applying it to a large material library. Cache invalidation must include availability and catalog revisions, not just a stable callback reference.

The search field appears on the first printable keystroke, captured at window level, unless another text input is active. The handler does not check IME composition, and keyboard selection handles Enter without a composition guard. For RFF's Japanese users, composition-aware input is a concrete requirement: confirming a character must not apply a material. A visible search affordance and keyboard access to category browsing are also needed when typing cannot reveal the field. This component supplies arrow/Enter/Escape handling in its search input, but does not implement equivalent category navigation or a general Escape handler before search opens. Disabled choices suppress selection callbacks without native disabled-state attributes, and arrow navigation includes them. Define keyboard and accessibility semantics independently of dimmed styling.

Placement uses estimated column widths and current window dimensions, with a side flip near the right edge. Categories may grow beyond their minimum width, and this effect does not subscribe to window resizing. RFF should position against measured content and the current work area, constrain oversized menus and update when a window/display changes. Do not treat this web menu as evidence about the known native Win32 popup flash. Selection closes the picker immediately after calling `onSelect`; that confirms a request, not asynchronous resource loading or shader application. Let the destination report accepted state or failure, retaining the previous valid resource until replacement succeeds.

**Proposed checks:** duplicate keys across categories; Japanese IME confirmation; capability changes while open; keyboard-only browse and search; a narrow work area with long labels; a large catalog; and failed image loading after selection. These are source-derived integration criteria for both 2D and relief editing, with no runtime measurement or new appearance ranking implied.

## Gradient reduction: separate preview choice from approximation guarantees

**Evidence read in full:** [gradientStopReducer.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/gradientStopReducer.ts), [ReduceStopsPopup.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/ReduceStopsPopup.tsx), and [BlendSpacePicker.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/BlendSpacePicker.tsx).

A useful RFF authoring extension is to simplify an imported or densely edited gradient into fewer editable stops while previewing the change before committing. GMT's reducer interface returns progressive plans containing a candidate at each stop count, named reduction levels and a pending flag. The popup separates a fixed count selected by dragging from a named amount whose count follows improvements to the plan. That distinction makes the control predictable during ongoing search. This interface does not establish an approximation error bound; the actual reducer owns its tolerances and candidate construction. Do not interpret a “Light” or “Strong” label, or fewer stops, as proof of preserved appearance or faster shader rendering.

For RFF, preserve the original gradient and stable target revision throughout the operation. Keep explicit Apply as one undoable edit, and let Cancel restore the original preview without regenerating frozen recipe IDs. Validate candidate completeness, stop count and finite positions before exposing a progressive plan. Search may optionally change the interpolation/blend mode as well as stop placement; report that change and save both together. Compare the resulting sampled gradient under RFF's actual color conversion, wrap behavior and resolution. A generic stop-count reduction must not silently simplify high-precision fractal data or a lossless map.

The popup previews a hovered named amount but applies the separately chosen candidate. Consequently the visible hover preview and Apply target can differ until hover ends. Make the distinction clear or bind Apply to a stable explicitly selected preview. A chosen count stays fixed as plans evolve, but its candidate colors can still change; freeze the accepted candidate at click time and reject plans for an obsolete source. Applying is allowed while a plan remains pending, so it means accepting the current candidate rather than waiting for optimality. Cleanup requests preview removal on unmount; hosts must scope that request so an old popup cannot clear a newer tool's preview.

The reducer slot advertises pulling one iterator step per macrotask. That is a cooperative scheduling contract, not a guarantee of frame responsiveness: a single expensive `next()` can still block. Measure and bound work within each step, provide cancellation, and avoid continuing search after the source/editor is gone. The slot itself is last-writer-wins registration and does not implement those execution guarantees. The large editor's caller remains a separate inspection item.

The blend picker supplies a complementary mechanism: hover/focus previews an interpolation mode without emitting a committed selection, and a retired mode remains visible when it is already used by the current gradient. RFF should preserve legacy rendering and identifiers even when a mode is no longer offered for new gradients. The picker accepts different mode lists for gradients versus three-axis curve editors; a pigment mixing model is not automatically a coordinate space with three editable channels. Keep that semantic distinction rather than presenting every method as interchangeable “color space.”

Pointer adaptation here is selected once at module load. This works as a fixed branch but does not react to a later change in input device. Preview clearing occurs on mouse leave, selection and explicit close; the picker does not itself provide general blur/unmount preview cleanup. RFF should cover keyboard focus changes and editor teardown through the same preview owner. For both 2D palettes and environment-color bands, the benefit is reversible comparison and easier editing, with no asserted GPU speedup.

**Proposed checks:** cancel during progressive search; apply while hovering a different amount; change the source gradient mid-search; compare periodic seams and narrow color bands; preserve an existing retired mode on load/save; and move keyboard focus out of the blend picker. Validate reduced gradients against the target renderer, not just the small editor strip. No implementation or runtime validation is claimed.

## Color acquisition: name the sampled representation

**Evidence read in full:** [pagePick.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/pagePick.ts), [eyedropperActive.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/eyedropperActive.ts), and [colorDrag.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/colorDrag.ts).

For RFF, distinguish picking a displayed pixel from retrieving an authored palette stop or linear HDR material value. GMT's page fallback reads 2D canvas pixels, samples image/video source pixels through a scratch canvas, or reads a computed background color. It returns six-digit RGB without alpha. This is not a reconstruction of the final composited screen: partially transparent pixels are returned without blending, filters and overlays are not evaluated, and background-image gradients/text are not generally sampled. RFF should label each acquisition mode and use an explicit render readback for displayed fractal pixels, with documented tone-map/color-space stage. An HDR source needs a separate representation rather than conversion through a display hex string.

Coordinate mapping is a critical transferable detail. The canvas path scales client coordinates into backing-store pixels, which handles a stretched one-row gradient. The media path assumes the source fills its rectangle and does not account for object-fit, crop or object-position. That can misidentify source coordinates throughout a letterboxed or cropped image, not only at its edges. Likewise, rotated/skewed display transforms cannot generally be inverted with a bounding rectangle alone. RFF should map through the actual image-placement transform and reject points outside displayed content. Pixel sampling must use the same view/crop definition as the preview.

The fallback searches hit elements and their media descendants, taking later descendants first. This is a heuristic rather than a complete stacking-order calculation; it does not reproduce opacity, clipping and all paint-order rules. Any canvas already using a WebGL context returns no 2D context here, regardless of its preserveDrawingBuffer setting. Thus this path cannot directly pick GMT's WebGL rendering. Borrow the useful fallback concept, not a claim that it samples every visible pixel. Browser-support statements in source comments were not checked against current browser releases during this local audit.

The page picker cancels a prior instance before opening another and guards completion by owner identity, then removes its overlay/listener. This is a useful lifecycle model for RFF's temporary pick mode. The separate eyedropper-active signal is only a shared boolean, so overlapping async callers require ownership or reference counting; an older caller's cleanup must not clear a newer pick. Temporarily removing thumbnail dimming makes screen picking more faithful to the displayed source, but does not turn a tone-mapped preview into raw scene data. Ensure the presentation change has painted before beginning screen acquisition.

Color drag uses a dedicated payload type distinct from whole-gradient drag and validates a six-digit hex value at drop time. That gives RFF a clear operation distinction: recolor a target stop versus replace an entire palette. The module's in-flight preview is local state and must not be treated as the authoritative payload for a drag from another window/process. Validate the actual dropped value, use stable stop IDs, and commit one undoable edit. This transport covers opaque display RGB only; retaining alpha, color-space identity or HDR energy requires a versioned richer contract. Do not reuse it silently for those domains.

**Proposed checks:** pick from a letterboxed/cropped image, transparent gradient and tone-mapped HDR preview; compare displayed versus authored-color acquisition; cancel/restart a pick rapidly; drag a color between windows; and reject malformed drops without changing the palette. These mechanisms apply to 2D palette creation and relief environment-color authoring. No screen capture, external sampling, application code change or runtime validation occurred in this review.

## Gradient commands must preserve sampled and editable representations

**Evidence read in full:** [gradientActions.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/gradientActions.ts) and [rampMode.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/rampMode.ts).

GMT explicitly distinguishes a sampled ramp from a stop-based gradient. An output-mode edit on a ramp retains its texels even though its stop array is empty; inversion reverses texels rather than calling an empty-stop operation. This is a useful RFF contract for image-derived palettes: preserve the sampled result until the user explicitly requests an editable stop approximation. Do not silently convert a dense imported palette into a few stops, or interpret an empty stop list as missing color data when a valid sampled representation exists. The inspected representation is 256 opaque RGB texels; it is not a universal resolution or HDR/alpha format to impose on RFF.

One command builder supplies both dropdown and context-menu actions, reducing semantic drift between entry points. Mutation wrappers delegate a single undo bracket to the host, while opening the reduction popup does not itself modify content. RFF can share operation definitions for inversion, distribution, interpolation and source conversion, with stable target IDs and validation at execution time. Menu state is a snapshot: selected IDs can become stale before invocation. Here the interpolation submenu tests selection-set size, then indexes the first matching stop without first proving that any selected ID still resolves. Revalidate the target set before generating or executing such operations.

The affordance helper separates visible knots, insertion, marquee selection, direct knot edits and menu actions. These are not identical permissions: `knotsStale` suppresses drawn knots and insertion but does not suppress every knot-edit route, and the menu builder passes it as false. A host tool taking over the strip blocks several stop operations, while output mode, reset and some other commands have separate behavior. RFF should define a complete operation matrix for temporary previews and paint tools, then apply it consistently to mouse, keyboard, drag/drop and menus. Editing hidden authored stops beneath a different displayed result should be an explicit mode, not an accidental bypass.

Preview selection follows a declared priority: local stop preview, host preview ramp, displayed ramp configuration, then stops. This is a useful start, but a complete preview must carry its matching interpolation and color interpretation too. `BarSource` here carries stops or texels, with blend mode supplied separately to the painter; callers must keep them from different revisions from being paired. A reduced candidate that changes blend mode cannot be represented faithfully by changing stops alone. Scope preview ownership so cancellation restores the correct underlying source.

The strip painter samples stops at each output column after sorting once, while sampled ramps are enlarged with nearest-neighbor selection to preserve discrete texels. The full editor converts to a 256-texel representation. These are deliberate editor-display policies, not proof of equivalence to RFF's filtered GPU lookup or roughness-filtered environment reflections. Validate narrow bands, step transitions and wrap seams using the final shader path. The helper also assumes valid positive dimensions and nonempty ramp data; a one-column stop strip computes a coordinate using `width - 1`, so callers need an explicit degenerate-size policy.

Finally, `sameGradientBody` intentionally ignores color/blend spaces and compares stop properties in order (or ramp strings). Use such a helper only for body identity, never whole-appearance cache invalidation. Its missing interpolation defaults to linear, while the menu displays missing interpolation as smooth; resolve legacy defaults through the authoritative sampler before promising that a mode is unchanged. Output-mode labels such as “Linear (Physical)” or “Inverse ACES” are not evidence of a complete physical lighting model or full standard implementation. RFF should name exactly the implemented transformation and preserve existing palette recipe IDs/order.

**Proposed checks:** change output interpretation on a sampled ramp; reverse twice and compare bytes; fit stops only on explicit request; invalidate a selection while its menu is open; change blend mode without changing stops; and compare one-column, stepped and periodic previews to shader output. These apply to flat 2D palettes and relief environment bands. No application changes or runtime tests were made.

## Palette-library integration: identify the destination and confirm storage separately

**Evidence read in full:** [gradientEditorEntrance.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/gradientEditorEntrance.ts), [gradientFavients.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/gradientFavients.ts), and [GradientContextMenu.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/GradientContextMenu.tsx).

The editor exposes a host-supplied header extension with the current gradient, optional feature/parameter identity and a host identifier. This lets a shared editor open the appropriate library or detailed editor without depending directly on a particular application. RFF can use the same conceptual boundary for ordinary palette stops and environment-color gradients, while keeping their destinations distinct. Include document/layer identity and revision when work can outlive the editor; feature/parameter strings alone are insufficient for multiple documents or repeated layer editors. A standalone editor with no destination must require an explicit target selection before applying elsewhere.

The library bridge offers `add(config)` and `isFav(config)`; naming and deduplication belong to the host. This interface neither implements durable storage nor returns a persistence acknowledgement. In RFF, distinguish an asset present in the current library model from one successfully written to disk, and preserve the exact accepted gradient snapshot during asynchronous saves. A content signature must include interpolation and color interpretation when those affect appearance, not merely stop colors/positions. Preserve source attribution separately from visual deduplication: identical rendered gradients do not establish identical provenance or recipe identity. Keep RFF's frozen recipe IDs and generation order intact.

Header extensions use a keyed registry, whereas the library bridge is a single replaceable slot. These are integration choices rather than multi-window ownership guarantees. Registration replacement and later cleanup need owner-aware lifetimes so an old editor cannot remove a newer provider. The header render callback receives a live configuration; any delayed action should capture or resolve the intended revision explicitly instead of retaining mutable data by accident.

Menu selection closes the menu, then invokes the captured action on the next animation frame. This helps separate menu teardown from subsequent work but is not proof that the action ran, succeeded or remained valid after a document change. Revalidate the target at execution and route errors to the owning operation. Hover preview clearing is tied to leaving the list in this component; keyboard focus and unmount cleanup require a host policy so temporary previews do not remain active after dismissal.

Preview swatches are generated lazily when their elements approach visibility. That can avoid generating offscreen CSS gradients, but all menu rows still mount, and a swatch receives stops rather than a complete gradient configuration. Such thumbnails should be treated as identification aids unless the renderer is shown to match the selected blend/output interpretation. For RFF's material or environment library, use the shared gradient sampler for fidelity-critical comparison, with caching keyed by the full appearance definition. Lazy visibility alone is neither virtualization nor a shader optimization.

**Proposed checks:** open two editors targeting different layers; replace a provider while an old owner is closing; change documents before a deferred menu action runs; fail a library write; dismiss a hovered preview; and compare thumbnails for identical stops in different blend spaces. These apply equally to 2D palettes and relief environment authoring. No persistence test, screenshot or RFF implementation was performed.

## Shared feature rows do not supply layer transactions automatically

**Evidence read in full:** [DynamicList.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/DynamicList.tsx), [FeatureSection.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/FeatureSection.tsx), and [StoreCallbacksContext.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/contexts/StoreCallbacksContext.tsx).

The dynamic list is a presentational container with optional search input, selection, disclosure and add/remove callbacks. It does not implement reordering, filtering, stable item identity, undo or asset ownership. Consequently it provides no basis for recommending “add layer ordering” to RFF, which already has that functionality. Its transferable value is consistent controls around existing layers and modulation sources, with the host retaining the authoritative ordered data and transactions. A maximum scroll height does not virtualize rows; filtering and large-list performance remain host concerns.

Feature sections subscribe to their own feature slice and setter rather than the entire store. This can limit unrelated editor updates when many material sections exist, provided unchanged slices retain identity. It is not a GPU performance result. Enabled state, disclosure state and pipeline status remain separate: `forceBodyOpen` bypasses the enabled gate but does not bypass a collapsed section. RFF should ensure a pending/error action remains reachable even when its body is closed, without making disclosure itself enable an effect. The fallback toggle parameter comes from feature metadata; explicit binding is preferable when several independent controls share one shader feature.

The callback context supplies gesture begin/end and context-menu integration, but defaults silently to no-op functions when no provider is present. An embedded editor can therefore change values while losing expected undo bracketing. For RFF's proposed reusable palette/environment/mask controls, make the editing contract explicit at construction, or provide a deliberate standalone transaction owner. Verify one undo entry per completed gesture and full cancellation at every host mount, including popouts. Merely sharing a widget does not prove it shares history behavior. The context interface also has no cancellation operation, so cancellation must be implemented through a separate documented contract.

Removal/expansion controls stop click propagation in the list, while arbitrary header actions are supplied by the host. Define whether interacting with an action also selects its row, and use stable IDs so filtering or reordering cannot redirect a captured callback to another layer. Conditional disclosure unmounts children; keep pending edits and active-gesture cleanup outside that lifetime. Empty-state detection counts supplied React children rather than resolved visible records, so a filtered child that renders nothing may still suppress the empty message. RFF should derive counts and empty state from the same filtered model that supplies actual items.

**Proposed checks:** edit the same control in main and detached editors and undo once; collapse during editing; delete a row while another action is pending; filter/reorder while preserving the selected layer; and verify pending compile actions remain discoverable when collapsed. These are integration requirements for both flat 2D layers and relief materials, not newly demonstrated rendering features. No runtime checks or application modifications were performed.

## Floating editors: closing a view must have an explicit content policy

**Evidence read in full:** [DraggableWindow.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/DraggableWindow.tsx) and [DotToggle.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/DotToggle.tsx).

GMT's floating-window adapter distinguishes registry-managed panels from standalone windows, and delegates movement, resizing and stacking to a shared primitive. It gates managed visibility by panel state and a capability predicate. This supports reusable detached palette/material editors, but this wrapper alone does not establish work-area clamping, resize cancellation or multi-display behavior. Those belong to the delegated primitive and native host in an RFF implementation. Do not infer them merely from a draggable-window component name.

Closing certain GMT panels also disables their associated feature, unless a custom close callback takes precedence. For RFF, explicitly distinguish closing an editor from disabling an effect: closing an environment or mask editor should retain the authored appearance unless the control clearly represents a temporary tool session. Keep the last accepted shader state and terminate only the editor's subscriptions, previews and gestures. Capability-driven hiding also unmounts content, so pending candidates must live in an owner whose lifetime matches the document rather than the visible panel.

The ordinary window forwards Escape dismissal only when closing is allowed; the bare-chrome branch uses a different set of options and does not forward that property here. Define consistent close/cancel semantics across compact and full editors. Dock dragging stops header-drag propagation while preserving a compatibility mouse-up required by the current drop implementation. Borrow the principle of one gesture owner, not a web-specific event sequence: RFF should make dock movement, window movement and embedded color drags mutually exclusive and handle cancellation explicitly. The grip here has no local primary-button test, so eligibility must be established before starting a move rather than assumed from the downstream handler.

The compact toggle correctly exposes switch role and checked state, but delegates all changes to its caller and has no disabled/busy contract. A small colored dot should not itself imply that an asynchronous shader change has completed. For RFF, provide a clear accessible name, a usable hit area and capability/pending behavior appropriate to the operation; keep source enablement separate from panel visibility. These are integration conditions for 2D palette/image editors and relief materials, not additional shading effects.

**Proposed checks:** close an editor while its effect is active; hide it through a capability change with pending edits; reopen and verify authored values; cancel docking during a color drag; compare Escape behavior across editor forms; and restore windows after a monitor/work-area change. No runtime window-management test or RFF modification was performed.

## Typed mode selection and exception-safe interaction cleanup

**Evidence read in full:** [Dropdown.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/Dropdown.tsx), [GenericDropdown.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/GenericDropdown.tsx), and [GenericToggleSwitch.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/GenericToggleSwitch.tsx).

The dropdown adapter wraps a selection in interaction begin/end calls and resumes temporarily paused rendering afterward. This establishes how ordinary discrete parameter changes join history, but cleanup is sequential rather than protected by a finally block. A throwing change handler can skip both interaction completion and this resume call. RFF should release its own interaction/pause lease even when a material update fails, preserving independent reasons for rendering to remain paused. Do not infer that a pause improves the known native Win32 menu flash; these files provide no such evidence.

The generic dropdown serializes option values as strings and reconstructs the selected value using the type of the first option. Mixed numeric/string options can therefore change meaning, and values such as numeric 1 and string "1" collide in display lookup and element keys. RFF shader modes should use explicit stable typed identifiers, with a lookup from the selected option token back to the original value. Reject unavailable or unknown identifiers at the command boundary and preserve saved enum numbering. Native disabled options are forwarded by this implementation, but the adapter's public option type does not declare that field and the adapter exposes no whole-control disabled prop; make capability propagation explicit across every wrapper rather than relying on casts or surrounding pointer suppression.

The selected label is measured and its font shrunk to fit, using a resize observer. This is an editor presentation mechanism, not a rendering optimization. At the minimum font size text can still exceed the space, so retain a readable full-name route for long material/field names and translated labels. Font changes without an element resize are not explicitly observed here. Labels also need an actual control association; adjacent text alone does not establish an accessible name.

Toggle variants have different semantics in this source: the soft boolean is a native button with pressed state, segmented options are native disabled-aware buttons, while dense/default booleans use clickable containers without keyboard handling here. RFF should preserve equivalent keyboard, accessibility and enable/disable behavior across compact and full presentations. The generic fallback applies boolean negation even though its type permits strings and numbers; use separate boolean and enum contracts so a missing options array cannot silently convert a material mode into a boolean. Re-selecting an active option still invokes its callback, so command-level equality handling should prevent unnecessary work without suppressing meaningful precision-sensitive changes.

**Proposed checks:** numeric and string mode identifiers; empty/changed option lists; capability loss while the selector is open; a setter that fails; concurrent render-pause owners; keyboard use in every toggle presentation; and long translated labels. These support both flat 2D shader settings and relief materials. No runtime test or application modification was performed.

## Contextual commands: keep live shader feedback and failure handling explicit

**Evidence read in full:** [GlobalContextMenu.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/GlobalContextMenu.tsx), [ErrorNote.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/ErrorNote.tsx), and [GhostButton.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/GhostButton.tsx).

GMT's global context menu combines actions with help topics associated with the clicked control. This is useful for RFF's roughness, field masks and image filtering options: contextual help can explain the actual input field, units and effect without crowding the normal control. Topic order drives indentation here; it is not a validated semantic hierarchy. Use stable feature/parameter help identities and maintain explanations alongside the implemented behavior, including the distinction between 3D lighting and 2D relief approximations.
