The root menu acquires a render pause while submenus share that lifetime. Yet menu items may contain live sliders and keep-open actions. For RFF, decide whether such controls require live appearance feedback; pausing all rendering while a material slider is visible can defeat that purpose. Separate optional background work from rendering the accepted edit, and preserve explicit user pause intent. This is not evidence of a fix for the known native-menu first-paint flash.

Action execution differs from the gradient-specific menu inspected earlier: this menu calls the action before closing, whereas the other closes then defers execution. A synchronous exception prevents the close here, and an asynchronous action is not awaited before dismissal. Shared command definitions therefore do not alone establish shared completion/error semantics. Route operations through a common owner that validates the target revision, reports failure and releases transient resources independently of menu visibility. Slider items also bypass the ordinary button branch's disabled handling, so capability constraints must be enforced on every control type and at the command boundary.

Submenus retain a captured child-item list and anchor rectangle from hover. If source items change while open, the retained submenu is not automatically reconstructed by this code. RFF should invalidate stale commands when a layer is removed or its capabilities change, and offer keyboard navigation equivalent to pointer hover. Menu placement measures bounds on relevant prop changes but not directly on window resize; large content still needs a bounded work-area policy. These web-menu observations do not establish behavior of RFF's native menus.

The error-note and ghost-button components only consolidate visual styles. They supply neither validation, error announcement, recovery, confirmation nor successful completion. Do not count them as such functionality in the adoption plan. For a failed environment upload or shader replacement, retain the prior accepted image and give a concrete retryable operation state; a red container alone does not implement recovery.

**Proposed checks:** adjust a keep-open material slider and verify visible feedback; invalidate an open submenu's target; execute a failing synchronous/asynchronous command; navigate submenus by keyboard; and resize the window while the menu is open. These are integration criteria for 2D and relief editing, with no new shader effect, runtime test or application change claimed.

## Gradient editor follow-up: selection identity and preview interpretation

**Scope:** [AdvancedGradientEditor.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/AdvancedGradientEditor.tsx), lines 1–640 only, plus a full read of [pickerIcons.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/gradient/pickerIcons.tsx). The large editor remains pending full-file coverage; later gesture, reduction execution and rendering paths are not verified by this section.

The caller resolves one earlier integration question: its preview blend mode explicitly prefers the reduction candidate's blend space, then hover preview, host preview and the authored mode. Thus the helper's separate stop-data/blend inputs are paired intentionally in this inspected setup. This does not yet prove every later drawing/application path uses the resolved pair. The editor also declares its strip an authoring-color preview, with output-texture conversion separate. RFF should name that distinction rather than promise a strip matches the final tone-mapped material or HDR reflection.

Selection ownership is addressed through a bounded history of hashes of knot lists. This avoids retaining a selected generic stop ID such as s0 when switching to a different gradient that reused the ID. The implementation hashes fields into a 30-bit value and retains up to 4096 entries, so it is a heuristic for content lineage, not guaranteed document identity. RFF should use an explicit gradient/document identity and revision for selection restoration; content hashes may accelerate comparisons but should not be the sole proof that selections belong to the same asset. A repeated or colliding body and a legitimate old revision evicted from the cache need defined behavior.

The prop synchronization path skips the next incoming stop update when a local emit flag is set, without checking equality against the emitted payload in that branch. It records the incoming hash as the same lineage. For RFF, acknowledge a specific edit revision instead: a concurrent preset load or externally normalized result must not be mistaken for an echo and skipped. The default discrete edit wrapper also calls start, mutation and end sequentially without finally cleanup. Keep transaction completion reliable when a conversion or host callback throws.

A direct preview ramp avoids the fit-to-stops/resample round trip, an important principle for image-derived 2D palettes and painted environment bands. However, the inspected code marks knots stale by the presence of previewConfig (and reduction preview), not previewRamp alone. RFF should carry explicit correspondence metadata when stop positions are an approximate or held fit of a live ramp. Hide or clearly distinguish controls that no longer describe the displayed result; do not infer correspondence merely from which optional prop was supplied.

The icon file contains decorative SVGs and records an owner-designed source sheet, including a verbatim eyedropper path. It adds no shader mechanism. Do not copy these distinctive paths into RFF without establishing the source's actual reuse license and appropriate NOTICE attribution. Generic independently drawn symbols remain a separate option. The source comment supplies provenance information, not license permission.

Next inspection should resume at editor line 641, tracing progressive reduction execution, change emission and gesture cleanup before claiming the editor fully audited. No runtime behavior or rendering improvement is claimed here.

## Gradient editor completion: edit light bands without losing the accepted source

**Scope:** the remaining lines 641–1985 of [AdvancedGradientEditor.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/AdvancedGradientEditor.tsx), completing the previously recorded lines 1–640. The source hash matches the audit inventory. This section supersedes the preceding section's instruction to resume at line 641; it records source inspection, not an executed interaction test.

**Useful transfer to RFF:** allow a group of gradient stops to move together, stretch about either selected edge, and duplicate as a group. For an environment gradient this makes a colored reflection band easy to reposition or widen; for a flat 2D palette it adjusts an entire color motif. GMT computes movement and signed scaling from a snapshot captured at gesture start, avoiding repeated incremental transformations. Crossing the scaling pivot can reverse the selection. In RFF, retain this stable baseline and define coincident-stop ordering, endpoint clamping and reversal semantics explicitly. This is editing of shader inputs; it does not change the Mandelbrot recurrence or MPA.

The drawing path now resolves the earlier preview-pairing question: both the 256-sample full editor and the wider strip receive the resolved `barSource` and `previewBlend`. Strip gutter colors come from that same wider buffer. However, the canvas backing widths are fixed at 256 or 1536 and then stretched to the displayed width. The wider backing is not evidence of exact physical-pixel sampling at every window size or display scale. RFF should distinguish the authored continuous gradient, a finite sampled ramp, and the final filtered reflection/palette. A crisp authoring strip alone does not establish correct roughness filtering, texture minification, HDR intensity or final display conversion.

**Reduction and acceptance:** the editor pulls one reducer iterator step per timer task and cancels future pulls when the subject changes or the popup closes. It preserves the old search plan as pending when only the search option changes, but clears it for a changed gradient. This is useful progressive preview behavior. One iterator step may still contain substantial synchronous work; there is no time budget, iterator `return()` or exception handling in this scheduling block, and completion relies on the reducer's yielded state. RFF should attach a source revision and search settings to every candidate, bound work between yields, dispose interrupted work, and check that revision again at Apply. Applying a candidate here closes the popup and emits its stops and color spaces through one edit bracket; emission itself is not proof that the host or GPU accepted the resource.

**Gesture termination:** ordinary drags begin an edit and an interaction session. The same handler is registered for pointer release and pointer cancellation; it emits the current stops and can delete stops when the removal flag is active. Thus cancellation currently follows commit behavior, rather than restoring the initial snapshot. Listener removal occurs after emission and edit completion, so a throwing callback can bypass that cleanup. The duplicate-drag branches begin an edit but call the shared drag starter with its begin-session step skipped. These details motivate one explicit RFF gesture owner with symmetric begin/end, a documented cancel policy and unconditional cleanup on release, cancellation, asset replacement and editor closure. Do not transplant browser comments about release outside a window as proof of Win32 input behavior.

**Control eligibility:** pointer insertion and color drops use the centralized affordances, while imperative insertion/drop methods primarily check ramp mode. The global keyboard handler checks ramp mode, selection and INPUT targets, rather than the same complete affordance state. Selection brackets render under a separate selection/takeover condition. RFF should validate the currently editable source at the command boundary for pointer, keyboard and host commands alike; disabling one visible handle cannot enforce that invariant. Delayed clipboard paste also needs to revalidate its destination after the read completes, and validate imported color/blend mode values rather than relying on a type cast.

Inserting a stop samples the current segment color, inherits its interpolation and assigns midpoint bias. This gives a sensible initial color but is not a general proof of curve-preserving subdivision of a biased or smooth segment. If RFF offers an explicitly non-destructive insertion operation, preserve the segment function or state the approximation. Group channel adjustment and replacing every selected color with one color should remain distinct operations; the portalled inspector wires the former separately.

**Proposed verification:** move and reverse a multi-stop light band; insert into biased/smooth segments and compare the entire ramp; cancel while dragging away to delete; change the asset during reduction or clipboard access; close the editor mid-gesture; compare preview and accepted color interpretation; and check flat palettes and relief reflections at multiple output sizes. None of these runtime checks has been performed in this audit. The findings support the existing environment and palette proposals and do not change the provisional top-ten appearance ranking.

## Color authoring for palettes and reflection sources: preserve intent beyond the swatch

**Scope:** complete read of [EmbeddedColorPicker.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/EmbeddedColorPicker.tsx), 1479 lines, verified against the inventory hash. The imported color-conversion implementations are a separate coverage item; their correctness and reuse licenses are not established merely by reading this caller.

**Transferable mechanism:** offer distinct operations for choosing one replacement color and adjusting a channel across several selected colors. GMT forwards a requested channel delta to the host when `onChannelAdjust` is present; otherwise it edits the current color. Thus reducing red across a palette need not collapse every selected stop to one RGB value. RFF should make the reference value, per-stop clamping and hue-wrap behavior explicit and evaluate the whole gesture against a stable source. This is useful for related 2D palette bands and colored reflection bands alike. Matching the first selected color at a limit must not silently stop the remaining selected colors from changing; test that policy independently of the single-color slider.

The internal HSV state preserves hue when an RGB edit becomes achromatic, and preserves both hue and saturation at zero value. This retains editing intent through black rather than forcing subsequent edits to restart from an arbitrary hue. That hidden intent is local state here: external RGB changes are converted afresh, and only six-digit RGB hex is emitted. In RFF, define which editing context survives undo, asset switching and reopening. Do not claim that this RGB picker stores arbitrary-precision, wide-gamut or HDR color. Keep a defined color-space conversion and an independent intensity/exposure parameter for environment and emission sources; alpha is also an explicitly separate optional callback in this component.

**Compact controls have a representational limit.** The mini pad varies hue and HSL lightness at full HSL saturation. It includes white, pure hues and black, but cannot represent every partially saturated color at its marker location. Its marker derives lightness from arbitrary HSV input, so the underlying pad color need not match that input. RFF can use such a compact pad as a quick color generator, while retaining saturation access and avoiding claims that it is an exact projection of all colors. The full saturation/value field and hue strip remain distinct controls. Their canvas remounts trigger repaint through callback refs; the mini pad's drawing effect instead depends on layout/minified state. Preview correctness should be checked after every relevant remount, not inferred from retained color state.

**Harmony and temperature are authoring aids.** Harmony handles are retained as a set so activating a member need not immediately regenerate all the others; changing the active color can regenerate followers under the selected rule. Keep selection, editing the set and applying a color as distinct commands. The Kelvin/tint controls generate replacement hex colors from local temperature/tint state; those values are not inferred from an arbitrary current color. For RFF, label them as proposed replacements, preserve the authored color until explicitly applied, and retain the earlier report's requirement to verify the conversion formula's provenance. These controls do not implement spectral lighting or establish a physically measured color temperature.

**Interaction contract:** the picker tracks whether it opened a parameter transaction and attempts to close it on unmount. A boolean is useful local bookkeeping but is not a token proving ownership of a shared transaction. Discrete edits call begin, emit and end without unconditional exception cleanup. Pad gestures keep an active flag but do not store/check the owning pointer ID, and their cancellation/lost-capture paths share the normal end behavior. Their initial press selects an absolute color even when a precision modifier is held. RFF should specify cancellation, multi-pointer rejection and modifier transitions, then bracket accepted changes with one owned transaction. The before/after swatch is driven by slider callbacks, not all pad paths; do not advertise universal before/after or Escape restoration without checking each route.

The eyedropper waits two animation frames after requesting a sampling presentation, then applies an asynchronously returned RGB color. That delay is not acknowledgement that every rendering resource is ready. Revalidate the target asset and edit revision before accepting a late result, cancel obsolete requests, and distinguish screen/display sampling from scene-linear material values. Recent swatches similarly describe emitted colors rather than acknowledged GPU results; persistent entries are filtered only by string type on load in this file. Validate their syntax and treat recents as convenience history, not a source-of-truth palette archive.

**Proposed checks:** cross gray and black while retaining hue intent; adjust multiple colors near channel limits; return to a partially saturated color in the compact pad; switch assets during sampling; interrupt a gesture; remount the field without changing color; and compare authored color, stored RGB/intensity and final reflection output. These source-derived integration criteria support the existing shader proposals in both 2D and relief rendering. No new effect ranking, benchmark or runtime test is claimed.

## Color interpolation completion: optional hue paths above RFF's existing Oklab

**Scope:** full read of [colorUtils.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/colorUtils.ts), 993 lines, with inventory SHA256 verification; targeted comparison with RFF's [palette_sampling.glsl](../shdsrc/palette_sampling.glsl), `blend_palette`. Earlier partial temperature inspection is now superseded by this full-file coverage. Source comments citing performance measurements and test invariants are not measurements or universal proofs reproduced by this audit.

**Actual RFF baseline:** `blend_palette` already selects encoded RGB, linear RGB or rectangular Oklab interpolation between adjacent palette entries. Therefore “add Oklab” is not a new proposal. A distinct optional extension is a polar OkLCh hue path, with an explicit near-neutral policy and gamut mapping. GMT's persisted `oklab` key means its polar mode, while `oklab-rect` means rectangular Oklab; never transplant these names as RFF enum values or change the meaning of an existing saved mode. Preserve frozen recipe generation and existing output when the extension is off.

**Mechanism worth evaluating:** GMT converts encoded sRGB endpoints to linear RGB and then Oklab. Polar interpolation linearly mixes lightness and chroma and follows the shorter angular hue arc. Near neutral endpoints, it blends the rectangular a/b result into the polar result using a smoothstep weight based on the smaller endpoint chroma divided by 0.02. This prevents an arbitrarily weak endpoint hue from receiving full influence. The threshold is an artistic policy in this coordinate system, not a universal perceptual tolerance. Antipodal hue ties, gray endpoints, near-zero chroma and out-of-range inputs need explicit behavior. The interpolation is not simply a standard polar blend once that fade is applied.

For out-of-gamut Oklab results, GMT tests the unclamped linear RGB channels and performs 24 bisection steps reducing chroma at fixed lightness and hue. The gamut predicate admits a small tolerance, followed by clamping in conversion. This is more deliberate than independent channel clipping, but finite iterations, tolerance, quantization and neutral inputs limit literal hue-preservation claims. RFF could evaluate this as an optional color-authoring/baking path first; do not automatically put a 24-step search in every shaded fragment. If a sampled lookup is used, verify that its resolution retains sharp palette features and that subsequent interpolation preserves the intended mode. CPU preview, fragment rendering and compute export must share the same semantics.

**Other modes have different contracts.** GMT's CIE LCh path uses D65 Lab conversions and a differently scaled neutral fade, but its inverse RGB helper clamps channels despite an “unclamped” comment; it does not share the Oklab chroma-reduction routine. The HSV far path has asymmetric conditional boundary behavior at exactly opposite hues, so specify a deterministic tie rule rather than copy branches blindly. Spectral mixing delegates to `spectral.js`, builds cached endpoint objects from rounded RGB hex and converts the mix back through a hex string. That is an optional pigment-like palette generator, not spectral light transport or an HDR mixing path. Its cache has no practical eviction limit in this module, unlike the capped hex parser. Verify dependency version/license and bound storage before any adaptation; the MIT attribution in a comment alone is not a completed license audit.

**Sampling and output are separate stages.** The canonical stop sampler sorts once per ramp, applies a power-law midpoint bias, optionally applies smoothstep (both `smooth` and `cubic` select that same easing), blends colors, then applies the output transform. Sharing this sampler with insertion and preview is valuable, but a sorted stop list still requires defined duplicate-position and step-boundary rules. A left-inclusive search can retain the previous segment's step color at an internal boundary. The CSS preview additionally decimates dense stop lists and does not apply smooth easing on its ordinary RGB branch. It is therefore an approximation, not a universal visual reference; evenly selecting stops can miss a narrow band.

The inverse-ACES-labelled helper is a particular scalar inverse curve with a hard branch at input 0.99, not a full inverse color-management pipeline. Its lower branch can produce channel values above 255, while texture output is assigned to `Uint8Array`; that conversion truncates and wraps finite out-of-range integers rather than preserving HDR or saturating them. RFF should retain its explicit scene-linear/HDR pipeline, select storage that represents the intended range and test the transfer boundary. Do not adopt this helper as a generic solution for matching authored colors through tone mapping. Empty/malformed inputs also have different grayscale versus transparent fallbacks across GMT readers, so give RFF one documented accepted-data contract.

Kelvin conversion is the named piecewise log/power approximation already discussed; tint is an encoded-RGB channel scaling with clipping, not a chromatic-adaptation transform. Channel nudging clamps each RGB/S/V component and wraps hue, but repeated hex output quantizes the operation and cannot preserve hidden hue at zero saturation. Retain high-precision editing state until the explicit storage boundary if that is required. Harmony families also need stable count semantics: GMT's analogous handle generator adds the base to an even-sized offset set, yielding one more handle than the requested even count. Transfer the ability to author related colors, not an assumption that every helper's UI label precisely states its result.

**RFF applicability:** optional polar interpolation and deliberate gamut handling can affect the entire flat 2D palette, as well as environment gradients, emission sources and masks derived from color. They are additional candidates for comparison against existing controls, not evidence that the earlier top-ten ranking has been experimentally superseded. Validate neutral sweeps, complementary colors, narrow steps, duplicate positions, gamut edges, all output paths and save/reopen stability. Reuse RFF's existing attributed conversion code where suitable; record verified provenance in NOTICE before adding distinctive formulas. No source implementation, runtime benchmark or visual comparison was performed here.

## Histogram controls completion: valid intervals and accepted readbacks

**Scope:** full reads of [Histogram.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/Histogram.tsx) (454 lines), [HistogramProbe.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/HistogramProbe.tsx) (49 lines) and [histogramUtils.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/histogramUtils.ts) (144 lines), each matching its inventory hash. The probe here is the shared `components/` implementation, distinct from the previously cited `engine-gmt/components/` path. Section B remains the primary RFF adoption proposal; this completion adds boundary and lifecycle requirements rather than another histogram feature.

**Useful editing mechanism:** the selected interval can be translated as a whole while retaining its width, or adjusted at either endpoint. A gamma handle marks the input position mapping to output 0.5: `p = pow(0.5, 1/gamma)`, inverted during dragging with `gamma = log(0.5)/log(p)`. Together with the palette overlay, this makes range and midtone edits concrete. RFF should use the corresponding formula only for a matching power-law mapping; other coloring curves need their own inverse or a separately defined control. This applies directly to flat 2D palette fitting and to fields driving relief roughness, masks or emission.

**New boundary findings:** the helper reads every fourth float, uses a numerical validity cutoff, and places values into 128 bins with `floor(normalized * 128)`. With fixed bounds, a value exactly at the upper bound produces index 128 and is discarded. Specify whether RFF includes the upper endpoint, and represent overflow separately if clipping is intentional. Reject nonfinite samples explicitly and validate finite ordered bounds; a numeric background comparison is not a general field-validity test. Constant data are given an arbitrary widened range in this helper, which should become a declared policy appropriate to the selected RFF field's units.

The smart-range routine ignores the first and last bins, derives a cumulative distribution from logarithmic display heights, expands toward neighboring nonempty bins and adds padding. As already noted in section B, this is a visual heuristic, not raw-count percentiles. Additionally, it maps both selected indices to bin starts. If both cuts land in one isolated bin, start and end can coincide and the proportional padding remains zero. A RFF fit should use documented bin-edge semantics and enforce a meaningful positive interval even for a single occupied bin. Avoid a fixed 0.001 minimum for every field: preserve precision and define scale-aware bounds without collapsing nearby deep-iteration values through float conversion.

**Enforce one accepted range contract:** mouse endpoint drags repair ordering locally, but numeric endpoint callbacks emit values directly and the Fit result is also passed straight through. Validate the entire range at the common command boundary. Gamma dragging additionally divides by a pixel width derived from the interval; guard zero, tiny and nonfinite dimensions before the logarithm. Snapshot the analysis revision used for a gesture so a new distribution cannot silently reinterpret its coordinate scale. Finish or cancel the owned transaction on editor closure and input interruption; the inspected mouse listeners are removed on release, with no component-unmount cleanup in this file.

**Readback acceptance:** the shared probe checks manual triggers and every 60 animation callbacks in automatic mode. Callback identity changes restart its local counter, source changes alone do not force a manual read, and cleanup cancels the animation callback but not an in-flight promise. There is no rejection handler or generation check in this component. Therefore a loading boolean cannot prove which source is current, and a late response can outlive its request context. Use an explicit field/view revision, one bounded outstanding request, error/finally handling and a stale-result rejection rule in RFF. Display data age independently of whether automatic updating is enabled; here the stale badge is suppressed in automatic mode.

The overlay uses the approximate CSS gradient helper and separate repeat/phase transforms, so it is an explanatory view rather than a proof of final shader equivalence. RFF should validate the overlay against its actual mapping, especially nonlinear curves, phase wrapping and frozen animation. Proposed cases now include exact upper-bound values, one occupied bin, all-invalid/nonfinite data, numeric endpoint crossing, source changes during readback, rejected readback and closing a panel mid-drag. No runtime tests or RFF implementation are claimed.

## Shader editing and precision controls: connect text and values to an accepted revision

**Scope:** full reads of [GlslEditor.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/inputs/GlslEditor.tsx), [usePrecisionTrackDrag.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/inputs/usePrecisionTrackDrag.ts), [numberDragRate.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/inputs/numberDragRate.ts) and [HueControl.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/HueControl.tsx), with inventory hash verification. A targeted caller search locates the editor in FormulaWorkshop; it does not establish any additional formula or compiler capability.

**Transfer to RFF:** an optional shader-expression editor can highlight detected constants/variables and let a user promote a selected occurrence to an adjustable parameter. GMT's editor supplies offset ranges, stable callback IDs and click handling for this purpose. It maps decorations through text changes and accepts replacement decorations from its caller. This is a useful bridge from code to ordinary material controls, but mapped character positions do not prove that the same semantic expression still exists. Associate detector results with the exact document revision, resolve the selected occurrence again before rewriting, and preserve the user's source/undo history. The control uses C++ highlighting; it is not a GLSL validator, compiler diagnostic mapper or proof that an expression is legal for RFF's Vulkan shader stage.

Keep draft text, a successfully compiled candidate and the currently displayed pipeline separate. Every editor change is forwarded here; compilation policy and acceptance belong to its host. Retain the last working display on failure and report diagnostics against the matching source revision. If an arbitrary expression can introduce descriptors, push constants or stage-specific operations, constrain or validate that interface explicitly. These authoring ideas apply to 2D coloring/masks and relief materials; they do not authorize replacing precision-sensitive perturbation or MPA computations with arbitrary float formulas.

The editor instance is rebuilt when read-only status or height changes, recreating document state. Its highlight synchronization effect depends only on the highlights reference, so rebuilding the editor with an unchanged reference does not itself reinstall those decorations. External document replacement is suppressed from onChange using a temporary flag without finally cleanup, and no explicit external-change undo policy is provided in the dispatch. RFF should preserve selection, undo and diagnostic state through layout changes and distinguish document replacement from typing. Keyboard propagation is stopped at the wrapper's bubble handlers; global capture handlers and other input routes still need an explicit text-editing context. A placeholder data attribute is set, but this file does not install a placeholder extension; do not treat the prop name as proof of visible guidance.

**Consistent fine adjustment:** GMT's track helper converts between the displayed coordinate and the parameter value, applies coarse/fine multipliers, and re-anchors when modifiers change. Its number-drag helper derives a rate from the displayed span and actual track width, bounded to a slower range than the track. This gives RFF a useful policy for roughness, reflection intensity, palette phase and nonlinear controls: match sensitivity to the visible domain instead of blindly multiplying a raw parameter step. Keep numerical precision separate from interaction sensitivity; a slower cursor does not justify reducing stored precision.

Before adopting that policy, specify whether step quantization is in display units or stored units. The track helper quantizes displayed coordinates before inverse mapping, and the number-rate helper receives a raw step that is only constrained into the chosen display-rate band. They are not universally equivalent under nonlinear mappings. Validate finite ordered bounds, positive widths, valid mapping outputs and hard limits. The track state retains an unclamped anchor, so dragging beyond an endpoint and reversing can require consuming the overshoot; decide whether this is intended. Modifier changes use the old rate for movement since the last anchor, then install the new rate. Test this at clamps and across resizing rather than claiming unconditional continuity.

Pointer capture is requested, but the helper does not retain an owning pointer ID, and marks the gesture active only after invoking the start/change callbacks. Release, cancellation and lost capture are supplied by callers; this hook has no own unmount cleanup. Pair one owned transaction with each gesture, make callback failures release it, and prevent another pointer or asset change from redirecting an active edit. The immediate visual callback should display the accepted or explicitly pending value, not imply shader acceptance merely because the thumb moved.

Finally, HueControl changes interface accent/surface colors through the theme store. These are editor preferences, not palette or lighting parameters. Keep them out of rendered-image state and avoid counting theme recoloring as a shader improvement. These four files add authoring and integration mechanisms; no runtime tests, compiler validation or new rendering-speed result is claimed.

## Range selection: paired material bounds need one validity and animation contract

**Scope:** full reads of [QualityRangePad.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/QualityRangePad.tsx) and [QualityRangePadConnected.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/palette/components/QualityRangePadConnected.tsx), with inventory hash verification, plus a targeted recheck of the already-read RangePairPad adapter in AutoFeaturePanel. Despite its name, this control selects palette-quality/filter or parameter intervals; it does not govern render sampling quality or speed.

**RFF application:** a shared interval control could adjust the selected band of a material mask, palette field or emission source. A horizontal body drag moves its center; vertical motion widens or narrows the interval; grabbing the nearer endpoint adjusts that bound. The source normalizes the domain for interaction and emits domain values for storage. This separates physical field units from pointer sensitivity and lets the same editor serve 2D color ranges and relief material masks. The painted backgrounds are illustrative color/stripe ramps unless a caller supplies actual distribution data; do not label them measured histograms.

**Define the final stored invariant.** GMT applies minimum separation in normalized coordinates before rounding each endpoint to the requested domain step. Coarse quantization can collapse that separation again. Validate ordering and minimum width after quantization, and define the quantization origin for domains not starting at zero. Reject reversed/nonfinite domains; `max - min || 1` is a fallback, not adequate domain validation. The body movement clamps its endpoints independently near the domain edge, which shrinks the visible interval instead of translating a constant-width window intact. RFF should deliberately choose between clipping and width-preserving translation so an apparent move does not unintentionally change mask coverage.

The track always clamps into its visible domain, while soft-range numeric fields may exceed it. Thus returning from a typed off-track interval to a track gesture can substantially alter the authored range. Show off-track bounds explicitly or expand the view without silently rewriting them. Starting an edge drag uses the press position as its target baseline rather than preserving the offset to the original endpoint; a near-edge press followed by movement can snap the endpoint to the cursor. The Alt modifier scales the entire displacement from the original press by 0.25 and does not re-anchor when toggled, unlike the shared precision-track helper inspected earlier. A common RFF range gesture should specify these behaviors and use the same fine-adjust policy as adjacent controls.

**Pair updates and keyframes.** The palette adapter writes both bounds as one vec2-shaped value, but the scalar-pair adapter invokes two change callbacks sequentially. A single visual control does not ensure atomic range acceptance. Publish one validated pair to the renderer and history so no consumer observes an intermediate inverted interval. Likewise, the keyframe diamond calls separate endpoint actions; its combined status is presentation rather than proof of an atomic animation edit. Validate animated intervals between keys, not only at the keyed frames, especially when endpoints use different tangents or interpolation modes.

The palette adapter creates animation bindings even when the keyframe button is hidden and does not forward drag-start/end callbacks to the pure range pad. The scalar adapter does forward transaction/session callbacks and auto-key operations. Do not assume these routes have identical undo or recording semantics merely because they share the same visual component. RFF should explicitly connect each host to one transaction owner, including numeric edits, track drags and keyframe commands. Pointer state here contains no pointer ID, and the track wires release/cancel but not lost capture or an unmount cleanup; interruption must not leave a range transaction open.

Finally, the helper background painters assume dimensions greater than one when dividing by width/height minus one, although their current backing store is fixed at 200 by 44. Keep that precondition explicit if generalized. A chroma-track comment calls its endpoint teal-like while its actual endpoint is a reddish RGB color; transfer the intended field meaning rather than unverified labels. These are source-derived requirements supporting existing mask/palette proposals. No RFF code, render-quality policy or runtime test was changed.

## Numeric editing completion: preserve the value before improving the feel

**Scope:** complete reads of [useEditMode.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/inputs/hooks/useEditMode.ts), [useDragValue.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/inputs/hooks/useDragValue.ts), [screenEdgeFold.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/inputs/screenEdgeFold.ts) and [DraggableNumber.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/inputs/primitives/DraggableNumber.tsx), verified against inventory hashes.

**RFF transfer:** combine direct numeric entry with relative dragging, preserving display-unit mappings and applying hard limits in stored units after inverse mapping. GMT also keeps an immediate drag value for updating text without waiting for a component render. This can make roughness, environment rotation and palette-phase adjustment easier, but instant text is feedback about a proposed value, not confirmation that a shader resource or displayed frame accepted it. Reconcile that text with the authoritative value if validation rejects or normalizes an edit.

The most important precision requirement appears in the text path: starting an edit formats the number to six decimal places, then a blur commits that draft even if the user changed nothing. In RFF, entering and leaving a field must preserve the original value exactly when the text is untouched. Keep full round-trip precision in the editing buffer, independently of a compact idle display. Deep coordinates require the existing high-precision representation, not conversion through a JavaScript-style double or fixed six-decimal text. The helper's comment describes mapped text as the default, but its actual default is raw text; explicitly label the unit being edited.

Text and drag paths do not enforce the same constraints locally. The primitive passes hard limits to the drag hook, but not to the text hook. The latter accepts parseFloat prefixes and rejects NaN without requiring finiteness; it also does not recheck disabled state when committing. Establish one RFF parser/validator for typed, dragged, pasted and programmatic values, with full-token parsing, domain checks and a target revision. Do not confuse rejection of a malformed shader parameter with permission to lower fractal precision. Keep Enter, blur and Escape as an idempotent commit/cancel state machine, and close transactions even when callbacks fail.

**Dragging at the edge:** GMT proposes using vertical movement when a horizontal cursor becomes pinned, and horizontal movement when a vertical drag becomes pinned. The actual detector compares client coordinates with viewport bounds and accepts a primary-axis movement below 0.5 pixels near either edge. This is a heuristic, not authoritative physical-monitor detection; a nearly stationary primary coordinate near a window boundary can satisfy it too. For a Win32 RFF adaptation, validate windowed and multi-monitor behavior, mixed display scaling and the direction handoff. Do not inherit the source comment's general claim about pointer-lock permission prompts as a platform fact.

The drag hook correctly converts displayed values back to stored values before applying hard limits. It retains an accumulated movement baseline through modifier changes and quantizes displayed values only when a neighboring track width exists. However, it can retain overshoot beyond a clamped endpoint, checks NaN rather than all nonfinite outputs, and does not freeze every mapping/sensitivity input for the gesture. Define behavior if the range, selected asset or mapping changes mid-drag. Its pointer ID is stored but not used as an equality guard, and a second press is not explicitly rejected. The primitive wires pointer-up only, with no pointer-cancel/lost-capture handlers or unmount cleanup in these files; pointer-up also returns early when disabled. A RFF control needs a single gesture owner with unconditional release when interrupted or disabled.

**Proposed checks:** focus/blur an unchanged tiny value; type a nonfinite or partially valid token; enforce the same bound through typing and dragging; toggle modifiers at a clamp; disable or close the control mid-drag; switch targets before committing text; and traverse window/monitor edges. These support the same shader authoring improvements for flat 2D and relief, without introducing a new visual effect or a claimed speedup. No runtime tests were performed.

## Parameter mappings: choose units and zero behavior explicitly

**Scope:** full reads of [FormatUtils.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/inputs/primitives/FormatUtils.ts), the input types, drag-feel and skin providers, and the three input/hook/primitive export modules. All seven files match their inventory hashes. The exports and type declarations establish available interfaces, not proof that every caller honors them.

**Useful RFF transfer:** use a logarithmic or power-mapped slider to give useful travel to small roughness, intensity or pattern-scale values, while preserving the underlying parameter and its units. GMT normalizes these display domains to 0–100 and separately specifies their endpoints. It offers a pure log mapping, a log mapping with a reserved zero region, and a log(1+x)-style mapping that reaches zero continuously. These are alternative interaction policies, not interchangeable mathematical representations. Prefer an explicit parameter capability such as “zero disables this effect” to GMT's heuristic that a minimum of 0.1 or less implies zero should be available. A small positive minimum may be a real constraint.

The reserved-zero mapping snaps the lower half of its five-unit display band to zero; just above that threshold its inverse can return a positive value below safeMin. The forward map clamps such positive values up to safeMin, so those mappings are not mutual inverses throughout the band. This may be acceptable as a deliberate snap policy, but must not be described as a lossless coordinate transform. RFF should preserve authored off-track values, validate hard limits separately and test the zero/positive transition. Domain validation is also necessary for max <= 0 in log mappings, max = 0 in log1p, equal/reversed endpoints, invalid exponents and nonfinite inputs. The helpers' fallback denominators do not establish validity for all of those cases.

**Angle parsing needs a unit contract.** The degree mapping's parser returns displayed degrees, which the edit hook then converts to stored radians. In contrast, piMapping parses explicit pi notation into radians, while its fromDisplay multiplies by pi. Feeding that parser through the inspected mapped-text hook would convert twice; with mapped text disabled the hook bypasses the specialized parser altogether. This is a contract mismatch for that combination, not proof that every current angle control exercises it. The separate piUnitMapping correctly expresses a plain count of pi for that hook. Define parser output units in RFF's interface, accept a complete documented grammar, and apply conversion exactly once. The pi parser's `parseFloat(...) || 1` also substitutes one for zero fraction terms, so malformed/zero-denominator inputs cannot be accepted by copying it verbatim.

**Formatting is not storage.** The general formatter returns zero below 1e-9 and rounds to eight decimal places; values slightly above that cutoff can still round to zero. The timeline formatter uses exponential notation outside its chosen range, which is more informative for tiny nonzero parameters, but its `toExponential(2)` yields three significant digits despite the comment saying two. RFF should display tiny values without implying an effect is exactly off, and keep a round-trip edit buffer separate from either compact display. Approximate pi fraction labels should likewise never replace the underlying angle on an untouched edit.

The drag-feel provider separates sensitivity preferences from visual skin, a useful design for RFF's compact and expanded controls. It merges optional overrides without validating finiteness or ordering; normalize that policy at the preference boundary. The types describe soft bounds, hard bounds and live values, but enforcement must remain in the actual command path. These improvements apply to flat 2D image transforms, palette phase and masks as well as relief lighting. They do not change shader math or justify reducing fractal precision. Proposed checks cover typed/displayed unit round trips, zero snaps, tiny nonzero values and identical stored outcomes across visual skins; no runtime tests were performed.

## Scalar and vector controls: distinguish working composition from declared capabilities

**Scope:** complete reads of [ScalarInput.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/inputs/ScalarInput.tsx) and [VectorInput.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/inputs/VectorInput.tsx), matching inventory hashes. A targeted import search finds this VectorInput in mesh-export FormulaParams and BoundsPanel. This finding concerns that implementation; it must not be generalized to GMT's separate vector-input components or all application panels.

**Potential RFF transfer:** display authored and animated/evaluated values separately on the same parameter track, and provide component-wise numeric control for image transforms or light direction. ScalarInput has separate value/live/default indicators and can replace a generic progress background with a meaningful color ramp. These are useful authoring aids for both flat 2D and relief. The host must define what the live value represents and which frame/revision produced it; a pulsing dot or colored marker is not evidence that the displayed GPU image has caught up.

This VectorInput's local DualAxisPad is explicitly a placeholder: it renders a hover target and directional tooltip but does not consume its update or drag callbacks. Likewise, the declared animation track keys, interaction mode and rotation-gizmo option are not connected to those capabilities in this file. Do not cite this component as a working two-axis gesture, keyframe transaction or rotation gizmo to transplant. The useful design idea remains paired-axis manipulation, but any RFF implementation needs an actual validated gesture path and tests of the resulting vector, not merely matching appearance.

Per-axis mapping also requires care. The generic mapping helper ignores its axis argument and falls back to shared, X or Y mapping; later per-axis prop spreads can override it. Those spreads can also override disabled state and drag callbacks. Establish a clear precedence table in RFF and keep mandatory lifecycle/validation rules outside cosmetic overrides. A rotation display mode is initialized locally from the prop without later synchronization, so mode changes need an explicit owner rather than competing local and external states. Rotation units must follow the parser contract discussed above.

The vector component suppresses incoming value synchronization while dragging. Ending the drag changes only a ref, so an external value skipped during the gesture is not automatically replayed unless the synchronization dependencies change again. RFF should either freeze the asset revision intentionally or reconcile the newest accepted vector when the gesture ends. Build a whole-vector edit from a stable snapshot while preserving unrelated components; publish it as one accepted update. Local state and a drag snapshot alone do not provide host undo or animation recording.

**Scalar route differences:** compact/minimal numbers omit the soft-domain and drag-feel inputs passed by the full variant, so changing presentation can also change sensitivity and quantization behavior. The soft variant derives decimal precision from the textual form of step, capped at three places; scientific notation such as `1e-6` contains no decimal point and therefore selects zero decimal places. That is inadequate evidence of a useful readout for small parameters. Preserve parameter-aware formatting independent of skin, including tiny nonzero values and mapped units. A fixed override string can also remain unchanged during direct drag updates; validate that the user can see the actual proposed value.

Reset sends the default straight through the common callback bracket without local hard-limit validation. The soft reset tick first permits the track press, then may issue a separate reset on click; the default skin's reset button prevents the track press. Define one logical undo action across these routes, with final validation and exception-safe cleanup. Hiding the numeric field or rendering a full control without a label can remove the typing route, so ensure precise keyboard entry remains reachable where required. These observations refine RFF's input design; they add no shader algorithm and do not change the current appearance ranking. No runtime tests were performed.

## Animated shader controls: display status must not decide whether a change is saved

**Scope:** complete reads of [Slider.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/Slider.tsx), [KeyframeButton.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/KeyframeButton.tsx) and [useTrackAnimation.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/hooks/useTrackAnimation.ts), all matching inventory hashes. These finish the inspected connection between scalar input gestures and timeline actions; no animation was executed.

**Useful RFF transfer:** put a parameter's keyframe state beside the control, distinguish a matching key from an edited value and from interpolation between keys, and expose explicit Set/Update, Delete Key and Delete Track actions. That helps animate environment rotation, material roughness, emission strength or flat 2D palette/image transforms. A single click can be a convenient shortcut, but the underlying commands must remain explicit and independently accessible. GMT's diamond is removed from the tab order, so equivalent keyboard access needs deliberate design in RFF rather than assuming a visible button provides it.

**Precision-sensitive finding:** the hook identifies a nearby key within 0.1 frame, treats an absolute value difference no greater than 0.0001 as keyed, and uses 0.001 to classify differences from an interpolated value. `setKey` then returns early when that presentation status is keyed. Consequently a small but intentional change can be omitted from an explicit save; the button can also choose deletion when status says the key exactly matches. RFF should separate a visually tolerant status indicator from exact/parameter-aware mutation decisions. Preserve meaningful small values and use declared frame identity, angle wrapping and parameter units. A fixed tolerance cannot cover both tiny scales and large iteration-related values, and none of this permits reducing the precision of the fractal calculation.

**One gesture, one owner:** the connected slider begins parameter history, begins an interaction session, snapshots recording state and then invokes optional host callbacks. Updates change the parameter and add auto-keys separately. End reverses only part of that sequence before invoking the host. Callback failures and nested host transactions therefore need explicit ownership and unconditional cleanup. The previously inspected color picker supplies its own transaction callbacks to this connected slider, illustrating why sharing a visual primitive does not prove one history entry. In RFF, compose these layers under one edit transaction that records the accepted parameter and matching keyframe together, or clearly separate histories with a coherent restore policy.

Reset also has multiple paths. ScalarInput already brackets a reset, calls its onChange, then invokes onReset; Slider passes an onReset callback that brackets and writes the default again. This source chain can therefore issue repeated updates/auto-key work for one reset. Route tick, context-menu and keyboard resets through one canonical command, revalidate the current default and bounds, and snapshot before the first mutation. Do not treat an absence of visible change as proof that no redundant history or keyframe actions occurred.

The animation hook captures sequence, frame and recording state from the current render. It publishes per-track actions, while paired controls inspected earlier call them sequentially. RFF should decide whether a drag records at its start frame or follows the playback clock, and resolve the current target revision at the mutation boundary. A menu opened at one frame must not silently operate on an unintended later or stale frame. Grouped keys should share one snapshot and commit rather than depend on two independent action sequences.

The hook uses narrower store selectors than a full-store subscription, but still subscribes to sequence/frame/recording values even without a track ID. Its historical rerender measurements in comments are not reproduced here and do not prove zero cost for inactive controls. Optimize such subscriptions only after measuring RFF's actual update path; this is authoring responsiveness, not a shader arithmetic speedup. Proposed checks cover sub-threshold value edits, reset while recording, paired keys, playback during dragging, menu/frame changes and undo across parameter plus timeline state. The mechanisms apply equally to 2D and relief appearance animation.

## Compact parameter controls and picking: retain one command contract

**Scope:** full reads of [Knob.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/Knob.tsx), [Stepper.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/Stepper.tsx), [NumberInput.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/NumberInput.tsx) and [InteractionPicker.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/InteractionPicker.tsx), with inventory hash verification.

**RFF relevance:** a compact knob with direct numeric entry can place phase, rotation or material intensity controls close together. GMT's knob is a vertical relative drag represented by a 270-degree arc, not an angular pointer gesture or cyclic-value control. An unconstrained value merely pins the displayed arc at its limit. For RFF, explicitly distinguish a bounded amount from a cyclic angle and from an unbounded phase; preserve the stored value and show turn count or an out-of-range indication where useful. The same controls can author flat 2D patterns and relief lighting, without introducing a shader effect themselves.

The knob's precision modifiers differ from the shared slider: Shift multiplies by five and Alt by one tenth. They scale displacement from the original press without re-anchoring, so toggling modifiers can change the proposed value at the same cursor position. Clamping precedes step rounding, allowing a rounded value beyond a non-step-aligned bound. Its numeric entry receives soft min/max, not hard limits, through RawDraggableNumber. RFF should route all representations through one validated command, enforce bounds after quantization and use consistent modifier semantics. Validate nonzero finite ranges and sensible sizes before dividing or constructing arc geometry.

The knob captures the event target, which may be an SVG child, and releases the event target without an ownership check or exception cleanup. No pointer-button filter, pointer-ID guard, cancellation/lost-capture handler or unmount cleanup appears in this component. It opens host history before capture and closes history before release, so failure handling must not strand either resource. Reuse an owned gesture mechanism rather than treating this separate widget as automatically equivalent to the shared scalar input.

**Small counts need a draft, too.** Stepper deliberately leaves bounds to the caller, but its `parseInt(text, 10) || min` also treats a successfully parsed zero as the fallback when min is nonzero. It accepts numeric prefixes and emits on every text change. For sample counts, pattern sectors or dimensions in RFF, keep temporary text separate from accepted integer values, require full-token parsing, validate range and capacity, and define when one typed edit becomes one undo action. The minus/plus buttons are excluded from normal tab navigation; provide equivalent keyboard adjustment deliberately. NumberInput adds labeling and a value override to the connected numeric control, but does not convert its soft min/max into enforced limits. A wrapper name such as Width or Rows does not ensure a valid allocation size.

**Picking is a mode request, not a completed selection.** InteractionPicker toggles a global interactionMode and displays help plus a Cancel label. It does not itself acquire a point, validate a selected object, restore a previous mode, or guarantee resource cleanup on dismissal. For a RFF light-direction, color or mask-source picker, associate the mode with its target/revision, provide explicit acceptance/cancellation, and prevent the navigation gesture from also consuming the selection. Switching to a different picker should have a defined replacement policy. These integration findings extend the existing authoring recommendations; no new appearance ranking or runtime test is claimed.

## Graph display: cache stable geometry while keeping edits and time aligned

**Scope:** full reads of GraphCanvas.tsx and GraphToolbar.tsx in `components/graph/`, plus GraphUtils.ts, GraphRenderer.ts, GraphRendererCache.ts and toolColumn.ts in `utils/`, all under the audited GMT root and all matching inventory hashes. Curve construction and the underlying generic canvas cache remain separate coverage items; this section does not prove interpolation agreement with playback.

**RFF transfer:** draw mostly static curves/grid separately from the moving playhead and selection marquee. GMT uses two stacked canvases and separate redraw dependencies, so a frame change alone need not rebuild the back layer. It also groups selected key IDs by track and builds per-track lookup maps instead of repeatedly searching all keys. These mechanisms can improve responsiveness of a RFF palette, emission or light-animation editor without changing shader output or reducing precision. Historical timing and cache-hit numbers in comments are not reproduced measurements.

**Cache contract:** GraphRenderer's polyline lookup passes track ID, keyframe-array identity and a view key containing scale, pan, normalization range, highlight weight, gutter and keyframe-visibility mode. Its key does not include canvas dimensions or the track color selected from visible-list order. The retrieved bitmap is drawn without a dimension check at this call site. RFF should include every baked dependency and instance identity, with explicit invalidation for resize, ordering/color changes and immutable data revisions. Check the generic cache before attributing all possible behavior to this caller, but do not assume that storage of width/height makes them lookup conditions.

The soft-selection mask cache is directly inspectable here: its get method compares only a key string. That string omits the sequence/key positions, track list, normalized ranges and dimensions even though those are inputs to mask construction. It hashes selected IDs by XOR and collapses non-string selection types to one tag. A hash collision or omitted dependency can persist until another included input changes; the comment's “one frame” characterization is not a guarantee. For RFF, use a source revision plus the actual selection/viewport contract, and bound cache memory per editor. Module-global caches can also evict one editor's visible tracks when another editor draws; prefer per-instance ownership unless sharing is deliberate.

**Coordinate agreement:** the graph adds a configurable left gutter to frame positions, normalizes values per track and draws selected tangents separately. The same transform must drive rendering, hit testing, marquee selection and editing, including device scaling. Require finite positive scales, a valid drawable rectangle and nonzero normalized spans. The time-grid helper chooses from a finite interval list but falls back to 1000 when even 5000 frames is insufficient for label spacing; a generalized RFF grid should continue to larger nice intervals and bound drawing work. Also guard floating-point loops against a step too small to advance the accumulator at large offsets.

`hideKeyframes` is forwarded into cached curve construction, but the selected-key overlay loop does not check it. Thus hiding ordinary key markers is not by itself a proof that modal tools own all visible handles. Explicitly disable both stale handles and their hit tests while another tool owns the surface. Track colors follow visible-list position and repeat after six entries; stable track identity and labels are preferable for comparing many animated shader parameters.

**Input and commands:** touch is translated into synthetic mouse events, retaining one touch identifier. Cancellation is translated into mouse-up, while unmount removes listeners without sending an end/cancel to the mouse interaction owner. Define cancellation and transaction cleanup across both routes. The toolbar exposes normalization, fitting, Euler filtering, baking, smoothing, simplification and drawing, but those buttons delegate to callbacks and do not establish those algorithms' correctness. Several tools have a no-op click and rely on pointer-down; provide a keyboard alternative. The height-balancing helper limits column height relative to its computed minimum, not horizontal overflow or a plot shorter than one button. Keep editing access valid in narrow panels.

These are practical 3D-to-2D authoring transfers: the same graph mechanisms can edit flat palette/color motion and relief material/light animation. Verify curve/display/playback agreement in the builders and evaluators before claiming a faithful graph, and test resize, track reorder, selected-key motion, two simultaneous editors and interrupted touch gestures. No runtime benchmark, image comparison or algorithm implementation was performed in this batch.

## Curve builder follow-up: one evaluator for the segment and its continuation

**Scope:** complete reads of [canvasCache.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/canvasCache.ts), [GraphRendererBuilder.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/GraphRendererBuilder.ts) and [keyframeShape.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/keyframeShape.ts), plus lines 1–228 of [timelineUtils.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/timelineUtils.ts). Hashes match the inventory. timelineUtils remains partially read; resume at line 229. This is source tracing, not a runtime comparison with playback.

**Resolved cache question:** RefViewKeyCache.get compares only ID, token equality and the supplied view key. It returns stored dimensions but does not validate them. Thus the dimension omission identified in the preceding GraphRenderer section is not repaired by the generic cache. The builder paints viewport-sized bitmaps, so RFF must invalidate or rebuild those bitmaps on a size change. Include post-behavior, track color/order and registry-driven interpolation mode as well as keyframe revision in the dependency contract; these influence the pixels without necessarily changing the keyframe-array reference. Four-decimal scale rounding should be justified by a screen-space error bound over the visible data extent, not assumed harmless for every zoom and frame magnitude.

**Curve construction:** GMT draws Step and ordinary Linear segments directly and ordinary Bezier segments as canvas cubic paths. Positive log-track segments instead sample evaluateTrackValue with its log flag set, using approximately four-pixel spacing. The evaluator wrapper delegates in-range segments to AnimationMath and returns endpoint values outside the key range. This use of the actual segment evaluator is a useful RFF design principle, but the four-pixel polyline is still an approximation and can miss sharp curvature. Sampling is based on the entire segment's screen span before clipping, so a very long offscreen segment can generate unnecessary work. Clip the evaluated interval to the visible region and use a bounded error-driven subdivision policy while retaining discontinuities exactly.

**Continuation differs from the main segment.** Loop, PingPong and OffsetLoop tails use five-pixel samples and call evaluateTrackValue without its log flag. They recognize rotation only through a camera.rotation prefix, whereas timelineUtils exposes a broader name-based classifier. Continue tails separately derive a raw-value slope from the last key's interpolation/tangent data. RFF should use one metadata-driven evaluator for segments, extrapolation, repeated cycles, status comparisons and export. Declare whether offset repetition is additive in raw units or in a logarithmic domain, and specify whether rotations retain authored turns or unwrap. A parameter name containing “rot” is not sufficient proof of angular semantics. The graph must represent what the animation actually evaluates; separate hand-written tail math makes that harder to guarantee.

The soft-selection builder measures temporal distance on the same track and takes the largest falloff from selected keys; it is not a two-dimensional distance in the plotted graph. Explain this when offering nearby-key influence for RFF palette or light animation. Cached drawing does not remove rebuild cost: this builder still searches for each selected ID and compares every candidate key with selected keys on its track. Use indexed IDs and sorted temporal neighborhoods if profiling justifies it. Its zero-span normalization fallback also differs from the main curve builder, reinforcing the need for one transform contract.

The partial live-value helper returns zero while playing, uses a stub for legacy light extraction, recognizes vector x/y/z but not w in its generic suffix branch, and adds camera offset components with ordinary number arithmetic. These are concrete limits of this helper, not evidence that all GMT runtime tracks are unsupported. RFF should represent unavailable data explicitly, consult the accepted evaluated frame for live values, and preserve its high-precision camera/location representation instead of copying this additive stub.

Key shapes provide a useful non-color distinction between Step, Bezier and other interpolation modes. Their actual diamond bounding extent is larger than the nominal size used for circles/squares, so hit testing must agree with geometry rather than just a shared size label. These findings support truthful, responsive editing of flat 2D color motion and relief materials. Runtime visual parity, remaining tangent utilities and full timelineUtils coverage are still unverified.

## Curve processing completion: preserve shader motion when smoothing or baking

**RFF opportunity.** If editable animation curves are extended to palette phase, environment orientation, material masks or emission strength, offer smoothing and baking as explicit authoring operations. Their value is predictable motion in both flat 2D and relief rendering; they do not require GMT's 3D camera or a change to fractal iteration math. This is a supporting workflow recommendation, not a newly measured shader effect or a change to the provisional top ten.

**Evidence.** The complete 526-line [timeline utility](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/timelineUtils.ts) was inspected, including its remaining tangent, Euler-filter, smoothing, spring and resampling paths. [AnimationMath](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/math/AnimationMath.ts) and the [log-track registry](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/engine/animation/logTrackRegistry.ts) were reread to check the evaluation contract. Comments describing other investigations are not treated as independently verified measurements here.

### One value-domain contract for every operation

GMT's tangent-mode and global-interpolation builders pass `isLogTrack(tid)` when generating Auto/Ease handles. Positive log-track endpoints are evaluated in log-value space, and tangent Y components then represent log units. However, the utility's spring and resampling calls omit the evaluator's log argument, whose default is false. Therefore these transformations need not sample the same curve as log-aware playback. For RFF, carry explicit track metadata through drawing, playback, editing, smoothing and export: units, periodicity, interpolation domain, valid range and unavailable-data behavior. Preserve RFF's high-precision location representation separately; this ordinary-number utility is not suitable evidence for replacing it.

The Euler filter chooses the nearest successive value modulo 2 pi. That is useful for an explicitly requested shortest-path repair, but removes intentional full revolutions. Its broad name-based classifier also includes phase and selected generic parameter names, whereas resampling only recognizes `camera.rotation`. RFF palette phase may use cycles rather than radians. Store the period and winding policy as metadata; offer shortest-path and preserved-turn behavior explicitly instead of deriving units from a name. The scalar filter is not a full quaternion-orientation filter.

### Smoothing should describe time and selection boundaries

Positive-radius smoothing applies Gaussian weights to neighboring key indices, not elapsed time. Unevenly spaced keys therefore receive a different temporal effect from evenly spaced keys. Selected blocks determine which keys are changed, but the kernel can still read unselected neighbors outside those blocks. End sampling extends the first/last track values. No angular unwrapping or log-space projection is applied in this positive-radius branch.

For RFF, specify smoothing width in frames or seconds, choose whether unselected neighbors may influence the result, and smooth in the declared value domain. A palette phase crossing its wrap seam should not average toward the opposite phase. Keep a stable source snapshot throughout the adjustment so dragging the strength control does not repeatedly smooth already modified data. GMT accepts such a source sequence; its radius-zero restore only restores matching key values, not a complete key/tangent/interpolation snapshot. RFF cancellation should restore the complete affected command state.

The negative-radius spring path advances one simulation step per frame and writes results only at existing keys matching the sampled frame within 0.1. This is not a dense baked spring curve, and differently offset fractional-frame keys may be missed. Unselected matching keys reset position and velocity. If adopted, define time units and solver stability, sample all requested key times, and keep the preview consistent with the committed representation. Bound work by duration and key count; the inspected loop repeatedly traverses keys.

### Baking must preserve endpoints and declared discontinuities

GMT resampling starts at the ceiling of the first frame and ends at the floor of the last; fractional endpoints are dropped, and the step need not land on the final frame. It emits new IDs with Linear interpolation. Even correct sample values do not preserve a Step discontinuity or an arbitrary Bezier curve between samples. The helper itself has no finite-positive step validation, so it is not a safe standalone contract for arbitrary inputs; caller restrictions have not been established by this read.

For an RFF baking command, require a finite positive step, bound generated key count, preserve exact original endpoints, and retain explicit discontinuities. Evaluate through the same domain-aware function used for playback. State whether accuracy is guaranteed only at output frame times or within a chosen error tolerance between them. Preview the change and commit it atomically, including selection and stable references affected by replacement IDs.

**Verification proposed, not executed:** irregular key spacing; a phase seam with and without intentional extra turns; positive values spanning several decades; a non-positive log-domain boundary; fractional endpoints; a step that does not divide the duration; Step and curved segments; selected/unselected boundaries; repeated strength adjustments from one snapshot; cancellation; and preview/video agreement at identical timestamps. No RFF application code or shader was changed for this audit.

## Drawn animation curves: retain the visible shape through fitting and commit

**Useful transfer to RFF.** A freehand curve tool could author palette phase, environment rotation or emission envelopes over a selected time interval. The same infrastructure can serve flat 2D coloring and relief material animation. GMT separates the interaction tool from its storage through target, source-key, preview and commit callbacks; this is a useful architectural reference if RFF expands curve authoring. It is not a recommendation to transplant the React editor or its ordinary-number representation into high-precision fractal coordinates.

**Full source inspected:** [GraphEditor.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/GraphEditor.tsx), [usePencilTool.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/hooks/usePencilTool.ts), and [keyframeViewBounds.ts](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/utils/keyframeViewBounds.ts), totaling 843 inventory lines. These observations cover host wiring and stroke construction; they do not prove all downstream fitting or seam-healing behavior.

### Freeze the editing basis, then fit in the intended domain

At mouse-down, the pencil retains its target, view and original key array. Preview and final fitting use that original array rather than recursively fitting previous previews. Preserve this principle in RFF with an immutable source revision and explicit cancellation. The inspected timeline host does not supply the optional preview callback: it shows the stroke overlay and commits replacement keys on release. Therefore shared-hook support for live previews is not proof that this particular timeline updates the rendered scene while drawing.

The host provides a log-aware pixel-to-value conversion in normalized mode, but supplies the fitting epsilon as `max(1e-6, rawValueRange * 0.02)`. The pencil converts points to ordinary values, samples them at integer frames, then passes those samples and that epsilon to the fitter without value-domain metadata. This establishes a domain mismatch in the interface; it does not establish a measured amount of visible error. For RFF, transform samples into the same domain used by playback, and define fitting error in displayed pixels or a meaningful parameter tolerance. Validate the resulting playback curve, not just the input samples. Logarithmic magnitude, wrapped phase and bounded material amounts need different contracts.

The normalized-range builder uses logarithms only when the minimum key value is positive. Its forward conversion instead logs each positive value independently, and the inverse exponentiates whenever the track is registered as logarithmic. A track containing a non-positive value can consequently have a linear range paired with logarithmic conversion. Resolve one domain policy for the entire operation and use it in both directions. Reject or explicitly handle out-of-domain values before computing bounds; do not silently mix mappings.

### Preserve the stroke's intended time interval

Points are sorted by frame, so drawing backward or revisiting one frame is not equivalent to an ordered pen path. Endpoints are rounded to integer frames. Linear sample interpolation does not clamp its interpolation fraction, so rounding outward can extrapolate beyond the first or last sampled point.
