Full reads of [PanelRouter.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/PanelRouter.tsx), [ComponentRegistry.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/registry/ComponentRegistry.tsx) and [RuntimeSection.tsx](https://github.com/gamazama/GMT-fractals/blob/ad28b8bbca3c01b4d2cfebebd727c5bcd951a2e1/components/RuntimeSection.tsx) establish another useful RFF architecture: describe the arrangement of palette, material, environment and effect controls separately from their implementation. Standard feature sections can share parameter metadata, while complex editors retain a dedicated implementation. This applies to flat 2D and relief controls without importing GMT's React framework.

GMT resolves a bespoke component first, otherwise renders an ordered item list of features, widgets, collapsible sections, accordions and compilation-aware sections. A legacy feature/widget shorthand is expanded into the same item renderer. Contextual help IDs can be assigned at the grouping boundary. RFF could use this pattern to organize the proposed shader additions consistently and connect each setting to the relevant help, availability and preparation status.

The actual fallback differs from a literal “explicit items wins” rule: an empty items array falls back to the shorthand, and shorthand widgets are discarded if there are no features. Define empty versus omitted content explicitly in a RFF layout schema. Use stable item IDs rather than array position for persisted collapse state and component identity; GMT includes indices in many render keys, so inserting or reordering items can remount controls. Validate all referenced components and parameter IDs before presenting a panel. Missing widgets currently warn and render nothing, whereas a missing bespoke panel shows a placeholder.

The component registry is a module-global map with warning-and-overwrite registration, no removal or notification API. That supports startup composition but is not a complete dynamic-plugin lifecycle. If RFF adds extensions or optional panels, use namespaced stable IDs, explicit replacement ownership and invalidation when registrations change. Widget extra properties are spread after standard state/actions/navigation properties; constrain reserved fields in a typed schema so layout metadata cannot accidentally replace the adapter contract.

**Keep conditions and accepted state aligned.** The router subscribes to the entire engine store to cause rerenders, but passes its parent-supplied state into visibility predicates and dynamic labels. A rerender alone does not ensure that a stale parent snapshot has become current. Derive all conditions from one accepted state revision and subscribe only to relevant dependencies where practical. The runtime wrapper uses a truthy toggle value and always marks the section compiled; it does not verify that the declared toggle is actually a runtime-only parameter. Validate that distinction in metadata before exposing it. Hiding a control, switching a runtime flag and preparing a new shader variant are separate operations.

The router also resets divider styles and measures later siblings after every commit to hide a trailing decorative edge. With a full-store subscription this can create layout work unrelated to the current panel's settings. Prefer deriving decoration from the visible layout tree, or invalidate measurements only when layout changes. This is a source-supported performance candidate, not an observed bottleneck. Preserve ongoing value-edit transactions if visibility changes unmount a child section.

**Proposed checks:** empty versus omitted item lists, widget-only panels, dynamic feature availability, reordered sections with active edits, missing or replaced registrations, runtime toggles mislabeled as compile-free, and state changes unrelated to the open panel. This is a code-architecture audit, not a screenshot-based interface review or an implemented RFF panel redesign.
## Shader workspace completion: keep panel placement and availability coherent

**Sources read in full:** `components/layout/Dock.tsx`, `components/layout/DropZones.tsx`, and `components/ScrollSpaceReserver.tsx` in GMT. This is source-level integration evidence for the proposed RFF shader controls, not a visual interface audit or a new shader effect.

**Transferable value.** A dock can collect related appearance controls while keeping panel identity, placement, order, collapse state and active selection separate from rendering settings. For RFF, that can support a workspace with palette editing on one side and material/environment editing on the other. Preserve layout independently of scene appearance so arranging controls does not alter an image or require shader compilation. The reviewed code provides tab selection, drag reordering and side/float drop targets; it does not establish that RFF currently lacks equivalent workspace facilities.

**Availability needs its own reactive dependencies.** Dock uses granular store subscriptions for panel and layout state, then evaluates manifest visibility predicates against an imperative engine snapshot during render. Changes used only by those predicates do not themselves appear in its subscriptions. Parent rerenders may refresh the result, but this component alone does not guarantee timely availability updates. It also passes imperative snapshots into PanelRouter, reinforcing the prior finding that a child's store subscription does not refresh parent-supplied props automatically. A RFF adaptation should derive control visibility and values from a consistent accepted revision, with dependencies for feature availability explicitly subscribed. Avoid subscribing every layout component to every animation update merely to repair this gap.

The visible active tab falls back to the first eligible panel without replacing the stored active ID. Thus the former tab can return automatically when eligible again. Define whether RFF should restore that previous selection or retain the fallback, and distinguish temporary feature unavailability from closing a panel. Mobile detection is sampled during render from viewport width/coarse-pointer state, with no local resize/media-query subscription. Mobile left-to-right remapping and summon-only panel rules are useful policies, but one shared effective-location calculation should govern rendering, reordering, drop targets and restoration.

**Gesture completion must be explicit.** The dock resize handler installs window mouse listeners and removes them on mouseup; it provides no local unmount cancellation. Its 200–800 pixel clamp is not an available-viewport constraint. The drop overlay cancels when mouseup reaches the window, but that cannot guarantee delivery of a release outside the browser, despite the source comment. No local blur, Escape or pointer-cancel path supplies that guarantee. For RFF, use the platform's capture/cancellation mechanisms, restore prior gesture state on cancellation, and release all temporary cursor/listener state on teardown. Keep accepted layout changes distinct from drag previews. Validate the dragged panel still exists and supports the destination: the overlay's optional floatability check alone also permits a missing panel to activate the float target. The store may reject invalid moves, but the overlay is not proof of that protection.

Side drop widths are calculated from stored sizes or a fixed collapsed width rather than measured mounted docks. A hidden dock or responsive remapping can therefore require a separate destination policy. Resolve destinations from actual workspace geometry, constrain the remaining canvas area, and commit a move against a valid current layout revision. These are adoption conditions, not claims that a browser interaction failure was reproduced.

**Height reservation has a narrower guarantee than its comments suggest.** ScrollSpaceReserver remembers the largest measured content height and adds bottom space when content shrinks. For short content, it adds an additional buffer so the preserved area can be scrolled into view and then out; that transition releases the reservation. Dock resets the reservation on tab changes using a key and bypasses it for bespoke panels that need a fixed full-height container. These are useful distinctions between document-like controls and canvas-like editors.

However, preserving total height does not by itself keep controls inside the content wrapper at their old positions: collapsing an earlier section can still move later sections upward. The mechanism primarily retains scroll extent, and its additional buffer can even increase that extent. Initial measurement runs in an effect, followed by ResizeObserver updates; this is not proof of an unconditional first-paint stability guarantee. The visibility-release handler runs only on scroll, not immediately on attachment or on every geometry change. The nearest scroll parent is discovered at effect setup and is not independently tracked through reparenting. Initial `offsetHeight` and later `contentRect.height` also use different box measurements, though the present inner wrapper has no explicit border or padding.

For RFF's shader controls, first choose the desired behavior: preserve the current scroll anchor, retain a recently collapsed section's space, or deliberately bring the next controls into view. Implement that specific policy with consistent geometry measurements and bounded lifetime. Do not introduce large blank areas solely to let a spacer satisfy its own release rule. Independently scrolling graph or image editors need their own boundary treatment.

**Proposed validation:** toggle feature availability without a layout change; hide and restore the active tab; change viewport mode during a gesture; remove a dragged panel; release outside the window; destroy the panel during resizing; collapse content near the bottom; switch between long controls and a full-height editor. Confirm layout edits leave rendered pixels and persisted scene parameters unchanged. No application changes, runtime reproduction or performance measurements are claimed by this follow-up, and it does not change the shader-effect ranking.
## Shader setting status: distinguish drafts, accepted pipelines and preferences

**Sources read in full:** `components/panels/engine/EngineFeatureRow.tsx`, `components/StatusDot.tsx`, `components/SettingsAccess.tsx`, and `components/SettingsPanel.tsx`. Previously reviewed `store/safeLocalStorage.ts` was reread in full; the relevant dense-control and apply paths in `AutoFeaturePanel.tsx` and `engine-gmt/components/panels/ShaderCompilerPanel.tsx` were checked again selectively. This section concerns reliable operation of future RFF appearance controls, not an additional visual effect or measured optimization.

**Tie status to the event it actually establishes.** EngineFeatureRow accepts four externally computed statuses: synced, pending, runtime and overridden. It does not inspect the renderer. Its synced tooltip always says compiled and active even when the checkbox is inactive. More fundamentally, the reviewed dense caller assigns synced to compile parameters when no entry exists in the local pending-change map. ShaderCompilerPanel clears that map after dispatching feature setters, without awaiting pipeline acceptance in this path. Absence of a draft therefore does not establish that the GPU is using the new shader. A separate scheduler/progress system can supply that evidence, but the row does not consume it here.

For RFF, distinguish requested settings, an unapplied draft, compilation in progress, the accepted pipeline revision and a failed replacement that retains the last working pipeline. Show disabled/off independently of synchronization. Runtime eligibility describes an update route, not proof that a particular value has already reached a presented frame. Likewise, a quality override should identify the effective value and controlling policy without destroying the stored user value. StatusDot is a presentation primitive with active/pending/off/instant variants; it cannot validate these semantics on its own. Prefer one shared status model to several incompatible color vocabularies.

**Preserve typed parameter identity and actual disabled behavior.** EngineFeatureRow compares option values loosely for the displayed label and converts any numerically parseable selection string into a number. This can change the identity of a string-valued option such as a numeric-looking preset ID. Resolve a selection back to its declared typed option instead. Numeric drag sensitivity is derived as one percent of the configured range per pixel divided by step; require finite, ordered bounds and a positive finite step, and choose appropriate logarithmic or angular behavior for relevant shader parameters. Do not let an incidental integer-valued current sample determine the domain of a floating-point parameter.

The disabled prop applies opacity and pointer-event CSS to the row, without setting native disabled attributes on the select or checkbox or guarding the row's callbacks. Reviewed callers have some independent update guards, but the reusable row alone is not an authoritative disabled contract. RFF should enforce unavailable edits at the command boundary as well as in controls. Tooltip placement is sampled on mouse entry, not continuously updated for scroll/resize; descriptions and status explanations should remain available independently of a hover-only indicator. These are source-level observations, with no claim of screenshot or keyboard testing.

**Keep preferences separate from image-generating parameters.** SettingsAccess supplies a shared open/close host, while SettingsPanel organizes registered preferences by tab and section and lets each subsystem own get/set/subscribe behavior. That division is useful for RFF interface preferences and hardware policy, while material values remain scene data subject to their established persistence and undo rules. Visibility predicates are recomputed on registry changes or a refresh tick; external dependencies need a subscription that triggers that tick. Custom controls own their own writes and refresh responsibility. Merely reopening the panel does not necessarily invalidate memoized conditional sections.

The generic number input forwards `Number(inputText)` on every edit. Empty text becomes zero, and HTML min/max attributes do not constitute setter-side clamping or validation. Keep temporary editing text distinct from an accepted finite value and report rejection rather than silently accepting an unintended zero. Synchronous setters are followed by a refresh tick; the wrapper supplies no asynchronous success/failure protocol. A persistence failure or pending device change needs explicit subsystem feedback if exposed through this interface.

**Reset through the owning subsystem.** The storage inspector lists all localStorage keys returned by the guard, with no app-prefix filter. Its shared-origin scope is broader than the visible wording about this app. Removing a key only removes persisted bytes; `safeLocalRemove` neither resets in-memory state nor announces success, and swallowed storage errors are not a confirmed reset. The panel rereads storage after deletion but does not invoke preference defaults. The inspector also enumerates storage in a memo before the closed-panel return, even when its storage surface is disabled. For RFF, use namespaced storage, subsystem-owned reset commands and clearly scoped reset choices; synchronize active state with the resulting persisted state. Do not treat deletion of a configuration field as equivalent to applying its default. Preserve the existing append-only ConfigIO rules when adding preferences.

**Proposed checks:** apply a compile change while retaining an older pipeline; fail compilation; toggle a synchronized feature off; edit an overridden value; select a numeric-looking string ID; edit empty/out-of-range numeric text; change a visibility dependency externally; reset while the subsystem remains live; simulate unavailable storage. Verify the displayed status follows the accepted operation and that resetting interface preferences does not alter saved palette recipes or scene appearance. None of these checks has been executed in this source-review follow-up.
## Appearance snapshot workflow: compare looks without losing state ownership

**Sources read in full:** `components/StateLibraryPanel.tsx`, `components/StateDebugger.tsx`, and `utils/Sharing.ts`. The previously completed `engine/store/createStateLibrarySlice.ts` was reread to check the panel's callback contract against actual storage operations. Source comments about historical production failures and smoke tests are context, not newly reproduced results.

**RFF opportunity.** Thumbnail-backed appearance snapshots could let users retain several palette/material/environment combinations and switch among them on the same fractal view. GMT separates list presentation from capture/apply handlers, which is a useful reusable boundary. Define an explicit appearance-only payload, preserve the fractal location and calculation settings, and make applying a look one undoable operation. This extends the earlier selective-import proposal; it is not evidence that a complete RFF look library is missing or that the generic panel alone implements comparison rendering.

The slice is specifically a single-active-state library. Reusable materials or gradients shared by several layers need target-aware asset references and independent ownership rather than a single active ID. The panel's broad examples should not obscure that distinction. Its modified marker is evaluated only for the active snapshot. In RFF, compare the relevant appearance fields and referenced asset revisions, excluding transient progress, thumbnail bytes and unrelated camera changes. Freeze palette recipe identity and retain image dependencies so a saved look can actually be reconstructed.

**Keep administrative actions separate from applying a look.** Row clicks call select even on the already active row. Label double-click stops the double-click event, but not the preceding click events that reach the row; entering rename can therefore first invoke selection/application. The slice reapplies on select, so a host must explicitly protect unsaved live edits if that is its intended policy. Duplicate also selects and applies the copy in the reviewed slice; it is not merely a library insertion. For RFF, make save, duplicate, rename and apply separate commands with deliberate side effects. Empty rename text is correctly treated as cancellation, and a fallback label keeps older blank entries visible. These safeguards do not resolve click-versus-apply semantics.

The list claims drag-over/drop only after it starts an internal drag, allowing unrelated file drops to remain available to the outer application. Preserve that event-ownership boundary. Reordering records indices, however, so an insertion/deletion while dragging can change which snapshot those indices identify. Commit by stable source/target IDs against the current collection. Slot hints are presentation only: the first nine rows show a configurable prefix, but the panel does not register shortcuts. Keep displayed hints synchronized with actual shortcut ownership and the host's slot count. Delete, persistence and undo remain host responsibilities, so a library callback must not be mistaken for durable saving or recovery support.

**Bind thumbnails to immutable captures.** The slice captures state before asynchronous thumbnail work. Add patches the thumbnail into a current array by ID, whereas update and existing-slot save retain an older array across the await and later replace the whole collection. Concurrent rename, reorder, delete or another save can therefore be overwritten by that captured array. A RFF implementation should commit immutable state with a snapshot revision first, request a thumbnail for exactly that state/render revision, and patch only the matching still-current snapshot. Ignore superseded results and keep thumbnail failure separate from data-save success. Domain-specific cloning is also required: the slice's JSON round-trip duplicate is not a suitable general serializer for arbitrary precision numbers, typed data or asset handles.

**Share preparation must not mutate its input.** `generateShareStringFromPreset` deletes antialiasing settings, a resolution-mode field and optionally sequence/animation fields directly from the supplied preset before encoding. Its catch does not undo those deletions. Callers may supply detached data, but this utility itself does not ensure ownership. For RFF, build a detached, explicitly scoped export record and report omitted settings. The reviewed code strips specific fields; its broader comment about stripping render settings does not prove all device-dependent fields are removed. Decoding first peeks the formula against a skeleton, then decodes using formula defaults and the current feature dictionary. Stable schema/default semantics and migration validation remain necessary; a cast to Preset is not runtime schema validation or cross-version compatibility proof.

**Inspection and application are different operations.** StateDebugger usefully exposes a decoded representation before applying it and reuses the centralized parser. Yet editing the input does not invalidate a previous decoded preset; the apply button still refers to the last decoded object. Failed decode clears that object but leaves the previous JSON output, and dumping current state does not clear an earlier error. For an RFF inspector, bind the displayed result and apply command to the exact input revision, label the capture/export scope, and invalidate stale success/error state consistently. A nonthrowing load invocation followed by closing the inspector does not establish renderer acceptance. Preserve useful decode diagnostics and wait for the relevant acceptance boundary when reporting application success.

**Proposed checks:** rename an active modified look; duplicate an inactive look; reorder while the collection changes; delete during thumbnail capture; finish two saves out of order; fail thumbnail generation or persistence; export while retaining the original input unchanged; edit a decoded string before applying; fail decode after a successful inspection. Verify appearance-only application preserves the view and high-precision calculation state. These are proposed checks, not executed tests, and no shader-effect ranking changes follow from this workflow review.
## Supporting appearance controls: contextual help and popup ownership

**Sources read in full:** `components/Popover.tsx`, `components/Hint.tsx`, `components/ParentSection.tsx`, `components/SectionLabel.tsx`, `components/PanelHeader.tsx`, and `components/WarningNote.tsx`. These are control-integration references, not shader implementations. They do not alter the ten-effect ranking. This is code inspection, not a rendered design audit.

**RFF application.** Contextual descriptions can explain which field drives a material mask, what roughness filtering changes, or why a control requires a shader rebuild. A globally switchable short hint plus a stable help-topic link is a useful pattern for both flat 2D and relief workflows. GMT's Hint subscribes directly to the shared visibility state and provides a topic opener. Its close action hides all hints, not just that row; preserve that meaning in the wording. The stated H shortcut is hardcoded presentation and does not itself register a command. Both hint buttons explicitly leave the normal tab sequence. RFF should derive shortcut hints from actual bindings and provide a keyboard-accessible path to the same explanations rather than depending on pointer hover. No new renderer capability follows from adding help chrome.

**An overlay owns more than its stacking order.** Popover places content in a shared overlay tier and retains an inline marker to measure the trigger wrapper before paint. It updates the wrapper rectangle on resize and captured scroll events, recognizes both trigger and popup as inside for outside-mousedown dismissal, and cleans up its delayed listener installation. Forwarded mouse-enter/leave callbacks let a hover-driven host maintain continuity across the portal boundary. These are useful mechanisms for image-source pickers and environment controls that must appear above other panels.

The local position calculation always places the popup below the wrapper and applies horizontal alignment without collision handling. An 80dvh height cap does not guarantee fit in the space remaining below a low trigger; it also does not constrain an oversized width. A RFF adaptation should measure actual available space, flip or clamp where appropriate, and keep the anchor indication consistent with the final placement. Wrapper size/position changes without a scroll or resize event are not tracked by this component, so dynamic panel changes need explicit geometry invalidation. The measured wrapper is not necessarily the button itself; make the anchor contract precise.

Outside detection uses DOM containment. A nested child popup portalled elsewhere is not automatically inside its parent's content element, so nested overlay ownership needs a shared dismissal policy rather than an assumption that portal stacking provides it. The component itself supplies no Escape handling, focus restoration or edit-transaction commit/cancel policy. Check the host and layer mechanisms before declaring those missing application-wide; for RFF, define them at the command/overlay boundary. Closing a transient editor must not leave a partially applied material edit or commit it twice. The actual implementation of padding='none' removes horizontal padding but retains vertical padding, which matters when composing tightly fitted internal controls.

**Visual grouping is not parameter semantics.** ParentSection removes null/empty children and wraps the remaining top-level children in bracketed rows. It does not recursively discover the visible output of child components, and index-keyed wrappers do not provide stable identity when conditional rows are inserted or removed. Use stable parameter/section IDs so changing availability does not unnecessarily replace an active editor. Group dependencies, disabled behavior and compile requirements must come from the parameter model, not the bracket appearance.

SectionLabel, PanelHeader and WarningNote primarily centralize presentation; they introduce no rendering settings, help navigation or state transitions. SectionDivider distinguishes top-level, nested and in-feature separators, which can make a material's dependent controls easier to understand. Derive those distinctions from the visible section tree, as recommended in the prior PanelRouter review. A warning-colored container alone does not establish error severity, recovery behavior or announcement semantics. Keep decorative styles independent of shader data and avoid copying presentation-only components as supposed feature additions.

**Proposed checks:** open a source picker at each window edge; resize or collapse its parent while open; interact with a nested picker; dismiss during a numeric gesture; navigate help without a pointer; hide all hints and restore them through the configured command; toggle conditional sibling controls while another is being edited. Verify these operations preserve the accepted material values unless an explicit edit is committed. No visual interaction test or runtime performance measurement was performed for this source-review batch.
## Viewport and timeline hosts: separate presentation from render ownership

**Sources read in full:** `components/TimelineHost.tsx` and `components/ViewportArea.tsx`. The already-reviewed animation dispatcher and AppGmt were selectively revisited to verify actual host ownership. App.tsx uses this generic viewport shell; AppGmt builds its own ViewportFrame tree. Findings about the generic shell must not be presented as universal GMT renderer behavior.

**RFF transfer.** A lazily opened timeline and a fixed-resolution canvas fitted within the workspace are useful supporting mechanisms for animated palettes, material masks and environment rotation. Keep the evaluated appearance state independent of whether the editor is visible. Keep export resolution independent of the displayed canvas size, and use the same declared full-image coordinate system for decorative mappings, overlays and tiled output. This supports both flat 2D and relief rendering without adopting a 3D camera model.

TimelineHost owns only the editor's open state and command registration. Its hidden prop returns no visible content after registering shortcuts; hiding the host does not disable T or Space. Space acts only when the track dictionary has entries, not necessarily playable keyframes. The general Space binding excludes Fly camera mode, while a higher-priority timeline-hover binding intentionally overrides that exclusion. For RFF, decide explicitly which commands remain active in clean-preview/export modes and which context owns a conflicting navigation key. Derive those conditions from capabilities and scopes rather than importing a hardcoded 3D mode name. The lazy-loading boundary has a null suspense fallback, so any useful load progress or recovery must come from its helper or host, not an assumed indicator in this file.

**Do not infer playback ownership from component names.** ViewportArea conditionally mounts AnimationSystem outside clean-feed mode, but the current AnimationSystem React component returns null. Its exported tick dispatcher owns the live work through another driver. Therefore hiding this component does not, by itself, stop animation; equally, merely mounting it does not prove animation is driven. A RFF integration should establish one live evaluation owner, one deterministic export evaluation route and an explicit synchronization contract, with timeline visibility affecting only editing presentation. This avoids accidental duplicate ticks or an editor-dependent playback lifecycle.

**Resolution has several distinct meanings.** The generic viewport observes the outer area's CSS dimensions and publishes floored dimensions multiplied by the window device-pixel ratio, skipping publication during bucket rendering. Fixed mode separately uses requested width/height for the inner wrapper, scales it down to fit, and positions controls from that visible size. The overlay Canvas receives state.dpr, which is a separate input from the window ratio used for publication. These values can legitimately serve different consumers; they should not be silently treated as one render extent. Validate finite positive fixed dimensions and name CSS size, backing size, render target size and export size separately in RFF.

The observer does not explicitly publish again when bucket rendering ends without a resize, or when device-pixel ratio alone changes without a content-size notification. Other code may handle those transitions; this shell is not proof that they are covered. Ensure the accepted target extent is refreshed on each relevant transition. The once-per-mount onSceneReady callback follows shell setup, before any demonstrated shader/asset/first-frame readiness, and can fire even when no positive initial rectangle was obtained. Use separate shell-ready and render-ready events if status depends on the distinction.

**Overlays need bounded subscriptions and explicit visibility policy.** DOM and scene overlays look up registered components and render them when the corresponding feature slice exists. They subscribe to the whole store, so unrelated updates can rebuild the overlay tree. Registry reads are imperative, and registration changes alone do not establish a reactive invalidation path here. Scope subscriptions to the relevant state and define how dynamic registrations invalidate the tree. This is a potential integration improvement, not a measured bottleneck.

Clean-feed mode hides composition guides, compile/performance indicators, histogram probes and fixed-resolution controls locally, but the general DOM and scene overlay components remain mounted. Some scene components may be the actual rendering surface, so suppressing them indiscriminately would also be incorrect. RFF should classify image content, interactive controls and diagnostics explicitly, then apply its clean-output policy to those categories. Histogram consumers are reference-count gated; preserve that demand-driven analysis pattern while ensuring analysis samples the intended accepted render revision and resolution.

The shell's canvas-hover flag describes the whole outer area, including margins, rather than only the visible fixed-resolution image. Cursor-based image operations need an additional image-bound test and inverse display transform. Proposed checks include hidden timeline shortcuts, no-keyframe tracks, repeated open/close, clean-feed transitions during playback, differing display/render pixel ratios, resize during export, zero-size startup, and pointer operations in fitted-image margins. These remain source-derived validation requirements; no runtime failure, performance improvement or new RFF implementation is claimed.
## Mode selectors: separate selection, enablement and interface appearance

**Sources read in full:** `components/TabStrip.tsx`, `components/ToggleSwitch.tsx`, `components/TopBarToggle.tsx`, and `components/ThemeControls.tsx`. These are supporting source contracts for RFF controls, not additional shader effects or a rendered interface review.

**Transferable structure.** TabStrip keeps the selected item ID separate from an item's indicator flag. That is useful for a future RFF list of light directions or material layers: selecting an item for editing need not enable it, and an enabled item need not be selected. Keep both states visible and separately named. The current implementation exposes an optional add command but no remove callback, despite introductory comments describing add/remove. Likewise, the implemented item property is indicator, not the introductory active/color description. Adopt the actual contract rather than treating comments as implemented functionality.

Items use strict identity for selection but stringified IDs for React keys. A mixed ID domain containing numeric 1 and string '1' is therefore ambiguous for component identity even though selection distinguishes them. Use a stable, consistently typed ID namespace for shader layers/lights. The component does not repair an active ID that disappears, impose the list's capacity, register undo or manage shader resources; those belong to the host command. The native add button accepts a disabled flag, but resource limits must also be checked when the command executes. Give selected/enabled states non-color semantics appropriate to the platform instead of relying solely on the chip color and tiny dot.

**Interaction bracketing is not accepted-state completion.** ToggleSwitch wraps its callback between handleInteractionStart('param') and handleInteractionEnd, then delegates presentation to GenericToggleSwitch. The calls are synchronous, with no finally cleanup: a throwing callback can bypass the end call, while asynchronous work is not awaited. For RFF, guarantee gesture cleanup and let the render/pipeline system separately report acceptance or failure. A command transaction should capture one intentional toggle, while asynchronous shader compilation keeps the previous working state until its replacement is accepted. The forwarded LFO toggle is a separate callback and is not wrapped by this handleChange path, so its own transaction policy must be checked. Passing a disabled prop to the child does not replace command-side validation.

TopBarToggle is presentation only. Its active prop selects classes; it does not expose pressed state itself or provide a disabled contract. Below its breakpoint the label disappears, leaving the optional icon/title to convey identity. For RFF, retain a meaningful accessible command name and state in compact layouts. Do not infer render-engine switching, compile status or preview-region behavior from a generic toggle's appearance.

**Interface brightness is not image exposure.** ThemeControls operates on a separate color-scheme store. Preset highlighting compares brightness, surface tint and high contrast exactly; it identifies a combination of those axes, not an immutable scene preset. The brightness slider and high-contrast checkbox edit interface settings only through that store. Keeping these controls separate from the palette, exposure and tone-mapping model is useful for RFF: changing the surroundings should not change saved image pixels, shader parameters or recipe regeneration. The apparent color of an image may be judged differently against different surrounds, so a neutral interface/viewing background is a workflow option, not a color-calibration claim. The controls alone do not establish contrast compliance or renderer color accuracy.

**Proposed checks:** delete the selected light/layer; preserve enablement while switching selection; reject additions at capacity; fail a toggle callback; finish an asynchronous pipeline replacement; exercise the LFO action's history behavior; use compact controls without a pointer; change interface brightness while comparing exported pixels. No such runtime tests were performed in this batch. These integration conditions apply to flat 2D and relief controls and do not change the provisional shader-effect ranking.
## Touch navigation and startup: transfer input mechanisms, not 3D assumptions

**Sources read in full:** `components/MobileControls.tsx` and the generic `components/LoadingScreen.tsx`. These complete two supporting component reads; they are not the richer app-gmt loading screen previously inspected. Search confirms MobileControls is mounted by both App and AppGmt and that joystick events have a consumer in `engine-gmt/navigation/useInputController.ts`; the consumer was only located in this follow-up, not re-audited in full.

**2D transfer.** A normalized two-axis input can drive optional continuous panning, a light direction or environment rotation in RFF. GMT's Move/Look pair and Fly/Orbit switch are explicitly 3D navigation choices, so their labels and behavior should not be copied into a Mandelbrot view. Preserve high-precision location arithmetic: normalized input is only a gesture signal, not permission to convert a deep-zoom center to ordinary floats. A host can integrate a bounded velocity against elapsed time; the reviewed component itself publishes samples on pointer movement and does not establish frame-rate-independent integration.

The joystick computes displacement relative to its current bounding rectangle, clamps its magnitude to one and flips vertical sign for the published vector. It associates subsequent move/up/cancel events with a pointer ID, which supports independent fingers on separate sticks. However, a new pointerdown on an already engaged stick overwrites that ID because start has no ownership guard. Start updates local values and the displayed position without immediately calling onMove, so a stationary off-center initial press does not publish the same signal as a move event. For RFF, acquire one pointer per gesture, publish the intended initial state, and define whether the control is displacement- or velocity-based.

The visual knob multiplies the already normalized displacement by its magnitude again inside the unit disk, producing a squared radial response while the output remains linear. The dragging CSS scale also changes the bounding rectangle used for later input normalization. Neither is necessarily an artistic problem, but visual displacement should not be mistaken for the exact control response. Choose a stable coordinate basis and a deliberate dead zone/response curve if needed, and test slow precision movement as well as full displacement.

Pointerup and pointercancel publish zero. Listener cleanup merely removes listeners; it does not publish zero, and changing active from true to false does not itself cancel the active gesture. Global listeners also are not equivalent to explicit pointer capture. For RFF, clear held input on mode changes, focus loss, teardown and cancellation, with the input owner responsible for the final neutral state. Do not infer an observed stuck-camera defect without checking the downstream consumer's own reset policy. Treat optional vibration as feedback only; its success must not determine whether an edit or navigation command completes.

**Startup completion needs a lifecycle contract.** The generic loading shell boots once after isStartupReady, then fades after isReady and calls onFinished after 600 ms. It has no numeric progress model. Its startupMode prop is declared but not used by the implementation. This separation between configuration readiness and scene readiness is useful, but the source of each flag must establish the corresponding event; the splash does not verify the renderer itself.

The boot latch is set before invoking the callback, with no local retry/error state. Changes to onFinished identity restart the fade effect while ready remains true; once hidden, the component remains mounted and a later dependency change can schedule another completion callback. If readiness turns false during the fade, timer cleanup does not restore opacity. A RFF adoption should use a startup generation and explicit loading/ready/failed/completed states, with one completion notification per generation and a recoverable failed boot. Keep this logic distinct from renderer replacement or device recovery after startup.

**Proposed checks:** hold an off-center initial press without movement; add a second finger to one stick; change navigation mode while held; hide/unmount controls during motion; vary event and frame rates; boot failure; readiness reversal during fade; repeated parent renders while ready. The transferable mechanisms apply to 2D interaction and startup reliability, not a new shader effect, and no runtime validation was performed in this batch.
## Contextual shader documentation: make explanations reachable and technically faithful

**Source read in full:** `components/HelpBrowser.tsx` (627 lines). The component consumes a separately supplied topic map; this read does not establish the completeness or accuracy of every help article. It is a source-level documentation integration review, not a rendered usability audit.

**RFF opportunity.** Stable topic IDs can connect a roughness control, UV field selector or emission-source selector directly to its explanation. GMT expands the selected topic's ancestor path and limits ordinary reading to its category, while search includes titles and article text across the entire map. That structure can support RFF documentation explaining what an effect changes, which data it samples, whether it works in flat 2D or relief, what numerical/quality limits apply, and how to compare it with a disabled baseline. Keep these explanations tied to actual parameter IDs and accepted functionality rather than presenting 3D-only features as available 2D effects.

**Use a declared documentation format.** The local renderer recognizes a small line-oriented subset: second/third-level headings, simple bullets, asides, rules and a few inline tokens. Dollar-delimited expressions are styled text, not mathematical typesetting. There is no implemented fenced-code, table, image or general nested-markup renderer here, and headings bypass the inline formatter. Shader mechanism documents containing equations, code or diagrams therefore need a richer renderer or an explicitly limited source format. Do not assume that a Markdown document displaying correctly elsewhere will render equivalently in this help window. Ordinary text is rendered as React text rather than injected HTML; links are emitted directly with a new target and noopener/noreferrer. If RFF accepts external help packages, validate link schemes and document provenance at ingestion rather than treating a simple regex parser as a complete content policy.

**Navigation must override incompatible filters deliberately.** Search remains local state when an external activeTopicId changes. If the requested topic does not match the search, it is absent from the rendered reading list, so repeated scroll attempts cannot reach it. Define whether contextual help clears search, temporarily includes the target or opens a separate exact-topic view. Clicking a currently selected sidebar topic sets a force-scroll flag but may not change the selected ID or visible-topic dependencies, so that alone does not guarantee a new scroll effect. Use an explicit navigation request/revision independently of the highlighted topic.

The scroll effect tracks its initial timeout and animation frame, but recursive retry timeouts are not retained for cleanup. An old retry can therefore outlive navigation changes or unmount. Cancel the whole navigation generation and let only its current request alter scroll-lock state. The observer chooses among entries delivered in the current IntersectionObserver callback, not a persistent set of all intersecting topics; it is a heuristic for the reading position, not proof of the globally nearest section. Separate passive reading-position updates from commanded navigation so scrolling does not accidentally trigger another jump. The custom 220 ms scroll animation has no local user-interruption or reduced-motion branch; decide those policies in the host if not handled elsewhere.

**Validate the topic graph, not only recursion.** Ancestor and rendering traversals have visited sets that prevent infinite recursion. However, a same-category cycle with no root can disappear entirely because traversal begins only at roots. Reject malformed parent relationships or expose a safe orphan fallback. Ordering also differs by view: browsing sorts roots/children by title, search applies the preferred category list, and sidebar/chips follow topic-map insertion order. Unknown categories receive index -1 in search sorting and precede known categories. Specify one intended order and a defined fallback rather than assuming the preference list governs every surface. Ancestor expansion depends on activeTopicId alone, so changed topic metadata with the same selected ID also needs reconciliation if dynamic updates are supported.

The narrow layout measures the window body instead of a child whose dimensions depend on the chosen layout; that is a useful way to avoid responsive feedback loops in dockable help. Category-scoped rendering also limits ordinary document work. Neither guarantees that a very large search result is cheap: search renders every matching article, and input changes rebuild that result. Consider a result index with excerpts and explicit article opening if the future RFF manual grows substantially, after measuring actual cost.

**Proposed checks:** open contextual help while an unrelated search is active; navigate twice to the same topic; switch categories during a delayed scroll retry; load a parent cycle or unknown category; update topic metadata in place; resize the help window; render the actual roughness/UV formulas and code examples. No such runtime checks were performed here. This is a documentation-workflow proposal for the already-ranked shader mechanisms, not a new effect or a change to the ranking.
## Coloring documentation and lazy topic loading: preserve mathematical meaning

**Sources read in full:** `data/help/useHelpTopics.ts`, `data/help/registry.ts`, `data/help/topics-bundle.ts`, `types/help.ts`, and `data/help/topics/coloring.ts`. The coloring articles establish intended user explanations, not independent proof of every current shader formula or supported range. Earlier shader analysis remains the implementation evidence.

**Documentation supports the adoption priorities.** The coloring help describes a field-to-transform-to-gradient pipeline, independent U/V field inputs for images, a live field histogram, separate color blending versus normal perturbation, and adjustable gradient transitions. These support the proposed RFF improvements in independent coordinate selection, histogram-assisted range placement and material-source explanation. RFF already has image layers and other related mechanisms, so documentation alone does not make those new features. Reuse the explanatory structure: identify the sampled quantity, transformation, lookup and material consumer separately, then specify whether the input exists in flat 2D, relief or actual 3D geometry.

**Correct the interpretation during transfer.** The article's bias description associates the ends of a gradient with brightness. A general palette can have any luminance order, so a coordinate remap shifts occupancy toward an endpoint, not inherently toward brighter or darker colors. Similarly, using the same radial scalar for both image axes produces a diagonal one-parameter lookup (or its independently transformed curve); it does not by itself provide the two independent coordinates of a spherical projection. Angular mappings need an explicit seam and center policy, and an angle alone is not a logarithmic spiral. Distinguish layer Screen/Add brightening from actual emitted radiance, and normal perturbation from changed geometry or silhouette. These distinctions matter directly to RFF's shader controls and avoid promising lighting or depth that the operation does not calculate.

The help gives fixed numeric ranges and formula-specific descriptions for color iterations, escape radius and orbit fields. Treat these as documented intent until matched to current metadata and implementation. Do not copy a 3D ray-marched surface's iteration/solid terminology into RFF's Mandelbrot escape calculation. Do not raise RFF's bailout solely because a help article recommends it for an artistic mapping: retain its numerical invariants and verify any additional orbit-dependent data against perturbation and MPA semantics. The noise article's named algorithm also does not settle its implementation provenance; existing source/NOTICE checks still apply if code is adapted.

**Lazy loading needs retry and source-generation ownership.** The registry caches a loaded map and shares an in-flight promise, which avoids repeated imports and can keep detailed documentation out of initial application work. A rejected promise is not cleared, however, so later calls reuse the failure until the source is reset. Neither the hook nor idle prefetch handles rejection locally. Give RFF a visible loading/error/retry state rather than presenting an empty help map as successful absence of topics.

Replacing the loader clears cache/promise fields but does not invalidate an older request's completion. An earlier loader can subsequently publish its old map into the shared cache. Use a generation token and notify subscribed readers when the accepted source changes. The hook captures its initial map and updates only from its own first effect's load promise; when the cache becomes populated between initialization and that effect, the early return does not copy the newly cached map into local state. A subscribed external-store interface or a consistently adopted promise result avoids that timing gap. Cancellation already prevents the hook's pending completion from updating an unmounted reader, but it does not solve source replacement.

Topic aggregation uses sequential object spreads, allowing later duplicate keys to replace earlier articles without a collision check. HelpSection specifies ID, title, content, category and optional parent, but does not enforce key/ID agreement, valid parent references, acyclicity or links to actual controls. Validate those relationships when building the topic collection. Its Markdown-like declaration is consistent with the small renderer reviewed previously, not evidence of full Markdown or math support. The same types file defines snapshot-style and live-element context menu variants; those are menu contracts, not topic-loading state or renderer-acceptance signals.

**Proposed checks:** reject and retry a load; replace a source while its earlier request is pending; resolve prefetch between hook initialization and effect; detect duplicate IDs and invalid parents; compare all documented ranges against current parameter metadata; demonstrate U=V radial sampling and a nonmonotonic-luminance palette to check explanation accuracy. No runtime tests or shader comparisons were executed in this documentation batch. These findings refine RFF adoption requirements without changing the current visual-effect ranking.
## Lighting and effect help: separate artistic controls from renderer guarantees

**Sources read in full:** `data/help/topics/lighting.ts` and `data/help/topics/effects.ts`. These document authoring intent. Timing, convergence, physical-accuracy and export-parity statements in them are not benchmark evidence from this audit. Previously inspected implementations remain the basis of the RFF proposals.

**Useful lighting controls for RFF.** The lighting articles describe independently controlled lights, logarithmic exposure-style intensity, color/temperature choices and view-attached versus world-attached coordinates. The low-cost transferable concept is explicit direction, color, intensity and coordinate ownership for relief shading. If RFF adds an EV-style presentation, one increment can represent a factor of two relative to a declared reference intensity; it must not imply calibrated physical brightness merely because the slider uses photographic terminology. Kelvin input should be described according to the actual RGB approximation and color space, with source/license attribution for any adopted conversion. Check existing RFF controls before treating either presentation as a new capability.

The documented attachment switch preserves the visual position while converting coordinates. For RFF, an analogous canvas/view-relative light policy needs a precise transform and a stable relief-space convention. A positional light additionally requires a declared surface scale for attenuation. Absolute deep-fractal coordinates are not automatically a meaningful physical lighting space, and a visually preserved direction does not establish identical attenuation for a positional source. Keep any such conversion independent of high-precision fractal calculation.

**Do not transplant area-light promises into a normal-only relief renderer.** The articles distinguish a finite sphere emitter requiring path tracing and a compile-time feature from a direct-mode point-light fallback. They also distinguish emitter visibility, illumination, ray-jitter softness and actual sphere sampling. These are valuable semantic boundaries for RFF controls: visible glow, self-emission, direct reflection and lighting of another surface are separate effects. True area shadows and visibility require geometry/occlusion evaluation beyond an existing relief normal. They are not a drop-in extension of environment reflection or the current extra-light proposal.

The help's approximate 600 ms compile time, roughly doubled convergence and particular accumulation-frame counts are scene/hardware-dependent claims, not transferable estimates. Its maximum-slot wording and later discussion of 8+ sphere lights also need reconciliation with the current implementation before reuse. Likewise, statements that shadows hold at every zoom or that a PBR approximation is physically correct need finite numerical and scene limits. The hardness slider's described direction must be checked against the actual parameter transform and shadow formula; its name and examples are insufficient to choose a convention. Do not promote this documentation into evidence of a measured RFF speedup.

**Post-processing still consumes a budget.** The effects overview says post-processing has virtually no performance impact and is always fast. Applying an operation after fractal evaluation does not make its texture reads, passes, intermediate targets or memory bandwidth free. For RFF, benchmark at the actual target resolution and record the cost per effect, including HDR targets and tiled export. The claim that viewport, bucket and video outputs match is a validation requirement: test full-image coordinates, effect radius, tile borders/halos, color transform order and resource precision. It is not established by the help text. Bloom remains outside the requested ten-item ranking but shares these integration requirements.

Tone-mapper names in the help identify intended styles, not proof of a full reference pipeline. Match any label to the specific implemented approximation, input primaries/transfer function, exposure convention and output transform. A no-tone-map mode must still declare clipping and display encoding. Do not imply standards compliance or copy distinctive matrices/constants without the provenance checks already required by RFF's NOTICE policy. Existing RFF color processing must be compared before adding another named mode solely because this menu lists it.

**Decorative log-polar mapping is the strongest direct 3D-independent transfer in these effect articles.** The Droste topics explain radius ratio, periodic repetition, signed strands, tiling, independent source-image/structure transforms and optional nonlinear distortion. This reinforces the existing screen-anchored spiral proposal, not a new fractal formula. In RFF, specify valid positive radii and a nondegenerate ratio, center handling, negative/zero strand behavior and full-canvas anchoring. Mirror tiling can match edge values but does not guarantee matching derivatives or eliminate all filtering seams. A magnification smoothing control does not replace minification footprints near the rapidly repeating center. Keep source-image rotation distinct from log-polar phase and test their meanings against the actual coordinate equations rather than repeating informal camera/axis descriptions.

**Proposed validation:** illumination versus visible-emitter toggles, attachment conversion, unit/temperature round-trips, actual hardness direction, tone-map input/output contracts, full versus tiled post-processing, spiral seams and center stability during animation. This batch adds documentation constraints and 2D-transfer clarification; it implements nothing, runs no benchmarks and does not change the provisional ranking.
## Scene and parameter help: share environment sources without conflating geometry

**Sources read in full:** `data/help/topics/scene.ts` and `data/help/topics/parameters.ts`. These supply intended workflows and terminology. Statements about implementation accuracy, infinite precision or fixed compilation times remain documentation claims, not verified guarantees.

**Environment-source reuse reinforces the first-ranked relief proposal.** Scene help describes one solid/gradient/image environment consumed separately by background visibility, illumination, reflection and fog. For RFF, one source asset with explicit consumer strengths avoids duplicating environment definitions and lets a reflective surface remain lit against a quiet backdrop. Existing relief normals can support directional reflection without converting the Mandelbrot image into 3D geometry. Background visibility zero should have a declared output meaning: the article specifies black, which is different from transparent output. Specify alpha separately when exporting composited images. The help calls sky images HDR, but that word does not prove the complete decoder/upload/storage pipeline retains HDR range; the existing environment-adoption requirements still apply.

**Depth-dependent effects require depth evidence.** The article describes distance fog, direction-dependent sky tint, reflected-ray fog, volumetric scattering and stochastic lens blur. A flat 2D iteration field is not a camera-space distance field. RFF could use a chosen scalar mask for an artistic haze or blur, but should name the controlling field and approximation rather than presenting it as physical distance fog or depth of field. Relief normals alone do not supply reflected-ray path length, volumetric visibility, occluders or a focus plane. An optional height/depth model would be additional scope requiring its own units, sampling and visibility rules. Keep such proposals separate from the immediately reusable environment reflection source.

The documentation's policy that quality presets do not silently enable volumetric scattering is a useful general principle for RFF: presets may adjust the quality of an opted-in expensive effect without changing scene intent. Report compile-dependent availability and retain the accepted image while preparing a replacement. The stated disable-during-motion lens behavior is a preview-quality policy; exports must evaluate the requested effect rather than inherit transient interaction flags.

**Separate display-coordinate decoration from changing the iteration.** Scene geometry help lists pre-rotation, absolute-value modifications, Julia mode and many folds. These modify the mathematical iteration or its inputs; mirror/sector transforms applied only to texture coordinates do not. The previously ranked decorative symmetry proposal must preserve this distinction. Supporting a new formula in RFF requires new or verified perturbation, reference, derivative and MPA behavior rather than routing the change through a postprocess control. MPA uses periodic structure and is not BLA. A help article describing a generic abs modification as a Burning Ship variant of any formula is not sufficient to establish the resulting dynamics or algorithm support.

There is also a documentation-level hybrid-order discrepancy to resolve before reuse: scene help describes folds injected before the formula step each iteration, whereas parameter help distinguishes an initial separate fold loop from advanced interleaving. Those can describe separate modes, but the explanatory scope must say which mode is active. Its zero-compilation and 30–60 second recompilation statements are not measured current budgets. Base user feedback on actual runtime/compile classification and measured progress, not those fixed estimates.

**Precision language must match RFF's numerical model.** Recentring local coordinates can reduce cancellation but does not establish arbitrary-depth precision. Do not repeat the scene article's infinite-zoom guarantee or substitute an ordinary local/world split for RFF's high-precision reference orbit. Likewise, 3D formula examples with small iteration counts are not suitable defaults or limits for deep Mandelbrot rendering. Distinguish non-escape within a finite iteration budget from a proof of set membership when explaining results. Julia documentation usefully distinguishes varying C from varying z0, but its generic 4D phrase and three-component controls should not define RFF's complex-plane parameter domain.

**Low-risk workflow transfer.** Cursor-local parameter controls and LFO indicators can help explore palette phase, environment rotation or material masks while watching the image. In RFF, select targets by stable parameter IDs, display base and evaluated values separately, respect wrapped/angular domains and preserve deterministic export evaluation. These controls do not imply that every formula parameter is safe or inexpensive to modulate. Scope numeric shortcuts to avoid existing navigation/snapshot commands.

Proposed checks include one environment with independently disabled consumers, opaque-black versus transparent background export, preview versus export effect activation, documented hybrid order against generated code, precision-preserving view changes and modulation of appearance-only fields. No runtime checks or new implementation occurred in this batch. The findings clarify both immediate 2D/relief transfers and geometry-dependent longer-term ideas without changing the provisional top ten.
## Animation and graph documentation: define the domain before promising preservation

**Sources read in full:** `data/help/topics/timeline.ts` and `data/help/topics/graph.ts`. The positive smoothing branch of previously reviewed `hooks/useGraphTools.ts` was rechecked selectively. These articles describe intended editing behavior, not a new execution of the timeline or graph tests.

**Useful RFF appearance workflows.** The timeline help separates curve visibility from selection, groups related parameters, offers frame-preserving versus time-preserving FPS changes, and distinguishes manual keys from recording modulation. Those distinctions transfer well to palette phase, light direction, environment rotation and material-mask animation. Keep a hidden curve active unless the user explicitly mutes its contribution. When changing FPS, state whether times, frame indices, duration, playhead and Bezier time handles change together, and define collision handling instead of silently claiming exact preservation after quantization. A grouped capture should snapshot all intended channels from one evaluated revision.

**Several documentation promises require narrower wording.** Linear interpolation has constant speed only in the interpolated coordinate domain; logarithmic scale, wrapped phase and nonlinear shader response change the visible motion. Euler unwrapping can remove equivalent-angle jumps but is not a general cure for gimbal lock and can discard deliberate multi-turn intent. An affine retime with correctly transformed handles can preserve a curve, whereas key rounding, collisions, frame-zero clamps, nonlinear domains and local edits can break that equivalence. Exact Bezier insertion requires splitting the original segment at the correct parameter and updating adjacent handles; the earlier insertion-path review must take precedence over the help's unconditional no-shape-change claim.

The help calls positive smoothing Gaussian. The current `useGraphTools` branch instead calls `calculateConstrainedSmoothing` when r > 0; the negative branch uses the smoothing/bounce utility. Name the actual algorithm in RFF documentation and describe its domain and boundary constraints. Fixed neighboring values do not automatically establish tangent continuity or fidelity in logarithmic display space. Simplification and baking likewise need an error measure appropriate to the rendered parameter, not only key count or a raw-value tolerance. These points reinforce the earlier curve-processing findings rather than adding a separate feature ranking.

The deterministic-preview description promises an exact project-frame rate independent of monitor refresh. A UI playback policy alone cannot guarantee delivery when rendering or the host misses deadlines. Distinguish deterministic evaluation times and sample ordering from real-time playback throughput. RFF export should evaluate requested timestamps independently of how many interactive frames were presented, including modulation and random-source seeds. Frame stepping must explicitly specify output timestamps and duration; neither skipping frames nor a storage-mode name establishes that contract.

**Duplicate topic IDs are now concretely demonstrated.** Both the previously read parameter topics and this timeline file define `lfo.system`. The reviewed bundle spreads timeline topics after parameter topics, so the timeline article wins, including its category and parent. This confirms that collision validation is practically relevant rather than a hypothetical concern. Treat its maximum count and any-slider language as claims to match against the current registry and routing capabilities. Maintain one authoritative article or explicit aliases; do not let import order choose public documentation silently.

**Transfer graph authoring selectively.** The graph article describes typed operations, connection insertion, bypass, global parameter bindings, conditional iteration execution and manual/automatic compilation. The reusable idea for RFF's appearance work is a graph of existing scalar fields, coordinate transforms, masks and material consumers with clear socket types and stable IDs. A formula graph that outputs a distance estimator is substantially different: arbitrary folds, CSG or iteration changes cannot be assumed compatible with RFF's perturbation and periodic MPA acceleration. That would require separate numerical implementations and validation.

Even for an appearance graph, preserve input/output types when bypassing or reconnecting a node, validate cycles and resource dependencies, retain the last accepted shader on compilation failure, and keep parameter bindings distinct from local fallback values. The help explicitly gives different reconnect behavior for a node's close button and keyboard deletion; decide and document a consistent command policy for RFF. The article's runtime conditional controls and structural compilation claims should be checked against generated shaders before using them to promise no recompilation.

**Proposed checks:** compare linear/log/angle tracks; retain intentional full rotations; retime with collisions; insert and simplify around extrema; hide versus mute tracks; export with irregular preview timing; validate duplicate topic IDs; bypass a multi-input appearance node; fail graph compilation and preserve the last working image. None was executed in this documentation batch. These findings support controlled 2D/relief animation without treating a 3D formula editor as a drop-in RFF extension.
## Audio-reactive appearance: document the analysis and modulation contract

**Source read in full:** `data/help/topics/audio.ts`. This is an audit of documented behavior alongside the earlier audio/modulation implementation reviews. It does not verify device capture, current browser capabilities, named-algorithm fidelity or measured latency.

**RFF transfer.** Frequency-band links can drive palette phase, emissive intensity, mask thresholds or environment rotation without changing the Mandelbrot formula. Level-following suits gradual changes; an onset-like response suits short accents. A shared link model for audio and LFO sources can reuse target routing, limits and animation recording. Start with runtime appearance parameters whose cost and domain are known; an arbitrary formula or iteration setting is not an equivalent safe target. Keep the saved base value separate from the live evaluated value and define how multiple links, keyframes, gain and offset combine. The help's informal statement that offset prevents zero does not establish that composition order.

**Show measured bands, with honest resolution.** The articles describe logarithmically spaced frequency bands, Hz-valued selection, presets, a visible low-frequency resolution limit and separate overall/per-band normalization. Those are useful authoring concepts: a user can identify which measured signal drives an effect rather than adjust an unexplained percentage. Fixed examples such as 23 Hz/43 ms depend on sample rate and analysis size; derive labels from the actual configuration. Narrow display bands cannot manufacture frequency information absent from the analysis window. Treat an 8-bit spectrum's saturation and a source waveform's clipping as distinct diagnostics rather than assuming either proves the other.

The claim that the displayed bars are exactly what links consume needs verification across normalization, thresholding, interpolation and update throttling. In RFF, expose the selected band's raw/normalized envelope and the final modulated value when diagnosing a link. Apply attack/decay and smoothing with an explicit time basis so different preview frame rates do not change the response. Overall auto-gain and per-band balancing address different scales but can still interact dynamically; silence, a large onset and source changes need bounded recovery behavior. Preset frequency ranges are practical starting points, not guaranteed isolation of an instrument.

**Named transient detection needs precise attribution.** The article calls its method SuperFlux and describes comparison with neighboring-band maxima. That description alone does not establish the full published algorithm or its license. If RFF adopts a recognizable implementation, verify the original source, actual processing stages and license, then add matching code/NOTICE attribution. If using only an independently implemented approximation, describe its actual neighborhood/temporal comparison instead of implying complete algorithm fidelity. No external algorithm code or constants are copied by this documentation review.

**Separate analysis, monitoring and live-session persistence.** The help distinguishes file monitoring volume, live-input trim, input capture and two-deck crossfade. For RFF, make the analysis tap and audible output routing explicit so turning a monitor down has a predictable effect on modulation. A live-device session can reasonably survive an appearance preset load, but persisted artwork should not silently acquire hardware ownership. Preserve live routing only by a declared session policy and define what happens when the new scene lacks a target. The articles describe scene restoration while idle versus rig preservation while active; that is a useful scope distinction, not proof that every load path implements it.

**Video reproducibility is additional work.** A microphone or system-input envelope is transient. To reproduce the look offline, record resolved modulation or retain a supported source asset plus analysis settings, timing and initial state. Existing audio cache/clip findings still apply: a waveform thumbnail or remembered filename is not a durable source. Crossfade position, trims and transport alignment must be evaluated at output timestamps, not inherited from wall-clock playback. Preview monitoring behavior should not determine whether audio is encoded into the output file.

Proposed checks include silence-to-hit transitions, changing analysis size/sample rate, two links targeting one parameter, wrapped rotation targets, scene loads during live input, preview frame-rate changes and repeated offline exports from the same recorded data. These are validation requirements, not completed tests. Audio-reactive controls are a broader RFF authoring proposal and do not displace the current shader-effect top ten on evidence from this read.
## Rendering help completion: export quality depends on spatial and temporal contracts

**Source read in full:** `data/help/topics/rendering.ts` (608 lines). This closes the rendering-help file, not the entire documentation audit. Browser support, timing, memory limits and quality recommendations quoted in that file remain source claims; they were not verified against current platforms or benchmarked here.

**Strong RFF workflow transfer: inspect at output density.** The distinction between refining the present view, interactively previewing a selected region at export pixel density, and locked final export is useful when judging the top-ranked footprint filtering and relief reflections. A RFF preview should carry an explicit full-image rectangle and accepted settings revision. Changes to output dimensions or image geometry must invalidate that mapping. Show both region size and actual density so users do not mistake an enlarged low-resolution preview for export detail. Compare the region with the corresponding final crop, including sampling and color processing, before promising parity.

**Internal buckets and output tiles are different.** The article correctly separates GPU work buckets from separate saved image tiles. It says spatial effects can show seams across the latter, whereas post-processing occurs on each completed tile composite. This qualifies earlier help's blanket viewport/export parity language. Equal sample counts alone cannot guarantee seams disappear: full-image coordinates, jitter identity, reconstruction filters and effect neighborhoods also need agreement. RFF's image-layer footprints, mirror/spiral decoration and environment sampling must use the same mapping on both sides of a boundary. Effects requiring neighbors need sufficient overlap/halo or a full-composite stage; disabling an effect is a documented limitation, not successful parity.

The stated VRAM estimate is for one tile. A useful RFF estimate should distinguish render attachments, intermediate effect buffers, readback, CPU assembly and encoder queues. Tiling limits per-target memory but does not make total output arbitrary or unbounded. Streaming and backpressure remain necessary, particularly when SSAA increases pixel count quadratically. Fixed sample counts reduce stochastic noise only under the applicable estimator and do not guarantee a noise-free image or eliminate aliasing in unresolved texture fields.

**Material explanations reinforce source routing.** The file describes final-color, individual-layer, noise and constant-color emission sources. That supports the existing proposal to select emission independently of visible paint, without claiming indirect illumination in RFF. Metallic, roughness and specular controls require the actual BRDF convention: a fixed 4% dielectric reference is a model assumption, not every non-metal's universal reflectance, and rough microfacet reflection is not synonymous with Lambertian diffuse scattering. AO multiplied into emission/rim is an artistic compositing decision that should remain explicit. Raymarched scene reflections, volume glow and water geometry require spatial information beyond a 2D normal map; environment-only reflection remains the immediate transferable option.

**Quality policies need error and reset semantics.** Region accumulation and convergence feedback can focus work on a detail, but unchanged pixels outside the region may represent an older scene revision after parameter edits. Label or invalidate that history. A small change between successive images is a convergence heuristic, not proof of numerical correctness or absence of missed detail. Adaptive resolution is a preview resource policy, not permission to reduce perturbation precision or silently leave exports at a lower resolution. Do not import raymarch epsilon/fudge controls as substitutes for RFF's established calculation accuracy. The documented volumetric rate-independent final image also requires proper sampling weights and accumulation validity; the slider description alone cannot establish unbiased equivalence.

**Export channels need precise data definitions.** Beauty, alpha and depth are useful separately named outputs. For RFF, define alpha coverage, background treatment, straight/premultiplied storage and color encoding independently. A normalized depth image requires an actual chosen depth/height model, range, units and no-hit convention; iteration count cannot silently become physical depth. Avoid lossy storage for channels promised as quantitative data. Image sequences can support recovery and external encoding, but durable frame completion, missing assets, numbering and timestamps need explicit manifests or equivalent state. Codec/container availability should be queried from the active backend rather than inferred from browser names or the article's fixed bitrate and memory figures.

**Documentation collisions and conflicting statements are concrete.** This file defines export.video after the timeline bundle, so its Export-category article replaces the earlier Timeline-category version.
