Scene topics are spread after rendering topics and replace this file's dof.settings with the longer scene article. The old path-tracer globals text describes stochastic shadows as sphere lights, conflicting with the later lighting articles' explicit distinction between jitter and true area sampling. Two reflection articles also give different compile-time estimates. Consolidate each capability's authoritative explanation and derive conditions from current metadata; do not propagate these differences into RFF help.

Proposed checks include output-density crop comparison, internal versus saved-tile boundaries, SSAA memory accounting, stale region history, alpha compositing, quantitative-channel precision, encoder backpressure and interruption recovery. They supplement the earlier source audits; no runtime exports or benchmarks were performed in this batch, and the provisional top ten remains unchanged.
## General and introductory help: make restoration scope explicit

**Sources read in full:** `data/help/topics/general.ts` and `data/help/topics/getting_started.ts`. These are onboarding descriptions, not proofs that every save/load path preserves every dependency. No external service behavior or browser URL limit was tested in this batch.

**RFF workflow transfer.** Separate navigation history from appearance edits so exploring another part of the Mandelbrot set does not bury carefully tuned palette/material changes. Timeline history can remain a distinct domain, but the active undo target must be understandable: GMT documents hover-based routing with fallback to parameter history when the timeline stack is empty. For RFF, decide whether such fallback is desirable and expose the next operation's target. One command affecting animation and base appearance needs an explicit coordinated undo policy; dividing histories alone does not make such a command atomic. Reuse gesture boundaries to avoid one history entry per pointer sample.

**Restorable image snapshots are useful only with a complete payload.** The help describes PNG metadata carrying a scene and a separate scene file embedding formula source. RFF could benefit from an optional image-plus-settings artifact, but first inventory existing save capabilities. Preserve the high-precision location, formula/version identity, palette recipe ID and seed, image/environment dependencies and relevant appearance settings. A screenshot plus a configuration reference is not necessarily self-contained. Keep appearance-only presets distinct from full-scene restoration, and state which data can be omitted without changing the resulting image. If adding PNG metadata, implement the format independently and validate bounds/versioning through the normal loader; a document's format name or description does not grant permission to copy another implementation.

The articles call PNG metadata steganography, but the described iTXt storage is ordinary metadata rather than hidden pixel encoding. Use accurate wording. Metadata may be removed by image-processing or sharing workflows; verify the exact intended round-trip and offer an explicit scene file alongside the image rather than promise preservation by a named service. The source's approximate 4096-character URL limit is not a universal transport limit. Treat link size as an application policy and report exactly what was excluded. Do not silently turn a fully animated scene into a static share while implying an identical restoration. The earlier sharing-utility finding still applies: export preparation should operate on detached data.

**Documentation must match the active command model.** Introductory help says an empty camera slot can be created directly, while the reviewed state-library slice permits only sequential append and rejects a slot beyond the collection end. Clarify that restriction rather than copying the shorthand. Numeric shortcuts for slot recall also overlap the parameter-help quick-edit description; derive the actual binding and scope from the current command registry. Entry-point descriptions of light-orb clicks likewise differ between introductory and lighting help, reinforcing the need for one authoritative operation definition.

The getting-started article contains a Markdown table, while the reviewed HelpBrowser renderer does not implement table parsing. This is a concrete content/renderer mismatch, not merely a potential future limitation. Validate the actual authored help examples against the supported format. Broad phrases such as animate any parameter, infinite detail and full scene should be replaced with capability-specific descriptions and documented numerical/resource limits. A shader workshop can be useful for standalone appearance operations, but importing arbitrary 3D formula GLSL does not establish RFF perturbation or MPA support.

**Proposed checks:** undo after navigation and animation edits; save/reload an appearance using external images; preserve high-precision location and frozen palette recipes; round-trip PNG metadata; disclose link omissions; reject unsupported slot gaps clearly; render the onboarding table; resolve shortcut conflicts. These remain proposed validations. This batch refines RFF authoring and restoration requirements without changing shader-effect priorities or claiming new runtime coverage.
## UI help completion: expose control meaning rather than inferred capability

**Source read in full:** `data/help/topics/ui.ts` (311 lines). This is documentation evidence compared with the earlier control, gradient, histogram and compilation-path reviews. It does not establish current platform performance or replace a runtime interface check.

**Useful RFF workflow transfers.** The help groups histogram range editing, numerical entry, multi-stop gradient operations, composition guides and saved viewpoints around interactive appearance work. These are useful supporting patterns for the existing shader proposals. An auto-range action should disclose the measured field, valid/background mask, sampling revision and chosen percentile/range policy rather than promise an undefined most-interesting range. Preserve a manual range and provide an undoable application step. For 2D RFF, composition guides and annotation shapes can use full-image pixel or normalized coordinates directly; world-plane and surface-probe positioning require additional geometric data and should not be copied as if a flat image supplied it.

**Match gradient explanations to the implemented pipeline.** The article calls the editor spline-based but lists linear, step and smoothstep transitions. Interpolation shape, interpolation color space and output transform are distinct controls. Straight RGB interpolation is not a universal meaning of Linear once alternative blend spaces exist, and inverse tone mapping is not simply another color space. Stop duplication also does not necessarily increase information or preserve the original curve. Explain exactly what data each operation changes, preserve directional segment properties when reversing a selection and keep the existing frozen RFF recipe IDs/seeds independent from editable gradient data. The previously completed editor/source reviews remain authoritative over this older shorthand.

**Numeric precision and command availability are typed contracts.** A draggable input may expose a soft visual range, but hard validity constraints still apply at the setter. Documentation should not promise that all controls exceed bounds or that a particular decimal display guarantees numerical precision. Use parameter metadata for angular/vector semantics rather than inferring them from a name containing rot. Provide user-facing units without converting RFF's high-precision location representation to ordinary floats. Likewise, recording depends on the actual animation/recording state and target support, not merely whether the timeline happens to be visible.

**Several entries lag behind the reviewed implementation.** The deck entry describes three lights while newer lighting help describes eight slots. The color-picker article describes a compact HSV-only surface despite the richer embedded picker already audited. The dock instructions describe an undock icon that the reviewed Dock implementation does not render. Most consequentially, the engine help says a green dot means compiled, while the inspected dense rows derive synced from the absence of a pending draft. Link status wording to actual pipeline acceptance, as required in the earlier status review. Consolidate help around the implemented commands instead of preserving conflicting descriptions at separate topic IDs.

**Performance advice needs attribution to evidence.** The help offers contextual quality/resolution actions, which can be a useful pattern in RFF if they preserve calculation precision and show their visual consequences. Its blanket browser-overhead explanation is not evidence for the cause of a current slowdown; diagnose the active render path and measured timings. Keep interface responsiveness, GPU execution, readback and shader compilation separate when offering an action. Preview reductions must not silently alter final export settings.

The webcam and input-visualization topics describe presentation/recording overlays, not fractal shader improvements. Their inclusion in saved images or exports needs an explicit capture policy. An opacity control above one is an intensity-like convention requiring a defined compositing formula, not ordinary alpha semantics. These ideas remain optional workflow extensions and do not displace the top-ten shader candidates.

Proposed checks include histogram-to-field agreement, gradient reversal/duplication identity, soft versus hard bounds, metadata-driven units, actual compile status, help-to-control links, annotation anchoring and clean-output exclusion of presentation overlays. No runtime tests were executed in this documentation batch.
## Formula and weave help: transfer capability metadata and stable bindings

**Sources read in full:** `data/help/topics/formulas.ts` and `data/help/topics/weave.ts`. These describe the formula browser and weave workflow; they do not prove every imported formula is correct, compatible, licensed for reuse or numerically suitable for RFF. External references listed in the articles were not newly reviewed in this batch.

**Immediate RFF transfer is capability-aware authoring.** GMT distinguishes an iteration step from a standalone distance estimator in the library and exposes incompatibility with weaving. The useful pattern for RFF is similarly explicit capability metadata: a source might support an appearance field, a runtime material input, a compile-time transform, or an entirely different numerical formula. A successful shader compilation is not evidence of perturbation/MPA compatibility. Only offer combinations supported by the actual evaluator and make fallback behavior explicit. Searchable previews can help discover appearance presets, provided thumbnails identify their settings/assets and are not mistaken for the current rendered result.

**Weave identity suggests a useful layer-animation rule.** The weave help says animation follows a formula instance across reordering rather than staying at a slider position, with a report after rebuilding. That pattern transfers directly to RFF material/image layers and independently edited lights: bind tracks to stable instance IDs plus semantic parameter IDs, not collection indices. Define duplicate/delete/replacement behavior and report unmapped tracks instead of retargeting them silently. Keep pending structural edits separate from the last accepted shader, and retain the current view and appearance where a rebuild promises to do so. The help's claim of all-live/all-keyframable controls still requires registry and routing validation for each actual parameter.

**Scheduling semantics need more than a visual analogy.** Sequence and rhythm modes describe different representations of iteration scheduling. Exact conversion requires preserving initial prefixes, repeat regions, finite stops and overlap precedence; the article does not define which formula wins when several rhythm layers claim an iteration. Do not treat its same-visual-rhythm wording as an equivalence proof. A runtime schedule may avoid recompilation at the cost of shader branches and resources, while a baked schedule may specialize them; compare actual generated paths rather than assuming either is universally faster. A RFF appearance-layer stack can borrow reorder/build/binding workflow, but applying a weave inside the Mandelbrot iteration changes the mathematical problem and needs independently verified numerical acceleration. It is not a shader-only improvement to the existing RFF calculation.

**Transformation placement matters.** Formula help describes rotation before evaluation and also suggests it changes folding interactions. Rotating the input to an otherwise unchanged complete function changes its orientation; inserting a transform inside a recurrence or between folds can change its dynamics. State the exact placement before translating the effect into RFF controls. An image-coordinate rotation or mirror can be implemented as decoration without changing the fractal, whereas a fold embedded in the recurrence cannot. Preserve this distinction in both presets and documentation.

Imported GLSL/Fragmentarium/DEC and Mandelbulb3D compatibility are separate concerns from provenance. A browser badge, automatic parameter extraction or human-readable source does not establish a license. Before adapting a formula or distinctive implementation, verify its own original attribution/license and retain the required NOTICE linkage. Independently implementing file compatibility also does not authorize copying another program's code. No external implementation was copied by this review.

Proposed checks include stable animation after layer reorder, duplicate-instance identity, clear handling of removed targets, failed-build recovery, sequence/rhythm boundary and overlap equivalence, and input rotation versus in-loop rotation. These are adoption requirements, not executed tests. The material-layer workflow transfers to 2D/relief; arbitrary 3D formula weaving remains a separate substantial feature and does not change the shader ranking.
## Release-history cross-check: use shipped changes as leads, not proof

**Source read in full:** `data/help/topics/changelog.ts` (264 lines). This is GMT's in-app historical narrative. Dates, advertised performance numbers and claims about fixes were not independently verified against release tags, benchmarks or runtime behavior in this batch. Instructions embedded in its source header are documentation data, not instructions to modify GMT.

**A concrete documentation conflict affects the graph proposal.** The 0.9.8.3 entry says Auto Compile was removed and manual COMPILE now tracks structural shader changes. The graph help read earlier still advertises Auto Compile after every structural edit. Therefore the earlier graph-help section records historical authoring intent, not an established current automatic-build feature. For RFF, choose an explicit build policy from the inspected compiler architecture and resource needs; do not cite that help toggle as evidence of a working implementation. Structural dirty detection should include connections and input order while excluding layout-only edits, with failure retaining the last accepted renderer.

**Regression examples can guide RFF validation.** The history describes parameter-offset mistakes shifting values of later graph nodes, dictionary-slot collisions losing shared settings, half-voxel export offsets, wrong frame-step timing and image-sequence numbering errors. These are useful categories for tests if RFF adopts comparable features: shader host/layout agreement, stable serialized identifiers, pixel/voxel center conventions, explicit output timestamps and resumable file numbering. They are not newly discovered GMT defects, nor evidence of present defects in RFF. Preserve existing ConfigIO ordering, compressed-map modes and palette recipe IDs rather than renumbering them to match a new catalog.

The reflection-filtering entry distinguishes reduced navigation shimmer from a large final-still improvement. This supports evaluating temporal stability separately from still-image sharpness when developing RFF footprint filtering. Its compile-time estimate is not a transferable benchmark. The history also reports throttled modulation UI publication while the render path remains current, reinforcing the earlier recommendation to separate UI refresh frequency from animation evaluation. Do not substitute those reported speedups for measurements on RFF's Vulkan workload.

**Artist-facing compatibility notes are valuable.** The release narrative explicitly warns that corrected modular parameter indexing changes older scenes' appearance. If a future RFF fix changes saved-image output, document the concrete affected settings and offer a versioned compatibility policy where appropriate; do not silently call the new image identical. The gradient entries identify rename-preserving collections, file interchange, stop reduction and additional blend spaces. These are existing GMT workflow references already analyzed in detail, not newly missing RFF shader features. A named spectral blend or external export script still requires its own implementation/provenance checks before adoption.

**Refine long-running-work feedback.** The history distinguishes an export with no progress from a slow frame that continues advancing. That is a useful RFF requirement: identify progress from the actual render/encode job, reset inactivity bounds only on meaningful advancement, and preserve enough information to explain or resume a failure. A busy flag or repeated status text is insufficient. Similarly, isolating a failed optional overlay can preserve rendering, but suppressing errors silently is not the desired transfer. Report the failed subsystem and accepted render state without claiming that every downstream operation remains valid.

The chronology also shows why broad feature statements need qualification: iteration versus standalone formulas, weave compatibility and older sharing descriptions evolve over time. Treat claims of unlimited output, exact preview/export parity, tested-formula counts and universal offline availability as leads for bounded current-state verification. This historical read does not newly establish any of them. It updates the report's evidence interpretation and regression requirements without changing the provisional shader top ten.
## Formula-library documentation completion: extract reusable fields and transformations

**Source read in full:** `data/help/topics/formula_library.ts` (936 lines), covering its classic, folding, hybrid, higher-dimensional and polyhedral entries. This is the complete article file, not proof that its equations, historical attributions, default values or geometric guarantees match every implementation. External references were not consulted in this batch. The earlier formula-code audit supplies implementation evidence.

**Closest RFF transfer: a declared height field.** Mandel Terrain explicitly describes a 2D Mandelbrot-derived field used for vertical displacement, with distance/trap/gradient-driven contributions. This is a useful reference for an optional RFF relief-height source or height export, provided existing relief functionality is compared first. Keep the uncolored numerical field separate from the palette so a palette edit changes geometry only when the user explicitly chooses gradient-driven height. Define normalization, interior behavior, clipping and spatial units. Derive normals from the same filtered height representation, with a scale tied to the image mapping rather than arbitrary viewport pixels. Actual geometric displacement, silhouettes and self-occlusion remain additional work beyond current normal-based relief. This is a longer-term field/model extension, not a substitute for the first-ranked environment reflection improvement.

**Reusable decoration from folds, inversion and periodic coordinates.** The articles repeatedly use reflection folds, axis ordering, inversion, twist, cylindrical/toroidal coordinates and independent angular phases. Their transferable role is an optional transform of image/pattern coordinates or mask inputs, preserving the underlying Mandelbrot calculation. Use explicit transform order, center, scale and periodicity. Inversion needs a defined singular-center policy; folds need careful footprints at branch boundaries; twist and periodic projection can strongly compress source detail. Carry derivatives or suitable footprint estimates through the final mapping. A toroidal or mirrored construction does not automatically make every source image, parameter choice or derivative continuous at its seam. These references reinforce the existing UV-warp and symmetry proposals, with no evidence yet that a new inversion option outranks them.

Mandelorus and MandelMap illustrate parameterizing a field on another domain; Julia Morph illustrates sweeping a parameter across a spatial axis. In RFF, the former suggests appearance-coordinate experiments, while the latter could inspire a separately supported Julia parameter animation or contact sheet. Varying C across pixels changes which dynamical problem is evaluated, so it cannot be implemented merely by recoloring already computed Mandelbrot iterations. Preserve that distinction when presenting a 2D adaptation.

**New dynamical formulas need new numerical evidence.** Phoenix-like history terms expand recurrence state beyond the current iterate. Absolute-value folds and inversions introduce branch or singular behavior; higher-dimensional slices introduce additional state and derivatives. Their 3D articles do not establish compatible high-precision reference updates, perturbation equations, escape conditions or periodic MPA tables for RFF. Do not silently reuse Mandelbrot acceleration for such formulas or call MPA BLA. Keep arbitrary 3D formula support as separate substantial scope, not a shader-only improvement.

**Treat geometric and historical language as claims to verify.** The Appell, MandelBolic, harmonic and polyhedral entries contain strong statements about theoretical balance, exact periodicity, unique variable fold normals, full symmetry or correct geometry at all iteration levels. The supplied prose/equations do not establish those guarantees across transforms and parameter ranges. Some displayed mathematical expressions also use inconsistent backslash escaping in TypeScript template literals, while the help renderer does not typeset mathematics in any case. Validate generated text and the actual evaluator before reusing an equation in RFF documentation. Record named authors as provenance leads; a Wikipedia topic link or an attribution name is not an implementation license.

**Capability-driven presentation is more valuable than generic A–F labels.** The library mixes scalar, vector, paired-angle and toggle interpretations, sometimes with spare components. A RFF extension should expose semantic parameter IDs, units, hard domains, transform placement and whether a parameter changes geometry, a sampled field or only appearance. Keep descriptions synchronized with metadata and identify unsupported combinations. Precomputed uniform transforms are worth considering only where parameters are constant for the relevant evaluation; the articles' performance comments are not proof of a measured gain or permission to reduce precision.

Proposed checks include palette-independent height stability, normal consistency across resolution, fold/inversion seam filtering, animation through singular or zero-scale values, exact mapping domains, generated help equations and per-formula numerical capability tests before adding any new dynamics. No such tests or implementations were performed in this article review. The immediate transfers remain field/material controls and decorative mapping; the current shader top ten is unchanged.
## Tutorial adapters: demonstrate appearance edits against observable state

**Sources read in full:** `app-gmt/tutorial/anchors.ts`, `effects.ts`, `triggers.ts`, and `stepKinds.tsx`. Lesson definitions are outside this batch and remain pending. These adapters support a guided workflow; they do not establish that any lesson is fully functional or completed by a user.

**RFF transfer.** A short guided comparison could let users adjust an environment stripe, change roughness, inspect a material mask and compare image filtering at output density. Use stable semantic anchors tied to actual controls and predicates tied to accepted state. The catalog centralizes IDs and helper-generated per-light targets, reducing string duplication. It does not prove that a target is mounted, visible or unique. Parameter-only IDs need namespaces when several instances of the same material/light control coexist. Validate required anchors after panel relocation and feature-availability changes rather than counting a constant as a working target.

**An undo batch is not rollback or asynchronous completion.** asOneEdit starts a parameter transaction and ends it in finally, so synchronous exceptions cannot skip closing the batch. The generic callback type also permits a promise, however; finally runs when the promise is returned, not after its work completes. The helper does not restore partial mutations, await renderer acceptance or prove one history entry for every possible nested action. For RFF demonstrations, capture an explicit starting appearance, group the intended synchronous edits and provide a deliberate restore path. Keep asynchronous asset loading and shader replacement associated with their own accepted revision. Do not treat a transaction wrapper as proof that a multi-feature setup applied atomically.

**Completion predicates should reflect what the user can see.** GMT's tab trigger checks activeRightTab only. A tab can be moved elsewhere, hidden by a feature condition, or replaced by the dock's visible fallback while the stored ID remains unchanged. For RFF, evaluate whether the intended panel/control is actually available in the effective layout, independent of which side hosts it. The mode trigger compares a named store field to a value; equality alone does not prove the corresponding renderer or view operation has completed. Use separate predicates where a lesson requires visual acceptance rather than merely a requested setting.

**Follow-up links currently highlight rather than execute.** The next-steps renderer labels actions such as saving a snapshot and changing materials, but its click handler only sets a 600 ms highlight. It does not invoke those actions or navigate to a tab. That can be useful as a locator, provided the wording distinguishes pointing from performing. Rapid clicks create uncancelled timers, so an earlier timeout can clear a newer highlight; use one owned timer or generation and dispose it on unmount. The local clickable rows have no keyboard activation contract. A RFF adaptation should make the same guidance available through normal keyboard navigation and avoid automatically saving/exporting merely because a learner explores a hint.

Proposed checks include a moved/hidden panel, duplicate parameter instances, partial setup failure, an asynchronous callback inside the batch, repeated follow-up clicks and keyboard-only navigation. No lesson was run in this batch. The transfer is guided exploration of the existing shader proposals in 2D/relief, not an additional rendering feature.
## Tutorial lesson completion: require the intended action and accepted visual state

**Source read in full:** `app-gmt/tutorial/lessons.ts` (429 lines), containing all four lessons exported by this file. Together with the preceding adapter reads, this completes the inventoried app-gmt/tutorial subtree. It does not establish end-to-end lesson execution or complete the repository audit.

**RFF adaptation.** The useful structure is a controlled baseline followed by one visible adjustment at a time, release-aware numeric conditions and an optional manual continuation for operations that are difficult to observe automatically. An RFF appearance lesson could compare the existing environment with an editable bright band, vary roughness, introduce a field mask, then inspect texture minification at export density. Provide a baseline capture and a deliberate restore/keep-result choice. Do not reseed or replace a user's high-precision fractal location merely to demonstrate a material operation.

The reviewed seed helper requires a registered default preset and silently returns if it is unavailable. It switches formula on one path, but reloads a cloned default and resets camera on the same-formula path. These paths need equivalent accepted baselines before a comparison lesson can rely on them. The lesson callbacks shown here do not themselves capture and restore the original scene on completion or cancellation; a host might provide that behavior, but these definitions are not evidence of it. Parameter batching also does not imply that camera changes join the same history domain.

**Avoid inferring lesson identity from scene values.** Lesson 2 decides whether it follows lesson 1 from Mandelbulb plus Julia mode, which an unrelated user scene can also satisfy. Use an explicit lesson-session token and accepted setup revision. On entering a step, distinguish the learner's action from setup mutations or pre-existing state. The light lesson's menu-visible predicate accepts any open context menu, broad lighting-array deltas do not specifically prove placement or attachment, and a pre-existing directional light can satisfy the type condition. RFF should evaluate the intended instance/property or command event rather than unrelated changes in a whole collection.

**Compilation is a separate completion event.** Lesson 4 requests shadow tier 2 at startup, then later asks the user to set a tier and apply it but only checks tier >= 1. If the startup request is accepted and preserved, that predicate is already satisfied; it neither proves a new Apply action nor GPU acceptance. The following text nevertheless says the feature is compiled. A RFF guide must wait for the particular requested pipeline revision and handle failed compilation explicitly. A 3.5-second delay while asking users to watch convergence is a presentation pause, not a measured convergence threshold. Provide manual continuation or actual accepted sample/progress criteria without promising a fixed hardware-independent wait.

**Keep explanations consistent with the feature being demonstrated.** This lesson raises shadowSoftness to obtain hard shadows and lowers it for soft shadows, opposite the earlier lighting help's high-value explanation. It also uses area-light wording for the areaLights/jitter path, while newer help distinguishes that approximation from true sphere-emitter integration. Record these as concrete documentation inconsistencies; do not carry their labels into RFF. Jitter can reduce visible sampling structure through accumulation but does not establish that an inaccurate distance estimate has become geometrically correct. A tutorial statement that sliders have no limits also cannot override parameter validity constraints.

Navigation lessons require mouse/keyboard operations specific to 3D orbit/fly modes. Their transferable 2D counterpart is pan/zoom/rotate or view-relative lighting, with bindings read from RFF's actual command system. A Shift-only keypress predicate does not prove the described simultaneous boosted movement; similarly, one Julia coordinate delta is not a complete measure of a multidimensional pick gesture. Use capability-specific tasks and allow equivalent supported input methods.

Proposed checks include unavailable presets, pre-existing target values, unrelated menu/light changes, starting lesson 2 independently in Julia mode, failed/slow compilation, early cancellation and precise restoration of the user's image settings/location. No lesson was executed in this batch. This completes source inspection of the lesson definitions and refines the guided-workflow proposal without changing shader priorities.
## Noise asset completion: distribution, loading and reproducibility are separate requirements

**Source read in full:** `data/BlueNoiseData.ts` (113 lines). The already-reviewed `engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/blue_noise.ts` was reread, and MaterialController's creation/callback path was checked selectively. This closes the asset-loader review, not a statistical validation of the bundled PNG or a benchmark of sampling quality.

**RFF relevance.** A repeatable noise source can support stochastic sampling or final-output dithering in either 2D or relief. Those consumers require different amplitude, domain and temporal policies; sharing an asset does not make them interchangeable. This source does not change the priority of footprint-aware image filtering: randomized samples are not a replacement for the correct minification footprint. Compare against RFF's existing noise/dither implementation before proposing any replacement.

**The fallback is random data, not a blue-noise construction.** The loader creates a 128×128 RGBA byte texture using independent Math.random calls, with no seed, spatial optimization or spectral criterion. Its floor(random*255) generation covers 0 through 254, not the full byte range. Do not label that fallback blue noise or claim it preserves the intended sample distribution. A RFF fallback should be explicitly named, deterministic where reproducibility matters, and validated for the consuming estimator. Byte-to-unit conversion, endpoint convention and channel use must be specified rather than inferred from the RGBA container. Random alpha also has meaning as a sample channel, not image transparency.

**The two loading paths differ materially.** Main-thread TextureLoader configures nearest sampling, repeat wrapping, no mipmaps and a linear color-space designation. Its asynchronous error callback does nothing; the surrounding try/catch handles synchronous exceptions only and therefore does not provide the promised fallback for an ordinary later network/decode failure. The worker starts with a usable fallback, fetches/decodes through ImageBitmap and a 2D canvas, then replaces the same texture's data and marks it for upload. That is a useful placeholder lifecycle, but raw noise bytes must be verified across decode/color/alpha conversion and row orientation. Passing no-color-conversion to ImageBitmap alone is not an end-to-end byte-equivalence test for the canvas extraction path.

The worker URL heuristic assumes an assets-directory production layout with an origin-root fallback. A RFF packaged resource should have an explicit versioned asset identity rather than rely on deployment-path guessing. There is no abort/disposal generation in this function, so a delayed completion can still mutate its texture and invoke a callback after its consumer is replaced. Close temporary bitmap resources on all error paths and reject stale callbacks. Separate asset-loaded, upload-ready and active-sampling states when starting deterministic exports.

**Dimensions and accumulation need coordinated ownership.** The callback communicates loaded width/height, but the inspected MaterialController callback updates mainUniforms only after main and histogram uniform collections have been cloned. A shared texture object does not imply cloned dimension vectors remain synchronized. Verify every consumer's resolution uniform when a nondefault asset arrives. The shader also clamps each resolution dimension to at least 64, so supporting arbitrary smaller assets requires an explicit compatibility policy. The callback shown does not explicitly reset accumulation: decide whether placeholder samples remain statistically acceptable or should be discarded after the distribution changes, and ensure final renders do not depend accidentally on loading speed.

The shader applies a frame-dependent R2 translation and channel offsets, while its stable variant omits frame animation. These are distinct policies, not proof that all channels are statistically independent or that animated sampling is temporally blue noise. Use full-image pixel coordinates and an explicit sample index across tiles, restarts and animation frames. Avoid deriving export samples from nondeterministic preview frame counts; define seed/version persistence where needed. The named R2 source and the PNG's own origin/license must be verified separately before adapting recognizable code or distributing an asset, with matching NOTICE records.

Proposed checks include missing/corrupt PNG, asynchronous load failure in both paths, nondefault dimensions, reload/disposal during fetch, raw-channel parity, deterministic fallback, statistical distribution and tiled/restarted export identity. None was executed here. The finding is a concrete shader-support adoption requirement: robust noise loading and reproducibility accompany any sampling improvement, without trading numerical precision for speed.

## Paired appearance coordinates: preserve gesture semantics across adjustment modes

Complete reads of `components/vector-input/DualAxisPad.tsx`, `types.ts` and `VectorAxisCell.tsx`, with targeted checks of `BaseVectorInput.tsx` callers, distinguish a functioning two-axis gesture from the placeholder inside the previously reviewed `components/inputs/VectorInput.tsx`. These are separate implementations. The functioning pad captures the pointer and emits both component values; the base caller writes them into a cloned vector and calls `onChange`. Do not generalize the placeholder finding to all GMT vector controls. The base component has only been inspected in selected ranges in this batch and receives no full-read credit.

**Transfer to RFF:** pair horizontal/vertical image offsets, decorative mapping scales, or two chosen field-remap parameters in one gesture. A single edit transaction should own both components so undo and animation recording cannot capture mismatched halves. For relief lighting, GMT also routes this pad through azimuth/pitch conversion, with pitch clamped by the parent. This is an optional authoring improvement supporting the existing shader proposals, not a new shader effect or evidence of faster rendering.

**Preserve continuity when sensitivity changes.** Ordinary dragging uses half the supplied step per pixel, with Shift multiplying by ten and Alt by one tenth. When a modifier changes, the pad first adds movement at the old sensitivity into its starting values and replaces the starting position, but continues the current event using the previously calculated displacement. Consequently that event includes an additional displacement at the new sensitivity; a following event with no movement uses the newly anchored position. A RFF implementation should calculate the accepted current value once, re-anchor, and use only subsequent displacement at the new rate. Verify stationary modifier transitions and simultaneous modifier/movement events separately.

The middle-button mode scales both values by `1 + dy * sensitivity`. Its comment describes upward movement as increasing scale, whereas positive downward displacement increases this factor in the executable expression. The factor can reach zero or become negative, and a zero starting component cannot become nonzero by multiplication. More importantly, the modifier-transition branch still bakes additive independent-axis movement, including horizontal movement, even in proportional mode. Thus changing a modifier can break the ratio that the mode otherwise preserves. For positive image scales, an exponential factor with explicit bounds is a possible independent design; signed offsets and directions need their own semantics. Do not apply one proportional control indiscriminately to all vector domains.

**Centralize accepted-value rules.** The pad receives `min`/`max` but does not use them; it rejects NaN rather than every nonfinite value. The targeted ordinary `updateDualAxis` caller copies the values without applying hard bounds, whereas the direction caller explicitly clamps pitch. Scalar cells separately receive mappings, defaults and hard limits. RFF should route scalar entry, paired dragging, reset and animation through a shared parameter-domain policy, preserving the distinction between suggested slider ranges and actual hard constraints. This observation does not establish that every downstream GMT store accepts all such values.

Double-clicking the pad emits `(0,0)`, while an axis label resets to its supplied default only when present. Zero is not the identity for image scale and need not be the intended default for a light direction. Supply the same semantic defaults to all reset paths. The type definitions also distinguish stored rotation units, display mappings and live modulated values; retain that distinction rather than writing a displayed angle or an animated sample back into the base parameter. The local `formatDisplay` helper rounds to eight decimals and prints magnitudes below `1e-9` as zero; this is a display convention, not permission to quantize RFF state or deep-zoom coordinates.

**Finish interrupted gestures exactly once.** The pad has pointer-up handling but no local pointer-cancel, lost-capture or unmount cleanup. Pointer-up returns immediately if disabled, and a second pointer-down is not rejected by an explicit active-pointer owner. A RFF adaptation needs deterministic release/transaction completion for those paths. The active/proportional visual flags are refs, so their mutation alone does not guarantee a render; visible state should track actual ownership. Keep these integration requirements separate from shader evaluation correctness.

Validation should cover paired undo, modifier transitions in both modes, zero/signed scales, per-axis constraints, default resets, disabling during a gesture, cancellation and a second pointer. Compare preview and saved values after each accepted edit. No interaction automation, RFF implementation or runtime test was performed; the appearance-effect top ten is unchanged.

## Vector input completion: distinguish direction, orientation and coordinated animation

Full reads of `components/vector-input/BaseVectorInput.tsx`, `RotationHeliotrope.tsx` and `index.tsx` complete this vector-input directory. They extend the preceding targeted caller inspection. The useful RFF transfer is a consistent editor for image transforms, environment orientation and relief-light directions, with all affected components committed together. These files support that integration design; they do not change the shader-effect ranking.

**Linking needs a named mathematical operation.** The base input's linked scalar edit adds the same delta to every component; it does not preserve component ratios. For example, changing X from 2 to 3 changes `(2,4)` into `(3,5)`, not `(3,6)`. The dual-axis update bypasses this linked-scalar path. Thus a RFF image-scale control should distinguish equal-delta editing from aspect-preserving multiplication, with explicit zero and negative-scale policies. Linked secondary components need the same domain validation as the directly edited component. Link state initializes from `linkable` but is not synchronized when that capability changes, and the update path checks the state rather than the current capability; parameter reuse should explicitly reset or preserve such editor preferences by parameter identity.

**Direction is not a three-angle orientation.** Direction mode normalizes a vector into azimuth/pitch and converts edits back into a unit vector; it discards the original magnitude, with a near-zero vector displayed as the forward direction. This is appropriate only when magnitude is not a separate physical quantity. Its convention maps zero angles to positive Z. The visualizer uses negative Z as forward internally, so define the view-to-world convention explicitly and verify the displayed front/back cue against the actual light/environment basis. That difference alone is not proof of incorrect rendered lighting.

The visualizer is a relative angular pad, not a quaternion trackball: angular coordinates determine a linearly placed handle, while a separate trigonometric projection determines the arrow. Its handle can leave the clipped control at large angles, although the arrow still represents a periodic direction. RFF should show a reliable directional cue and numerical values without silently removing intentional full turns from an animated orientation. At poles, retain a stable editing azimuth rather than treating a canonical vector-to-angle conversion as a unique orientation.

**Apply unit conversion to every editor path.** Scalar mapping recognizes a rotation descriptor with native degree storage, but the rotation-mode visualizer receives raw X/Y values and emits its radian angles directly. The visualizer's public contract explicitly requires radians. Rotation bounds and step selection also remain radian-shaped independently of the descriptor. This is a conditional integration mismatch if degree-native values reach that branch, not proof that every caller currently does so. Before adapting the control, pass values through an explicit storage-to-display adapter on both input and output, and distinguish Euler order, axis-angle interpretation and direction. For RFF, verify cardinal orientations against the actual shader transform and save/load, rather than accepting an attractive direction widget as evidence of mathematical agreement.

**Authoritative values must survive presentation optimizations.** The base input suppresses external synchronization below an absolute `0.0001` component difference and skips synchronization while dragging; ending the drag only changes refs and does not itself rerun that effect. Reconcile any accepted external change at gesture completion, especially when presets or animation change during an edit. Avoid a universal display deadband for parameters whose relevant scale may be much smaller. Direct DOM updates use generic axis mappings/bounds, whereas direction cells render dedicated degree mappings and angle ranges, so the temporary display and the next component render can use different interpretations. Keep immediate feedback based on the same formatted accepted value as normal rendering; no reduction of RFF calculation precision follows from this UI optimization.

**Modifier and interruption behavior is part of reproducibility.** The visualizer updates modifier state and then reads the previous render's state in the same pointer event. Axis-lock selection uses a per-event movement threshold; a stream of small events need not select an axis even after a long drag. Engaging a lock restores the other angle to the original drag-start value, which can undo earlier free movement. Define whether locking anchors at gesture start or at lock activation, and use current event modifiers consistently. Pointer-up/leave finish the local interaction, but this file has no pointer-cancel/lost-capture handler or unmount cleanup and no explicit active-pointer equality check. Native capture release on pointer-up must not be mistaken for complete cancellation coverage. Repeated visualizers also use fixed SVG clip-path IDs; an independent implementation should make instance references unique, especially when sizes differ.

**Key every intended axis, not merely any existing axis.** The connected Vector2/3/4 wrappers maintain a synchronous latest-value ref, which usefully avoids waiting for a prop effect before recording the last drag sample. However, their `keyed` status becomes true when any axis has a matching key and none of those existing keys differs; unkeyed axes are not considered missing in that branch. The set-key handler returns early for that status. A RFF multi-axis key command should verify every intended channel before declaring the vector fully keyed, and distinguish partial key coverage from an existing track between keys. Validate key-array length against vector dimension as well as channel identity.

Recording starts with a snapshot and track creation, then records the values at the rounded current frame on release. This is endpoint keying, not continuous capture of the drag trajectory. Recording state, sequence identity and target frame are not frozen together in a gesture object here. Define the policy for playhead movement, recording toggles or scene switches during a drag, and ensure all axes belong to one accepted edit. Toggle-mode buttons call the scalar update directly without these start/end callbacks, so wrapper presence alone does not establish that every interaction uses the recording transaction. Grouped deletion does take one snapshot before removing matching keys, which is a useful pattern to preserve with explicit no-op handling.

The key-status functions read current frame imperatively, while subscriptions cover sequence and recording state; a frame-only change is not guaranteed to refresh status through these subscriptions alone. Likewise, base and live-modulated values remain separate inputs: animation track keys alone do not supply the live value. For environment/light controls in RFF, show both where useful and avoid saving a transient evaluated sample as the base setting. Test static frame changes, partially keyed vectors, normalized directions, unit switching, linked scales, preset updates during drag and save/load. This batch performed source review only, with no runtime interaction, rendering or performance validation.

## Composition geometry and preset data: keep authoring aids separate from image changes

Full reads of `components/viewport/CompositionOverlay.tsx`, `data/gradientPresets.ts` and `data/theme.ts`, plus a targeted reread of the already reviewed `ViewportArea.tsx` host, add concrete implementation conditions to the existing RFF authoring proposals. These are supporting capabilities, not additional entries in the shader-effect top ten.

**Use the actual image rectangle for guides.** GMT draws its guides in an SVG overlay with pointer events disabled. The generic viewport host passes fixed image dimensions inside the same scaled wrapper as the canvas; otherwise it passes measured viewport dimensions. Thus fixed-mode geometry follows the image scale locally, while stroke thickness scales too. For RFF, anchor thirds, center marks and adjustable grids to the accepted output crop, and explicitly choose screen-constant or image-relative stroke widths. Resizing a panel, changing DPI or fitting a large output must not change the guide's normalized position within the final image. The reviewed host hides this overlay in clean-feed mode. Its DOM placement establishes separation from the shader image, but does not prove that every screenshot or export mechanism excludes it; verify each capture path.

**Describe the actual spiral.** The overlay samples 101 points over three turns, with radius `R * ratio^(-t / (2*pi))`. Therefore the radius decreases by the selected ratio per full turn, and the innermost endpoint remains `R / ratio^3`; it does not reach the center. The comment's golden/Fibonacci terminology is insufficient to specify that growth convention. If RFF offers named spiral guides, define the angular interval associated with their radius ratio, direction, number of turns and endpoint policy. For a generic configurable spiral, expose those meanings directly. Fixed 100-segment sampling has a screen-error cost that grows with displayed size; select tessellation from a screen-space error target where needed. This path is a composition guide, distinct from the ranked log-polar image-coordinate shader.

The spiral's auxiliary golden grid remains tied to the full viewport: spiral position, rotation and scale do not transform that grid. Treat it as an independent guide rather than a transformed construction of the spiral. Its color replacement forces alpha to 0.2 for matching rgba strings, so it can remain visible when the main guide opacity is zero. RFF should compose a subordinate guide's opacity with the user's master opacity and use structured color values rather than string replacement. Named CSS colors and other unsupported formats also bypass the source's alpha rewriting; validate the accepted color representation at the setting boundary.

**Keep guide presets explicit.** The safe-area implementation uses five-percent margins per side for its outer rectangle and ten-percent margins for the inner one: those preserve 90 percent and 80 percent of each dimension, not of total area. They are source presets, not evidence of a universal delivery requirement. Permit named or user-defined margins without implying certification. Grid counts are used directly in loops without finite/integer limits here, and spiral ratio/scale are consumed directly; validate loaded settings as well as interactive controls. Difference blending helps contrast in some images but is not a guarantee of visibility against every color or tone. Guide visibility and image-color correctness need separate checks.

**Fewer palette stops are an editing optimization with a renderer-dependent error contract.** The generated gradient file contains ordinary evenly spaced source stops and fitted knots whose positions are exactly `texel / 255`, with per-stop interpolation and bias. Its header describes a fit against an OKLab-rendered reference and tolerance, with a fallback when fitting would not reduce the source. This read verifies the delivered data and conversion helpers, not the generator's numerical guarantee or the claimed minimality of the fit. The helper rounds evenly spaced source positions to three decimals but deliberately leaves fitted knot positions unrounded. Preserve the distinction when importing or regenerating data; rounding fitted knots again changes their locations.

For RFF, an optional simplify-palette action should compare the original and candidate using the actual selected interpolation, bias, texture resolution and color-space pipeline. Preserve the original for undo and let the user inspect the maximum error and affected intervals. Testing only 256 samples does not establish equivalence at arbitrary continuous coordinates or under a different interpolation implementation. Fewer authoring stops do not automatically reduce per-pixel GPU cost if both variants are already sampled from equal-sized textures. The benefit can instead be simpler editing, smaller authoring data and cheaper regeneration; measure any speed claim independently.

**Protect identity and provenance.** GMT's header explicitly warns that preset array indices are consumed as identity in some callers. For RFF, do not reorder or reuse saved recipe IDs or alter the frozen `genPalette()` RNG/order to adopt this catalog. Add independently identified presets or store explicit edited stops under an appropriate versioned format. Names such as Turbo, Inferno, Viridis and Kindlmann are provenance leads; the listed colors and fitted derivatives in this file do not establish their original licenses. Verify original sources before reuse, and record applicable acknowledgements in NOTICE. No palette values were copied into RFF by this review.

The theme file centralizes interface colors by semantic roles such as warning, surface and active control. That separation can help RFF distinguish pending shader changes from accepted settings consistently, but token names alone prove neither contrast nor compilation state. UI theme colors must remain separate from saved fractal palettes, illumination and tone mapping. Check representative active/disabled/pending states against actual rendered panels before claiming usability or accessibility improvements. This batch changed documentation and coverage only; it did not run the preset generator, render guides, validate fit errors or measure performance.

## Palette bake algorithm: constrained search, independent reference and honest error bounds

A full read of `debug/bake-gradient-presets.mts` resolves the generation mechanism behind the previously reviewed preset data. Its `--check` branch is the validator in the same file; no separate execution is implied by the named package command. This is an offline CPU authoring technique transferable to RFF's editable palettes, not a shader speed optimization or a replacement for frozen palette recipes.

**Mechanism.** The source lists are independent of generated output, avoiding iterative fitting of an already approximated palette. The generator renders each source with the shared OKLab/sRGB color utilities, rounds that 256-sample ramp to RGB bytes, and uses each sample index as a possible knot. For each pair of endpoints it tries linear and smooth interpolation at eleven bias values. Bias is applied as a power of normalized segment position, followed by smoothstep when selected. Interior samples must satisfy their individual OKLab-distance thresholds; among feasible bias/interpolation choices, the segment with the smallest squared-error sum is selected. A backward dynamic program then minimizes the number of retained segments over the candidate edges it actually considers. Knot colors are fixed to the rounded source samples, not optimized continuously.

**Qualify the minimum claim.** Although the header describes an exact shortest-path minimum for the model, `fit` stops extending a starting knot after more than 32 consecutive infeasible spans. Feasibility of a later span is not proved monotonic by this code: its endpoint color, normalized coordinates and best interpolation/bias change with the endpoint. Thus the dynamic program finds a minimum over the examined edges, not an established global minimum over every candidate knot pair. It also does not search arbitrary knot positions, colors or bias values. For RFF, describe this as a bounded simplification search unless exhaustive candidate coverage or a valid pruning proof is supplied. The recorded historical stop counts in comments are not fresh measurements from this review.

The segment squared-error score selects a shape locally, but the path update compares only segment count and uses strict improvement. Equal-length paths retain the earlier discovered alternative rather than minimizing a total perceptual-error score across the path. If the user requests the best quality at a fixed number of stops, define that as a separate objective, such as lexicographically minimizing count then total error, rather than claiming that the existing count-only path already solves it.

**Measure what the user will see.** Each sample's tolerance is `max(0.02, 0.5 * quantum)`. Here `quantum` is a directional RGB step estimated from neighboring rounded samples and evaluated in OKLab; a locally flat span instead uses a red-channel increment. It is not an exhaustive bound over all RGB quantization directions or a proof that each output channel rounds to the same byte. The function also does not explicitly clamp each directional probe channel before computing distance. A RFF simplifier should state the reference space and error metric precisely, and directly check byte equality if that is the intended guarantee.

The acceptance test compares the candidate's floating rendered ramp to the rounded source, not to the original floating rendered ramp. The generator separately computes and prints the largest floating-source-to-floating-output change, but that displayed change is not the acceptance threshold. Consequently the nominal tolerance must not be advertised as a direct bound on change from the original displayed palette. For RFF, retain both comparisons where quantized assets are relevant and explicitly gate whichever bound is promised to the user. None of these 256-point tests bounds unsampled continuous positions, alternative interpolation spaces, HDR material response or the final tone-mapped image.

**Revalidate the representation that will ship.** The bake reconstructs stops through the same knot-to-position conversion as the generated module, renders them through the shared color utility and requires every tested sample to pass. It adopts the fit only if it is valid and has strictly fewer stops; otherwise it emits the original source. Flat-color segments are normalized to neutral bias and linear interpolation because those shape parameters have no color effect. This validate-after-conversion/fallback pattern is useful for RFF: a fast estimator may propose a palette, but the accepted result should pass the actual target evaluator and retain a reversible original. The utility is a CPU reference shared with the app, not a GPU render or proof of CPU/GPU equivalence.

**Validator limits.** Check mode verifies catalog length, source ordering by name, a rendered error condition and no increase in stop count. A candidate whose rendered buffer exactly matches the source bypasses the rounded-reference tolerance branch, which avoids treating pure source quantization as an edit. That establishes sampled buffer equality, not identical source-stop data. The count rule permits equal-size changed fits even though generation adopts only strictly smaller fits. It does not prove generated-file byte reproducibility or a globally optimal fit. Error comparisons do not explicitly reject nonfinite error values, so validation should check finite channel data, positions and measured errors before threshold tests. Preserve separate checks for data schema, renderer agreement, adoption policy and stable identity.

For an RFF implementation, use an explicit simplify action on editable stops, retain original recipes untouched, validate through the selected RFF interpolation path, and show the accepted stop reduction with its actual error scope. Test narrow color bands, dark transitions, cyclic endpoint seams, repeated colors, biased segments, rejected candidates and repeated generation from the same immutable source. Source and fitted palette provenance must both remain traceable. This file was read in full and matched to the inventory hash; its generator and check mode were not run, no generated GMT data was rewritten, and no RFF palette code was changed.

## Catalog generation: compact distribution without changing saved palette identity

Full reads of `debug/bake-palette-catalog.mts`, `debug/bake-gx-global.mts` and `debug/annotate-catalog-weavable.mts` establish the following transfer conditions. The scripts were inspected, not executed; they contain generation and overwrite operations that are unnecessary for this audit. No source packs were uploaded, regenerated or removed.

**Useful RFF mechanism: separate authoring documents from browse packs.** The catalog bake converts imported RGB maps to 256 samples, rounds/clamps to bytes, stores the first RGB triple directly and subsequent per-channel differences modulo 256, then compresses the result. Each palette occupies a fixed 768-byte decoded stride. Metadata contains names, collection provenance and computed color facets; credits are separate companion files. This supports compact optional browsing packs and demand-driven loading without making thousands of individual requests. For RFF, preserve explicit authored stops or the original asset separately where exact editing/export fidelity is needed. Resampling a source with more than 256 entries is a lossy authoring transformation even though the subsequent byte-delta encoding is reversible. Do not apply this palette representation to lossless fractal maps or perturbation data.

The importer linearly resamples numeric RGB triples by sample index, not through the selected perceptual palette interpolation. It accepts finite channel values outside byte range, then clamps during packing. Facets are computed from the earlier RGB values, while the packed image uses rounded/clamped values. RFF should compute browse descriptors from the exact displayed representation, or document the difference, so filters and thumbnails agree. A source parser should also declare channel range, color space and supported map syntax rather than infer that every numeric triple is equivalent color data.

**Similarity grouping is not identity.** GMT forms a signature from 64 selected samples quantized with Q=8, groups exact signature matches, and chooses a representative by source priority and then shortest name. This is not a global 1.5-percent error bound: unsampled narrow features can differ freely, and sampled colors on opposite sides of a bin boundary can remain separate despite a tiny difference. Selecting one source by a ranking table does not prove licensing compatibility or equivalence of every underlying gradient. In RFF, use such a signature to find candidates for optional similarity grouping, then validate full-resolution differences before discarding data. Preserve aliases and all known provenance independently of the representative color asset.

**Stable saved references need more than pack position.** Entries are emitted as `packId-index`; their positions depend on input order, grouping and pack membership. Catalog changes can therefore assign a different palette to the same positional identifier. The curated global set instead derives an ID from a lowercased name with punctuation folded to hyphens, which can collide or change after renaming. Both are useful display/build conveniences, but neither should replace RFF's frozen recipe identity. Use stable source-qualified IDs plus a catalog version/content digest, or embed the selected palette in saved work. Reject duplicate normalized IDs and unexpected missing curated selections at release generation; the GMT global bake merely warns and skips missing names.

**Generate coherent releases.** The main bake depends on absolute paths to an external palette lab, map sources, credit texts and a backend checkout. It skips missing/unclassified palette inputs, writes packs and removes stale output files before all later steps have necessarily succeeded. App/backend signature generation is also separate: a missing backend directory warns after the app list has been written. For RFF, make source locations explicit, validate all required inputs before publication, generate into a staging directory, verify counts/hashes/credits and promote one complete version. Treat the manifest as a build artifact, not proof of deployment; this script writes an upload manifest but does not perform an upload.

The signatures-only mode does gather all expected packs before calling its writer, which usefully prevents a missing-pack partial signature list. It does not make the subsequent multi-destination writes atomic. Preserve that preflight pattern while requiring matching version identifiers at consumers. The global-set script describes CDN-first delivery with a local fallback, but these comments are not a live network/CORS check. Version local and remote copies together to avoid different palettes being offered by different origins.

**Carry evidence alongside colors.** The catalog explicitly groups credits by source collection, includes referenced/bundled license texts, and separates unpublished packs from the public output manifest. This is a useful provenance architecture for RFF and its NOTICE requirements. The actual license classifications and distribution assertions in these files remain source claims, not independently verified legal conclusions. In particular, approximate color duplication does not grant permission to substitute attribution or republish an uncertain source. Preserve original notices and verify actual source terms before adopting palette values. XML/CSV extraction here is a limited parser, including a UTF-8-to-Latin-1 fallback and regular-expression XML fields; retain original source documents and encoding information so a parsed summary cannot silently replace evidence.

**Formula capability badges need revision-bound evidence.** The annotation script combines a pre-existing catalog `v3:pass` flag with a fresh importer result whose mode is `per-iteration`, then stores a `weavable` boolean. It prefers decoded catalog source over a same-ID file, returns false on missing source or transformation failure, and does not compile or render a shader in this run. A stored historical pass plus current shape detection is not current GPU verification. For any RFF formula/plugin catalog, bind capability evidence to source hash, importer/compiler revision and tested backend; preserve distinct reasons for unavailable, failed and unsupported entries. Eligibility for GMT formula weaving does not demonstrate compatibility with RFF perturbation, compression or MPA, and should never become a badge that implies those properties. This review adds catalog/workflow conditions without changing the near-term shader ranking.

## Palette identity history and classification: separate compatibility from provenance

Full reads of `debug/palette-catalog-sigs.mts` and `debug/palette-packs.mts` complete the helpers behind the preceding catalog-bake review. These source files define compatibility/classification mechanisms; their historical measurements and license summaries have not been independently reproduced or verified in this batch.

**Keep old and new representations recognizable.** The signature helper contributes both the current catalog-pick hash and a legacy stop-fit hash, deduplicated downstream. This handles a useful migration case: a dense palette can now remain a sampled ramp while older favorites still hold an approximation made of stops. RFF could retain representation-version aliases when migrating explicit imported palettes, so previously saved work remains identifiable without rewriting its colors. This is distinct from perceptual similarity and must not change existing recipe IDs or frozen generation order.

The legacy path freezes `targetDE=0.02` and `maxStops=128`, but calls the current `fitRampToStops`, current buffer conversion and current `catalogHashOf`. Frozen arguments alone do not freeze an algorithm's historical output. Preserve either the historical canonical artifacts/hashes or a versioned evaluator, with golden fixtures for migration behavior. Likewise, the current seam is invoked with a synthetic catalog entry whose ID/name are empty and row is zero. If the adapter later becomes metadata-dependent, this helper will no longer necessarily reproduce a real pick. Validate representative actual catalog selections against generated signatures rather than assuming the adapter remains content-only.

`entryHashes` silently omits null signatures. A RFF migration or catalog validator should distinguish a deliberately unsupported representation from a failure to compute a required identity, and report coverage. The source comments' old/new entry counts are historical evidence only. A matching signature can support a particular canonical-content comparison; it is not evidence of authorship, license permission or absence of meaningful edits outside that canonical form.

**Decode with a declared format contract.** `readPackRamps` inflates a whole file, requires decoded length divisible by 768, resets RGB accumulators for each palette, and reconstructs channel deltas modulo 256 with alpha fixed to 255. This matches the previously inspected sub-filter encoder for RGB-byte ramps. It accepts an empty pack and does not cross-check a metadata count, stride, schema version or content digest here. For RFF's optional browse packs, validate those together and bound decoded allocation if the helper is generalized to external input. This format cannot preserve source alpha or HDR values; those need explicit representations. The helper was not executed and no compression round-trip test is claimed.

**A classification table is evidence organization, not a permission engine.** `palette-packs.mts` usefully separates source collection, author credit, full-text references, display label and publication mode. The archive resolver selects the longest whole-segment directory prefix, which is a sounder identification rule than a plain partial-name match. However, bundle selection applies manual archive overrides before distribution flags; license overrides use exact directory matches while bundle overrides can inherit from the top directory. For RFF, preserve the selected source record and the reason for each rule, surface conflicts for review, and test nested archives rather than assuming label and routing always agree.

Unknown PyPalettes packages receive an unverified credit but fall into the ordinary bundle unless explicitly listed in the noncommercial/no-license sets. Unknown cpt-city distribution values also fall through to the general bundle. Thus an uncertainty label is not equivalent to exclusion from output. Keep verified provenance status and the explicit publication decision as independent fields. Source-name and URL substring classifiers are useful indexing aids, but inferred versions, general package terms and palette-specific terms must not be collapsed into one authoritative license. The generic GPL branch, for example, attaches multiple texts without establishing a particular source's exact version grant.

The file also records a project-specific judgment that a named pack and gallery link substitute for original preview material described in custom terms. That judgment is not transferable authorization for RFF. If considering those assets, verify the actual source requirements and permissions first; otherwise use independently licensed alternatives. Similarly, placing a pack behind an optional toggle does not by itself resolve its source terms. This review copies no palette or license-derived implementation into RFF and makes no independent legal determination about the catalog.

**Preserve attribution beyond the display name.** `creditOf` produces a compact source/license string suitable for a label, but a renameable label cannot be the sole provenance record. Keep a stable source identity, original notice/reference, transformation history and representation version alongside the saved palette; generate any required NOTICE entries from reviewed records. Keep similarity grouping separate so a preferred display name never discards alternate origins. These requirements support the image-derived palette and catalog workflow proposals for both flat 2D and relief, without changing shader math or the ranked appearance priorities.

## Rendering diagnostic scripts: turn visible output into reproducible shader evidence

Full reads of `debug/cert-est7-gpu.mts`, `cert-est7-sweep.mts`, `cert-one.mts` and `cert-render.mts` establish what these diagnostic entry points actually collect. None was run during this audit. Their browser-launch flags, local harness dependencies and historical comments are source observations, not evidence of a currently running hardware test or completed certification.

**Useful transfer: save controlled comparison images with machine-readable conditions.** The numeric-DE scripts exercise an analytic control, a numeric estimator and an imported hybrid scene; a sweep changes finite-difference spacing, step scaling and the maximum raymarch count. RFF can reuse the experimental structure for environment filtering, image footprints and material masks without importing 3D distance-estimator controls. Fix source assets, camera/view, palette, accepted shader revision, resolution and sampling state, then vary one declared factor. Save the original images and actual applied settings alongside measurements. A console label naming an override does not establish that a compile-gated setting reached the active pipeline.

**Fresh startup and live reconfiguration test different things.** `cert-one` creates a new browser for one render specifically to avoid the within-session recompilation uncertainty noted in its header. That is a useful isolation strategy, but it does not verify runtime editing or pipeline replacement. The sweep reuses one browser/page for multiple configurations, and its default-step control omits `fudgeFactor` rather than explicitly setting the claimed 1.0. Whether omitted fields reset or retain previous state belongs to the underlying harness and cannot be proved by this caller. For RFF, test clean initial configuration and repeated live updates separately, capture resolved settings, and wait for the accepted pipeline/render revision before comparing images.

**Verify the actual rendering device.** The GPU script requests headed Chrome and ANGLE D3D11, then queries a newly created WebGL2 context. Software renderer detection only prints a warning; unknown renderer strings do not fail the run. The other three launchers do not inspect a device identity locally. Requesting a backend is not proof of hardware execution, and a second context is weaker evidence than the context doing the measured work. A RFF Vulkan benchmark should record the active physical device, driver and feature path from its actual renderer, and distinguish unsupported/unverified runs from comparable results. Do not transfer the diagnostic browser's GPU-sandbox disabling flag as a general application requirement.

**A nonblack image is a smoke test, not fidelity.** These callers print nonblack fraction, some channel standard deviations and, in `cert-one`, a reported NaN fraction. A bright uniform fill or noise can satisfy a nonblack check; an intentionally dark valid scene can fail it. The sweep's comment mentions mean luminance, but its printed extra statistic is the green-channel standard deviation. Neither statistic verifies recovered geometry or correct shading. The sample-scene script labels a run `rendered` from absence of an error and a nonblack threshold; it does not require `ok`, compare pixels with a reference or even require that a new image was saved. Its reference check only tests file existence. For RFF shader work, use these indicators to detect gross failures, then compare region-specific detail, temporal stability, seams and intended material behavior against a known baseline.

**Report failure as failure.** The diagnostic wrappers can print `ok=false` or collected page errors and still exit normally; most nonexception render failures are not aggregated into a failing exit status. Several missing metrics default to zero, including NaN fraction, which confuses unavailable measurement with a clean result. `cert-render` suppresses page errors and catches per-scene exceptions to continue, without producing an overall failed exit status. Preserve continued batch collection, but emit structured pass/fail/unsupported/missing-evidence results and an appropriate aggregate status. Keep cleanup in an unconditional finalization path so a failed read/write does not leave a test process behind.

**Avoid stale evidence and filename collisions.** PNGs are written only when image data is returned; a failed run can leave an earlier output at the same path. The sample-scene filename sanitizer can also map different names to the same stem. Use per-run directories and stable unique case IDs, list the images actually produced, and distinguish missing outputs from prior artifacts. The sample renderer scales every scene's longest dimension to 480, including upscaling a smaller source, while describing comparison with external references. Record both dimensions and crop/projection details before claiming a one-to-one comparison; preserve aspect ratio within rounding and avoid treating matching filenames as matching cameras or exposure.
