For RFF extensions, make one-time registration/lifetime explicit and keep default initialization separate from loading an authored scene. Node-layout positions can be retained for editing without confusing them with render topology or polluting unrelated native-formula presets.

**Profile the layer whose cost is being claimed.** `BenchProfiler` conditionally installs React's Profiler callback from a page-init hook; without it, it returns its children through a fragment. That avoids Profiler instrumentation in the ordinary path, but the component and callback lookup still exist, so the header's zero-overhead phrase should not be read as a measured literal zero. These callbacks measure React rendering/commit-related work, not Vulkan GPU execution, shader compilation or total frame presentation. An RFF comparison should separate editor responsiveness, CPU preparation and GPU work instead of crediting a UI-cache improvement as a fractal-shader speedup.

## Camera utilities and saved-view slice: transfer navigation workflow without collapsing RFF precision

Fully read: `engine-gmt/utils/CameraUtils.ts` and all 584 lines of `engine-gmt/store/cameraSlice.ts`. This is source-level review; bookmark recall, undo, rendering and saved-file round-trips were not exercised.

**Useful RFF transfer: capture the live view at the save boundary.** `flushCameraToStore()` reads the current viewport camera rather than waiting for a debounced store update, combines local displacement with the low offset components and normalizes the result before saving. The transferable idea is to save the view the user actually selected, with a coherent revision, rather than an older settings snapshot. RFF should do this using its existing arbitrary-precision location representation and reference/map contracts. Coordinate capture and asynchronous screenshot capture must identify the same requested view; a thumbnail arriving later is not itself proof of that association.

The saved-camera payload includes position, quaternion, split offset, target distance and optics, and the apply path restores camera state and optics while resetting accumulation. This is a useful checklist for capture/recall symmetry. For 2D RFF bookmarks, decide explicitly whether the item stores location/scale only or also coloring/material/lighting; do not accidentally turn a view bookmark into a partial scene preset. Existing RFF saving facilities remain the starting point, not a reason to add a duplicate library.

**The unified-coordinate bridge is not a deep-zoom representation.** `CameraUtils.getUnifiedPosition()` adds high, low and local components into JavaScript numbers; teleport/capture paths then split that rounded number again. Re-splitting cannot recover information lost during the sum. The camera slice's claim about reconstructing the captured double addresses that intermediate value, not preservation of every original split component or arbitrary-precision coordinates. Even a rotation-only utility rebuilds position through this bridge. RFF must preserve mathematical center/scale independently when rotating a decorative map or changing a 3D-style view. Do not use this conversion path for saved deep locations, perturbation references or map identity.

The utility returns zero position or identity rotation when no camera is available, and distance is the local camera-vector length above 0.001, which is not generally a surface distance or the orbit radius after the local coordinate is recentered. A missing camera should be distinguishable from an intentionally centered view in any RFF adaptation. `teleportRotation()` checks NaN inputs but not infinities; its default Euler convention also needs to remain explicit when other light paths use YXZ. The underlying orientation can be preserved with quaternions while providing a defined editable Euler representation.

**A modified marker should compare its promised payload.** `isCameraModified()` compares summed offsets, quaternion components and only three optics fields (projection type, orthographic scale, FOV). It does not compare targetDistance or the rest of the captured optics. Thus an unchanged marker is not proof that the complete saved payload equals the live state. Quaternion q and -q encode the same orientation but differ under component-wise subtraction. For RFF, define whether the marker means numerical state changed or visible view changed, include the intended fields, and use an orientation comparison invariant to quaternion sign where appropriate. None of GMT's fixed tolerances is suitable as an RFF deep-zoom equality test.

The at-default check uses `max(0.05, coordinate-magnitude * 1e-4)` as its position tolerance and ignores optics/target distance. That can serve a coarse recovery prompt, not certify a visual no-op at all scales. The one-world-unit Step Back action is likewise a 3D navigation heuristic. A 2D recovery operation should instead use meaningful zoom/location history or viewport-relative movement with preserved precision. Do not equate mathematical Mandelbrot zoom with a camera's physical dolly distance.

**Snapshot ownership and history categories are worth retaining.** Capture creates fresh objects, but recall installs snapshot rotation/offset objects directly into live state and relies on immutable writers. A future mutable writer could alter the saved view. RFF should own/deep-copy the necessary value state or use explicitly immutable snapshots. GMT separates navigation undo from edits to the saved-camera library: the latter registers a normal parameter-history provider, and deletion is bracketed in one transaction. This separation avoids a navigation undo unexpectedly deleting a bookmark. The provider returns live array references here, so final snapshot isolation depends on the history infrastructure, not this callback alone.

The installer subscribes to teleport events to retain the latest early request until the renderer is ready, which is useful for scene loads before viewport initialization. That queued request still needs a clear lifetime/revision when adapted to RFF. The installer has no local repeat-install guard and wraps existing undo/redo actions, so its one-time lifecycle is material. Thumbnail capture center-crops to 128-pixel JPEG and returns undefined on errors; it does not preserve the whole composition or prove a completed matching frame. Its comment calling history-thumbnail memory small relies on assumptions about image and library size: a 50-entry history bound alone does not bound bytes independently of the number of saved views. Keep preview assets separate from mathematical correctness and measure memory if this workflow is expanded.

Finally, depth fallback conditions are not uniform in this file: capture selects a measured distance only when it lies in (0,1000), whereas flush rejects only <=0 or >=1000 and thus does not explicitly reject NaN. For any RFF depth-dependent control, require finite, semantically valid data from the correct frame and distinguish orbit distance from a sampled surface depth. This is an integration requirement for the proposed workflow, not a license to change RFF's numerical algorithms or a claim that these GMT source observations were reproduced interactively.

## Weave scheduling adapter and synthesized scenes: preserve operation semantics across composition

Fully read: `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/weaveSequencer.ts`, `sceneSynth.ts`, and `importM3pFile.ts`. Targeted searches in the loader and fused emitter confirmed current calls to camera/lighting mapping; those larger files are not credited as full reads in this batch. No import or shader execution was performed.

**RFF transfer: an operation schedule is separate from the operation's mathematics.** The adapter converts six MB3D iteration counts and wrap bounds to a shared counts plan/LUT emitter. It explicitly distinguishes alternate ordering from interpolation, distance-estimator combination/CSG and KIFS modes. Returning an order for the latter modes does not implement their blending or distance semantics; the caller must enforce support. For RFF, ordered decorative UV/material operations could use a similarly explicit sequence, with any noncommutative operation order saved and reproducible. This is not a shortcut for adding new Mandelbrot formulas: those would require suitable reference, derivative and perturbation mathematics. RFF's periodic-structure-based MPA is not this iteration scheduler and must not be described as BLA or replaced by a counts LUT.

The adapter returns the original mode separately while constructing a spec with mode zero. Dropping the separate result would therefore lose the unsupported-mode distinction. It reads six slots regardless of `formulaCount`; mode zero derives EndTo from the last nonzero count. The RepeatFrom expression bounds the requested index by a discovered nonempty endpoint, but does not itself ensure that the chosen earlier index is nonempty. The shared scheduler's handling of skipped/empty slots remains necessary. An RFF composition format should validate supported modes and bounds explicitly, and retain both the introductory sequence and repeat segment rather than flattening everything into a generic loop.

**Pure scene construction is a useful migration/test boundary.** `sceneSynth.ts` constructs scene objects without importing the live store, allowing migration and tests to share a deterministic scaffold. Its missing camera basis, empty lights and zero scene-DE/reflection fields intentionally request downstream defaults, not faithful reconstruction of an authored scene. RFF could use a comparable pure normalization stage before publishing shader settings, while distinguishing absence from a deliberate zero/off value. The synthesized header's default iteration count of 32 is an authoring default, not a recommended Mandelbrot quality setting.

These helpers do not validate slot/count inputs: a multi-slot scene can carry more than six slots although the adapter reads only six; a positive fractional or infinite iteration input passes the current condition; RepeatFrom is bit-masked to four bits. Slot arrays/objects are passed through by reference rather than cloned. Before using this pattern in RFF, establish accepted ranges, ownership and versioning at the public boundary. Silent bit wrapping or truncation must not change a saved procedural composition. Pure construction aids testing, but purity with respect to the store does not imply immutable ownership of inputs.

**Import completion should report actual outcomes.** `importM3pFile.ts` opens a hidden input under a user gesture, reads bytes asynchronously and calls the loader. Its success message always says camera, lighting and color use GMT defaults, although the current fused emitter calls both mapMB3DCamera and mapMB3DLighting and installs available mapped values. The message cannot accurately distinguish mapped, approximated, missing and defaulted fields. A future RFF compatibility path should report those outcomes from the importer result instead of hard-coding a blanket success claim. A returned loader success is also not proof of completed shader compilation or a matching rendered image.

The input is removed in the change handler, but this file has no explicit cancel-event cleanup; a cancelled picker that produces no change is not handled locally. File extension filtering is a picker hint, not content validation, and the generic exception message attributes failure to an unsupported format without classifying the actual cause. For RFF, use separate parse/unsupported-feature/compile outcomes and retain a valid previous scene on failure where feasible. These are transferable boundary requirements, not authorization to repair GMT or implement MB3D compatibility now. Distinctive source-derived constants and conversions still require provenance/license review before adoption.

## Formula-library overlay and catalog: expose capability without overstating mathematical fidelity

Fully read: `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/mb3dFormulaLibrary.ts`, `mb3dCatalog.ts`, and `mb3dSceneThumbs.ts`. The large generated corpus imported by the library is not credited by reading its import; it still requires its own full audit. No oracle, transpilation, GPU compile or render was run in this batch.

**Detailed shader mechanism: exponent-based folding is a decorative 2D candidate, not a precision shortcut.** The manually supplied Amazing Surf 2 body scales x/y, optionally takes absolute values, extracts sign/exponent bits and replaces the remaining magnitude with a normalized significand in its inner branch. It applies a triangular fold and an exponent-parity sign flip, then continues through rotation, sphere-inversion-related scaling and the c-add tail. This creates folds tied to binary magnitude intervals rather than a single spatial repeat period. A separately authored, explicitly decorative 2D UV treatment could explore that visual idea; it is not an appropriate transformation of RFF's mathematical Mandelbrot coordinates or perturbation equations. Its derivative discontinuities also make footprint-aware filtering and fold-boundary tests necessary.

The code translates float64 bit manipulation to float32 layout. The header's claims of byte-exact verification and a nonzero maximum absolute error need a precise oracle/rounding interpretation; neither alone proves equality of iterated or rendered results. `highp int` supports the bit representation operations but does not make all floating-point edge behavior identical across devices. With an enabled bend bit, the expression involving v/abs(v) has no explicit zero guard; scale is later used as a divisor without a local nonzero check. Zero, signed zero, subnormal, very large and non-finite inputs need defined behavior before adoption. Source comments describing tested edges are not substitutes for inspecting/running the corresponding validation. Preserve the original operation order unless a separate equivalence argument supports a rewrite.

**Distance-estimator tuning is distinct from formula equivalence.** The same file supplies a per-formula override from a raw r/dr-style estimator to an offset (r-2)/dr-style estimator, with a separately tuned stepping factor. This affects where marching stops and the rendered surface; it is not merely a faster implementation of an unchanged distance estimator. The comments cite an owner-verified appearance, not a general conservativeness proof. RFF should keep any future artistic relief/DE approximation explicit and never infer that a decompiled formula's arithmetic cross-check certifies its raymarching quality or makes it compatible with MPA. Verify known origin and actual licensing before adapting distinctive generated or hand-translated bodies; this batch does not establish permission to copy them.

**The generated-plus-manual overlay is maintainable only if its records remain coherent.** Manual dictionaries are spread after generated dictionaries separately for bodies, options, DE metadata, defaults and scratch declarations. This protects a hand port from being overwritten by regeneration. However, precedence is per dictionary: the manual scratch map is empty, so a future same-name generated scratch entry would still survive while the manual body wins. A corresponding RFF shader-module library should validate one coherent record per stable identifier, with explicit provenance, supported domains, parameters and validation status. Do not assume a body override automatically overrides every associated metadata field.

**Catalog inclusion is weaker than successful rendering.** `getMB3DCatalog()` dry-runs the transpiler for generated entries at authored defaults and excludes an explicitly named empty standalone case. It does not compile the resulting shader, render every entry or validate all editable parameter combinations. The five built-in entries are inserted without that dry-run filter. A successful catalog count therefore describes this selection process, not a count of fully verified GPU formulas. Name-derived categories are browsing heuristics and cannot establish mathematical family, standalone suitability or 2D portability. The separate stored loader reference usefully avoids relying on prettified display labels as identity.

For RFF's possible material/UV operation browser, distinguish independently useful effects from transforms that need a host composition, and expose unsupported cases before applying them. Keep 'available', 'compiled' and 'visually validated' separate. The memoized catalog returns mutable arrays with no invalidation in this file, which is fine only under a stable corpus/ownership contract; dynamic registration would need a revision or rebuild. `slotFromCatalogEntry()` copies option arrays, an appropriate boundary against edits mutating library defaults, while fallback empty defaults should still be validated before activation.

The thumbnail helper derives filenames by replacing every non-ASCII-alphanumeric character with an underscore. Different scene names can therefore collide, and on case-insensitive storage additional names can share a destination. A missing thumbnail intentionally leaves a loadable entry, which is a useful distinction: absence of a preview should not automatically mean unsupported functionality. For RFF, prefer a stable unique asset identifier and keep thumbnail availability separate from shader/preset validity; do not use a sanitized display name or attractive preview as a correctness certificate.

## Constant packing and live bindings: precompute invariant shader work while preserving semantics

Fully read: all 431 lines of `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/constPacker.ts`. No shader was generated, compiled or timed in this batch. Its source-derived offset/constant claims require the original-source and license checks described elsewhere before adaptation.

**Concrete optimization mechanism for RFF: derived rotation inputs.** Angle options retain editable scalar/vector lanes, but their shader operands reference CPU-derived sin/cos pairs, 3-by-3 Euler matrices or 4-by-4 six-plane matrices. `DerivedRotationSpec` records the source components and conversion; a separate manager updates the resulting uniforms. This removes angle conversion and matrix construction from per-fragment/per-iteration formula bodies. The same pattern is useful for RFF's image/UV transformations and environment/light orientation when uniform over the draw. Cache by actual input revision, including animation/export inputs, and compare the final transform rather than assuming CPU/GPU transcendental results are identical. No speedup percentage is established by this source review.

The mapper explicitly translates a flat row-major matrix element j into GLSL column/row indexing. That small detail is essential to preserving orientation when moving work between CPU and shader. An RFF implementation must also match C++ storage layout, shader matrix convention and upload rules; correct symbolic indices alone do not prove the bytes match. The bank limits are six mat3, six sin/cos and two mat4 derived records. Sharing an allocator across composed slots avoids collisions, but exceeding a bank leads to fallback, not unlimited live rotation capacity.

**Two representations of the same option need differential verification.** `packConstBuffer()` walks byte offsets from a fixed prelude, applying scalar, angle, matrix, square, reciprocal and folding transforms. `bindOptions()` mirrors that walk while producing live GLSL expressions or baked literals per option. Multi-angle options consume three or six raw values but one logical label; a folding type reserves an additional pointer-sized gap without a numeric binding. This is a useful design for separating author-facing parameters from shader-ready data, but offsets must follow the original format rather than a convenient packed C++ struct.

A notable semantic difference is visible in box-scale handling. The numeric/baked path clamps the minimum radius before squaring using 1e-40; the live expression uses 1e-9, and its initial slider value clamps negatives to zero. The corresponding squared denominators differ greatly near zero, and an extremely small baked literal may underflow in a float32 shader. Sharing the same byte-offset walk therefore does not prove numeric equivalence. For RFF, toggling a material/UV control between fixed specialization and editable uniform should not silently change its domain, clamp or result. Test boundary values in both paths and keep any intended approximation explicit; never propagate this kind of precision change into Mandelbrot computation.

Other domain details are similarly material. Reciprocal options replace sufficiently small magnitudes with a positive floor, so tiny negative inputs lose their sign in that fallback. SINGLE versus DOUBLE controls change offset stride but the host map still contains JavaScript numbers rather than typed byte writes at those points. Integer defaults are rounded by Math.round, while live bindings read the lane directly and rely on the control/update path to keep it integral. Literal formatting has no local finite-value rejection. These distinctions should be validated at the import/parameter boundary, not inferred from the comments calling the packing exact.

**Packing for storage is not grouping by meaning.** Consecutive named X/Y/Z options can be exposed as one true vec3 even when their input order is Z/Y/X; each binds to its named component. Unrelated scalars also share spare vector components through a separate allocator. For RFF, retain labels and stable semantic identifiers independently of physical storage. Name-pattern grouping is a convenience heuristic, not a substitute for typed metadata: an integer default of zero/one is not necessarily a Boolean domain, and a default scalar range of [-8,8] does not establish valid limits for every formula. Preserve authored values and explicitly state units/ranges for new controls.

Allocation failure returns null after allocations may already have occurred in the supplied allocator. This file does not roll those reservations back. Callers using a shared allocator must therefore make fallback transactional, restore a snapshot or intentionally account for consumed capacity. This is an integration obligation, not a confirmed end-to-end defect from this file alone. The separation between baked and live options should also remain visible to users when it changes editability or triggers recompilation.

**Distance metadata remains approximate compatibility mapping.** `mapDEMeta()` routes dIFS to a special running-distance estimator, log and Julia flags to one analytic estimator, and other cases to a raw estimator. Its own comment states there is no exact GMT analogue for the Julia expression. It clamps step scale and bailout, with the implementation's general bailout ceiling at 1e7 despite older prose mentioning 1000; the dIFS branch separately fixes 1000. A running minimum over a finite set of visited iterations does not by itself prove a conservative bound to all later surfaces. These choices require formula-specific validation and are not transferable quality constants for RFF. Keep this compatibility mechanism separate from RFF's MPA, reference compression and numerical precision guarantees.

## Slot transpiler: preserve iteration state and distinguish editable code generation from verified mathematics

Fully read: all 522 lines of `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/slotTranspiler.ts`. No generated shader was compiled or executed. Source comments claiming agreement with MB3D are provenance pointers and historical claims, not independent numerical verification in this batch.

**RFF transfer: explicit state contracts make composed shader operations safer.** Each generated slot receives position, derivative, trap and c by reference; external formulas can additionally receive persistent scratch fields. In particular, c-mixing operations must carry the modified c into later iterations rather than silently reseeding it. Four-dimensional formulas may use w as a spatial coordinate and a separate scratch derivative, while other formulas use w as the derivative. The wrapper selects this role from DE metadata and scratch declarations. A RFF material/UV composition can benefit from equally explicit input/output meanings; a shared vec4 lane must not ambiguously alternate between color, coordinate and validity data. This does not establish compatibility with RFF's Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA equations.

**The actual caller resolves the earlier allocator concern for this path.** The previous constant-packer section warned that a failed bind could consume reservations in a caller-supplied shared allocator. Here `transpileSlot()` supplies a fresh `LaneAllocator` for each external formula's binding attempt. If it fails, only that slot falls back to literals; it does not consume another slot's shared allocation through this call. The header's older statement that hybrids must all be literal is superseded by the later per-slot banking contract. RFF can use this pattern to isolate optional editable shader modules, while making fallback/editability visible and verifying that fixed and live paths produce the same intended result.

The external-formula path canonicalizes names, pads a truncated option prefix using library defaults and types, resolves per-option and fixed-table constant references, and rejects missing references rather than accepting the temporary zero substitutions. Those are useful normalization and failure-reporting boundaries. However, the literal formatter explicitly converts any non-finite host number to 0.0, so unresolved names are rejected more strictly than invalid numeric values. In RFF, an invalid derived constant should produce a diagnosed unsupported input or defined fallback, not silently change the effect. Name canonicalization also relies on an assumed absence of case-fold collisions; the lowercase index itself overwrites collisions instead of checking them.

**Detailed fold mechanism and its 2D use.** The folded integer-power body applies `abs(p-fold) + p - abs(p+fold)` independently to each axis before its latitude-based bulb mapping. This is the sign opposite the obsolete formula still quoted in the preceding docblock. A sign reversal changes the composed geometry even if an isolated fold looks symmetric. A separately authored 2D mirror/fold UV effect can use such piecewise mappings, but must define order, orientation and filtering at the fold boundaries. It is not enough to recognize a familiar operation name. This code's scalar derivative update and min-length trap describe its own 3D iteration path, not an automatically valid derivative for a new 2D complex formula.

The latitude bulb computes azimuth and elevation with atan, raises radius to the selected power and updates the derivative before rebuilding xyz. Integer Power rounds its imported/baked default, yet its exposed control uses the shared bulb parameter schema with fractional step 0.001 and range through 16; the uniform expression itself is not rounded. Thus integer-versus-real semantics depend on the path and subsequent edits, not merely the catalog label. The Folding Int Pow control separately specifies integral steps. RFF should carry the intended numeric domain explicitly through manual entry, animation, persistence and shader consumption.

The built-in box body clamps/folds coordinates, selects scale divided by an inner squared radius, scale divided by current squared radius, or scale outside the sphere, then updates the derivative with the absolute multiplier. Its squared-radius floor and treatment of negative radius differ from the external constant-packer's clamp-before-square rule. Do not unify same-named formulas or parameter types on visual resemblance alone. The quaternion and triplex bodies likewise have their own cross terms and parameter conventions; copying them as a standard named mathematical operation requires independent derivation and provenance checks.

**Writing a derivative is only a syntactic capability signal.** External `writesDeriv` is inferred by regular expressions finding assignments to w or mb3dDr1. That does not prove the derivative is correct, written on every path or transformed correctly under composition; source text can also contain matching comments. Built-in formulas set the flag unconditionally. A renderer may use this as a routing heuristic, but RFF must not treat it as sufficient evidence for distance estimation or precision-preserving acceleration. Validate the actual derivative/range assumptions separately for every mathematical extension.

The option metadata helper reports whether a type can be exposed in principle, not whether this specific binding fits all lane/rotation-bank limits. It also reports raw spans for multi-angle controls, which is important for bake directives and editing identity. A successful transpiler return establishes source assembly with resolved constants, not shader compilation, finite execution, conservative distance estimates or image equivalence. Keep those stages distinct when evaluating RFF shader extensions, and retain source/algorithm attribution for any distinctive adapted implementation.

## Live weave loading and parameter continuity: preserve the user's look through structural edits

Fully read: all 462 lines of `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/loadMB3DScene.ts`. No scene load, animation retarget, GPU compile or rendered comparison was executed.

**RFF transfer: separate replacing a scene from rebuilding one component.** Fresh imports register a generated definition and load its default preset, while editor rebuilds explicitly retain camera, lighting, atmosphere, optics, materials, coloring and geometry settings. Global calculation settings and surviving parameters are preserved while genuinely new slots receive defaults; the rebuilt estimator type is refreshed. A corresponding RFF material/UV composition editor should preserve unrelated authored choices when a user inserts or reorders an operation. This is a workflow benefit for both flat 2D coloring and relief shading, not permission to retain incompatible computed maps after a mathematical change. Preserving quality settings also requires checking their validity for the new operation, rather than assuming a former step size or bailout remains appropriate.

**Parameter identity must survive storage relocation.** `mergeWeaveBanks()` maps each new slot to the first unclaimed old slot with the same kind/ref, then moves old bank values to the new bank index. `mergeDenseLanes()` clears/reseeds physical lanes and transfers surviving values by parameter label and shape within matched slots. Both emit routing renames intended to move animation/LFO targets consistently with values. This addresses a real integration problem: reordering shader modules should not make a slider or keyframe drive a different physical lane merely because packing changed.

The matching is deterministic but not instance identity. Two occurrences of the same formula claim old banks left-to-right, so swapping those occurrences cannot be distinguished by kind/ref alone when they have different authored parameters. Label-plus-type matching is likewise vulnerable to renamed or duplicate labels. RFF should use stable operation-instance and parameter IDs for values, tracks and references, with explicit migration when schemas change. Bank copying retains mutable object references in this helper, while dense-lane transfer shallow-copies objects; neither is a universal deep-snapshot guarantee.

The bank transfer emits a full lane vocabulary when an old slot changes index, helping tracks that have not written a current live value. It does not itself apply the renames: `loadUserWeave()` returns them for the editor to consume. Successful value transfer therefore does not prove animation continuity, especially for swaps, deleted slots or collisions. Apply any RFF retargeting as one mapping transaction against the old state so sequential A-to-B/B-to-A updates cannot overwrite one another. Define behavior for removed targets and undo the rebuild and retarget consistently.

**Building and publishing are not the same as a pure preparation step.** Despite its 'pure make the fused def half' description, `buildWeaveDef()` registers the definition and emits REGISTER_FORMULA. The live scene is loaded later. `loadUserWeave()` retrieves the old definition after this registration; whether an ID collision can replace that definition depends on ID generation/registry behavior outside this file. An RFF adaptation should capture the prior state first and stage the replacement before publishing it, with an explicit failure outcome. Here `ok: true` means this synchronous path built/registered/loaded settings; it does not wait for shader compilation or a completed valid frame.

The fresh-import path can also load a substitute native formula when the emitter returns one, carrying that choice in the ledger note. A substitution can be useful if visibly identified, but must not be reported as exact mathematical compatibility. The file header's blanket wording about unsupported external CODE formulas is stale relative to its explicit decompiled-library loading path. Preserve distinctions among imported exactly, approximated, substituted and unsupported in any RFF import report; do not collapse them into a generic loaded count.

**Editable source and runtime schedule need an explicit source of truth.** Imported weave source copies slot options and retains counts/repeat metadata; editor builds attach the supplied source and stamp runtime rhythm values into the preset. Rebuild then deliberately gives existing live rhythm keys precedence. Consequently the resulting runtime rhythm may differ from the freshly supplied source if the editor has not already synchronized it. RFF should normalize authored structure and live parameters into one consistent snapshot before serialization or compilation. Filtering absent slots in imported source can also compact indices while repeat metadata remains positional; validate holes and index mappings at the boundary rather than relying on source comments saying alignment is preserved.

These mechanisms support a richer shader-authoring workflow, but do not require importing GMT's entire formula engine into RFF. Apply the identity, normalization and staged-publication lessons to relevant material, image-layer or UV extensions while preserving RFF's existing file-format, precision and MPA contracts.

## Legacy weave migration: preserve authored intent when shader composition evolves

Evidence: full read of `engine-gmt/utils/weaveMigration.ts` (365 lines), checked against the inventory hash. This is source inspection, not an executed migration or a rendered comparison.

GMT converts old interlace and Hybrid Box settings into a registered fused weave, remaps parameter values into per-slot banks, retargets animation routes, and removes the old active configuration. Its useful transferable idea is a single load-time normalization boundary: every supported loading route can receive the same schema conversion before feature setters apply values. RFF can use this principle when extending shader layers or material controls, while retaining its append-only ConfigIO contract and frozen palette recipe generation.

### Mechanism and limits relevant to RFF

- The pure enabled pre-loop fold becomes a **counts** schedule: a fold intro of `hybridIter` steps followed by the host, with `repeatFrom = 1`. Combined/interleaved cases use modulo layers. The implementation is more specific than the header's blanket modulo description. Moving previously uncounted work into the iteration loop can change iteration coloring and bailout behavior even when some orbit positions agree. RFF must preserve the meaning of its iteration field; transferring this scheduling idea does not authorize changing MPA or perturbation mathematics.
- Host, secondary, and fold parameters receive bank keys. Vector values are normalized component by component, boolean values become numbers, and unsupported or nonfinite scalar inputs fall back to zero. This is a value conversion, not proof of semantic equivalence: RFF needs parameter type, units, domain, and old defaults to remain explicit when changing controls.
- Animation retargeting renames route strings and track IDs without transforming keyframe values. The suffix fallback accepts any final underscore suffix, not only vector axes. Renaming tracks in place can overwrite an existing destination; two legacy enable controls may converge on one master gate. RFF should build a complete collision-checked destination map before publication, preserve stable layer identities, and distinguish route renames from conversions of values or units.
- A counts intro bakes its length, so the corresponding `hybridIter` animation does not receive the modulo case's beats retarget. `hybridSwap` is used for an initial start value but has no animation retarget here. Preserving one still frame therefore does not establish animation fidelity.
- When the two legacy enable states disagree, only the enabled subsystem migrates. Disabled configuration can still matter to future editing or animation; treating it as visually inert at load time does not mean it is disposable authoring data. RFF should retain inactive layer settings and independently addressable enables.
- Some fold variants deliberately change appearance; custom folding values and nondefault permutations can be lost, with console warnings. Compatibility reporting should identify such transformations in the loaded document's review information rather than claiming that a successfully generated shader preserves the original image.
- This module is store-free but has side effects: it mutates the supplied preset, registers a definition, and emits an event. Some legacy cleanup occurs before unsupported-input checks; the catch handler does not roll back mutations. For RFF, stage a converted document and validated shader configuration, then publish them together. A failed conversion should retain the previous usable document and its authoring data.

### 3D-to-2D application

The strongest transfer is safe evolution of **2D palette/image/material layer composition**, including animation bindings and disabled effects. It does not require porting the 3D fractal formulas. An optional geometric fold can operate on decorative UV coordinates, but moving a fold into the Mandelbrot iteration count would change the mathematical and coloring contract. Validate migrations with old-document fixtures, inactive layers, colliding animation destinations, changing enables, and before/after rendered frames; these validations remain recommendations, not completed tests.

## External scene parsing: retain shader authoring information without claiming render equivalence

Evidence: full read of `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/parseMB3D.ts` (470 lines), inventory hash verified. The cited Pascal sources and historical 32-block verification in its comments were not independently verified in this reading; no parser or image tests were run.

The useful architecture is a plain scene-data stage separate from target-specific mapping and shader emission. The parser retains the decoded byte stream as well as typed camera, iteration, formula, lighting, palette, reflection, and quality fields. This permits a mapper to explain which values it actually supports. For RFF, optional import of palettes or relief-light authoring settings could follow this separation without promising to reproduce a 3D fractal or copying its numerical engine.

### Data mechanisms that matter to a shader-oriented importer

- The text codec uses the alphabet `./0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz` and packs four six-bit groups least-significant first into three bytes. Standard base64 decoding is not interchangeable. The parser splits an 840-byte header from an eight-byte addon head and up to six 188-byte formula records by byte counts, not textual separators.
- The addon reader examines all physically available slots up to six instead of trusting `formulaCount`. Each slot preserves its iteration count, formula identity, 16 option type tags, and 16 double values. The transferable lesson is to distinguish a saved count or compression hint from the actual semantics of independently enabled layers. Do not apply this foreign convention to RFF's existing versioned formats without their own specifications.
- Light positions use seven stored high bytes of a little-endian double, reconstructed with a zero low byte. Light amplitude uses signed mantissa times `10^(clamp(exponent,-25,25)-1)`. Packed light flags separately describe activity, positional lighting, angle space, and shadows. An importer must decode these representations before selecting a target intensity or coordinate convention; their numerical values are not automatically RFF light units.
- Palette anchors retain separate diffuse and specular colors, while the parser also exposes two ambient colors and two depth colors. These distinctions can inform optional 2D relief material authoring and independently colored highlights. They do not make depth fog meaningful for a flat image without an explicitly chosen scalar field.
- Raw parsing retains reflection recursion depth even though downstream direct-reflection mapping does not support it. This is a useful capability-reporting pattern: decoded, mapped, and rendered are separate states. Retaining raw bytes alone does not establish a lossless export path.

### Compatibility boundaries to carry into an RFF design

The text parser accepts marker versions 16 and above through one fixed layout; the binary entry assumes the 840-byte layout and labels the result version 18. Its own comments exclude the 868-byte binary layout, but the length check alone does not reject that layout. A production RFF importer should identify supported variants explicitly and report unsupported ones before applying controls.

The decoder skips invalid characters and does not require a closing delimiter. A partial final group is padded and produces three bytes; encoding arbitrary byte lengths also pads to complete three-byte groups. Consequently, the codec functions are not a byte-length-preserving inverse for every possible input length merely because a comment calls them inverse. Byte-exact tests need specified input framing and lengths, independent fixtures, and semantic assertions. The current parser's size checks prevent short header reads but do not establish finite values, valid dimensions, sane parameter domains, or a complete addon; incomplete trailing slot data is simply not parsed.

For RFF, validate imported values and format identity in a separate stage, retain useful unsupported authoring fields with their provenance, and present a concise conversion report before replacing the active scene. Implement public format compatibility independently; the source references in GMT are leads for provenance research, not evidence that source code may be copied under an assumed license. These are adoption requirements, not a request to repair GMT.

## Fused shader assembly: isolate effect parameters and explicitly own intermediate quantities

Evidence: full read of `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/emitFusedHybrid.ts` (808 lines), checked against the inventory hash. This section follows the previously inspected transpiler, constant packer, scheduler adapters, and loader. No generated shader was compiled or rendered in this pass; historical certification and timings in source comments are not new measurements.

### Mechanisms worth adapting to RFF shader composition

1. **Private parameter banks.** Each woven MB3D slot receives a private allocation, then its scalar/vector uniform reads are rebound to `uWs<slot>*`; UI parameter IDs and initial values move to the same bank. Native slots use bank bindings from their resolver. This prevents one effect's controls from consuming another's shared scalar/vector pool. For RFF image/material layers, use stable layer identities and one explicit parameter layout contract between C++ and GLSL. Slot numbers help routing but are not sufficient persistent identities across reorder operations.
2. **Precompute invariant transformations.** Rotation specifications retain source parameters while CPU-derived uniform matrices receive definition-wide indices. Renaming uses a single simultaneous replacement, avoiding cascading renames such as M0→M1 followed by M1→M2. RFF can similarly prepare UV transforms and decorative rotations when their inputs change rather than rebuilding them per fragment. Numerical equivalence must be checked at the actual storage precision; do not transfer this optimization into sensitive perturbation equations without proof.
3. **Local fallback for exhausted capacity.** Derived rotation capacity is checked before consuming global indices. A slot that does not fit is re-transpiled with baked values, without forcing every other slot to lose live controls. This is a useful containment pattern, but losing a live control is a user-visible capability change. An RFF design should report it explicitly and preserve animation intent, or reject the unsupported configuration. “Own bank” does not prove unlimited device uniform capacity or guaranteed compilation.
4. **Separate structural composition from live rhythm.** Counts scheduling uses a generated lookup plan; modulo scheduling reads interval/start/beats uniforms and resolves the first matching layer. A whole-weave enable gate can select the base behavior without recompilation. RFF can apply this distinction to decorative effect activation or animation while retaining deterministic layer order. Per-fragment branching cost and compilation savings require measurement; these are not automatic performance gains.
5. **Explicit ownership of shared outputs.** The fused dispatcher threads a union of scratch variables through slot functions, seeds scale/derivative quantities to one, and seeds other scratch to zero. An iteration-derived value is refreshed from `i` rather than treated as persistent scratch. RFF composite fields likewise need documented initialization, ownership, and update frequency so a disabled or skipped producer cannot leave stale data for downstream masks.

### Distance-estimation mechanisms and transfer boundaries

The dIFS path illustrates why intermediate names must include semantics. In ordinary routing, `mb3dRout` is refreshed from `dot(z.xyz,z.xyz)` **before dispatch**. In the dIFS route, the same scratch name represents a formula-produced surface-distance value, so that refresh is disabled. Only a dIFS-owning slot contributes `mb3dRout / max(abs(mb3dVary),1e-9)` to the running minimum. Folding the accumulator after an unrelated transform would instead consume an old value. The global minimum starts at 65535 per distance evaluation. These constants and estimator assumptions are not generic guarantees about distance bounds.

A useful 2D adaptation is a decorative field graph where each producer declares its units and validity, and only valid producer results enter a mask reduction. An orbit minimum, squared radius, derivative magnitude, and signed surface distance must not be treated as interchangeable floats. Keep such decoration separate from RFF's accurate Mandelbrot iteration data and MPA machinery.

Estimator selection here is partly heuristic: editor/migration builds with `enableGate` can prefer a derivative-writing analytic slot over a dIFS owner, whereas plain imports retain their other routing. If no slot claims derivative output and the result is not dIFS, a numerical estimator is selected with tuned epsilon/smoothing/detail values. A `writesDeriv` flag does not prove a correct derivative through the entire composed function; nor does finding one derivative-writing slot validate every intervening transform. Native custom distance splicing uses the first used slot, which is distinct from the optionally selected modulo base row. Capability unions ensure needed declarations, but do not prove that arbitrary formula combinations are mathematically compatible.

The code distinguishes a fourth spatial coordinate from derivative storage and enables 4D radius behavior only for one metadata family. This reinforces the need for typed field semantics rather than transferring its estimator choices or numerical constants into RFF.

### Import fidelity must remain separate from successful assembly

- A failed composition can return a name-based native substitute with `ledger.supported = true` and a `code-sub` flag, while using that formula's defaults. The opening “faithful-only” description is therefore not the full current behavior. Callers must inspect the outcome and flags, not just the boolean.
- The preset's iteration count is raised to cover each scheduled slot at least once. That may intentionally depart from the saved count; the final maximum with coverage occurs after `clampIter`, so that helper alone does not prove the final count is within the hard cap. Do not use this behavior for RFF mathematical rendering or silently alter an imported iteration budget.
- The neutral preset explicitly disables glow and imports available lighting/material/color data instead of inheriting an unrelated formula's aesthetic defaults. This is a useful RFF principle: adding a source layer should not introduce unrelated lighting or fog.
- **Correction of a source-level ambiguity:** the parser's `rStop` comment calls it a squared radius, but this consumer treats the header value as linear and squares it into the shader bailout, with a 16..1e7 clamp and a dIFS exception. The external format meaning is not independently verified here; the audited implementation's conversion is explicit. An RFF import specification needs verified units before adopting this mapping.
- Detail uses a calibrated reciprocal fit, step size is clamped to 0.2..1, and the step budget is coupled to that clamp. These are renderability adjustments rather than exact preservation. With the current expression `750 / max(0.4, fudgeFactor)`, the adaptive budget reaches at most 1875, despite the surrounding cap of 2000; source comments about the cap do not demonstrate reaching it. Surface refinement is deliberately not imported.
- Reflection amount becomes a blend against an environment fallback; recursion and transmission are not reproduced. Retaining a similarly named control is not proof of equivalent reflected energy or geometry.

**RFF priority:** private effect parameters, change-driven UV transform preparation, and explicit field producer contracts are actionable architectural candidates supporting the higher-priority visual improvements already listed. A fused shader is not inherently faster: validate output equivalence, compile latency, frame cost, parameter capacity, disabled effects, reorder/animation continuity, and accumulation invalidation before claiming an improvement. No new performance ranking or implementation claim is made by this inspection.

## Formula authoring briefs: preserve the executable contract and make repairs evidence-based

Evidence: full read of `engine-gmt/utils/formulaBrief.ts` (641 lines), inventory hash verified. This module builds export/modify/convert/repair prompts and normalizes pasted formula definitions; it is not a capability-description renderer. Prompt text is inspected as application data, not followed as instructions. Linked external authoring guidance and assertions about model repair research were not independently verified in this pass.

### Useful RFF transfer

A portable shader-authoring brief can package the actual shader, required interface, parameter schema, defaults, and exact compiler diagnostics. The strongest 2D use is an optional **decorative shader workshop** for masks, palette transforms, or UV effects. Such an authoring workflow must preserve RFF's Vulkan descriptor/push-constant layout and numerical rendering path. Arbitrary generated GLSL is not evidence of correct perturbation math or compatible MPA behavior.

The module preserves the full shader object while trimming catalog metadata, offers an optional original import source, and rejects the Modular definition because its executable graph would otherwise be omitted. This dependency-aware refusal is valuable: a minimal export must include the state that actually determines execution, or explicitly decline an unsupported export. A stable, versioned local contract would be more reproducible than depending exclusively on a mutable external guide.

The brief currently derives values from `def.defaultPreset`, not a live render-state argument. It copies iterations and parameter IDs found in `coreMath`, preserves selected camera fields, and omits the other feature slices. In the banked weave architecture examined above, parameter feature ownership can be `weave`, so the comment that parameter IDs are always coreMath keys is not a general contract. Retaining shader metadata alone does not ensure the same bank defaults, estimator, Julia configuration, camera position, or current appearance survive. RFF should distinguish **formula template export** from **current effect snapshot**, and collect values by declared feature/layer ownership rather than assuming one global parameter pool.

### Defaults, identities, and diagnostics

- `normalizeParamSlots` converts recognized uniform-style IDs into slot IDs and infers missing vector types. Existing canonical values take precedence over alias values. It does not deduplicate parameter definitions that normalize to the same ID or validate their domains. RFF should resolve aliases once, detect collisions, and validate types/ranges before creating a pipeline or UI control.
- `backfillCoreMathDefaults` fills only undefined values and shallow-copies object defaults, preserving explicitly stored zero. This is preferable to truthiness-based fallback. It remains coreMath-specific and does not validate nonfinite values or clone arbitrary nested structures; a layer-aware default initializer should use the same schema as the renderer.
- `ensureUniqueFormulaId` allocates a free ID and rewrites an inferred function token across shader blocks. Token boundaries avoid prefix collisions, but the fallback finds the first call in loop text and can select a helper; the regex is not a GLSL parser and does not namespace every helper or mutable global. RFF should carry an explicit entry-point identity and verify symbol ownership during composition. A renamed document ID does not establish shader-wide collision freedom.
- Compiler hints classify common log substrings while preserving the exact log in a repair prompt. This is a useful authoring aid, not a diagnosis guarantee. Keep source-to-generated-line mapping and raw compiler output available, and validate the repaired shader against the existing pipeline interface before replacing the last working version.

### Tolerant paste handling is not validation

`sanitizeGMF` removes BOM/fences, replaces nonbreaking spaces, filters certain formatter-only lines, and requires the presence of Metadata and Shader_Function tags. It does not parse JSON, verify closing tags, require a valid loop block, reject trailing prose, or compile the shader. The comment about retaining only an immediately preceding header is stronger than the actual test, which accepts any earlier comment opener. Global fence removal and whitespace normalization can also change metadata text. For RFF, preserve the raw pasted source and keep cleanup, structural validation, interface validation, compilation, and visual verification as distinct stages with actionable messages.

The embedded conversion prompts correctly emphasize initialization, per-step state, and explicit parameter defaults, but their blanket derivative-update requirements, recommended estimator numbers, and fixed step factor are authoring heuristics. They are not universal mathematical rules; the fused emitter inspected previously explicitly supports dIFS and numerical-estimator paths. Likewise, forcing a self-contained formula into a per-iteration interface does not by itself preserve its escape conditions or full-orbit dependencies. RFF should make any generated changes reviewable against the actual effect contract, retain source/license metadata and NOTICE provenance, and avoid promising fidelity merely because generated code compiles.

This authoring workflow is a secondary extensibility opportunity, below the already identified direct visual improvements. It introduces no new claim of rendering speed or image-quality improvement, and no implementation was made during this audit.

## Decompiled formula library, first tranche: folds and coordinate-dependent waves as decorative fields

Evidence: contiguous full reading of **lines 1–1000 only** of `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/decompiled-formulas.ts` (26,467 total lines), plus targeted option/default/DE metadata searches for the discussed names. Whole-file hash matches the inventory. This is partial coverage, not completion of this file. The first eight bodies through ABoxVSWavy are complete; ABoxVS_icen1 begins at line 900 and remains incomplete in this tranche. No decompiler/interpreter or GPU equivalence tests were executed. The generator's opening verification claim is not independent evidence obtained by this audit.

### Concrete mechanisms and possible 2D transfers

- **ABoxMod1:** a first-use guard initializes a persistent scale, followed by the recurrence `v := v + (abs(v)-1)*k`. Shifted absolute-value folds are applied per component, a piecewise radius-dependent scale is selected, and coordinate/constant components are permuted before output. This provides a design lead for bounded, user-controlled fold variants, not a new RFF Mandelbrot iteration. Persistent state must reset per evaluation; if incorporated into a decorative iterative UV effect, its iteration budget and initial value become part of the effect's reproducibility contract.
- **ABoxMod2:** the generated fold reduces algebraically to `abs(p+L)-abs(p-L)-p` for each relevant component, with separate fold limits for the z component. Its inversion measure combines x/y squares with the squared excess of `abs(z)` beyond a threshold. A planar decorative variant can use independent U/V fold widths, but discarding z changes that inversion measure and must be presented as a new 2D effect. These algebraic summaries describe the operation for analysis; rearranging floating-point arithmetic is not automatically bitwise equivalent.
- **ABoxMod4d:** all four coordinates are folded and enter the squared radius; a radius-conditioned multiplier updates the coordinate state and a separate derivative accumulator. The literal `1e-60` is added to the radius. That is not a representable positive binary32 guard, so its presence in generated source does not establish a nonzero GPU denominator. Actual downstream compilation behavior was not measured. RFF should define a domain-aware policy for decorative inversion singularities and preserve its existing precision guarantees in the fractal core.
- **ABoxModKali:** generated paired temporary variables carry coordinate lanes, not high/low compensated arithmetic merely because their names end in `h` and `l`. The body folds absolute coordinates around per-axis constants and uses a piecewise squared-radius scale. Do not mistake this naming for a deep-zoom precision technique or transplant it into RFF's high-precision coordinate representation.
- **ABoxPlatinum / ABoxPlatinumB:** fold operations are interleaved with plane rotations, optional axis absolute-value switches, offsets, radial inversion, and a final linear transform. The variants differ in how rotated/intermediate coordinates are reused; name similarity does not prove equivalence. For RFF UV decoration, folding in a rotated coordinate frame can create directional mirror patterns. Fixed angle coefficients can be prepared when controls change, while the coordinate folds remain per sample. Preserve operation order because rotation and folding do not generally commute.
- **ABoxSphereOffset4d:** the inversion radius includes the fourth coordinate, with offsets removed before radial scaling and restored afterward, plus a separate W addition. This directly supports the earlier caution that a 4D coordinate is not interchangeable with a derivative accumulator. A 2D reinterpretation should explicitly define its center and two-coordinate radius, rather than silently omitting state from the original formula.

### ABoxVSWavy: the wave field is coordinate-dependent

After a box fold, let the resulting coordinates be x, y, z, the frequency be f, and the Euclidean radius be r. The body computes:

- `G = cos(f*x)*sin(f*y) + cos(f*y)*sin(f*z) + cos(f*z)*sin(f*x)`;
- `H = cos(f*x) + cos(f*y) + cos(f*z)`;
- one mode uses `q = A*G + B*H + C*r`, while the alternate uses `q = A*G + (B*H + C)*r`.

It then squares q and uses that value to select the inversion scale. This is a spatially varying wave-based inversion measure, not just noise added after coloring. It provides a 2D design idea for a wave mask or a bounded UV displacement. A planar slice or an independently designed two-coordinate version needs explicit naming and controls; neither should be called an equivalent port of the 3D fractal.

The trigonometric arguments depend on the current coordinates, so these sine/cosine evaluations cannot all be replaced by CPU-side constant preparation. Frequency and amplitude constants can be uploaded efficiently, but the field remains sample-dependent. Increasing frequency or repeatedly folding coordinates creates fine structure that needs the footprint-aware filtering already prioritized in this report. Singular reciprocal behavior should not be introduced merely to imitate the source look; a bounded decorative interpretation is an option whose changed semantics must be clear.

**Provenance and validation:** these are decompiled/generated bodies referring to original MB3D formulas. This inspection does not establish permission to copy the library or its distinctive implementations. Before adapting a named formula, establish its original author/license and record the applicable acknowledgement in NOTICE. For independently designed 2D decoration, validate fold boundaries, zero radius, parameter extremes, zoom-dependent aliasing, and animation continuity. This tranche adds mechanism-level evidence, not an implementation, benchmark, or new priority ranking.

## Decompiled formula library, second tranche: generalized radius fields and oriented folds

Evidence: contiguous lines **1001–3000** read in full, extending the previous tranche to lines 1–3000 of 26,467. Whole-file inventory hash verified. This completes ABoxVS_icen1, ABoxVS_icen2, ABoxVaryScale, ABoxVaryScale2, ABoxVaryScale4d, ASurfMod1, ATetraVS, and ATetraVS2. Aex-TorusPow begins near the end and remains incomplete; no conclusion about that complete formula is made here. No generated shader was executed.

### Generalized radial shaping for 2D masks

ABoxVaryScale applies box folds, computes a squared radius, and runs an expanded logarithm/exponent sequence before selecting a radius-dependent scale. For positive finite input, the sequence algebraically represents a power: natural-log and log2 conversion constants cancel in real arithmetic, and the exponent is split into a rounded integer part and a fractional part before exp2 reconstruction. ABoxVaryScale2 instead forms a sum of powered absolute coordinate components, then applies another power. This is a useful design lead for a 2D field of the form `(abs(u)^p + abs(v)^p)^q`, with explicitly chosen domains; it is not always a norm or signed distance.

For RFF, such a decorative field could drive a material mask or transition between rounded and angular contours, independently of Mandelbrot iteration values. Keep the field's meaning distinct from Euclidean distance. A spatial field used for shading needs derivatives or sampling appropriate to its local variation; a visually plausible mask does not provide a mathematically safe raymarch step.

The generated log2/exp2 chains require special care at zero, negative bases, and large exponents. Even an intended ordinary power at zero can pass through logarithmic infinities and invalid intermediate subtraction in this expanded form. Replacing it with a shorter pow expression is not a proven bitwise-equivalent optimization. RFF should implement a documented decorative field with defined endpoint behavior and validate it independently, rather than copy decompiler temporaries as a numerical primitive.

### Distinguish variants by their dataflow

- ABoxVS_icen1's completed body has mode-dependent final offsets. In its earlier pre-radius section, offset additions flow into a temporary that is subsequently overwritten; they do not modify the coordinates used by that radius calculation. This is the emitted text's dataflow, not a verified statement about the original executable. Do not infer an inversion-center implementation from its name alone.
- ABoxVS_icen2 uses offset-dependent cross terms before the exponent sequence, so its base can differ from a sum of squares and is not guaranteed nonnegative by that structure alone. Any 2D reinterpretation needs an explicit domain and parameter limits.
- ABoxVaryScale4d folds four coordinates and uses a separate derivative accumulator. Its conditional compares `Cm52` numerically with `1065353216.0`; that number is recognizable as the integer encoding of binary32 1.0, but the visible GLSL comparison is not a bit reinterpretation. Packing/transpilation and original-machine evidence would be needed to establish the intended semantics. This is a reason to validate translated arithmetic, not a recommendation to change RFF's precision model.
- ASurfMod1 folds only selected coordinates before radius scaling and a matrix transform, then assigns permuted coordinate/constant components. Omitting an axis fold does not turn the entire 3D operation into a 2D formula: the remaining coordinate still affects the radius and matrix output.

### Oriented folding and 2D mirror patterns

ATetraVS repeatedly transforms coordinates by a coefficient matrix, folds one transformed component, and transforms back with its transposed coefficient arrangement. It changes coefficient signs between stages and selects stage ordering with a mode value. The scalar fold is either `L - abs(t-L)` or the two-sided fold `abs(t+L)-abs(t-L)-t`. The transpose acts as an inverse only if the coefficient matrix is orthonormal; the body alone does not validate that property. Its long generated body therefore describes a sequence of oriented folds rather than one freely replaceable global matrix.

ATetraVS2 implements offset diagonal-plane folding through conditional coordinate swaps and sign changes across coordinate pairs, followed by radius-dependent scaling. These mechanisms suggest an independent RFF UV effect with an explicit fold angle, fold offset, and number of stages. In two dimensions, a chosen orthonormal rotation can move UVs into the fold frame, apply the scalar fold, then return them to the original frame. Multiple fold stages generally depend on their order.

This would extend the already identified mirror/sector decoration candidate. It is not evidence that a new effect outranks filtering or environment authoring. Fold seams reverse local coordinate direction and can expose texture aliasing; evaluation should include rotated thin lines, zoom changes, boundary pixels, and animated parameters. Matrix coefficients may be prepared when controls change, but coordinate-dependent fold choices remain per sample. Source/license provenance must be resolved before adapting distinctive named implementations, as recorded in the preceding tranche.

## Decompiled formula library, third tranche: angular sectors, coupled state, and polynomial fields

Evidence: contiguous lines **3001–5000** read completely, cumulative coverage now 1–5000 of 26,467. The inventory hash matches. This completes the preceding Aex-TorusPow body and the bodies through Beth641; Beth651 starts but remains incomplete. No original executable, rendered comparison, or GPU test was run.

### Angular-sector folding is a concrete 2D decoration candidate

Apollo3D-IFS first scales/offsets planar coordinates, derives an angle with atan, rounds a sector index, rotates by a sector-sized angle, and conditionally reflects one resulting component according to integer parity. The subsequent stages apply a 3D matrix and a rational planar transformation. The first stage provides a specific mechanism for the mirror/sector UV decoration already recommended: expose a positive integer sector count, center, orientation, and reflection mode, then sample an existing RFF image or palette field through the transformed coordinates.

The source's rational stage divides by `x*x + (y+1)*(y+1)` in its intermediate frame, so there is a pole at that frame's (0,-1). A secondary square-root denominator and scale divisors also require defined domains. This later stage should not be included merely because it follows a useful sector fold. A separately designed bounded effect would change the original semantics and should be described accordingly. Sector edges, the atan origin, parity boundaries, and a pixel footprint spanning multiple sectors need filtering-aware handling; counting sectors correctly alone does not establish crisp output.

Aex-TorusPow combines a powered azimuth, a second angle based on planar radius and z, and a radius measured relative to a ring centerline. Its expanded exponent reconstruction mixes a truncation-based remainder with a floor-based integer exponent. For negative noninteger exponents these decompositions differ, so it cannot be summarized as an exact ordinary power across its full domain without verification. A ring-coordinate decoration could still be independently designed for RFF, but this body supplies no reason to replace RFF's accurate escape computation or its existing mapping behavior.

### Coupled state is not removable by dropping a coordinate

Aexion1 changes both the orbit and the iteration constant on first invocation, generating four components from absolute linear combinations before a quadratic update. A wrapper that treats c as immutable, repeats initialization on every step, or discards w would implement a different system. Any future formula-composition extension needs explicit mutable-state ownership; it is not a drop-in improvement to RFF's Mandelbrot core.

Amazing Surf folds x/y, optionally includes z in the radius, scales/translates all three components, then applies a matrix. Its planar-radius option does not by itself make the result two-dimensional. AmazingBox2 contains a related but distinct ordering of oriented fold, offset inversion, final rotation, and translation. Operation ordering remains part of the effect contract.

Barnsley2_4Dc and Barnsley2_4Dnc share a threshold-dependent translation stage but differ in signs and cross terms in their four-component multiplication. Barnsley4Dc2 mixes coordinates into paired channels, applies separate threshold translations and selectable constant transformations, then recombines them. In the emitted second pair computation it reads the already modified x, so a presumed pair-independent rewrite is not justified from the name. Their transferable idea is conditional region-dependent decoration, not interchangeable quaternion or complex arithmetic.

### Axis singularities and output ownership matter more than concise formulas

BPine_only, BT2Pine, Benesi1Pow2, Benesi2Pow2, Benesi2Pow6, BenesiPine1, and BenesiPine2 use combinations of squared coordinates, coordinate-frame changes, absolute folds, and rational power-like updates. Several divide by a planar squared radius or its square root. Setting a discarded coordinate to zero can therefore place a proposed 2D slice on a singular set instead of producing a usable planar formula. A decorative adaptation needs an explicit analytic extension or a clearly documented changed behavior at those points, plus finite-output tests; an arbitrary epsilon is not mathematical equivalence.

The Beth bodies in this range reuse coordinate squares/fourth powers in cyclic polynomial expressions. These suggest polynomial scalar fields as another possible mask source, but their distinctive coefficient sets are not established here as licensed material for reuse. Dataflow also matters: Beth1032 and Beth1522 store computed x/y results in local temporaries without assigning them back before their bodies end, whereas Beth323 explicitly restores all three final components. That is an observation about these generated strings, not a verified diagnosis of the original formulas or a request to fix GMT. It prevents this audit from claiming that each named body realizes its apparent cyclic map.

**RFF adoption judgment:** the angular-sector stage is the clearest practical transfer in this tranche and fits the existing optional UV-decoration recommendation. Ring maps and polynomial masks are lower-confidence extensions requiring independently specified mathematics, provenance, and filtering. None of these observations proves a new performance gain, raises their priority above the earlier visual improvements, or authorizes reducing RFF computation precision.

## Decompiled formula library, fourth tranche: scalar shape fields versus orbit transforms

Evidence: contiguous lines **5001–7000**, reread in two untruncated chunks after the first oversized output was truncated. Cumulative coverage is 1–7000 of 26,467; inventory hash verified. Beth651 is completed, followed by the bodies through IQ_NormBulb_NoYZ. IQ_PineTree is incomplete. This is source analysis without runtime validation.

### Scalar shape fields can feed RFF material masks

CitrusIFS, CommaIFS, DecoCubeIFS, and DevilIFS share an important structural distinction: they prepare transformed coordinates, optionally write those coordinates and a scale accumulator back to the orbit, and finally write a scalar to `mb3dRout`. When the transform mode is off, their final value is divided by a scale instead. Thus evaluating a field and changing the coordinate state are different operations, even inside one formula body. An RFF field-driven material system should declare these roles separately, allowing a mask to sample transformed UVs without unexpectedly modifying coordinates used by later layers.

- CommaIFS makes an angle-dependent tube radius using a cubic expression in normalized atan angle, then takes a minimum with an offset sphere-like field. A separately designed 2D ring or curved mask can use the same broad authoring concept: center, thickness variation, and an optional joined circular cap. The atan seam and origin need deliberate treatment; a cubic of the principal angle is not automatically periodic.
- CitrusIFS separates positive and negative polynomial contributions, takes fourth roots, and combines the result with radial/slab bounds using maxima. DevilIFS subtracts two fourth-root expressions and takes a maximum with a sphere boundary. Their zero contours may be useful shape fields, but neither algebraic structure alone proves unit-gradient signed distance or a conservative raymarch bound.
- DecoCubeIFS multiplies three polynomial terms, takes a fourth root, subtracts a control, and switches to radial magnitude when its result exceeds one. This conditional fallback is part of its behavior. A scalar mask should not silently inherit a distant-region switch simply because the source calls the result a distance.

For RFF, independently specified 2D masks can control palette/image mixing, roughness, or emission. Use compatible field units and appropriate edge widths when combining them; min/max preserve certain inside/outside combinations but do not guarantee a uniform visible border width for arbitrary fields. This supports the previously ranked field-mask feature rather than adding a separate high-priority effect.

### Symmetry and conditional transforms

CantorIFS, CrossBiFold, and HalfOctIFS combine matrix transforms, coordinate comparisons/swaps, sign changes, and scaled translations. HalfOct4a/4b extend related operations across four components and update a separate derivative accumulator. DodecahedronIFS additionally performs repeated conditional plane reflections using a fixed normal, interspersed with absolute-value folds. These offer design references for planar symmetry operations with explicit fold axes and order. A 2D reflection should use a defined normalized 2D normal; dropping a component from a 3D normal without renormalizing does not retain a reflection.

FernTransform selects different affine transformations from a wedge-like test involving x and abs(y), then the sign of y, and updates its scale accumulator alongside coordinates. The RFF opportunity is region-dependent UV decoration with visible region controls. It is not a random fern sampler, and no probabilistic behavior should be inferred from its name. Region boundaries require sampling tests during zoom and animation.

### Planar restrictions require invariant-state checks

BristorBrot's visible update leaves z=0 invariant when c.z=0. Under that restriction and `Cm16=2`, x/y reduce algebraically to the familiar quadratic complex map. This is an actual conditional planar reduction, unlike simply hiding a 3D axis, but it adds no new Mandelbrot capability or precision advantage to RFF. CommQuat and CubicQuat contain coupled fourth-coordinate terms, and Hopf4D divides by both paired squared radii: setting a whole coordinate pair to zero can create a singularity instead of a useful 2D port. Faehrten also has cross-coordinate terms, so its apparent planar slice must be checked for invariance before treating it as a 2D iteration.

Fuzzy explicitly uses `(iteration + 1)` to vary angular multiplication and reads the current squared-radius scratch. Its output depends on iteration indexing and scratch freshness, not just coordinates and parameters. The completed IQ bulb variants differ in axis conventions, radial/angular powers, quadrant handling, and whether y/z constants are added. Their expanded power sequences retain the truncation/floor concern recorded in the prior tranche. Similar names are insufficient evidence for substituting one variant.

CosinePow2 divides by a planar radius; CosinePow8 adds `1e-40` to a denominator. Unlike the earlier `1e-60`, this value lies in the binary32 subnormal range, so underflow/denormal handling must be established for the actual execution path before calling it a reliable guard. Beth651, like earlier Beth entries, leaves computed x/y values in temporaries at the end of the emitted body; original-source fidelity remains unverified.

No formula body was copied into RFF. Named implementation provenance, field-domain tests, filter behavior, and actual renderer measurements remain prerequisites for any adoption; RFF perturbation precision and MPA semantics remain binding constraints.

## Decompiled formula library, fifth tranche: twisted ring fields and regularized inversion

Evidence: contiguous lines **7001–8000** fully read; cumulative coverage 1–8000 of 26,467, hash verified. Completes IQ_PineTree, IQ_PineTree_NoYZ, IcosahedronIFS, IdesFormula, KaliDucks, Kalisets1, KleinBagelIFS, KnotsIFS, Lambda4Dc/nc, LimpetIFS, and MagVsXYZ. MagVsXYZabs remains incomplete. Findings are source-derived, without runtime or original-binary equivalence testing.

**Twisted ring masks:** KleinBagelIFS derives a half-angle-scaled twist from planar atan, then mixes ring-radius offset with the third coordinate.
