These are reasonable boundaries to tighten if RFF adopts a registry: scoped subscriptions, stable setting IDs, explicit defaults/migrations, and idempotent registration that can recover from partial failure. The first-run reset removes a storage key for the next reload; it does not immediately redisplay the banner. Interface preferences and hardware capability settings should retain their distinct persistence and application semantics.

### Direct light controls and reusable 2D lighting workflows

Full source read: `engine-gmt/topbar/CenterHUD.tsx` (509 lines). This is a source-level interaction audit, not a screenshot-based interface review. It complements the previously read placement coordinator and light-setting components rather than demonstrating a new lighting model.

**RFF opportunity: adjust several lights without repeatedly reopening controls.** GMT presents three compact light slots and an expanded eight-slot grid. Hover settings can detach into persistent floating panels keyed by light ID. This is useful when comparing a key light, fill, and rim/secondary light on a 2D height-derived surface: keep relevant settings visible and manipulate direction/intensity independently. Reuse RFF's existing lighting capability where present rather than describe a compact controller as new shading functionality. For flat 2D output without a normal/height field, define the intended appearance model explicitly; 3D shadow controls have no automatic physical counterpart.

Detached panels retain identity by ID and resolve the current index from the current light array each render. That is preferable to persisting an index across deletion/reorder. Hovered lights, menu selections, slot keys, and context-menu callbacks still use indices, and callbacks capture light visibility. A RFF editor should carry stable light identity through every route, especially while a menu is open or another operation changes the array. Removed lights stop rendering their detached panel but its position entry remains locally; decide explicitly whether restoring the same ID should restore its panel.

**One user gesture should produce one reversible lighting change.** Existing-light drag opens a parameter transaction before setting the dragged-light ID. Empty-slot pointerdown opens the transaction before creating the light, allowing creation and placement to become one undo entry. This supplies the missing transaction boundary around the previously inspected placement loop, whose interaction session serves rendering policy rather than undo. Keep those responsibilities distinct in RFF: an adaptive-rendering interaction flag is not an undo snapshot. The release handler ends the transaction on either pointerup or pointercancel, so cancellation here means closing the edit, not demonstrated rollback. There is no pointer-ID ownership or unmount cleanup for these temporary transaction listeners in this component. Specify cancel/commit semantics and balance them across window changes and interrupted gestures.

Empty-slot addition assumes addLight succeeds and then takes the last light in the fresh array. The slot display checks MAX_LIGHTS, but an intervening capacity change or rejected creation could leave the prior last light as the drag target. A RFF add-and-place command should return the new stable ID or a failure result, then begin placement only for that ID. Keyboard activation also needs its own addition route: this button's creation handler is pointerdown, with no onClick action in this file.

**Do not infer geometric behavior from the control's header.** The CenterHUD header says positional lights land at the ray-hit surface. The audited useInteractionManager instead places them along a ray at half the retained measured distance, clamped to a fixed interval. For RFF, direct placement should mean a documented image coordinate plus an explicit height or direction, with image-anchored and viewport-anchored behavior distinguished. An orb and a drag gesture are presentation mechanisms, not proof of a physically meaningful placement rule.

**Make persistent controls and transient hover behavior independent.** Desktop clicking toggles visibility; mobile clicking an enabled light first opens settings and clicking it again disables it. Mobile has no expand trigger for the additional five slots. A RFF design should keep selection and enable/disable discoverable and give every supported light an accessible editing route. The expanded view leaves the collapsed slots mounted with reduced opacity/pointer interaction; popup rendering is not explicitly gated by expansion, so duplicate mounted popup instances for shared indices need consideration. The full store is subscribed to twice, unlike the narrow selectors used by the navigation HUD; adopt scoped subscriptions if light controls become expensive during animation.

The hover bridge is a transparent 240×480 pointer-active portal placed at a former menu position. Entering it cancels its expiry, so it can continue covering content until the pointer leaves. Outside-click handling exempts any data-popover element, not just this control's own popup. A RFF port should use explicit popup ownership and bounded hover transitions rather than broad transparent input capture. Hover/bridge timers and panel-drag listeners also need lifecycle cleanup. Detached panels do not participate in the activeLightPopup index effect, which only follows hovered/mobile-menu indices; persistent editing and highlighted viewport light can therefore describe different selections unless unified.

**Adoption priority.** This is a control improvement for making existing or planned multi-light shading easier to tune, below the direct image-quality priorities in the shader ranking. Validate combined add/place undo, per-light identity after reorder, canceled gestures, detached-panel selection, and matching control/viewport state before proposing it as complete. Source inspection alone does not establish those behaviors in either GMT or RFF.

### Reproducible appearance packages and shared-scene restoration

Full source reads: `engine-gmt/gallery/sharedScene.ts` (103 lines), `engine-gmt/gallery/openSharedScene.ts` (37), `engine-gmt/gallery/loadGalleryScene.ts` (81), and `engine-gmt/topbar/ShareLinkButton.tsx` (126). No network requests, uploads, messages, or backend changes were performed. Client comments about access controls, deduplication, and deployment describe intended backend behavior; these reads do not verify those claims.

**RFF opportunity: make a saved look reproducible beyond a screenshot.** GMT serializes a scene with its embedded formula shader, uploads it, and returns a short ID. The important transferable idea is dependency completeness: a saved RFF appearance should contain or identify the exact palette recipe, shader/effect schema, textures/environment assets, and high-precision location needed to reproduce the view. A local package can deliver that benefit without an online service. Keep RFF's existing map/config/recipe compatibility and third-party attribution contracts. A serialized shader alone cannot guarantee the same output across changed runtime contracts or unavailable external assets.

The share action rejects serialization without a Scene tag, preventing its known raw-JSON fallback from being advertised as reconstructible. That string-presence check is not structural or shader validation. getPreset is invoked before the serialization try block, so a thrown snapshot error bypasses this helper's normal status return. The scene snapshot is taken before upload, which is a useful temporal boundary, but no pixel/render revision comparison is made here. A RFF export should identify which accepted state it represents and separate successful serialization, successful storage, and successful restoration.

**Resolve definition identity by content/version, not just a short name.** Both shared-scene and gallery restoration register embedded definitions only if their ID is absent. An existing different definition with the same ID is retained. Therefore the claim that embedding a full shader reconstructs any scene requires a collision policy not supplied by these loaders. A RFF package should verify dependency hashes or allocate a source-qualified identity before applying appearance settings. Parse and validate the complete candidate first, then commit it with its required resources as one operation. These loaders register and load sequentially without a visible rollback or successful-compile acknowledgement; returning true means the load was dispatched, not that the intended image rendered.

**Asset externalization trades payload size for dependency lifetime.** Gallery loading prefers inline scene data, otherwise resolves an owner/public/shared record, then falls back to scene metadata embedded in an image. If sky_url exists, it is reinserted into the material preset only when that feature object is present. This supports smaller scene records but relies on external asset availability. The newly fetched record is used for its scene text while the original item's sky URL is used later; keeping metadata and assets from one version is an explicit requirement for a RFF design. Store content hashes and color-space/type metadata, and offer packaging of assets when offline reproduction matters.

The image fallback downloads the entire response and wraps it as a PNG File before metadata extraction; the MIME label itself does not verify content. No size limit, timeout, or cancellation appears in this wrapper. An absent scene record and a legacy record lacking scene text both reach that fallback, so distinguish those states if the distinction affects expected restoration. Gallery loading emits a loading/compiling status before parsing without a local finally path to clear it on failure; status ownership belongs in the load controller. Both async open routes lack a request-generation check after fetching, so a slower earlier selection can overwrite a later editing choice unless callers prevent it. RFF should make load completion conditional on the current target/request identity.

**Report storage and clipboard results separately.** copyShareLink awaits upload, then attempts clipboard writing and offers a manual-copy toast on failure. It nevertheless returns 'copied' for either outcome, causing the button badge to say Copied even when only a link was displayed. The button's reset timers are not canceled on a later request or unmount; an old timer can reset a new in-flight status. Use distinct created/copied/failed states with owned timers or request tokens. Build query parameters with URL encoding rather than interpolating an unconstrained returned ID. The response cast is not runtime validation of that ID.

The client optionally attaches an existing authentication token to creation and uses separate exact-ID and owner-list routes for reads. That is useful separation of public lookup and personal management, but backend ownership and non-enumerability cannot be proven by client code. RFF does not need account integration to adopt reproducible appearance packages. Prioritize local save/load round-trip tests with duplicate definition IDs, missing assets, canceled loads, and precise deep locations before considering optional sharing infrastructure.

### Preserve lighting assets separately from display and diagnostic images

Full source reads on 2026-10-08: `engine-gmt/gallery/submitGalleryItem.ts` (258 lines) and `engine-gmt/feedback/feedbackScreenshot.ts` (103). No submission, screenshot capture, or external communication was executed; this section describes code paths and RFF adoption requirements.

**RFF opportunity: separate a lightweight preview from the data that reproduces shading.** Gallery submission captures/transcodes a display JPEG, serializes the scene, and externalizes its environment map. The primary environment path asks the worker for its bound texture; the returned blob may be Radiance HDR, selected by MIME type when choosing the multipart filename extension. This corrects the helper's older JPEG-only header description. It does not, by itself, verify radiometric fidelity of the worker capture or server storage. RFF should keep HDR lighting data, encoding/color-space metadata, and the display thumbnail as separate resources. A visually attractive JPEG is not a replacement for the environment radiance driving highlights and reflections.

The helper clones the preset and clears embedded envMapData before attempting extraction. An existing HTTP URL is restored inline; otherwise worker failure falls back to browser image decoding, and total failure returns the stripped preset with no sky blob. Consequently a submission can proceed with missing lighting data. A RFF package should report missing dependencies and provide an explicit choice or fail reproducibility validation, rather than silently claim an equivalent saved look. URL-backed assets also need an integrity/lifetime policy if the package must remain reproducible offline.

The fallback independently clamps width and height to maxEdge, rather than applying one aspect-preserving scale. A 2048×1024 environment becomes 1024×1024, changing the projection of a 2:1 map. Preserve aspect and projection metadata in an RFF port. The fallback JPEG also loses HDR range and alpha; distinguish that degradation from successful preservation. Bitmap resources are not explicitly closed in these helpers, so repeated captures warrant bounded resource ownership. These are portability requirements, not a request to implement a gallery in RFF.

**Bind the preview, scene, and captured environment to one accepted revision.** submitGalleryItem obtains a display image first (or accepts a previously prepared image), then reads the live preset, then awaits capture of the worker's bound environment. Those can represent different states if editing or asset loading occurs between steps. The cloned preset avoids later mutation of that object but does not make the earlier screenshot or later GPU capture match it. RFF should capture an immutable export job containing its high-precision location, appearance settings, and exact resource identities; image and environment readbacks should acknowledge that job's revision. User-provided title/formula metadata should describe that same snapshot.

The scene-size limit is checked using JavaScript string length, despite a byte-oriented limit description. Non-ASCII text makes code-unit count differ from UTF-8 byte count. The diagnostic breakdown counts only top-level preset fields and therefore may not explain embedded shader growth in the serialized GMF. Validate the encoded artifact size and report the actual contributing sections. Server response casting is not a runtime schema check, and this client has no request cancellation/timeout contract. None of these observations proves backend behavior or upload success.

**Keep signatures and thumbnails downstream of the archival result.** Display transcoding preserves aspect by scaling to a maximum width, but does not bound the longest edge for portrait images. Signature baking decodes and re-encodes JPEG, adding another lossy generation; it does not constrain long text to the available width. RFF can produce a signed presentation copy from the original rendered buffer once, while preserving an unmodified high-quality render and reproducibility metadata. These functions use browser canvas conversion without establishing an explicit export color-profile or alpha-compositing contract.

**Diagnostic screenshots are evidence of UI state, not image-quality references.** feedbackScreenshot lazily imports a DOM capture library, excludes marked subtrees, captures once, then tries JPEG qualities 0.8 through 0.3 at up to five image sizes. It measures the complete wrapped text using UTF-8 bytes, accounting for base64 and metadata overhead rather than budgeting the image alone. That is a useful bounded-diagnostic pattern for RFF, but downsampling and JPEG must not become the oracle for fine shader detail, banding, or precision errors. Attach an original crop or suitable lossless render when diagnosing those issues.

The helper relies on DOM/canvas capture; its comments explicitly limit WebGL capture without a preserved drawing buffer and do not establish real-device iPhone verification. Prefer RFF's renderer-owned readback for the image and a separate application screenshot when UI context is needed, instead of changing rendering policy solely for screenshots. The wrapper callback runs for each encoding attempt, so callers should snapshot metadata once and keep wrapping deterministic. Default computed body background can be transparent, and font capture is disabled based on an application assumption; diagnostic completeness should be checked rather than inferred. Marked-element exclusion is an explicit control, not comprehensive automatic removal of sensitive content. Capture and sending remain distinct user actions.

### Preview approval must identify the same export artifact as its settings

Full source reads on 2026-10-08: `engine-gmt/gallery/SubmitGalleryModal.tsx` (499 lines), `engine-gmt/gallery/galleryStore.ts` (92), and `engine-gmt/gallery/installGallery.tsx` (95). **RFF adoption: carry an output artifact, not only a picture.** The modal captures or transcodes a base JPEG, optionally bakes a signature, displays finalJpg, and passes that same blob to submitGalleryItem. This usefully ensures that the selected final image bytes can be reused. However, galleryStore.submitSource carries only a Blob, not the originating preset, view revision, resource identities, or render configuration. The submission helper subsequently obtains live scene state. Thus the caller does not close the earlier image-versus-settings gap, including when the image came from a completed bucket render. RFF should retain an immutable output record containing both image and exact reproduction data, allowing appearance packages, comparison, and optional presentation copies to derive from it.

**Ready means the current requested transformation is finished.** Capture and signature effects have local cancellation flags that prevent obsolete promise results from overwriting newer results. That is a useful pattern, but starting another signature bake does not clear the prior finalJpg or mark a separate busy state. canSubmit checks only that some finalJpg exists. A quick submit after changing the signature toggle can therefore use the previous image while the new operation is pending. Bake failure silently substitutes the unmarked base image while the checkbox can remain enabled. For RFF, bind readiness to the base-image hash plus current transformation options; disable confirmation until that exact candidate is ready, and surface failed optional processing accurately.

A successful replacement creates a new object URL and revokes the previous one through effect cleanup. Closing the modal, however, does not clear baseJpg/finalJpg in the shown effects: the reset effect returns when closed, and the installed wrapper keeps the modal component mounted. Consequently the image URL can remain retained while closed until replacement or unmount, despite the comment claiming both blobs reset on close. Reopening resets those images, but previewExpanded is not reset. Define lifetime explicitly in RFF: either retain a named output artifact intentionally or release transient captures on close.

**Draft form state should not depend on unrelated live updates.** The reset effect depends on project name and watermark preference as well as open state, so a change to those values while open resets title, description, tags, visibility, result, and captured-image state. Capture depends instead on profile identity/auth/source/open, not project name. A project-name-only change can clear the image without starting another capture. Snapshot the initial defaults once per editing session, then keep user edits independent of ambient profile/project changes. Formula labeling is derived from the live registry and may summarize weave slot labels; this is a descriptive display label, not a complete algorithm/provenance record.

The submit request itself has no cancellation or session-generation guard. The form can close while submission runs, and a later completion can update state after a close/reopen. Distinguish closing presentation from canceling a job, and attach completion to its original job identity. The success view does distinguish pending moderation from public approval, a useful example of separating accepted work from externally visible completion. Client text about private visibility is not backend permission evidence.

The slug validator accepts one character or lengths three through sixty, excluding two characters, while the displayed guidance says three through sixty. ASCII slug generation also discards Japanese names and can truncate to a trailing hyphen. RFF should retain Unicode display names and use a separate stable identifier, with one canonical validator. These details concern metadata reliability rather than shader image quality.

**Scope optional infrastructure cleanly.** The gallery store keeps browsing state outside render state and balances pause acquisition/release for opening and closing the browse overlay. Submission and personal-list flags do not acquire that pause in this store; they are not equivalent overlay policies. The installer exports a permanently mounted submission wrapper and registers menu actions with an idempotence flag. Uninstall defaults to the File menu rather than remembering a custom installation target. If RFF adopts optional library/export panels, give registrations and pause ownership explicit handles that can be disposed independently. This remains a lower-priority workflow improvement supporting reliable 2D/3D appearance reproduction, not a recommendation to add online moderation or account services.

Individual/owner lookup retrieves scene data only when needed. RFF can use the same separation for a local library of locations, palettes, lighting setups, and complete appearances: searchable metadata and thumbnails should not force every reference orbit, map, or texture to load. Keep preset identity and compatibility information available even when the thumbnail fails. The tile provides an explicit preview-unavailable state and remains selectable, a useful distinction between a missing preview and an unusable preset.

It retains previous items while loading or after failure, so the presentation must identify stale results rather than imply they match the new filter. Its dependencies are JSON.stringify(opts) and a refresh counter; authentication identity is not part of the query key even though the underlying client session can change the visible result set. Stringification is stable for the same property order, not a canonical equivalence test for reordered objects. RFF should use an explicit query key including library/source revision, filters, sorting, and any access context, with retryable errors and stale-result labeling.

The feed uses offset pagination ordered only by created_at. Concurrent insertions or tied timestamps can duplicate or skip entries; a stable secondary ID and cursor/snapshot policy are better for a large changing library. Limits/offsets are passed through without local validation. The owner listing has no pagination here. These are scaling considerations for a possible RFF library, not proof of observed data loss. Query return values are cast to interfaces without runtime validation; malformed optional arrays or URLs should be handled at the data boundary.

**Do not conflate absent from browsing with access restricted to an owner.** The list defaults to approved rows and may include the signed-in owner's private rows under the intended backend policy unless publicOnly is requested. This conflicts with the previously inspected submission modal's blanket 'Only you can see' wording at the documented client-contract level. Backend enforcement has not been established by these source reads. If RFF ever adds sharing, distinguish local-only, owner-restricted, unlisted-by-link, and public states in both model and presentation; a title-derived slug is not a secret access token.

Visibility updates request returned IDs and reject an empty affected-row result, avoiding a silent no-op success. Deletion instead delegates to an authenticated endpoint and checks HTTP status; the comment promising database/object cleanup as one transaction cannot be verified from this wrapper. The unused userId parameter is not an ownership check. For RFF local resource management, confirm the intended record was changed and preserve dependency-aware cleanup, without deriving success from an optimistic UI change. These catalog improvements support managing reproducible 2D/3D appearances and remain secondary to the direct shader improvements already prioritized.

### Preview navigation and applying a selected appearance

Full source reads on 2026-10-08: `engine-gmt/gallery/GalleryPage.tsx` (215 lines) and `engine-gmt/gallery/Lightbox.tsx` (328). This is a static interaction/data-flow review; no gallery was opened or scene loaded.

**RFF opportunity: inspect before applying, with an explicit application scope.** GMT separates selecting a thumbnail from opening the full scene in the editor. The detail view offers fit/native-size image inspection, metadata, related entries, and a deliberate load action. RFF can reuse this separation for appearance presets, ideally offering a clear distinction between applying colors/lighting and replacing the high-precision location. Keep the preview tied to its saved state and disclose unavailable dependencies. Opening an image is not validation that its shader package can reproduce it.

The Lightbox's '100%' mode removes CSS size constraints and uses auto dimensions; it does not explicitly establish one image pixel per physical display pixel at non-unit device-pixel ratio/browser zoom. RFF should label actual magnification if this mode is intended for assessing shader aliasing or fine detail. Here the underlying image may be the gallery's lossy display JPEG, so it remains insufficient as a precision or HDR reference. The image has an onLoad handler but no onError path, leaving loading text when retrieval fails. State resets on item ID, not a changed resource URL under the same ID. Use resource revisions and explicit failure/retry states.

**Loading belongs to a request, not whichever item is currently visible.** GalleryPage prevents a second load while loadingItem exists, but allows browsing to another item. The child then receives loading=false for that other item and presents an enabled load action, while the parent silently ignores it. An error from the earlier item is stored globally and can appear under the newly selected one. A successful older request closes both views regardless of subsequent selection or close/reopen. For RFF, attach progress and errors to the originating preset/request, either lock selection deliberately or allow cancellation/replacement, and commit only the currently accepted request. The underlying loader resolves after dispatching scene state, not after verified rendering, so closing the gallery is not evidence of compile success.

**Bounded results need honest counts and discoverable continuation.** This page asks for sixty rows without a pagination control. It divides those rows into featured, ordinary public, and owner-private groups, so any group can be absent simply because it fell outside the fetched window. The displayed count is fetched rows, not the total library. Related entries are at most six matches from that same public subset, not an independent author search. A RFF library should describe partial results and expose continuation or search rather than imply exhaustive coverage. Keep tags/source identity stable independently of their display labels.

The query hook is called before the isOpen early return, so a mounted but hidden gallery can fetch at startup and on refresh/filter changes. Configuration-disabled messaging also does not gate that hook here. Make optional catalog I/O and pause ownership follow an explicit lifecycle. Closing the gallery does not clear selectedItem in this component, so reopening can restore the old lightbox; decide whether this is desirable restoration or stale state, especially after the library/account context changes.

Deep-link resolution correctly ignores canceled effect results and clears the pending slug after success/failure. However, the failure message is stored in loadError and is only rendered inside a selected Lightbox; a missing deep link with no selected item has no corresponding error presentation in this page. Use an overlay-level failure channel for failures that occur before an item exists. Public browsing and exact-link lookup remain distinct contracts; the 'only visible to you' label should not be taken as proof of owner-only access given the separate unlisted-link behavior documented by the client.

**Keyboard actions should respect focused controls.** The Lightbox captures Arrow/Enter/Escape at window level. Enter invokes scene loading whenever this item is not marked loading, without checking the focused button or preventing its default activation. Thus the source does not establish that keyboard activation of another button stays limited to that button. Escape is zoom-aware, but stopPropagation alone is not a substitute for a single modal action owner when several global listeners exist. RFF should route navigation shortcuts through the focused view and retain standard activation semantics. Image-link copying and entry-link copying are usefully separate actions; direct download links here delegate behavior to the browser and do not confirm a completed save. These workflow improvements help users choose and compare 2D appearances but do not change the shader-priority ranking.

### Personal preset management: partial results and operation identity

Full source read on 2026-10-08: `engine-gmt/gallery/MySubmissionsOverlay.tsx` (342 lines). No account operations, deletion, or sharing were executed. The useful RFF transfer is reliable management of saved appearances, not the online account/tier system itself.

**Keep independent collections useful when one source fails, but expose partial failure.** The overlay loads submissions and quick-share records concurrently. A share-list failure becomes an empty array so submissions remain available. That preserves useful work, but it also makes an unavailable collection appear empty. RFF's local preset browser should retain separate loading/error states for locations, appearance recipes, textures, and external libraries, with targeted retry. A failure in one source should not erase successfully loaded records or claim that none exist. Here a primary-list error can coexist with the empty-state message because the latter does not check error.

**An alive component is not the same as a current request.** mountedRef prevents state writes after unmount, but the component returns null when closed and can remain mounted. It has no refresh-generation guard or account-ID comparison after awaiting. Overlapping refreshes or a profile change can therefore publish older results into the current view. Existing arrays are retained during profile changes and sign-out. RFF should bind every response to a library/document generation and clear obsolete ownership context immediately, while optionally retaining explicitly labeled stale results for the same source.

A single busyId is used for mutations, but other rows remain actionable and the wrapper has no mutual-exclusion guard. If operations overlap, one completion can clear the busy state of another and competing refreshes can overwrite each other. Pointer-events-none on a row is not a disabled control contract for keyboard activation. Use per-operation/per-record state or an explicit serialized command queue. The namespace should include record kind because submissions and shares use separate ID domains. Shared-scene Open has no busy guard here, so multiple loads can race through the previously audited loader. Apply the same accepted-request rule to loading a RFF appearance.

**Distinguish successful mutation from successful refresh.** The wrapper performs a remote operation, then refreshes, then increments the general browse refresh counter. refresh catches its own errors, so a mutation can succeed while its reconciliation fails; that is not the same as the mutation failing. Show those outcomes separately and allow a retry of reading state without repeating a successful destructive command. The confirmation text explicitly distinguishes deleting an image submission from invalidating a share link. For RFF local libraries, make deleting an entry, removing a link, and deleting shared texture dependencies distinct operations, with recovery appropriate to the storage design.

Capacity labels are computed from duplicated client tier constants and fetched rows, with values of 1000 displayed as infinity. Those labels are not authoritative backend capacity evidence. Likewise the header's database-trigger description is not verified by this file. RFF should derive limits from actual resource constraints or a single capability source and keep item count, storage use, and unsupported presets separate. This overlay renders every row/image without pagination or explicit lazy image loading; large libraries need bounded fetching/rendering rather than merely a scroll container.

The submitted-image section opens an image URL, while the quick-share section can load a scene. These are different capabilities despite appearing in one personal collection. A RFF library should label whether an entry is only an image, a reproducible location, an appearance recipe, or a complete package. This prevents a saved preview from being mistaken for the shader and high-precision state required to recreate it. The finding adds workflow detail to the existing reproducibility recommendation and does not change the direct shader priorities.

### Diagnostic attachments need a declared reproduction scope

Full source read on 2026-10-08: `engine-gmt/feedback/FeedbackClient.ts` (284 lines). This audit only reads the collection/submission implementation; no feedback was sent and no scene data was uploaded.

**RFF opportunity: prepare a local, reviewable shader diagnostic package.** The client separates application-declared attachment choices from a generic submission envelope, supports a prepared attachment that was already previewed, and records the application version plus attachment-specific context. RFF can reuse this separation for exporting a diagnostic bundle containing exact appearance settings, pipeline/shader identifiers, relevant device capabilities, and a suitable reference crop. Collection should be useful without requiring a network service. The built-in GMT context here includes version, URL, and formula, but no explicit GPU/driver, shader hash, or compiled-pipeline revision; those cannot be claimed present from this client alone.

**Small is not necessarily reproducible.** captureSlimGmf clones the preset, then clears environment data, drawing strokes, and a scene thumbnail when they are nonempty strings/arrays. It records which fields were removed. Keeping a removal manifest is useful, but an environment or drawing-dependent shader issue may disappear with those fields. A RFF diagnostic should distinguish a complete reproducer from a settings-only report and preserve the minimal relevant dependencies for the reported effect. Use asset hashes/references and explicit missing-resource notices when a size budget prevents inclusion. Arbitrary alternate representations are not removed by this fixed path/type check; it is not a general data-minimization or redaction pass.

The size constant is named in bytes, but the slim-GMF check uses JavaScript string length. The later Base64 conversion correctly encodes UTF-8, so non-ASCII content can expand beyond that earlier limit. Custom and prepared attachment text has no final common byte-limit check in submitFeedback. Apply one encoded-byte validation after the attachment is finalized, including wrapper overhead where relevant. A successful clone/serialization is not proof that the stripped scene loads or renders equivalently.

**Freeze context together with the reviewed attachment.** A prepared file takes precedence even when includeScene is false; callers must clear it when the user chooses no attachment. Attachment capture may await, and collectAppContext then reads the current store and location. A previously prepared screenshot/scene can therefore be paired with later live formula/context values unless the prepared file supplies its own snapshot metadata. RFF should build the attachment and its immutable manifest under one revision, then present the exact data that will be saved or sent. A null capture silently omits the requested file here; an RFF diagnostic workflow should report that outcome distinctly from successful inclusion.

Configuration is a mutable module-level singleton, and getFeedbackAttachments returns its actual array. Availability is exposed as a helper but is not rechecked by submitFeedback. Unknown attachment IDs can silently produce no file. Validate the selected capability at the execution boundary and avoid mutating shared configuration through returned references. Application/file context merges can overwrite built-in version, URL, or formula keys; reserve canonical identity fields or document authoritative precedence.

The default context collects the complete current URL, including any query/hash content. For an RFF diagnostic design, collect only fields needed for reproduction and show the export manifest rather than assume every contextual string is appropriate to include. The helper validates a nonempty message but relies on external code/server for category, size, response-schema, timeout, and retry policy. The envelope's declared JSON attachment handling also does not establish that a .gmf file is semantically JSON. A local diagnostic format should name its content type and schema accurately. This is support tooling for verifying shader improvements, not an image-quality feature or evidence that a report reaches its recipient.

### Reviewed diagnostic candidates and modular panel installation

Full source reads on 2026-10-08: `engine-gmt/feedback/FeedbackPanel.tsx` (311 lines), `engine-gmt/feedback/installFeedback.tsx` (95), and `engine-gmt/feedback/index.ts` (24). These complete the currently inventoried feedback module's executable files together with the preceding client/screenshot reads. No feedback was sent. This is a source-contract review, not verification of the comments' contrast measurements or device behavior.

**RFF opportunity: a reusable local diagnostic panel with a reviewable attachment.** The form supports no attachment, one checkbox option, or several mutually exclusive choices. It avoids choosing a capture-on-select screenshot by default and can show the exact prepared file's preview before submission. The same pattern can let RFF users prepare a shader diagnostic crop or settings package locally, inspect its scope, and save it. Text prompts distinguish expected/actual behavior from feature requests. These are support-workflow ideas, not direct improvements to rendered image quality.

**A selected option needs a generation-bound candidate.** Attachment preparation has no request ID or cancellation guard. Choices remain enabled while preparing; two captures can overlap and resolve out of order, while either finally handler clears the single preparing flag. A failed older capture can reset a newer selection to Nothing. Returning to an already prepared ID reuses its prior file, without a recapture action here. RFF should maintain a candidate keyed by choice, source revision, and preparation generation, with explicit recapture and truthful readiness. Unmounting or changing choice must invalidate old callbacks.

The submit path only passes a prepared file when its ID matches the chosen capture-on-select option. That prevents directly passing a different option's file, but a missing/null prepared file causes the previously audited client to invoke capture again at submission. Thus 'what was previewed is what is sent' is not guaranteed merely by the selection guard. A single-option captureOnSelect attachment is treated as an ordinary checkbox and captured at send, because preparation exists only in the multi-option route. Validate those capabilities at configuration time or implement the same preparation contract for both presentations. Availability is sampled once on mount; long-lived/docked panels need an explicit update policy if source data changes.

The visible Send button is disabled while submitting/preparing, but trySubmit itself only checks message content. An operation-level in-flight guard is stronger than presentation state alone. The panel's own close action blocks during submission; external dock/window closure is owned elsewhere, and these promise handlers have no unmount guard. Explicitly define whether closing hides a continuing job or cancels preparation. The email field has type=email, but the action is a button outside a native form submission and does not invoke validity checking here; input type alone is not proof of validation. The completion wording is a product promise, not evidence of delivery or a reply time.

**Install capability, presentation, and state together.** The helper supplies a panel manifest entry, separately registers its component, and opens it through a stable Feedback panel ID. This allows smaller hosts to reuse one panel without installing all GMT controls. The code documents that the manifest must reach an existing store or opening can silently do nothing. RFF can use the modular principle for diagnostics or appearance tools, but installation should validate every required dependency and expose a clear unavailable state rather than a dead menu action. The registration guard is module-scoped and has no disposal/re-registration contract.

Opening seeds a floating position and size only if absent, retaining user geometry afterward. The initial placement has minimum margins but no maximum-edge clamp in this helper; actual on-screen containment depends on the window host. Do not infer complete layout behavior from the installer. The public index exposes capture and submit helpers as well as the panel, so callers can bypass the form's readiness controls; enforce critical candidate/size checks at the shared execution boundary. For RFF, keep diagnostic export independent of remote sending and preserve the exact high-precision state and relevant shader dependencies identified in the preceding sections.

### Shader composition editing: preserve identity, compiled bindings, and complete undo

Full source reads on 2026-10-08: `engine-gmt/components/WeaveEditor/WeaveEditorPane.tsx` (1,534 lines), `LoopStrip.tsx` (69), and `index.ts` (7). This completes the inventoried WeaveEditor component directory. The observations below concern source behavior; no GPU compilation or interactive replay was performed.

**RFF opportunity: durable identities for appearance layers.** GMT separates a row's persistent editor key and color from its current list position. Reordering therefore retains visual identity. At Build, the loader returns parameter renames; the editor passes these to animation retargeting and reports displaced/orphaned tracks, LFOs, and audio links. This is useful for RFF's shader effects, masks, texture layers, and any future animated appearance controls: a reorder should preserve the user's parameter values and their intended animation targets. Use stable effect-instance IDs plus parameter IDs, with an explicit migration mapping at compilation. This recommendation does not require importing GMT's formula weaving into RFF's Mandelbrot recurrence or changing MPA.

**Mechanism and transfer boundary.** The pane offers counts-based sequences with intro blocks and a repeating tail, or live layered timing with one elected base and up to five other active layers. The live schedule uses interval/start/beats uniforms, with row order determining priority when layers coincide; changing the formulas still requires a build. The editor derives a preview through the pure scheduling functions. RFF can adopt the distinction between structural shader changes and uniform-only changes. A 2D appearance stack could change intensities or mask thresholds live while recompiling only topology/specialization changes. Applying a periodic selection rule to visual effects is a separate artistic feature, not an equivalent port of the 3D fractal math, and should not be confused with RFF's reference-orbit periodic structure.

**One transaction must include structure, live values, and routing.** Structure history stores cloned drafts, capped at 50 entries; rhythm values live in a different store. Reorder, removal, activation changes, and base changes call syncRhythm immediately, reading old values before one batched write and issuing simultaneous target renames. That batching is useful. However, editor undo/redo only restores the draft; it does not reverse these live writes or retargeting. Consequently, reversing a row swap can restore the displayed order without restoring the original timing assignment. RFF should snapshot or reversibly map all affected state in one operation, including animation routing and generated bindings. Keep canceled gestures and committed operations distinct. The drag implementation has pointer capture but no pointer-cancel/lost-capture handler or active pointer-ID validation; it is not a complete transaction model to copy.

**Keep draft bindings separate from the running shader.** The pane keeps live timing controls mounted while the draft is dirty, disabling them to avoid driving an old compiled slot under a new label. Preserving layout during dragging is a useful interaction principle. But syncRhythm still changes the shared live timing immediately during structural edits, before Build; disabling the controls alone does not isolate the running scene. In addition, the dirty signature compares slots, counts, option values, bake directives, schedule kind, and dividers, but omits the explicit base selection. A base-only change can therefore leave the UI reporting a clean structure despite requiring a different layer-to-slot binding. RFF should compute a complete structural signature, stage draft uniforms by effect identity, and publish the compiled layout with its matching values as one revision. Do not infer GPU readiness from a clean draft signature: this pane's success path observes loadUserWeave's synchronous result, not a GPU compilation acknowledgment, and the clean-state text can also appear for an empty draft.

**Conversions should preserve meaning, not merely change the control mode.** The pane first certifies equivalence and otherwise calls conversion helpers. Failed conversions still switch mode while retaining the previous target-mode data and displaying a reason; this is explicitly not proof of a preserved pattern. Successful rhythm-to-sequence conversion duplicates rows when the same source appears in separated runs. Those copies receive new identities and parameter banks on rebuild, so a preserved formula-selection sequence does not by itself establish preserved live parameter or animation semantics. For RFF, classify conversions as exact, current-frame-only, or unsupported, and stage the result for review when meaning changes. Include time-dependent modulation in any equivalence claim; a warning that current timing was baked is not equivalent to retaining an animation.

**Scope editor caches and reports to a document revision.** GMT caches modal drafts globally and panel drafts by formula ID, while a module-global relay passes the transfer report across a remount. These preserve session edits but do not encode a scene/document revision; the report initializer consumes the relay without checking the receiving formula. RFF should scope retained drafts, orphan reports, and cleanup operations to the document and build revision they describe. Revalidate orphan targets before removal rather than treating an old report as current authority. Title edits also bypass structure history here; decide explicitly whether names belong to the same undo transaction.

LoopStrip renders at most 96 blocks in its normal fallback path, marks the cycle boundary, and fades later repeats. Its labels and colors can explain effect order in either 2D or 3D, but fading denotes repetition, not reduced numerical strength. Colors remain stable because the caller indexes a six-color palette by row identity; distinct rows can share a color. The component treats zero iterations as an unspecified count, relies on callers for integer/range and plan validation, and may show no cycle boundary when a long intro consumes the display limit. Show truncation explicitly and label the preview as draft or compiled. The pane's optional hint names the first active row as the base even when another base is elected; derive every label from the same resolved mapping used by compilation. The public index is only an export, not evidence of host-independent state isolation.

### Portable reference-scene generation and honest validation levels

Full source read on 2026-10-08: `plans/mb3d/decompiler/gen-sample-scenes.mjs` (56 lines). Partial data audit: `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/sampleScenes.ts`; its complete non-payload wrapper was read, and every one of its 43 JSON scene records was parsed and base64-decoded. All decoded payloads are 1,976 bytes and round-trip to the exact canonical base64 input. This checks packaging integrity only. The embedded binary fields and rendered outputs have not been individually verified in this pass, so the generated file remains partial in the coverage ledger.

**RFF opportunity: an offline shader comparison suite.** GMT bundles named scenes with formula labels and encoded source bytes, enabling click-to-load samples without external files. For RFF, create original, licensed reference locations and appearance settings covering high-frequency palettes, fine boundaries, grazing relief lighting, roughness extremes, transparent image edges, emission, and deep zoom precision. Include 2D and relief-shaded variants of the same location so a proposed 3D-derived appearance feature can be assessed without changing the mathematical image. Record the exact coordinates/precision, dimensions, exposure, palette recipe identity, relevant shader revision, and dependencies. Preserve existing recipe generation and file-format contracts.

The generator sorts source filenames and embeds exact bytes, which supports repeatable packaging given a fixed input tree and implementation. It nevertheless uses developer-specific absolute input/output paths and imports through a different relative workspace layout. It has no pinned source revision, payload hashes, explicit license manifest, or per-file rejection output; parsing/emission exceptions are silently swallowed. A portable RFF generator should accept explicit paths, pin and hash inputs, produce an inclusion/rejection manifest, and make unexpected omissions fail visibly. Verify asset provenance separately: naming the originating repository and authors is not a license determination.

Most importantly, a non-null emitted definition is the generator's automatic acceptance gate. Its own curated exclusion list documents scenes that import but render incorrectly, demonstrating why successful translation is weaker than visual fidelity. Do not repeat the generated header's 'faithfully-renderable' description as verified evidence. Store separate results for decode, semantic validation, shader compilation, and image comparison. Include difficult cases in a clearly labeled validation corpus even when they cannot be offered as supported examples. The browser decoder itself simply uses atob and copies characters into a Uint8Array; it provides neither semantic validation nor a resource bound for arbitrary caller input. For shipped trusted fixtures, build-time validation is the appropriate first boundary; user-imported data needs its own bounded parser and actionable errors.

Targeted implementation checks revisited the already-audited native resolver, dispatcher, bank feature, and Phoenix recurrence. Historical session prompts were read as evidence of design intent, not executed as instructions. No browser or GPU probe was launched.

**RFF benefit: parameter identity should not depend on packing.** The fidelity plan records the move from one dense parameter pool to independent per-slot banks, motivated by duplicate formulas competing for the same named controls and vectors being split into unrelated scalar lanes. The current native resolver has explicit bank bindings that preserve vector types and provide feature-routed parameter metadata; the current feature declares bank state and the editor reviewed above handles MB3D banks too. Earlier sections of these documents describe native-only banks and a shared MB3D pool, and a later update supersedes the original animation-transfer sketch. Treat the documents as a design history, not a single current specification. For RFF, independent effect-instance parameter records can preserve control meaning for repeated image/mask/material effects in 2D or relief rendering. Derive C++ buffer layouts, shader bindings, and serialization mappings from one schema, with layout verification. Do not copy WebGL uniform names into a Vulkan design without defining offsets, alignment, descriptor ownership, and hardware limits.

**Do not generalize the recorded uniform benchmark.** The fidelity plan reports approximately 2% added compile/link time when adding unread uniforms to a particular production shader on Chrome/ANGLE/D3D11 and RTX 2070, with the same active-uniform count. Its claim of zero runtime cost concerns optimized-away uniforms. This is not evidence that actively reading six banks is free, that extra mutable temporaries have no register cost, or that the result transfers to RFF's Vulkan pipeline. A useful RFF evaluation separates cold pipeline creation, cache hits, host uploads, GPU time, and live register/storage pressure for representative active combinations. Keep precision fixed in those comparisons. Replacing globals with a struct does not itself prove reduced physical register usage; the compiler's lowered code and measurements decide that.

**State ownership is the more transferable shader technique.** The struct-state document distinguishes shared orbit accumulators from independent per-slot history, and recommends namespaced variables, initialization before the iteration loop, and save/restore brackets around helpers using shared rotation globals. Current `emitWeave.ts` does compose per-slot initialization and preCall/call/postCall branches, while `nativeResolver.ts` hoists eligible initialization locals and implements rotation save/capture/restore. For RFF's shader composition, classify every value as immutable parameter, per-evaluation scratch, shared accumulation, or persistent history. Independent effects must not accidentally share names or retained state; shared quantities need an explicit contract. Test a repeated effect with different transforms and parameters to expose collisions. A 2D shader stack benefits from the same rule, especially for UV transforms and multi-pass accumulation; cross-frame history belongs in explicit resources and reset rules, not in shader invocation-local globals.

The design document's statement that the wide types are non-recurrent is too broad: Phoenix's vector history is updated inside its formula (`z_prev2 = z_prev`, then `z_prev = vec4(z3, 0.0)`) and read on later calls. Passing that history as explicit arguments solves visibility, not recurrence semantics. More generally, two independently stateful instances alternating their calls need not equal one standalone instance called every iteration. Identical names and parameters are insufficient to prove image equivalence. Use a stateless identity case for namespace checks, then test stateful compositions against a reference with the same state-sharing and call schedule. This is an important limit on adopting GMT canary ideas; it does not justify altering RFF's Mandelbrot recurrence or MPA.

**Separate diagnostic captures from enforceable acceptance tests.** `probe-native-weave.mts` requests headed Chromium with D3D11, creates four shots, saves returned images, and prints success/nonblack/sigma/compile-time fields. It does not itself assert the actual GPU renderer, compare baseline pixels, enforce nonblack/sigma thresholds, or set failure status when a shot returns an error. Per-shot exceptions are converted into printed results and execution continues; page errors are ignored. The optional pair argument can change the identity pair while the reference stays Mandelbulb. Thus reading this probe does not substantiate the document's GPU-certification language or prove equivalent output. RFF should retain the convenient four-case concept, but use explicit backend/device capture, matched fixtures, numerical/image acceptance criteria, failing exit status, and a completion token tied to the rendered revision. An aesthetically nonblack image can still be mathematically wrong.

The two small schedule probes are inspection tools as well. The fields probe uses substring matching and silently skips unmatched names; its `menger trees` query does not match the current `MengerTrees` sample name. The order probe assumes a match, prints aggregate counts over the entire stored order even though its label says 'one cycle', and truncates printed GLSL to 400 characters. Neither asserts a schedule invariant. RFF's validation fixtures should use stable IDs, fail on missing cases, distinguish intro from repeating segments, and validate the full relevant program/dispatch sequence. These probe limitations inform the proposed RFF validation design; they are not a request to repair GMT.

Finally, migration and editor-lifecycle claims need the same scrutiny. The historical struct-state document says local undo survives remount, whereas current undo stacks are component refs and only drafts are cached on unmount. Its later statement that values and tracks 'can never diverge' is stronger than the editor undo behavior established in the preceding review. For RFF, document exactly which state persists, record schema/version ownership to prevent double application of migrated effects, and verify save/load plus undo/redo together. Preserve the existing append-only ConfigIO and frozen palette-recipe rules. A source-emission equality check, a compile result, a saved-scene round trip, and an image comparison each establish a different property; none should be substituted for all the others.

### Exact schedule conversion versus preserved appearance and editing semantics

Full document reads on 2026-10-08: `plans/mb3d/weave-seq-rhythm-conversion.md` (246 lines), `plans/mb3d/sessions/S-weave-p4-7-consolidation.md` (91), `S-weave-p3b.md` (68), `S-weave-p4-3-picker.md` (83), and `S-weave-p4-45-absorption.md` (102). The already-audited `engine-gmt/engine/weave/convert.ts` was revisited at its bounds, simulators, equality certificate, and run-materialization boundaries. These documents describe successive development decisions; their embedded commands and approval requests are historical material, not instructions for this RFF investigation.

**A reusable mechanism: prove finite-prefix and periodic-tail equivalence separately.** The conversion specification models a sequence by an initial segment of length a followed by a repeating period p. Two valid eventually-periodic schedules with structures (a,p) and (b,q) are equal everywhere if their phase functions agree through the exclusive bound max(a,b) + lcm(p,q). This follows because both are in their periodic tails after max(a,b), and one joint period covers all subsequent combinations. The current helper implements this window but caps it at 4,096 and returns both equal and capped. The cap is a work bound, not a proof of unlimited equality. The editor's shortcut checks only equal and can present 'same pattern' without propagating capped. RFF should use distinct outcomes such as exact, prefix-checked, different, and unsupported. Do not reduce them to a success Boolean. The structure supplied to the certificate must itself be valid; the algorithm cannot prove an arbitrary caller's claimed period.

This is applicable to future RFF cyclic appearance animation, repeating mask schedules, or preset conversion. It is not a proposal to replace MPA's period analysis with a visual schedule simulator. For conversions constrained to a known export duration, a bounded comparison can be sufficient if that exact duration is stated. For an indefinitely repeating preset, use an uncapped proof within explicit resource limits or decline exact conversion. Ensure preview and conversion share a simulator, then separately check that emitted shader dispatch matches that simulator; sharing JavaScript alone does not prove GPU equivalence.

**Live-to-baked conversion has real resource bounds.** GMT computes a conservative start of the periodic tail and the least common multiple of endless-layer intervals, simulates enough samples to reduce the tail period, moves the intro boundary backwards, and run-length-encodes the resulting intro and cycle. Current limits include six rows and 192 baked steps. Co-prime intervals can make the tail period large even with small slider values. This motivates explicit complexity limits and informative refusal messages for an RFF effect scheduler. Validate integer/finite values at the shared boundary and bound intermediate work, not just the final output. A capped one-shot layer and an endless layer have different semantics even when their early previews look identical.

**Preserve control roles as well as output samples.** The document's addendum identifies a useful example: an introductory fold A followed by repeating formula B can have an identical phase sequence with either A or B designated as the live base, yet changing a layer's interval then affects the opposite conceptual element. GMT separates an explicit base key from list position and elects a default using repeating-tail dominance. RFF can apply the same principle to a primary material plus accent layers, or a base image plus animated masks: persist the semantic role explicitly and allow users to select it. Frequency of occurrence is a useful default heuristic, not proof of user intent. A mode conversion should preserve values, identities, role assignments, enabled behavior, and animation routes, not only sampled phase indices.

The document claims tail-dominant base selection makes disabled counts and modulo modes agree by construction. That is not generally implied by dominance: a repeating cycle A,B,B has first cycle element A but dominant element B. If a counts bypass returns its first cycle element while modulo bypass returns its elected base, those policies differ despite identical enabled schedules. Treat this as a logical limitation of the stated rationale, not a new runtime reproduction. Define bypass semantics independently and include disabled states in RFF migration fixtures. A render-preserving conversion at one instant also cannot establish animation preservation when live timing is baked into fixed runs.

**Preprocessing is not interchangeable with counted iteration.** The consolidation session explicitly retires GMT's legacy pre-loop Hybrid Box path and accepts a look change when representing it as counted introductory weave steps. Those steps consume iterations, affecting bailout and iteration coloring; the earlier absorption session instead leaves the fast path untouched. The later document supersedes that earlier intent, and its historical owner's acceptance belongs to GMT. For RFF, keep coordinate preprocessing, fractal iteration, scalar-field shading, and postprocessing as explicit stages. Porting a 3D fold to a 2D UV or shading-coordinate effect can preserve RFF's underlying Mandelbrot image; moving it into the recurrence is a different mathematical feature requiring its own precision and compatibility design. Never present those two operations as equivalent.

**Useful integration patterns without inheriting historical assumptions.** The picker plan separates discoverability from enforcement: unavailable formulas remain visible with a reason, while the engine rejects unsupported capabilities independently. RFF could expose effect compatibility with flat 2D, relief shading, export tiling, and animation from one capability schema, while enforcing the same rules at load/build time. The old documents' shared-pool overflow behavior and two-slot-only live mode are historical; current banks and layered scheduling supersede them. Similarly, consolidation into a Formula-panel section replaces the earlier proposal for a separate floating panel. These are evidence of design evolution, not additional missing features to implement in RFF.

The migration plan usefully treats formula definition, live feature state, and animation routes together, clears legacy state to avoid double application, and calls for both old-file loading and new-format save/reload checks. Adapt that discipline to RFF's actual formats: retain frozen palette recipe identities and append-only ConfigIO behavior, and distinguish exact compatibility from an explicitly versioned appearance change. Include viewport and export consumers in the same migration audit. Documented test counts, side-by-side approval requirements, and requested GPU runs establish intended gates only; this document review did not execute or verify those historical outcomes.

### Composition matrices: structural coverage, production shading, and resumable evidence

Full source reads on 2026-10-08: `debug/probe-dec-weave.mts` (190 lines) and `debug/native-weave-sweep.mts` (511). No probes were executed. These reads establish what the tools check, not the current pass/fail status of GMT's formula corpus.

**RFF opportunity: ordered effect-pair coverage.** The native sweep enumerates eligible primary/secondary pairs, including identical pairs unless explicitly excluded, emits two alternating slots, and assembles shader source through the real factory. This is a useful model for detecting interactions between RFF effects: A then B and B then A are different cases, and two instances of one effect reveal naming or binding collisions. Add selected three-or-more-effect cases because pair coverage cannot prove larger stacks correct. The same matrix can cover flat 2D, relief shading, and tiled export configurations while keeping the Mandelbrot computation and precision unchanged. Record unsupported combinations as explicit exclusions with reasons.

The sweep includes a formula-count floor of 52 to detect accidental registration loss. This is stronger than accepting an empty green run, but a count alone cannot detect one missing formula replaced by an unexpected one. For RFF, use an explicit expected-ID manifest plus configuration/source hashes, and distinguish the intended matrix, executed cells, excluded cells, failures, and unfinished cells. A subset run should report its subset scope; it should never imply that the complete matrix passed.

**Correct the backend assumption in the preceding historical documents.** This sweep's launch function explicitly requests ANGLE SwiftShader and enables unsafe SwiftShader regardless of the show flag. The flag only changes headless versus headed presentation. Therefore historical directions to use this sweep with --show as proof of a physical GPU are not supported by the current launch code. Its declared purpose is compile safety, and its sole hard gate is webglCompile; thumbnail sigma and NaN fraction are diagnostic only. A real-GPU RFF validation stage should capture the selected Vulkan device/driver and production pipeline configuration independently. Do not extrapolate WebGL software compilation to Vulkan descriptor-layout correctness, image fidelity, or runtime performance.

**Understand exactly which shader is compiled.** The sweep generates the engine shader, removes its final main function/output declaration with a text replacement, and appends a custom sphere-tracing main. It therefore exercises shared generated formula machinery through a diagnostic entry point, not the original lighting/material/postprocessing entry point. Dead-code elimination can also make resources irrelevant that the production main uses. RFF should keep a separate full production-pipeline gate, including descriptors and push constants, in addition to small diagnostic shaders. Text-based replacement assumes main is last and the declaration shape matches; a defined diagnostic entry-point interface is more robust for a reusable validation tool.

The diagnostic shader marches at most 140 steps from a fixed camera, uses distance times 0.9 with a minimum step, and declares a hit below a fixed 0.001 threshold. It estimates normals with six distance evaluations separated by 0.01, then encodes proximity, log-normalized orbit trap, and iteration information into RGB. This is a useful visual-debugging technique: RFF can expose separate raw field views for smooth iterations, distance/gradient, normals, masks, and footprint/filtering decisions before artistic grading obscures them. A single combined RGB image is harder to interpret quantitatively; pair it with labeled individual channels and finite-value counters. The fixed 3D distance thresholds are not suitable precision policies for deep-zoom 2D rendering.

The orange invalid-value marker only checks the distance returned during primary marching. It does not cover trap/log validity, iteration-channel validity, the six normal samples, or normalization of a zero gradient. A low reported orange fraction therefore cannot prove all shading intermediates finite. Its uniform setup also supplies selected defaults and bank values rather than replaying the entire scene, which the script itself acknowledges when explaining why numeric sampling is not a gate. For RFF, bind a complete validated fixture and check each relevant stage; do not count an attractive diagnostic thumbnail as a correctness oracle.

**Resume only compatible evidence, and retain failures.** The sweep resumes by primary/secondary names alone, skipping every previously recorded pair regardless of result or source revision. Historical failures are not included in the new invocation's counters; when all pairs are present it exits successfully without re-evaluating them. Interrupting a run can also lead to a success exit when the processed prefix has no failures. A robust RFF matrix should key results by shader/configuration/harness/device revisions, preserve failed cells in the aggregate verdict, and mark interrupted or incomplete runs explicitly. Its Promise.race timeout does not cancel the browser operation; closing the page is the subsequent isolation step. Retain that distinction in any asynchronous RFF test runner and record failure details, rather than treating an observation timeout as completed computation.

**Imported-shader checks need current end-to-end provenance.** The DEC probe mirrors a V3 import pipeline, filters dead parameters, registers a definition, checks capability rejection, fuses it with Mandelbulb, and generates shader text. It clearly distinguishes structural gates from GPU compilation in its final message. However, its list mode filters on a catalog's earlier V3 pass flag, only prints build failures, and exits zero; the ordinary mode also prints a control-pair failure without adding it to the final failure count. A missing secondary namespace is diagnostic text rather than an assertion. Census mode counts translator outcomes, not rendered support. For an RFF shader-import feature, key compatibility records by exact source and translator revision, enforce control failures, and report each achieved validation level separately. A copied mirror of production import code can drift; prefer a shared import entry point with explicit options. These are adoption requirements for RFF's potential tooling, not a diversion into modifying GMT's probes.

### Preserve appearance when rebuilding reusable shader compositions

Full document reads on 2026-10-08: `plans/mb3d/sessions/S-weave-p4-build.md` (199 lines) and `S-nformula-weave-unification.md` (197). These complete the previously listed weave-session design/handover documents. Their dated delivery reports are historical claims, not independently reproduced measurements in this audit.

**RFF opportunity: rebuild an effect composition while keeping the surrounding scene.** The delivery history explicitly distinguishes building/registering a reusable definition from loading it with a preserve-current-look merge. This separation supports two useful operations: create a fresh preset with defaults, or revise an existing composition while retaining its camera, lighting, palette, and material choices. RFF should similarly separate effect-definition construction from scene-state application. Make the merge policy explicit for each parameter family, preserve unchanged instance values and animation routing, and only initialize newly introduced instances. A shared builder can serve an editor, importer, and preset picker without giving all three identical state-reset semantics.

The handover records an exception for adding layers to a gallery scene: authoring a fresh weave could lose the scene's own parameters, so that route retained legacy-shaped migration. This illustrates why a formula ID plus its default preset is not a complete replacement for an edited scene. For RFF's 2D or relief appearance presets, compose against an immutable snapshot of the actual loaded values and dependencies, not against a reconstructed default. Treat rebuild publication and scene revision as one operation so a later completion cannot apply an older merge to a newly selected location. This is a workflow recommendation, not a claim that RFF currently has GMT's scene-composition path.

**Unify contracts while preserving distinct semantics.** The original plan proposed one uniform packer, one parameter-mapping primitive, one emitter, and typed options for kernel features. Its own amendments correct earlier claims: multi-slot literal baking was a fallback, live scheduling could not be replaced by a static lookup table without losing animation, and within-iteration graph composition was different from between-iteration scheduling. Those distinctions remain useful for RFF: centralize parameter metadata and binding generation, but keep mathematical iteration, appearance graph order, and time-dependent control separate. Consolidation is successful only if the observable behavior and precision contract survive. Do not add a generic fractal-weaving engine merely to obtain reusable shader controls.

The delivery notes also record a compositional capability union after missing cutting-plane declarations were encountered. For an RFF effect graph, calculate required textures, intermediates, sampling support, and shader features from all enabled nodes, not only a designated primary effect. Validate the combined resource layout against the C++ pipeline configuration. Conversely, unioning capability flags does not prove that two mathematical distance estimators compose correctly; geometry semantics need their own derivation and validation. Both flat 2D effects and relief lighting can benefit from dependency-aware assembly without changing the fractal recurrence.

**Historical evidence has a bounded scope.** The document reports zero differing subpixels for a specific set of synthesized legacy migration fixtures, then separately describes the later accepted non-pixel-exact fast-path retirement. These claims are not contradictory when scoped to their respective changes and fixtures, but neither proves universal compatibility for arbitrary saved scenes. It also reports metadata-only differences while shader bytes remained identical; those are distinct artifacts and should be compared separately. RFF validation should preserve exact fixture IDs, source revisions, old/new settings, numerical output, and image comparisons. A later documentation statement that animation transfer remained unfinished is superseded by the subsequent implementation already read; do not turn historical 'next' sections into current missing-feature recommendations.

### Optional help and online services: limited relevance to rendering improvements

Full source reads on 2026-10-08: `engine-gmt/components/FirstRunHint.tsx` (51 lines), `DonateButton.tsx` (146), `engine-gmt/support.ts` (32), and `engine-gmt/supabase.ts` (41). These peripheral modules offer no direct shader-quality improvement and do not change the priority ranking of appearance proposals.

FirstRunHint is a small dismissible overlay pointing to help and the formula picker. It loads a single persisted dismissal flag and hides immediately after dismissal; its positioning assumes a particular top-bar height. RFF could use a similarly optional first-use hint for new lighting or mask tools, with a persistent route back to help and placement derived from actual layout. This read does not verify screen fit, accessibility contrast, or the historical screenshot measurements quoted in the comments. A storage write failure can still dismiss the current instance but does not establish persistence across sessions.

The support configuration centralizes labels and components across GMT applications. Its appName option changes menu/title wording while retaining GMT donation destinations and introductory text. It is therefore a branding reuse example, not a portable RFF support implementation. The donation component has ordinary external links and a decorative mouse-hover image reveal; it does not itself process a payment. The reveal cleans up event listeners but contains no reduced-motion branch, and its externally hosted icons add network dependencies. No donation links were followed or services contacted. There is no reason to copy this branding or add payment functionality as part of the shader work.

The Supabase module lazily creates a shared client only when both public configuration values exist, names its session storage key, and enables session persistence, token refresh, and URL-session detection. Its enabled flag proves configuration presence only, not connectivity, authorization policy, or service health. The comment about Row Level Security describes the intended server boundary; this client file cannot verify that boundary. Access to window.localStorage is direct, so environments where storage access throws need handling at a suitable integration boundary. For RFF, optional online preset browsing could share an explicitly owned service client, while local rendering and saved-scene access remain independent. Keep project/session namespaces distinct if multiple installations share a storage origin, and do not infer a need for account infrastructure from this source review alone.

### Optional preset-sharing accounts without interrupting local rendering

Full source reads on 2026-10-08: all six inventoried files in `engine-gmt/auth/`: `authStore.ts` (208 lines), `installAuth.tsx` (60), `index.ts` (5), `AuthTopbarWidget.tsx` (135), `AuthOverlay.tsx` (381), and `AccountPanel.tsx` (474).
