This tests reconstruction under its local numeric model; it does not open Blender/Cinema 4D, validate their color management or cover arbitrary multi-stop, alpha, cyclic or discontinuous palettes. The same stop budget selected for C4D is used throughout this comparison.

The useful RFF idea is allocating export stops where reconstruction error is largest, especially around gamut-mapping bends, instead of assuming uniform spacing captures every palette. Treat this as a derived export representation: preserve frozen recipe IDs, seeds, RNG ordering and source palette data. Report or reject unmet approximation tolerance rather than implying lossless interchange. A named adaptive algorithm needs appropriate provenance if adapted, and target interpolation/color-space behavior needs separate validation.

The guard also checks Python payload-marker presence and exact agreement between generated template text and its source renderer. Those are useful drift checks but do not execute the importers. Two limitations matter when interpreting its success message: NaN error values evade `greater than budget` checks, and the final 'no rescued pair' failure is appended only after the sole failure/exit branch, so that condition cannot fail the process. These details explain why RFF validation should explicitly require finite errors and evaluate all acceptance conditions before returning success. No observed palette quality or speedup is inferred from merely reading this test.

## Measuring shader improvements through the real export path (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/bench-pt.mts` (872 lines) and `debug/opus-cam.ts` (30 lines). The already reviewed `debug/render-harness.ts` bucket loop and output path were rechecked to establish what the benchmark actually measures. No benchmark was run. The value for RFF is a controlled quality/performance comparison design, not a measured endorsement of GMT's path tracer.

### Separate sampling quality, tiling correctness and execution cost

The benchmark drives the real bucket-render integration rather than a standalone shader approximation. Its suites compare increasing samples against a higher-sample reference, isolate internal GPU buckets from separately exported image tiles, sweep seam error versus samples, and record render time across resolutions. It toggles bloom and chromatic aberration independently and compares each with a matching single-image reference. This factorization is directly useful for RFF: test the actual output path used by users, then isolate the effect whose behavior changed.

For the previously prioritized roughness/environment and pixel-footprint filtering improvements, compare the same camera, geometry/field, palette, exposure, output dimensions and sampling policy with only the selected change varied. In 3D, include smooth and rough surfaces, bright environment features, fine geometry and dark backgrounds. In flat 2D, include narrow bands, high-frequency palette transitions, interior boundaries and deep locations. One canonical formula is useful for a smoke, but common pipeline code does not make all scene content or numerical workload equivalent. The benchmark's default one-scene choice is therefore not broad material or fractal coverage.

The helper makes camera framing explicit: spherical eye position about the origin, a look-at quaternion, zero local camera position, and the eye stored in the scene offset with zero low components. This is suitable for its ordinary-scale 3D fixtures; it is not a template for RFF's deep-coordinate fixtures. Preserve precise center/scale and reference identity in 2D comparisons. The helper itself supplies no finite/distance validation or special pole policy beyond the underlying look-at implementation.

### A nested reference is not an independent ground truth

The convergence suite uses one tile and one GPU bucket to preserve the intended sample-index relationship. It requires the reference count M to exceed every sweep count N, then divides raw MSE by `1-N/M`. For independent, equal-variance samples averaged linearly, a shared-prefix comparison has variance proportional to `1/N-1/M`; this explains the correction. The source acknowledges nonlinear tone mapping, but deterministic Halton/blue-noise sequences also do not by themselves establish that independent-sample statistical model. The corrected number is a heuristic under these output conditions, not a proved estimate of true rendering error.

Measurements are taken from final 8-bit RGB, ignoring alpha for MSE/PSNR. Quantization, clipping and tone mapping can hide linear-HDR differences. The repeat comparison uses the whole RGBA buffer, so its identity definition differs from RGB `maxAbs===0`. A single repeated count is recorded but a mismatch does not fail the run or disable the correction. Effective per-bucket counts are reported, not asserted against the requested count before applying nominal N/M. Buffer length is not validated against width×height×4; malformed buffers can generate NaN metrics. These details limit what the resulting charts would prove.

For RFF, retain final-output comparisons because users see them, and add relevant pre-display linear/field checks where those establish the shader contract. Require valid buffer sizes, expected dimensions and actual sample counts. Use independent reference sequences or multiple controlled sequences when estimating stochastic error, and label a nested-reference approximation explicitly. Keep numerical fractal correctness separate from appearance error. Infinite PSNR needs explicit serialization: assigning JavaScript Infinity still becomes null in JSON, despite the source's attempt to guard the zero-error case.

### Measure a seam against the same image content

The seam suite constructs boundary positions using the same bottom-up tile convention and compares a narrow boundary band against both a full-image reference and the remaining interior. It also computes adjacent-pixel step magnitudes at boundaries and measures the same positions on the reference. The reference baseline is important: a genuine shape edge crossing a tile boundary can increase a step ratio even when there is no rendering seam. Conversely, a ratio near one is not proof of invisibility, especially for chromatic errors with small weighted-RGB differences or a localized defect diluted by averaging.

The source uses weighted encoded RGB bytes for its luma-like metrics. Whole-image RGB maximum error and a magnified difference image complement them, but region maxima, chromatic differences and edge-focused fixtures remain useful. The ×8 heatmap saturates large errors; it is a visual locator, not a full error-scale replacement.

The cases labeled natural convergence now run every bucket to a fixed cap four times the reference sample count, as confirmed by the render harness. Their labels/notes retain older early-out terminology. They cannot isolate unequal-convergence seams because that mechanism is no longer present in this path, and their unequal budgets confound a simple tiled-versus-reference interpretation. The separate seam-versus-samples suite does use matched counts, but its expected decaying/plateau patterns are hypotheses in notes, not fitted or enforced acceptance criteria. Increasing samples cannot be assumed to eliminate every systematic tile artifact.

For RFF, compare matched sample counts first, verify the actual output coverage, and vary one cause at a time: sample-coordinate mapping, filter footprint, material UV, tile halo or output transform. Add non-square dimensions, odd sizes and partial edge tiles; the current square, divisible-by-two-and-three fixtures do not exercise those boundaries. These tests apply equally to 3D roughness/refraction filters and 2D palette/normal/mask processing.

### Record what the timing and backend labels actually mean

`renderMs` comes from wall time around the harness bucket loop, excluding scene compilation and final canvas stitching/PNG conversion. The loop awaits animation frames and includes its CPU orchestration and bucket work. It is not an isolated GPU shader timer or complete end-to-end export time. Even the timing suite, which disables returned pixels and PNG strings, still follows the capture/stitch path in the harness. Normalize costs only after verifying actual work, and report shader GPU time, render-loop time and export time separately when those distinctions matter.

The headed `--gpu` flag selects default Chromium launch behavior but does not query and certify the actual graphics device/backend. Headless explicitly requests SwiftShader. The code's claims that relative noise/seam metrics transfer across GPUs and that long sessions lose precision are not established by this source read; hardware/compiler numerical behavior must be checked on the intended target. Restarts and one retry for context-loss-like errors are operational measures, not evidence of the underlying cause or bit-identical retries. Page/console errors are collected but only attached when the returned result is already unsuccessful.

RFF comparisons should record device, driver, code/shader hashes, resolved settings, resource formats and run identity. Include repeated warmed measurements and variation, not a single fixed-order time per case. Saving intermediate results is valuable for lengthy studies, but the append mode here retains rows solely by suite, not scene/backend/tier/source identity; top-level metadata is replaced and per-scene determinism extras are not merged. Mixed historical results can therefore look like one current run. Use immutable run manifests or verify compatibility before merging.

Finally, this script is principally a measurement/report generator: poor PSNR, high seam error and failed repeat identity do not trigger a quality-failure exit. Unknown scene names are silently filtered, and unsupported suite selections can yield no meaningful cases. RFF's eventual acceptance gate should assert that the intended cases ran, enforce the particular quality contract and preserve the evidence behind any claimed speedup. Until such measurements exist, the adoption priorities remain source-informed engineering judgments, not measured performance rankings.

## Reproducible appearance galleries for RFF shader presets (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/frag-gallery.mts`, `debug/frag-retry-singlecolor.mts`, `debug/frag-report.mts`, `debug/frag-contact-sheet.mts`, `debug/frag-thumbs-commit.mts`, and `debug/gen-dcc-templates.mjs`. These scripts were read without launching their browsers or changing their outputs. Together with the previously reviewed auto-levels utility, they show how generated previews can become disconnected from the settings that produced them.

### Useful feature transfer: compare materials and palettes under known conditions

The gallery renders source formulas through the engine harness and records a thumbnail plus status. Each job receives a fresh browser context, an optional explicit orbit camera and optional material/glow overrides. A worker pool limits concurrent jobs. The retry utility detects low RGB standard deviation, then tries several orbit distances with camera-relative lights, disabled shadows and fixed material/glow settings. It saves the candidate with the greatest mean component standard deviation, preserving the original image separately.

For RFF, an analogous appearance gallery would make roughness, independent lighting, masks and palette mappings easier to compare. A 3D gallery should hold geometry and camera fixed while varying one material control; a 2D gallery should hold precise location and numerical field fixed while varying color/mask/relief settings. An optional diagnostic light can reveal surface structure without rewriting the saved artistic lighting. Store the complete resolved preset alongside each preview so selecting it can reproduce the image. Keep existing palette recipe identities and generation order unchanged.

The retry score is a visibility heuristic, not correctness or aesthetic quality. A grayscale edge can have high RGB standard deviation; noise or a wrong rendering can score well; an intentionally smooth/dark image can score poorly. The implementation does not measure the additional unique-color spread mentioned in its header. Its successful candidate can remain below the recovery threshold, and the returned status records best distance/score without a complete snapshot of all camera, lighting, source and engine inputs. RFF should label such results as suggested framing/diagnostic previews and retain the original scene, rather than claim that a high-variance image repairs the shader.

### Thumbnail identity must include source and appearance revisions

The gallery resolves files from a hardcoded developer root and reference folders, with a basename-search fallback. That fallback can choose a different file when names collide; it is not proof of the exact public formula used by the application. Sanitizing IDs by replacing punctuation with underscores can also map distinct IDs to one filename. The retry's reverse lookup overwrites collisions. Explicit IDs bypass the gallery's usual recommendation filter, allowing a non-renderable recommendation into a nominally V3/V4 job. Numeric CLI parameters and empty selections are not comprehensively validated.

RFF should use canonical source IDs plus hashes and collision-resistant artifact names, and record resolved renderer capability/settings. Generate previews from the same saved data and rendering path that opening the preset uses. The committed-thumbnail builder shares its safe-ID helper with the picker, which is better than independently evolving naming rules, but matching transforms alone does not establish uniqueness or freshness.

The builder selects report categories, reads their leveled PNGs, downsizes with browser image smoothing and emits JPEGs plus an index of successfully written IDs. It does not itself select the best retry image; it reads the configured levels directory. Thus inclusion in the recovered category does not by itself prove that the thumbnail depicts the recovered configuration. It preserves aspect ratio by allocating a reduced rectangular canvas, rather than padding arbitrary input into an exact square. JPEG output also has no alpha-preservation policy. These choices are reasonable for curated thumbnails but should not be confused with faithful full-quality shader output.

For RFF, keep thumbnails explicitly derived and disposable, associate them with source/settings/output-transform revisions, and regenerate stale entries. Missing thumbnails should not mean an otherwise supported effect is unavailable. A transactional manifest can prevent a partially generated batch from presenting an incomplete catalog as the complete supported set. The current builder reports missing files without failing, permits duplicate IDs from categories, leaves old images in place and overwrites the index after the run. Those mechanics do not constitute verified visual coverage.

### A gallery report needs an explicit untested state

The triage report treats every catalog-recommended entry that is neither in selected failure logs nor in the flat-image list as working. It does not require a current successful render record or an existing PNG. An unresolved, unrendered or omitted entry can consequently receive the working label. Duplicate or stale failure-log rows can also distort totals. The gallery's own JSONL status is overwritten for each batch, while the report reads selected text logs rather than using a versioned complete run manifest. A statement that a row works out of the box is therefore stronger than the evidence required by this script.

RFF should distinguish not attempted, source unavailable, compile failed, rendered, visually reviewed and verified against a reference. Persist per-item completion immediately, tie it to a run manifest, and require positive evidence for success. Keep image quality separate from import capability. This makes a future shader preset browser useful without presenting attractive previews as proof of numerical accuracy or feature support.

Contact sheets are useful for spotting broad regressions, but this implementation stretches every input into a square and shortens labels. Its HTML supplies the fuller filename but no settings/source evidence; it embeds images rather than linking every image as its comment suggests. RFF comparison sheets should preserve aspect, expose unambiguous IDs, show the original output on demand and provide the settings needed to reproduce it. HTML labels and paths derived from imported names should be escaped when generating a report.

### Keep generated exporter templates mechanically traceable

The DCC template generator reads the two canonical Python scripts, removes carriage returns, and embeds their contents as JSON-escaped TypeScript strings. Its exported pure rendering function allows the drift checker reviewed earlier to compare without intentionally writing. This is a useful source-of-truth pattern for any RFF exporter template: author one implementation, generate embeddings reproducibly, retain provenance and compare generated artifacts in the relevant check.

Its normalization removes all carriage returns, not exclusively CRLF pairs, and its direct-execution test is a filename-suffix check on `process.argv[1]`. Neither proves the generated Python is semantically correct in a target application. Preserve intentional content and validate the exported behavior separately. The reusable contribution here is maintaining one authoritative template, not adopting a new rendering effect or claiming a measured shader improvement.

## Numerical estimator diagnostics and editable shader constants (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/probe-numeric-de-rebuild.mts`, `debug/probe-scene-de.mts`, the four `debug/probe-theli-{isolate,iters,ray,sweep}.mts` scripts, `debug/probe-autoroute-est7.mts`, `debug/probe-mb3d-bakereason.mts`, and `debug/probe-mb3d-param-regress.mts`. The already reviewed render harness was searched to confirm that `qualityOverride` is merged into compile-time quality configuration. None of these probes was executed. Their comments describe intended investigations, not verified outcomes of this review.

### Distinguish mathematical correctness from visible geometry

The numerical-DE probe compares one analytic-estimator case with numerical estimator 7 at probe multipliers 0.4, 1 and 2.5, then renders six additional sample scenes. It requests headed ANGLE D3D11, disables fog, saves thumbnails and prints non-black/NaN fractions. It does not assert successful rendering, finite metrics, smoothness, probe invariance or agreement with an independent distance reference. Missing NaN statistics default to zero. Per-render exceptions are caught and logged without failing the process. Thus the header's description of proof that parameter sensitivity is gone is stronger than the acceptance logic.

For RFF, separate a surface-visibility diagnostic from a numerical validation. A numerical derivative used for 3D normals, displacement or a distance estimator needs a defined perturbation scale and an error check across relevant coordinates, scales and parameters. A visually smoother result alone does not certify a conservative distance bound or accurate normals. Compare trusted numerical/analytic values where available, hit positions and normal continuity separately from the lit image; retain finite/status checks before interpreting any statistic. These probes do not justify adopting estimator 7 into RFF's Mandelbrot calculation or relaxing its precision requirements.

The 2D transfer is narrower and useful: appearance derivatives for a height/relief field can be checked at several pixel footprints, and masks can be inspected independently of color. They must not replace precise orbit/perturbation computation. An orbit-derived DE also requires the correct derivative information through RFF's MPA path; a finite difference of displayed RGB is not an equivalent quantity.

### Use controlled isolation to explain an effect

The Theli isolation probe disables either formula slot by setting its iteration count to zero, compares the full composition, and varies the relative slot count. This is a useful experimental pattern for future RFF effect stacks: render each contribution alone and then combined to identify which layer creates a feature. However, changing a fractal formula sequence changes the geometry itself, unlike muting a post-processing layer. Do not assume linear addition or identical DE behavior between the isolated and combined scenes. The code relies on fixed slot positions rather than asserting their identities.

The iteration probe changes the scene's iteration limit over five values while holding ray quality overrides fixed. The ray probe varies step multiplier and ray-step budget in a two-by-two grid. Those are distinct quantities: formula iterations affect the evaluated field, while ray steps affect traversal. The comment that iterations only affect speed is not established by this script. Increasing a ray-step multiplier is also not a generally safe acceleration: it can skip features if the estimator is not sufficiently conservative. For RFF, never turn a missing-detail problem into an unverified speed/precision tradeoff.

The repeated max-step sweep is especially useful as a diagnostic design: it revisits earlier settings within one session to look for order-dependent state. But it saves images and prints brightness/spread rather than comparing the repeated results. A RFF regression test should assert the resolved settings and resource revisions, compare the repeated outputs under controlled sampling, and distinguish mathematical changes from stale pipelines/history. The ray probe's wall time includes the remote render call and image write before logging, so it is not isolated shader execution time.

Across these probes, page errors are swallowed, failures can become zero-valued visual metrics, and normal browser cleanup is not protected by a complete failure-path finally block. The local path/port choices are developer-specific. These are investigative scripts, not portable correctness gates. Reuse the experimental questions and controlled comparisons, not their success labels or browser flags.

### Capability-driven estimator selection needs explicit checks

The autoroute probe emits every bundled scene and prints the chosen default estimator and slot names, counting estimator-7 selections. It does not assert the expected set named in its comment, reject unexpected routes or fail on caught per-scene errors. For RFF, an effect requiring derivatives should resolve against declared field capabilities, with unsupported combinations reported explicitly. Verify the exact expected cases and the resulting shader path; do not infer mathematical compatibility from a name, a count or successful import.

The scene-header probe prints iteration, bailout, distance-stop and step-related fields at fixed binary offsets. It skips missing named samples and does not independently validate the file version, buffer length or decoded values before reading. Such a tool can help compare known fixtures, but it is not a specification or a general parser. RFF format compatibility should continue to use independently validated, versioned decoding rather than copying diagnostic offsets as an authoritative format definition.

### Preserve behavior when exposing baked constants as controls

The bake-reason probe measures each used formula slot with a fresh lane allocator, then adds demand to distinguish scalar/vec3 capacity pressure from an option that cannot bind even alone. That separation is valuable: accumulated resource exhaustion should not be mislabeled as an unsupported parameter type. The script uses 24 scalar and three vec3 lanes as its model, classifies any nonempty parameter list as parametric, special-cases a quaternion slot and otherwise reports one selected cause. It does not prove that all parameters are editable, that emitted GLSL compiles or that those hardcoded budgets match every target. A missing emitted definition is not separately classified as unsupported before this analysis.

For an RFF material/effect system, resolve descriptor/uniform capacity before exposing controls, preserve meaningful failure reasons and keep C++/GLSL layouts exact. Prefer a validated resource plan over silently baking some advertised editable values. Baked and dynamic variants should reproduce the same output at the same settings. Resource allocation improvements must not alter precise fractal calculations or existing saved-setting interpretation.

The parameter-regression probe attempts that equivalence at the constant level: it packs literal options, binds them to uniform expressions, evaluates expressions at their defaults and compares matching offsets with a relative tolerance. However, only selected scene-name substrings and decompiled formula slots are visited; missing baked offsets and failed bindings are skipped. Its ad hoc JavaScript expression evaluator supports a restricted subset and can return NaN, which the greater-than tolerance check does not reject. It prints mismatches without a failing exit, and it compares JavaScript-number evaluation rather than actual GLSL floating-point execution. Matching defaults alone does not verify nondefault ranges, shader layouts or complete formula behavior.

The RFF transfer is a meaningful equivalence gate: validate finite values and complete offset coverage, test representative nondefault/boundary values, verify CPU-to-GPU bindings, then compare rendered or numerical output for the specific effect. Evaluate known expression forms structurally rather than executing imported expressions as JavaScript. Distinctive imported formulas still require source/license provenance; successful constant binding is not permission to copy their implementations.

## Shader composition metadata and parameter-packing evidence (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/probe-tm-compose.mts`, `debug/probe-tm-opts.mts`, `debug/probe-tm-params.mts`, `debug/probe-oxnot-consts.mts`, `debug/probe-oxnot-usage.mts`, `debug/probe-mb3d-packgain.mts`, and `debug/probe-mb3d-slots.mts`. These are inspection/reporting tools, not executed tests in this audit. Their main contribution to RFF is making shader inputs and state dependencies inspectable without confusing diagnostic heuristics with verified capabilities.

### Explicit field ownership makes composable effects safer

The TimeMachine composition probe prints generated loop initialization/body, estimator configuration and full emitted GLSL, then searches each slot function for writes to the derivative-like `w` and constant `c`. Inspecting intermediate generated code alongside the source options and resolved defaults is useful for diagnosing formula composition. However, the regular expressions recognize a limited textual shape: direct assignment detection misses compound assignments, helper-mediated writes and other component forms, while matching text does not establish execution on a relevant control-flow path. The function-body extraction also assumes a particular newline/brace layout. Its output is not a complete dataflow analysis.

For RFF, attach explicit input/output metadata to any future composable appearance stage: scalar field, normal, mask, color, coordinate transform and required history. Declare which values a stage reads or changes, resolve the stage order, and validate required producers before compiling/binding. This supports 3D layered materials and independently controlled lighting, and transfers to 2D relief, palette and mask chains. Mathematical formula composition requires stronger derivative/state rules than post-processing composition; do not treat the two as interchangeable or infer MPA compatibility from emitted text.

The options and parameters probes print decoded types/values/names and the exposed parameter list/core defaults for one scene. They do not assert equal counts, correct names, semantic units or default equivalence. A nonempty parameter list only proves that some controls were emitted. For RFF, a developer-facing resolved-parameter report should map each saved field to its validated range/unit, shader binding and effective value, while the normal user interface stays focused on the visual control. Verify that every advertised control changes the intended output and survives save/reload without modifying frozen palette recipes.

### Dense parameter storage is an implementation option, not a measured win

The packing-gain probe classifies emitted formulas as gaining editability when parameters exist and generated function text contains a `uVec2` or `uVec4` component reference. It assumes those component accesses uniquely identify newly packed scalar lanes and that the historical six-scalar budget would have forced baking. It does not run the old allocator, compare prior results, verify all editable fields, compile the shader or render a changed value. A missing definition is grouped with baked cases, and the reported number of sliders is the number of parameter descriptors, including vector descriptors, rather than necessarily the number of scalar UI controls. Exceptions are counted and printed without an acceptance failure.

The reusable RFF idea is capacity-aware packing when shader parameter storage actually limits useful features. First inspect RFF's existing Vulkan limits/layout; do not transplant GMT's fixed WebGL lane budget. Keep semantic parameter IDs independent of physical storage, generate matching CPU/GLSL layout information, and test component offsets, alignment and update behavior. Resource-efficient storage can make additional 3D material or 2D mask controls practical, but this probe provides no GPU speedup measurement and does not justify reducing numeric precision. Preserve an explicit unsupported result rather than silently treating failed generation as a baked-but-working shader.

### Similar scenes are clues, not proof of decoding correctness

The Oxnot constants probe prints detailed scene/header values, camera basis, options and a derived step-width expression using the literal 2.1345. Its own radius-squared label contains uncertainty. Neither the literal nor that interpretation is independently established by this diagnostic file. Before adopting any distinctive camera/step conversion, trace its documented origin and units, confirm the target format version and retain provenance. Printed decimal values with reduced precision are useful for inspection but cannot serve as exact numerical fixtures.

The usage probe scans external sample files, records selected emitted slot names and calls a formula's decoding exonerated if it appears in another bundled scene. Bundled membership is only a name-based proxy for prior curation here; no images or reference comparisons are checked. Another scene can exercise different parameters, branches, slot order and derivative context. Parse/emit failures are silently skipped, and repeated uses of the same formula in a scene can enter the list more than once. The resulting count and labels should not be read as verified scene coverage.

For RFF, reuse cross-scene occurrence analysis to select representative tests, not to declare a shader correct. Cover the parameter/branch combinations that matter to the proposed feature and keep unsupported or failed cases visible. The slot-inspection probe similarly prints only the first six option values and selects the first name-substring match, with an empty filter selecting the first sample; it is not a complete scene export. Canonical fixture IDs, complete resolved settings and source hashes are necessary before those observations can support a reproducible 3D or 2D regression claim.

## Coordinate roles and verified overrides in shader comparisons (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/probe-mb3d-4d-uniqueness.mts`, `debug/probe-mb3d-campose.mts`, and `debug/probe-hyper-glow.mts`. The current render-harness wrapper and camera application were inspected again. No probes were run. These files add validation requirements for RFF; they do not establish a new 4D rendering implementation or a measured glow benefit.

### Keep fourth coordinates separate from derivative state

The uniqueness probe explicitly recognizes that a variable named `w` can be a fourth coordinate in one formula and derivative-related state in another. It attempts to identify derivative support from internal formula IDs, scratch-variable metadata and regular-expression matches in decompiled/generated text. Some results intentionally remain unknown, but the aggregate `anyDeriv` only checks for true and therefore does not preserve the distinction between all-false and partly-unknown inputs. Later headings call another regex-based classification accurate, although direct-write matching still cannot establish complete derivative propagation through helper calls, branches or composition. The presence of any custom `getDist` is labeled a 4D bulb path without independently establishing that semantic role.

For RFF, encode semantic roles explicitly in any future formula/appearance interface. A fourth coordinate, derivative accumulator, distance result and mask channel must not be interchangeable merely because their storage type matches. A stage that writes a derivative does not establish that the entire composed formula carries a valid derivative. Propagate unsupported/unknown capability information instead of converting it into apparent absence or support.

The probe's deOption grouping uses substring matching on serialized metadata rather than exact option membership; its quaternion exclusion also suppresses a mixed scene containing that marker. It ignores source files that fail parsing/emission and can count repeated slot occurrences as repeated scene uses. These reports can guide investigation but cannot certify the corpus or select a mathematically valid estimator by themselves. For 2D, the transferable feature is explicit field contracts for relief, normal and mask effects. Rendering slices/projections of a new 4D formula would require a separately defined mathematical feature, not a shader-only transplant into the existing Mandelbrot path.

### Validate the complete camera transformation

The camera probe compares a mapped MB3D camera with a locally constructed no-Z-flip variant on five asymmetric scenes. Asymmetric fixtures are a good choice for exposing handedness/mirroring errors that symmetric fractals can conceal. However, it only saves images and brightness/spread statistics; it contains no reference-image assertion or orientation landmark check.

Its alternate pose supplies position, quaternion and target distance but omits `sceneOffset`. The current harness independently falls back to the preset's scene offset when that override is absent. Thus this is not necessarily a comparison that changes only handedness: a nonzero imported offset remains active alongside the alternative absolute-looking position. The local construction also does not establish equivalence with every camera/projection field in the production mapper. A prettier or brighter alternative cannot determine the correct convention.

RFF should test complete coordinate transforms with an explicit origin/offset, orientation, projection, aspect and precise-position policy. Use known asymmetric landmarks and verify transforms numerically as well as visually. In 2D this applies to Y inversion, axis transposition, tile origins, image-layer UV and cursor-to-fractal mapping. Preserve high/low or arbitrary-precision coordinates instead of validating deep views with only ordinary-scale camera positions.

### Check that the experimental control reaches the shader

The Hyperben glow probe supplies four atmosphere variants through `stateOverride`. A search of the current render harness finds no consumer of that property. The MB3D wrapper forwards the specification to `runOne`, whose actual configuration path uses `configOverrides`; the glow probe therefore does not apply its intended intensity/sharpness variations through this interface. Different output images, if observed, would not by themselves prove the requested glow sweep occurred. Missing render values again become zeros, and errors are logged rather than used as a quality gate.

For RFF shader comparisons, record requested and resolved values and verify the corresponding GPU binding or compiled variant before attributing an image difference to a control. An off/on experiment should demonstrably change that control while holding the rest of the scene fixed. Test any field-based glow/emission separately from screen-space bloom and retain the prior distinction between those effects. This source finding does not change the existing non-bloom priority ranking; it strengthens the evidence required before reporting effectiveness.

## Independent numerical checks and end-to-end import boundaries (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/probe-decomp-menger3.mts`, `debug/probe-menger3-import.mts`, `debug/probe-mb3d-genmenger.mts`, and `debug/probe-pxdb-sim.mts`. No script was executed. These sources sharpen the validation plan for any RFF formula/field extension; they do not demonstrate a production improvement by themselves.

The raw Menger proof of concept substitutes a fixed constant buffer into externally generated GLSL, rejects remaining `Cm` tokens, wraps position/derivative/trap state and renders through the raw-formula harness. It uses only scale 3, unit component scales and identity rotations. The companion import probe supplies a synthetic decoded scene object with the same ordinary defaults to the fused importer. It therefore exercises scene-to-shader integration, not binary-file decoding. The two probes also use different iteration limits, dimensions and explicit quality settings, so their images are not a controlled equivalence pair. Neither compares to an independent reference or fails merely because the returned render is unsuccessful; it logs the result and saves an image when available.

For RFF, keep three separate checks when extending a formula or shader field: mathematical function evaluation, serialized-data decoding, and actual renderer integration. Use matched settings and nontrivial parameter fixtures, including nonzero rotations and unequal component scales when relevant. A recognizable sponge at identity settings cannot validate rotation order, packed offsets, derivative propagation or all imported behavior. The raw probe removes leading `//` lines from its external GLSL before embedding it; that is not a provenance-preserving production workflow. Trace the original source/license before adapting decompiled or generated implementations, and retain the required attribution in RFF source and NOTICE.

The parameter-gate probe shows cumulative allocation per active slot, including per-slot initialization, and tries to mirror default-option padding. It duplicates the recognized option-type set and fixed pool capacities instead of querying a single authoritative capability description. It also predicts the overall verdict without invoking the full emitter in this file. Such a diagnostic can drift from the real decision. RFF should expose the actual resolved resource/capability plan, with reasons returned by the producer, rather than reimplement its logic in a second reporting path. This helps both 3D material controls and 2D color/mask controls remain editable without silently changing semantics.

The PseudoXDB CPU probe explicitly rounds many intermediate operations with `Math.fround` and compares aggregate orbit outcomes against ordinary JavaScript arithmetic on an 80×80 grid in one Z slice. Its denominator `sqrt(x*x+y*y)` exposes an axis singularity worth testing. However, the even-sized symmetric grid excludes exact x=0 and y=0 sample coordinates initially, so it does not directly test an initial point on that singular axis. The initial coordinates and constants are not uniformly rounded before every operation. This is a chosen sequence of rounded JavaScript operations, not a full emulation of GPU execution, fused arithmetic, subnormal handling or x87 behavior. The file's claim of an exact CPU float32 simulation is consequently too broad.

It starts the orbit at the pixel coordinate, uses a fixed iteration limit/bailout and one component multiplier, and groups both NaN and infinity under one fate label. It prints aggregate counts rather than comparing each pixel's first divergent value or asserting a reference result. Equal totals could conceal different pixels being misclassified; a float32/float64 difference would be evidence of sensitivity, not proof that the named singularity is the complete rendering cause. The later printed radius-squared trace is computed in ordinary JavaScript arithmetic rather than the same explicitly rounded expression used by the orbit classifier.

For RFF, use targeted finite/singular-boundary fixtures, record per-point first divergence and compare against an appropriately precise independent reference. Preserve actual initialization and operation semantics. Do not repair a sensitive fractal formula by blindly adding an epsilon or replacing its derivative with an appearance approximation; any mathematically justified limit or alternative path needs validation. A 2D transfer can use these diagnostics for an added relief/normal field while keeping the existing high-precision Mandelbrot and MPA computation intact. None of these small probes establishes permission to trade precision for speed.

## Formula building blocks need contextual previews (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/probe-mb3d-bulb-sweep.mts`, `debug/probe-mb3d-difs-scan.mts`, `debug/probe-mb3d-fused-shot.mts`, `debug/probe-mb3d-scene-shot.mts`, and `debug/probe-mb3d-triage.mts`. These scripts were not executed. They provide examples of controlled exploration and catalog presentation, not verified shader-quality results.

The bulb sweep varies three estimators, three bailout values and two step multipliers, yielding eighteen cases for one selected scene. Its `qualityOverride` uses the compile-time merge already verified in the current harness. The resulting labels come from non-black coverage and summed RGB standard deviation: structured, solid, sparse, empty or flat. They can prioritize images for inspection but do not identify the mathematically correct estimator. A large spread can be caused by noise or wrong geometry; bailout changes can alter the evaluated field itself. For RFF, use such a sweep as an explicit experiment with trusted numerical/visual references, never as an automatic quality optimizer that trades precision for a more contrasted picture.

The dIFS scan selects metadata option 20 only when defaults exist, then renders synthetic single-slot scenes. The general triage similarly constructs standalone scenes for every catalog entry, substituting empty options when defaults are absent. Both use fixed small square outputs and fixed iteration budgets, supply slot iteration count zero, and rely on downstream interpretation for the actual execution sequence. Neither asserts which estimator or sequence finally ran. Their GOOD category requires sufficient coverage and RGB spread, not coherent geometry, derivative correctness or source-image equivalence. Missing defaults, chosen framing and unsupported standalone context must remain distinguishable from a broken shader.

A useful RFF feature is a library that distinguishes complete appearances from component effects. A coordinate transform, mask generator or lighting modifier may produce no meaningful image on its own. Show it applied to a stable representative input and disclose its required fields. In 3D, preview a material or transform on suitable geometry; in 2D, show the same effect on a known precise fractal field or a diagnostic height/mask input. Do not hide a useful component merely because a standalone render looks empty. Numerical dIFS formulas themselves are not automatically interchangeable with RFF's Mandelbrot DE or MPA computation.

The fused-shot probe compares two standalone formulas with their alternating composition, using synthetic decoded scenes and an explicit shared orbit camera. This is useful for seeing that composition changes the result, but the mathematical sequence is nonlinear and a shared outer iteration budget does not imply equal component-evaluation work. It prints metrics and images without testing the intended order, derivative updates or equivalence to an independent implementation. RFF appearance chains should expose ordering and provide per-stage inspection; any actual formula-composition feature needs separate numerical validation and compatibility work.

The scene-shot probe does read three external binary scene files before rendering, unlike the synthetic probes, but it overrides their cameras with one orbit framing and forces a square output. It therefore exercises decoded formula integration without establishing faithful imported composition/framing. Render failures are logged and skipped. Source file hashes, resolved parameters and original reference images are not saved in the result. For RFF, preserve the distinction between an import smoke, a diagnostic reframing and a fidelity comparison, with fixtures chosen for the specific claim.

These probes share previously identified limitations: requested browser backend is not independently verified, errors or missing statistics can collapse into coarse classifications, visual failures do not necessarily fail the process, and fixed developer paths limit portability. The scans save numeric JSON but not their thumbnails or a full reproducibility manifest. Transfer the useful batch exploration and contextual-preview design, while grounding success in explicit positive evidence. No additional runtime pass or shader speedup is claimed by this review.

## Preserve saved appearance and editable intent during shader evolution (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/probe-legacy-migration.mts`, `debug/probe-live-single.mts`, and `debug/probe-q.mts`. These files were inspected, not executed. They add concrete compatibility requirements to the RFF adoption plan.

The legacy migration probe constructs seven old-shaped scenes: a plain baseline, generic interlacing with an off-default secondary value, two hosts requiring custom distance functions, disabled-but-configured interlacing, an interleaved hybrid and a pre-loop hybrid. These are useful fixture categories. Off-default values detect migrations that accidentally substitute defaults; disabled configurations distinguish stored intent from currently active behavior; custom distance functions expose dependencies that a generic estimator cannot replace.

For RFF, retain analogous fixtures when adding or reorganizing material, mask, palette and lighting settings. Preserve disabled effect settings for later re-enabling, keep default additions visually neutral where compatibility requires it, and verify complete saved values alongside representative images. Follow RFF's append-only ConfigIO rules and frozen palette recipe identities. A 2D relief/material preset should reopen with the same precise location and appearance; a future 3D scene needs its full camera, geometry and lighting state preserved as well.

The script's round-trip label overstates its actual path. It writes synthesized presets to disk but renders the in-memory objects, and the migrated phase calls a migration harness directly rather than opening those files through the application's full save/load flow. Both phases regenerate fixtures from the current registered defaults and overwrite their JSON files, so running them against different revisions can change the supposed reference input. The source comments correctly warn that a retired legacy rendering path cannot be recaptured later, but the script records no immutable source/settings manifest to enforce that boundary.

RFF should freeze fixture bytes, source revision and reference output before retiring a rendering path. Load the same fixture bytes through the actual loader when testing compatibility, and separately test migration idempotence, unknown fields and save/reload of the migrated result. Compare supported values exactly where appropriate and define an image tolerance only for changes intended to be approximate. This probe explicitly acknowledges a color/bailout change for the pre-loop hybrid migration; that case cannot serve as evidence of pixel-exact compatibility. Any intentional visual change needs its own documented policy rather than being hidden in a general round-trip success claim.

The migration script prints whether the harness reported a changed formula ID, which helps detect a no-op migration, but does not assert the expected result per fixture. A disabled/plain case may legitimately retain its formula, whereas an enabled legacy case requires stronger evidence. Render errors and metrics are printed without failing the run; image equivalence is left to human review. Complete camera overrides are supplied from the preset, an improvement over the partial-camera probes discussed earlier, but this alone does not prove whole-scene fidelity. An unmatched `--only` filter can run zero scenes without a coverage failure.

The Live single-formula probe is a stronger automated structural check: it accumulates failed assertions and exits unsuccessfully. It checks that a one-slot modulo schedule builds, is registered, retains modulo authoring metadata and omits the layer-dispatch marker, then checks that a two-slot case retains that marker and a truthy interval setting. The useful RFF pattern is to simplify execution for a one-effect stack while retaining the editable authoring model. The user should be able to add a second effect later without losing scheduling or saved intent merely because the first compiled variant was optimized.

Its limits remain specific: generated-source substring presence is not shader compilation or numerical equivalence, registration presence does not verify every stored definition field, and a truthy interval does not assert exact interval/start/beat values. It does not render, reopen a saved stack, test reordered layers or compare the one-slot result to the native formula. RFF should validate the particular semantic simplification, including cache invalidation when a second layer is added. This architectural transfer applies to both 3D appearance stacks and 2D palette/mask chains, without implying that arbitrary formula weaving is compatible with Mandelbrot MPA.

Finally, `probe-q` prints four default quality fields for the first matching sample names and silently skips missing samples. It is a compact diagnostic, not coverage of effective GPU settings or a fidelity test. Record resolved values and explicit missing/unsupported cases when using such reports to support an RFF improvement claim.

## Cache diagnostics and parity between shader output paths (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/diag-polyline-cache.mts`, `debug/dump-gsd-linear.mts`, `debug/dump-mesh-cp.mts`, `debug/dump-cp-interlace.mts`, and `debug/dump-interlace-c.mts`. These tools were read without execution. The previous goal turn made persisted progress; this section continues the uncovered diagnostic-code inventory.

The polyline diagnostic loads a timeline seed, opens Graph mode, attempts to reset cache/draw counters, plays for two seconds and prints hit/miss reasons, background/overlay draw counts and environment details. This is a useful instrumenting pattern: distinguish a missing cache entry from a changed view key or changed keyframe-array identity, and distinguish expensive static drawing from a moving overlay. It does not measure shader execution, GPU time or a before/after speedup. Optional hooks and seed loading can silently do nothing; counter reset assumes the returned statistics object is mutable live state; neither seed contents nor playback advancement is asserted. A fixed delay is not proof of successful mounting or completed playback.

For RFF, use explicit revision-based reuse for numerical fractal fields, palette/material results and display-only overlays. Measure why a resource was regenerated and whether edits invalidate only dependent stages. A moving cursor or timeline marker should not require recomputing an unchanged fractal field. Conversely, an unchanged object identity must not allow stale results after an in-place mutation. In 3D this supports material/lighting edits over stable geometry data where the renderer permits reuse; in 2D it supports recoloring or mask edits over existing numerical maps. This diagnostic only motivates instrumentation: the actual valid cache boundaries must follow RFF's producers and consumers, preserving precision.

The mesh cutting-plane dump invokes five source builders: SDF, Newton, Preview, Escape and Color. It checks for the `cp_dmin` declaration according to formula capability, and for `abs(cp_dmin)` on distance-producing paths when estimator 5 is selected. Excluding Color and Escape from that distance-expression check is a useful semantic distinction: output paths consume different fields. However, no shader compiler is called, despite the header's compilation claim. Text presence does not prove that an expression occurs in the intended function, executes, or produces a valid result. Missing registry entries are skipped, failures are printed without a failing exit and only the last stored error survives within a case. The non-capable fallback cases do not assert the actual fallback estimator semantics.

RFF should share field/estimator capability resolution across preview, high-resolution export and any future geometry export while allowing each output to request its proper subset. Validate generated bindings and actual compilation, then test representative numerical/output parity. A generic distance fallback is not automatically mathematically valid for every formula. Mesh/3D cutting-plane geometry does not directly transfer to flat Mandelbrot coloring; the transferable part is consistent field contracts across output modes and capability-aware shader selection.

The linear GSD dump prints `getDist` plus cutting-plane declarations after selecting estimator 1. Its comment says cutting-plane writes remain unused, but declaration presence alone does not establish read/write liveness or compiler dead-store elimination. The interlace cutting-plane dump similarly prints a declaration count with an expected total, selected function excerpts and all matching references, without asserting uniqueness, initialization or execution order. Its `gsdWrites` expression tests the formula regex against an empty string, so that unused count cannot verify the advertised writes. The function extraction is brace/text based rather than a GLSL parser, and one excerpt is capped at sixty lines.

Finally, the interlace-C dump prints construction and call sites for the secondary constant vector. This is explicitly inspection-only and useful for locating fourth-component plumbing, but it neither asserts the argument passed nor tests a nonzero fourth component. The legacy interlace fields used by these scripts must still be checked against current capability handling before treating a generated dump as the requested composition. No dumps were generated in this review.

For RFF's proposed composable appearance effects, carry explicit channel meaning and initialization through each stage, inspect the resolved source when debugging, and add focused behavior checks for nondefault inputs. Avoid interpreting a found identifier, a declaration count or an empty diagnostic report as proof that a shader feature is enabled and correct. This applies to 3D normal/material channels and 2D relief/mask/color channels alike.

## Separate 2D opportunities from 3D importer exclusions (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/find-recoverable-frags.mts`, `debug/dec-probe.mts`, `debug/helpers/canvas-signature.mts`, and `debug/helpers/webglHarness.ts`. None was executed. This section also resolves the previously deferred question of which errors the shared WebGL smoke helper treats as fatal.

The recovery script compares reference and public `.frag` paths, then joins excluded files to historical V3/V4 results using only the filename stem. It classifies entries as restoration candidates, architectural skips, broken or lacking data. A 3D DE importer may deliberately reject 2D programs or direct-color outputs; those exclusions should not be interpreted as lack of value to RFF. They can identify candidates for a separately designed 2D appearance stage, provided their coordinate inputs, output domain, dependencies, precision requirements and licenses are individually established. A full multipass or stateful program is not automatically a single post-process shader.

The script itself cannot certify those opportunities. Basename-only joins can conflate different source files; duplicate JSONL names overwrite earlier rows; malformed rows are silently ignored; source/compiler versions and hashes are not checked. One-sided absent/incomplete evidence can become the broken category rather than untested. Both-skip classification precedes the compilation check, despite a comment saying nothing compiled must also hold. Its reference root is a relative `features/...` path, unlike the `engine-gmt/features/...` paths used by other reviewed tools, and missing directories quietly produce empty inventories. The optional output branch requires a literal `--out` flag, so `--out=path` alone does not activate it.

For RFF, preserve separate states for unsupported architecture, untested source, parse/compile failure and validated appearance behavior. Join by canonical path plus source hash, retain explicit missing evidence and confirm inventory coverage. Compilation in one historical pipeline is a useful lead, not proof of correctness or present support. The single DEC probe tries one source at four orbit distances through V3, saves successful thumbnails and prints visibility metrics; it provides no broader fidelity assertion or current support catalog.

The canvas-signature helper standardizes a specific overlay selector and samples RGB at 144 grid centers. Its mean absolute difference is useful as a coarse indication that an interaction changed output, while a count of 4-bit RGB bins estimates coarse variety. It reads back the entire canvas before selecting samples, so the small signature does not imply a small readback cost. Narrow features between sample centers, alpha-only changes and resize semantics are not reliably detected; dimensions are not included in the signature. A missing canvas returns an empty array and shape mismatch returns -1, requiring explicit caller handling. Nonfinite values are not rejected. For RFF, use a completed render revision and full or targeted regions when validating fine shader detail; keep sampled signatures for suitably coarse smoke checks rather than precision claims.

The shared WebGL helper collects page and console errors but only fails on a regex matching TypeError, ReferenceError, 'is not a function', FeatureRegistryFrozenError or Uncaught. Shader compilation errors, context loss or other console errors are not necessarily fatal under that gate. This narrows the interpretation of earlier fluid smoke scripts using it. The documented fallback printing when no error sink is provided is not implemented: errors are collected into a local array. Browser launch arguments request particular automation/process behavior but the helper does not verify hardware rendering, and the stated causes of watchdog/autowait problems are historical explanations rather than demonstrated measurements here.

Several comments differ from implementation: drag down/up calls do not pass the advertised `noWaitAfter` option; the oscillation uses `sin(i*0.3)` rather than the documented `sin(step)`; fixed 20/50 ms delays do not establish frame completion. Force-click explicitly bypasses actionability, and shortcut dispatch explicitly blurs focus, so these helpers cannot prove ordinary focused/obstructed user interaction works. Drag failure has no finally release for held buttons/keys, and launch/navigation failure lacks comprehensive browser cleanup within this helper.

For RFF effect validation, require the actual conditions at risk: correct target and dimensions, finite output, shader/pipeline success, expected input handling, and completion of the tested render revision. Use deterministic gestures and explicit synchronization where needed. Retain separate coarse UI smokes and detailed 2D/3D appearance comparisons; neither a changed 144-point signature nor absence of selected JavaScript error strings establishes shader correctness.

## Reduce shader-edit latency without confusing it with render throughput (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/measure-direct-costmap.mts` (223 lines) and `debug/measure-pt-costmap.mts` (192 lines). These measure compilation-related latency, not per-frame shader execution. Neither was run, and their historical estimates/noise-floor comments are not newly measured results.

The Direct script starts from a defined subset of minimal lighting, reflection, AO and glow settings, then requests shadow variants, environment/raymarched reflection, specular models, AO and glow individually, followed by a maximal combination. The PT script similarly compares reflection sampling, light sampling and shadow variants against a minimal PT setup, plus Direct/PT and maximal cases. The useful RFF technique is measuring interactive pipeline creation separately from steady-state rendering. Frequently adjusted artistic controls may benefit from uniforms or push constants within a compatible prebuilt pipeline; genuinely structural choices may still need distinct pipelines. Measure the runtime/compile tradeoff before retaining every possible branch in one shader, and never change fractal precision to reduce waiting.

For both 3D material editing and 2D palette/mask/relief controls, first identify which setting changes numerical data, which changes a shader variant, and which can update an existing binding. Preserve exact Vulkan descriptor/push-constant layouts. Cache pipeline variants by complete relevant state and consider preparing likely variants only when device memory and measured behavior justify it. These are adoption candidates, not evidence that RFF currently recompiles unnecessarily.

The cost-map implementations request headed Chrome with the shader disk cache disabled, but that does not establish a truly cold compiler across in-memory driver/application caches. They compile variants once in fixed order, do not verify device identity or emitted shader hashes, and do not repeat measurements to estimate variance. Patches reset listed fields rather than every resolved feature; PT's Direct baseline initially supplies `ptEnabled:true` before requesting Direct mode, so the final effective configuration must be inspected before interpreting that delta. Optional Direct setters can silently be absent, and missing formula matches are skipped.

Timing watches a shared compiling flag and parses the last newly collected compile log. If parsing fails, it labels a wall-clock polling duration as GPU milliseconds. No observed recompile can become a near-zero value; a timeout can return a still-compiling interval without an explicit failed measurement. Settle returns false on timeout but callers ignore that value. Several sequential setters can create multiple transitions, while the chosen log has no per-request identity. Require matched request/pipeline revisions, successful completion and a declared metric; do not combine fallback wall time and compiler-reported GPU time into one unlabeled number. Port readiness also checks localhost even when the configured URL names another host.

The claimed additive marginals need care. Some rows contain nested combinations: robust shadows plus jitter includes the robust-shadow change, and environment MIS plus importance sampling includes the lower reflection tier. Alternative shadow tiers cannot all coexist. The PT sum nevertheless adds positive deltas for these rows, double-counting mutually exclusive/nested choices and discarding negative deltas. Its difference from the maximal case is therefore not purely interaction/noise. Use sequential contrasts within a quality ladder, and independent factors or explicitly selected combinations when assessing joint cost. Neither script enforces its stated control-based contamination threshold.

The Direct script also flips `areaLights` after preparing jitter capability and reports whether the compiling flag or log count changes within three seconds. This is a useful regression question for a runtime-only control, but FAIL is only printed, the uniform/output change is not checked, and unrelated/asynchronously delayed compile events are not identified. The PT comments promise a corresponding runtime-toggle probe, but that file ends after its tables and contains no such check. RFF should verify both parts of a runtime-control contract: the intended visual parameter changes and no unnecessary pipeline creation occurs. Keep this edit-latency evidence separate from claims about visual improvement or frame-rate gains.

## Isolate measurements and preserve uncertainty in scene diagnostics (2026-10-08)

Full source review: `debug/helpers/bench-lock.mts`, `debug/mb3d-dr-audit.mts`, `debug/mb3d-fudge-audit.mts`, and `debug/mb3d-scene-thumbs.mts`. No lock was acquired, no benchmark was started and no thumbnails were regenerated.

The benchmark helper uses exclusive file creation to serialize cooperating scripts, stores PID/host/start metadata, checks same-host process existence and returns a release callback with exit/signal handlers. This is useful for reducing concurrent benchmark interference, but it is a repository-working-directory lock, not a GPU-wide reservation. Other checkouts, tools and ordinary applications remain outside it. Disabling interference needs measured conditions and device identity, not merely a lockfile.

The stale-recovery path reads ownership, then unlinks without an atomic ownership recheck; two contenders recovering the same old lock can race with a newly acquired owner. Release compares PID only, not host plus a unique acquisition token. A malformed/partially written lock reads as null but still blocks exclusive creation, potentially leaving indefinite waiting; PID reuse can also make an old lock appear live. Force mode explicitly steals a live or cross-host lock, contrary to the unconditional cross-host guarantee in the header. Cleanup listeners accumulate on repeated acquisitions and are not removed by release. For RFF benchmark orchestration, use a well-defined ownership primitive and bounded recovery policy, retain run identity and verify a process/measurement handle before treating work as ongoing. These are measurement-infrastructure lessons, not rendering-speed improvements.

The derivative audit compares an old any-slot-derivative rule with a proposed DE-owning-slot rule. The actual proposed decision uses numeric metadata and excludes option 20; the underscore transform-name heuristic is printed but does not decide the refinement, unlike the header's description. It filters slots by nonzero iteration count rather than using the complete sequence planner, and catches transpilation failures as no derivative. This can mix unknown/failed analysis with a genuine mathematical capability absence. It reports a hypothetical route without comparing the final emitter decision or rendered output. RFF should preserve unknown/error states and derive required fields from the actual active sequence, validating derivative propagation rather than selecting a path from names alone.

The step-multiplier audit duplicates a header conversion and clamp, sorts the resulting values and prints them. It does not render or demonstrate that raising a lower bound preserves detail in previously valid scenes. The constants and interpretation require their original provenance before adaptation. For RFF, keep authored parameters separate from any proposed derived rendering policy, and test that policy on known precise references. A brighter image or fewer exhausted ray steps cannot establish that a larger step multiplier is geometrically safe. This 3D traversal policy has no direct replacement role in the 2D perturbation/MPA engine.

The scene-thumbnail script renders at native aspect before center-cropping to a 176-pixel square JPEG, and leaves scenes selectable through an icon fallback when no thumbnail exists. That separation of availability from preview quality is useful for RFF's 3D material or 2D effect catalog. However, it classifies output using error presence and a 2% non-black threshold rather than an explicit successful result plus validated image; a rendered label can be counted without a URL being written. It does not remove an existing thumbnail when a later render is empty/failed, so old images can persist instead of the promised icon fallback. The image-decode promise handles load only, not failure, and no immutable source/settings manifest accompanies the image.

For RFF, treat thumbnails as versioned derived artifacts, preserve full-aspect output for inspection, document any crop and report written, skipped and failed states separately. Keep a last-known-good preview only when identified as such. Thresholds intended to omit blank previews should not become claims that a shader or numerical formula is valid. These recommendations transfer to both 3D and 2D without changing saved artistic state or computation precision.

Full source review: `debug/make-fbx-test-scene.mts` and `debug/make-fbx-anim-scene.mts`. These scripts construct binary-export fixtures through GMT's FBX writer. They were not run or imported into a DCC. They contain mesh/camera data, not a material or lighting interchange test, and their comments about target applications are not newly verified compatibility results.

The static fixture explicitly constructs header/global settings, document, object definitions, cube geometry, per-polygon-vertex normals, camera model/attribute and object connections. Its cube spans -100 to +100 in the chosen coordinate units; its later comment/output describe two meters, whereas the initial geometry heading says one meter. Camera placement is stored in the model transform, while the camera attribute also contains a different Position vector. Without target import evidence, do not assume every consumer resolves redundant fields identically. A symmetric cube and one-axis camera pose are a limited handedness fixture; asymmetric labeled landmarks would reveal mirrors and axis swaps more clearly.

The animated fixture bakes 121 samples at 30 frames per second, including both endpoints from time zero to four seconds. Translation follows a circular X/Z path and rotation uses an unwrapped yaw from 90 to 450 degrees. Separate scalar curves are connected through translation/rotation curve nodes, an animation layer and an animation stack. This explicit connection graph and integer time-key construction are useful patterns for validating camera/timeline interchange. The authored values are float arrays for animation and double arrays for static geometry; precision requirements must be evaluated for their actual coordinate scale.

RFF's direct 2D opportunity is deterministic export of view/appearance animation: precise center and zoom, palette phase, light direction, roughness or mask parameters evaluated at defined frame times. Preserve the native high-precision location in its own supported representation rather than flattening a deep view into ordinary float translation keys. Define whether an endpoint sample is included, how looping handles a duplicate endpoint and which interpolation reproduces the intended path. For 3D camera motion, retaining unwrapped rotation can avoid an artificial wrap in this simple yaw-only orbit. It does not establish a general quaternion-to-Euler conversion or correct compound rotation near singular orientations. Linearly interpolated baked position keys follow chords between samples; a circular path at key times is not an exact circle at arbitrary subframes. Test intermediate times, changing lens/aspect, compound rotations, nonuniform scale and long durations if those are supported. For 2D animation, the analogous requirement is preserving log-zoom and precise-center interpolation, not merely matching the start and end screenshots.

These builders demonstrate serialization input construction, not round-trip correctness. They perform no independent parse, import, projected-landmark comparison or curve evaluation. The animation Definitions Count literal is 13 while its listed per-type counts sum to 15; that arithmetic mismatch merits an independent structural check, without claiming that a particular importer will reject it. Fixed IDs work for these standalone fixtures but do not test scene merging, collisions or large files. The static fixture also cannot validate every production camera field simply because an application opens it.

For RFF, validate graph references and counts mechanically, then inspect the imported camera and sampled motion in each intended target. Retain the original saved scene as authoritative and document what the interchange format omits. Implement compatibility independently and trace any distinctive conversion constants/formulas before adapting them. A successful small-file import would be useful evidence for that fixture, not proof of complete format support or shader appearance parity.

Full source review: `debug/opus-candidate-template.mts` and `debug/opus-shot-gpu.mts`. The generator was not run: it writes formula source and registration files. The screenshot script was also not executed.
