## Camera actions and modeless panel ordering (2026-10-08)

Full document review of ADR-0057 (67 lines) and ADR-0081 (40), without a live interface audit. ADR-0057 disables an automatically generated library menu in favor of a custom camera menu while retaining shared save/select actions. This separates presentation from state operations and avoids duplicate entries. For RFF, menus, shortcuts and view-manager controls should call the same validated action for camera/palette/material selection, with deliberate separation of camera history from parameter history. Shared action functions reduce divergence but do not alone guarantee equal arguments, slot indexing, enabled state or shortcut ownership. Verify the affected snapshot ID and resulting render revision through each entry point. Legacy event rebroadcast should not duplicate the underlying save or undo transaction.

ADR-0081 introduces session-local click-to-front order for participating floating panels and a lower browse-overlay tier that leaves panels usable. Its amendment generalizes the original panel stack to per-tier layer stacks; the older helper name is not a separate competing mechanism. Participation is conditional on coordinate positioning and the default panel tier, so the record does not mean that all windows participate. Raising in pointer-capture phase also catches presses inside children that stop bubbling, but visible stacking does not automatically establish keyboard focus, Escape ownership or accessibility semantics.

The arithmetic Z.panel + rank stays in a reserved band only while the participating count fits its capacity; the record's 'handful' is an assumption, not an unbounded guarantee. It also identifies nested browser stacking contexts as a reason a menu cannot escape merely by increasing its own z value. A browse surface built from a modal component but intended to leave panels interactive needs corresponding focus/input behavior, not just a different visual tier. The historical topbar limitation requires current implementation or runtime evidence before being presented as unresolved.

For RFF, preserve a clear distinction between blocking dialogs and modeless palette/material browsers, coordinate visual and keyboard ownership, and ensure opening a new floating editor cannot hide essential recovery or commit controls. Temporary focus order need not be serialized with fractal artwork. In 2D, this supports comparing palette/pattern candidates while keeping the canvas visible; in 3D, it supports several light/material panels without redirecting edits to the wrong target. Native window ownership and focus rules should implement these requirements rather than copying CSS z-index numbers. This is workflow guidance around shader experimentation, with no shader-speed or image-quality claim.

## Save feedback must identify the actual committed destination (2026-10-08)

Full review of ADR-0119 (105 lines), without an interface run. The September 16 amendment supersedes the original assertion that the heart action saves to Recent: it files into the last-used group or Kept, while a separate pending Recent update can also occur. The September 24 amendment moves shared-set feedback to server acceptance and changes the contribution label. These corrections are essential when interpreting the original mechanism.

The record places visual confirmation at the destination that receives the gradient, using the in-flight preview only for valid targets and treating completed-save feedback separately. That distinction is useful for RFF palette/material libraries: hovering a target is an intention, while an accepted save is a result. The described local mechanism infers the destination from set-count growth. Excluding day bins addresses one known competing write, but count deltas alone cannot identify a particular operation under concurrent updates, deduplication, replacement or same-count changes. A RFF save action can return a destination/item ID and completion result directly, so feedback follows the committed operation rather than reconstructing it from aggregate counts.

The shared-contribution flow centralizes confirmation and feedback around one transport operation; reading this document does not authorize any contribution or external write, and none was performed. For a possible RFF shared library, success feedback must wait for actual acceptance, and failures/cancellation must leave local work intact. A local library and a remote publication should not be visually indistinguishable operations.

The CSS preview helpers are explicitly approximate and not byte-equivalent to the texture renderer. They can communicate which gradient is being saved but must not supply sampled color values or serve as the image-fidelity oracle. Apply the same separation to native RFF swatches versus the full 2D palette or 3D material rendering pipeline. Preview the actual export subject: a continuous ramp and discrete swatches differ, while a multi-palette set cannot be faithfully represented by one member alone.

The animation test described here checks a transform changing over time, which is stronger than checking a declared animation name. It still does not prove that the intended data was saved, and the record explicitly leaves the drop-specific feedback call untested. Shared animation code does not establish that every caller invokes it. In RFF, verify committed payload/destination and visible feedback separately, including no-op saves, rapid repeated operations and cancellation. A shared duration parameter can keep effect lifetime and cleanup aligned, but rendering feedback is supporting workflow polish, not a fractal shader or a measured rendering improvement. The principle applies equally to 2D palette presets and 3D material/view libraries.

## Editing handles must refer to the displayed field (2026-10-08)

Full review of ADR-0118 (147 lines), including its later amendments, without a visual audit or runtime reproduction. The central transferable mechanism is distinguishing editable base stops from a transformed preview. When the displayed gradient represents a different configuration, showing the underlying stops as if they directly describe that picture is misleading. The record hides stale markers and their gestures while retaining layout space; baking restores handles for the newly committed representation.

The distinction is semantic, not simply 'a drag is active' or 'a preview exists'. The document separates previewConfig from previewRamp and permits handles to reappear when a transformation crosses through identity. For RFF, track which representation and revision each handle edits, and disable or relabel it when the displayed result is not directly editable in that representation. An approximation fitted to a ramp may be useful, but should not be described as exact merely because it derives from that ramp. Preserve the original source until an explicit bake/conversion and keep that action undoable. This applies to 2D palette stops and 3D material ramps; geometric handles additionally need to match the current coordinate space and camera revision.

Cursor selection in the record shares hit testing with the action and stays owned by the active gesture until it ends. This avoids advertising a new action merely because a captured pointer crosses another control. It also separates a zoom-tool tap from a middle-button reset even though their drag implementation is shared. For native RFF, retain gesture origin/type and release ownership on cancellation as well as completion. A common drag routine does not imply identical click semantics. Verify action state and results, not just cursor appearance.

The toolbar-gutter amendment distinguishes physical clearance from the width that authorizes row labels. This avoids accidentally exposing labels/counts when a host requests extra space. A RFF panel should likewise pass explicit layout constraints rather than relying on unrelated label widths, and hit tests should use the same final geometry. These browser layout details do not transfer as literal pixel constants to native DPI-aware controls.

The final section records an event/state boundary issue: a changed callback identity retriggered an effect and manufactured a selection notification, undoing a user's panel switch. Storing the current callback separately avoids treating handler replacement as a new selection. For RFF, emit semantic selection/edit events only when the relevant state changes, with clearly defined initial-notification behavior; refreshing subscriptions must not reapply an old command. The record's tests and historical failures are not newly verified here. This is supporting editor consistency for shader experimentation, not a measured rendering improvement or a claim of an existing RFF defect.

## Constrained editing layouts and state ownership (2026-10-08)

Full review of ADR-0115 (123 lines), including its September 24 update; no screenshots or live layout were inspected in this batch. The record describes moving controls and preview content rather than uniformly shrinking them, scrolling bounded sections while retaining useful image space, and retaining model state outside components that change location or unmount. These principles can support RFF in narrow windows or high-DPI configurations without implying a mobile port is required.

Its phone flag combines width and coarse-pointer detection, while CSS breakpoint variants depend on width. Equal numeric breakpoints do not make those predicates identical on a wide touch device. The document deliberately assigns structural decisions to one and styling to the other; combinations still need testing. The assertion that desktop remained pixel-identical is a historical seven-screenshot result, not a universal guarantee, and the later amendment explicitly extends filter-space behavior to short desktop windows. Read the amendment before treating that older consequence as current behavior.

The host requests zoom through a factor plus rising serial while the wall owns its transform. For RFF, a command identity can distinguish repeated equal zoom requests, but specify whether rapid requests compose or coalesce and which coordinate/pointer anchor they use. Moving an image preview between containers is safe only if the persistent model and required resources survive independently; editor focus, scroll and in-progress gestures may still need explicit handling. Automatic folding to make room should restore only the fold it caused, as the amendment describes, rather than undoing a later user choice.

Measuring available space from an element's actual top addresses the failure of a fixed viewport-height fraction when headers consume space. Clamp the available extent and account for native work areas/DPI in RFF; a sizing formula alone does not guarantee that required controls or the render canvas remain usable. A title attribute is not sufficient evidence that an omitted action explanation remains discoverable for touch/keyboard users. The record also explicitly excludes internal editor gestures, so layout assertions cannot be used as gesture correctness evidence.

For 2D palette/pattern editing and 3D material/light editing, preserve the document state while adapting panel placement, keep the main preview large enough to judge changes, and verify the renderer's actual dimensions/aspect after layout changes. Browser CSS units and safe-area rules are implementation-specific; the transferable benefit is clear ownership of persistent editing data and explicit available-space constraints. This is a workflow improvement candidate, not a shader-quality or performance result, and no current RFF layout defect is asserted.

## MB3D parser fixtures: unique coverage and codec independence (2026-10-08)

Full source review of `debug/test-mb3d-parse.mts` (116 lines), without execution or independent verification of the external posts cited in comments. The harness combines synthetic codec roundtrips, selected known-value header/addon assertions and five real-fixture sanity checks. Its asymmetric 1400-by-840 dimension assertion is useful: square fixtures alone cannot distinguish swapped width/height offsets. The parser and fixture inventory were reviewed separately; reading this harness is not new proof that imported scenes render faithfully.

The headline 100,000 synthetic cases contain only 256 distinct three-byte inputs: each component is a multiple of t masked to eight bits, so the entire tuple repeats every 256 iterations. This exercises every value in each byte position, but not arbitrary combinations, short/partial groups or varied lengths. Checking three returned bytes does not enforce exact decoded length. The alphabet assertion requires 64 unique characters but does not require total length exactly 64. A codec encode/decode roundtrip can preserve paired mistakes in both directions; independently known encoded vectors are a distinct requirement.

The real-fixture re-encoding covers only the first 840 raw bytes, not the addon or complete stream, and re-encodes original bytes rather than reconstructing bytes from parsed fields. It therefore does not prove correct field offsets beyond explicit field assertions. Hardcoding 840 here while another check uses MB3D_HEADER_BYTES also gives two sources of the header-size assumption. The selected golden fields constrain specific interpretation, but remaining camera, constants, matrices and hybrid data need their own evidence. The harness lacks malformed/truncated/invalid-character cases and resource-limit checks. Missing fixture reads or thrown parser errors fail execution, and recorded assertion failures produce a nonzero exit status; those are useful fail-closed properties of this test's actual scope.

For RFF file compatibility, distinguish raw codec equivalence, field interpretation, scene application and rendered fidelity. Use independent encoded/decoded examples, asymmetric vectors/matrices, full payload checks and explicit unsupported-version behavior. Preserve high-precision coordinates without a display-number roundtrip. New 3D formula imports require validated seed/DE/hybrid semantics beyond a correct binary header; 2D palette or location imports require their own stable schema and precision checks. These lessons support independent format implementations and reproducible cross-tool comparisons, not permission to copy proprietary code or evidence of a current RFF parser defect.

## Mandalabeth matrix notes: orthogonality, orientation and a conflicting definition (2026-10-08)

Full review of `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/Kashaders/Fractals/Mandos/mandalabeth/C5n_6-matrices.txt` (53 lines). The note attributes its matrices to a Beth Chen paper but supplies no title, publication identifier or per-file license. This is a provenance lead, not enough to identify or verify the original derivation; no external paper was consulted in this batch.

The stated positive constants satisfy p squared plus q squared equals one. Accordingly the displayed gamma has orthonormal rows and preserves Euclidean length, but its determinant is minus one: expanding along the first row gives -(p squared + q squared). It is orientation-reversing, not a proper 3D rotation as the closing note says. The cyclic permutation g has determinant plus one and g cubed is identity. Multiplication by its powers gives the displayed gamma1 and gamma2, and the later gamma4/gamma5 products are likewise consistent with the displayed preceding matrices. Norm preservation and proper orientation are distinct properties.

There is a separate inconsistency in h: its initial definition has a q in row two, column one, while the multiplication used to derive gamma3 uses diag(1,-1,-1). With the initial h, gamma times h would instead have second-row first entry q-p*q and third-row first entry p+q*q, rather than q and p. The listed gamma3 through gamma5 therefore follow the diagonal version, not the first definition. Do not silently select one as the intended original mathematics from this note alone. The diagonal version is orthogonal; the initial sheared definition is not generally length-preserving.

For RFF's optional 3D fold/symmetry formulas, represent each transform's actual contract: orthogonal versus general linear, determinant sign, composition order and coordinate convention. An orientation-reversing orthogonal transform preserves distance but affects handedness; a shear cannot inherit the same unit-scale distance-estimator reasoning. GLSL column-major constructors must be matched explicitly to the row-written matrices, and transformed normal/tangent conventions must follow the chosen mapping. Validate the actual consumer before deriving any ray-step or normal claim from this reference note.

For 2D pattern or material-coordinate generation, plane rotations/reflections and cyclic transform families can provide useful symmetry variants, but taking a 2-by-2 corner of a 3D orthogonal matrix does not guarantee a 2D isometry. Define an invariant plane or an explicit projection with its own scale/metric behavior, then apply footprint-aware filtering at fold boundaries. These are candidate mechanisms for masks/textures or distinct fractal formulas, not changes to RFF's existing Mandelbrot/MPA equations. This review identifies mathematical consistency and provenance requirements; it does not establish a current production shader bug or a verified new formula.

## Path-tracing research memo: useful mechanisms versus unverified shortcuts (2026-10-08)

Full review of `docs/specs/fractal_pathtracing_research_2024_2026.md` (385 lines). This is a research proposal, not evidence that its techniques exist in GMT or that its quoted speedups transfer to RFF. Its broad source list does not map individual numerical claims to experiments. The 30-70% step reduction, 5x formula speedup, 2-4x distant-geometry speedup and universal ranking of analytical normals remain unverified for these applications. Browser support/version and vendor performance claims were not adopted as current facts. Selected primary research was checked below; other proposals retain explicit validation requirements.

### Safe stepping and screen footprint

The memo's prose reverses the overlap interpretation: overlapping empty bounding spheres justify the speculative segment; disjoint spheres trigger fallback. Its displayed less-than test is consistent with detecting disjointness, not with the prose saying overlap means overshoot. The original work proposes a guarded algorithm, not simply multiplying every march step. RFF would need to retain the prior safe state, validate the speculative step and recover correctly, including inside/outside handling and finite-value checks. This also requires a valid distance-bound contract for the actual formula and transforms. [Keinert et al., Enhanced Sphere Tracing (2014)](https://diglib.eg.org/items/8ea5fa60-fe2f-4fef-8fd0-3783cb3200f0).

The Lipschitz section contradicts itself by asserting L greater than one and then recommending L between 0.5 and 0.8. Underestimation alone supplies no such constant. As a mathematical check, an L-Lipschitz scalar field f with zero surface satisfies abs(f(x)) <= L*distance(x,surface); dividing by a proven positive bound L yields a conservative distance bound. An empirical factor is not that proof. A true distance function is 1-Lipschitz, but its gradient need not exist everywhere. Do not import a formula-wide assumption that every Mandelbulb/Mandelbox variation remains conservative under arbitrary folds, hybrids and parameters.

A pixel footprint can guide termination and filtering, but testing footprint greater than a distance value is not itself integration over the pixel. It can leave missed thin geometry or unstable silhouettes. The memo's distance-only iteration reduction changes the evaluated shape and can change its distance bound. Derive a bounded approximation error and a transition policy before using it; camera distance alone does not encode projection, resolution, zoom or deformation. A perspective cone model also needs a separate orthographic treatment. For RFF's existing 2D Mandelbrot computation, these are not permission to shorten escape iterations, lower precision or alter MPA. Transfer footprint-aware filtering to palette/pattern detail, and use actual subpixel sampling where needed.

### Derivatives, specialized formulas and caches

A scalar running derivative `dr` does not contain a full spatial gradient. For the displayed DE `D = 0.5*r*log(r)/dr`, differentiating a smooth branch requires both grad(r) and grad(dr): `grad(D) = 0.5*((log(r)+1)*grad(r)/dr - r*log(r)*grad(dr)/(dr*dr))`. Iteration/bailout changes and folds introduce additional branch issues. Computing the orbit Jacobian alone is therefore not automatically the gradient of this DE, and differentiating a useful potential is a different normal construction. Count the derivative state, register pressure, branch behavior and occupancy before ranking the optimization. A practical RFF experiment would compare candidate normals against a converged finite-difference reference at singularities, folds and silhouettes, then measure complete frame time. The memo's operation counts do not establish savings.

Double-angle identities can specialize fixed integer powers, but eliminating explicit trig calls still requires obtaining the initial angular components, preserving the formula's axis convention and handling poles, square roots and divisions. Verify equivalence against the intended formula across axes, signs and parameter ranges. A power-eight specialization is not a replacement for arbitrary-power behavior. This targets a prospective 3D formula evaluator; RFF's 2D quadratic recurrence has no corresponding trigonometric loop to eliminate.

Sparse SDF bricks/octrees could reduce repeated evaluation for static 3D scenes. Interpolation must carry an error allowance or conservative bound before controlling ray steps; exact evaluation near the surface does not recover geometry already skipped by an unsafe cached value. Cache identity must include formula, parameters, transforms and relevant iteration settings. Track bake time, memory and invalidation, not only lookup time. Similarly, reusing a nearby primary hit's orbit trap for another surface substitutes material data and can smear discontinuities; proximity alone is insufficient. For 2D, reuse exact per-pixel scalar fields across recoloring when their inputs are unchanged, rather than replacing high-precision orbits with spatially interpolated geometry.

### Sampling, reconstruction and temporal state

A fixed 128-by-128 blue-noise fetch provides spatial variation but no frame, bounce or sample-dimension progression. Repeating it can repeat the same paths; hashing it indiscriminately need not preserve its useful distribution. Define separate dimensions for pixel jitter, lens, light and scattering samples and deterministic indexing for reproducible exports. Research specifically distinguishes spatial blue noise from distributions designed for temporal reuse. Test sampling error and temporal stability, and verify the actual asset/code license before adaptation. [Wolfe et al., Spatiotemporal Blue Noise Masks (2022)](https://research.nvidia.com/publication/2022-07_spatiotemporal-blue-noise-masks).

SVGF combines temporal accumulation, luminance variance and a hierarchical spatial filter; adding an arbitrary blur is not equivalent. A limited RFF candidate is an optional guided reconstruction pass for genuinely noisy 3D lighting, with depth/normal/material guides, history confidence and a bypass/reference mode. Preserve fine fractal structures rather than treating all high-frequency content as noise. The original method explains why guide images matter at low sample counts. This does not justify filtering RFF's deterministic 2D escape field or promise improvement for already clean shading. [Schied et al., Spatiotemporal Variance-Guided Filtering (2017)](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/rtr/publication/schied2017spatiotemporal/).

Reprojection requires valid correspondence, not just a camera delta: formula edits, material/light changes, deformation, resolution changes and disocclusion can invalidate history even when a sampled point remains on a zero surface. A secondary hit position alone does not describe the changing reflection path through a moving curved surface. Likewise, primary surface replacement requires a coherent specular-path/guide convention; it is not simply storing another hit. Keep those advanced mechanisms conditional on an actual path-traced 3D renderer.

Variance-guided tile allocation can improve efficiency, but a tile with too few samples or no observed rare event can look falsely converged. Require minimum sampling, conservative stopping/revisit rules, and invalidation after edits. Treat estimator variance, changing content and reconstruction confidence separately. For 2D progressive supersampling, tile scheduling and document revision tracking are useful transfers, provided all requested samples/precision requirements remain satisfied. Projection/subpixel jitter is also distinct from physically moving the camera; it must preserve the intended view and high-precision pixel-coordinate construction. It is not automatically importance sampling of illumination.

### Architecture and prioritization for RFF

The WebGPU migration proposal is browser-specific: RFF already uses Vulkan, so the transferable questions are dispatch scheduling, storage layout, synchronization and bandwidth. In-place accumulation does not remove races or synchronization requirements merely because storage buffers exist. Tile compaction and indirect dispatch are candidates to benchmark, not guaranteed wins; convergence is scene-dependent, not necessarily fastest in the image center.

Hardware AABB traversal is a conditional 3D extension. A grid of boxes does not itself reduce expensive fractal evaluations. Empty-cell rejection is valid only with a trustworthy distance/Lipschitz bound covering the cell; an arbitrary DE at the center cannot certify it. Budget acceleration-structure construction, memory, duplicate traversal and parameter-change rebuilds. Preserve a supported fallback rather than making this a prerequisite for ordinary RFF rendering.

ReSTIR, neural radiance caches and neural denoisers are separate research projects, not ordinary spatial blurs or ready-made improvements justified by this memo. Reservoir reuse requires correct sample weights/visibility and validity handling; learned caches introduce training, bias, memory and changing-scene behavior. A small number of lights does not by itself settle the value of indirect-light reuse. No implementation or performance claim is accepted here from the memo alone.

For current prioritization, this review supports testing footprint-aware material filtering, deterministic multidimensional sampling where stochastic rendering exists, and explicit history/cache invalidation before adopting aggressive marching or approximate geometry caches. The smooth-iteration formula in the memo also assumes a particular escape-growth model and convention; it is not a universal 3D distance proxy or an adaptive-sampling error bound. These findings do not replace the earlier source-based shader ranking with the memo's unsupported speedup ranking. Both 3D and 2D candidates must preserve RFF's precision and be evaluated with fixed scenes, matched output quality, full GPU cost and image/temporal differences. No renderer code or shader was changed in this batch.

## Minimal 3D application survey: reusable contracts and historical evidence (2026-10-08)

Full review of `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/t02-fractal-toy.md` (132 lines) and `plans/overnight-audit/results/t02-fractal-toy.json` (35 lines). The current renderer and entry-point statements relevant below were selectively rechecked; their earlier full-review coverage was not counted again. The historical survey's hashes and line ranges are records of another audit, not coverage credit for the current tree. Its open-question list labels all fourteen source files orphan candidates despite describing their imports and entry points; the later result records no orphans. Neither list is a reason to remove application code without current reachability evidence.

The useful architecture is a formula contract separated from camera/ray construction, host lifecycle, parameter state and lighting. Formula metadata can expose controls and uniform setters while the renderer owns ray generation and resource lifetime. For a prospective RFF 3D extension, make escape radius, distance-estimator expression, iteration cap, coordinate space and supported transformations explicit contracts. Registering a shared feature is insufficient if its injection function expects configuration that a minimal host supplies only as an empty object. Validate actual host capabilities before presenting a feature as available. For 2D, the same separation can support independent coloring/material modules without rewriting Mandelbrot/MPA computation.

The survey describes setup as post-mount in two places but enumerates it before mounting. Current `fractal-toy/main.tsx` confirms `setupFractalToy()` at line 158 before `createRoot` at line 170. This is an example of why the executable sequence takes precedence over an architectural summary. In RFF, distinguish schema registration, default-state initialization, resource readiness and first successful frame; a registration hook must not silently depend on a view already existing. Per-view renderer ownership is preferable to importing this example's module singleton if multiple previews or export views are supported.

The current shader replacement code deletes the previous program before compiling the replacement. However, the survey's stronger claim that a compile exception necessarily leaves a null program and makes subsequent render calls no-ops is not supported: `this.program` is not cleared by `setShader`, and the render guard only tests its truthiness. A failed replacement can therefore leave a stale object reference; exact driver/API behavior was not tested here. The RFF improvement principle is transactional replacement: build and validate a candidate, verify its resource interface, then publish it and retire the old resources only when safe for in-flight work. Keep the user's shader draft and diagnostics separate from the last successfully active pipeline. This applies equally to 3D formula editing and 2D coloring shaders and is not a claim that RFF currently has the same failure.

Likewise, a compiling-false event means the attempt ended, not that the shader succeeded or an image is ready. Distinguish completion, success, installation and rendered-frame readiness when resetting history, exporting images or taking screenshots. An unknown formula silently resolving to the first registered formula can conceal a partially supported imported scene; preserve the requested identity and report unsupported selection explicitly. Normalize identities consistently before duplicate checks, rather than checking original-case formula IDs and later generating lower-case state keys that may collide.

The documented fixed hit epsilon, normal offset, march range and iteration ceiling describe a compact demonstration. They are not suitable universal quality settings across arbitrary scale and projection. Step-count darkening is a shading heuristic rather than a visibility integral for ambient occlusion. Gamma 2.2 is likewise an approximate output operation, not proof of a complete color-managed pipeline. A 2D transfer can use a deliberately labeled iteration/field-derived contrast mask, but should not present it as physical occlusion. RFF already has substantial shading functionality; these simple operations are not automatically new features or visual upgrades.

The historical result reports a mutation test that removed lighting registration and caused the smoke assertion 'lighting slice missing' to fail. That is evidence about one historical registration guard, not proof of correct light direction, color, rendered pixels, formula geometry, camera projection or compile-failure recovery. Typecheck and orphan checks cover different properties. No commands or mutations described by this audit artifact were executed in this review. For RFF, make validation match the promised behavior: registration checks for parameter availability, interface checks for shader bindings, image comparisons for visual behavior, and explicit failed-rebuild/state-retention checks for editing reliability. This keeps the adoption proposal focused on RFF's useful contracts rather than turning the historical GMT audit into a new defect-fixing project.

## Surface refinement guards: consistent fields before extra iterations (2026-10-08)

Full source review of `debug/test-trace-refine.mts` (238 lines), plus selective inspection of the already-reviewed trace and DE generators. No test or GPU workload was executed. This harness is valuable for emission and importer contracts, but its introductory claims exceed what its assertions establish. Its opening importer-mapping description is also superseded by block D: the current checks require refinement to remain absent from imported quality settings, even for nonzero source steps-after-stop values.

The refinement mechanism remembers the previous ray distance, takes the current accepted hit distance as the other endpoint, repeatedly evaluates their midpoint, and replaces the endpoint according to whether the distance estimate is below `finalEps`. After k genuine bisections a valid initial interval has width divided by 2^k in exact arithmetic. This refines a threshold crossing, not necessarily the exact geometric zero surface or the nearest visible surface. It needs endpoints classified with the same predicate, a valid bracket and appropriate continuity assumptions. Multiple crossings, initially-inside rays, discontinuities and skipped thin components require separate handling. The emitted loop uses arithmetic midpoints; its 'damped-bisection' label does not establish an additional damping mechanism in this block.

A particularly important adoption condition appears across blocks C and E. C checks that the analytic `map` and distance-only `mapDist` contain identical injected formula/init snippets and share a distance helper. E explicitly expects the numerical primary path to use `numericDistance(p, uNumDESmooth)` while the secondary path uses `numericDistance(p, 2.5)`. The current generator confirms both expressions, and refinement calls `mapDist`. When the primary smoothing parameter differs from 2.5, a bracket obtained from the primary field is not automatically a bracket of the midpoint field. Shared orbit source is not enough to establish equality of the resulting distance estimates. For an RFF implementation, use the primary estimator with exactly its settings during refinement, or revalidate endpoints under the chosen refinement field. This is a contract issue identified by source inspection, not a measured image defect.

The current refinement block retains trap/iteration/decomposition values from the original hit while changing the hit distance. Its comment assumes the displacement is subpixel and visually identical, but the harness does not measure displacement or color variation. A narrow geometric displacement can still cross a sharp material/orbit-trap boundary. Choose explicitly whether RFF recolors at the final point, preserves a cached approximation within a justified tolerance, or disables refinement for unsupported combinations. Test material alignment as well as silhouettes and normals. Refinement cannot repair an incorrect seed, formula, metric or estimator; the harness itself records a historical decision not to auto-enable it for an import-fidelity problem.

The OFF checks compare explicit false against the current default and check a few markers/adjacent strings. They do not compare the entire generated kernel against an independent historical baseline. Both outputs could change together. Identical kernel text under the same conditions is useful, but it does not establish identical complete shaders, pipeline inputs or pixels, and 'zero compile cost' should mean no additional refinement code rather than no shader compilation. ON assertions establish selected emitted strings, not successful GLSL compilation, bracket validity, finite arithmetic or convergence. The lean-path assertion checks the default invocation; it does not prove that every secondary/physics call configuration disables refinement.

Block D now proves a definition exists, the import ledger reports support and a populated quality object exists before checking that the refinement key is absent. That closes the obvious vacuous-success case where no scene was emitted. Counting at least four keys does not establish their names or values, and importer-reported support is not rendered fidelity. Historical mutation results in the header are not current test runs. Block E checks log-domain expressions and probe wiring but does not measure overflow, cancellation, normal direction or estimator error. In particular, a finite difference of logarithms is not exactly a finite difference of radii divided by the center radius; the equivalence used in the rationale is a local derivative approximation. Clamping can still make distinct inputs coincide, so emitting a log and overflow limit does not prove saturation is impossible.

For RFF, the reusable 3D feature is optional, bounded hit refinement with consistent estimator settings, explicit bracket checks, meaningful stopping criteria and a defined final material evaluation. Validate thin features, inside starts, nondefault numerical smoothing, fold boundaries and zero/nonfinite gradients against an independent reference. The 2D transfer is narrower: consistent scalar-field sampling between shading passes, optional refinement of deliberately defined continuous contours, and tests that prove their subject exists before asserting absent features. Do not bisect Mandelbrot membership or alter perturbation/MPA under an assumption that the escape field is a smooth signed distance. This batch adds adoption requirements rather than promoting extra refinement steps as a universal quality improvement.

## Shader importer analysis/generation matrices: acceptance must mean more than parsing (2026-10-08)

Full review of `debug/test-frag-v3-analysis.mts` (162 lines) and `debug/test-frag-v3-generation.mts` (164 lines). Each explicitly lists 64 reference examples, spanning IFS, bulbs, boxes, quaternion formulas, hybrids and dual-number material. Neither harness was executed. Their imports refer to the absent `features/fragmentarium_import/v3/...` paths; the corresponding implementation paths exist under `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/v3/...`. Both also hardcode `h:/GMT/gmt-0.8.5` for input files. They are therefore historical harness source, not current runnable proof of those 64 examples' support. This review does not grant new full-review credit to the referenced shader files.

The analysis harness preprocesses recognized DEC input when confidence exceeds 0.4, then counts a case as passed whenever `analyzeSource` returns success. It prints the inferred DE, loop counter, parameter ranges, global categories and once/per-pixel initialization counts but asserts no expected values for them. A successful result with no detected DE still increments passed. For an RFF shader importer, explicit analysis output is useful, but acceptance should check the intended entry point, parameter types/defaults/units, initialization dependencies and supported language constructs against fixture expectations. A confidence threshold is a format-routing heuristic, not semantic validation. Keep the original source and preprocessing diagnostics available for comparison.

Generation selects the auto-detected DE, otherwise a function literally named `de`, otherwise the first function. That last fallback can produce syntactically valid code for a helper with the wrong meaning. Loop mode is inferred from the selected function's loop metadata and parameters are assigned slots automatically. RFF would need an explicit semantic selection or an unambiguous validated contract, including return type, coordinate/seed convention, parameter bindings and whether extracted iteration logic preserves initialization and exit conditions. For stable saved scenes, persist parameter identity independently of incidental source declaration order; do not silently reinterpret a saved slot after an importer change.

The parser checks only the concatenation of emitted uniform declarations and `functionCode`, not a complete renderer shader. It does not validate the separate `getDist` result, full host declarations, stage interfaces or resource layout against RFF's Vulkan bindings. Parser success is not shader compiler/link success or mathematical equivalence. More seriously for interpreting this harness, a caught GLSL parse error increments `glslErrors` but execution then prints success and increments `passed`. A case can therefore appear in both the pass count and the parse-error count. Neither script explicitly sets a failing exit status for its accumulated failures. Unhandled exceptions or unresolved imports can still fail the process, so this is not a claim that every invocation exits successfully.

Missing input files are skipped rather than counted as failures: the analysis script warns, while generation returns silently. A filter matching no labels likewise exercises zero cases. Summary totals include only passed and failed, hiding skipped/unselected coverage. A portable RFF verification matrix should record expected, selected, found, analyzed, generated, compiled and numerically checked counts separately and reject an unintentionally empty run. Unsupported examples need explicit expected outcomes rather than disappearing from the denominator. The source arrays here are a useful diversity checklist, but 64 listed cases are not 64 verified conversions.

The most useful RFF feature candidate is a staged shader-import workflow: preserve source/provenance, analyze dependencies and editable parameters, present the selected formula role, generate into a defined host interface, compile and reflect that interface, then compare representative outputs before treating an import as supported. Keep the last valid renderer active on failure. For 3D, numerical comparisons should cover distance values, seeds, derivative state, branch/fold behavior, normal orientation and ray-hit consistency, not just a colorful image. For 2D, the same infrastructure could accept restricted coloring, masks or coordinate-pattern modules with explicit scalar/vector inputs; it must not imply that arbitrary GLSL formulas are compatible with high-precision Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA. Per-file licensing and original attribution remain separate acceptance requirements. This proposal draws on the importer's architecture while avoiding the weak success criteria in these historical exploratory scripts.

The harness covers a complete existing pair, not the one-endpoint case, invalid numbers, reversed bands or out-of-range input. ## Live/export modulation parity: shared planning is necessary but not the whole pipeline (2026-10-08)

Full source review of `debug/test-modulation-parity.mts` (217 lines), without execution. Its useful architectural idea is one target planner producing uniform writes, engine-side offsets and live display values, followed by a composite flush. RFF could use that separation to keep interactive playback and offline export consistent for animated 3D lighting/materials and 2D palette or pattern parameters. The source-level harness tests that planner; it does not run both playback/export consumers at matched timestamps or read GPU values/pixels. Therefore the headline 'same writes' is only partly constrained by this test.

Composite accumulation matters for vector parameters: modifying X and then Y must produce a vector containing both changes, retaining untouched components. Emitting a fresh base vector after each axis can reset the previous edit. The harness's first case exercises two axes of the first eligible registry vec3 and checks that both differ from their base and Z stays unchanged. It does not assert exact expected X/Y values. Its collection Map also overwrites duplicate uniform keys, so the assertion text saying the vector was emitted 'once' does not actually measure emission count or conflicting intermediate writes. For RFF, assemble a complete per-frame parameter block from one base-state snapshot and then publish it, with an explicit combination order for multiple rules targeting the same component.

The registry sweep broadens target discovery beyond a hardcoded coreMath/geometry naming regex and includes vec2/vec3/vec4 axes in its loop. However, the final checks require only some reachable targets and some targets outside the old regex. A broken individual axis or missing vec4 family could remain undetected as long as another succeeds. It also treats any uniform output as reachability, rather than verifying the expected binding and value for each target. An RFF contract should enumerate required targets and compare each resolved binding, type, component, unit conversion and value; shader reflection/resource-layout validation is a separate check.

The Julia-zero case is a strong discriminating fixture: it seeds a nonzero base and applies an offset that should land exactly at zero, so a truthiness fallback cannot hide behind a zero default. It also seeds an untouched axis nonzero and restores the original state in finally. This generalizes to zero light intensity, black/emission values, zero palette phase and signed offsets. Missing values and legitimate zero values must remain distinct. The rotation checks likewise verify all three named stages route an offset, but only their X axes; they do not establish transform composition order or rendered orientation.

Running the planner twice and comparing serialized outputs checks repeatability on the chosen store state. It does not prove purity: deterministic mutation can produce the same outputs, and the harness does not compare the input before/after or freeze it. Serialization also erases distinctions such as some nonfinite values. For RFF, keep base document values, transient evaluated animation values and displayed values distinct; record finite typed values and use deterministic time/sample inputs for export. This should not require feeding transient modulation back into the saved document or the high-precision reference orbit unless a deliberate geometric parameter actually changes.

The final source scan finds textual reads of modulationEngine.offsets in selected roots and rejects unexpected paths. Its allowed-path check does not prove exactly three consumers exist, and checking for the substring planModulationTarget in two files does not prove the relevant execution branch calls it. Aliases, computed access, another root or dead code can evade or satisfy those checks. Comment stripping with regular expressions is not a parser. In this workspace's non-ASCII source path, converting a file URL via pathname and a drive-prefix replacement also does not perform URL decoding; that portability issue should be resolved before treating a local run as authoritative. No failure or pass is claimed from execution here.

The concrete RFF adoption candidate is a common, typed evaluation plan used by both preview and export, with atomic vector composition, explicit missing-value semantics and a final validated GPU parameter upload. Verify matched outputs at fixed times, including zero crossings, repeated targets, multiple vector axes, rule removal and seek/restart. Keep 3D rotation/lighting and 2D coloring targets separate from formula recomputation dependencies so inexpensive color animation does not unnecessarily invalidate geometry, while geometry changes never reuse stale results. This review supports that architecture and its validation boundaries; it does not establish a current RFF export discrepancy or a measured speed improvement.

Full review of `debug/test-param-mapping.mts` (304 lines), without execution. This harness covers the relationship between control curves and modulation composition: iteration power curves, type-dependent light intensity, logarithmic radius/range, angle units, curve roundtrips, clamping and shared call sites. The transferable RFF feature is a canonical parameter description used by controls, animation and export, so the same adjustment does not acquire a different meaning in each path.

For curved parameters the tested policy converts the base to display space, adds travel proportional to offset divided by the physical range, clamps to the mapping's display domain, then converts back. This gives predictable slider movement away from saturation. It is a policy choice, not behavior-neutral physical addition: a fixed travel on a logarithmic scale generally produces a multiplicative physical change. If RFF offers both physical-unit offsets and normalized control travel, label and persist the chosen mode. Preserve existing saved animation semantics when adding the latter. Treat angle-unit conversion separately from nonlinear curvature, and do not apply another logarithmic curve to a parameter already represented in logarithmic units, such as an exposure stop value.

The first compatibility comparisons reconstruct historical mappings using the same current mapping constructors as the resolver under test. They constrain which constructor and arguments are selected, but a shared regression in a constructor can change both sides together. Likewise, invertible yet incorrect forward/inverse functions can pass a roundtrip. The sampled points and tolerances are useful regression checks, not proof of identical behavior across every real value. Store independently specified anchor values and expected endpoint behavior for RFF parameters whose physical meaning matters. The registry sweep checks only the forward direction for selected declared scales; its greater-than-fifteen coverage gate does not guarantee every previously expected parameter remains present. NaN comparisons in that sweep can also evade a greater-than-tolerance test, so finite-value checks need to precede comparisons.

The constant-travel case checks five interior bases under one positive offset. Saturated movement is necessarily smaller, and the harness tests extreme saturation separately. It does not demonstrate constant movement at endpoints, negative offsets, every mapping type or changing light types. A light-kind-dependent intensity mapping needs explicit unit/range and animation behavior when its kind changes. RFF's 3D point/area-light intensity, radius and roughness controls can benefit from suitable curves, but their displayed responsiveness should not be confused with equivalence of radiometric units or energy output.

The reserved-zero logarithmic mapping is a particularly important shader interface condition. Here a declared minimum of 0.1 can still map the bottom of the control to exactly zero. That can be useful for disabling a contribution, but any shader division, logarithm or normalization consuming it needs a defined zero case. The two extreme-offset finite assertions establish only those specific outputs, not that the mapping can never produce NaN/Infinity. RFF should distinguish an allowed off state from a strictly positive parameter domain, rather than assuming the declared UI minimum protects every GPU input. For 2D, zero repeats, zero pattern scale and zero contrast width can have different meanings and must not share an accidental fallback.

Linear composition is tested against ordinary base-plus-offset for four cases. A degenerate range falls back to addition, which avoids division by zero but does not keep the output within that zero-width range. The curved path clamps while the linear path deliberately does not, so this is not one universal bounds policy. Specify whether clamping belongs to modulation evaluation, the final semantic parameter validator or the shader, and make preview/export follow the same policy. Test negative and nonfinite inputs, signed zero where relevant, tiny positive values and fractional/integer conversion independently. Sampling a one-to-five-hundred iteration curve does not establish correct integer rounding or a formula's supported iteration budget.

The source scans discourage local mapping constructors and selected raw-addition patterns, but do not prove all controls use the canonical resolver or all runtime branches call composition. Alternate spellings, aliases or arithmetic forms can evade the regular expressions; matching a function name can be satisfied by an import. The script explicitly records such a historical weakness. As in the parity harness, converting file URLs through pathname without decoding creates a portability concern in this non-ASCII checkout. No current test-pass claim is made from these source checks.

For RFF, prioritize a typed parameter schema carrying physical value, unit, valid domain, optional display transform, explicit zero/off behavior and animation combination mode. Use it for both 3D lighting/material controls and 2D palette/mask controls, with one final evaluation path before upload. Confirm behavior through independent values and matched preview/export evaluation rather than only repeated copies of the same formula. This can improve precise artistic adjustment without reducing fractal computation precision or changing MPA; it is a control/animation improvement, not a measured rendering-speed gain.

The observed data is a synchronous event Map, not GPU state. The animation tick is not invoked: the curved expected value calls the shared helper directly. Thus agreement with that helper is established by the test design, not runtime equality of both writers or absence of visible flicker. No historical half-frame-rate claim is generalized to current RFF behavior.

Removing a rule should restore the base on the next appropriate update. Preview and export should use the same evaluation order and units. Verification should capture the complete write sequence and scheduler effects, then compare actual rendered frames where flicker is the promised outcome. This is an adoption design and test-scope analysis, not a claim that RFF currently suffers the historical GMT problem.

Full review of `debug/test-eyedropper-active.mts` (83 lines), plus selective inspection of the current `doEyedrop` implementation in the already-reviewed `components/EmbeddedColorPicker.tsx`. No native picker was opened or test executed. The transferable feature for RFF is direct color sampling into a palette/material editor with an explicit choice of sampled representation: displayed appearance, source palette color or another documented renderer buffer. A displayed shaded pixel is not interchangeable with a material's base color, and an sRGB hex result is not scene-linear HDR radiance.

GMT's current picker announces an active operation, waits for two animation-frame callbacks, then uses a native picker or page fallback and clears the active flag in finally. The temporary active state lets an image lose its dimmed presentation before sampling. That mechanism illustrates a useful requirement: temporary overlays or presentation effects must not accidentally contaminate the color the user intends to capture. In RFF, synchronize sampling with the intended completed render/presentation state; merely counting two UI frames is not proof that GPU work or a display transformation has completed. Specify whether tone mapping and exposure are part of the sampled result, then convert the result to the destination color representation deliberately.

The harness proves initial/set/clear flag values, non-counting boolean behavior and visibility through a repeated import of the same module. That does not prove cross-window ownership, subscriber notifications or concurrent-operation safety. A single boolean is appropriate only with a single-operation contract: if two picks overlap, the first completion can clear the state while another remains active. RFF can reject overlapping picks or attach ownership to each operation. Cancellation, focus loss, view disposal and failure should release temporary presentation state and leave the previous selected color intact unless a result was successfully accepted.

Its cleanup guard reads only a 900-character source slice starting at the first matching declaration and searches regular expressions. A stalled wait or teardown needs lifecycle handling beyond that check. The header's explanation that a rejecting native picker necessarily skips a clear after a catch is also too broad: a caught rejection followed by ordinary continuation would run it; the later test comment correctly narrows that observation. For an RFF picker, separate cancellation from a sampling failure so an ordinary Escape action remains a neutral exit. For 2D, this supports sampling a displayed fractal into palette stops while offering direct palette-color access when the user wants unshaded values. For 3D, it supports material/color exploration while making the distinction between lit appearance and material input visible. Validate lifecycle behavior independently from color correctness, using known pixels/colors and the intended output transform. Preserve source-image/palette provenance where appropriate. This is a workflow and color-semantics proposal, not evidence that copying a screen pixel reconstructs the original shader parameters.

The offset assertion accepts any number unequal to zero, which also admits NaN; finite expected values would be a stronger check. More importantly, no worker message is captured and no worker/GPU consumer is run. The comment promising a payload assertion is not fulfilled in this file: reaching the proxy dictionary does not prove transport of that dictionary to the worker. For RFF's rendering boundary, test the actual submitted parameter block and its consumer, including clearing/removal, stale frames and renderer replacement. Define whether messages carry complete state or deltas so a disappeared animation cannot leave its last value active. The camera exception explicitly reflects a degrees-versus-radians mismatch. Full source review of `debug/test-liquify-mesh.mts` (280 lines), without execution. The harness exercises a coarse 2D deformation mesh, handles, seven brush modes, optional relaxation toward the authored sculpt, corrective smoothing and finer render-grid interpolation. The useful RFF candidate is an optional editable warp of material/pattern coordinates or a clearly identified image effect. It should not silently deform the coordinate system used to claim an exact Mandelbrot view or replace high-precision computation with a warped screenshot.

The architecture implied by the calls separates authored sculpt from live simulated positions and increases render-grid density independently of the control grid. This can provide direct artistic control without requiring a handle at every output vertex. For 2D palette fields, masks or procedural textures, persist the authored deformation and evaluate the visual warp at output resolution. For 3D, a UV/material-coordinate warp is the more direct transfer. Deforming actual raymarched geometry additionally needs a distance-bound/metric treatment, transformed normals and a policy for foldovers; a finite 2D mesh is no evidence that a 3D distance estimator remains safe.

The tests use fixed grids of 48 or 8 and mostly one 800-by-600 viewport. They verify finite/bounded outputs and that displacing brushes move something, but those checks alone do not establish intended brush direction, falloff, aspect correction, pin behavior or absence of inverted cells. In particular, the pin block checks only finiteness after simulation, not that the pinned location stays fixed. Reset is checked through handle count and in-bounds finite positions, not equality to the flat grid. Index count and upper bounds do not prove triangle connectivity, consistent winding or nondegeneracy. RFF should verify signed cell areas/Jacobians and explicit pin positions for any no-fold contract, alongside extreme strokes and varying aspect ratios.

The settlement test checks a center-adjacent vertex remains displaced after 600 fixed steps; it does not compare the whole mesh to its authored target or measure residual velocity. A mesh frozen at an arbitrary deformed state could satisfy the 'kept deformation' condition. Test target error and kinetic/residual change if the promised behavior is convergence to the sculpt. The physics-off fixture calls syncToSculpt and then one step, so it covers that synchronized state rather than every way of disabling ongoing physics.

The repaired smoothing fixtures correctly start from a nonflat mesh and require measurable movement, avoiding a no-op implementation passing only finite/bounded checks. However, the local roughness metric uses horizontal second differences for both position components; it does not measure vertical roughness. The global test compares only initial/final displacement after 400 steps, so 'never inflates' and 'no fold' are stronger than the assertions: transient expansion and local inversion could occur between samples. Test both axes and intermediate states where those guarantees matter. Strength, time-step, grid-size and repeated-edit dependence remain separate questions for deterministic RFF video export.

The interpolation fixtures distinguish a nonlinear result from a bilinear replacement and verify control-point passage, selected flat interior behavior and finite values. Nonzero deviation from a straight line does not uniquely establish the intended Catmull-Rom polynomial or correct tangents. Boundary cells are explicitly excluded from linear-reproduction checks because their clamped extension differs. RFF would need independent expected samples and continuity/boundary tests, plus overshoot and fold checks after interpolation. A smoother mesh does not by itself filter the texture it warps: stretched/compressed coordinates still need footprint-aware sampling to avoid aliasing at fine fractal detail.

The named MLS-rigid, XPBD, Taubin and Catmull-Rom descriptions are algorithm/provenance leads, not licenses established by this harness. Before adapting implementations, verify original sources, the actual variant and its license and record attribution in NOTICE. This review neither verifies those algorithm implementations anew nor promotes all of them as required RFF features. The immediate candidate is a separate, reversible material-coordinate deformation layer with stable controls, optional deterministic motion and clear export semantics. It is applicable to both 2D pattern editing and 3D materials, while actual fractal geometry deformation remains a distinct, more demanding feature.

Averaging flux across a band range avoids a simple count-proportional increase but does not guarantee range-width invariance for arbitrary spectral content. RFF should label the resulting signal as a visual control value and preserve its aggregation mode in saved rules.

The range checks cover one bass interval and a zero-width selection that still resolves to a band. The 'brackets requested frequencies' assertion only checks inequalities at the first/last selected bands; it does not prove exact selection boundaries or all intersecting bands. Negative, reversed, above-Nyquist and nonfinite requests are not covered. Define those cases before exposing arbitrary user-editable frequency ranges in RFF. Stable physical-frequency rules should be resolved again after a table change rather than retaining old bin indices.

Adaptive gain lifts a quiet but significant band toward the available control range, limits amplification of a near-silent band, freezes remembered peaks through silence and releases during sustained quieter content. This is an artistic policy that can keep material/emission or palette motion responsive without amplifying noise into a full-scale effect. It is not a neutral loudness measurement. The tests cover selected levels and fixed 60 Hz follower steps; they do not prove all outputs are finite/nonnegative or that adaptive history is equivalent across frame rates, pauses and irregular snapshot arrival. A divisor held through silence can also carry history from a previous track unless an explicit reset policy is applied.

The same-settings rebuild fixture is useful: changing array length alone could hide a missing reset, so it verifies a reset when the band count is unchanged as well. Yet it checks the resulting normalized level at one band, not complete state reset or zeroed stale flux across all buffers. The matches checks independently vary sample rate, FFT size and bands per octave, which constrains all three identity fields. For RFF, attach that identity or a generation number to snapshots and reject old-generation data after reconfiguration; matching array length does not imply matching frequency meaning.

The helper runFollower reproduces the stated normalization branch of WorkletAnalysis.update rather than calling that integration path. Thus the harness cannot establish that the real consumer selects the right branch, uses the right delta time, receives coherent arrays or avoids repeated processing of the same sample. For deterministic export, evaluate adaptation against audio time and a defined initial/history state, not incidental render-frame cadence. Seek, source replacement, normalization toggles and offline preroll require explicit behavior. Test those separately from the arithmetic holder.

The practical RFF candidate is optional per-band automatic gain with a noise floor, configurable reset behavior and a reproducible control history. Apply it to 3D light/emission/material or 2D palette/pattern parameters through the shared typed modulation path; geometry modulation remains a separate recomputation decision. This can improve artistic responsiveness, but no live audio, GPU output, latency or performance result was verified in this batch.

## Numeric drag sensitivity: precision control distinct from update throttling (2026-10-08)

Full review of `debug/test-number-drag-rate.mts` (97 lines), without execution. Here 'rate' means parameter change per pointer pixel, not event frequency or render-update throttling. The RFF improvement candidate is a consistent fine-adjustment policy for numeric fields paired with sliders: derive a baseline from step and sensitivity, then constrain its movement relative to the slider's span and width. This can make 3D light/material parameters and 2D palette/pattern parameters easier to adjust across very different numerical ranges.

The harness sweeps twelve step sizes, three sensitivities, seven spans, seven widths and two mapped states for two feel configurations: 3528 cases per configuration. It checks a bounded slowdown relative to the corresponding track, then pins representative tiny-step/log and coarse integer examples. The specific slowdown ranges are GMT/Gradient Explorer choices, not universal RFF defaults. A finer step matters inside the allowed band but saturates at the maximum slowdown; consequently sensitivity need not remain proportional once clamping engages. Preserve direct numeric entry for values requiring finer resolution than pointer travel conveniently provides.

A significant assertion limitation is that the broad sweep counts only slowdown values below/above bounds. NaN satisfies neither comparison, so a NaN result can escape both counters. The named examples have stronger numerical comparisons but do not prove finiteness for the full sweep. RFF should require a finite positive rate before evaluating bounds and define zero/negative/nonfinite step, width, span and sensitivity inputs. The infinite-span fallback is explicitly tested; other malformed or degenerate cases are not.

For mapped controls, the tested span can be display-space travel rather than physical-value range. Returning a plausible rate does not establish the control applies it in that same domain. Verify integration with the actual log/power/angle mapping, rounding and clamping, including negative drags and zero/off regions. The rate helper also does not establish behavior under DPI scaling, resize during a drag, pointer capture loss, modifier keys or integer quantization. An integer field can feel sticky if fractional pointer progress is discarded on every event; the helper tests do not exercise that state.

No drawing, uniform upload or event coalescing is measured here, so this cannot support a claim of lower GPU load or smoother frame scheduling. RFF should treat sensitivity and update scheduling separately: accumulate input accurately, apply the latest intended value coherently and always publish the final value when the gesture ends. For 2D this can support precise coloring controls while keeping high-precision coordinates out of ordinary float UI arithmetic; for 3D it can support stable tuning of roughness, light radius or other parameters without changing their physical meaning. This is a control-behavior proposal, not a shader optimization or a verified current UI defect.
