The substantive addition over MengerSmooth is Transform2. It constructs all three new components from the same incoming vector: abs(length(yz)-T2offset), abs(length(xz)-T2offset), and abs(length(xy)-T2offset), then scales the vector by T2Scale. Each channel is an unsigned cylindrical-shell feature around a different axis for nonnegative offset. This is a vector coordinate transform, not the distance to the union of three cylinders. A negative offset instead adds magnitude before abs and has no corresponding positive-radius shell zero. Sequentially assigning x, then using that changed x to assign y would implement a different transform; preserve simultaneous input semantics.

**RFF transfer:** these three signals could be exposed as independent material masks for color, roughness, or emission, or composed into an optional procedural coordinate source. This avoids requiring an unverified geometry estimator merely to obtain tube/ring motifs. In 2D, circle-shell distances around selected centers or line-distance channels offer an independently defined equivalent design. A z=0 slice of this particular three-channel operation produces abs(abs(y)-offset), abs(abs(x)-offset), and abs(length(xy)-offset): two axis-band signals plus a ring. That can be useful as a 2D mask set, but it is not a two-component recurrence and should be named accordingly.

Transform2 multiplies w only by T2Scale. Its unscaled vector map can have Euclidean amplification sqrt(2): each output's difference is bounded by the norm of the corresponding input-coordinate pair, and summing the three squared pair bounds gives 2*length(delta)^2. At equal positive components away from the shell cusps, its Jacobian can attain that amplification. Thus the scalar T2Scale alone does not bound the whole vector transform's derivative. A new geometry implementation would need to account for this and the other nonlinear stages; a material implementation still needs appropriate footprint and normal propagation. This derivation is an analytical observation, not an executed numerical test or proof of the final fractal estimator.

T2Scale ranges from -5 to 5. Its sign is carried into w, while the terminal return is abs(length(z))/w, so a negative scale can produce a negative reported field even though the numerator is nonnegative. Zero scale causes a zero denominator when the transform executes. This is not a recommendation to silently repair source behavior: RFF should define signed coordinate scaling separately from positive derivative magnitude in a new effect contract, with preserved source behavior only in an explicitly compatible importer.

All main-loop schedule comparisons now use one-based n from 1 through Iterations. This changes total-warp semantics from the earlier MengerSmooth version: zero disables Total_Sphere_Iter here but selected the first iteration there. Section controls remain one-based in effective application count. A saved schedule cannot be migrated by blindly copying every integer. The Web variant also removes the tetrahedral pretransform and adds selective rather than unconditional per-iteration rotation.

Rotation has two independent conditions. The first applies once when n==RotIter1 OR n>=RotEverAfter; the second applies again when n==RotIter2. Therefore matching RotIter1 to RotEverAfter does not itself double the rotation, but matching RotIter2 to either active first condition does. Transform2's preset has RotIter1=RotIter2=2 and RotAngle=33.33333, so the second iteration applies the matrix twice. Transform2no2 does the same with 130 degrees. This is ordered composition, not duplicate metadata. A RFF schedule editor or serializer should explicitly preserve repeated operations and define overlap rules instead of deduplicating same-stage transforms.

The order per step is scheduled rotation(s), optional Transform2, total warp(s), smooth abs, section warps around sorting/z folding/scaling, orbit sample, then total restoration. Transform2 therefore alters both later geometry and color samples. As in the earlier source, the second unSphere section invokes unSpheric on both sides of the z fold. The ratio-based Spheric/Octalizer singularities and the scale-only accumulator limitations still apply. They do not disappear because the file is labeled forWeb.

The Default preset runs 12 geometry steps and eight color steps. Its total sphere and unsphere schedules both equal 11, and all six section schedules equal 12. Those events execute even though the initial Sphere/unSphere/HoleSphere booleans are false; the booleans are not master enables for scheduled operations. They occur after the color window, which makes this preset an example of late geometry transformations that do not add new trap samples. It does not establish color independence under arbitrary changes to earlier transforms or the camera.

Several inherited presets omit T2Iteration1, T2offset, T2Scale, and rotation schedules. Under a reset-to-declaration interpretation, Transform2 defaults to step five and remains active whenever there are at least five iterations. Under patch loading it can inherit a different transform from the preceding preset. Thus names such as Balls or Water1 are not evidence that their behavior matches identically named presets in the older file. A RFF importer should materialize defaults and preserve formula-version identity; a new procedural feature should have a separate enable flag rather than rely exclusively on an unreachable iteration index to disable it.

**Adoption value:** cylindrical-shell feature channels and a precise ordered transform schedule can improve RFF's 3D materials and 2D procedural masks. Keep these outside the core Mandelbrot/MPA calculation and preserve existing recipes. ## Concrete shader mechanisms: stereographic wireframes and explicit thickness spaces (2026-10-08)

Full reads: `public/formulas/frag/Knighty Collection/polychora-special.frag` (259 lines, three presets) and `polychora-special02.frag` (244 lines, two presets). Both identify Knighty (2012) and a forum source. The active implementation contains vertices and edges, not filled faces or transparency; comments proposing faces are not implemented functionality. No rendered comparison, compilation, or estimator proof was performed.

Both map an input position x with radius r to the unit 3-sphere in four coordinates: q=(2*x,1-r*r)/(1+r*r). For finite exact arithmetic this is an inverse stereographic projection, not a fixed-w slice through a 4D object. A rotation mixes w with the spatial component along a normalized axis, leaving orthogonal spatial components unchanged. Three rounds of absolute xyz and reflection in n=(-0.5,-0.5,-0.5,0.5) then fold the point. The principal node is a normalized weighted sum of four specified chamber nodes. All-zero weights or a zero rotation axis require an explicit policy in a new implementation.

When useCameraAsRotVector is enabled, the axis comes from normalize(Eye-Target). Camera changes therefore affect the evaluated pattern itself, not just its view. RFF could offer camera-linked material orientation as an intentional mode, but a stable world/local-coordinate mode should remain separately defined for reproducible exports. Eye==Target is not a usable rotation axis, even if some surrounding camera code supplies a view fallback. Camera-dependent coefficients also need invalidation when the camera changes if cached.

For a vertex, ca is the dot product between two unit vectors and sa is computed as 0.5*length(p-q)*length(p+q). In exact arithmetic this equals the nonnegative sine of their angular separation. Compared with sqrt(1-ca*ca), it avoids that explicit subtraction near coincident/antipodal vectors, but is not a blanket floating-point accuracy guarantee. Edge evaluation constructs normalize(alpha*p+min(0,beta)*n), with alpha=dot(q,p)-dot(q,n)*dot(n,p) and beta=dot(q,n)-dot(q,p)*dot(n,p). The one-sided beta restriction is part of the spherical edge construction; this is not the ordinary Euclidean segment-distance helper reviewed elsewhere. Degenerate projected vectors still need handling.

The main variant difference is thickness space. Define F(a,r)=(2*r*cos(a)-(1-r*r)*sin(a))/((1-r*r)*cos(a)+2*r*sin(a)+1+r*r). The first file returns F(radius,r)-F(separation,r), separately for vertex and edge radii. Its radius is an angular parameter used inside sine and cosine. The second returns r-F(separation,r)-radius, subtracting radius after conversion. Identical VRadius/SRadius values therefore do not describe equivalent thickness. In the second file the precomputed sine/cosine radius values are unused. This is a concrete RFF design lesson: distinguish angular thickness, local/world-space thickness, and screen-space width in the effect schema rather than sharing an unlabeled scalar across modes.

The rational conversion can approach a zero denominator near projection singularities; the initial r*r construction can also overflow for extreme inputs. Rotation and folding preserve norm ideally but do not remove those hazards. Nor does a formula converting a spherical separation automatically prove exact Euclidean distance to every projected edge neighborhood. For RFF geometry, validate the complete bound independently. For decorative masks, an explicitly bounded material-coordinate domain and footprint filtering may be sufficient, without making a geometric distance claim.

**3D and 2D transfer:** stereographic domain mapping can produce curved wireframe or cellular material patterns and animate their layout using a compact rotation parameter. A 2D counterpart can lift local (u,v) to the ordinary unit sphere as (2u,2v,1-u*u-v*v)/(1+u*u+v*v), rotate there, and evaluate an independently defined spherical line/point pattern. Alternatively, sampling this exact 3D input field at z=0 gives a planar mask of the 4D-derived field, not a regular 2D polygon construction. State which approach is implemented. Both should operate in local material coordinates, preserving RFF's deep-zoom fractal arithmetic.

These shaders overwrite orbitTrap with the final folded four-vector; they do not take a running minimum and do not store squared radius in its fourth lane. The w channel is a coordinate and should not be interpreted as the radial trap statistic from other formulas. A RFF feature interface should tag channel meanings or return a dedicated projected-coordinate field, allowing it to drive color/roughness without reusing incompatible trap assumptions. If a renderer calls DE for normals or shadows, ownership of this mutable trap also matters; this local body alone does not prove that the final displayed color always uses the intended surface sample.

Both combine the vertex and four edge estimates with min, but do not return the winning feature ID. Adding an explicit vertex/edge material mask could enable different highlight or emission treatment; it would be an RFF extension, not existing per-feature coloring in these files. The providesColor macro is commented out. The first 24-cell preset disables orbit coloration, while the Default presets enable a small contribution. The partial 24-cell? preset changes geometry controls only. These differing cameras, lights, radii, and defaults prevent treating the presets as a controlled comparison of the two thickness formulas.

**Adoption value:** curved projected masks, meaningful thickness units, and optional camera-linked orientation are practical material ideas for RFF's 3D and 2D output. Validate the projection origin and far field, axis/weight degeneracy, spherical edge endpoints, rational denominators, thickness conversion, and camera/export consistency. Keep presets versioned by formula semantics and resolve source/license provenance before adapting recognizable implementation details into RFF and NOTICE.

## Concrete shader mechanisms: serial versus simultaneous domain deformation (2026-10-08)

Full read: `public/formulas/frag/Knighty Collection/Pseudo-MandalayBox.frag` (492 lines), including Default, The_town, Julia_without_boxfold, Mandelbox, Extrusions, and Spaceship. The local body credits a reinterpretation of DarkBeam's fold. It provides source evidence for a procedural coordinate operation, not a measured improvement to RFF or proof of a safe distance estimator. No compilation, rendering, or timing was performed.

DBFold first swaps y/z if needed, then combines shifted absolute values, maxima, and minima. With x as the selected output axis and y the larger of the other two coordinates, it forms v=max(abs(x-fo)-fo,y-4*fo), v1=max(x-2*fo-g,y-w,-abs(x)), and returns min(v,v1,x). The nested piecewise-linear constraints create pull/extrusion-like regions. They are not just an orthogonal reflection, despite the helper name. The surrounding iteration applies this to absolute coordinates and restores the saved signs afterward.

Parallel mode evaluates all three axis permutations against an unchanged copy of the input. Serial mode overwrites x, then evaluates y using the modified vector, then evaluates z using both earlier changes. Serial here describes mathematical dependency, not GPU scheduling or a performance mode. A RFF procedural graph could use both as distinct effects: simultaneous channels preserve a symmetric input reference, while ordered updates create coupled patterns. Any shader refactor must preserve the source snapshots and update order; replacing one by the other is an appearance change.

For simultaneous mode, equal fo/gh/gw across axes give a natural permutation-symmetric construction because each channel treats the other two coordinates through their maximum. Unequal per-axis parameters intentionally break that symmetry. Serial evaluation can break it even when parameter values match, since the first axis is privileged by update order. This provides an interpretable control for RFF pattern variety rather than another opaque preset collection. A 2D adaptation can define two axis channels with the same simultaneous/ordered choice and a line-based constraint construction, but dropping a dimension from the three-axis formula requires an explicit definition.

The optional box fold is p-2*clamp(p,-1,1), the negative of the commonly written 2*clamp(p,-1,1)-p. Its sign interacts with later sign restoration and Julia translation; substituting the familiar form is not an equivalent cleanup. After DBFold, the radial multiplier is clamp(1/r2,1,1/MinRad2), followed by p=Scale*p+constant and left-multiplied rotation. MinRad2 is a squared-radius threshold. The original input is the constant when Julia is false; JuliaC is used when true. Consequently this formula's Mandelbrot-like option is not RFF's quadratic Mandelbrot calculation and does not justify changes to its perturbation or MPA equations.

The scalar accumulator follows dd=dd*t and then dd=dd*Scale+parameterTerm, where parameterTerm is one in input-dependent mode and zero in Julia mode. Only after the loop is abs(dd) taken. Negative Scale can therefore cause cancellation in input-dependent mode; it is not the same recurrence as an accumulated nonnegative Jacobian norm. The DBFold vector operation also has no explicit derivative contribution. In Julia mode taking the final absolute value accounts for the sign of repeated uniform scales, but does not by itself establish the bound for the entire deformation. RFF should separate a useful material coordinate warp from any claim that this denominator makes the terminal field safe for ray marching.

The loop tests squared radius against 10000 before each update and samples color after rotation. The terminal field is (sqrt(r2)-30)/abs(dd), using a fixed radius set in init, rather than an exact box terminal or the inactive cube alternative. Zero iterations return length(input)-30, with no trap update. Zero dd, the inversion origin, MinRad2=0, and a zero rotation axis require deliberate handling in a new implementation. Preserving source precision and semantics is preferable to inserting arbitrary epsilons into unrelated RFF arithmetic.

With fo=gh=gw=0, DBFold returns its selected nonnegative x input, so its parallel stage reduces to identity before sign restoration. This explains why the Mandelbox preset can use zero deformation parameters as a baseline. It still retains this file's box-fold orientation, terminal sphere, bailout, and derivative conventions; the preset name does not prove exact equivalence to every other Mandelbox implementation. The_town and Spaceship enable serial mode, while Spaceship additionally uses negative Scale and Julia mode. Their different cameras, constants, colors, and lights prevent an isolated serial-versus-parallel quality comparison.

The orbit trap reduces abs(xyz) and squared radius after the complete iteration, including rotation. There is no independent ColorIterations limit, feature ID, or stage mask. RFF could optionally expose the DBFold constraint winner, per-axis displacement, or pre/post-deformation difference as material signals. Such features could drive 3D roughness/emission or 2D coloring and relief without importing the whole fractal. They are proposed outputs, not already implemented channels, and should be introduced as new versioned modes that preserve existing palette recipes.

**Adoption value:** explicit simultaneous versus ordered deformation and readable per-axis pattern controls offer material variety in 3D and 2D. Keep the effect in local material coordinates. Validate the zero-parameter identity, axis permutations, update dependencies, sign-plane boundaries, radial thresholds, negative-scale cases, and preview/export consistency. If geometry use is pursued, independently validate derivatives and marching bounds. Resolve DarkBeam's original contribution and this adaptation's actual license before copying distinctive code and adding matching RFF NOTICE attribution.

Full read: `public/formulas/frag/Knighty Collection/PseudoKnightyan.frag` (162 lines), including its complete Default preset. The file credits Knighty and includes DE-Kn2cr11 with hash, cloud, volumetric, shadow, and multisample-AO feature defines. All Iter updates execute for ordinary finite input. The trap records abs(xyz) and squared radius after inversion for i<ColorIterations. The default uses nine geometry updates and only three color updates, a clear instance of independent color sampling depth. This differs from the earlier PseudoKleinian formula, which samples both before and after the radial operation and has exact fixed-point termination.

The distance divisor starts at DEfactor and multiplies by k+0.05, although coordinates scale only by k. Consequently even an identity radial branch, k=1, shrinks the returned field through a 1.05 multiplier per step. Relative to a product of k, the divisor contains the additional factor product(1+0.05/k). It is iteration-dependent damping, not a directly derived Jacobian update. It can make marching more cautious in finite positive cases but does not by itself prove the terminal field or complete fold is safe. An RFF effect interface should distinguish coordinate scale, derivative magnitude, and an artistic or marching safety factor rather than combine them under one ambiguous accumulator.

Let rho=length(p.xy) and a=TwiddleRXY. The numerator is max(rho-a, abs(rho*p.z)/length(p)). For nonzero p and positive divisor it is nonnegative. For a>=0 its zero set includes both the xy disk with radius a and the z axis; it is not simply distance to a cylinder or a thickened plane. At p=0 the second term is undefined. For negative a the first term is positive everywhere, so the finite terminal field has no zero set. This explains why the full allowed control range cannot be interpreted uniformly as a positive object radius.

**RFF transfer:** expose the cylinder-offset term and the plane/axis proximity term separately as material signals before choosing a combination. They could drive distinct color, roughness, or emission layers on a 3D surface, with a deliberate mask remapping. The existing source combines them into one scalar and does not provide separate feature IDs. A new mode would be an extension, not a source-compatible reinterpretation of the current orbit trap.

For a direct planar input z=0, this recurrence preserves z=0 as long as the fold and inversion are finite and CSize is valid. Its terminal then reduces to max(length(xy)-a,0)/j. This has a flat zero disk and cannot directly supply a unique signed boundary or useful interior normal. A 2D material could deliberately use it as an exterior radial mask, or independently define a signed circle/annulus terminal after the same planar fold. State that change explicitly rather than claim a literal 3D-to-2D port preserves the same geometric meaning. All such patterns should use local material coordinates without altering RFF's deep-zoom perturbation or MPA calculation.

The CSize controls allow negative components, which reverse the corresponding clamp bounds; a new implementation must define or reject that domain. DEfactor can be zero, Size can be negative, and Size/dot(p,p) remains undefined at zero radius for zero Size. For negative Size at nonzero radius, k becomes one, so inversion is disabled but the 0.05 damping continues. These observations inform RFF parameter semantics and validation; they are not a request to repair the archived formula or introduce arbitrary precision-reducing clamps.

The Default preset requests a nonzero aperture, two reflection bounces, fog intensity, strong shadows, and independently weighted AO channels. Unlike some earlier presets, those saved values are not all disabled, but the preset alone does not prove the complete renderer's execution path or the cost of each feature. Bloom remains false despite its stored intensity and tap count. Ambient light strength is zero despite a nonzero AO_ambient value, so a large ambient AO control need not create visible ambient shading in that preset. A controlled RFF comparison should isolate material fields from these renderer settings rather than attribute the full appearance to this short DE function.

**Adoption value:** independent color depth, explicit terminal-feature channels, and separation of derivative tracking from distance damping can improve RFF's procedural-effect design in both 3D and 2D. Validate zero/negative parameter cases, the planar zero disk, axis singularities, trap-window limits, and the effect of extra iterations with unchanged coordinates. Resolve the named source's actual license before copying distinctive expressions or constants into RFF and NOTICE. The present work is documentation-only source analysis.

## Concrete shader mechanisms: verifying the archived Mandalabeth Jacobian variants (2026-10-08)

Full reads of all three files in `public/formulas/frag/Knighty Collection/Mandalabeth-generic-with-jacobian/`: M3 (123 lines), M4 (125), and M5 (136), including each default preset. Each update sums planar power-like maps embedded in three dimensions: M3 has three coordinate-plane orientations, M4 has four tetrahedrally arranged orientations, and M5 has six orientations built from two golden-ratio-derived constants. The M5 name is not the number of summed planes. Each map is evaluated from the same incoming orbit vector, transformed back with the transpose-equivalent row-vector multiplication, and added to par times the original input. This is a sum of plane contributions, not serial composition of three/four/six power maps.

The planar helper with exponent e returns r^(e+1)*(cos((e+1)*a),sin((e+1)*a)). Its supplied derivative matrix instead uses e*r^e times the rotation by e*a. Away from the polar branch cut, the derivative of the returned map requires the coefficient e+1. Thus the output and derivative do not describe the same local map even at the integer default exponents. Noninteger e also requires a defined branch-seam policy because atan chooses a principal angle. This is relevant to a future RFF power-domain material: derive the derivative from the actual displayed transform rather than from the control's name.

The next issue is embedding. Converting mat2(pj) to mat3 with mat3(pj) fills the new diagonal element with one, while the embedded output is vec3(planarResult,0). The absent third output coordinate should have zero derivative for this contribution. Conjugating that enlarged matrix by the plane basis therefore adds an inactive-axis contribution that is not present in the orbit update. A new implementation should explicitly construct a zero-extended derivative, not assume language matrix-conversion defaults match the mathematical embedding.

The outer chain-rule structure j=ppj*j+par*I is appropriate in form for an update F(v)+par*input with initial v=input. It should not be discarded merely because the local ppj construction is inconsistent. For an independent RFF implementation, validate each planar derivative, basis embedding, summed contribution, and chain update separately. These maps are not a reason to replace or relax the precision of the existing quadratic Mandelbrot perturbation and MPA equations.

After taking absolute matrix entries, multiplying by (1,1,1), and selecting the largest component, the denominator is the maximum absolute row sum: the induced infinity norm. It is not universally an upper bound on the Euclidean operator norm. For example, a matrix with first column (1,1,1) and other entries zero has maximum row sum one but Euclidean amplification sqrt(3). If a 3D marcher requires a Euclidean derivative bound, choose and justify the matching norm; merely storing a full matrix does not settle that requirement. For material filtering, the directional Jacobian itself may be more useful than collapsing it to one scalar.

This can improve filtering under anisotropic procedural warps in both 2D and 3D. The benefit is a reusable derivative-aware material interface, not copying these unverified matrices. Keep orientation-specific feature layers optional; a 2D mode can directly use the planar power map with explicit exponent/branch semantics, while a slice of the sum of 3D plane maps is a different effect.

All three compare squared radius with Bailout despite the radius comment. Their traps take minima of abs(xyz) and squared radius, then replace the fourth channel with its square root at return. Thus the outgoing fourth channel is radial magnitude, unlike the squared-radius convention of many nearby formulas. The terminal numerator is abs(0.5*r*log(r)) in M3/M4 and abs(r*log(r)) in M5. This factor-of-two difference must be preserved in source-compatible descriptions; it is not evidence that either choice is a proven distance bound. Zero radius, singular denominators, and nonescaped finite-iteration states require an explicit policy.

The M5 declaration defaults expo to five but its preset sets six, yielding degree seven in the active planar helper. M3's preset requests 1620 ray steps with FudgeFactor below one, while M4/M5 request 100 with different camera/fog settings. Those numbers do not constitute a speed comparison or demonstrate safe stepping. RFF evaluation should use controlled geometry/material parameters and report actual measured quality and cost if a prototype is later authorized.

**Adoption criteria:** analytical derivative checks followed by meaningful numerical comparisons away from and near branch seams, explicit zero embedding, correct metric selection, channel-unit labels, and preview/export footprint consistency. The projection lifts an input x of radius r to q=(2*x,1+r*r)/(1-r*r). With the implemented Minkowski product hdot(a,b)=dot(a.xyz,b.xyz)-a.w*b.w, this has hdot(q,q)=-1 in exact arithmetic. The operation named Rotate is a Lorentz boost between the chosen spatial axis and w. Its parameter is used directly in cosh/sinh, unlike the degree-based spherical rotation reviewed earlier. Each folding pass takes abs(xy), reflects across nc using the Minkowski inner product, then reflects across nd. The loop always performs the requested number of passes, with no convergence test. Near the ball boundary the projection produces large coordinates and increasingly fine visible structure. Color is recomputed from the same projected/folded point and four edge fields plus the vertex field. Sequential equality assignments give vertex priority, then edge D, C, B, A on exact ties. The baseColor path repeats projection, boost, and all folding passes; a combined geometry/material result at a confirmed hit could reduce repeated work, but caching must respect differing sample positions and mutable trap state. ## Concrete shader mechanisms: Pengbulb branch conventions and derivative-dependent color (2026-10-08)

Full read: `public/formulas/frag/3DickUlus/Pengbulb.frag` (643 lines), including six presets. The source credits Peng Kuan's algebra, Edgars Malinovskis' code, 3Dickulus' GLSL conversion, alef's Lambda formula, and mermelada's derivative bias. Those are distinct provenance contributions, not evidence of one license covering the complete file. This analysis concerns the local implementation; the linked mathematical paper was not reviewed here, and no broader algebraic properties are asserted. No compilation, rendering, or benchmark was performed.

pengPow converts a vector to radius, azimuth acos(x/length(xy))*sign(y), and elevation asin(z/r), multiplies both angles by the exponent, and raises the radius to that exponent. pengMul adds those angles and multiplies radii. These definitions must not be assumed to have every familiar complex-number algebra property. In particular, at y=0 and negative x the implemented azimuth becomes zero because sign(0)=0, rather than the pi direction. At the z axis its xy ratio is undefined, and the origin also makes the elevation undefined. Replacing the azimuth with atan(y,x) would be a deliberate semantic correction in a new implementation, not a guaranteed appearance-preserving refactor.

Before iteration, the entire input is right-multiplied by prerot. Non-Julia mode starts z at m1 and uses the transformed input as c; Julia mode starts at that input and uses JuliaC. Optional componentwise abs occurs before the power operation. Ordinary mode computes pengPow(z,P)+c*Scale. Lambda mode computes pengMul(c,pengPow(z,P))-Scale*pengMul(c,pengPow(z,P+Q)). Other algebraic-looking forms in comments are inactive. Q has no effect in ordinary mode, and m1 has no effect in Julia mode. RFF should distinguish active control dependencies and preserve an explicit initial-orbit convention in any new procedural family.

The two modes update their scalar derivative heuristic at different times. Ordinary mode uses the old radius in max(dr*DerivativeBias, pow(r,P-1)*dr*P+1), then updates r. Lambda mode computes the new radius first and uses it in the same expression. Neither expression contains the full derivative of the two Lambda terms or their c/Scale dependence. Initialization dr=length(z)*P+1 is also not a generic Jacobian initialization for both input conventions. For negative powers, zero radii, and negative dr, the max expression needs separate analysis. This is not evidence for a precision-safe replacement of RFF's existing Mandelbrot derivative or perturbation logic.

The fourth trap channel is abs(r*dr), not radius or squared radius. Changing DerivativeBias can therefore change coloring even when every orbit coordinate and bailout decision is unchanged. It can also change the terminal estimate 0.5*log(r)*r/dr and thus ray-march behavior. **RFF transfer:** separate a derivative-based artistic feature from a geometry derivative or safety factor, so a quality adjustment does not unexpectedly recolor a saved material. If derivative-like features are exposed, label the actual statistic and sampling stage. Here trap xyz is sampled before the per-iteration rot, unlike many neighboring shaders; the radius is invariant under an ideal rotation but the coordinate channels are not.

For 2D, restricting z=0 with compatible constants and rotations can motivate complex-power and polynomial/Lambda material patterns. A fresh planar implementation should use well-defined complex arithmetic and branch conventions, particularly for noninteger powers and the negative real axis. It would be a new mode rather than a literal copy of this azimuth behavior. Such patterns can drive masks, color, or relief without replacing RFF's high-precision fractal data. The existing AbsX/AbsY option similarly inspires folded planar patterns, but a preset named BuringShip does not alone prove equivalence to every Burning Ship convention.

The Default uses m1=(1e-9,0,0), while another non-Julia preset uses a negative-real seed. These are semantically significant initial states, not interchangeable numerical cleanup values. P2Q8lambdajulia and Teddy store Scale=1.0000001; rounding that to one would change their polynomial combination. Preserve serialized precision and explain any intentional normalization. time and pengDiv are unused by the active body, so their presence does not demonstrate animation or a division-based fractal.

A future prototype should compare the actual material/geometry path at matched settings and isolate derivative-bias effects from orbit changes.

## Concrete shader mechanisms: normalized terrain noise, directional warp, and eased terraces (2026-10-08)

Full read: `public/formulas/frag/3DickUlus/AndyPolygon-Landscape.frag` (762 lines), including Default, OldWest, nice, test5, Trees, and Lagoon. The file credits AndyPolygon and 3DickUlus, embeds an Ashima/Ian McEwan simplex implementation with an MIT-license notice, and references a separate source for sdBox. The local noise notice does not establish licensing for the surrounding terrain adaptation. No compilation, rendered terrain, or performance benchmark was produced.

The 2D simplex noise uses skewed triangular cells, permutation modulo 289, three gradient contributions, and compact-support fourth-power weights. Its distinctive normalization constants and gradient construction have explicit local attribution; they should not be treated as unattributed generic arithmetic if copied. RFF already has procedural noise infrastructure, so this file's existence is not a reason to replace it. Evaluate the terrain transforms as new modes using an appropriately licensed noise implementation while preserving existing recipe outputs.

The fbm loop starts amplitude at 0.5, doubles frequency and adds (100,100) each octave, multiplies amplitude by roughness, and divides the sum by total amplitude. Type zero uses signed noise then remaps the average; the other types start at half input frequency and transform each octave separately to abs(n), 1-abs(n), or (1-abs(n))^2. These are different spectral constructions, not a final contrast adjustment on one shared height map. Type three is a squared ridge response despite the menu's exponential wording. octaves is a float converted to int, so fractional values truncate rather than smoothly blend the last octave.

An optional fractional final octave would be a new interpolation behavior, useful for avoiding detail pops during animation, not a source-compatible interpretation. Footprint-aware octave attenuation is also separate from amplitude normalization: dividing by total amplitude does not prevent high-frequency aliasing. Preserve fixed octave order and seeds for saved recipe stability.

The distortion adds the same scalar fbm(pos)*distort to both coordinate components. Its displacement always points along (1,1), with signed strength; it is not independent two-channel vector noise. RFF could offer this as a directional warp and separately derive a two-channel warp if less directional bias is desired. With distortion enabled there are two fbm evaluations, potentially doubling local noise work before any normal/AO sampling by the renderer. Account for the warp derivative when deriving gradients or selecting octave footprints; no speed or visual-quality advantage was measured here.

Terracing computes a height interval H/(steps+1), splits height into integer interval and fraction f, then applies a quadratic ease-in/ease-out InOut(f) inside the interval. It is continuous, maps endpoints to endpoints, has zero slope at the endpoints and matching slope two at the midpoint. It does not quantize to flat constant steps. The derivative flattening creates terrace-like shoulders while retaining continuous height variation. steps is also a float, and Lagoon deliberately stores 0.95. This could transfer to RFF as a continuous band/relief remapping, distinct from palette quantization or hard contour lines.

The final scalar map is unusual and should not be imported as an assumed height-field distance. Let H=volume_size.z*hscale and h=H times the remapped noise height. The code sets q=(v.z/H)/h, then returns q*q-q. For finite nonzero H and h the zero surfaces are v.z=0 and v.z=H*h; before terracing the upper height therefore scales as H^2 times normalized noise. The returned quantity is dimensionless and is not z-height divided by a justified slope bound. Zero h is singular. For a new RFF relief material, use the well-defined height signal directly, and derive normals or a geometry bound separately. Silently correcting the scalar while claiming to reproduce the source would be misleading.

volume_size controls height and horizontal scale but does not bound the active terrain: the sdBox clipping call is commented out. Likewise the DE body writes no orbitTrap, even though presets carry orbit color fields. Object and background colors are supplied through object_and_background_gradient, not implemented by the local fbm. These boundaries prevent attributing the full saved appearance to the noise function alone. time is not referenced by the local terrain body; possible wind/cloud animation belongs to included renderer code.

The presets mix terrain parameters with gradient settings, floor, fog, clouds, lighting, and older renderer fields. Default requests 10000 ray steps; other examples use small FudgeFactor values and varying step limits. Those are saved settings, not evidence of acceptable RFF performance or estimator safety. Some presets store fields absent from the local terrain declarations, such as random, waterz, or ColorIterations; import support must be checked against the complete active schema, not inferred from their names.

**Adoption value:** ridge/valley noise modes, directional domain warp, and eased terraces are concrete RFF material/2D-relief candidates. Keep them in local coordinates and preserve the core fractal's precision. Validate octave truncation and filtering, warp direction, terrace boundaries, zero heights, height units, and preview/export consistency. Separate geometry and background effects during visual comparisons. ## Concrete shader mechanisms: product-form Magnet variants and typed orbit statistics (2026-10-08)

Full read: `public/formulas/frag/3DickUlus/Magnetic-Curiosity.frag` (775 lines), including Default and seven Curiosity presets. The header records derivation from TriplexMagnetbulb, a triplex reference, and replacement of division with multiplication. No linked external theory, rendering, compilation, or benchmark was verified in this pass. The active source must be distinguished from the rational Magnet formulas retained in its comments.

Type I computes a=triMul(z,z)+c-m1 and b=triMul((2,0,0),z)+c-m2, then triPow(Power,triMul(a,b)). It multiplies the two terms; triDiv is unused. Type II also multiplies its two composite terms before applying the power. In its second term, triPow(2,triMul((3,0,0),z)) squares the scaled input, rather than multiplying a squared input by three. On an ordinary nonsingular complex plane this corresponds to (3z)^2, not 3z^2. A RFF formula catalog should give these product-form variants distinct identities rather than label them as exact implementations of the commented rational forms.

triMul computes a coordinate product using both inputs' xy radii and a factor 1-z1.z*lc.z/(r1*r2). It is singular when either xy radius is zero, even if the full 3D vector is nonzero. triPow instead uses spherical angles and adds 1e-10 to the radius before exponentiation. That changes the radial map everywhere and does not repair the independent triMul singularity. Its atan arguments can still both be zero. A new RFF procedural family needs explicit axis/origin behavior and derived formulas, not copied numerical offsets presented as precision improvements.

Non-Julia mode starts from vec3(1e-14) and uses input position as c. Julia mode starts from the position and uses JuliaC. The initial r is dot(z,z), but subsequent loop updates replace r with length(z). Thus the first bailout compares squared radius and later ones compare radius; a zero-iteration return also uses the squared initial value. This difference is significant for source compatibility and estimator interpretation. A new mode should have explicit, consistent bailout units, with any correction versioned rather than silently changing saved scenes.

After the complete product-power map, the scalar derivative heuristic uses the new radius in max(dr*DerivativeBias,pow(r,Power-1)*dr*Power+1). It contains neither the full product derivatives nor the separate c-dependent terms of the two variants. The final log-radius expression therefore cannot be treated as a proven distance bound simply because it resembles a familiar escape estimator. The fourth trap channel is abs(r*dr), so adjusting DerivativeBias also changes the color feature while leaving orbit coordinates unchanged. Trap xyz is sampled before the per-iteration rotation. time is declared but unused in the local body.

**RFF transfer:** use typed orbit statistics and separate artistic derivative-like modulation from geometry derivative/safety controls. Feature channels should specify whether they contain radius, squared radius, a derivative product, a minimum over a window, or a final state. This makes future roughness, emission, and palette masks more predictable in both 3D and 2D. These sources do not justify changing RFF's precise Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA computation.

A planar adaptation can use independently implemented complex arithmetic for a clearly named product polynomial, with fixed initial-state and parameter conventions. With z components zero and nonzero xy magnitudes, triMul reduces to the usual complex multiplication in xy; at zero inputs the source expression still encounters 0/0, so literal slicing is not a robust complex implementation. The radius bias also prevents triPow from being an exact complex power. Preserve the distinction between an intended 2D mathematical mode and an appearance-compatible port of these GLSL operations.

The eight presets explore mostly Type I Julia scenes, with Curiosity-02 enabling Type II. All use Power=2, so they do not establish behavior throughout the 0-to-16 exponent range. Several use near-zero constant components, negative or near-right-angle rotations, and AbsX/AbsY. Those small serialized values should not be rounded away as cosmetic. Curiosity-11 stores FudgeFactor=0.002 and 10000 ray steps; other scenes also request thousands of steps. These settings are not a benchmark, proof of convergence, or evidence of an efficient RFF geometry path.

**Adoption value:** preserve precise formula identities and decouple color features from geometry heuristics before considering a new product-fractal material. Validate axis/zero inputs, first versus later bailout behavior, constant/Julia dependencies, pre/post-rotation sample stages, and parameter precision. Prototype masks in local coordinates with matching preview/export semantics and measured quality/cost. Resolve provenance of the triplex implementation, adaptation, and credited derivative tweak before copying distinctive code or constants and updating RFF NOTICE. The current audit modifies documentation only.

## Concrete shader mechanisms: scheduled norm features and an open color window (2026-10-08)

Full read: `public/formulas/frag/Benesi/pinewithoptionsDE.frag` (650 lines), including all five presets. Fast-Raytracer is the active include; preset names referring to other renderers do not switch that include. No compilation, image comparison, or timing was performed. Transform1 changes to an orthonormal basis, applies componentwise abs and T1Scale, optionally rotates from Rot1Iteration onward, changes back, and subtracts T1offset along x. The optional transforms use the same basis sandwich but different three-channel features: T2 uses pairwise Euclidean radii, T3 sums pairwise absolute coordinates, T4 uses pairwise squared radii, and T5b uses (a^8+b^8)^(1/4). T5b is degree two, the square of an L8 norm, not an L8 norm itself. Its offset therefore has different dimensional meaning from T2's radius offset. RFF should label feature units and keep mode-specific settings rather than interchange their offsets under one generic radius control.

These operations can generate related rounded, diamond-like, quadratic, and superellipse-like material motifs. All output components are computed from the same preassignment vector in each transform. T2's vector coupling can amplify Euclidean differentials beyond its scalar scale, as discussed in the earlier Web Menger review. T3 does not update dr at all, while T4/T5b multiply it only by their uniform scales despite their degree-two coordinate maps. T1Scale and the other scales can also be negative. Thus the shared scalar is not a demonstrated Jacobian bound for every enabled sequence.

The loop starts i=1 and continues only while i<Iterations, so its maximum update count is Iterations-1. At each step T2, T3, T4, and T5b run in that fixed order if their scheduled indices coincide, followed by T1, optional unSpheric, PinePart, and optional Spheric. Rotation inside T1 is a threshold behavior, not a one-time event. An RFF transform schedule should explicitly preserve one-shot versus from-this-step-on behavior and multiple operations at the same index. SphereIteration=0 is unreachable under this loop.

Color sampling has both bounds strict: i>ColorIterationsMin and i<ColorIterations. The default and test1 presets use bounds one and two, producing no color samples at all. The trap is explicitly reset to vec4(10) on every DE call, so the result in this case is a known constant rather than an accumulated history. Knighty2DE's bounds zero/four sample i=1,2,3 when reached; FastandFunny's one/three samples only i=2. This is a strong reason for RFF to specify an inclusive/exclusive window contract and display the effective sample range instead of relying on ambiguous min/max labels.

Samples are taken before adding JuliaC or PixelMult*pos, and contain squared xyz and total squared radius, not abs(xyz). Even when samples exist, the initial value ten caps every channel's minimum at ten. RFF could expose a bounded orbit-feature mode with explicit units and sentinel behavior, or derive a separate uncapped mode, but those are different appearances. A source-compatible importer should not silently replace this with the more common post-addition absolute-coordinate trap.

PinePart uses a special expression at exactly manPower=2, including division by sqrt(y*y+z*z), and a general angular expression elsewhere. Negative manPower uses abs(manPower) for radial magnitude and the signed value for angles; it is not a reciprocal-radius negative power. The two branches have separate numerical behavior on axes. After adding the constant, dr is updated as 2*r*dr+1 using the new radius regardless of manPower, Julia, or PixelMult. This does not account for arbitrary exponent, anisotropic parameter addition, or the nonlinear scheduled transforms. Do not reuse it as RFF's precision-sensitive derivative computation.

Several saved operations are unreachable: for example the default's Iterations=5 permits i=1..4, so T4 at six and T5b at eight cannot run. Some presets omit T2 or SphereIteration values, making baseline defaults relevant. The uniform-dependent rot1 initializer is outside the empty init function; acceptance and update behavior depend on the shader environment and were not compiled here. These facts suggest a resolved operation schedule for reproducible RFF presets, with inactive settings retained but clearly distinguished from executed steps.

**3D/2D transfer:** the pairwise norm features can become local material masks for roughness, color, emission, or relief. For a planar implementation, choose an explicit 2D basis and norm family with its own dimensional offset; arbitrary 3D basis changes and pairwise outputs do not define a closed 2D recurrence by simply setting one coordinate to zero. Keep the new pattern independent of the Mandelbrot/MPA calculation. Independent color windows are useful if their endpoints, stage, units, and empty-window output are explicit.

**Adoption criteria:** validate coincident schedule events, threshold rotations, effective iteration count, empty/single-sample color windows, norm scaling, zero axes, negative scales, parameter derivatives, and preview/export parity. The presets also mix different renderer-era controls, lighting, and floor settings, so their names are not isolated quality or speed evidence. Resolve the original Benesi and helper provenance and licensing before adapting distinctive implementations into RFF and NOTICE. The audit changes documentation only.

**Evidence:** full reading of `public/formulas/frag/Benesi/BenesiFoldedBulb.frag` (829 lines), including all ten presets: Default, Dragon, Bat, Mask, Details, Detail2, Detail3, FireWithin, ChantingShaman, and Crown. The Pine routine saves the incoming point, computes a candidate, and restores the saved point when the candidate's length is greater. A continuous material mask around the decision boundary can be filtered independently of the geometry. This is a proposal, not evidence of an existing RFF implementation or measured visual improvement.

The radius gate is not a clamp to a sphere and is not a smooth interpolation. It selects between two potentially different points; equal radii do not imply equal directions. Consequently, the selection can be discontinuous at a finite, nonsingular equality boundary. A smaller output radius also does not imply a smaller local derivative or a conservative distance estimate. The branch is useful as a pattern idea, but should not be transplanted into RFF's ray-step calculation on that reasoning alone.

Evaluation order is part of the formula. In BenesiFold, the first stage performs an orthonormal basis change followed by absolute values. In the following reconstruction, b.z is overwritten before b.x reads it. The executed reconstruction therefore differs from an inverse basis change using the original folded coordinates. Even with bscale=(1,1,1) and boffset=0, this is not simply an orthogonal fold followed by its inverse. A refactor to matrix notation must preserve that sequential map for compatibility, or explicitly define a different new pattern. The final componentwise scale and offset occur only once before the loop, not at each bulb iteration.

BenesiPine likewise has a dependency: t uses the incoming x and incoming y/z radius, then b.z is replaced before b.y=t*b.y*b.z+sqrt(1/2) is evaluated. Treating all three output components as simultaneous expressions changes the shape. The denominator sqrt(y*y+z*z) is singular on the x axis. The later radius comparison is not a reliable NaN repair: an invalid candidate can survive an ordered greater-than comparison. A new material feature should define its axis behavior directly and propagate a validity flag rather than assume the gate handles it.

The event schedule is `PineIterAt == i` with i starting at zero, after the bulb power but before adding the Julia constant or original position. It executes at most once and may never execute after an early escape. The UI default PineIterAt=10 is unreachable with the declared default Iterations=9; the saved presets override it with values one through four. The saved Iterations values are eight except Detail2's six. All ten presets select the ordinary power-eight, non-Julia branch and zero rotation, so they provide no coverage of alternate-power, Julia, or rotated behavior. Dragon and Bat have identical formula parameters but different cameras: their names do not identify distinct formulas.

The scalar dr starts at one after an already transformed input and is updated only by the chosen bulb-power expression, including a fixed +1. It omits the initial fold's actual derivative, anisotropic bscale, the scheduled Pine transform, and the acceptance branch. For Julia mode the fixed +1 is also not the derivative of a spatially constant JuliaC. These facts limit reuse of the returned 0.5*log(r)*r/dr as a geometrically justified step. The two angular power functions also require deliberate origin and angular-domain handling. Keep RFF's Mandelbrot and MPA precision contracts separate from this artistic recurrence.

Color samples occur after constant addition and the row-vector rotation `z*=rot`. They minimize absolute xyz and squared radius for i<ColorIterations; the loop starts at zero, so the nominal color window is [0,ColorIterations), truncated by escape and Iterations. Radius is measured before rotation, which preserves it for a valid orthogonal matrix. The routine relies on the enclosing renderer to initialize orbitTrap; it does not reset the trap locally. The time uniform and the commented intersection code do not animate or intersect the active geometry.

**3D/2D transfer:** for 3D, retain the acceptance bit, radius margin, and selected iteration as independent procedural material channels. For 2D, construct a deliberate planar candidate transform and the same radius-selection feature, or evaluate a documented slice solely as a texture. The full recurrence does not preserve the z=0 plane: basis folding, offsets, and the Pine constants generate an out-of-plane coordinate. A slice is therefore not a closed 2D fractal recurrence. Apply these ideas to color or relief without changing the high-precision Mandelbrot computation; filter the binary mask using the pixel footprint and keep its stage and units explicit.

**Adoption criteria:** verify sequential versus simultaneous updates, early escape before the event, unreachable event settings, axis validity, equal-radius branch boundaries, trap initialization, and parameter derivatives. Separate material-mask experiments from any claim of safe geometry. Preset ray budgets range from 300 to 2000 and differ in camera, lighting, and fudge factor, so they are not comparative performance evidence. The file credits Benesi, 3Dickulus, and separate power-function sources; those credits alone do not establish adaptation licenses. Resolve the original sources and license scope before copying recognizable code, and update NOTICE if material is adopted.

Non-Julia initialization at c corresponds to a shifted iteration convention relative to starting at zero, affecting bailout and color windows. Generic 3D rotations and nonzero JuliaC.z break the planar restriction.

For a 2D finite-difference diagnostic, two in-plane offsets suffice to estimate the 2x2 Jacobian; retaining the third offset would measure a different, out-of-plane response. This does not justify replacing RFF's Mandelbrot formula or its perturbation machinery. Treat the planar formula as an explicit new mode with its own precision design, or use the folded recurrence as a material pattern. On the RFF side, the current `src/rff2/attr/ShdPalColorInterpolationMethod.h` and the blendPaletteColors implementation in `ShdPaletteAttribute.h` confirm RGB, Oklab, and linear-RGB interpolation already exist. This batch does not newly certify all referenced modules or execute the document's test commands. Historical measurements and mutation-test claims in the document remain source-reported.

**Highest-value transfer from this material:** preserve a sampled gradient when a compact stop approximation cannot reproduce it sufficiently well. GMT's rampToGradientConfig fits with one stop of headroom above a capped budget, then re-renders the candidate and measures missed texels before accepting the stop representation. The inspected code uses a default cap of 48, a minimum effective limit of two, and permits at most four of 256 samples to exceed max(0.05,2.5*targetDE) in its Oklab-distance metric. Otherwise it stores an encoded ramp with an empty stop list. These thresholds are GMT policy, not perceptual constants or recommended RFF defaults.

For RFF, this suggests an explicit fidelity contract for imported or painted palettes: keep authored stops when present; for sampled inputs, compare any fitted representation against the samples, especially narrow bands, sharp transitions, and cyclic seams. Preserve a sampled representation when fitting fails the chosen contract. A count-only rule cannot prove fidelity. A sampled ramp preserves those samples, not an arbitrary continuous original signal or infinitely narrow feature between samples. Texture filtering, resolution, color encoding, and wrap mode remain part of the visible result. Do not silently force RFF's palettes to 256 samples or reinterpret existing recipe IDs and seeds.

The document's uniform reader contract is also transferable: every preview, shader upload, export, and signature calculation must understand both authored-stop and sampled forms if such a representation is introduced. Treating an empty stop array as an empty gradient while ignoring the ramp produces a different image. The inspected helper always returns an sRGB-tagged result on its fallback path, with surrounding code responsible for another intended encoding; RFF should make such conversions explicit at the CPU/GPU boundary. Format changes must follow the existing append-only configuration and palette-recipe stability rules, not introduce a new meaning for an old saved value.

**Avoid a redundant interpolation recommendation:** current RFF already decodes sRGB for linear-RGB interpolation and interpolates rectangular Oklab coordinates in its Oklab branch, with output encoding/clamping and linear alpha interpolation. GMT's historical saved key `oklab` instead denotes polar OkLCh, while `oklab-rect` denotes rectangular Oklab. An importer must map semantics rather than matching strings or integer values. A future polar mode could be independently evaluated for hue-path control and achromatic behavior, but this document is not evidence that replacing RFF's existing Oklab mode would improve it. Preserve its current saved enum values.

The documentation describes reducing chroma for polar out-of-gamut colors rather than clamping RGB channels. That is a candidate to compare on saturated gradients, with explicit target gamut and hue policy, not a universal replacement for all color conversions. It also requires storing the curve space alongside channel tracks: RGB, Oklab, OkLCh, CIE LCh, and HSV use different axes and scales. RFF would need the same unit and space agreement if it later adds editable color-channel curves. A curve's labels alone do not make its saved samples unambiguous.

**Editing and reproducibility concepts:** the documented working pipeline preserves authored stops under identity operations and separates preview from committed edits. Its paint model distinguishes per-stroke opacity ceiling from deposition rate, and Apply can commit a stroke or adjustment as one undoable action. Variants restore only their relevant authored state rather than reloading a whole scene. These are useful product behaviors to compare against RFF's current palette tools, not confirmed gaps in this batch. In particular, preview must not unexpectedly modify a frozen generated recipe or scene settings. Export should use an explicitly selected committed or preview state rather than accidentally differ from what the user sees.

**Provenance and import/export:** the document treats catalog publication, source identity, and export credit as data carried through the pipeline. RFF should retain provenance even after a palette edit; loss of an unchanged-content signature does not erase attribution or license obligations. GMT's policy of changing an export filename after modification is not itself a licensing rule. Do not copy catalog assets based on this rule file's labels. Independently verify source permissions and record adopted algorithms/material in NOTICE. Its PNG gradient payload and stripped-image recovery are design references only: exact metadata roundtrip and color recovery from pixels are different fidelity classes, and file-format compatibility grants no right to copy an implementation.

**3D/2D transfer and validation:** narrow-band fidelity, cyclic boundaries, and preview/upload parity benefit both 2D fractal coloring and 3D surface palettes. For material roughness or emission ramps, use their intended scalar or linear-radiometric units rather than automatically applying a display-color metric. Validate CPU preview, Vulkan sampling, save/load, and export on the same fixtures, including shifted sharp bands and out-of-gamut transitions. The document explicitly notes that core tests cannot establish component rendering correctness; its listed passing histories were not reproduced here. The batch changes documentation only and does not claim measured visual or performance improvement.

### Format and composition documentation: semantic imports and one parameter-layout contract (2026-10-08)

**RFF composition improvement:** if procedural material or formula graphs are introduced, derive shader parameter references and CPU packing from the same resolved layout. The inspected GMT packer clears the array, skips unreachable and disabled nodes, reserves active condition modulus/remainder slots before ordinary inputs, and omits slots for inputs bound to named uniforms. Any divergence in these choices shifts subsequent parameters. RFF's Vulkan descriptor/push-constant rules already require exact agreement; the analogous graph layer should emit a layout description once and use it for both generated GLSL and C++ upload. Include node identity, binding type, component count, and order in the structural cache key, while allowing value-only changes to avoid recompilation when appropriate.

The inspected setP drops writes beyond MAX_MODULAR_PARAMS; nearby source documents corresponding compiler literal fallbacks, and the compiler search shows separate condition defaults. For RFF, compute required capacity before compilation and report an unsupported graph instead of silently changing its arithmetic. Removing dead nodes is useful only when distance, color, traps, and derivative outputs are represented in the liveness model. A material-only contributor must not disappear merely because it does not determine geometry. Disabled nodes also need explicit bypass/identity semantics, rather than an accidental empty shader body.

The graph document warns that a generic formula smoke or a similarly named hybrid sweep may not compile the modular path at all. Its stated modular parity test checks slot allocation and structure, not emitted GLSL execution. The RFF acceptance plan should therefore distinguish layout checks, generated-shader compilation, and rendered output for actual supported graph combinations. Known inputs must reach the intended formula, with a distinguishable output; a default scene that happens to share the same formula name is weak evidence of successful loading. Historical test names and counts are not substitutes for inspecting the current test's scope.

**RFF import/save improvement:** treat scene identity, formula identity, and parameter semantics as versioned contracts. The format document links local saves and shared scenes to the same serialization path and emphasizes append-only migration history. For RFF, use its actual existing ordered binary ConfigIO and recipe rules rather than transplant GMT's migration structure: preserve older files with explicitly defined defaults, append additive settings in the required order, and never renumber recipe IDs or reinterpret old enum values. Test a distinctive old fixture through load, render-state construction, and save/load again. **Concrete dimensional distinction:** the inspected MB3D transpiler checks deOption 5/6 together with an mb3dDr1 scratch derivative to decide whether w is a fourth spatial coordinate. In that case it initializes w from z.w, writes the updated coordinate back, and routes the separate derivative into dr. Otherwise w is initialized from dr and returned as the derivative. This illustrates why a vec4 is not a sufficient semantic type for importing a formula. RFF should keep position dimension, derivative state, and orbit-feature channels distinct; treating a fourth coordinate as a scale accumulator changes both shape and distance. The original Pascal implementation cited in the comment was not inspected in this batch, so the excerpt verifies GMT's routing, not full MB3D equivalence.

The MB3D document also identifies formula constants overriding decoded sign masks, a lighting/fog conversion, and an external canonical decompiler location outside this checkout. Those are boundaries to verify if such an importer is ever selected, not a reason to copy binaries, decompiled bodies, or assume fog equivalence. Imported distance, fog, camera, and material settings should carry conversion status: exact semantic mapping, supported approximation, or unsupported. Public format names and a local decompiler do not establish permission to reuse source-derived implementations.

The scene-format document separates diagnostic scans from regression gates and reports former false-green and permanently-red suites. A full corpus scan remains useful for discovering unsupported families, but expected rejection, parser failure, shader compile failure, and rendering mismatch should be separate outcomes. Keep a supported fixture matrix with nonempty coverage and reliable failing exit status. Do not refresh a compatibility baseline merely to remove a failure without reviewing what semantic capability changed. This is an RFF validation proposal; the historical GMT counts in these documents are not current audit measurements.

**3D/2D transfer:** one parameter-layout and save-format contract benefits both 3D material graphs and 2D palette/relief graphs. Dimensional reduction must explicitly retain or eliminate coordinates and replace the derivative calculation accordingly; it cannot reuse a fourth-channel convention by position alone. A 2D shader rejected by GMT's 3D DE importer may still be useful to RFF's 2D material path, so importer rejection is not evidence that a technique is worthless. Preserve distinct import targets rather than force every source into float DE(vec3). No importer, shader, test baseline, or saved format was modified; only this report and its reading ledger were updated.

### Modulation documentation: shared evaluation, explicit clocks, and convergence after motion (2026-10-08)

**Evidence:** complete readings of `.claude/rules/audio-mod.md` (51 lines), `modulation.md` (37), and `interaction-session.md` (92). The documents' historic test results were not reproduced, and audio/render timing was not measured. This batch marks the three documentation entries complete; previously audited code is supporting evidence rather than additional newly counted coverage.

**RFF feature opportunity:** deterministic parameter modulation can animate palette phase, material roughness, emission, or existing relief controls in both 3D and 2D. Audio-reactive rendering is an optional extension, not a prerequisite for the shader quality improvements elsewhere in this report. If introduced, the main architectural benefit is one parameter evaluator for interactive preview, recording, and offline export, with separate delivery mechanisms. The inspected GMT dispatcher creates planned uniform writes, engine-side offsets, displayed values, and recording entries rather than independently recomputing each path's semantics.

The dispatcher aggregates vector axes before flushing a single composite uniform. This avoids an X update followed by a Y update resetting X to the base vector. It also uses missing-value checks, not truthiness, for Julia components, so an intentionally modulated zero remains zero. RFF's analogous acceptance fixtures should include two simultaneous axes, a zero crossing, target removal restoring base, and a changed target binding. Scalar, vector, rotation, palette phase, and camera parameters must retain their own composition rules; an offset consumed later by a matrix builder is not the same as an already composed uniform value.

GMT composes many targets in their slider's mapping space, making a fixed modulation gain represent comparable control travel. This could give RFF predictable control sensitivity, but it is a chosen artistic policy rather than a physically uniform change. Positive logarithmic parameters, bounded roughness, cyclic phase, signed displacement, and rotations require distinct mappings and explicit boundary behavior. The inspected dispatcher even treats coloring repeats through a derived scale ratio and phase through a separate offset field, demonstrating why matching parameter names is insufficient. Preserve authored bases and compute transient values from them rather than feeding the previous modulated value back unintentionally.

Recording needs separate scrutiny: generic branches can ask for a clean pre-recording base to avoid compounding. However, the inspected Julia branch deliberately uses the store's natural base, and the vector branch uses the natural base for emitted values while recording can use the clean base. A shared dispatcher reduces duplication but does not by itself prove recording, live display, and export are identical in every branch. For RFF, test those contracts explicitly, particularly simultaneous vector modulation while recording, rather than infer parity from code reuse alone.

**Audio timing:** the audio document describes analysis on an AudioWorklet at a 256-sample hop, approximately 187.5 analyses per second at 48 kHz, with band results batched near 60 Hz. This is documented architecture, not a measured rate in this audit. It warns against treating audio-analysis blocks as render frames. For an RFF implementation, express smoothing/attack/release in time or sample units and evaluate source values at the export frame's exact timestamp. Precompute or reproducibly resample a recorded audio envelope for offline export; a live microphone cannot be replayed deterministically unless its signal or analysis data is captured. Do not copy WebAudio-specific mechanics into a native Vulkan application when its own audio architecture differs.

The same document distinguishes persistent audio equipment state from scene-owned modulation rules: a scene swap may retain the input connection while replacing its routing. This is useful as an explicit product contract. Analysis failure should be visible rather than silently substituting a different algorithm or freezing apparently valid values. The document rejects duplicated main-thread DSP and per-band adaptive gain in its chosen design; these are GMT decisions to evaluate, not universal requirements for RFF.

**Convergence after motion:** the interaction document separates active gestures from autonomous animation, render dirtiness, and camera blocking. Current renderInteractionState preserves three fields: gesture activity, playback-or-active-modulation, and a filtered hold state. Its source predicate requires both the LFO master enable and an enabled oscillator, or audio enabled plus an enabled audio rule. This checks enabled sources, not a proof that their output changes a valid rendered target on every frame. A stronger RFF dirty-state policy can compare effective state where appropriate, while retaining deterministic evaluation and avoiding false static classification during active animation.

For 3D accumulation or 2D progressive refinement, clearing a gesture flag must not incorrectly declare an animated scene static; disabled modulation entries must not permanently hold the renderer in preview quality. Equally, a color edit should not freeze a stale accumulation buffer simply because it is a gesture. Keep the decisions separate: what changed, which history is invalid, whether the user is interacting, and whether further frames are needed. The document's edge-triggered notifications can reduce redundant application updates, but its module-level singleton and React-specific details are not a prescription for RFF's native architecture.

**3D/2D transfer and acceptance:** palette phase and emission modulation can be inexpensive material-only changes when the renderer retains sufficient geometry/iteration data; geometry or high-precision location changes require their existing recomputation paths. Do not lower precision to make audio-reactive deep zooms faster. Compare preview/export at the same timestamps and source samples across different frame rates, verify base restoration after stopping, and verify full-quality convergence on a truly static scene. Historical static scans and pure state-machine tests do not establish the final rendered behavior; representative end-to-end frames remain necessary. No RFF modulation feature was implemented or asserted missing in this batch; this section records candidate behavior and validation conditions only.

### Timeline benchmark: measuring whether shader improvements reach the user (2026-10-08)

**Evidence:** read all 1,034 lines of debug/bench-perf-timeline.mts, including page instrumentation, synthetic/recorded seeds, ten scenarios, aggregation, output, and baseline gating. The benchmark was not executed; no timings or speedup claims follow from this reading.

**Transferable RFF design:** measure interaction responsiveness separately from rendering throughput and GPU pass cost. GMT observes main-thread animation-frame intervals, worker messages, accumulation count, store notifications, React commit costs, long tasks, heap changes, and renderer counters. It runs idle, scrub, playback, zoom, and track-selection workloads in both dope-sheet and curve views, with three repetitions. Scrubbing calls both seek and the animation engine's scrub method, which is a useful distinction: moving a playhead without evaluating its bound parameters would underrepresent real render work. RFF comparisons should likewise exercise actual palette/material upload or location recomputation, not merely control repaint.

The deterministic heavy fixture generates 1,500 keys on each of six camera component tracks (9,000 keys). This is useful for stressing animation editing, but arbitrary sinusoidal quaternion components without a qw track are not proof of a physically representative camera path. The recorded fixture is a different workload. For RFF, retain both a deterministic stress fixture and representative user animations, identify the fixture and its contents in results, and separate color-only animation from precision-sensitive zoom/geometry work. Do not assume the same frame cost for either.

**Metric interpretation matters before ranking shader changes:**

- Main FPS percentiles come from requestAnimationFrame intervals, not GPU timestamps. workerFps uses FRAME_READY counts when nonzero, but falls back to *all* incoming worker messages when no frame notification was observed. Therefore a nonzero value need not demonstrate a rendered frame. RFF should record actual completed/rendered frames separately from control/progress traffic and treat unavailable counters as unavailable.
- Estimated workerPostBytes samples every sixteenth outgoing message, takes JSON string length, and extrapolates. That is a sampled character-count proxy, not structured-clone/transfer byte volume; periodic message patterns can bias it. Use it to investigate notification pressure, not as measured transport bandwidth.
- Accumulation delta is an endpoint difference and can reset during scene changes. It is not the total samples computed during a scrub. For progressive 3D accumulation or 2D refinement, record completed work and invalidations separately, together with output quality.
- Renderer readbacks can fail and return null; the difference helper substitutes zeros. The resulting counters cannot distinguish genuinely zero work from missing instrumentation, and their before/after requests surround a slightly different interval from the page capture. Keep validity and measurement boundaries explicit in an RFF harness.
- Profiler medians use only the first 1,000 commit durations per bucket, while counts and totals continue. Summary fields are independent medians across successful runs, not one representative run or a pooled distribution. Preserve raw observations and valid-run counts; do not infer a causal cost breakdown by combining unrelated medians.

**Reproducibility and acceptance:** mode changes occur before capture and wait eight frames, despite a comment claiming their cost is implicitly measured. Run a separate transition scenario if opening a shader/material editor is the target. The zoom workload uses a fixed screen coordinate without asserting that timeline zoom changed; scrub tolerates an absent engine hook; empty track selection becomes idle; fit-to-view can be skipped with a warning. For RFF, assert the intended operation actually changed its target and produced the expected rendered output before accepting performance results. Such assertions prevent an accidentally inactive effect from appearing to be a major optimization.

Individual failed runs are skipped, page errors are recorded rather than automatically fatal, and an entirely empty run set reduces many summary values to zero. The optional gate only acts on selected relative regressions with an available baseline; missing or unreadable baselines skip comparison. Its zero-baseline rule substitutes a 100 percent change rather than expressing an undefined relative ratio. Consequently successful process completion alone is not proof of a complete, comparable benchmark. An RFF comparison should require the expected valid samples, workload identity, renderer/device/build metadata, compatible settings, and explicit handling of absolute changes from zero. The heavy run also serializes the constant 600-frame seed duration in config despite applying 1,500 frames, so metadata needs verification against the actual fixture rather than trust in its label.

**Application to shader priorities and 3D/2D transfer:** compare candidate effects at fixed precision, resolution, scene, and intended quality; report GPU pass time, interaction latency, export throughput, and visual improvement as different outcomes. A slower frame may be acceptable for higher-quality offline output, while an inexpensive palette or normal change may have greater interactive value. Use fixed-time animation samples for comparisons: this harness's frame-count workloads can span different elapsed times at different frame rates. Add separate export measurements because this timeline harness does not measure export throughput. These principles apply to 3D lighting/materials and 2D palette/relief animation alike. They improve the evidence behind an RFF priority ranking without claiming any measured ranking or importing GMT-specific instrumentation unchanged.
