The archived description says an exception aborts the rest of the frame. Also, suppression itself is not restricted to development; only its warning is conditional. Do not carry the old failure behavior into RFF recommendations as a current GMT defect.

For RFF, decide failure handling by dependency. A failed optional overlay should not freeze rendering, but a failed required parameter/snapshot update must not silently export a frame assembled from inconsistent state. Return structured status and retain a last-known-valid state or stop the affected job where necessary. Continuing every callback is not automatically transactional correctness. A live mutable handler array also needs an explicit policy for registering/unregistering during dispatch, so disposal cannot accidentally skip the next callback; a per-frame snapshot or deferred mutation can provide that contract.

Duplicate-name registration currently keeps the first handler and returns a no-op disposer. This prevents accumulation but is not equivalent to replacing a stale callback or managing multiple owners. An RFF registry should define ownership, replacement and disposal, and be scoped per renderer/job if simultaneous previews or exports are supported. The archived suggestion to fork a worker does not alone establish isolation of all main-thread state. These are rendering-lifecycle and animation-reliability lessons, with no new visual shader effect or measured speedup. No runtime test was executed in this batch.

### Archived audit reviews 1–3: retain evidence boundaries and adjacent-file coverage

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/state/reviews/review-2026-05-19-1.md` (61 lines), `review-2026-05-19-2.md` (47 lines), and `review-2026-05-19-3.md` (84 lines). These review the mechanics of an earlier documentation audit. Their clean-iteration counts, citation spot-checks and proposed protocol edits do not prove full source coverage, runtime correctness or resolution of the underlying code findings. A discrepancy between a comment and implementation also does not alone identify which side is wrong without the intended contract.

For this RFF-focused review, the useful distinction is between historical architecture aspirations, current implementation behavior and proposed adoption. The reviews themselves identify adaptive-resolution APIs described in old docs but absent from the surveyed code, and feature/plugin contracts that had diverged. Those references are leads to compare with source, not functionality that RFF can obtain by following the old API examples. Likewise, differing plugin state-capture patterns may be intentional; unifying them needs a concrete lifecycle benefit, not uniformity for its own sake.

The adjacent-file nomination pattern is valuable when documenting RFF's shader pipeline: a shader's C++ configurator, parameter registry, serialization and UI trigger may live outside its nominal subsystem. Record those relationships explicitly. However, nominations cannot guarantee a complete worklist; independently reconcile the actual file inventory, including generated/resource paths, against reviewed coverage. A valid hash identifies content, not proof it was read. Multi-path hash tooling should fail clearly on missing inputs and preserve exact path identity; partial output before a later error must not be mistaken for a successful whole batch.

The review's draft changes and agent/workflow instructions were not applied or executed. No new shader algorithm or direct 3D-to-2D feature is established by these process documents. They reinforce the evidence discipline used by the report and independent coverage ledger, while preserving RFF improvement as the objective rather than adopting GMT's historical audit process as a new task.

### Archived mobile-layout contract: separate layout preference from render quality

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/mobile-layout.md` (84 lines), with a current-source recheck of `hooks/useMobileLayout.ts`. The archived claim that the hook duplicates HardwareDetection's breakpoint is outdated: the current hook imports isMobileViewport, although its header still identifies a separate boot initializer copy. A shared predicate improves consistency only when initial state and subsequent updates use the same contract.

For RFF's resizable desktop workspace, the transferable idea is to separate preferred control layout, actual available viewport, input capabilities and rendering-quality policy. GMT's raw 'device mobile' flag is itself a coarse-pointer OR narrow-width heuristic, so it does not prove a real touch device despite the document's wording. Narrow desktop windows and hybrid input hardware illustrate why a layout classification should not automatically lower numerical precision or final export quality. Interactive preview resolution can follow an explicit performance policy; deep-zoom calculation accuracy and output dimensions remain separate.

The hook suppresses state writes when its boolean classifications do not change. That is useful for avoiding redundant UI updates, but renderer viewport sizing still needs actual dimensions: a resize within the same classification can require new render targets and coordinate transforms. A non-reactive snapshot accessor also only stays visually current when the host has an independent update trigger. Document that dependency rather than treating a getter as a subscription.

Browser address-bar collapse, dynamic viewport units and safe-area padding are browser-specific mechanisms, not direct Win32 improvements. Their claimed keyboard/address-bar behavior was not verified here. For RFF, use actual client-area and DPI changes, preserve reachable controls in small windows and keep coordinate conversion consistent with the rendered image. The current hook retains a lifetime resize listener; its inequality guard suppresses duplicate writes, not the number of listeners created by repeated module evaluation. An RFF multi-window or reloadable subsystem should own and release its listeners explicitly. This batch adds lifecycle/layout guidance only, with no shader algorithm or measured rendering improvement.

### Historical shader audit claims versus current schema enforcement

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/state/reviews/review-2026-05-20-10.md` (53 lines) and `review-2026-05-20-11.md` (102 lines). Re-read both current implementations, `engine/UniformSchema.ts` and `engine-gmt/engine/UniformSchema.ts`, to resolve the historical uniform-collision claim rather than carrying it forward as a current defect.

Review 11 describes silent base-versus-feature filtering and feature-versus-feature last-wins defaults. Both current schemas instead check these two collision classes and throw before constructing UNIFORM_DEFAULTS. Thus the transferable RFF recommendation is early validation of composed shader interfaces, not a proposal to repair that historical GMT behavior. Prefix conventions alone are insufficient. For Vulkan, validation must cover descriptor set/binding identity, resource type/count, push-constant offsets and ranges, and host/shader layout compatibility; JavaScript uniform-name uniqueness does not establish those properties. Apply this to optional 2D coloring and post-processing passes as well as any future 3D renderer. This is reliability work, not an asserted frame-rate improvement.

Both schemas also separate CPU-derived values from their feature-owned source parameters. Rotation matrices, pixel-size values and color conversions can be prepared once per relevant parameter change instead of repeated for every fragment. The GMT-specific schema extends this with six mat3 rotation entries, six sin/cos pairs and two mat4 entries. RFF can use the same dependency principle for image-space transforms and lighting parameters, but these particular capacities and 3D formula bindings should not be copied blindly. An animated parameter or output-resolution change must invalidate the appropriate derived value, and moving calculations must not reduce deep-zoom numerical precision. The schema documents the intention; this recheck does not measure savings or prove every update path.

The backingOnly flag distinguishes a host-side value from an automatically emitted GLSL declaration. The schema comments locate enforcement in the uniform chunks, while createUniforms constructs backing objects regardless. For RFF, distinguish the availability of a host parameter from actual bindings required by a compiled variant; do not interpret a feature toggle as proof that its interface or code is absent. Explicit variant/interface validation is useful for both 2D and 3D adoption.

Other historical claims remain historical evidence: review 10's production preset-registration failure is not established as a current failure by these documents, and review 11's BloomPass and shader-assembly descriptions are source pointers rather than new runtime verification. The latter review corrects earlier adaptive-quality field names and an omitted minQuality field, illustrating why even an audit summary needs checking against implementation before defining RFF settings.

These process documents add no measured shader quality gain. Their PASS labels, speculative future bug rate, projected review-time savings and answered-question percentages are not full-file coverage or experimental evidence. Review 10's heading mentions an overshoot despite its listed maximum of five under an eight-file budget; review 11's proposed frontmatter warning claims resumption incompatibility while its risk paragraph says variants are tolerated. Neither should become an implementation requirement without checking the consumer. Cross-references can guide investigation but do not replace the full reads requested for this audit. Historical workflow edits and delegation instructions were not executed.

### Gradient artboard generator: design intent is not a color-processing implementation

Fully reviewed: `plans/ge-v2-canvas/gen.py` (232 lines), `_shared.css` (26 lines), and `TrayMix.dc.html` (53 lines). These are static design artifacts, not the production palette evaluator or shader. The generator writes six artboards and canvas.json at module execution; it was read, not executed, so the external source tree was not regenerated. Its generated outputs remain independent audit entries: reading the generator does not count as reading every output.

The Mix artboard presents independent lightness, chroma and hue mixing amounts, with Link and Swap actions, while other generated faces describe curve fitting, source-image extraction and palette adjustments. This supports a useful RFF feature direction: preserve the current fractal calculation while auditioning palette transformations, with an explicit source palette and a reversible commit. It applies directly to 2D iteration coloring; a 3D implementation can reuse the palette operation while keeping lighting and material interpretation separate. These artifacts do not establish that these controls work or specify their mathematical semantics.

In particular, the hard-coded labels 'blend Oklab' and 'output Linear' are not evidence of implemented color conversion. Their ramps are ordinary CSS gradient strings with no explicit Oklab interpolation, and the slider graphics are divs whose percentages are formatted to whole numbers. RFF already has OKLab interpolation; this is not a proposal to add it again. An independent lightness/chroma/hue mixer needs a defined cylindrical-space conversion, hue wrapping and achromatic-hue policy, plus gamut handling and preview/export agreement. Reuse a tested palette evaluator or sampled ramp for the visible preview instead of inferring color fidelity from a labeled mockup. Display rounding must not quantize the stored control value or shader input.

Similarly, the Curves face contains three fixed SVG paths, the Image face contains a decorative path and a color-cloud placeholder, and the hero's preview/live text is selected from a string argument. These do not implement curve fitting, image analysis or transactional preview state. The canvas annotation describes Escape-to-close and one-open-tray behavior, but the generator supplies no application event handlers for those semantics. Source inspection here is not a rendered UI or accessibility assessment.

For any RFF adoption, retain palette recipe identity and deterministic regeneration, and store additional transformations without silently changing existing recipe behavior. Separate a temporary appearance preview from saved palette state and from expensive fractal recomputation. Export must consume the same committed color transformation as the viewport. The hard-coded artboard dimensions, fixed CSS colors and SVG path data are reference presentation material, not reusable rendering algorithms or measured performance improvements. The script duplicates board dimensions between generated markup, tuples and the canvas manifest, while doc's width/height arguments are unused; therefore the manifest alone cannot establish actual content sizing. No shader-priority ranking changes follow from this batch.

### Working-palette harness: preservation, approximation and history are separate contracts

Fully reviewed: `debug/test-palette-working.mts` (948 lines), including all 16 assertion groups and the historical mutation-test notes. This is a CPU/pure-core and store-integration harness. It supplies a minimal in-memory browser/storage environment, manually registers features and history providers, and invokes store operations directly. It was not executed in this audit batch. Its recorded mutation results and final success message are not current test results, and it does not render shader pixels.

The strongest transferable quality requirement is preserving authored representation when no actual transformation is requested. Identity Adjust returns the original stop config or encoded ramp object; opening an untouched curve fit must not replace authored stops with a lossy refit. The fixture checks stop identifiers, bias, step interpolation and positions because visually similar samples can still destroy editing identity. For RFF, opening a palette editor or viewing a curve approximation should not regenerate a recipe, move stops or rewrite saved data. Preserve existing preset IDs, seeds and generator order. This applies directly to 2D palettes and to 3D color ramps independently of lighting.

An important qualification appears in group 14: the restated output deliberately returns the original config while its ramp remains the curves' drawing. Config preservation therefore does not establish exact preview/export equivalence. A future RFF implementation should explicitly define which representation drives the visible preview, saved palette and final shader texture. If the curve drawing is an approximation, keep it as an editor visualization or an explicitly temporary preview; do not silently export a different appearance. Test actual GPU texture sampling at intermediate coordinates and boundaries, not only CPU texel arrays.

The period-two zebra and phase-shifted eight-wave fixtures are useful adversarial cases for narrow color features. The harness distinguishes a dense automatic ramp result from a cheaply fitted stop result, while authored stop inputs retain stops even when the Detail budget is exhausted. This is an editing-policy decision, not a guarantee that every resulting stop fit meets a maximum perceptual error: the over-budget assertion checks representation and count rather than reconstruction error. For RFF, retain an exact sampled-ramp fallback where permitted, and make an explicit editable-stop conversion reversible. Neither a 256-sample fixture nor its OKLab error threshold establishes preservation of arbitrary higher-frequency palettes, discontinuity placement, wrap filtering or the final tone-mapped image. Do not transfer its numeric thresholds as universal visual acceptance criteria.

The harness also checks that a held drag result updates to the live ramp rather than retaining stale colors, and that unchanged values can reuse the previous object. This suggests separating stable editing topology from current color values in an RFF preview cache. Same-seed repetition is tested for noise, but these checks do not establish seed diversity, cross-version recipe stability or CPU/GPU noise equivalence. The maxDiff helper compares only the shorter array; use equal-length and finite-value checks alongside numerical comparisons in any RFF port so truncated outputs cannot appear identical.

History integration is substantive: one explicit stop conversion creates one undo entry, canceled gestures create none, a deferred Recent write waits outside a parameter transaction, and a bracket reopened before the deferred callback drains keeps that write waiting. A direct-write control proves that the registered history provider can capture the shelf at all. For RFF, automatic recent-palette recording should not accidentally join an unrelated slider undo operation; an explicit Save can have a different transaction boundary. Recheck ownership when deferred work executes, rather than relying solely on the state when it was queued. These direct calls simulate debounce firing, not the real browser timer or component subscription wiring.

The edited/untouched flag is restored with curve data because it changes whether leaving the editor bakes or discards a fit. The tests separately exclude flag-only changes from creating an undo entry. Preserve this distinction in RFF: restoration needs all state that determines subsequent behavior, while change detection should represent a meaningful user edit. Palette replacement and baking also have distinct reset policies here: a fresh pick resets every Adjust control, whereas baking retains inactive noise frequency/target choices. Define these policies explicitly rather than reusing a reset helper indiscriminately.

Recent-palette integration uses the actual shelf store after an initial fake collector, testing pick/edit isolation, save feedback and local-day rollover. The explicit re-pick path promotes an old entry to the current day; the resumed-edit path preserves the previous day's entry and creates a new one. Consequently these tests do not describe universally immutable dated history. RFF should choose and document its own history policy, including rename and undo behavior, rather than importing the collection semantics incidentally. The injected clock provides deterministic boundary tests but does not cover every timezone or persistence-failure case. This batch adds concrete preservation and verification requirements; it does not claim a new shader algorithm or measured speed improvement.

### Audit dashboard generator: completion labels are not verification evidence

Fully reviewed: `plans/overnight-audit/scripts/build-dashboard.mjs` (219 lines). This script reads saved JSON and generates a static dashboard. It was not executed or published. Its comments about orchestration and its suggested review/merge commands are historical workflow material, not actions taken in this audit. Reading this generator does not mark its large generated dashboard or underlying result files as reviewed.

Several distinctions matter when interpreting GMT's historical audit evidence. The header prints Complete whenever state.stopped is truthy, without requiring all worklist entries to be done or all guards to pass. Its progress percentage measures done subsystem rows, not files read, shader variants validated or visual quality. The verifier-confirmed change count accepts either a commit or a change field; it does not inspect commits or independently verify a result. Moreover, the 'Applied — orchestrator-verified' section receives every Tier V finding, whereas the numerical applied count uses only its filtered subset. A finding's position in that section is therefore not sufficient evidence that it was applied. Tier A likewise receives a self-verified label from its category rather than a fresh test run.

Input failures can reduce apparent coverage: the read helper returns a fallback for missing files and invalid JSON alike, malformed result files are dropped, and there is no schema validation. Historical guard entries are accumulated without selecting the latest outcome per guard or source revision; truthiness of pass is used rather than requiring a boolean. This is an aggregate record, not a current regression-test status. Result findings are also not deduplicated against worklist IDs or validated for matching source revisions. The footer's claims that nothing was pushed and main was untouched are fixed text, not repository checks.

The relevant RFF lesson is to keep stopped, canceled, failed and successfully completed states distinct in rendering/export jobs and any future verification report. Report the actual denominator: completed output frames, tiles, shader variants or inspected files, as appropriate. Missing evidence must remain unknown rather than silently becoming zero failures, and a saved historical success should retain its source/build identity. For 2D and 3D shader comparisons, preserve the tested preset, resolution, sample settings, GPU/build and numerical or image result instead of inferring correctness from a green dashboard category. This batch changes no shader recommendation ranking and provides no measured rendering benefit.

Most textual template fields are escaped, but presumed numeric counters and the appended line field are interpolated without type validation or escaping. An RFF HTML-report exporter should validate typed fields and escape all external text consistently; this observation alone does not establish exposure to hostile data in GMT's local workflow. Likewise, no visual behavior of the dashboard was tested. The existing report and independent file ledger, not this historical dashboard's counts, remain the basis for this audit's completion percentage.

### Shared icon source: state indicators do not establish renderer behavior

Fully reviewed: `components/Icons.tsx` (282 lines) and `components/Icons2.tsx` (207 lines). These modules contain SVG geometry and presentation props, not shadow, path-tracing, adaptive-resolution or palette algorithms. No new shader technique or performance improvement follows from their names. Their source was inspected without a rendered interface assessment.

AdaptiveIcon distinguishes pixelated, smooth and fire variants plus a default arc/check. The useful RFF concept is showing the current preview-resolution state separately from the user's quality policy. The comment equating adaptive Off with a GPU running flat-out is not measured telemetry: disabling resolution adaptation does not prove full GPU utilization or prevent other throttling. Neither a smooth glyph nor full spatial resolution proves numerical convergence or final sample quality. In both 2D and 3D, derive such indicators from renderer state and keep final-export quality and deep-zoom precision independent of the preview-resolution policy.

The icon modules alone also do not establish distinct presentation for every semantic state. Loop and PingPong share geometry, BakeIcon accepts but does not use active, and KeyIcon distinguishes some states through fixed color rather than shape. A port must preserve the owning control's actual state explanation instead of treating icon props as a complete interaction contract. Labels, focus behavior and accessible names belong to those controls; their presence or absence cannot be established globally from these SVG definitions. This is a source-level limitation, not a visual accessibility verdict.

Icons2 provides a parameterized chevron factory, but the older module still exports separate chevrons with different sizes and stroke properties. Its claim of a unified style should therefore not be interpreted as proof that every call site has migrated. Current pixel-ring code uses seven cells spanning 20 units, despite an inner comment describing an eight-cell grid with 2.5-unit cells. InfoIcon also uses cy on line elements where a y1 endpoint would be expected. These details reinforce checking actual geometry and consumers when adapting an asset; they are not proposed GMT repair work. For RFF, reuse an established native asset/style contract where practical and verify DPI scaling separately from render resolution. Distinctive SVG path data should not be copied without establishing provenance; this batch establishes no new license permission and copies no asset into RFF.

### Global style entry: preview chrome and renderer quality remain independent

Fully reviewed: `index.css` (369 lines). It supplies Tailwind build directives, fallback theme variables, shared control styles, scrollbar rules and animation definitions. These are presentation facilities, not fractal shaders. In particular, set-save-bloom is an opacity animation for save feedback, not HDR bloom in the rendered fractal. No rendering-speed claim or shader-priority change follows from this file.

The fallback colors are channel triples, while support/kept/metal colors are full CSS color expressions. That distinction matters to consumers: wrapping an already complete color expression in an RGB-triple parser is not equivalent to reading a triple. RFF can preserve the broader architectural separation between semantic UI colors and fractal palette data, with a clearly typed representation at each boundary. UI theme changes should not change saved palette recipes, render buffers or export color transforms. The CSS comments describe cached inline boot variables overriding the fallback; this file alone does not prove every application initializes those values consistently or establish the quoted contrast measurements.

The dock scrollbar rule reserves layout space to prevent width-dependent wrapping from repeatedly changing content height as a scrollbar appears and disappears. This is a useful general layout-stability mechanism for resizable RFF panels, but its CSS property is browser-specific. A native implementation should reason about available client width, scrollbar allocation and DPI using its own layout system. Do not conflate this application-controlled reflow with RFF's separately documented native Win32 menu show-before-first-paint interval. Neither phenomenon was visually tested in this batch.

The save-feedback duration is supplied through a variable, with a fallback, so a controller and its visual animation can share timing. The reduced-motion block replaces the collapsing fill with a fade and suppresses the white bloom; it does not disable the text brightness animation or all directional/pop animations defined earlier. Thus this is a targeted adaptation, not evidence of a global reduced-motion policy. An RFF feedback controller can share a duration with its presentation without treating animation completion as proof that a save succeeded; confirmation must originate in the operation result.

The directional animations retain a final identity transform through forwards fill. That retained transform can matter to stacking and positioned descendants even after visible motion stops. The comments' historical observation that no fixed descendant was affected and their assertion about removed compositor layers are not current measurements. If analogous overlay effects are adopted, verify final positioning and hit testing independently of the fractal viewport. Do not assume that replacing a translucent surface or removing an animation necessarily improves shader throughput; any performance claim requires measurement on the actual presentation path. This source review adds implementation-boundary guidance, not a rendered UI audit.

For RFF this reinforces staged validation and complete dependency preparation before committing a preset, without claiming the historical GMT fallback-sphere issue is still present.

The historical hardware-capability discussion also separates numerical precision mode from render-buffer precision. Those are different controls: changing an image attachment format does not establish that deep-zoom perturbation arithmetic is safe at a lower precision. ### Embedded MB3D sample catalogue: structural checks completed, payload semantics pending

Inspected all non-payload source in `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/sampleScenes.ts`, all 43 record names and formula lists, and programmatically decoded every embedded base64 payload. All 43 decode to 1,976 bytes and round-trip to the identical canonical base64 string. This is a structural data check only. The initial full-text output was truncated, and the binary scene fields have not all been semantically inspected in this batch; the coverage entry therefore remains partial rather than being counted as fully reviewed.

The module stores each scene as name, ordered formula-name array and an encoded .m3p payload. Its decoder calls atob, allocates a Uint8Array and copies each decoded character code. It does not validate a scene header, resolve formulas, check importer compatibility or render an image. The header describes qualification by successful decompilation and weaving in mode 0; that condition alone cannot substantiate the broader phrase 'faithfully-renderable'. Formula order and repeated slots matter: several examples repeat Amazing Box, MengerKochV2 or SphereIFS. A catalogue consumer must not deduplicate the sequence as if it were merely a dependency set.

For RFF, adopt the idea of deterministic, versioned example fixtures for testing appearance changes, rather than treating imported 3D payloads as directly compatible with 2D perturbation/MPA rendering. Separate decode success, semantic import success, supported feature coverage and reference-image agreement. A 2D fixture should preserve exact location/precision data and its palette recipe or explicit palette, with rendering settings sufficient to reproduce the result. Select examples that expose narrow palette bands, interior/exterior boundaries and deep-zoom detail; for a future 3D path also cover normal estimation, shadowing, reflections and hybrid formula ordering. Their names alone do not prove those features were exercised successfully.

These embedded scenes identify external authors/source material in names and a repository reference, but the inspected module supplies no per-scene license grants. No sample bytes or assets were copied into RFF, and no external license conclusion is made here. A distributed RFF example pack needs established provenance for the selected material or independently authored fixtures. The structural checks performed here are not a shader benchmark or a visual equivalence test; full binary-field inspection remains outstanding.

### Embedded sample follow-up: slot-count hints cannot define the executed formula sequence

Re-read the complete current `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/parseMB3D.ts` and inspected dimensions, total iteration limits and active-slot descriptors from all 43 embedded scenes using its documented byte offsets. This follow-up checks selected binary fields, not every camera/light/option value, so sampleScenes.ts remains partial. No scene was rendered and the TypeScript parser itself was not executed by this check.

The binary samples concretely support the parser's decision to scan all six physical slots rather than bound the scan by the stored formulaCount hint. Genetic Menger has hint 0 with two active slots; TimeMachine has hint 0 with four; QuatP4hybridJulia has hint 1 with two. Conversely, AureliusCat - Bamboo has hint 3 with two active slots and Virtual tubes world has hint 4 with two. Treating that field as the execution count would both omit meaningful formulas and risk treating inactive data as active. RFF format work should distinguish capacity, hints and semantically active records explicitly, following each format's real contract rather than generalizing this MB3D exception to RFF's own formats.

The samples also contain distinct global and per-slot iteration counts. For example, Lenord - ASurf 2 has a global limit of 76 and a slot count of 100; Abominog uses 16/1/1 across its three slots. Neither a name list nor a sum of slot counts describes the complete iteration schedule. A 3D hybrid implementation must preserve ordering, repetition and termination rules. These sequences are not MPA skip levels and cannot be transplanted into RFF's Mandelbrot perturbation engine without separate mathematical derivation.

The embedded transport uses ordinary base64, whereas the parser's clipboard-text path uses MB3D's custom little-endian six-bit alphabet. Keep these layers separate. The raw-binary entry checks minimum header length and assumes the 840-byte layout; its comment explicitly excludes an 868-byte layout. Successful transport decoding therefore does not prove layout compatibility. The parser preserves raw bytes, exposes some unmapped fields and interprets others, such as camera basis, squared bailout radius and light coordinates, using format-specific units. An RFF importer should report unsupported semantics rather than silently claiming a faithful image, and should not infer safety from a plausible title or sufficient byte length alone.

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine-gmt/modular-graph.md` (135 lines). Shared graph traversal alone cannot guarantee alignment: repeated parameter use, reordered calls or an unused declared input can change the sequence. Canonical binding comparison can avoid recompiling merely because dictionary keys were inserted in a different order. Stripping punctuation from IDs can collapse distinct IDs to the same GLSL name. Missing or unknown nodes that merely pass inputs through need an explicit compatibility policy. A 2D effect graph should define its neutral operation without changing the fractal recurrence.

The distance override's numeric sentinel window is meaningful only within that renderer's contract. Prefer explicit validity/type information when designing new RFF intermediate values rather than borrowing a magic distance range. Condition modulo/rem values need defined integer conversion, bounds and behavior when the remainder exceeds the modulus. Those iteration conditions refer to actual iterations, not MPA skip levels; evaluating only at skip endpoints changes semantics unless the skipped behavior is accounted for.

For RFF, a graph over already-computed coloring quantities and postprocessing passes is a plausible 3D-to-2D transfer with a narrower mathematical contract than a graph defining arbitrary fractal formulas. Reachability pruning is valid only for nodes whose omitted effects are irrelevant; shared state or hidden side effects require explicit dependencies. Screen-space effects also need typed color/data inputs, pass ordering and resource lifetime rules. This is an architectural extension candidate, with no claimed implementation or measured rendering gain.

### Archived navigation: precise cursor anchoring and generation-aware feedback

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine-gmt/navigation.md` (215 lines). This describes historical Orbit/Fly integration, local-origin absorption, input ownership, asynchronous picks and HUD/probe updates. No interactive navigation or GPU readback was measured in this batch.

The transferable 2D invariant is keeping the complex-plane point beneath the chosen cursor fixed during zoom. If the view maps a screen offset u to c + s*u, a new scale s' requires c' = c + (s - s')*u, with rotation/aspect and display-to-render coordinate conversion included in u. Evaluate the center update with RFF's required precision and scale representation; ordinary floating-point subtraction at a deep-zoom center can erase the requested motion. The finite-resolution pointer offset is not justification for reducing the stored center's precision. GMT's local-origin/high-low strategy is a useful separation of world state from local motion, not a replacement for RFF's arbitrary-precision coordinate handling.

GMT freezes a local pivot for a gesture and rejects asynchronous picks from an older absorption generation. RFF can use an analogous view revision for delayed pixel inspection, coordinate readouts or render results. That revision must cover every input that invalidates the result, including viewport mapping and view changes, not just origin normalization. A purely 2D cursor anchor can usually be computed analytically without a GPU depth pick. Fit scale, letterboxing and display scaling must be applied consistently to input coordinates and overlays.

Normalization of an internal coordinate representation is not necessarily a visual change. Distinguish it from actual navigation when deciding whether computed data or accumulation is reusable. Conversely, a local position returning to zero after absorption does not prove the view stayed unchanged: invalidate from the authoritative view revision. Save/undo/export snapshots must include the effective center during interaction, not only a delayed end-of-gesture value. A final exact endpoint commit cannot retroactively make a transition path computed through lower-precision coordinates exact.

One owner should apply each navigation gesture. The document's custom/drei split and avoidance of duplicate damping updates illustrate why two handlers can produce doubled or inconsistent motion. Route keys away from text editing and controls, release captured input on cancellation/focus loss, and separate UI activity from actual view changes. Animation playback, scrubbing and recording also require distinct ownership rules; suppressing live input and suppressing playback writes are related but different decisions.

The probe's eight-percent-per-frame smoothing has a frame-rate-dependent time constant. For comparable responsiveness across rendering speeds, a new RFF smoothed indicator can use alpha = 1 - exp(-dt/tau), with a clearly specified immediate response where desired. GPU readback from a previous target can reduce contention but does not by itself guarantee a nonblocking transfer. Frame-count warmup is not a substitute for target readiness, and invalid/missing measurements should have explicit validity rather than share numeric sentinels with real values. A 2D iteration count is not surface distance and should not drive a copied 3D collision-speed rule. These are transfer requirements, not assertions of present GMT defects.

### Archived audio synchronization: deterministic shader animation and honest export status

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/audio-fps-sync.md` (147 lines). The document covers live deck ownership, an offline PCM mix, frame-window conversion and a transient file cache. Audio support is an optional extension for RFF; these findings do not change shader-quality priorities or establish a missing current feature.

For audio-reactive 2D palette/shader animation, export should evaluate a reproducible envelope at each frame's defined sample time from the source audio, independently of rendering throughput. A live audio element's clock cannot supply deterministic offline frames when fractal rendering takes variable time. Preserve the audio identity, trim interval, analysis settings and time convention used by the animation. The archived mix covers inclusive video endFrame through (endFrame + 1)/fps; keep that convention explicit and consistent with video encoding, or convert deliberately if RFF uses an exclusive endpoint. Rounded audio sample counts require an equally explicit duration/timestamp policy.

The documented live strategy avoids steady-state seeking and detects scrubs with a half-second jump threshold. Such a threshold cannot distinguish intentional scrubbing from every slow frame, while small scrubs can fall below it. An adopted design should expose seek/scrub events and clock ownership explicitly, handle initial entry into a clip, and define bounded drift correction. Never infer that a playback request succeeded merely from setting ownership. The archival claim that every seek causes a click is a motivation for limiting seeks, not a universal guarantee about all playback systems.

The offline mixer sums clips then clips amplitudes. That prevents values exceeding its output range but does not preserve overlapping waveforms without distortion. A future RFF exporter should specify gain/headroom and channel mapping; linear interpolation alone is not an anti-alias filter for downsampling. Decode/analysis caches should identify asset revisions and settings, and longer exports should account for the memory cost of a complete interleaved PCM buffer. The transient raw-file cache described here is not persistence: reopened metadata cannot reconstruct a missing audio source.

Missing media and decode failure should produce an explicit export outcome instead of silently converting an intended sound-bearing video into a silent one. Auxiliary image passes can omit audio by design, but that should not accidentally govern the beauty-video path. Module-global state likewise needs lifecycle/reset ownership; its mere existence does not prove preservation across every hot-reload mechanism. This batch adds timing and export-integrity requirements, without claiming that the archived implementation or RFF currently satisfies them.

### Archived scene serialization: preserve executable meaning, not just parameter values

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine-gmt/save-load-gmf.md` (362 lines). It covers GMF formula/scene containers, PNG metadata callbacks, camera utilities and an unrelated React profiler wrapper. Historical parser limitations and serialization field lists are not new findings about current code. No files were imported into a renderer and no output equivalence test was run in this batch.

For RFF, reproducible shader settings require the source/algorithm identity, interpretation version, effective parameters and needed assets together. The archived GMF description separates formula defaults in Metadata from the current state in Scene; a loader must deliberately choose the correct layer rather than accidentally overwrite a saved scene with defaults. The shaderMeta mechanism demonstrates why non-text capabilities are part of executable meaning: losing loop ownership or shared-state flags can change rendering even if every GLSL string survives. Maintain an explicit serialization contract for every capability rather than assuming an object spread covers fields removed into separate blocks.

A formula-only document, a complete scene and a scene whose formula definition is missing are different load outcomes. Parsing should return a validated result without changing active renderer state; registration, asset resolution, shader compilation and state activation should then commit coherently. A fallback that saves parameter JSON when a formula is unknown does not make the file self-contained. RFF should disclose unresolved dependencies and retain the old working state when reconstruction fails. Preserve existing ConfigIO field ordering, palette recipe identities/RNG semantics and compressed-map versions; this recommendation does not authorize replacing those formats with GMF or JSON.

The described tag parser stops at the first closing tag, including one inside a GLSL comment. An independently designed source container should escape delimiters or use an unambiguous length/structured representation, and distinguish malformed, unsupported and valid-but-scene-free inputs. Prefix sniffing is only dispatch, not validation. The archive's BOM warning is too broad: JavaScript trimStart removes the standard U+FEFF BOM, so that particular prefix claim does not follow from the described implementation. Similarly, a local object-URL lifetime is not inherently governed by network speed; a delayed browser download claim needs actual browser evidence.

Embedding scene metadata in a PNG is a useful optional 2D transfer: an exported fractal can carry a path back to its exact location and settings. Pixels and metadata must come from the same render revision, including asynchronous capture. Preserve high-precision coordinates with an exact representation rather than converting them to ordinary JSON numeric values. State whether external textures, custom shader source and audio are embedded or merely referenced. Support recognized legacy metadata keys without ambiguously choosing between conflicting payloads. Metadata recovery is a convenience rather than a guarantee after an image editor strips ancillary chunks, so retain an explicit scene-file option.

The camera helper's high + low + local conversion to a single ordinary vector can discard precision before any later split. For RFF, rotating the view or editing a shader must not round-trip the center through a display-precision coordinate merely because a whole-state event expects a position. Use the canonical precise state when constructing transactions, and protect whole-state updates against stale snapshots. A display conversion should not become the source of truth for saving or subsequent edits.

Finally, the profiler wrapper measures React rendering rather than GPU shader execution. Its inactive passthrough still has a wrapper/check cost, so the archive's absolute zero-overhead wording should be read as avoidance of active profiling instrumentation, not a measured zero cost. RFF performance claims require measurements of the relevant CPU work, GPU passes and end-to-end interaction separately. This document supplies serialization and reproducibility guidance, not evidence of a shader speedup.

### Archived worker contract: distinguish a usable renderer from a typed stub

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/worker-contract.md` (237 lines). Its main subject is explicitly the generic no-op stub, not GMT's functioning render worker. Null picks, empty histograms, ignored commands and synthesized boot status in this document must not be reported as defects of GMT's installed renderer. Historical installer scope gaps are documentation ownership observations, not evidence that installation is absent.

For RFF, use an explicit renderer capability/state contract if UI, background rendering and export share an abstraction. A placeholder returning true for half-float support is not a GPU capability measurement. Likewise, a stub's synchronous boot callback exists to unblock its generic shell; a real Vulkan renderer should signal the appropriate initialized/compiled/presented milestone rather than imitate a fictitious successful boot. Unsupported operation, valid empty result, pending result and failed operation should be distinguishable. This is particularly relevant to histogram-driven coloring: an unavailable readback must not masquerade as a measured empty distribution and overwrite useful controls.

The singleton installer only affects future lookups; replacing its stored pointer cannot update consumers that already captured the stub. Define initialization order or supply an explicit stable owner whose implementation changes safely. A C++ adaptation also needs clear object lifetime and synchronization, rather than copying JavaScript global-reference patterns. Multiple viewports or export sessions should carry their own state and capabilities where needed. The archive's early-install assumption is not a substitute for checking every actual consumer.

A render/export request should bind camera or precise 2D view, shader configuration, frame time, modulation values and resource revisions into one coherent snapshot. Public mutable modulation fields are not sufficient evidence of atomic submission. Tag asynchronous shader compilation, histogram readback and frame completion with the revision/request they belong to; discard stale completions when a view or shader is superseded. Distinguish request acceptance from GPU completion and output delivery. For RFF, retain exact center/scale representation across the boundary, not GMT's fixed high/low coordinate schema by default.

Cancellation and renderer restart need explicit outcomes for every outstanding request. Flipping an exporting boolean does not settle promises, release in-flight GPU resources or prevent old callbacks from affecting a later export. An adopted contract should define completion, cancellation, failure and device-loss transitions and retire resources only after their real GPU lifetime ends. Backpressure should prevent obsolete interactive work from growing without bound while preserving the exact requested frame sequence for offline export. These are architectural requirements, not new measurements of either renderer.

The display-camera snapshot illustrates a useful 2D overlay invariant: projection/view mapping, viewport extent and displayed image must describe the same frame. Falling back to a live camera before the first snapshot weakens that guarantee; RFF should provide an explicitly valid transform or defer dependent overlays. Per-window overlay state prevents one viewport from replacing another's references. Mouse-hover state can stay lightweight, but lightweight storage alone does not prove downstream adaptive-resolution behavior is correct or fast.

This batch therefore supports a renderer interface with honest capabilities, coherent state snapshots and revision-aware results. It does not justify importing a browser worker framework into RFF or claim that moving work off the UI thread by itself accelerates shader execution.

### Archived feature schema: one semantic update across shader, texture and history paths

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/feature-system.md` (205 lines). This historical API description explicitly distinguishes implemented registry/slice behavior from earlier aspirational APIs. Its corrected duplicate-preset-field report must not be revived as a current defect. Registration-time warnings, development replacement rules and historical downstream tolerances are not fresh findings in current RFF or GMT.

For RFF, a shared parameter description can reduce drift among controls, shader bindings, serialization and animation, but those consumers still need explicit contracts. Stable parameter IDs should replace reliance on independently reconstructed setter names or ambiguous string paths where practical. Numeric-index enums must retain persisted meanings; inserting/reordering labels must not renumber stored palette or mode IDs. Validate finite integral enum values at the boundary rather than assuming a float-typed dropdown can only produce legal indices. GLSL boolean-as-float conventions also must not be mistaken for the host representation of a Vulkan block member.

The archived setter emits configuration, individual uniforms, textures and an accumulation reset through separate paths. One batched config event alone does not establish an atomic renderer update across those channels. An RFF transaction should stage related changes, derive composite values from the complete updated state, and activate them with a shared revision. Preserve explicitly provided preset values when a dependency hook supplies defaults; distinguish default derivation from hard validation so an invalid explicit value is not accepted merely because it was explicit.

The documented reverse composite map stores one composite key per dependency. That description alone cannot represent several composite uniforms depending on the same field. A new schema should model dependency fan-out explicitly, update each dependent once per transaction, and reject cycles. Gradient composition is described as regenerating the whole gradient rather than assembling component values; such special behavior belongs in the parameter contract, not an implicit exception that a generic caller must guess.

Suppress redundant work before expensive gradient generation or texture upload where semantic equality permits it. A downstream config equality check cannot recover the CPU work and events already performed upstream, and does not necessarily suppress an independent reset event. For RFF, avoid adopting the archived absolute 1e-6 tolerance for precise coordinates or fine shader parameters; use exact canonical equality or a justified parameter-specific rule. No-op detection must also account for resource revisions and requested side effects. Treat numerical-map recomputation, shading refresh, texture rebuild and accumulation reset as distinct invalidation categories.

Custom reducers in the document merge state and request a reset without necessarily following the auto-setter's uniform/texture routes. An adopted RFF system should ensure edits made through undo, presets, animation and bespoke controls reach the same synchronization boundary. Reducers receiving live state must not mutate it in place if history and change detection rely on immutable snapshots. Transient modulation should remain separate from authored values so preview/playback does not silently rewrite saved settings; persistent defaults containing mutable objects require independent ownership between sessions.

Registration dependencies should be validated after the relevant registry is complete. An early warning about a not-yet-registered dependency is not proof that the final graph is invalid, while falling back to insertion order after a cycle does not satisfy shader dependencies. Freeze should stabilize the schema used by serialization and pipelines; replacing a definition after state construction needs an explicit migration/rebuild policy. UI-component validation at a later registration phase is a different gate from shader dependency and host-layout validation.

The archived gradient path uses a 256-by-1 RGBA byte buffer. This is a storage choice, not a sufficient quality target for RFF: fine palette features, HDR values, interpolation space and output quantization have different precision requirements. Consider the effective sampled result and existing RFF palette implementation before changing texture resolution or format. In particular, RFF already has OKLab interpolation; this schema review does not propose it as a missing feature. The direct 3D-to-2D transfer is coherent parameter/data flow, with potential reductions in redundant updates requiring measurement rather than an assumed speedup.

### Archived shortcut and history routing: predictable shader experimentation

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/shortcuts-undo.md` (150 lines), with the truncated tail of the initial combined tool output subsequently read separately. Historical shortcut behavior is not new runtime validation. In particular, the document's assertion that a stable descending sort places the later registered equal-score element first contradicts the stated stable insertion-order mechanics. The tie direction cannot be established from that prose claim; earlier source-level findings in this report take precedence.

For RFF, shader/palette experimentation benefits from explicit history scope and transaction boundaries. A slider drag should restore a complete prior parameter state in one action, while navigation and animation editing need a predictable routing policy. Separate history lanes can prevent accidental camera undo during color editing, but do not by themselves make incorrect routing impossible. Buttons, menus and shortcuts should reveal which action they will undo, and restoring a parameter transaction must also synchronize renderer state and dependent resources.

Scope precedence should be compared lexicographically rather than encoded as scopeIndex*10000 + priority unless priority bounds are enforced; otherwise a large priority can cross scope boundaries. Specify whether a highest-ranked binding whose predicate fails blocks lower candidates or permits fallback. Text-entry/IME handling, repeat behavior and supported redo equivalents also need a consistent policy. The archive lists a timeline override for Mod+Y but not Mod+Shift+Z, illustrating why equivalent keys should be checked across contexts rather than inferred from a common label.

Registration ownership matters when a component replaces a binding and an older component later unregisters the same ID. Scope instances and binding registrations can use ownership tokens to make cleanup exact; a plain matching name cannot distinguish duplicate owners. Teardown should remove dependent plugins before clearing their shared registry or reset their installed state coherently. These lifecycle lessons transfer to native command routing without copying browser event handling.

History should retain canonical precise locations and authored shader/palette data, with immutable ownership or well-defined diffs. UI-only state can be excluded deliberately, but renderer-affecting state cannot be omitted merely to reduce history size. RFF's palette recipe reconstruction and MPA precision requirements remain unchanged. This is an interaction/reliability improvement, not a shader performance measurement.

### Archived snapshot-library primitives: stable IDs, complete saves and reversible audition

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/state-library-ui.md` (151 lines). It describes controlled list, toast and active-feature panel components; persistence, undo and asynchronous capture are owned elsewhere. The archived collision scenarios are conditional risks, and the same document says the named current consumers do not collide. No live UI or current slice behavior is claimed verified by reading these primitives' documentation.

A transferable RFF feature is a library of shading or palette variants applied to the same precise fractal view. Clearly define whether an entry captures only color/shader settings or the entire location, and keep live edits distinct from updating the saved entry. The active marker should compare the fields actually captured. A footer exposing a whole feature can include fields outside a restricted snapshot unless filters and payload agree; the panel's presence does not prove every displayed edit will be saved.

Use stable snapshot IDs for selection and asynchronous completion. Reorder indices and numbered shortcuts are presentation positions, not identities. A drag begun before the list changes should resolve its original ID against the current list before committing. Shortcut hints must reflect the real bindings and scope rather than assume Ctrl plus the first nine indices. Likewise, Enter/blur rename submission and Escape cancellation should have explicit single-commit behavior.

Capture settings and thumbnails from one revision, with a defined policy for overlapping save requests. A completion for an older capture must not overwrite a newer snapshot, recreate a deleted entry or attach an image of another view. A saved toast should indicate the intended completed operation; rendering a toast string does not establish durable storage. Button debouncing alone cannot solve races originating from shortcuts or other callers, so ownership belongs in the save operation.

Immediate deletion is reasonable when actual undo can restore the entry, ordering, active selection and required resources. This controlled component does not prove that the host supplies such undo. An adopted RFF library should implement that contract rather than add unnecessary confirmation prompts. Preserve palette recipe seeds/IDs and any explicit stop data according to their existing semantics when duplicating or saving variants.

The catalog's reusable shell is valuable, but app-agnostic presentation is not identical to store independence: the toast and active-feature components still read a particular store interface. A native RFF implementation can preserve the controlled-data boundary while using its own command and persistence layers. This is a direct 3D-to-2D workflow transfer for comparing visual settings, with no new claim about rendered quality or speed.

### Archived animation contract: parameter-aware interpolation and reproducible evaluation

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/animation.md` (300 lines). It describes evaluation, modulation, binders, camera pairs and audio/export connections. Historical implementation claims and numerical performance ranges are not newly executed tests. The introductory absence-of-singletons claim is qualified by the document's own exported animationEngine singleton; store injection and object lifetime are separate properties.

The strongest RFF transfer is a shared evaluator that derives shader parameters from authored state and an explicit frame time for both preview and export. Frame-stepped interactive playback that discards a wall-time backlog is not, by itself, proof of frame-for-frame export equivalence. Export must evaluate every requested sample independently of rendering speed; modulation phase, seeds, audio-derived values and base-value composition must agree across both paths. Reset transient offsets before each evaluation so values do not accumulate unintentionally, and restore a clean baseline when the last modulator is removed.

Interpolation belongs to parameter semantics. Positive zoom/scale values can use log-space interpolation for multiplicative motion, with defined handling for nonpositive values and extremes. Boolean, enum and resource selections need step/hold behavior rather than numeric blending or silent omission. Angular wrapping should come from declared units and topology, not a substring such as rot/phase/twist in a track name. Colors need a declared interpolation space and gamut/output policy; RFF's existing OKLab option is already part of that design space. Compile-time shader choices require scheduled variant changes, not arbitrary per-frame uniform treatment.

The document describes a four-iteration Newton inversion of cubic time. A fixed iteration count and clamping alone do not guarantee a correct root for every permitted curve: constrain time handles for a single-valued curve, handle flat derivatives and degenerate intervals, and use a bracketed fallback where required. De Casteljau insertion preserves a particular cubic only if its controls and parameterization are retained; automatic tangent recomputation afterward can change it again. A stored Bezier label should not imply Bezier evaluation on a log track when the implementation intentionally uses linear-in-log interpolation.

The paired pan formula c(t) = c0 + (c1-c0)*(s(t)-s0)/(s1-s0) can maintain constant screen-space pan speed when s denotes world-units-per-screen scale and changes exponentially with time: c'(t)/s(t) is then constant. That conclusion does not hold unchanged for arbitrary eased scale curves, and a magnification variable requires the appropriate reciprocal convention. Near-equal endpoints need stable evaluation; a fallback threshold alone does not prove cancellation error is controlled. RFF must retain its required precision throughout center interpolation. GMT's double-double representation and quoted deep-zoom ranges are not substitutes for RFF's arbitrary-precision requirements.

Cache validity includes the sequence revision, frame, track/pair registration, interpolation mode and other dependencies actually used. Sequence reference equality works only when edits replace that reference; it does not cover mutable edits or external registry changes automatically. Likewise, an explicit binder taking precedence over a cached fallback does not prove the fallback remains correct after reconnecting stores or replacing schemas. Ownership-aware unregister callbacks are a useful pattern, but cached bindings still need a documented invalidation policy.

For partially modulated vectors, filling absent axes with zero is appropriate for an offset vector, but not automatically for displaying or replacing the complete effective value. Merge with the correct authored/current base and batch axis updates before dependent uniforms are submitted. Keep recording source state distinct from the growing recorded result to avoid feedback, and flush buffered final samples before relinquishing modulation ownership. The archive's 400 ms flush interval implies 2.5 scheduled flushes per second, not the stated approximately six rerenders; other updates would need separate measurement to support that count.

These mechanisms apply directly to 2D palette cycles, shading animation and deep-zoom video. They also require clear distinction between reusing a computed map for color-only animation and recomputing when view or mathematical inputs change. No new runtime validation, speedup or visual-equivalence result is claimed by this archival review.

### Archived camera adapters and migrations: reusable libraries without weakening saved-state guarantees

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/camera-plugin.md` (223 lines). It covers two distinct snapshot systems, generic handles, migrations and the state-library factory. Its known-issues table explicitly marks the library collision guard fixed on 2026-07-12 while earlier paragraphs retain the old behavior. Those paragraphs are historical context, not evidence that the same defect remains. Previously reviewed companion UI documents must be interpreted with that correction in mind.

The useful RFF abstraction is a payload-specific capture/apply contract shared by location and shading libraries. A 2D payload can carry exact center, scale and intended view settings without a 3D pose; a palette payload can omit location deliberately. GMT's parallel fixed slots and managed library do not share storage, so RFF should define whether quick slots reference library IDs or are independent snapshots before exposing both. Hiding duplicate shortcuts does not synchronize their saved content. Persist the chosen semantics and preserve existing file identities.

Snapshot duplication must use a representation-aware clone. The described JSON clone is adequate only for supported JSON data, not a generic guarantee for precise numbers, class instances, special numeric values or mutable resources. Capture and apply should own their data independently; returning an object from an adapter does not prove it is detached from live state. Duplicating an inactive snapshot is documented as immediately applying it, whereas deselection only clears the active ID. RFF should make those distinct actions explicit so library management does not unexpectedly move the view or change shading.

Slot bounds should validate integer indices as well as numeric range, and persisted arrays need shape/size checks. Sequential-fill slots and fixed sparse slots have different meanings: a request for slot five must not silently become item three. Adapter failure should produce an operation result without leaving the active ID, stored payload and renderer in disagreement. Group related capture/apply changes into the established undo and renderer transaction paths. A returned promise should document whether it confirms initial state insertion, thumbnail completion, or durable persistence.

The migration description warrants special care for any RFF format extension. Catching an exception does not restore the input if the migration already mutated it. Continuing later migrations and stamping the highest version can also hide an unapplied earlier transformation. Migrate a detached validated representation, preserve the original on failure, and advance version markers only under a defined successful completion policy. Version numbers must impose an unambiguous sequence; adding another migration at an already-applied version can be skipped by a single highest-version marker. RFF's append-only ConfigIO and stable palette recipes remain authoritative rather than adopting a new version policy from GMT.

The archive describes nullish coalescing as accepting any falsy return as no change, but the shown expression only falls back for null or undefined; false, zero and an empty string do not satisfy that claim. Validate migration output shape explicitly. Field rename/merge helpers also need a declared conflict policy, preservation of unknown supported extension fields and clear behavior when source/destination paths coincide. Migration success should mean preserved intended scene semantics, not merely parsable output.

Generic mutable handles with a revision counter provide a lightweight notification mechanism, but writes that omit notification can leave subscribed readers stale. Reset must not reuse an initial object already mutated through an alias. Native RFF can use explicit ownership and notifications for transient render/input state while keeping authored settings on the regular persistence path. This batch contributes save-state correctness and 2D library reuse guidance, with no runtime benchmark or new shader implementation.

### Archived host plugins: explicit load orchestration and reversible render overrides

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/plugins-host.md` (255 lines). This historical catalog covers registries, scene IO, help, pause, bucket rendering and export dialogs. Its corrected phantom-import report and distinction between retained state and a DOM leak are retained as evidence limits, not revived as current GMT findings. Old installation/API descriptions are architectural context rather than instructions for this audit.

For RFF, keep file decoding separate from applying a validated scene, but expose a clear complete load operation that callers cannot confuse with a partial setter. The archived loadScene orchestration includes shader compilation and renderer synchronization that loadPreset alone bypasses. An equivalent RFF boundary should validate precise coordinates and settings, resolve resources, prepare the necessary pipeline and commit a coherent scene revision. A successful parse does not prove a usable rendered scene; menu, drag/drop and metadata recovery should converge on the same activation path.

Installation and reconfiguration need distinct semantics. The described SceneIO reinstall refreshes captured dependencies before an installed guard, while menu registration remains based on the first install's capabilities. This is a general lesson for RFF extensions: either recompute dependent commands when capabilities change or make configuration immutable for that lifetime. Replacing a registry entry is not complete idempotency when subscriptions, timers, commands or resources remain from an earlier owner. Explicit teardown should cover those owners without deleting unrelated registrations or persisted user state.

Bucket preview temporarily changes resolution and adaptive behavior. Preserve the original display geometry for fitting so repeated output-size edits do not compound shrinkage. Restore only the overrides still owned by that operation, accounting for user changes and overlapping dialogs. Merely remembering that a resolution swap occurred does not prove restoration is current. RFF can apply this to 2D high-resolution/region previews while retaining exact view coordinates. Tile rendering also needs consistent full-image coordinates and border support for neighborhood effects; a shared dialog/controller contract alone does not prove seam-free shading.

Export defaults should distinguish an automatic recommendation from an explicit user value. The archived resolution-only bitrate formula ignores frame rate, codec and scene complexity, and overwriting a user bitrate on a dimension change is a policy choice rather than a required consequence. RFF can retain a manual override and refresh recommendations only in automatic mode. Progress callbacks need defined units, finite values and phases; clamping a ratio to a percentage does not make NaN valid or establish that final file writing is complete. Sampling completion, rendering completion and output finalization should remain distinguishable.

Event deferral requires precise claims. A microtask runs after the current JavaScript stack, but is not a general guarantee that every React commit or GPU update has completed, nor does enqueueing one callback per store change automatically coalesce updates. The transferable RFF concern is avoiding reentrant notifications and batching relevant changes at a known boundary. Similarly, sharing a serializer between text and PNG saves establishes compatible encoding, not byte-identical payloads from separate captures unless the state and serialization are deterministic and identical.

The archive's universal claim that browser Ctrl+S never reaches JavaScript is too broad and should not determine native RFF bindings. Keep platform-appropriate existing commands and resolve actual conflicts. Claims that a fixed-width popup never clips also require viewport-size evidence; fixed offsets from GMT's timeline layout should not be copied into an unrelated host. These observations constrain adoption rather than constitute a visual UI audit. No renderer performance or export-completeness test was performed in this batch.

### Archived bundled features, checked against current grading and post-effect source

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/features.md` (536 lines, two complete chunks). Also re-read the complete current `engine/features/color_grading.ts` and `engine/features/post_effects.ts` to separate the archived descriptions from actual shader expressions. Those source re-reads are not counted as newly reviewed files. No rendering or timing experiment was performed.

The current grading helper first subtracts the black point and clamps below zero, divides by max(0.0001, whitePoint-blackPoint), optionally raises channels to 1/gamma, then mixes the result against its weighted luma according to saturation. This is concrete 2D-compatible postprocessing. The denominator guard prevents division by zero but does not define a desirable reversed-levels curve; validate or specify that case. Gamma is skipped within 0.001 of one, so this shader is not a fully continuous exact gamma transform across that branch threshold. Saturation above one can create negative channels, and levels/gamma can generate values above one; downstream handling must be deliberate.

The luma coefficients and gamma operation require a specified working color space. The user-facing Gamma control is an artistic levels operation, not automatically the output transfer function. The same file declares five tone-mapping choices, but applyColorGrading itself contains no tone-mapping curve; actual tone mapping is supplied elsewhere in the pipeline. Do not infer full ACES/AgX behavior, pass order or certification from dropdown names. RFF should adopt only the intended operations, with a known linear/HDR-to-display sequence and existing NOTICE/provenance requirements respected.

Current chromatic aberration computes a centered UV displacement proportional to cc*dot(cc,cc)*amount. Twelve samples use t=i/11, wavelength-like RGB weights from caSpectrum(t), and signed amounts 0.15*strength*(t-0.5). It accumulates weighted source-map RGB and divides componentwise by the accumulated weights. This normalization preserves a spatially constant sampled color, subject to finite positive weight sums and boundary sampling, but does not make the RGB heuristic a physical spectral simulation. The helper attributes its spectrum approximation to YACA by Fu-Bama; this comment identifies an origin, not a verified reuse license. No implementation is copied into RFF here.

For 2D RFF this is an optional lens-style effect, not an improvement to fractal detail. Its twelve texture fetches require an actual cost comparison; cache behavior and bandwidth matter, so sample count alone is not a measured slowdown. Distortion uses normalized UV radius without aspect correction in this helper, so equal screen-pixel radii can receive different distortions in a nonsquare image. Define whether that anisotropy is intentional, specify sampler behavior beyond image edges, and use full-image UV coordinates for tiled exports. Include the displaced source extent when planning tile borders.

The chromatic-aberration block replaces col by resampling map, then the bloom block adds its texture contribution. Consequently, the assembled pass order and the meaning of map determine whether earlier col-only effects survive. RFF must follow actual data flow rather than merely concatenate attractive effects. The bloom sampler is declared here but owned/bound elsewhere, reinforcing that a shader snippet is not a complete render pass. Both current feature files use noAccumReset rather than the archive's noReset wording. Avoiding accumulation reset is distinct from persistence/reset-to-default behavior, and is valid only when the effect operates downstream of the reusable accumulated data.

The archived modulation chain has attack/decay and smoothing coefficients expressed per update, not in elapsed-time units. For RFF audio-reactive shading, define time constants and deterministic sampling so slower fractal frames do not change the envelope. Validate period, negative-time wrapping, seeds and summation order for LFOs; disabling a source must clear both direct outputs and rules reading cached values. Multiple rules accumulate offsets, so compose the authored base once rather than repeatedly at each rule. Hidden DSP parameters are not evidence of implemented filtering merely because they serialize.

Webcam composition in the archive is a DOM overlay, which does not establish inclusion in a GPU image export or shader color-space pipeline. Audio analysis similarly has distinct signal paths for decks, microphone and system capture; a shared control label does not prove equal gain/analysis semantics. These peripheral features remain optional and lower priority for RFF than existing rendering quality and responsiveness. The actionable shader transfer from this batch is explicit levels/saturation behavior and optional normalized multi-sample color separation, with precision, pass order and export consistency specified.

### Archived Fractal Toy catalog: a minimal 3D baseline, not a 2D deep-zoom engine

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/sibling-apps/fractal-toy-catalog.md` (241 lines). Despite its generic name, the catalog describes a 3D Mandelbulb/Mandelbox raymarcher. It explicitly lacks accumulation, MRT, convergence, history buffers and path tracing. Its small renderer is an architectural baseline, not evidence that those capabilities are unnecessary in GMT or that it replaces RFF's 2D computation engine. Historical code descriptions were not executed in this batch.

The described shader traces up to 200 ray steps with distance limit 20, hit epsilon 0.001 and step factor 0.9. Each distance evaluation iterates at most 32 times; finite-difference normals replay the inner loop at three additional offsets with hStep 0.002. These constants are scene-scale choices, not general precision guarantees. A factor below one does not make an arbitrary distance estimate conservative. Fixed hit and normal offsets can trade away small detail as scale changes. Any adaptation needs an error model appropriate to the represented geometry and viewing scale.

For a 2D RFF relief-shading extension, this suggests deriving normals from an explicitly chosen height-like quantity, with derivatives consistent with pixel spacing and zoom. Neighbor samples from an already-computed map may be much cheaper than replaying the fractal recurrence, but they do not automatically reproduce analytic normals or remain stable at escape/interior discontinuities. Specify missing/invalid samples, border handling, multiresolution behavior and tile halos.
