A 3D DE gradient, a smooth iteration gradient and a screen-space height gradient represent different surfaces; their lighting must not be described interchangeably.

The catalog's AO is based on ray step count. It can add visual depth cues but is not a general geometric ambient-occlusion estimate and can change when tracing parameters change. Do not map RFF's iteration count or MPA work count directly to physical occlusion: those values describe computation/fractal escape behavior, not visibility over a hemisphere. Likewise the final gamma-2.2 operation is a particular output approximation, not a complete display color-management pipeline. Treat Lambert/ambient/step-count shading here as a minimal readability demonstration.

The renderer/schema split is useful when each formula declares its parameters and distance-estimator contract. Mandelbox's r/abs(dr) and Mandelbulb's logarithmic DE are not interchangeable, nor do either formulas automatically supply RFF perturbation/MPA support. UI iteration limits must agree with actual loop limits; changing a slider maximum does not change a hard-coded ceiling. Formula identity should survive any case normalization, and an unknown saved ID should not silently select the first registered formula when faithful restoration is expected.

RFF shader replacement should compile and validate a candidate before retiring the last working pipeline. The archived delete-old-before-compile sequence illustrates a failure path where rendering stops even though only the new candidate is invalid. Clearing a compiling indicator on every exit is good status cleanup but does not mean compilation succeeded. Feature injection also needs the real configuration contract; passing an empty cast object is not proof that future features can safely compose. A renderer behind the same import/API shape can still differ in initialization, synchronization and output semantics.

The resize path trades interactive pixel resolution for speed by shrinking the drawing buffer, which must remain visibly distinct from final-quality output and must not lower arithmetic precision. Zero-sized windows should suspend or defer allocation coherently; frame callbacks count submitted rendering activity unless GPU completion is separately measured. The archive's preserveDrawingBuffer requirement describes its chosen browser capture path, not a universal requirement for screenshots; RFF's Vulkan export should use its explicit render-target/readback lifetime instead. This review adds adaptation constraints and no measured speedup or new 2D formula implementation.

### Archived shared controls: preserve numeric meaning through every edit route

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/engine/shared-ui.md` (288 lines). This is an architecture/API review of historical scalar/vector controls and compile sections, not a screenshot-based usability audit. Earlier aspirational context APIs are explicitly distinguished from the implementations described here. Historical missing-provider and coupling observations are not asserted as current RFF defects.

For RFF shader controls, keep the authored numeric value separate from its display mapping. A logarithmic slider should transform coordinates once; passing already-mapped bounds through another mapper produces different semantics. Define parse/format round trips, units, valid domains and soft slider limits separately from hard mathematical limits. Merely displaying fewer digits must not quantize a saved shader value or precise location on an untouched edit. Text entry, drag, reset, animation and preset load should share validation and the same underlying value representation.

Composite vector inputs must decompose into canonical scalar fields before both ordinary and staged-update routing. However, dispatching each axis individually does not by itself make the operation atomic: RFF should group a multi-axis gesture or reset into one coherent update and undo transaction. Preserve unmodified axes from the correct base state. The same canonical IDs should connect controls, live-value indicators, animation tracks and shader writes; display labels and array position should not determine bindings.

Staged compile settings should evaluate visibility and dependent bounds against the same staged configuration they display. Mixing a forced local state with live global predicates can show controls for a configuration other than the one being prepared. A pending toggle, current runtime enable and compiled capability are distinct states. Writing compile/runtime flags in one host setter prevents one kind of intermediate state but does not prove the asynchronously compiled pipeline is ready; activate the new pipeline and compatible bindings only upon successful completion, retaining the prior valid output on failure.

A fixed timer that waits for an engine panel to mount is not a completion barrier. RFF should route compile requests through a renderer/scheduler capability independent of whether a settings panel is visible. Defaults and overrides also need a deliberate merge rule: an absent override should not erase a feature default, while an explicit null/disabled value may have a distinct meaning. Validation should live at the shared operation boundary rather than exist only on one UI route that other callers bypass.

Optional interaction callbacks can support reusable controls, but silent no-op fallback means a moving slider is not proof that undo and context actions are integrated. Verify one start/end transaction across mouse, keyboard, direct text commit, cancellation and focus loss. Keep required capabilities explicit for the RFF host. Narrow subscriptions can reduce update fan-out, but an imperative global read alone does not arrange a rerender when that dependency changes; track the actual dependencies of dynamic conditions instead of assuming that reduced subscriptions preserve correctness.

The two-canvas animation editor described here separates static curves from a frequently changing playhead. That pattern transfers to RFF overlays: redraw transient markers without regenerating a fractal map, but invalidate cached backgrounds for every relevant curve, viewport, theme or sizing change. Lazy gradient previews similarly need cache keys covering the full palette definition and rendering settings. These are potential responsiveness improvements requiring measurement, not proof that moving work into a different UI abstraction improves GPU speed.

For 3D-to-2D transfer, retain common scalar/vector editing and parameter transactions while avoiding unnecessary 3D rotation gizmos. Existing RFF OKLab interpolation remains an existing capability; the archive's color-space rationale is not evidence that RFF needs that feature added. This batch adds control-to-renderer consistency requirements and no visual or performance test result.

### Archived Fluid Toy catalog: direct 2D transfer with separate numerical and visual contracts

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/archive/sibling-apps/fluid-toy-catalog.md` (543 lines in two complete chunks). This catalog describes a 2D Julia/Mandelbrot-driven fluid pipeline, its shaders, deep-zoom worker, gestures and export. File listings and historical quality/precision claims are not new execution evidence; referenced source files do not gain coverage merely by appearing in the catalog.

For RFF, the direct visual candidates are scalar-field color mappings, gradient LUTs, optional refraction-like image displacement, and multi-output separation of fractal quantities from final appearance. A force field driving fluid motion is an artistic use of fractal data, not an improvement to the numerical Mandelbrot calculation. If adapted as a separate effect, preserve the original map and label the displaced/composited result accordingly. Refraction and caustic-style controls here do not establish a physically traced 3D optical simulation.

The architecture separates full view synchronization from c-only modulation so a shader animation cannot overwrite an in-progress gesture's center/zoom. RFF should assign ownership to transient navigation and authored settings, merge only the fields an operation owns, and produce a coherent snapshot for saving/exporting mid-gesture. Bypassing the store until pointer-up can improve interaction cost but requires cancellation, focus-loss and teardown handling; a delayed commit must not overwrite a newer preset or animation frame. Subscription fan-out can be expensive, but it alone does not prove an infinite React update loop without an actual feedback cycle.

The deep-zoom path uses a reference orbit plus LA/AT under specific formula restrictions, with a separate mantissa/exponent representation for tiny shader values. RFF's MPA derives skips from periodic structure and is not BLA or this catalog's LA implementation. Do not replace its precision or algorithm merely because another renderer exposes similar acceleration toggles. A UI minimum scale of 1e-300 does not prove that double-double center navigation resolves distinct points there: exponent range and significand precision are different limits. Similarly, a high-precision reference cannot recover coordinate information lost before its construction. Preserve RFF's existing exact center and validated perturbation equations end to end.

Superseded worker results need generation-aware rejection, but a canceled closure alone does not prove the worker stopped spending CPU time or released transferred/GPU resources. Validate the reference payload against the current formula, view and iteration requirements before activation. Diagnostics should distinguish building, uploading, usable reference and rendered output. GPU timer queries need readiness/disjoint handling and sample attribution; an EWMA-smoothed number is useful telemetry but not an A/B benchmark or proof of end-to-end responsiveness.

The catalog couples display and simulation grid resolution. That means an adaptive resize can change the simulated dynamics, not just the sharpness of presentation. A proposed RFF decorative simulation should separate those roles if stable behavior is required. For ordinary RFF maps, dynamic preview resolution must remain separate from final computation and arithmetic precision. A claimed clean image after 64 TSAA samples is scene-dependent, and a sample-cap fraction used to gate adaptation is not a convergence certificate.

The nested image-tile/sub-bucket export preserves full-output aspect and world mapping, but its described RGBA8 stitching and absence of per-tile bloom do not guarantee parity with the interactive HDR/post-effect path. RFF tiling needs full-image coordinates, sufficient neighborhood borders and a consistent color/output pipeline. Gradient LUT versions should invalidate precisely the caches containing their effects; when raw numerical maps are stored separately, palette changes can reuse those maps. Initializing each preset from defaults avoids state leakage, but must not erase deliberate persistent settings outside the preset's documented scope.

For video, separate simulation advancement from repeated antialias samples of one frame. Freeze the simulated state while sampling, advance by the defined timestep exactly once, and specify whether frame zero represents pre-step or post-step state. Reproducibility also requires initial simulation state, seeds, modulation timing and a bounded/stable integration scheme; calling a ratchet deterministic does not prove all of them. Saved-view smooth transitions likewise need exact high/low or arbitrary-precision interpolation, not just a final precise endpoint. The archive's constant-screen-speed paired-pan claim has the scale/time assumptions documented earlier in this report.

Optional brush/particle effects should preserve spatial stroke density independently of pointer event frequency and preserve timestep semantics independently of preview FPS. The described two-radius collision probes improve selected thin-wall cases but do not guarantee that particles cannot tunnel across a boundary. These effects are exploratory additions, below core shading quality and correctness in RFF priority. Any adaptation of the explicitly FractalShark-derived or named bloom/noise material requires source/license provenance verification and NOTICE synchronization; no code was copied in this batch.

### March architecture snapshot: distinguish historical milestones from shader evidence

Fully reviewed: `docs/history/archive/context2.md` (171 lines). The document explicitly identifies itself as a March 2026 snapshot. Its DDFS-complete and 64/64-importer-test claims describe that historical scope; they do not establish current comprehensive shader correctness or this audit's coverage. The embedded test command was not executed. Mixed V2 usage instructions and V3 status also require following the actual importer path rather than inferring a single current API from the snapshot.

For RFF, the stable architectural idea is separating formula/iteration injection from image postprocessing and deriving parameter plumbing consistently. Registry-driven saving does not make a format future-proof without versioned semantics, exact numeric representation and explicit ownership of fields outside that registry. The snapshot itself recognizes lighting as a custom interaction surface despite schema-driven parameters, supporting the same split for RFF's specialized palette or location controls.

The path-tracing section lists all-light next-event estimation, environment sampling, volumetric scatter and a per-sample luminance clamp. Their mechanisms have different tradeoffs: evaluating more lights changes sampling cost and variance, whereas clipping bright samples changes the estimator's expected output. A firefly clamp should not be marketed as unbiased noise removal. Environment sampling must use matching densities/weights in the actual integrator; a toggle name or one-extra-ray description is not a proof of correct importance sampling. None of these 3D integrator features is directly applicable to a flat RFF escape map. A 2D highlight limiter would be an explicitly artistic or output-range operation, not the same estimator treatment.

The snapshot calls every listed PT quality parameter compile-time even though one is represented as a uniform. Declaration form and update policy are independent; the current scheduler and shader must determine which changes really require a new pipeline. RFF should not add expensive compilation merely to imitate that historical table. The bounce-zero-only rim-light note similarly describes a particular nonphysical artistic term's placement in a 3D integrator, not a transferable requirement for 2D relief shading.

AST transformation reduces classes of token-substitution mistakes but does not eliminate all import bugs. Scope, initialization lifetime, helper dependencies, loop semantics and output quantities still need validation. A statement that initialization inlining is implemented but untested on real files is explicitly incomplete evidence, regardless of nearby green status labels. This reinforces the earlier requirement that arbitrary GLSL acceptance does not imply perturbation or MPA compatibility.

The vector controls' one-decimal display and six-decimal text-entry policy must not become RFF storage precision. A formatting limit can be acceptable for presentation only when an unchanged edit preserves the original value and exact input remains possible where needed. Alt-drag bypassing step quantization improves granularity but does not increase arithmetic precision. Declare angular units and topology explicitly rather than detecting them only from parameter names; preserve canonical track IDs despite abbreviated historical axis examples. These are 2D-compatible editing lessons, with no new implementation or runtime result.

### Wave editing smoke: observable palette previews and reversible shader controls

Source reviewed in full: `debug/smoke-ge-wave.mts` (667 lines). This is a browser test definition, not a shader implementation or a fresh test result. Its header records historical mutation experiments; those experiments were not rerun in this review.

- **Transfer to RFF:** use a single reversible editing session for procedural palette waves and multi-control color adjustments. Capture the pre-session state once, show intermediate changes, commit one undo entry, and restore the original state on cancellation. Nested drag sessions or a panel-close bake must retain the original snapshot. Delayed recent-palette persistence must not inject unrelated library changes into the open editing transaction. These principles apply directly to 2D Mandelbrot coloring without changing perturbation or MPA calculations; new recipe behavior must respect RFF's frozen recipe IDs and RNG sequence.
- **Test the visible result while input remains active.** The script samples the working RGB ramp and 48 pixels from the hero's 2D canvas during an eight-move amplitude drag. It requires at least seven distinct ramp samples and four distinct hero samples, in addition to changes at moves four and eight. This can detect a release-only preview even when numeric controls update correctly. In RFF, extend the observable chain to the uploaded palette resource and the rendered Vulkan image at the same state revision. A CPU ramp or separate palette canvas alone does not prove that the fractal shader consumed the new data. Double `requestAnimationFrame` is a browser scheduling aid, not a Vulkan completion fence.
- **Capture must survive leaving the control.** Four square handles are deliberately dragged outside the overlay while the mouse button remains down; capture acquisition, absence of premature capture loss, and continued numeric progression are checked. This distinguishes proper capture from events merely bubbling within the overlay. RFF's native controls need the equivalent outside-control drag and release checks. Pixel-to-parameter conversion must use the actual plot transform, including margins and zoom; the smoke separately compares handle displacement against the 96-pixel pointer displacement with a two-pixel tolerance.
- **Cancellation should survive focus loss and delayed background work.** Separate cases press Escape with focus in the tool and after arming has removed the focused toolbar button. A dropdown consumes the first Escape; the editing session consumes the next. Dwell cases exceed the documented recent-item debounce before canceling. Adopt the ownership and transaction invariants rather than the particular 700 ms delay: deterministic tests should establish that the relevant delayed work actually became eligible or ran. This script explicitly does not prove that deferred persistence is eventually flushed after the session closes.
- **Color-domain tests need targeted edge cases.** The seeded gradient starts near red, and a hue wave crosses zero. The smoke checks that HSV conversion preserves substantial saturation and does not introduce near-black texels; cancellation compares the serialized unrounded RGB ramp exactly. For RFF, exercise negative and multi-turn hue wrapping, percent-versus-unit S/V scaling, and the final shader transfer function independently. The smoke's allowed RGB difference of 16 and saturation thresholds are regression tolerances for this chosen gradient, not a colorimetric accuracy standard. Its ramp equality proves sampled RGB restoration, not equality of all editing metadata, HDR values, or high-precision fractal coordinates.
- **Controls make negative assertions credible.** An unarmed double-click is required to add a key, showing that the armed-mode no-add test can observe the behavior. Conversely, the header reports that removing underlying editor guards still passed while the overlay intercepted input: passing behavior does not identify which layer enforces it. Preserve this distinction when testing shader UI lockouts and disabled controls.
- **Coverage boundary:** this fixed desktop mouse scenario does not establish touch behavior, all display scales, every waveform/preset, shader numerical accuracy, export parity, or GPU performance. The helper resolves the application's already-loaded module URL to avoid querying an independent development-server store instance; the transferable lesson is to inspect the authoritative state instance. Historical PASS text and failure-injection claims are not current execution evidence.

### Phone and desktop smoke: transferable input and export checks, with evidence limits

Source reviewed in full: `debug/smoke-ge-phone.mts` (696 lines). Static inspection only: no browser was launched, no clipboard was modified, and no feedback was submitted. Historical measurements and mutation-test reports in the header are not new validation results.

- **RFF application:** the strongest transfer is resilient palette editing and compact-window behavior, including touch-capable Windows devices. The script distinguishes mouse input from a touch sequence, checks whether a control is actually under its center, and verifies that a dragged palette knot changes working state. For RFF, identify the selected stop by stable ID and assert its expected mapped displacement, ordering constraints, and rendered color update. This smoke only requires that some indexed stop changes by more than 0.01; it does not establish which stop moved correctly, continuous preview, or final shader consumption. These improvements apply directly to 2D rendering and require no 3D geometry.
- **Geometry and reachability are different checks.** The test combines viewport containment with hit testing, and combines overflow size with a scrollable overflow policy. Those are useful independent conditions, but computed styles still do not prove that a user can reach the last item. An RFF equivalent should exercise scrolling and activate the final control. The fixed 390-by-844 phone and 1280-by-800 desktop cases do not cover arbitrary window sizes, high-DPI transitions, virtual keyboards, or all input combinations. The header's phone-without-keyboard assumption is a historical product decision, not a general rule for hiding shortcuts on touch-capable devices.
- **Modal lifetime includes restoration.** The wallpaper overlay test checks gesture ownership and body scroll locking, then compares the pre-open and post-close overflow state. Transfer the ownership model to RFF's gesture capture and temporary input modes: restore the prior owner or mode, including cancellation and nested surfaces. CSS `touch-action` and body overflow themselves are browser-specific. The smoke reads the HTML element's overflow but only asserts body restoration; it should not be cited as proof of complete document-state restoration.
- **Export preview and action must refer to the same output.** A long touch opens a pinned CSS preview without triggering a download; the next ordinary tap must still copy exactly the previewed text, allowing only clipboard CRLF normalization. This is a useful contract for RFF palette text export and shader-parameter previews. Test a shared immutable export snapshot so a changing selection cannot produce preview/action divergence. Do not adopt the specific 800 ms hold threshold or implicit gesture-only discovery as a universal design requirement.
- **A nonblank image is not a correct rendering.** The feedback test downsamples an attached JPEG to 64 by 64 and computes the standard deviation of the unweighted mean of encoded R, G, and B values. Although comments call this luminance spread, it is not linear-light luminance. A value above eight can reject a uniform placeholder but cannot prove that the fractal region is correct, current, or even present: surrounding UI can supply variation. Conversely, a legitimate nearly uniform image can fail. For RFF shader capture validation, compare a known rendered region at the requested frame revision and test orientation, transfer function, dimensions, and GPU-readback completion separately. Screenshot JPEGs are unsuitable as lossless shader-reference images.
- **Attachment semantics should be explicit and independently checked.** The script checks distinct gradient-versus-screenshot document kinds and a selected attachment indicator. It estimates decoded JSON attachment size as floor(0.75 times the base64 length), matching the stated endpoint convention rather than measuring the exact whole network request size. Top-level absence of `config`, or a string search for `data:image`, is not a complete schema or disclosure audit. For a future RFF diagnostic-export feature, build the selected payload from an explicit schema and keep exact location/state export separate from a display screenshot. This recommendation does not authorize sending a report. The source test installs a route interceptor for its feedback endpoint; this review did not execute that route or its Send actions.
- **Attribution needs content, not only a passing label check.** The smoke checks that About exposes attribution, a core credits link resolves with an expected heading, and built-in preset source names appear. These checks can catch missing presentation, but do not establish that every loaded pack is credited, that licenses are compatible, or that distinctive formula provenance is complete. RFF's canonical NOTICE and source-level acknowledgements remain the authoritative records when adapting code, constants, or palettes. App-specific help, seen-version keys, and attachment schemas should remain namespaced when components are shared.
- **Boundary:** this is an integration test of a sibling palette application. It supplies useful acceptance criteria for RFF's palette and export paths, but no new shader algorithm, GPU speedup, precision result, or completed mobile port. Caught UI error fallbacks are inspected separately from uncaught page errors, a useful diagnostic distinction for testing whether an editor actually opened.

### Animation module specification: requirements for reproducible 2D shader animation

Source reviewed in full: `docs/history/animation-refactor/03_SPEC.md` (851 lines), a May 10 design specification with elided bodies and forward-reference types. Its proposed APIs, implementation schedule, historical performance observations, and test requirements do not prove that those implementations exist or pass today. The document's next-action and sign-off language is historical material, not an instruction to implement its refactor in RFF.

1. **Adopt a common evaluation path, with explicit state.** Sharing interpolation and modulation evaluation between preview and offline rendering is valuable for RFF palette phase, exposure, relief strength, and other shader parameters. However, the proposed `evaluateOffsetsAt(doc, magnitudes, time, dt)` is described as pure while its runtime also owns persistent envelope and smoothing values. Equal explicit arguments cannot guarantee equal offsets unless that prior state is also equal or the result is reconstructed from a defined history. Specify a state-in/state-out evaluator, or deterministic replay from a reset/checkpoint, including seek, reverse playback, loop boundaries, and frame zero. Resetting only at bake start does not reproduce an arbitrary live preview's previous history.
2. **Evaluate one immutable frame context before uploading it.** The specification separates track evaluation, modulation, host mapping, and recording. For RFF, combine the resulting shader values into one frame snapshot and upload compatible uniform/descriptor data together. Host-specific mapping can preserve 3D composite parameters in GMT while using palette and 2D view parameters in RFF. A binder that writes one float is not sufficient for a high-precision complex center or a coordinated pan/zoom update. Preserve full-precision values through interpolation and serialization; convert only at the established renderer boundary. This does not alter MPA or justify reduced precision.
3. **A determinism key must include all effective inputs.** The specification promises byte-equal binder writes for `(document version, time)`, but also allows provider binders, hooks, log-track registrations, recorder overrides, and host state. Two different documents can share a numeric version. Cache/evaluation identity therefore needs the document identity or immutable content, relevant provider/algorithm revision, override context, and any dependencies read by hooks. Distinguish deterministic values from an identical sequence of emitted writes: a last-value cache may intentionally suppress redundant writes without changing the rendered result.
4. **Separate seconds, frames, and parameter precision.** Storing key times in seconds and branding time/frame APIs can prevent unit mistakes, but type casts alone do not validate finite values or positive FPS. The document simultaneously says that `matchTime` preserves output at the same seconds and drives a time-remap patch. A seconds-based RFF animation should normally preserve key times when only output sampling FPS changes; an actual speed change or frame-locking policy is a separate operation. Derived frame bounds depend on FPS as well as track version, so a cache keyed only by track version is insufficient after an FPS change. Define whether an export of N frames uses indices 0 through N-1 or includes an endpoint; the proposed inclusive bake range must not silently add a video frame.
5. **A version number is not a recording snapshot.** `SnapshotHandle` is shown as only `{docVersion}`, while evaluation accepts an `AnimationDocument`. RFF needs retained immutable data or a resolvable versioned store, with a lifetime spanning the bake, to guarantee that editing during recording cannot change the reference sequence. A label naming an old version cannot reconstruct discarded values. This is a missing detail in the historical specification, not evidence of a current GMT failure.
6. **Cancellation must restore data, not merely discard undo bookkeeping.** The bake design appends keys in chunks inside one transaction and promises no partial commit on cancellation. Its history API describes discarding an open transaction but does not state how already-visible mutations are reversed. For RFF, stage generated keys before publication or apply inverse changes atomically on cancellation/error. Include exceptions, nested transactions, and concurrent edits in that contract. Time-based 400 ms coalescing is useful for repeated edits but cannot by itself guarantee one undo entry for a long drag; use explicit gesture boundaries and preserve the earliest inverse state.
7. **Audio parity requires matching the analysis pipeline.** A common magnitude-array type does not equate live and offline FFT results. Fix the source samples, timeline placement, gain/crossfade, windowing, FFT normalization, frequency-bin interpretation, smoothing history, and byte-range conversion. Treat a documented tolerance as an acceptance criterion to measure, not an achieved result. For deterministic offline 2D shader animation, use prepared audio analysis indexed by the exact export time or replay with known state; do not consume the live analyser's current sample. Stateful audio smoothing also needs defined warm-up on random seeks.
8. **Keep useful ownership boundaries without copying unsupported guarantees.** Explicit dependencies, narrow change notifications, no-op gates, typed binders, and provider teardown can reduce redundant work and stale bindings. Separate maps do not make evaluation of all tracks O(1); every active track still needs processing. The recommended bare construction plus `init()` pattern checks boot order at runtime, despite a later sentence claiming type-system enforcement. Readonly TypeScript views do not by themselves ensure deep immutability. In RFF, verify provider collision policy, cleanup ownership, re-entrancy, error handling, and precise no-op comparison rather than relying on architectural labels.

**Practical priority:** retain the shared preview/export evaluator and atomic frame snapshot as concrete adoption targets. Use a small deterministic fixture to compare final shader inputs and rendered output across sequential playback, direct seeks, and offline export. The archived module rewrite and its estimated schedule are not necessary prerequisites for adopting those contracts in RFF. The mechanisms apply directly to 2D shader animation; GMT-specific camera split handling should be adapted to RFF's existing high-precision coordinate representation rather than copied as a precision limit.

### Historical harvest batch B: current-source corrections and bounded shader adoption claims

Reviewed all 271 lines of `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/state/harvest/batch-B.md`. This is a proposed documentation-harvest plan, not a current implementation inventory. Targeted current-source checks were also made in `engine/UniformSchema.ts`, `engine/plugins/Shortcuts.ts`, and `engine/RenderPipeline.ts`; these already-reviewed files are not counted again. No historical commands, source-edit proposals, or runtime tests were executed.

- **Uniform validation is an adoption reference, not an unresolved GMT defect.** The harvest claims base/feature collisions are silently filtered and feature/feature collisions overwrite defaults. Current `engine/UniformSchema.ts` explicitly throws for both cases before constructing `UNIFORM_SCHEMA`. Preserve the previously established correction in this report. For RFF, the useful extension is an explicit host/shader interface contract covering binding, type, count, offsets and layout, in addition to semantic-name collisions. A name check alone does not verify Vulkan ABI compatibility. The harvest's claim that even a types-only import necessarily executes registration is also too broad: an erased type-only import does not evaluate the module.
- **Do not infer dispatch priority from confident historical comments.** The harvest says later registrations win equal shortcut scores. Current `Shortcuts.ts` sorts descending by score and returns `matches[0]`, and documents stable insertion order and FIRST-registered precedence. Replacing an existing Map entry retains its position. RFF should make scope/priority/tie policy explicit when binding shader and palette controls, particularly Undo and cancellation; copying the historical explanation would invert that policy. This supports the earlier source-based finding rather than a new GMT bug claim.
- **Compile-target matching is not a measured speedup.** Current `RenderPipeline.ts` explicitly corrects the harvest's Three.js program-hash explanation: the target texture type is not the claimed input to that hash. Its comment describes a possible backend output-signature effect and states that the RGBA16F/RGBA32F performance difference has not been measured. The actual getter recreates a compile target when its type no longer matches the live target. For RFF, preserve the compatible pipeline/render-target configuration and resource lifetime needed by its Vulkan path, but assign no performance percentage to this historical warm-up rationale without measurement. Retaining a target across asynchronous compilation is a lifetime contract, not proof that every format requires a different compiled shader.
- **A fence makes readiness polling nonblocking, not all readback free.** The current convergence path inserts a GPU fence, polls with zero timeout, and then calls `readRenderTargetPixels` on success. It handles `WAIT_FAILED` by clearing the pending fence and returning the last result. This can avoid waiting for unfinished rendering, but the subsequent transfer/conversion and CPU scan still have costs; a returned previous value is not a fresh measurement. For a RFF diagnostic or adaptive sampling feature, use a revision-tagged result with explicit fresh/pending/failed state, bounded staging resources, and completion-aware readback. Measure transfer overhead separately from polling. Apply convergence only to stochastic sampling or progressive image estimates that justify it, not as a substitute for Mandelbrot iteration precision or MPA correctness.
- **Gate optional diagnostics by actual consumers.** The harvest's consumer-driven convergence idea remains useful for 2D histogram, variance, or render-quality diagnostics: do work only while it is needed. Multiple panels require balanced ownership or subscriptions rather than a single component clearing a shared boolean. A default or stale numeric value must not masquerade as a measured result. This is a conditional architectural recommendation, not a claim that RFF currently runs unnecessary convergence passes.
- **Keep established adaptation limits.** The paired pan/zoom formula in this harvest provides constant screen-space speed only under the associated scale/time assumptions already explained in this report; double-double interpolation is not sufficient for arbitrary RFF deep zoom. The deterministic-preview backlog discard is a responsiveness policy, not evidence that offline export may skip frames. The shared-fullscreen-geometry ownership note transfers to RFF resource ownership; the WebGL scissor-after-target-binding rule must be translated to the actual Vulkan command/state model rather than copied literally. The harvest itself marks the old bloom-header discrepancy clean, so it is not a remaining improvement candidate.

The value of this material is the set of contracts to preserve when adopting shader infrastructure. Its proposed documentation cleanup and historical GMT defects are not the objective of this RFF improvement review.

### Historical harvest batch C: adaptive preview cost and precise snapshot boundaries

Read `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/state/harvest/batch-C.md` in full (338 lines), including rereading the portion omitted by output truncation. Also rechecked the current activity-input and full-resolution-cost portions of the already-reviewed `engine/AdaptiveResolution.ts`. Historical proposed comments and ADRs are evidence of design intent, not current tests or instructions to edit GMT.

- **Current adaptive logic is more specific than the harvest.** The inspected implementation now distinguishes explicit interaction from accumulation-drop inference using `ignoreAccumDrop` and `gateOnAccumOnly`, and can sample cost only while interacting through `costSampleInteractingOnly`. It also accepts an explicit grace override. For RFF, declare which input gestures change the rendered view or shader output; distinguish those changes from UI-only activity and from a renderer's own resize/reset. Otherwise a resolution change can trigger another apparent activity event. Avoid simultaneously selecting mutually contradictory activity policies.
- **The full-resolution estimate has an important model boundary.** Current code normalizes tick duration as `frameMs * scale * scale`, where scale is a downsample factor, and smooths accepted samples as 0.7 times the previous estimate plus 0.3 times the new sample. Samples above four times the existing estimate are clamped, limiting one accepted update to 1.9 times the old estimate. Samples at or below 17.5 ms are treated as potentially cadence-limited and generally cannot raise the estimate; an unseeded full-resolution estimate is a documented exception. These guards reduce contamination by pacing and stalls but do not turn a tick interval into measured GPU execution time.
- **Adapt the model to RFF's actual work.** Pixel-area normalization can approximate a full-screen shader whose cost is dominated by per-pixel work. RFF also has high-precision reference generation, MPA preparation, uploads, and potentially nonuniform per-pixel iteration work. A fixed setup cost multiplied by scale squared would inflate the estimate; cheap display-only or partial-tile frames can bias it in the opposite direction. Separate computation, upload, and post-processing measurements, associate observations with the view and workload, and verify whether resolution scaling improves the active bottleneck before applying this heuristic. It is suitable for an optional interactive preview policy, not for lowering fractal precision or treating a low-resolution preview as final output.
- **Restore exact output deliberately.** The harvest's hold semantics allow quality recovery while blocking further downscaling, and its self-resize distinction is useful. For RFF, interaction completion should request the intended full-quality image and invalidate incompatible preview samples. Export must use its requested dimensions and sampling settings independently of a viewport's temporary adaptive factor. Validate physical pixel dimensions, including DPI and borders, rather than treating a UI rectangle as the saved image size. These ideas apply directly to 2D Mandelbrot rendering; no 3D DE loop cap should be copied into RFF's iteration or precision settings.
- **View libraries need typed, precision-preserving capture.** The harvest separates lightweight camera slots from richer snapshot libraries. The useful 3D-to-2D transfer is an adapter that captures a coherent RFF center, scale, palette, and chosen shader settings, with explicit ownership and stable IDs. Opaque JSON and JSON-based cloning are not a guarantee of high-precision round trips. Serialize precise coordinates through RFF's established representation, make thumbnail and saved state refer to one revision, and reject incompatible payloads. A successful toast does not establish durable persistence, and a controlled list component does not by itself supply delete undo.
- **Do not carry forward inaccurate historical guarantees.** `m.apply(preset) ?? preset` falls back only for null/undefined, not every falsy value; catching an exception does not roll back in-place mutation. Module-scope variables alone do not guarantee HMR persistence. A live audio deck that free-runs without a corrective seek is not guaranteed to reconverge with the timeline on the next tick. These repeat earlier report cautions and remain reasons to define RFF's migration, snapshot, and animation contracts explicitly rather than copying the harvest wording.
- **Separate a renderer capability from a placeholder API.** The worker portion describes a core stub and even combines a historical unbooted symptom with an immediate-boot stub method. Neither description is evidence that GMT's real worker fails. For RFF, initialization success, export support, rendered-frame readiness, and cancellation completion should be distinct states. Overlay or picker snapshots need the same view revision as the displayed image; installing a new provider does not update a previously captured object reference automatically. Multi-window use should keep such state per renderer.

This material strengthens the conditions for adaptive 2D preview, shader-control snapshots, and export parity. It does not establish a measured speedup or require a new parallel camera library in RFF.

### Historical harvest batch D: shader replacement and tiled-output contracts for RFF

Read all 376 lines of `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/state/harvest/batch-D.md`, recovering the truncated shader-assembly/ADR passage separately. This historical harvest covers features, mobile layout, the GMT renderer, shader assembly, and bucket/video export. Its compile times, browser limitations, proposed invariants, and performance descriptions were not benchmarked here; cited source filenames do not count as newly reviewed files.

- **Publish a shader together with its compatible parameter layout.** The harvest describes retaining the current shader while a replacement compiles, and postponing modular-array remapping until the replacement is installed. This is directly relevant to future RFF shader variants: stage the pipeline, bindings, and associated values as one compatible generation. Keep the old generation intact until the replacement is ready; retire resources only after submitted work no longer references them. A generation counter rejects stale publication but does not cancel underlying compilation or establish GPU resource completion. The harvest's statement that synchronous JavaScript portions can race needs care: ordinary event-loop callbacks do not interleave within a synchronous call stack; yields, re-entrancy, or independently shared state must identify the actual hazard.
- **Adapt feature dependencies, not the literal 17-stage 3D layout.** GMT's documented positions separate DE construction, materials, tracing, integration, and post-processing. RFF's 2D shader composition needs its own explicit dependency order for map sampling, palette mapping, relief/lighting, filtering, and output conversion. Disabled features need defined interfaces when callers remain, or callers must be removed consistently. An empty stub is only correct when its return value is the intended neutral operation. Exact-string deduplication is not symbol-conflict detection; distinct formatting of the same function can still collide. Use stable chunk identities and validate generated variants. The historical silent-uniform-collision claim remains superseded by the source corrections already recorded in this report.
- **Derive frame parameters after choosing the actual render geometry.** The harvest emphasizes resize and tile setup before pixel-footprint calculation. For RFF, compute sampling offsets, derivative spacing, and filter radii from an explicit full-output coordinate system plus the tile origin and internal sampling scale. Otherwise a 2D relief normal or edge effect can change with tile size. Preserve high-precision center/scale independently of pixel-grid bookkeeping. GMT's toward-light direction convention transfers to optional 2D relief shading only with a defined normal orientation and coordinate system; it is not physical illumination of a flat escape-time map by itself.
- **Tiled export needs global coordinates and filter support beyond tile edges.** The documented full-output resolution stays constant while image tiles and smaller GPU work regions change. That distinction is useful for RFF large-image export. Use global positions for palette phase, grain/dither, procedural effects, and sample sequences, and provide overlap or a shared intermediate for spatial filters. Scissoring can reduce raster work outside a region, but does not remove the need for correct sampling bounds and halos. Restore viewport, scissor, region, and pixel-size overrides on success, cancellation, and failure. The harvest's percentage-threshold wording is not a proof that a fractional value can never converge: passing a fraction to an API that divides by 100 instead makes the threshold much stricter.
- **Give data passes explicit meanings.** The harvest describes alpha sometimes carrying distance and other export passes carrying coverage. RFF should keep iteration data, distance estimates, validity, and image alpha semantically distinct even if storage is reused between mutually exclusive passes. Associate readback with pass, format, dimensions, and frame generation; “previous target” alone does not prove that its data matches the requested operation. A 3D depth picker is generally unnecessary for a 2D complex-plane view, while the synchronization and format-size contracts still apply to map diagnostics and export readback. Histogram absence should be represented as unavailable rather than as a measured empty distribution.
- **Share color math across output drivers, with explicit encoding.** Separate still-image and video scheduling can be sensible while sharing shader post-processing. Verify that each path applies the intended transfer function once, and excludes artistic grading/filtering from numerical data passes. A fixed bitrate multiplier or browser-specific cap in this historical document is not a universal quality setting for RFF. Independently normalizing the first timestamp of audio and video can alter their intended relative offset unless that offset is restored elsewhere; preserve a shared media timeline when extending video export. A cleanup method being idempotent does not by itself settle pending file writes or encoder work.
- **Modulation must return to baseline when disabled.** The harvest's additive-rule model requires clearing per-frame offsets before summing enabled rules, and suppressing both source updates and consumption of stale source values when an LFO is off. For RFF animated palette/lighting parameters, make this a shared preview/export evaluation rule, with explicit phase units and negative-time wrapping. These are optional animation features, not changes to reference-orbit or MPA precision. Browser mobile-layout policies in the same harvest are not prerequisites for adopting the shader mechanisms in native RFF.

The practical contribution is a set of compatibility and image-consistency requirements for richer 2D shaders and large exports. It does not establish new speed measurements or request fixes to GMT.

### Historical harvest batch E: formula extensibility without weakening RFF precision

Read all 445 lines of `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/state/harvest/batch-E.md`, rereading the truncated registry ADR passage. This is a historical documentation proposal spanning navigation, registries, graph compilation, serialization, features, camera libraries, and formula import. The final ADR renumbering differs from earlier references in the same file; those draft numbers are not stable evidence identifiers. No proposed edits or catalog-generation commands were executed.

- **A 2D effect graph is the more direct adoption target.** The harvest's modular graph illustrates live-node elimination, ordered execution, and runtime parameter packing. RFF can use those ideas for palette transforms, relief shading, masks, and post-processing while retaining its existing fractal computation. Generate one binding plan keyed by node and parameter identity, and use it for both shader references and host writes; relying on template call order matching a separately walked input list is unnecessarily fragile. Reject overflow and cycles at every graph-import boundary. The reported fallback `z.xyz += c.xyz; trap = min(trap, length(z.xyz))` is not an identity operation, despite the harvest's label. A disconnected RFF effect graph should have an explicit pass-through or invalid-state policy.
- **Formula capability is separate from successful GLSL compilation.** Self-contained DE functions and outer-loop per-iteration formulas support different composition contracts. Arbitrary imported GLSL does not supply perturbation equations, valid MPA skip behavior, or high-precision derivatives automatically. For any future RFF formula importer, state which precision/computation modes and observables are supported. Orbit-trap minima cannot generally be reconstructed from only MPA skip endpoints. A formula rejected as 2D by a 3D SDE importer can still be relevant to RFF; rejection by that pipeline is not a judgment of its 2D usefulness.
- **Preserve source and transformation metadata for re-editing.** A compiled formula alone does not preserve editable source, dependency versions, parameter mappings, loop extraction choices, and defaults. The harvest's V3/V4 re-edit distinction reinforces the need for a versioned import record if RFF adds custom effects. Validate identifiers beyond stripping punctuation: empty names, leading digits, reserved identifiers, and collisions remain possible. Treat a catalog recommendation as a result for a particular importer revision and test set, not a guarantee for arbitrary pasted source. A 3D SDE preview need not share RFF's high-precision execution path.
- **Saved appearance needs both capabilities and scene state.** Preserve every behavior-relevant shader flag, referenced definition, precise coordinate, and effect parameter required to reconstruct the image. A fallback to scene-only JSON is not self-contained if the formula is unavailable. Decode and validate before atomically activating a preset; protect existing definitions from accidental ID collisions. The harvest repeats the false BOM warning: `trimStart()` removes U+FEFF, so that prefix claim is not evidence of a BOM failure. Literal closing tags in a regex-delimited shader container are a separate issue. RFF's existing ConfigIO and palette-recipe stability rules still govern any adopted settings.
- **Keep coordinate precision distinct from representation management.** The harvest describes recentering and split coordinates, but its statement that Three.js `camera.position` itself is f32 conflates JavaScript numeric state with typical GPU float representation. For RFF, preserve its established high-precision center throughout navigation, animation, history and serialization. A coordinate rebase must not change the represented view; asynchronous results need a relevant view generation, not only an absorb counter. Fixed absolute dirty tolerances such as 0.0001 are inappropriate for arbitrary deep zoom. Use exact saved-state comparison where required, or a separately defined screen-space significance test for display-only indicators.
- **Treat compile gates and namespace rules as explicit contracts.** The historical AreaLights/ANGLE rationale does not establish that Vulkan should use the same compile-time switch. Measure each expensive alternative in RFF and choose runtime controls versus pipeline variants accordingly. Sharing canonical shader chunks and mutable-state namespaces avoids duplicated definitions, but Map replacement does not inherently reorder an existing key as the harvest's historical explanation implies. Validate actual dependency order rather than relying on that narrative. Distinguish staged settings from the values applied by the active shader so previews, saved presets, and exports refer to an intentional state.

These findings refine earlier recommendations rather than adding new claimed shader speedups. The most directly transferable mechanisms are stable graph bindings, reproducible effect imports, precise view snapshots, and explicit shader capability metadata; copying GMT's 3D formula pipeline wholesale is not required.

Consequently, a historical audit's completion percentage or a followup's existence cannot establish that the present source has been fully inspected or that its claims remain correct. This RFF adoption report continues to rely on its own file inventory and source checks. Referenced files do not become read-in-full merely because a historical writer claimed them.

### Earlier architecture-document survey: preserve rationale without promoting aspirations

Read `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_docs/d01-engine-docs-1.md` in full (159 lines). It summarizes ten historical engine documents and explicitly labels many APIs as possibly stale or aspirational. Its frontmatter references and claimed read ranges do not add those source documents to this audit's completed count.

The useful RFF transfer is a separation of shared effect controls from renderer-specific computation: a common parameter schema can drive controls, serialization, animation and shader bindings, while the precision and quality policy remain owned by RFF. The survey's proposed six automatic derivations, bridge/derive APIs, capability registry, and viewport hooks are not evidence that all those facilities shipped. Adopt a concrete contract only where it solves an RFF need; a wholesale framework migration is not a prerequisite for improved shading.

The survey also reinforces three limits already established here. First, OKLab is already available in RFF and must not be ranked as a new feature merely because the historical document advocates it; neither OKLab nor RGB interpolation has universally superior artistic results. Second, whole-gradient crossfade and interpolation of individual stops are different operations. Any proposed animated-palette extension should define interpolation space, stop correspondence, cyclic hue treatment, and how saved recipe identities remain stable, rather than silently changing recipe generation. Third, double-double tween arithmetic and logarithmic scale interpolation are useful mechanisms, but an approximate 1e-32 precision claim is not an absolute-coordinate guarantee for arbitrary magnitudes or sufficient for RFF's deepest views.

The historical arguments for separate undo scopes, explicit dependencies, and narrow subscriptions supply design alternatives, not proof that one history model eliminates every interaction ambiguity. Similarly, the suggested generic quality fraction cannot define what RFF may reduce: temporary sampling resolution, reference precision, and iteration/MPA correctness are distinct concerns. This survey adds architectural context, not a newly verified shader optimization, measured benefit, or implementation requirement.

Read five previously pending files in full: `.gitignore`, `debug/.gitignore`, `.claude/settings.json`, `debug/compat-snapshot.jsonl`, and `debug/interaction-latency-baseline.json`. The editor permissions/hooks are configuration data for another tool; they were neither executed nor treated as authorization. Ignore rules describe repository packaging intent, not proof that files are absent from this downloaded tree.

The compatibility snapshot contains two cases: JuliaMorph and MandelTerrain disable geometry's `preRotMaster` because of `shape:self-contained`. This is evidence of those recorded decisions only, not an exhaustive feature/formula matrix. For RFF, expose a specific unsupported-capability reason when a proposed shader effect needs data the selected computation path does not produce. Missing compatibility rows must not imply universal support, particularly for orbit-derived effects across MPA skips.

The interaction baseline records five camera and five slider gestures under a legacy model, with target 30 FPS and configured full-resolution time 66 ms. Camera engagement latencies are 330, 66, 66, 66, and 66 ms; sliders never engage in that artifact. A targeted recheck of the already-reviewed harness confirms that frame duration is calculated as `FULL_RES_MS / (sim.scale * sim.scale)`: these are simulation outputs, not GPU or end-to-end input-to-display measurements. Its `fpsReachedTarget` permits a relative error below 10%, explaining why 27.8 FPS passes a 30 FPS target. The five-sample p95 is not a reliable hardware latency characterization. Use the fixture to understand gesture coverage; do not transfer its milliseconds or improvement rates to RFF. Real validation must include render completion/presentation and workloads whose fixed reference/MPA costs violate the model's pure pixel-area scaling.

The root ignore file documents that some palette baking inputs live outside the repository, while selected baked core assets and credits are retained and optional packs are fetched separately. For an RFF palette-library extension, preserve a reproducible source/version manifest, bundle the matching credits, and specify offline behavior. Do not infer an individual palette's adaptation or redistribution permission from an aggregate pack name or these comments. Likewise, ignored benchmark outputs and a named tracked reference image do not prove that a fresh benchmark ran or that its comparison covers all shaders.

Eight files were read in full: `debug/palette-upload-manifest.json`, `engine-gmt/tsconfig.json`, and six files under `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/Examples/`: `.gitmodules`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`, `Kashaders/.gitattributes`, `Include/Ditch-River-License.txt`, and `neozhaoliang/LICENSE`.

### Amazing Surface reference GMF: planar folds, inversion, and a degenerate 2D trap

Read the complete 480-line `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/KalisCreations-AmazingSurface.gmf`, including its metadata, preset, and all GLSL blocks. This is a reference definition, not evidence that the current built-in formula is identical or that this preset renders correctly. No shader was compiled or rendered in this inspection.

**Mechanism.** Each iteration copies `z.xyz` to p, applies one of three componentwise XY folds, computes `k = scale / clamp(dot(p,p), minRad2, 1)`, scales p by k and the scalar derivative accumulator by abs(k), adds the Julia constant or c.xyz, and optionally rotates about normalized (1,1,1). It writes p back to z and accumulates `min(trap, abs(p.z))`. The custom distance expression is `(r - abs(1-scale)) / dr`, with the second returned component equal to iter. That returned coloring coordinate is not the local trap value, so a future adapter must specify which observable the host actually uses.

**2D adaptation.** The first XY fold is `abs(x+a)-abs(x-a)-x` per component; it leaves the interval [-a,a] unchanged and reflects the exterior branches. The second, `a-abs(abs(x)-a)`, has different branch behavior and should be offered as a distinct transform. The third, `abs(x+a)`, translates before reflection and is not symmetric about the origin. These folds and a planar inversion can create optional procedural coordinates, masks, or secondary color layers in RFF. Applying them to the iteration recurrence instead creates a different fractal and needs its own computation/precision capability; it is not a shader-only upgrade to the Mandelbrot set.

For a genuinely planar recurrence with p.z = c.z = 0 and rotation disabled, the recorded `abs(p.z)` trap is identically zero. Replace it with an intentional 2D observable, such as distance to a chosen line or circle, and define pre-fold versus post-fold sampling. Keeping the (1,1,1) rotation generally leaves the plane; a planar rotation must be an explicit adaptation. MPA endpoint samples cannot in general reproduce minima over skipped intermediate iterations. A display-coordinate mask avoids that dependency but should not be labeled as an orbit trap.

**Parameter and numerical contract.** Metadata allows MinRad2 up to 2 even though the inversion upper clamp bound is 1. A port needs a defined ordered-bound domain, not just the UI limits from this reference. Scale can be zero, which can drive dr to zero before the final division; define singular/invalid behavior explicitly. The saved preset uses scale -1.06, whereas the parameter's declared default is 2: initialization and reset need a clearly chosen source. The metadata's “exact analytical” description is not a proof that the expression is an exact signed distance for every allowed fold, scale, constant, and iteration count. In particular, the position-dependent c addition and derivative initialization belong to the host recurrence contract; this one-step `dr *= abs(k)` alone cannot certify a derivative with respect to the original pixel. Preserve those assumptions rather than importing the descriptive claim into RFF.

**Shader work that can be moved out of the loop.** The rotation axis and matrix depend on uniform parameters, not the current orbit point. Preparing the matrix once per parameter change, or at least outside the iteration loop, avoids expressing normalization, trigonometry and matrix construction in every iteration. The compiler may already hoist some of this, so no measured gain is claimed. Preserve the code's row-vector `p *= rot` convention when moving the matrix to the host, and preserve or deliberately revise its abs(angle) > 0.001 activation threshold, which introduces a small discontinuity in animated rotation.

**Preset interpretation.** The primary palette is a single white stop; secondary coloring has zero blend opacity, additional color/bump strengths are zero, and several optional features are disabled. Merely listing their settings does not show that they contributed to the image. Point lights, AO and reflections describe the intended 3D presentation; for 2D RFF the direct transfer is optional relief-based shading, with separately defined normals and depth semantics. The file attributes the formula to Kali and its basis to Tglad, but contains no full formula license grant; retain that attribution as a provenance lead and establish the applicable source license before copying a recognizable implementation into RFF.

### Kalibox reference GMF: piecewise inversion and preset identity

Read all 457 lines of `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/KalisCreations-Kalibox.gmf`, including the complete preset and shader blocks. Despite the filename, its metadata ID and emitted function identify `RrrolaMandelbox`; its description attributes the distance estimator to Buddhi and optimization to Rrrola. Preserve the embedded identity and attribution when cataloguing references instead of inferring them from the filename. No implementation was copied or rendered, and the file does not establish an applicable formula license by itself.

**Iteration mechanism.** The shader optionally rotates p about normalized (1,1,0), applies `p = abs(p) + trans`, sets q = dot(p,p), then computes `k = clamp(max(m/q,m),0,1)` with m = MinRad2. It updates p by `p * k * (scale/m) + p0`, where p0 is either the Julia uniform or c.xyz, and uses `dr = dr*k*abs(scale)/m + 1`. The orbit observable is the running minimum of length(p). The final distance expression subtracts abs(scale-1) from r before division by dr and returns iter as the second component.

For 0 < m <= 1 and q > 0, the combined position multiplier is piecewise scale/m when q < m, scale/q when m <= q <= 1, and scale when q > 1. This makes the fold/inversion structure explicit and provides a useful equivalence target for a future independently implemented 2D transform. The metadata also permits m > 1; there k is 1 for positive q and the multiplier is scale/m, so the usual three-region interpretation no longer applies. At q = 0 the written expression divides by zero; a port should define the limiting branch explicitly rather than add an arbitrary epsilon that changes the fractal. m = 0 is excluded by the declared controls but still needs validation at load/API boundaries.

**What transfers to RFF.** Absolute-value folds plus radial inversion can drive optional planar procedural masks or a separate fractal experiment. Unlike the Amazing Surface z-coordinate trap, a radial length trap remains nontrivial in two dimensions. However, this saved preset is not planar: its translation Z is nonzero and its scalar Julia Z is nonzero, and rotation about (1,1,0) generally mixes the plane with Z. A 2D version needs a defined planar recurrence and trap sampling convention. It does not inherit Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA support merely because its shader compiles. Applying such folds only to a display mask is a different feature and should be described as such.

**Derivative and state caveats.** The code adds 1 to dr unconditionally, while its own comment describes an original mode-dependent update. That is evidence of a preset-oriented adaptation, not a proof of an exact derivative or conservative distance bound in every mode. Review initialization, the pixel dependence of p0, bailout behavior, and each fold's nondifferentiable boundaries before using this estimate for ray steps or normals. The source also stores conflicting Julia representations: nonzero scalar juliaX/Y/Z alongside a zero `julia` vector. A loader must define migration/precedence rather than silently choose whichever representation is read first. RFF's precise coordinates should have one canonical saved representation.

**Optimization and reproduction.** Rotation is uniform-dependent and can be prepared outside the orbit loop, subject to preserving matrix orientation and the abs(angle) > 0.001 threshold; this remains an unmeasured candidate. The preset's parameters retain more decimals than the parameter defaults, so initializing from defaults does not reproduce the saved scene. It also records maxSteps 522 and compilerHardCap 500: the host's effective cap must be resolved before comparing images or timing, and neither value is an RFF precision recommendation. The equal-color environment gradient, white primary palette, zero secondary blend opacity, and disabled texturing mean the stored 3D presentation primarily calls for checking lighting/material behavior rather than assuming visible multicolor texture detail. Current built-in behavior and rendered quality were not inferred from this reference file.

### Tree Broccoli reference GMF: shifted planar folds and mode-dependent derivative bounds

Read the complete 462-line `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/KalisCreations-TreeBrocolli.gmf`. Its actual metadata ID is `SurfaceKIFS`, distinct from the filename, with attribution in the description to Buddhi and Rrrola. No shader execution, visual match, or license verification was performed.

The iteration rotates p using a row-vector matrix about normalized `(paramE, 1, paramF)`, folds XY as `abs(p.xy + fold) - fold`, then applies `p = scale*p + p0`. For one component, the fold leaves x unchanged when x >= -f and maps it to -x-2f otherwise: its mirror boundary is x = -f, not the origin. Alternating this shifted reflection with rotation and scale creates repeated branch structure. A planar version can supply an optional procedural mask or a separate 2D folded system; a two-dimensional rotation must be specified explicitly because the current 3D axis generally moves points out of the XY plane. The fixed Y component makes the axis nonzero for finite input values, so a zero-axis normalization guard is not the primary issue here.

Unlike the preceding Kalibox reference, this function distinguishes derivative updates: Julia mode multiplies dr by abs(scale), while the pixel-dependent constant mode also adds 1. Away from fold boundaries, rotation and reflection preserve vector lengths, and uniform scaling contributes abs(scale). This supports the form of a scalar derivative-norm bound under the relevant initialization and constant-dependence assumptions; it does not establish an exact signed distance to the resulting fractal. This file contains no `Shader_Dist` block, so final distance/escape interpretation depends on the host's default estimator. A saved recurrence without that host contract is insufficient to reproduce a DE render independently.

For RFF, the radial minimum `min(trap,length(p))` could be a meaningful observable in a separately supported 2D recurrence, but MPA cannot be assumed to preserve it across skipped intermediate states. Display-space procedural use avoids modifying Mandelbrot computation but is a different effect. Keep high-precision recurrence requirements distinct from post-process texture arithmetic. Scale zero is allowed by the metadata and collapses Julia's derivative multiplier; zero, unit-magnitude, contracting, and expanding cases need deliberate estimator/bailout behavior rather than treating every allowed scale as the same regime.

The rotation matrix depends only on uniform parameters and can be prepared outside the orbit loop, preserving row-vector orientation. That is a candidate reduction in expressed per-iteration work, not a measured speedup. Unlike the other two reference files, this function does not gate rotation with a small-angle threshold. Do not introduce such a threshold merely to imitate their code: it would change this recurrence's animated behavior.

The preset again differs from the parameter defaults and stores nonzero scalar Julia coordinates alongside a zero vector Julia field. It also contains both feature-level lighting settings and root-level render/light fields. Resolve schema version and precedence before replay, rather than infer the active integrator from one flag. Its `sceneOffset` carries explicit high/low components, including low components of substantial magnitude; preserve their defined combined value instead of dropping them because of the field names. RFF view import would require its own precision-preserving conversion. The white primary palette, inactive secondary blend, and lighting/AO/material settings provide context for a 3D appearance, not proof of a rendered reference image. Provenance attribution remains a lead to follow before adapting recognizable source.

### MixPinski reference: shader blocks inspected; embedded scene remains partial

Inspected lines 1–100 and 906–1149 of `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/darkbeam_MixPinski.gmf`. All emitted shader blocks have been read, but the metadata body, escaped original source and embedded JPEG have not yet been fully inspected. This file remains **partial** and is not added to the completed-file count.

The emitted `frag_DE` lifts a 3D point to `(x,y,z,w)`, applies six conditional signed pair swaps across XY/XZ/YZ/XW/YW/ZW, scales by scaleS, performs a scaleM-dependent offset and Z fold, and optionally applies six ordered 4D plane rotations. Each signed pair swap reflects across a plane where the two coordinates sum to zero. The bailout uses the squared four-dimensional Euclidean norm, while the final estimate uses the maximum absolute component (the infinity norm), subtracts offsetD, and divides by abs(Dd). Those norms have different roles; replacing either without analysis changes behavior. In particular, the parameter named bailout is compared to squared radius, not radius.

The wrapper caches the inner DE result, samples the inner vector orbit trap, and forces the host loop to escape by replacing z with a very large vector. `Shader_Dist` returns the cached distance and a fixed second component of 1. This is a self-contained-loop adaptation, not a normal one-step recurrence: outer-loop transforms and traps cannot assume the post-call z describes the actual orbit. The source maps a rotate toggle onto `uJuliaMode`; that name does not mean Julia-constant selection in this function. Any RFF importer should preserve semantic parameter identities rather than infer behavior from a shared slot name.

The orbit trap updates only for i < ColorIterations and only after the overshoot bailout check. Thus the escape-causing iteration is omitted, and ColorIterations = 0 produces no inner updates. Correct coloring also depends on the host resetting `g_orbitTrap` for each evaluation; the wrapper alone does not prove that reset. The exposed scaleM range includes zero, but the Z transform divides by scaleM, and scaleS = 0 can collapse Dd. Define valid domains and degenerate cases before adapting. offsetD directly changes the final estimated field; it should not be presented as equivalent to a render-quality threshold merely because a comment suggests similar visual results.

For 2D RFF, the pair-reflection idea can produce a separate procedural mask or folded-coordinate coloring layer. Merely setting z and w to zero does not establish a planar invariant: signed pair swaps, offsets, and rotations can move values into those dimensions. A true planar adaptation requires selecting its own folds and rotation order; a 2D slice through the 4D-derived field is a different option. Neither supplies Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA support automatically. Uniform-dependent trigonometric values or the ordered composite rotation can be prepared outside the inner loop, but preserve noncommuting rotation order and measure the actual compiled effect before claiming a speedup. Remaining metadata and source comparison are required before assessing full import fidelity.

### MixPinski completion: source fidelity, hard palette boundaries, and embedded lighting

Completed the remaining metadata inspection of `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/reference/darkbeam_MixPinski.gmf`, including the decoded original GLSL, every import mapping, the complete preset, and visual inspection of its embedded 3000-by-1500 JPEG panorama. Together with the preceding emitted-shader inspection, this completes the file review. The preceding partial-status paragraph records the earlier checkpoint; the coverage ledger now records this file as read in full. No shader was compiled or rendered.

**Preserve the editable parameter model.** Original `offsetS` and `offsetM` are four-component uniforms, but the import mappings label both as ignored and the emitted shader supplies their default constants. Keeping the original text permits later source editing; it does not preserve their runtime adjustability. The original MI control permits 250 iterations, while its mapping caps the UI at 100. ColorIterations has original default 3, mapping default 0, and saved preset value 5. RFF should distinguish original defaults, runtime capabilities, reset values and saved values when adding an effect importer or reusable shader presets. A saved mapping version and an explicit list of fixed/unsupported parameters make reproducibility reviewable. These requirements apply equally to 2D procedural coloring and future 3D experiments.

The six plane rotations retain their original order. The generated temporary used for the Y/Z signed swap preserves simultaneous swizzle assignment rather than overwriting a component before using it. Uniform-dependent angle initialization moves into the generated function. These are concrete examples of transformations whose semantics matter beyond successful compilation. The original includes external MathUtils and DE-Raytracer files; retaining that source string alone is not a complete dependency archive. DEtweak is exposed and mapped, but is not used by the inspected original DE or its generated counterpart. This does not establish whether unrelated host code uses the corresponding shared slot. An RFF parameter should describe a verified effect, not inherit a label merely because a generic slot exists.

**High-value 2D transfer: deliberately discontinuous palettes.** The primary gradient contains 21 stops and repeats positions 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625 and 0.75, each with white followed by black. Such pairs can express intentional hard color transitions. A palette representation must preserve stable stop order and define the value at an exactly coincident position. Blind deduplication can remove the authored boundary, while interpolation across a zero-width interval can divide by zero. For RFF, combine explicit hard-stop semantics with pixel-footprint filtering across rapidly varying palette coordinates. Filtering should integrate the colors covered by a pixel without silently smoothing the stored palette itself. This is a proposed quality improvement requiring image tests at seams, coincident stops, zoom transitions and animation; no measured improvement is claimed here.

The primary gradient is tagged sRGB; the secondary has ten stops and is tagged linear, with nonzero blend opacity 0.49. Those tags require interpretation through the actual gradient consumer, not an assumption that every stage already uses a common color domain. For an RFF layer feature, specify decoding, interpolation, blending and final output encoding separately, then test mixed-domain inputs. RFF already provides OKLab interpolation; adding it again is not the recommendation. The useful extension is reliable composition and boundary handling around existing interpolation choices. Preserve palette recipe IDs and deterministic generation while extending any optional saved representation.

**Separate scene settings from visible evidence.** The preset enables path-tracing-related settings, AO, environment lighting and reflections, but includes material reflection zero, zero fog/glow contributions and an enabled third color layer with zero strengths. Rotation is enabled through the repurposed Julia toggle, yet all six angles are zero. Flags alone therefore cannot establish a visible effect or its performance cost. The environment image is a neutral studio panorama with bright light panels, not a rendered MixPinski validation image.
