It is an LDR JPEG; its filename, brightness multiplier or environment-map role does not establish HDR radiometric data. Its applicable image license is not established by the embedded bytes.

For 2D relief shading in RFF, an optional environment contribution would need defined normals, decoding and intensity behavior, with a known-provenance environment asset or an independently generated analytic light field. This file supplies a presentation example, not proof of a physically calibrated material system. Saved gamma, saturation, black/white adjustments and environment strengths also mean an appearance comparison must reproduce the whole active color pipeline. Keep that comparison separate from validating the underlying folded distance field or Mandelbrot computation.

### Chrome smoke harness: useful interaction coverage, separate from shader correctness

Read all 902 lines of `debug/smoke-chrome.mts`, including the in-page discovery helper, session cleanup, per-control execution, network interception and final reporting. This is static inspection: the historical falsification and timings in its comments were not rerun here. No browser was launched, origin data cleared, request sent or renderer exercised.

The harness discovers controls in the topmost wide visible header, presses menu triggers, then discovers newly mounted controls outside the header. It checks page exceptions, an application error-boundary marker, fallback text and navigation. Its practical lesson for RFF is to exercise settings and effect controls after startup: a successful first frame does not establish that opening a shader configuration panel, changing modes, or closing a dialog is safe. Capture a reproducible action sequence together with the current view and effect settings. On Win32, adapt this principle using stable command identities and application state rather than porting DOM-specific discovery.

**What discovery does and does not establish.** A menu row must be both a new DOM node and an increase in the count of its tag/label combination. Revealing an already-mounted hidden row is not sufficient; neither is replacing a row with another of the same kind when the count is unchanged. Nested candidates collapse to the outermost candidate. Menus lacking recognized trigger metadata are not traversed, nested windows are not explored, and state-dependent advanced options are outside the initial snapshot. Controls outside the viewport and menus yielding no discovered rows become warnings rather than failures. A green result therefore means the selected, discovered interactions passed, not that every control was exercised. For RFF, maintain a coverage list of effect modes and parameter transitions alongside any automatic control enumeration.

The cleanup criterion is primarily structural: no boundary error, the same top-bar control count, no newly discovered controls, and no reload. It does not compare application settings, camera, palette, shader selection or history with the initial state. A persistent toggle can remain changed without altering that structure. Reboots clear selected origin storage categories but swallow clearing errors. For deterministic RFF image checks, restore and verify a precise view/effect snapshot before each independent case; retain intentional multi-step sequences as separately named cases. Do not clear user preferences as an incidental consequence of a renderer test.

**Identity and attribution of failures.** Top controls can be reidentified by index and element tag alone when their count is unchanged, while row matching normalizes labels and chooses the first match. These shortcuts cannot prove semantic identity after reordering or duplicate labels. RFF tests should use stable command or setting IDs. The click helper hit-tests multiple points and checks the captured target, which usefully avoids silently clicking through an overlay. However, accepting a missing capture result when a document is replaced requires the separate navigation/error checks to interpret success. Errors and network attempts are attributed to the most recent press, so a delayed asynchronous result can be assigned to a later action. Attach a request/effect generation to asynchronous shader work if precise failure attribution is needed.

**Shader-specific extension for RFF.** The waits of 200 or 300 milliseconds are observation windows, not GPU completion signals. This file neither validates shader compilation nor compares pixels, descriptor layouts, uniform values, accumulation resets or color-space behavior. Pair an interaction check with a verified settings transition, successful pipeline generation, completion of the corresponding render submission, and an image or numerical assertion appropriate to that effect. Include reopening a preset, undo/cancel, rapid parameter edits, and changes during progressive rendering. For 2D RFF, verify palette seams and relief normals without changing recurrence precision; for any 3D extension, validate geometry/DE behavior separately from material and lighting changes. Avoid adopting a single UI-smoke pass as proof of shader correctness.

The harness blocks non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS HTTP requests and declines various labeled actions, downloads and dialogs. These are useful test-environment precautions but are not a proof that every possible side effect is blocked: method classification alone does not establish server semantics, and this code contains no explicit WebSocket-message interception. Its software option also changes launch arguments without explicitly selecting a named software GL backend; the printed renderer is evidence to inspect rather than inferring the backend from the option name. Concurrent passes and their wall-clock durations are not isolated GPU benchmarks. RFF performance measurements should record the actual device/backend and workload, apart from interaction-smoke timing. None of these observations is a request to repair GMT; they define what evidence to require when applying its testing approach to RFF.

### Palette-ground smoke: reversible editing context and import completeness

Read all 1,006 lines of `debug/smoke-ge-ground.mts`. The script exercises catalogue/set switching, recent picks, grouping, saved selection, search dismissal, mixed file drops, source labels, mocked remote availability, new gradients, and contextual undo. Historical falsification comments describe prior work; this inspection did not execute or repeat those experiments.

**RFF feature opportunity: one reversible operation across palette state and editing context.** The New Gradient scenarios require a single undo to restore the previous selection or empty state, and, when replacing a live mix, to restore the live input kind and its editing panel together. This is useful for RFF's future layered coloring: switching from a procedural mixture to explicit stops should be one operation with enough retained source state to return to the procedural controls. Do not bake a mixture and then retain only its sampled colors if undo or later parameter editing is promised. Preserve deterministic recipe identity and generator order. The tests check several state properties, but the live-mix restoration check verifies kind and panel rather than exact prior mix parameters or output pixels; an RFF equivalent should compare the complete source configuration and resulting palette as well.

The Escape scenarios establish a specific priority: dismiss the nearest temporary tool or window first while leaving the underlying adjustment and its phase value live. Clearing a nonempty search must not also close the adjustment panel. A later Escape may close the next layer. For RFF, handle cancellation and effect commitment explicitly so closing an export window cannot accidentally bake a color adjustment. The test sets the phase through the store's interaction bracket, not by dragging the actual slider, so it establishes state/shortcut behavior rather than physical slider event coverage or shader-update delivery.

The filter-fold scenarios additionally distinguish an automatic layout change from a subsequent user choice. Closing Filters reverses its own automatic fold, but does not reverse a fold the user made later. Undo restores the panel context without treating restored state as a new opening gesture. This distinction transfers to RFF when effects or palette tools temporarily alter panel visibility: restoration should not generate new edits or apply transformations again. It is not a reason to include all transient window layout in fractal file formats; choose history context independently from persistent rendering data.

**Mixed imports should process every supported item.** The script dispatches both image-first and gradient-first drops, then checks for an imported gradient name in local storage and an open image panel. The transferable requirement is order-independent dispatch with per-item results. The assertions do not verify decoded image pixels, imported gradient colors, segment midpoint behavior or alpha: an open panel and a saved name alone cannot prove import fidelity. RFF should validate the decoded content of each item and define partial-success behavior, while implementing format compatibility independently. These synthetic DataTransfer events also do not exercise native OS drag initiation.

**Persistence and identity need stronger observables than counts.** Working-gradient comparisons round stop positions to thousandths and omit interpolation/color-space settings. Group creation compares counts and a label, and reload checks selected group ID and chip state; these do not establish that every member or color survives unchanged. Use stable palette IDs plus full relevant configuration when testing RFF save/load, and test exact recipe regeneration separately. A moving scroll marker proves movement, not a correct mapping over the full scroll range. The phone checks establish horizontal bounds/overflow for selected elements, not complete two-dimensional visibility or accessibility.

The source-label assertions are presentation checks, not verification of the actual license attached to each palette. The two-item remote fixture checks count changes, while the failed-source case checks an unticked disabled row with a failure marker. Both remote cases open new pages in the same browser context as earlier tests, so they are not independent fresh-storage environments. For RFF optional catalogues, distinguish loading, empty, failed and loaded states, test retained offline entries explicitly, and preserve per-item provenance in NOTICE or catalogue metadata as appropriate. No remote endpoint was contacted during this review.

Overall, this harness supplies useful examples for reversible palette workflows and catalogue behavior, but contains no pixel readback or shader output comparison. RFF can adopt those workflow requirements for 2D coloring and future 3D materials, then add generation-matched palette/render assertions. A fixed delay or a correct UI state is not evidence that the corresponding Vulkan output has completed or matches the intended color pipeline.

### Palette-hero smoke: export fidelity, reduction fixtures, and provenance retention

Read all 1,088 lines of `debug/smoke-ge-hero.mts`. This inspection covers its reveal/double-click cases, name selection and dragging, export subjects and previews, reduction notices, filename/content checks and intercepted sharing tests. No browser test, download, clipboard access or sharing request was performed. Historical falsifications remain reported history, not results of this audit.

**Strong transferable check: preview the exact export representation.** The harness compares nine ramp text formats and a swatch JSON preview against copied text, normalizing CRLF to LF on clipboard readback. It separately compares a set's AI text preview with the downloaded UTF-8 file and checks that both named members are present. The former is normalized text equality, not literal clipboard-byte identity. This is a useful design for RFF palette export: build the preview and final output from the same resolved configuration, including subject, stop budget, name and provenance options. Associate that representation with an immutable configuration generation so edits while a preview is open cannot cause an unexplained mismatch. The inspected tests use stable inputs during each comparison; they do not establish behavior under concurrent editing.

Matching preview and output proves consistency, not destination-format validity or visual equivalence. Both could share the same conversion error. RFF validation should additionally parse the exported representation independently where practical and compare the reconstructed palette under the intended interpolation/color-space rules. Binary export rows deliberately have no text preview in these cases; absence of a preview is not a validation of those binary files. Do not infer that every offered format is tested merely because the registry's rows were enumerated.

**Use a fixture that makes reduction observable.** The script introduces 60 alternating black/white stops, contrasts it with a two-stop gradient, and checks both lossy-notice behavior and a forced two-stop CSS export. That is more informative than a nearly collinear three-color gradient that simplifies identically under several budgets. For RFF, evaluate palette simplification with sharp transitions, repeated-position stops, narrow features, nonuniform spacing and the existing interpolation modes. Measure reconstructed color error as well as stop count; a two-stop output can satisfy a budget while discarding almost all of an alternating pattern. A notice is useful, but the notice and regex count of hex colors here do not quantify retained visual detail. Export reduction must not silently replace the precise internal palette or alter deterministic recipe generation.

**Do not mistake storage geometry for rendered evidence.** The helper named `heroState` calls the sum of canvas widths `gradientPixels`; a positive width establishes allocation, not painted, nonblank or correct pixels. The file-chooser test also compares a truncated text summary and canvas presence, not the complete working configuration. Similarly, double-click reveal checks compare stop counts with a retained source count, which catches an extra knot but not a color/position mutation that leaves the count unchanged. A corresponding RFF shader check should read the actual palette texture or rendered output and verify the relevant configuration, rather than infer output fidelity from dimensions or item counts.

The reveal scenarios do verify that a second press lands in the newly moved gradient area before interpreting the result. The name-selection case verifies unchanged text, full selection and absence of a drag, and the header-drag case checks the advertised gradient MIME type. The latter does not inspect the dragged payload. Transfer the input principle to RFF: a layout change during a double-click must not reinterpret the second press as an unrelated color edit, and selecting a name must not drag the entire palette. Keep normal controls outside that narrowly defined reveal handling.

**Separate source identity from mandatory attribution.** GMT's tested naming policy removes the catalogue credit suffix after an edit and restores it when the content key matches again. That can express whether a palette is an exact catalogue item; it must not be adopted as RFF's provenance policy. Retain source/author/license and transformation history independently of an editable display name or exact-content match, in accordance with the project's NOTICE rules. An edited or reversed palette is not automatically free of its source obligations. The sharing scenarios check application-specific refusal and confirmation paths with an intercepted endpoint and dismissed dialogs; they do not establish rights, successful publishing, or permission to contact a service during this audit.

For both 2D color maps and 3D material palettes, the most useful transfer is a single resolved export representation with explicit reduction behavior, preserved provenance and independent color-fidelity checks. The preview/export consistency assertions are materially stronger than the canvas-presence checks, but neither substitutes for validating the Vulkan coloring pipeline itself.

### Palette-tray smoke: prevent repeated transforms and preserve untouched source data

Read all 1,162 lines of `debug/smoke-ge-tray.mts`; recovered the omitted region of an initially truncated tool response before marking the file complete. The review includes all setup, mixed-palette cancellation, adjustment baking, picker repaint, drag/drop, selection/history, and curve-refit scenarios. No browser or rendering tests were executed.

**RFF quality requirement: applying an adjustment must consume it exactly once.** The script seeds a phase shift before entering Mix, checks that Escape restores both the previous stops and phase, then checks that tab-based commitment resets phase and that another open/close cycle does not move the displayed stop positions. This illustrates why a baked result and the still-live transform must not both feed the next pass. In RFF, keep source palette, editable transform state and committed output distinct, and make their transition atomic. Test repeated apply/open/close cycles using complete stop configuration and sampled colors; this particular drift check compares DOM `style.left` values, so it cannot rule out color, bias or interpolation drift with stationary stops. Preserve the project's deterministic palette recipes when introducing such editing state.

**An untouched fit is a representation for editing, not a replacement for its source.** A pinned five-stop palette includes step segments and nonuniform positions. The harness explicitly checks that a forced curve refit would change its knots, then requires opening and leaving untouched Curves to preserve the original working input. This is directly relevant to RFF curve-based color editing: retain the original palette until a user edits the fitted curves, rather than repeatedly fitting and reconstructing it on panel navigation. Otherwise small approximation errors can accumulate without an intentional color edit. Keep the edited/untouched flag in undo state alongside the curve values; later tests restore edited curves, verify that flag, redo to an untouched fit, then commit the restored edits. A history snapshot containing coordinates but omitting their interpretation can silently discard the user's changes.

The adjustment tests distinguish Cancel, which resets controls without replacing input, from Apply, which commits the adjusted ramp and resets picture-changing controls while keeping the panel open. Cancellation verifies noise frequency and target channels as well as visible changes, and checks two parameters outside the panel remain untouched. Applying intentionally checks a smaller reset set: frequency and channel choices need not affect the image while noise strength is zero. For RFF, define neutral output separately from default control values and specify which preferences survive an apply operation. A new palette pick should have an explicit policy for retaining or resetting live adjustments; GMT's tested policy resets them and refits an open curve editor to the new palette, with one undo restoring the prior input and controls.

**Bound the numerical evidence.** The Apply test compares CPU-derived ramp samples using mean absolute RGB-channel difference, requiring distance below 12 channel levels and less than half the distance to the unadjusted ramp. This is evidence aimed at distinguishing the adjusted result from doing nothing, not a perceptual error bound or exact preservation. Its helper compares only the shorter array and returns zero for an empty overlap; require nonempty equal lengths in an RFF equivalent. The later curve-edit helper does reject empty/mismatched lengths, but its final commit assertion is relative to the unedited result without an absolute quality limit. Neither reads the Vulkan palette texture or final fractal pixels. Establish output-specific tolerances and an independent renderer check before claiming faithful shader output.

**Resource recreation must invalidate drawing even when color is unchanged.** The picker test toggles a mode off and on and counts pixels with nonzero alpha in its canvas. It can detect a blank backing store after remount, but equal alpha coverage does not prove equal RGB values. The transferable Vulkan principle is to include resource generation in upload/redraw validity: a recreated palette image needs initialization even if its palette parameters equal the last uploaded values. Validate actual data after recreation rather than relying only on a cached parameter key.

Selection belongs to a palette instance as well as a stop ID: separately fitted gradients can both contain `s0`. Preserve selection across edits of the same palette, clear it on replacement, and prune a selected stop removed by undo. The harness uses names to distinguish some undo transitions, so duplicate names need stronger identity-based coverage in RFF. Its overlay Delete case checks both that the foreground spline loses a point and that background palette stop count stays unchanged, a useful two-sided input-routing assertion. Synthetic color-drop checks inspect a displayed knot fill and insertion count, not native drag initiation or shader texture content. These distinctions keep the proposed 2D palette and 3D material-editing improvements grounded in what the source actually verifies.

### Hybrid-weave test suite: typed effect instances, scheduling, and migration evidence

Read all 1,668 lines of `debug/test-mb3d-weave.mts`, covering schedule construction, GLSL emission, native/imported slot resolution, parameter banks, estimator policy, legacy migrations, sequence/rhythm conversion and animation retargeting. No tests, shader compilation or rendering were executed. This file's assertions define intended contracts; they do not by themselves show that the current implementation passes.

**Direct RFF transfer: independently parameterized effect instances.** The suite checks multiple copies of the same formula with separate uniform banks, including scalar/vector controls, defaults, helper namespaces and derived rotation matrices. This is useful for a 2D coloring graph containing two instances of the same adjustment or procedural mask: each needs independent values and stable semantic identity. Keep vector components and rotation-axis ordering explicit, rather than allocate shared unnamed scalar lanes and infer their meaning from position. The boxIFS fixture specifically checks a Z/Y/X option order mapped to the correct vector components. RFF should generate host layout and shader bindings from a shared typed description and verify Vulkan offsets, descriptor ranges and limits; merely checking uniform names in emitted text does not prove binary layout compatibility.

Uniform-dependent rotations can be prepared on the host and updated when their source angles change. Menger3 tests require derived matrix descriptors and no in-shader rotation helper, but do not numerically compare matrix orientation, handedness or angle conversion. Retain those conventions and compare transformed vectors before claiming a faithful or faster port. Per-option baking is also explicit: replacing a uniform with a constant removes its live control. Treat that as a saved capability choice and pipeline specialization, not an invisible fallback when parameter storage fills. No compile-time or runtime speedup is established by this suite.

**Stateful composition requires more than renaming parameters.** Phoenix pairs receive distinct previous-orbit globals and per-evaluation resets; rotation-using slots save and restore shared rotation state around their calls. These checks illustrate why shader effects need explicit scratch-state ownership and initialization. Two alternating copies of a stateful recurrence with separate histories are not automatically identical to repeatedly evaluating one copy with one continuous history, even if the formula names match. Likewise, a self-contained distance loop cannot be inserted as though it were a single orbit step; the suite expects such slots to be rejected. For RFF, use declared input/output/state capabilities when composing effects. Mixing Mandelbrot recurrences is a separate mathematical feature and does not inherit perturbation or MPA support. MPA derives skips from periodic structure; an arbitrary weave schedule or orbit trap cannot be added under an assumption that existing skips remain valid.

**Schedule semantics should be saved and compared explicitly.** The tested modes include an intro followed by a repeating count sequence, modulo-selected layers with precedence, finite beat caps, an elected base slot and a whole-weave gate. Disabled count schedules select the first active slot, which need not be slot zero. A one-time fold intro is deliberately different from a periodic interleave. Those distinctions can inform 2D procedural pattern or animation scheduling without changing the Mandelbrot recurrence. The test helper `expand` removes negative slot encoding before producing its sequence, so its early comparisons cannot verify any semantics carried by that sign. Later conversion cases explicitly reject silent slots.

Sequence-to-rhythm and rhythm-to-sequence conversions reject unsupported patterns and resource bounds instead of pretending every representation is equivalent. The randomized cases use unseeded Math.random, up to 400 attempts per direction, and compare finite windows of 240 or 300 iterations. They require at least one successful conversion. These are useful sampled checks, not exhaustive equivalence proofs over every permitted schedule or arbitrary future iteration. For RFF, log a reproducible seed and counterexample, include boundary fixtures, and where possible compare the complete finite intro plus a justified common repeating period. Do not silently approximate a saved schedule merely to fit a small lookup table.

**Estimator selection is a policy, not a proof of safe distance steps.** The suite checks numerical-estimator fallback for a formula that does not write dr, selected lead-formula metadata, a custom lead getDist, and union of a cutting-plane capability so required shared declarations exist. A dr assignment is not proof of a correct derivative bound, and carrying a capability does not establish that every possible hybrid has a conservative distance estimate. Nor does choosing a lead estimator prove the composed geometry matches the source renderer. Any RFF 3D experiment needs separate numerical/visual evaluation of distance estimation, normals and ray-step behavior. For existing 2D shading, a display-space effect graph is a more direct application than importing these estimator choices.

**Reordering must move values and all animation links together.** Tests check simultaneous bank swaps, vector-axis target variants, keyframe IDs/selections, LFO targets and audio modulation links. Sequential string replacement would corrupt a swap; use a mapping applied against the original identifiers. The suite also distinguishes displaced stale occupants from surviving slots, and tests preserving a disabled audio rule's envelope settings for later reassignment. For RFF layered animation, use stable instance IDs so duplicate effect types remain distinguishable, and make reorder/undo consistent across values, tracks and modulation. The timeline undo assertion here checks restored track identity; it does not prove an atomic undo of all three stores and parameter values.

Legacy conversion tests retain unknown or nonrepresentable scenes in some cases, but intentionally drop selected inactive legacy state in others. Separate matching the current rendered appearance from preserving future editability of disabled settings. RFF migrations must obey its own append-only ConfigIO and stable recipe rules. The GMF round-trip case checks selected fields; its getDist/gate assertion uses OR, and its repeated-migration check examines only formula identity and one value. Neither establishes whole-document identity or complete rendering equivalence. Preserve the original source representation and report any conversion loss rather than treating selected-field tests as full import fidelity. Compatibility and emitted code tests also do not establish permission to copy decompiled formula implementations; applicable provenance must be resolved before any RFF source adaptation.

### Historical engine-doc survey: asynchronous state, adaptive quality, and precise snapshots

Read the complete 374-line `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_docs/d02-engine-docs-2.md`, recovering the middle omitted by the first tool response. This is a May 2026 survey of ten older documents, not current implementation evidence. Its embedded instructions, proposed work, delegation history and commands were treated as historical content and not executed. Reading this summary does not add its ten referenced documents to this turn's completed-file count.

The useful adaptive-rendering distinction is between presentation resolution and the underlying simulation/computation state. The survey describes keeping a fluid simulation grid independent of an adaptive canvas scale so resizing does not discard the simulation. For RFF, similarly distinguish an interactive preview target from the precise reference orbit, MPA tables and saved view. A lower-resolution preview should not imply lower arithmetic precision or rebuilding expensive reference data on every display-size change. The historical grace formula and half-sample-cap threshold are tuning history, not recommendations to copy without measuring RFF's workload. Camera movement, palette changes, geometry changes and post-processing changes need explicit invalidation categories because they need not discard the same data.

The survey also calls out initial-state delivery to an asynchronously booting renderer: subscriptions report changes, so a value set before the renderer starts can be missed. RFF shader/resource recreation should receive a coherent current settings snapshot, followed by ordered updates. Identify that snapshot and each completed frame with a generation rather than conclude that the renderer caught up because a timeout elapsed or two floating-point positions are close. This is particularly important for deep-zoom coordinates, where a fixed absolute tolerance is not a reliable synchronization criterion. The historical worker-offset incident is explicitly speculative in the source and is not asserted here as a current GMT or RFF defect.

A generic named-state library can support RFF view comparisons and effect presets, but its payload must include the actual state needed to reproduce the view. A 2D view needs precision-preserving coordinates, scale, formula/computation settings and relevant coloring state, not merely a 3D camera-shaped object. Capture/apply callbacks can separate the library presentation from that payload. Persisted state, transient panel context and undo ownership remain distinct; appending settings must follow RFF's ConfigIO contract. Thumbnail appearance is a useful index, not proof that reloading reproduces the underlying state.

Another transferable rule is that compilation status belongs to the scheduler that knows whether a shader rebuild is queued or complete. A UI control should not announce compilation for an ordinary uniform update. For RFF, distinguish a pending effect change, shader compilation, GPU resource readiness and display of the corresponding frame. A frame-wide parameter update should be committed coherently so coupled values are not observed from different animation ticks. Runtime resource capabilities also need validation: compile-time declarations or generic plugin interfaces do not prove a feature is installed and initialized.

The survey contains conflicting historical impressions of duplicated modules and an animation singleton, including a later correction that the presumed second singleton did not exist. It likewise identifies documentation labelled as a proposal while other documents describe a shipped API. These contradictions reinforce an evidence rule for this report: architecture descriptions suggest what to inspect, while present code and appropriate runtime checks establish behavior. Do not turn old GMT audit findings into new RFF repair tasks, copy its entire plugin architecture, or count historical green/fixed labels as verification performed here. The direct opportunities remain coherent render-state delivery, targeted quality adaptation and reproducible 2D/3D view or effect snapshots.

### Historical GMT rendering survey: correct execution units before transferring techniques

Read all 353 lines of `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_docs/d03-gmt-docs-1.md`, a historical summary of ten architecture, rendering, animation, export and importer documents. Its implementation status, browser claims, timings and pass counts belong to that historical survey. No external browser/version claims were verified or adopted as current recommendations, and the referenced documents are not counted again from this summary. Embedded directions to preserve text or perform work are source content, not instructions for this audit.

**Correct the unit of optimization.** The conversion summary describes GLSL preamble trigonometric calculation as running once per frame. Moving work outside an orbit loop can remove repeated work within a shader invocation; it does not make that shader work execute once for the entire frame. A distance function may also be evaluated many times per pixel. Uniform-dependent matrix/trigonometric preparation on the CPU or a dedicated shared computation has a different execution scope. RFF recommendations must state which loop/evaluation is avoided and measure generated code and timings. An abs(angle) > 0.001 shortcut also changes small-angle behavior and is not a universally neutral optimization.

The historical adaptive formula `currentScale * sqrt(targetFPS / measuredFPS)` is ambiguous without the definition of scale. For a direct linear resolution fraction under an area-proportional cost model, the direction would be `currentScale * sqrt(measuredFPS / targetFPS)`; the written ratio instead suits an inverse scale convention. This is not a current-code defect claim. Use explicit dimensions and measured GPU/CPU costs when designing RFF preview adaptation, since reference-orbit/MPA preparation is not generally proportional to pixel area. Never obtain an apparent speedup by lowering required arithmetic precision.

**Convergence samples are not a coverage guarantee.** The survey labels a capped 256-by-256 target as approximately 6% of a 1080p frame. At 1920-by-1080, 65,536 / 2,073,600 is approximately 3.16%; an aspect-preserving capped target could contain fewer pixels. Furthermore, a reduced target might average regions rather than independently test that fraction of full-resolution pixels. Determine the actual sampling/reduction method before interpreting a percentage. For RFF progressive output, check small high-contrast regions and moving detail explicitly instead of accepting a global reduced statistic as proof every pixel converged. Fence polling with zero timeout avoids waiting in that poll; it does not establish zero cost for subsequent readback or guarantee readiness after a failed fence.

**Direct 3D-to-2D transfer: consistent output coordinates and post-process footprints.** The survey records integer tile bounds, full-output camera coordinates and full-resolution noise coordinates. RFF image export can use the same principles: derive palette/procedural noise from consistent global pixel or precise view coordinates and supply enough neighboring samples for spatial filters. A half-pixel region expansion alone is not enough for a multi-pixel filter. The historical suggestion to reuse a viewport bloom image across export tiles would couple high-resolution output to viewport sampling; treat it as a proposed compromise, not an established full-quality solution. Even without bloom, relief normals, blur, chromatic offsets and antialiasing need appropriate tile support and boundary handling.

Alpha coverage and depth require different semantics from display color. The cited per-sample hit mask can average to subpixel coverage under a defined sampling distribution, but a normalized eight-bit depth pass loses metric precision. In RFF, specify whether an exported mask describes Mandelbrot membership, iteration availability or visual opacity; a 3D miss-depth test does not define those 2D quantities. Keep data passes outside display tone mapping and verify alignment with the beauty pass. Applying fog once or moving a constant color conversion out of a pixel loop is useful only after the relevant working/display color domains and composition order are explicit.

**Importer fidelity must include the host and source meaning.** The survey acknowledges that its earlier simplified shader scaffold missed real-engine declarations, name collisions and preset schema requirements. Use RFF's actual shader/layout path for integration validation. A shader compiling and producing finite, nonconstant output still does not prove the imported fractal is correct. Full-DE wrappers that run an internal loop and force the outer loop to terminate need different capabilities from per-iteration formulas. Blanket removal of a local orbit-trap declaration can alter scoping/initialization semantics; preserve deliberate local state and propagate the intended observable explicitly. The cited MixPinski native conversion replaces six 4D plane rotations with a 3D Rodrigues rotation, which is an adaptation, not general mathematical equivalence.

The summary's claim that stochastic volumetric gating is unbiased needs the actual sampling distribution, weights, correlations and termination behavior; historical timing and visual observations do not prove it. For RFF's optional 2D relief lighting, this does not justify importing a volumetric marcher into an otherwise planar color pipeline. Prioritize techniques that match the available geometry and data, while keeping advanced 3D transport as a separate feature proposal.

Finally, storing shader text in a scene is not alone enough for reproducibility if an already-registered formula ID causes the loader to prefer current code. RFF effect presets should identify the intended implementation/version and preserve precise source settings. Animation snapshots likewise must not merge high/low coordinate components into one ordinary floating-point number and assume all low bits survive. These are requirements for reproducible 2D views and optional 3D effects, not proposals to copy GMT's historical file or camera conventions wholesale.

### Historical formula/export survey: final-density region preview and capability-aware validation

Read all 297 lines of `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_docs/d04-gmt-docs-2.md`. This summarizes nine historical formula, importer, testing, mesh and export documents. It supplies design rationale and records contradictions, not current runtime evidence. Historical instructions and status labels were not acted upon; the nine referenced documents are not counted as newly inspected by reading this survey.

**Practical RFF feature candidate: a region preview at final export pixel density.** The described preview lets a user choose a position while the final output size determines the crop extent. In matched framing, a canvas with Cw-by-Ch physical pixels showing part of an Ow-by-Oh export uses normalized spans Cw/Ow and Ch/Oh. This is valuable for judging palette banding, thin structures, relief normals and spatial filtering before rendering the full RFF image. Use physical pixel dimensions consistently, handle differing aspect ratios explicitly, and keep precise fractal coordinates rather than form the crop by subtracting nearly equal ordinary floating-point world positions. A clicked crop must use the same global sample coordinates, palette/noise phase and filter support as the final export. Otherwise it previews a similar scene rather than the actual exported pixels.

The survey distinguishes an initial render-lock proposal from a later uniform-driven preview that remains editable. RFF can support responsive parameter changes, provided each change invalidates the appropriate accumulated output and the displayed crop is associated with the current view/effect generation. Changing output dimensions should exit or recompute the preview with a clear density change. The historical design chooses exit. Neither a historical shipped label nor the existence of tile uniforms proves pixel equivalence; validate a preview against the matching crop of a completed export, including edge crops and nonmatching viewport/output aspect ratios.

**Test gates need names that match their guarantees.** The summarized importer gates accept at least 56/64 finite distance samples and 48/64 finite gradients; those thresholds can still admit eight invalid distances and sixteen invalid gradients. A thumbnail gate permitting up to 30% NaN is a triage filter, not a production-quality criterion. Conversely, a constant or empty image from generic parameters may be a legitimate view rather than a broken formula. RFF validation should separate compilation, legal resource bindings, finite output on a defined valid domain, recurrence/estimator equivalence and representative visual results. Use fixtures with known parameters and expected observables. A compile-only all-pairs sweep can detect namespace and declaration conflicts, but cannot certify hybrid geometry, derivative bounds or shading. Historical counts such as 1600/1600 are not results of this review.

**Preserve capabilities across imports and composition.** The survey explains why wrapping a complete DE loop improves source preservation while losing outer per-iteration transforms. Report that tradeoff as an explicit capability, not a successful import with silently inert controls. Similarly, shared cutting-plane declarations allow code to compile but do not prove an arbitrary composed formula has a valid cutting-plane estimator. For RFF 2D, apply this model to effects that need normals, a scalar field, iteration values or full orbit observations. Do not supply invented data or assume MPA-skipped intermediate states are available. Precise Mandelbrot computation and a post-processing graph have different contracts.

The old formula reference's rules about constant initializers and declaration order are described as driver/assembly quirks; this survey does not establish universal restrictions for Vulkan GLSL. Determine required language and compiler behavior through the actual RFF shader toolchain before adopting workarounds. Likewise, the survey's source-license summary is a provenance lead, not a substitute for inspecting the exact original implementation and its applicable license before adapting code. Formula cross-reference tables help identify that source; a no-reference entry does not prove originality or unrestricted reuse.

**Mesh ideas need a defined 2D meaning.** Sparse blocks and bit-packed sign data can reduce memory for occupancy/mask products, but they cannot replace the precise iteration/approximation data required by RFF rendering. An IFS field shifted by half a voxel deliberately defines an offset extraction surface; it is not a recovered exact signed distance. A 2D contour or relief-mesh feature would similarly need a stated scalar field and isovalue, boundary policy and projection behavior. Do not infer these from a generic distance-estimator label. The survey repeats a roughly 3 GB saving claim at 2048 cubed without enough layout detail to justify it: a complete float32 grid at that size is 32 GiB and one bit per cell is 1 GiB, so the stated figure must refer to a subset or another allocation scope. Size RFF allocations from actual dimensions and retained buffers.

The strongest direct transfers from this historical batch are final-density crop preview, memory-bounded output tiling and explicit effect/input capabilities. They apply to existing 2D coloring as well as future 3D shading, while arbitrary hybrid recurrences and mesh generation remain separate feature projects requiring mathematical and rendering validation.

### Animation survey: reliable shader time and measured editor costs

Evidence: `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_docs/d05-animation-refactor-1.md`, `d06-animation-refactor-2.md`, and `d07-animation-refactor-3.md`, read in full. These are historical summaries of 26 underlying documents; reviewing the summaries does not mark those referenced documents as reviewed or establish that their implementation claims still hold. Their old branch, push, pause and worktree instructions are historical material, not actions for this review. No benchmark or renderer was run for this batch.

**Give animated shader parameters one logical clock.** The audio-sync survey reports two render drivers advancing the same tick registry, doubling timeline, LFO, audio and recording progress. For RFF, one owner should supply the logical time and evaluation identity used by palette phase, exposure, relief lighting and other animated uniforms. Offline output should evaluate explicitly specified frame times, independent of display refresh and GPU completion. A 1 ms duplicate-call guard, as described in GMT, is only a heuristic: distinct offline evaluations can occur closer together, while duplicate evaluations can arrive farther apart. Ownership and explicit evaluation identifiers provide a clearer contract. Temporal accumulation samples must also have a defined relationship to frame time; advancing animation once per sample would change the exported motion.

**Keep frames, seconds and evaluation history distinct.** Preserving wall-clock placement when changing frame rate requires remapping frame-valued clip starts by newFps/oldFps, while trim positions already stored in seconds remain unchanged. Keeping frame indices instead intentionally changes their time positions. Use explicit units at interfaces and validate finite values and supported ranges; type branding alone supplies no runtime validation. A shared time value is insufficient for audio-reactive preview/export parity when FFT windows, attack/release envelopes or oscillator integration depend on earlier samples. Define initialization, seek and backward-seek behavior, and use an identical evaluation order or a reproducible baked parameter stream. Keep precise RFF view coordinates in their existing representation rather than reducing a deep-zoom trajectory to ordinary floating-point camera values.

The historical audio duration issue also separates playback duration from the duration of available waveform-analysis data. That is a useful data contract if RFF adds audio-driven shaders: missing analysis is not a fabricated one-second clip, and a shorter waveform must not be stretched over a longer playback interval. Represent metadata readiness explicitly. The survey's codec-specific explanation is historical evidence, not a current guarantee about decoders.

**An off switch must remove its contribution.** Skipping analysis while retaining the last FFT values can freeze a modulation offset. RFF modulation should combine base settings with currently enabled contributions, removing stale contributions when a source, individual rule or master is disabled. An early return must not leave the previous frame's computed value in the uniform buffer. Decide separately whether disabling resets or preserves envelope/oscillator history. Validate the audio/LFO master 2-by-2 matrix, individual rules, save/load, seeking and offline output. Editing a disabled rule can remain possible. If settings are added to RFF, use its append-only ConfigIO contract and explicit missing-field defaults, not GMT's JSON layout.

**Measure the work that delays the image.** The first two summaries retract a broad animation-store refactor's performance rationale after narrower subscription probes showed no benefit. Later canvas reports describe major interaction gains, but the third summary invalidates app-gmt benchmarks predating the duplicate-tick fix. These numbers therefore cannot rank RFF shader optimizations or promise comparable speedups. Measure RFF CPU parameter evaluation, command submission, GPU passes and user-visible latency separately on a fixed scene and output size. Commit counts, cache-hit percentages and editor frame rates are not shader execution timings. Count multiplied by median duration is not measured total work, and nested profiler boundaries cannot safely be summed as independent costs. Capped sample medians and medians across runs also do not preserve the complete latency distribution.

**Use precise invalidation before adopting an editor rewrite.** GMT's proposed graph cache excluded pan, while the reported implementation included it and rebuilt on pan. Its DopeSheet used one canvas despite a three-canvas proposal. Adopt the actual dependency contract rather than assuming the original design shipped. For any future RFF animation editor, cache identity must account for document/track identity, keyframe content or trustworthy revision, scale, range, row geometry and physical pixel density. Array identity only works when every writer replaces modified arrays; a hash without collision handling is not proof of equality. Selection indexing by track and key avoids repeatedly scanning all keys. These changes can make shader controls responsive but do not accelerate the shader itself. A claimed layout bottleneck inferred from a successful rewrite still needs direct attribution if that distinction affects the next optimization.

The direct 3D-to-2D transfer is deterministic parameter evaluation and responsive editing: the same mechanisms support 3D material/light animation and RFF's 2D palette, tone and relief effects. They do not require changing Mandelbrot recurrence, perturbation precision or MPA. A proposed class hierarchy, initialization guard or throw-only skeleton is not evidence of a working runtime; migrate only boundaries justified by RFF's actual data ownership and measured needs.

### Research-survey qualifications: shader rankings and shaped lighting

Evidence: `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_docs/d09-root-research-specs.md`, read in full, with targeted current-source checks in `types/graphics.ts:60`, `engine-gmt/engine/managers/UniformManager.ts:426`, and `engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/pathtracer.ts:756`. The survey summarizes ten documents; its historical speedups, paper references and browser support table are not independently verified results of this review. Referenced documents are not promoted to full coverage by reading this summary.

**Do not import its optimization ranking into RFF.** The research summary calls blue noise inexpensive and high-impact, adaptive iteration depth the strongest fractal-specific optimization, and power-eight trigonometric elimination a free speedup. Each depends on a particular workload. RFF's precise Mandelbrot perturbation/MPA computation must not adopt distance-dependent iteration reduction that changes membership, escape values or detail. Algebra for a 3D Mandelbulb is not an acceleration of the quadratic Mandelbrot recurrence. RFF already uses Vulkan; WebGL-to-WebGPU migration comparisons from unrelated applications are not evidence for changing its backend. Historical ANGLE/D3D11/fxc branch-predication and inlining observations should become hypotheses to test on RFF's actual shader compiler and devices, not GLSL rewrite rules.

Blue noise can be considered for stochastic presentation effects, but replacing a random sequence requires checking sample dimensions, temporal evolution, tiled-export coordinates and estimator weights. A spatially pleasing mask does not by itself prove unbiased accumulation or faster convergence. The survey's volumetric claim that both quality endpoints converge identically needs estimator and image evidence; it cannot be inferred from a compensated probability alone when the gate and sampled contribution share correlated inputs. Likewise, coherent gates can reduce execution cost while introducing structured error. Separate navigation appearance, equal-time error and converged output in any RFF comparison. Do not reduce recurrence precision to improve a presentation benchmark.

**Spotlight shaping is a useful optional relief effect, with an unresolved historical schema reservation now clarified.** The old shaped-emission proposal assigned Spot the numeric value 2. The checked current source instead declares only Point, Directional and Sphere, packs Sphere as 2.0, and recognizes that interval in path-traced area-light sampling. Thus the historical Spot specification cannot be copied as an existing implementation or reuse that code unchanged. A future light type needs consistent CPU packing, shader dispatch, saved-format compatibility and controls. This finding is about interpreting GMT as a reference, not a request to change GMT.

For RFF's 2D relief shading, a spotlight can multiply a light's contribution by an angular cone mask computed from the reconstructed surface position and a declared light axis. Precompute the inner and outer angle cosines when parameters change, then interpolate the dot-product threshold per pixel. Since cosine decreases with angle, the wider outer cone has the lower threshold. Enforce ordered angles, handle coincident thresholds explicitly, and document whether the stored direction points toward or away from the light. Otherwise apparently symmetric vector conventions can reverse the cone. This feature needs a defined relief height and coordinate space; a screen-space decorative mask is a different effect and should be described accordingly.

The proposed early-out at attenuation below 0.001 drops a small nonzero contribution. It is an approximation, not an exactly equivalent optimization; a bright light or exposure increase can reveal the difference. An exact zero outside the cone permits skipping contribution work, including a shadow query if such a query exists, without introducing that particular threshold error. RFF's 2D shading may not have expensive shadow tracing, so the volumetric performance benefit cannot be assumed. This is primarily an artistic feature candidate, below correctness, filtering and stable color evaluation when those are unresolved.

Temporal denoising and reprojection also need their input contracts. A depth/normal/velocity G-buffer for 3D path tracing does not automatically exist for a 2D iteration image. RFF can reject history using precise view and effect generations and, where justified, reprojection derived from the 2D mapping. Membership boundaries, palette changes, newly revealed regions and unresolved fine structure require separate treatment. Filtering away boundary detail is not successful denoising. The survey's SDF over-relaxation and Lipschitz ideas likewise require valid distance bounds; they are not transferable step-size multipliers for Mandelbrot perturbation.

### Archived shader/importer survey: preserve mathematical meaning

Evidence: `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_docs/d08-archive-docs.md`, all 593 lines reviewed, plus a targeted check of `engine-gmt/features/coloring/MappingModes.ts:78`. The survey summarizes ten retired documents. Its status tables, parser generations, hook signatures and test counts remain historical claims; reviewing this file does not independently verify those documents or execute their tests.

**Correct the log-domain explanation before transferring it.** The archive summary says natural `log(log(r))` is NaN for `1 < r < e` and presents `log2(log2(r))` as the fix. That claim is mathematically incorrect. Both expressions have real finite values for finite r greater than 1; the outer logarithm may be negative without being invalid. As a numerical sanity check, at r=1.5 the two values are approximately -0.90272046 and -0.77358395. Both become singular at r=1 and leave the real domain below it. Changing the logarithm base changes the mapping, not this domain boundary. Current GMT mapping code clamps its input with `max(result.y, 1.0001)` before the base-two expression. That clamp, subject to valid finite input, provides the domain guard; it also flattens all smaller values and can change visible bands.

For RFF, specify whether a coloring input is radius, squared radius, a trap statistic or an escape-potential quantity. A generic trap is not automatically an orbit magnitude. Replacing one with another or changing logarithm base alters palette phase/scale and potentially saved appearances. Keep the bailout normalization and recurrence-specific smooth-iteration derivation consistent. Test the threshold neighborhood, very large values and invalid inputs separately. Do not present an arbitrary clamp as an exact recovery of the intended potential.

**A compiling importer can still change the image's mathematics.** The archived `min(float, vec4)` repair wraps the vector in `length()`. This resolves a type mismatch but loses four independent trap channels and chooses a particular metric; it is not a universal semantics-preserving conversion. Likewise, replacing every `length()` with a customizable metric can alter normalization, rotation construction or an estimator's assumptions, not just the intended distance display. A formula importer should classify expression roles and disclose unsupported state or explicit adaptations. This matters to 2D orbit-trap coloring just as much as 3D distance estimation. RFF cannot recover intermediate orbit minima merely from endpoints skipped by MPA.

The old rules to strip a counter increment, inline initialization and extract only the first DE function are also context-dependent. A counter may advance more than once or affect early-exit logic; initialization may need to run once per evaluation rather than once per recurrence step; overloads and helper calls require an actual selected entry point. Two names such as Offset and OffsetV must not silently share a slot when they are independent parameters in the same source. Generating an unknown uniform's name does not establish a CPU binding or saved value. Preserve resolved bindings, call dependencies, evaluation lifetime and user-selected mappings, and reject or explicitly qualify transformations that cannot preserve them.

AST-based rewriting helps distinguish variable identifiers from swizzles such as `z.z`, but a prefix alone does not guarantee collision freedom and an AST does not prove mathematical equivalence. Macros, included dependencies, scopes, overloads and host-generated declarations still need validation. Imports of complete DE loops should declare which outer transforms and hybrid operations they support. Historical statements that all formulas share an engine-owned loop must not override an imported formula's actual control flow.

**Transfer the registry contract, not historical driver folklore.** A common stable identifier can connect a mapping's settings, control and shader implementation, reducing accidental mismatches. Preserve existing serialized IDs, including RFF palette recipe IDs. The archive's claim that a uniform-controlled branch implies dead-code elimination is too strong: a runtime uniform can be coherent across a draw without being a compile-time constant. Choose branch structure from RFF's compiler output and measurements. Ordered shader hooks additionally need dependency/cycle validation, declaration compatibility and explicit variant capabilities. A harmless-looking stub must not silently substitute for data required by another pass. Vulkan descriptor and push-constant layouts remain exact host/shader contracts regardless of registry convenience.

**Vector editing and image effects need explicit semantics.** Additive vector parameters with independently animated axes can serve 2D light positions, gradient transforms and 3D material controls. Reconstruct a vector from one coherent evaluation before upload, with explicit units and valid ranges. Interpolating components suits some positions but does not automatically preserve a unit direction or provide a desired rotation path. Name-based rotation detection is an editing heuristic; schema metadata should carry units and interpolation meaning. Rounded display text must not quantize stored values or RFF deep-zoom coordinates. Group related edits into one undo operation and follow RFF's existing file-format rules.

The historical per-sample luminance clamp is an optional firefly suppression tradeoff: clipping before accumulation changes the estimator and can darken legitimate highlights. A bounce-zero rim light is an artistic direct-view effect, not recovered physical indirect illumination. These can inspire labeled 2D relief controls, but neither should be presented as a free accuracy-preserving shader improvement. Their strength is visual control with an explicit effect contract.

### Boot and panel follow-ups: state contracts behind reliable shader controls

Evidence: historical follow-ups `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_followups/q-001.md` through `q-010.md`, all read in full; targeted current-source verification in `engine-gmt/renderer/GmtRendererTickDriver.tsx:121-172`. The ten follow-ups concern startup, panel registration, light controls, feature menus, layout state, plugin boundaries and tutorial anchors. Their cited files are not additionally counted as fully reviewed in this batch. Historical PASS/high-confidence labels are not independent validation of present behavior.

**Distinguish compilation readiness from an image actually displayed.** q-001 describes a delayed boot request after startup initialization; q-002 originally described polling and later records event-driven boot/failure handling. Current code has evolved further: readiness checks `isBooted`, a `hasCompiledShader` latch and `!isCompiling`, then re-sends viewport size, replays a stashed camera teleport and pending textures, and calls `onLoaded`. This targeted code does not wait for an acknowledgement that those replayed resources have contributed to a presented frame. Thus q-002's wording that readiness proves a first frame was produced is stronger than the displayed check establishes. The current source also has a 30-second startup watchdog and a 120-second compile ceiling, so the historical statement that timeout waits are gone is not a complete current description.

For RFF shader changes, track the requested configuration, completed pipeline, uploaded resources and displayed output as separate states. Tie acknowledgements to the relevant generation so a previous compile or texture upload cannot satisfy a newer request. A one-way first-compile latch helps initial boot but is not a universal generation check for later changes. Keep the last valid image available while a replacement is prepared, and surface a recoverable error when preparation fails. A progress animation can represent estimated progress, but must not certify GPU completion. In Vulkan, rendering submission and completion themselves must also be distinguished from presentation when that distinction matters to an image-ready claim.

A fixed delay can permit pending UI work to run but is not a general synchronization primitive. Capture the intended view and shader configuration coherently and explicitly order resource preparation. Replaying a captured teleport avoids accidentally using a later drifting view; RFF's equivalent must retain precise coordinates. Replaying pre-start textures requires an acknowledgement and generation policy if the first displayed result is expected to contain them. The useful 3D-to-2D transfer is reliable switching of environments/material inputs versus palettes/relief textures, not copying a web startup timeout into the native application.

**Separate registration, activation and stable identity.** q-005 distinguishes the registered Camera Manager component from a host-supplied action that opens it; its visible label changed to View Manager while the internal ID remained unchanged. RFF can use the same distinction for saved views and effect panels: a display-name change should not invalidate saved references. An unavailable command should explain the missing capability or binding rather than falsely claiming that its component was never registered. q-004's multiple panel declaration forms also show why explicit precedence matters; silently ignoring one of several supplied forms makes configuration mistakes difficult to diagnose. These are implementation-contract lessons, not a request to reproduce GMT's dock layout.

q-006 reports independent local state in the docked light editor and floating Light Studio, sharing persistent light data but not hover or active-tab state. Independent transient interaction can be appropriate; shared editing must still address the intended light by stable identity when lights are inserted, removed or reordered. Clamping an index after removal does not preserve identity after every reorder. High-frequency gizmo state may avoid general UI notifications, but any secondary channel needs an owner, cleanup and a clear relationship to committed shader parameters. For RFF, apply this to multiple controls editing one palette/effect/view, without unnecessarily sharing hover state.

**A state snapshot is not a subscription.** q-007 and q-008 describe registry-generated menu entries and snapshot predicates whose reevaluation depends on their host. RFF menus and controls should be invalidated when their actual visibility/enabled dependencies change; reading current state once does not make them reactive. Distinguish a user's layout preference from device classification and from physical render resolution. Changing the arrangement of controls must not silently change final image quality. The injected-hook discussion in q-003 is specific to the web UI: its transferable point is that replaceable providers need a stable lifetime and an explicit contract. It does not justify a React-style architecture in RFF.

**Apply architectural rules to the layer they govern.** q-009 retracts a purported violation that mistakenly applied a reusable-control rule to integration plugins. RFF improvements should similarly follow its actual ownership boundaries; global state access is not automatically evidence that an integration layer needs a rewrite. Require a concrete coupling or correctness problem before recommending that work.

Finally, q-010 distinguishes immediate anchor remeasurement from ongoing resize observation. Measuring a newly registered element once does not subscribe to its later size changes; disconnecting an observer at final cleanup does not by itself keep its live target set current. If RFF adds guided highlighting or parameter overlays, update their subscriptions as targets appear, move, resize or disappear. A documented acceptance of stale positioning is a tradeoff, not proof that the positioning remains correct. This is a secondary workflow improvement, with no demonstrated shader throughput gain.

### Feature wiring follow-ups: precise invalidation and persistent effect state

Evidence: `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_followups/q-011.md` through `q-016.md`, read in full. Targeted current checks cover the GMT event-bus re-export, `utils/PresetFieldRegistry.ts`, `utils/defaultPresetFields.ts`, `engine/plugins/camera/presetField.ts` and numeric comparisons in `engine-gmt/engine/managers/ConfigManager.ts`. Referenced source files are not newly credited as full reads unless independently recorded elsewhere. This batch is static analysis, not a runtime or performance test.

**Classify changes by the data they invalidate.** q-016 describes four outcomes from configuration diffing: shader rebuild, uniform update, render-mode change and accumulation reset. This is a useful RFF design reference: changing a shader's structural capabilities differs from updating an effect strength, and changing the computed fractal differs from recoloring an existing map. Keep authoritative effect settings available to repopulate a replacement pipeline. Commit related settings coherently so mode switches do not transiently bind an incompatible pipeline or trigger redundant compilation. A versioned structural graph can identify topology changes, but its revision must change for every relevant structural edit; a revision token is not a substitute for defining those dependencies.

A post-processing parameter can avoid resetting upstream accumulation only when it truly acts after the retained data and leaves their interpretation unchanged. Palette changes may reuse a precise iteration map while still requiring the color image and dependent filters to rerun. Relief parameters can invalidate normals or lighting even if the underlying fractal map remains valid. Exposure applied after a retained linear-light buffer differs from exposure baked into each accumulated sample. RFF should express these dependencies by stage rather than assign a universal no-reset flag to an effect name. This is a direct transfer from the 3D pipeline to 2D map, color, relief and final-image stages, with potentially useful responsiveness gains that remain unmeasured here.

**Equality must respect the parameter's mathematical role.** Current ConfigManager code uses absolute differences below 1e-6 for numeric/vector/color comparisons. That policy is not suitable for RFF's high-precision coordinates or sensitive perturbation inputs. Use their native exact/revision representation and preserve all meaningful changes. Even ordinary presentation values need a stated equality policy: if successive changes are each judged below a tolerance while the comparison baseline still advances, a long sequence can diverge substantially from the data whose accumulation was retained. Compare invalidation against the state that actually produced retained output, or otherwise ensure small changes cannot evade the required refresh indefinitely. Keep any intentional control quantization separate from stored precision.

**Sharing declarations is not sharing a bus.** q-015's historical duplicate-module note suggests that keeping two singleton files identical would make their events reach one another. Identical implementations still create separate instances unless they share an exported instance or explicit bridge. Current `engine-gmt/engine/FractalEvents.ts` re-exports `../../engine/FractalEvents`, resolving that particular same-realm identity issue. Worker realms still require message transport; a shared source module does not share live memory across threads. For RFF, use one clearly owned dispatch path per execution domain, with request generations, ordering and completion acknowledgements where needed. Event emission alone does not prove a texture upload, pipeline replacement or accumulation reset has reached the renderer.

**Automatic feature integration has explicit limits.** q-013 traces settings, animation binding and undo through registry iteration and string conventions. Such a registry can reduce omissions when adding a shader control, but its contract must include storage identity, type, units, default, serialization, animation eligibility and invalidation scope. Indexed light bindings and composite camera tracks already need escape hatches in the described GMT design. In RFF, build on existing settings infrastructure and append-only ConfigIO requirements; do not replace its stable binary stream with the registry's incidental iteration order. Generic JSON snapshots also cannot be assumed to preserve high-precision numbers, native object types or all undo state. A version checkpoint is useful only while sufficient historical data remain available to reconstruct it.

q-014 raises a historical possible duplicate registration of five camera fields. The current targeted camera-plugin file registers `cameraSlots`, while the default registrar retains the separate camera fields: the described five-key duplication cannot be asserted from these current files. The current PresetFieldRegistry also has distinct duplicate policies: the same object is a no-op, a different existing field is replaced with a warning in development, and production throws; late new keys are rejected after freeze. Consequently, a development run accepting registration does not prove release behavior. For RFF, make registration ownership and collision policy explicit and validate persisted-field coverage before relying on generated save/load wiring.

**Tutorial state is distinct from rendering state.** q-011 and q-012 describe a lesson that seeds a registered formula and separately tracks tutorial completion. A silent missing seed can make later steps operate on the wrong scene. If RFF gains guided shader demonstrations, verify the prerequisite preset/effect exists, preserve the user's precise view for restoration, and record completion separately from scene contents. Initialization should be an explicit prerequisite rather than depending on an incidental import path. Multiple imports of the same module are not independent recovery mechanisms when both ultimately populate the same registry. These are optional discoverability improvements, not higher-priority shader optimizations.

### Gradient and image follow-ups: preserve sampling and saved intent

Evidence: `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_followups/q-017.md` through `q-021.md`, read in full, with targeted current reads of `utils/colorUtils.ts:669-752`, `engine-gmt/engine/MaterialController.ts:381-388` and `store/createFeatureSlice.ts:221-253`. Historical referenced files and tests are not independently credited by these five follow-ups. No images were rendered for this batch.

**The palette texture is part of the coloring algorithm.** q-017 describes a 256-by-1 byte texture bridge. Current code additionally supports a baked ramp representation: nonempty stops take precedence, while empty stops plus a valid ramp use its decoded texels. The checked material helper uses linear minification/magnification and repeat wrapping. These choices affect the final image beyond the interpolation used to generate stops. Linear filtering blends neighboring texels, including across a repeating boundary, and can soften a deliberately stepped palette. Conversely, nearest sampling preserves discrete texels but introduces quantization where continuous gradients are intended. RFF should define periodic endpoint behavior, texel-center mapping and the intended footprint filtering for each palette mode, then compare preview, renderer and export at boundaries and narrow features.

A fixed 256-sample byte ramp is a compact approximation, not a universal fidelity target for RFF. Higher-frequency stops can be undersampled; conversion into byte channels limits amplitude precision before later interpolation. Greater table resolution addresses spatial sampling, whereas higher channel precision addresses quantization: they solve different problems. Consider a higher-precision or adaptive-resolution LUT only where actual RFF artifacts justify it, while preserving existing recipe generation and saved appearance. RFF already supports OKLab, so merely adopting that blend-space name is not a new feature. The useful reference is a single, specified evaluation path whose results agree across all consumers.

**Distinguish interpolation space, texture storage and display encoding.** Current GMT helpers distinguish a display ramp forced to sRGB from a texture ramp using the configuration's output transform. A display export need not contain the same numeric samples as a linear-light shader input to represent the same intended color. Validate equivalence after the appropriate transforms and sampling, and avoid applying the transfer function twice. A named inverse tone curve does not recover highlight information lost by clipping or constitute a full color-management standard. Preserve provenance before copying any distinctive transform.

Malformed input handling also differs: current `renderGradientToRamp` falls back to grayscale, while `generateGradientTextureBuffer` can return zero RGBA bytes. The historical phrase 'black ramp' omits that alpha is zero in this path, unlike ordinary generated ramps with alpha 255. Whether that appears black or transparent depends on the consuming shader. For RFF, malformed data should have one explicit validation/fallback policy and should not silently masquerade as a successfully loaded palette. Baked ramps, empty editable gradients and invalid data are distinct states.

**Image-byte persistence is weaker than a visual round trip.** q-020 traces image data through scene serialization and a separate texture event, correctly separating large asset transport from small configuration patches. Its PASS does not by itself prove decoded texture format, color interpretation, enable state, GPU upload completion or rebind after pipeline recreation. In the current feature setter, assigning an image can enable its environment/texture flag when false. That can be useful for an explicit image-import action, but is not automatically appropriate when restoring a saved image that was intentionally disabled. Preserve the saved intent atomically; validate that case separately from a newly imported enabled texture. Clearing an asset, restoring it before renderer startup, replacing it during an in-flight upload and recompiling afterward also exercise different contracts. A delayed old upload must not overwrite the latest selection.

For RFF's 2D texture/relief inputs, retain a durable asset identity and metadata independently of transient Vulkan resources, and recreate bindings from authoritative state. Excluding bytes from ordinary uniform messages can reduce unnecessary traffic, but does not remove the need to track resource generation and readiness. A future 3D environment-map input can use the same lifecycle contract.

q-018 and q-019 reinforce registration-order and collision concerns already covered above. q-019's historical claim of duplicate camera registrations is qualified by the current cameraSlots-only plugin check in the preceding section; it is not carried forward as a present GMT defect. q-021's stale render-loop installation example likewise must not motivate installing a second driver: use one actual owner of logical animation time. These architectural notes support reliable controls and loading; they provide no measured shader-speed improvement by themselves.

### Tick and uniform follow-ups: invariants before optimization

Evidence: historical follow-ups `docs/history/doc-audit-state/survey/_followups/q-022.md` through `q-029.md`, all read in full. Targeted current checks include `engine/TickRegistry.ts:144-186`, both UniformSchema collision guards and the environment/fog writers in UniformManager. This batch does not rerun their historical tests or independently review every referenced file.

**Do not equate elapsed wall time with logical tick identity.** q-022 usefully distinguishes seconds passed to tick handlers from milliseconds in old examples. Its described 0.1-second delta clamp, however, bounds an update rather than preserving arbitrary elapsed time: after a long stall, simply discarding the excess slows delta-integrated animation relative to wall-clock audio. RFF should distinguish absolute presentation time, bounded integration steps and explicit offline frame times.
