Their commercial/SEO priorities do not determine RFF shader priority. The later implementation also supersedes parts of their GMT feature-gap descriptions.

For RFF, compare candidates against one fixed iteration/escape-angle dataset and fixed lighting/exposure so palette differences remain interpretable. Do not recompute high-precision fractal orbits for every palette tile when the required numerical fields are already available. Current `RenderScene::applyShaderAttr` separately sends palette, textures, warp, stripe, slope, color, fog and output settings to renderer passes; this confirms an existing shading-control boundary, not a ready-made thumbnail renderer. It also waits for device idle, so invoking that entire path per visible tile should not be assumed inexpensive. A thumbnail path needs its own measured scheduling/resource contract.

Historical day estimates and catalog sizes are not RFF budgets.

The research correctly separates deliberate visible grain from quantization dither as different artistic intents. Current RFF already exposes `setDither` in its output pass, so adding 'dither' is not an unimplemented feature by default. Moreover, current GMT's shared engine tail uses slope gating and 4/8-LSB ceilings, despite the older fullscreen wrapper/document describing an approximately one-LSB tail. Its channel sums share inputs between output channels. Evaluate the actual implementation and output-domain behavior rather than importing its 'best-in-class', independence or universal moment claims. Grain, if desired, should have a separate saved control and an explicit compositing stage; it is not a substitute for banding prevention.

Monotonic-lightness and simulated color-vision checks are optional palette diagnostics, not proof of universal accessibility or scientific suitability. Sequential magnitude maps, diverging maps and cyclic fractal palettes have different structural goals; imposing a globally monotonic ramp on all of them would reject valid intentional designs. An editable 2D color field built from gradient stops is likewise a separate artistic mapping, not a drop-in replacement for a one-dimensional iteration LUT. These ideas transfer from GMT's 3D presentation to RFF's 2D coloring without requiring 3D geometry, and refine the existing preview, palette and output-quality proposals rather than outrank core shading fidelity on the strength of competitor marketing.

### RGBA noise and font atlas: inspect channel relationships before shader reuse

Inspected the complete decoded Font_1 (1024²), RGBA_Noise_Medium (256²) and RGBA_Noise_Small (64²) images and measured every stored channel. All are RGBA. Both noise images span every 8-bit code in every channel, including alpha. The medium image has means R=G=127.15663 and B=A=127.55177; small-image means are approximately 127.83252, 128.24487, 129.24683 and 129.30737. Their finite-tile distributions are not exactly uniform. Zero-lag channel correlation alone is misleading: a full circular cross-correlation followed by exact all-pixel equality establishes that medium G equals R rolled by +17 rows/+37 columns, and medium A equals B rolled by the same offset. This is an exact spatial relationship in the stored data, not four independently generated image fields. It does not mean two differently addressed samples are necessarily unusable; it means their dependence must be evaluated for the actual lookup pattern.

For RFF noise/dither or stochastic lighting experiments, do not infer independent sampling dimensions from an RGBA filename or a small same-coordinate correlation. Offset taps can select identical underlying samples when combined with these packed offsets; periodic reuse and temporal shifts can likewise expose correlations. Select the resource and addressing together, preserve alpha as numerical data, avoid premultiplication/sRGB conversion, and test the actual estimator or quantization output. These measurements do not establish the small image's channel-generation algorithm, a white/blue-noise spectrum, temporal independence or sampling convergence. No direct basename consumer was found in the searched Examples shader/text/Markdown files for these three assets.

The font image visibly contains a regular glyph atlas with Latin, accented, Greek and symbol shapes, but its RGB channels show substantially different fields rather than one grayscale coverage mask. Red spans 0–255 with 167 distinct values; green and blue span 0–254 with 254 distinct values; alpha spans 58–255 with 191 distinct values. These observations do not identify a signed-distance convention, gradient encoding, threshold, glyph mapping or usable font license. Do not implement a guessed MSDF median decode or treat the composed RGB preview as glyph color. If GPU text is eventually useful for RFF overlays/export annotations, require a documented atlas-generation and decoding contract, cell padding/filtering rules, correct glyph layout and provenance. This asset does not by itself justify a new text-rendering subsystem or add a high-priority fractal shader improvement.

A shader optimization must also preserve the output, not merely keep a UI heartbeat near refresh rate. This data pass refines the existing measurement strategy; it does not recommend porting a web timeline or rank a shader effect based on unrelated browser counters.

### Mock B: useful color operations, with explicit approximation boundaries

Read all 567 lines of plans/ge-v2-mock-b.html, covering CSS, markup, color math, state transitions, generation, filtering and handlers. Unlike Mock C, this prototype contains executable CPU color processing. It samples each stop segment into a 64-point Oklab ramp using smoothstep interpolation, converts to encoded sRGB and clamps channels for display. Its deterministic generated library contains 1,000 tiles, not the search placeholder's 3,076. Randomly assigned collection labels and hand-authored Turbo/Inferno approximations are not proof that the corresponding official palette data is included. No export codec, clipboard write, actual image extraction or GPU shader is implemented here; the respective actions are static data or toasts.

| Mechanism in this source | Transfer to RFF's 2D coloring | Required refinement before adoption |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Independent lightness, chroma and hue blend weights | Mix two evaluated palettes while keeping their source controls available; no 3D geometry is required. | The shortest hue delta is wrapped across ±π, but hue near zero chroma is unstable or arbitrary. Define achromatic and exactly opposite-hue behavior. Preserve endpoint identity deliberately rather than assuming a fitted representation is exact. |
| Blend reconstruction from samples at indices 0,7,…,63 | A compact editable result can reduce editor complexity. | All ten knots include both endpoints, but resampling a reconstructed smoothstep ramp is not the original continuous palette. Even a blend weight of zero can change interior colors after reconstruction. Measure fitting error and retain hard boundaries; fewer knots alone imply no GPU speedup. |
| Cumulative Oklab path length for perceptually spaced swatches | Offer color-diverse palette extraction as an optional rule. | The cumulative distance is evaluated on only 64 samples; each target selects the first sample whose cumulative distance reaches it, without interpolation. Flat stretches can repeat colors, and thin features can be missed. This is approximate path-length spacing, not guaranteed equal displayed perceptual differences. |
| Hue rotation, chroma scale and lightness contrast before display conversion | Reversible palette adjustments can operate independently of expensive Mandelbrot field computation. | Chroma is not gamut constrained; final RGB channel clipping can distort hue and lightness. Keep working data separate from display mapping, identify the chosen gamut policy, and use the same evaluation for preview and export. Preserve current recipe generation. |
| Sparse sampled palette distance | Candidate retrieval can compare whole ramps instead of names or one swatch. | rampDist uses 16 indices (0,4,…,60), omitting the endpoint at 63. meanH is the angle of sample 32, not an average hue. Narrow features and cyclic phase differences need explicit handling; these prototype descriptors are not robust quality metrics. |

The display helper discards most ramp samples and emits hex colors with no explicit stop positions. CSS distributes those colors equally: for step 4, original sample 60/63 becomes stop 15/16; for step 2, sample 62/63 becomes 31/32. The last shortened sample interval is therefore expanded relative to its original location, in addition to 8-bit quantization and interpolation between encoded display colors. For RFF, use the actual palette evaluator or correctly positioned samples for previews, and validate against the renderer at endpoints, narrow transitions and the cyclic seam. Do not use this CSS output as a shader-reference oracle.

State handling also reinforces the prior snapshot recommendation. Adjustments live separately in S.adj, while starring retains the unadjusted gradient object; Build evaluation creates a fresh object, making reference-based membership unsuitable as durable identity. The edited-state action clears flags without resetting adjustment values. These are prototype semantics, not established defects in current GMT or RFF. For RFF, identify a saved variant by its complete effective shader/palette state, including adjustment parameters and a stable revision, and distinguish a candidate from a committed palette. Validate return-to-source and neutral-operation identity with pinned time and identical fractal fields.

This source adds detail to the existing perceptual mixing, gamut handling, palette fitting and preview-consistency recommendations; it does not justify a new high-priority shader effect. Any adaptation of the named color transform or distinctive constants still requires the original-source/license verification and NOTICE attribution described earlier. No source constants or prototype code were copied into RFF, and no runtime or visual parity is claimed from this source-only review.

### Shipped palette and thumbnail indexes: distinguish content identity from render identity

Completely parsed public/palette/gxglobal.json and read every palette field. It contains 20 uniquely identified stop-based palettes, all declaring sRGB input and Oklab blending. Each has 3–15 ordered stops spanning 0 to 1, valid six-digit hex colors and locally unique stop IDs. Parsed all of public/palette/catalog-sigs.json and inspected every fixed-width hash: version 1, 13,278 unique sorted entries, exactly 212,448 lowercase hexadecimal characters in 16-character chunks, matching its count. The consumer catalogSigs.ts confirms that these are canonicalized stop-or-ramp signatures. Stop signatures round positions to 1/1000, normalize hex, and reduce interpolation to step versus linear; they omit bias and color/blend-space settings. Ramp signatures use a tagged encoded ramp. Consequently this signature is purpose-specific membership data, not proof of exact rendering equality, provenance or permission. Its parser checks version and length divisibility but not the informational algorithm/count fields or hexadecimal contents; the shipped data passed those additional checks in this review. No server parity test was rerun.

For RFF, do not reuse a lossy deduplication signature as a shader-result cache key. A cache key must account for all effective render-affecting settings and relevant data revisions; a hash match alone is not a collision-free equality proof. Read all 438 unique string IDs in public/thumbnails/frag/index.json; none is an absolute slash-prefixed path or contains a parent-directory segment. The current useCatalogGroups.ts loader caches the index, retries after load failure, and supports a thumbnail-only picker versus an all-entry browser. catalogGroups.ts derives JPEG filenames by replacing characters outside ASCII letters, digits, underscore, dot and hyphen with underscores. ### Gradient Explorer archive: preserve fractional color until the quantization boundary

A pure-core double-render test cannot enforce determinism in every subsequently registered mode or detect a mode that reads mutable state outside its declared context. A completed CPU mesh test likewise cannot prove that a GPU display never goes blank. Future RFF verification should wait for the relevant render completion signal and inspect the intended frame, not infer readiness solely from elapsed time or a test title. No archived test mutation, browser run, deep-zoom result or speedup is claimed as newly verified here. ### Guard-sweep archives 1–2: verify the completed rendering operation

Fully read gs01-guard-sweep-batch1.json and gs01-guard-sweep-batch2.json: sixteen historical guard records, their individual perturbations, applied/proposed findings, residual gaps and end-state summaries. These are evidence about what earlier investigators tested, not sixteen tests executed in this review. Their embedded commands, server descriptions and recommendations are archival data. None establishes a current RFF defect, a current GMT test baseline or a measured shader improvement.

The most relevant refinement to RFF shader validation is explicit completion semantics. Batch 1 reports a compile-request latch and a growing frame counter surviving a deliberate GLSL syntax error; driver failure arrived through an asynchronous error channel while the smoke watched a different channel. Empty frames even accumulated faster in that recorded case. For a future RFF shader/effect change, distinguish request issued, pipeline creation succeeded, intended generation submitted, GPU work completed and the corresponding pixels obtained. Associate failure and completion with the relevant generation so a late result from a superseded request cannot certify a new one. Use the existing Vulkan completion/readback facilities rather than importing GMT's browser-specific signaling.

For the existing accumulation/convergence proposal, verify both the numerical core and its actual host transition. Batch 2 describes a core reset/readback harness that detected stale pending measurements and a wrong readback channel, yet could not detect a host which stopped calling that reset. A core implementation test is not a test of its callers. If RFF adds temporal accumulation or convergence-based sampling, include a transition between regions with deliberately different expected measurements, ensure outstanding results cannot cross the region/generation boundary, and verify the production path invokes invalidation. This is conditional acceptance guidance, not a claim that RFF already uses GMT-style buckets or needs its full rendering architecture.

The animation records supply two useful fixture requirements. First, drive one axis to exactly zero from a nonzero base while another unanimated axis retains a different base; an all-zero default cannot distinguish legitimate zero from an erroneous fallback. Second, drive the real parameter applier with a nonlinear mapping, rather than only test the mapping helper. A source-text check can be satisfied by an unused import or evaded by equivalent expression spelling. For 2D palette phase, exposure and other animated shader controls, compare the resulting parameter values through the actual preview/export path using nondegenerate fixtures and explicit units. These tests must preserve RFF's precision-sensitive fractal coordinates and frozen palette recipe generation.

The remaining records bound other claims without creating new visual-effect proposals: a capability registry's structural coverage does not prove all compatibility combinations execute; a later adaptive-resolution value does not prove the immediate interaction handler ran; logging a missing control or stopped tick without failing is not verification; and save/load should first establish that the destination state actually differs from the saved state. Distinct input routes to the same action can require separate evidence. A static checker with exemptions around its central implementation cannot certify that implementation, and a simplistic comment-line filter is not a general parser. Historical claims of a filter having no possible false negatives are not adopted as a universal guarantee here.

These additions consolidate the report's verification requirements. They do not promote auditing tools, menu layering or archived test repairs above the actual RFF shader improvements, and none of the recorded timing, mutation or pass-count results was rerun.

GMT raymarch refinement is a 3D distance-estimation technique, not a direct replacement for RFF's 2D perturbation/MPA. Only the conditional-feature discipline transfers directly: preserve established behavior when the option is off, verify both enabled and disabled rendering, and do not infer a valid shader or scene from a missing property.

Other records refine existing numerical and timeline criteria rather than adding an audio roadmap. Nonuniform inputs distinguish RMS, mean and maximum; phase-shifted inputs exercise both complex components; same-size rebuilds distinguish state reset from incidental reallocation. Apply the same reasoning to any RFF image-statistics, exposure or cached-effect work: flat fixtures and allocation-size changes alone can conceal the wrong operation. For frame-rate conversion, nonintegral ratios and multiple independent tracks expose rounding and incomplete Undo snapshots. Quantized frame positions need not return to their original indices after a reciprocal conversion; distinguish a documented resampling policy from exact Undo restoration. Do not import JavaScript rounding assumptions into C++ without specifying the intended behavior.

Finally, neither a large metrics printout nor a composite suite name proves the production mechanism. Source matching can pin constants or expression spelling while missing equivalent rewrites or backend execution differences. This archive's UI clamping evidence concerns custom placement arithmetic, not native Win32 menu paint timing. All historical runs, repairs and reported performance remain archival; the additions here sharpen acceptance criteria for the existing RFF shader proposals.

### Apollonian saved scene: separate palette appearance from material response

Fully read all 1,293 lines of debug/test-scenes/apollonian.gmf, including its API banner, metadata/default preset, five GLSL sections and complete saved Scene. Both Metadata and Scene JSON payloads parse; the Scene has 26 feature blocks. This is a source/data inspection, not a render. The externally referenced HDR asset was not fetched, so neither its availability, appearance nor license is established here.

The file is a concrete example of why a palette preview cannot alone predict final material appearance. Its default preset uses a seven-stop purple/pink/orange/gold palette, roughness 0.187, reflection 0.12 and no environment map. Its authored Scene instead specifies a two-stop gray palette, roughness 0.068, reflection 1, specular 1.97, an enabled external HDR environment with rotation 0.58, and a different renderMode. The Scene's explicit lights are all marked invisible, and its legacy top-level lights array is empty. Bloom intensity, glow intensity and fog density are zero; those saved values should not be credited for an appearance which has not been rendered. Stored enable flags and parameter blocks alone do not establish that a pass executes; current loading/migration and renderer gating still determine effective state.

For RFF, this strengthens the existing separation between scalar-field coloring and lighting/material response. A 2D relief-style normal can drive a deliberately stylized diffuse/specular or environment-colored response, with controls independent of the palette, without pretending the Mandelbrot image is a physical 3D scene. Define the height/normal source, scale, gradient smoothing, silhouette handling and color space explicitly; do not infer geometric distances from raw iteration counts. Actual multi-bounce reflections, 3D AO and physical depth of field require geometry/depth information absent from an ordinary flat 2D image. Replacing that information with an artificial height field is a new approximation whose limitations should be visible in the feature description. This scene is a useful configuration reference, not evidence that those expensive 3D passes are the best RFF priorities.

The formula also illustrates a concrete shader organization technique. Shader_Init computes a position-dependent modulation factor once before iteration and recomputes it after the optional spherical-inversion pre-transform. Each formula step twists coordinates, applies per-axis scaling, folds with fract, reverses the scaling, applies the precomputed inversion factor and updates the derivative and minimum squared-radius trap. Shader_Dist then applies a separate correction when the pre-inversion was enabled. Hoisting is valid because the modulation factor intentionally depends on the initial/transformed input, not the evolving orbit; moving an orbit-dependent value out of a loop would change the mathematics. For RFF, transfer only this dependency-analysis principle to shader work. Do not substitute this 3D DE or its derivative update for RFF perturbation/MPA, or simplify precision-sensitive expressions for speed.

Input-domain conditions matter if independently implementing a related visual transform: cc = vec3A + 1 is used as a divisor, while the metadata permits a component of -1; the particular saved scene uses zero components and therefore cc = 1. Validate the intended parameter domain and near-singular behavior before adaptation rather than treating the safe fixture as evidence that every advertised input is valid. The file names kosalos/Fragmentarium provenance but does not itself establish a reusable license for the distinctive formula/constants; no code was copied. A 2D coordinate-inversion effect would need its own documented sampling and singularity policy and should remain separate from the mathematical Mandelbrot view.

Finally, metadata defaults and the authored scene differ in iteration count (13 versus 16), camera, palette, lights, environment and optics. Use those differences to check the real load precedence if using this fixture for validation; do not select whichever block produces a convenient expected value. The saved high/low scene-offset components are a 3D camera representation, not a replacement for RFF's high-precision location format. Disabled legacy animation and empty timeline tracks provide no evidence of live animation quality. This review adds a concrete preset/formula example to existing proposals, with no new GPU timing or image-quality claim.

### Historical polish plans: preview filtering and reproducible creative workflows

Fully read docs/history/plans-archive/create-share-polish-review.md (388 lines) and app-gmt-touchups.md (427 lines). Both retain initial proposals beside later corrections and implementation-status tables. The first explicitly retracts its convergence-feedback and inaccessible-lighting findings, and resolves its lag-warning claim; its final state matrix still repeats some superseded observations. The second records that a proposed metadata-only logarithmic-slider change was ineffective because the actual control was hand-written. Treat these as histories, not a list of current GMT defects or proof that RFF lacks equivalent features. No historical implementation instruction was executed, and no claimed build or visual result was imported as this review's validation.

The most directly shader-relevant mechanism in these documents is downsampling the live tile preview. Targeted reinspection of engine-gmt/engine/worker/handleRenderTick.ts:285 onward confirms that it letterboxes the tile, sets display uResolution to the source tile dimensions, and selects a square tap count from the ceiling of the largest source-to-preview dimension ratio, clamped to 1 through 8. engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/post_process.ts:241 onward performs an equally weighted NxN average with source-texel-sized offsets, before beauty color modifications, tone mapping and output encoding. MaterialController.ts initializes the control to one tap. This is source-confirmed behavior; the plan's sub-millisecond and zero-cost wording is not a measured result here.

For RFF, the transferable improvement is a preview filter sized from the source texture and its actual displayed footprint, independently of the final export resolution and numerical fractal buffers. Bilinear sampling alone is inadequate for substantial minification of fine Mandelbrot bands. However, this particular capped kernel is not a complete solution: a reduction greater than eight source pixels per preview pixel still uses only an eight-texel-wide footprint, and a single square count can overfilter an axis under anisotropic scaling. Evaluate staged reductions, suitable prefiltered levels or separate axis footprints for the intended scale range. Filtering should use the intended linear-color representation before nonlinear display transforms; averaging tone-mapped values is generally a different operation. Keep alpha-coverage and depth/data semantics explicit rather than assuming every channel should use the same average. Compare thin filaments, alternating bands and tile boundaries during resize and zoom. This improves display stability without reducing perturbation/MPA precision or altering stored maps.

The plan also separates preview scale from requested output dimensions and proposes avoiding accumulator resets caused solely by opening a controls panel. For RFF, retain accumulation only when its defining inputs and sample domain remain valid. A real render-target size, projection, palette or shading change can require invalidation; do not adopt a blanket rule that resolution changes are presentation-only. Likewise, neither the historical last-tile-export diagnosis nor its proposed common cause was established by the deferred retest. Use a non-square output, multiple tiles and non-unit preview scale to validate the actual export path. The document's default reduction from 256 samples to 64 is an application-specific historical choice, not evidence that 64 is sufficient for RFF.

Two workflow ideas support existing RFF proposals without changing their priorities. First, a positive palette-frequency control can use logarithmic interaction to allocate useful travel across orders of magnitude, provided the actual widget, stored value, animation mapping and shader uniform agree; zero or signed domains need a separate mapping. Second, an exported image may optionally carry a versioned scene/settings payload so an author can reopen a look. Exact deep-zoom coordinates, palette recipe identity and relevant shading settings must survive that payload; a preview image alone cannot reconstruct them. Embedded metadata can be removed by external image processing, so the saved-location/settings format remains the authoritative recovery artifact. The archive's social-reach multipliers and claims about universal PNG remixability are not evidence for RFF priorities.

For session recovery, do not copy the archive's camera-excluded dirty-state policy blindly: navigation to a new Mandelbrot location can itself be valuable authored work. Protect the prior recovery snapshot from startup autosave overwrites, report actual export completion/failure, and keep optional UI layout state separate from animation data. The timeline section reinforces stable track IDs despite improved display labels, shared view state, and explicit time-versus-value transform semantics. Its initial suggestion to scale both tangent components differs from the later time-only implementation description; choose tangent transformations according to the actual coordinate change, not that initial prose. These remain supporting workflow considerations rather than additional top-ranked shader effects. No RFF code or formats were changed.

### Public blue-noise assets: measure the composed dither, not only the inputs

Visually inspected both complete public/blueNoise.png (128 by 128) and public/blueNoiseRGBA.png (1024 by 1024) and decoded every stored pixel for numerical analysis. Both are RGBA, despite the smaller filename lacking an RGBA suffix. In each channel, every byte value occurs exactly 64 times in the smaller image and 4,096 times in the larger; every channel mean is 127.5. Alpha contains noise data, not opacity. The larger asset's SHA-256 matches the previously reviewed LoicVDB/Include/Shadertoy_Textures/Blue_Noise.png exactly. That establishes duplication within this checkout, not an independent original-source license verification.

For each channel, computed the two-dimensional FFT of its mean-subtracted byte field. Mean power at radial frequencies between zero and 0.1 cycles/pixel divided by mean power between 0.25 and 0.5 is approximately 0.000082 to 0.000102 across these assets. This supports low-frequency suppression for these finite periodic tiles; it is not a proof of an ideal blue-noise distribution or of temporal quality. Wrapped one-pixel horizontal correlations range from approximately -0.183 to -0.195. Zero-lag cross-channel correlations are at most about 0.010 in magnitude for the small tile and 0.00190 for the large tile. Low linear correlation alone does not establish statistical independence.

Reread engine/fractal/shaders/ditherTail.ts and engine/utils/createBlueNoiseWebGL2.ts in full, plus the createDitherNoise wrapper in glHelpers.ts. The dither wrapper selects the large tile and overrides the generic loader's linear filtering with nearest sampling. The shader forms output noise as (R+G-1, B+A-1, A+R-1), then applies its slope gate, amplitude and endpoint taper. Distinct channel pairs do not imply uncorrelated output channels: the third pair shares R with the first and A with the second. Evaluating that exact combination at every large-tile texel gives output correlations of approximately 0.500485 and 0.499456, while the first and second outputs have correlation 0.000282. The small tile gives the same qualitative result. Means remain approximately zero. Thus the source comment describing the three outputs as decorrelated is too strong, even though the input channels have low measured correlation. These are CPU measurements of the stored tile and the pair-sum expression, not rendered-image measurements or a claim of a visible GMT defect.

For RFF, decide deliberately between shared luminance noise, partially correlated color noise and independent color-channel noise. Measure the final combination's spectrum, channel correlation, clipping bias and grain on actual dark gradients and near-neutral colors. A marginal triangular distribution does not establish independent RGB noise, and changing the channel pairing may trade chromatic grain against luminance structure. Treat this as refinement of the existing adaptive-dither proposal, not a reason to copy GMT's 4/8-LSB amplitude limits. Preserve data-texture semantics: no sRGB decode, alpha premultiplication or unintended interpolation; anchor static output noise in full-image pixel coordinates for tiled export consistency. Animation or accumulation needs a separate temporal-sampling design rather than an assumption that a static tile suffices.

The generic loader's nominally neutral fallback is RGBA8 value 128, which normalizes to 128/255, not exactly 0.5. The pair-sum expression consequently produces +1/255 in each channel before amplitude/taper scaling while that fallback is sampled; the wrapper comment's no-dither claim is not exact. In an independent RFF implementation, disable noise until the asset is ready or choose a fallback representation/expression with an exactly zero result. The current inspection does not establish whether users see a startup artifact. The code names Christoph Peters as the large tile's source, but no external source or grant was verified in this pass. Keep provenance attached to any later adapted asset and do not mistake a duplicate file or a source comment for completed licensing work.

### Full HDR payload review: concentrated light and spherical weighting

Completed the four public/skies HDR bodies previously left at header-only status. Inspected a full-extent common-scale log-luminance diagnostic of all four, generated at native raster resolution and displayed slightly reduced by the image viewer. It shows the outdoor sun/cloud structure, the natural studio's windows and ceiling strips, and the two synthetic-looking studio light arrangements. This supersedes header-only coverage for these four files; it does not certify the application's GPU decode/upload or asset licenses.

Local reproducibility artifacts are debug/gmt-audit/inspect_hdr_assets.py, hdr-asset-measurements.json and hdr-luminance-diagnostic.png. These are diagnostic scratch artifacts, not additions to RFF's renderer. The measurements use Y = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B as a comparison proxy; no physical radiometric calibration or independent color-primary identification is established. The display uses log2(Y) clipped to [-12,12] only for visualization. Measurements use unclipped values.

| Asset | Maximum stored RGB component | Median Y across texels | Maximum Y | Spherical-weighted mean Y | Energy share in brightest approximately 1% of texels |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cloudy Sky | 62.75 | 0.16783 | 61.90845 | 0.47755 | 14.91% |
| Natural Studio | 66.5 | 0.06640 | 50.48570 | 0.45439 | 25.48% |
| Softbox Studio | 2.265625 | 0.08104 | 2.10096 | 0.22855 | 10.66% |
| Window Studio | 2.265625 | 0.16301 | 2.08684 | 0.35769 | 5.82% |

For the spherical statistics, each latitude row is weighted by sin(pi*(row+0.5)/height), appropriate to an equirectangular pixel's relative solid angle. The brightest set is selected by the unweighted 99th-percentile texel threshold, then its contribution is summed with those spherical weights; it is not exactly 1% of sphere area, and ties can include slightly more than 1% of texels. These values describe the files under the stated decode and luminance convention, not rendered illumination on a particular surface.

For RFF's optional environment-based relief shading, the main implication is to retain HDR range through the lighting computation and apply display mapping afterward. Clamping the source to [0,1] or using its JPEG preview would discard substantial light information in these examples. If sampling the environment stochastically, build the sampling distribution from nonnegative radiance importance times the spherical Jacobian and use the matching PDF in the estimator; a bright texel selected without accounting for its solid angle gives a different distribution. Include a defined black-map fallback and validate small intense sources, rotation and polar rows. These observations support the existing environment-importance-sampling proposal; they do not measure its speed or variance improvement in RFF.

If using deterministic prefiltered environment lighting instead, validate energy preservation and the intended roughness response independently. The similar filenames and identical image sizes conceal large differences in peak intensity and concentration; keep scene exposure separate from asset selection or offer explicit normalization with a documented meaning. Equalizing mean radiance is an artistic control, not a physically neutral transformation. For a 2D transfer, all such lighting still acts on an explicitly chosen artificial normal field, so compare readability of the actual Mandelbrot structures as well as attractive highlights. No perturbation precision, MPA behavior, palette recipe or saved-map data was changed.

### Doyle Spirals GMF: solve parameter-dependent geometry once, evaluate the field many times

Fully read public/gmf/fragmentarium/DoyleSpirals.gmf, including all metadata/preset settings and the complete solver, coordinate reduction, four-sphere evaluation and inversion code. The default uses P=2, Q=20, radius scale one, inversion enabled and zero core iterations; the formula body is deliberately empty because its getDist computes the field. It uses a white primary palette, a constant green environment, a point light, roughness 0.2, specular 3.5 and reflection 0.34. Fog, glow and depth of field are zero. The saved legacy Julia components differ from the zero vector field, which matters because getDist uses uJulia as the inversion center. These settings are source evidence, not a rendered appearance or an established load-precedence result.

The expensive setup is explicit. getDoyleConstants initializes a two-variable system from P/Q, takes exactly two Newton steps using an analytically constructed 2-by-2 Jacobian, forms a lattice matrix and its inverse, then derives four sphere centers/radii and a projection vector. DE_Doyle calls this setup each time the distance function is evaluated. The setup depends on P, Q and radius scale, not the sample position. A directly transferable shader-engine principle is to cache parameter-dependent derived constants on a parameter change, then reuse them across pixels and ray steps. For RFF, apply it only to relevant shading/palette/optional-field setup and retain the precision required for each computation; this is not a proposed replacement for MPA. Inspect generated code and measure actual cost before claiming a speedup, since compiler optimization and host integration affect the result.

The spatial reduction takes a position into log-radius/angle coordinates, maps it into a lattice basis, uses floor to reduce to a fundamental cell, and transforms back through an exponential scale and rotation. It then evaluates four sphere distances and divides by the local scale. This provides a concrete optional 2D extension: a planar circle-packing or logarithmic spiral pattern evaluated as its own field or compositing layer. It does not improve Mandelbrot orbit accuracy. A plane slice of the sphere field is not automatically the same as a projection, and the optional spherical inversion changes the geometry again; choose and label the intended construction. Account for angular wrapping, lattice-cell boundaries and rapidly shrinking repeated features when filtering a 2D image.

The metadata's description of a perfect packing is not a numerical guarantee. The implementation takes a fixed two Newton steps without a residual/convergence check, divides by Jacobian and lattice determinants, and forms sqrt(1-rs*rs) after applying the user radius scale. The spatial evaluator also divides by radial distance and takes a logarithm; the inversion divides by squared distance to its center and uses a further denominator in the distance correction. For any independent implementation, define valid parameter domains and explicit unresolved/singular outcomes, then verify tangency/residuals and seam continuity. Do not infer that every advertised P/Q/radius combination is valid or silently use a plausible image as proof of a converged solve.

Because the cached setup controls the entire geometry, animation and preset loading must invalidate it when any dependency changes, including rounded P/Q and radius scale. Distinguish a failed solve from a valid previous cache entry so stale geometry is not presented as the requested setting. Bind derived matrices/vectors with matching C++/GLSL layouts in a Vulkan port, and preserve the intended matrix orientation. The file credits Jos Leys in prose without establishing a reusable implementation license; no formula or constants were copied. This example adds a specific mechanism and validation contract to existing shader-precomputation and optional 2D-pattern proposals, with no runtime or visual-quality claim.

The image shows a spiky, reflective-looking gray structure with orange highlights on the left, bright white highlights on the right, a dark central recess and a large white circular light shape partly outside the upper-right frame. Its 26-feature Scene differs materially from Metadata defaults: two formula iterations instead of sixteen, Radiolaria enabled at limit 0.725, roughness 0.224 instead of 0.75, reflection 0.29, useEnvMap false, and renderMode one with path-tracing/area-light settings. The visible white sphere light has radius about 0.28105 and intensity three; an orange directional light has intensity 2.2801, while the blue point light is invisible. Bloom, glow, fog, volumetrics and depth of field are zero/disabled in this saved scene. The white primary palette helps isolate lighting color. These facts support a material-and-lighting example without crediting bloom, but the exact contribution of each pass has not been isolated experimentally.

For RFF's 2D relief shading, the transferable visual controls are light direction/color, highlight width, roughness and the chosen normal field. A white/gray palette provides a useful comparison fixture. A broad light source and a rough material can both broaden highlights, but they are different controls and require different shading treatment. A flat image with artificial normals cannot reproduce this scene's occlusion, visible light geometry, multi-bounce transport or silhouette merely by adopting the saved numbers. Implement a clearly labeled stylized response first if appropriate, and evaluate fractal-detail readability independently of the attractive material effect. The filename's metallic description is an appearance label, not evidence of a calibrated conductor BRDF.

The included Mandelbulb shader reuses pow(r,power-1) for the derivative and radial power, and caches repeated trigonometric terms. Its comments record earlier approximate acos/atan experiments as neutral on an ANGLE/D3D11 stack with reported image drift, and a function-wrapping experiment as neutral after inlining. Those are historical claims, not benchmarks repeated here or predictions for Vulkan. For RFF, pursue measured redundant-work removal while keeping numerical precision; do not replace intrinsic math with approximations based only on nominal instruction counts. The formula's acos argument clamp does not by itself define z/r at r=0, so its caller's initialization/domain remains relevant. Radiolaria modifies the iterated coordinate after addition; it changes geometry and is not a postprocessing shader effect transferable to ordinary Mandelbrot coloring.

This pair also provides a concrete saved-look requirement: preserve the exact authored settings with the exported image and identify which snapshot is authoritative. Small camera differences can matter to reference-image comparisons. A successful metadata extraction does not prove the exporter waited for the matching rendered frame or that a subsequent import preserves every setting; those need an end-to-end test. Keep full-precision location information and stable palette recipes in any RFF equivalent. No embedded shader was executed, no third-party asset was copied, and no current render-path correctness or speedup is claimed.

### Branding assets and desktop reference: visual evidence boundaries

Decoded and visually inspected all seven public application-icon PNGs and every embedded favicon.ico frame (16, 32 and 48 pixels). They use a cyan/white fractal motif with GMT lettering. The 192- and 512-pixel icon files are byte-identical to their corresponding android-chrome files. The ICO's 16- and 32-pixel frames are not byte-for-byte pixel matches to the separate PNGs: respectively 34 and 48 pixels differ, with at most one code value per RGB channel and unchanged alpha. This is packaging/image-conversion variation, not a shader feature. These branding assets offer no RFF shader implementation to adopt and should not be mistaken for sampled rendering textures.

Also decoded and viewed public/guy.png (168 by 119, RGBA) and public/screenshots/desktop.png (900 by 600, RGB). The former is a portrait, not a fractal or shader input. Its two XMP representations describe Photoshop creation, conversion and saving; this metadata does not establish a redistribution license. The desktop PNG has no decoded metadata payload. It shows a white/gray Mandelbulb, differently colored illumination, two light-position gizmos, white/orange/blue toolbar swatches and visible formula controls including iterations, power and Radiolaria. Its 60 FPS label is part of a saved screenshot, not a reproduced performance measurement. It does not establish which renderer revision, material parameters, antialiasing method or postprocessing settings produced the pixels.

For RFF, the screenshot is useful as a qualitative reference for colored lighting that leaves fine relief visible. A neutral palette can help compare normal construction, light direction and highlight width separately from palette coloring. A 2D synthetic-normal implementation can reproduce a directional shading style, but cannot inherit the 3D object's silhouette, hidden-surface shadows or world-space light positioning. Evaluate it on actual RFF fractal maps with the existing lighting controls before proposing additional controls; no new feature is justified merely by a toolbar swatch. No rendering benchmark, UI interaction test, or asset reuse is claimed by this image inspection.

### Historical code-health report: useful mechanisms versus unsupported guarantees

Fully read docs/history/gmt/07_Code_Health.md (869 lines), including its architecture, typing, resource management, export, error-handling, camera ownership, initialization and shader-constant sections. It combines successive historical updates rather than a single current-state audit. For example, the rapid-teleport collision is first described as a risk and later explicitly dismissed after checking the actual setter path; offset-guard and initialization entries similarly retain pre-fix text beside later completion notes. Its statement that no core automated tests exist is historical and must not override the test scripts already inspected in the present checkout. Neither its grades nor its completion checklist proves current runtime correctness.

The transferable shader design ideas are to distinguish uniform-only work from per-fragment work, separate compile-time feature permutations from frequently adjusted runtime parameters, and give numerical thresholds explicit meanings. RFF can evaluate precomputing shared screen-footprint factors or other uniform-only expressions, but must preserve its coordinate precision, descriptor layouts and distinction between actual shading resolution and output/reference resolution. A disabled feature saves shader work only if its generated/compiled path actually omits that work; a saved toggle or a historical claim of zero GPU code is insufficient. Vulkan specialization or separate pipelines also carry compilation/cache costs, so this is a targeted design option rather than a recommendation to port GMT's feature framework wholesale.

Rechecked the present engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/pathtracer.ts bounce sampling block against the report's noise explanation. The source still calls 17.123/23.456 and 7.31/11.17 mutually irrational and says their offsets ensure uncorrelated texels. Finite decimal constants are rational, and their stored floating-point representations are rational too. Distinct offsets, especially after texture wrapping and nearest-texel lookup, do not prove statistical independence or a low-discrepancy sequence. This is a limit on the justification, not a measured rendering defect. Do not transplant that rationale into RFF's dithering, stochastic antialiasing or any future sampled lighting. Verify the actual indexed samples across pixels, channels, frames and sample purposes, including repeated indices and visible temporal patterns; preserve a stable seed policy for reproducible exports. No noise-quality or performance improvement has been measured here.

The report's descriptions of an inverse-square-root approximation and five-coefficient ACES tone mapping are not sufficient provenance or standards-conformance evidence. Follow the earlier source/licensing review and RFF's NOTICE requirements before adapting recognizable code; keep an approximate tone curve labeled as an approximation. The report's precision ratios and GGX denominator guards address specific 3D operations and cannot replace the error requirements of Mandelbrot perturbation or MPA.

For 2D interaction and export, the broadly useful architecture is explicit ownership of the current view and a captured authoritative export snapshot. GMT's world-offset camera convention itself is 3D-specific; RFF should retain full-precision complex coordinates and its existing location/map formats. A saved image fallback without metadata can still preserve pixels while losing editability, so success reporting should distinguish those outcomes. Historical recommendations for arbitrary 50 ms readiness delays or timeout-based guard release are not synchronization guarantees. These observations add RFF adoption criteria, not a GMT repair backlog, and no production code or runtime behavior was changed.

### Cross-audit findings map: validate mechanisms before adopting conclusions

Fully read docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/state/related-findings-map.md (435 lines), including all untracked, tracked, source-annotated, ADR-captured and observational categories. Its approximately 218 findings and 65 untracked items are historical classification totals, not new verified defects or additional audit coverage here. Suggested destinations inside that document are archival proposals; no GMT backlog or source edits follow from this review.

A current-source check changes one concrete interpretation: the map says an early quality-threshold crossing writes qualityFraction without updating fps/fpsSmoothed. In the present store/slices/viewportSlice.ts, that branch writes all three fields immediately. The sample-window timestamp advances only when its 500 ms window is due. Thus, quality changes can cause additional HUD state updates, but the historical claim of unchanged FPS fields is not applicable to this checkout. This reinforces the earlier RFF proposal to distinguish render-throughput measurements from display refresh and to throttle reporting independently of rendering decisions; it does not establish an RFF performance defect.

The same source confirms the unit conversion interactionDownsample = 1/max(0.01, qualityFraction), with adaptive output converted back through 1/result.scale. A fraction of 0.5 denotes half the linear resolution, whereas a divisor of two expresses the same request on the other side. For RFF, name and validate these units explicitly when adding interactive preview scaling; half resolution in both dimensions is approximately one quarter of the pixels, not one half. Neither that pixel-count estimate nor reduced preview resolution permits lower perturbation precision. Track actual allocated dimensions and avoid exposing a nominal fraction as guaranteed frame-time improvement. The hold deadline is module state consumed by the next FPS update, not an immediate render-state notification.

The map's shader-schema observations also distinguish useful contracts: CPU uniform backing, GLSL declaration emission and variant-specific use are separate responsibilities. Current UniformSchema.ts explicitly documents backingOnly and its declaration-enforcement site; the old missing-documentation observation is therefore not a new action item. RFF's equivalent requirement is exact agreement among Vulkan bindings, descriptor types, push-constant layouts and each compiled shader variant. A broad registry refactor is unnecessary to benefit from that invariant. Likewise, main render, mesh sampling, picking and histogram shaders need their own validated assembly contracts; a main-pass ordering diagram does not automatically describe every variant.

Other clusters cover lifecycle readiness, worker/store ownership, export capability checks, gradient parity, typed boundaries and historical duplicate implementations. They add navigation context to previously reviewed sources, not evidence that those issues remain open. For 2D adoption, prioritize cross-path consistency of palette evaluation, export settings and interactive preview state over copying GMT's 3D camera/gizmo framework. Retained objects or old diagnostic arrays alone do not prove an unbounded memory leak; inspect ownership, replacement and repeated-operation behavior before using that label. No runtime failure, GPU speedup or new third-party implementation is claimed from this archival map.

### Archived audit protocol: what its validation records can establish

Fully read plans/overnight-audit/PROTOCOL.md (416 lines), including both run amendments, verification tiers, finding/result schemas, concurrency incidents and the final cross-cutting sweep queue. This is the operating procedure of an earlier GMT audit, not authorization to execute its commands, spawn agents, change GMT, commit, schedule work or adopt its historical subscription assumptions. Its references to prior test results are claims about that run; no tests were executed while reading this document.

Its most useful contribution to RFF shader adoption is the distinction between a passing command and a check that actually exercises the intended rendering path. The protocol records tests that succeeded with missing input corpora, source scans with no assertion, and browser tests aimed at sibling apps that did not import the relevant code. These historical examples do not establish that the current guards remain broken. They do establish why this report must not treat a generic build, a generated shader string, or a passing unrelated test as proof of visual correctness. For a future RFF change, identify the exact affected Vulkan pipeline and exercise the feature on and off, verify that the intended cases actually ran, and inspect image differences appropriate to the claimed benefit. A case-count floor catches an empty or reduced matrix but cannot by itself prove that the right cases or assertions were retained.

For 3D-to-2D ideas, tests must cover the adapted operation rather than a superficially similar source operation. A raymarched 3D shadow check does not validate a 2D height-field shadow approximation; a shader compile check does not demonstrate that dithering reduces banding; and a palette preview test does not establish export parity. Preserve high-precision Mandelbrot results and separately evaluate downstream appearance. Where only static source evidence exists, keep the proposed benefit conditional rather than presenting it as a measured improvement.

The protocol also records loss of findings that existed only in agent return messages and two ways concurrent staging mixed unrelated work. Those are workflow lessons, not RFF product features. This review therefore persists its findings and source hashes in the report and coverage ledger, but does not inherit the protocol's old coverage totals or treat annotations marked invariant as proof. Its unresolved mesh-bound and loadScene claims remain historical pointers; this document alone neither confirms nor reopens them as current defects. No additional GMT repair tasks arise from this review.

### Salvaged shader-contract diff: mesh declarations are a distinct valid path

Fully read the 177-line text patch plans/overnight-audit/salvage/g02-partial-cycle6.diff, recovering the long table rows separately where output truncation obscured them. Although the inventory originally classified this extension as a binary asset, it is a readable unified diff affecting the uniform-contract document and ShaderBuilder comments, not an additional executable shader implementation. It was not applied.

The patch's strongest wording is superseded by current source. Its added comment says the only legitimate builder.addUniform use is a backingOnly uniform. Current engine-gmt/engine/ShaderBuilder.ts explicitly also permits Mesh declarations because that variant begins with a smaller uniform preamble. Rechecked engine-gmt/features/weave.ts: inject returns unless variant is Mesh, then emits each parameter's uniform with its vector type or float. The main variants obtain these declarations through the schema-generated chunk. Thus, the present mesh path is a concrete counterexample to treating backingOnly as the sole legitimate use. The current method still stores entries with Map.set(name, {type,arraySize}), so a later same-name builder entry replaces the earlier metadata; schema collision checks do not inspect those separate calls.

For RFF, the useful adaptation is to validate the complete interface of each actual pipeline variant, including arrays, types and resource bindings, rather than checking only one common declaration list. A compact offscreen or auxiliary pass may legitimately consume fewer resources than the main pass. Avoid deriving descriptor-layout expectations from a filename, UI parameter list or source comment alone. This applies equally to 2D color, blur, relief and export paths; it does not require adopting GMT's text-based shader builder.

The patch also documents different header ordering in main versus physics/histogram templates. Current comments retain that distinction, but label the uniform assertions as assumptions and include the Mesh exception. A macro-only current caller does not establish that arbitrary future header functions would be safe at every insertion point. If RFF introduces shared generated shader snippets, define their dependencies and compile the affected variants; do not infer correctness from main-pass success. The patch's historical WebGL probe is not a probe repeated by this review and gives no direct Vulkan validation. This is an adoption constraint, not a request to repair or restore the archived GMT patch.

### Gradient Explorer design-token snapshot: preserve semantic state, not fixed colors

Fully read plans/ge-v2-figma/tokens.json (249 lines), covering every color, radius, spacing, typography and size entry. Its own description and the companion hero-spec.md caveat identify these values as a snapshot of a runtime-generated light-gray theme, not the application's authoritative theme generator. Consequently, copying its hexadecimal colors or pixel dimensions into RFF would not reproduce the live system across settings or display scales.

The useful transferable distinction is semantic: selected, live-source, baked/edited, next-pick target and kept/favorite are different states. If RFF extends its palette workflow, preserve the difference between a deterministic recipe, an editable result and an actively selected target. A changed panel color cannot substitute for persistence of the actual recipe/seed and edit state. Do not change frozen recipe generation or reuse preset IDs to accommodate a UI convention. The file's green/amber/violet suggestions are optional visual encodings, not shader inputs or evidence of accessibility; meaningful states need a readable label or other non-color cue.

The recorded expanded, empty-source and quiet hero heights describe a particular layout, including a roughly 900 ms pointer-triggered quiet mode. They are not rendering optimizations, and the supplied metadata does not establish that layout contraction improves RFF interaction. Retaining the last gradient while a newly selected source is empty is useful only if the displayed result and pending source are clearly distinguished; otherwise users may save a look they believe came from the new source. Apply that state-consistency principle to any future RFF live palette preview without importing GMT's fixed layout. This file adds no shader mechanism or performance claim, and no interface was changed or tested.

Reviewed all ten engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/fixtures/*.txt inputs by decoding their complete custom-base64 blocks with the repository parser, inspecting all exposed header, light, palette and addon fields, and reading all text outside the encoded block. A scratch-only diagnostic saved the decoded records under debug/gmt-audit. All ten decoded raw byte arrays survived encode/decode byte-exactly. This checks codec self-consistency on these inputs, not independent correctness of every field offset, interpretation of opaque bytes, successful formula transpilation or rendered equivalence with Mandelbulb3D. No scene was rendered.

| Fixture | Decoded bytes | Formula slots and iteration counts |
|---|---:|---|
| arcimboldo | 1602 | Amazing Box 32; Menger3 4; Hopf4D 41; _CelticMode 29 |
| asymmetric-amazingbox | 1413 | _AmazingBox 7; _Transform 1; Amazing Surf 1 |
| ds_00 | 1413 | Amazing Box 9; _SinY 0; Menger3 1 |
| ds_01 | 1413 | Amazing Box 32; Menger3 1; _Rotate 1 |
| ds_02 | 1602 | OctKoch 4; Folding Int Pow 2; empty index -1 slot 0; MengerIFS 1 |
| ds_03 | 1413 | Amazing Box 1; _Rotate 1; Menger3 1 |
| ds_04 | 1602 | Mandalay-KIFS 1; Menger3 3; empty index -1 slot 0; Amazing Box 1 |
| hybrid-intern-demo | 1224 | Amazing Box 2; unnamed built-in index 1 slot 1 |
| menger3-decompiled | 1038 | Menger3 1 |
| singleslot-amazingbox | 1038 | Amazing Box 1 |

All report block version 18, header mandId 44, addon version 16 and bailout radius-squared 1024. Global iteration limits span 14 to 2000 and differ from each slot's repetition count. The asymmetric fixture uses 5000-square output and a 37.5-degree field of view; arcimboldo uses 5680-square output and a five-degree field of view; the remaining eight use 1400 by 840 and 30 degrees. Their stored navigation matrices are scaled bases, not interchangeable with the zero-valued world-rotation fields. These settings describe source data, not validated target camera mappings.

The fixtures expose several important import boundaries. A named slot can have zero repetitions, and an empty index -1 slot can retain nonzero option-array values, including very small values in ds_02. Conversely, hybrid-intern-demo has a nonempty built-in formula identity despite an empty name. Parse all storage faithfully, but derive execution from the actual identity, activation, option-count and sequencing contracts; do not execute a slot merely because its array contains numbers or discard a built-in merely because its name is blank. Stale values beyond optionCount occur in several records and are not automatically active parameters. This is especially relevant to any optional future RFF formula/preset importer; it is not a reason to alter Mandelbrot's existing iteration semantics or MPA.

The appearance fields also separate data channels that a lossy mapping could collapse. Every fixture supplies ten diffuse/specular color-stop pairs; diffuse and specular colors are often different. ds_00 has all six lights enabled, including three positional lights and a specular exponent of two in one slot, so a simplified three-light target cannot preserve all source lighting automatically. Other fixtures include disabled lights with meaningful positions/colors. None of these decoded light slots has its hard-shadow flag set. The three reduced/demo fixtures share the entire decoded appearance-field set with ds_03, which makes them useful for separating formula changes from appearance changes, but no image comparison has been performed.

For RFF's 2D relief, independently adjustable diffuse palette and highlight color are a possible artistic extension, provided their compositing space and intensity controls are explicit. A full MB3D material/light model is neither required nor automatically equivalent to that extension. Keep exact recipe/map data separate from imported appearance approximations, identify any unsupported lights or formula operations, and preserve source precision where applicable. The fixture named decompiled is test data, not evidence of a license grant for a decompiled implementation. No third-party formula code was copied into RFF.

### Embedded MB3D samples: material channels and honest transfer boundaries

Reviewed the complete `engine-gmt/utils/mb3d/sampleScenes.ts` wrapper and decoded all 43 embedded payloads. Each is 1,976 bytes (840-byte header, eight-byte addon header, six 188-byte slots), and each round-trips to its original standard-base64 string. Inspected parsed camera, iteration, Julia, lighting, color-stop, hybrid and active-slot option fields; checked all exposed numeric fields for non-finite values (none). These checks establish data consistency under GMT's parser, not independent verification of every binary offset, fidelity to MB3D rendering, or meaning for every reserved byte. The parser supplies version 18 for binary input; this is not a version marker independently recovered from each payload.

The catalog contains 258 physical formula slots, of which 99 have positive iteration counts and nonnegative formula indices. Some meaningful stacks have `formulaCount == 0`; others carry inactive named slots. The current parser deliberately reads all six physical slots. There are 331 nonzero values beyond the declared per-slot option counts, including extremely large finite numbers in Getting Loopy's unused option storage. A blanket finiteness check therefore cannot substitute for respecting active fields and formula schemas. This is a compatibility lesson for any future RFF importer, not a request to alter GMT or to port these 3D recurrences into RFF's precision-sensitive Mandelbrot/MPA computation.

The samples expose 77 active lights, including six positional lights, and zero active hard-shadow flags. They contain 370 differing diffuse/specular color pairs among 430 stored anchors. `material colors` includes black diffuse regions with near-white specular colors; `Wada basin - Reflect test` uses black diffuse anchors and pale specular anchors throughout. Conversely, Ozosphere and Surreal shell use matching neutral channels. This supports independent control of base and highlight appearance, but does not establish that every channel survives GMT conversion: `mapLighting.ts::mapColoring` builds the gradient from `colorDif`, clamps positions, removes nearby equal-color duplicates and applies a saturation gate. Its own comments identify external-map and fidelity limitations. RFF should preserve authored neutral palettes and explicit equal-position-stop semantics if adding an importer; GMT's heuristic gate is not a general palette rule.

**RFF delta, not a duplicate feature proposal:** current `shdsrc/vk_slope.frag` already has independent specular RGB/intensity/direction, and `shdsrc/studio_surface.glsl` has a material-lighting path. The additional candidate illustrated by these data is an optional **spatially varying highlight-color ramp**, sampled from an explicitly chosen stable relief/color coordinate, separate from the base palette. Evaluate both ramps in their declared color spaces and combine lighting in the selected compositing path; do not silently change existing palette recipes or defaults. This is directly applicable to RFF's 2D relief rendering because it needs a scalar coordinate and the existing surface normal, whereas true reflection, visibility and multi-bounce transport need extra scene information. Treat a black-base/bright-highlight preset as an artistic material test, not evidence that a flat 2D iteration map supports MB3D ray-traced reflections. Useful acceptance cases are flat normals, sharp boundary masks, neutral base colors, duplicate ramp positions and palette cycling; no such GPU comparison was executed in this review.

Read all entries in `plans/overnight-audit/worklist.json`, `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/state/progress.json` and `docs/history/audit-2026-05-20/state/phase-2-carry-in.json`. The carry-in explicitly records refuted survey claims, aspirational APIs, changing subsystem boundaries and hashes synthesized after the original review. Its priority labels are not RFF priorities.

The useful adoption constraint is to follow the exact implementation and its consumers. In particular, the generic and GMT `UniformSchema.ts` modules select different feature registries (`./features` versus `../features`); superficially similar code is not sufficient evidence that they can be replaced by one re-export. Their previously completed source reviews remain the evidence for the respective behavior. The generic schema now explicitly documents throwing on uniform-name collisions, so the older carry-in description of silent collision handling cannot be presented as its current behavior. For RFF, the corresponding requirement is agreement between the concrete C++ pipeline layout and each GLSL variant, plus explicit classification of runtime parameter changes versus changes requiring a pipeline rebuild. Historical descriptions of hook counts or depth sentinels must not become copied constants or supposed current defects without checking the relevant path.

This batch adds no shader effect and does not change the visual-benefit ranking. It strengthens the report's separation between GMT implementation evidence, historical design rationale, and a proposed RFF change. In particular, browser/Three.js cleanup items are not substitutes for improving RFF's Vulkan renderer, and 3D camera/focus behavior alone supplies no depth model for a 2D Mandelbrot image.

### Gradient amendment plan: preserve editable intent, distinguish historical proposals

Read `plans/gradient-explorer-amendments-plan.md` in full, including its later decision overrides. It is a June planning record, not a current feature inventory. The current `palette/core/gmtGradient.ts` already re-exports the canonical engine sampler and documents ramp-native gradients; current `generatorPipeline.ts::buildColorBoxRamp` already implements separate OKLCh channel easings, shortest-path hue interpolation, nonnegative chroma and gamut mapping. Thus the plan's former missing-feature descriptions must not be repeated as present GMT gaps. Its older instruction to fit incoming ramps also cannot override the newer explicit ramp representation.

For RFF, the strongest authoring lesson is to retain the original editable representation and make approximation explicit. Keep authored stops, interpolation modes and bias when transferring a gradient; do not unnecessarily reconstruct them from a 256-sample raster. If a ramp-to-curve fit is offered, show the original sampled channels and prospective fitted curve together and commit replacement explicitly. Changing fit detail should not silently erase hand edits. A shader preview and its editor should sample the same accepted gradient definition, with explicit distinction between authoring space, interpolation space and output transfer function. GMT's fixed 256-sample authoring choice is not a recommendation to reduce RFF palette precision or resolution.

The plan withdraws its own inexpensive two-point monotone-cubic proposal. Current `sampleSorted` applies bias and then uses `t*t*(3-2*t)` for both `smooth` and `cubic`; this is a two-endpoint interpolation weight, not a neighbor-aware cubic spline. Adding a differently named identical branch would not produce a new capability. Conversely, bounded interpolation weights alone do not prove that a path through a perceptual color space remains inside the display gamut; gamut handling remains a separate requirement. A future neighbor-aware spline must define endpoint tangents, repeated stop positions, cyclic seams and overshoot behavior, and preserve the old modes' outputs.

Other transferable design ideas are one undo entry per completed edit gesture, saving the complete authoring document rather than only scalar controls, stable saved-palette identities with explicit update/save-as-new behavior, and an explicit current-frame snapshot when exporting animated colors. These are editor and persistence improvements supporting shader use, not new GPU effects. In RFF they must respect frozen palette recipe IDs/RNG ordering and append-only configuration rules. Spatial preview geometries (radial, angular or mirrored ramp displays) can help choose palettes for 2D coloring, but changing the preview geometry should not mutate the palette or be mistaken for a new fractal formula. No implementation or runtime validation is claimed for these RFF candidates.

### Public DEC payload: exact equivalence to the reviewed reference implementations

The complete `public/formulas/dec.json` contains 315 records with exactly the `id`, `author` and `code` fields. Every decoded GLSL string and author label is case-sensitive identical to its uniquely matching entry in the already fully reviewed 339-entry `engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/random-formulas.ts`. Both current file hashes match the audit inventory. Thus the reference implementation analysis above covers all public DEC shader bodies, not merely their identifiers or metadata. The public catalog omits 24 reference entries; this comparison does not establish why they were excluded. The first 80 public bodies were additionally read directly; completion of the remaining bodies relies on exact-content equivalence to the reviewed reference, not a new shader execution.

The useful RFF distinction is between a procedural field and an observable coloring channel. Repeated absolute-value folds, coordinate swaps, periodic wrapping and reciprocal-radius scaling generate geometry or scalar fields. A final distance-like value divided by accumulated scale is not automatically an exact signed distance or a valid Mandelbrot derivative. These constructions can inform optional planar patterns or relief inputs, but do not replace RFF's perturbation recurrence or MPA. A return expression using `p.xy` can still depend on Z through earlier transformations.

Two concrete material mechanisms merit retaining in the adoption design. `fractal_de8` accumulates a minimum squared radius in `orb`, but does not return or consume it: orbit-based coloring needs an explicitly exported observable and a defined stage at which it is sampled. `fractal_de93` compares two terminal primitive distances and writes a branch selector through `escape`; a corresponding RFF material mask should come from the same branch decision used to construct the field, rather than an unrelated second evaluation. These are data-contract ideas, not evidence that GMT provides a ready-made postprocess pass. Orbit observables also require accounting for iterations skipped by MPA before promising equivalent coloring.

Smooth folds such as `fractal_de17` and rounded absolute values such as `fractal_de19` change the procedural shape; they are not substitutes for filtering over a pixel footprint. Cell-dependent rotations or iteration counts can create discontinuities and variable work. Multioctave sine products need footprint-aware attenuation if adapted as a surface pattern. In particular, the zero-Z slice of `fractal_de108` makes its sine-product contribution vanish, illustrating why a 3D formula cannot be advertised as a useful 2D port solely by setting Z to zero. Choose an explicit slice, a separate planar recurrence, or an independently defined height field and evaluate that choice on its own terms.

This closes the public DEC source payload review without adding a new priority solely for catalog size. No shader was compiled, no GPU timing or image comparison was performed, and author labels remain provenance leads rather than verified adaptation licenses.

### Core palette payload: reconstruction, discontinuities and repeat semantics

Fully decompressed `public/palette/core.json.gz` and `core.bin.gz`, validated every metadata record and reconstructed every channel of all 2,952 ramps using the Sub-filter reversal in `palette/core/catalogLoader.ts`. The payload is 2,267,136 bytes: 2,952 rows of 256 RGB8 samples, each row occupying 768 bytes. Those stored bytes are channel differences after the first sample, not directly displayable RGB colors. Re-encoding every reconstructed row reproduced the original decompressed bytes exactly. Metadata has unique IDs, five finite normalized facets per entry, finite hue descriptors, and valid bundle/collection links. All 74 collection labels, credit strings and recorded license tags were inspected. This is complete data traversal and reconstruction, not a visual assessment of every ramp or independent verification of upstream license claims.

The payload contains 2,485 PyPalettes, 377 uiGradients, 55 Matplotlib and 35 ColorBrewer entries. Its ten-bundle manifest and counts intentionally describe sources across all groups; they do not mean the core binary contains the optional or non-commercial packs. The decoder supplies opaque alpha. All 2,952 reconstructed RGB ramps have distinct byte content and none is constant. Only 19 have identical first and last RGB samples. Forty-two contain an adjacent-sample change above 64/255 in at least one channel. For example, the stored `tab10` ramp has ten unique colors and a largest adjacent channel jump of 224/255. Such transitions may be intentional categorical boundaries; these measurements are not a defect count or a perceptual distance score.

For RFF's 2D coloring, imported sampled ramps should preserve their sample order, quantization and source identity separately from any editable approximation. Do not force every imported ramp through a small stop set or assume that its endpoints form a seamless cycle. Expose repeat behavior independently from interpolation: wrapping can introduce a large boundary transition, while optional endpoint blending changes the artwork and belongs in a user-selected transform. Likewise, nearest/discrete sampling preserves categorical divisions; linear interpolation softens them, and pixel-footprint filtering addresses minification rather than proving the original ramp was smooth. An endpoint match alone does not establish derivative continuity. These mechanisms transfer directly to 2D palette lookup and also apply to 3D material ramps.

The compact RGB8 catalog representation is useful for previews and storage, but it is not a reason to reduce RFF's internal color or calculation precision. Retain existing stable recipe IDs and RNG order; represent imported data through an explicit compatible persistence path instead of changing historical recipe generation. Palette-file metadata includes two collections tagged unverified (`wanteeed.com` and `data-to-viz.com`), alongside numerous differing recorded terms. Keep collection-level provenance visible and verify original sources before actual adoption; this inspection does not endorse copying the entire core pack. No source palettes or rendering code were added to RFF.
