### Documentation disposition matrix: preserve mechanisms, not obsolete performance claims

Read every rationale and preservation field in `docs/history/doc-audit-state/phase-2-disposition.json`, plus its header, metadata, targets and summary. Its 87 unique document records reproduce the declared totals: 51 preserve-with-pointer, 18 keep-as-is, 10 minor-edits, seven rewrite and one migrate-target. All 106 evidence references resolve to already reviewed files. The May 20 matrix includes old `dev/docs/` paths and instructions for a different documentation project; it neither directs edits in this review nor establishes present implementation status. Statements that an older doc is canonical or that a feature shipped are dated source claims requiring current-source confirmation.

The most useful shader lesson retained here is to preserve the assumptions behind a technique. In stochastic volumetric work, a spatially constant fallback seed can make many pixels take the same sampling decision; a random-looking formula alone does not establish useful spatial decorrelation. For any analogous stochastic RFF surface effect, define the noise source, pixel coordinate system, seed and temporal policy together. Preserve deterministic export behavior, and assess both noise appearance and convergence if the effect accumulates samples. This is applicable to a 2D effect only when it actually uses stochastic sampling; it is not a reason to add volume transport to the Mandelbrot renderer.

The matrix also emphasizes full-output coordinates for tiled work: camera/aspect conventions, sample positions and noise origins must describe the same image across tiles. Local neighbor effects need their separately defined border treatment. A global pixel origin addresses coordinate-dependent noise seams but does not by itself solve blur, chromatic displacement or other neighborhood sampling boundaries. These distinctions remain useful to RFF's 2D export pipeline and are already reflected in the report's tile/preview validation proposals.

Historical shader benchmarks in the referenced material are explicitly tied to ANGLE/D3D11/fxc, specific compiler behavior and previously discovered measurement mistakes. They are not Vulkan speed predictions. Likewise, small epsilon constants can alter a sharp specular lobe substantially; any optimization of such math must preserve the intended response and RFF's precision requirements. Formula-import AST success, target compilation, finite samples and nondegenerate images are separate checks; even their combination does not prove equivalent 2D recurrence semantics or compatibility with MPA. The document's own retracted animation-performance hypotheses reinforce this measurement discipline rather than supporting an unrelated RFF refactor.

No new runtime results were produced in this batch. The matrix contributes rationale and verification requirements; its old benchmark percentages, browser support tables, proposed APIs and rewrite commands are not adopted as current facts or RFF implementation work.

The container reports ten seconds. All 250 decoded frames were processed with passthrough timing and per-frame checksums; no decode errors were reported. Twenty temporally sampled images were inspected as a 4×5 contact sheet at 320×180 per sample. This is full-stream decoding plus sampled visual inspection, not a claim to have individually examined every frame at native resolution.

The sampled sequence shows a bright cloudy sky, a pale hazy horizon and a dense dark terrain-like foreground, with changes in the cloud pattern across time. These are visible results, not proof of a particular lighting integrator. Its local fractal DE uses four-component folds, scale/offset operations, optional logarithmic transforms and an orbit-trap minimum; its animation preset also names rotation amplitudes. Adjacency and matching scene vocabulary make it a useful reference, but do not prove that this shader revision and preset exactly generated the encoded clip.

For RFF's 2D renderer, the actionable decomposition is independent background appearance, a deliberately defined relief/height interpretation, and material/occlusion cues derived from that field. A 2D background or animated procedural layer is feasible without importing a 3D camera and volumetric transport; depth-dependent haze or self-shadowing requires additional meaningful geometry/height data. The foreground detail in this clip is not evidence that flat escape-time color alone contains such data. The file also illustrates why media metadata is not a benchmark: its reported average-frame-rate field is 1000/1, while the nominal rate is 25/1 and decoded timestamps span 0 to 9.96 seconds with some out-of-order values. ### Interaction rollout: distinguish source recomputation from display-only shader edits

Read all 270 lines of `plans/interaction-session-rollout.md`, including its long chronological status entries and retracted performance diagnoses. This May rollout describes a gesture-session primitive, separate autonomous animation, per-consumer adoption, cancellation/cleanup, hold timing, undo boundaries, export suppression and subsequent latency investigations. Its instructions and user-approval checkpoints belonged to that historical implementation; they do not request implementation or a new approval in this review. Reported latency and throughput values are that investigation's results, not measurements on RFF.

A particularly important current-source correction is that the final May claim of retiring accumulation-drop inference is no longer the complete behavior. Current `engine-gmt/engine/managers/UniformManager.ts` uses `sceneChangingMove = interacting && accumulationCount <= 1`, combines this with filtered camera/gizmo/scrub activity and autonomous animation, and passes `ignoreAccumDrop: false`. Its comments explain why display-only color/post-effect edits must not trigger a resize that discards the expensive source buffer. Current `FractalEngine.compute()` still composes activity with the recent invalidation wake signal and extends its filtered hold through adaptive settling. Current `renderInteractionState.ts` also recognizes enabled live audio modulation as well as LFO sources. These present implementations supersede the older phase narrative where they differ.

For RFF, this supports a concrete evaluation rule: classify an edit by the data it invalidates. If a color/material/postprocess edit can be evaluated from existing fractal data, update that stage without automatically restarting expensive fractal computation or resizing its source. An edit to the mathematical view or to required source observables may need recomputation; do not misclassify it as display-only. Reuse existing RFF behavior where it already provides this separation. This is a responsiveness opportunity and validation criterion, not a claim that RFF currently recomputes unnecessarily.

Keep gesture activity, render invalidation, autonomous animation, movement permissions and undo transactions distinct. A typed value or preset change must wake the display even though no drag is active. An active effect slider must show fresh output; adopting a global hold for every interaction would defeat that purpose. On release, coordinate resolution restoration and accumulation so expensive refinement does not begin in a buffer about to be resized. Balance cancellation, capture loss and teardown in the native input lifecycle, and treat watchdog recovery as a backstop rather than normal release handling. The concept applies directly to 2D RFF shaders; browser events, Three.js hold behavior and the recorded debounce constants are not a literal implementation prescription.

Finally, the record's early irreducible-latency explanation was later retracted in favor of a one-time allocation diagnosis, and its apparent slider-specific cost was attributed to unequal geometry and automation overhead. Preserve matched scenes, input methods and warm/cold conditions when testing an RFF change. The browser `desynchronized` throughput result is not a Vulkan present-mode recommendation. Offline export needs its own deterministic state and quality policy regardless of interactive responsiveness settings. No runtime test or shader implementation was performed in this batch.

### Overnight proposals: completed reading and RFF adoption constraints

Read all 3,174 lines of `plans/overnight-audit/PROPOSALS.md`, including later closures and corrections. This is a July/August historical decision queue, not a current GMT defect inventory. Its recommendations sometimes differ from the subsequent implementation: stepped export ultimately preserves duration by reducing encoded frame rate; the reflection controls were already driven by quality tiers; the orbit check needed a software-renderer timeout correction, not a weakened assertion. Duplicated findings here are not additional independent evidence and do not raise their priority.

For RFF shader adoption, retain the following requirements rather than porting the queue's application-specific repairs:

- **Color and parameter contracts:** keep source color interpretation, working color space, interpolation space and output encoding explicit across palette import, editing and GPU use. A conversion-boundary mistake can alter every color even when each individual conversion is internally consistent. Independent known-value checks are stronger than comparing a re-export with itself. Vulkan descriptor/push-constant layout checks must exercise actual field offsets and values; a future generated effect graph should allocate stable parameter identities rather than allocate a new slot each time an expression reads a parameter.
- **Dependency-aware invalidation:** a structural change includes connections and input ordering, not just node values. Display-only shader edits should reuse valid fractal data; edits requiring new mathematical observables must invalidate that data deliberately. Changing a refinement budget is a separate policy from invalidating an already better image. These are design criteria, not newly established RFF defects.
- **Coordinate and sampling conventions:** preserve pixel-center conventions through sampling, reconstruction and export, and distinguish per-axis coordinate extents from scalar physical distances. For a 2D relief effect, derive normals and spatial filter radii in a declared coordinate system, account for unequal pixel spacing, and preserve the same global coordinates across tiles. GMT's historical mesh problems illustrate this requirement; their literal voxel/DC repairs are not needed for flat RFF coloring.
- **Reliable shader outcomes:** distinguish requested compilation, successful pipeline creation, completed GPU work and correct visible output. An advancing frame or accumulation counter alone does not establish that the intended shader produced an image. For new RFF effects, validate output against an independent reference or meaningful image property as appropriate, and check each enabled variant rather than counting duplicate shader sources as different coverage. Parsing an imported formula is not proof of numerical correctness, valid generated shaders or compatibility with deep perturbation and MPA.
- **Deterministic animation/export:** use explicit frame time, stable seeds and a defined relation between frame skipping and output duration. Tangents and fitting tolerances for logarithmic controls must use the same domain as evaluation. A watchdog needs genuine progress and cancellation semantics; the proposal's claim that a progress-based timeout cannot abort legitimate work is too strong when a long operation emits no intermediate progress. Do not use arbitrary interactive wall-clock suppression to skip offline frames.
- **Reachable controls and preserved state:** before proposing an extra control, inspect all existing routes including presets and quality tiers. Keep persisted identifiers stable even when a visible control is retired. Gradient stop reduction should measure error at each export format's actual budget; a warning threshold for one format does not establish fidelity at another budget.

These requirements apply to 2D color/postprocessing directly and to height-field lighting when RFF supplies an explicit height interpretation. They do not justify importing GMT's entire 3D renderer, browser UI, importer or testing framework. The backlog adds no measured RFF speedup and does not change the visual-impact ranking by itself. No historical test result was rerun or presented as a current GPU measurement, and no GMT repair or RFF shader implementation was performed in this batch.

### Development history cross-check (partial: lines 1–610)

Read lines 1–610 of `docs/CHANGELOG_DEV.md`; the remainder is still pending. The September entries explicitly supersede several July backlog descriptions: node parameter reads were hoisted, edge-aware structural keys replaced node-only comparisons, compilation failure gained a separate signal, export gained sample-loop heartbeats, and guard tooling changed. The September 1 environment-sampling explanation reinforces section H's distinction between reconstruction and minification. In the current `engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/lighting/env.ts`, cubic B-spline reconstruction combines four bilinear samples with compensating weights. Its auxiliary tap coordinates jump at texel boundaries even though the reconstructed result is continuous. Using derivatives of those tap coordinates for implicit mip selection therefore introduces a false footprint. Explicit base-level taps remove that particular artifact; they do not by themselves solve minification. The separate `envConeLod` computes a texel span from the angular footprint (including longitude compression near the poles), takes its base-two logarithm, and combines that demand with the roughness demand using the larger level. Current source was rechecked for both mechanisms.

For RFF's 2D image layers and procedural fields, estimate the footprint from the underlying mapping before wrap/fold/reconstruction discontinuities. Do not copy the environment's spherical conversion or roughness term into ordinary 2D image sampling. Fragment and compute paths need explicitly compatible footprint policies; temporal accumulation cannot be assumed to remove a repeatable wrong sampling decision. The changelog's compile/GPU timing numbers belong to GMT's historical experiment and are not RFF benchmarks. This confirms the existing footprint-filtering proposal rather than adds a duplicate effect.

The palette history gives a complementary responsiveness rule: show the authoritative sampled ramp during live edits, rather than repeatedly converting ramp to fitted stops and resampling an approximation. Recoloring held stop positions is insufficient when a curve edit moves features along the ramp. Reuse sorted stops and decoded colors across a batch of samples instead of sorting/parsing per texel. An exact ramp preview and editable stop controls can have different update policies, but stale controls should not falsely describe the currently displayed ramp. Preserve RFF's frozen palette recipe generation; such preview optimizations must not change saved recipe reconstruction.

Finally, the recorded geometry preview speedup used a GPU mirror during interaction while retaining the existing settled-frame dithering path. Its numerical equivalence and speed figures are specific to that CPU-to-WebGL transfer; RFF already uses Vulkan and must not be promised the same gain. Likewise, image-sequence filenames require timeline-frame identity while video timestamps and progress may require sequential output indices. Keep those domains separate. ### Development changelog completed: estimator semantics and 2D transfer

Completed lines 611–1,759 of `docs/CHANGELOG_DEV.md`, completing the file. One oversized output was truncated; the affected 831–1,030 range was reread in smaller complete batches. The chronology contains mutually superseding designs (for example, decoupled simulation resolution followed by unified render sizing, and successive light-direction conventions). Treat each entry as a dated record, not simultaneous current requirements. Source-level mechanisms already reviewed elsewhere remain authoritative.

**Average the intended observable.** The fluid example moved palette color and coverage evaluation inside the per-sample work, then accumulated those values. In general, applying a nonlinear palette to an averaged iteration/escape/orbit value is not equivalent to averaging the corresponding colors. For RFF, this supports color/coverage-aware antialiasing and rough refraction, while retaining raw precise fractal data separately for recoloring. It is not permission to replace or blur the mathematical map. Means of depth, normals, iteration counts and coverage have different meanings; designate attachment semantics explicitly. A matte or data pass should bypass beauty-only bloom, tone mapping and grading unless the output contract deliberately specifies otherwise.

**Relief/refraction is the practical 3D-to-2D subset.** A smoothed height gradient can drive a 2D displacement and normal-based lighting; a small disk kernel can broaden the refracted image for a frosted appearance. Color and coverage must sample consistent displaced footprints, with valid boundary handling. Wider finite-difference spacing alone is not a general smoothing filter. The historical equal-weight eight-neighbor Laplacian reduces some axis preference relative to a four-neighbor stencil but is not exactly rotationally invariant; the prose claim of no axis bias should not be imported as a guarantee. These are artistic height-field approximations, not volumetric caustics or a physically complete refractive transport solution.

**Keep the 3D estimator distinct.** GMT's area-light record distinguishes point-light shadow jitter from explicit sphere-light sampling, hard visibility per sampled emitter direction, BSDF sampling and MIS weighting. The same record leaves an unbiasedness benchmark pending. Do not claim validated unbiased transport or a transferable twofold RFF speedup. Full sphere-light MIS needs geometric intersections and consistent probability densities; a flat 2D palette has neither. Use the material/normal and relief subset first. The historical roulette change described as decorrelation is also not proof of statistical independence merely because it transforms a reused random value.

**Preserve sample validity across interaction and export.** Bilinear reprojection of an old accumulation buffer may provide a useful temporary preview, but it does not manufacture independent samples at a higher resolution. Do not retain a sample count as proof of new-resolution convergence without a justified estimator policy. Define effect radii in output-pixel or explicit scene units, preserve global coordinates through tiles, and apply spatial postprocessing to the composite or supply sufficient tile overlap. Region-average convergence can miss small detailed failures and cannot replace crispness checks. Store-to-render coalescing must preserve pending invalidation/synchronization obligations even when newer numeric values replace older ones.

**Do not adopt historical shortcuts as RFF guarantees.** GMT's LA/AT acceleration is separate from RFF's periodic-structure MPA; the changelog's depth and speed claims neither benchmark RFF nor justify reducing its precision. Inserting timestamps into shader source to defeat caches is not a default optimization recommendation. Replacing a gradient interpolation default may preserve file readability while changing saved appearance: new RFF interpolation options must preserve old recipe/output semantics. The Oklab-labelled entry actually describes polar Oklch interpolation with an achromatic fallback; its claim to preserve lightness/chroma is not a guarantee of gamut safety. Historical compiler lowering claims such as every ternary becoming one GPU operation are not portable performance evidence.

This completes the changelog inspection without introducing shader code or inheriting its historical runtime tests. It reinforces the existing RFF recommendations on independent field mappings, filtered image sampling, relief/material shading, deterministic output and truthful quality state.

### Handoff completed: shader sampling, state identity and round-trip fidelity

Completed `HANDOFF.md` through its final line (the inventory counts 1,204 lines including the terminal newline). Lines 481–1,203 were read in complete batches. All earlier partial status notes are superseded. The document retains April extraction scaffolding beneath September release history; its remaining-work list, deleted feature descriptions and commands are not current instructions or a current feature census.

**3D sampling mechanisms and the portability boundary.** The reflection record describes a two-stage environment CDF: per-row luminance-times-sine totals form a marginal distribution, with a conditional distribution across each row. Direction sampling and PDF evaluation must use matching environment rotation and the spherical-coordinate Jacobian. Environment NEE and BSDF-hit contributions use complementary MIS weights; the density must match the actual diffuse/specular mixture. Sobol direction samples address one sampling dimension, not every stochastic decision. The sphere-light record separately requires emitter intersection, finite-area PDF conversion, hard visibility to the sampled surface, and the originating bounce's material state. Its own variance and unbiasedness benchmarks were still pending: shader emission and successful compilation alone did not establish those properties. These are reference mechanisms for future genuine 3D transport, not directly useful replacements for RFF's flat 2D palette lookup. Relief normals and controlled environment shading remain the smaller transferable subset already ranked in this report.

**Precompute only invariants, with explicit semantics.** GMT moved parameter-only MB3D rotation matrices out of repeated marching work into derived uniforms, carrying units/order and bank assignments across serialization and worker messages. The RFF counterpart is to hoist truly frame-constant artistic transforms where profiling warrants it and preserve exact C++/GLSL layout and conventions. Do not hoist orbit-dependent values or change sensitive perturbation precision. Same-named fractal formulas are not evidence of mathematical equivalence; a transpiler's finite random cross-checks also do not prove equivalence over all inputs or preserve an extended-precision execution model.

**Values, animation targets and capabilities form one contract.** Reordering parameter banks must move keyframes and modulation targets with the same simultaneous mapping used for values, including displaced/deleted targets. Saved shader capabilities must survive parse, registration and worker transfer; supporting a file's syntax is not sufficient when its estimator or shader body is lost. For RFF, optional future effects need stable identities and deterministic save/load behavior, subject to its append-only ConfigIO and frozen recipe rules rather than GMT's specific migration format.

**Verify complete state transitions and real timing.** The repeated custom-formula loading repairs show why boot, normal file load, embedded-image load and quick-save entry points must all preserve the same state. A full configuration and precise viewpoint must reach the renderer before publishing the new frame. Likewise, a setting sent before engine initialization may need an explicit post-initialization synchronization. Accumulation suppression must reach the actual rendering controller; a UI flag that never crosses the worker boundary cannot protect buffers from resizing/reset. The handoff's audio performance hypotheses were later corrected and remained unresolved; CPU frame counters and dispatch timing are not GPU timing. These observations support the report's RFF validation plan, not an assertion that the corresponding defects exist in RFF.

### Unified-shell plan completed: exact neutral edits and palette diagnostics

Completed the remaining lines 1,661–2,858 of `plans/ge-v2-unified-shell-plan.md` in full batches (inventory line count 2,859 includes the terminal newline). Earlier partial-reading notes are superseded. This completes the last pending inventory file; report consolidation and final source-inventory verification remain separate tasks.

**A useful authoring extension: procedural channel filters.** The recorded wave tool reuses sampled curve fitting and span splicing to apply sine/triangle/saw/pulse/noise functions to one color channel. Each preview derives from the snapshot at tool activation, not the previous preview, preventing cumulative drift. One transaction covers the session; cancel restores the original before closing it. Strength is a wet/dry envelope multiplying the difference between base and target, separate from waveform amplitude. Zero strength must bypass approximate refitting and preserve the original keys exactly. These mechanisms could support optional RFF palette authoring without modifying the Mandelbrot map or historical recipe generation.

**Local curve edits need valid joins.** Replacing a span can leave neighboring manually authored Bezier arms longer than the new gap. The recorded splice fix clamps the retained seam-facing arm and sets the replacement arm to compatible lengths; a monotone x control polygon is sufficient to prevent a newly introduced backward fold under those assumptions. It is not a guarantee for arbitrary pre-existing manually folded curves. A generic pre-bake would increase key count and hide rather than remove the join condition.

**Color-space and quantization conditions matter.** Channel metadata needs explicit units, angular wrapping, role and fitting tolerance; HSV percentages are not normalized values, and identically named L/C/h axes cannot identify both CIE LCh and OkLCh. Switching representation with clipping/refitting can change the palette and should be undoable. The later stop-fitting correction rejects a universal small perceptual threshold for 8-bit steps: dark sRGB quantization can create much larger OkLab differences than midtone quantization. A local, direction-aware quantization floor should be checked both against false dark bands and against real subtle bands. Those are relevant test cases for RFF dithering and fitting, not proof that any one GMT threshold is universally perceptual.

**Do not call wave presets scientific certification.** A monotone lightness-channel wave alone does not establish a perceptually uniform sequential colormap; a cyclic wave on one channel does not ensure the full RGB endpoints and their derivatives match. HSV value is not perceptual lightness. Diverging palettes also need appropriate two-sided semantics, gamut handling and an intentional center. The prose claim that the Penner families are all covered by gamma plus sine is too broad: polynomial powers cover some in-curves, not general elastic, bounce, back or exponential/circular families. Keep preset labels descriptive rather than guarantees of accessibility or standard compliance.

**Import and UI identity complete the mechanism.** Network/storage color stops may need fresh unique local editing IDs without changing their canonical public signature; repair already-saved malformed entries as well as the importer. Rendering, hit-testing and cache keys must share geometry, while off-screen handle clamping should not silently clamp the authored value. The plan records real-app export checks by its owner, but those are historical reports, not tests run in this audit. Several wave gestures were explicitly unguarded by its pure-math suite. No implementation, external publishing, or inherited test execution was performed here.
